Corroboration, and together they are the strongest evidence yet for the open question of how an agent comes to use reflow2's disciplines unprompted. That idea compares embedded engines on the assumption that the engine is what costs. Measured with NO engine at all — in-memory backend, no RocksDB, no tantivy — hydrate is still 8.8s at 3,140 nodes, with 95% of it inside import_graph and only 4% in JSON parsing. Whichever engine wins that comparison, it cannot move the number that matters, so the premise the comparison rests on is contradicted rather than merely unsupported.

That measurement implied the fix was more enforcement, reading the 23/23-versus-5-18 spread as an argument for checking more mechanics. This one shows the spread is not an enforcement shortfall but a SCOPE limit: every existing check asserts a universal predicate and none can express a per-class obligation, so adding exhaustive checks cannot close the gap it identified. The counts stand; the implied remedy does not.

Corroboration across two different mechanisms, same underlying shape: a discipline that is written down, correct, and read by the agent still fails at the moment it applies. One is a warning read hours before it was ignored; the other is a computation that answers correctly and cannot reach the case it was built for. Both were caught by a human noticing, not by the mechanism, and both are direct evidence for the open question of how an agent comes to use reflow2's disciplines without being prompted.

The roll-up half of this proposal IS an altitude view. Declaring a contract at the lowest level is only usable if a higher altitude can answer 'is there an interface between A and B', and that projection does not exist — so this idea is worth nothing unless that one lands first.

A factory can only guarantee mechanics somebody has named. Until the class contract question is answered — which axes, obliging what — there is nothing for a factory to build in, so this is worth nothing until that one lands.

That requirement establishes a design as a unit that composes with the designs around it, which is the ground the hub relation stands on. The hub case asks for a THIRD composition mode beside peer linking and merging — ownership and roll-up without absorption — so it extends that requirement rather than contradicting it, and is unbuildable without it.

An address through the spine only means anything because that requirement already demands nesting as deep as the design needs. Without recursive containment there is no path to address, so this idea rests entirely on that requirement holding.

A view that slices by ALTITUDE needs to know what the altitudes ARE, and this decision is what settles that. It is the precise dependency: the altitude view is the missing half of the lowest-level-contract rule (that rule is accepted, its roll-up view is not built), and an open ladder means the rungs it projects onto are per-design rather than a fixed five. ⚠️ AND IT IS NOT ONLY A VIEW: `seam_coverage` ALREADY takes an altitude argument and answers differently per rung — 72/8/64 at module, 11/11/0 at subsystem — so at least one shipped tool keys on the ladder today. That dependency is NOT in the five unsettled items listed on the ladder decision and belongs there.

Option (a) here — a proxy-injected identity header — runs into that decision's recorded rejection of deriving identity from request headers. The objection was about the MCP client's OWN headers, which are caller-supplied, and a trusted proxy's injected header is a different object; but this option cannot be taken without that distinction being made deliberately, and option (b) is that decision's mint-and-carry shape applied to contributors instead of seats.

Option (a) reads transcripts, and a script's source IS design content — the exact thing that requirement forbids carrying. Any transcript-side form of this instrument is only buildable if it can report the SHAPE of hand-rolled work without its content, so that requirement governs whether the most promising option exists at all.

The linking step is nearly free only because the search has already run — it judges the near-matches already in hand rather than sweeping for candidates. If search-before-capture ever stopped being universal, linking at capture would become an expensive extra pass and the argument for putting it in the brainstorm skill would collapse. Drawn 2026-08-21.

That Constraint IS the evidence. If it turns out to be the only budget anyone ever writes, the skill is instructing people to do something nobody does, and this node should be revisited against that.

Overconfident diagnosis — fixing a symptom while believing it is the cause — is an AI-agent failure mode, and that node asks which such modes reflow2 can actually reach as opposed to merely assert it addresses. Whether this idea is worth building turns on that answer: if this pitfall is in the class reflow2 cannot reach, a served RCA method would be the overstating failure that node warns against.

properties.evidence: Retires its framing, not its measurement. That node proposed computing the NUMBER OF LAYERS from a 3-7 span-of-control bound, treating the count as the generator of depth. Doctrine puts span of control downstream: structure is derived from grouping FUNCTIONS by cohesion and coupling, and 3-7 is the sanity check on the result. Twenty children means the functional grouping lacked an intermediate cohesion level, not that a rung is owed. Its fan-out measurements stand and remain useful as a check; its causal story does not.

The first real discontinuation, and the case that raised the question. Built, shipped, correct, used zero times in every project that had it; four served tools, the core module, the --content-path flag and both test files were removed for v0.27.0. Until this edge, the graph still said the capability was `realized`, its check `passing` and its requirements `accepted` — two days after the code was deleted. The Decision is the source because a discontinued thing has no successor to put there, which is exactly what made this look like it needed new vocabulary.

Parallel work is what turns this from an annoyance into the cost Anthony actually named. Isolation and claims stop two people COLLIDING while they work; neither tells user B that user A already FINISHED. So the more successfully two people work in parallel, the more exposed they are to duplicating a completed task — and the result is two independent implementations, which the design-record merge driver cannot reconcile because the divergence is in code, not in the graph. Drawn from the capability TO the requirement: the hazard rides on the capability succeeding.

Option (a) puts a single node with edges to everything needing attention into the same graph the structural detectors run on. Betweenness centrality, Leiden community detection and articulation-point analysis all reason about connectivity, so a worklist hub would be read as topology — reported as a god-node or a sole bridge by machinery that cannot tell a scratchpad from structure.

Both carry the same hazard from opposite directions: that node's option B was rejected because a Task type is 'the road to being a tracker', and roll-up of children's status is the portfolio-management version of the same step. Recorded so whoever weighs the hub relation meets the objection that already killed its sibling, rather than re-deriving it.

Option (b), a STORED dotted id, encodes a part's position into its identity — and that capability exists precisely so parts can be moved. Every use of it would make a stored address wrong. The idea as written threatens a capability shipped three days earlier.

That capability is aggregate-keyed on the same anti-flood argument and is backlog-shaped (33 of 85 leaf components on reflow2's own design), so a single acknowledgement would silence it permanently in exactly the way `unreviewed_ideas` was silenced. The hazard is identical and was noticed only after it shipped.

One is a hazard to the other. That requirement's overwrite refusal compares an export file's current hash against what this seat believes it last wrote there — a guard designed for an occasional deliberate act. Under continuous export with two sessions on one design, every write by one seat invalidates the other's belief, so a check meant to fire rarely runs on a hot path and would either refuse constantly or be turned off.

CONDITIONAL, and the edge exists mainly so the tension is findable: this decision is still `proposed`, so nothing is risked today. Answering it YES is what would bear on req:deterministic-core, because an ANN index is approximate by construction and embeddings need a model. Recorded 2026-08-04 because the node had NO design edges at all — its only edge was AUTHORED_BY, so propagate_from reported 0 impacted and no detector could see it (the BL-162 shape: a Decision that governs nothing is invisible). The scope is narrower than the blanket reading: the risk is real for search_design and anything feeding a gate, and materially weaker for ingest resolution, whose output under dec:ask-not-repair is a merge_candidate a human rules on rather than a verdict.

Option (b) — describe reflow2's own MCP surface — would spend the idea entirely on self-hosting, which that rule exists to resist. Recorded as a hazard on the option rather than as a reason to drop the question, because options (c) and (d) do not carry it.

That requirement rests on last_synced: the export-overwrite refusal compares a file's current content hash against what this graph believes it last wrote there. A seat hydrated from the document starts with an EMPTY last_synced map (measured: sync_status returns checked:0 against the live seat's 6 entries), so on its first export it has no baseline to refuse against. The risk is specific to a document-as-truth model and does not exist today, and it is narrow: the map is path -> content hash and could be carried in the document, kept beside it, or recomputed.

Document-as-truth rests on hydrate being faithful. This measures that it IS — 3,140/3,140 nodes and 13,167/13,390 edges unchanged, the 223 differences all one materialised default, converging to a fixed point on the second pass. So the risk it names is bounded and one-time rather than fatal: a single normalising migration, not compounding drift. It is filed as a risk rather than a clearance because the same measurement did NOT test whether accumulated store state outside the design survives the trip, which is the way this model would fail late.

That idea proposes computing required depth from a 3-7 span-of-control bound. This is the hazard it runs into: the only systems available to calibrate that bound against are organically grown, and Conway's Law — rule 3 of the very same doctrine — predicts organic growth will LOOK conformant at some boundaries without any SE having occurred. So a threshold tuned on this evidence would be fitted to what accretion produces rather than to what good decomposition needs. It does not refute the idea; it says the number cannot be calibrated from anything currently in reach, which is a reason to REPORT fan-out rather than ship a threshold.

WAS `planned` UNTIL 2026-08-11, AND THE EVIDENCE FIELD SAID SO: "nothing in the script checks the lineage chain today, so this edge records WHERE the work lands rather than claiming any of it is done." A contributor can still export twice locally; they simply cannot merge it. Calling that `full` would claim the refusal half that was decided against.

properties.description:
DECISION 4, built 2026-08-20 on Anthony's word. DISTINCT FROM the fact that measured the defect: that node is the MEASUREMENT and is now closed with valid_to; this is the REMEDY. Conflating them would leave the design unable to say whether the fix happened.

THE DEFECT, found by running the loop honestly rather than looking for it: epoch:the-declared-walls-hold was set arrived with BOTH its capabilities genuinely delivered, and arrival_delta reported both `outstanding`. Delivery required an Artifact on disk; model work produces none. `outstanding` means "nobody has said whether this was deferred or discontinued - that is the question to put to the user", so reflow2 asked a question about finished work and would ask it again every run. Re-decompositions, retirements, governance rulings and corrections all produce no file; every one would pile up as a phantom incompletion until somebody stopped scheduling that kind of work, which is most of what systems engineering is.

WHAT SHIPPED: Capability.delivery, an enum of `artifact` (default) or `model`, plus set_capability_delivery to declare it.
  · `artifact` - a file realizes it AND a check passes. Unchanged, and the case almost every capability is in.
  · `model` - the deliverable IS the design change, so the check is the whole of the evidence.

⭐ IT DECLARES THE KIND, NEVER THE SUCCESS, and that is the whole reason it is safe to let an author state it. Both kinds still demand a passing check: the declaration loosens WHICH evidence is required, never WHETHER any is. Delivery stays computed from the golden thread, there is still no `achieved` modality, and there is still no way to mark anything done. Same shape as Interface.designation and Artifact.volatility - the author says the one thing only they can know, the computation earns the rest.

🛑 THE REJECTED FIX, recorded because it was the version first proposed AND first approved, and it is wrong: inferring `model` from the ABSENCE of an artifact. The commonest reason a capability has no file is THAT NOBODY HAS BUILT IT YET. cap:graph-registry is in exactly that state today - unbuilt, unrealized - and under the inferred rule it would report DELIVERED the moment any check was pointed at it. A false green on unbuilt work, in the same dangerous direction as a detector reporting clean because it had nothing to run on. an_unbuilt_capability_with_a_passing_check_is_not_delivered pins it.

⭐ THE REMEDY IS REACHABLE FROM THE MESSAGE THE READER SEES. Fixing the rule alone would have left the declaration built, tested and invisible - the same failure found FOUR separate times on 2026-08-20. arrival_delta now names set_capability_delivery when it reports an outstanding item that HAS a passing check and nothing on disk, and stays silent when there is no check at all, because then declaring model would not help either and the suggestion would be noise. It also does not accuse: it ends by saying that if the work is simply unbuilt, `outstanding` is correct.

PROVEN ON THE CASE THAT FOUND IT, not only on fixtures: both capabilities of epoch:the-declared-walls-hold were declared `model` through the served tool against the live graph, and the increment went from two `outstanding` to two `delivered`.

STATED LIMIT, unchanged by this: an increment with nothing scheduled `required` is still reported as not ready to cut, while the plan-increments skill says `required` must be asked for and never assumed. A user following reflow2's own guidance still builds an increment reflow2 calls unscoped. That tension is recorded and NOT fixed here.
properties.name: A capability declares WHAT KIND of thing delivers it, so model work can be reported delivered

properties.description:
`set_capability_signature` writes `capability_type`, `inputs` and `outputs`, which were declared in schema/functional.yaml, indexed, documented — and set on 0 OF 170 CAPABILITIES. Not unwanted: UNWRITABLE. `add_capability` writes name, description and status, and nothing anywhere else in either crate touched them, so no project using reflow2 could record a capability's functional signature by any route the product offered.

`req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` says every element of a design is a black box with inner function AND INTERFACES. At the capability tier these two lists ARE that interface.

A SETTER, NOT THREE MORE CONSTRUCTOR PARAMETERS, for the reason `set_interface_spec` is one: a contract is enriched onto a node that already exists, usually long after it was created. `add_capability` also has 276 CALL SITES, so widening it would churn the codebase to reach three optional fields — and backfilling far outnumbers declaring at birth.

OMITTING A FIELD LEAVES IT ALONE, so two people describing the same capability from opposite ends cannot overwrite each other. AN EMPTY LIST IS A STATEMENT: 'this takes nothing in' is a real design claim about a source or a generator, and it is distinguishable from nobody having said. AN UNKNOWN CAPABILITY IS REFUSED rather than created — a typo must not mint a capability whose only content is a signature.

⚠️ NO DETECTOR FIRES WHEN A SIGNATURE IS MISSING, deliberately. 170 capabilities lack one today, so a gap apiece would put 170 findings in front of a reader overnight — the wall-of-red failure the vocabulary-coverage trial was run to avoid. This is the TOOL leg; the INSTRUCTION leg is `epoch:the-discipline-arrives-at-the-tool`.
properties.name: A capability can state what it takes in and puts out — the black-box interface at the capability tier

properties.description:
`add_change_event` takes `summary` (what changed — indexed for full text and used as the embedding field) and `rationale` (why, and the lesson), alongside the id, name, change type, subject axis and the affected list. The reasoning therefore lands in the same act as the record, and no second write is needed to make the event complete.

SATISFIED BY MAKING DECLARED FIELDS REACHABLE, not by adding vocabulary: both fields were already on the schema and only the constructor omitted them. The tool prose also states that there is no `description` field and names the two that exist, because reaching for one is the mistake both reporting projects made.
properties.name: A change event is written complete in one call — what changed, why, and what it touched

properties.description:
THREE THINGS, and the corpus had two of them while authors wrote all three into one. `name` is what a list renders; `description` is what the check IS; `findings` (new) is what a RUN found. `add_verification` gains `description`; `set_verification_status` gains `findings`; `loop_status`'s rollup shortens a long name AND says that it did. (The guard matched the OBSERVATION that named this defect and the REQUIREMENT that answers it; this is the built thing that closes both.)

⭐⭐ THE REQUIREMENT NAMED ITS OWN PRECONDITION AND THE ANSWER WAS NO. It asked, in its own words: "THE LOAD-BEARING UNCERTAINTY, to answer BEFORE building: WOULD A NEW FIELD ALONE CHANGE ANYTHING? A declared field nobody writes to leaves the corpus exactly as it is." Measured before writing any code:

    Verifications                        164
    median `name`                         76 words   (72 over 100, 17 over 300, longest 654)
    `description` — DECLARED, fulltext,
    and the node's EMBEDDING FIELD         1 use in 164

⇒ SO A `findings` FIELD ALONE WOULD HAVE BECOME THE SECOND UNUSED FIELD. The uncertainty was real and the answer sat in the corpus for anyone who counted.

⭐ AND THE ROOT CAUSE WAS REACHABILITY, NOT NEGLECT — found by reading the constructor rather than inferring from the number. `add_verification(id, name, method, level)` HAD NO PARAMETER FOR `description`. The only route was raw `create_node` and essentially nobody took it. Authors wrote reports into `name` because **`name` was the only string the constructor accepted**. The field was not ignored; it was unwritable. That is `dec:how-should-a-temporal-fact-carry-its-date-when-there-is-no-epoch` one door along — there, 112 nodes wrote an UNDECLARED property because the declared route did not fit; here, one node wrote a declared property because the route did not exist.

WHERE EACH FIELD IS WRITTEN IS THE DESIGN, not a convenience:
• `description` on the CONSTRUCTOR — what the check is, stated once.
• `findings` on `set_verification_status` — what a RUN found, restated whenever an outcome changes. Evidence belongs to a run, so it is recorded when the run produces it, by the caller holding it.
• Omitting `findings` LEAVES IT ALONE, exactly as `last_run_at` does since 2026-08-08 — re-marking a check passing without restating evidence must not erase it. Erasing is a deliberate act deserving an explicit one, the convention `set_interface_spec`, `set_decision_status` and `set_epoch_status` all state and which this function's own first line already promised.

THE ROLLUP, their second ask: `loop_status`'s `verifications.attention[]` shortens a `name` past 25 words — and carries `name_truncated`, `name_words`, and a top-level `names_truncated` note saying how many and where the full text is. ⭐ THE ANNOUNCEMENT IS THE POINT, not decoration: a silently shortened name reads as "that is the whole name", a vacuous zero one layer over, and it is the SIXTH of Anthony's own engineering principles — no silent caps or truncation. Truncating without fixing reachability would have been the stopgap `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap` forbids; cause and symptom were fixed together.

⚠️ BOUNDS, stated rather than discovered later:
• NOTHING IS MIGRATED. The 164 existing long names stay as they are. A property once written cannot be removed, so the best available repair would duplicate rather than move — and rewriting 164 authored names is not a mechanical act. New checks get the shape; old ones keep theirs. The median will fall slowly or not at all, and that is honest rather than disappointing.
• `findings` IS NOT VALIDATED OR PARSED. reflow2 records what an author says a run found and never judges it (`dec:non-goal-reflow2-does-not-judge-whether-a-check-is-meaningful`). A `passing` status beside findings describing a failure is a contradiction only a reader can catch — dev_storyflow's 2026-08-07 report exactly, where a check recorded "EXIT 0, verdict STALE" and stayed passing forever. This gives that evidence a home; it does not make the contradiction computable.
• The schema gains a PROPERTY, not a type, so the version stamp (counting node/edge types, 29/61) does not move and an older reflow2 can still read the graph.
properties.name: A check records what it FOUND separately from what it IS, and the rollup that made a cheap call expensive to read says when it shortened a name

properties.description:
PROPOSAL 1, built 2026-08-20 on Anthony's word. DISTINCT FROM the two nodes nearest it: one was a single re-placement of reflow2's own kernel, the other measures whether walls hold. This is the OPERATION a user of any project needs to do either.

THE GAP, found by using reflow2 and MEASURED the way a user would hit it. Asked in a user's own words — "move a component to a different parent, re-decompose" — find_tools ranked contain_component top of 152 served tools. contain_component ADDS a parent and removes nothing, so the discoverable route is also the wrong one: the spine stops being a tree, and hierarchy_issues reports multiple_parents AFTERWARDS, which is the wrong end of the act. Re-decomposition is not exotic — adopting a brownfield system, acting on a design review, and severability work all consist of it.

VERIFIED THE SAME WAY THE GAP WAS MEASURED: the identical query now ranks move_component first of 153, scoring 67.5 against add_component's 44.9.

WHAT IT DOES: move_component(child_id, new_parent_id) detaches EVERY parent the child had and names them.
  · It detaches a Project parent too. A component with no subsystem is often wired straight to the project PRECISELY BECAUSE it is homeless, so a move that only looked for Component parents would create the very defect it exists to prevent. That is not hypothetical - it happened to cmp:identity the same day.
  · An EMPTY detached list is reported rather than folded into success: "placed for the first time" and "moved" are different facts, and a caller who believed they were moving something learns they were not.
  · The level relation is REPORTED in level_note, never enforced - hierarchy_issues is the authority, and one rule with two homes is one rule that can disagree with itself. But it fires AT THE MOMENT OF THE MOVE, which is the difference between a defect avoided and a defect found.
  · It does not snapshot for the caller - choosing the epoch is their call - but history_note names the record_change that preserves the previous parent whenever anything was detached.

FIRST USE ON A REAL DESIGN, not a fixture: cmp:skills had carried two parents since before this session. One call detached the stale proj:reflow2 containment; hierarchy_issues went 3 findings to 2.

A BUG FOUND BY USING IT, fixed before it shipped: history_note originally stayed silent whenever the child had ANY snapshot. A snapshot from an earlier epoch is no evidence that THIS move was recorded, so the rule went quiet for exactly the long-lived node whose history matters most - silent in the dangerous direction. It now fires on any detachment and states a fact rather than making an accusation. an_earlier_snapshot_does_not_silence_the_history_note pins it.

STATED LIMIT: this fixes the CONTAINMENT spine only. DEPENDS_ON, PROVIDES and CONSUMES edges follow the component unchanged, so a move can put a contract across a wall it did not previously cross and nothing says so.
properties.name: A component can be MOVED on the decomposition spine, not merely given another parent

properties.description:
BUILT 2026-08-23 on Anthony's word. DISTINCT FROM `dec:idea-a-contract-is-declared-at-the-lowest-level-and-rolled-up`, which records the QUESTION and stays `proposed`: he authorised the roll-up PROJECTION, not the wider rule that would move the detector's altitude too. And DISTINCT FROM `fact:lifting-both-sets-is-what-made-the-two-vocabularies-meet`, which is the MEASUREMENT behind it — that node holds the numbers and the near-miss; this is the thing that was built. Keeping them apart is what lets the design say whether the fix happened, separately from what it found.

ALSO DISTINCT FROM `dec:idea-a-view-can-slice-by-altitude-not-only-by-aspect`, which stays open and is a different thing wearing the same word. That one asks which nodes are TOP LEVEL for a management reader — an ABSTRACTION filter, and its own text records why it is stuck: a filter chosen by the renderer rather than derived from the graph is the renderer fill-in the doctrine calls a defect. This is a ROLL-UP ALONG CONTAINMENT — answering a question at the level it was asked by walking down the spine. No filter, no new property, no schema change, which is exactly why it was buildable today and that one was not.

WHAT IT DOES: `seam_coverage {altitude}` lifts BOTH the couplings and the contracts to the nearest container at a chosen `Component.level`, then compares them. `covered_by` names the finest-level pair where each contract actually sits, so "yes, A and B interface" always arrives with where to look.
properties.name: A boundary question is answered at the altitude it was asked, naming the leaf where the contract actually lives

properties.description:
Step 6 of `flow:release-cut`, and it is last of the graph work because it is destructive of MCP access.

ONLY ONE COMMIT IN THE INCREMENT MAY TOUCH `docs/design/reflow2.json`. A squash keeps only the last `prev_content_hash`, so two exporting commits leave the chain pointing at an intermediate `main` never saw (BL-156). Fold with `git reset --soft`, then restore the file FROM `origin/main` — never from the branch, because `export_graph` builds `prev_content_hash` from whatever file is already at that path, and exporting over the branch's own copy chains to a document about to be amended out of existence.

EXPORT DIRECTLY FROM THE REAL STORE WITH THE NEW BINARY. The temp-store replay route injects schema defaults the source never stated — 182 injected values on the v0.28.0 cut, and `export_via_binary.py` now prints its own refusal saying so. Free the lock (`fuser .reflow2/graph/LOCK`, `kill -TERM`), drive the freshly built binary over stdio, and call `export_graph` with a `path`; `--export` is stdout-only and a copied stdout export has no lineage at all.

VERIFY THREE THINGS IN THE WRITTEN FILE before committing: `stamp.reflow2_version` is the new version, `prev_content_hash` equals main's `content_hash`, and injected-value counts are unchanged against the baseline.

COST: killing the server ends MCP tool access for the session, which is why every graph write happens before this step.
properties.name: A cut exports the design record exactly once, from the freshly built binary, chained from main

properties.description:
`flow:release-cut` — eight ordered steps with their TRIGGERS transitions, read back by `flow_report`. reflow2 dogfooding `cap:model-process` on itself: before 2026-08-21 this design contained ZERO Flow nodes, having shipped the vocabulary and never used it.

WHY IT HAD TO BE RECORDED RATHER THAN COMPUTED. `dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written` refused a START-HERE file because orientation is derivable. Release steps are NOT derivable from the graph: which registry, which workflow, which credential, what the tag format is, which files carry a version claim. Those are facts about the world outside the design, and no projection can compute them. The same derivability test that forbade the one argues for this.

WHAT IT REPLACES. The seven steps existed only in an agent's private session notes, recovered for the v0.19.0 cut from `git show v0.18.0` plus grepping AGENTS.md for "release". At least three were unguessable from the repo: the upgrade note is owed if and only if the schema stamp moved; the manifest must be complete rather than hand-typed; the Release needs an AT_EPOCH edge and creating the epoch node is not enough. Every one of those was learned by getting it wrong.

THE COST OF NOT HAVING IT, MEASURED: v0.17.0 shipped with no epoch edge and still lacks one; v0.19.0 repeated that four hours before `changelog_view` needed it; v0.20.0's export was stamped with the previous version; v0.22.0's changelog silently dropped 35 shipping changes; and v0.38.0 was published with an empty manifest. Five cuts, five different steps, each recorded only after it failed.

DISTINCT FROM the requirement it satisfies: that obliges ANY design holding Releases to record how it ships, and is a general rule reflow2 may one day detect the absence of in a user's project. This is reflow2's own instance of complying with it — one Flow, about this repo's cut, naming this repo's registries and files. The requirement would still stand if this Flow were deleted.
properties.name: reflow2's own release procedure is recorded as a Flow, so a cut is read from the design rather than from the last one

properties.description:
Step 1 of `flow:release-cut`. The version is claimed in more places than one: `Cargo.toml`, `reflow2.toml`, `Cargo.lock` (via `cargo update -p reflow2-core -p reflow2-mcp --offline`), the upgrade-note list in `docs/overview.md`, and two spots in `AGENTS.md`. `tools/check_doc_versions.py` verifies the documentation half.

THE TRAP, AND IT COSTS A RETRY EVERY TIME IT IS MISSED: `reflow2.toml` IS a registered artifact (`art:dependency-manifest`), so bumping it drifts the coherence gate with a `checksum_change`. Accept that drift two-sided as `design_holds` with a note — the design meaning of a cut lives in the Release and its epoch, never in a version string — and accept it BEFORE the manifest is frozen. `release_includes_all` freezes each artifact's CURRENT checksum, so accepting afterwards records that the release shipped the pre-bump file. Accepting first is one step; accepting after is two plus a second export.

ALSO REBUILD THE BINARY AFTER THIS STEP. A schema stamp carries the version of the binary that wrote it, so exporting later with a pre-bump build stamps the OLD version. That is why v0.20.0's committed export said 0.19.0.
properties.name: A cut moves every version claim together, and accepts the drift it causes before freezing the manifest

properties.description:
The `dangling_reference` HEAL rule walks every property the schema declares `node_ref` and reports a non-empty value naming no node — independent of the carrier's degree, its status, and any ruling that parks it.

DELIBERATELY NAMED AFTER ITS SIBLING `cap:a-node-attached-to-nothing-is-reported-whatever-its-type`, because it closes the same shape of hole one axis over. That capability's promise was "whatever its type"; the unstated qualifier was "and whatever its degree", which was false. Measured 2026-08-29 on reflow2's own graph: of nine dangling `subject_id` values, seven were reported and two were silent, and the two silent ones were exactly the two carrying edges — because `orphan_node` fires only when a subject "resolves to no node AND it carries no edge either".

TWO NEAR-MATCHES WERE OFFERED AND BOTH READ; THE THREE ARE DIFFERENT KINDS OF RECORD, which is why this is its own node. `fact:a-dangling-reference-is-only-detected-when-the-node-is-also-edgeless` is the MEASUREMENT of the hole and keeps its own numbers and scope caveat. `chg:a-dangling-reference-is-detected-on-its-own-terms` is the EVENT that changed the code, and dates it. This is the standing capability the design now claims — the thing that stays true after the event is history and the measurement is superseded.

THREE PROPERTIES IT HOLDS, each a decision rather than a default:

① SELF-LIMITING BY POPULATION. It reports how many declared node REFERENCES it walked, not how many nodes exist. A schema declaring no `node_ref` property gives `examined: 0`, and the sweep's starved-rule note then says in words that this rule had nothing to examine — so a clean result can never be read as a clean design. Counting nodes would have claimed thousands examined while inspecting none.

② ONE DEFECT, ONE FINDING. It runs before the zero-degree rule and that rule skips whatever it reports, so an edgeless node with a broken pointer arrives once. Reporting it twice would put one fault in two vocabularies suggesting two different repairs — the duplication BL-176 measured a field reporter stopping work over.

③ NOT SUPPRESSIBLE BY A PARK, unlike its sibling. `GOVERNED_BY ruling: parks` says a node is deliberately attached to nothing, which is a state a person can hold. Nobody can decide that a record is ABOUT a node the design does not have, so a park must not silence this.

It proposes no repair and says why: choosing the intended target is a judgement, a near-spelling match is not evidence, and a tool guessing would fabricate the same class of false record the rule exists to find. `propose_heal` reports it as a skipped operation carrying that reason, rather than emitting the generation stub every other non-repairable category emits.
properties.name: A reference that resolves to nothing is reported on its own terms, whatever else the node is attached to

properties.description: `add_decision` takes an OPTIONAL `status`, defaulting to `proposed` exactly as today. Nothing changes for a caller who omits it, and `dec:certainty-derived`'s guarantee is untouched: recording a choice is still not the same as settling it, and the default still refuses to assert the user's word. WHAT IT FIXES, and it is not convenience: Alex's fleet reported `set_decision_status` failing with `Node not found` immediately after a successful `add_decision`, and asked for read-after-write. Read-after-write already holds (fact:the-decision-race-is-caller-ordering-not-read-after-write). The real cause is that a parallel tool batch imposes NO ORDER on create-then-modify, so the modify can win the lock first. An optional status removes the pair entirely — one call cannot be misordered against itself. THE GUARD THAT MUST COME WITH IT: a status passed here is still the USER'S word, not the agent's. The same forgery rule that governs set_requirement_status applies, and the parameter description has to say so, or this becomes a convenient way for an agent to accept its own proposal in a single call. Sibling ask, cheaper and possibly sufficient on its own: say in the tool descriptions that parallel batches carry no ordering and a create-then-modify pair must be sequenced — no tool currently says it.
properties.name: A decision can be created with its status, so a settled choice is one call rather than two that can be misordered

properties.description:
The second check `req:design-dependencies-declared` names and only half-delivered. A dependency declaration that names another reflow2 design may also name that design's COMMITTED EXPORT; reflow2 records the export's content hash when the declaration is made, and later reads report whether the upstream has moved since.

SERVED AS `upstream_status`, and carried on `loop_status` as `upstream_moved` — the same shape `record_moved` already has, and for the same reason: that is the orientation call the session-start hook points sessions at. Deliberately NOT folded into `sync_status`, which answers the other direction (has MY record moved) and would blur two different questions into one list.

📌 THE NEAR-MATCH OFFERED WAS `chg:a-declared-dependency-can-be-watched-without-being-imported`, which is the EVENT of building this on 2026-08-26. This is the standing CAPABILITY.

⭐ WHY IT IS NOT THE EXISTING MECHANISM. `provenance::last_synced` already answers "has that file moved", but the only two paths that write into it are `export_graph` and `import_graph` — and importing a design into a store that already holds one KEEPS THE HOST'S NAME and upserts the incoming nodes into it. So watching a child by importing it ABSORBS the child, which is exactly what the hub case says a hub must not do. This watches without taking.

⭐ THE CHILD LIST IS THE COMMITTED MANIFEST, not a per-machine config. `reflow2.toml` already names each dependency's design by `graph_id`, version-pinned and reviewable in a diff, and it inherits the direction the dependency edge carries.

🛑 IT MUST NOT SILENCE ITSELF. The baseline is taken at DECLARATION time and a read never touches it — a check that refreshed what it compares against would report `moved` once and then be permanently quiet. Re-declaring is the acknowledgement (`dec:ask-not-repair`).

WHAT IT REPORTS, and absence is reported rather than assumed: `moved`, `unchanged`, `never_seen` (a path is declared and nobody has looked yet), `missing`, `unreadable`, `graph_id_mismatch` (the export at that path belongs to a different design than the one declared), `not_watched` (a dependency names another design but gives nothing to watch) and `not_observed` (the bounded pass did not open it). Only `moved`, `missing`, `unreadable` and `graph_id_mismatch` reach `loop_status`'s `next` list.

⚠️ THE PLACEMENT IS THE DESIGN. `reflow2-core` does no file I/O, so the core holds the declarations and the COMPARISON and the caller supplies what it found on disk — the same split `reconcile_dependencies` and `reconcile_artifacts` already make. The reading lives at the MCP layer in `upstream.rs`, beside `sync_debt`, for the reason that module already states. It does not NAVIGATE: every path read is one this design pointed at itself, in its own committed manifest.

⚠️ CHEAP WHEN UNUSED. `loop_status` gates on the manifest, so a design declaring no upstream export — every design until somebody deliberately points at one, this one included — pays a single node scan and reads no files. The pass is bounded at 16 exports and NAMES what it skipped.

⚠️ WHAT IT DOES NOT DELIVER. A declaration says I DEPEND ON that; a hub says I AM ANSWERABLE FOR that. Where a hub merely owns a child, saying so as a dependency would be modelling fiction. Cross-design realization and verification roll-up are untouched, and so is decisions-inherit-downward.
properties.name: A design says when the design it depends on has moved, without importing it

properties.description:
Given the upstream exports this design named in its OWN committed manifest, opens each one, computes its content hash from content, and reports what was found — so the comparison living in `cmp:depends` has something to judge. Implemented in `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/upstream.rs`.

⭐ WHY THIS IS A FUNCTION AND NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL. `reflow2-core` does no file I/O, deliberately and repeatedly, so the module holding the judgement CANNOT open a file. This is the half that can. It is the same split `reconcile_dependencies` and `reconcile_artifacts` already make, where the caller supplies what it observed and the core judges it.

⚠️ THREE PROHIBITIONS, EACH ONE LOAD-BEARING:
- IT DOES NOT NAVIGATE. Every path opened is one this design pointed at ITSELF, in its own committed manifest. reflow2 does no file navigation; reading a self-declared path does not breach that rule, and searching for candidates would.
- IT DOES NOT WRITE. Not the baseline, not a sync record. A read that refreshed what it compares against would report `moved` once and then go permanently quiet.
- IT DOES NOT IMPORT. Importing a design into a store that already holds one keeps the HOST's name and upserts the incoming nodes into it, which ABSORBS the child — exactly what the hub case forbids. This looks without taking.

⚠️ ABSENCE IS REPORTED, NEVER ASSUMED. `never_seen`, `missing`, `unreadable`, `graph_id_mismatch` and `not_observed` are distinct answers, so a pass that found nothing can never be read as a pass that found nothing WRONG. The pass is bounded at 16 exports and NAMES what it skipped.

📌 IT SATISFIES THE SAME REQUIREMENT AS `cap:a-declared-dependency-is-watched-not-imported`, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. `req:design-dependencies-declared` names two checks; "has what I depend on moved since" is unanswerable without this reading. Two capabilities against one requirement is the honest shape here — the requirement asks for a check, and the check has a judging half and a looking half. No new need was invented to justify this part.
properties.name: What a declared upstream actually holds is read where it lies — without navigating to it, writing to it, or taking it in

properties.description:
BUILT 2026-08-20 as tools/wall_check.py against req:modularity-computed. GENERALISED 2026-08-21 (PROPOSAL 3, Anthony's word) from a reflow2-only script into something that works on whatever project a design describes.

⭐ IT NEEDS NO CONFIGURATION, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN. The design already says where its code lives: every Artifact carries a `location`, and REALIZES says which Component that file is part of. So the file set, the component mapping and the project layout all come from the graph. Nothing to point at a repo, no language to declare, no paths to keep in step. A reflow2 user gets this the moment they have registered artifacts, which link-artifacts already asks them to do.

WHAT IT REPLACED, and the measurement that justified it: the first version GUESSED. It walked `crates/*/src` — hardcoded — and matched a Rust module to a Component BY NAME. Held against the declared mapping on reflow2's own graph the two disagreed IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: name-matching reached 48 components, the graph 45, with 4 only in the graph and 7 only in the name match. A tool answering 'is your decomposition sound' cannot be guessing which file belongs to which part of it. The guess is also structurally blind to every non-Rust file, while a location is just a path — the declared mapping reaches .py, .yaml and .md.

WHAT IT REPORTS: cycles at EVERY declared level, not only subsystems; coupling lifted through containment; and a comparison of what the DESIGN says against what the SOURCE does, in both directions.

⭐ IT NEVER QUIETLY GUESSES, which is the property the tests pin hardest. Files in a language it has no reader for, files the design names and disk lacks, components pointing at no file, and imports resolving to no registered file are each COUNTED AND NAMED. A file the tool cannot parse is not a file with no dependencies, and reporting it as clean would be the vacuous zero this whole increment exists to end.

⚠️ AND IT DOES NOT CALL A DIFFERENCE A DEFECT. A pair the design declares and the source lacks is reported as exactly that, with the reason stated: a contract can be real without an import — a process boundary, a file format, a human step — and this reads imports only.

PROVEN ON ITS FIRST REAL RUN: it found `cmp:compare -> cmp:report`, declared a `function_call` with `weight_basis: evidence`, made FALSE eight hours earlier by PR #265 when `is_design_type` moved to `nodes`. Nobody had updated the design. Snapshotted and removed under epoch:wall-check-works-on-any-project.

STATED LIMIT, unchanged and load-bearing: an import graph is COUPLING, NOT A CONTRACT. These numbers answer 'does the wall I declared hold' and must never be written back as CONSUMES — see fact:adopt-ran-on-reflow2-and-the-mechanical-contract-recovery-collapsed, where a mechanical scan proposed 91 against a real 17.

IT REMAINS AN INSTRUMENT, NOT A GATE, and exits 0 always. Whether a subsystem cycle should stop the build is a governance question with an owner. Its own test suite IS a gate (tools/test_wall_check.py, wired into ci.yml and the AGENTS.md gate block).
properties.name: A declared wall is checked against the coupling it contains — on any project, with no configuration

properties.description:
`vocabulary_coverage` answers a question nothing else in reflow2 asks. The detectors check the CONSISTENCY OF WHAT EXISTS; the absence-checkers it has (unsatisfied_requirement, unallocated_capability) check absences of REQUIRED structure. So vocabulary a design has never touched is invisible to every other computation, in every project, forever.

(The FACT records the trial; this is the built thing the trial chose the shape of. `cap:the-design-says-what-its-own-tools-cannot-write` is the repo-side INSTRUMENT that reads reflow2's own files; this is the PRODUCT capability that works on any graph.)

PORTABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: the schema is embedded in the binary and the corpus comes from the caller's own graph, so the answer needs nothing about any project's file layout. That was the deciding property — the earlier prototype read reflow2's schema directory and toolsnaps and would have generalised to nobody.

FOUR DECISIONS, ALL TAKEN FROM A TWO-ARM TRIAL RUN ON REFLOW2 ITSELF rather than from argument:
  SHIP THE FIGURES — they passed both arms. '0 of 61 edge types' on a day-one design is a true and useful statement, not noise.
  GROUP THE LIST — by the SCHEMA'S OWN eleven domains, never a grouping this code invented. The trial found unused vocabulary clustering into whole subsystems and the clusters turned out to BE the domains, so a mature design reads about four findings instead of thirty-one.
  MAKE IT PARKABLE — an ACCEPTED Decision at `decision:vocab:<domain>` declares a domain deliberately unused. Needed because OWNED_BY's absence is already ruled deliberate; without it the report would name a settled decision as a hole forever (`req:a-deliberate-state-is-not-a-defect`). No new tool: add_decision + set_decision_status, and the id is stated on every finding so the remedy rides on the output rather than on a skill nobody loads.
  KEEP THE FLAT LIST BEHIND A REQUEST — measured through the shipped tool, a day-one design produces 88 items and a mature one 31. The list is LONGEST for the user least able to act on it, so pushing it would have made the feature worst for exactly the people it is for.

AND A FIFTH THE TRIAL FORCED: a design under ten nodes gets a `note` saying the figures mean it has BARELY STARTED. Straight out of genesis every figure is near zero, and reporting that as coverage would hand a new user a wall of red on their first read.

A SIXTH, 2026-08-22 — THE LIST NAMES PROPERTIES, NOT ONLY TYPES. As shipped, `unused` named node types and edge types only, so an unused PROPERTY was counted in `properties_on_used_types` and never named: a set of named things reduced to a scalar, inside the one instrument built to report absence. The consequence was concrete — a design that had declared no `Artifact.audience` anywhere was silent in every report reflow2 served, and the only thing that could name it was a hand-written script pointed at reflow2's own files, which generalised to nobody. Found by writing the assertion and watching it FAIL, not by reasoning.
  Fixed at the root rather than special-cased for `audience`, which is what makes one change serve every optional field in every project: `Capability.inputs`/`outputs`/`capability_type` (0 of 170), `ChangeEvent.subject`, `Fragment.*`, the five never-set timestamps.
  THE WITHHOLDING DECISION WAS KEPT. The names ride the flat list that was already behind `include_unused`; the default reply grew by ONE figure per domain (`domains[].properties`), never by a wall of names. Extending the withheld list was the only shape that could close the hole without re-creating the noise the fourth decision measured.
  EDGE PROPERTIES CAME TOO, on the same walk that already had the edges in hand (`GOVERNED_BY.ruling` was 0 of 912 and nothing shipped could say so), reported as a second figure so the vacuous-zero rule stays visible.
  🛑 HONEST LIMIT, PINNED BY A TEST: a property carrying a schema DEFAULT can never be named unused, because the store materialises defaults on write and every instance carries one. What this names is the UNDEFAULTED optional — which is the class that matters precisely because `req:defaults-do-not-assert` is why the fields worth asking about have no default. And the naming is REPORTABLE rather than REPORTED: it arrives only when somebody asks for the list.
properties.name: A design reports which of the vocabulary it has never used, grouped by domain, parkable, with the list on request

properties.description:
The remaining two parts of req:a-report-says-what-it-swept-and-whether-its-checks-ran, plus one instance the work itself created. (The guard matched that Requirement, which this SATISFIES rather than restates: the requirement says what must be true, this is the built thing that makes it true.)

(b) `disconnected_community` SAID "disconnected from the rest of the design" AND WALKED SOMETHING NARROWER. dev_storyflow's report is exact and both halves are true at once: the nodes it named WERE reachable by an undirected walk of the graph. `design_network()` is not the graph — it drops nine node types and every review record, and CONTAINS is not a traceability edge, so a node reachable only through AUTHORED_BY, or only downward through containment, is an island there and connected here. MEASURED 2026-08-17: the walk covers 1133 of 2413 nodes. More than half the graph sits outside the thing whose absence the message called "the rest of the design". The message now states what it computed (no traceability edge to the main body), how much of the graph the walk held, which exclusions most often explain a false island, and how many singletons the rule does not report. THE CATEGORY KEY IS DELIBERATELY NOT RENAMED: consumers match on `disconnected_community` and it is an ility source, so renaming it to be accurate would break them to fix a sentence. The other half of their report — "the genuinely unreachable node was never mentioned" — is answered by the degree-zero rule of the previous epoch, since a node with no edges is unreachable in the full graph and is now reported whatever its type.

(c) `open_questions` RETURNING 0 READ AS AN ALL-CLEAR while `loop_status` in the very next call reported 31 other owed items — and it is the orientation call a session runs FIRST. It now carries a `loop_hint` on an empty answer, un-throttled. THE THROTTLE IS THE INTERESTING PART: `dec:read-hint-shape` option C surfaces a hint once and then stays quiet so reads do not nag, which is right while the reader is being handed findings and INVERTS when the answer is empty — the throttle then removes the only sentence in the reply and leaves a zero to speak for itself. So empty answers are exempt and non-empty ones are not, and an empty answer always says which zero it is: the other non-zero debt named, or an explicit all-clear. "Nothing to show you" and "nothing is owed" stop sharing a reply.

⚠️ AND THE CHANGE CREATED A THIRD INSTANCE, CAUGHT BY DRIVING THE BUILT BINARY RATHER THAN BY A TEST. The scoped detectors attach a note saying "`in_scope: 0` is VACUOUS rather than clean — nothing could have been found here", gated only on the region being one node. That was true while every structural rule needed an edge to fire. The degree-zero rule ended it: a node attached to nothing IS the finding and lives in exactly that one-node region. The first scoped call against the new binary returned `in_scope: 1`, a real finding, and that note beside it. The gate is now region-of-one AND found-nothing. Nothing was comparing the prose to the number it described.
properties.name: A finding describes the walk that produced it, and an empty orientation read says which zero it is

properties.description:
`orphan_node`'s repair note and the BL-199 self-host gate's failure text both name `governed_by(..., ruling: "parks")` as the second honest way on when a node's unattached state is deliberate, say plainly that deleting the node is the repair that looks clean and loses the most, and state the boundary: parking is read by `orphan_node` and the unsatisfied-requirement gap and by nothing else — it does not quiet `unthreaded_cluster` and does not cover the unproven-capability loop debt. The `link-artifacts` skill carries the same case for documents that correctly describe and implement nothing.

THE LIMIT IS PART OF THE CAPABILITY, not a caveat on it: a mechanism named without its scope produced the failure where a reporter found it, could not confirm it applied, and backed off.
properties.name: A structural finding names parking as the honest alternative, and names its limits

properties.description:
`GraphRead` (crates/reflow2-core/src/graph_read.rs) — the Rust trait realizing `ifc:graph-read`, and the second trait ever to exist in this crate. `LlmBackend` was the first and the only, since 2026-07.

`impl GraphRead for DesignGraph` delegates to the inherent methods and hides nothing, so the 274-function struct is untouched and every existing caller keeps working. What it adds is the option to ask for `&dyn GraphRead` instead.

THE PILOT IS `granularity`. Its body moved out of `impl DesignGraph` into a free `granularity_report(g: &dyn GraphRead)`, with a one-line inherent method left behind so `report.rs`, `ility.rs` and the existing tests never noticed. A refactor that forced its callers to change would be paying for the boundary twice.

WHAT THE MOVE BUYS, demonstrated rather than asserted, in three tests:
  — RUNS WITH NO STORE. The same report computed over a design that is two Vec's: no RocksDB, no schema, no disk, no lock.
  — CANNOT TELL WHICH IMPLEMENTATION IT IS READING. Population, mean and the flagged artifact ids are asserted EQUAL between a real DesignGraph and a hand-built fake sharing no code with it. Had the module reached past the contract for anything at all, this would not compile, let alone agree.
  — LETS A REFUSAL THROUGH. An unknown node type arrives as an error, not as an empty design — with a control case proving an empty-but-valid design is `Ok`, so the assertion is not vacuous.

AND THE COMPILER NOW ENFORCES WHAT THE DOCS ASSERTED: `GraphRead` has no writes, so a module behind it cannot change what it reads.

NOT YET DONE, and deliberately not overstated: 15 other read-only modules are recorded as consuming this contract but still take `&self` on DesignGraph. This is one module, proven end to end, so the cost of the next is known rather than guessed.
properties.name: A module stands behind the read contract, so it can be swapped, tested with no store, and held still to be measured

properties.description:
The degree-zero rule inside `orphan_node` ran on `Decision` alone (heal.rs:879) and now runs on every node type nothing else asks about. That narrowness is why the pass whose job is structural soundness returned a false green: dev_storyflow's fleet got `clean` back over a DesignEpoch carrying NO EDGES AT ALL, in two packages, through every health call of a session.

MEASURED ON REFLOW2'S OWN GRAPH, 2026-08-16: 75 of 2406 nodes are degree-zero. The old rule reported 7 of them; the new rule reports 21. The 14 newly visible are 3 DesignEpochs marking nothing, 3 Fragments with no source, `ver:the-export-survives-being-read-back` — a check counted among the 159 passing that says what it checks to nobody — and 7 TemporalFacts whose `subject_id` names a node THAT DOES NOT EXIST, including `prj:reflow2` (the Project is `proj:reflow2`) and `cap:thin-install` (the node is `req:thin-install`).

THREE BOUNDS, and two of them exist because the first cut was wrong:

(1) NOT EVERY ATTACHMENT IS AN EDGE. `TemporalFact.subject_id`, `Snapshot.target_id` and `Question.gap_id` are required indexed PROPERTIES: those nodes name what they are about without ever drawing a link. The naive rule would have reported 48 of reflow2's own 212 TemporalFacts — 48 false findings shipped inside the change whose subject is instruments that overstate. A degree-zero node is now skipped when any property resolves to a live node id, which keeps the case that IS wrong: a pointer to a node the design no longer has. The unit test caught this, because `subject_id` is required and the fixture could not be built without one.

(2) BL-42 STAYS CLOSED. Requirement, Capability and Interface are excluded — DETECT asks about those by name (`unsatisfied_requirement`, `unallocated_capability`, `unprovided_interface`), and reporting them here as well is the same finding in two vocabularies that became 20 of 31 defects on the storyflow trial.

(3) A RESTING STATE IS NOT A DEFECT. Project and DesignRule are excluded. A Project alone means the design is EMPTY — what genesis produces on day one — and the phase rollups already say so. An advisory DesignRule can bind the PROCESS rather than a node, and demanding an edge would push authors to draw a relationship nobody meant. Widening a sweep without asking that question is how the correct action starts degrading the instrument (`req:a-deliberate-state-is-not-a-defect`).

Three fixtures were genuinely incomplete and were fixed rather than silenced: a "v1 baseline" epoch that was the baseline of nothing, a "v1.0" release that shipped nothing, and a recency test whose Verification verified nothing.
properties.name: A node attached to nothing is reported whatever its type, and a property that names a live node counts as attachment

properties.description:
TWO FINDINGS, and the split is the point.

`unverified_published_contract` names an Interface designated `published` or `both` that no PASSING check verifies. Per-contract, severity 0.6 — level with `unverified_enforced_rule` and above `unverified_capability`, on that finding's own reasoning: an unproven capability is work not yet confirmed, while this is an obligation to somebody ELSE that nobody can observe compliance with. Publishing is what raises it; an internal boundary with no check is not this finding. `both` is billed because it offers a contract as well as needing one; `required` is not, because a contract this design needs from OUTSIDE is somebody else's promise to prove.

`no_published_boundary` asks the posture question ONCE, aggregate, severity 0.3, when a design records boundaries and designates none of them published.

⭐ WHY THE SECOND ONE HAS TO EXIST, AND IT IS A FACT ABOUT THE SCHEMA RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE. `Interface.designation` DEFAULTS to `internal`, so a boundary nobody classified and one deliberately kept internal are stored identically — the schema says so in as many words, and `pair_designs` already refuses to paper over it. That makes a ZERO from the first detector genuinely ambiguous, and reporting it as clean would be the "a detector answering zero over an empty population reads exactly like one that ran clean" failure the loop refuses everywhere else. So the zero asks a question instead.
  Contrast `Artifact.audience`, which is deliberately UNDEFAULTED: silence there is legible as silence, so `internal_only_delivery` needs no such companion. The two detectors are siblings whose population reporting differs ONLY because one property has a default and the other does not — the clearest argument yet for `req:defaults-do-not-assert`.

🛑 IT COULD NOT HAVE EXISTED BEFORE 2026-08-21. `VERIFIES` could not reach an `Interface` at all until #291 (`fact:a-contract-is-the-one-thing-reflow2-cannot-attach-evidence-to`), so every contract in every design read as unverified and this would have fired on all of them — correctly and uselessly. The edge landed and exactly ONE check has been drawn since, on reflow2's own design: vocabulary with no detector, seen from outside. The finding's evidence SAYS SO, so a reader of an older design does not mistake the absence for neglect.

NARROW BY CONSTRUCTION: it fires only on what a design has already CHOSEN to publish, and a design with no boundaries at all is asked nothing — it has not declined to publish one, it has not got there, the same reasoning as `vocabulary_coverage`'s barely-started note.

MEASURED ON REFLOW2 ITSELF the day it was built: 3 published boundaries, 2 reported — `ifc:graph-export` and `ifc:mcp-tools-http`, both with zero incoming VERIFIES. `ifc:mcp-tools` is silent because it carries a passing check. Design-wide gaps 73 to 75.

DISTINCT FROM `dec:idea-a-black-box-owes-an-interface-the-way-a-capability-owes-a-requirement`, which was read before this was created. That Decision is an OPEN brainstorm holding four options; this is the one that got built, and it is idea B in that node's own lettering. The relationship is the same as `cap:a-design-says-which-vocabulary-it-has-never-used` to its idea node: the Decision records what was considered, the Capability records what exists. Ideas A, C and D there remain open and unbuilt.

⚠️ NOT BUILT, AND DELIBERATELY: nothing here asks whether a published contract's SPEC is complete. `req:interface-spec-complete` is accepted and still unimplemented — 3 of 3 published boundaries here have 4 to 5 agreement fields unset. Adjacent, different work, and folding it in would have made one finding answer two questions.
properties.name: A published contract is asked for its evidence, and a design that publishes nothing is asked whether it meant to

properties.description:
`incomplete_published_contract` — an Interface designated `published` or `both` with any of the nine structured agreement axes unanswered. Per-contract, severity 0.45: below `unverified_published_contract` (0.6), because a published promise with NO evidence at all is a stronger finding than one whose description has gaps; above the ordinary 0.3 notes, because an undescribed seam is what makes two designs uncheckable against each other.

SERVES `req:interface-spec-complete`, accepted and unimplemented until now. Its point is not completeness for its own sake — two designs cannot be checked for INCOMPATIBILITY at a seam unless the seam is described in comparable terms, so `mirror_surface` could link two designs and still not tell you they disagree.

⭐ THE ONE THAT NEARLY GOT AWAY: `unspecified` IS UNSET. Five of the nine axes are enums DEFAULTING to `unspecified`, and the store materialises defaults on write — so a presence test counts the word as an answer, and the first cut of this detector was GREEN OVER EXACTLY WHAT IT EXISTS TO CHECK. Measured before the fix: `ifc:mcp-tools-http` read 9 of 9 complete while its `medium` said `unspecified`, and `ifc:graph-export` reported 4 gaps where there are 6. Recorded in full as `fact:a-materialised-default-defeats-a-completeness-check` — read before this node was created and judged DISTINCT: that fact is the general lesson about defaults across three instances in one day, this is the built thing whose repair produced it.

⚠️ AND THE OPPOSITE ERROR IS EQUALLY AVAILABLE: `none` IS AN ANSWER. `auth: none` on an unauthenticated local pipe is a deliberate statement and `ifc:mcp-tools` makes exactly it; sweeping `none` in with `unspecified` would nag a design that had answered honestly.

IT REPORTS, IT DOES NOT JUDGE. Some axes are genuinely meaningless for some boundaries — a library linked into its callers has no endpoint, a one-way feed has no error model a consumer parses. This NAMES which axes are unset and leaves applicability to the design (`dec:report-dont-judge`); a list of required fields would be reflow2 deciding what a mechanical, human or physical interface must look like.

AND IT ASKS IN THE REQUIREMENT'S WORDS, NOT THE COLUMN'S: each unset axis carries its gloss — `payload_schema` reads as "which fields are mandatory, and their types". Pinned by a test, because it is trivially strippable in a refactor and nothing else would notice.

🛑 HONEST LIMIT, ON THE FINDING ITSELF RATHER THAN ONLY IN A COMMENT. `req:interface-spec-complete` names SIX characteristics; the schema has fields for FIVE. There is nowhere to record performance and constraints — rate limits, concurrency, timeouts — so a design can clear this finding completely and still not say what it promises under load. The evidence string says so, because a detector that quietly checks five sixths of a requirement and reports clean is the green-gate-over-what-it-does-not-cover failure.

DISTINCT FROM `cap:a-published-contract-is-asked-for-its-evidence`, built the same day and walking the same published set: that one asks whether anything SHOWS the contract holds, this asks whether the contract is DESCRIBED well enough for anyone to compare it. A design can be in either state alone — a fully specified contract nobody checks, a checked contract nobody described — and one acknowledgement must not settle both. Pinned by a test.
DISTINCT FROM `cap:interface-spec`, which is the WRITE side: `set_interface_spec` and the nine fields. That capability made the axes recordable; this one notices when they were not recorded.
DISTINCT FROM `dec:idea-a-black-box-owes-an-interface-the-way-a-capability-owes-a-requirement`, an OPEN brainstorm where this is idea B. That node's own measurement is now STALE — it recorded 3 of 4 published boundaries incomplete including `ifc:core-api`, which is no longer designated published; the figures above supersede it. Ideas A, C and D there remain unbuilt.

MEASURED ON REFLOW2 ITSELF: of 3 published boundaries, `ifc:graph-export` fires with 6 unset axes; `ifc:mcp-tools-http` fires on `medium` alone; `ifc:mcp-tools` is silent at a genuine 9 of 9.
properties.name: A published contract is asked which of the agreement axes it never filled in

properties.description:
`get_skill` refusing an unknown name first says what the name IS, when it is one of the slash commands: "'rules' is the slash command; it is served as 'governance-proposal'". Six of the eight advertised commands map to a skill.

TWO OF THE EIGHT MAP TO NO SKILL AT ALL and the table says so rather than inventing one — `/decisions` calls `scan_nodes` for the Decision type and `/debt` calls `loop_status`. Answering those with a plausible skill name would send the caller somewhere that cannot help them, which is the failure the refusal exists to prevent.
properties.name: A refusal maps a user-facing command name to the skill actually served — or to the tool, when there is no skill

properties.description:
`release_without_manifest`: a Release with an AT_EPOCH edge, at least one DEPLOYED_TO edge and zero INCLUDES edges raises a gap at **severity 0.85, which FAILS `reflow2_check`** (default `--gap-threshold` 0.8). Anthony's call, 2026-08-21 — `dec:an-empty-manifest-on-a-shipped-release-stops-the-build`. It sits with the findings that say the design asserts something untrue, not with the questions that wait for a human, because a note was demonstrably not enough: the v0.38.0 cut passed the gate green with 96 notes scrolling past it.

Keys on structure and never on `status`, deliberately: rel:v0380 was tagged, published, deployed and asset-verified while its status still read `planned`, so a status-based exemption would have excused the single instance the rule exists for.

Guarded against flooding the same way `unreleased_component` is: if NO release in the design carries a manifest, release contents are simply not modelled here, and that is one whole-graph fact rather than one alarm per release. Measured against reflow2's own 40 releases before it was written — zero false positives — and then proved live by stripping v0.37.0's 275 INCLUDES edges from a copy of the real design and watching the gate go red.

A genuinely contentless release — a re-tag, a docs-only republish — stays acknowledgeable with a reason on the record. Red until somebody says why, never red forever.

The read half of the same capability: a cut ENDS by calling `release_report` for the new release and reading the counts. Hundreds of artifacts, components and capabilities is the healthy answer; `artifacts: []` means the manifest never landed. This is the eighth and last step of `flow:release-cut`.

Also hardened its sibling: `release_without_epoch` exempted any `planned` release, and now exempts one only while it is UNDEPLOYED — found by this detector's own tests. The sibling stays at 0.6 and stays a question, because which epoch a release belongs to is a judgement and its absence asserts nothing false.
properties.name: A release that is out and records shipping nothing stops the build, and a cut ends by reading it

properties.description:
The record that did the work names the finding it answered (`INVALIDATES`, `* -> *`, carrying `note` and `at`), and every surface that quotes a verdict reads it back.

WRITE: `invalidates`. READ: `invalidated_findings`, plus `loop_status.verifications` (per-row `invalidated_by` / `rerun_owed` / a sentence, and a top-level `rerun_owed` summary) and `graph_report` from the same code. The `where-am-i` skill now gathers `Constraint` — where repairs are commonly written up — and calls `invalidated_findings` before quoting any failing verdict.

⭐ THE READER SHIPPED WITH THE EDGE, deliberately. A marker nothing consults is a comment, a failure this project has now found in `enforced`, in `SUPERSEDES` and in `OBSOLETES` itself.

⭐ IT REPORTS AND NEVER JUDGES. The claim says the last RESULT is stale; it never says the check now passes, never touches the target's `status`, and never removes the check from `attention`. `rerun_owed` is three-valued and null means one side is undated so nobody can say.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: nothing infers staleness. A finding with no claim against it is reported as having none, which is a real answer rather than a silence.
properties.name: A repair can say what it invalidated, and the reader says whether a re-run is owed

properties.description:
The `revision` block a write returns now carries `prior_state_preserved_in` — the Snapshot holding the replaced state — and says one of two DIFFERENT things depending on what the graph actually holds.

THE DEFECT IT CLOSES. That block already said '`record_change` BEFORE the merge is what puts the old state in the design's own timeline' — UNCONDITIONALLY, in identical words, to a caller who had just done exactly that and to one who had destroyed something. Advice that never varies is advice a reader learns to skim, and the one time it mattered looked like all the times it did not. That is the catalogue problem in miniature, inside the very mechanism `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` names as the one that works.

COMPUTE THE OUTCOME, DO NOT TRACK THE INVOCATION — the requirement's stronger form, and the reason this survives an agent that ignores every hint: it reads graph state, not run history. dev_storyflow's dragon Boss proposed the identical shape independently ('report whether the target has a snapshot — NOT BLOCK, JUST SAY'), which is two consumers arriving at one design from opposite ends.

MATCHED BY CONTENT HASH, NOT BY EPOCH. 'At the current epoch' needs a notion of CURRENT that reflow2 does not have, and it answers a weaker question. The hash answers the one a caller actually has — is what I just replaced recoverable? — and it makes a stale snapshot of a DIFFERENT state correctly NOT count as preservation. Verified 2026-08-18 that a Snapshot's stored `state` hashes to exactly the `prior_content_hash` a revision reports.

NOTHING BLOCKS. A tool that blocks becomes a tool people route around, and then the graph stops matching reality — the one failure it cannot survive. Every probe asserts the write landed.

HONEST COST: `snapshot_preserving` scans every Snapshot, so it is O(snapshots) per revising write. At 144 that is nothing; at a hundred thousand it would need an index on `target_id`.
properties.name: A revising write computes whether the state it replaced is preserved, instead of restating the rule at everyone

properties.description:
A `GOVERNED_BY` edge carrying `ruling: parks` records that a node's UNATTACHED or UNSATISFIED state is correct and deliberate. `orphan_node` and `unsatisfied_requirement` skip it; `detect_defects` reports it in `swept.parked`. `governed_by` gains a `ruling` parameter so the property is reachable from the tool people use. (The guard matched the two OBSERVATIONS that named this defect and the REQUIREMENT that answers it; this is the built thing that closes them.)

⭐⭐ THE FINDING THAT REFRAMED THE WORK, reproduced live BEFORE anything was designed: an Artifact carrying ANY `GOVERNED_BY` edge ALREADY escaped `orphan_node`, because the detector saw an EDGE and never a RULING. So silence was already available and was never the problem. WHAT WAS MISSING WAS THE COUNT — "deliberately parked" and "never looked at" gave the identical answer, a vacuous zero in different clothes, in the very increment named for instruments that overstate. A reader can now see "34 defects, 8 parked" instead of "97" or instead of nothing.

THE MEASURED FAILURE (dev_storyflow): defects 88 → 97 across ten artifact writes, EIGHT of them deliberate no-claim registrations a standing ruling prescribed, with 31 more owed in the same genre. Their framing is the requirement: the disposition rule and the defect detector make each other unreadable, and THE CORRECT ACTION DEGRADES THE INSTRUMENT — self-reinforcing, because a later seat watching the count climb has an incentive to stop registering documents, which is the worse state.

WHY THE EDGE (Anthony's call, 2026-08-17). On the NODE it needs declaring on every parkable type and a bare flag is an unevidenced claim. On the DECISION it parks everything that ruling governs, so a later GOVERNED_BY silently inherits parking. On the EDGE it is per-node and precise — one ruling parks the 31 documents it covers and nothing else — and TWO-SIDED BY CONSTRUCTION: the claim IS the edge to the ruling, so a deliberate state cannot be asserted without a Decision that says why.

⚠️ THE RULING MUST BE ACCEPTED. A `proposed` Decision is somebody thinking out loud — the discriminator `loop_status` already uses — so parking on an unsettled ruling would let a musing suppress a finding.

⚠️ AND A PROBE FAILED ON ITS FIRST RUN, WHICH FOUND THE REAL DEFECT. `parking_on_an_unsettled_ruling_does_not_count` proved the node was not COUNTED as parked, then failed on its second assertion: the finding did not come back either, because the `GOVERNED_BY` edge itself made the artifact "attached". So an UNSETTLED parking claim silenced a real defect. Fixed at the cause: a `ruling: parks` edge no longer counts as attachment — it is a claim that the node is deliberately attached to NOTHING, so counting it as attachment was self-defeating.

⭐ AND THE REACHABILITY TRAP WAS CAUGHT BY APPLYING THE SAME DAY'S LESSON. `governed_by` had no way to set `ruling`, so the property would have been reachable only through raw `create_edge` — the FOURTH instance of one pattern in a day, after `Verification.description` (declared, unreachable, 1 use in 164), `SUPERSEDES` (declared, 0 edges, successor named in prose 9 of 9), and `create_node` shipping a compare-and-swap whose precondition value it did not return. The parameter exists because the property would otherwise have gone unused.

📌 THE REPORTER'S OPEN BOUND IS CLOSED. They asked whether BL-176's DOCUMENTS/REALIZES guard was meant to cover this and misses it, or never contemplated it. NEVER CONTEMPLATED: BL-176 widened attachment for artifacts that DO carry a describing edge; this is an artifact that deliberately carries none.

⚠️ NOT DONE, and it is the music_graph half: F9 and F14 report that recording PLANNED work manufactures gaps (each planned capability immediately raises unrealized/unverified), so the gap list punishes writing a plan down. That is the same shape from a third direction and is NOT addressed here — parking is per-node and deliberate, whereas that case wants a whole class of tautological gap understood as planning rather than debt.
properties.name: A ruling can declare a state deliberate, and parked nodes are counted rather than silenced

properties.description:
`Scoped` carries `share_of_anchored` — the fraction of the design's ANCHORED findings this 'narrowed' answer holds — plus a `narrowing_note` that appears in words when that exceeds SCOPE_IS_BARELY_NARROWER_AT (0.5).

THE DENOMINATOR IS THE DESIGN. It is `in_scope + out_of_scope`, deliberately not `total`: unanchored findings are statements about the design as a whole and could never fall inside ANY region, so dividing by `total` would flatter every scoped answer by a constant and make regions look narrower than they are.

THE THRESHOLD IS A JUDGEMENT AND IS ADMISSIBLE ANYWAY. `dec:report-dont-judge` normally forbids one. It is allowed here because the finding is about THIS TOOL'S OWN ANSWER rather than about the design: saying 'the narrowing you asked for did not narrow' is the instrument reporting on itself, which is the one place a judgement is owed rather than withheld. The threshold is named in the message so a reader can disagree with it rather than having to discover it.

MEASURED AGAINST THE OLD DEFAULT AS A CONTROL: over all 56 Components of reflow2's own design the note fires 56 of 56 at depth 3, and 0 of 56 at the new default of 2.

BOTH DETECTORS GET IT. Gaps and defects both return `Scoped`, and a self-check only one of them performed would be exactly the half-applied rule that made the vacuity note need repairing twice.
properties.name: A scoped read reports how much of the design it still holds, and says in words when that is most of it

properties.description:
`report_manual_work` writes it; `manual_work_report` reads it back; the `capture-session` skill asks for it at session end. Delivers `req:a-session-says-what-it-did-by-hand-that-reflow2-already-serves`.

📌 DISTINCT FROM THE TWO THE GUARD OFFERED, BY ROLE. `req:a-session-says-what-it-did-by-hand-...` states WHAT MUST BE TRUE. `dec:idea-can-reflow2-see-the-work-a-session-did-by-hand` is the open QUESTION the requirement was promoted out of, and keeps the roads not taken. This is the thing that DELIVERS the requirement — what a capability is, and what a `SATISFIES` edge needs on its other end.

⭐ WHY IT IS WORTH MORE THAN AN ABSENT CALL. Every other measurement reflow2 has of its own adoption looks at what a session DID with it. `dec:bl-155` measured 40 of 132 tools never called and states the consequence outright: it **cannot tell unused from unreachable**. Hand-rolled work discriminates between them because it carries INTENT — a session that wrote a script to do X proves somebody wanted X, at a moment, badly enough to build it.
