⭐ THE `diagnosis` IS THE WHOLE VALUE AND THE SET IS CLOSED. `tool_missing` (nothing does this — build one) · `tool_not_found` (something does and the session missed it — a DISCOVERABILITY failure, a different repair) · `tool_refused` (one was reached for and would not) · `unknown` (the session cannot say). Unknown values are REFUSED and the refusal names what would have worked. `unknown` is kept as a legitimate answer because forcing a guess corrupts the other three.

Naming a `reflow2_tool` the surface does not serve is refused too — that means the diagnosis is really `tool_missing`, and a phantom would sit in the one table somebody reads to decide what to improve. That check lives at the TOOL rather than in the core, because `tool_router.has_route()` asks the live router while a core-side list would be a second copy of the tool surface maintained by hand.

ALL THREE LEGS SHIPPED TOGETHER, deliberately: the surface audit hours earlier found 13 declared types with no legs at all and five carrying all three and still unused. The reader is the leg whose absence kills vocabulary — `DECOMPOSES` reached zero edges while shipping a detector for them.

🛑 TWO LIMITS THAT BUILDING THIS DID NOT RESOLVE. It depends on the agent having NOTICED the tool existed, which is the same blind spot it exists to see — so an empty report is NEVER evidence that nothing was hand-rolled, and `manual_work_report`'s own description says so. And `dec:how-should-reflow2-log-its-own-usage` argues a tool is the wrong shape for self-measurement at all, which is correct and here unavoidable: the server observes calls, and work done by hand happens where it cannot look.

🛑 THE RECORD STAYS LOCAL. `what` is free text naming the user's own domain — exactly the field `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` warns "the next contributor will put something useful in". It must never be lifted into a telemetry payload.
properties.name: A session records the work it did by hand, with the diagnosis that separates a missing tool from an unfindable one

properties.description:
`design_regions` — a SEEDLESS read that answers 'what parts does this design have, how big is each, and what is owed in each', so a session with no lane, no scope and no topic can find a seed rather than needing one to start.

THE BASIS IS THE DESIGN'S OWN CARVE-UP, NEVER AN INFERRED ONE. Regions are the nodes the design already declares as parts — its Project and its Components/systems — not clusters a community-detection pass invented. A clustering answer would be reflow2 telling a reader 'these are the parts of your design' on the strength of a heuristic, which is the exact failure the epoch it belongs to exists to remove.

WHAT EACH REGION CARRIES: its seed id and name, `region_size` at the stated depth, how many open gaps and structural defects fall inside it, and who (if anyone) currently claims it. So the reply is directly actionable: pick a row, then scope to that seed.

IT REPORTS WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER. Named parts do not reach the whole graph — most of a mature design is bookkeeping (ChangeEvent, Snapshot, TemporalFact, Fragment) that no component contains. The reply states how many nodes lie in NO region, broken down by type, and how many lie in MORE THAN ONE, because a list of overlapping regions read as a partition would be a false map. This is `cap:a-finding-describes-the-walk-that-produced-it` applied to a region list.

DEPTH IS A PARAMETER AND ITS EFFECT IS VISIBLE. The caller sets it; the reply echoes it and the sizes move with it, so the cost of a wide radius is something a reader sees rather than something they must be told.
properties.name: A design says what parts it has, so a session holding nothing can pick where to stand

properties.description:
`reflow2-mcp --read-only` refuses every write and still answers every read. Delivers `req:the-hosted-surface-is-read-only-so-it-can-ship-before-authentication-exists`.

📌 The near-match offered was `chg:a-read-only-surface-refuses-at-the-write-guard`, which is the EVENT of building this on 2026-08-26. This is the standing CAPABILITY. The event is what happened once; the capability is what the system can do from now on, and it is the thing a requirement is satisfied BY.

⭐ THE ENFORCEMENT POINT IS THE DESIGN. It refuses in `ReflowService::write_lock` — the graph's write guard, which every mutating handler must obtain and no write can avoid. So it covers all 98 write sites that exist and every write added later, including by an author who never heard of the mode.

The alternative was a list of mutating tool names, or a check keyed on the `readOnlyHint` annotation each tool declares. Both are rules maintained BY HAND with nothing checking them — the defect class this project fixed three times on 2026-08-26 (`unallocated_component` and the parking ruling; F-01's replay contract; three detectors not reading `proposed`). Choosing that form here, the same day, would have been remarkable.

⭐ THE COMPILER PROVED THE SWEEP COMPLETE. Making `write_lock` fallible turned all 98 call sites into compile errors until each was updated — no list, no audit, no chance of missing one. It also found a case review would not have: `share()` is a SECOND assembly point, minting a service per CLIENT SESSION (`req:sessions-share-a-graph`), and read-only had to be INHERITED there. Reset, the mode would have held for the process and evaporated for every actual client — read-only in name only, testing green at the process level.

⚠️ WHAT IT DELIVERS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. **INTEGRITY** is answered outright: no write means nothing to attribute, so the caller-supplied `contributor_id` — an unverified claim over a network — is never accepted. **CONFIDENTIALITY** is NOT eliminated, only RELOCATED to the network, which is what binding to a tailnet is for. This is not authentication and must not be read as making authentication unnecessary; it is what lets a reachable surface ship BEFORE authentication exists.

🛑 OFF BY DEFAULT. `read_only: false` in `wrap_at`, the single assembly point; the flag appears in no shipped config. `a_normal_service_still_writes` pins that an ordinary service is writable and passed both before and after the refusal landed.

The refusal is LOUD, naming the mode and the reason, so a caller can tell "this server refuses writes" from "this write was wrong" — the same call `dec:stateless-seat-handle` makes about a missing seat: a loud refusal beats a quiet wrong answer.
properties.name: A server can refuse every write, at the one point a write cannot avoid

properties.description:
TWO BREAKING CHANGES TAKEN ON PURPOSE, both DECLINED hours earlier on the ground that they would break consumers. `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap` (Anthony, 2026-08-17) reversed that ground: before a stability commitment exists the price of a break is at its lowest and rises with every user, so "it would break consumers" argues for doing it NOW. (The guard matched `dec:a-misnaming-is-fixed-in-the-message-not-the-key`, which is the DECISION that first declined this and now records its own reversal; this is the built thing that carries it out. Also distinct from `cap:a-finding-describes-the-walk-that-produced-it`, which fixed the MESSAGE and left both of these standing.)

(1) `disconnected_community` IS NOW `unthreaded_cluster`. The old key asserted unreachability while the detector computed something narrower — connected components over `design_network()`, which drops nine node types and every review record and does not count CONTAINS, covering 1133 of a 2413-node graph. `unthreaded` names what is actually missing, a traceability edge, and cannot be misread as "unreachable in the graph". The ility source string moves with it.

⭐ THE COST THAT DECIDED AGAINST IT WAS NEVER MEASURED, and measuring it is what made the call obvious: the key appears in 14 source/test files, 6 live docs and 41 prose mentions in the export, and is PERSISTED AS DATA NOWHERE — no node property holds it as a value. No observation, acknowledgement or ility reading needed migrating. A rename feared as a migration was a sed and a doc pass.

(2) UNSCOPED `detect_defects` RETURNS `{swept, defects}` INSTEAD OF A BARE LIST. `swept.nodes` is what it examined, `swept.rules` names the checks that ran, `swept.design_network_nodes` reports the narrower topology walk rather than hiding it, and `swept.note` appears ONLY when the sweep could not have found anything. An empty result now says which empty it is — exercised and found nothing, or nothing to examine — instead of leaving a zero to be read as permission before `apply_heal`, which deletes nodes. The scoped sibling has answered this way since 2026-08-09, so one tool was answering one question two ways and the honest half was the one fewer people call. `open_defects()` is the bare list for engine-internal callers.

WHAT IT COST, recorded as evidence for the rule rather than for the change: five real consumers of the old shape broke and were FIXED rather than shimmed — `smoke_mcp.py` in three places, `model_the_loop.py`, `build_design_graph.py`, and `bl124_instrument.py`, which now reads both shapes deliberately because it is an instrument that may be pointed at an older server. 53 test call sites moved to `open_defects()`. One toolsnap golden moved.

⚠️ AND A FALSE CLAIM WAS CAUGHT IN THE WRITING. The first draft of `HealCategory::ALL`'s doc comment said the compiler enforced that every variant is listed. It does not — `as_str`'s exhaustive match forces an author into the impl block, but nothing makes them extend the list, and a missing entry would make `swept.rules` UNDERSTATE the sweep. The comment now says it is hand-maintained and names the test that actually holds it. Shipping an unchecked claim about a check, inside the change whose subject is reports that overstate, would have been the joke writing itself.
properties.name: A defect sweep returns what it examined, and the category names what it computes

properties.description:
DECISION 5, built 2026-08-20 on Anthony's word. DISTINCT FROM the wall-check instrument, which reads the SOURCE from outside; this is reflow2 telling you, from inside detect_defects, what its own answer does not cover.

THE MEASURED FAILURE: circular_dependency walked 182 dependency pairs on reflow2's own graph and found nothing - a large, healthy-looking population. ZERO of those pairs joined two subsystem-level components. So "no circular dependencies" was true of the flattened network and said nothing whatever about the subsystems, while reading exactly like a clean bill of health for them. The two real subsystem cycles were found with a hand-written Python script, not with reflow2.

⭐ THE FIRST DESIGN WOULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT, and that is worth keeping. The approved shape was "name the checks that had nothing to examine". Measuring first showed it would print NOTHING on this graph - no rule has an empty population - and would have missed the motivating case entirely. Anthony was told before it was built rather than after. The failure is not a starved rule; it is that A RULE'S POPULATION CAN BE HEALTHY WHILE THE SUB-POPULATION THE READER CARES ABOUT IS EMPTY.

WHAT SHIPPED, two mechanisms because one was not enough:
  · rule_populations - what each of the 8 rules actually walked, and in what unit. Computed with THE SAME EXPRESSION THE RULE USES, never re-derived, because two implementations of one number can disagree. A rule that walked nothing reports clean for the same reason an empty graph does.
  · coupling_by_level - components and dependency pairs AT each declared Component.level. This is the one that bites, and it generalises to any project that declares a hierarchy: the answer is computed over a flattened graph and the reader assumes it holds at the level they asked about.
  · coverage_note - ONE line naming both, present only when there is something to name, so its presence is the signal. A summary rather than a per-finding annotation, because the detail is already in the two lists and a sentence on every finding would crowd the findings.

ON REFLOW2'S OWN GRAPH it now says: "the subsystem level has 10 component(s) and ZERO dependency pairs between them, so every topology result here - cycles, severability, single points of failure - is SILENT about that level rather than clean about it." That is the sentence that would have saved two days.

A FALSE POSITIVE CAUGHT BY TESTING AGAINST REALITY: a level holding ONE component can never have a pair joining two components at it. That is arithmetic, not a modelling gap, and naming it would be the false positive that teaches a reader to skip the line - which is how a signal dies. Fixed before shipping, pinned by a_level_holding_one_component_is_never_called_blind.

THE TOOL DESCRIPTION MOVED WITH IT. detect_defects told readers that swept.rules and swept.note were the whole story, which went stale the moment these fields existed. Updating it pushed past skill_lint's 1500-char cap at 1728; the trim came from a sentence coverage_note now states better. A mechanism is not finished until the message a reader actually sees points at it.
properties.name: A defect sweep says what it could NOT have found — per-rule populations, and coupling at each declared level

properties.description:
COMPARE-AND-SWAP ON THE WRITE PATH. `create_node` accepts `expected_content_hash`; supply what you read and the write is REFUSED when the node has moved since, naming both hashes. Omit it and the old behaviour is unchanged. In the core: `upsert_node_if_unchanged`, with `node_content_hash` as the canonical hash.

THE FAILURE, measured from BOTH SIDES of one collision on a shared graph: a worker read a node, ninety seconds later another attached session wrote it, the write returned a normal success with the full node body, and THE WINNER WAS NEVER TOLD. The loser found out only because `record_change` happens to return the snapshot it took — a diagnostic side-effect of an unrelated tool, not a guard.

⭐ WHY A REFUSAL RATHER THAN A FIFTH REPORT, and this is `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap` deciding the shape. The `revision` block already REPORTED what a write replaced — that is detection, it tells the loser afterwards and tells the winner nothing. The requirement's own words were that the block's hash "is exactly the raw material a compare-and-swap needs; nothing consumes it yet". This consumes it. Another report would have been the workaround.

FOUR DESIGN CALLS, each with its reason:
(1) IT GUARDS THE UPSERT, NOT THE RAW CREATE. The upsert is the merge path every surface writes through; a guard on a path nobody calls reports success and defends nothing.
(2) ABSENT IS A MISMATCH, NOT A CREATE. If the node is gone, somebody DELETED it while the caller was deciding, and silently recreating it would undo their removal — the same silent loss pointed the other way. Refused with its own message.
(3) THE HASH MOVED INTO THE CORE. The MCP surface computed it for the `revision` block; the moment it became a PRECONDITION, two implementations of one number became a way for a caller's correct expectation to be refused by an engine that agreed with them — and the divergence would appear only under contention, the one condition nobody tests by hand.
(4) OPT-IN. A caller who never read the node has no honest expectation to state, and making it mandatory would break every existing writer — a worse defect than the one being fixed.

⚠️⚠️ AND IT SHIPPED BROKEN FOR ONE COMMIT, CAUGHT ONLY BY DRIVING THE REAL SURFACE. Generic `create_node` carried NO `revision` block at all — the block was attached by the TYPED constructors and never by it. So the compare-and-swap existed with its precondition value UNOBTAINABLE FROM THE VERY TOOL THAT DEMANDED IT. Every core test passed. The MCP probe failed on its first run, at the line that reads `revision.prior_content_hash`. `create_node` now returns the block. This is AGENTS.md's "compiling is not the finish line, and neither is a green unit test" earning its place for the second time in two days.

MUTATION-CHECKED RATHER THAN TRUSTED: discarding the guard's refusal makes exactly the two probes that should fail, fail (stale read, deleted node), while the counterweight and the hash-stability probe correctly survive — so the suite is not vacuous in the way `dec:non-goal-reflow2-does-not-judge-whether-a-check-is-meaningful` says reflow2 cannot detect for you.

⚠️ HONEST BOUND, and it is the next question rather than a defect: the TYPED constructors (`add_decision`, `add_requirement`, `add_capability`, …) still merge with no expectation available. They are the commonest write path in practice, so the hole this closes is real but partial. Whether they should carry the parameter too is not settled — it is ~10 more surface changes, and the case for it is exactly the case made here.
properties.name: A write can be made conditional on what the caller read, so a lost update is refused rather than reported afterwards

properties.description: Read requirements, functions and structure back out of a running system.
properties.name: Recover a design from an existing system

properties.description: `gap_id` keys an AGGREGATE gap — one per project, whose affected set is the population its rule ranges over — on the rule alone, so its id is stable while the design grows and an acknowledgement of it carries instead of being re-asked on every addition. Every other gap keeps hashing its affected nodes, because there a changed subject genuinely deserves a fresh judgement. The discriminator is an explicit exhaustive `GapSource::is_aggregate()`, so a new aggregate detector must decide rather than inherit. Paired with the `retired` reporting `reviewed_gaps` already had: a stable id is only safe because a review whose rule stops firing is still shown, rather than silently kept.
properties.name: A gap about the whole population is keyed on its rule, so a standing judgement carries

properties.description: Score function-to-structure allocation; cluster coupling.
properties.name: Analyse and propose allocation

properties.description:
BUILT 2026-08-23 on Anthony's word, closing `fact:acknowledge-gap-records-a-judgement-without-recording-whose`. DISTINCT FROM that fact, which is the MEASUREMENT: it holds the numbers and how the defect stayed hidden; this is the remedy, so the design can say whether the fix happened separately from what it found.

`acknowledge_gap` and `acknowledge_gaps` take an optional `approver` (and `acted_at`) and draw `AUTHORED_BY role=approver` on the Decision they mint. The bulk form carries it PER ITEM, for the same reason `reason` is per item: a batch under one shared approver would record a judgement nobody made for every gap but one.

THREE BEHAVIOURS, and the middle one is a decision about consequence rather than a shortcut.
1. A named approver is recorded.
2. AN ABSENT APPROVER IS ALLOWED AND REPORTED. Refusing would leave a design that has modelled no Contributor unable to accept a gap at all — which is most solo designs on day one. So the reply says the acknowledgement carries nobody's name and will be reported by `check_intent_authority`, rather than accepting it in silence. That silence is what let 49 unattributed nodes be written in a single pass.
3. AN APPROVER NAMING NO CONTRIBUTOR IS REFUSED AND NOTHING IS WRITTEN. A typo would otherwise attach the owner's authority to somebody who does not exist, which is worse than recording none.

ADDITIVE: `acknowledge_gap`'s old signature is unchanged, so every existing caller still compiles and still works — it simply now gets told when it recorded nobody.
properties.name: An acknowledgement records whose judgement it was, and says so plainly when nobody's name is on it

properties.description:
An idea that connects to nothing is now visible AS SUCH — and an idea somebody judged and found genuinely new is not mistaken for one.

THE THIRD LEG of `dec:idea-do-ideas-form-a-graph-or-only-a-list`, accepted by Anthony 2026-08-21 as option (b): detect always, invite at a boundary.

WHAT IT DOES. `review_relations` records what a node relates to, or that nothing does. It is ONE DOOR for both outcomes and REFUSES when given neither — because the two honest endings of an act of relating are an edge and the finding that there is nothing to draw, and only the first left a trace before this. `Decision.no_relation_note` is where the second ending lives. `unreviewed_ideas` is the detector: one AGGREGATE finding naming the proposed Decisions that carry neither.

⭐ WHY THE NOTE IS THE WHOLE DESIGN AND NOT A DETAIL. Without it, "nobody looked" and "somebody looked and there was honestly nothing" are the SAME STATE — both carry no relation. A detector built over that would report the people who did the work, which is worse than not detecting at all: the careful answer becomes indistinguishable from the missing one, and then both get complained about.

🛑 WHY IT IS AGGREGATE AND LOW-SEVERITY. Per-idea it would have fired 115 times on reflow2's own graph the day it shipped — every one of them correct, and the whole category filtered by the end of the week. One finding names the practice and lists the ideas.

🛑 AND WHY NOTHING SUGGESTS RELATIONS. A false neighbour is worse than a missing one: a missing edge leaves an idea hard to find, an invented one puts a wrong neighbour in front of every later reader, and anything that searches by neighbourhood repeats it forever. So the tool takes judgements and never offers them.

THE TIMING IS AN INSTRUCTION, NOT CODE, which is how `req:detecting-is-not-asking` was delivered the first time (`cap:the-loop-holds-the-invitation`, a timing rule in three served surfaces). Detection is unconditional; the count is put to the user at a boundary — a capture-session, an increment close — never at the moment of thinking. The brainstorm skill's rule against running detect-and-ask over brainstormed nodes stands unchanged.

📌 PROVENANCE OF THIS NODE, recorded because the repair is the interesting part: it was created by a PROBE. The dedup guard refused the real write, I re-sent a differently-worded call to read the near-matches it had truncated, and THAT call was not refused — so the node landed carrying the placeholder text "probe of the guard's near-matches only". The lesson was already written down from 2026-08-20 and repeated anyway. **A refusal message that does not say "a reworded retry will land" is a message that invites one.**
properties.name: An idea that connects to nothing is visible as such — and one somebody judged is not mistaken for it

properties.description: At an epoch or release, answers "what didn't we achieve that we were supposed to?" — every scheduled item returned as delivered, deferred (and where to), discontinued, or OUTSTANDING (still due here, not delivered, and nobody has said which of the previous two it is — the question to put to the user rather than default). Work scheduled after the baseline comes back separately, because a delta measured only against the plan cannot see the work that was not in it. `required` claims that did not land are reported as computed violations rather than slips — the scheduling face of a KPP. The baseline is the target's FIRST snapshot with every later one as the movement trail, so a total slip stays visible across repeated replans; where no snapshot exists the plan never moved and the live edges are the baseline. NOTHING IS STORED: the plan lives in the snapshots and delivery is computed from the golden thread, so writing the outcome down would create a second source of truth able to disagree with the first (`dec:arrival-delta`, `req:completion-computed`).
properties.name: What was planned against what arrived, computed and never stored

properties.description: BL-188 and BL-191, built together because both are Artifact properties and a schema change costs the same for two as for one. THE SHARED FAILURE, which is why they are one capability rather than two: in each case the graph held two OPPOSITE states that produced an identical reading, and the tool reported the wrong one confidently. GRANULARITY (atomic / opaque / pending_expansion) — a directory Artifact claims its whole subtree, which is the adopt skill's own rule, so a registration check reported "every live doc is registered", truthfully, across 359 individually unreferenceable files, and coverage_report counted the directory as covering everything beneath it. A settled archive claimed on purpose and a placeholder nobody has got to yet were indistinguishable. coverage_report now returns pending_expansion and opaque_claims SEPARATELY, which makes "53 artifacts, of which 3 stand in for the rest" producible from the graph — a sentence that could not be formed at all before. Deliberately stores NO count of what a placeholder stands for: reflow2 does no file IO, so a stored number would be a caller-supplied figure nothing can recompute, the exact staleness BL-187 names. VOLATILITY (stable / append_only / living) — five coordination buses modelled with checksums, exactly per the adopt skill's instruction, produced five checksum_change divergences within minutes, all correct and all meaningless, with the disposition owed again on every reconcile forever. A content change on a volatile artifact now reports as expected_change and is not written to the drift ledger. IT IS REPORTED, NOT SUPPRESSED, and that is the load-bearing restraint: silence would trade a false positive for a false negative and let a wholesale replacement pass unmentioned, which is strictly the worse bug and the trap BL-176 was careful to avoid. Absence still fires at full severity whatever the volatility. SHRINK DETECTION IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT and stays open: a shrink is the genuinely alarming event for an append-only file, a checksum cannot express it, it needs a size baseline nothing records, and the reporting team's own compaction shrinks those files on purpose — so the heuristic needs the design's consent rather than a bare rule. BOTH VALUES ARE READ FROM THE NODE, NEVER INFERRED: no amount of looking at a tree recovers whether opacity was a decision, and no amount of hashing distinguishes a log that grew from a source file that was edited. Written by set_artifact_intent, a dedicated setter rather than arguments on add_artifact, because a constructor taking a partial property set and writing the whole node erases what the caller did not name (BL-183). Adding the properties without a tool to write them would have created two more properties reachable from nothing, which is BL-202's exact defect.
properties.name: An artifact declares what it stands for and how its content behaves, so a report can tell two opposite states apart

properties.description: A query surface on the graph's own time axis: what the design said at a given epoch, answered by the graph rather than by checking out an old export and reading it by hand. Anthony's acceptance tests, in his words (2026-07-30), are the target and the measure: which capabilities are due to be released in epoch 5, and what did we not achieve that we were supposed to in increment 10. The second is the harder half — it is a PLANNED-VERSUS-DELIVERED DELTA, computable only once an epoch has arrived, which is why this sits downstream of cap:planned-epochs. Reworded on Anthony's word 2026-07-30: the requirement previously described indexing git refs (the graph tracking where each snapshot lives), and that framing was retired when dec:where-plans-live settled that forward-looking plans describe graph content and stay in the graph — git keeps only the narrower job of pinning a version combination at an ARRIVED epoch. The original text is preserved at snap:epoch:planning-axis-intent:req:graph-indexes-snapshots. Approved for build by Anthony 2026-07-30.
properties.name: The graph answers as-of-epoch-n itself, without a git lookup

properties.description:
`scan_nodes` takes `level` — component / subsystem / system / system_of_systems / enterprise — so "what are the top-level boxes?" is one call with one answer. It refuses an unknown rung, and refuses `level` on any type other than Component rather than returning an empty list, because "no Components at that rung" and "that is not a rung" are different facts and the second silently reads as the first. A node with no level answers to `component`, matching the schema default, so older nodes are not lost by the filter.

WHY IT IS A CAPABILITY AND NOT A CONVENIENCE: the field was indexed and populated all along, and with no way to ask by it every caller derived the top tier from the containment spine — which returns leaves nobody wired to a parent. Measured on this design: 8 subsystems by declared level, 2 leaves by spine position.
properties.name: Ask for one rung of the decomposition ladder directly, instead of deriving it from the containment spine

properties.description: The stopping rule for the tree cap:requirement-lineage now holds (Anthony, 2026-07-25). A requirement is ATOMIC when it cannot be split further without losing meaning and one person or team can build and test it. Without a termination condition a decomposition goes wrong in BOTH directions, and the second is the dangerous one because it looks like rigour: under-decomposed leaves a compound requirement nobody can test cleanly; OVER-decomposed turns requirements into task lists and code design (\"the system must lock the account after three failed attempts\" is atomic; \"the system must query the login_attempts column and check if the integer equals 3\" is not a requirement at all). THE SIGNALS SPLIT THE SAME WAY THE QUALITY CRITERIA DO (dec:three-party-checks), which is what makes this buildable rather than advice. CHEAP AND DETERMINISTIC — build first: NO CONJUNCTIONS, a literal scan of the statement for \"and\", \"or\", \"additionally\", which is a text check needing no model and catching the most common compound requirement; SINGLE OWNER, computable from the graph as whether the capabilities satisfying it allocate to ONE component, since a leaf whose delivery is spread across several parts is not one team's to own; SINGLE TESTING POINT, partly computable as whether it has exactly one check rather than several. SEMANTIC — the agent proposes, the human decides: ESTIMABLE, and OVER-DECOMPOSED, which is the same judgement as the minimally-constrained criterion in cap:requirement-quality seen from the other end — a requirement that dictates implementation and a requirement decomposed into implementation are the same error, and noticing that they are one thing means one detector can serve both. Pairs with cap:missing-sibling: that asks whether a family is missing a member, this asks whether its members are the right SIZE, and a family of uneven grain is a signal for both. PLANNED.
properties.name: Know when to stop decomposing — and when someone went too far

properties.description:
"Rubber-ducking" mode — think it through before committing anything to the graph

*Idea file, line 7: "work through planning and idea realization before committing concepts to graph… agent-assisted thinking process."* This collides head-on with a recorded position, which is why it should be decided rather than drifted into: the git prior-art study explicitly listed the index/staging area under explicitly do NOT import — *"continuous-capture doctrine deliberately rejects a staging gate."* Rubber-duck mode is a staging area wearing a friendlier name. That is not a reason to drop it; the original rejection was aimed at a gate that sits between *every* edit and the graph, whereas this is an opt-in mode for a specific activity (early, exploratory thinking where most ideas are meant to be discarded). Note what already works today: a thinking session that simply makes no write calls is rubber-ducking, and the read tools (search_design, graph_report, propagate_from, alternatives_for) are exactly the ducking aids. So the real feature is narrower than it first looks — capturing the outcome of such a session in one deliberate act, with the discarded branches either dropped or preserved as unchosen alternatives (which is what the [BL-70] fork layer just built the vocabulary for: register_alternative under a proposed Decision). Design it as *"end the session by choosing what survives"*, not as a staging buffer in front of every tool. Size M

properties.description:
The inherited-project onboarding path: "where and how do I add this feature?"

*Idea file, line 9: "assume you inherit a mature project and your boss says, hey, we need to add a new feature. As the new worker, you don't know where to start."* Half of this exists and is good — where-am-i answers *what is this, what has been decided and why, what is still open*, which is the "summarize what it does" clause. Nothing answers the second and harder clause: where does this new thing GO. The pieces are all present and unassembled: search_design maps the user's words onto the components that already exist; propagate_from shows the blast radius of touching each candidate; alternatives_for / the Decision layer says what already governs that area and must not be casually contradicted; hierarchy_issues and the allocation view say which component *should* own a new capability; [BL-96]'s KPPs say what it must not break. A skill that runs that sequence and hands a newcomer "here is where this belongs, here is what it touches, here are the three decisions you must not violate, here is who authored them" is arguably reflow2's single strongest demo — it is the moment the graph pays for itself to someone who did not build it. Cheap relative to its value: a skill over existing tools, no core change. Pairs naturally with [BL-95] (a newcomer must be told which parts of the codebase the graph does NOT cover, or they will trust it too far). Size S–M

properties.description:
The README does not explain what this is or how it runs on your machine

*Idea file, line 13: "Needs a simple explanation of the architecture in the main README.md. How it runs on your computer. Very simple how to put the AGENT.md. Need some simple use cases. Probably need to create some cool images."* Fair and checkable: the README currently runs Vision → What this is → the hallucination question → the design vocabulary → Layout → three structural axes → phases → status → heritage → license, with the entire "how do I run this" reduced to one line at the top pointing at getting-started/SETUP.md. A reader who lands on the repo cold learns the philosophy before they learn that it is an MCP server that keeps a graph in a file in their repo. Wants: a one-paragraph plain-language architecture ("a binary you run locally, a graph in a file in your repo, your coding agent talks to it over MCP"), the AGENTS.md placement in two lines, two or three concrete use cases (greenfield capture, brownfield adopt, "what breaks if I change this"), and diagrams. Adoption-critical and cheap — it is the same req:frictionless-update family as BL-51, and the first thing a new user or Anthony's brother's colleagues actually hit. The images are the only expensive part; do the prose first and do not let it block on them. Size S (prose) + M (diagrams)

properties.description:
Design the simulator, and test there before the real thing

*Anthony, 2026-07-27, offered explicitly as a future idea rather than current work — captured as req:design-the-simulator (proposed, wants his word), and this row is the pointer.* The argument: a design has to operate in an environment, and where a simulated environment or a digital twin is reasonable to build, exercising the design there first removes risk while it is still cheap — an issue found in simulation costs a rebuild, the same issue found in the field costs a deployment. So the simulator is something to be designed, not an implementation detail that shows up later, and the progression simulation → progressively more realistic tests → fielding is part of the design process rather than an afterthought. The caveat is part of the requirement: not every design admits a meaningful simulation, and a tool that insisted would generate elaborate fictions for the ones that do not — so *is a simulator feasible and worth it for THIS design* is asked, never assumed, and a design that answers no says so on the record without being nagged. What already exists to build on (checked, not assumed): Verification.method accepts simulation, so a check CAN already be recorded as having been run in one; Environment and EnvironmentRule hold deployment and platform context. What is genuinely missing: nothing treats the simulator as a designed thing with its own requirements and fidelity claims; nothing expresses that a check run in simulation is weaker evidence than the same check run for real, which is the whole point of the progression; and there is no place to record the feasibility judgement. Note the fidelity axis reflow2 already has — as-designed / as-built / as-fielded — is the natural home for 'as-simulated' sitting before as-built, and that is probably the shape rather than a new subsystem. Size M–L

properties.description:
Link three real repos and find where their interfaces disagree — the composition proof of concept

*Anthony, 2026-07-27, captured while fresh rather than worked. Graph elements are the record: dec:linked-repos-poc (proposed), req:interface-spec-complete and req:seam-incompatibility (both proposed); this row is the pointer.* Build a reflow2 graph inside storyflow (adopt under way, unfinished) and another inside dynograph-foundation, then link them through their published surfaces and identify incompatibilities. The case is well chosen and not a toy: reflow2 AND storyflow both depend on dynograph-foundation, so it is a real three-way seam between three real repositories — built by the same author at different times against a foundation that moved, which is exactly how interface drift happens. The linking half already exists (dec:nested-graphs decided, cap:mirror-surface and cap:publish-surface built); the comparing half does not, and the reason is concrete. Measured against the six characteristics an interface spec needs — protocol *and* sync/async paradigm; payload format *and* field-level schema; endpoints *and* permitted methods; authentication and data protection; status vocabulary and parseable failure structure; rate limits, concurrency and timeouts — reflow2 structures roughly one and a half: Interface.medium and designation. Everything else is one free-text spec string or absent. So two graphs can be linked today and still not be comparable, and unprovided_interface only ever answers the wiring question (does the contract have both sides), never the one that bites in SoS work: both sides exist, both are confident, and they disagree. One note in reflow2's favour — #6 may need wiring rather than vocabulary, since Constraint already carries quantity/limit/direction and CONSTRAINS already rolls up, so rate limits and timeouts may be expressible now. Sequencing is the open choice in the decision: structure the spec first, or run the PoC against today's thin spec precisely to find out what it cannot say. Second payoff either way — it would be the first time reflow2 is pointed at a design it did not author, twice, which is the adopt path Anthony says his real work almost always starts from. PINNING, added by Anthony the same day as req:design-dependencies-declared (proposed): the consumer of a dependency should declare WHICH version/commit/tag of it they depend on, in a checked-in manifest — a reflow2.toml in the spirit of Cargo.toml / pyproject.toml / pixi.toml — so that when the two evolve separately you know what yours was built against. Half of this exists and the distinction is the point: cap:mirror-surface already records mirror_content_hash (the content hash of the surface a mirror was taken from) and mirrored_at, deliberately as a *dated claim* rather than live truth — that is what you GOT. A manifest is what you MEANT: human-meaningful (v0.11.0, not 64 hex characters), authored not derived, reviewable in a diff, readable before any graph is opened. Having both is what makes two checks possible that neither half supports alone — *declared vs mirrored* (am I composing against the version I said?) and *declared vs upstream* (has it moved since?). Must also handle a declared dependency that cannot currently be resolved, since that is a normal state and silence about it would be the failure, and must record which reflow2 wrote it — the same discipline the export stamp already follows, because a manifest read by an older or newer binary that cannot say which vocabulary it was written against forces the reader to guess. THE MECHANISM, added by Anthony the same day and better than what this row first implied (req:composed-analysis, proposed): checking whether two projects line up should be IMPORTING one graph into the other and running reflow2's ordinary checks — detect_gaps, check-health — over the combined design, so seam problems surface as the gaps they already are rather than needing a bespoke comparator nobody else benefits from. Same principle this project keeps rediscovering: make the existing computation SEE more rather than write a new one. What blocks it is concrete: import_graph writes every node under its ORIGINAL id with upsert semantics, so importing Z into A means Z's cap:store silently overwrites A's — it was built for layering a design onto *itself*. The other two mechanisms do not do this either: mirror_surface imports only the published surface and keeps it foreign; merge_designs is a three-way merge of two versions of the SAME design. So a fourth thing is needed — a namespaced import where both designs coexist and stay separately attributable. Two things not to lose: an export of A must never start shipping Z's internals, and project-level detectors would otherwise show a consumer its dependency's gaps — noise that gets a feature switched off, for which cap:scoped-analysis is the likely answer since it already narrows and reports what it left out. Note the tension with dec:nested-graphs (a graph per ownership boundary, because edges cannot cross stores): this does not overturn it — ownership and release stay separate — but it does add a THIRD, analysis-only composition. Size L

properties.description:
Nothing asks what order an increment can be built in, and budget.rs hand-rolls the algorithm that would answer it

*Found 2026-08-01 by a review of what dynograph-foundation v0.12.0 offers that reflow2 does not use, at Anthony's request. The headline number: reflow2 consumes 8 of 17 dynograph-graph exports, 2 of ~35 dynograph-vector functions, and none of dynograph-game — there is more unused foundation than used. The full option set, including the ideas NOT filed, is recorded as proposed Decisions (dec:idea-*) so the roads not taken stay in the design's memory.* Two findings, one function. (1) A simplification available today: budget.rs:312 implements Kahn's algorithm in about forty lines under a comment that says *"Kahn's toposort; leftovers mean a cycle"* — while dynograph_graph::topological_sort is exported, is Kahn's, is deterministic (the lexicographically-smallest valid order, so it is stable run to run) and returns None on a cycle. It was reimplemented because nobody knew it was there, which is itself the finding. (2) A capability that does not exist: capabilities form a DEPENDS_ON DAG that detect_defects insists stays acyclic, and nothing ever asks what order that DAG implies. reflow2 can say what is scheduled for an increment (SCHEDULED_FOR) and what has been delivered (the golden thread), but not *what can be started now*. Lands on [BL-68] (TRL/MRL readiness gating): that item asks whether a thing is ready, this asks whether its DEPENDENCIES are — the other half of the same question — and on epoch planning generally. THE SHAPE IS OPEN (dec:idea-build-order), and the objection is real: a topological order is ONE valid order among many, and presenting it as THE order would assert a schedule reflow2 has no business asserting — the overreach dec:report-dont-judge exists to prevent. The honest output is probably the READY FRONTIER (what currently has no unbuilt dependency) rather than a full ordering. Note also that (1) is not free: the local version works on string-id arcs while the foundation one wants a Graph built through GraphBuilder, so it trades forty tested lines for an adapter. properties.description:
A restructuring is safe exactly when function is provably preserved — and nothing computes that, so today it can only be asserted

*Anthony chose this, 2026-08-02, as the first step under [BL-179] / dec:maturity-restructuring-delta — of the two offered (this, or fork-and-measure on the 14 seams).* The invariant, from the decision: a maturity restructuring holds the function set INVARIANT and moves everything else, so it is safe exactly when no Capability was added or removed, no Requirement was added or removed, and no SATISFIES edge changed — only ALLOCATED_TO / CONTAINS / Interface edges moved. Why it is buildable now rather than invention: compare_designs already diffs two as-designed records at node and edge granularity, directionally and deterministically; what is missing is the classification that turns a diff into a verdict. The move it makes is dec:passing-is-verified's, applied to structure — the difference between a refactor someone hopes is safe and one the graph checked. Where it must not cheat, and this is the whole risk: a classifier with a hidden inclusion list would call a divergence it does not recognise "structural" and certify a design it never examined — [BL-170]'s fourth quadrant exactly. So the default is unclassified → indeterminate, never a silent pass, and an exhaustive test over the schema's own vocabulary fails the build when a new node or edge type lands with no class. Property changes on function-bearing nodes are indeterminate too: a reworded description may be a rename or a scope change, and the graph cannot tell — dec:three-party-checks says it counts and the human judges. What it deliberately does NOT claim: it compares two design records, so it says nothing about whether the code preserved function. Size M

properties.description:
Point at a folder of specs and ingest the lot — the missing half is identity resolution ACROSS documents

*Idea file, line 1: "somebody has an obscene amount of markdown files documenting specs of an application. He'd like to point at a folder and ingest all files… adds its graph components and the attached markdown (or pointers)."* Single-document extraction already exists and is good: ingest does multi-pass LLM extraction, and every claim keeps a provenance Fragment pointing back at the source text (YIELDED), which is exactly the "or pointers" half of the ask. What is missing is the folder driver and, underneath it, the hard part: cross-document identity. Forty specs mentioning the same service must converge on ONE node, not forty near-duplicates — and the primitive for that is already declared per node type in the schema (resolution: { strategy: fuzzy_then_vector, fuzzy_threshold: 80–85 }), so this is wiring an existing mechanism at batch scale rather than inventing one. Watch for: ordering effects (whichever file is read first wins the canonical name — needs to be deliberate, not incidental), the possible_duplicate gap firing N² times on a large corpus (BL-42's noise-floor lesson: a detector that punishes correct bulk work needs a different question, not a tuned threshold), and dec:ask-not-repair — suspected duplicates are asked, never merged, which at 500 files means the asking has to be batched or it is unusable. Sequencing note: BL-95's coverage sweep is the natural companion — ingest a folder, then measure what the ingest did not claim. SCOPED 2026-07-26 ([scope-corpus-ingest.md](scope-corpus-ingest.md)), and the reading moved the work in BOTH directions — this row's own framing was wrong in two places. (1) Cross-document identity is largely BUILT, not missing: fuzzy_match (ingest.rs:916) resolves each extracted node against *every existing node of that type in the whole graph*, so ingesting forty specs already converges — merges reported in IngestReport.fuzzy_merges, prior states snapshotted with a ChangeEvent rather than clobbered. What is missing is cost: scan_nodes is a full type scan run once per extracted node, so a corpus is quadratic. An indexing problem, not a research one. (2) The gap nobody had named is coverage of the ask. ingest creates exactly eight node types — Project, Requirement, Constraint, Capability, Component, Interface, plus Fragment and DesignEpoch. Verification and Decision have no extraction pass. The request was *"requirements, test results, designer intent"*: reflow2 extracts the first and neither of the others, so a corpus run today returns a design with no test evidence and no recorded rationale, from documents containing both, and nothing says so. Decision is the pass that makes an old corpus worth ingesting at all — *why* it was built that way is exactly what is lost when the people leave. (3) The real blocker is reachability: ingest takes an LlmBackend, reflow2 ships no provider, and no ingest tool exists among the 108 served — so core ingest cannot be called from a session at all, and the only working path today is the adopt skill. The fork is recorded as dec:corpus-ingest-mechanism (proposed, wants Anthony): an agent-driven skill, or the SP-3b handshake with the agent as the backend. (4) Two smaller findings: this row's claim that the schema's per-type resolution: { fuzzy_threshold } is the primitive is wrong — nothing reads those declarations; ingest uses a hardcoded FUZZY_MATCH_THRESHOLD: u32 = 90 (the fifth instance of declared-but-never-read, after BL-70, BL-96, BL-35 and BL-106). And auto-merging at 90 across a corpus is in tension with dec:ask-not-repair in a directional way — *"Auth Service"* and *"Auth Service v2"* score high. Named user waiting (a colleague of the author's brother, years of work markdown). Size M–L

properties.description: BUILT 2026-07-25 as the brainstorm skill + the /brainstorm command. Anthony's brother's original ask ("work through planning and idea realization before committing concepts to graph... an agent-assisted thinking process"), reframed by Anthony into what it actually is: not a staging gate but a KIND of record. Ideas enter the graph immediately as `proposed` Decisions named as open questions, with the options in the decision text and the honest counter-argument beside each; nothing waits outside in a buffer where it could be forgotten, and nothing is claimed as intent. THE MECHANISM THAT MAKES IT WORK WAS ALREADY THERE, found while building: detect_gaps raises undecided_decision_point ONLY on a proposed Decision with two or more REGISTERED alternatives, so a Decision whose options live in prose is silent by construction — and the nudge to choose arrives exactly when register_alternative turns an option into a fork with a design behind it. The loop stays quiet while someone thinks, and speaks the moment the ideas stop being ideas. No label, no schema change, no upgrade doc. THE GUARDS, all prose because none is machine-checkable: never create Requirements or Capabilities from a brainstorm (promotion is a separate step needing the user's word); never argue an idea down in conversation — record the objection beside it, because an idea killed in dialogue loses its reasoning; never run detect-and-ask over brainstormed nodes, which would ask the user to firm up exactly what they left soft; and never promote the last idea standing, since one remaining idea nobody chose is still an idea nobody chose. set_decision_status to `proposed` is mandatory, because add_decision defaults to `accepted` and would assert a settlement that never happened. Ends as a PROMOTION step, not a commit step: chosen ideas go through capture-intent, the rest stay recorded as considered rather than deleted (req:roads-not-taken). The one honest weakness is readability — a person scanning the decision list cannot tell a musing from a choice without reading the prose, which is what the open vocabulary question in dec:exploratory-staging is now reduced to.
properties.name: Work an idea through without committing to it, on the record

properties.description: Sum contributions along the thread; refuse a total it cannot honestly compute.

properties.description:
The surplus half of DETECT. Every existing gap asks what is MISSING; this asks what is SURPLUS — realized or verified, and downstream of nothing.

THE SIGNAL, computable from the graph as it stands: a Capability at `realized`/`verified` with no incoming DEPENDS_ON, no PART_OF_FLOW into any Flow, and no Actor INTERACTS_WITH. The same shape generalises to a Component whose Interfaces nothing CONSUMES, and to an Artifact realizing only capabilities that are themselves unconsumed.

⚠️ THE WORDING IS THE FEATURE, not a caveat on it. The graph knows DESIGN-LEVEL demand and nothing about runtime usage, so the honest finding is \"NOTHING IN THIS DESIGN CONSUMES X\" — never \"X is unused\". A feature real users call daily whose consumer was never modelled produces exactly the same graph shape as a dead one, and a detector that did not say so would confidently recommend deleting working code. Reported as a FACT rather than a gap for the same reason granularity_report and surprising_connections are: which side is wrong is the user's to say.

WHY IT IS NOT unmotivated_capability: that fires on a capability satisfying no REQUIREMENT — a question about intent, gated on requirements existing at all. A capability can satisfy a requirement perfectly and still be consumed by nothing, and that is the expensive case, because the paperwork is complete and the code is dead.

DELIBERATELY NOT COVERED HERE: runtime usage. dec:bl-155 and dec:idea-measure-the-surface hold that question, and answering it needs telemetry rather than the graph.
properties.name: A built thing that nothing in the design consumes is surfaced, and says so as a design-completeness finding rather than a verdict on the system

properties.description: Bulk forms for every tool BL-153's surface measurement caught calling itself: create_nodes, create_edges, set_artifact_checksums, acknowledge_gaps, gaps_to_prompts. 52.9% of all tool-to-tool transitions across 46 sessions and 6,095 calls were self-loops; these answer set_artifact_checksum 244, create_node 112, contains 109, acknowledge_gap 90, gap_to_prompt 83, contain_component 77 and satisfies 74. create_edges is ONE tool rather than six because contains/contain_component/satisfies/allocate/realizes are thin wrappers that only fill in the endpoint types, and BL-155's 40-never-called count makes near-identical tools a cost. Every form is all-or-nothing WITH per-item findings, and every form that records a judgement keeps that judgement per item.
properties.name: One call where the surface measured N

properties.description:
When a session captures intent by READING a document — a feedback file, a brief, a handover note, a spec someone emailed — the skill registers that document as an Artifact and draws DOCUMENTS from it to every node the reading produced. The link is made at capture time, by the skill that is already holding the file open, rather than by anybody remembering to come back for it.

WHY IT IS NEEDED, measured on reflow2's own design 2026-08-11 rather than assumed. `req:no-idea-goes-quiet` is ACCEPTED and requires the backward half explicitly — "BACKWARD to the document and location it was written in. The user must never again have to recall that they wrote something, hunt for the file, and hand-point an agent at it." Its statement also says the backward half is handled: "already carried by ingest: every extracted node gets YIELDED to its provenance Fragment."

  Requirements in the design                                        154
  with ANY backward provenance edge (YIELDED or DOCUMENTS)            1
  without                                                           153

⇒ THE CLAIM IS TRUE OF A PATH THIS DESIGN BARELY USES. 148 Fragments exist, and they hang off Artifacts, not Requirements. Requirements here arrive by CONVERSATION — an agent reads something or listens to somebody and calls `add_requirement` — and that path records no source at all. The covered path and the used path are different paths, which is why an accepted requirement can be 1/154 satisfied without anybody noticing.

⭐ THE PROOF IS THE SESSION THAT FOUND IT. On 2026-08-11 Anthony had to tell an agent that reflow2's governance work came from `dev_storyflow/reflow2_feedback.md`, because nothing in the graph said so. `req:no-idea-goes-quiet` was captured on 2026-08-04 FROM HIS COMPLAINT ABOUT DOING EXACTLY THAT — "It was always manual process of me trying to find the document or documents that I had written the idea/requirement in and then purposefully point the agent to it." Seven days after recording the complaint, the design made him do the thing he complained about.

SCOPE, deliberately narrow. This covers capture FROM A DOCUMENT, where a file exists to point at. It does NOT attempt the harder case — intent that arrives in conversation with no document behind it, where the honest source is a session rather than a path — because inventing an Artifact for a conversation would put a fabricated file location in the graph, and `req:a-repair-suggestion-never-proposes-fabrication` is accepted. That case is left open rather than half-answered.

WHAT IT MUST NOT DO, taken from the parent requirement's own warning: it must not auto-draw SATISFIES or REALIZES from similarity. DOCUMENTS is a provenance edge — "this text is where that came from" — and carries no claim that anything was delivered. The parent is explicit that auto-linking delivery "would make every captured idea read as delivered and the completion reading say 100% forever."

ORIGIN: promoted from `dec:idea-should-a-requirement-trace-back-to-its-demand-signal`, option (b), on Anthony's word 2026-08-11. Option (a) — a detector for a Requirement with no origin edge — was NOT taken, because at genesis nobody has a source document and such a check would fire against an entire design on day one, with fabrication as the only way to green it.
properties.name: Capture FROM a document registers that document and links what came out of it, so the backward half of the thread exists by construction

properties.description:
The `capture-session` skill, shipped 2026-08-12 as the FIRST STEP settled in dec:idea-a-capture-session-skill-the-user-types. Served like every other skill (19 in the catalogue) and invocable at any point in a session, not only at the end.

WHAT IT IS, PRECISELY: a TRIGGER, not a memory. cap:session-memory stays PLANNED and this does not realize it — the connective tissue still has no node type of its own, which the skill states as one of its own limits rather than papering over.

THE TWO PROBLEMS IT HAD TO SOLVE, both left open by the brainstorm node:
  1. WHO JUDGES IMPORTANCE. Not solved by judgement — solved by removing the judgement. The skill gives six concrete tests (a reason that exists nowhere else / somebody measured something / the user corrected you / something was tried and abandoned / a finding arrived sideways / the user stated a rule in passing) under one question: would a session six weeks from now redo this work because nobody wrote it down?
  2. NO HOME FOR THE TISSUE. Routed to nearest neighbours, explicitly and reversibly: reasoning into its Decision, a road not taken into that same Decision's text, a measurement to a TemporalFact, a project change to a ChangeEvent, a lesson to a DesignEpoch, a stated rule to a DesignRule, new intent OUT to capture-intent.

HONEST STANDING: req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session is ACCEPTED, says the user must never be the trigger, and is NOT met by this. The skill says so in its own text so a reader cannot mistake shipped for satisfied.

═══ FIRST DOGFOOD, 2026-08-12, WITHIN THE HOUR — AND IT FOUND A HOLE IN ITS OWN ROUTING TABLE ═══

Anthony ran the skill to close the session it was built in ("can we try our new skill out?"). It worked, and the most useful output was a defect in itself.

🛑 THE ROUTING TABLE HAS NO ROW FOR A FACT ABOUT THE USER. Test 3 ("did the user correct you?") and test 6 ("did the user state a rule in passing?") both fired on the same correction from earlier in the session: Anthony was referred to in the THIRD PERSON in a reply addressed TO HIM ("the owner reports…"). The rule that came out of it — SECOND PERSON when speaking to the user, THIRD PERSON in graph node text, because a node is a durable record for later readers who need a name — is exactly what test 6 is for. But the table's only offer is DesignRule, and that is wrong: this is not a rule about reflow2's design, it is a fact about a person. Writing it as a DesignRule would put a user preference into the design vocabulary where every future reader has to route around it.

⇒ THE CORRECT HOME WAS THE AGENT'S OWN MEMORY, NOT THE GRAPH, and the skill does not say so. The gap is narrow and real: the six tests are written to catch things about the PERSON as readily as things about the DESIGN, while the routing table below them only knows how to place design content. An agent following the skill literally would either drop the finding or mis-file it.

FIX DIRECTION (not applied — recorded so the next reader does not re-derive it): the routing table needs a row for "a fact about the user, or how they want to be worked with" pointing OUT of the graph, the same way "new intent" already points out to capture-intent. The skill already has the shape for this; it is one row.

📌 WHAT THE SKILL GOT RIGHT ON ITS FIRST RUN, worth recording because it is the failure mode it was written against: it DECLINED to capture. A drifted prose count in getting-started/README.md ("the 15 workflows" while the kit served 18) was noticed, fixed in the same commit, and deliberately NOT given a node — a later session would have re-fixed it in two minutes, so nothing would have been lost. And the session's MCP outage was routed to an EXISTING fact as an addendum rather than a fifth near-duplicate node. Two of the four candidates that came up were correctly refused.

⚠️ CAVEAT ON THIS RUN'S EVIDENCE, per the skill's own instruction to say what could not be verified: the session was COMPACTED, so its earlier hours survive only as a summary. Everything above is from the post-compaction stretch, which was directly observed.
properties.name: A user-typed trigger for capturing what only the session holds

properties.description: Classify every divergence between two as-designed records as function-bearing, structural, or unclassified, and return a verdict — preserved / not_preserved / indeterminate — naming the invariant checked and what the check could not see. Function is the Capability and Requirement population plus the SATISFIES links between them; structure is allocation, containment, interfaces and the seams between components. Unclassified never passes: an unrecognised divergence makes the verdict indeterminate, so a classifier that has not been taught a new part of the vocabulary cannot certify a design it never examined.
properties.name: Certify that a restructuring preserved function

properties.description: Snapshot prior state at an epoch, then edit — axis Z.
properties.name: Record a change

properties.description: Anthony's B+K / B-K case, 2026-07-25: the project does A, B, C and D, and the ask is to make B do something more (or less). Distinct from cap:onboarding (BL-101), which answers where a NEW thing belongs — this answers where an EXISTING thing gets extended or narrowed, and the difference matters because the answer is shaped by what B already touches rather than by where a gap is. Mostly composition of machinery that exists and has never been aimed at this question: search_design maps the user's words onto B; propagate_from gives the blast radius of touching it; the Decision layer says what already governs B and must not be casually contradicted; cap:requirement-lineage would say whether B is a decomposed child (so the parent's other children are siblings that may need the same change) or carries derived requirements that the extension might invalidate. THE SIMPLIFICATION DIRECTION IS THE INTERESTING HALF and is not symmetric with extension: removing capability from B means asking what still depends on it, which is propagate run the other way, and then whether any requirement is left unsatisfied by the removal — a question retire-from-design already forces for a whole node but nobody asks for a partial reduction. Removing is where designs are damaged quietly, because the thing that breaks is usually not the thing being edited. PLANNED.
properties.name: Show where to extend or simplify a feature that already exists

properties.description: Derive a Keep a Changelog-shaped draft (keepachangelog.com, Anthony's pointer 2026-07-28) between any two Releases or Epochs, from what the graph already records: the INCLUDES delta between two Release manifests (what appeared, what left) plus the dated ChangeEvents and drift accepts between their epochs, classified into the KaC buckets — Added / Changed / Deprecated / Removed / Fixed — mapped from the vocabulary the graph already carries (new nodes and link_artifact baselines -> Added; design_updated accepts and amended statements -> Changed; retire-from-design with history -> Deprecated/Removed; design_holds accepts with change_type test_failure_fix -> Fixed). The [Unreleased] section is the standing case: everything dated after the last deployed Release — which makes 'what would this increment's changelog say?' answerable BEFORE cutting it, the capability-increment sibling of what-next. Two KaC principles carried over as constraints: changelogs are FOR HUMANS, curated — this emits a DRAFT a person edits, never a commit-log dump (KaC names raw logs an antipattern; dec:report-dont-judge is the same rule here) — and every entry says what a CONSUMER does about it, which the graph cannot know alone. Kin to cap:compare-designs (two as-designed records); this compares two moments of ONE design and renders the difference in the format industry already reads. DIRECTIONALITY, Anthony's formulation 2026-07-28, which is the load-bearing claim: 'our delta is a graph/machine version of a human changelog; the agent could derive the human changelog from the graph delta. Basically: graph delta --via_agent--> human changelog.' The graph delta is the primary, machine-readable record; the human changelog is a derived rendering, and never the other way around -- when the two disagree, the graph is what is interrogated and the changelog is what gets regenerated.
properties.name: A changelog is a derivable view of the graph's own delta

properties.description: claim_region accepts a QUERY describing the region, alongside the existing seed+depth. The query is evaluated at read time, every time, so the claim still follows the design as it changes — the property the seed+depth rule was chosen for, and the reason an explicit stored node list is refused (dec:a-claim-may-need-a-list-rather-than-a-radius). Serves cross-cutting duties a radius cannot describe: an audit, a sweep over everything of one kind, cold-validating what another session recorded. Two questions are deliberately left to the build: which query language, and whether an unevaluable or empty query is refused at claim time or reported at read time. claim_report must be able to say which shape a claim used, or a reader cannot tell a narrow region from a query that stopped matching.
properties.name: A claim describes its region by a query, for work no radius can express

properties.description:
Every claim records a seat — machine:pid:mint, minted once per session with zero coordination — defaulting to the session making it, overridable with a durable handle (a fleet worker name). claim_report then COMPUTES liveness rather than storing it: nothing writes 'I am alive', so nothing can be stale. A claim whose session is no longer attached is reported `gone`, listed in `stale` with its note intact, and EXCLUDED from overlaps, because a collision with nobody is not a collision and reporting it as one is how an advisory report starts lying. A claim from another machine, or from before seats were recorded, is `unknown` and still counts as a possible collision — reading it as free would invite somebody to take work that is actively being done.

HOW LIVENESS IS COMPUTED DEPENDS ON WHO MINTED THE SEAT, and this is the part that was wrong until 2026-08-08. A seat carrying ANOTHER process's pid is answered by asking the operating system whether that process still exists — so a seat left behind by a previous shared server correctly reads `gone` after a `--stop-shared` bounce. A seat THIS process minted cannot be answered that way, because under `--shared` every seat is minted by the daemon and the daemon's pid is alive by definition: the probe asked 'is the server running?', to which the answer is always yes, and `gone` was unreachable. Measured in dev_storyflow (w-613d836b, 2026-08-07): a worker that had died hours earlier still read as holding its region, and this capability was status `verified` throughout. Those seats are now answered from the sessions the server is actually holding — a lease registered on attach and released by Drop, so a client that crashes retires its seat exactly like one that exits cleanly. The registry answers only for seats the process itself issued; anything else falls through to the probe, so a bare mint_seat elsewhere in the process cannot make an unrelated seat read as a ghost.

WHY THE ORIGINAL CHECK DID NOT CATCH IT, recorded because the shape recurs: the property was true under the stdio transport, where the serving process WAS the session. `--shared` became the installed default, the world moved, and nothing recomputes a check when the deployment model changes underneath it. The test that covered it still passed, because in a test process the server and the session are the same thing.
properties.name: A claim names the session that made it, and a claim nobody is working says so

properties.description: Three parts, smallest first. (1) CAPTURE-TIME GUIDANCE: when a statement asserts what the system is right now, the capture path names TemporalFact rather than letting prose be the path of least resistance — subject_id is its only required property, and VALID_FROM / VALID_TO attach it to epochs. (2) A DETECTOR: a Requirement whose statement asserts current system state, with no TemporalFact and no VALID_TO, is unfalsifiable by construction and nothing reports it today. (3) AGE AT READ-BACK: where-am-i and search_design mark how old a node's factual half is, so a six-week-old observation is not narrated as current. Part 3 belongs with the read-half increment; parts 1 and 2 stand alone.
properties.name: Time-bound claims land in a TemporalFact, and age is visible where claims are read

properties.description: Claim a region of the design so two people do not collide in it (BL-44). BUILT 2026-07-25 as claims.rs, exposed as claim_region / release_claim / claim_report (96 tools). A new CLAIMS edge, Contributor → any node, carrying depth / claimed_at / note. THE SHAPE IS SET BY dec:multi-writer-architecture, and every part of it follows from having no server. A CLAIM IS NOT A LOCK. Nothing in the module refuses a write and nothing anywhere consults a claim before allowing one; a second writer who ignores a claim gets a correct three-way merge exactly as if it did not exist. That is pinned by a test rather than promised in a comment, because a claims layer that READS like locking is worse than none — it invites reliance on a guarantee it cannot make. THE REGION IS COMPUTED, never stored: a claim holds a seed and a depth, and the membership is derived through the same traversal propagate_from uses, so it follows the design as the design changes instead of freezing a list that silently goes wrong the moment someone adds an edge (pinned: new work inside a claimed area is covered without re-claiming). OVERLAP IS REPORTED, NEVER PREVENTED. Two people may claim the same ground and both claims stand; claim_report names the shared nodes and ranks collisions by size, because a two-node brush and a forty-node collision should not read alike. Two claims by the SAME person are not a collision — reporting them would train people to ignore the list, which is how a signal dies. The advisory limit ships IN the payload, not only in the docs, since whoever reads it over the wire never sees the docs. CLAIMS is deliberately NOT a traceability edge, like AUTHORED_BY: who is working on something is coordination, not design structure, and propagating it would drag people into every blast radius (pinned by a test). 9 tests. Schema change: edge types 54 → 55.
properties.name: Claim a region of the design so two people do not collide in it

properties.description: Load N alternative design exports (branch-by-file) and report each branch on the same measures — graph_report snapshot (nodes, open gaps, allocation health, verification coverage) side by side — plus each branch's structural divergence from a named baseline (compare_designs). Alternatives comparable on measures, not advocacy. BL-70 v1; the collapse (merge winner + retire losers) reuses BL-80. Rung 2 wires the decision point.
properties.name: Compare parallel alternatives on the same measures (AoA)

properties.description: Diff two export documents (or the live graph against one) into added / removed / changed relative to a named base, banded into design content vs bookkeeping, property-level on changes.
properties.name: Compare two as-designed records

properties.description:
CHANGE 2 of epoch:the-declared-walls-hold. Anthony's word, 2026-08-20. DISTINCT FROM change 1: that one moves nothing in the code and this one moves ~15 lines; they share an epoch and neither blocks the other.

THE WHOLE DEPENDENCY, read rather than assumed: `compare.rs` line 45 is `use crate::report::is_design_type;` and that is ALL of it. The function is two lines — `SNAPSHOT_TYPES.contains(&node_type)` — answering "is this design content, or supporting material like provenance and history?". So a 974-line module reaches into a 2025-line reporting module to borrow a lookup in a constant list, and that single edge is the whole `sys:time-history -> sys:coherence-loop` back-edge behind the second subsystem cycle.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: duplicate the list. The sharing is CORRECT and report.rs says why in as many words — compare reuses it so "design vs supporting" means one thing everywhere. Two copies would drift.

WHAT IT DOES: move SNAPSHOT_TYPES and is_design_type down into `nodes`. Three reasons, and the third is why this is a better home rather than a cycle-driven contortion:
  1. the list is built ENTIRELY out of `node::` constants — it is a statement about node types, so it belongs with the node types;
  2. `report` and `compare` BOTH already depend on `nodes`, so this adds no coupling at all — it only stops compare reaching sideways;
  3. one shared definition survives, which is the property worth protecting.

SIMULATED: with change 1 also applied, dropping this edge makes all eight subsystems a DAG — no cycles at any level.

SHAPE WORTH NAMING: this is the same shape all three of PR #262's cycles had — ONE back-edge, and the fix is to ask what the borrowing module actually needed rather than to restructure anything.
properties.name: Comparing two designs stops reaching into the reporting layer for a two-line lookup

properties.description: compare_designs reads the `reflow2_version` each side's stamp already carries and, when they differ, says so in its result alongside the finding counts — naming build skew as a possible cause of property-only differences without suppressing, reweighting or hiding any of them. The reader is told what could confound the reading; nothing decides on their behalf.
properties.name: A comparison discloses that its two sides came from different builds

properties.description:
`Interface.designation` carries the boundary's external ROLE — `published` (offers), `required` (needs one from outside), `both`, or `internal` — and `pair_designs` matches COMPLEMENTS across two designs: published/both against required/both, never like with like. The `required` half did not exist before 2026-07-30, which is why a design could say what it offered but not what it needed in any form another design could be matched against.

Two boundaries pair when their names match fuzzily (reusing ingest's two-band resolution rather than a second matcher) AND they agree on `medium`, `transport_security` and `auth`. Five outcomes: paired, CONFLICTS (names match, axes refuse — reported with every refusing axis), unmet needs, dead surface, and duplicate providers. Uncertain names are candidates to ask about, never actions. Boundaries with no role are counted and named, because `internal` is the default and cannot distinguish a deliberate choice from an unlabelled one. Produces the pairs `seam_report` previously had to be handed by a person.
properties.name: Two designs pair by complementary role, so the seam is computed rather than hand-wired

properties.description: compose_and_analyse imports another design alongside this one and runs reflow2's ORDINARY checks — detect_gaps and detect_defects — over the combined whole, so seam problems arrive as the gaps they already are rather than needing a bespoke comparator. Anthony's mechanism, and better than the comparison the requirement first implied: make the existing computation SEE more rather than write a new one. WHY IT IS NOT import_graph: that writes every node under its ORIGINAL id with upsert semantics, because it exists to layer an export onto the design it came from — point it at a DIFFERENT design and the dependency's cmp:store silently overwrites the consumer's, which is corruption with no error. Ids are therefore namespaced to {namespace}::{id}, edges rewritten with them, and an empty namespace is REFUSED rather than allowed to collide by omission. NOTHING IS WRITTEN TO EITHER DESIGN: the combined graph is built in memory and thrown away, following the ingest handshake's prepare-round precedent. That disposes of both hazards the requirement named — an export of yours can never start carrying theirs, and there is no residue to clean up — and it is pinned by a test asserting your export's content_hash is byte-identical afterwards. FINDINGS ARE ATTRIBUTED ours / theirs / seam, because a consumer shown its dependency's internal gaps as if they were its own will switch the feature off, and rightly. The seam bucket is the point: findings neither design could have produced alone. Sits alongside the two composition mechanisms that already existed without replacing either — mirror_surface takes the published surface only and keeps it foreign, merge_designs reconciles two versions of the SAME design — and it does not overturn dec:nested-graphs, since ownership and release stay separate; this is a third, analysis-only composition.
properties.name: Analyse two designs together without merging them

properties.description:
