properties.description: A first baseline and a clean check are recorded as what they are, rather than as changes that never happened. `set_artifact_checksum` gains a third disposition, `baseline_established`, for an artifact registered with no checksum getting its first one — the record moves and the code does not — and which disposition is available is a fact about the artifact rather than a preference: an accept against no baseline is refused, and a baseline_established that would MOVE an existing one is refused, so the new word cannot launder real drift past the two-sided accept. A recording reconcile stamps `Artifact.last_confirmed_at` on every artifact observed to still match, so a pass that found everything correct is distinguishable from a pass nobody ran; the confirmation ledger counts those toward examined, and reports first baselines apart from accepts because a first baseline is not a judgement anyone made.
properties.name: The ledger can say that nothing moved

properties.description:
The loop-nudge state carried on the handshake instructions and on `loop_status` distinguishes a harness that has no hook reflow2 can register from one that supports the hook and lacks it, so only the actionable case reads as something to fix. Consumes the harness answer collected at install time, since the state cannot be derived from the filesystem alone.

Extends `cap:nudge-path-proven` (verified) rather than duplicating it: that capability proves the hook path end to end and reports `installed | absent | broken | unknown`. This narrows `absent`, which today means both "not registered" and "not registerable here".
properties.name: The nudge report says whether the trigger is missing or impossible

properties.description: Two halves. PROOF: tools/test_nudge_path.py reads .claude/settings.json, takes the command the harness would run, and runs THAT with the JSON a real Stop hook receives — asserting the {"decision":"block"} the harness actually consumes, that the reason names what happened, that a session which ran the loop check is left alone, and that the nudge fires once (on the harness's stop_hook_active) rather than holding a session hostage. BACKSTOP: the server looks for a registered Stop hook and reports installed | absent | broken (registered but the script is missing — the dangerous middle case, since the settings file looks right) | unknown (project dir undeterminable, never reported as absent). The advisory rides the HANDSHAKE INSTRUCTIONS, the one channel every session reads unasked, and loop_status carries the same as a machine-readable field. This matters because reflow2_init installs no hooks at all: every consumer project has no session-end nudge, and until now nothing said so.
properties.name: The loop's own safety net is checked, and its absence is announced

properties.description:
Answer "we need to add this — where does it go?" from the graph, for someone who did not build the system. Assembles machinery that already exists and had never been pointed at this question: map the newcomer's words onto the parts that exist, show what touching each candidate would reach, name the decisions already governing that area and who authored them, name the intent it must not break, and say honestly which parts of the real system the design does not cover. Distinct from saying where the design stands, which answers what the system is and what was decided but not where new work belongs. No core change — a skill over existing operations.

✅ BUILT 2026-08-29 — BL-101, accepted in the eight-requirement batch and unbuilt until now. `getting-started/skills/onboarding/SKILL.md`, served and mirrored, reachable by the `/where-does-it-go` command as well as by name.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES, in order: `search_design` on THE USER'S OWN WORDS before any paraphrase (a mismatch between their vocabulary and the design's is itself the finding, and is why a newcomer cannot find anything); `scan_nodes` with `level` for the rung a person reasons about, passed rather than derived from containment, because deriving it returns leaves nobody wired to a parent; `design_regions` and `granularity_report` to narrow, since a part already realizing many capabilities is where new work lands badly; `propagate_from` per candidate for the number that changes minds — 6 nodes against 40; `GOVERNED_BY` with `alternatives_for` and `recall_resolutions` for what already rules there; `claim_report` for who is in that ground now.

⭐ TWO THINGS IT INSISTS ON. **A NAME, not just a ruling** — `AUTHORED_BY` lets a decision be handed over as "this was Anna's call and here is why", which is a thing a new hire can ask about rather than a wall. And **ONE RECOMMENDATION FIRST**, not a survey: a newcomer handed five balanced candidates has been given the original problem back with more words attached.

🛑 AND THE CLAUSE THAT IS NON-OPTIONAL: step 5 says what the design CANNOT see — `coverage_report` for files no Artifact points at, `detect_gaps` scoped to the candidate, `seam_report` for whether the boundary is stated or assumed. A design is silent about what it does not model, and silence reads exactly like "no problem here". A confident answer drawn from a design that does not cover the relevant part is worse than no answer, because the person receiving it cannot tell which kind of silence they got.
properties.name: Tell a newcomer where a new piece of work belongs

properties.description:
A project can optimise one of its own modules against a target it wrote down FIRST — so the work has a condition under which it is finished, and leaves a measurement a later session can re-run.

THE 21st SERVED SKILL, and the first about improving something rather than describing it. Anthony, 2026-08-21: "reflow2 is a tool for other projects... should we introduce an /optimize skill that any project could do on its modules?"

WHAT IT ACTUALLY CARRIES IS THE ORDER AND THE REFUSALS, not technique. Techniques belong to the project's own stack and reflow2 cannot supply them. It supplies: measure before forming an opinion and be willing to conclude NOTHING HERE; measure the product surface before the developer surface; find the cause by falsifiable experiment on a COPY; write the budget down BEFORE the code, derived rather than picked; re-measure against the BUDGET rather than the starting point and STOP when it is met; leave a guard asserting the STRUCTURE that makes the code fast rather than a wall-clock duration; and when a rule refuses the change, pay it in prose rather than weakening it.

THE THREE STEPS THAT EARNED THEIR PLACE each caught a real mistake in the two runs it was written from: a 14.8x speedup that was still over budget and would have shipped as a success; a duration gate that failed on suite contention and would have been fixed by raising the threshold, retiring it; and an architectural rule a cache quietly traded away, which cost one paragraph to pay honestly.

IT DOES NOT WAIT FOR CONTRACTS. The first framing put optimisation after black boxes are identified. Measured: optimising needs a WALL, a TARGET and a MEASUREMENT, and both runs succeeded with the wall ABSENT because the other two were supplied. Gating on declared interfaces would withhold the cheapest return until the most expensive one is finished.

HONEST LIMIT, WRITTEN INTO THE SKILL RATHER THAN OUT OF IT: the procedure has been run TWICE. skill_lint's OPTIMIZE_CONTRACT pins that admission alongside the nine other load-bearing clauses, so it cannot be quietly deleted once the skill feels established.
properties.name: A project can optimise a module against a budget written down first

properties.description:
A contributor scope on the loop's own reporting: today loop_status answers "what does this design owe?" and takes no arguments at all, while detect_gaps already accepts a scope for one part of the design — so this follows an established pattern rather than inventing one.

The input already exists and is already structured: AUTHORED_BY with role=approver is the graph SAYING that a named contributor owes an answer here. Nothing computes on it today. The narrowest useful first cut is a loop_status field counting Decisions that are proposed AND carry an approver edge, which closes the concrete instance without disturbing the deliberate quiet around brainstormed decisions.

Larger shapes recorded but not chosen: a distinct gap source for a Decision proposed-and-assigned-but-not-settled (separate from undecided_decision_point, which reasonably wants real forks); and letting a Question be raised against a node directly, decoupling the Question machinery from gap derivation — the largest change, and the one that would let a specific question be put to a specific person and the answer tracked.

NOTIFICATION IS DELIBERATELY NOT PART OF THIS. proxy.rs holds that the server never initiates a message, verified against the service rather than assumed; that property is worth keeping and a consumer can poll. What must live here is the ANSWER to "what is owed to this person", because only the graph knows.
properties.name: The loop answers what is owed to a named person, computed from edges the graph already carries

properties.description:
The third "who" axis. AUTHORED_BY says who WROTE something (past tense, never changes); CLAIMS says who is IN it right now (transient, released at checkout); OWNED_BY says whose ground it is, and it survives every session.

BUILT: the edge (`* → Contributor`, with `note` and `since`), a served `owned_by` tool, and the read that makes it earn its keep — loop_status(contributor_id) reports `gaps_on_owned_ground`, each entry naming WHICH owned nodes the gap stands on, and `not_attributable` shrinks by exactly that many.

DELIBERATELY NOT A TRACEABILITY EDGE, the third of a kind after AUTHORED_BY and CLAIMS: owning something says who ANSWERS for it, not that a change to it changes them. A Contributor must never appear in a blast radius, and a test asserts it.

⚠️ AND AN UNOWNED NODE RAISES NOTHING. Most of a mature design legitimately has no owner, so absence is ordinary rather than a finding. Whether unowned ground should be detected at all is open in dec:idea-detect-ownership-orphans and turns on a per-project answer to which types are even ownable — a question this capability deliberately does not answer.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE DESIGN: "is this gap on ground you own?" is a FACT the graph can answer; "should this have an owner?" is a JUDGEMENT it cannot.
properties.name: Whose AREA a node is, recorded durably and read where debt is reported

properties.description: BUILT 2026-07-25 as the parallel-work skill — the procedure that ties the pieces together, chosen over the three alternatives in dec:concurrent-work-isolation because it needed no new architecture: a git worktree already gives each person a separate checkout, the graph store is single-writer PER DIRECTORY so each worktree can run its own server, and cap:git-merge-driver now merges the design semantically on the way back. Claim the region (advisory, never a lock), work isolated, export before every commit that touched the design, let the driver merge, release the claim, reconcile. WHAT THE SKILL IS REQUIRED TO SAY OUT LOUD, because these are the things people assume are handled: a claim is invisible to the other person until they pull, and nothing refuses a write; the design merges semantically but the CODE beside it merges exactly as before, so two people can hold disjoint design regions and still collide in the same module; and `--ours`/`--theirs` on a design conflict discards a node someone wrote, with nothing to tell you afterwards. This is parallel work with good merges, not simultaneous editing — the live-collaboration road stays open in dec:central-host with its counter-argument recorded.
properties.name: Two people work one design at once through isolation, not through a lock

properties.description:
The plan-increments SKILL. The temporal axis has one of the richest tool surfaces in the product — plan_epoch, add_epoch, set_epoch_status, schedule_for, arrival_delta, forecast_readiness, add_release, release_includes, release_report, changelog_view, pin_at_epoch, precedes, gate_on, add_readiness, readiness_report, budget_report — and, until now, ZERO skill coverage. Sixteen skills, none touching planning.

WHAT THE SKILL CARRIES THAT NO AGENT GUESSES, which is the whole justification under req:conventions-ride-the-tool-not-only-the-skill: plan_epoch (has not happened) versus add_epoch (has); SCHEDULED_FOR meaning DUE AT against AT_EPOCH meaning BELONGS TO, separate on purpose because one edge carrying both would be indistinguishable to every detector; modality expected (a plan) versus required (an obligation whose miss is a computed violation, the scheduling face of a KPP); and THE DELIBERATE ABSENCE OF `achieved`, because delivery is computed by arrival_delta and never asserted — a plan recording its own success is a second source of truth able to disagree with the first.

⭐ IT ALSO NAMES A FAILURE THE OTHER SKILLS DO NOT: a delivery plan kept OUTSIDE the graph — a numbered list in a conversation, a roadmap in a README, "next up" in a commit message. Anthony, 2026-08-06, pointing at this agent's own conversational queue of proposed next work: "your queue of proposed next work should also be a reflow2 skill". That is the third instance of the shadow-list class in one session — flo2's README list of open decisions, [BL-215]'s hand-copied decisions from the hxm_program field report, and an agent's own to-do list — and the first where the agent was the one keeping it. A list in a session is worse than a stale document: it vanishes at session end, so the next agent rebuilds it and loses the ordering the user had already reasoned through.

PROVEN AGAINST A REAL STALE PLAN on the day it was written (see ver:plan-increments): reflow2's own temporal axis held 24 releases and 72 epochs, and ELEVEN SCHEDULED_FOR edges, all pointing at three retired releases. Nothing was scheduled into any of the five planned future increments. arrival_delta on the just-arrived v0.24.0 answered `items: []` and `ready_to_cut: false` — for an increment that had already shipped and deployed — because its plan lived in the node's NAME as prose and never as structure.
properties.name: The practice of planning delivery in increments is served, so a consumer does not have to reconstruct it from fifteen tool descriptions

properties.description:
When a planned epoch's content changes — a requirement moves out of epoch 5, a date slips — the movement itself is recorded and dated, rather than the plan being silently rewritten to look as though it always said the new thing. The forward-looking sibling of the snapshot machinery the backward axis already has.

THE OPEN DESIGN QUESTION IS ANSWERED (2026-07-31, by measurement rather than choice): filing in the arrived epoch IS sufficient, and planned epochs need no revision chain of their own. `record_change`'s planned-epoch refusal keys on the epoch you FILE INTO, not the node you snapshot, so a replan is recorded in the current arrived epoch with the planned epoch as its SUBJECT — and because a snapshot captures incoming edges, snapshotting that epoch captures the entire plan pointed at it in one call.

BUILT as the `SCHEDULED_FOR` guard: removing, re-pointing or rewriting the modality of a schedule edge is REFUSED while the plan is unrecorded, so the movement cannot fail to be dated. Adding to a plan stays free — it destroys nothing. `cap:arrival-delta` is what then reads the trail (`dec:arrival-delta`).
properties.name: A plan's movement is dated, so what we believed back then stays answerable

properties.description: DesignEpoch.status carries `planned` (a claim about a point that has not happened) or `arrived` (a record of one that has), with plan_epoch to create the forward kind and set_epoch_status to move between them. Status is a property in its own right rather than a value in epoch_type, because kind and tense are orthogonal — a planned MILESTONE and a planned RELEASE CUT are both sayable, and those are the two a roadmap is made of. It mirrors Release.status, which already carries `planned` for the capability view. The default is `arrived`, which is a record rather than a choice (req:defaults-do-not-assert): add_epoch's 27 call sites have only ever meant recording the point you are at, so every epoch written before the property existed did arrive. THE LOAD-BEARING HALF IS THE REFUSAL — record_change rejects a planned epoch, because a snapshot captures the present and cannot belong to a point that has not happened. Without it, status would be a declared-and-unconsulted field: stored, never read, true only by politeness. Delivered 2026-07-30 in 56a8388; both guards mutation-tested rather than merely covered, since a test that still passes with the check deleted is not evidence the check works.
properties.name: An epoch can be planned, and arrival is the event that makes it history

properties.description: Move a design across machines and versions.
properties.name: Export and import a design

properties.description: Walk the golden thread to compute a blast radius.
properties.name: Propagate impact

properties.description: BUILT 2026-07-25 as `export_surface`. The first piece of req:design-composes, and deliberately the piece that EVERY answer to dec:nested-graphs needs: whatever composes, it composes through a published boundary rather than by reaching into another system's internals. Also the openness half of req:key-interfaces ("a design that publishes a surface should be able to export exactly that surface"). Contents: every Interface designated `published`, the artifacts that SPECIFIES or REALIZES it, the Components on each side, and the Project so a recipient knows whose surface they hold. Requirements, capabilities, decisions, verifications, history and every internal component stay home. Nodes are exported AS STORED — nothing trimmed or rewritten, because a fabricated node would import as a lie; what leaks internals is the graph BENEATH a component, and that is what is excluded. THE HONEST HALF, and the reason this is not just a filter: a recipient cannot tell a small design from a heavily filtered one, so the result counts and NAMES what it withheld, and says what the document is not ("not a backup"). A design with no designated boundary gets an EMPTY SURFACE warning rather than a quietly empty file — that case is dangerous precisely because it is indistinguishable from having nothing to share, and someone could publish it believing otherwise. It is NOT refused, because "prove I publish nothing" is a legitimate question. FOUND BY IMPACT-CHECK, before writing any code: propagate_change on cap:portability put dec:export-hash-chain in the direct ring, which is what stopped the surface from joining the file's hash chain. A derived view that advanced prev_content_hash would make compare_designs treat a published surface as an ancestor of the full design. FOUND BY A TEST: link_artifact writes REALIZES while the schema's intent for a contract artifact is SPECIFIES, so an ICD registered the ordinary way was missing from the surface. Both edges are honoured now — one is the contract as written, the other as built, and a recipient needs whichever exists. 7 tests, including the round trip: the other side imports it with zero skipped edges, gets the contract, and does not get our requirements.
properties.name: Publish just the boundary — the contracts others may rely on, and nothing internal

properties.description: A Requirement can be designated `published`, and `export_surface` then carries it alongside the boundaries — so a design can state what it UNDERTAKES TO DO, not only what it exposes. Opt-in per requirement, `internal` by default because publishing is a commitment; undesignated intent is still withheld and still counted. A surface with no promises says so in as many words, so "none stated" never reads as "none exist".
properties.name: Publish a promise, not just a boundary

properties.description:
`Decision.quality_target` (the nine axes of DimensionAssessment.dimension, no default), the `set_quality_target` tool that writes it while preserving every other property, and the `quality_target_unstated` gap that reports its absence.

THREE STATES, NOT TWO. An ACCEPTED Decision carrying a target settles the question and the finding goes quiet. A PROPOSED one carrying a target is somebody LEANING — weighed but not committed — and the finding reads "still being weighed" at severity 0.40 instead of "unstated" at 0.55. Nothing at all means nobody was asked. Superseded and rejected targets are history, not a position.

The finding names `set_quality_target` as the answer and names `acknowledge_gap` as the WRONG move, because the gap is aggregate-keyed and accepting it once would silence a deferral permanently.

Gated on the design having said what it DOES: silent at 0 capabilities and 0 requirements, which is `design_without_intent`'s ground.
properties.name: Record what a design is built for, and report when nothing says

properties.description: Questions outlive the session; answers stay visible.
properties.name: Remember what was asked

properties.description: A conditional loop_hint rides the orientation-shaped reads (graph_report, graph_report_markdown, scan_nodes, search_design, get_node) and surfaces outstanding coherence-loop debt at the agent's most frequent action — the mid-session trigger between SessionStart (fires once) and Stop (fires at the end). Option C of dec:read-hint-shape: the pointer appears ONLY when loop_status would report real debt (never static-every-read), and only when the owed-set has CHANGED since it was last surfaced (fire-on-change). The owed-set can change only on a write, so the recompute is gated on a service write-generation counter, bounding per-read cost. The read-side sibling of the write tools' static loop_hint (dec:loop-status-state-not-history).
properties.name: Reads surface loop debt when it's real

properties.description: TRL/MRL readiness as its own construct — a `ReadinessAssessment` carrying an integer level 1-9 and a kind, attached to the enabling technology — plus a `GATED_ON` edge from the increment to that technology carrying the level it demands, and a `TemporalFact` forecast series marking itself `forecast` rather than `measured` with author-stated confidence. From those three the delivery epoch is computed FORWARD: the earliest epoch by which every gating technology clears its stated level, reported with the reason ("2036 because this component is TRL 3 today, projected 7 in 2035, and this increment needs 7"). Refuses to invent a threshold: an ungated increment is reported ungated, never ready.
properties.name: Readiness gates an increment, and the roadmap says why

properties.description: Compare registered artifacts against observed files and report divergence.
properties.name: Reconcile against what was built

properties.description: Compare the design against what is actually deployed.
properties.name: Reconcile against what is running

properties.description: Compare recorded verification status against a real test run.
properties.name: Reconcile against what was proven

properties.description:
Three additions to the vocabulary, each a MODELLED fit rather than a widened wildcard, and each with a computation that reads it.

· **`IMPLEMENTS`, Artifact → Verification** — "this file is the executable form of that check". New edge type. Lets `never_run` split *nobody ran it* from *it has no executable form at all*.
· **`COMPLEMENTS`, DesignRule → DesignRule** — "these two stand beside each other and must not be merged". New edge type. Read by `possible_duplicate`/HEAL, which then refrain.
· **`SUPERSEDES` accepts Verification → Verification**, and `Verification.status` gains `superseded` — a retired check stops reporting a stale `passing` or a misleading `skipped`.

⚠️ TWO OF THESE MOVE THE SCHEMA STAMP AND ONE DOES NOT, AND THAT IS THE INTERESTING PART. `GraphStamp::current` counts `schema.edge_types.keys()` — TYPE NAMES ONLY. So the two new edge types take it 61 → 63 and owe an upgrade note, while widening `SUPERSEDES`'s endpoints and adding an enum value are INVISIBLE to it. Measured from `provenance.rs`, not assumed.

⭐ WHICH INVERTS THE USUAL INSTINCT: moving the stamp is the SAFE kind of change, because an old binary refuses the graph and `unreadable_by` names the type and says whether to migrate or update. A widened endpoint or a new enum value passes the stamp check, opens fine, and then faults on one specific edge at import — the stamp-blindness pattern this design has now recorded four times. Shipping the invisible changes ALONGSIDE a stamp-moving one is deliberate: the stamp catches what they cannot.
properties.name: A file can be named as the executable form of a check, two rules can be declared complementary, and a replaced check can say so

properties.description: Read requirements, functions and features back out of tests and their results, for the case where that is most or all of what survives — no specification, thin documentation, sometimes not even readable source, but a suite that says what the system was expected to do and a result set saying whether it did. Alex's observation, 2026-07-24. An expansion of cap:adopt rather than a rival: adopt already names tests among its evidence sources and already registers each suite as a Verification on the component it covers. What is new is the degenerate case, where tests are the PRIMARY source, so adopt's ordinary method does not apply — 'structure from imports and calls, never from prose' assumes a repo to read, and there may not be one. THE LOAD-BEARING CONSTRAINT, and the reason this needs its own computation rather than a paragraph in the adopt skill: a requirement recovered from a PASSING test is verified by construction. The test that produced the requirement is the same test that would prove it, so the golden thread closes on itself and the recovered design reads as fully delivered the moment it is created, having demonstrated nothing. This is the schema's `inferred` provenance trap one turn sharper — with code you get satisfied-by-construction, with test results you get satisfied AND verified by construction, which would defeat cap:derived-completion (BL-104) outright. So: intent recovered from a test must be marked as such, and must NOT count that same test as its verification evidence. A test-derived requirement is a claim about what someone once intended, not proof that it holds today. Corollary worth keeping: a FAILING test is the more informative artifact of the two, because it states an intent the system does not currently meet — which is a genuine gap, and the one thing in this whole area that cannot be circular. PLANNED.
properties.name: Recover intent from test evidence, without letting the tests prove themselves

properties.description:
`relation_candidates` — read-only, index-free ranking of what a node might relate to, plus the `link-ideas` skill and command that drive the backlog, plus the `what_next` fix that stops an idea contradicting settled intent from scoring zero.

TWO SIGNALS: a shared neighbour (both nodes relate to some third node) and distinctive shared terms (IDF-weighted across the pool, so words true of everything count for nothing). Structural presence is the PRIMARY SORT KEY, not a multiplier — an asserted edge outranks a vocabulary coincidence categorically.

REFUSALS ARE THE DESIGN: it never writes and never proposes an edge; a candidate whose reason cannot be stated is dropped rather than offered; nodes already related are excluded from the ranking and returned in `already_related`; and an empty answer names which of three empties it is.

Lives in its own module rather than in `relate.rs`, whose docs reserve suggestion for "the dedup guard's job and the skill's" and forbid a machine proposing edges there.
properties.name: Offer an unlinked idea its likely neighbours, with the walk that produced each

properties.description:
`release_without_epoch` raises a gap per Release that has no `AT_EPOCH` edge to a DesignEpoch, so a release that was CUT without being placed on the time axis is caught instead of discovered later by whatever tried to compute from it.

WHY IT HAD TO BE A DETECTOR RATHER THAN A PROCEDURE STEP. The computation already existed: `changelog_point` resolves such a release to a position carrying no sequence, so any window bounded by it loses its lower bound and silently widens to the beginning of the design. What was missing was the rung that says so. The step lived in a memory-only procedure and failed twice — `rel:v0190` was cut without the edge four hours before `changelog_view` needed it, and `rel:v0170` still lacks one while v0.18.0's own commit message boasted of not repeating the fault.

THE INVISIBILITY IS THE DEFECT, not the absence. A matching name plus an existing epoch node make a missing edge look exactly like a present one to every reader, so nothing about the graph's appearance distinguishes correct from broken. The rule therefore counts only `AT_EPOCH`; a corresponding name, or any other edge between the two nodes, does not pin anything, and a test asserts precisely that with a non-`AT_EPOCH` edge in place.

PLANNED RELEASES ARE DELIBERATELY EXEMPT. The epoch is minted when a release is cut, so demanding one beforehand would be an alarm on correct work — the shape BL-115 names — and would hold the gate red for every release on the roadmap. The rule fires the moment status leaves `planned`, which is when the omission becomes real. "When is this planned release due?" is a genuine but different question, wanting the schedule thread rather than this rule.

A STATED LIMIT, recorded as a test rather than left to be discovered: `Release.status` defaults to `planned`, so a release that shipped but never had its status set inherits the exemption and reads exactly like one still to come. This rule cannot tell those apart and does not try — a status claiming less than the structure shows is `status_contradiction`'s territory.

Keyed per release, not aggregated: accepting "v0.17.0 predates the epoch spine" must not also accept the next release cut without one.
properties.name: A release that names no moment is reported, because an unplaced release makes every window computed from it silently wrong

properties.description:
One more job in release.yml, which already builds a per-platform binary matrix (linux-x86_64, macos-arm64, macos-x86_64) and packages the consumer kit — this is not new machinery.

Builds for linux/amd64 (and linux/arm64 if consumers may land on arm hosts), tags the image with the version already in [workspace.package] so a consumer pins rather than chasing latest, publishes to a registry the consumer can pull from, and runs as a non-root user with the mounted data volume writable by that uid — the commonest way a first container run fails.

There is no Dockerfile in the repo today, so this starts from nothing. The image's own documentation must state plainly that reflow2 has NO authentication and must not be reachable from outside a private network.
properties.name: The release workflow publishes a tagged container image alongside the binaries

properties.description: --http-allow-host <HOST>, repeatable, names a host or host:port this server will answer for, so sessions on other machines can attach to the same process. It is needed because the streamable-HTTP transport answers only requests whose Host header is on an allowlist — localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1 by default. That is DNS-rebinding protection, and with no authentication on reflow2 it is the only thing between a web page the user visits and their design, which is why reaching the server from another machine is an explicit flag rather than a side effect of binding a public address. The flag EXTENDS the default allowlist rather than replacing it, so naming a remote host cannot lock out the local sessions already using the server. And binding a non-loopback address without naming a host prints a warning naming what would have worked, because the failure mode it prevents is an opaque 403 with nothing saying why.
properties.name: Reachable from another machine, but only on purpose

properties.description: One rollup answering 'what should I look at?'.
properties.name: Say where the design stands

properties.description: Hold the requirement tree. BUILT 2026-07-25. A new DECOMPOSES edge (Requirement → Requirement, child→parent, a traceability edge so requirement families cluster on their own meaning) plus a `lineage` property (original / decomposed / derived). Before this reflow2 had ZERO requirement-to-requirement edges: a systems-engineering tool holding requirements as a flat list. THE COMPUTATION THAT EARNS IT, and the half that is built: DELIVERY NOW ROLLS UP. cap:derived-completion credits a decomposed parent through its children instead of demanding it carry a capability of its own — EVERY child, not any, because a parent half-delivered is not delivered and `any` would let one finished slice of a checkout system report the whole thing done. The roll-up inherits the property that made delivery a derivation rather than an assertion: it goes backwards, so a child's check starting to fail un-delivers the parent with nobody editing anything. `decomposes` refuses a cycle, because a tree containing itself has no leaves and could never roll up honestly; it also sets the child's lineage, so the edge and the label cannot disagree — letting them would make the classification a second thing to maintain, which is how the requirement lifecycle went unused in the first place. Exposed over MCP as `decomposes` and `set_requirement_lineage` (93 tools), because a capability with no door is the failure this project found in `ingest` earlier the same week. SCHEMA CHANGE: edge types 53 → 54, so a graph written by this build is refused by older binaries with 'update reflow2' — the additive direction, which is loud and correct, and the one BL-86's set-based stamp made unambiguous. STILL TO BUILD: the derived half's teeth — naming, when a Decision is re-opened, the requirements that existed only because of the road taken. The vocabulary and the link are in place (lineage `derived` + GOVERNED_BY the Decision); the query is not.
properties.name: Hold the requirement tree: original, decomposed, derived

properties.description: The INCOSE-style criteria Anthony brought from acquisitions, 2026-07-25: a good requirement is unambiguous, verifiable, necessary, minimally constrained (implementation-free), traceable, feasible and consistent. THE USEFUL STRUCTURE IS THAT THEY DO NOT ALL BELONG TO THE SAME PARTY (dec:three-party-checks). THREE ARE STRUCTURAL and the core can judge them deterministically today or nearly so. TRACEABLE is already half-built — unsatisfied_requirement asks downward (nothing satisfies it), and cap:requirement-lineage supplies upward (a requirement claiming decomposition with no parent is a defect; an original with no parent is correct). VERIFIABLE splits: whether anything CHECKS it is structural and already computed; whether the statement contains a measurable threshold is semantic. CONSISTENT splits the same way: CONTRADICTS already exists as an edge, so a recorded contradiction is checkable — finding an unrecorded one is not. FOUR ARE SEMANTIC and belong to the agent, never the core. UNAMBIGUOUS (does it say "fast" where it means a number), NECESSARY (would removing it leave a real capability gap), MINIMALLY CONSTRAINED (does it dictate a solution instead of stating a need — the one engineers violate most, and the one that quietly forecloses design alternatives before the fork layer ever sees them), FEASIBLE (needs domain knowledge and cost/schedule context the graph does not hold). Bound exactly as cap:missing-sibling is: the agent may flag and propose, the human decides, and nothing enters above `proposed`. WHY IT IS WORTH BUILDING THE STRUCTURAL THREE FIRST: they are cheap, they never produce a false accusation about meaning, and they give the semantic four somewhere to attach. PLANNED.
properties.name: Judge whether a requirement is well formed, and say which part a machine can judge

properties.description:
A gap acknowledgement records a human judgement about specific text. Today its expiry is keyed on the gap id, which hashes the affected node IDS — so a review expires when the affected SET changes membership, and NEVER when the affected nodes change CONTENT. Found live on 2026-07-30 while promoting the planning axis: acknowledgements written on 2026-07-28 reading roughly deferred, scheduled for a later increment went on suppressing gaps for requirements that had since been accepted and were being worked, so two things Anthony had just committed to were invisible as open work. Sharper still, req:graph-indexes-snapshots' acknowledgement was still justifying a framing that had been removed an hour earlier — an accepted review left defending a requirement that no longer said that. THE REASON IT MATTERS, and why this is not cosmetic: a review outliving the wording it reviewed is worse than no review, because it reads as a human having agreed to something they never saw. The nearest working sibling is defect-side expiry-by-shape, which already does content-sensitive invalidation. Approved for build by Anthony 2026-07-30.

REPRODUCED AGAIN 2026-07-31, AND THE SECOND OCCURRENCE IS THE STRONGER EVIDENCE BECAUSE OF HOW IT AROSE. Anthony accepted four `unverified_capability` gaps that morning. The recorded rationale for all four asserted — wrongly — that THIS capability would expire the review if the capability were reworded; it is `planned`, not built, so nothing of the kind happens. Within the hour he asked for the recommendation-with-options behaviour to be cemented, and cap:gap-carries-a-reading was substantially rewritten: RENAMED, given three new shape obligations and a language rule, and its check rewritten with two new negative assertions. The acknowledgement carried across untouched and went on suppressing the gap, and `reviewed_gaps` now renders the OLD judgement against the NEW title — the failure visible in a single tool result.

WHAT THE SECOND OCCURRENCE ADDS BEYOND THE FIRST: the 2026-07-30 case was drift over DAYS, which is easy to dismiss as staleness nobody could reasonably catch. This one took UNDER AN HOUR, inside one session, with the same agent doing both the acknowledging and the rewriting — and it still went unnoticed until `detect_gaps` was run and the expected gap did not reappear. An agent that had just written the sentence "rewording expires this review" then reworded the capability and did not notice. That is not a memory failure that better discipline fixes; it is the case for computing the expiry.

AND IT NAMES THE DIAGNOSTIC WORTH BUILDING ALONGSIDE: the failure was detected only because someone predicted the gap would return and checked. A silent non-return is indistinguishable from a correct suppression, which is why this cannot be left to review discipline.
properties.name: A sign-off expires when the thing it judged is reworded, not only when the affected set changes

properties.description: The credit-assignment half of the fork layer (BL-81's open question, rung 3). When new evidence lands — a fresh structural defect, a failing verification, an accepted drift, a field-trial finding — trace its blast radius back through GOVERNED_BY to the Decisions that shaped the affected nodes, and surface those decisions as "this road may be worth re-opening". Reports the trace and the evidence; never re-opens anything, never ranks the alternatives, never scores a fork (dec:report-dont-judge, dec:alternatives-unranked-forkable). The human decides whether the surprise is large enough to mint a reconsidering Decision (dec:reopen-supersedes). Precedent that the trace works by hand: dec:merge-survivor-provenance carries a "reconsider" note found by exactly this path. PLANNED — the threshold ("how much evidence counts as enough") is the open axis and is deliberately not fixed until the detector has run against real history.
properties.name: Surface when a settled road may be worth re-opening

properties.description:
THE 22nd SERVED SKILL, and the second about doing work rather than describing it. Anthony, 2026-08-28: a `/rca` that walks the design systematically and returns possible root causes — "trying to stem the agent's tendency to be over-confident in identifying an issue without doing proper RCA."

⭐ WHY A SKILL WHEN THE RULE ALREADY EXISTED, and this is the whole design. `rule:an-issue-is-root-caused-then-pinned-by-a-test-then-fixed` already carried the ordered method in Anthony's own words, is `enforced: false`, and its own text records that the fix which prompted it skipped the load-bearing step. A RULE is read once at handshake and states an intention; a SKILL is pulled at the moment of the work and states an action. The same distinction `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` already makes for conventions.

⭐⭐ THE PART THAT MAKES IT MORE THAN A CHECKLIST, and it came from Anthony correcting a first draft that had swung too far toward guiding the agent: THE DESIGN IS A CAUSE-GENERATOR. Step ③ does not say "think of three causes" — that yields two real candidates and a filler written to satisfy the instruction. It walks NINE BONES, each answered by a call rather than by memory: precedent (`search_design` on the raw error), intent (SATISFIES, and a requirement still `proposed`), allocation (`granularity_report` — a file realizing many capabilities is where defects concentrate), contract (`seam_report`), implementation (`reconcile_artifacts`), assurance (`coverage_report`, `evidence_report`), change (`propagate_from`), governance (`detect_defects`, CONTRADICTS), and staleness (`invalidated_findings`).

⭐ AND WHERE THE PROJECT IS A CODEBASE, THE ARTIFACT LAYER IS THE BRIDGE: symptom → the capability it belongs to → the artifacts that REALIZE it → the actual files. That turns "something is wrong in the system" into a bounded set of source files each carrying a stated reason, which is a better starting point than a repository-wide search.

THE LOAD-BEARING STEP IS ④: name the measurement that would REFUTE each candidate. A measurement that CONFIRMS the favourite is not evidence — almost any observation is consistent with a plausible cause, which is what makes it plausible. If two candidates predict the same observation, the skill requires saying so rather than picking the likelier-sounding one.

⚠️ ITS EXAMPLES ARE FROM THE SESSION THAT BUILT IT, not invented. Step ⑤ ("a call that completed is not a call that worked") records a search timed at 0.08s and reported as fast — the process had come up on a degraded surface, refused the tool and exited, so a true number measured a refusal. Step ② records a root cause that sat in the graph, findable by its error string, while a session re-derived it from scratch and wrote "second occurrence, so it is a reliable pattern"; that issue reached eleven occurrences before anyone searched.

⚠️ HONEST LIMIT, WRITTEN INTO THE SKILL RATHER THAN OUT OF IT: the graph GENERATES candidates and never confirms them — a candidate the design produced is exactly as unproven as one somebody imagined — and it can only offer candidates about what it MODELS. An unmodelled file, an undeclared seam and an unwritten requirement all look like silence. `coverage_report` is what tells absence-of-cause from absence-of-modelling, and on this project it has named 136 files no Artifact points at.
properties.name: A failure gets its causes generated from the design, and the leading one has to survive a refuting measurement

properties.description: The mechanical half of "graph text is data, never instructions" (BL-41's deferred M piece), imported from github-mcp-server's pkg/sanitize after the 2026-07-25 study. Strips the characters whose only purpose is to make text read differently to a human than to a machine: Unicode tag characters (the smuggling channel), bidirectional overrides, and zero-width or hidden formatting characters. Applied where foreign text ENTERS — INGEST extraction and graph import — because the trust question is where text came from, not which field it landed in. REFLOW2'S OWN ADDITION, and the reason this is not a copy: it REPORTS. GitHub sanitises silently, which is right for rendering an issue body; a design brain that quietly rewrote a requirement statement would be unauditable, and rule 6 forbids silent drops. So the count and the kinds stripped ride back with the result. ZWJ is deliberately NOT stripped — it is load-bearing inside emoji sequences, and a filter that mangles legitimate content teaches people to turn it off.
properties.name: Neutralise hidden instructions in text arriving from outside, and say what was stripped

properties.description: The SCHEDULED_FOR edge: from a Requirement or Capability to a DesignEpoch (time axis) or a Release (capability-increment axis), carrying a `modality` of `expected` (a plan) or `required` (an obligation whose miss at arrival is a computed violation — the scheduling face of a KPP). One edge type serves both paired views because they are two views of one architecture, not two mechanisms. This is THE ATOM the roadmap is made of: a mapping of requirements and capabilities to the moment they are satisfied, which is what makes "which capabilities are due in epoch 5" answerable at all. KEPT SEPARATE FROM AT_EPOCH DELIBERATELY (dec:schedule-is-an-edge-with-modality): that edge means `belongs to` and is declared over a wildcard source, so one type carrying both meanings would be indistinguishable to every detector — the same shape as the wrong-direction edge found on 2026-07-30, which read correctly and was still undetectably wrong. THERE IS NO `achieved` MODALITY AND THE ABSENCE IS LOAD-BEARING: delivery is computed from the golden thread and never asserted (req:completion-computed, dec:arrival-delta), so recording it here would create a second source of truth able to disagree with the first. Prerequisite for dec:arrival-delta, which refers throughout to "its schedule edge" — a thing that did not exist until now. Delivered 2026-07-30; both guards mutation-tested.
properties.name: A requirement or capability can be scheduled against the moment it is due

properties.description: BUILT 2026-07-25 on Anthony's choice of option (a) from dec:nested-graphs. His case: an organisation builds a satellite capability with a space segment, a ground/user segment and a control segment; his team owns the satellite, and specifically inter-satellite laser communications. He needs to understand the system of systems, but day to day he needs his own part's gaps — not the program's. Every detector until now took the whole design as its subject, which is the unbounded-read failure (cap:bounded-reads) one level up: technically complete, practically unusable, and the human response is to stop looking. `detect_gaps` and `detect_defects` now take `scope` (a node id) and `depth`. FOUND WHILE BUILDING, and it cost a failing test worth keeping: A SCOPE IS NOT A BLAST RADIUS. The first implementation reused the propagation radius on the reasoning that claimed_region and propagate_change already agree what a region is; the test that scoped to a Project and expected the whole design failed, because CONTAINS is deliberately excluded from the traceability rules (propagating along it would make the Project a hub short-circuiting every sibling to two hops). That exclusion is right for IMPACT — a change to a segment does not implicate every screw inside it — and wrong for OWNERSHIP, where a segment lead owns what is inside their segment by definition. So a scope is containment closure (unbounded: ownership does not attenuate with distance) then traceability radius (bounded: the thread reaches into other people's work and must stop). A CONSEQUENCE RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENTLY FIXED: claim_region still uses the radius alone, so claiming a segment does not claim the subsystems inside it — possibly a defect in the claims layer, but changing what a claim covers changes what two people believe they hold, so it is Anthony's call. SECOND FINDING, also from a test: the first filter silently dropped gaps that anchor on nothing — the lifecycle-phase gaps, which are statements about the design as a whole. That was the exact silent-drop this feature exists to prevent, so findings now land in exactly one of four buckets that sum to the total: in_scope, out_of_scope, unanchored, and project_level counted within in_scope. A scoped answer can therefore never imply the rest of the program is clean, and filtering never becomes the tool deciding what a team is allowed to worry about — a project-level rollup still reaches a team when it touches their work, carrying its own scope so they can see whose finding it is. NOT DONE: graph_report is a rollup, not a detector, and scoping it means per-subtree delivery denominators and modularity — a different job, deliberately not smuggled in here.
properties.name: A team asks the detectors about its own part, and is told what it did not see

properties.description: Compares paired boundaries across the eight axes an interface spec carries and reports where two designs conflict, where they merely differ in wording, and where NOBODY HAS SAID. Built because a measurement showed the ordinary detectors cannot do it: with a seam hand-drawn between two real designs they produced zero findings, since they reason about structure and a contract mismatch is a comparison of properties across a pair. Always names its own blind spot — the types that cross a boundary are part of the contract and invisible to it.
properties.name: Say when two linked designs disagree at a boundary

properties.description: BM25 keyword search over every fulltext property, ranked, type-scopable.
properties.name: Find design nodes by what they say

properties.description:
Creating a Requirement, Capability, Component, Decision or Constraint searches the design with the new node's own words. When something close already exists the write is REFUSED and both routes are named: sharpen the existing node by calling the same tool with ITS id (constructors merge, BL-183), or create anyway by passing `distinct_from` with the ids you read and rejected. Interface is report-only, because its parameter struct is shared with other tools and a field there would leak onto all of them.

WHY THE TOOL AND NOT A SKILL. "Search before you add" was already written into FIVE served skills — capture-intent, revise-design, brainstorm, kpp-proposal, retire-from-design — and capture-intent's wording is almost exactly the ask. It still only fired when somebody loaded one. `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` (accepted) says skill use must be triggered by the situation and "THE USER MUST NEVER BE THE TRIGGER": measured here 2026-07-31, and confirmed from the field 2026-08-11 by a second user whose four-step working path named exactly the two skills he types and neither of the two that would have fired on situations he was already in.

⭐ ANTHONY'S SHARPENING IS WHAT MAKES IT A REFUSAL RATHER THAN A REPORT. The first cut created the node and then listed what looked similar — useless, because by the time the list is read the near-duplicate exists. His words: "there needs to be a deliberate decision of either update already existing node or if it is unique enough, create a new node." So it is the TWO-SIDED ACCEPT (BL-33), the shape `set_artifact_checksum` already uses when it refuses a first baseline and names `baseline_established` as the way through.

HOW THE THRESHOLD AVOIDS THE BM25 TRAP. Scores are not comparable across queries — measured on this design, one topic scored 4.48 and 35.75 for two phrasings — so no absolute cutoff means anything. The node is written FIRST, so it is in the index and ranks for its own text; every other hit is compared to THAT score, inside one query against one corpus. A refusal then rolls the node back. Nothing is compared across queries at any point.

MEASURED CONSERVATIVE, deliberately. During development a moderately-similar pair did NOT clear the bar, and that is the wanted behaviour: a check that refused often would be routed around, and a rule people route around is worse than no rule. The cost is recall — it will miss pairs that are similar but not strongly worded alike.

WHAT IT NEVER DOES: it never merges, never edits, and never refuses a REVISION. Saying the same thing twice in different words is sometimes real signal — `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` exists because a body of intent that contradicts itself is still a design — so the override is a first-class route rather than an escape hatch.

BULK PATHS ARE UNAFFECTED: genesis, `create_nodes` and `import_graph` do not route through these tools, so seeding many similar nodes at once still works.
properties.name: A capture tool tells you what the design already says, and makes you choose — sharpen or start new

properties.description: `mint_seat` returns a durable name for a session; `claim_region` takes it as `seat` and records it as the claim's owner. Where the transport gives the server a session of its own (stdio, Streamable HTTP below MCP 2026-07-28) the seat may be omitted and this session's own seat is used, exactly as before. Where it does not — from 2026-07-28 on, where rmcp builds a handler per REQUEST — omitting it is REFUSED with a message naming `mint_seat`, rather than answered by minting a seat that would differ on the caller's next call. Identity therefore stops being inherited from whatever the transport happened to do and becomes something the caller holds, which works the same on every transport.
properties.name: A seat is minted on request and carried by the caller, and a claim that cannot name one is refused

properties.description:
Per-session selection of which design a session is attached to, replacing --graph-path fixed for the process lifetime.

SELECTION IS BY graph_id, NOT BY PATH. A path is a property of the server's filesystem and leaks it to clients; graph_id is the durable name the design already answers to, and the registry maps id to path. This also matches how identity already works — graph_id, the version stamp and the sync marker live in sidecar files designed to be read BEFORE the design is opened.

Preferred carrier is an HTTP path prefix (/g/<graph_id>/), because the selection is then visible in logs and routable by ordinary proxies. An MCP initialize parameter is the second option. A tool call that attaches the session is the worst: it makes every session stateful in a way a reconnect silently loses, and it leaves a window in which a session is connected to nothing.

Contributes an answer to dec:how-a-session-is-pointed-at-a-design, which holds this as an open shape question.
properties.name: A session names the design it wants by graph_id, and the server maps id to path

properties.description: Diagrams, mockups and rendered explanations produced during a session are captured into the content store and linked from the design node they explain — the visual half of a Decision's rationale, which is otherwise thrown away at session end. THE FILTER IS THE LINK, on Anthony's word 2026-07-31: a rendering is kept when a Decision or Capability actually points at it, so the store holds what someone will look at again rather than every intermediate. Capture must be TRIGGERED rather than remembered — a rule depending on the agent choosing to store its own diagram decays exactly as `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` measures — so this belongs with the trigger work rather than beside it. PLANNED.
properties.name: Keep what a session drew, when the design points at it

properties.description: Session takeaways as first-class graph content: each key decision, finding or realization written when it happens, anchored to the epoch of the session that produced it, and queryable afterwards by the agent as its own prior context. THE FRAMING THE USER SETTLED 2026-07-25, which moves this out of 'agent convenience' entirely: a session's context IS documentation — the how-and-why record of a design's evolution — and documentation is part of the product (sys:documentation, his fighter-jet argument). So this is not memory for the agent's benefit; it is internally-derived design documentation, produced by the work rather than written about it afterwards. That reframing matters because it changes the standard: a convenience can be skipped under load, a deliverable cannot. Decision.rationale and ChangeEvent already capture fragments of the why; what lives only in the session is the connective tissue — what was tried, what was rejected and on what grounds, which findings turned up while doing something else. The substrate landed with the fork layer: an epoch is a session-addressable point, decisions anchor to epochs, change events pin there. The trigger is the load-bearing gap: the existing handoff enforcement watches the modification time of MARKDOWN files, so the only mechanism forcing a session to leave takeaways behind points AWAY from the graph. Reflow2's own doctrine already states the principle in the authored_by contract — record it when a decision is made, not at session end. THE TRANSCRIPT POINTER: each session has a full local record at ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<uuid>.jsonl, modelled as a Fragment, with nodes distilled from the session YIELDED from it. Two constraints. The session UUID is the portable identity and the absolute path only a machine-scoped hint, because a path stored as identity resolves for one person on one machine and silently misses for everyone on a shared graph. And a pointer to a 3 MB transcript is a RECEIPT, not documentation: leaning on it recreates the markdown problem one level down, since 'it is all in the transcript' is the same excuse as 'it is all in the backlog file'. PLANNED.
properties.name: Record and query what a session learned

properties.description: --http <addr> serves the design over streamable HTTP so many client sessions share one process. The store is single-writer PER PROCESS, so this satisfies the constraint rather than working around it: one server means exactly one writer. rmcp builds a service per session through a factory, and ReflowService::share decides the split — the graph and the write generation are shared because they are properties of the design; the seat and the read-hint memory are minted fresh because they are properties of whoever just connected. The graph moved from a Mutex to an RwLock so concurrent reads do not queue behind each other, and the compiler audited the read/write split in the process: all 32 read sites genuinely need only &DesignGraph. No authentication — the flag's help and the startup line both say to bind loopback or a private network.
properties.name: Several sessions work one design at once, through one server

properties.description:
The hook counts get_skill calls per session, and the Stop backstop names it when a session did real work, engaged reflow2, and loaded ZERO skills. Closes the hole chg:undefer-skill-adherence-measurement names: cap:skill-triggers recognises shapes, every shape it knows lives in the graph-write stream, and "no skill has been loaded" is not a graph write — so the one situation a human kept having to correct by hand was the one situation the mechanism structurally could not see.

WHERE THE COUNT LIVES, and why that is the whole design: the per-session tally file the hook already keeps, which is session state and not graph state. Nothing here is written into the design, and no adoption field is read by loop_status, detect_gaps or detect_defects — the line dec:adoption-is-reported-the-loop-still-computes draws, held by a check that the loop's answer is unchanged whether or not the count exists.

THE CONJUNCTION IS THE COUNTERWEIGHT, because this ARMS a nudge rather than refining one, which ver:skill-triggers deliberately never did: the session must have TOUCHED reflow2 (a total bypass is caught upstream and needs the blunter message), must have edited at least the bypass threshold of files (so a trivial or read-only session stays silent), and must have loaded zero skills. It is placed LAST, after every other Stop branch declines, so it never adds an interruption to a session already being interrupted — it fires only on the session that did everything else right and still never opened a skill.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM: it measures LOADING, not FOLLOWING. An agent can call get_skill and ignore every word, and nothing here would know. The offline half (tools/surface_usage.py) answers the same question across many sessions rather than inside one.
properties.name: A session that never opened a skill is visible, and says so before it ends

properties.description: The loop hook stops merely COUNTING writes and starts recognising SHAPES, so a skill is named when the situation calling for it arrives rather than when the agent happens to remember: a file edit with no ChangeEvent means impact-check; a change recorded but never PROPAGATED also means impact-check (BL-163); a recorded change with no artifact link means link-artifacts; a capture batch with no gap pass means detect-and-ask; a rendering written and nothing stored means session-artifacts. Extends `req:nudge-covers-bypass`, which already arms on file-edit events and already names those skills — what was missing was the pattern, not the trigger. This is the half of BL-74 the existing rungs structurally cannot reach: they compute loop debt from graph state, and these situations are invisible to the graph. BL-163 CORRECTED THE FIRST SHAPE AND ADDED THE ONE ARMING BRANCH THIS CAPABILITY HAS. As shipped, impact-check keyed on `changes == 0` — it fired only when a session recorded NOTHING — so a session that edited code and wrote its ChangeEvents up AFTERWARDS had `changes > 0` and was met with silence, while every one of those events was the bookkeeping-after the hook's own message says is not the loop. It measured a ChangeEvent's PRESENCE where it meant its PRECEDENCE, and the root cause was that `CHANGE_OPS` held only RECORDING ops while no set counted `propagate_change` or `propagate_from` at all: the hook could not separate recording from looking because it never counted looking. Every other shape refines a nudge already firing and adds no interruption; this one had to ARM, because the session it catches has no unchecked writes and has touched reflow2, so there was no nudge for a shape to refine.
properties.name: The moment tells the agent which skill it needs

properties.description:
Every served skill carries `composes: [...]` in its frontmatter naming the attribute classes it owes, and `skill_lint` checks each skill ONLY against the classes it declares. Seven classes: STANDING, WRITES, MINTS, REVISES, REPORTS, MEASURES, DESTROYS.

⭐ IT FILLS A MISSING MIDDLE TIER, and the tier is the whole point. UNIVERSAL obligations are checked by exhaustive loops over every skill and work perfectly — the graph-text-is-data rule sits at 23/23. PER-SKILL obligations are the three hand-written contracts (`ASK_CONTRACT`, `LINK_CONTRACT`, `OPTIMIZE_CONTRACT`). Between them, PER-CLASS obligations had NO MECHANISM, which is why a mechanic present in one skill never propagated: a flat loop can only carry a predicate true of every member.

📌 IT DOES NOT REPLACE THE PER-SKILL CONTRACTS. Some of their clauses were class-level and were lifted; the rest are specific to one skill and stay. A class that swallowed them would assert that every REPORTS skill owes `review_relations`, which is false.

⚠️ MINTS IS NARROWER THAN WRITES, AND THE SPLIT WAS FOUND BY RUNNING IT. "Search before creating" guards against a near-duplicate CONCEPT and is not owed by every writer: `genesis` runs on an empty graph by definition, `impact-check` records a ChangeEvent which is new by nature, `parallel-work` records a claim. Charging all 18 writers with it produced 11 failures of which several were the class being too coarse rather than the skill being deficient.

⚠️ OBLIGATIONS ARE TUPLES OF ACCEPTABLE PHRASINGS, NOT SINGLE LITERALS. A one-phrase version reported 29 unmet of which 13 were matching artifacts — `brainstorm` says "searched before", `check-health` says "lose" not "lost". The rule written into the code is the one that keeps this honest: ADDING A PHRASING FOR THE SAME OBLIGATION IS LEGITIMATE; REMOVING THE OBLIGATION IS NOT.

⚠️ WHAT IT CANNOT DO: supply judgement. Requiring a section produces a section. What composition buys over a single factory is that the obligation lands only on the skills that OWE it — "states what it could not establish" is meaningful for the 7 that MEASURE and would be filler in the 16 that do not. The manufactured-ambiguity trap comes from UNIFORMITY, not from construction.

⚠️ AND THE CARVING IS ONE READING. Seven classes with one obligation each is a starting set, not a taxonomy. It holds by its own stated test — no skill lands in four classes excluding the universal base — but MEASURES and DESTROYS carry a single thin obligation apiece and nobody has tested the carving against a skill it was not derived from.
properties.name: A skill declares the attribute classes it composes, and is checked only against those

properties.description: Both the fifteen skills and the ~20 KB instruction document are compiled in at build time (build.rs embeds getting-started/), served by list_skills, get_skill and get_instructions, and advertised by a catalogue plus a call-get_instructions-first line in the server instructions — the one channel a client puts in the agent's context unasked. What an install leaves in a project is a 2.4 KB pointer file naming those three tools, the MCP configs, .reflow2/ and a gitignore line; nothing else, and nothing that a later release rewrites. The installer removes the skill copies an older kit left: untouched ones deleted with the reason, edited ones kept and reported as SHADOWING the served skill, because a harness does auto-load those.
properties.name: Serve the skills AND the working instructions from the binary, so a project holds only a pointer

properties.description: --export-snapshot copies the store's flat files to a scratch directory (skipping LOCK), opens the copy, exports it, and removes both the copy and its provenance sidecar. Best-effort and loudly labelled as such: it is a live-database read, not a backup. A graph that is NOT locked gets an ordinary export and is told so.
properties.name: Export a design another session is holding

properties.description: Before replacing an export file, compare what is on disk against what is about to be written and answer one question: would this DROP nodes or edges the file holds? The file where this seat left it is the silent fast path (one hash comparison against a marker in <graph-path>.sync.json); a file that moved but loses nothing is allowed and reported; a write that would delete somebody else's work is refused, naming the ids and the three-step remedy, overridable only by an explicit accept_divergence. import_graph gained a path argument so the remedy it names is a thing the tool can actually do.
properties.name: Refuse to write a design over work the shared record already holds

properties.description: Stamp and check, refusing a graph from the future.
properties.name: Say which reflow2 wrote a graph

properties.description:
Every branch of the loop nudge to date reasons from the session's own op TALLY — writes since a loop check, edits, ChangeEvents recorded, skills loaded. That is a proxy for design debt, and it is blind in the direction that matters: a session that does the loop's motions correctly (write, then loop_status) trips nothing, whatever it actually left behind in the graph.

This capability adds the branch that asks the GRAPH. A detached probe calls `loop_status` over the shared server's stateless MCP surface, records a BASELINE at SessionStart, and compares later probes against it. The nudge fires only on a count this session RAISED — never on a level, because the standing debt is weeks old and a level fires forever.

It speaks LAST, where the counting branches are silent, and shares their once-per-session budget: the session that already got a counting nudge does not get a second interruption.

DEGRADATION IS SILENT AND DELIBERATE. No `.reflow2/graph.server.json` (no shared server), an unreachable server, or a probe that never returns all leave the nudge saying nothing. A hook that guesses when it cannot read is worse than one that does not speak.

⚠ THE READING CAN BE STALE, AND THAT IS THE PRICE OF THE ASYNC SHAPE. The verdict is whatever the last probe found — held at up to a couple of minutes by the debounce, and longer where no probe has been spawned since. A session genuinely in flight RAISES counts and then SETTLES them: capture intent and the gaps appear, wire the thread and they close. Observed on the session that built this, where unsurfaced gaps read 7 → 10 while the new nodes were unwired and finished at 6. So the message states the reading's AGE and tells the agent to confirm with `loop_status` before acting. Waiting for a fresh probe at stop time is the 23-second block the whole design exists to avoid.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO, stated because the gap is real: the graph cannot see the transcript, so this reports what the DESIGN says changed, never what the conversation held and failed to write down. It complements the capture-session skill; it does not replace it.

(The Decision this implements is `dec:the-stop-hook-asks-the-graph-asynchronously`; that node holds the cost measurement and the roads not taken, this one holds what the mechanism does.)
properties.name: The Stop nudge asks the graph what this session left, instead of counting the session's own tool calls

properties.description: A typed vocabulary of node and edge types, validated on write, over a pluggable graph storage backend — the foundation everything else hangs off.
properties.name: Schema-validated graph store

properties.description: The contradiction detector reads `alignment`: a CONTRADICTS edge marked `supporting` reinforces and is not reported as a defect, while an `opposing` edge and an edge that says nothing both stay contradictions — so existing designs keep their meaning and real conflicts still surface.
properties.name: Corroboration reads as corroboration

properties.description: Turn a gap into a question in the user's words.
properties.name: Ask the user a plain question
Orientation asks what lens the reader brings, once, and matches their vocabulary from then on

properties.description:
Two halves, and neither is useful alone.

INTERVIEW STEP — `genesis` and `capture-intent` gain an explicit early step: establish what KIND of thing is being designed by probing questions in the user's own domain (what must it do, what is it made of, what meets what, what counts as finished, what will you hand someone when it is done), and NEVER by asking the user to choose a node type. Modelled on reflow's S-01A semantic-matching interview, without its framework registry.

ROUTING TABLE — a served mapping from the user's phrasing to the node type it belongs in, plus the artifacts to expect for that kind of thing (structural / electrical / plumbing drawings for a facility; schemas and migrations for an IT system). Looked up rather than improvised. Follows `capture-session`'s precedent, whose own routing table's first dogfood found a hole in it — a table can be wrong in public, an improvisation cannot.

📌 THE ANSWER SHAPES EXTRACTION AND PHRASING AND GATES NOTHING. Which questions get asked and which vocabulary is spoken back may vary by the kind of thing; which analyses reflow2 runs must not. A cycle detector runs wherever there are dependency edges, whoever calls them interfaces or interactions.
properties.name: The agent asks about the thing, not about the schema — an interview step and a routing table

properties.description:
Option B, and it needs BOTH halves because git splits them deliberately.

  · `ensure_gitattributes` writes the repo-side rule naming `docs/design/<project>.json merge=reflow2`. This TRAVELS, so every collaborator's clone agrees on which file needs the driver.
  · `ensure_merge_driver` sets `merge.reflow2.name` and `.driver` with `git config --local`. This CANNOT travel: git refuses to let a repository configure an executable, which is why the rule alone was never enough.

🛑 THE GAP IT CLOSES WAS SILENT AND OLD. reflow2's own `.gitattributes` has carried `merge=reflow2` for months, and nothing ever set the driver — so a fresh clone fell back to git's LINE merge on a multi-megabyte JSON graph, where two people who edited entirely different parts of the design still collide. `.gitattributes`' own comment calls that *"safe — it just means you resolve the JSON by hand"*, which is true and is not a thing anyone will do.

📌 IT LEAVES ALONE A DRIVER SOMEBODY ELSE SET, and reports that it did — the same rule `write_mcp_config` and `ensure_hooks` follow, because a merge driver is exactly the kind of thing a person customises and an installer that silently repoints one is not trusted near a config again. Silent when the repo does not ask for the driver, and silent outside a git checkout: configuring one there would answer a question nobody asked.
properties.name: The installer registers reflow2's merge driver, so a collaborator's clone merges the design per node rather than by lines

properties.description:
`tools/vocabulary_reach.py` reports declared vocabulary that NOTHING in a real design has ever carried, split three ways so no bucket can be over-quoted:

  CANDIDATES        the type IS used, the property NEVER is, and no typed tool accepts the name — 18 on reflow2's own design
  UNUSED BUT OFFERED  zero uses but a tool does accept it: probably unused, not unreachable — 10
  SAYS NOTHING      the node type has no instances at all, so a zero on its properties is VACUOUS — 46

THE PRIMARY SIGNAL IS CORPUS USAGE, NOT A NAME MATCH, and that choice is the whole design. The obvious instrument compares declared names against served tool parameters; it was tried first and reported 70 of 215 (32%), including `TemporalFact.valid_from`, which is perfectly writable. A name match cannot see a tool that sets a property under another parameter name, nor one written indirectly by `record_change` or `link_artifact`. Usage in a mature graph is evidence rather than inference — and it is how three of the four known instances were spotted.

THE GENERIC ESCAPE HATCHES ARE EXCLUDED. `create_node` / `create_edge` accept an arbitrary property bag, which is precisely why they hid all four instances; a check computed against them answers clean forever. `req:declared-vocabulary-is-reachable-from-the-surface` states this as a thing the computation MUST NOT do.

⭐ THE THIRD BUCKET EXISTS BECAUSE THE FIRST RUN DID NOT HAVE IT. Six node types have no instances at all, and every property on them landed in the candidate list looking like evidence — a design that has never created an EnvironmentRule says nothing about whether EnvironmentRule.authority is writable. Reporting them together would have been this instrument committing the exact defect its own epoch is named after, and it took reading its own output to notice.
properties.name: The design measures which of its declared vocabulary nothing can write, from the corpus rather than from a name match

properties.description:
CHANGE 1 of epoch:the-declared-walls-hold. Anthony's word, 2026-08-20. DISTINCT FROM the fact that measured the problem: that node is the MEASUREMENT, this is the REMEDY, and conflating them would leave the design unable to say whether the fix happened.

WHAT IT DOES: moves cmp:nodes and cmp:schema so they sit with cmp:graph and cmp:provenance, and places cmp:identity, which today is in NO subsystem at all. PURE MODEL BOOKKEEPING — not one line of Rust changes.

WHY: the code has a kernel of five modules everything sits on — nodes (46 of 52 modules transitively depend on it), provenance (44), identity (44), schema (43), graph (42). The declared decomposition CUTS IT IN HALF: nodes/schema in sys:vocabulary, graph/provenance in sys:store. graph reads nodes and schema; vocabulary and flow read graph. Traffic therefore crosses that boundary BOTH WAYS, and that is the entire sys:store <-> sys:vocabulary cycle. Any bisection of a mutually-dependent kernel produces a cycle one level up whatever the code does.

A boundary only earns its keep if a change can be handed TO it and stop there. Two-way traffic leaves nothing for a blast radius to stop at, so "a change inside the store stays in the store" is false today.

SIMULATED BEFORE PROPOSING, against the real import graph: the cycle disappears, NO new cycle appears anywhere, and the eight subsystems come one step closer to a DAG.

OPEN SUB-QUESTION FOR ANTHONY: sys:store currently means "where the data lives". After this it means "the foundation everything is built on", which is a bigger idea and may want a different name. A naming call, not a technical constraint — the move is correct either way.

IT IS A CORRECTION, NOT ONLY A FIX: those five modules ARE one layer, and the model currently says they are two.
properties.name: The foundation is one subsystem, not two halves — the kernel stops being bisected by the decomposition

properties.description:
The complement of `cap:a-repair-can-say-what-it-invalidated`, and the reason that one sat unused. That capability lets a record SAY it answered a finding. This one makes the saying happen: it computes which open observations a session's work touched that nobody has claimed, tells the skills to ask, and puts the question in front of the session that did the work.

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE CAPABILITY. #321 shipped the edge WITH its reader, deliberately, so the marker would not become a comment nobody consults — and a day later, with the tool served the whole time, **zero edges had ever been drawn.** A vocabulary reaches real work only with three legs: a typed TOOL, an INSTRUCTION that names it, and a COMPUTATION THAT NOTICES ITS ABSENCE. #321 built the first. This is the other two, and they are a different thing to build, test and get wrong.

WHAT IT IS:
  • `unclaimed_findings` — given the ChangeEvent ids a session recorded, the OPEN TemporalFacts their changed subjects carry that nothing has claimed. Reads the `subject_id` PROPERTY as well as the subject edges, which is most of the coverage: 151 of 270 open observations are reachable by edge (56%), 261 once the property is read (97%).
  • `capture-session` test 7 and `impact-check` step 4 name the tool and the moment.
  • The Stop hook's async probe asks it and RIDES ALONG on a nudge already firing, or is carried to the next SessionStart.

⭐ ASK, DON'T BLOCK — Anthony 2026-08-24. It never arms an interruption of its own; it only appends to a message already going out. A brand-new trigger keyed on a computation nobody has field-tested is exactly what becomes wallpaper. 🛑 The honest cost: a non-blocking Stop message reaches the TRANSCRIPT, not the agent, so the two paths that genuinely reach one are the ride-along and the next SessionStart.

🛑 EVERY ROW IS A CANDIDATE AND NEVER A VERDICT. Nothing infers that an observation is false — only that the thing it describes has moved and nobody has said either way. The judgement is the author's.

🛑 TEMPORAL FACTS ONLY, NEVER VERIFICATIONS, and it is NOT a gap source.
