That is what keeps it from reversing `dec:verification-freshness-not-a-gap`: a stale-looking CHECK is a standing property that fires on every refactor; a TemporalFact is a dated OBSERVATION, asserted once, re-derived by nothing.

MEASURED BOUNDS, stated rather than glossed: 71% of this design's 639 ChangeEvents touch no open observation at all and the median when one is touched is 1 — but mean 4.3, p90 13, max 40, because hub subjects carry many observations each (`proj:reflow2` alone has 25). Work that records no ChangeEvent, or one with no CHANGED edges, is unreachable, as are the 9 observations whose `subject_id` names a node that does not exist.
properties.name: The graph asks what a session made FALSE, so a finding that has been acted on stops proposing work already done

properties.description:
On `initialize`, reflow2 records the client's self-reported name and version, the protocol revision it REQUESTED, the revision negotiated, and what this server offers — to `<graph>.client.json`, beside the existing `.meta.json` and `.server.json` sidecars.

⭐ THE PLACEMENT IS THE DESIGN. This exists for a client whose every structured tool reply is unreadable, so the question it answers — *"which client am I, and what did we agree on?"* — cannot be answered through a tool reply. It has to reach disk, where a person can open it with an editor and paste it into a report. Putting it on `graph_report.served_by` would put the answer inside exactly the channel that is broken.

⚠️ IT RECORDS WHAT THE REVISION CONTAINS, NEVER WHAT THE CLIENT READS. The derived field is `protocol_has_structured_content` and it carries a note saying so in the file itself. A negotiated version is what a client CLAIMS to speak; it is not evidence of what that client implemented. Naming it `supports_structured_content` would assert the thing the field cannot know.

⚠️ MOST RECENT CONNECTION ONLY, and no timestamp inside. The file is overwritten on every handshake, so it always describes the current client; the file's own mtime says when. A shared server serving two clients will show the later one — recorded as a known limit rather than solved with a ring buffer nobody has asked for.

⚠️ IT MIRRORS A RULE IT CANNOT CALL. `negotiate_protocol_version` is `pub(crate)` in rmcp, so overriding `initialize` means reproducing four lines: echo the client's version if `supported_protocol_versions()` contains it, otherwise the server's fallback. A test pins that rule so an rmcp change is loud rather than silent — the same precedent as the test pinning what `ProtocolVersion::LATEST` resolves to.

WHY IT IS WORTH BUILDING FOR ONE REPORT. Every field report so far has had to hand-assemble which reflow2 it was talking to — the 2026-08-27 report carries a four-row table of sources the reporter checked, one of which (`kit-version.json`) was stale and misleading. This removes a question the server already knows the answer to from the list a reporter has to work out.
properties.name: A server writes down which client connected and what they agreed to speak, where a broken protocol cannot hide it

properties.description:
DELIVERED 2026-08-19, `epoch:the-loop-holds-the-invitation`. **This is the DELIVERY; `req:detecting-is-not-asking` states what is owed.**

A timing rule added to all THREE served surfaces that instructed the post-capture push, because each was individually correct and only their combination was the defect:
1. **served `AGENTS.md` step 2** — the canonical loop statement.
2. **`capture-intent` step 7** — where the post-capture push originates.
3. **`detect-and-ask`** — where the asking actually happens; its own trigger is *"after capturing new intent"*, so fixing the other two while leaving this one would let an agent reading this skill alone still interrupt.

Each carries Alex's report inline as its reason — including *"three gaps, not three hundred; the volume was never the problem"* — so a later session cannot revert it as fussiness without meeting the evidence. Each also states the counterweight in its own words: **this defers the INVITATION, never the RECORD.** Written three times deliberately, because the failure mode of a "be quieter" rule is that someone implements it as silence.

Also registers `art:detect-and-ask-skill`, which **had never existed** — the second such hole found this week, after `art:where-am-i-skill`.

🛑 **STATUS IS `realized`, NOT `verified`, AND THE GAP IS THE SAME ONE AS EVERY OTHER SERVED-PROSE FIX.** `skill_lint` proves the text is present in all three surfaces and byte-identical across the mirrors. **It cannot prove an agent honoured it.** That is precisely the shape of the instruction which lapsed within four days in `dec:idea-the-enum-question-came-back-four-days-after-it-was-fixed`, and it is stated here rather than discovered later.

⚠️ AND ONE JUDGEMENT REMAINS THE AGENT'S: *"plainly still pouring things in"* is not computable from the graph — the signals are conversational and live where reflow2 cannot see them. The explicit boundaries (they type the skill, ask what is open, or turn to building) are named in the text so the rule can never be read as "never ask".
properties.name: The loop detects on every capture and waits for a boundary before offering to close

properties.description:
`loop_status` carries `served_by` with an explicit `stale` bit, and when that bit is not `false` the remedy LEADS `next` — the list an agent acts on — naming `--stop-shared` and killing the assumption that a session restart is enough.

CHEAP WHEN CURRENT, LOUD WHEN NOT. The ~1 KB remedy note is dropped when the answer is `false`, so the ordinary call pays three fields; `cap:loop-status`'s "one cheap call" is not eroded the way the per-check roll eroded it once.

WHAT WAS ALREADY BUILT, so this is reachability and not detection: the bit itself has existed since 2026-08-08 under `req:the-server-is-the-authority-on-its-own-currency` — derived from `/proc/self/exe` rather than a version string, precisely because four sessions once read one true version and drew opposite conclusions. It rode on `graph_report` alone, which nothing points a session at.
properties.name: The orientation call says whether the server answering it is the code on disk

properties.description:
Checks every file this seat has synced with before, and reports one finding each: `in_step` (exactly where this graph left it), `behind` (THE ACTIONABLE ONE — the record holds nodes this graph lacks, named, with `import_graph` as the remedy), `moved_but_current` (somebody exported, this seat already holds it all), `missing`, `unreadable`.

Served as the `sync_status` tool, and carried on `loop_status` as `record_moved` when there is something to say.

THE GATE IS THE DESIGN, not an optimisation on it. A seat merely AHEAD of the record is silent, because the file has not moved and every difference is its own unexported work. The check speaks only when the record's content hash differs from what this seat recorded — meaning somebody else has been there. That is what keeps it rare enough to be read.

⚠️ THE HASH IS COMPUTED, NEVER READ OFF THE DOCUMENT. `effective_content_hash` believes the `content_hash` a file states about itself and computes one only when absent, so a record edited by anything other than `export_graph` — a merge, a hand-fix, another tool — keeps its old stamp and reads as untouched. A check must never believe a claim made by the thing it is checking. The discrepancy is itself reported, as `stamp_disagrees`.

IT NEVER ACTS. No auto-import: `import_graph` is an upsert, so an unasked one would silently overwrite live session work (`dec:ask-not-repair`). It names the remedy and leaves the choice.

AN EMPTY ANSWER MEANS THIS SEAT HAS NEVER SYNCED WITH ANY FILE — never that all is well. Every known target is listed, including the quiet ones, so "checked three records, all in step" and "checked nothing" cannot share an answer.

COST: the export to compare against is built LAZILY and never on the in-step path, which is the one every ordinary session takes.

NOT COVERED: anything about a record this seat has never synced with, and any design held somewhere this seat has no path to.
properties.name: A seat reports which shared records have moved ahead of it, and names what arrived

properties.description:
Option D. `read_loop_hint` now computes the sync debt alongside `loop_status` and attaches the record-moved finding to the `loop_hint` that already rides on orientation reads.

⭐ THE FINDING ALREADY EXISTED AND WAS UNREACHABLE. `loop_status` computed `record_moved` correctly and had done since `dec:idea-the-graph-notices-the-record-moved-without-being-asked`; the read hint built itself from the CORE `LoopStatus`, which has no sync knowledge at all. So the pull half of "he pushes, I pull" — the only one of four steps that is loud — was loud only inside a call nobody makes on the way past. Same shape as everything else in this increment: the information existed where the person was not.

📌 EITHER DEBT ALONE FIRES. A design whose loop is otherwise CLEAN can still have a record that moved under it, and gating on `clean` would have made that the one case nothing says.

🛑 IT SAYS, IT DOES NOT ACT. The hint names `import_graph` and stops there; import is an upsert and an unasked one would silently overwrite live session work (`dec:ask-not-repair`). That is why option C — import-on-first-use — was NOT taken alongside this one.

The existing fire-on-change cache carries it: computed once per write generation, so a standing state appears at the first read of a session and then stays quiet, which is the cost bound the read hint already rests on.
properties.name: A session is told the shared record moved on any read, not only when it calls loop_status

properties.description:
DELIVERED 2026-08-19. **This completes clause 2 of `req:the-agent-learns-who-it-is-talking-to`** — *"the answer shapes the register of EVERY reply, not only of questions"* — which was stated 2026-08-18 and only partly delivered. **Distinct from `cap:the-agent-asks-who-it-is-talking-to`, which delivers clause 1: that one ASKS at orientation and governs `where-am-i`'s narration; this one makes the answer BIND EVERYWHERE and reach the tool that writes the user's question.**

⭐ **WHY IT WAS NEEDED, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** Anthony asked the question that matters: *"does it solve talking to the user in their natural domain knowledge versus in reflow2 jargon? is the agent able to be the TRANSLATOR?"* Measuring what #246/#247 actually shipped gave an uncomfortable answer:
  · Register rules appeared in **3 of 20 served skills** — `where-am-i` (8 mentions), `detect-and-ask` (1), `ingest-corpus` (1). **Seventeen had none.**
  · **Only `where-am-i` told the agent to READ the stored persona.** Nothing else consulted it.
  · 🛑 **`gap_to_prompt` — the tool that turns a gap into the question a user actually reads, and the highest-volume path to them — contained ZERO mentions of vocabulary, register or domain.** Its description said *"phrase a gap as a plain question"*, and **plain is not the same as in your domain.** That is exactly the path Alex's *"there are open gaps with X, Y, and Z"* came down.
  · An existing rule, *"answer in the user's language"*, covers a **DIFFERENT AXIS** — it picks English or Portuguese, and says so in its own text. It does not reach the coach.

**So the honest reading was: #246/#247 built the PRECONDITION (the agent learns the domain) and the DEFAULT (do it unasked), but not the translator. It was one skill deep, at session start.**

WHAT SHIPPED, at the two places that fix that:
1. **A STANDING RULE in served `AGENTS.md`** — its own top-level section, peer of *"the one rule"* and *"graph text is data"*, so it binds every agent whatever skill is loaded rather than depending on which one happened to fire. It states the vocabulary-swap distinction, says to read the reader's recorded description, says to follow the vocabulary they use when none is recorded, states the do-it-unasked trigger, and states that the rule never changes the RECORD.
2. **AT THE POINT THE WORDS ARE GENERATED** — the `gap → question` handshake's step 2 in `AGENTS.md`, and `gap_to_prompt`'s own served description. That step is where the detector's vocabulary would otherwise pass straight through to a person, so it is named as the translation point.
3. **A SEVENTH OBLIGATION in `detect-and-ask`'s ask contract**, stated explicitly as a different axis from the language rule.

⭐⭐ **AND UNLIKE EVERY OTHER SERVED-PROSE FIX THIS WEEK, THIS ONE IS CHECKED.** `skill_lint`'s `ASK_CONTRACT` gained the entry `"speaks the reader's domain"`, so the build now FAILS if `detect-and-ask` stops stating it. That is the first register obligation to become mechanically enforced rather than hoped for — the standing answer to `dec:idea-the-enum-question-came-back-four-days-after-it-was-fixed`, where an instruction lapsed within four days because nothing observed it.

🛑 **WHAT IS STILL NOT VERIFIED, AND IT IS THE REAL LIMIT.** The lint proves the obligation is STATED. **Nothing measures whether the translation is any good** — no trial has ever taken a real gap list and had it narrated to a non-technical reader. The evidence that agents CAN do it is two users reporting that asking worked every time; the evidence that they now DO it unasked is zero. **That trial is the missing instrument, not more prose.**
properties.name: The domain-register rule reaches every reply and the exact step where the user's question is written — and it is lint-checked

properties.description:
BUILT 2026-08-21 on Anthony's word, promoting option (a) of dec:idea-a-gap-can-be-scheduled-into-an-increment-like-any-other-work. DISTINCT FROM that Decision, which records the four options and stays as the reasoning; this is the one that was taken.

HIS WORDS, 2026-08-20: "add gaps that need to be closed to increments/epochs." The design carried 89 open gaps, 85 never put to anybody — a list that endures and is skimmed is durable and useless at the same time. Scheduling is what turns a standing list into work with a moment attached.

⭐ IT SCHEDULES THE QUESTION, NOT THE GAP, and that is the whole design. A GAP IS NOT A NODE: gaps are recomputed from the condition on every run, which is why one carried the same id all day and why it vanishes when the condition is actually fixed rather than needing closing by hand. That property is worth keeping, and it means there is nothing to hang a schedule on. But gap_to_prompt already mints a durable question:<id> the moment a gap is put to somebody, and open_questions already tracks it until answered. The durable node already existed; only the edge did not. SCHEDULED_FOR now accepts Question alongside Requirement and Capability.

⭐ DELIVERY IS ANSWERING, and nothing could stand in for it. There is no artifact to look for and no check to run — the whole content of closing a gap is that the person whose judgement it needed gave one. answer_question is the only thing that sets it, so delivery stays COMPUTED rather than asserted, exactly like every other scheduled item.

🛑 A WITHDRAWN QUESTION REPORTS `discontinued`, NOT `outstanding`, and this was added beyond the plan. `outstanding` means "nobody has said whether this was deferred or discontinued". Somebody said. Letting it fall through would put the question again on every run about something already taken off the table — the identical false reading fixed hours earlier in fact:a-capability-delivered-as-a-model-change-can-never-be-reported-delivered, shipping on day one of a brand-new mechanism.

⚠️ STATED LIMIT, and it is a real one. Delivered means THE QUESTION WAS ANSWERED. It does NOT mean the answer was written back into the design — that is separate work, and the loop already counts it separately as `unwritten_answers`. A scheduled question can therefore read `delivered` while the gap it came from is still open, because the gap closes when the DESIGN changes and the question closes when the PERSON speaks. Those are two different acts and the schedule tracks the second.

⚠️ NOT DEMONSTRATED ON LIVE DATA, said rather than left to be assumed. This graph holds exactly ONE Question and it is already answered, so there is no natural outstanding-to-delivered transition to show here. The six tests cover the behaviour; manufacturing a live schedule that did not fit the data would have been theatre.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKED, and why it could not have shipped yesterday: closing a gap is almost always MODEL work rather than a file. Before Capability.delivery existed, every scheduled question would have inherited the artifact-required blindness and sat `outstanding` forever. The Decision said these two had to be answered together or delivery first — delivery was first.
properties.name: The resolution of a gap can be scheduled into an increment — by scheduling the Question it became

properties.description: `served_by` carries `stale` and `stale_note` alongside the version. THREE-VALUED — true (the binary was replaced under this process), false (still the file it started from), null (the question could not be asked; unknown NEVER reads as current). DERIVED, NOT COMPARED, and that is the whole design: the block used to report a version LITERAL and leave the comparison to the reader, which dev_storyflow measured as four sessions reading `0.22.1` on two days and drawing opposite conclusions from the same true value — one reporting a PASS on a broken invariant. A version string also cannot answer at all when two builds share a version, which is every `cargo build` in a working session. THE MECHANISM IS ONE SYSCALL: when a running binary is replaced the kernel marks that process's `/proc/self/exe` link `(deleted)` while the inode lives on, which is exactly why the process keeps serving and nothing else notices. No second binary read, no path re-resolution, no assumption the launch path still exists. `stale_note` carries the remedy in the payload rather than in a doc, INCLUDING the part that is easy to get wrong: a bare session restart changes nothing because `--shared` re-attaches to the same daemon, and `--stop-shared` alone can fail when the client's own binary was replaced too. DOES NOT CLAIM the graph is current, the checkout matches, or the answer is right — only whether this process's own binary moved under it.
properties.name: The server says whether its own executable has been replaced since it started

properties.description:
**REALIZED 2026-08-26 — `get_skill` and `list_skills` carry a `lens` field**, so the reminder rides the response the agent reads immediately before doing the work. Built 2026-08-19 on Anthony's idea.

🛑 **IT SAT ON AN UNMERGED BRANCH FOR A MONTH, AND THE DESIGN SAID IT EXISTED THE WHOLE TIME.** This description previously read *"status is `in_progress`, NOT `realized`, and that is deliberate… move to `realized` when the branch merges."* The branch (`lens-hint-rides-the-loop-rail`, commit e01c760) never merged. Meanwhile the capability appeared in `capabilities_covered` on release reports, because that list derives from shipped components and artifacts and never from a capability's STATUS — **so every reading of the release record said the mechanism shipped.** Measured and recorded in `fact:the-lens-that-carries-the-persona-was-built-on-a-branch-and-never-shipped`.

**Distinct from the two neighbouring capabilities, and the split is the point:** `cap:the-agent-asks-who-it-is-talking-to` ASKS at orientation; `cap:the-register-rule-reaches-the-words` puts the RULE in served prose everywhere; **this one makes the reminder arrive on the wire, so it survives the context distance that prose does not.**

WHAT IS BUILT
· **`DesignGraph::reader_lens()`** in core (`claims.rs`), returning `ReaderLens { with_background, without_background }`. **Six tests passing** in `the_design_says_whose_words_to_use.rs`.
· **`lens_line()`** in `skills.rs` turns it into the sentence an agent reads.
· **`lens_for_response()`** attaches it best-effort to both skill tools in `tools/skills_tools.rs`. **Five handler tests passing** in `a_skill_response_says_who_it_is_for.rs`.
· Verified against the REAL binary over stdio: a `get_skill` response returns keys `[body, description, lens, name]`.

⭐ THE FOUR PROPERTIES PINNED BY TESTS, because each is where this could have gone wrong:
1. **IT REPORTS ABSENCE.** A design where nobody carries a background says so and NAMES who could be asked — the half reflow2 has never had, since every detector reasons over what EXISTS.
2. **IT NEVER CLAIMS TO KNOW WHO IS AT THE KEYBOARD.** A `seat` names a session, never a person. It reports what the DESIGN holds and leaves matching the reader to the agent. **Confidently addressing the wrong person would be worse than silence.**
3. **AN `automated_agent` IS NEVER COUNTED.** A bot's `description` is provenance about a tool; counting it would let a design claim it knows its AUDIENCE when it only knows its AUTHORS.
4. **WHITESPACE IS NOT A BACKGROUND**, and `kind` unset reads as a person.

📌 **BEST-EFFORT BY CONSTRUCTION.** `lens_for_response` swallows a graph error and returns `None`, so a skill is still served when the graph is busy, missing or unreadable. **A reminder that could withhold a skill would trade a nudge for an outage.**

📌 **THE IDEA WAS AN INPUT PARAMETER; THIS IS AN OUTPUT.** `session_user` as an argument has a chicken-and-egg — the agent must already know who it is speaking to. As an output, **absence becomes the signal** and the caller passes nothing.

🛑 **TWO DEFECTS THE MONTH-LONG DELAY CREATED, both caught only because landing it was done by hand:**
- **`lens_for_response` took a WRITE lock to do a READ.** Harmless in August; not now — `write_lock` became fallible AND refuses outright on a `--read-only` server, so the lens would have returned `None` on every read-only deployment. **That is exactly the surface a stranger reads a design through**, and no test would have caught it. Now `graph.read()`.
- **The five handler tests never ran because they never COMPILED** — `GetSkillReq`/`ListSkillsReq` had moved modules and `name` had become `Option<String>`. The commit called them "unrun"; unrunnable is a different and softer-sounding state.

🛑 **AND THE REAL LIMIT IS UNCHANGED BY ANY OF IT.** The tests prove the lens computes correctly and that the field is attached. **They do not prove an agent acts on it, and nothing proves the translation is any good.** This fixes "the agent forgot"; it does not touch "the agent translated badly". The trial — a real gap list narrated to a reader with a stated non-software background — is still the missing instrument.

⚠️ OPEN, DELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED HERE: whether the lens needs `loop_hint`'s fire-on-change throttle.
properties.name: A skill response says who the design knows how to speak to — or says plainly that it knows nobody

properties.description:
Two decomposition detectors, surfaced as gaps: `multiple_parents` — a Component contained by more than one parent, so "which box is this in?" has no single answer and every containment walk silently picks whichever it reached first; and `level_spine_disagreement` — a Component sitting at the root of the spine while declaring a level something else claims to be above, which is what makes the two ways of asking for the top tier return different sets.

SELF-LIMITING BY CONSTRUCTION: the second compares against the highest level actually PRESENT, so a design where every part is a `component` has no ladder to disagree with and reports nothing. Nothing here prescribes a ladder depth.
properties.name: The containment spine is checked for a box in two boxes, and for a declared level that disagrees with spine position

properties.description: Each served tool's description carries at most one sentence of reflow2 CONVENTION — the fraction a capable agent reconstructs incorrectly or not at all, such as the distinction between answering a gap and acknowledging one, or that a check left at `planned` is not confirmation. It arrives with the call, so it cannot be skipped by an agent that never loads the skill. Deliberately bounded at a sentence per tool: descriptions are context paid for on every session, and `cap:tool-search` exists because the surface is already large. Does not reverse `dec:skills-served` — the served skill keeps the depth, the worked examples and the reasoning; the tool carries only the irreducible minimum. PLANNED.
properties.name: The tool carries what an agent would never guess

properties.description: BUILT 2026-07-25 as the `find_tools` tool. Imported from github-mcp-server's pkg/tooldiscovery, which fuzzy-searches its own tool list with weighted scoring and returns three results by default. reflow2 serves 97 tools, and req:agent-native's promise — every capability reachable from a coding agent over one surface — is only true in principle if the agent can find the tool: a surface too large to hold in context is reachable the way a library with no catalogue is readable. Scored over `tool_router.list_all()`, the served surface itself, so the catalogue cannot drift from the tools that exist — the failure mode skill_lint exists to catch in prose, avoided here by construction rather than by a second list. Weights follow the source: an exact name outranks a name substring, which outranks a description hit, which outranks a parameter-name hit. Ties break by name so the same query answers the same way twice, because a ranking that reshuffles teaches an agent not to trust it. Summaries come back trimmed to the first sentence — a catalogue that costs as much to read as the surface it indexes is pointless — and the result names `matched`, `omitted` and `searched`, so a query that found nothing says so instead of falling back to the whole list.
properties.name: Find the right tool on a surface too large to hold in context

properties.description:
The `unallocated_component` gap: leaf Components carrying zero incoming ALLOCATED_TO, reported as ONE aggregate rollup rather than one alarm per box.

Excludes any component holding a child Component — a parent is allocated through its children. Silent when the design has no capabilities, because there is then no allocation to have performed and that phase belongs to `concept_without_design`. Distinguishes NEVER STARTED (nothing allocated anywhere — the deferred allocation step never picked back up) from PARTIAL, because those are acted on differently. Aggregate-keyed so the standing judgement "our boxes are namespaces, not functional parts" survives somebody adding a component.

The mirror of `unallocated_capability`, and the visible half of the answer to `dec:idea-does-the-deferred-structuring-step-need-a-skill-of-its-own`.
properties.name: Report leaf components no capability is allocated to

properties.description:
DETECT names every Component pair joined by DEPENDS_ON with no Interface carrying BOTH a PROVIDES and a CONSUMES between them, as one aggregate gap (`undeclared_seam`) keyed on the rule.

WHY IT IS A CAPABILITY AND NOT A CHORE: the set was already computed. maturity_report's `seams` band divides `declared` by `couplings` on every run, for every design, and discarded the difference. `DesignGraph::seam_sets` is that computation extracted, so the band and the detector cannot disagree about what a contract is.

IT NAMES THE PAIR AND ASKS. It never drafts the Interface — reflow2 can see THAT two parts are coupled and cannot know WHAT crosses the boundary, so proposing a medium/payload/direction would be the fabrication `cap:no-fabricated-repair` exists to prevent. A test asserts the finding stays interrogative and carries no invented contract vocabulary.

TWO SILENCES: no Component depends on another (an absence, not a deficiency — matching the band's own wording), and every coupling already declared.

AGGREGATE, so the standing judgement survives a new coupling while the count in the title moves. reflow2's own design has 73 of these; `unexpected_coupling` was retired for exactly that flood.

Complements `unprovided_interface` / `unconsumed_interface`, which run the opposite direction and both require an Interface to already exist.
properties.name: An undeclared coupling is named as a finding, not just counted into a ratio

properties.description:
`reflow2 update` brings THIS project's installed reflow2 files — instruction file, slash commands, MCP config, hooks, ignore and merge rules — up to the version already installed on the machine. `--check` previews and writes nothing. It reuses the harness recorded at first install, keeps files the user edited, and never touches the design graph.

THE MECHANISM PRE-EXISTED THE WORD, which is why this is small: `reflow2 init <dir>` already did the refresh. What was missing was a name anybody would type at an initialised project, and `req:frictionless-update`'s update half went unbuilt for that reason alone.

REFUSES RATHER THAN PERFORMING A FIRST INSTALL. The install receipt is the test. A directory holding a design but no kit is the ordinary shape of `dec:install-once-per-machine` — registered machine-wide, in-repo half never run — and updating there would be a first install under a word that promises otherwise. It exits non-zero and names `reflow2 init`.

OWNS ONE OF TWO UPDATE SURFACES AND SAYS SO. Purely local; never downloads. Updating the binary remains the installer's job, and this command reports when it is behind rather than doing it.
properties.name: A project already set up is brought forward by one word, and a project that was never set up is told so instead

properties.description: Extends the confirmation ledger (cap:freshness) with the verification side of the same question. Per capability: the newest dated last_run_at across its passing VERIFIES checks, set beside the dates the ledger already computes for baseline accepts on its realizing artifacts — so a reader can see that a capability is claiming `verified` on a check that predates the code it covers. A SIGNAL, NOT A GAP, deliberately (dec:verification-freshness-not-a-gap): it is a standing property of the claim rather than an event, it fires on every legitimate refactor as readily as on a real hole, and a list that can never reach zero gets skimmed — which is the failure the whole gap workflow exists to prevent. THREE CONSTRAINTS THE CORE ALREADY IMPOSES AND THIS MUST HONOUR: the core takes no clock, so this compares recorded timestamps supplied by callers and never asks the system what time it is; undated events are not comparable, which the ledger already states; and where either side is undated the answer is an explicit `unknown` that is REPORTED, never a silent pass — an unanswerable freshness question presented as freshness is the same lie in a new place.
properties.name: Say whether a check is older than what it checks

properties.description: Tell a client what types exist and what may join them.
properties.name: Describe the vocabulary

properties.description:
The answer to "what is the most pressing item?" once the backlog lives in the graph. NOT detect_gaps and NOT check-health, and the distinction is the design: detect_gaps asks what the design has not yet decided, check-health asks what shape is wrong, and this asks which of the agreed things to do now. Three questions needing three actions, often from three people. A view, never a second source of truth.

THE RANKING RULE THAT MATTERS MOST: an unmade decision outranks the work waiting on it. A proposed Decision with things GOVERNED_BY it is a blocker, and pointing someone at blocked work is worse than saying nothing, because it looks like progress.

BUILT 2026-08-10 as the served `what_next`, in FOUR BANDS. (1) `marked` — open decisions carrying AUTHORED_BY role=approver, which is the user's own durable self-prioritisation and is never reordered by any score. (2) `ranked` — the top few of what is NOT marked, scored by live governed count, work it blocks in an increment, and contradictions with settled decisions. (3) `unexplored` — one decision drawn from the zero-scoring pool, a required exploration term rather than a wooden spoon. (4) `shaping` — the few ACCEPTED decisions most of the live design hangs off.

THE PREREQUISITE THAT EXPIRED UNNOTICED, kept because it is the lesson rather than the history: this capability recorded its own blocker — "distinguishing allocated from delivered needs cap:derived-completion (BL-104)" — and that dependency reached `verified` long before anyone came back to it. Nothing watches for a park whose CONDITION has expired, which is precisely what `cap:revise-trigger` exists to surface and did not. A prerequisite written into prose is a trigger nothing fires.

THE WHICH-DECISIONS-SHAPE-EVERYTHING SECTION IS BUILT, and its recorded caveat turned out to need exactly one refinement. Anthony asked for it 2026-07-31: the reader who has just cloned the repo needs the few choices that explain why the rest looks as it does. The caveat said RAW IN-DEGREE IS THE WRONG SIGNAL because the top hit was a pruning decision governing ten DROPPED requirements. Measured 2026-08-10: that decision governs 10 nodes of which 9 are retired, so EXCLUDING DEAD NODES removes it outright and nothing further was needed. Live means: not a dropped or deferred Requirement, not a superseded or rejected Decision.

BREADTH WAS TRIED AND REJECTED ON MEASUREMENT, which is worth keeping so nobody re-proposes it. Weighting by how many DISTINCT node types a decision governs is the obvious reading of "weight by what the governed nodes are" — and it demotes every exemplar named here as the right sort of thing, because functional decomposition governs eight Components and the three-party division seven Capabilities: one type each. GOVERNING EIGHT COMPONENTS IS SHAPING; SINGLE-TYPEDNESS IS NOT SHALLOWNESS. The type breadth is reported as `shapes` for the reader and deliberately kept out of the ranking.

WHAT IT STILL CANNOT DO, stated rather than left to be discovered: a Decision carries no timestamp, so staleness cannot enter any of this; and a decision nothing points at scores zero however important it is, which is why band three exists and why the size of that pool is reported rather than hidden.
properties.name: Say what to work on next, as a projection with its reasoning shown

properties.description:
`Artifact.audience` records `consumer` or `internal`, set through `set_artifact_intent` alongside granularity and volatility. The `internal_only_delivery` finding then names a Requirement whose every DECLARED delivering artifact is internal, with none declared consumer. Per-requirement rather than aggregate, because accepting "this need is served by our own tooling on purpose" is a claim about one need. Never inferred from a path: a directory rule would encode one project's layout, which is the failure the requirement exists to prevent. An undeclared artifact is evidence of neither side and its count goes in the evidence.

WAS KNOWN INCOMPLETE, AND THE HOLE IS NOW CLOSED (2026-08-22, #296). This node used to end: "a design that has declared no audience anywhere is silent in every surfaced report, because vocabulary_coverage names unused node and edge TYPES but never unused PROPERTIES." That was true when written and is no longer. `vocabulary_coverage` now names the properties it counts, so a design that has declared no audience comes back as `build: node property Artifact.audience` — fixed at the root for every optional field in every project rather than special-cased for this one.

🛑 WHAT REMAINS TRUE, so this does not get rounded up to "closed": that naming rides the FLAT LIST, which is withheld unless asked for. The silence is REPORTABLE, not REPORTED — the default reply says the `build` domain's properties are under-filled without saying which one. `detect_internal_only_delivery` carries the same limit note, and `tests/internal_only_delivery.rs` pins both halves.

⚠️ AND REFLOW2 HAS NOT USED IT. `Artifact.audience` is 0 of 190 on this design: the field exists so a deliverable declares who it reaches, and not one of reflow2's own is classified. `rule:the-self-host-always-trails-what-it-teaches`, visible now instead of inferred.

AS-BUILT, recorded 2026-08-22 after `detect_gaps` reported this capability allocated to no component and realized by no artifact — both true of the RECORD and neither true of the code, which #295 shipped. Allocated to `cmp:artifact` (the declaring half) and `cmp:detect` (the reporting half); realized by `art:schema-build` (the property), `art:artifact` + `art:tools-built` + `art:service` (the write path), and `art:detect` (the finding).
properties.name: A deliverable declares who it is for, and a need nothing consumer-facing delivers is reported
The half-ideas get a way to be joined
properties.rationale:
Closes the three gaps measured against half-idea linking on 2026-08-25, on Anthony's word, queued behind the store question exactly as he asked.

⭐ THE INTERESTING PART IS THAT ALL THREE LEGS ALREADY EXISTED. The vocabulary (`review_relations`), the structural home (`no_relation_note`), the detector (`unreviewed_ideas`) and the instruction (brainstorm step 4) were all fitted, and 110 of 183 ideas still reached nothing. The three-legs model predicts that should work. What it does not cover is that an instruction can be correct AT ONE MOMENT and useless at another: "judge the near-matches you already have" is right when a duplicate-guard search is in hand, and gives a session working the BACKLOG nothing, because the idea was written weeks ago.

⭐ AN ASSERTED EDGE OUTRANKS A VOCABULARY COINCIDENCE CATEGORICALLY, NOT BY A MULTIPLIER. The first cut weighted structure 3x; a test showed four shared words beating it. The fix was to make structural presence the primary sort key rather than to raise the constant until the example passed — a weight chosen to make one case come out right is taste presented as arithmetic, and this project already ranks asserted above inferred elsewhere (HEAL merges only on a human-drawn DUPLICATES edge).

🛑 THE MODULE BOUNDARY WAS SET BY THE GRAPH, NOT BY PREFERENCE. `relate.rs` states in its own docs that it deliberately does not suggest, because a machine proposing edges there would manufacture the false neighbours the brainstorm skill forbids — while assigning candidate-offering to "the dedup guard's job and the skill's". So the suggester is a separate read-only module and drawing stays a human act.

⚠️ AND IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT ON `search_design`, the obvious tool, which is gated behind `fulltext` and fails loud without it: a BM25 suggester would be absent from every index-less build and untestable by the core gate that holds 1,486 of the tests.

TWO DEFECTS THE TESTS CAUGHT, both real rather than cosmetic: the background-term filter rejected every term on a small pool (any shared word is 50% of a two-node pool by arithmetic, not by being common), and text could outrank structure.

THE `what_next` HALF IS OPTION E of `dec:idea-should-an-idea-be-linked-to-the-intent-that-scopes-it` — fix the reader, leave the vocabulary. An idea contradicting an accepted Decision scored +2 and surfaced; one contradicting a Requirement stored the edge and scored ZERO, because the set was built from Decisions alone. The unread case is the more serious one. Requirements settled OUT are excluded: contradicting something already abandoned is not a live tension. The SCOPING half of that decision stays open.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Added `relation_candidates` (read-only, index-free, in its own module), the `link-ideas` skill and command in all three mirrors, and the `what_next` fix that scores an idea contradicting settled intent. Nine tests; one new toolsnap golden; four field terms added to skill_lint's known list.

properties.name: A design can say what it is for
properties.rationale:
Builds `dec:the-ility-target-is-a-governing-decision-asked-at-genesis`, which Anthony settled 2026-08-25 against three rejected homes.

WHY A PROPERTY AND NOT A REUSE. `DimensionAssessment` records a SCORE on an axis — what a system IS. This records what it is FOR. Overloading the first with the second is what made `Interface.designation` ambiguous, where an unclassified boundary and a deliberately internal one became indistinguishable. Measured the same day: 0 DimensionAssessment and 0 DimensionObservation nodes exist, so the nine-axis vocabulary had been fully defined and never once used — the vocabulary was never the missing piece.

⭐⭐ THREE STATES, AND THE THIRD CAME FROM THE USER MID-BUILD. Anthony, after the detector was already written: "a user may not know at genesis, so should be able to defer (becomes a gap until the user determines??)". The first half was already true — the gap fires until an accepted target exists — but the second half exposed a real flaw: a design that WEIGHED the question and a design nobody ASKED were reported identically. That is the failure `Decision.no_relation_note` exists to prevent on this same node type, and the fix is the same shape: a proposed target now reads "still being weighed" at severity 0.40 rather than "unstated" at 0.55.

🛑 AND THE OBVIOUS WAY TO DEFER WOULD HAVE BEEN THE WORST ONE. `acknowledge_gap` on an aggregate finding silences it permanently and for every capability added afterwards — the trap measured hours earlier on `unreviewed_ideas` and held open at `dec:idea-an-aggregate-acknowledgement-never-expires`. A deferral closed that way never comes back, which is the opposite of deferring. The finding text, the genesis skill and the repair row all say so, and a test pins it.

NO MIGRATION, DELIBERATELY. The property is optional with no default: absence must read as "nobody was asked" for the detector to work, and a default would be materialised onto every existing Decision when an export is read back — the failure `Capability.delivery` records, where a design whose export does not restore to itself is a backup that would not restore. Old graphs simply carry none.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: whether the allocation step needs a skill. It builds the FIRST STEP of one and leaves the method open, because only maintainability is runnable today, performance needs coupling data almost no design declares, and reliability and security have no substrate at all.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Added `Decision.quality_target` (nine axes, no default), the `set_quality_target` tool, and the `quality_target_unstated` gap with three states. Genesis asks the question; detect-and-ask carries the repair row; all three skill mirrors updated. Eight tests in tests/a_design_says_what_it_is_for.rs. One new toolsnap golden, nothing else on the surface moved.

properties.name: The two oversized subsystems gain a functional rung
properties.rationale:
Anthony's word, 2026-08-25, on a grouping put to him with alternatives.

THE QUALITY TARGET PICKED THE CUT, six hours after being settled. `dec:reflow2-is-built-for-observability` wants the INSTRUMENT SEPARATED FROM THE SUBJECT, and that is exactly the Finding/Telling split: a part that finds a problem must not be the part deciding how loudly to report it. Without that target the grouping would have been taste.

TWO GROUPS BREAK THE BAND ON PURPOSE, argued rather than apologised for. Tool surface stays at 12 on his explicit word, because those slices are already a partition of ONE surface and splitting them to reach 7 would use span of control as a GENERATOR. Install is a subsystem of ONE because it is the only part that writes into a repository that is not reflow2's own.

THE LADDER HAD NO ROOM between subsystem and component, so either 53 modules were demoted to `part` or 2 containers promoted to `system`. Promotion preserves what every existing node means and changes 2 levels instead of 53. The cost is a mixed top tier of 8 subsystems and 2 systems, honest because these two hold 84 and 49 of 211 capabilities.

THE LEAF FILTER FROM #336 PROVED ITSELF ON A REAL CHANGE. Adding 10 grouping components left `unallocated_component` at 33 of 85 leaves rather than jumping to 43, because parents are excluded. That exclusion was a judgement measured at 40-vs-33 when it shipped; a real structural change has now shown it prevents a false alarm.

MEASURED AFTERWARDS AND REPORTED HONESTLY: only 20 percent of component dependencies with both ends inside the split systems fall WITHIN a group; 80 percent cross. That does not validate the grouping by a modularity standard and was never going to. The dependency graph is a star, 57 of 72 edges reach outside the split systems, and the dominant cross-edge is Telling depending on Finding, a DIRECTED LAYER dependency that is the observability cut working rather than failing. Same disagreement the 2026-08-21 co-change experiment found at 71 percent.

SURFACED RATHER THAN CREATED: `cmp:claims` and `cmp:operate` may not belong in the coherence loop, and `sys:foundation` at 10 children is still over the band.
properties.subject: record
properties.summary: Split sys:coherence-loop (28 children) and sys:agent-surface (25) into 5 functional groups each: 10 new subsystem nodes, 53 components moved with move_component, both containers promoted to `system`. 95 to 105 components; depth {1:13,2:80,3:2} became {1:13,2:37,3:55}; span-of-control violations 3 to 2; hierarchy_issues 0, multiple_parents 0.

properties.name: The allocation question gets its second half
properties.rationale:
THE RESOLUTION OF `dec:idea-does-the-deferred-structuring-step-need-a-skill-of-its-own`, option E: make the absence visible first, decide about a skill later. Anthony chose it 2026-08-25 over three alternatives (a new /allocate skill, extending genesis, extending detect-and-ask).

⚠️ OPTION E'S PREMISE WAS HALF WRONG AND THE CORRECTION IS THE FINDING. E read "nothing notices that a design has capabilities and no components, OR components with no allocation." The first half was already covered — that is `concept_without_design`. Only the second half was real, and it was larger than the option implied: 33 of reflow2's own 95 components are leaf boxes owning no capability, with every detector reporting clean. Checking a stated premise before building on it is what turned a half-true option into a measured one.

WHY LEAF-ONLY IS THE FINDING AND NOT A DETAIL. A parent is allocated through its children, so counting parents would file every well-formed hierarchy as a defect — 40 against 33 on the same design. Note the interaction with the adopt nesting step added the same day (#335): recovering a hierarchy MOVES components off this list by giving them children, which is honest, because a box that groups other boxes has a job.

WHY AGGREGATE, WITH THE LOSING SIDE RECORDED. Per-component keying is the more honest key for the answer people actually give — "this box is a namespace, not a functional part" is a claim about ONE box — and it loses to BL-73 at 33 findings raised at once, because a per-node flood is acknowledged in bulk without being read.

THE THIRD LEG IS WHY THE SKILL ROW SHIPPED WITH THE DETECTOR. `propose_allocation` and `evaluate_allocation` were served, correct, and named in NO skill — the exact shape of `fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it`. A detector that notices the absence without an instruction telling anyone what to do about it would have reproduced the failure it was built to fix, so the detect-and-ask repair table gained the row in the same change.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Added the `unallocated_component` gap: LEAF Components no Capability is ALLOCATED_TO, one aggregate rollup, naming `propose_allocation` as the method. Registered in skill_lint's known terms, docs/gap-surfacing.md, and the detect-and-ask repair table in all three skill mirrors. Nine tests in tests/structure_with_no_function_is_asked_about.rs.

properties.name: The 117 unattributed gap acknowledgements were backfilled to who:ajs
properties.rationale:
⚠️ THESE 117 EDGES DELIBERATELY CARRY NO `acted_at`, AND A LATER SESSION MUST NOT READ THAT AS AN OVERSIGHT. Stamping them 2026-08-29 would assert that Anthony judged 117 gaps in one morning, which is false; the real judgement dates are spread over 2026-07-23..2026-08-28 and were never recorded per-acknowledgement, so null is the only true value. Absent means "not recorded", and that is the honest answer.

THE SECOND REASON MATTERS MORE, because it protects a measurement. #368's root-cause analysis turned on dates: all 51 pre-existing approver edges on the gap side are dated 2026-08-23/24, the day `acknowledge_gap` shipped its `approver` parameter, and THAT CLUSTERING IS WHAT REFUTED the comfortable reading that 30% attribution meant careless callers. It established that the parameter gets used when it exists, which is what made its ABSENCE on `acknowledge_defect` the cause rather than caller behaviour. Backdating or same-dating this backfill would drop 117 synthetic points into exactly that distribution and destroy the evidence — a future session re-running the analysis would see 168 attributed acknowledgements clustered on two days and conclude something that was never true.

So the record of the backfill lives HERE, in one event that says what happened and when, rather than in 117 timestamps that would each say something slightly false.

This closes the caller-side half of `cap:an-acknowledgement-says-whose-judgement-it-was` for the gap family: the parameter shipped 2026-08-23, the sibling tool was fixed in #368, and this is the history the parameter could not have carried because it did not exist yet.
properties.subject: record
properties.summary: Every `decision:ack:*` gap acknowledgement that carried no approver — 117 of the 168 — was given an AUTHORED_BY role=approver edge to who:ajs, on Anthony's explicit word this session ("for the 117 unattributed acknowledgements, you can attribute them to me"). Written as one atomic create_edges call. Nothing about the acknowledgements themselves changed; only the record of whose judgement they were, which is why this is on the `record` axis. The set was verified against the committed export before writing: 117 is exactly the residue #368 measured, and no rationale in it attributes the judgement to anyone else. Four mention another name (Alex, the storyflow fleet) and all four are incidental — the trials programme lists storyflow among the real designs reflow2 is used on, and the Alex one is who:ajs's own standing policy re-firing because a capability joined the affected set. Thirty-one name no person at all; every one of those is an agent re-application of a standing disposition Anthony set (the trials-programme policy of 2026-07-23, dec:intent-preserved's post-cut rule), so the approver is his even though the prose does not say a name. The 9 unattributed `acknowledge_defect` acknowledgements are NOT in this set and remain unattributed.

properties.name: A budget is what makes optimisation stop
properties.rationale:
THE FIRST PERFORMANCE BUDGET THIS PROJECT HAS EVER STATED, and it was written BEFORE the code was touched, on purpose. `con:graph-construction-is-setup-not-work` (1 ms) was derived rather than picked: construction is setup, so a caller that builds a graph and does twenty writes should spend most of its time on the writes.

THE CAUSE, found by measuring rather than guessing: `open_in_memory` cost 41.3 ms against 54.7 us for an `add_capability` write - 750x - because `load_schema()` re-parsed and re-merged eleven include_str!'d YAML documents on every call, in a binary where those bytes are fixed at compile time.

THE FIX caches the parsed Result in a LazyLock. The Result and not the Schema, so a malformed domain still fails loud on every call; and `load_schema()` hands out a CLONE, because StorageEngine takes the schema by value and two graphs must not share one.

WHAT THE BUDGET BOUGHT: the first re-measurement read 2.79 ms - a 14.8x speedup AND OVER BUDGET. Without a number written down beforehand that is exactly where the work stops. The warm figure was 266 us, under budget, so it stopped there - leaving the obvious next move (Arc instead of cloning, worth 252 of those 266 us) undone because it needs a dependency's API in another repo. A defensible stopping point at a repo boundary.

TWO LESSONS FOUND BY DOING. (1) A DURATION ASSERTION IN A PARALLEL SUITE MEASURES CONTENTION: the first durable test asserted 5 ms, measured 266 us alone and 6 ms inside `cargo test --workspace`, and failed. The usual response - raise the threshold until it stops complaining - retires the gate without anyone deciding to. It now asserts a cold-versus-warm RATIO, which survives contention because both halves are slowed equally and which pins the thing that actually broke. properties.rationale: Reported by music_graph, verified by reproduction rather than taken as filed. The reporter graded it "harmless" for their own use, and the grading is what makes it worth fixing: the harm is not the wrong entry but the loss of trust in a field whose entire purpose is to be believed when it says something was missed.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
music_graph F10, reproduced and fixed.

THE DEFECT. `coverage.rs` matched each observed path with `claims_list.iter().find(...)` — the FIRST claim covering the path absorbed the observation, and every other claim covering the same path was left out of `matched_claims`. A design that legitimately registers `archive/` as a whole AND `archive/reco.py` inside it therefore got the individual files back in `unobserved_locations`, in the reporter's words "despite being right there in `observed`".

REPRODUCED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED, on their exact shape: one directory artifact plus two file artifacts beneath it, both files swept. Both came back as unobserved. The test was written first and failed with precisely the reported symptom.

⭐ WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A WRONG NUMBER, and the reporter had the better framing so it is preserved in the code: `unobserved_locations` exists to answer "did you forget to sweep something". An entry meaning "a parent also claims this" is A FALSE ALARM ON CORRECT MODELLING, and one is enough for a reader to stop trusting the only thing the field was for. They said so themselves: "harmless here, but it makes the field untrustworthy as a 'you forgot to sweep this' signal, which is what it is for."

THE FIX: mark EVERY claim covering the path, not just the first. The COUNT deliberately stays one per observed path — two claims covering one file is still one file, and incrementing per claim would trade this bug for an inflated `claimed`.

⚠️ THE MUTATION THAT MATTERS MOST was the cheapest wrong fix: make the field silent. Emptying `unobserved_locations` also makes the false alarm disappear, and it is strictly worse than the bug, because silence reads as "nothing was missed". THREE cases catch it — a genuinely unswept claim is still named; a sibling that merely shares a path prefix (`src/foo` vs `src/foobar`) does not count as swept; and an EXCLUDED path does not mark its claim swept, since an exclusion rule must not be able to launder an unswept claim into a clean report.

VERIFIED: 6 cases, all passing. Three mutations, each killed by the right tests — reverting to `find()` fails both defect cases; counting per claim fails the count case; reporting nothing fails three, including both counterweights.

CONTEXT WORTH CARRYING: F10 is from §2 of the music_graph feedback file, which is FOUR sessions appended under one name. §1 (F1–F9, written against 0.20.0) was already triaged on 2026-08-01 — see `fact:the-music-graph-feedback-file-is-four-sessions-and-its-first-batch-was-fixed-long-ago`. F10 is the first genuinely open item in that file.

properties.rationale:
Recorded before the edit rather than after, so the snapshot catches the code as it stands.

THE FIX IS AT THE ROOT AND NOT BESIDE IT. The tempting repair was to widen the zero-degree rule's escape clause so a dangling pointer survives the degree check. That would have left dangling-reference detection as a side effect of a rule about attachment, which is the actual cause: `orphan_node` fires only when a subject "resolves to no node AND it carries no edge either", so the conjunction — not the coverage — is the defect. A rule that owns one thing can be reasoned about; a side effect cannot.

WHY IT IS SELF-LIMITING, which is the property worth having: population is the count of declared node-reference VALUES walked. A schema declaring no `node_ref` property gives `examined: 0`, and the sweep's existing `coverage_note` then says in words that this rule had nothing to examine — so a clean result can never be read as a clean design. That is `loop_status` refusing an unknown contributor_id, applied to a detector.

PARKING DELIBERATELY DOES NOT SUPPRESS IT, and the reason is not an oversight to be corrected later. A `GOVERNED_BY ruling: parks` says a node is deliberately attached to NOTHING, which is a statement about attachment. A pointer that resolves to nothing is not a deliberate state anybody can hold — the design cannot decide that a record is about a node it does not have. Letting the park quiet it would make the one rule that finds broken references suppressible by an unrelated ruling.

NOT MECHANICALLY REPAIRABLE, and it belongs in `repair_is_a_judgement` for a reason this session can attest to: repointing the four bad capability references this morning took reading each fact and confirming the target owned what the fact was about, and one was settled only by a VERIFIES edge rather than by any resemblance in the words. A tool guessing the target would fabricate the same class of false record the rule exists to find.

properties.summary: Adding a `dangling_reference` HEAL rule that walks every property the schema declares `node_ref` and reports a value resolving to no node — on its own terms, whatever the node's degree. Closes `fact:a-dangling-reference-is-only-detected-when-the-node-is-also-edgeless`, measured this morning: 7 of 9 dangling references on this graph surfaced and 2 did not, and the 2 invisible ones were exactly the 2 that carried edges. Reuses `declared_node_refs` — already documented as "THE ONLY READER of `node_ref` IN THE CRATE" — so the detector cannot come to disagree with the write-time guard about what counts as a reference. Also de-duplicates against the existing zero-degree rule, whose TemporalFact/Snapshot arm currently reports "points at nothing that exists AND it carries no edge either": that arm conflates a broken pointer with an unattached node, and once the new rule owns the pointer case, reporting both would be the same defect twice in two vocabularies — the exact noise that made a field reporter stop work (BL-176).

properties.rationale:
Anthony's word 2026-08-26, manifest-driven form chosen over a stateless caller-supplies-paths form: the child list should live in the committed manifest rather than in a per-machine config or the agent's head, which is the property that made this route worth taking at all.

WHY THIS RATHER THAN A HUB RELATION. `fact:the-hub-wants-what-an-accepted-requirement-already-half-built` carries the measurement. Two of the hub case's four wants are the unbuilt half of an ACCEPTED requirement, not new vocabulary — so they arrive with no tracker objection to answer and no third composition mode to define.

⚠️ THE RULE THIS BENDS, NAMED BEFORE IT IS BENT. reflow2-core does no file I/O, deliberately and repeatedly, and `describe_designs` makes the CALLER find candidate paths because reflow2 does no file navigation. Reading an upstream export means reading a file this design was pointed at BY ITS OWN COMMITTED MANIFEST, which is a weaker claim than navigating — but it is not nothing, and it is why the read belongs at the MCP layer beside `sync_debt`, never in the core. That placement is the same call `sync_debt` already made and for the same stated reason.

⚠️ IT MUST NOT SILENCE ITSELF. The recorded hash is what the declarer LAST LOOKED AT, and re-reading must never quietly update it — a check that refreshed its own baseline would report `moved` exactly once and then go permanently quiet. Re-declaring is the acknowledgement, which is `dec:ask-not-repair` applied here: name the remedy, never take it.

⚠️ WHAT IT DOES NOT DELIVER. A dependency declaration says I DEPEND ON that; a hub says I AM ANSWERABLE FOR that. Where a hub merely owns a child, expressing that as a dependency would be the modelling fiction the hxm_program report objected to. Hub wants #1 (cross-design realization) and #3 (verification roll-up) are untouched, and so is the downward-inheritance direction.

A fact may carry its date as a property, and search_design reads it back with its age
properties.rationale: Measured first: 112 of 205 TemporalFacts carried the property, 76 the edge, ZERO both. A clean split with no node caught between the two conventions is what a missing word looks like, not what carelessness looks like — the edge demands a DesignEpoch and a writer holding a date has nothing to point it at. Anthony chose (a) over migrating the 112 into invented epochs, and over making the edge polymorphic. The scope then grew on evidence: there was no reader to fall back, so one was built.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
Implements `dec:how-should-a-temporal-fact-carry-its-date-when-there-is-no-epoch`, option (a), settled on Anthony's word 2026-08-16.

WHAT CHANGED. `TemporalFact` declares `valid_from` and `valid_to` as date-string properties (`schema/temporal.yaml`). A new `reflow2-core::dates` module converts `YYYY-MM-DD` to a day number and subtracts. `SearchHit` gains a flattened `ClaimAge`, so `search_design` returns `as_of`, `age_days` and `expired` for any node carrying a date, and returns nothing extra for any node that does not.

⭐ THE SCOPE GREW ON EVIDENCE, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The decision said "declare the properties, and have readers prefer the edge and fall back to the property". Checking what actually reads `VALID_FROM` found ONE reader — `readiness.rs:653` — which filters to `basis: forecast`, AND THERE ARE ZERO FORECAST FACTS IN THE DESIGN. All 189 dated facts are `measured`. So the 76 edge-bearing facts were just as unread in practice as the 112 property-bearing ones, and there was no reader to teach. Declaring the property alone would have changed the schema and left the corpus exactly as inert as before — which `dec:edge-orthogonality` forbids: a vocabulary distinction earns its keep only if a computation reads it. So the reader was built, and the property ships with it.

⭐ THE READER WAS ALREADY DESIGNED AND UNBUILT. `cap:claims-carry-their-age` part 3 reads: "where-am-i and search_design mark how old a node's factual half is, so a six-week-old observation is not narrated as current." A date string is exactly what that needs; an epoch reference is not, because an epoch carries a `sequence` for ordering and not a calendar position. This lands that part.

THE EXTRACTION HINT IS CORRECTED, and it was the cause rather than a detail. It read "a satisfaction fact whose VALID_FROM is a later epoch; a dropped requirement = a fact with VALID_TO set" — describing as fields two things that were edges. That is what taught 112 writers to invent the properties. It now states plainly that there are two ways to say when, that they are not interchangeable, and which to prefer.

DELIBERATE SHAPE, each chosen against a cheaper alternative:
- NO `chrono`. The core is dependency-light and the requirement is one subtraction; the civil-date conversion is a known closed form in fifteen lines.
- `today` IS A PARAMETER on everything that decides. Only `today_utc()` reads the clock, at the edge. A function that reads the clock cannot be tested, only observed — and a module about staleness must not have tests that pass today and fail in a fortnight.
- THE CLOCK IS READ ONCE PER RESULT LIST, not once per hit, so two hits can never disagree about what day it is.
- `as_of` AND `age_days` ARE SEPARATE FIELDS so that "dated, but the date will not parse" is sayable. Collapsing them would make an unreadable date indistinguishable from no date.
- AN UNREADABLE `valid_to` NEVER EXPIRES A CLAIM. Guessing would silently retire live facts.
- A FUTURE DATE REPORTS A NEGATIVE AGE rather than clamping to zero, because clamping renders a forecast or a typo as "current" — the exact misreading the capability exists to prevent.

VERIFIED. 15 cases in `a_claim_carries_its_age.rs`, all passing, including the Gregorian century exceptions (1900 not a leap year, 2000 one) that a naive `% 4` or `% 100` gets wrong. FOUR MUTATIONS, each killed by the right case: dropping the century exception fails the leap and anchor cases; clamping a future date fails the negative-age case; expiring on the last valid day fails the boundary case; treating an unreadable end date as expired fails the counterweight. END-TO-END on the real store through a restarted server: a fact dated today returned `age_days: 0`, one dated 2026-08-07 returned `age_days: 9`, and an undated fact returned no age fields at all — all three in one reply.

NO SCHEMA STAMP MOVEMENT: properties are not counted by the version stamp, only node and edge types are, so no upgrade document is owed.

NOT DONE, and named rather than left to be discovered: the 112 existing facts are not migrated or normalised — they are simply read now. Nothing writes `valid_from` automatically; it remains something an author states. And `where-am-i`, the other half of `cap:claims-carry-their-age` part 3, still does not mark age.

mirror_surface gains a REFRESH. FOUND BY RUNNING THE TOOL TWICE, 2026-08-12: a second mirror of the SAME design collided with its own first — 12 of 13 ids refused as collisions, mirrored_edges 0, mirror_content_hash null — leaving the stale node in place with the host edge still pointing at it while `mirrors` reported the OLD pin. THE QUESTION SETTLED FIRST: what happens to a host edge whose foreign target is gone from the new surface? properties.rationale:
THE ROOT CAUSE IS THE HAND-MAINTENANCE, NOT THE THREE CALL SITES. The principle "a proposed Decision asserts nothing" was already written down in FOUR places and implemented in ONE: `zero_degree_finding` grades a proposed Decision to `info` as "a parked thought that correctly shapes nothing yet"; schema/inference.yaml says "ONLY AN ACCEPTED DECISION DISCONTINUES ANYTHING"; `loop_status` stays quiet on a proposed Decision with no approver; and the `parks` ruling requires an accepted Decision, which is why parks could not reach this case. Every detector nevertheless re-derived its qualifier set by hand, so `contradiction` grew `alignment=supporting` and then `rejected`/`superseded` one incident at a time while the other two grew nothing.

THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE CLASS, AND IT WAS PREDICTED IN ADVANCE. `chg:unallocated-component-reads-the-ruling` recorded hours before the field report arrived: "nothing checks that a NEW structural detector reads the ruling. The next one written will have the same hole for the same reason." F-01's replay contract, enforced field by field with nothing checking it, is the same shape. So the guard is the deliverable: `every_category_states_whether_it_reads_proposed` is an exhaustive match over `HealCategory`, and a new category cannot compile until its author has written down where it stands. Both answers are legitimate; an unconsidered category is not.

⭐ THE FIRST CUT WAS WRONG AND AN EXISTING TEST CAUGHT IT. Folding `proposed` in with `rejected`/`superseded` broke `a_proposed_decision_is_not_treated_as_withdrawn`, a deliberate counterweight holding that "a parked idea that conflicts with an accepted decision is a real thing to settle". That test is right and was not overridden: a withdrawal is a positive act that RETIRES a conflict and skips on EITHER side, while being unclaimed skips only when NEITHER side claims anything. hxm_program's field case was proposed-vs-PROPOSED, which nothing covered; the counterweight's case is proposed-vs-ACCEPTED. Both shapes now have a test.

⚠️ A SECOND WRONG ASSUMPTION, ALSO PINNED. The change was first documented as inert on existing designs by analogy with "silence keeps its historical meaning". False: `Decision.status` carries `default: proposed`, so silence was never reachable and every proposed Decision in every design changes behaviour. `a_decision_has_no_unlabelled_state` exists to kill that assumption for the next reader. The scope counterweight is the node TYPE — `CONTRADICTS` is declared `from: "*" to: "*"` and `Requirement.status` also defaults to `proposed`, so an untyped predicate would have silenced conflicts between the 51 requirements merely awaiting the user's word.

FIRST WORKED EXAMPLE OF `rule:an-issue-is-root-caused-then-pinned-by-a-test-then-fixed` DONE IN FULL: the pin was written first and OBSERVED FAILING (4 of 10, reproducing all three finding kinds, with the counterweights passing before the fix so they are not vacuous), then the fix, then green. F-01 could only claim the test passed after; this one saw it fail first.

properties.name: The hosted surface can refuse every write, enforced at the one point a write cannot avoid
properties.rationale:
WHY THE WRITE GUARD AND NOT A LIST OF TOOL NAMES. A write cannot happen without taking the guard, so refusing to hand one out is a rule the type system enforces rather than one somebody maintains. The alternative — a list of mutating tools, or a check keyed on `readOnlyHint` — is a rule maintained by hand with nothing checking it, which is the exact defect class this project fixed three times on 2026-08-26 (`unallocated_component` and the parking ruling, F-01's replay contract, and three detectors not reading `proposed`). Choosing the hand-maintained form here, on the same day, would have been remarkable.

⭐ THE COMPILER PROVED THE SWEEP COMPLETE, which is the property the factory brainstorm was reaching for. Making `write_lock` fallible turned all 98 call sites into compile errors until each was updated — no list, no audit, no chance of missing one.

⭐ AND IT FOUND A CASE REVIEW WOULD NOT HAVE. `share()` is a SECOND assembly point, minting a service per CLIENT SESSION for `req:sessions-share-a-graph`. Read-only had to be INHERITED there. Had it been reset, the mode would have held for the process and evaporated for every actual client — and a client session is the only way anybody reaches a shared server, so the feature would have been read-only in name only while testing green at the process level. Pinned by `a_session_on_a_read_only_server_is_read_only_too`.

⚠️ WHAT THIS DELIVERS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. INTEGRITY is answered outright: no write means nothing to attribute, so the caller-supplied `contributor_id` — an unverified claim over a network — is never accepted. CONFIDENTIALITY is NOT eliminated, only RELOCATED to the network, which is what binding to a tailnet is for. The requirement says this in its own words and it must not be read as authentication being unnecessary, only as it not blocking the first cut.

⚠️ AND IT CHANGES NOTHING FOR AN ORDINARY SESSION, verified rather than asserted. `a_normal_service_still_writes` asserts a default service is writable and passed BEFORE the refusal existed and after it. Every shipped config launches without the flag. This change event was itself written through a shared server running the new binary, which is the same demonstration a user would want.

properties.summary: `--read-only` added to reflow2-mcp, delivering `req:the-hosted-surface-is-read-only-so-it-can-ship-before-authentication-exists`. properties.rationale:
MEASURED 2026-08-29 on this design's own 3388-node export: with the guard on the walk, restoring it failed with 23 faults and wrote NOTHING. Only nine were real dangling references. Three were nodes present in the SAME document at indices 3342, 3360 and 3169, referenced from 2854, 3167 and 3063 — refused because `TemporalFact` sorts before `Verification`. One was a cascade, and ten were edges orphaned by the thirteen. A design with no dangling references at all would still have failed this way, which is what makes it a class rather than this graph's data problem.

THE CAUSE: the unit of validation did not match the unit of atomicity. The import is all-or-nothing, so the document is what becomes true — and a reference must be judged against that, not against a partial state no caller ever observes. The edge guard already gets this for free by running after every node is written.

WHY REPORT RATHER THAN REFUSE, once the ordering was fixed: nine real dangles remained and the import still wrote nothing, so a graph holding ONE bad reference had an unrestorable backup, remediable only by hand-editing the export — the one thing this project tells users never to do. The write guard already stops a NEW false record being made; an import asserts nothing new, it reproduces a state that already existed. `ImportReport` had answered this exact question three times already (`skipped_edges`, `integrity_note`, `provenance_note` — all "the import still proceeds but never silently"), so this follows the house answer rather than inventing a fourth policy.

Round trip after the fix, measured: 3388/3388 nodes, 15122/15122 edges, node and edge ORDER identical, zero properties gained, dropped or changed. The export is a lossless durable artifact.

ALL THREE LEGS, DELIBERATELY, because the surface audit run hours earlier (`fact:the-three-legs-audit-run-at-last-...`) found 13 declared types with NO legs at all and five carrying all three and still unused. Shipping a writer without a reader would have added to that count on the same day the count was taken. The reader is the leg that kills vocabulary when it is missing: `DECOMPOSES` reached ZERO edges while shipping a detector for them, and a record nothing reads back is a record nobody writes twice.

⭐ A TEST FAILED FOR THE RIGHT REASON AND MOVED THE DESIGN. "A report may not name a tool reflow2 does not serve" was written into the CORE suite and failed there — the core does not know what the surface serves, and answering it there would have meant a second copy of the tool list maintained by hand, which is the defect class this project fixed three times the same day. The check moved to the tool, where `tool_router.has_route()` asks the LIVE ROUTER: nothing maintained, nothing that can drift. Both files carry a note saying why the test lives where it does, so the layering is not rediscovered later as an accident.

WHY THE DIAGNOSIS IS CLOSED: it is the one field that separates "nothing does this" from "something does and I did not find it" — a feature to build versus a feature to surface. `dec:bl-155`'s central finding is that reflow2 cannot otherwise tell unused from unreachable. Free text would let that distinction rot one report at a time, so an unknown value is refused and the refusal names what would have worked. `unknown` is kept as a legitimate answer because forcing a guess corrupts the other three.

🛑 TWO LIMITS RECORDED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED. First, it depends on the agent having NOTICED the tool existed, which is the same blind spot it exists to see — so an empty report is never evidence that nothing was hand-rolled, and the reader's own description says so. Second, `dec:how-should-reflow2-log-its-own-usage` argues a tool is the wrong shape at all: "a tool must be CALLED, and the population most worth measuring is precisely the one least likely to call it." That is right, and here unavoidable: the server observes CALLS, and work done by hand happens where it cannot look. Asking is the only route that exists.

🛑 AND THE REPORT MUST NEVER BECOME TELEMETRY. `what` is free text naming the user's own domain — precisely the field `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` warns that "the next contributor will put something useful in". The prohibition is written into the module header, the tool description AND the skill, because those are the three places somebody wiring telemetry would look.

🛑 THIS FIXES A DEFECT THE PARKED-IDEA WORK ITSELF INTRODUCED, CAUGHT BEFORE IT MERGED. Making three finding kinds read `is_parked_idea` took reflow2's own design from 89 to 61 defects, and nothing anywhere said the missing findings had been suppressed. A reader seeing 61 could not tell it from a design that genuinely has 61 — which is exactly the vacuous zero `SweepScope.parked` was built to prevent, reintroduced one rule over BY THE CHANGE THAT WAS FIXING IT.

`art:heal` realizes `cap:a-sweep-says-what-it-could-not-have-found`, and the sibling `parks` mechanism COUNTS parked nodes rather than silencing them. The new rule now does the same, so the two deliberate-state mechanisms behave alike instead of one reporting and one hiding.

⭐ IT IS A `swept.` FIGURE, NOT A DEFECT TALLY, and that distinction is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. The complaint that started this whole thread was that a DEFECT count grew when you brainstormed, which teaches people to stop reading it. A description of what the sweep did not look at costs a brainstormer nothing and lets an auditor reconstruct the total.

⚠️ THE COUNTERWEIGHT PIN IS THE ONE THAT MAKES THE FIELD TRUSTWORTHY. `a_clean_sweep_reports_nothing_suppressed` asserts the map is EMPTY when nothing was parked — without it, a wired-but-never-incremented field reads exactly like a design with no parked ideas, which is the same failure mode wearing the new field's clothes. It was written deliberately: the implementation was landed with the plumbing but WITHOUT the increments, the pin was run and went red for that reason, and only then were the three increment sites added.

📌 WHERE THE NUMBERS DIFFER AND WHY, so nobody reconciles them wrongly: the 89 -> 61 delta is 28, while the suppression count on the same design reads 33. Both are right — the graph grew by three brainstormed Decisions and four relations between the two measurements, and those added suppressible findings. The reconciliation that holds at any instant is `reported + suppressed`, not a delta against an older count.
