Reads the designs this one DEPENDS ON, without taking them in. Opens each declared upstream export named in the committed manifest, computes its content hash from content, and reports what is there — so `cmp:depends` can judge whether the upstream has moved. Implemented in `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/upstream.rs`.

⚠️ IT READS, IT DOES NOT NAVIGATE, AND IT NEVER WRITES. `describe_designs` makes the caller find candidate paths because reflow2 does no file navigation; that rule is intact here, because every path opened is one this design pointed at ITSELF in its own committed manifest. Nothing on this path writes — not the baseline, not a sync record — because a check that refreshed what it compares against would report a move once and then go permanently quiet.

Given a part of its own on the ruling recorded as `chg:allocation-follows-the-code-not-the-neighbour` (2026-08-25), the same call made for `cmp:manual-work` earlier the same day: it is a real, checksummed module, so crediting its function to `cmp:sync-debt` or `cmp:depends` next door would be the neighbour-misfiling that ruling corrects. Placed under `sub:across-designs` beside `cmp:depends` and `cmp:seam` because what it does is cross a design boundary — not under `sub:serving`, where it merely happens to live in the crate.

📌 THE CAPABILITY IS ALLOCATED TO `cmp:depends`, NOT HERE, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. `cap:a-declared-dependency-is-watched-not-imported` spans two modules — the judgement in `depends.rs`, the reading here — and the standing ruling says move it, do not dual-allocate. The declaration and the comparison are what the capability IS; this supplies what was found on disk, exactly as a caller supplies `observed` to `reconcile_dependencies`. The artifact layer records both files as realizing it, which is the honest reading and the reason the two layers can be compared at all. It is also a live instance of `dec:idea-a-capability-is-a-set-of-functions-and-a-black-box-delivers-functions`, which asks whether a capability should be a SET of functions across parts — open, and this is a real case for it rather than a hypothetical.

properties.name: verify
properties.purpose: The verify module.

properties.name: vocabulary
properties.purpose: The vocabulary module.

properties.name: Across designs
properties.purpose:
The parts that reason about MORE THAN ONE design at once: composing two without merging them, declaring and checking a dependency on another design's version, and saying when two linked designs disagree at a boundary.

The smallest group at three, and deliberately not folded into a larger one. Everything else in this system assumes a single design and can read whatever it needs; these three cannot, and each has to handle a design it does not own and cannot write. That is a different set of assumptions, and burying it inside a bigger box would hide the one boundary in the system where the other side is out of reach.

properties.name: Change and structure
properties.purpose:
What a change touches, and how the design is shaped — impact propagation and its budget, the decomposition spine, allocation of function to parts, the relations between nodes, and the coordination of who holds which region while it all moves.

Grouped because they answer one question from different sides: WHAT IS CONNECTED TO WHAT, and therefore what moves when something does. Propagation reads the shape; allocation and structure write it; relate records the reasoning edges; claims says who may be writing it right now.

⚠️ `cmp:claims` sits here uneasily and the discomfort is recorded rather than smoothed over: coordination of parallel work is arguably not coherence-loop machinery at all. It was placed here because it is about the design MOVING, and flagged because this split surfaced the question rather than created it.

properties.name: Evidence
properties.purpose:
Where the design meets reality — the parts that hold what was actually checked, built, deployed or observed, and what has since moved: verifications and their outcomes, artifacts and their checksums, the confirmation ledger, drift, field observation, and the operating world.

Distinct from Finding and Telling because those two reason ABOUT THE DESIGN, and these reason about the WORLD THE DESIGN CLAIMS TO DESCRIBE. That is the boundary where as-designed and as-built are allowed to disagree, and keeping it a boundary is what makes the disagreement visible instead of silently resolved.

properties.name: Finding
properties.purpose:
The detectors — the parts whose job is to NOTICE something the design cannot see in itself: gaps, structural defects, hierarchy problems, undeclared seams, granularity mismatches, coverage and consumption holes.

Separated from Telling deliberately, and that separation is the point rather than tidiness. `dec:reflow2-is-built-for-observability` says this design is built so its answers never misrepresent what it knows, and observability-driven allocation wants THE INSTRUMENT SEPARATED FROM THE SUBJECT — a part that finds a problem must not be the same part that decides how loudly to report it. Fusing detection and reporting is how a green gate over uncovered ground gets built without anybody choosing to.

Every part here owes the same obligation the target imposes: it must be able to say it COULD NOT TELL, rather than reporting clean over ground it never ran on.

properties.name: Install
properties.purpose:
Getting reflow2 INTO somebody else's project: asking which harness, writing only that harness's files, and leaving a committable record.

⚠️ A SUBSYSTEM OF ONE, AND KEPT THAT WAY DELIBERATELY. It is the only part of this system that WRITES INTO A REPOSITORY THAT IS NOT REFLOW2'S OWN — every other part reads a design or answers a call. Folding it into a larger box to avoid a group of one would hide the single place where the blast radius leaves this project, which is exactly the boundary `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself` cares about.

Group size is a check on whether a grouping is doing work, not a quota to fill.

properties.name: Serving and transport
properties.purpose:
How the surface is actually reached: the service that answers, the process entry point, the MCP-over-HTTP primitives, the stdio-to-HTTP session proxy, the shared-mode manager, and the registry that maps a graph_id to an open design.

These are the parts that would still exist if every tool were deleted — the machinery of BEING a server, distinct from WHAT is served.

properties.name: Session posture
properties.purpose:
What a session knows about WHERE IT IS and WHETHER IT IS CURRENT: the latent server in a directory that has not opted in, the staleness of the shared record since this seat last looked, and saying what design lives at a path without binding to it.

Grouped because all three answer a question asked BEFORE any design work — am I somewhere with a design, is what I hold current, and what is here. Each is also a place where an honest "I cannot tell" matters more than an answer, which is why they sit together under an observability target.

properties.name: Surface shaping
properties.purpose:
How the surface presents itself rather than what it does: the DTOs a reply is built from, the batched forms that collapse N calls into one, and the served skill catalogue with its embedded bodies.

All three shape what an agent MEETS — the shape of a reply, the shape of a call, and the instructions served alongside. None of them decides anything about a design.

properties.name: Telling
properties.purpose:
The reports — the parts whose job is to SAY where the design stands, to a person or to a gate: the snapshot, the quality axes, the maturity trajectory, the dimension readings, the regions a newcomer can orient by, and the scoping that narrows any of it honestly.

The other half of the observability cut. These parts summarise what Finding produced, and they are separate BECAUSE summarising is where a true finding becomes a misleading answer: a count without its denominator, a page presented as the whole set, a zero that meant "nothing to run on". Nearly every honesty rule this project has — `omitted`, `not_shown`, `budget`, `share_of_anchored`, `modularity: null` — lives in a part that belongs here.

properties.name: Tool surface
properties.purpose:
The served tool surface, cut into twelve slices by lifecycle phase: capture, ingest, ask, coherence, assure, as-built, claims, exchange, query, operate, temporal and skills.

⚠️ TWELVE CHILDREN, DELIBERATELY OVER THE 3-7 BAND, and the excess is the finding rather than a defect to fix. These slices are already a partition of ONE thing — a single surface, divided once by the phase of the loop each tool serves. Splitting them further to reach seven would be using span of control as a GENERATOR, which `dec:idea-the-decomposition-ladder-is-open` and the whole depth-is-a-consequence argument forbid: the band said 25 was wrong, it does not say 12 is.

Anthony's call, 2026-08-25, put to him with the alternative: *"leave it at 12 — don't invent a rung."*

properties.name: Agent Surface
properties.purpose: The boundary the agent lives behind: the reflow2-mcp binary spoken to over stdio, and the consumer kit that installs it.

properties.name: Coherence Loop
properties.purpose: The engine: on any change, find the ripples and surface them — detect gaps, propagate impact, heal structure, reconcile against what was built, proven and deployed, and report where the design stands.

properties.name: Documentation
properties.purpose: The explanation reflow2 ships with itself. Modelled as a subsystem of the product rather than as material about the product, on the user's call (2026-07-24): documentation is part of any deliverable, and a system handed over without it has not been fully delivered — his analogy was designing a fighter jet in reflow2 and shipping no documentation to the people who must operate it. The consequence taken seriously here is that documentation gets the same treatment as code: its files are registered Artifacts with checksums, so a README that drifts away from what the system does is a detectable defect rather than a thing someone eventually notices.

properties.name: Foundation
properties.purpose:
The layer everything else stands on: the typed node and edge vocabulary, the schema that validates it, the graph the store is reached through, the provenance stamped on every write, and the identity that says which design this is. Five modules that cannot be separated from one another — graph reads nodes and schema, and the vocabulary reads graph — which is exactly why they are one system and not two halves of two.

DISTINCT FROM the three nodes that surround it, and the distinction is the point: the FACT measured the bisection, the DECISION chose this remedy over two others, the CAPABILITY is the work of moving the boxes. This is the box itself — the part of the system that exists once the work is done.

CREATED 2026-08-20 under dec:the-kernel-is-its-own-system. Before that, nodes and schema sat in sys:vocabulary while graph and provenance sat in sys:store, and identity sat in no system at all. That bisection was the whole cause of the sys:store to sys:vocabulary cycle: traffic crossed the boundary both ways, so neither box was a wall a change could be handed to and stop at.

MEASURED WEIGHT: 46 of the 52 other core modules transitively depend on nodes, 44 on provenance, 44 on identity, 43 on schema, 42 on graph. Nothing else in reflow2 carries anything like this reach, and a change here is the one change that genuinely does go everywhere.

properties.name: Human Channel
properties.purpose: Turn an underspecified design into a plain-language question for the human, and remember what was asked.

properties.name: Intake
properties.purpose: The front door: bring intent into the graph, greenfield (genesis from a brief) or brownfield (adopt/ingest from an existing system).

properties.name: Design Store
properties.purpose: Durable, deterministic memory: the schema-validated graph that persists in the project, exports and imports byte-identically, is searchable, and stamps which reflow2 wrote it.

properties.name: Time & History
properties.purpose: The change axis: epochs, decisions, the roads not taken — hold and compare alternatives, diff and merge divergent designs, so the past survives being updated.

properties.name: Vocabulary
properties.purpose: The neutral type system — the node and edge types that ARE a design. What any design is made of, before any of it is stored or checked.

properties.name: A defect sweep builds its network a fixed number of times, never once per candidate
properties.statement:
`detect_defects` shall build the design/operational network **no more than 4 times per call, independent of how many single-point-of-failure candidates it examines**.

THE DERIVATION, and it is a statement about what ought to be true rather than a round number. The question the sweep asks of each candidate is "does removing THIS node split off a non-trivial component?" The graph DOES NOT CHANGE between candidates — only which node is masked. So the network has to be constructed once and interrogated N times; nothing about the question requires reconstructing it per candidate. Four is what the sweep legitimately needs: a design network for the structural rules, one for the sweep scope, one operational network for the articulation scan, and one baseline component count. A fifth would need an argument; a per-candidate one cannot have one.

MEASURED BEFORE THE BUDGET WAS WRITTEN, 2026-08-21, on reflow2's own design (2871 nodes) with the in-memory backend in a debug build:

  detect_defects                  71.5s
    sweep_scope                   15.1s
    all_defects                   56.3s
      detect_structural_defects   44.5s   <- 62% of the whole
  operational_network(None) x1   401ms    (329 nodes)
  articulation_points            191µs    -> 56 candidates
  is_single_point_of_failure x1  878ms    = TWO network builds

  56 candidates x 878ms = 49s, which IS detect_structural_defects.

So the sweep currently builds ~115 networks per call where 4 would do. Each build calls `outgoing` once per included node — 329 of them — so this is roughly **37,000 store reads spent re-deriving a graph that never changed**. Of those builds, HALF are the `operational_network(None)` baseline, which is byte-identical on every one of the 56 iterations.

WHY BUILDS AND NOT SECONDS. A count is what the code controls and what survives a loaded machine; a duration assertion in a parallel suite measures contention, and the standing response is to raise the threshold until it stops complaining, which retires the gate without anybody deciding to. It is also the quantity that carries across backends, which seconds do not.

⚠️ HONEST LIMITS. The breakdown above is the in-memory backend in a debug build, which is NOT what users run. The RATIO is the transferable part; on RocksDB with a release binary the same call measures 10.3s. Two candidate counts (56 here) is one design's shape, and a design with more subsystems has more candidates and pays more — which is exactly what the "independent of candidates" clause exists to stop.

📌 WHAT THIS IS FOR, so the number is not mistaken for tidiness: `detect_defects` is paid by `loop_status` and, through the loop hint, by `open_questions` — the first call every session makes, measured at 11.7s of which 10.3 is this. The sweep is not a background chore; it is on the critical path of saying hello.

properties.name: The granularity reading costs one store read per artifact it reports on, plus a constant
properties.statement:
`granularity_report` shall make no more than **N + 2 store reads**, where N is the number of Artifact nodes.

THE DERIVATION, and it is a statement about what ought to be true rather than a round number. The reading's answer is ABOUT ARTIFACTS: how many capabilities each one realizes. So the reads it structurally needs are one scan to find the artifacts, one `outgoing` per artifact to find that artifact's REALIZES edges, and one scan for whatever population it must compare against — N + 2. Nothing about the question requires a read per EDGE, and a cost that grows with edges is the reading paying for the shape of the data rather than the shape of its own answer.

MEASURED BEFORE THE BUDGET WAS WRITTEN, 2026-08-21, over reflow2's own design (2853 nodes, 218 artifacts): **552 reads** — 1 `scan_nodes`, 218 `outgoing`, and **333 `get_node`**. The budget at N=218 is 220, so it is currently at **2.5x**. The 333 are one per REALIZES edge, each asking only "is this id a Capability?", which one scan answers for all of them.

WHY READS AND NOT MILLISECONDS. Per-read cost was measured as FLAT: `get_node` cost 58.0µs over a 2853-node graph and 55.1µs over a 199-node one, a 1.1x spread across a 14x size difference. Nothing is scanning linearly, so the store indexes correctly and the cost is fixed per-call overhead. That makes the READ COUNT the thing a module controls and the wall clock the thing it does not — and a count is also immune to the trap where a duration assertion in a parallel suite measures machine contention and gets its threshold raised until it stops complaining.

⚠️ HONEST LIMITS. Measured on the in-memory backend in a debug build, which is NOT what users run — they get RocksDB. The read COUNT is a property of the module and carries across backends; the per-read microseconds above do not, and are quoted only to justify counting reads instead of timing them.

⚠️ AND THIS IS NOT A SPEED ARGUMENT. `granularity_report` costs ~250ms against `graph_report`'s ~78s in the same configuration — 0.3% of it. Optimising it for wall clock would be manufacturing work, and the optimize skill says to say so. This budget exists for the STRUCTURAL property: a reading about artifacts should cost per artifact. The real speed target is whatever makes `graph_report` cost 78s, and that has not been measured.

properties.name: Constructing a design graph costs under 1 ms
properties.statement:
CONSTRUCTING A DESIGN GRAPH MUST COST NO MORE THAN 1 MILLISECOND.

MEASURED BEFORE THE BUDGET WAS SET, 2026-08-21: 41.3 ms per `DesignGraph::open_in_memory()`, against 54.7 microseconds for an `add_capability` write. **Construction costs 750x a write.**

WHY THIS NUMBER AND NOT A ROUND ONE. The budget is derived rather than picked: construction is SETUP, not work, so a caller that builds a graph and then does twenty writes should spend most of its time on the writes. Twenty writes is about 1.1 ms, so 1 ms is the point at which setup stops dominating the thing it is setting up. Anything tighter would be arbitrary; anything looser leaves the same defect with a smaller number on it.

WHAT IT IS PROTECTING. `open_in_memory` calls `schema::load_schema()`, which parses ELEVEN embedded YAML documents and merges them, every single time. 103 test files construct graphs, several dozen times each; the suite's slowest file by cost-per-test (`edges_need_both_ends.rs`, 2.44 s per test against a 0.92 s median for an entire binary) builds roughly sixteen graphs per test and does almost nothing else.

⭐ THE POINT OF WRITING THIS DOWN BEFORE OPTIMISING, which is the whole experiment: **a budget is what makes optimisation STOP.** Without one there is no condition under which the work is finished, so it ends when attention runs out — which is gold-plating with a performance label on it. With one, the question "should I also cache X?" has an answer that is not a matter of taste.

📌 HONEST LIMITS. (1) This is a DEBUG-BUILD number on one machine; it is a budget for a ratio that happens to be expressed in milliseconds, not a portable performance guarantee. (2) It says nothing about the RocksDB path, which pays a real filesystem cost no caching removes. (3) reflow2 held no other performance budget — this is the first one the project has ever stated, and the design carried exactly ONE Constraint before it, which was a semantic limit rather than a budget.

properties.name: Pairing sees boundaries, not the types that cross them
properties.statement:
A HARD LIMIT ON WHAT `req:complementary-pairing` CAN EVER CATCH, found by the dynograph-foundation trial on 2026-07-28 and not by review.

THE CASE, verified from both sides. dynograph-foundation's `ifc:storage-api` exposes `search_fulltext`, whose signature returns `Vec<dynograph_text::TextHit>`. reflow2 consumes that call and reads all three of the struct's public fields — `node_id`, `node_type`, `score` (`crates/reflow2-core/src/search.rs:67-79`). So reflow2 structurally depends on a type belonging to `dynograph-text`, a crate it NEVER NAMES as a dependency, through a boundary belonging to `dynograph-storage`. Two separately published boundaries are entangled by a type that crosses one of them, and the offer document says they are separate.

WHY PAIRING CANNOT SEE IT. Every axis in the pairing key is a property OF A BOUNDARY: `medium`, `transport_security`, `auth`, the name, the payload format. This seam agrees on all of them. Provider publishes a `library` boundary, consumer requires a `library` boundary, both `unspecified` on transport and auth because a linked crate has neither — the match is clean and correct at every level the rule inspects. The break lives one layer down, in a struct's field list, which no boundary property mentions. A change to `TextHit` breaks a consumer that no document either side holds would predict.

THE GENERAL FORM: a type that crosses a boundary is part of the contract, and the offer models boundaries, not types. `payload_format` says `json` and not which fields; `payload_schema` can point at a schema for a wire format, but nothing does the equivalent for a linked-library signature, where the "wire" is the type system itself.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PAIRING RULE — this is what makes it a constraint rather than a to-do. Pairing must NOT report a clean match as evidence of compatibility. It can honestly say "these two boundaries can be connected"; it cannot say "and nothing crossing them will break you". Those are different claims, and conflating them rebuilds the false green the same trial already produced once. The pairing report should say what it did not examine, the way `coverage_report` says what it never heard of.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLOSE IT, noted so the constraint is not mistaken for permanent: comparing the TYPES that cross a boundary, not just the boundary. For a library seam that is signature and struct-shape comparison — real work, language-specific, and nothing reflow2 does today is close to it. For a wire seam `payload_schema` already points at the answer if both sides fill it in. Until one of those exists, this limit stands and must be STATED rather than discovered.

TWO SMALLER LESSONS FROM THE SAME FINDING. First, the counterparty found it, not the owner of either half — reflow2 could not see that its own `cmp:search` edge pointed at the wrong boundary, and dynograph could not see that its type had escaped. Second, both sides had over-attributed a DIFFERENT risk (`TextError::ReadOnly`) in opposite directions for a day, because both were reasoning about the type and neither had read the call: `search_fulltext` flattens `TextError` to a string, so it never crosses at all. The type that crosses is the one that matters, and only the signature says which that is.

properties.name: Claude (Fable 5)

properties.description:
Author and owner of reflow2. Decides the design — the human in the three-party loop (dec:three-party-checks). **100% of reflow2's actual development is his** (stated 2026-08-18); other people named in this graph are USERS whose reports are field evidence, not developers.

═══ BACKGROUND — in his own words, 2026-08-18 ═══
**Develops software.** Career background is **space acquisitions and systems engineering** (Space Force). **BS Electrical Engineering; MS Electrical Engineering in electro-optics, focused on space object detection.** UAF/DoDAF-fluent.

⭐ THE TRAINING AND THE DAY JOB DIVERGE, AND THE DIVERGENCE IS THE USEFUL PART. He writes software, but he did not come up through software — he came through acquisition and hard EE. So requirements, cost, risk, verification and lifecycle are his FIRST instincts, and signal-versus-noise is a physical intuition rather than a metaphor. That is why an over-engineered answer reads to him as a failure mode with a name, and why "what did you actually measure?" is his standing question.

═══ PERSONA — how to speak to him ═══
First trial of `dec:idea-a-user-carries-a-persona-that-shapes-every-reply`. **Stored in `description` because Contributor has no persona field; whether it deserves one is the open question in that decision.** Agent-drafted from prior sessions, then corrected and enriched by him — which is the SELF-DESCRIBED vs ASSIGNED distinction that decision says is load-bearing.

⭐ **HIS LENS IS NOT "SIMPLIFY" — IT IS A VOCABULARY SWAP, AND GETTING THIS BACKWARDS WOULD PATRONISE HIM.** Requirement, interface, allocation, verification, TRL, KPP, blast radius, signal-to-noise are his native language and must NOT be softened. What he wants dropped is **reflow2's INTERNAL vocabulary** — gap, loop, detector, node id, "the loop owes" — and anything needing knowledge of how the tool is built to follow the sentence. Say what it MEANS for the design, then name the mechanism only if it earns its place.

· **Lead with a recommendation, always, unasked.** Options he can pick from, recommended one first and marked, every option carrying its consequence — including the ones not recommended. `req:a-question-arrives-with-a-reading`, accepted on his word; having to ask for it again is itself the defect.
· **Give him the honest counter-argument.** He overrules recommendations and that is useful; one with no stated counterweight reads as steering.
· **Numbers over impressions.** He notices when a claim was asserted rather than measured. Say plainly what was not checked.
· **Watch for over-engineering** — from the acquisitions side; *"engineers often over design something, it is kind of their nature."* A simple answer that fits is the better answer.
· **Fix at the root, never patch around** — standing, and he wants it built into reflow2 itself.
· **Second person to him; third person in this record**, because other people read the graph.

⚠️ FOR ANY OTHER READER: this describes how to TALK to him. It must never shape what gets written INTO the design — the record stays in its own register whoever is in the room.

properties.name: storybug Boss (storyflow fleet)

properties.decision:
ACCEPTED by Anthony, 2026-08-17 ("accept the black box decision"). This is now the settled mechanism the SE increment will use when it runs.

HIS DIRECTION, looking ahead to a future increment doing proper SE on reflow2 itself: 'we talked about 8 subsystems of reflow2, but currently there were not really any black-boxes... when we do this SE task, this SPECIFIES edge will be needed between each black-box.'

THE DIRECTION IS RIGHT AND THE MECHANISM NEEDED ONE CORRECTION, settled here so the increment does not start by drawing the wrong edges. SPECIFIES does not run BETWEEN two black boxes. It runs from a machine-readable contract ARTIFACT to the INTERFACE that sits between them. Three distinct edges are needed and they answer three different questions:

  PROVIDES / CONSUMES   Component -> Interface   WHO offers this boundary, and who needs it. This is the edge between black boxes, and it is what is missing today (`fact:the-eight-subsystems-are-groupings-not-black-boxes`: 0 of 8 subsystems provide anything).
  SPECIFIES             Artifact  -> Interface   WHICH FILE is the authoritative contract. This is what makes the boundary CHECKABLE instead of prose, and it is the edge that has never been drawn anywhere in the graph.
  REALIZES              Artifact  -> Component   which code implements the box. Already drawn everywhere.

SO THE SE INCREMENT OWES, PER BOUNDARY: an Interface node, a PROVIDES and one or more CONSUMES, and a SPECIFIES to whatever file actually defines the contract. Drawing SPECIFIES alone between subsystems that provide nothing would attach contracts to boundaries that do not exist.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. `req:interface-spec-complete` says a published interface must carry enough to check compatibility rather than prose; `seam_report` and `granularity_report` read the interface tier. With 0 of 8 subsystems providing anything, those computations have nothing to read above the leaves — the decomposition is invisible to every tool that reasons about seams.

⚠️ A CORRECTION THE INCREMENT MUST MAKE BEFORE IT ADDS ANYTHING. `fact:three-of-five-foundation-consumes-edges-name-the-wrong-component` — the CONSUMES edges to the foundation already in the graph are wrong three times in five (`cmp:propagate`, `cmp:search` and `cmp:heal` are credited with crates they do not import). Those are the same edge type this decision rests on. Building new boundary edges on top of a tier that already misattributes three of five would bake the error in.
properties.name: A black box is defined by PROVIDES/CONSUMES; SPECIFIES is what makes its contract checkable rather than prose
properties.rationale:
ACCEPTED ON ANTHONY'S WORD after the mechanism was put to him with the correction stated plainly. What he agreed to is the THREE-EDGE SHAPE, not a schedule: the SE increment itself remains governed by `dec:idea-should-reflow2s-own-design-be-re-derived-through-a-principled-se-process`, which is separately accepted as 'DO IT, BUT NOT YET'.

WHAT WAS REJECTED: drawing SPECIFIES directly between subsystems, which is the form his own words took. It was rejected on the mechanism rather than the intent — SPECIFIES is declared `Artifact -> Interface|Capability|Component` and has no meaning as a component-to-component edge, so the version he described would not have expressed what he wanted even if drawn.

HIS STANDING GROUND, stated in the same breath and closing the cost objection in advance for what will be a large increment: 'I'm more interested in doing things right. If that requires redoing work, so be it - I prefer quality. So if adding SPECIFIES is right, then we have our answer regardless of the amount of work that it includes.'

A COUPLING THE SEQUENCING MUST RESPECT, found while answering this and unchanged by the acceptance. Adding subsystem interfaces adds PROVIDES/CONSUMES edges, which ARE traversed by propagation (Lateral, both directions). Making SPECIFIES propagate would add more. Both ENLARGE every blast radius and therefore every scoped region — at exactly the moment `dec:the-default-scope-depth-should-be-two` is shrinking depth to make regions mean something. The two pull against each other, so the depth change should land and be re-measured BEFORE the SE work adds edges, and re-measured again after. Otherwise a region that got usable will quietly stop being so and nothing will say which change did it. `dec:should-specifies-propagate-impact` holds that question and stays open deliberately.

properties.decision: DECIDED 2026-08-08, Anthony's word: a claim may be described by a QUERY in addition to seed+depth, and an explicit stored node LIST is refused. Seed+depth remains and is unchanged for the work it already fits. WHY THE LIST IS THE ONE OPTION REJECTED, and this is the whole of the reasoning: the original choice — 'the region is COMPUTED from seed+depth rather than stored as a node list, so it follows the design as it changes' — was made to stop a claim going stale the moment the design moves. A query PRESERVES that property, because it is still evaluated fresh every time anyone reads the board; a stored list is the single option that throws it away. So this widens how a region may be DESCRIBED without weakening the guarantee the original decision bought. WHAT IT UNBLOCKS: cross-cutting duties — an audit, a sweep over everything of one kind, cold-validating what another session recorded — which are a general category rather than one team's oddity, and which no radius can express. SUPERSEDES NOTHING: the seed+depth rule stands as the default; this is an addition, so the earlier choice is neither re-opened again nor un-accepted (dec:reopen-supersedes). STILL UNANSWERED and deliberately not decided here: what query language, and whether an unevaluable or empty query is refused at claim time or reported at read time. Both are build questions; the shape is settled, the surface is not.
properties.name: A claimed region may be defined by a QUERY as well as by a seed and a depth — and never by a stored node list
properties.rationale: Because the cost was measured rather than argued. dev_storyflow w-aa0607ff, 2026-08-08: their lane was 'cold-test the retrievability of nodes another session mined', spanning two unrelated slices — there is no seed whose depth-2 radius is that work. They claimed a representative node and put the truth in the `note`, so claim_report's PROSE was right while its STRUCTURED answer was wrong for them, which is the exact failure a structured board exists to remove. THE STRONGER EVIDENCE IS BEHAVIOURAL AND IT IS THREE FOR THREE: both prior workers on that lane skipped claim_region entirely and kept a text file of document paths, because a flat list described their region better than the graph could. A tool losing to a text file is the same shape as the finding that drove the read-half increment — 'today a document BEATS the graph for making a decision, and that is a fair fight the graph loses'. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT WAS PUT AND WEIGHED, not skipped: a claim is ADVISORY and never a lock, so a wrong region misleads a colleague rather than corrupting a write, which argues for keeping the mechanism simple. It was outweighed because an advisory board whose structured field is routinely wrong is how a signal gets trained into being ignored — the same objection that condemned permanently-`live` seat liveness in the same session, and the reason both were treated as real rather than cosmetic.

properties.decision:
THE RULING, for a genre rather than for two files. Anthony, 2026-08-19: *"restore and park two field reports."*

**THE GENRE:** a dated report ABOUT this system's behaviour, written from outside its development — an agent-authored field report from a project that uses reflow2, a bug report, an incident write-up, a user complaint, a beamline observation, a vendor's test certificate. Its defining property is that it is a FROZEN OBSERVATION: true of a moment, and it must not be revised as the design moves.

**WHAT TO DO WITH ONE:** REGISTER the Artifact so the design knows the evidence exists and where it lives, draw NO claim edge, and GOVERN it by this ruling with `ruling: parks`. Detectors then report it as parked and COUNT it in `swept.parked`, rather than filing a deliberate state as a structural defect.

**BOTH ALTERNATIVES ARE FALSE, and this is why the ruling is needed rather than a convention:**
· **A `DOCUMENTS` edge would lie about the direction of obligation.** DOCUMENTS means "this file describes the design and would be WRONG if it drifted out of step with it". A field report is the opposite: it is correct precisely by NOT tracking the design. Under DOCUMENTS, every future design change would read as staling a report that is simply history.
· **Leaving it unregistered loses the evidence.** The file exists, it is cited, and a design that cannot say where its field evidence lives has to rediscover it. This is the state the graph was in between `fbc8e55` and this ruling.
· **Deleting it is the worst of the three**, because it is the one that LOOKS clean: the defect count falls, the gate goes green, and the design quietly stops knowing what it was told.

**THE ONE EDGE THAT IS TRUE:** none of REALIZES / DOCUMENTS / SPECIFIES / PRODUCES / SATISFIES applies, and that is not a gap in the report — it is the accurate description of a document that implements nothing, specifies nothing and describes nothing. `parks` is how the design says so out loud instead of leaving it to be inferred from an absence.

**WHAT IT IS NOT.** Parking is not acknowledgement and not suppression. `acknowledge_defect` is per-instance and expires when the shape changes; this is a standing ruling over a genre whose shape is deliberately fixed. The parked nodes stay visible and counted — `dec:report-dont-judge` is respected, because reflow2 is reading a ruling the design already made rather than deciding anything on its own.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, named so it is not read as settling it:** whether `artifact_type` should gain a value for human evidence. It has `test_result` for the machine kind. "Attaches to nothing on purpose" is not the same claim as "this is dated evidence and it ages" — cf. `req:evidence-carries-the-date-it-was-taken`. That question stays open under `dec:idea-parks-shipped-and-was-still-not-reached-the-instruction-is-missing-where-the-person-is-stuck`.

GOVERNS, as of 2026-08-19: `art:ophyd-service-feedback-2026-08-19`, `art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-08-19`. The genre is expected to grow; new members are parked under this same ruling rather than under a new one each time.
properties.name: A dated field report is REGISTERED and PARKED — its unattached state is correct and deliberate, and neither deleting it nor giving it a DOCUMENTS edge is honest
properties.rationale: Written as a ruling over a GENRE rather than a note on two files because that is the shape the case actually has, and because per-instance acknowledgement was already judged the wrong tool for it in req:a-deliberate-state-is-not-a-defect: acknowledging findings one at a time to record one standing rule does not scale and expires on nodes whose shape is fixed on purpose. Accepted on Anthony's explicit instruction of 2026-08-19 — `parks` refuses a `proposed` ruling by design, so that a musing cannot suppress a finding, which means this decision could not have been made by the agent alone. It exists at all because the same design's own accepted requirement predicted that an agent watching the defect count would delete such documents instead, and then one did.

properties.decision: Verification gains an OPTIONAL criterion — what the check was measured against. A `failing` carrying one is reported as a MEASUREMENT; a `failing` without one is reported as a bar never stated, and is never presented as though a threshold existed. Nothing is refused and no existing check breaks.
properties.name: A failing check may state what it fell short of; where it does not, the report says the bar was never stated
properties.rationale:
Anthony's call, 2026-08-01, from three options. THE PROBLEM, from the music_graph adopt pass (BL-143): that repo's central fact is that everything runs and almost nothing is correct. A smoke run was recorded `passing` (it truly does run) and an accuracy measurement `failing` — but nothing in the repo states an acceptance threshold, so `failing` was the reporter's judgement stored as if it were data. Their words, and the caveat went into a description where no detector reads it.

WHY OPTIONAL RATHER THAN REQUIRED. Option (b), refusing `failing` without a criterion, is the strongest version and was rejected on two counts: it breaks every existing failing check until someone supplies a bar retroactively, and it blocks the honest case where something is plainly broken and no threshold was ever written down. More importantly it is OUT OF STEP WITH THE FAMILY. BL-106, BL-126 and BL-136 all REPORT the gap rather than refusing the work — an unscoped check is counted as unscoped, an undated one as unknown, a consumed one as consumed, and none of them is forbidden. This is the fourth axis and it should behave like the other three.

WHY NOT A NEW STATUS. Option (c), adding `inconclusive`, is the cheapest and gives 'it runs but correctness is unknown' a home — but it treats the symptom. Someone can still write `failing` as a pure opinion and nothing notices, which is the exact defect. It is not foreclosed and could still be added later for its own reasons; it simply does not answer this question.

THE SHAPE THIS COMPLETES. The evidence-quality family now has four faces, all asking whether a green or red tick means what a reader will take it to mean: BL-106 a check stale in TIME, BL-126 narrow in INPUT SPACE, BL-136 not INDEPENDENT of what it validates, and this one — no CRITERION, so there is nothing for the evidence to be evidence of. The first three ask how good the evidence is; this asks what it was evidence FOR.

NOT YET BUILT. The shape is settled; the build is BL-143.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS A FINDING PLUS AN OPEN QUESTION, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Found 2026-08-04 IMMEDIATELY AFTER accepting `dec:coord-board-in-graph`, while updating AGENTS.md to match the move — by noticing that a sentence in it had silently become false. Nothing here is settled, and this does NOT reverse the move.

THE COLLISION, BETWEEN TWO RULES THAT ARE EACH CORRECT ALONE. (1) `dec:export-once-per-pr` and AGENTS.md: "a branch may hold as many commits as you like; only one of them may touch `docs/design/reflow2.json`, and it should be the LAST" — because PRs squash-merge, so only the final export's `prev_content_hash` survives and an intermediate export puts a hole in the lineage chain. (2) `dec:coord-board-in-graph`, accepted minutes earlier: a claim is graph state, recorded by `claim_region`, and it travels in the committed export. TOGETHER THEY SAY: A CLAIM MADE BEFORE THE WORK BECOMES VISIBLE TO ANYONE ELSE ONLY WHEN THE PR MERGES — which is after the work is finished. Claiming first is exactly what a claim is for.

⭐ THIS FALSIFIES A CLAIM MADE ON THE DECIDING NODE, AND THE CORRECTION BELONGS ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN BEING QUIETLY ABSORBED. `dec:coord-board-in-graph` argued, both while open and at acceptance: "both travel in the committed export exactly as COORD.md travels in git — so VISIBILITY IS UNCHANGED." That is wrong, and the asymmetry is precisely the one that matters. COORD.md could be committed and pushed AS ITS OWN COMMIT the moment work started — AGENTS.md even prescribed it ("put the COORD claim commit, which carries no export, FIRST"). The export cannot be, because writing it early is the thing that breaks the lineage chain. The old advice was not merely superseded; the property it depended on — that a claim costs no export — is the property the move removed.

WHAT IT COSTS TODAY: NOTHING, AND THAT IS WHY THE MOVE STANDS. reflow2 has one writer. `dec:coord-board-in-graph` already records that the claims layer is "UNPROVEN under contention" and that the single-writer proof is all that was obtained. This is a second, sharper instance of that same limit — and it is worse than the general statement, because it is not that contention is untested but that a KNOWN MECHANISM makes pre-announcement impossible.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) ACCEPT IT AND SAY SO — with one writer a claim is a note to your future self, and the export at PR time is soon enough. Cheapest and honest; the counter is that it silently retires "claim before you work", which is the discipline the board existed to enforce. (b) LET A CLAIM COMMIT EXPORT, AND EXEMPT IT FROM THE CHAIN — the export gate would need to distinguish a claims-only delta from a design delta. Counter: the gate exists because silent chain breaks happened repeatedly ([BL-107], six commits in a row; [BL-156]), and an exemption is a hole in exactly the check that catches them. (c) CLAIMS LEAVE THE EXPORT — a separate small committed file, written per claim, merged by union like COORD.md was. Counter: that is COORD.md with extra steps, and re-splits the fact into two places, which is the failure the move existed to end. (d) PUBLISH CLAIMS OUT OF BAND — a hosted surface or live tier, which `dec:central-host` and `dec:live-tier` both already ask about. Counter: both are open, both are much larger than this, and `dec:multi-writer-architecture` settled on the repo file with no hosted service.

WHAT MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED: that COORD.md's `merge=union` in `.gitattributes` is what made the old claim commit cheap and conflict-free, and that `docs/design/reflow2.json` uses the `merge=reflow2` three-way driver instead — the two files were never merging the same way, and any option here inherits that difference.

NOT CHECKED: whether `release_claim` has the same problem in reverse — a claim released mid-branch is also invisible until the PR merges, which would mean a finished lane still reads as held by exactly the mechanism that was supposed to fix stale claims. Liveness would cover the case where the session ended, but not the case where the same session released and kept working.
properties.name: OPEN — a claim in the graph cannot be announced before the work, because the export it rides in may only be written once per PR
properties.rationale:
Filed the moment it was found rather than after, because it was found by the cheapest possible route — updating a document to match a decision, and noticing that one sentence in it had become false — and that route only exists while the change is being made. An hour later the sentence would have read as merely stale.

Recorded as its own node rather than as an amendment to `dec:coord-board-in-graph` because that decision is ACCEPTED and this does not reopen it: the move was right, one of its supporting arguments was wrong, and those are different facts. Folding a falsification into an accepted node would either weaken a decision that should stand or hide the correction — `dec:reopen-supersedes` sets the rule that a settled choice is not un-accepted, and this is not a re-opening.

The unchecked item about `release_claim` is named so its absence reads as a hole rather than as completed analysis — and it is the more alarming half, since it would undo the stale-claim fix that was the whole justification for the move.

properties.decision:
⛔ SUPERSEDED 2026-08-17, HOURS AFTER IT WAS WRITTEN, by `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap`. The original text is in `snap:epoch:the-key-is-renamed-and-the-sweep-says-what-it-swept:dec:a-misnaming-is-fixed-in-the-message-not-the-key`, and its reasoning is still the right shape for a project that HAS made a stability commitment — this one has not.

WHAT IT DECIDED, AND WHAT CHANGED. It declined to rename the `disconnected_community` defect category, on the ground that the key is a consumer contract in three places (a documented HEAL category, what `detect_defects` callers match on, and a named ility source) and renaming it would break every consumer to fix a sentence. Anthony's rule reversed exactly that ground: before 1.0 the price of a break is at its lowest and rises with every user, so "it would break consumers" argues for doing it NOW. THE CATEGORY IS NOW `unthreaded_cluster`, which names what is actually missing — a traceability edge, the golden thread — and cannot be misread as "unreachable in the graph".

⭐ AND THE COST ESTIMATE THIS DECISION RESTED ON WAS NEVER CHECKED, which is the part worth carrying forward. It said renaming would "break every consumer" without measuring what that meant. Measured before the rename: the key appears in 14 source and test files and 6 live docs, and 41 times in the committed export — ALL OF THEM PROSE. It was NEVER PERSISTED AS DATA: no node property anywhere holds it as a value, so no observation, no acknowledgement and no ility reading needed migrating. The rename was a sed and a doc pass. A cost asserted rather than measured decided the original call, in a project whose own standing rule is that claims in the records must be evidence-backed.

THE SECOND HALF WAS TAKEN TOO. This decision deferred giving unscoped `detect_defects` the envelope its scoped sibling already returns, as a consumer break out of scope for finishing (b) and (c). Also done: it now returns `{swept, defects}`, so an empty answer says whether it was exercised and found nothing or had nothing to examine.

WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED, and it is the load-bearing half. "Make it compute what it claims" is still the wrong fix, for a reason that has nothing to do with cost: the computation is not broken. It runs connected components over `design_network()` correctly, and the narrowness is the deliberate exclusion of provenance types and CONTAINS — each with its own record (BL-84, BL-124). Widening the walk would undo those and report every Fragment as an island. The requirement's own text misdescribes the detector as computing modularity, which it does not. So the third option was right about the ALGORITHM and wrong about the NAME.

📌 THE GENERAL LESSON, sharpened by being wrong: when a name overstates a computation, ask which of the three is actually wrong — the algorithm, the name, or the message — and do not let the cost of fixing one decide the answer before that cost has been measured.

📝 HOW THIS NODE'S OWN HISTORY WAS NEARLY LOST, recorded because it is `req:a-write-cannot-silently-lose-someone-elses-work` happening to the agent writing about it. The supersession was first written by calling `add_decision` on the existing id, which REPLACED three properties. The reply's `revision` block said so and warned that the prior values existed nowhere else — the mitigation that requirement describes as "detection rather than prevention", working exactly as documented. The fix was to restore the original text, `record_change` to snapshot it, and only then apply this one. The lesson is the ordering: record_change BEFORE the merge, never after, or the snapshot captures the replacement and the history is confidently wrong.
properties.name: SUPERSEDED — the message was fixed and the key was not; the key has since been renamed too
properties.rationale: Superseded by rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap. Its cost argument — that renaming would break every consumer — was asserted and never measured; the key turned out never to have been persisted as data, so the rename needed no migration at all. The algorithm half of its reasoning stands unchanged: the computation is correct and the narrow walk is deliberate, so "make it compute what it claims" remains the wrong fix.

properties.decision:
🛑 RECORDED AS `proposed` DELIBERATELY, AND IT MUST STAY THERE UNTIL ANTHONY SAYS OTHERWISE. This is the agent's judgement about how to model its own work, not his word — the same call made for `dec:an-interchangeable-backend-is-named-by-its-contract-not-by-a-function` on 2026-08-25, and for the same reason. A PROPOSED ruling PARKS NOTHING (there is a test pinning exactly that), so `cmp:upstream` goes on being reported as a part holding no function until this is accepted or replaced. That is correct behaviour, not a leak.

📌 The near-match offered was `cmp:upstream` itself — the PART this rules about. This is the ruling; that is the thing ruled on.

═══ THE SITUATION ═══

`cap:a-declared-dependency-is-watched-not-imported` is implemented across two modules. The JUDGEMENT — the declaration, the baseline, the comparison, what counts as `moved` — is in `crates/reflow2-core/src/depends.rs` (`cmp:depends`). The OBSERVATION — opening each declared upstream export and computing its content hash — is in `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/upstream.rs` (`cmp:upstream`). The split is FORCED: reflow2-core does no file I/O, deliberately and repeatedly.

The standing ruling (`chg:allocation-follows-the-code-not-the-neighbour`, 2026-08-25) says allocate to the module whose code implements the function, MOVE IT, DO NOT DUAL-ALLOCATE. Both halves are real code, so obeying it leaves one of the two modules empty whichever way it goes.

═══ THE PROPOSAL ═══

A module whose whole job is to SUPPLY AN OBSERVATION to a judgement living elsewhere is not an implementer of that judgement's function. It is the caller's half of a caller-supplies-the-observation split — the same shape in which `reconcile_dependencies` takes `observed` and `reconcile_artifacts` takes hashes. The function is "does the design I depend on differ from what I recorded"; reading a file is not that function, it is the material the function consumes.

So allocation stays on `cmp:depends`, and `cmp:upstream` is PARKED as deliberately empty.

═══ WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS WRONG, and it is not a small objection ═══

⚠️ **This is one loose reading away from a licence to leave anything empty.** "It only supplies input to something else" describes a great many modules, and applied loosely it becomes the excuse that quietly covers every unallocated part — the opposite of what the 2026-08-25 sweep achieved, which was to find 19 real functions hiding behind exactly that kind of reasoning. If accepted, the boundary must be stated tightly: NOT "helps another module", but "performs the I/O a deliberate no-I/O boundary forbids the judging module from doing, and makes no judgement of its own."

⚠️ **The alternative is not absurd.** `cmp:upstream` could carry a capability of its own — *"another design's record is read without opening its store"* — which is arguably a real function and is close to what `describe_designs` already does for `cmp:latent`. That means MORE parts and MORE capabilities, which cuts against the over-engineering instinct, but it is honest and needs no new ruling at all.

⚠️ **AND IT IS A LIVE INSTANCE OF AN OPEN QUESTION.** `dec:idea-a-capability-is-a-set-of-functions-and-a-black-box-delivers-functions` asks whether a capability should be a SET of functions across several parts, with a black box delivering functions rather than capabilities. This is exactly that case, arriving from real work rather than from thinking about the model — and if that question is answered YES, this ruling becomes unnecessary, because the capability would name both functions and both parts would hold one.

═══ OPTIONS ═══

(a) ACCEPT this ruling and park `cmp:upstream`, with the tight boundary above written into it.
(b) GIVE `cmp:upstream` ITS OWN CAPABILITY and allocate normally. No ruling needed; one more capability and one more part that is genuinely for something.
(c) DUAL-ALLOCATE to both parts, amending the 2026-08-25 ruling for the multi-module case specifically. Honest about the code, and it should amend that ruling rather than quietly break it.
(d) LEAVE IT UNALLOCATED AND UNRULED — reported as a defect until the black-box question is settled, on the grounds that a real open instance is more useful pressure on that question than a ruling that makes it comfortable.
properties.name: REJECTED — option (b) chosen instead: the reading half was given its own function, so no general rule about observation-suppliers was needed
properties.rationale:
SETTLED BY ANTHONY, 2026-08-28: option (b) — give `cmp:upstream` its own capability — with the explicit instruction to DEFINE THE NEED FIRST rather than mint the capability and back-fill a reason.

═══ WHY IT WAS RAISED (preserved from the original proposal, 2026-08-27) ═══
Raised because building `cap:a-declared-dependency-is-watched-not-imported` produced a genuinely empty part, and the standing allocation ruling gives no answer for a function that spans a deliberate architectural boundary. Left proposed because accepting it would be the agent ruling on the tidiness of its own work, which is precisely the case reserved for the user. The counter-arguments were written at full strength rather than as caveats, because this ruling's failure mode is that it GENERALISES: "supplies input to another module" would excuse nearly any empty part, and the 2026-08-25 sweep found 19 real functions behind that kind of reasoning. Option (d) was listed as a real option for the same reason — an open instance may be worth more than a comfortable answer.

═══ WHY (b) WON ═══
The proposal's own stated failure mode decided it: "supplies input to another module" describes a great many modules, and that reasoning has a 19-to-1 record of being the wrong read. A general rule with that record is a bad rule to accept off a single instance.

(a) WAS ALSO THE WRONG TOOL. Under UAF/DoDAF a resource performs FUNCTIONS and a capability emerges from functions across resources, so "reading a file is not a capability" is defensible doctrine — but reflow2 has no `Function` type, so (a) would have been a doctrine rule papering over a schema limitation. (b) works honestly inside the vocabulary that actually exists.

(c) was declined because it would break a working allocation ruling for one case. (d) was declined because parking a fully-explained defect as "pressure" degrades the defect list, and the pressure would have been aimed at adding a `Function` type to the schema — a change driven purely by reflow2's own design, which nobody using reflow2 has asked for. That is the wrench problem: do not reshape the tool because the tool's own model itched.

⭐ THE NEED WAS DEFINED FIRST, AND IT WAS NOT A NEW ONE. `cap:a-declared-upstream-is-read-where-it-lies` satisfies the already-accepted `req:design-dependencies-declared`, whose statement names the check "has what I depend on moved since" — unanswerable without opening the upstream file. No requirement was invented to justify the part. The separation of the reading half from the judging half is an ARCHITECTURAL CONSTRAINT (reflow2-core does no file I/O), not a separate need, and constraints do not need their own requirements.

📌 `dec:idea-a-capability-is-a-set-of-functions-and-a-black-box-delivers-functions` REMAINS OPEN and is untouched by this. It should be settled when a real user's design needs it, not because of one empty box in reflow2's own graph.

properties.decision:
✅ **DECIDED 2026-08-14 ON ANTHONY'S WORD, WITH A SCOPE CONDITION: BUILD EXACTLY ONE SLICE FIRST — CENTRALITY OVER THE `reasoning` PROJECTION — AND DO NOT SHIP THE GENERAL SURFACE UNTIL THAT ONE HAS PROVED USEFUL.**

The shape below is accepted. The sequencing is the ruling: the highest-value slice was already named inside this node, and `dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written` already records the missing capability in its own words — *"WHICH FEW DECISIONS SHAPE EVERYTHING ELSE... neither what-next nor where-am-i answers it today, and it is what a newcomer actually needs"* — and says it should be a COMPUTATION rather than another paragraph. **That computation is one call away and has never been made.**

⚠️ **THE TWO TRAPS TRAVEL WITH THE FIRST SLICE, NOT WITH THE GENERAL SURFACE**, so neither is deferred by narrowing scope: the exclusion list is part of the projection (the first hand run returned the ten most influential "decisions" as all `decision:ack:` review records; excluding them took the edge set 867 → 255), and the result is a READING, never a defect. Emitting defects from a broad projection is BL-42's exact shape, where one detector became 20 of 31 defects and had to be cut back.

⚠️ STILL NOT SETTLED BY THIS, and deliberately left to the first slice to answer in practice: whether this is a new served tool, an extension of `graph_report`, or an argument on existing detectors; whether a projection is a node type or a static list in code; and whether centrality should be betweenness (already imported) or reachability (what was computed by hand) — `dec:idea-is-betweenness-the-right-centrality` asks that and this does not answer it.

═══════════════ THE ACCEPTED SHAPE, AS PROPOSED ═══════════════

Anthony's framing 2026-08-10, and it is correct: graph algorithms run on any set of nodes and edges, so the analyses should be available across the design rather than wired one-per-detector. Measured basis in `fact:graph-analysis-covers-a-third-of-the-edge-types` — 23 of 35 populated edge types and 31% of edges get no graph analysis at all, including the entire golden thread and the delivery plan.

THE SHAPE: a PROJECTION is a named edge set plus its exclusions. Given one, run the standard battery — strongly-connected components and cycles, connected components, centrality, communities and modularity, articulation points, toposort depth — and REPORT IT AS MEASUREMENT, NEVER AS A VERDICT. `flow.rs` already uses exactly that language for its own cycles ("reported, never judged") and `dec:views-are-projections` already says every view is a projection, so this adds a surface rather than a concept.

FIVE STANDARD PROJECTIONS, each already exercised by hand on 2026-08-10: golden thread (SATISFIES+REALIZES+VERIFIES+ALLOCATED_TO), reasoning (GOVERNED_BY+OBSOLETES+CAUSES+ANTICIPATES), the plan (PRECEDES+SCHEDULED_FOR), structure (the existing DEPENDS_ON + contract-derived set, unchanged), and risk (RISKS+BLOCKS+CONTRADICTS+VIOLATES+MASKS).

THE EXCLUSION LIST IS PART OF THE PROJECTION, NOT A CAVEAT. `structure.rs` already excludes review records and `heal.rs` already names ARTIFACT_BOOKKEEPING (INCLUDES, CHANGED, YIELDED, AT_EPOCH). Those exclusions exist as private constants inside detectors; a projection surface has to lift them into the projection definition or every general run gives a confident wrong answer.

MEASUREMENT AND JUDGEMENT STAY SEPARATE. A battery result is a reading. A finding becomes a DEFECT only where somebody has decided what that finding MEANS for that projection — a cycle in DEPENDS_ON is a defect, a cycle in CAUSES+OBSOLETES turned out to be an ordinary time sequence.

WHAT IS EXPLICITLY NOT PROPOSED: running every algorithm over every edge type and raising what it finds. That is the naive reading of "run it on all edges" and it fails twice over — once on exclusions, once on meaning.
properties.name: DECIDED — a named edge-set projection gets the standard graph battery as MEASUREMENT; build ONE slice first (centrality over the reasoning projection) before the general surface
properties.rationale:
Anthony asked for this to be captured after measuring the coverage gap himself in conversation — his assumption that the ops are edge-agnostic was right, and the measurement confirmed the wiring is what limits them.

Recorded as `proposed` with him as approver rather than accepted, because the shape has three unsettled sub-questions and because the last time this project shipped a broadly-firing structural detector it cost a cut-back (BL-42). The counter-argument is therefore recorded INSIDE the decision rather than left for a reviewer to supply.

The evidence deliberately includes the failed first run. A proposal for a general analysis surface that did not mention that its own first trial returned garbage would be arguing from the successful half of one experiment.

properties.decision:
`import_graph` writes a node whose `node_ref` property names a node that is in neither the document nor the graph, and names it on `ImportReport.dangling_node_refs` (printed by `--import`). It does NOT fail the import. `create_node` is unchanged and still refuses such a write outright.

ORIGINALLY RECORDED AS PROPOSED, because it was Claude's engineering call taken to keep this design's own export restorable, and it was Anthony's to settle or overturn.

✅ SETTLED 2026-08-29 — ACCEPTED on Anthony's word, after its rationale was corrected twice the same day and a root-cause pass was run on dangling references. He settled the behaviour as drafted: report, do not refuse.
properties.name: A restore reports an unresolvable node reference rather than refusing the whole document
properties.rationale:
THE ALTERNATIVE, and why it lost: refuse the import, matching `create_node`. Measured 2026-08-29 — this design's own export carried nine references written before the guard existed. Under refusal the export could not be restored AT ALL, and the only remedy on offer was hand-editing the export document, which is the one thing this project tells users never to do. Any user upgrading into the guard with a single pre-existing dangling reference would silently acquire an unrestorable backup.

THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES IT: a write ASSERTS something new, and refusing a new record about a node the design does not have is right. An import ASSERTS NOTHING — it reproduces a state that already existed, and the document is the evidence that it did. Refusing there is the tool substituting its judgement for a reality it is being handed.

NOT A NEW POLICY. `ImportReport` had already answered this same question three times — `skipped_edges` (an edge whose endpoint is missing is skipped and named, not fatal), `integrity_note` and `provenance_note`, each documented as "the import still proceeds but never silently". A dangling property reference is the other shape of a missing endpoint, so answering it differently would have one import refusing what its neighbour two lines up reports.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
⚠️ CORRECTED TWICE ON 2026-08-29, BEFORE THIS WAS PUT UP FOR A RULING.
The second correction reverses part of the first. Both are kept.
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

🛑 ① THE RENAME LEG WAS WITHDRAWN — CORRECTLY, BUT TOO BROADLY. The original said the nine were "five instances of a `prj:`/`proj:` typo, four capabilities renamed after the fact was written" and concluded that "the renames that produce most real dangles are unreachable by ANY write-time check". Measured: those four ids never existed as nodes under any prefix, and the root-cause pass sharpened it further — 6 of the 9 are PREFIX ERRORS on a real slug (`prj:`→`proj:`, `cap:thin-install`→`req:thin-install`) and 3 are slugs INVENTED FROM THE NAME OF A SERVED TOOL. None is a rename. All nine would have been refused at write time.

⭐ ② THE ADMITTED COST IS SMALLER. The original accepted one price — "an export/import laundering route the write guard closes" — as a permanent blind spot. `dangling_reference` (#373) now reports an unresolvable reference on its own terms whatever the node's degree, so anything an import launders in is named on the next sweep rather than never.

🛑🛑 ③ AND THE RETIRE CASE IS REAL AFTER ALL — IT WAS IN THE PROPERTY NOBODY HAD SWEPT. Correction ① was true of `TemporalFact.subject_id` and was over-generalised to the whole class. The root-cause pass swept the other two pointer properties `heal.rs` names, which `fact:defect-seven-temporal-facts-name-a-subject-id-that-does-not-exist` asked for on 2026-08-16 and nobody had done. `Snapshot.target_id` holds 195 values, 191 resolve, and ALL FOUR THAT DANGLE ARE RETIRES — `art:content`, `art:content-test`, `art:tools-content` snapshotted at `epoch:content-store-discontinued`, and `ctr:anthony` at `epoch:the-owners-identity-is-one-node-again`. Every one resolved when written and broke when its target was deleted or merged.

⭐⭐ THIS IS NOW THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT ON THE RECORD FOR REPORTING RATHER THAN REFUSING, and it is measured rather than hypothesised: THOSE FOUR DANGLING REFERENCES ARE CORRECT. A Snapshot exists precisely to preserve what a node was; when the node is deliberately deleted, the snapshot pointing at nothing is the mechanism working, not a fault. So a refusing import would reject this design's own export over four records that are doing their job — and a refusal cannot tell a broken reference from a correct historical one, because at the point of restore they are the same bytes. Only a report can hand that judgement to the person who owns the design.

⚠️ WHAT THAT COSTS THE OTHER SIDE, stated plainly: `Snapshot.target_id` is NOT declared `node_ref`, so those four are invisible to the guard and to `dangling_reference` today, and this argument bites only if anyone declares it. The point stands anyway — the four exist, they are correct, and any rule that treated pointer properties uniformly would refuse them.

📌 WHAT SURVIVES UNTOUCHED, and is what actually carries the decision: assertion versus reproduction, the unrestorable-backup measurement, and the three existing `ImportReport` precedents. None rested on any corrected claim.

properties.decision:
DECIDED on Anthony's word, 2026-08-24, choosing between three costed options: "An edge: a claim". A record that did the work says so, with `INVALIDATES` (`* -> *`, carrying `note` and `at`), rather than a detector inferring staleness from dates.

WHAT THE ALTERNATIVE WAS AND WHY IT LOST — and it lost on a MEASUREMENT, not on taste. The cheaper option was a computed bucket: `loop_status.verifications.stale`, a failing check whose verified nodes changed since its last run. It needs no discipline, which is the strongest argument any option here had. It is also unbuildable honestly: the inference has to order a change against `last_run_at`, and of 439 hand-written ChangeEvents only 37 (8%) carried a date, against 84% of the 192 written by the reconcile paths. The difference was not care — `add_change_event` had no `detected_at` parameter, so the ordinary path could not date anything. A bucket built on that would have over- or under-reported and been unable to say which.

⭐ THE EDGE IS GENERAL AND THAT IS THE POINT. dev_storyflow proposed `INVALIDATES_RUN` for Constraint -> Verification. The same missing relation was measured independently on this project and on Anthony's other machine, both times on a TemporalFact rather than a Verification — see `dec:idea-how-does-the-graph-learn-what-a-session-invalidated`, whose option C asked for "an edge from a ChangeEvent to the finding it ANSWERS". Two projects, three sightings, two node types, one relation. So the `_RUN` suffix came off and both endpoints stayed open.

⭐⭐ IT CLAIMS THE RESULT IS STALE AND NOTHING MORE, which is why it is not called `RESOLVES` — the first name tried. A repair does not make a check pass; it makes the last RESULT untrustworthy, and only a re-run can say what is true now. `RESOLVES` would have reflow2 asserting an outcome nobody measured, which is `dec:non-goal-reflow2-does-not-judge-whether-a-check-is-meaningful` one step along. Three consequences follow and all three are load-bearing: the edge never touches the target's `status`; the check is NOT dropped from `loop_status.verifications.attention`, because silencing it would swap one wrong reading for another and would be the truncation `parks` was careful not to become; and `rerun_owed` is THREE-VALUED, with null meaning one side is undated and nobody can say — never collapsed to false.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE. The computed bucket is deferred, not refused: `add_change_event` now takes `detected_at`, so the ordering it needs becomes possible as dates accumulate. Whether to build it then is open, and the parent brainstorm's options A, B and E are untouched.
properties.name: A finding is closed by a CLAIM, not by an inferred staleness
properties.rationale:
Prompted by dev_storyflow's 2026-08-23 report, which cost a real user a real instruction: a session read a `failing` check dated that same day and reported its two defects as the live state of the system, when both had been repaired hours earlier and written up on two Constraint nodes. `describe_schema(from: Constraint, to: Verification)` returned ZERO exact matches; the reporter drew `CONTRADICTS` with `alignment: opposing` and called it "obviously a stand-in".

The prior decision on this ground was READ BEFORE DECIDING AND DOES NOT COVER THIS CASE. `dec:verification-freshness-not-a-gap` (accepted, Anthony, 2026-07-26) ruled that a check older than its code is a freshness FACT rather than a gap, because it is a STANDING PROPERTY that "would fire on every legitimate refactor as readily as on a real hole". This is a different question: a repair landing against a FAILING check is an EVENT, it fires once, and it fires only where there is both a failure and a repair. So this settles new ground rather than reversing a settled decision — and it honours that decision's reasoning by making the result a REPORT beside the check rather than a new nag.

properties.decision:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION of the standing contradiction between `dec:merge-survivor-provenance` and the two facts that contradict it (`fact:apply-heal-would-have-destroyed-the-wrong-contributor`, `fact:defect-merge-survivor-ignores-priority-and-status`). AWAITING ANTHONY'S WORD — recorded at `proposed` with him as approver, so the loop reports it as owed rather than letting it read as settled.

DO NOT RE-OPEN THE PROVENANCE RANKING. It is correct and it is not what fails. The failure is entirely in the TIEBREAK beneath it: provenance ranks authored > planned > imported > reconciled > inferred > healed, and in practice both sides of a real collision are hand-authored, so the rank TIES and `a <= b` on the node id decides. Twice observed, twice choosing the worse node — `req:backend_as_product` (medium, accepted) over `req:graph_is_the_content_bible` (critical, proposed) at dev_storyflow 2026-08-08, and `ctr:anthony` (8 edges, no description) over `who:ajs` (161 edges, full description) here on 2026-08-09.

THE ARGUMENT THAT UNBLOCKS THIS, and it is the whole point of the node: DEGREE IS NOT A POLICY. The reason the rule was deliberately left alone is recorded in `fact:defect-merge-survivor-ignores-priority-and-status`: ranking priority above status, or the reverse, asserts a claim about what matters more in a design, and `dec:readiness-is-an-observation-the-threshold-is-the-judgement` says reflow2 must not default that — it is the user's. THAT REASONING IS SOUND AND IS NOT BEING OVERTURNED. But "destroy fewer edges" is not a claim about what design content matters; it is a property of the MERGE OPERATION. And the thing it would replace — alphabetical id order — is arbitrary by construction. Substituting a non-arbitrary tiebreak for an arbitrary one asserts no policy at all, which is exactly why this can be done while the priority/status question stays the user's.

FOUR PARTS, SMALLEST FIRST.

(1) WHERE PROVENANCE TIES, BREAK BY DEGREE — keep the node whose deletion destroys less of the design. Degree is already computed and 161 against 8 is not close.

(2) WHERE DEGREE ALSO TIES, REFUSE RATHER THAN PICK. A merge that genuinely cannot distinguish should ask. `dec:ask-not-repair` already holds this shape for the suspicion half; this extends it to the survivor half. A refusal that names both candidates is strictly more useful than a coin toss that names neither.

(3) KEEP PRIORITY AND STATUS OUT OF THE RULE, PUT THEM IN THE DISCLOSURE. "You are deleting a critical, still-unconfirmed node in favour of a medium, accepted one" is INFORMATION, not a policy, and the machinery to say it already exists — `chg:a-merge-proposal-discloses-what-it-would-destroy` built `would_destroy` and the alphabet-chose-the-victim line in August. This adds a sentence to an existing disclosure rather than a rule to an existing ranking.

(4) THE SCORING HALF IS SEPARATE AND PROBABLY WORTH MORE. Similarity is prose-only, unweighted by shared referents, which is what let two requirements sharing no requirement, surface or actor score 81-85. Fixing the survivor rule makes a bad merge less destructive; fixing scoring stops the pair reaching a merge at all. Recorded here so the two halves are not confused, NOT claimed by this decision.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated because the defect count will not move and somebody will look for it: recording this does not clear `heal:0fc0362a90ff913b` or `heal:7456a4d260ca45ce`. The contradiction detector fires on every CONTRADICTS edge whose alignment is not `supporting` and NEVER LOOKS FOR A RESOLVING DECISION, despite its own doc comment and its `suggested_fix_type: generate_decision` saying otherwise. The honest closure path is that when the tiebreak actually changes, the two facts become historical observations about the OLD rule and their CONTRADICTS edges should be retired as part of that change — not silenced now.

EVIDENCE GAP, stated rather than papered over: degree is KNOWN to decide the contributor case correctly (161 v 8). Whether it separates dev_storyflow's pair is UNVERIFIED — that is their graph and it was not read. If their two nodes have similar degree, part (1) helps less than this decision implies and part (4) carries more of the weight.
properties.name: PROPOSED — when provenance ties, the merge survivor is the node whose deletion destroys less, and a genuine tie refuses instead of picking
properties.rationale:
Written at Anthony's request on 2026-08-10 after he asked for the merge-survivor pair in plain English and then for the recommendation to be recorded. The recommendation is mine; the decision is his to make, which is why this is `proposed` with an approver edge rather than accepted.

The load-bearing move is separating the tiebreak from the ranking. Reading `fact:defect-merge-survivor-ignores-priority-and-status` first is what made that possible — it states plainly that the rule was NOT re-opened on purpose, and names the principle. Without that, the obvious proposal is "consult priority and status", which walks straight into the judgement reflow2 refuses to default and would have been rejected for a good reason. The finding that the blocked path and the open path are different paths came from reading why it was blocked.

Deliberately does not claim the scoring half, and deliberately records the unverified half of its own evidence.

properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-24 by Anthony: *"keep rocksdb 0.24 as-is. We can switch to rust-rocksdb in a future session that creates a PR for this switch."*

═══ WHAT HE SPOTTED, AND IT IS RIGHT ═══

There are TWO separate crates wrapping the same C++ engine, with independent version numbering:

    crate            declared      resolved            latest
    rocksdb          "0.24"        0.24.0              0.25.0     ← in use, historically unmaintained
    rust-rocksdb     --            --                  0.52.0     ← active, community-standard
    librocksdb-sys   --            0.17.3+10.4.2       --
    tantivy          --            0.26.1              --

reflow2 uses `rocksdb`, pinned at `dynograph-foundation/Cargo.toml:60`, one minor behind its own latest and on the less-maintained of the two. `rust-rocksdb` tracks current stable C++ RocksDB releases and carries the fuller feature set (transactions, backups, column families).

⚠️ **THE TWO VERSION NUMBERS ARE NOT COMPARABLE.** 0.24 vs 0.52 is not "28 versions behind" — they are different crates that never shared a numbering line. Reading them as one series would overstate the gap.

═══ WHY THIS BECOMES REFLOW2'S DECISION NOW ═══

Increment 4 of `dec:absorb-the-foundation-subset-and-end-the-dependency` absorbs `dynograph-storage`, which means reflow2 declares this dependency in its OWN manifest for the first time. "Which rocksdb crate, at which version" stops being dynograph's call and becomes reflow2's, on that branch, that day.

═══ WHAT WAS DECIDED, AND THE REASONING ═══

**Absorb `rocksdb = "0.24"` verbatim.** The migration stays purely mechanical: the same crate, the same version, the same API, so nothing about the 86-file absorption can fail for a reason other than the absorption.

**Then switch to `rust-rocksdb` in a separate PR**, with its own test run and its own revert.

⭐ THIS IS THE SAME PRINCIPLE THAT SPLIT THE ABSORPTION INTO INCREMENTS: one variable at a time, so a failure has one cause. Bumping even to `rocksdb` 0.25 inside this increment would mean a breakage had two candidate explanations, and the increment is already the largest by a wide margin — ~5,516 lines across ~86 files, bringing rocksdb and tantivy into the manifest together.

🛑 AND THE COST OF THE ALTERNATIVE IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL HERE. This project has already paid for attributing one effect to the wrong cause today: a 40-second regression was blamed on the wrong code because two numbers happened to agree. Mixing a dependency swap into a migration is the same shape, set up in advance.

═══ ROADS NOT TAKEN ═══
• **Bump to `rocksdb` 0.25 during the absorption** — smallest possible change, same crate. Declined for the two-causes reason; it buys one minor version at the price of an ambiguous failure.
