--- WHERE IT LIVES: THE QUESTION HE FLAGGED ---

(1) BESIDE THE STORE, NOT IN THE GRAPH — the recommendation. The graph is the DESIGN; usage is telemetry about a SESSION and belongs to the process, not to the design. Putting it in the graph means every export carries it (already 4.1 MB), every diff churns with it, and `compare_designs` reports telemetry as design divergence. `rule:per-design-state-is-never-a-process-global` draws the same line from the other side: the test is whether a second design open in the same process would need a different value, and session usage would not. PRECEDENT EXISTS AND IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL — reflow2 already keeps session-scoped state beside the store rather than inside it (the shared-mode rendezvous and log; `shared.rs` pins "log sits beside the store too" and "rendezvous sits beside the store NOT INSIDE IT").

(2) IN THE GRAPH — what it would buy: usage becomes queryable with the same tools as everything else, and survives in the export. COUNTER: it makes the design record grow with facts that are not design, and the export is the thing consumers merge.

⭐ THE RESOLUTION THAT USES BOTH, and it is an existing pattern rather than a compromise: LOG RAW TO THE SIDECAR, PROMOTE FINDINGS DELIBERATELY. `dec:manifest-derived-is-not-manifest-accepted` already holds that a bulk derivation is not a bulk accept and writes nothing until asked. Raw usage is derivation; a finding worth keeping ("this rule was violated four times") is something a human accepts INTO the design.

--- WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT SOUNDS ---

**NOBODY HAS EVER MEASURED SKILL USAGE.** `dec:bl-155` measured TOOL calls — 6,095 across 46 retained transcripts — and found 40 of 132 tools never called. There is no equivalent for `get_skill`, which is server-side and trivially countable. So `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` proposes to improve a rate NOBODY HAS EVER OBSERVED, and without this instrument there is no way to tell whether any hint changed anything.

⚠️ AND BL-155'S CAVEAT TRAVELS WITH IT, because it is the trap: absence is WEAK evidence. `set_project_mode` appeared as text in ten transcripts with zero recorded calls despite having been used. A tool can be discussed far more than used; a skill can be FOLLOWED FROM MEMORY without being fetched, which this session did for revise-design. **So a usage log measures FETCHES, not COMPLIANCE, and reporting it as compliance would be exactly the false confidence the loop exists to prevent.**

--- OPEN SUB-QUESTIONS ---
- Does it log ISSUES as well as usage (his words: "usage and issues")? A refusal is already visible to the server; recording refusals would surface the enum-rejection class of defect without anyone filing a report.
- Is it opt-in? `dec:idea-measure-the-surface` already asks how far usage telemetry may go, and this is that question made concrete.
- Retention. `dec:content-growth-is-bounded-by-what-not-by-size` says what bounds a store is WHAT gets stored, not how big it is.

NOTHING IS PROMOTED. Recorded so the shape is chosen deliberately rather than by whoever builds it first.
properties.name: OPEN — how should reflow2 log which of its own skills and tools a session used, and where does that log live?
properties.rationale: Anthony's idea, with his own doubt about the tool shape carried into the record rather than smoothed away, because that doubt is the part that decides the design. Kept OPEN rather than accepted: the storage question turns on how far telemetry may go, which is already an unanswered decision (dec:idea-measure-the-surface), and answering it here by implication would settle it without him.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-20: *"just as reflow2 checks that a capability had a requirement, I feel like that a defined black box should have an interface... reflow2 should define black boxes (part of the functional allocation to a system) and define/enforce interface contracts (MOSA I don't think would be possible without contracts)."* He named the exceptions himself: designs with no black boxes at all, boundaries where a contract is deliberately not enforced, and a single black box with nothing to interface with.

SEARCHED FIRST, at his instruction. Read: `dec:mosa-conformance`, `req:key-interfaces` (accepted), `req:modularity-computed` (accepted), `cap:key-interfaces`, `ver:key-interfaces`, `req:interface-spec-complete`, `fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it`, `dec:idea-how-does-a-users-project-acquire-vocabulary-it-never-uses`, and the three interface detectors in detect.rs. **MUCH OF THIS IS ALREADY SETTLED AND BUILT** — what follows is only what is not.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ WHAT MOSA ALREADY PRODUCED HERE, so it is not re-litigated

`dec:mosa-conformance` (2026-07-25) found exactly two things missing and BOTH WERE PROMOTED THE SAME DAY on his word and are now ACCEPTED: `req:key-interfaces` — the design says which boundaries are published — and `req:modularity-computed` — severability is computed, not asserted by the diagram. `Interface.designation` (internal / published / required / both) IS the key-interface marker MOSA needed, and it is built and tested (`cap:key-interfaces`, `ver:key-interfaces`, 8 cases).

So the vocabulary half of his instinct is DONE. What is missing is checks.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📐 THE ANALOGY IS EXACT, AND MEASURED 2026-08-20 ON THIS DESIGN

  a Capability with no Requirement   → `unmotivated_capability` FIRES
  a Component with no Interface      → NOTHING FIRES

  56 Components
    14  carry any PROVIDES or CONSUMES
    42  carry none
      · 24 of those are in a DEPENDS_ON pair, so `undeclared_seam` sees them —
        but AGGREGATED into ONE project-scoped gap at severity 0.45
      · 18 are NEITHER coupled NOR interfaced: **nothing in reflow2 sees them at all**

Those 18 are the finding. They are black boxes in name only — no boundary, no coupling, nothing to sever along — and every instrument reports clean over them.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 AND THE SECOND HOLE IS WORSE, BECAUSE IT IS ON THE PUBLISHED BOUNDARIES

`req:interface-spec-complete` is ACCEPTED intent — a published contract must carry what two systems have to AGREE on, in terms a computation can compare. **NOTHING CHECKS IT.** Measured on this design:

  4 interfaces designated `published`
  3 of the 4 have unset contract fields:
     ifc:core-api        7 of 9 unset
     ifc:graph-export    6 of 9 unset
     ifc:mcp-tools-http  1 of 9 unset

reflow2 publishes a boundary whose medium, paradigm, payload format, auth and error model are all `unspecified`, and calls the design green. That is MOSA step 4 — DEFINE INTERFACES — unenforced on the tool's own published surface.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📋 MOSA'S FIVE STEPS, AGAINST WHAT REFLOW2 HAS — vocabulary vs check

  1 PLAN                    Flow/process modelling exists          check: n/a
  2 MODULARIZE              modularity computed                    check: FIXED 2026-08-20
                                                                   (it read 1.00 over nothing;
                                                                    now NOT MEASURABLE, honestly)
  3 IDENTIFY INTERFACES     `designation` built and tested         check: NONE — nothing says
                                                                   you never identified any
  4 DEFINE INTERFACES       10 structured fields, `set_interface_spec`  check: NONE — 3 of 4
                                                                   published are incomplete
  5 STANDARDIZE INTERFACES  DesignRule with `enforced` (17 rules,  check: NONE binding a rule
                            6 enforced)                            to an interface as a standard

FOUR OF FIVE HAVE THE VOCABULARY AND NO CHECK. That is the three-legs pattern (`fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it`) landing on the interface layer specifically: typed tool yes, instruction yes, DETECTOR THAT NOTICES ABSENCE no.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
IDEAS

**A. `uninterfaced_component` — a black box with no boundary at all.** The exact sibling of `unmotivated_capability`. Catches the 18 nothing currently sees.
   ⚠️ Noise: 42 of 56 on this design. Aggregate like `undeclared_seam` does, or per-component? Aggregation is what made the 73 uncontracted pairs read as one 0.45 note nobody acted on for months — so the aggregation that controls noise is also what buried the last finding of this shape.

**B. `incomplete_published_contract` — a boundary designated `published` with the agreement axes unset.** Directly satisfies `req:interface-spec-complete`, which is accepted and unimplemented. Narrow by construction: it fires only on what the design has already CHOSEN to publish, so it cannot nag a design that has not started.
   ⭐ Cheapest of these, most defensible, and it is the MOSA step that makes severability mean anything.

**C. Let a ruling declare the exceptions.** His three cases — no black boxes yet, contract deliberately unenforced, a single box — are DELIBERATE STATES, and `governed_by(..., ruling: "parks")` already exists for exactly that. It would need extending to these detectors, which is the same reachability problem `parks` already has.

**D. Self-limit rather than enumerate exceptions.** Precedent from 2026-08-20: `level_spine_disagreement` compares against the highest level PRESENT, so a flat design reports nothing and no ladder depth is prescribed. The same move here — fire only where the design has ALREADY used interfaces somewhere — handles "no black boxes yet" and "single box" without anyone declaring an exception.
   ⚠️ But it also means a design that never draws a single interface is never asked about it, which is `dec:idea-how-does-a-users-project-acquire-vocabulary-it-never-uses` — open, and the harder half.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐ ONE PUSHBACK ON HIS OWN EXCEPTION, offered because it may sharpen the rule

He asks whether a design could have no black boxes, and treats "a single black box with nothing to interface with" as an exception. IN SE TERMS IT MAY NOT BE ONE. A system is defined by its boundary — that is what makes it a system rather than a region of the universe. A single black box still has an interface: to its ENVIRONMENT. reflow2 already supports this (an Interface may sit between a Component and an ACTOR, not only between two Components), so the vocabulary is there.

If that holds, the rule is stronger and simpler than he proposed: **every black box has at least one interface — to a sibling or to the environment — and a box with none has not been bounded yet.** The genuine exceptions then are not about EXISTENCE but about ENFORCEMENT: how complete the contract must be, and whether both sides are held to it.

⚠️ COUNTER, recorded beside it: that is an SE-domain claim, and `req:design-anything` keeps the vocabulary neutral. Whether "every element has a boundary" is a universal truth or a systems-engineering convention is exactly the kind of thing this project refuses to assume on a user's behalf.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⚠️ HONEST BOUNDS

· Every number here is from reflow2's own graph. Whether 42-of-56 is typical of a user's project is unknown — and by the standing rule, what this means for an arbitrary project is the question that matters, not what it means here.
· Nothing is costed. B looks small; A's noise question is unresolved and is the one that decides whether it helps or joins the 80 unsurfaced gaps.
· `dec:mosa-conformance` stays OPEN on its own narrower question — whether to ship a MOSA-BRANDED report — and nothing here decides that. Its own answer leans: a view over computations that exist, never schema, because adopting one domain's language is what reflow2 has refused since the beginning.
properties.name: OPEN — should a Component with no interface be a finding, the way a Capability with no Requirement already is? And should a PUBLISHED contract have to be complete?

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-24: *"what else is out there besides rocksdb that perfectly meets what reflow2 needs, but is much faster to compile than rocksdb?"*

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📐 WHAT A REPLACEMENT ACTUALLY HAS TO DO — read from the code, not assumed

The seam is far narrower than "replace RocksDB" sounds. `KvBackend` (dynograph-storage/src/backend.rs) is **six byte-level primitives** over six named column families:

    get(cf, key) -> Option<Arc<[u8]>>      put(cf, key, value)
    delete(cf, key)                        prefix_scan(cf, prefix) -> Vec<(k,v)>
    prefix_delete(cf, prefix)              commit_batch(ops)

`ifc:kv-backend`'s own spec says everything schema-aware — validation, the reverse index, the read cache, the write-buffer overlay, the full-text sidecar — sits ABOVE this trait, and that **ordered prefix iteration is the one structural assumption**.

⭐⭐ AND IT ALREADY HAS TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS. Besides RocksDB there is an in-memory HashMap backend in the same file. **The swap this question asks about is already demonstrated once**, which makes this an unusually cheap thing to try — and is the sharpest difference from `dec:idea-swap-dynograph-foundation-as-the-substitutability-demo`, which was REJECTED for costing as much as the real thing. That node measured 48 files importing `dynograph_core`; this touches ONE file behind a six-function trait. **Its cost argument does not reach this question.**

⭐ THE FIT NOBODY HAS EXPLOITED: reflow2 is SINGLE-WRITER by design — the whole graph is held under a single-writer lock. RocksDB is a concurrent LSM built for many writers. An engine whose model IS single-writer/multi-reader is not a compromise here; it is a closer match than what is there.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 THE PREMISE, MEASURED BEFORE ANSWERING — and it is only half true

Recorded because the question names compile time as the reason, and the reason is worth checking:

    release build of reflow2-mcp (~19 min)  — recompiled RocksDB: 0 times
    workspace test run #1 (~10 min)         — recompiled RocksDB: 0 times
    workspace test run #2 (~10 min)         — recompiled RocksDB: 0 times

Every long wait on 2026-08-24 was recompiling **reflow2-core and reflow2-mcp**, because they were being edited. RocksDB was cached throughout — reflow2's own Cargo.toml already calls it "a one-time, cached cost", and that holds.

⇒ **THE ANSWER MUST NAME WHICH COMPILE IT SPEEDS UP.** A cold first build, a CI cache miss, a new contributor's first `cargo build`, and a profile switch each pay the RocksDB cost in full — those are real and recurring. Day-to-day iteration does not, and a swap justified on day-to-day iteration would be justified on a cost that is not being paid.

⚠️ THE DISK COST IS UNCONTESTED THOUGH, and is a separate argument: one cached `librocksdb-sys` build directory measures **1.7 GB**. That compounds `[profile.dev]`'s own note about cargo having no GC.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
IDEAS, UNRANKED, each with what it costs

**A. redb — pure Rust, ACID, ordered B-tree, single-writer/multi-reader.**
   ⭐ Named tables map to column families; ordered iteration is native; zero C or C++, so it compiles in seconds. Its concurrency model is EXACTLY reflow2's.
   ⚠️ Younger and less battle-tested than RocksDB; single file rather than a directory of SSTs, which changes what backup and the `.reflow2/graph` layout mean.

**B. fjall — pure Rust LSM, partitions ≈ column families.**
   ⭐ The closest SEMANTIC match: same shape as what is there, so the port is the most mechanical of the options.
   ⚠️ Also young — and being an LSM it inherits the compaction question that surfaced the same day (a live store at 7.4× the bytes of its content). Choosing it keeps that problem rather than dissolving it.

**C. LMDB via `heed` — small C, memory-mapped, single-writer/multi-reader.**
   ⭐ Decades of production use, named databases ≈ column families, ordered cursors, and it is SMALL — it compiles in seconds despite being C, so "it is C" and "it is slow to build" are not the same objection.
   ⚠️ The map size must be declared up front and grown deliberately; a write that outgrows it fails rather than expanding. Still a C dependency, which the pure-Rust options remove outright.

**D. libmdbx via `mdbx-rs` — LMDB's successor.**
   ⭐ Keeps C's virtues and fixes the map-size ergonomics that are LMDB's sharpest edge.
   ⚠️ A smaller community than any of the above; the bus factor is a real consideration for a store that holds the only copy of a design.

**E. sled — pure Rust, ordered, embedded.**
   ⚠️ Named for completeness rather than as a candidate: it has been pre-1.0 for years with a rewrite signalled. A design store is the wrong place to take that bet.

**F. SQLite via `rusqlite` (bundled) — and it could collapse TWO dependencies.**
   ⭐⭐ The interesting one, because SQLite's FTS5 could replace **tantivy** as well — the 847-line `dynograph-text` crate that increment 5 of the absorption would otherwise bring in. One dependency instead of two, and the most battle-tested storage engine in existence.
   ⚠️ A relational engine wearing a KV trait is a mismatch in spirit, and prefix scans become index scans; performance would have to be measured rather than assumed. Bundled SQLite is still a C compile, though a far smaller one.

**G. KEEP RocksDB AND ATTACK THE COST THAT IS ACTUALLY PAID.** sccache or a prebuilt artifact for cold/CI builds; or feature-gate it out of the builds that do not need it (`--no-default-features` already runs the core suite without it).
   ⭐ The honest status quo, and the only option that needs no port. It is also what the measurement above argues for if the pain is day-to-day iteration rather than cold builds.
   ⚠️ It does nothing for the disk cost, nothing for the C++ toolchain requirement, and nothing for a contributor's first build.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📌 WHAT NOBODY HAS COSTED, so the list is not read as an estimate

No measurement exists of a COLD build's RocksDB share (the number that would justify A-F), of any candidate's compile time in this tree, or of any candidate's read latency on a 3,100-node design. The seam's narrowness makes a spike genuinely cheap — one file, six functions, and an existing in-memory implementation to copy the shape from — so **the honest next step is to build one behind the trait and measure, rather than to choose from this list on paper.**

⚠️ AND A BOUND ON THE WHOLE QUESTION: `KvBackend` lives in dynograph-foundation, not reflow2. Until the absorption's increment 5 lands, changing it means changing somebody else's repository — which `dec:idea-dynograph-crates-independent-in-code-coupled-in-release` says reflow2's design has no standing to decide. **Absorb first, then swap** is the ordering that keeps this inside reflow2's own walls.

Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`. Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-24, immediately after the RocksDB DEBUG_LEVEL exchange. Nothing here is intent and nothing is planned.

The premise was measured before the options were listed — not to argue the question down, but because it changes what a good answer has to be. "Faster to compile" is true of every option here for a COLD build and true of none of them for the iteration loop that was actually slow today.

DEDUP: read three near-matches in full. `dec:idea-swap-dynograph-foundation-as-the-substitutability-demo` is REJECTED and asks about reimplementing the whole foundation — its cost argument (48 files import dynograph_core) does not reach a six-function trait with an existing second implementation. `dec:absorb-the-foundation-subset-and-end-the-dependency` decides WHAT to absorb, not what the bytes land on. `dec:idea-where-does-the-10k-work-actually-land` already records that "the byte store is already swappable" and asks a scaling question instead.

properties.decision: UNSETTLED. Reported 2026-08-08 by dev_storyflow's sb-boss: they demoted a capability from `realized` to `in_progress` after a failing walk, and between the walk and the demotion the graph went on asserting something false with no way to say so — a window that, on a `--shared` graph, every attached session reads as current. Two shapes, both theirs: (a) a lightweight `contested` marker or status value; (b) let a FAILING `kind=validation` VERIFIES edge automatically flag the capability's status as unsafe to trust. THE SECOND FITS THIS DESIGN'S GRAIN BETTER ON ITS FACE AND THAT IS WORTH STATING, THOUGH NOT DECIDING: dec:passing-is-verified already computes "verified" from a check that PASSES rather than from a status field, so computing "contested" from a check that FAILS is the same move inverted, needs no new enum value, and cannot be forgotten the way a marker can. The argument against it is equally real — a failing check does not always mean the claim is wrong, and auto-flagging would make every red test a challenge to the design rather than to the code.
properties.name: OPEN — how does a capability say its own status is under challenge, in the window between evidence arriving and someone being ready to restate it?
properties.rationale: Recorded because demoting early is itself a claim — it asserts a position on work that may turn out fine — so the absence of a middle state pushes a reporter toward one of two wrong assertions. Adjacent and worth reading together: req:blocking-is-partial applies the same instinct to drift rather than to a failing check. Evidence: fact:defect-no-way-to-mark-a-capability-contested.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From StoryFlow's principle #5, "Real-path tests — unit-green is not live-green": a test that feeds synthetic objects to a pure function proves the function is pure, and says nothing about whether anything calls it or whether the wire shape matches. Their worked case was a prose-rendering suite that was GREEN while the surface rendered no prose at all.

THEIR PROPOSED CHECK IS ALREADY COMPUTABLE HERE, WITH NO NEW VOCABULARY: "assert that each capability has at least one verification at `integration` or `system` level rather than `unit`."

MEASURED, 2026-08-22. Verification.level across 191 checks: integration 105, unit 72, system 11, acceptance 3. 154 capabilities carry a check; 47 of them are verified ONLY at unit level. The field has existed the whole time and NOTHING READS IT — no detector, no report, no rollup. That is the three-legs pattern with the tool and the data present and the detector missing, which is the same diagnosis as `change_axis_unstated` and cheaper to close, because no schema change is needed.

A SIBLING ALREADY EXISTS AND IS INSTRUCTIVE: `component_granularity_verification` fires when a capability is covered only by a check aimed at its COMPONENT rather than at itself — 9 capabilities here. That is the same argument on a different axis (WHAT is checked rather than HOW DEEP), and its existence is evidence the shape is acceptable in this design.

⭐ THE HONEST CAVEAT, and the document states it first: level is a PROXY. It does not measure path realism, it measures a label the author chose. A unit test can cross a real boundary and an "integration" test can mock everything. The document's own words — "cheap, and it makes the gap visible without pretending to measure path realism" — are the right register, and any finding must be worded that way or it will overclaim. This is also uncomfortably close to StoryFlow's own rule A(f): substituting a proxy that is easy to compute for the question actually asked.

AGAINST BUILDING IT: 47 of 154 is a third of the design, and a finding that fires on a third of everything on day one is a finding people filter. If built, aggregate — one question about the practice, not 47 about capabilities.
properties.name: OPEN — should a capability whose every check is `unit` level be a finding? 47 of 154 here, and the field is already recorded and never read
properties.no_relation_note: Searched 2026-08-22 on verification level and check granularity. Nearest were dec:component-verified-computed (ACCEPTED — component-granularity verification as a computed third state) and dec:idea-verification-is-planned-with-the-requirement (OPEN — planning a check when the need is stated). Both READ and judged NOT related in the relation vocabulary's sense: they are siblings arguing adjacent things about checks, not causes, dependencies or contradictions of this one. Component-granularity asks WHAT is checked; this asks HOW DEEP. Neither has to land first, neither blocks the other, and both could hold at once. Recorded as a note rather than a DEPENDS_ON, which would be false and would make a later reader think this waits on something. NOTE WRITTEN BY HAND because review_relations was not on this session's served tool surface.
properties.rationale: Recorded because it is the cheapest of the three mechanisms — the data is present, the field is populated, and only a reader is missing — and because its caveat is unusually clean: the proxy is admitted by the source that proposes it. Left open rather than proposed because a third of the design lighting up at once is a real adoption risk, and because whether a label-based proxy is worth having at all is a judgement about how much reflow2 should infer.

properties.decision: UNSETTLED. dev_storyflow's most-wanted ask, 2026-08-08: express "this capability needs a surface where a person (or an upstream system) actually writes the data it consumes", so a capability that is realized, built and rendering — but dead because nothing ever writes its input — is caught by a detector rather than by three people producing three wrong root causes. Shapes worth weighing rather than a recommendation: (a) a new edge — cap FED_BY ifc/Actor — with an unrealized_input_path gap when a capability that consumes a field has no writer; (b) a property on the Capability (`needs_input_path: true`) with the detector reading it, which is cheaper and weaker because nothing forces the flag; (c) generalise the existing INTERACTS_WITH by adding a `required` property, so "an actor interacts with this" can become "this does not function unless an actor does"; (d) decline it as out of scope, on the ground that reflow2 models the design and not the operational data path. NOTE WHAT ALREADY EXISTS AND WHY IT IS NOT ENOUGH: req:the-store-is-reachable-from-a-session says "a capability nothing can call is not delivered — the content store needs a surface", which is exactly this insight scoped to ONE capability and written by hand; nothing generalises it and nothing detects it.
properties.name: OPEN — should a capability be able to declare that it needs a human INPUT path, so that the absence of one is DETECTABLE rather than diagnosable only by three people failing?
properties.rationale: Recorded because it is the one thing the fleet said would have saved the most time, and because it is a VOCABULARY question rather than a detector bug — detect_gaps structurally cannot ask about a surface the design has no way to say is required, which is req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots in its sharpest instance to date. Left `proposed` deliberately: every shape above changes the schema or the detector set, and which one is right is Anthony's call, not a field report's. The evidence is fact:defect-a-realized-capability-can-be-dead-for-want-of-an-input-path.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-23, and he flagged it for checking himself: "may have to verify this statement against true systems engineering doctrine."

HIS WORDS: "I believe a capability is a set of functions working together to deliver that capability. Black boxes deliver functionality, not necessarily a capability... then capabilities can be expressed at subsystem_B.component_1 (delivers function_K) <--> subsystem_A.component_2 (delivers function_L) <--> subsystem_C.component_5 (delivers function_J)... function_K + function_L + function_J = capability_R."

✅ THE DOCTRINE CHECK HE ASKED FOR, and it supports him. UAF places Capability in the STRATEGIC domain — an ability to achieve a desired effect under specified standards and conditions — and it is realized by a CONFIGURATION of resources performing functions, never owned by one resource. DoDAF says the same through its matrices: CV-6 maps Capability to Operational Activities, and SV-5a is literally the Operational-Activity-to-Systems-Function traceability matrix — an N-to-N mapping, which only exists because one capability spans many functions across many systems. So 'a black box performs functions; a capability emerges from functions across boxes' is the doctrinal position, not a deviation from it.

🛑 AND IT CONTRADICTS WHAT REFLOW2 DOES TODAY, which is why this matters more than the other two. Measured 2026-08-23: there is NO `Function` node type in the schema (29 types, none of them Function). Capability is joined to Component by ALLOCATED_TO, and `fact:reflow2s-black-boxes-hold-no-functions-allocation-went-straight-to-the-modules` measured 177 of 178 ALLOCATED_TO edges pointing at a MODULE, one at a subsystem, and DECOMPOSES at ZERO. reflow2 currently models a capability as belonging to ONE part. Under his reading that is the wrong shape: it collapses the function layer out and makes a capability something a box owns rather than something a configuration achieves.

THE OPTIONS:
(a) ADD A `Function` NODE TYPE. Component PERFORMS Function; Capability is COMPOSED OF Functions. Doctrinally clean and it makes his three-part example expressible. COUNTER: a schema change is the most expensive kind here — it needs an upgrade doc and a foundation migration — and 182 existing allocations would have to mean something afterwards.
(b) LET A CAPABILITY BE ALLOCATED TO SEVERAL COMPONENTS and read the set as the configuration. Cheap; no schema change; the edge already permits it. COUNTER: it loses WHICH function each part contributes, which is the whole content of his example — K, L and J are not interchangeable.
(c) TREAT `Flow` AS THE FUNCTION LAYER. It already models an ordered process with steps and roled transitions. COUNTER: a Flow is a SEQUENCE and a capability is not necessarily sequential; forcing one into the other would misrepresent both.
(d) DO NOTHING — one-part allocation is a simplification reflow2 chose, and it is adequate for the projects it serves.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any USER of reflow2 has hit this. Every measurement behind it is from reflow2's own design, and `reflow2 is a wrench` says the test is whether a user's project needs it — nobody has asked that question yet.
properties.name: OPEN — is a capability a SET OF FUNCTIONS across several parts, with a black box delivering functions rather than capabilities? It would need a Function type reflow2 does not have
properties.rationale: Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`. Kept separate from the nesting and contract-level questions because it is the only one of the three that would change the SCHEMA, and it can be answered no whatever the other two decide.

properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-12 by Anthony. OPTION A, knowingly and as a first step. Originally recorded as brainstorming under the question "should closing a session be a SKILL the user types, when the accepted requirement says the user must never be the trigger?" — that question is now answered.

⭐⭐ HIS DECIDING ARGUMENT, AND IT INVERTS THE TENSION THIS NODE WAS BUILT AROUND. His words: "I don't mind the capture-session skill being manual and I can use it as I see fit throughout a session. I would prefer it be automatically done by the agent, but as seen elsewhere, then it is dependent upon the agent remembering or placing hooks to do so... so just being able to run this manually myself as a first step is fine with me."

The node above recorded option A as CONCEDING the central clause of `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` ("the user must never be the trigger"). Anthony's reasoning reframes that: options B and C depend on THE AGENT REMEMBERING — and agent forgetting is the documented, four-times-observed failure this whole thread exists because of (`epoch:skill-use-still-needs-reminding`, `chg:user-is-still-the-reminder`, `fact:second-user-report-2026-08-11`, and his own habit). ⇒ THE MANUAL TRIGGER IS NOT THE WEAK OPTION. It is the only one whose reliability does not rest on the thing that keeps failing. A human who types a skill remembers; the mechanism proposed to replace him is the one with the measured defect rate.

📌 THE CLAUSE IS STILL CONCEDED, AND THAT IS RECORDED HONESTLY. `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` remains ACCEPTED and still says the user must never be the trigger. This decision does not amend it, does not weaken it, and does not close it. It ships a manual trigger AS A FIRST STEP while the requirement stands unmet — which is the accurate state, and better stated than papered over.

═══ WHAT THIS DECIDES ═══

A `capture-session` skill the user types, served like every other skill, invocable AT ANY POINT IN A SESSION and not only at the end — his words, "I can use it as I see fit throughout a session". That clause was NOT in the original option A and it matters: it directly answers counter-argument ⚠️2 ("session end is the worst moment to ask, and this session is the evidence"), because a skill usable mid-session is capture-as-you-go with a defined contract rather than a closing sweep over a compacted transcript.

═══ WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE ═══
  • OPTION C REMAINS THE DESTINATION. "First step" is his phrasing. The skill defining WHAT capture means is precisely the half C needs; a later hook deciding WHEN sits on top of it without rework. Choosing A does not foreclose C — it builds C's first half.
  • ⚠️1 WHO JUDGES "ANYTHING IMPORTANT" is untouched and is the skill's hardest content problem. The skill must STATE ITS CRITERIA rather than ask an agent to introspect on the significance of its own session.
  • ⚠️3 THE CONNECTIVE TISSUE HAS NO NATURAL NODE — still true, still unresolved, and now load-bearing in a way it was not before: a skill that captures must write SOMETHING somewhere. `cap:session-memory` stays PLANNED.

═══ THE ROADS NOT TAKEN (kept, per brainstorm doctrine) ═══
B — automatic at the Stop hook. Not rejected; deferred. Its mechanism exists and works (it blocked this very session), but it fires per-TURN and cannot tell design-relevant work from any other edit.
C — both, split by role. THE DESTINATION, not a rejection.
D — build `cap:session-memory` instead. Not taken as a substitute, but the skill must answer D's question — what gets written — before it is worth much.
properties.name: SETTLED — a capture-session skill the user types, chosen as the FIRST STEP because it is the only trigger that does not depend on the mechanism that keeps failing
properties.rationale: Captured because the trigger question is genuinely open while the content question is not: dec:idea-is-session-context-already-in-the-graph settled that the connective tissue is what only the session holds, and cap:session-memory has been planned since 2026-07-25 with no trigger. What makes this worth its own node is the tension rather than the idea — req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session is accepted and says the user must never be the trigger, and a skill the user types institutionalises exactly that. Recorded with the counter-arguments beside it, including that this session was compacted, which makes session-end the worst moment to ask for a faithful account of session start.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-09, describing what has already happened rather than a hypothetical.

THE SHAPE, in his numbering: projectA = **dynograph-foundation**, projectB = **reflow2**, projectC = **flo2**, projectD = **storyflow**. C depends on B; B depends on A; **D ALSO depends on A, and not on B.** A diamond, with A at the point. (projectE = embeddings-rs, and whether it is even a reflow2 project is undecided — recorded as unknown rather than assumed either way.)

⚠️ THE INCIDENT, WHICH IS THE EVIDENCE AND IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. Anthony: \"projectB caused changes in projectA, which I implemented real time. **The risk was that the changes that projectB required on projectA might have caused issues with projectA now being able to support projectD** (I thought about it, but really didn't test that anything didn't break in projectD by using an updated projectA).\"

⇒ A change was levied UP one arm of the diamond and shipped, and **nothing checked the other arm.** The owner noticed the risk by thinking, and the check was never run. That is the failure mode, already realised, on the real projects.

=== WHY THIS IS NOT `dec:who-needs-to-know`, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS STRUCTURAL ===

That node asks whether notification is SUBSCRIBED or DERIVED from the blast radius, and prefers derived because `propagate_from` already computes who a change impacts. Its recorded counter-argument is: *\"a blast radius is only as good as the edges that exist, so an unrecorded dependency means a silent non-notification.\"*

**IN THE CROSS-GRAPH CASE THAT COUNTER STOPS BEING A RISK AND BECOMES A CERTAINTY.** The edge D→A lives in **D's graph**. A's graph does not hold it and cannot. So A's blast radius is not *possibly* incomplete — it is **NECESSARILY TRUNCATED AT THE GRAPH BOUNDARY**, every time, by construction. Derived notification cannot work from the upstream side, and no amount of edge hygiene in A fixes it.

⭐ AND IT IS THE SAME STRUCTURAL FACT `dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency` already turned on, pointing the other way. There, Anthony's Google-service argument defeated \"the upstream pulls\": a widely-depended-on design **cannot enumerate its dependents**. That killed pull for RECEIVING requirements. Here the identical fact kills push for SENDING warnings — A cannot warn D because A does not know D exists. **One fact, two directions, two different unbuildable mechanisms.** Which is a strong hint that the answer has to live on the CONSUMER side in both cases.

=== OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ===

**(A) THE CONSUMER MIRRORS AND NOTICES.** Each dependent mirrors the upstream's published surface and detects when the mirror drifts from the real one. **The machinery is already built and shipped** — `export_surface` (upstream publishes), `mirror_surface` / `mirrors` (consumer mirrors), `pair_designs`, `seam_report`. FOR: it scales exactly where push fails, because it needs no registry and no knowledge of who depends on you; each consumer looks after itself. It also inverts the burden onto the party who actually cares. COUNTER: it is a PULL, so it only fires when the consumer runs it — D learns it is broken when D next looks, not when A changes. For a project nobody has opened in three months, that is late.

**(B) A COMPOSITION RUN ACROSS ALL THE GRAPHS AT ONCE.** `compose_and_analyse` and `pair_designs` exist; `dec:linked-repos-poc` RAN this on reflow2 + flo2 + dynograph-foundation on 2026-08-06 and found \"the linking works, the labelling does not exist.\" **THAT BLOCKER HAS SINCE CLEARED** — reflow2 now declares 9 `required` interfaces, five of them pointed at dynograph (`ifc:req-dyno-*`). FOR: it computes the diamond directly — two consumers requiring the same interface means a change to it touches both — and Anthony HOLDS ALL FOUR GRAPHS, so it is runnable today. COUNTER: it needs somebody with every graph in hand, which is exactly the arrangement the Google-service argument says does not generalise. **Fine for the trial, not the answer.**

**(C) THE UPSTREAM KEEPS A REGISTRY OF ITS CONSUMERS.** FOR: A could then warn D. COUNTER: refuted twice already — registration is a write, so pull cannot bootstrap, and a heavily-depended-on design will not maintain it. Retained only for the small-federation case.

**(D) NOTHING MECHANICAL; THE OWNER REMEMBERS.** COUNTER: this is what happened, and the record above is what it cost — the risk was identified and the test still was not run. Not because anyone was careless, but because nothing made the omission visible afterwards.

=== THE FIRST TESTABLE STEP, WHICH COSTS ALMOST NOTHING ===

**Does storyflow (D) DECLARE its dependency on dynograph-foundation (A) as a `required` interface, the way reflow2 (B) now does?** reflow2's five `ifc:req-dyno-*` interfaces exist; whether D has any equivalent is UNKNOWN AND CHECKABLE. If it does not, no mechanism in any option above can work for D, and declaring it is the prerequisite for all of them. If it does, the diamond is already computable with tools that shipped.

📌 AND THE METHOD IS ANTHONY'S OWN, STATED THE SAME DAY: *\"the best development of reflow2 has been propose something — trial it with a real project — then learn from it — iterate upon the solution and try again.\"* These four projects are that trial, and the diamond is the first thing to run it on.

NOTHING IS PROMOTED.
properties.name: OPEN — when a change to a shared upstream is driven by one dependent, how does the OTHER dependent find out? (the diamond: B and D both depend on A, and A's blast radius stops at its own graph)
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill, and kept SEPARATE from two neighbours it would otherwise be merged into — a node holding two questions can only ever be half-answered. `dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency` is the UP direction (how a dependent levies a need on its upstream); this is the DOWN-AND-SIDEWAYS direction (how a change to a shared upstream reaches a sibling that never asked). `dec:who-needs-to-know` is the SAME-GRAPH version and prefers derived notification; the point of this node is that derivation is structurally impossible across a graph boundary, which that node's own counter-argument anticipates without naming the cross-graph case.

Recorded because the failure has already occurred on the real projects and was survived by luck rather than by a check — and because the prerequisite that blocked every mechanism (no labelled seam) cleared three days after it was written down.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From StoryFlow's unnumbered rule A, clause (d): "A test never observed red proves nothing. Red-then-green, or mutate the fix and confirm the suite notices. A green suite says the tests pass — not that they would catch a regression."

⭐ THE EVIDENCE THAT THIS IS REAL IS ALREADY IN THIS GRAPH, AND IT IS THE SAME SHAPE THAT JUSTIFIED `subject` EARLIER TODAY. 51 of 191 Verifications contain the word MUTATION in their prose — "MUTATION-CHECKED FIVE WAYS, each failing exactly the tests that name it", "MUTATION-CHECKED against five seeded regressions", "WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIX: the four bug cases failed and all five counterweights passed". The discipline is being practised, carefully, by whoever writes these. IT IS BEING WRITTEN INTO FREE TEXT BECAUSE THERE IS NOWHERE ELSE TO PUT IT. Nothing can count it, query it, or notice its absence — which is the exact argument that carried `ChangeSubject`, one field over.

WHAT IT WOULD BE: a Verification records whether it has ever been observed FAILING — not as a status (status is now), but as a fact about its history. `set_verification_status(failing)` already exists, so the honest cheap version is derived rather than declared: has this check ever been written `failing`? On this design that answer is currently NO for essentially all 191, because a check is created and then set passing.

THREE FORMS, increasingly strong:
(a) DERIVED — compute "ever observed failing" from the status history. Free, no new vocabulary, and worth nothing here because the history does not exist: statuses are overwritten, not journalled.
(b) A FIELD the author sets — "this check was observed red, on this date, by this means (red-then-green / mutation / seeded regression)". Cheap, honest, and it makes the 51 prose paragraphs into something countable.
(c) A REFUSAL — the document proposes reflow2 "refuse to accept a `passing` verification that has never recorded a `failing` run".

🛑 (c) DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS AN ACCEPTED NON-GOAL and must not be built without overturning it. dec:non-goal-reflow2-does-not-judge-whether-a-check-is-meaningful says a passing Verification is a claim reflow2 RECORDS and never one it VALIDATES. Refusing a passing status is reflow2 judging the check. (b) does not cross that line — it records what the author says, exactly like `provenance` and the drift dispositions, and leaves the judging to a human.

HONEST LIMIT, the same one req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause states about itself: this records what the AUTHOR SAYS about their check. It cannot detect a check that was never really red but is claimed to have been. Worth having because the alternative is no signal at all; worth never overselling.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS PROJECT: 42 of this design's checks have never run at all, and nothing distinguishes them from the 188 marked passing in any rollup a user reads. "Passing" and "never able to fail" and "never executed" are three different states wearing one word.
properties.name: OPEN — should a Verification record that it was once observed FAILING, so a check that could never have failed is distinguishable from one that passes? 51 of 191 already say so in prose
properties.rationale: Recorded because the prose count is unusually strong evidence — 51 independent authors' paragraphs working around a missing field is the same measurement that justified the change-event axis, and it was found by reading the graph rather than by reasoning about it. Left open because form (c) contradicts an accepted non-goal, which is Anthony's to overturn or uphold, and because (b) adds vocabulary that will stay empty without the third leg.

properties.decision:
ACCEPTED 2026-08-23 on Anthony's word. Captured the day before as brainstorming and promoted unchanged when he was asked to settle the seam question — the wording below is his, from the capture, and is preserved rather than rewritten.

THIS IS HIS ANSWER TO THE QUESTION `fact:coupling-and-contract-are-recorded-in-vocabularies-that-never-meet` DELIBERATELY LEFT TO THE OWNER: which level should carry contracts.

HIS WORDS: "say we have a subsystem_A <--> subsystem_B interface - my thoughts this should be defined at the lowest level that actually defines the interface and the rest is rolled up so that if somebody asked at a high level, 'is there an interface between subsystem_A and subsystem_B?' the 'view' capturing at subsystem to subsystem level would say 'yes', but the graph would actually show it is actually subsystem_A.component_2 <--> subsystem_B.component_5 that the interface contract is actually defined."

THE DESIGN ALREADY DOES THE FIRST HALF, AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT CALLED IT A DEFECT WAS READING IT AS ONE. `fact:the-eight-subsystems-are-groupings-not-black-boxes` (2026-08-17) recorded '0 of 8 subsystems provide an interface - EVERY interface in the design is provided by a LEAF component one level down' and read that as the tier having no contracts. UNDER THIS RULE THAT IS NOT A DEFECT, IT IS THE RULE BEING FOLLOWED. A contract belongs where it is defined; a subsystem carrying its own copy would be duplicating its child's. (Re-measured 2026-08-23: it is now 4 of 10 subsystems providing, so the tier is no longer silent either way.)

=> SO WHAT IS MISSING IS NOT CONTRACTS, IT IS THE ROLL-UP. That is already an open question of its own: `dec:idea-a-view-can-slice-by-altitude-not-only-by-aspect` records that reflow2's ten views all slice by ASPECT and none by ALTITUDE, so 'show me the top level' has no projection behind it. This rule and that one are the same need approached from opposite ends — and that one is STILL OPEN, so accepting this does not mean the roll-up view exists.

WHAT IT SETTLED, and this is the sharp part: `undeclared_seam` reports 64 of 72 module pairs uncontracted, and `fact:coupling-and-contract-are-recorded-in-vocabularies-that-never-meet` measured that the number CANNOT MOVE - couplings come from DEPENDS_ON and contracts from PROVIDES/CONSUMES and the two sets are disjoint by construction. Verified independently 2026-08-23: all 64 pairs are inside ONE crate, zero cross a crate boundary, and 44 of the 55 files in reflow2-core carry `impl DesignGraph`, so most of those 'couplings' are impl blocks of the same struct. Under this rule the question becomes not 'does this pair share a contract' but 'is this coupling covered by a contract declared at or below it' — and `seam_coverage {altitude}` answers it: 72/8/64 at module, 11/11/0 at subsystem. The gap itself was acknowledged once on this design (`decision:ack:f384097e7d8b01b0`), NOT silenced by changing a detector default.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea before it was settled and still live:
* A roll-up VIEW must be a pure projection - this project's standing rule is that a view is a projection and renderer fill-ins are defects. Answering 'yes, A and B interface' when the edge exists only between two leaves is a DERIVATION, and it must be derived on read, never written back as an edge between the subsystems, or the graph starts asserting contracts nobody declared. `seam_coverage` honours this: it writes nothing back.
* It does not say what to do about coupling covered by NO contract at any level. That is still the real finding, and a carelessly written roll-up could hide it. THIS IS WHY the detector was left answering at module level when the alternative was offered.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether DEPENDS_ON between two impl blocks of one struct is a dependency worth recording at all - the other half of what that fact left open, offered to him as the root fix on 2026-08-23 and not taken in that pass.
properties.name: A contract is declared at the LOWEST level that actually defines it, and higher levels answer by ROLL-UP
properties.rationale: Captured at `proposed` via the brainstorm skill, 2026-08-23, as the owner's answer to a question `fact:coupling-and-contract-are-recorded-in-vocabularies-that-never-meet` explicitly left to him. ACCEPTED the same day, on Anthony's word, when he was asked to settle the 64-uncontracted-pairs seam question and chose to promote this position rather than restate it. He was offered, and declined, defaulting the undeclared-seam detector to subsystem altitude — so this rule governs how contracts are DECLARED, and changes nothing about what the detector REPORTS.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's idea, 2026-08-10, in his words: *"is there a way to assess unmade decisions as 'risk' in getting towards the projects goal? like you need to make this chain of decisions before your project can be implemented... almost like the critical path on decision making. for each project (to include reflow2), when I first do where-am-i, I get the critical path of decisions I need to make."* And the pain behind it, also his: *"I generate many many ideas and really use the brainstorm skill a lot... but I often come up with another idea before making a decision on the previous brainstorming idea. sometimes this is on purpose as I just have a thought and want it captured and I'll decide later."*

THE ANSWER MUST BE BOUNDED TO HUMAN THROUGHPUT, added by Anthony in the same conversation and it constrains every option below: *"many projects have hundreds of decisions and a person can only make a small subset of decisions a day. especially with somebody like me, I think about 25 ideas a minute (exaggerating)... having something that says, these are your top 5 priorities would be great."* SO THE OUTPUT IS A SHORT RANKED LIST, NOT A FULL ORDERING. This matters more than it sounds: a ranked list of 83 is the same as no ranking, and it is the shape the pile already has. A top-5 also changes what the ranking must be GOOD at — it need only get the head right, not the tail, which makes several of the weaker signals below usable that would be useless for a total order. It also means the cut line is a claim: whatever is at rank 6 is being said not to matter today, and that claim should be visible rather than silent.

HALF OF THIS IS ALREADY ACCEPTED INTENT AND MUST NOT BE RE-DECIDED. `req:what-next` (status ACCEPTED, his own earlier words) already says: *"The answer must rank an unmade decision ABOVE the work that waits on it, because being told to build something blocked on a choice only the human can make is worse than being told nothing."* `cap:what-next` is PLANNED, and its recorded blocker HAS EXPIRED — `cap:derived-completion` reached `verified` and the park was never revisited, which the capability itself notes with "NOBODY NOTICED". It also already wants the which-decisions-shape-everything section, with the measured caveat that raw in-degree is the wrong signal because the top hit was a pruning decision governing ten DROPPED requirements. SO THE RANKING HALF IS DESIGNED, AGREED AND UNBLOCKED. What is genuinely new here is the CHAIN, the RISK framing, the BOUND, and putting it at the FRONT of where-am-i.

MEASURED BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS RECORDED, and it inverts the premise:

    open (proposed) decisions                                    83
    of those, governing ANYTHING at all                          22
    of those, governing NOTHING — no downstream, so NO PATH      61
    decision->decision precedence edges among open decisions     12   (mostly CONTRADICTS, not precedence)
    items scheduled into an epoch                                23
    of those, blocked by an open decision                         2

THE CRITICAL PATH IS NOT UNCOMPUTABLE FOR WANT OF AN ALGORITHM — budget.rs already runs Kahn toposort and longest-path, and `cap:bl-150` records that it is hand-rolled there and unavailable elsewhere. It is uncomputable because THREE QUARTERS OF THE PILE HAS NO SUCCESSOR. A path needs something downstream and 61 of these have nothing.

⇒ THE QUESTION THAT ACTUALLY MATTERS, and it is not the one asked: are those 61 ideas genuinely not blocking anything yet — in which case the honest answer is "your undecided pile carries almost no risk to the goal, and that is why you can safely keep deferring" — or are they blocking things the graph was never told about? THOSE TWO LOOK IDENTICAL FROM INSIDE THE GRAPH AND NEED DIFFERENT ANSWERS. Everything below is downstream of that.

THE OPTIONS.

(A) BUILD `cap:what-next` AS ALREADY DESIGNED AND STOP. It ranks the 22 that govern something, says plainly that 61 are unranked because they connect to nothing, and leaves it there. Cheapest by far; the intent is already accepted so nothing new needs deciding. WITH THE BOUND, this gets stronger: a top-5 drawn from 22 rankable items is a real answer, where a total ordering of 83 would not be. Counter: it answers "what should I decide next" only for a quarter of the pile, and the 61 are exactly the ones he feels buried by.

(B) ASK ONE QUESTION AT CAPTURE TIME — when a brainstorm is recorded, ask what it bears on, and draw that edge. Converts a musing into something rankable without deciding it. Counter, and it is the serious one: THE BRAINSTORM SKILL IS FRICTIONLESS BY DESIGN AND THAT IS WHY HE USES IT. It explicitly forbids manufacturing links, and adding a question at capture taxes the one habit that is working. It would also often be unanswerable — half-formed ideas frequently do not yet know what they bear on, which is what makes them ideas.

(C) DERIVE THE LINKAGE, ASK RATHER THAN ASSERT — use the search index to propose what an idea probably bears on, and surface it as a question at read time instead of an edge at write time. Keeps capture frictionless and fits `dec:ask-not-repair`'s standing shape (a suspicion is a DETECT gap, never a repair). Counter: similarity over prose is exactly the scoring that produced 81-85 scores on unrelated requirements (`fact:defect-merge-survivor-ignores-priority-and-status`), so the proposals would be noisy — and a noisy proposal at orientation time is the cry-wolf failure this project has now named three times.

(D) A REAL CRITICAL PATH, FOR THE 22 THAT HAVE ONE. Declare decision-to-decision precedence (DEPENDS_ON between Decisions already exists, 10 edges design-wide) and run the toposort and longest path budget.rs already implements. Counter: with 12 precedence-ish edges among open decisions, mostly CONTRADICTS, the longest chain today is likely 1-2 hops. A "critical path" of length two is a list with a promotion.

(E) RISK, SCORED RATHER THAN PATHED. Score each open decision by what it blocks — how much is GOVERNED_BY it, how deep the downstream goes, and whether any of it is SCHEDULED into an epoch. That is computable TODAY with no new edges and no new vocabulary, and a score is exactly what a top-5 needs. Counter, and it is the honest one: run it now and the answer is that risk is nearly zero, because only 2 of 23 scheduled items are blocked by an open decision. That may be true and reassuring, or it may mean the schedule is what is under-modelled rather than the decisions.

(F) THE PILE'S REAL PROBLEM MAY BE AGE, NOT BLOCKING. Rank by staleness — how long has this been open, has anything touched its region since — rather than by path. `cap:revise-trigger` already exists for surfacing a settled road worth re-opening, and `cap:what-next`'s own expired park is a worked example of a condition nobody watches. Counter: age is not importance, and a stale-first ranking would put genuinely deferred ideas above newly urgent ones.

(G) RANK BY ATTENTION RATHER THAN BY CONSEQUENCE — `dec:idea-what-gets-searched-repeatedly-is-becoming-important`, recorded separately the same day. A node the user keeps circling back to may be ripening whether or not it blocks anything. NOT A SUBSTITUTE: a decision can draw attention and block nothing, or block everything and never be searched. Whether the two compose into one ranking, or are two lists, is open in both nodes and settled in neither.

WHAT IS NOT AN OPTION: deciding things to shorten the list. Anthony said the deferral is often deliberate — *"sometimes this is on purpose"* — so a mechanism whose success is measured by the pile shrinking would be optimising against how he actually works. The bound makes this concrete: a top-5 that never changes because he keeps not deciding is working correctly, not failing.

ONE THING TO SETTLE BEFORE ANY OF THESE, because "risk to the goal" needs a goal: the Project's objective is one sentence, "keep a design coherent from concept through operations", and nothing decomposes it. Risk is currently measurable only against EPOCHS, which are the nearest thing to a target the graph holds. Whether the goal itself should be modelled is a separate question this node does not open.
properties.name: OPEN — can unmade decisions be ranked as risk to the goal, bounded to what a person can actually decide in a day, when 61 of 83 of them govern nothing and so have no path?
properties.rationale:
Anthony's idea, recorded as an open question because the measurement changed what the question is. He asked for a critical path; the graph says three quarters of the undecided pile has no successor to path through, so the prior question is whether that disconnection is true or merely unrecorded.

REVISED the same session it was created, to fold in the top-5 bound he added minutes later, rather than minting a second node. The bound is a constraint on the answer to THIS question, not a new question — and given that the complaint driving all of it is a pile of 83 open decisions, answering "how do I triage the pile" by adding another node to the pile would be a poor demonstration. Recorded without a snapshot because the node had not yet been exported or committed and both versions are this session's own capture; a fold after the record ships would need `revise-design` proper.

Kept as one node rather than several because all seven options answer the same question — how to triage undecided work — and splitting them would create a set that can only be half-answered. Options are not registered as alternatives, so `undecided_decision_point` stays quiet and the loop says nothing while this is still thinking.

No approver edge, deliberately, per the brainstorm discipline: this is thinking out loud, and attaching an approver would make `loop_status` start reporting it as owed. If it becomes a real fork — most likely between (A) and (E), which are both buildable now and compose naturally under a bound — `register_alternative` is what promotes it.

Recorded WITHOUT wiring it to `req:what-next` or `cap:what-next`. Those are cited in the text and the relationship is real, but drawing edges from a musing to accepted intent would assert that this idea shapes them, which nobody has decided. That restraint is also the subject of option (B), which makes it worth stating rather than doing silently.

properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Anthony, 2026-08-26, in his own words:

*"can we construct skills or tools in a factory that ensures they get the required mechanics/functions? then when we need to make a 'class' change, it is fixing the factory, not the individual skill."*

📌 DISTINCT FROM `dec:idea-a-tool-class-should-carry-a-contract-that-something-checks`, which asks WHAT a class must guarantee. This asks HOW the guarantee is delivered — by construction, or by inspection after the fact. Both answers are available for any contract, and the choice between them is the whole content here.

═══ THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS ═══

**A CHECK finds the omission after somebody made it. A FACTORY makes the omission unconstructable.** Today's fix is the first: `every_category_states_whether_it_reads_proposed` catches an unclassified category at compile time, but only after somebody wrote it. A factory would mean a finding kind cannot come into existence without answering.

This is the shape Anthony is reaching for, and the payoff he names is real: **a class change becomes one edit instead of N.** Today's change edited three call sites for one rule. The three instances this week each edited between one and three sites. Nothing has yet needed editing across all 173 tools — which is either evidence the problem is small, or evidence it has not bitten yet.

═══ WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, because the answer is not "nothing" ═══

- **`#[tool]` is already a proc macro** — construction already runs through a single point. Whether it can be made to REQUIRE annotations is a technical question nobody has asked. This is the most promising unexamined lead here.
- **`skill_lint.py`, 1126 lines** — the inspection route, already built and already large.
- **`HealCategory::ALL` plus two exhaustive-match tests** — the compile-time route at its smallest, and it works.
- **The 12 tool-surface slices** — a classification that already exists and deliberately holds no function.

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) EXTEND THE `#[tool]` MACRO to require the annotation set.** The factory Anthony describes, in the place construction already happens. Missing annotation = compile error, no list to maintain. ⚠️ Counter: proc-macro work is unpleasant to debug, and a required field with a default is not required at all — the design would have to refuse silence, which means touching all 173 declarations once.

**(b) A CONSTRUCTOR FUNCTION / TRAIT rather than a macro change.** Each tool built through a typed builder that cannot be finished incomplete. ⚠️ Counter: heavier than the macro that is already there, and the macro is the thing standing between the author and the surface.

**(c) KEEP INSPECTION, MAKE IT EXHAUSTIVE.** No factory; just ensure every class has one test asserting every member answers. ⚠️ Counter: this is what the repo already does, and it is what let three instances through — each guard was written after its own incident, never before the next.

**(d) NOT WORTH IT YET.** No class change has ever required editing more than three sites. ⚠️ Counter: the cost being counted is wrong — the expensive part was never the editing, it was the DISCOVERY, and each discovery came from a user hitting it in the field.

═══ ⚠️ THE COUNTERWEIGHTS, and there are two real ones ═══

**1. A factory guarantees the mechanics are PRESENT, never that they are RIGHT.** Every instance this week was a case where the mechanism existed and the JUDGEMENT was missing — `unallocated_component` could have read the ruling, the replay contract was written down, `proposed` was documented in four places. A factory that injects a required field produces 173 tools with a field filled in to satisfy the compiler. That is the `internal`-by-default trap the interface `designation` field already documents: *"BECAUSE it is the default, `internal` cannot distinguish 'deliberately internal' from 'nobody classified this'."* **A factory can manufacture exactly that ambiguity at scale.**

**2. Over-engineering, and it is his own standing concern.** *"designs get so overcomplicated when often a simple solution will do."* A factory, a registry and a class taxonomy is the shape an engineer reaches for. The measured alternative is one exhaustive match per class — roughly fifteen lines, no new machinery, and it has now worked twice in the same file.

⇒ Which suggests the cheapest honest test: **name a change that WOULD have required editing all 173 tools.** If one exists, the factory earns itself. If none does, option (d) is the answer and the exhaustive-match habit is enough.
properties.name: DECIDED — skills are COMPOSED of attribute classes, not stamped by one factory and not swept by one exhaustive check
properties.rationale:
SETTLED BY ANTHONY, 2026-08-28, on option (f) — an option the original (a)–(d) did not contain, because they all assumed ONE factory stamping every member of a class identically.

HIS FRAMING: *"I didn't mean we have only one factory... like in python, a class can inherit a class which can inherit a class (I actually prefer class composition versus class inheritance). so a particular class of skills inherits a set of classes that determine what that skill should have."* And: *"I prefer building skills with composable blocks (and potentially using dependency injection if that can be done in rust). I also feel like it fits the MOSA type concept better than exhaustive checks."*

═══ WHAT SETTLED THE TWO COUNTERWEIGHTS ═══

**COUNTERWEIGHT 1 IS DISSOLVED, NOT OVERRULED.** *"A factory guarantees the mechanics are PRESENT, never that they are RIGHT."* True of a single factory, which must demand a section from all 23 and would get filler from the 15 that do not need it. COMPOSITION DEMANDS IT ONLY OF THE CLASS THAT OWES IT — "honest limits" from the skills that MEASURE, where its absence is a real omission. **The manufactured-ambiguity trap comes from UNIFORMITY, not from construction.**

**COUNTERWEIGHT 2 — OVER-ENGINEERING — WAS ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT, AND THE MEASURED ALTERNATIVE FAILED.** This node's own recommendation was that one exhaustive match per class is enough. CHECKED AGAINST SOURCE 2026-08-28: the exhaustive check was BUILT and IS RUNNING over every skill — `served_skills.rs` iterates `SKILLS` three times, `skill_lint` walks every directory. And every one of its assertions is a UNIVERSAL predicate. A flat loop over a flat set cannot express "this skill owes REPORTS mechanics and that one does not". It did not fail; it succeeded at its scope, which is why the one universal mechanic is at 23/23 and every other is at 5–18. **"Just add an exhaustive check" was tried and is structurally unable to reach the case.** See `fact:the-exhaustive-check-was-built-and-can-only-carry-universal-obligations`.

═══ THE NODE'S OWN TEST, ANSWERED ═══

It posed: *"name a change that WOULD have required editing all 173 tools."* Unanswered for tools; answered for skills. "Speak the reader's domain" is §35 of the SERVED INSTRUCTIONS, stated as applying to every skill — carried in ONE of 23 skill bodies, enforced by ONE of three hand-written contracts, added only after two users independently invented the same workaround. A universal rule, implemented once, discovered late.

═══ ⭐ AND A SECOND REASON, WHICH IS ANTHONY'S AND IS NOT SUPERFICIAL ═══

*"having reflow2 reflect all the principles it says it will do for other projects is not necessarily a functional win, but it is a 'marketing' win in terms that reflow2 'looks the part'... little details like these make a difference."*

It is stronger than he states it. `dec:mosa-conformance` asks whether reflow2 should REPORT MOSA CONFORMANCE for other people's designs, given it already computes most of the criteria. **Its own skill surface would fail the severability criterion** — three contracts that cannot be composed, applied selectively, or replaced independently. That is not presentation; it is the tool exhibiting the property it flags. And it sits with the dogfooding rationale already on `chg:user-is-still-the-reminder`: using the thing is the instrument that finds its defects.

⚠️ THIS IS NOT A BREACH OF `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself`. That rule forbids building FEATURES for reflow2's own sake. This applies reflow2's OWN STATED PRINCIPLES to its own construction, which is the rule's premise rather than an exception to it.

═══ 🛑 WHAT IS STILL UNCHOSEN, AND IT IS NOT SMALL ═══

**WHERE THE COMPOSITION LIVES.** Three candidates with materially different costs, none priced: (i) `skill_lint.py` — cheapest, Python, refactors the three existing contracts into composable sets, blocks in CI; (ii) a `composes:` list in each SKILL.md's frontmatter that the lint reads — makes the obligation legible to the AGENT reading the skill, not only to CI; (iii) the Rust build, strongest and most expensive. **Rust has no inheritance at all, so composition via traits is the only idiom available there — and the codebase already does constructor injection at `KvBackend` (a six-method trait, two implementations, `Box<dyn KvBackend>` in `StorageEngine`).**

**AND THE CLASS CARVING IS UNTESTED.** STANDING / WRITES / REVISES / REPORTS / MEASURES / DESTROYS is one agent's reading of 23 skills. A skill landing in four of them is a sign the carving is wrong, and nobody has tried it against the real set.

properties.decision: UNSETTLED, and it must be settled as ONE question rather than two. Two dev_storyflow reports a day apart ask for different fields on the same node for the same underlying reason — a Verification's qualifications have nowhere to live except its name. (A) 2026-08-07: structured RESULT fields — `exit_code`, `command`, `observed`/`expected` — so the graph can flag `status: passing` beside a non-zero exit as incoherent, and a re-run can be compared mechanically. (B) 2026-08-08: a `bounds`/`caveats` field and ideally a `grade`, plus a `findings`/`report` field, so `name` can go back to being a name and the qualifications become data the loop can reason about. Also on the table, and cheaper than either: truncate `name` in loop_status's rollup, or return `name` + `detail` separately, which fixes the READ cost without touching the schema. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT DESERVES AIRING: reflow2 already has cap:evidence-scope (what a check pinned and swept, on the VERIFIES edge per dec:evidence-scope-on-the-verifies-edge) and reconcile_verification for feeding real outcomes back, so the machinery for "evidence is structured, not prose" is PARTLY BUILT — and the honest question may be whether these are extensions of it or a second, competing home for the same information.
properties.name: OPEN — does a Verification gain structured fields for its BOUNDS and its FINDINGS, and is that the same decision as giving it structured RESULT fields?
properties.rationale: Recorded as one decision because settling either half alone would put two structured homes for a check's qualifications into the same node type, which is how a schema acquires an overlap nobody can later explain. The urgency is not theoretical: the missing field has already become fleet DOCTRINE at dev_storyflow ("carry the grading and all bounds in the node NAME"), it has made graph_report.top_gaps titles ~2,000-character essays, and reflow2's OWN loop_status digest reads the same way for the same reason. Evidence: fact:defect-a-finding-has-no-bounds-so-grading-goes-in-the-name and fact:defect-verification-evidence-is-prose-so-passing-can-contradict-itself.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-20.

HIS WORDS: "add gaps that need to be closed to increments/epochs."

WHY IT LANDS EXACTLY WHERE IT SHOULD: this design carries 89 open gaps, 85 of which have never been put to anybody. Two of them were surfaced and answered today only because he said, in as many words, that he does not like something identified and then dropped. A list of 89 that endures and is skimmed is durable and useless at the same time. Scheduling is the mechanism that turns a standing list into work with a moment attached.

⚠️ THE MODELLING PROBLEM, stated first because it shapes every option: A GAP IS NOT A NODE. Gaps are COMPUTED from the condition every run — that is why gap:4e24a202aa6f1737 carried the same id this morning and this afternoon, and why it disappears the moment the condition is fixed rather than needing to be closed by hand. That property is valuable and should not be traded away. But it means there is nothing to hang a SCHEDULED_FOR edge on, and SCHEDULED_FOR is declared `from: [Capability, Requirement]` only.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
  (a) SCHEDULE THE QUESTION, not the gap. `gap_to_prompt` already mints a durable `question:<id>` node when a gap is put to somebody, and open_questions already tracks it until answered. Widening SCHEDULED_FOR to accept a Question would let 'these twelve questions get answered in increment 4' be said, with no change to how gaps are computed. Cheapest, and it reuses a node that already exists for exactly the purpose of making a gap durable.
  (b) SCHEDULE THE AFFECTED NODE. Every gap names `affected_ids`; scheduling those is already possible where they are Capabilities or Requirements. Weak: the gap and the node are different things, and a component can carry several unrelated gaps.
  (c) A GAP BECOMES A NODE when somebody accepts it as work — promotion rather than computation. Strongest expressive power, and the biggest change: it creates a second source of truth about whether the gap is still real, which is precisely what the computed-every-run design avoids.
  (d) ACKNOWLEDGE, which already exists — `acknowledge_gap` records a reviewed judgement with a reason. But acknowledging says 'we looked and accept this', not 'we will fix this in increment 4'. Those are different answers and only one of them is a plan.

RECOMMENDATION IF ASKED, and it is a finding rather than a decision: (a). It needs no change to gap computation, it reuses the Question node that already turns a computed gap into something durable and addressed to a person, and it composes with the work-package idea — a package could then hold questions as well as capabilities.

CONNECTED TO A DEFECT ALREADY ON THE RECORD: `fact:a-capability-delivered-as-a-model-change-can-never-be-reported-delivered`. Closing a gap is almost always MODEL work, not a file, so if gaps become schedulable before delivery stops requiring an artifact, every scheduled gap would sit `outstanding` forever — the new mechanism would inherit the existing blind spot on day one. These two should be answered together, or the delivery one first.

RELATED: dec:idea-lining-work-up-in-increments-should-be-the-default-not-a-skill-you-remember, dec:idea-an-increment-can-be-sliced-into-work-packages-with-an-owner.
properties.name: OPEN — can a gap that needs closing be scheduled into an increment, the way a capability or requirement is?

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-14, in the same breath as settling the page and explicitly flagged as thinking out loud: *"might even be fun to create/generate a small video explaining what reflow2 is for somebody new to it /brainstorm"*.

Nothing here is intent. It is his idea and it is recorded so it is not lost, not so it is claimed.

DISTINCT FROM the page decision on purpose: that one is SETTLED and covers what the page renders. This is an unsettled question about a different artefact, in a different medium, with a different failure mode. Folding it in would have made a decided node read as half-decided.

═══ ⭐ WHY IT IS BETTER THAN "A NICE EXTRA", AND WORTH KEEPING EVEN IF DECLINED ═══

It plausibly answers the cost he accepted one sentence earlier. `dec:idea-what-is-on-reflow2s-public-page` rules that the page carries ONLY renderings, which means **it cannot carry a hand-written "here is what reflow2 is"** — so a newcomer meets a systems-engineering view before knowing what they are looking at. **An explainer is the orientation the ruling removed.** That is not why he suggested it, and the connection is recorded as an observation rather than attributed to him.

═══ ⚠️ THE TENSION, RECORDED BESIDE THE IDEA RATHER THAN AGAINST IT ═══

**A video is the least renderable artefact there is.** The page's whole claim is that its contents come out of the graph and are periodically refreshed. A video is hand-made, expensive to remake, and therefore **the one thing on that page guaranteed to go stale** — and it would sit there asserting, by adjacency, the same provenance as the renderings around it. That is the exact failure `dec:idea-outward-docs-are-rendered-from-the-graph` was opened about, in the medium where it is hardest to fix.

⇒ Not an argument against it. An argument that **if it ships, it must be visibly a different KIND of thing from the renderings** — or the renderings' credibility pays for it.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.
(a) **A HAND-MADE VIDEO.** Best quality, highest staleness cost, remade by hand every time reflow2 moves.
(b) **A GENERATED WALKTHROUGH DRIVEN BY THE GRAPH** — a scripted tour whose narration and visuals are projected from the same source as the views, so it re-renders with them. Closest to the page's own doctrine; unclear that the tooling exists.
(c) **NOT A VIDEO — AN ANIMATED OR INTERACTIVE RENDERING.** The loop, drawn from the graph and stepped through. `docs/loop-dag.html` already exists as a rendered page and is the nearest thing to a starting point. Keeps the only-renderings rule intact.
(d) **NOTHING, AND LET THE CONFESSIONS DO THE TALKING.** The page's honesty is the pitch; a newcomer who does not get it was not the audience. Cheapest, and consistent — at the cost of the orientation gap being real.

📌 NOT ASSESSED: whether anything in reach can actually generate (b). Nothing in reflow2 renders video, and no attempt was made to find out — recording the idea is not the same as scoping it.

⇒ SEQUENCED AFTER THE RELEASE, like the page. Nothing here is started.
properties.name: OPEN — a short generated video explaining reflow2 to someone new, and the tension that it is the one thing on the page that cannot be rendered from the graph
properties.rationale:
Recorded under the brainstorm skill because he marked it as one. The skill's rule is followed exactly: the idea is not argued down, and the objection — that a video is the one artefact on that page which cannot be re-rendered — is recorded BESIDE it as an option-shaping constraint rather than used to dismiss it. An idea killed in conversation loses its reasoning; recorded with its objection, it keeps both.
