Split from the page decision rather than appended to it, per the skill's rule that several unrelated questions mean several Decisions — and because that one is now settled, so anything unsettled living inside it would make a ruling look tentative.

The connection to the orientation gap is the one thing here he did not say. It is attributed as an observation, not to him, so a later reader can tell his idea from the reason it might matter.

properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-09, about using reflow2 behind a web app. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen. DISTINCT FROM dec:live-tier, and the distinction is the whole point: that decision is about MANY WRITERS ON ONE DESIGN (the state-funeral case — thousands replanning one echeloned plan, which needs consensus and would mean replacing single-writer RocksDB). This is the opposite shape: N TENANTS, EACH WITH THEIR OWN graph_id AND ONE WRITER. No write contention, no consensus, no shared-store rewrite. The two cases share a tier and share almost none of their difficulty. THE SCALE STEPS ARE NOT EVENLY SPACED. 1k is a deployment problem and the design already points at it: cap:graph-registry (planned) specifies a bounded, evict-when-idle map from graph key to open design, and cap:select-graph-by-id (unrealized) lets a session name what it wants. Hold a few hundred designs hot, evict the rest. THE STEP CHANGE IS 1k TO 100k, and it is forced by one measured number: reflow2's OWN design is 1,828 nodes = a 3.8 MB export and a 33 MB store on disk — roughly 9x inflation, being RocksDB plus the tantivy index. At 100k tenants that is ~3.3 TB if all were resident, so the hot set is necessarily ~1% or less, which INVERTS the problem: cold open stops being an edge case and becomes the steady state. shared.rs budgets 30 SECONDS for a cold open today. The engineering question changes from 'hold many designs' (which the registry answers) to 'make opening a design cheap' (which it does not address at all). 100k TO 1M IS THEN HORIZONTAL: ~4 TB of cold blobs is unremarkable for object storage and the hot set grows with concurrency, not with registrations. A FIFTH ROAD, alongside dec:live-tier's four, and it fits what reflow2 already believes: OBJECT STORAGE HOLDS THE EXPORT AS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH, a node HYDRATES a RocksDB+tantivy cache on demand, and eviction is free because the cache is derived. This dissolves placement (any node can serve any tenant), dissolves durability (the object store's problem), and makes an idle tenant cost a ~3.8 MB cold blob instead of a 33 MB live store. reflow2 already has the primitive: the export is deterministic, sorted, content-hashed and self-contained — that IS a per-tenant blob, and the store is already derived rather than authoritative. WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING TODAY, recorded as unbuilt rather than merely absent: cap:graph-registry is planned and nothing builds it; cap:select-graph-by-id is unrealized and unverified; ver:a-session-cannot-name-another-design is PLANNED, and dec:one-process-many-stores was accepted CONDITIONAL on it, so that condition is half met; and dec:live-tier names 'no identity or authorization', which at this scale is not a gap but the product. THE FOUR WAYS TO FORECLOSE, all cheap to avoid now: (1) PROCESS-GLOBALS THAT ARE REALLY PER-DESIGN — cap:graph-registry's own text already lists graph_path, content_path, identity and write_gen as things that must become per-graph; every new static that is secretly per-design is a future migration. (2) PATH AS IDENTITY — cap:select-graph-by-id frames it correctly as 'the server maps id to path', id primary and path derived; sidecar files beside the store (.id.json, .sync.json) want to become object metadata resolved by a resolver. (3) A WHOLE-DOCUMENT WRITE ON A HOT PATH — the export being whole-document is correct for an archival action and fatal on a per-change path, which also makes BL-198 (stop serializing defaults) a SCALING decision rather than tidiness, since blob size is hydrate time. (4) BUILDING MULTI-TENANCY BEFORE PROVING ISOLATION — at this scale that is a security boundary, and retrofitting one into a running multi-tenant system is the sequencing mistake that cannot be walked back. WHAT IS NOT A PROBLEM, worth stating because it is counter-intuitive: the scaling axis is the NUMBER OF TENANTS, not the size of one design. A tenant's graph is small, so full scans, Leiden, modularity and every detector remain cheap per tenant. Single-writer-per-design is a FEATURE here rather than a limit — it is what makes N tenants embarrassingly parallel — so the box would be removing it, not keeping it. THE ONE MEASUREMENT WORTH TAKING NOW, while nothing depends on the answer: hydrate-and-index time as a function of design size (200 / 2k / 20k nodes, import to first query). Under a second for a typical tenant and the cache model is routine engineering; seconds and a read model in front becomes necessary — and that is better known before designing around the opposite assumption.
properties.name: OPEN — what does reflow2 look like at 1k / 100k / 1M tenants each holding their OWN design, and what must not be foreclosed now?
properties.rationale: Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the thinking survives without being claimed as intent. Kept SEPARATE from dec:live-tier rather than appended to it, because one node holding two questions can only ever be half-answered and these two differ in their hardest part: many-writers-one-design needs consensus, many-single-writer-tenants needs cheap hydration. Worth keeping even if none of it is built, for three reasons: the 9x store-to-export ratio is a measured anchor that decides the architecture and was not previously written down anywhere; the fifth road follows from a primitive reflow2 already has rather than from new invention; and the four foreclosures are cheap now and expensive later, which is exactly the class of thing a design graph exists to hold. Anthony's framing was explicitly about not painting into a corner rather than about building this, and the record should keep that distinction.

properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-08-26, in his own words: *"could we create a very dynamic and fluid node that has edges to other nodes in the graph that a user asks something to be done or the agent identifies that something needs to be addressed. once a task is dealt with, the edge to that the hotspot node could be deleted?... the task node then almost becomes a scratchpad of what needs to be done and once something is done, it is removed from the node text field (aka scratchpad) because the node isn't designed as an enduring record (that's what git commit history and changelog files are for). mostly just thinking about how the agent can start using the graph itself."*

**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.**

═══ 🛑 SCOPE — CORRECTED BY ANTHONY THE SAME DAY, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE HERE ═══

*"just a quick note, the task node wasn't strictly for reflow2's own purposes. it is for every reflow2 project and any agent (Claude, grok, openai, etc). I just want to reiterate that."*

**THIS IS A PRODUCT QUESTION, NOT A SELF-HOSTING ONE.** The first draft of this node reasoned almost entirely from reflow2's own repository — its handoff hook, its detectors, its claims. That is the pull `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself` exists to resist, and he has now stated the general form three separate times. The self-hosting evidence stays because it is real evidence, but it is a WITNESS rather than the SUBJECT.

⭐⭐ **AND THE CORRECTION MAKES HIS ORIGINAL ARGUMENT MUCH STRONGER THAN THE VERSION FIRST RECORDED.** He argued a markdown handoff is not transportable ACROSS MACHINES. The sharper fact is that it is not transportable ACROSS AGENTS: `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/` is Claude Code furniture. **A grok, OpenAI or Codex agent working the same design has no such directory, no such file, and no way to read one.** So the pattern does not merely degrade on a second laptop — it is unavailable to most of reflow2's intended users on day one.

⭐ **THE CONSEQUENCE THAT FOLLOWS, AND IT ARGUES FOR THE IDEA:** the design graph is the ONLY thing every agent working a project shares. Not the harness, not the memory store, not the hooks, not the slash commands. `dec:skills-served` already made this argument for skills — served from the server so they match the running version and nothing in the repo goes stale — and a working set is the same shape of problem. **Whatever carries "what needs doing" has to live where every agent can reach it, and the graph is the only candidate.** That is a far better reason to build this than anything in the first draft.

⚠️ **A WARNING THIS OPENS, WHICH BELONGS WITH `dec:idea-where-does-tool-use-actually-fail-four-layers`:** reflow2's mechanisms for making an agent USE it are themselves Claude-Code-shaped — Stop and PostToolUse hooks, `.claude/settings.json`, 23 slash commands. Those reach one harness. The MCP tool surface reaches all of them. **So the layer-② trigger work measured so far may be less portable than the layer-③ and layer-④ work, and nobody has stated that.**

═══ WHAT IS ACTUALLY BEING PROPOSED, and it is sharper than a to-do list ═══

Not a Task type. A single node whose **edges ARE the worklist** — draw one at a node needing attention, delete it when dealt with — and whose **text is a scratchpad that shrinks as work completes**. Explicitly *not* an enduring record, on the stated ground that git history and the changelog already are.

⭐ **THE INVERSION THAT MAKES IT INTERESTING.** Everything else in a reflow2 graph is built to endure. `retire-from-design` forces one question before anything leaves — *"was this ever true?"* — because history is retired on the record while a mistake is deleted, and confusing the two either erases the past or embalms a typo. `OBSOLETES` exists so a withdrawal has an author. `Snapshot`, `DesignEpoch` and `ChangeEvent` all exist to stop things vanishing. **A node designed to be erased would be the first construct to deliberately opt out**, and the question is whether that discipline leaks once one exists.

═══ THERE IS ALREADY A PRECEDENT, AND IT WORKS ═══

**Claims.** `claim_region` draws an advisory marker whose liveness is COMPUTED rather than stored; `release_claim` deletes it and leaves nothing behind. Exercised on reflow2's own design 2026-08-26 — drawn and released, no history lost because none was owed. **So an ephemeral construct already exists in the product and nobody argues it corrupts anything.** That is the strongest evidence for the hotspot being admissible in principle, and it generalises to any project because claims are a shipped feature rather than a local habit.

═══ THE OBJECTION THAT MATTERS MOST ═══

🛑 **Deleting an edge cannot say whether the work was DONE or ABANDONED**, and those are the two states `retire-from-design` exists to keep apart. A worklist that forgets which is which will, over months, lose the record of things decided against — and *"we considered that and dropped it"* is exactly the memory this project keeps saying is worth more than the thing itself.

⭐ A possible answer, untested: a real completion writes a ChangeEvent, so **an edge deleted with no ChangeEvent in the window IS the abandoned case, computably.** That would make the distinction derivable rather than stored — the same move `dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written` already makes.

═══ THE SPLIT THAT DECIDES HOW MUCH IS NEEDED ═══

- **COMPUTABLE** — open gaps, failing checks, drift awaiting disposition, capabilities claiming built with no check, answers never written back. `loop_status` computes ALL of it today in one cheap call, for any project. **A hotspot holding these would duplicate a computation and immediately risk disagreeing with it.**
- **EXOGENOUS** — *"Jakub said finish the tests"* (his own words, from NSLS-II rather than from reflow2), *"the vendor confirmed the API changes in March"*, *"CI was pending when I stopped"*. Facts about the world, underivable from any design. **This half has no home in any reflow2 project**, and is what `dec:idea-is-there-a-lightweight-task-capture-below-the-increment-grain` opened on 2026-08-25 — also from real work rather than from reflow2's own development.

So the hotspot may be far smaller than it first looks: a home for the exogenous half, with the computable half left where it already lives and never mirrored.

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) One hotspot node per design, edges as worklist, text as scratchpad.** As proposed. ⚠️ Counter, and it is specific rather than aesthetic: a single node accumulating edges from everywhere becomes a **hub that distorts the structural detectors** — betweenness, community detection, articulation points and `surprising_connections` all reason about connectivity, and they would read a scratchpad as topology. **This hits every consumer's design, not just reflow2's** — any project running `detect_defects` would start seeing its own to-do list reported as a god-node or a sole bridge.

**(b) Exogenous items only, as small nodes, with the worklist COMPUTED as "these plus what loop_status owes."** Avoids the hub problem and the duplication. ⚠️ Counter: close to option C of the 2026-08-25 task question and inherits its objection — a translation step at the moment the user wants to dump three sentences and move on.

**(c) Do not store it at all; make the working set a projection, like orientation.** Most consistent with `dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written`. ⚠️ Counter: cannot hold the exogenous half by construction, and that is the half worth carrying.

**(d) Keep the scratchpad OUT of a text field, whatever else is decided.** A prose field edited by successive sessions has no merge story, and reflow2 is explicitly multi-writer through a shared server — and now explicitly multi-AGENT. Two sessions erasing different lines of one scratchpad is a lost update with no conflict, exactly what `expected_content_hash` was added to prevent, and it would not even be detected. **With several different agents on one design this stops being a corner case.**

📌 His closing framing, now read in the corrected scope: *"mostly just thinking about how the agent can start using the graph itself."* Not *this* agent, and not on *this* project — **any agent, on any design, reaching for the one thing they all share.**
properties.name: OPEN — can a design brain hold a deliberately EPHEMERAL node, whose edges are the live worklist and whose text is erased as work completes?
properties.rationale:
Judged distinct from the handoff question after reading it: that one is about a contradiction in the repository and could be closed by deleting a hook; this is about whether an ephemeral construct belongs in a graph built to endure, which survives that answer either way.

The claims precedent is recorded because it settles the in-principle objection with evidence rather than argument — an ephemeral, computed, deletable marker already exists here and has caused no harm. What remains is not "may we?" but "what shape, and which half of the worklist".

The hub objection sits at option level rather than as a verdict because it is a specific structural consequence — this design's own algorithms would read the node as topology — and it is the kind of thing that is obvious afterwards and expensive to discover after building.

properties.decision:
From `art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-08-26`, opportunity O-01 — the report's own top priority, raised from a real program rather than from thinking about reflow2.

**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.**

═══ THE USE CASE, WHICH IS NOT THE ONE REFLOW2 WAS BUILT FOR ═══

*"`hxm_program` is not a product; it is a hub — a living, agent-maintained source of truth for a program of beamlines whose actual code lives in ~10 other repos... The graph is used less as 'the design of a system' and more as the program's memory and coherence engine."*

**Eight `.reflow2` stores on one machine**: the hub, two sim-scoped sub-designs (one of which has since moved into a *different* repo), a vision design, three unrelated projects, and reflow2's own. Only one person runs reflow2; ~6 collaborators read markdown.

═══ THE GAP, STATED PRECISELY ═══

Two designs can today **LINK as peers** (`published`/`required` boundaries, `pair_designs`, `seam_report`, `mirror_surface`) or **MERGE** (absorption). The hub needs a third: *this design is the hub of those* — ownership and roll-up **without absorption**. Four things it wants to say, none of which the current vocabulary expresses:

1. *"Capability X here **is realised by** their design"* — a cross-design REALIZES/SATISFIES, **so the hub stops keeping shadow copies of the sim's capabilities, which it does today and nothing flags the duplication**
2. *"When their committed export moves, tell me"* — `sync_status` against ANOTHER design's export
3. *"Roll their verification state up"* — the hub's `loop_status` showing the children's pass/fail without owning those checks
4. `describe_designs` reporting each design's **last export date**, so a hub can see which children have gone dark

⭐ AND THE REASON IT IS NOT AN INTERFACE PROBLEM, in their words: *"the seam vocabulary (medium, auth, payload, error model) fits interfaces; the hub's relations are dependency/ownership, and forcing them into `Interface` nodes would be modelling fiction."* **That is the argument, and it is a good one** — reflow2's contract vocabulary describes what two systems must agree on at a boundary, which is a different relation from one design being answerable for another.

═══ 🛑 THE OBJECTION THAT MUST BE MET FIRST, AND IT IS THIS PROJECT'S STANDING ONE ═══

**Is a hub-of-designs a design brain, or a programme-management tool?** The same objection killed the Task node type on 2026-08-25 (*"this is the road to being a tracker"*) and shadows the MCP-contract idea recorded the same day. Roll-up, ownership and portfolio status are recognisably PPM features, and every step toward being good at that is a step toward being worse at holding WHY.

⭐ **THE COUNTER, AND IT IS WHY THIS ONE MAY EARN ITS PLACE:** item 1 is not portfolio reporting, it is a **coherence** claim — *the hub is keeping shadow copies of another design's capabilities and nothing detects the duplication*. That is exactly the class of thing reflow2 exists to catch, and it is invisible today. Items 2–4 are reporting; item 1 is the design brain failing at its own job across a boundary it cannot see.

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen (the report records link / merge / index / hybrid with costs) ═══

**(a) A cross-design REALIZES/SATISFIES only.** Solve item 1 alone — the coherence half — and leave roll-up out. Smallest, and it attacks the one thing that is a design defect rather than a status report. ⚠️ Counter: needs a way to name a node in another design that survives that design moving repo, which is `dec:a-design-is-named-by-an-id-not-a-path` territory and not free.

**(b) An index/registry design that knows about others.** `describe_designs` already reads sidecars safely without minting. Extend to last-export-date and a declared parent. ⚠️ Counter: filesystem-scoped, so it works on one machine and not for a hub whose children are in other people's repos.

**(c) Full hub relation with roll-up.** What the report asks for. ⚠️ Counter: the tracker objection lands hardest here, and roll-up of verification state means the hub reports numbers it cannot verify — a `report-dont-judge` problem.

**(d) Do nothing; say the hub case is out of scope.** ⚠️ Counter: it is a real user with a real program, and `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself` says field use is the point. Declining should be explicit rather than by neglect.

📌 **PREREQUISITE THE REPORT NAMES ITSELF (O-02):** *zero of seven sibling designs on that machine has a committed export or a published surface*, and `link-projects` correctly forbids opening a sibling's store. **So none of this is reachable until partners export** — which is a nudge problem (their F-07: *"there is no export at all" is still silent*) before it is a vocabulary problem.
properties.name: OPEN — a design can LINK to a peer or MERGE with one; hxm_program needs a third thing — to be the HUB of others, with roll-up and ownership but no absorption
properties.rationale:
Recorded because it is the report's own top priority, it comes from live program work rather than from reflow2's development, and the gap it names is real: the vocabulary genuinely has link and merge and nothing between them.

The tracker objection is written in at full strength rather than as a caveat, because it is the objection that has already killed one adjacent idea in this design and would apply here unexamined. What distinguishes this case is item 1 — undetected shadow copies across a design boundary — which is a coherence failure rather than a reporting gap, and is the only part of the request that reflow2 is uniquely placed to answer.

The O-02 prerequisite is recorded on the node rather than left in the report, because it changes the ORDER: no hub relation is usable while zero siblings export, so the cheap nudge may unblock more than the expensive vocabulary would.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-23, thinking out loud about how reflow2 should express its own decomposition.

HIS WORDS: "I want express reflow2 as 10 subsystems. Then say one of the subsystems is A and say there are 5 components associated with subsystem_A. They should be 'nested' as something like subsystem_A.component_1, subsystem_A.component_2, and so on. If component_2 [has] 3 sub-components, it'd be subsystem_A.component_2.sub_component_1."

⭐ MEASURED THE SAME DAY, AND IT CHANGES THE QUESTION: THE TEN SUBSYSTEMS ALREADY EXIST. reflow2 declares exactly 10 Components at `level: subsystem` (sys:agent-surface, sys:coherence-loop, sys:documentation, sys:foundation, sys:human-channel, sys:intake, sys:store, sys:time-history, sys:vocabulary, plus cmp:packaging), and ZERO components sit outside one — every component is parented on the CONTAINS spine. `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` already requires nesting 'as deep as the design needs', and `Component.level` already carries the rung. So the STRUCTURE he is describing is built and populated.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN is narrower and it is about IDENTITY, not shape: should the path through the spine be expressible as an ADDRESS a person can read, write and search by? Today `cmp:detect` says nothing about where it sits; you learn that by walking CONTAINS.

THE OPTIONS AS THEY STAND:
(a) DERIVE the path on read — a computed `path` field on any component, never stored. Cheap, cannot go stale, and it is a pure projection, which is what this project already demands of views. COUNTER: it is not an identity, so you cannot address a node by it, and two components with the same leaf name in different subsystems still collide in search.
(b) STORE the dotted id — `sys:coherence-loop.detect`. Reads exactly as he wrote it. COUNTER: an id that encodes position BREAKS THE MOMENT SOMETHING MOVES, and `cap:a-component-can-be-moved-not-just-given-another-parent` was built three days ago precisely so parts CAN move. This option makes the id a lie every time that capability is used.
(c) DO NOTHING — the spine is the answer and an address is a rendering concern.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether anybody needs to ADDRESS a node by path, or only to SEE the path. Those want different answers, and nothing measured says which is wanted.

⚠️ ONE ANOMALY FOUND WHILE MEASURING, worth its own look: `cmp:packaging` is at `level: subsystem`, contains NOTHING, provides nothing and consumes nothing — a subsystem with no inside. It is also the only one named `cmp:` rather than `sys:`.
properties.name: OPEN — should a nested part have an ADDRESS (subsystem_A.component_2.sub_component_1), or is the containment spine enough?
properties.rationale: Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`. Split from the contract-level and capability-composition questions he raised in the same breath, because each can be answered without the others.

properties.decision: ACCEPTED on Anthony's word, 2026-08-08 — shape (a), and he named why it is the right one: it is the only option where the question STOPS EXISTING rather than being answered. No plan ever holds a number it can lose, so neither slipping nor inserting is a problem. THE RULE: a planned increment's identity names its CONTENT (`epoch:planned-read-half`, `epoch:planned-status-accounting`). The version number is not part of the plan at all. At cut time the number is derived from what actually shipped, by the CHANGELOG's own bucket table — patch for fixes, minor for a change to the shape of the tool surface or the schema. WHAT IT DISSOLVES: (1) The id churn. An id cannot be renamed, so a version-named plan guarantees either a lying id or a node replacement that breaks the snapshot trail `dec:arrival-delta` reads plan movement from. A content-named plan never needs renaming, because content is what the plan IS. (2) The slip-versus-insert question entirely. `dec:an-unplanned-cut-slips-every-later-increment-by-one` (accepted an hour earlier) and `dec:idea-an-unplanned-cut-takes-an-in-between-number` were competing answers to "what happens to the planned numbers when unplanned work takes one" — and under this rule there are no planned numbers to disturb. The slip rule is not WRONG; its subject ceases to exist. Recorded with an OBSOLETES edge rather than by un-accepting it, per dec:reopen-supersedes: an accepted Decision is never un-accepted. (3) The pressure to mislabel. With numbering decided at the cut from shipped content, semver stays honest by construction — nobody is tempted to call a shape change a patch to protect a planned number, which is the concrete harm the in-between-number idea carried (the CHANGELOG's own table says patch means the consumer updates blindly). THE OBSERVATION UNDERNEATH, which generalises past versioning: a version number is assigned LAST, at the cut, and a planned increment exists LONG before that. Baking it into the identity records a GUESS as a NAME. That is the same shape as `ver:plan-increments`' finding that a plan's content lived in an epoch's NAME as prose rather than as structure — both are a plan carrying, in its identity or its label, something that belongs elsewhere. COMPOSES WITH THE HYBRID rather than competing: content-named plans plus semver-honest numbering at cut time is the same destination reached from two directions, which is why `dec:idea-an-unplanned-cut-takes-an-in-between-number` stays recorded rather than rejected — its numbering instinct survives, only its premise (that plans own numbers) is gone. NOT CHOSEN: (b) a `version` property on DesignEpoch — smaller, but it leaves the misleading ids in place; (c) redefining the pre-1.0 buckets — cheapest to write, most expensive to be wrong about, since it weakens the one signal consumers act on blindly; (d) keeping version-named ids and reading them as birth numbers — makes every id a small trap for a future reader.
properties.name: A planned increment is identified by what it DELIVERS; the version number is assigned at the cut, from what actually shipped
properties.rationale: Raised immediately after applying the slip, because the cost was concrete rather than theoretical: four planned epochs needed renaming and none could have its id corrected, so the graph now holds ids whose numbers are one behind their content. Recorded rather than fixed — changing how the plan is ADDRESSED is a bigger act than the slip Anthony asked for, and picking (a) would re-point every future reference.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-20, thinking past both hypotheticals: *"I feel like we could do this and set a far off target epoch for reflow2, then the question becomes how to change/morph reflow2 to that future state."*

DISTINCT FROM BOTH SIBLINGS, which were read before writing this. `dec:idea-genesis-reflow3-from-the-requirements-alone` asks what a fresh pass on the requirements would PRODUCE — a sufficiency test. `dec:idea-run-adopt-on-reflow2-itself-as-a-ground-truth-test` asks what reading the CODE would RECOVER. Both are EXPERIMENTS that end in a measurement. This is a MECHANISM that ends in a roadmap, and it needs neither experiment to be run.

⭐ THE MACHINERY IS ALREADY BUILT, which is what makes this cheap where reflow3 is expensive:
  `plan_epoch`      an Epoch that has NOT happened yet — the forward half of the time axis
                    (`req:epochs-can-be-planned`). A planned epoch REFUSES record_change,
                    because a snapshot captures the present.
  `schedule_for`    points a Requirement or Capability at the epoch it is due in
  `arrival_delta`   planned versus delivered, per item, with FIVE outcomes — delivered,
                    deferred, discontinued, and `outstanding`, which means nobody has yet
                    said which of the previous two it is. It refuses to default that, and
                    names it as the question to put to the user.
  `set_epoch_status` marks arrival when the moment comes

⇒ SO "HOW DO WE MORPH REFLOW2 TO ITS FUTURE STATE" IS ALREADY A COMPUTABLE QUESTION. Record the end state as a planned epoch, schedule the intent that belongs to it, and the delta between now and then IS the roadmap — recomputed on demand rather than maintained as a document that drifts.

⭐⭐ AND IT DISSOLVES THE EXPENSIVE HALF OF THE REFLOW3 QUESTION. reflow3 was proposed to discover whether the recorded intent determines the product. But the reason a fresh pass would diverge is already measured and is not in doubt: 18 capabilities no requirement asks for, 43 requirements nothing delivers, and a design governed more than twice as heavily by Decisions (877 of 901 GOVERNED_BY edges) as by Requirements — and genesis does not take Decisions as input. A target epoch does not need to answer that question. It needs the target STATED, which is a thing Anthony can say directly.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⚠️ WHAT IS GENUINELY HARD ABOUT IT, and it is not the tooling

A planned epoch is only as good as the target written into it, and NOBODY HAS WRITTEN ONE. Today's audit gives candidate content — every 15288 process with vocabulary and no check, the interface half of the black-box requirement, a risk register, validation that has never once been used on 175 checks. But turning that into a stated end-state is a design act, not a scheduling one.

🛑 AND ONE TRAP THIS SHARES WITH EVERYTHING ELSE TODAY: `arrival_delta` computes against the epoch's FIRST snapshot as baseline. A target epoch with nothing scheduled at it returns a clean delta — the same green-over-emptiness shape as `modularity 1.00` over one dependency, `hierarchy_issues: 0` over an incomplete spine, and `0 gaps` over ten unused schema domains. A far-off epoch nobody has scheduled anything into would report no shortfall at all.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
OPTIONS

**A. STATE THE TARGET, SCHEDULE NOTHING YET.** One planned epoch, named, with the end-state written in its own text. Cheapest possible move and it makes the direction a fact rather than a conversation. ⚠️ On its own it changes no computation.

**B. STATE IT AND SCHEDULE THE KNOWN GAPS INTO IT** — the accepted-but-unbuilt requirements, starting with `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` and `req:interface-spec-complete`. `arrival_delta` then answers "how far is reflow2 from what it says it should be" as a computation. ⭐ This is the one that makes the morph measurable.

**C. INTERMEDIATE EPOCHS BETWEEN NOW AND THE TARGET** — the increments. `plan-increments` already exists for this. ⚠️ Premature until the target has content; sequencing toward an unstated end is how a roadmap becomes a wish list.

**D. DO IT AFTER ADOPT.** Anthony's own leaning is adopt-on-a-copy first. Its predicted prize is a RECOVERED CONTRACT SET, which is precisely the largest item any target epoch would contain — so running it first would populate the target rather than guess at it.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a planned epoch far enough out to hold a whole end-state is a shape reflow2 has ever exercised. Every epoch in this graph is a release cut or a revision that has already happened.
properties.name: OPEN — record reflow2's target end-state as a PLANNED EPOCH and let arrival_delta drive the morph, instead of building reflow3 to find out what the target is

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. The sharpest technical problem inside `dec:idea-does-reflow2-ship-design-principles-to-every-project`, and the one that decides whether shipping is even possible.

THE PROBLEM, read straight off dev_storyflow's own text. Every one of the seven principles is a universal idea wearing storyflow's clothes:

  #2 "no silent fallbacks" — the IDEA is universal (a failure must never report success). The STATEMENT names `try/except: pass`, `console.error`, toast UI. A beamline control system has the same failure and none of those words.
  #4 "verify your own claims" — universal. The statement names `npm run check`, foreground cargo, Playwright on a real surface.
  #5 "real-path tests" — universal. "Unit-green ≠ live-green" survives translation; "the path the UI actually calls" does not.
  #7 "modular, no monoliths" — the modularity half travels; the Python DI / `typing.Protocol` / flat-hierarchy half is a language ruling and travels nowhere.
  #3 "done = end-to-end + lens-exposed" — travels as "built is not delivered"; "lens-exposed" is storyflow vocabulary.
  #1 and #6 travel almost verbatim, which is itself informative: they are the two most abstract.

⇒ SHIPPING THE PROSE AS-IS WOULD PUT A JAVASCRIPT TOAST IN A BEAMLINE'S DESIGN GRAPH. And reflow2's operating context is explicitly not one domain — greenfield and brownfield, several orgs, currently a ~10-year-old bluesky stack at a synchrotron. A principle that arrives wearing the wrong clothes gets waived for the clothes, and the idea goes with them.

THE SHAPES, none chosen:
(A) CORE ONLY. Ship the domain-free statement; each project writes its own instantiation if it wants one. Cheapest and most portable. COST: the abstract version is the forgettable version — "fail loudly" is a poster, whereas "no `try/except: pass`" is a thing you can be caught doing. The teeth are in the clothes.
(B) CORE + WORKED EXAMPLES, marked as examples. The statement is domain-free; illustrations are labelled as one domain's instantiation, not as the rule. Keeps the teeth without asserting them elsewhere. COST: longer nodes, and `req:a-finding-has-somewhere-to-put-its-evidence` already says this design writes too much into single fields.
(C) CORE + A PROJECT-LOCAL INSTANTIATION SLOT. The shipped rule is the core; the project fills in what it looks like HERE, and the filling-in is the act of adopting it. Turns adoption into something visible and checkable rather than a silent inheritance. COST: new vocabulary, and a slot nobody fills is the declared-field-nobody-writes-to trap `req:a-finding-has-somewhere-to-put-its-evidence` names explicitly.
(D) DOMAIN PACKS. A software pack, an instrument-control pack, and so on. COST: reflow2 would be asserting what a domain is, and it has no basis for that.

⭐ AN OBSERVATION WORTH CARRYING WHICHEVER WAY THIS GOES: the two that travel verbatim (#1 root-cause-first, #6 no silent caps) are the two reflow2 has ALREADY adopted for itself, independently. That is weak evidence that portability and abstraction are the same axis here — and that the right test for "should this ship" may simply be "does it survive being stated without naming a language, a framework, or a tool?"
properties.name: OPEN — a shipped principle has a universal CORE and local CLOTHES; does reflow2 ship only the core, and how does a project put its own clothes on it?
properties.rationale: Recorded as brainstorming. Every one of the seven is a universal idea in local clothes, and the clothes are where the teeth are — "fail loudly" is a poster, "no try/except: pass" is something you can be caught doing. Shipping the prose unchanged would put JavaScript toasts in a beamline's design graph; shipping only the abstraction may ship something too weak to bite. Not resolved.

properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-08-26, from the same brainstorm: *"what would make the agent say, I have the perfect skill or tool needed for problem X?"*

**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.**

═══ THE MISMATCH, STATED PRECISELY ═══

An agent holds a PROBLEM in the user's words. reflow2 offers ~150 tools named for the OPERATION they perform. Retrieval has to cross that gap, and `find_tools` crosses it by matching text against tool names and descriptions — which works when the user already speaks reflow2 and fails exactly when they do not.

**Two measurements, both from asking a user's question in a user's words:**

- *"does my declared decomposition match the real coupling?"* — best of 152 tools was **`set_interface_designation`**, and the session's actual finding came from a hand-written Python script.
- *"move a component to a different parent"* — returned **`contain_component`**, which ADDS a parent and never removes the old one. The discoverable sequence CAUSES the `multiple_parents` defect.

The second is worse than a miss: retrieval succeeded, was confidently wrong, and produced a defect. **A ranked list with no notion of "this is not what you want" is not a weak answer, it is a misleading one.**

And `dec:bl-155` names the same disease from the other end — its group (c), the *"uncomfortable middle"*: `evidence_report`, `seam_report`, `budget_report`, `dimension_drift`, `analyze_alternatives`, `arrival_delta` are READS that answer real questions on designs that exist today, and nobody reaches for them. Its own words: *"a capability nobody can find is worth what an absent one is worth."*

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) A question-shaped index, HARVESTED rather than authored.** Map "questions a user actually asks" → tool. The corpus already exists: `tools/surface_usage.py` read 46 transcripts and 6,095 calls. Mine the prose that PRECEDED each call and you get real question→tool pairs, in users' words, for free. ⚠️ Counter: it learns what agents already do, so it can only reinforce the tools already being found — the 40 never-called tools have no preceding prose to mine. It would sharpen the head of the distribution and do nothing for the tail, which is the part that hurts.

**(b) Question-shaped ALIASES over the existing names.** `"what will this break?"` → `propagate_change`; `"has this been decided?"` → `search_design`; `"what did I just make false?"` → `unclaimed_findings`. Additive, no consumer breakage, and it puts the user's register on the surface where `find_tools` can match it. ⚠️ Counter: a second naming system to keep in step with the first, and nothing detects an alias that has gone stale.

**(c) Rename the tools after the question they answer.** The honest version of (b), and the one `fix-properly-not-patch` argues for before 1.0. ⚠️ Counter: ~150 renames, every consumer breaks, and it trades a retrieval problem for a migration problem. Also the operation name is the RIGHT name for the agent that already knows what it wants.

**(d) One door: a dispatcher that takes free-text intent and returns the skill, the tools AND the traps.** *"I am about to X"* → everything relevant, including what will go wrong. ⚠️ Counter: an agent that would not call `list_skills` has no more reason to call the door. Adds a layer to a surface already accused of being large.

**(e) Make the tool say when it is the WRONG answer.** The `contain_component` case argues this is worth more than better ranking: a tool that knows the adjacent mistake can name it in its own description. Some already do. ⚠️ Counter: it improves precision after retrieval, not retrieval itself — no help for a tool never surfaced at all.

═══ THE OBSERVATION UNDERNEATH ═══

Retrieval is a fourth leg beside the three already recorded (**typed tool + instruction + detector that notices absence**). Those three make a vocabulary REACHABLE. None makes it RETRIEVABLE from a problem in someone else's words — and reachable-but-not-retrievable is exactly what BL-155's group (c) measures.
properties.name: OPEN — what would let a problem stated in the USER'S words retrieve the tool that answers it, when the tool is named for the operation it performs?
properties.rationale:
Kept separate from the four-layer diagnostic because it is a different question with a different answer shape: that one asks WHERE use fails, this one asks HOW a problem finds its tool. Retrieval sits mostly in layer ① (known) with a foot in ② (recognised), and could be built and tested without settling which layer is the bottleneck.

The two failed retrievals are recorded with the tool each returned, rather than as "find_tools is weak", because the second one — a confidently wrong answer that causes a defect — argues for a different fix than the first, and collapsing them would lose that.

properties.decision:
**DECIDED 2026-08-19 BY ANTHONY — option (f), on his instruction "yes, build it as you recommend".** Delivered the same day, `epoch:the-loop-holds-the-invitation`; what is owed is stated in `req:detecting-is-not-asking`.

**THE RULING: REPORTING A GAP AND INVITING ITS CLOSURE ARE DIFFERENT ACTS, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS URGENT.** Detection stays unconditional and cheap. The *invitation* waits for a boundary — the user asks, pauses, says they are done, or turns to building. **The gaps stay LOUD throughout: this defers the invitation, never the record.**

He chose it over a user-set posture, a computed phase, and full lifecycle phases — all of which ask the user to declare something, when the measured complaint was simply being interrupted.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐⭐ ALEX'S ANSWER IS WHY THIS WAS ANSWERABLE, AND IT KILLED THE FAVOURITE HYPOTHESIS

Asked what was actually pushing him to close: *"I would enter some information about the application. Like this data model does this and this does this and then it basically would respond with, **'I have those all recorded. There are open gaps with X, Y, and Z. Do you want to fix them?'**"*

**IT WAS NOT VOLUME.** Three gaps — "X, Y, and Z" — not three hundred. The leading hypothesis was the chatty `unsatisfied_requirement` detector burying a corpus, and **that fix would not have touched his problem.** `dec:gap-reporting-when-most-intent-is-unbuilt` is a real defect and a genuinely different one; the two only looked alike.

**AND HE REQUESTED NONE OF IT.** No `loop_status`, no `detect_gaps`, no status readout. Every prompt was volunteered and ended in a question he had to answer in order to keep doing what he came to do.

**HIS ASK WAS A DEFERRAL, NOT A SILENCING:** *"let me finish inputting the knowledge into this, **then we can discuss how to close gaps and issues**."*

📌 THE QUESTION WAS PUT TO HIM PRECISELY BECAUSE THE ANSWER WOULD PICK THE OPTION, and it did. Recorded because it is the cheapest move in this whole node: one question to the affected user eliminated one option outright, demoted two others, and produced a fix nobody had proposed.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 IT WAS NOT A BUG — THREE SERVED SOURCES INSTRUCTED IT, EACH CORRECT ALONE

  1. `capture-intent` step 7 — *"when it names debt, run detect-and-ask before the next operational task, not after."*
  2. served `AGENTS.md` step 2 — *"DETECT gaps and ask… ask the user… Do this before building."*
  3. `detect-and-ask`'s own trigger — *"after capturing new intent."*

**Each was written for a real failure** — the agent that only ever adds nodes and surfaces nothing, which `capture-intent` step 7 names in as many words. **Together, on a user doing nothing but capture for days, they produce a prompt to close after every message.** That is why the fix is a timing rule added to all three rather than the deletion of any one, and why none of them was wrong to exist.

⭐⭐ **CORROBORATED FROM THE INSIDE, SAME WEEK.** During the session that recorded this node, the Stop hook fired at the agent — *"6 graph write(s) this session and no loop check… intent was captured this session and detect_gaps was never run"* — **in the middle of a BRAINSTORM**, the one workflow whose own skill says *"do not run detect-and-ask over brainstormed nodes… it would ask the user to firm up exactly what they deliberately left soft."* The loop pushed toward closure at the moment its own doctrine forbids it. Alex's report and that observation are the same defect at two distances, and the ruling covers both.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
ANTHONY'S ORIGINAL FRAMING, AND WHY IT IS NOT WHAT SHIPPED

His proposal was user-defined phases — *"design conception, initial systems engineering, design implementation, testing, fielding."* ⚠️ **He qualified it in the same breath:** *"projects like reflow2 often will be continually developed and I will probably always have ideas, so the phases would probably need to be more advisory and fluid than hard phases."* The evidence backs the caveat: `fact:the-owner-uses-reflow2-as-a-funnel-for-random-order-input` measured nine inputs in one day arriving in random order, with *"both my brother and I kind of work like this."* **No ordered phase list predicts that — and in the end no phase concept was needed at all**, because the complaint was about interruption, not about stage.

📌 `maturity_report` already sees where a design sits and deliberately refuses to say where it SHOULD be. 📌 `set_project_mode` gates only `apply_heal`; it was never this. 📌 `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` (**`proposed`, still unaccepted**) already states Alex's mode — *"every capability is `planned`, every requirement `proposed`… which is honest and must not read as catastrophic."*

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
OPTIONS AS THEY STOOD

(f) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — separate reporting from prompting in the served text. Changes no computation, no schema, no detector; keeps every gap loud; fixes the brainstorm collision too.
(a) **NOT CHOSEN** — a stated, user-set posture. Heavier than the evidence demanded: Alex never asked for a mode, he asked not to be interrupted. A stale posture would also silence the loop exactly when it matters.
(b) **NOT CHOSEN** — derive from `maturity_report`'s frontier. Would make what the loop asks depend on a computed phase, converting a reading into a judgement.
(c) 🛑 **ELIMINATED BY THE ANSWER** — aggregate the chatty detector. Three gaps, not three hundred. Still a live defect elsewhere.
(d) **NOT CHOSEN** — a session capture mode. reflow2 has no clock and no session identity; "for this session" is the harness's concept.
(e) **NOT CHOSEN** — full lifecycle phases; retracted by their own author.

⚠️ **THE HONEST WEAKNESS OF WHAT SHIPPED**, stated rather than discovered later: served prose with nothing able to observe whether it holds. `skill_lint` asserts the text is present and mirrored; it cannot assert an agent honoured it. **Same shape as the instruction that lapsed within four days in `dec:idea-the-enum-question-came-back-four-days-after-it-was-fixed`.**

⚠️ AND ONE JUDGEMENT STAYS THE AGENT'S: *"plainly still pouring things in"* is not computable from the graph — the signals are conversational and live where reflow2 cannot see them. The explicit boundaries are named in the served text so the rule can never be read as "never ask".
properties.name: DECIDED — detecting is not asking: the loop keeps finding gaps and holds the invitation to close until the person stops pouring things in
properties.rationale: Raised 2026-08-18 from Alex's report, answered by him 2026-08-19, and settled the same day on Anthony's instruction to build the recommendation. The answer is preserved verbatim because it eliminated the volume hypothesis — which was the favourite and would have sent the fix at a different defect entirely — and because the whole episode is the cheapest thing in the node: one question to the affected user killed one option, demoted two, and produced a fix nobody had proposed. The three served sources are named with file and step so a future session does not simply delete one; each was written for a real failure and only their combination was the defect. The Stop-hook self-observation is kept because self-measurement of the defect under discussion, during a brainstorm the skill explicitly protects, is stronger than a relayed report alone. Anthony's own phase proposal and his same-breath retraction are both retained so the record shows the idea was taken seriously and then rendered unnecessary rather than rejected.

properties.decision:
**DECIDED 2026-08-26 on Anthony's word: option (a), NARROWED, plus option (d) as the guard — and option (b)'s reporting half was added the same day.** The question this node opened — "is `proposed` itself a sweep class?" — is answered YES, per finding kind rather than globally.

═══ WHAT WAS BUILT ═══

`is_parked_idea` (crates/reflow2-core/src/heal.rs) — ONE predicate, read by every detector that needs it: a Decision whose `status` is `proposed`. Three finding kinds read it, and **each states how it COMBINES it, because the combination differs and the difference is the content**:

- **`contradiction`** — skip when **BOTH** endpoints are parked ideas.
- **`unresolved_setup`** — skip when **EITHER** endpoint is a parked idea.
- **`unthreaded_cluster`** — skip an island where **EVERY** member is a parked idea.

⭐ THE ASYMMETRY BETWEEN THE FIRST TWO IS DELIBERATE and falls out of what each finding CLAIMS, not from taste. `unresolved_setup` says *"X anticipates Y but nothing follows through"* — the complaint is that **Y is unresolved**, and when Y is a parked idea that is exactly what `proposed` MEANS: the recorded idea IS the follow-through. A contradiction is real as soon as **one** side asserts something, so it needs both sides parked before it goes quiet.

Three kinds deliberately do NOT read it, and say so: `duplicate` (two parked thoughts can still cover the same ground, and merge is still the remedy) and the pure-topology rules `single_point_of_failure` / `dead_end` / `circular_dependency` (statements about the shape the design HAS, which a node occupies whatever its status claims). `orphan_node` already read it from the start.

═══ 🛑 THIS TOOK THREE CUTS, AND EACH WAS CAUGHT BY SOMETHING DIFFERENT ═══

**Cut 1** had `unresolved_setup` requiring BOTH endpoints parked. **Twenty minutes after it shipped, recording a brainstorm exactly as the `brainstorm` skill instructs** — step 4, relate the new idea to what is already there — drew ANTICIPATES edges from an ACCEPTED Decision and from a TemporalFact to parked ideas. Both fired. Defects went 78 → 80 **for following the instructions**, the same complaint hxm_program filed, surviving the fix meant to answer it. ⚠️ A rule keyed on both endpoints could never have reached the second case at all: a TemporalFact is not a Decision and can never be parked. **The shape had to change, not the threshold** — a predicate scoped to one node type cannot express a rule about edges whose other end is any type.

**Cut 2** widened `unresolved_setup` to either side, and took reflow2's own design 89 → 61.

**Cut 3** fixed a defect *the first two had introduced*: 33 findings were disappearing with nothing saying they had been suppressed, so a reader seeing 61 could not tell it from a design that genuinely has 61. That is the vacuous zero `SweepScope.parked` exists to prevent, reintroduced one rule over by the change that was fixing it. `SweepScope.suppressed_by_parked_idea` now counts them by category, so the total reconciles: **61 reported + 33 suppressed (contradiction 3, unresolved_setup 27, unthreaded_cluster 3)**. That is option **(b)**'s reporting half, and it makes the two deliberate-state mechanisms behave alike instead of one reporting and one hiding.

═══ ⚠️ THE OPTION (a) COUNTER-ARGUMENT THIS NODE RAISED, AND WHAT HAPPENED TO IT ═══

This node's own objection to (a) was: *"`CONTRADICTS` between two proposed ideas may be genuinely worth surfacing — 'you are holding two ideas that cannot both hold' is useful, and this silences it too."*

**That objection stands and was overruled deliberately, not answered** — but cut 3 blunts it considerably: those contradictions are no longer invisible, they are counted as suppressed. If brainstorm-time contradictions later prove worth surfacing in full, the channel now exists and is not the DEFECT count.

═══ ⭐ THE WITHDRAWN/PARKED DISTINCTION ═══

**Withdrawn skips on EITHER side for `contradiction`; parked skips only when NEITHER side claims anything.**

A first cut folded `proposed` in with `rejected`/`superseded` and broke `a_proposed_decision_is_not_treated_as_withdrawn` — a DELIBERATE counterweight recording that *"a parked idea that conflicts with an accepted decision is a real thing to settle."* That test is RIGHT and survives: a withdrawal is a positive act that RETIRES a conflict; being unclaimed is not.

═══ SCOPE — DECISION ONLY ═══

`is_parked_idea` checks the node TYPE. `CONTRADICTS` is declared `from: "*" to: "*"` and `Requirement.status` ALSO defaults to `proposed`, so an untyped predicate would have silenced conflicts between requirements merely awaiting the user's word — 51 of them in reflow2's own design.

═══ 🛑 NOT INERT ON EXISTING DESIGNS ═══

`Decision.status` carries `default: proposed`, so there is no unlabelled Decision and silence was never reachable. Every proposed Decision in every existing design changes behaviour the moment this lands. Measured on reflow2's own design: **89 → 78 → 61 reported, with 33 now declared as suppressed rather than dropped.**

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
═══ 📌 THE QUESTION AS ORIGINALLY POSED — PRESERVED VERBATIM ═══

*Restored deliberately. Answering this node REPLACED its text, no snapshot held the prior value, and the only copy came back in the write's own reply. A record that erases the question it answers cannot be reviewed, and `unclaimed_findings`' standing rule is to close a finding "never by overwriting what you are closing". Everything below is the node as it stood before 2026-08-26.*

From `art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-08-26`, item F-03. **RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.**

📌 Distinct from `fact:the-same-four-frictions-hit-two-independent-sessions-on-different-projects-the-same-day`, which the guard offered: that node MEASURES what happened across two sessions; this asks what `proposed` should MEAN to the structural layer, which is a design question that outlives the measurement.

WHAT HAPPENED. The hxm_program hub followed the `brainstorm` skill exactly — ideas as `proposed` Decisions, linked with `CONTRADICTS` / `ANTICIPATES` / `DEPENDS_ON` and evidence on each edge, which is what step 4 instructs. `detect_defects` then reported the `CONTRADICTS` edge as a **`contradiction`** warning, the linked ideas as an **`unthreaded_cluster`**, and each `ANTICIPATES` edge as **`unresolved_setup`** (*"X anticipates Y but nothing follows through"*). **Defects went 2 → 7 over a day of doing the prescribed thing**, and `loop_status` repeated *"7 structural defects outstanding"* at every hand-off. ⭐ Their diagnosis is exact: *"the skill says 'do not run detect-and-ask over brainstormed nodes', but the defect detectors have no such exemption."*

🛑 THIS IS THE PREDICTED CLASS, ARRIVING THE DAY IT WAS PREDICTED. reflow2 fixed the same disease for ONE detector on 2026-08-26: `unallocated_component` counted twelve deliberately-parked tool-surface slices as holes, so recording the correct judgement degraded the instrument. `chg:unallocated-component-reads-the-ruling` recorded the class as still open in as many words: *"nothing checks that a NEW structural detector reads the ruling. The next one written will have the same hole for the same reason."* F-03 is that, from a different project, on the same day.

⚠️ BUT THE `parks` MECHANISM DOES NOT REACH IT, AND THAT IS THE INTERESTING PART. `GOVERNED_BY ruling: parks` requires an **ACCEPTED Decision** to point at — deliberately, so a deliberate state can never be asserted without a ruling that says why. Right for a tool-surface slice. **Wrong for a brainstormed idea.** An idea has no ruling to point at and should not need one: **its `proposed` status IS the statement that it asserts nothing.** Demanding a parking Decision per brainstormed idea would add exactly the ceremony the brainstorm skill exists to remove. ⇒ So this is not "apply the existing fix more widely". It asks whether **`proposed` is itself a sweep class**, alongside parked.

OPTIONS, none chosen at the time:

**(a) Structural detectors skip relation edges on `proposed` Decisions.** Narrow: the node still exists, still counts, still searchable — only its inference-layer edges stop being read as commitments. ⚠️ Counter: `CONTRADICTS` between two proposed ideas may be genuinely worth surfacing — *"you are holding two ideas that cannot both hold"* is useful, and this silences it too.

**(b) A `proposed` sweep class reported like `parked` — counted, never silenced.** `detect_defects` already carries `swept.parked`; add the same treatment. ⚠️ Counter: two sweep classes with different rules to learn, and it does not answer WHICH detectors should sweep.

**(c) Fix it per-detector, as `unallocated_component` was.** Honest and slow. ⚠️ Counter: that is exactly how the class got here — `req:a-deliberate-state-is-not-a-defect` was implemented detector by detector and nothing noticed the gaps.

**(d) ⭐ A CHECK THAT EVERY STRUCTURAL DETECTOR ANSWERS THE QUESTION.** Not a fix but a gate: no structural detector ships without stating what it does with deliberate states — parked, proposed, discontinued. ⚠️ Counter: meta-work, fixes nothing already broken, pays only on detectors not yet written. **But it is the only option that stops the next one.**

📌 A SECOND-ORDER COST WORTH NAMING: the defect count is a NUMBER THE USER IS SHOWN AT EVERY HAND-OFF. reflow2's own graph reports 91 today. A count that grows when you do the right thing teaches people to stop reading it — which is how a real defect hides.
properties.name: DECIDED — a parked idea asserts nothing, and each finding kind states whether it reads that
properties.rationale:
Option (d) — "a check that every structural detector answers the question" — was marked on this node as the only option that stops the NEXT one, and it shipped as `every_category_states_whether_it_reads_proposed`: an exhaustive match over `HealCategory` in the test suite, so a new category cannot compile until its author has written down where it stands. Both answers are legitimate; an unconsidered category is not. It is the sibling of `every_category_is_listed_in_all`, which exists one rule over for the same reason.

That guard is the point of the change, not the three call sites. This is the THIRD instance of one class — `unallocated_component` never reading a parking ruling though two siblings did, F-01's replay contract enforced field by field with nothing checking it, and now this — and `chg:unallocated-component-reads-the-ruling` predicted this exact recurrence in advance: "nothing checks that a NEW structural detector reads the ruling. The next one written will have the same hole for the same reason." It was found in the field the next day. A rule maintained by hand with nothing checking it is a rule that silently stops being true.

The principle was already written down in FOUR places and implemented in ONE — `zero_degree_finding`'s "a parked thought that correctly shapes nothing yet", the schema's "ONLY AN ACCEPTED DECISION DISCONTINUES ANYTHING", `loop_status`'s silence on a proposed Decision with no approver, and the parks ruling's requirement of an accepted Decision. Writing a principle down four times is not implementing it.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS A FINDING, 2026-08-19, split out of `fact:changing-one-sentence-in-a-long-decision-cost-a-full-6242-character-resend` because it had been filed under the wrong fix. Nothing built, nothing asked for.

**WHAT HAPPENED, twice in one session.** A `Decision` was written with a closing tag and the `rationale` ARGUMENT emitted inside the `decision` parameter. Both calls **succeeded**. What landed was a decision body ending in tool-call markup, and no `rationale` property at all:

  1. `dec:idea-parks-shipped-...` — body ended `</decision>` then `<parameter name="rationale">…`
  2. `dec:idea-what-is-reflow2s-part-in-an-automated-translation` — body ended `</decision>` then `<rationale>…</rationale></invoke>`

**NO LAYER NOTICED.** Not the schema (a string is a string), not `undeclared` (the property is declared and was simply absent), not the revision block (it faithfully reported replacing one property — it just cannot know the replacement is corrupt), not the dedup guard, not `detect_defects`. Both were caught only because the reply was read. **A design brain silently carrying `</invoke>` inside a Decision's prose is a worse outcome than any awkward edit**, because everything downstream — `search_design`'s index, the embedding field, a `where-am-i` narration, an export a person reads — treats it as content.

🛑 **AND IT IS NOT THE `resolve_decision` CASE.** Both were FIRST writes of NEW nodes. A resolution-append tool would not have been reachable and would have prevented neither. Filing these with the resend measurement was an error, corrected the same day when Anthony asked for the evidence to be walked through.

✅ **MEASURED, AND IT IS THE REASSURING ANSWER: THIS IS NEW, NOT LONG-STANDING.** The committed export was scanned — all 2,607 nodes, every string property, for closing tool-call tags and `<parameter name=` — and found **0**. So no earlier session left absorbed markup in this graph, and the two instances above (both since corrected) are the only ones. The scan is ~10 lines of Python and is the cheap form of the check any guard would institutionalise.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
IDEAS, and none is as cheap as it first looks

**A. Reject a text property whose value contains tool-call markup.**
   ⚠️ COUNTER, AND IT IS FATAL TO THE NAIVE FORM: this very node, and the fact it was split from, both quote `</decision>` and `</invoke>` ON PURPOSE — and the scan above found exactly those two as its only hits once they existed. A rule matching those strings anywhere would refuse the only two nodes in the design that document the bug. Any guard has to key on SHAPE — markup at the TAIL of a value, immediately followed by what parses as another parameter name — not on the strings appearing at all.

**B. Warn rather than refuse.** Surface it the way `undeclared` surfaces an unknown property: the write lands, the reply says "this value ends in what looks like a tool-call boundary". Cheaper, no false-refusal risk, and it fails in the safe direction. ⚠️ But it inherits `undeclared`'s own disease if it ever fires on correct writes — which is the exact complaint hxm_program filed about `ChangeEvent.description`.

**C. A periodic scan rather than a write-time check.** The 10-line scan above, run in CI over the committed export. Catches the class with no false-refusal risk and no per-write cost, at the price of finding it later rather than at the moment of the write. ⚠️ Later may be fine here: the failure is silent but not destructive — nothing else breaks while it sits.

**D. Do nothing, and treat it as a caller defect.** Defensible: the caller emitted a malformed call and the transport accepted it. ⚠️ Counter: reflow2's whole posture is that a silent wrong write is worse than a loud refusal, and this is a silent wrong write. `dec:two-sided-accept` and the dedup guard both exist because the design does not trust a write to be right just because it parsed.

**E. The generalisation worth naming.** `cap:a-revising-write-says-whether-the-state-survived` computes whether the REPLACED state survived. Nothing computes whether the REPLACEMENT is plausible. Those are different questions and only the first is built.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⚠️ HONEST BOUNDS, stated so this is not over-read

· n = 2, one session, one caller, one model. Not a rate.
· Both were on parameters over 4,000 characters, and none of roughly thirty short writes the same day malformed — suggestive that long free-text arguments are where boundaries get mis-emitted, but observational and confounded, since the long writes also carry the most retyped text.
· NO USER REPORTED THIS. It is a self-host observation, and by `dec:idea-field-evidence-is-a-prioritisation-input` it ranks below anything two projects filed this week. What makes it worth recording at all is that the failure is SILENT and lands in the durable record.
· STILL NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any USER's graph carries such markup. Only this design was scanned, and it is the one graph whose caller is known.
properties.name: OPEN — a prose field swallowed tool-call markup and the write SUCCEEDED: nothing refuses, flags or notices a node whose body ends in `</decision><rationale>…</invoke>`
properties.rationale: Split into its own node rather than left inside the resend fact because the two were filed together only by coincidence of timing, and that coincidence led to a wrong recommendation — that `resolve_decision` would fix both. It fixes one. Recorded as an open question rather than a proposal because the obvious guard is not obvious: the naive string match would refuse the very nodes that document the defect, which is a good reason to think before building. Kept explicitly below the field-reported items in priority, per the design's own rule that field evidence outranks self-host observation, so that recording it does not smuggle it up the queue. The dedup guard named the fact it was split from, which is correct behaviour and was read before declaring them distinct — the split is deliberate, not an accident of wording.

properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Anthony, 2026-08-29, taking the copy-vs-reference sub-question off `dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs` as the first thing to settle.

═══ FIRST, WHAT IS ALREADY ANSWERED — AND IT WAS ANSWERED HERE BEFORE ═══

The sub-question was posed as a fork: *does an inherited decision keep the hub's id, or get copied?* — "a copy is a second source of truth" against one horn, "a reference means the child's graph cannot be read alone" against the other.

**It is not a fork, and `dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs` already worked this out on 2026-08-12** under Anthony's mutable/immutable framing: `mirror_surface` writes the far side in as FOREIGN NODES, and that framing *"collapses three of the four costs the union framing raised"*. Re-read in `crates/reflow2-core/src/export.rs` on 2026-08-29 and it holds — a mirror is **a pinned copy that keeps the origin's id and is marked not-yours-to-edit**: nodes land in the local store so the child reads alone; each gets `provenance: imported`; the mirrored Project carries `mirror_of` / `mirror_content_hash` / `mirrored_at` / `mirror_nodes` so disagreement is COMPUTABLE; local edges attach as ordinary edges because *"foreignness is a property of the node, never of the link"*; collisions are refused, never merged.

📌 **AND THE BLOCKER THAT NODE NAMES IS NOW FIXED, WHICH IT DOES NOT KNOW.** Its trial ended: *"mirror_surface HAS NO REFRESH... 12 of 13 ids collided with the previous mirror of the same design... the staleness register READS FRESH after a failed refresh"*, and it calls that *"the concrete blocker under every option in this node"*. `mirror_surface` now detects a refresh by `mirror_of`, removes what it previously held (recorded in `mirror_nodes` on the mirrored Project), reports `withdrawn`, and **REFUSES before writing** when a withdrawal would orphan a host edge — citing that exact 12-of-13 measurement in its own comment. The blocker is gone; the three things that trial left explicitly open are not all gone with it.

═══ 🛑 SO THE OPEN HALF IS NARROWER, AND IT IS THE #368 SHAPE ONE BOUNDARY OUT ═══

Both nodes discuss authority in the abstract — *"who may accept intent in the overlap"*, *"is a mirrored decision BINDING or only VISIBLE"* — and the mutable/immutable framing concluded the rule becomes *"enforced by construction"* because you cannot write a design you cannot write to. **That is true for editing and false for the gate.** Measured 2026-08-29:

1. `published_promises()` (`graph.rs:1352`) scans **Requirements** carrying `designation: published`. A surface holds those, published Interfaces, the artifacts that SPECIFY/REALIZE them, and the Project. **No Contributor is ever in a surface.**
2. `mirror_surface` carries only *"edges wholly inside what we actually mirrored"*. A Decision's `AUTHORED_BY role=approver` points at a Contributor — outside the set, so **the edge is silently dropped**.
3. `tools/check_intent_authority.py` contains **zero** occurrences of `provenance`, `imported`, `mirror` or `graph_id`. It walks every node where `settles_intent()` holds and demands an approver.

⇒ **A published Decision arrives in the child `accepted` and unattributed, and the child's ENFORCED gate fails its build on a node it is structurally forbidden to fix.** Not a hypothetical: it is `cap:an-acknowledgement-says-whose-judgement-it-was` failing again — settled intent minted with no field able to carry an approver, tripping `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word`. #368 fixed that inside one graph on 2026-08-29; nothing has asked it across two, because nobody has ever published a Decision.

⭐ **THE QUESTION IS THEREFORE NOT COPY-VS-REFERENCE. IT IS WHETHER AUTHORITY TRAVELS WITH THE DECISION** — the concrete form of the "hard half nobody has answered" on `dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs`.

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══

**(a) The surface carries the approver as a foreign Contributor, and the gate reads foreignness.** The hub owner arrives beside the decision, marked `imported`; `check_intent_authority` accepts approved-by-a-foreign-approver instead of reporting missing. ⭐ It answers *"whose word governs a child that inherited a decision it never approved?"* **by name, in the record, permanently** — the honest form of the authority claim rather than a silent one. ⚠️ Counter: child graphs accumulate foreign people, and every scoped read taking a `contributor_id` must then tell a local person from a mirrored one — `loop_status`'s scoped mode included. Making the claim explicit and durable is also exactly what a reader hostile to the whole feature would point at.

**(b) Decisions cross as VISIBLE ONLY — no `GOVERNED_BY` across the boundary.** The child reads the hub's reasoning and inherits no authority, so the gate never meets foreign settled intent and none of the above is built. ⚠️ Counter: a sibling can still re-derive a ruling its neighbour already made, which was the original complaint. **But note this counter is weaker than it looks here:** the argument for the downward direction was that it moves WHY rather than status, and visibility delivers WHY in full. Binding adds only enforcement.

**(c) Both — publish for visibility now, defer binding.** ⚠️ Counter: `dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs` records that *"leaders decide and sub-projects inherit"* is the BINDING reading said out loud, so shipping visibility alone answers a question Anthony did not ask.

**(d) Nothing crosses.** ⚠️ Counter: declining should be explicit rather than by neglect.

📌 **PREREQUISITE UNDER EVERY OPTION EXCEPT (d):** `Decision` carries no `designation` property at all today, so the opt-in shape `set_requirement_designation` uses would have to be given to it first.

⚠️ **AND THE OTHER TWO THINGS THE 2026-08-12 TRIAL LEFT OPEN ARE STILL OPEN**, so this must not be read as clearing them: whether a host's committed export should CARRY mirrored nodes or merely NAME them by pin, and what a refresh owes a host edge whose foreign target was RENAMED rather than withdrawn — the refusal handles withdrawal, and a rename is the case where both ids arrive.
properties.name: OPEN — copy-vs-reference is already settled by mirroring; what nothing has asked is whether a published Decision's APPROVER survives the crossing, and measured today it does not
properties.rationale:
Started as its own node rather than folded into either near-match, after reading both in full at the duplicate guard's prompt. `dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs` asks WHAT MAY CROSS a boundary; `dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs` asks WHICH GRAPHS A SESSION SEES and works out the mirroring mechanics. This asks a third thing neither reaches: given that mirroring is the mechanism, does the APPROVER survive the crossing — and it is answered, negatively, by three facts about code that were true the whole time.

Folding it into the several-graphs node was the close call, since that is where the mutable/immutable framing lives. Kept separate because that node's conclusion — the ownership rule becomes "enforced by construction" — is exactly the claim this refutes in one specific place, and a refutation buried inside the node it refutes cannot be found by anyone reading either.

THE METHOD IS THE POINT AND IT IS THE THIRD TIME ON THIS THREAD. `dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs` carries its own correction: "the claim was made from the capability's one-line description rather than from the code... READ THE EXPORT, NOT THE SUMMARY." Applied here it dissolved the copy-vs-reference fork instead of answering it, and then produced a defect prediction with a file and line for each of its three legs — refutable by reading rather than arguable.

The options are kept as four rather than collapsed toward the interesting one, and (b) is written at full strength deliberately: visibility-only needs none of this machinery, and the strongest argument for the downward direction — that it moves WHY rather than status — is fully served by visibility alone. That cuts against the option this session found most interesting, which is why it is on the record rather than in the conversation.

Recorded as brainstorming. Nothing here is proposed for building, and the approver-loss finding is a prediction about code nobody has run, not an observed failure.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From StoryFlow's principles document (art:storyflow-engineering-principles), whose closing note states the case better than a summary can: "Structure alone found none of these. The leverage of a graph is not tidiness — it is that a graph CAN bind each rule to an executable check and then report which rules have none."

MEASURED ON THIS DESIGN, 2026-08-22. 19 DesignRules. 16 have NO Verification pointing at them. Of those 16, only 3 are `enforced: true` — and `unverified_enforced_rule`, the detector that exists, fires ONLY on enforced rules. So 13 unchecked rules are structurally invisible: written down, checked by nothing, and never mentioned again.

THE SHAPE IS fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it, one level up. There it was optional FIELDS staying empty because no detector noticed their absence. Here it is whole RULES, and the same enforced-only blind spot that hid change_axis_unstated hides these.

THE OPTIONS:
(a) Widen `unverified_enforced_rule` to all rules. Simple, and it turns 3 findings into 16 overnight on this design alone — probably too loud, and loud-on-day-one is how a whole category gets filtered forever.
(b) A separate AGGREGATE finding: "N of M rules have no check" — one question, one acknowledgement, the shape `change_axis_unstated` and `unreviewed_ideas` already use. Naturally quiet, and it asks exactly the question the document says is the point.
(c) Require a rule to state WHY it has no check, rather than to have one. The document's own note says "this rule has no detector and here is why" is a legitimate end state — so the finding becomes not "you lack a check" but "you have neither a check nor a reason".

⭐ (c) IS THE INTERESTING ONE and it is not obvious. It reframes the goal: not that every rule is automated — several of these nine explicitly cannot be — but that no rule is SILENTLY unautomated. That is the distinction review_relations already makes for ideas, where a written note is a full answer and not a weaker one.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded rather than resolved: reflow2 has an accepted non-goal that it does not judge whether a check is MEANINGFUL. Reporting that a rule has no check at all stays the right side of that line — an absence, not a quality judgement — but (c) edges closer, because "is that reason good enough?" is precisely the judgement the non-goal refuses.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 report a rule that nothing checks, including the UNENFORCED ones? 13 of this design's 19 rules are invisible to the detector that exists
properties.rationale: Recorded because the measurement is concrete and the blind spot is the same one this session already fixed once for change events. Not proposed as intent because (a), (b) and (c) are a real fork with different costs, and because it may be subsumed by the governing question about whether reflow2 ships rule machinery at all.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-12.

HIS WORDS: "I think the 'immutability' of satisfied requirements should be a big safety measure of reflow2 projects (including itself, which is a reflow2 project). I mean it shouldn't be impossible to change a satisfied requirement or capability, but there should be safety checks in place that make it hard to change without specific confirmation. maybe once a requirement is satisfied, particularly if it had been tested and demonstrated, should basically become a python tuple."

⭐ THE FIELD EVIDENCE IS A SECOND USER, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH RECORDING. His brother Alex, evaluating reflow2 for his own work: "Yes potentially. As long as it doesn't mess with the core functionality." Anthony's read of the concern: "he really likes using reflow2 and he's concerned that we'll somehow change reflow2 away from what it currently is and what he likes." That is `rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party` arriving on its own terms — the worry is not deletion, it is DRIFT.

⚠️ WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, AND WHY THIS IS NOT IT. `req:inviolable-intent` is ACCEPTED and covers the same family: "intent that no downstream decision may trade away — a key performance parameter... COMPUTE a violation rather than rely on anyone remembering... A KPP that nothing checks is a comment." But a KPP is DECLARED — opt-in, stated up front, about a THRESHOLD VALUE. Anthony is describing something EARNED — a requirement acquires protection by having been satisfied and demonstrated, retrospectively and automatically, and it is about the requirement's TEXT and STATE rather than a numeric threshold. The KPP protects what you said mattered; this would protect what you have already built and proven. Alex's concern is the second one, and it has no mechanism.

═══ WHAT PROTECTION ACTUALLY EXISTS, MEASURED 2026-08-12 ═══

  accepted requirements                              110
    with a satisfier carrying a PASSING check    102  (92%)
  unproven_capabilities (built, no passing check)     0
  unexamined_claims                                   0
