properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-18, with Anthony reporting the same experience independently and sharpening the idea the same day.

🔒 **REDACTED 2026-08-19 ON ANTHONY'S INSTRUCTION.** The illustrative example originally named a real third party by full name and employer. He is not a user of reflow2, never consented, and was described here alongside a judgement about his technical ability — in a PUBLIC repository. **The design point never needed the name**, so it is stated generically below. Nothing else in this node changed. *(The name remains in git history at `e695506` and later; removing it there would mean rewriting a public repo's history, which was judged disproportionate.)*

⚠️ WHO IS WHO, corrected by Anthony 2026-08-18: **100% of reflow2's actual development is Anthony's.** Alex is a USER of reflow2 on his own work project. His reports are FIELD EVIDENCE about the product, never development of it.

ALEX'S SITUATION, AND IT IS WHAT MAKES THIS URGENT: he is using reflow2 on a real project AT WORK and is about to show it to coworkers. His worry is not his own comprehension — he has already found the workaround — it is that **his coworkers will meet the jargon cold.** So this is a barrier to reflow2 SPREADING inside an organisation, met by a real user at the exact moment he tries to spread it.

THE WORKAROUND BOTH USERS INDEPENDENTLY INVENTED:
  · ANTHONY: *"I often state when I'm given a decision by reflow2 of 'please walk me through this in plain and simple English with your recommendation'."*
  · ALEX: *"when he usually asked the agent to remove reflow2 jargon from the dialogue, it gave him some really good answers."*

⭐ **THE WORKAROUND WORKS EVERY TIME, WHICH IS THE FINDING.** Neither user reports the agent being UNABLE to speak plainly — they report having to ASK. The capability is present and the default is wrong. Same shape as `req:a-question-arrives-with-a-reading`, whose own evidence paragraph reads: *"a shape a user has to request each time is a default in the wrong place."* Two independent instances of one mechanism: the agent has the behaviour and performs it only on demand.

THE IDEA, IN ALEX'S FRAMING: a **PERSONA** stored per person on a project, which the agent uses to shape every response back to them — *"kind of a lens."* **His example was a friend who is not technical at all but knows baseball deeply — a professional coach.** If that person used reflow2, the agent should talk to him **like a baseball coach**. Not simpler English. A different domain's language.

⚠️ **ALEX NAMED THE DIVISION OF LABOUR HIMSELF:** *"this is really the agent's job, but reflow2 can store the persona for a person using reflow2 on a project."* reflow2 REMEMBERS WHO IT IS TALKING TO; the agent does the speaking. That matches `dec:three-party-checks` — the LLM speaks, the graph remembers.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐ ANTHONY'S REFINEMENT, 2026-08-18 — WHERE THE QUESTION GETS ASKED

*"maybe ask as an initial question after the user types /where-am-i, the agent can ask: 'who are you? This will shape how I interact with you and so that I can respond in an appropriate manner'."* Plus: *"you can probably make an educated guess by that me logging in on this machine is AJ or Anthony, so you could probably store a tiny blurb in my contributor about who I am."*

**WHY `where-am-i` IS THE RIGHT PLACE.** That skill already fires *"at the start of any session on an existing design"*, so it is the one moment reliably reached before the agent starts talking — no new trigger needed, and it is what a NEW person hits first.

🛑 **AND THE SKILL ALREADY CARRIED A PERSONA-SHAPED ASSUMPTION WITH THE WRONG DEFAULT BAKED IN.** Its own words were *"Write it as prose for the person who described this project to you."* **It assumed the reader had briefed you.** Alex's coworkers briefed nobody; nor did the coach in his example. Fixed in #246.

⚠️ **"WHO ARE YOU?" DOES NOT VIOLATE THE NEVER-ASK RULE.** `dec:idea-the-graph-vocabulary-never-reaches-the-user` forbids making the user choose an INTERNAL CATEGORY — a question about reflow2's schema only reflow2 can answer. Asking about their background asks for the one fact reflow2 cannot look up. **They are opposites.**

📌 **ON GUESSING FROM THE LOGIN:** machine identity is available to the AGENT through its harness, never to the graph. So a login guess is the agent's to make and the graph's to store. **But a guess must be OFFERED AND CONFIRMED, never assumed** — `req:defaults-do-not-assert`.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐⭐ THE BIGGEST FINDING, FROM WRITING ANTHONY'S OWN PERSONA

**A PERSONA IS A VOCABULARY SWAP, NOT A DIFFICULTY DIAL — and implementing it as "simplify" would be wrong for every user tested so far.**

Anthony is a practising systems engineer: *requirement, interface, allocation, verification, TRL, KPP* are NATIVE and softening them would patronise him. What he wants dropped is **reflow2's internal vocabulary** — gap, loop, detector, node id, "the loop owes". **The baseball coach wants baseball.** Alex's coworkers want their own domain. **None of the three wants "simpler English"; each wants a DIFFERENT vocabulary**, and only one wants less technical density.

🛑 So the obvious implementation — a plain-language mode, a reading-level setting — **would be wrong for the primary user, wrong for the coach, and only accidentally right for a generic newcomer.**

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ WHAT WAS DONE, so option (a) is TRIALLED rather than theorised

📌 **`Contributor.description` ALREADY EXISTS** — free text, optional. **A persona needs NO schema change to trial.**

**Anthony's persona was written into `who:ajs`.description at his request** — agent-drafted, then corrected and enriched by him.

⚠️ **AND IT SHARES A FIELD WITH SOMETHING ELSE.** `description` means *who this person is in the design's authorship* — provenance. A persona is *how to speak to them* — presentation. **Two purposes, one field.** Whether Contributor should get a real `persona` property is THE question this node turns on; the trial is reversible.

⚠️⚠️ **AND A PERSONA DOES NOT TRAVEL BETWEEN GRAPHS — established 2026-08-19 when Anthony asked whether Alex would meet his own stored background by cloning this repo.** He would not, in the sense that matters: `who:alex` lives in REFLOW2's design graph, while Alex uses reflow2 on HIS OWN project, whose graph has its own Contributor nodes. The installer sets up the `docs/design/<project>.json` convention and **never copies reflow2's graph into a user's project** (verified in `tools/reflow2_init.py`). **So a persona is PER-GRAPH, not per-person: someone working across three projects answers three times and nothing carries the answer between them.** That may well be right — a design graph is a shared team artifact, not a user profile — but it is an unstated consequence of storing personas on `Contributor` and it belongs in whichever option wins.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
WHY THIS IS DISTINCT FROM THE ADJACENT NODES, all read first

· `req:a-question-arrives-with-a-reading` + `cap:gap-carries-a-reading` govern **the shape of a QUESTION**. **This covers EVERY reply** — status readouts, gap lists, explanations — most of which contain no decision at all.
· `dec:idea-the-graph-vocabulary-never-reaches-the-user` governs **what the agent may ASK**. This governs **what it SAYS BACK**.
· AND THE AXIS IS NEW: all three say *plain, in the user's own language*. **None contemplates a DIFFERENT DOMAIN'S language.**

WHAT THE DESIGN ALREADY HOLDS

📌 `req:no-se-knowledge` — *"the user never needs systems engineering."* ⚠️ The twist: for Anthony it must NOT be read as "hide SE" — he wants it.
📌 `req:a-question-arrives-with-a-reading` states the register rule language-independently. **A persona pushes that axis further: not just WHICH language, but WHICH DOMAIN'S.**
📌 `ver:gap-carries-a-reading` (PLANNED) specifies a `skill_lint` whose load-bearing half is a NEGATIVE check — no served text hardcodes English as the answer language. ⭐ **The sibling — no served skill hardcodes an AUDIENCE — is the route to making this mechanically enforced, and it would have caught the defect #246 fixed.**
📌 `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` (dropped) wrote this answer's surviving half in its own closing words: *"domain as a hint to EXTRACTION and phrasing… keeps the honest part of reflow's insight (a biologist should not be told about 'services')."* **Dropped as a REGISTRY; a future session must not read that drop as rejecting this.**
⭐ `chg:bl179-maturity-profile` records Anthony's ruling that **a name no computation reads does not earn its keep.**

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
OPTIONS

(a) **A PERSONA IN `Contributor`** — ✅ **TRIALLED** in `description` for `who:ajs` and `who:alex`. CHEAP and reversible. AGAINST: overloads a provenance field, and free text no computation reads is the shape `Project.domain` already has.
(b) **A SKILL-LEVEL RULE ONLY.** AGAINST: cannot do the baseball case, which needs a fact about a PERSON no skill can know; and it repeats *"a discipline that exists only as an instruction, with nothing able to observe whether it held."*
(c) ⭐ **BOTH, WITH THE ASK AT `where-am-i`** — Anthony's refinement, **and what shipped in #246/#247.** Reasoning: **neither half is useful alone.**
(d) **A PROJECT-LEVEL AUDIENCE.** AGAINST: Alex's problem is a MIXED audience. FOR: the only option that works when the reader is not a modelled Contributor at all.

⚠️ THE HONEST COUNTER TO THE WHOLE IDEA: a persona is a place to store a stereotype. *"Talk to him like a baseball coach"* is charming when the person wrote it themselves and condescending when someone else wrote it about them. **SELF-DESCRIBED vs ASSIGNED is probably the difference between a good feature and a bad one.** The trial took the middle road (agent-drafted, user-confirmed) and that third state should be named, not collapsed into either. **Alex's own entry is marked RELAYED, not self-described, and awaits his correction.**

⚠️ SECOND COUNTER: **a persona shapes the REPLY. It must not shape what gets written down**, or the design's memory degrades into whichever register the last reader preferred.

🔒 THIRD, ADDED 2026-08-19: **a persona is personal data in a shared, possibly public artifact.** This design's own export is public, and the first personas written into it included a third party's full name and employer. **Whatever ships must say what belongs in a persona and what does not** — a self-description, not a dossier, and never a third party who is not present to correct it.

🛑 WHAT NOBODY HAS MEASURED: how much jargon actually reaches the user today, per reply. Both reports are impressions from users who noticed. **reflow2 cannot see it happen** — the leak lives in the conversation and leaves no node.
properties.name: OPEN — should a person using reflow2 carry a stored PERSONA that shapes how the agent speaks to them, the way a lens shapes a photograph?
properties.rationale: Raised from Alex's field report 2026-08-18, sharpened by Anthony the same day, and REDACTED 2026-08-19 on his instruction after he asked whether Alex would encounter his own stored background by cloning this repo. That question surfaced two things worth keeping: the persona does NOT travel between graphs (verified against tools/reflow2_init.py, and now recorded here because it is an unstated consequence of storing personas on Contributor), and this repository is PUBLIC — so an illustrative example naming a real third party by full name and employer, beside a judgement about his technical ability, was a privacy exposure the design point never required. The name is replaced by the generic description that carries the whole argument. A new counter-argument is added stating that whatever ships must bound what a persona may contain, because the first personas written under this idea already overreached.

properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** From a user report, 2026-08-26, relayed. Deliberately written WITHOUT the user's domain or employer: what generalises is the shape, and the specifics belong to them.

═══ WHAT HAPPENED ═══

A user working in a data-intensive domain found that the words their field uses do not map onto reflow2's node types. **So they wrote their own skill to translate between the two** — a private glossary sitting between their vocabulary and what reflow2 will accept.

The worked example, generalised: their domain has a first-class thing that behaves like a *request against a structured body of records*. Their translator decided it was an **Interface**. That may be right, or it may be a category error nobody will notice for months — and **nothing in reflow2 can tell them which.**

⭐ **THE TELL IS THAT THEY BUILT THE TRANSLATOR AT ALL.** That is `req:a-session-says-what-it-did-by-hand-...`'s signal arriving before the tool that records it existed: a user reached for something reflow2 does not serve and built it themselves. Hand-rolled work carries intent, and this is a user saying *the vocabulary gap is real enough to write code about*.

═══ WHY THIS IS HARDER THAN IT LOOKS ═══

The obvious reading is "reflow2's vocabulary is too small". That is probably wrong, and worth saying plainly: SE vocabulary is deliberately abstract so it spans a house, a spacecraft and a service. **The difficulty is not coverage, it is ROUTING** — which of several defensible node types a domain word belongs to, and the fact that more than one is defensible.

A request against a structured body of records could honestly be:
- an **Interface** — it is a contract with a caller, and it has a shape
- a **Capability** — it is a function the system performs
- a **Requirement** — if what matters is the obligation ("answers within X")
- a **Flow** — if what matters is the sequence

**All four are defensible and they lead to different designs.** That is not a gap in the vocabulary; it is a modelling decision the user is being asked to make with no guidance and no way to check the answer.

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) A ROUTING GUIDE — worked examples from domains that are not software.** Not new vocabulary: a document or skill that says "here is a thing that looks like X, here is why it is modelled as Y, here is what breaks if you choose Z." ⚠️ Counter: prose that nobody reads at the moment of the decision, which is exactly what `dec:what-lives-where` argues against.

**(b) THE ROUTING QUESTION ASKED AT CAPTURE, BY THE TOOL.** `capture-intent` already routes a user's words to node types; make the ambiguity explicit — offer the two or three defensible readings with what each buys and costs, and record which was chosen and why. ⚠️ Counter: it slows every capture to serve the ambiguous minority, and the skill's own doctrine is that asking the user which node type to use hands them work that is the agent's.

**(c) MAKE THE USER'S GLOSSARY A FIRST-CLASS THING reflow2 holds.** They built a translator; reflow2 could record the mapping — *"in this design, 'X' means Interface, decided on this date, for this reason"* — so it is consistent, reviewable and inherited by the next session. ⚠️ Counter: a per-design glossary is real vocabulary surface with all three legs to build, and the value rests on an n=1 report.

**(d) NOTHING. The translator working is the system working.** A user extended the tool to fit their domain, which is what an extensible tool is for. ⚠️ Counter: the translation is unreviewable and unversioned, its author cannot tell a good mapping from a bad one, and a wrong early call propagates through every downstream analysis silently.

═══ ⚠️ THE COUNTERWEIGHT THAT MATTERS MOST ═══

**This is n=1, relayed, with no specifics available.** Everything above is inference from a second-hand description. Before building anything, the honest next step is the one this project keeps proving right: get the case in the user's own words. `report_manual_work` now exists precisely to catch reports of this shape — a user going by hand where a tool should have served — and it shipped hours before this was recorded.

📌 RELATED AND ALREADY OPEN: `dec:idea-a-problem-in-the-users-words-should-retrieve-the-tool-that-answers-it` asks the mirror-image question — retrieving the right TOOL from a problem stated in the user's words. This one is about retrieving the right NODE TYPE for a thing in the user's words. Same gap, two surfaces.
properties.name: OPEN — when a user's domain word has no obvious SE node type, they build their own translator; should reflow2 own that translation, and what does it cost to get it wrong?
properties.rationale:
Recorded without the user's domain or employer deliberately, at the owner's request and because the design record is public. The shape generalises and the specifics add nothing a later reader needs; a design graph that carries somebody's work context because it happened to arrive in a conversation is a graph that leaks.

Kept separate from the persona question because they fail differently. The persona is a DELIVERY failure — the mechanism exists and does not reach anyone. This is a ROUTING failure — the mechanism does not exist, and it is not obvious it should, because the difficulty is genuine ambiguity rather than missing vocabulary.

The strongest argument against acting is recorded at full strength: n=1, relayed, no specifics. The strongest argument for is that the user built code to work around it, which is the most expensive signal a user can send short of leaving.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-14, extending Alex's system-of-systems note.

HIS WORDS: *"the graph is the systems engineering 'object' and can have all vertical tiers. However, when a user requests, give me the 'top level management' view, the agent should be able to get the info from the graph and render the user the requested 'view'. I don't know all the DoDAF and UAF views, but there is probably something for 'management' or 'vision'."*

⚠️ **CORRECTED TWICE WITHIN THE HOUR. BOTH CORRECTIONS ARE ON HIS WORD AND BOTH MATTER.**

**CORRECTION 1 — this does not answer Alex.** The first version claimed it *"may dissolve half of the tier question"* and read Alex's UI/API/e2e case as an altitude-view problem. Anthony: *"I think my brother is more indicating that each tier is its own reflow2 graph that others are linked to vertically."* Alex wants SEPARATE GRAPHS PER TIER — a storage question. **The altitude view neither answers nor replaces it.** They compose: a tier-split design still wants an altitude view inside each graph.
  · **ALTITUDE** — how much detail a reader is shown. A VIEW question. No new store, no seam. *This node.*
  · **OWNERSHIP / TIER** — separate graphs, vertically linked. A STORE question. *`dec:idea-a-top-level-graph-holds-what-the-component-graphs-share`, option (b).*
  📌 Kept on the record because an agent reading only Alex's words could build the view, declare the ask satisfied, and leave the real thing unbuilt — which is what this node nearly did.

**CORRECTION 2 — option (c) is CLOSED: the UAF/DoDAF catalogue does not belong in reflow2.** It originally proposed rendering CV-1/CV-2/CV-3/AV-1 as first-class outputs. Anthony: *"we purposefully did not define every UAF/DoDAF view as those are not appropriate for every design project AND reflow2 was meant as 'design anything' and 'build anything'… I left rendering the reflow2 graph to be able to store any design structure/content and left the agent the responsible party for 'rendering' the drawing."* **The division is deliberate: the graph stores any structure, the AGENT draws — mermaid, HTML, markdown, whatever suits.** `req:design-anything` (ACCEPTED) is what forbids binding a design-anything tool to one discipline's catalogue. See `dec:idea-a-view-that-does-not-apply-is-said-so-before-it-is-drawn` for the doctrine in full and for the idea it produced.

═══ ✅ MEASURED: TEN VIEWS EXIST, ZERO SLICE BY ALTITUDE ═══

`tools/render_views.py` renders `functional`, `flows`, `structural`, `traceability`, `released`, `decisions`, `evolution`, `provenance`, `fielded`, `budgets` — held to `dec:views-are-projections` (*"renderer fill-ins are defects"*) and `cap:bl-40` (no-extrapolation).

🛑 **EVERY ONE IS AN ASPECT VIEW: the whole design through one lens. None answers *"show me less."*** An altitude view trades depth for breadth by FILTERING what is shown — Anthony's *"exchange of breadth for depth"* done by the renderer instead of by a decomposition, and therefore **losing nothing**, since the detail stays in the graph. That is its one advantage over the tier-graph route, and it is not an argument against tier graphs, which exist for ownership reasons a view cannot supply.

📌 THE DoDAF MAPPING, KEPT AS CONTEXT AND NOT AS A BUILD TARGET (see correction 2): **CV-1 is titled "Vision"** and is the leadership-facing view with no reflow2 equivalent; **AV-1** is the executive summary; CV-2 taxonomy and CV-3 phasing are largely derivable from `Capability` + containment + Epochs, which `view_evolution` and `view_released` already partly cover. ⚠️ The exact UAF abbreviations were NOT verified against the spec and are deliberately not asserted. **The useful reading is that the MATERIAL for a leadership view is already in the graph — not that reflow2 should ship named standard views.**

═══ THE HARD PART ═══

🛑 **WHAT COMPUTES WHICH NODES ARE "TOP LEVEL"?** An altitude view is only honest if the filter derives from something the design already records. Candidates, none chosen: `Requirement.designation` (`published` vs `internal` — an audience distinction that already exists, and the strongest candidate), `priority`, `concern`, KPP status, distance from the Project root, an explicit tier property. **A filter chosen by the renderer rather than derived from the graph is precisely the "renderer fill-in" the doctrine calls a defect**, so this cannot be settled by taste.

🛑 MODELLING TRAP: `Component.level` (component → subsystem → system → system_of_systems → enterprise) is an **ASSEMBLY** ladder — *part of*. Management/vision altitude is an **ABSTRACTION** ladder. A subsystem is part of a system; a management view is not part of a worker view. Reusing `level` would make `hierarchy_issues` report nonsense.

OPTIONS.
(a) ALTITUDE VIEW DERIVED FROM AN EXISTING PROPERTY — most likely `designation`. Cheapest, no schema change, testable against the no-extrapolation standard.
(b) AN EXPLICIT TIER PROPERTY, projected on. `req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read` demands a computation read it, which this supplies. ⚠️ If tier GRAPHS are ever built, this property and that boundary must not disagree about what a tier is.
(c) ~~RENDER THE NAMED DoDAF VIEWS AS FIRST-CLASS OUTPUTS~~ — **CLOSED on Anthony's word.** The catalogue belongs to the agent, not to reflow2.
(d) LEAVE IT — an agent can answer "show me the top level" conversationally from `graph_report`. Counter: unrepeatable between sessions. ⚠️ Note this is NOT the same as correction 2: leaving the DRAWING to the agent is doctrine, while leaving the FILTER to the agent's judgement is a renderer fill-in. The distinction is what separates this option from (a).

📌 RELATED AND SEPARATE: `dec:idea-document-generation` and `dec:idea-outward-docs-are-rendered-from-the-graph` ask what to DO with a rendered view; this asks whether the projection exists at all.
properties.name: OPEN — reflow2's ten views all slice by ASPECT and none by ALTITUDE, so "show me the top level" has no projection behind it (a SEPARATE need from tier graphs, and NOT a licence to hard-code the DoDAF catalogue)
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill and corrected twice on Anthony's word within the hour — once for misreading Alex's ask as a rendering need, once for proposing that reflow2 ship the named DoDAF views. Both corrections are kept in the text rather than silently replacing it, following `dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs`' precedent, because the two failure modes are worth seeing together: an agent that finds a cheaper adjacent problem and declares the original satisfied, and an agent that reaches for a familiar standard catalogue in a tool deliberately built not to have one. The second is the more likely to recur, since the catalogue is genuinely useful and the pull toward it feels like expertise rather than like a mistake. What survives both corrections is the measurement — ten aspect views, zero altitude views — and the open question of what could honestly compute the filter.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-14.

HIS WORDS, restating settled doctrine first and then adding the new part: *"we purposefully did not define every UAF/DoDAF view as those are not appropriate for every design project AND reflow2 was meant as 'design anything' and 'build anything' type construct. This is why I left rendering the reflow2 graph to be able to store any design structure/content and left the agent the responsible party for 'rendering' the drawing. It'd be like if I requested you to render me an OV-1 of reflow2 right now — you'd refer to the graph and pull what you need; then you'd build me a mermaid diagram or some html file or markdown file to show what the OV-1 is. That being said, sometimes not every systems engineering view is applicable to a given design. Feel like the agent should be able to also say, 'an OV-1 isn't applicable for your design; are you sure you want me to generate?'"*

═══ 📌 THE DOCTRINE THIS RESTS ON, RECORDED SO IT STOPS BEING RE-PROPOSED ═══

**THE UAF/DoDAF VIEW CATALOGUE IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN REFLOW2.** The division is: the GRAPH stores any design structure or content; the AGENT renders the drawing, in whatever medium suits — mermaid, HTML, markdown. Enumerating standard views inside reflow2 would bind a "design anything" tool to one discipline's catalogue, and `req:design-anything` (ACCEPTED) is the requirement that forbids it.
⚠️ **A SESSION PROPOSED EXACTLY THAT AN HOUR EARLIER** — option (c) of `dec:idea-a-view-can-slice-by-altitude-not-only-by-aspect` suggested rendering CV-1/CV-2/CV-3/AV-1 as first-class outputs. **Closed on his word.** It is recorded here because the pull toward hard-coding a familiar catalogue is strong and will recur.

═══ ⭐⭐ THE FINDING: APPLICABILITY AND INVENTION ARE THE SAME QUESTION ═══

`dec:views-are-projections` already holds that **a view is a projection of the graph and renderer fill-ins are DEFECTS**; `cap:bl-40` holds SYNTHESIZE to a no-extrapolation standard.

🛑 **NOW NOTICE WHAT "NOT APPLICABLE" ACTUALLY MEANS.** A view does not apply to a design precisely when the graph lacks the material that view projects from. And if the material is absent, **rendering it anyway REQUIRES the agent to invent the content** — which is the defect the doctrine already forbids. So:

  > *"Is this view applicable?"* and *"would drawing it force me to make things up?"* are **the same question asked at two different times.**

⇒ This is not a new principle. **It is the existing no-fill-in rule moved EARLIER — from a defect caught after the fact, to a question asked before the pen touches paper.** That reframing is what makes it worth building: the rule currently has no moment at which it is enforced, because the only party who could notice is the agent that is already mid-render and motivated to produce something.

⇒ AND IT MAKES APPLICABILITY COMPUTABLE RATHER THAN A JUDGEMENT. *"Does an OV-1 apply?"* is a matter of taste. *"Does this graph hold operational actors, activities and the exchanges between them, and how many?"* is a count. **The second is answerable by reflow2 without reflow2 ever knowing what an OV-1 is.**

═══ THE SHAPE THAT KEEPS THE CATALOGUE OUT ═══

The agent DECLARES the projection it intends to draw — the node types and edge types it will read. reflow2 answers with what it actually holds and what is absent. The agent then either renders, or says *"an OV-1 isn't applicable for your design; are you sure?"* **reflow2 never learns the view's name, so the catalogue stays with the agent and the counting stays with the graph.** That division is the same one `dec:three-party-checks` already sets: the LLM speaks, the graph counts, the human decides.

⚠️ AND IT MUST ASK, NEVER REFUSE. His wording is *"are you sure you want me to generate?"* — a warning with a way through, not a block. Consistent with `dec:ask-not-repair` and `dec:report-dont-judge`. A sparse view is sometimes exactly what the user wants to see; an empty OV-1 is itself a finding about the design.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.
(a) LEAVE IT TO THE AGENT — status quo. It can already look at the graph and judge. Counter: unrepeatable between sessions, and the party judging is the one being asked to produce a deliverable, which is the weakest possible position for saying "this cannot honestly be drawn".
(b) ⭐ REFLOW2 ANSWERS A DECLARED PROJECTION — the agent names node/edge types, reflow2 returns counts and absences. Keeps the catalogue out, makes the answer computable and repeatable. Counter: an agent can declare the wrong projection and get a confident answer to the wrong question.
(c) A SERVED SKILL carries the discipline — a render-a-view skill whose steps include checking the material before drawing. Cheapest, and consistent with skills being where disciplines live. Counter: it is another instruction, and `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` is the standing evidence that instructions lose to urgency.
(d) HARD-CODE PER-VIEW APPLICABILITY RULES. **CLOSED on Anthony's word** — this is the catalogue-in-reflow2 route `req:design-anything` forbids.

🛑 THE LIMIT WORTH STATING: material presence is necessary but not sufficient. A view can be structurally renderable and still be the wrong instrument for the domain — an OV-1 of a machine shop might have actors and activities to draw and still be a category error. **Counting cannot see that; only the human can.** So (b) at its best reports *"here is what I hold and what I lack"*, and the applicability verdict stays with the person — which is the same honest division reflow2 uses everywhere else.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 be able to tell an agent that a requested view does not apply to this design, given "would rendering it require invention?" is the same question as "is it applicable?"
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill. Recorded separately from the altitude-view node because they are separately answerable: reflow2 could learn to report what a declared projection would find without ever gaining an altitude view, and vice versa. The reason this is worth a node rather than a note is the equivalence at its centre — applicability and invention turn out to be one question asked at two times — which converts a matter of taste into a count, and gives the existing no-fill-in doctrine the enforcement moment it currently lacks. Anthony's restatement of why the view catalogue is deliberately absent is recorded here too, because a session proposed hard-coding it an hour earlier and the pull toward a familiar standard catalogue will recur.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-14, after relaying a Grok 4.6 feedback file from one of Alex's projects.

HIS WORDS: *"This type of feedback is generated by the agent for a project via something like the statement of 'reflow2 is still a development project - please note any issues or gaps or opportunities to improve reflow2 at path/to/feedback.md'. Then the agent provides this feedback. It is probably more 'machine-to-machine' type feedback… we should probably formalize this feedback option within reflow2 with the specific direction of that the agent writing it can write it specifically for another agent - this is cutting out the human to provide specific feedback from one agent to another (you in this case), so it can probably be very efficient and remove any fluff that is needed when a human is in the loop."*

═══ ⭐⭐ THE EVIDENCE FOR IT IS ALREADY IN: THE INFORMAL VERSION WORKED ═══

The file this idea came from produced **four independently reproduced defects** (`fact:agent-feedback-corroborated-2026-08-14`) — the near-duplicate guard firing on golden-thread siblings and across node types, `add_decision` unable to merge without resending the body, correct capture inflating loop debt, and `get_node` missing silently on a type with one instance. **A different agent, on a different model, on a different graph, hit four of them the same day without having read the file.** That yield came from an ad-hoc prompt with no format, no channel and no tooling. Formalising raises the yield of something already proven rather than betting on an untested idea.

😀 AND THE CAPTURE OF THIS VERY NODE SUPPLIED A SEVENTH INSTANCE OF ITS OWN HEADLINE DEFECT: creating this Decision was REFUSED as a near-duplicate of `fact:agent-feedback-corroborated-2026-08-14` — the TemporalFact recording that feedback, written two minutes earlier. A fact about what was reported and a decision about what channel should carry it are not the same write.

═══ 🛑 THE COUNTER, AND IT IS ABOUT WHICH HUMAN IS BEING CUT OUT ═══

**Two different humans are in this loop, and only one of them can be removed.**
  · **THE ROUTING HUMAN** — the person who currently has to read an agent's friction note, understand it, and relay it. Removing them is pure gain and is what Anthony is describing.
  · **THE CONSENTING HUMAN** — the person whose project the feedback was written inside. `report-friction` redacts the user's design content and **never files without asking**, and the Grok file honoured that unprompted: *"Per report-friction: do not open a public issue without asking. This file is the local log."*

⚠️ **A channel that carries agent-authored feedback off the machine without that second human is an exfiltration path**, however good the intent. `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` exists for exactly this, and the file shows the discipline working — *"Product/design content is summarized by type and count, not quoted."*
⇒ THE HONEST FORM: **the agent WRITES freely for another agent; the human still decides whether it LEAVES.** Efficiency is gained in the authoring and the reading, never in the consent.

═══ 🛑 A SHARPER COUNTER TO "REMOVE THE FLUFF" ═══

**What made that file valuable was not its brevity — it was that its claims were CHECKABLE.** Item 5 named the tool, the arguments and the observed result (`get_node({node_type: Project, id: "proj:…"})` → `{node: null}`), so it could be re-run here in one call and confirmed on reflow2's own graph. Its neighbours that were only narrated could not be.

⚠️ **Optimising for compactness could delete precisely what made corroboration possible.** The right target for a machine-to-machine format is REPRODUCIBILITY, not terseness: tool name, arguments, observed result, expected result, and an honest *what I did not check*. The Grok file has all of those — including a *"Gaps (mine / process)"* section admitting it skipped `compare_designs` and guessed a Project id. **That self-reporting is not fluff, and it is the first thing a brevity-optimised format would drop.**

📌 IT ALSO SEPARATED CONFIRMED FROM UNCONFIRMED WITHOUT BEING ASKED. Its `get_instructions` truncation report did NOT reproduce here — the payload arrived complete — which is only discoverable because the report was specific enough to test. A format should make that distinction structural rather than leave it to the writer's conscience.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.
(a) EXTEND `report-friction` WITH AN AGENT-TO-AGENT MODE — one skill, a second output shape aimed at a maintainer's agent rather than a maintainer. Cheapest, and it inherits redaction discipline already written and honoured in the field.
(b) A NEW SERVED SKILL, leaving `report-friction` human-facing. Cleaner separation; two skills that must not drift apart.
(c) A STRUCTURED FORMAT (fields, not prose) so the receiving agent can parse and triage rather than read. Highest leverage for the receiver. ⚠️ The four corroborated items were reproduced from PROSE that happened to name tools and arguments, so a schema helps only if it MANDATES exactly those fields.
(d) A GRAPH NODE TYPE for feedback. 🛑 Blocked by a real constraint: the authoring agent works inside SOMEONE ELSE'S design, so the note cannot be a node in reflow2's graph without crossing a boundary. It must travel as a DOCUMENT — the same wall `dec:idea-a-top-level-graph-holds-what-the-component-graphs-share` hit, where nothing crosses between graphs but a published surface.
(e) LEAVE IT AD-HOC — the prompt already works. Counter: it worked because Anthony happened to ask for it and happened to relay it. Nothing makes that repeatable, and the second and third user reports both arrived as email.

📌 THE CONSENT HALF IS ALREADY AN OPEN NODE, AND ALEX ASKED FOR IT HIMSELF: `dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded` — *"put in an update that asks me if I want to collect feedback and store my decision in the graph."* **This is the CONTENT half of the same mechanism: his node decides whether feedback may travel, this one decides what it says and who it is written for.** Neither is built.

⚠️ THE STANDING REASON THIS MATTERS: every defect in the last two increments was found by a first-time user, by running two real projects at each other, or by an agent writing down what fought it — none by reading code, none by a gate.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 formalize agent-authored feedback written FOR another agent, and what exactly is gained by cutting the human out of the loop?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill. Two counters are recorded ahead of the options because both cut against the framing rather than against the idea, and an implementer reading only the proposal would miss them: "cutting out the human" describes two different humans and only the routing one can go, and the value of the example file came from its reproducibility rather than its economy — so a format optimised for the stated goal of removing fluff would likely delete the self-reported process gaps and the tool-and-arguments detail that made four items checkable in a single session. Kept separate from `dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded` because that node asks whether feedback may be collected at all and this asks what it contains and who writes it for whom.

properties.decision:
✅ **DECIDED 2026-08-14 ON ANTHONY'S WORD, ON THE TWO SETTLED HALVES. The third sub-question is SPLIT OUT to `dec:idea-is-allocation-running-ahead-of-the-seams` (parked, trigger named) rather than left holding this one open.**

THE IDEA, Anthony's words 2026-08-08: *"the allocation of functions to systems/services should be done as late as possible (agreeing that doing it at genesis is too early). I feel like doing it at the last possible moment before functional allocation to system/service is the right call."* It answers a caution raised against `dec:idea-the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph`, which proposed asking at GENESIS what quality attribute a system is for: the objection was that at genesis you frequently do not know yet, and premature commitment costs as much as late discovery. His resolution keeps the question and moves WHEN it is asked — to the moment allocation must actually be committed.

THE HOOK ALREADY EXISTS: `unallocated_capability` is already a detected gap, so "capabilities exist, bound to nothing" is visible from graph state alone — the same state-not-history discipline `dec:loop-status-state-not-history` commits to. Nothing new needs remembering.

**(a) PER-PROJECT OR PER-CAPABILITY — SETTLED 2026-08-08. PER-CAPABILITY SCOPE, PROJECT-LEVEL DEFAULT, RE-ASKED ONLY ON DIVERGENCE.** The schema already leans this way: DimensionAssessment attaches to ANY node, not to the Project, and a telemetry path and a config service in one system genuinely want different objectives. The recurrence worry — a mature design allocates continuously, so the moment repeats — is answered by machinery that already exists: an acknowledgement LAPSES when the shape it was accepted about changes, so the answer is recorded once and re-asked only when a new capability diverges. Recurring without being repetitive. ⚠️ Held most loosely of the three by the person who proposed it, and worth revisiting if the divergence test proves hard to state.

**(b) IS 100% ALLOCATION AGAINST 0% SEAMS AN INVERSION — MOVED OUT 2026-08-14 to `dec:idea-is-allocation-running-ahead-of-the-seams`.** It is unanswerable from data the graph holds: 156 ALLOCATED_TO edges carry only `weight_basis`, nothing dates an allocation, and 1 of 320 ChangeEvents mentions one. Its trigger is "allocation timing becomes recordable at all". **Splitting it is the ruling: two settled halves should not read as undecided because a third is blocked on a substrate that does not exist.**

**(c) A DESIGN THAT NEVER REACHES THE MOMENT — CLOSED 2026-08-08**, answered by doctrine that already existed. `maturity_report` deliberately refuses to say where a design SHOULD be, and its own output says a demonstrator *"may sit here forever and be right"*. So never allocating is a **LEGITIMATE TERMINAL STATE**, not an error or a stalled process. The only thing any future prompt owes is to be acknowledgeable like every other gap — which every gap already is.

⚠️ **COUNTER-ARGUMENT, RECORDED BESIDE THE RULING RATHER THAN ANSWERED BY IT, AND FLAGGED TO HIM BEFORE HE ACCEPTED:** the last-responsible-moment principle assumes deciding late costs less than deciding wrong, which holds only when deferral is free. Here it may not be — artifacts get written against an assumed structure long before anyone calls `allocate`. **If real files already embody a de facto allocation, then deferring the decision defers only the RECORD of it, and the graph arrives late to something the build already did.** That is the as-designed-versus-as-built gap `granularity_report` exists to surface, and it argues the trigger should watch **ARTIFACTS APPEARING** rather than the `allocate` call. Accepted with this open.
properties.name: DECIDED — allocation is deferred to the last responsible moment: per-capability scope with a project default, and never allocating is a legitimate terminal state
properties.rationale: Revised under revise-design with a snapshot taken while all three sub-questions still read open (epoch:allocation-subquestions-narrowed, seq 289), so the state before the narrowing survives. Status stays `proposed` deliberately: two sub-questions closing does not settle the parent, and flipping it would assert a decision Anthony has not made. The most valuable thing added is not either answer but the finding under (b) — that the agreed method could not be executed, and why. A parked question with a stated trigger is recognisable when someone walks past the answer months later; a parked question with none is indistinguishable from a forgotten one, which is a distinction reflow2 cannot currently draw at all (detect_defects reports parked decisions as `orphan_node`, info severity, and two of the four outstanding structural defects are exactly that).

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. Raised by an external agent-side field report, 2026-08-11 (fact:external-agent-side-report-2026-08-11, redacted).

WHAT THEY OBSERVED. Several of their acknowledgements carried explicit retirement conditions written into the reason — of the shape "revisit when the first implementation exists", "replace this when that work is scheduled". One of those conditions had been true for weeks and nothing surfaced it. `reviewed_gaps` says an acknowledgement is "worth re-reading when the design shifts" and nothing detects the shift. Their line: acknowledgements are where gaps go to be forgotten SAFELY, and the safety decays silently.

⚠️ NARROWER THAN THEY WROTE, AND THE NARROWING IS THE POINT. Expiry machinery EXISTS: a review expires when the set of nodes it judged changes, and `req:set-scoped-acknowledgement-keys-on-its-rule` (accepted) already fixed the case where a set-scoped acknowledgement expired merely because the design grew. So this is NOT "acknowledgements never expire". It is that the trigger is always the same trigger — the affected set moved — and a human-stated condition ("when an artifact of this kind first appears") is invisible to it. Recording the narrow version matters, because the wide version reads as a defect in something that works.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) A typed re-review trigger on the acknowledgement: a node type appearing, a count crossing zero, an edge arriving. Expressive, and it is a small query language nobody asked for — every one of those is a new thing to specify, validate and explain.
(b) No new vocabulary: have `loop_status` flag acknowledgements older than N design-changes as re-review candidates. Crude, cheap, and it needs no condition to be stated correctly at write time — which matters, because the person acknowledging a gap is the least likely to predict what would falsify it.
(c) Let the acknowledgement name the NODE TYPE it is waiting on, and nothing more. Covers the reported case exactly ("when the first artifact exists") at a fraction of (a)'s cost.
(d) Nothing. `req:review-expires-when-what-it-judged-changes` is already proposed and unbuilt; finish that before adding a second expiry axis beside it.

⚠️ THE TRAP: a stated condition that is WRONG is worse than no condition, because it reads as watched. An acknowledgement saying "revisit when X" that nothing evaluates is the same false-assurance shape as a `planned` verification silencing a gap — which this project already refuses. Whatever is offered must actually be evaluated, or must not be offered.

📌 SITS BESIDE `req:review-expires-when-what-it-judged-changes` (proposed): that one is about the trigger being too NARROW (only the set, not the content). This is about the trigger being SINGULAR. Same subsystem, different complaint, and they should be read together.
properties.name: OPEN — should an acknowledged gap be able to declare a machine-checkable re-review trigger, rather than stating its retirement condition in prose?
properties.rationale: A real acknowledgement carried a condition that came true and nothing noticed. But expiry machinery exists and works on a different trigger, so the honest finding is that the trigger is singular rather than absent — and a stated-but-unevaluated condition would be a worse failure than the current silence, because it would read as watched.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. It comes from a cost that was PAID, not predicted.

═══ THE MEASURED INSTANCE, 2026-08-25 ═══

`unreviewed_ideas` fired correctly on 2026-08-23 with "110 of 181 open idea(s) connect to nothing", and Anthony accepted it: *"A parked idea legitimately governs nothing yet, and relating them on a guess would assert reasoning nobody did."* THAT REASONING IS CORRECT and matches the detector's own warning that a false neighbour is worse than a missing one.

🛑 BUT THE FINDING IS AGGREGATE-KEYED, so one acceptance silenced it PERMANENTLY — for every idea written since and every idea that will ever be written. Two days later, on 2026-08-25, the cost landed exactly where the gap predicted: a session reasoning about functional allocation never reached `dec:idea-the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph`, which had ANTICIPATED that session's central error seventeen days earlier and said so in as many words. **The user had to be the index.** He named it himself: *"these brainstorming ideas from the past should slowly be being linked together, so that next time we have a discussion on functional allocation, I don't have to remind you."*

Measured the same day: 174 idea nodes, **121 of them (70%) link to no other idea at all**; only 43 idea-to-idea edges exist across the whole set.

═══ WHY THE PENDULUM IS THE POINT ═══

`is_aggregate` EXISTS because the opposite failed: `unvalidated_capability` was re-acknowledged about twenty times — at 33, 34, 35 … 68 capabilities — always with the same disposition, because per-node keying expired the judgement on every write. That was a real defect and aggregate keying was a real fix.

⭐ SO THE TWO KNOWN STATES ARE "EXPIRES ON EVERY WRITE" AND "NEVER EXPIRES", and both have now cost something. The unexplored middle is an acceptance that carries the POPULATION IT WAS ACCEPTED AT and re-asks when that moves materially — accepted at 110 of 181, asked again at 150 of 220. Nobody has to re-judge an unchanged situation, and nobody silently inherits a judgement made about a much smaller one.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**A. POPULATION-DRIFT EXPIRY.** The acknowledgement records the numerator/denominator at acceptance; the gap re-fires past a threshold. Fixes all five aggregate kinds at the root.
 ⚠️ Cost: it re-opens existing acknowledgements across `unreviewed_ideas`, `undeclared_seam`, `change_axis_unstated`, `unvalidated_capability` and `no_published_boundary` at once. Threshold choice is a new knob, and a badly chosen one recreates the flood.

**B. LEAVE IT, AND TREAT THE BACKLOG AS THE ANSWER.** The gap is honest; the fix is to work the 110 down with `review_relations` rather than to change the mechanism.
 ⚠️ Cost: says nothing about the NEXT aggregate acceptance, and the same trap is available to every aggregate gap including `unallocated_component`, added the same day.

**C. PER-KIND CHOICE.** Some aggregates are about a PRACTICE that does not change with scale ("we publish nothing on purpose"); others are about a BACKLOG whose size is the whole point. Only the second kind expires.
 ⭐ This is the sharpest reading — `no_published_boundary` genuinely should never expire, and `unreviewed_ideas` genuinely should. It needs a per-variant judgement rather than one rule.

📌 DIRECTLY RELEVANT TO WORK LANDING TODAY: `unallocated_component` (PR #336) is aggregate-keyed on the same anti-flood argument, and is a BACKLOG-shaped finding — 33 of 85 leaf components on reflow2's own design. Under option C it is exactly the kind that should expire. It shipped before this was noticed, which is why this node exists rather than a quiet edit.
properties.name: OPEN — an aggregate gap accepted once stays accepted forever, however much the population grows. Should the acceptance expire when the population moves materially?
properties.rationale:
Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the reasoning survives without being claimed as intent, and LINKED on creation rather than left to a later sweep — which is the discipline this node is about. Anthony, 2026-08-25, on the half-ideas: they should be linked as they are written so a later discussion finds the line of reasoning instead of an orphan.

Kept as an open idea rather than filed as a defect because the mechanism is not wrong — aggregate keying fixed a real and worse problem, and both known settings have now cost something. What is missing is the middle, and choosing it is a judgement about each variant rather than a bug fix.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. The most concrete of the Class B candidates in `dec:idea-which-agent-pitfalls-can-reflow2-actually-reach`, separated because it is a specific buildable proposal rather than a triage, and because its measured bound is the interesting part.

THE PITFALL, in Anthony's words 2026-08-17: "Infinite loops: Agents can get stuck repeatedly adding and removing the exact same line of code to fix a recurring error."

THE IDEA. reflow2 does not read code, but it records CONTENT HASHES. An oscillation has a signature that needs no semantic understanding at all: an artifact's checksum returning to a value it already held. A → B → A is a loop, and A → B → C → B is a smaller one. No language server, no diff parsing, no judgement — just a repeat in a sequence.

⭐ THIS IS THE RIGHT SHAPE FOR REFLOW2 SPECIFICALLY, which is why it is worth separating out. Everything else in the pitfall list needs to understand code; this needs only to notice that the design has seen this exact content before. It is the same move `orphan_node`'s degree-zero rule makes — the finding that needs no judgement is the one worth computing.

⚠️⚠️ AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS IT CANNOT BE BUILT TODAY, which is the part that would have been missed by proposing it on plausibility. MEASURED ON REFLOW2'S OWN GRAPH, 2026-08-17:
    Artifacts with ANY snapshotted checksum history:      23   (of 187 artifacts)
    ...with more than one recorded prior value:             3
    ...showing a checksum that returns to a prior value:    0
The three deepest histories (`art:heal`, `art:detect`, `art:service`) hold TWO prior checksums each. A detector run on that data would report zero oscillations and mean nothing by it — the vacuous zero this whole epoch exists to stamp out, shipped inside the fix for it.

⇒ THE ROOT CAUSE IS ONE FIELD, NOT A SUBSYSTEM, and naming it is what makes this actionable. A Snapshot is taken by `record_change`, which the `design_updated` disposition calls and `design_holds` DOES NOT. So the commonest kind of code change — the refactor, the test fix, the churn where an oscillation would actually live — mints a ChangeEvent and records NO PRIOR CHECKSUM. The history is thin precisely where the signal would be.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
(A) HAVE `design_holds` SNAPSHOT THE PRIOR CHECKSUM TOO. Smallest change; the history starts accumulating immediately; the detector becomes possible later without further work. COST: a Snapshot per accept, on the commonest path.
(B) KEEP A CHECKSUM LEDGER ON THE ARTIFACT rather than snapshotting the whole node — cheaper per write, but new vocabulary and a second place history lives.
(C) DON'T BUILD IT. Oscillation may be better caught by the agent harness, which sees the edits as they happen, than by a design graph seeing them after the fact.
(D) BUILD THE HISTORY NOW, THE DETECTOR LATER — deliberately, on the record, so the data exists by the time anyone wants the answer. This is the option the measurement argues for.

📌 THE GENERAL LESSON, worth keeping whatever is decided: the detector was easy and the DATA was the constraint, and that was invisible until it was counted. Proposing it on plausibility would have produced a check that reports zero forever and is believed.
properties.name: OPEN — an artifact whose checksum RETURNS to a previous value is an agent going in circles; the detector is trivial and the history reflow2 keeps is too thin to run it on
properties.rationale: Recorded as brainstorming. The detector is trivial — a repeat in a sequence of content hashes, needing no semantic understanding — and reflow2 cannot run it: only 23 of 187 artifacts have any snapshotted checksum history and only 3 have more than one prior value, because `design_holds` accepts do not snapshot. The root cause is one missing write on the commonest path, not a missing subsystem. Proposing this on plausibility would have shipped a check that reports zero forever.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-20.

HIS WORDS: "allow a user to map out tasks in discretized increments (potentially, a manager could say, task package 1 is Alex's, task package 2 is AJ's, and so on)."

THIS IS A WORK BREAKDOWN STRUCTURE, and it is worth naming as such because it is standard practice in exactly the world he comes from. A WBS slices an increment into packages, each with a single accountable owner. It is the artifact a manager actually manages with, and it is what makes 'who is behind?' answerable.

WHAT REFLOW2 ALREADY HAS, and none of the three is this:
  · OWNED_BY — whose AREA this is. Durable, standing, never released. About a REGION of the design, not a bundle of work.
  · CLAIMS — who is IN it right now. Transient, advisory, session-scoped, released at checkout.
  · AUTHORED_BY (role=approver) — who was ASKED to settle a decision. The only thing loop_status attributes today.

A work package is none of those. It is a SCOPED BUNDLE OF WORK, inside an increment, with one accountable person, that exists until it is delivered. Standing like ownership, but about work rather than area; scoped like a claim, but durable and assigned rather than self-taken.

WHY IT MIGHT MATTER MORE THAN IT LOOKS: the graph today can answer 'what is owed?' design-wide and 'what needs this person?' only for decisions they were asked to settle. It cannot answer 'what is Alex's slice of increment 3, and is it done?' — which is the question a manager asks every week. `loop_status(contributor_id)` already reports that most debt classes are `not_attributable`, which is the honest version of the same absence.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
  (a) A NEW EDGE on the existing schedule — SCHEDULED_FOR already carries `modality`; a package identifier plus an owner could ride alongside. Cheapest, no new node type. Weak: a package is a THING a manager names and talks about, and a property on an edge cannot be named or discussed.
  (b) A WORK PACKAGE NODE contained by the increment, with capabilities and requirements scheduled into IT rather than directly into the epoch, and OWNED_BY the person. Most faithful to how WBS actually works, and it makes 'Alex's slice' a node you can ask about. Costs a schema addition and a level of indirection.
  (c) REUSE OWNED_BY over a claimed region — no schema change at all, and claim_region can already describe a region by a query. Weak: ownership is about AREA and is never released, while a package is finished and closed; and a region defined by a query is not a set of tasks somebody agreed to do.
  (d) DO NOTHING and let a manager keep the slicing outside reflow2. Honest option, and the status quo.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded beside the idea: reflow2 has deliberately kept people OUT of the blast radius — AUTHORED_BY, CLAIMS and OWNED_BY are all excluded from traceability so that a change never propagates into a person. Work packages are the point at which a design tool starts becoming a project-management tool, and that is a boundary worth crossing deliberately rather than by accident. The countervailing fact: `req:people-are-modellable-inside-the-design` is already an open requirement asking for organisation, role and who-performs-a-function, so the door is not closed.

RELATED: dec:idea-lining-work-up-in-increments-should-be-the-default-not-a-skill-you-remember.

properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony thinking out loud 2026-08-08, immediately after `dec:an-unplanned-cut-slips-every-later-increment-by-one` was accepted and applied, and in direct response to the id-churn cost that applying it exposed. HIS WORDS: "if we can't slip a version, just add the in-between version like v0.25.1 for the planned change, then preplanned versions can stay in place (their id stays the same) and we can add unplanned versions as v0.25.1 or v0.26.4 or whatever makes sense - I'm sure this has a drawback also as it probably doesn't fit when you should do a minor bump versus whatever the third decimal place is called." (The third decimal is the PATCH number, semver's MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.) THE IDEA: an unplanned cut is numbered BETWEEN the planned ones rather than consuming one of them, so `epoch:v0260-planned` stays v0.26.0 forever, its id keeps matching its content, and nothing renumbers. WHAT IT SOLVES, and it is the real prize: the id churn is not merely reduced, it is ELIMINATED — no renaming, no risk to the snapshot history `dec:arrival-delta` reads plan movement from, and no ids that lie about their content. It also removes the cascade entirely: today's slip touched four epochs, and a scheme where planned numbers are stable touches none. THE DRAWBACK HE NAMED HIMSELF, AND IT IS REAL AND MEASURABLE ON TODAY'S CUT: patch is not a free slot. This project's CHANGELOG defines its own buckets — patch is "bug fixes, doc fixes, tests, refactors, perf, and behavior changes that make a silent failure LOUD", minor is "a change to the SHAPE of the tool surface (new/changed params, changed result shapes)". v0.25.0 was MINOR by that table for exactly two reasons: `HealProposal.would_destroy` and `HealIssue.hubs`, both new result fields. Everything else in it was fixes. So v0.25.1 would have been WRONG for what actually shipped — by a hair, and the hair matters. THE HARM IS CONCRETE RATHER THAN PURIST, and the same table states it: patch means the consumer "updates blindly; skills and calls unchanged"; minor means they "may need to notice". Numbering a shape change as a patch tells Alex he can update without looking when a result shape moved. That is a signal saying SAFE without having checked — the failure family this whole session kept finding. OTHER SHAPES, none chosen: (a) HYBRID — insert as a patch when the unplanned work genuinely IS a patch (the common case), slip only when it is genuinely minor (rarer). Keeps ids stable most of the time and keeps semver honest; costs two rules instead of one and a judgement at each cut, though that judgement is one the CHANGELOG table already forces. (b) DISSOLVE IT — name planned increments by CONTENT and assign the number at cut time from what actually shipped (`dec:idea-a-planned-increment-is-named-by-content-not-by-number`). Then neither slipping nor inserting is a problem, because no plan ever holds a number it can lose. This is the only option where the question stops existing rather than being answered. (c) REDEFINE THE BUCKETS — pre-1.0 semver gives latitude and the project has not made a stability commitment ("Major 1.0 — Deferred"), so it could declare that 0.x.y patch admits additive-but-non-breaking changes. Cheapest to write and the most expensive to be wrong about, since it weakens the one signal consumers act on blindly. (d) KEEP THE ACCEPTED RULE and pay the id cost, treating ids as birth numbers rather than delivery numbers. WORTH NOTING: (a) and (b) COMPOSE — content-named plans plus semver-honest numbering at cut time is arguably the same answer reached from two directions.
properties.name: OPEN — should unplanned work take an IN-BETWEEN version (v0.25.1) so planned increments never renumber, instead of slipping them all up one?
properties.rationale: Recorded as an idea rather than as a change because Anthony was explicitly thinking out loud, offered the counter-argument himself in the same breath, and the accepted rule it revisits was settled minutes earlier. Nothing is superseded: `dec:an-unplanned-cut-slips-every-later-increment-by-one` stands and the slip has been applied. What makes this worth a node rather than a passing remark is that it is a genuine alternative to a rule with a known cost, and the cost is what prompted it — so a later session choosing between them needs both on the record, with the semver objection attached to the idea rather than lost in conversation.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-20: *"we probably need to pause slightly and do some honest research into what is 'systems engineering and how is reflow2 helping a user do SE?'. I feel like one of the core things we talk about is that reflow2 does SE - so we need to properly back that statement up."* Plus the standard he wants avoided: *"do what I say (those using reflow2), not what I do."*

SEARCHED FIRST. `dec:idea-does-reflow2-enforce-an-se-process-or-only-supply-the-vocabulary` and `req:a-user-can-see-that-the-process-was-followed` already hold his 2026-08-16 version of this and settle two things that are NOT re-litigated here: reflow2 is not a bare vocabulary (genesis and adopt both sequence function before structure and adopt forbids inferring a requirement from its implementation), and THE GAP IS EVIDENCE, NOT GUIDANCE.

⭐ WHAT IS NEW HERE: every prior node reasons from reflow2 OUTWARD. Nobody had taken a recognised definition of systems engineering and audited reflow2 AGAINST it. This is that audit, first pass.

⚠️ METHOD AND ITS BOUND, stated so the audit is not over-trusted: the yardstick is ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288's process framework as published in secondary sources (SEBoK, IEEE/ISO abstracts) — 14 technical processes and 8 technical-management processes. THE STANDARD ITSELF IS PAYWALLED AND WAS NOT READ. Process NAMES and groupings are reliable; any claim about what a specific clause REQUIRES is not made here.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📊 THE AUDIT — vocabulary / tool / CHECK, which is the three-legs test applied to SE itself

TECHNICAL PROCESSES

  System Analysis                   allocation, propagation, budget, ility,       check: YES — STRONGEST
                                    readiness TRL/MRL, alternatives, granularity
  Implementation                    out of scope by design; artifacts + checksums check: n/a
  Integration                       seam_report, compose, mirror, pair_designs    check: YES
  Verification                      Verification, VERIFIES, 8 methods, coverage   check: YES
  Transition                        Release, INCLUDES, deploy_to, Environment     check: partial
  Validation                        Verification.kind = validation                check: YES (unvalidated_capability)
  Operation                         fielded, Environment, performed_in            check: partial

TECHNICAL MANAGEMENT PROCESSES

  Assessment and Control            loop_status, graph_report, readiness          check: YES

⭐ WHAT THE AUDIT SAYS IN REFLOW2'S FAVOUR, and it is more than expected

The VERIFICATION/VALIDATION SPLIT is modelled correctly and most tools blur it: `Verification.kind` is an enum of exactly {verification, validation} — *"built right (meets the spec)"* versus *"right thing (meets the operational intent/need)"* — on a separate axis from `method`, which carries the four canonical DoD/INCOSE methods (test, analysis, inspection, demonstration) plus `observation` for as-fielded. There is a detector reading it (`unvalidated_capability`). That is real SE fidelity, not vocabulary cosplay.

CONFIGURATION MANAGEMENT and DECISION MANAGEMENT are genuinely strong — snapshots, epochs, content-hash lineage, an export chain that refuses to sever itself, and decisions that land `proposed` until a named person's word.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 THE SELF-HOST ANSWER, MEASURED 2026-08-20 — THIS IS THE "WHAT I DO" HALF

  175 Verifications in reflow2's own graph
  175 are kind = verification
    0 are kind = validation
  168 of 175 use method = test

reflow2 SHIPS the built-right/right-thing distinction, ships a detector for it, and HAS NEVER ONCE USED IT ON ITSELF. Every check it holds asks whether the code matches the spec. Not one asks whether a capability meets an operational need.

And the rest of the vocabulary is used about as thinly:
   1 Constraint          (hard limits: built, essentially unused)
   1 RISKS/MITIGATES edge (risk: no node type, and the edges are unused too)
   3 Actors              (stakeholders)
  42 of 56 Components carry no Interface
   0 of 8 subsystems provide anything
   1 capability-to-capability dependency across 182 allocated capabilities

⚠️ THE FAIR READING, because the prior node already established it: reflow2 has NO genesis epoch and was NEVER taken through adopt. Its graph records organic growth with good bookkeeping, not a guided design. So this is not evidence that the guided path fails — it is evidence that THE TOOL'S OWN DESIGN WAS NOT BUILT BY THE PROCESS THE TOOL SELLS, which is precisely the exposure Anthony named.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ THE HONEST SENTENCE, offered to replace "reflow2 does SE"

**reflow2 supplies a broad and unusually faithful SE vocabulary, enforces a real function-before-structure process on its guided paths, computes system analyses that few tools compute — and enforces very little of it. Its detectors check the CONSISTENCY OF WHAT EXISTS; almost nothing notices what was never done.**

That sentence is defensible, and "reflow2 does SE" unqualified is not.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
IDEAS

**A. A RISK NODE TYPE.** The one named 15288 process with no vocabulary at all. SE practice runs on a risk register — likelihood, consequence, owner, mitigation, burn-down — and reflow2 has an edge with a severity property and nowhere to put any of it. ⚠️ Counter: `dec:the-other-uaf-domains-wait-for-a-project-that-needs-them` set the precedent that a domain waits for a project that needs it, and no user has asked for risk.

**B. RUN ADOPT ON REFLOW2 ITSELF.** Already recorded as `dec:idea-run-adopt-on-reflow2-itself-as-a-ground-truth-test`. It is the only way to answer "does the guided path work" with evidence rather than testimony, and it would close the do-as-I-do gap directly.

**C. VALIDATE SOMETHING.** Zero of 175. Even a handful of `kind: validation` checks against operational intent would move reflow2 from self-consistent to self-validated — and would exercise a detector nobody has ever seen fire.

**D. A PROCESS-CONFORMANCE REPORT** — option (c) of the prior decision, now with a yardstick: report which 15288 processes this design has evidence for. ⚠️ Counter, and it is `dec:mosa-conformance`'s: a standard's vocabulary belongs in a VIEW, never in the schema, or a design-anything tool takes on one discipline's language.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any user's project uses the vocabulary more completely than reflow2's own does. That comparison would say whether this is a self-host problem or a product one, and nobody has run it.
properties.name: OPEN — the claim "reflow2 does SE" audited against ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288 for the first time: broad vocabulary, real process on the guided paths, thin enforcement, and a self-host that uses about a third of what it offers

properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-08-26: *"can't we do authentication at another layer (like middleware) so that reflow2 doesn't have to worry about authentication?"* — and then, sharply: *"my big concern is that reflow2 operates exactly like it currently does now (how we are using it now). I don't do any authentication and I don't want to change that by adding in some authentication step."*

**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.**

📌 Distinct from `req:the-hosted-surface-is-read-only-so-it-can-ship-before-authentication-exists`, which the guard offered and which was read before choosing: that requirement states what must be true of the first cut and treats authentication as ABSENT. This asks WHERE AUTHENTICATION SHOULD LIVE — a question that outlives the read-only cut, since delegated is not the same as missing.

═══ ⭐ FOR THE READ-ONLY SURFACE THE ANSWER IS YES, COMPLETELY ═══

The read-only surface needs one question answered: **who may REACH this server?** A network or proxy layer answers exactly that, and option (c)'s tailnet binding already does — a Tailscale/WireGuard peer is authenticated by the tunnel before a packet arrives.

**So the read-only surface needs ZERO authentication code in reflow2.** Not a workaround; the correct placement. It composes with what ships: `cap:remote-sessions`'s Host allowlist is DNS-rebinding protection, a different concern, still useful behind any proxy. The same holds for a reverse proxy doing OIDC on loopback. `rule:no-foreclosure` is satisfied — nothing about it prevents growing into a hosted multi-user service later.

═══ 🛑🛑 THE CORRECTION THAT MATTERS MOST: THE LINE IS REACHABILITY, NOT TRANSPORT ═══

**An earlier draft of this reasoning said "attributed writes over HTTP are refused unless reflow2 is told it is proxied". THAT WAS WRONG, and Anthony caught it by stating the constraint it violated.**

**His current daily setup IS HTTP.** `--shared` starts a detached server and proxies to it; every write in the 2026-08-26 session went through `http://127.0.0.1:40233/`. A rule keyed on "is this HTTP" would have broken the working local workflow — the precise outcome he was objecting to.

⭐ **THE DESIGN ALREADY DRAWS THE RIGHT LINE, AND NOBODY HAD NOTICED IT WAS THE SECURITY BOUNDARY.** The streamable-HTTP transport answers only requests whose Host header is on an allowlist — **`localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `::1` by default** — and reaching the server from another machine requires an explicit repeatable `--http-allow-host`. `cap:remote-sessions` (VERIFIED) says it in as many words: *"reaching the server from another machine is an explicit flag rather than a side effect of binding a public address."*

⇒ **So every write rule attaches to DELIBERATE REMOTE EXPOSURE, never to a transport:**

    stdio                                    → nothing changes
    --shared / loopback --http  (TODAY)      → nothing changes
    --http-allow-host <remote>               → the write rules apply

**He would never meet an authentication step, because he would never take the act that turns one on.** And if he did take it, he would have taken it deliberately — which is what makes the boundary honest rather than accidental.

📌 AND IT EXPLAINS WHY LOCAL NEEDS NO AUTHENTICATION AT ALL, EVER: a caller-supplied `contributor_id` is sound on a loopback surface precisely because anyone who can call that server can already edit the graph file directly. Authentication would add nothing but ceremony.

═══ THE LINE THAT REMAINS: MIDDLEWARE AUTHENTICATES A CONNECTION; IT CANNOT POPULATE A GRAPH FIELD ═══

    "MAY THIS CALLER REACH THE SERVER?"    → middleware's job, entirely. Tailnet, proxy, mTLS.
    "WHICH CONTRIBUTOR IS THIS, AND MAY    → NOT middleware's job. That identity must arrive
     THEY SETTLE INTENT?"                     INSIDE the tool call, as a `contributor_id` that
                                              `authored_by` and the confirmation ledger record.

A proxy can prove someone is Alex. **It cannot write `who:alex` into an `AUTHORED_BY` edge.** Today that argument is validated only for EXISTENCE (`require_contributor`), never for truth.

⇒ **Middleware removes the authentication problem and leaves the ATTRIBUTION problem exactly where it was.** They look like one problem and they are two.

═══ OPTIONS FOR THAT LAST HOP, none chosen, relevant only once REMOTE writes are wanted ═══

**(a) The proxy injects a trusted header** (`X-Forwarded-User`) mapped to a Contributor. Standard and cheap.
🛑 Trusting an injected header is sound *only behind a proxy*; bare on a port the same header is client-supplied and forgeable, against `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` (ENFORCED). If taken, it must be LOUD — reflow2 told explicitly, and REFUSING attributed writes when it has not been told. ⚠️ Residual risk reflow2 CANNOT check: a proxy that fails to strip a client-supplied header forges identity silently. That is a deployment property, and it should be stated in the design rather than discovered.

**(b) Mint-and-carry, as seats already do.** Consistent with `dec:stateless-seat-handle`; transport-independent. ⚠️ Counter: it moves the question to how the handle is OBTAINED, which is where the proxy returns.

**(c) The consuming app IS the Contributor.** Honest, and it collapses `loop_status(contributor_id=…)` and the confirmation ledger. `who:storyflow-api-boss` already carries this caveat; this makes it permanent.

⭐ **(d) THE REMOTE SURFACE MAY PROPOSE, NEVER SETTLE.** Remote writes land at `proposed`; approver edges and `accepted` status are refused, so settling intent still requires a session inside the machine boundary. **This needs NO new authorisation vocabulary** — `proposed` vs `accepted` already exists and the intent-authority gate already enforces it. It matches flo2's actual case (posting a brainstormed idea asserts nothing) and means the ENFORCED rule never depends on a network claim at all. ⚠️ Counter: Anthony could not approve anything from a web app, only propose. That is a real limit and his to weigh.

📌 **NOTHING HERE BLOCKS THE FIRST CUT.** The read-only surface ships without any of it.
properties.name: OPEN — authentication belongs in middleware, not in reflow2; that answers the READ surface completely and the WRITE surface only up to the contributor id
properties.rationale:
Recorded because the question has a genuinely good answer for the case being shipped and a partial one for the case after it, and conflating those would be expensive in the way this project keeps finding.

The two-question split is the whole content: "may this caller reach the server" and "which contributor is this" look like one problem and decompose cleanly. Middleware owns the first completely; the second has to cross into the graph as a field, which no network layer can do on reflow2's behalf.

Option (a)'s trap is written at length rather than noted, because trusting an injected header is the obvious implementation and its failure mode is silent: the same binary is safe behind a proxy and forgeable without one, with nothing in the design saying which situation it is in. That is the shape `req:no-silent-fallback` exists for, and it lands on an ENFORCED rule.

The `dec:stateless-seat-handle` caveat is recorded as a re-read rather than a contradiction, because that decision's header objection was about client-supplied headers and a proxy-injected one is a different object — a distinction that is real, convenient, and therefore one somebody should make deliberately.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony, 2026-08-04: "It's weak at holding what we learned about the tool while using it, because that lands in markdown by convention, and markdown doesn't get queried — it gets grepped, by someone who already knows what they're looking for. this needs to be solved. I wanted to stop using the BL, but it keeps growing as you say - instead, I wanted everything in the graph." His preference is stated and is NOT recorded as settled: what "everything in the graph" means mechanically is the open part.

THE MEASUREMENT, taken 2026-08-04. `docs/backlog.md` is 3,350 lines / 581,031 bytes across 132 rows. Of the 8 rows filed in one session (BL-205..212), SIX are referenced by ZERO graph nodes. The file is not a registered Artifact, so `coverage_report` does not count it and no checksum tracks it. FOUR things were re-derived in that same session that were already written down somewhere: BL-205 (third rediscovery), `dec:export-once-per-pr` (accepted, invisible, violated and then re-announced as new), BL-70's alternatives family (nearly re-proposed), and dev_storyflow's hand-made doc-intent scope table (re-derived worse from filenames).

THE FRAME IS ALREADY ACCEPTED AND THE BACKLOG VIOLATES IT. `dec:what-lives-where` states the rule: "the design record should stop being PROSE YOU NAVIGATE and become A GRAPH YOU QUERY, with the prose kept as provenance hanging off the nodes it produced." It carries a falsifiable test — "IF REFLOW2 WORKS, STORYFLOW WOULD NOT HAVE NEEDED dev_storyflow… If a user still ends up splitting their repo to stay sane, reflow2 has not delivered what this decision claims." THE SAME TEST GENERALISES AND REFLOW2 CURRENTLY FAILS IT ON ITSELF: if reflow2 works, reflow2 would not need a 581 KB markdown backlog. It is also the exact failure the dev_storyflow api-boss measured in that fleet's MEMORY.md — "an index that must be read IN FULL to be useful has a hard ceiling", 20 KB against a 17 KB limit with everything past the line silently invisible. The backlog is 29 times that size.

WHY IT HAS RESISTED THE OBVIOUS FIX — A BACKLOG ROW IS NOT ONE THING.
