Reading the eight rows from one session, they are at least four: (i) DEFECTS AGAINST SHIPPED CAPABILITIES (BL-205 loop_status too large, BL-206 the gate's truncated sweep, BL-208 the inert CI guard, BL-209 the blind orphan detector); (ii) UNBUILT WORK (BL-186 the folder driver, BL-211 genesis-from-a-folder); (iii) OPEN DESIGN QUESTIONS (BL-207's fix-shape fork); (iv) DISCOVERED LIMITS (BL-212, chronology cannot be recovered from a folder). Three of those four already have a home: unbuilt work is a Capability at `planned` behind a Requirement, an open question is a `proposed` Decision — which is what this very node is — and a discovered limit is a Constraint or DesignRule.

⭐ THE ONE THAT HAS NO HOME, AND IT IS THE LARGEST CATEGORY: a defect found by USING the tool. reflow2 has no way to say "this capability is built, VERIFIED, and does not do what it claims." `Verification` answers whether a check passes — and every one of BL-205/206/208/209 sat under a passing check. `DriftEvent` answers whether the code moved away from the design — and in all four cases the code and the design AGREED, and both were wrong. HEAL's issues are computed from graph shape, not recorded observations, so they vanish between runs. That absence is why these rows land in markdown: there is nothing to write them to.

OPTIONS, none chosen. (a) ROUTE EACH ROW TO THE TYPE IT ALREADY IS and add no vocabulary. Cheapest, and it works for three categories of four. Counter: for the defect category it loses the finding — "this is broken, here is the measurement, here is how it was found" becomes "here is a need", which erases the evidence and reads as intent rather than as a bug. (b) A `Finding`/`Defect` NODE TYPE carrying claim, evidence, when observed, and what it bears on. Counter, and it is strong: this project has proposed a node type and WITHDRAWN it after measuring TWICE in one week (`Attestation` → `TemporalFact`, `Hazard` → `DesignRule` + `CONSTRAINS`), so the prior against new vocabulary is heavy — and `TemporalFact` ("a time-bounded assertion true only between two epochs") may already be the shape, since a defect is exactly "this was true of the build from epoch X until the fix". (c) EVERYTHING BECOMES A PROPOSED DECISION. Counter: 132 proposed Decisions would swamp `where-am-i` and the decision list, and most rows are not forks between real alternatives. (d) KEEP THE MARKDOWN BUT DERIVE IT FROM THE GRAPH rather than maintaining it by hand. In-house precedent exists and is unused for this: `dec:views-are-projections` ("a view is a projection of the graph; renderer fill-ins are defects") and `tools/render_views.py` already render DoDAF-flavoured views into docs/viewpoints.md. The backlog is simply not one of them. Counter: this solves RETRIEVAL and not CAPTURE — it only helps once the content is in the graph, so it composes with (a)/(b) rather than competing. (e) DO NOTHING AND ACCEPT THE COST, recorded so it is a choice rather than a default: the backlog is readable by a human today, and the re-derivation cost, while real, has been paid without anyone stopping work.

--- ADDED 2026-08-04, ANTHONY ASKED WHAT A NODE AND AN EDGE CAN ACTUALLY HOLD. THE ANSWER IS THE CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPES EVERY OPTION ABOVE, AND IT IS MEASURED. ---

WHAT A NODE CAN HOLD. The schema's whole type system is `string` (170 declarations), `enum` (89), `float` (34), `bool` (10), `int` (7). There is NO dedicated text type and NO `max_length` anywhere in any schema file — `string` IS the narrative field and it is unbounded in practice: the `decision` property of this very node runs to several thousand characters without complaint. Every type carries at least one narrative-shaped field (`Decision.decision` + `.rationale`, `Requirement.statement`, `Capability.description`, `Component.purpose`), and Decision requires only `name` and `decision`. AND THE SCHEMA IS ADDITIVE: dynograph-core's own test is named `extra_properties_allowed` — "Extra properties should be allowed (schema is additive)" — so a property the schema never declared is stored rather than refused. It validates the TYPES of declared properties and enforces the required ones; anything else passes through.

WHAT AN EDGE CAN HOLD. More than assumed: 44 of the 60 edge types carry properties, across 46 distinct property names, and several are free text — `note`, `evidence`, `rationale`, `diff_summary`. SIXTEEN CARRY NOTHING, and they are all bookkeeping or temporal: AT_EPOCH, HAS_SNAPSHOT, VALID_FROM, VALID_TO, ABOUT_ENTITY, OCCURS_DURING, PERFORMED_IN, and — worth noting against [BL-212] — PRECEDES. The edge that would say "this document came before that one" can carry no evidence for the claim.

⭐ THE STING, AND IT IS WHY THIS BELONGS ON THIS NODE RATHER THAN AS TRIVIA: ONLY 52 PROPERTIES IN THE ENTIRE SCHEMA ARE `fulltext: true`, and those are the only ones `search_design` indexes. The distribution is name 20 · description 12 · statement 5 · summary 3, then singletons: rationale, decision, purpose, question, evidence, intent, effects, design_intent, criteria, context_setter, answer, title. So `Decision.decision` IS indexed and — measured — `Decision.rationale` is NOT. Every "why" written into a rationale field is stored and unsearchable. The same is true of any extra property invented under the additive rule: stored, not indexed, not returned by `describe_schema`, read by no report. That is this project's recurring declared-and-read-by-nothing shape one rung worse, because it is UNDECLARED and read by nothing.

THE CONSEQUENCE FOR EVERY OPTION ABOVE: UNLIMITED PROSE IN A NODE IS GREP BY ANOTHER NAME. What makes the graph queryable rather than navigable is the `fulltext:` flag, the typed properties and the EDGES — not the narrative. Moving the backlog into nodes therefore helps only to the extent a row becomes STRUCTURE: which capability the defect bears on (an edge), what was measured (a typed property), whether it is still true (a status or a temporal bound), with the prose hanging off that as explanation rather than as the record. A row moved in as one long `description` rebuilds `backlog.md` inside the graph with worse ergonomics and no gain — and that failure would be invisible, because it would look like progress.

AND IT PUTS A NUMBER ON THE DEPENDENCY WITH `dec:idea-embeddings-adoption`: with 52 lexically-indexed fields and no vector half, "query the graph" today means ranked keyword search over names, descriptions and statements. Better than grep — cross-node, ranked, no filename needed — but the same KIND of retrieval. The ceiling on "an agent can work from the graph alone" is set by that open question, so the two ideas should be weighed together rather than separately.

WHAT MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED WHEN THIS IS PICKED UP: `dec:what-lives-where` (the accepted rule and its falsifiable test), `dec:views-are-projections` plus `tools/render_views.py` (the rendering half already exists), [BL-198] (a serialized default is indistinguishable from a choice — the same "what does the graph actually record" family), and [BL-209] (22 Decisions invisible because `AUTHORED_BY` counts as attachment — a graph-native backlog would land straight into that blind spot and must not).
properties.name: OPEN — should the backlog stop being a 581 KB markdown file and become graph nodes, and what is missing before it can?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill at Anthony's request. The load-bearing content is the taxonomy and the single gap it exposes: three of the four kinds of backlog row already have a node type, and the fourth — a defect in a capability that is built, verified and wrong — has none, which is why those rows have no choice but to be prose. Recording the measurement (581 KB, 6 of 8 rows with zero graph representation, four re-derivations in one session) so the next session argues from numbers rather than from the impression that the file is getting long. Extended 2026-08-04 with the data-model constraint Anthony asked for — free text is unbounded and the schema is additive, but only 52 properties are indexed and `rationale` is not one of them, so the answer turns on how much of a row becomes structure rather than prose. Note the irony worth keeping: this rationale is itself unsearchable.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-14.

═══ ⭐⭐ ADDED 2026-08-14 (LATER, SAME DAY): HIS INHERITANCE-VERSUS-COMPOSITION FRAMING, WHICH CUTS AGAINST DEPTH AND IS THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT ON THIS NODE ═══

HIS WORDS: *"it reminds me [of] a python class that inherits another class that inherits another class and on (depth). this is different from composition architectures where there is no inheritance and everything is horizontal. In [that] case, is it good that reflow2 is horizontal or would there be some advantages in making things have some level of depth?"*

⇒ **THE ANALOGY IMPORTS A SETTLED ENGINEERING ARGUMENT, AND IT ARGUES FOR THE SHAPE REFLOW2 ALREADY HAS.** "Prefer composition over inheritance" is doctrine because deep hierarchies are rigid: the taxonomy has to be right before the work is understood, a change to a base ripples to every descendant, and the ladder is expensive to re-cut once things hang off it. **On that reading reflow2's flat shape is not a deficiency to be corrected but the safer default**, and the burden falls on anyone proposing depth to say what it BUYS.

⚠️ **BUT THE ANALOGY IS IMPERFECT IN ONE SPECIFIC WAY, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS LOAD-BEARING.** In code, inheritance and composition are ALTERNATIVES — two ways to reuse behaviour, and picking one excludes the other. In this graph they are NOT alternatives, because they answer different questions: `CONTAINS` says *what is this made of*, `DEPENDS_ON` says *what does this need*, and a design legitimately has both at once. So "horizontal versus vertical" is not the same trade as "composition versus inheritance", and reading it as one would make depth look like a competing architecture when it is an orthogonal axis.

⭐ **WHERE THE ANALOGY DOES BITE, EXACTLY: `DECOMPOSES`.** That edge is the one relation here that behaves like inheritance — a child decomposes a parent and **delivery ROLLS UP**, so satisfying every child satisfies the parent. That is a base-class contract with arithmetic attached, and it is brittle in precisely the way deep inheritance is. **AND THE COST IS NO LONGER HYPOTHETICAL — IT WAS PRICED THE SAME DAY:** `req:decomposition-covers-its-parent` → `cap:decomposition-coverage-is-asked` (built 2026-08-14, PR #181) exists because the roll-up never checks that the children AMOUNT TO the parent, so a requirement split into two children addressing a tenth of it reports `delivered` the moment both close. **Depth buys computable roll-up and costs the risk that the roll-up lies.** That is the trade, stated in one line, and it did not exist on this node before he raised the analogy.

📌 SO THE QUESTION IS NARROWED, NOT ANSWERED: not *"should the design be deeper?"* but **"which of the three depth ladders earns its brittleness?"** — and each is separable. `CONTAINS` (assembly) is cheap and carries no arithmetic. `DECOMPOSES` (requirement roll-up) is the expensive one and now has its counterweight built. `Component.level` / `Capability.tier` are labels that compute almost nothing today.

═══ 🛑 RE-MEASURED 2026-08-14 AFTER HIS QUESTION — AND A THIRD UNUSED LADDER APPEARS ═══
```
DECOMPOSES ................ 0        (requirement lineage: original 164, decomposed 0, derived 0)
Component.level ........... component 48 · subsystem 8 · system 0 · SoS 0 · enterprise 0
Capability.tier ........... operational 147 · UNSET 14 · strategic 0 · tactical 0   <- NEW
Component CONTAINS ........ 42 edges over 8 parents (of 56 components)
lateral ................... DEPENDS_ON 178 · ALLOCATED_TO 178 · SATISFIES 192
PART_OF_FLOW .............. 0   (zero Flow nodes)
```
⚠️ **`Capability.tier` WAS NOT ON THIS NODE BEFORE AND IS THE SHARPEST INSTANCE: 147 of 161 capabilities carry `operational` and NOTHING carries `strategic` or `tactical`.** A three-value ladder holding one value is not a shallow hierarchy, it is an unused field — and it is the SAME vocabulary Alex's tier request (`dec:idea-a-top-level-graph-holds-what-the-component-graphs-share`) would reach for. **Measured separately the same day: `Capability.tier` carries no schema description at all**, so nothing tells an agent what it means or how it relates to `Component.level`. Three ladders exist, and all three are close to empty.

⇒ **THE HONEST READING OF ALL THREE NUMBERS: reflow2's design is not flat because someone weighed depth and chose against it. It is flat because the depth vocabulary was never filled in.** That is a different fact from "horizontal is right here", and it means the composition-versus-inheritance question **cannot be settled from this design's shape** — the evidence is absence of modelling, not evidence of a considered choice. Which is exactly what option (b) below already warned it would be measuring.

════════════ THE ORIGINAL CAPTURE, 2026-08-14 ════════════

HIS WORDS: *"I almost want 'missing the wood for the trees' to be a skill of reflow2. that sometimes somebody becomes so wrapped up in some little detail that they forget the big picture… another way to look at it is 'breadth' vs 'depth' of a design… you can probably error in going too far in one dimension without considering the other dimension - need to find the correct balance. not sure if there is a way to measure in a graph depth vs breadth? if it can be measured, then there probably becomes a ratio of depth-to-breadth that is ideal to maintain. maybe in a graph you can count all the nodes (peer to peer nodes and this is your horizontal score). then count all the components nodes that make up a system (kind of looking at system-of-systems to systems to components and so on) and this is your depth score."*

═══ ✅ YES, IT IS MEASURABLE, AND HIS PROPOSED SHAPE IS THE RIGHT ONE ═══

Run on reflow2's own export (`c18a4a1`, 2026-08-14):
```
DEPTH                                   BREADTH
  Components ................ 56          lateral edges ........... 203
  component CONTAINS ........ 42            DEPENDS_ON 178 · CONSUMES 15
  MAX NESTING DEPTH ......... 2             PROVIDES 6 · INTERACTS_WITH 4
  components with no parent . 14          hierarchical edges ...... 122 CONTAINS
  DECOMPOSES edges .......... 0                                     + 0 DECOMPOSES
  Component.level used: component 48, subsystem 8
                        system 0, system_of_systems 0, enterprise 0
  Requirements 164 · Capabilities 161, all at one level
```

🛑 **REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN IS ALMOST PURE BREADTH.** 164 requirements with **zero** decomposition; 56 components nested at most **two** deep, using two of five `level` values; 14 components parented by nothing. **The project built around `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` — *"nested as deep as the design needs"*, which Anthony called *"one of the primary things I designed it for"* — has a flat design.**

═══ ⚠️ A CORRECTION MADE BEFORE THIS NODE WAS SAVED, AND IT MATTERS ═══

This session first wrote that the blind spot had **doubled from 6 to 14** since 2026-08-07. **That was wrong.** `fact:defect-allocation-health-is-green-over-an-empty-structure` already recorded BOTH numbers on the same day — `components_outside_any_subsystem: 6` and `component_roots: 14` — as two different measures, not a before and after. **The truth is less dramatic and arguably worse: the numbers are IDENTICAL a week later.** `hierarchy_issues` 0, roots 14, max_depth 2, `DECOMPOSES` 0 — a fully measured defect, unchanged.
📌 The error was caught by the near-duplicate guard surfacing that node — the same guard this session has documented firing wrongly seven times today. **Here it was right, and it prevented a false claim entering the record.**

═══ WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW HERE, beyond the 2026-08-07 measurement ═══

  · `Component.level` uses **two of five** values — nothing is a `system`, `system_of_systems` or `enterprise`. The ladder his idea depends on is three-fifths unused.
  · **Lateral 203 vs hierarchical 122** — the breadth/depth contrast stated as a single comparison, which is his proposed metric and which nothing computes today.
  · `DEPENDS_ON` has grown 171 → 178 in the week while `DECOMPOSES` stayed at 0. **The design is getting wider and no deeper**, which is the trend his idea is for and which no report shows.
  · 📌 **IMMEDIATE CONSEQUENCE FOR WORK ACCEPTED EARLIER TODAY:** `cap:decomposition-coverage-is-asked` is planned to ask whether a decomposition's children cover their parent. **With 0 `DECOMPOSES` edges it cannot be dogfooded on this graph at all** — it would ship doing nothing here and nobody would notice. Not an argument against building it; an argument for testing it elsewhere. (BUILT 2026-08-14, PR #181, and it shipped saying exactly this about itself.)

═══ ⚠️ THE "IDEAL RATIO" IS THE OVERFIT THIS IDEA EXISTS TO PREVENT ═══

**A depth-to-breadth target derived from any one design is exactly the specialisation Anthony warned against in the same message.** A house, a beamline, a shop and an MCP server share no natural proportion, and `req:design-anything` forbids binding the tool to one discipline's habits. Two recorded failures agree:
  · `evaluate_allocation` reports **modularity 1.0 from `total_internal: 1, total_external: 0`** — a perfect score over ONE dependency while the graph holds 178 `DEPENDS_ON` edges. **A ratio over a starved denominator is that failure again.**
  · BL-5's lesson, in `detect.rs`: **a loud detector needs a different QUESTION, not a tuned number.**

⭐⭐ **THE ANTIDOTE IS ALREADY BUILT: `granularity_report`.** It answers a structurally identical question — *is the build coarser than the design?* — and its contract says *"IT NEVER SAYS 'monolith', 'too big' or 'split it', carries NO severity… THERE IS NO SIZE THRESHOLD: artifacts are compared against THIS DESIGN'S OWN DISTRIBUTION."* ⇒ **A breadth/depth measure should report the numbers and the design's own distribution, name what it cannot see, and refuse a verdict.** No universal ideal, no target, no severity. `fact:defect-allocation-health-is-green-over-an-empty-structure` reaches the same conclusion from the other side: *"what is wrong is a metric reporting a value at all when its denominator is one, instead of saying it has too little to measure."*

═══ AND ON THE SKILL ITSELF ═══

⚠️ **A SKILL ALONE REPEATS A FAILURE THIS PROJECT HAS MEASURED REPEATEDLY.** "Step back and look at the whole" is exactly what a session under load stops doing; `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` exists because an agent keeps adding nodes while the loop silently stops, and `dec:idea-a-capture-session-skill-the-user-types` settled that the manual trigger is the only one not depending on the mechanism that keeps failing. **A wood-for-trees skill nobody remembers to invoke is the joke telling itself.**

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.
(a) **A USER-TYPED SKILL, NO METRIC.** Cheap, reliable trigger (human). Counter: tells the user little they did not already suspect when they typed it.
(b) ⭐ **MEASURE + SKILL, ON `granularity_report`'s NO-THRESHOLD SHAPE** — report depth, breadth and this design's own distribution; refuse a verdict; the skill puts the question. Counter: needs an honest answer to *what counts as depth* while `DECOMPOSES` is unused and `Component.level` is three-fifths empty — today it would mostly be reporting **absence of modelling** rather than a property of the system. ⭐ **THE RE-MEASUREMENT ABOVE STRENGTHENS THIS COUNTER: with `Capability.tier` also one-valued, ALL THREE depth ladders are near-empty, so a measure shipped today would report unfilled fields in three places and call it shape.**
(c) **A RATIO WITH A TARGET.** Argued against above on this node's own evidence.
(d) **NOTHING — `where-am-i` re-orients already.** Counter: it reports what the design SAYS and has no notion of proportion; it surfaced none of the numbers above.

📌 THE HONEST OPEN QUESTION UNDER ALL OF IT: is reflow2's flat shape a DEFECT, or a correct reading of a system that genuinely has 56 peer components and little natural hierarchy? **The measure cannot answer that and must not pretend to** — which is why `granularity_report` refuses a verdict, and why this stays a question rather than becoming a check. ⚠️ **AND THE RE-MEASUREMENT NARROWS EVEN THAT: with three ladders unfilled, the flatness is at least partly unmodelled rather than observed, so this design cannot be the evidence either way.**
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 measure a design's BREADTH against its DEPTH and prompt a step back? It is measurable, reflow2's own design is nearly all breadth, and an "ideal ratio" would be the overfit the idea exists to prevent
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill and measured on reflow2's own export before anything was written, because the central question — can depth and breadth be counted — is answerable rather than arguable. The measurement confirmed his proposed shape works and showed this design is nearly all breadth despite being built around recursive decomposition. A wrong claim is recorded in the node rather than quietly dropped: this session asserted the unparented-component count had doubled, and the prior fact node showed both figures were taken the same day, so the real finding is that a fully measured defect is unchanged a week later. The "ideal ratio" half is argued against rather than deferred, since a target derived from one design is the specialisation he raised the idea to avoid, and `granularity_report` already demonstrates the correct pattern — report the distribution, name what cannot be seen, refuse the verdict.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled.

THE OBSERVATION: capabilities form a DEPENDS_ON DAG that detect_defects insists stays acyclic, and NOTHING ever asks what order it implies. reflow2 can say what is scheduled for an increment (SCHEDULED_FOR) and what is delivered (the golden thread), but not what can be started.

THE IDEA: dynograph_graph::topological_sort — Kahn's, deterministic (lexicographically smallest order), returns None on a cycle. Two distinct uses:
(a) A SIMPLIFICATION available today: budget.rs:312 hand-rolls Kahn's algorithm in about forty lines with a comment that says so. The foundation exports it.
(b) A NEW capability: given the capabilities scheduled for an increment, a valid build order — and the frontier of what has no unbuilt dependency, which is "what can I pick up now".

WHERE IT LANDS: BL-68 (TRL/MRL readiness gating) is about whether something is ready; this is about whether its DEPENDENCIES are ready, which is the other half of the same question. Also epoch planning.

CHEAP for (a). Moderate for (b), which needs a scope (a whole design? one increment? one component's subtree?) and a rendering.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS: (a) is not free — the local version works on string-id arcs while the foundation one needs a Graph built through GraphBuilder, so it trades forty lines of Kahn's for an impedance adapter, and the local one is already tested. (b) risks asserting a schedule reflow2 has no business asserting: a topological order is ONE valid order of many, and presenting it as THE order would be the same overreach dec:report-dont-judge exists to prevent. The honest output is probably the READY FRONTIER (what is unblocked) rather than a full ordering.

Filed as a backlog row on Anthony's word (2026-08-01) — the work is tracked; the shape, especially frontier-vs-order, is open.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 answer "what order can this increment be built in, and what is buildable now?"
properties.rationale: Found by grepping reflow2 for any existing ordering concept and hitting a hand-rolled Kahn's in budget.rs — evidence both that the need is real and that the foundation function was not known to be there.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-18, proposing four techniques in his own words:

(a) TRANSITIVE REDUCTION — 'Remove shortcut links that carry duplicate logic. If the graph contains [A->B], [B->C], and [A->C], the link [A->C] is redundant and safely deleted.'
(b) ENTITY RESOLUTION — 'Merge nodes that represent identical concepts. If the graph treats AI and Artificial Intelligence as separate nodes, combine them to drastically reduce node count.'
(c) ONTOLOGICAL GENERALIZATION — 'Replace highly specific leaf nodes with their broader parent concepts. Map Apple, Banana, Orange up to a single parent Fruit.'
(d) DOMINATING PATH EXTRACTION — 'Calculate centrality metrics like PageRank or Betweenness Centrality. Keep only the top-scoring backbone nodes that connect the vast majority of knowledge.'

⭐⭐ THE OBJECTION THAT APPLIES TO ALL FOUR AT ONCE, and it is not an argument against the ideas but against one word in them: EVERY TECHNIQUE AS STATED DELETES OR MERGES, and reflow2's most load-bearing rule is that it does not. `req:intent-preserved` — the past is never overwritten. `dec:ask-not-repair` — findings are put to the human, never repaired automatically. `apply_heal` merges only on a HUMAN-ASSERTED `DUPLICATES` edge. A design graph is not a knowledge graph: a knowledge graph optimises for RETRIEVAL, where a redundant edge is waste; a design graph is a record of INTENT AND ITS HISTORY, where 'redundant' and 'said twice, deliberately, by two people' are indistinguishable from the topology alone.

⭐ SO THE INTERESTING FORM OF THE WHOLE IDEA IS: REDUCTION AS A PURE PROJECTION, NEVER AS A WRITE. That is Anthony's own doctrine from a different direction — views must be pure projections and a renderer filling anything in is a defect. A 'reduced core' VIEW answers 'what would someone new have to read?' without the graph losing a thing, and it can be recomputed as the design changes rather than going stale the moment somebody adds a node.

WHAT THE GRAPH ALREADY HOLDS, measured 2026-08-18 so none of this is built twice:
  (a) TRANSITIVE REDUCTION is the only one with NO prior art here — no node and no code mentions it. Genuinely new.
  (b) ENTITY RESOLUTION is half built and its trap is ALREADY ON THE RECORD: `dynograph-resolution` is a dependency, `token_sort_ratio` is used in seam.rs and ingest.rs, `possible_duplicate` fires at Jaccard >= 0.8 and ASKS rather than merges, and `dec:auto-merge-at-90-destroys-sibling-names` is an ACCEPTED decision recording that a similarity threshold destroyed sibling names — 'a merge needs a discriminator, not a threshold'. The DUPLICATES edge exists and has ZERO instances, deliberately: it is the human's assertion, not the machine's guess.
  (c) ONTOLOGICAL GENERALIZATION already has its spine — 122 CONTAINS edges — and its OTHER spine is empty: DECOMPOSES has ZERO edges while `req:decomposition-covers-its-parent` is accepted. So the rolling-up axis exists and is unused rather than missing.
  (d) DOMINATING PATH is partly built and partly proposed: `betweenness_centrality` IS used (structure.rs) and powers PROPAGATE's ranking; `pagerank` and `personalized_pagerank` are exported by dynograph-graph and UNUSED; `dec:idea-relevance-ranking` already proposes personalized PageRank for blast radius, and `dec:idea-other-centralities` asks whether betweenness is the right one. Both open since 2026-08-01.

⚠️ AND A SPECIFIC TRAP IN (a), which is why 'safely deleted' is the word to argue with. In a design graph A->B->C and A->C are often DIFFERENT CLAIMS, not one claim stated twice: a Requirement satisfied by a Capability allocated to a Component is not the same statement as that Requirement being directly traced to that Component, and `dec:foundation-cycle-is-a-warning` already turns on exactly this kind of distinction between a structural shortcut and a real relationship. Transitive reduction over a TYPED edge set would have to know which edge types compose — SATISFIES then ALLOCATED_TO does not compose into anything reflow2 declares — so the technique needs a composition table before it needs an algorithm.
properties.name: OPEN — can a design graph be reduced to an essential core, and must that reduction be a VIEW rather than a write?
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill: the ideas enter as ideas, nothing is promoted, and the objection sits beside each rather than replacing it.

AN AGENT'S READING, offered as a finding rather than an answer. The reduction FAMILY is worth having and the word 'delete' is the part to drop. Three of the four already exist in some form, which suggests the useful move is not four new features but ONE view that composes what is already there — and (a) transitive reduction is the only genuinely new member, and the one needing the most design (a composition table over 61 typed edge types) before any algorithm.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS DECIDABLE: who the reduced core is FOR. A newcomer reading a design for the first time wants the backbone; a merge tool wants duplicate resolution; an export wants size. Those three want different reductions, and answering 'reduce to the essential core' without naming the reader would produce a view that serves none of them. `cap:onboarding` and `req:onboard-newcomer` are the nearest stated audience.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-17, from Space Force capability development: designing against an adversary's deny/degrade/disrupt/destroy, with new intelligence arriving constantly — "we would start designing something and then we would find that the adversary was doing something else and we would have to adjust the design." His own framing of the general case: "the design was always evolving based on some new factor that hadn't been there when we first designed it."

⭐ THE ASYMMETRY THAT NAMES THE GAP. reflow2's `propagate_change` answers *what does this DESIGN change touch?* His domain needs *what does this WORLD change touch?* — and those are different questions, because the design graph is CLOSED UNDER ITSELF. Every node reflow2 can reason about is part of the design. External reality enters only as observations ABOUT the design — drift, verification, reconciliation — never as PREMISES the design rests on. So an assumption about an adversary, a competitor, a regulator or a supplier is invisible: it shaped the design and is not in it.

⇒ THE QUESTION IN ONE LINE: **when the intel is revised, can you find everything you built on it?** Today, no. There is nothing to propagate from.

⭐⭐ AND THE MECHANISM IS ONE STEP AWAY, WHICH IS THE INTERESTING PART. `set_requirement_lineage` already declares `derived` — "technical necessity nobody asked for, created by a design decision — pair it with governed_by to that Decision" — and its own description states the consequence that matters here: **"a derived requirement may lose its reason to exist if the decision behind it is re-opened."** That is EXACTLY the semantics he needs, already built, and pointed at an INTERNAL cause. The gap is that reflow2 models "derived from a decision we made" and has no notion of "derived from a fact about the world."

MEASURED ON REFLOW2'S OWN GRAPH, 2026-08-17, and the numbers argue against reaching for new vocabulary first:
    EVOLVES_INTO edges in use     0
    SUPERSEDES                    0
    SUPPLEMENTS                   0
    MITIGATES                     0
    TRIGGERS                      0
    MASKS                         0
    RISKS                         1
    EnvironmentRule nodes         0
    Requirement `lineage`         176 of 176 `original` — `derived` and `decomposed` NEVER USED
So the evolution vocabulary AND the threat vocabulary already exist and are almost entirely unexercised. Declared and never written to is the trap `req:a-finding-has-somewhere-to-put-its-evidence` names explicitly, and adding a node type here without understanding why the existing ones went unused would repeat it at a larger scale. ⇒ See `dec:idea-is-the-evolution-vocabulary-unused-because-nothing-asks-for-it`.

THE SHAPES, none chosen:
(A) A TemporalFact IS ALREADY THIS, USED DIFFERENTLY. It is a time-bounded assertion with `subject_id`, `valid_from`/`valid_to`, and `basis: measured | forecast`. An intel assessment is a forecast about a subject with a validity window; when it expires or is superseded, everything pointing at it is the blast radius. COST: `subject_id` points INTO the design, so a fact about an adversary has no subject to name — the shape fits and the anchor does not.
(B) THE PREMISE IS AN ASSUMPTION NODE, and design elements DEPEND_ON it. Cleanest propagation story: revising the assumption walks the existing machinery. COST: new node type, and reflow2 has been careful about that.
(C) THE ADVERSARY IS AN ACTOR. An Actor is "who the designed system serves" — an adversary is the anti-Actor, and their capabilities could hang off them. COST: inverts the type's meaning; and reflow2 holds only 3 Actors, so the type is barely exercised either.
(D) DON'T MODEL THE WORLD — model the DEPENDENCE. Do not try to hold what the adversary can do; hold only "requirement D exists BECAUSE of external premise P", where P is a named, dated, citable claim and nothing more. Cheapest, and it is the half that makes the blast radius computable. The design never pretends to model the threat.
(E) NOT REFLOW2'S JOB. Intel and market analysis live in their own systems; reflow2 records the design. COST: then the "why did we build this?" answer permanently leaves the graph, which is the thing he says was hardest.

⚠️ THE HONEST BOUND WHICHEVER WAY THIS GOES: reflow2 cannot tell you the adversary changed. It can only tell you what you built on the belief that they had not — which is the same class of limit as `dec:non-goal-reflow2-does-not-know-what-is-deprecated`, and worth stating in the same breath as the capability.

📌 WHY THIS IS NOT NICHE. Every long-lived design has premises that move: a regulation, a supplier, a platform version, a competitor, a funding line, a user population. Space Force is the sharpest instance because the premise is adversarial and therefore moves ON PURPOSE. NSLS-II has the same shape with a decade-old stack underneath it.
properties.name: OPEN — reflow2 computes the blast radius of a DESIGN change; can it compute the blast radius of a WORLD change, when the premise a design rested on turns out to have moved?
properties.rationale: Recorded as brainstorming. reflow2's graph is closed under itself: external reality enters only as observations about the design, never as premises the design rests on — so when an assumption is revised there is nothing to propagate from. The mechanism is one step away rather than absent: `lineage: derived` already means "may lose its reason to exist if the decision behind it is re-opened", pointed at an internal cause. But the evolution and threat vocabulary already present is measured at 0/0/0/0/0/1 uses, so understanding why it went unused should precede adding more.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent.

ANTHONY, 2026-08-21: "now that we've developed the 9 subsystems of reflow2, can we work on coming up with more exhaustive tests for each subsystem? things like edge cases and identify failure modes and other tests."

📌 FIRST, TWO CORRECTIONS OF FACT, both small and both worth having straight before anyone plans work against them. There are TEN subsystems, not nine. And one of them, `cmp:packaging`, carries a `cmp:` id at subsystem level with ZERO components under it — a naming and containment oddity that predates today and is not a defect anyone has been asked about yet.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑🛑 THE FINDING: EXHAUSTIVE TESTS CANNOT BE DERIVED FROM THIS DESIGN TODAY, AND THE REASON IS ONE NUMBER
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

    Capabilities:                          192
    ... declaring their INPUTS:              3
    ... declaring their OUTPUTS:             3
    ... declaring a SIGNATURE:               0
    Constraints (where a hard limit lives):  1

EDGE CASES ARE DERIVED FROM THE BOUNDARIES OF AN INPUT DOMAIN. FAILURE MODES ARE DERIVED FROM WHAT AN OUTPUT PROMISES. With neither stated for 189 of 192 capabilities, both can only be IMAGINED — which is what 1376 hand-written tests already are, and they are good ones, but imagining more of them is not what "exhaustive" means. `dec:idea-stated-module-function-is-what-makes-failure-mode-testing-derivable` (Anthony, 2026-08-20) said this a day early and named the mechanism: `Capability.inputs`/`outputs` exist in the schema with NO typed tool, NO instruction and NO detector — the three-legged failure again.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 AND THE PER-SUBSYSTEM PICTURE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY YET
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

    subsystem              components   verifications
    sys:coherence-loop         28            68
    sys:agent-surface          25            31
    sys:store                   2            16
    sys:foundation              6            14
    sys:time-history            6            14
    sys:intake                  4             6
    sys:vocabulary              2             6
    cmp:packaging               0             4
    sys:human-channel           2             2
    sys:documentation           1             0

    181 Verifications; 27 of them reach NO subsystem at all.
    127 real test FILES on disk; 47 are pointed at by an Artifact.
    ⇒ 80 TEST FILES THE DESIGN HAS NEVER HEARD OF.

⭐ SO "sys:documentation HAS ZERO VERIFICATIONS" MAY WELL BE FALSE. With 80 of 127 test files unmodelled, a zero in that table is as likely to be a MODELLING gap as a TESTING gap — and acting on it would mean writing tests for something already tested while something genuinely bare stays quiet. **A detector that reports zero because it had nothing to run on reads exactly like one that ran clean**, and this table currently has that defect. Anything built on these counts should re-measure first.

📌 AND THE OTHER AXIS IS STILL UNTOUCHED: 181 of 181 Verifications carry `kind: verification`. ZERO carry `validation`. reflow2 ships the built-right / right-thing split and has never once used it on itself. "More exhaustive" in the built-right direction is already 1376 tests deep; the axis with nothing on it at all is whether each subsystem does the RIGHT thing.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE OPTIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

(a) DECLARE THE SHAPE OF THE FUNCTIONS, THEN DERIVE. Populate `inputs`/`outputs` on one subsystem's capabilities, and generate the edge cases from the input boundaries and the failure modes from the output promises. THE ONLY ROUTE ON WHICH "EXHAUSTIVE" MEANS SOMETHING CHECKABLE rather than something claimed. EXPENSIVE, and it needs all three legs built first (a typed tool, an instruction, a detector), because 3-of-192 is what two missing legs look like. Worth doing on ONE subsystem as a trial before committing to ten.

(b) TEST AGAINST THE INTERFACES THAT ALREADY EXIST. 17 Interfaces, 13 carrying a spec — and a spec clause is a failure mode waiting to be written down: violate each clause in turn and assert the refusal. CHEAP AND AVAILABLE NOW. LIMIT, stated plainly: only 4 of the 10 subsystems publish an interface, and the other six present nothing because nothing consumes them. This covers 4 subsystems well and 6 not at all.

(c) START FROM THE THIN ROWS — documentation, human-channel, packaging. Intuitive and probably WRONG as stated, for the reason above: the thin rows are where the MODEL is thinnest, which is not the same as where the TESTING is thinnest. Do not do this without re-measuring.

(d) MAKE THE NUMBERS REAL FIRST. Map the 80 unmodelled test files to Verifications so the per-subsystem table stops being fiction. CHEAPEST OF ALL, mechanical, and it is what every other option's numbers depend on. It adds no tests — which is exactly the objection to it, and the answer is that it tells you where to add them.

(e) THE VALIDATION AXIS. Ask, per subsystem, "does this do the right thing?" rather than "does it do what it says?" — 181 Verifications and not one of them asks it. Different question from the one he asked, and possibly the more valuable one, which is why it is here rather than left out.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
WHAT IS NOT KNOWN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Whether declared inputs/outputs would actually yield tests nobody had thought of, or merely restate the ones already written. THAT IS MEASURABLE ON ONE SUBSYSTEM and is the honest gate on (a): declare the shape for `sys:vocabulary` or `sys:store` (2 components each, small enough to finish), derive the cases mechanically, and count how many were NOT already covered by the existing suite. If the answer is near zero, (a) is elaborate bookkeeping and should be dropped.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ ANTHONY CHOSE (d) THEN (a), 2026-08-21 — AND (d) WAS BUILT AS A TOOL, NOT A SCRIPT
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

`tools/link_tests.py`, sibling of `wall_check.py`, zero configuration: it reads Artifact.location and REALIZES from the export and derives the test roots from the paths the design already claims. Built as a TOOL because **tests the design has never heard of is every project's problem**, not reflow2's chore (`rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself`).

RESULT ON REFLOW2:
    81 source files mapped to a component
    127 test files found beside them; 80 the design has never heard of
    40 attributable on the two-clause rule (35 not yet registered)
    87 NOT attributed, all reported with the reason

🛑 THE SCORING APPROACH WAS TRIED FIRST, MEASURED, AND ABANDONED — recorded because somebody will propose it again and it looks obviously right. Ranking components by how many of their uniquely-owned functions a test calls left **27 of 80 files with no dominant owner** and put `cmp:graph` at the top of most of the rest, because opening a graph is SETUP and not SUBJECT. Excluding functions used by more than a third of all test files (setup by usage, not by opinion) improved it to 52 clear / 27 ambiguous — still guessing on a third of the corpus. **A guessed mapping is worse than a missing one here: it makes the per-subsystem table LOOK complete while filing tests under the wrong part.** So the rule is narrow — filename matches a mapped source file AND the test calls a function that file defines — and everything else is reported unattributed WITH ITS REASON.

⭐ A SECOND FINDING AROSE FROM THE SAME WORK AND IS ABOUT REFLOW2'S OWN ARCHITECTURE. Attributing a test to a module mechanically is HARD HERE because 43 of 54 core modules hang their functions off one shared `DesignGraph` struct (58 impl blocks). An import scan cannot see which module a test exercises, because the test calls `g.propose_heal()` and never names `heal`. That is the same god-struct property that limits what "optimise one module at a time" can reach — algorithms and query shape, yes; data representation, no.

📌 STILL OPEN AND UNCHANGED BY THIS: whether declared inputs/outputs would yield tests nobody had thought of. (a) has not been started.
properties.name: OPEN — can exhaustive per-subsystem tests be DERIVED, or only imagined? 3 of 192 capabilities state their shape

properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-08-26, from the same brainstorm — this one is the instrument his framing implies rather than an idea he stated.

**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.**

═══ THE SIGNAL NOBODY IS COLLECTING ═══

Every existing measurement looks at what a session **did** with reflow2: `surface_usage.py` counts calls, `cap:skill-loads-are-counted` counts loads, `dec:how-should-reflow2-log-its-own-usage` asks where to put the log. All of them are blind to the same thing —

**the work a session performed BY HAND that reflow2 already serves.**

That is the negative space, and it is a far stronger signal than absence-of-a-call, because it carries INTENT. A tool never called might be young, might have no use case yet, might be unfindable — `dec:bl-155` lists exactly those three explanations and says it *"cannot tell unused from unreachable."* **Hand-rolled work discriminates between them.** A session that wrote a script to do X proves someone wanted X, at a moment, badly enough to build it. That is not weak evidence of a retrieval failure; it is close to proof.

═══ IT IS ALREADY REPRODUCING, INCLUDING TODAY ═══

- **2026-08-26 (this session).** Comparing the allocation layer against the artifact layer — 212 capabilities, 59 agree / 23 disagree / 130 no evidence — was done with a hand-written Python script over the export. It found the session's central result. **No reflow2 tool does it:** `reconcile_artifacts` compares design against DISK, `compare_designs` compares design against DESIGN, and neither compares two layers of ONE design. Here the hand-rolled work names a MISSING tool.
- **2026-08-20.** *"does my declared decomposition match the real coupling?"* — again a hand-written script, again the session's finding.
- **The v0.19.0-v0.31.0 release cuts.** A ~40-line JSON-RPC driver written and rewritten to export through a specific binary, eventually promoted into `tools/`. Hand-rolled work that became kit — the same signal, acted on late.

⭐ Note the two different diagnoses the same signal produces: sometimes the tool is MISSING, sometimes it exists and was not FOUND. The instrument does not have to tell them apart — a human reading the list can, and either answer is worth having.

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) A transcript-side detector: scripts written during a session, matched against the served surface.** Bash heredocs, `python3 - <<`, one-off files under a scratchpad. ⚠️ Counter: it reads TRANSCRIPTS, which is a different privacy posture from anything reflow2 does today — `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` says usage telemetry carries the verb and never the object, and a script's SOURCE is design content. The instrument would have to report the SHAPE of the work and never its content, which may not be extractable.

**(b) Ask the agent, at session end, one question: "what did you do by hand that reflow2 should have done?"** Costs one prompt, no new surveillance, and both prior findings surfaced this way — by asking an agent. ⚠️ Counter: self-report, which is precisely the evidence `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` had to fall back on twice and complains about both times. An agent that did not notice a tool existed is the same agent being asked whether one should have.

**(c) Do nothing here, and treat hand-rolled work as a FRICTION report.** `report-friction` already exists for "reflow2 got in my way", and "I had to write this myself" is that. ⚠️ Counter: friction reporting is voluntary and fires on a wall, not on a quiet detour. Nobody files friction for a script that worked.

**(d) Narrow it to the highest-value case: hand-written analysis over the EXPORTED design file.** Much easier to spot than arbitrary scripting, and both 2026 findings are exactly this shape. ⚠️ Counter: a narrow instrument measures a narrow thing, and it would have missed the release-cut driver entirely.

═══ WHAT IT WOULD BE WORTH ═══

If it works it feeds all three open questions at once: it tells `dec:bl-155` which of its 40 are unreachable rather than unused; it hands `dec:idea-a-problem-in-the-users-words-should-retrieve-the-tool-that-answers-it` real question→tool pairs from the tail rather than the head; and it is a layer-④ instrument that does not depend on the agent volunteering anything.

🛑 **AND THE HONEST OBJECTION TO ALL FOUR:** the two findings this node rests on were both found by an agent noticing and saying so, unprompted. It is entirely possible the mechanism does not need building, only asking — and that (b), the cheapest option, is also the one already working.
properties.name: OPEN — can reflow2 detect work a session did BY HAND that a served tool already does, and is that the missing instrument?
properties.rationale:
Recorded separately from the other two because it is a buildable instrument rather than a frame or a retrieval question, and could be attempted without settling either. It is also the only one of the three that produces EVIDENCE rather than consuming it, which is why the closing objection matters: if asking already works, building is over-engineering, and that is the failure mode this project watches for by name.

Written down at all because the signal reproduced three times across five weeks and nothing in the design names it. Two of the three instances found the session's central result, so the pattern is not incidental.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's idea, 2026-08-15, framed by him as aspiration rather than intent — his own words end "but I don't think we are there yet", preserved here as part of the idea rather than trimmed off it.

HIS WORDS: "in some designs, actual design reviews are done and official direction to proceed and other formal docs are required (coming from the US Air Force and US Space Force, documentation is required — maybe we can eventually get to where the graph tracks authorizations to proceed or other official acquisitions documents are in the graph and organizations trust the graph to hold such docs and therefore, keeping external docs is no longer needed — but I don't think we are there yet)."

DELIBERATELY DISTINCT FROM `rule:design-information-lives-in-the-graph-not-in-documents`, which the guard named because this node cites it. THAT RULE GOVERNS THIS REPOSITORY and is settled and enforced. THIS IS A QUESTION ABOUT THE PRODUCT, in a domain where a document is not a convenience: a signed authorisation to proceed is what makes work lawful to start, and whether an organisation will rely on a graph instead is a question about trust, audit and legal standing rather than about storage. The rule can hold while this stays open, and it does.

WHAT ALREADY POINTS THIS WAY, so the starting position is not zero: `Contributor` with `AUTHORED_BY role: approver` records whose sign-off a node carries and when (`acted_at`); `Decision` with `status: accepted` records that something was settled and by whose word; `DesignEpoch` records when; and this project has already settled that rendered pages are ONLY projections of the graph rather than documents in their own right. An authorisation is structurally an approver plus a date plus a scope plus a decision — all four of which the schema can already say.

WHAT IS MISSING IS NOT VOCABULARY, AND THAT IS THE INTERESTING PART: it is EVIDENCE and NON-REPUDIATION. The graph can record that somebody approved something; it cannot today demonstrate to a third party that they did, that the record has not moved since, or that the approver had the authority. A `status: accepted` written by an agent and one written by a general are the same bytes.

THE OPTIONS:

(a) DO NOTHING; FORMAL DOCUMENTS STAY EXTERNAL and the graph points at them with `Artifact.location`. HONEST TODAY, costs nothing, and matches his own concession that a pointer "might be okay". COUNTER: it is exactly the arrangement the no-documents rule was made to end, so the product would be telling consumers to do what this project forbids itself.

(b) THE GRAPH HOLDS THE AUTHORISATION AS TYPED NODES, the signed document stays external as evidence. Cheap, mostly expressible already. COUNTER: it splits the record — authority in the graph, proof in a file — which is the worst of both for an auditor.

(c) THE GRAPH HOLDS THE BYTES TOO. A signed PDF is precisely "what the graph cannot hold inline", the sentence `cap:content-store` was built around — BUILT, VERIFIED, AND DISCONTINUED on his word on 2026-08-09 for zero use across three projects (`dec:the-content-store-is-discontinued`). ⭐ THIS WOULD BE THE FIRST REAL USE THAT DISCONTINUATION SAID DID NOT EXIST. COUNTER, and it is his own from that decision: bytes in a repo grow without bound, and in flo2 could reach terabytes needing backup, security and per-project separation — all MORE true, not less, for controlled or classified acquisition documents.

(d) THE DOCUMENT IS DERIVED FROM THE GRAPH — the official record is generated as a rendering, so there is one source and the document is an output rather than an input. Consistent with the settled doctrine that pages are only renderings. COUNTER: a rendering is not a signature. Something must still capture the act of approval by a person with authority, and that act happens outside reflow2.

⚠️ THE HONEST BLOCKER, stated so it is not rediscovered: whether an organisation trusts a graph is not a feature reflow2 can build. It is earned through audit, retention policy, access control and someone accepting liability. Everything above is necessary and none of it sufficient, and a version that shipped the mechanics while implying the trust would be the most damaging overclaim this project could make.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any real programme would accept it; what standard would have to be met (none has been named); and whether this is one question or two — TRACKING authorisations, versus BEING the authoritative record.
properties.name: IDEA — in acquisition work the formal documents ARE the artefact: design reviews, authorisations to proceed, official direction. Could the graph hold them well enough that an organisation trusts it and stops keeping external docs?
properties.rationale: Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`, options with counters beside them, nothing promoted. Started as a new node rather than merged into the rule after the guard named it: the rule governs this repository and is settled, while this asks whether the product could carry legal-weight documents for someone else — different scope, different decider, and merging them would bury a product question inside a house rule. His \"I don't think we are there yet\" is preserved inside the idea, because a later reader would otherwise read the aspiration as a plan.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-12, and he said plainly at capture time that he expects this to stay unaccepted — he wanted it on the record, not enacted. Nothing here is settled.

HIS WORDS: "should we have a 'purge' skill. I'm getting pretty happy with how reflow2 is now. There are a lot of still unrealized ideas and gaps that we still should work through, but say I'm happy with the current state of the project - can I just 'purge' all the additional things not yet accepted or built? It is a destructive action, but sometimes I'd like to continue reflow2 without every decision and thing I've submitted."

⭐ THE NEED IS REAL AND ALREADY EVIDENCED. `fact:the-owner-uses-reflow2-as-a-funnel-for-random-order-input` records that he pours instructions, ideas, feedback and requirements in as they occur to him. That is the tool working as intended, and its cost is exactly what he is describing: the open list grows faster than anyone decides on it, and eventually it stops being a to-do list and becomes noise.

═══ WHAT THIS WOULD TOUCH, MEASURED 2026-08-12 ═══

  Decision    proposed  104 of 341   carrying 248 edges   2 edgeless
  Requirement proposed   47 of 156   carrying 151 edges   0 edgeless
  Capability  planned    37 of 151   carrying 150 edges   0 edgeless
                        ─────────────────────────────────
                        188 nodes, ~549 edges

🛑🛑 AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT SHOULD DECIDE THIS: **26 OF THE 47 PROPOSED REQUIREMENTS ARE ALREADY SATISFIED BY SOMETHING.** They are built. Their status simply never moved off `proposed`, because status moves only on the owner's word and nobody went back to say so. A purge keyed on "not yet accepted" would delete more than half its own target set WRONGLY — deleting delivered work along with the speculation.

That is not a hypothesis. It is `req:supporting-is-not-conflict` at scale: during the 2026-07-30 prune that requirement was proposed for dropping as "an orphan in all but name", and checking its single edge revealed it was DELIVERED, by a `realized` capability. The lesson recorded then was "low edge count was read as low value, and for a requirement that has been built, edge count is exactly backwards". One hand-check caught one instance; the same reflex applied in bulk would now be wrong 26 times.

═══ THE PART THAT MAY MAKE THIS UNNECESSARY ═══

⭐ **THE THING HE WANTS MAY ALREADY EXIST, AND IT IS NOT DELETION.** `dec:proposed-requirements-pruned` (accepted, his own word, 2026-07-30) already did this once by hand — nine of twenty-six requirements retired — and its finding is the direct answer here:

> "All are `dropped`, not deleted... `dropped` also stops them raising `unsatisfied_requirement`, so the open list means what it says again."

So the BENEFIT he is asking for — an open list that means something again — is delivered by the STATUS CHANGE. Deletion adds nothing to that and additionally destroys the reasoning. That decision's rationale states the cost of going further: "Deleting them would erase why the surviving rules are shaped as they are, and would let the same captures be re-made next quarter by someone who could not see they had been weighed."

The `retire-from-design` skill already carries dropped-not-deleted as its central distinction. So what is missing is not the ACT; it is doing it in BATCH, and being prompted when the list has grown enough to be worth doing — the same shape as `dec:idea-the-graph-notices-the-record-moved-without-being-asked`, where the tool existed and the trigger did not.

═══ THE OPTIONS ═══

A — A BATCH DROP, never a delete. A skill that walks the unaccepted set in classes, proposes a disposition per class, and moves status to `dropped`/`deferred` on his word. Reuses existing vocabulary; nothing is lost; the open list clears. EXPENSIVE: it is 188 nodes, and a batch under one shared reason is precisely what `acknowledge_gaps` already REFUSES by design — "a batch under one shared reason is exactly the erosion the ask-don't-repair rule exists to prevent". So the batching has to be per-class with a stated reason each, which is what made the 2026-07-30 prune trustworthy and also what made it slow.

B — ACTUAL DELETION. What he literally asked for. Cheapest to state, and the only option that genuinely reduces graph size. EXPENSIVE, and the objections are unusually concrete: 549 edges would go with the nodes; the 26 delivered-but-unmarked requirements would go with them; and `dec:ask-not-repair` plus the whole `apply_heal` design exist to stop reflow2 destroying design without a human asserting each case.

C — SNAPSHOT-THEN-CLEAR. Export the design first, then drop hard, on the argument that git holds the memory. EXPENSIVE, and this is the one worth thinking hardest about: a design nobody can query is not memory. `search_design` cannot reach a node that only exists in a file, so "it is in git" means "nobody will ever find it again". The whole point of the graph over documents is that the record is QUERYABLE.

D — DO NOTHING NEW. `retire-from-design` exists and works; the 2026-07-30 prune proves it. What is missing is a nudge when the unaccepted set crosses some size. Free. EXPENSIVE: he has now asked for this, which is evidence the existing route is not discoverable at the moment he wants it.

E — FIX THE UPSTREAM CAUSE INSTEAD. 26 of 47 are stale STATUS, not surplus intent. A pass that asks "these 26 look delivered — accept them?" would shrink the open list by more than half WITHOUT dropping anything, and would make the remaining list honest. Not a purge at all; possibly the thing that removes most of the felt need.

═══ THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded beside the idea rather than used to kill it ═══

The brainstorm skill's own closing rule is that roads not taken are part of the design's memory — "recorded as considered, never deleted... a later session that finds an old idea knows both that it was thought of and that it was not chosen." A purge is the direct negation of that rule. If it is ever built, that rule has to be revisited deliberately rather than quietly broken, because half of what makes this graph worth keeping is that it remembers what was rejected and why.

⚠️ AND A SCOPE NOTE: "not yet accepted or built" is not one population. A `proposed` Decision that is an OPEN QUESTION is not surplus — it is unfinished thinking, and deleting it discards the question rather than answering it. A `planned` Capability nobody will build is different again. Any version of this has to say which of the three it means; the measurement above keeps them apart for that reason.

NOT DECIDED, and expected by its author to stay that way.
properties.name: OPEN — when the owner is happy with the current state, can everything not yet accepted or built be cleared in one deliberate act?
properties.rationale:
Captured on Anthony's explicit instruction to record it without pursuing it — "I expect this one to stay non-accepted, but I did want to capture." That is the funnel working exactly as `fact:the-owner-uses-reflow2-as-a-funnel-for-random-order-input` describes, and this node is itself an instance of the thing it proposes purging, which is worth noticing.

The measurement is what makes it worth keeping rather than merely polite: 26 of 47 proposed requirements are already satisfied, so the felt problem is substantially STALE STATUS rather than surplus intent, and option E addresses more of it than any purge would. The 2026-07-30 prune already established dropped-not-deleted and recorded that `dropped` alone restores the open list — so the benefit sought here is reachable without the destruction.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-23: *"should we ever just completely bring in dynograph-foundation into reflow2? we can cannibalize it and only take what we need/want and no longer have it as an external dependency?"*

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐ WHY THIS IS NOT THE QUESTION HE ALREADY SAID NO TO

`dec:idea-swap-dynograph-foundation-as-the-substitutability-demo` is **REJECTED** — his words, 2026-08-20: *"I don't want to really swap out dynograph-foundation (it works and putting a lot of effort into this is probably not worth it if we aren't going to really swap it out)."* The reason recorded there is general: **a demo that costs as much as the real thing is not a demo.**

THAT OBJECTION DOES NOT REACH THIS IDEA, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE POINT. Swapping means REIMPLEMENTING the functionality behind a contract. Cannibalising means KEEPING THE SAME CODE and moving it in-tree. The rejected option pays full replacement cost; this one pays relocation cost. They are answers to the same underlying question — what to do about the dynograph dependency — and only one of them was priced.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📐 THE MEASUREMENT THAT MATTERS HERE IS NOT THE ONE THE REJECTED NODE MADE

That node measured FILES IMPORTING each crate — 48 / 21 / 3 / 2 / 1 — and concluded that `dynograph_core` at 48 files "is not a module, it is the type vocabulary", so replacing it is a rewrite wearing substitution's name. **That is correct for REPLACEMENT and irrelevant to ABSORPTION**: blast radius measures how much would have to change if the types changed, and vendoring changes no types at all.

THE RELEVANT NUMBER IS THE IMPORTED SURFACE. Measured at HEAD 2026-08-23 from every `use dynograph_*` in `crates/` — **about 21 named items across five crates**:

  dynograph_core      DynoError · Value · Schema · PropertyDef · PropertyType ·
                      NodeTypeDef · EdgeTypeDef · EdgeEndpoint            (8)
  dynograph_storage   StoredNode · StoredEdge · StorageEngine · Value      (4)
  dynograph_graph     GraphBuilder · leiden · strongly_connected_components ·
                      connected_components · find_cycle · cut_structure    (6)
  dynograph_resolution  token_sort_ratio                                   (1)
  dynograph_vector      mean · linear_regression_slope                     (2)

⚠️ BOUND, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: this counts what is NAMED at an import site. It is a measure of the API SURFACE CONSUMED, not of the code volume behind it — `StorageEngine` is one name in front of a RocksDB-backed store, and `leiden` is one name in front of a community-detection implementation. It is a lower bound on work and an upper bound on interface.

⭐ TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE REJECTED NODE'S STATED RISKS, found by looking at what is actually imported rather than at which files import it:

· It warned *"vector search and HNSW are not trivial to reimplement well"*. **reflow2 does not use HNSW, or vector search, at all.** It imports `mean` and `linear_regression_slope` — arithmetic, in one file (`dimensions.rs`). Whatever the case against absorbing `dynograph_vector`, it is not that one.
· `dynograph_resolution` is one function, `token_sort_ratio` — fuzzy string matching, two import sites.

AND ONE RISK IT DID NOT NAME: `dynograph_graph` is where the real intellectual content sits — **leiden community detection, SCC, cycle finding, connected components, cut structure**. Six names, and the ones you would least want to reimplement. Under ABSORPTION that inverts into an argument FOR: you keep the implementation, so difficulty-to-rewrite stops being a cost and becomes the reason the code is worth having in-tree.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ THE OBVIOUS RISK THAT IS ALREADY ANSWERED

"Does this break storyflow, which also depends on dynograph?" — No. `fact:the-diamond-meets-at-dynographs-internals-not-its-interface` measured it: storyflow consumes dynograph as a **REST API over HTTP**; reflow2 consumes it as a **Rust library API**. Disjoint surfaces over one shared implementation. reflow2 dropping the Rust surface cannot touch storyflow's endpoints.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
IDEAS, UNRANKED, each with what it costs

**A. ABSORB EVERYTHING — vendor all five crates in, delete what is unimported, drop the git dependency.** What the question literally asks. Ends the upgrade treadmill, the tag pins, and the `[patch]` dance in `Cargo.toml`; makes reflow2 a single tree with no external source.
   ⚠️ You inherit maintenance of a RocksDB storage engine and a Leiden implementation forever, and you lose the upstream's fixes silently rather than by a pin bump you can read. **Vendoring converts a visible dependency into an invisible one** — the version pin at `reflow2.toml:11` currently carries a written reason for every bump, and that record has no successor once the code is in-tree.

**B. ABSORB THE THREE SMALL ONES ONLY — graph, resolution, vector (9 of the 21 items) — and keep core+storage as the external dependency.** The three that are algorithms rather than substrate.
   ⚠️ Honest counter, and it is the same one the rejected node made about its option C: **the dependency stays, so the treadmill stays.** The saving is partial and must not be sold as removal. What it does buy is that the two crates you would most struggle to justify rewriting are the ones you stop being able to lose.

**C. ABSORB ONLY WHAT IS TINY AND OWNED-BY-ACCIDENT — `token_sort_ratio` (1), `mean` and `linear_regression_slope` (2).** Three functions, almost certainly a few dozen lines, that reflow2 could own outright with no maintenance story worth the name.
   ⭐ Highest ratio of dependency-surface-removed to risk-taken. Removes two entire crates from the manifest.
   ⚠️ And it is nearly cosmetic: `dynograph-core` and `dynograph-storage` are what the dependency actually IS. Two fewer lines in `Cargo.toml` is not independence.

**D. DO NOTHING — it works, it is maintained, and the pin has a reason written on every bump.** The status quo, and what his own standing anti-over-engineering position argues for by default.
   ⚠️ The counter: the reason for absorbing is not technical, it is about what reflow2 IS. A design brain whose substrate is somebody else's repository has a supply chain; one that owns its tree does not. Whether that matters is a judgement about the product, not about the code.

**E. SETTLE THE PRIOR QUESTION FIRST — `dec:idea-is-the-foundation-a-subsystem-or-a-supplier`, still open.** Is dynograph a NINTH SUBSYSTEM of reflow2, or a supplier reached across required interfaces?
   ⭐ **This idea would answer that question by construction rather than by argument.** Absorb it and it is a subsystem; there is no supplier left to be. That may be the strongest thing in favour of A — it dissolves an open modelling question instead of settling it on paper — and equally the strongest reason to answer the prior question first, since doing it in this order decides by doing.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📌 WHAT NOBODY HAS COSTED, so the list is not read as an estimate

No measurement exists of the LINE COUNT behind those 21 names, of what the five crates carry that reflow2 never touches, or of how much of `dynograph-storage` is RocksDB glue versus reflow2-specific. "21 imported items" is an interface measurement and says nothing about how big the tree is that would move. **The cheap next step, if any of this is pursued, is to measure the code volume behind each crate and how much of it is dead from reflow2's point of view** — which is exactly the "only take what we need/want" half of his question, and the half that currently has no number attached to it at all.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 absorb dynograph-foundation outright, keeping only the ~21 items it actually imports, and stop having an external dependency at all?
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`. Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-23, immediately after the v0.39.0 cut.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⏸️ DEFERRED BY ANTHONY, 2026-08-23, THE SAME DAY IT WAS RAISED — and DEFERRED is not REJECTED.

His words: *"okay, let's leave dynograph-foundation as its own repo for now. defer absorbing into reflow2."*

**Status stays `proposed` deliberately.** Nothing was settled, so nothing should read as settled — but this node is now in a different state from one nobody has opened: the question was put to him with a costing and a recommendation, and he chose to wait. A later reader must be able to tell "considered and deferred" from "never looked at", which is the same distinction `review_relations`' note half exists to preserve.

⭐ **THE RECOMMENDATION HE DEFERRED, recorded so the deferral has something to be a deferral OF.** Put to him: absorb `dynograph-resolution` and `dynograph-vector` only (option C), leave `core`, `storage` and `graph` alone. He took none of it for now.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ THE COSTING THE TEXT BELOW SAYS IS MISSING — IT IS NO LONGER MISSING

Measured 2026-08-23 against `../dynograph-foundation` at the checked-out tree. The "📌 WHAT NOBODY HAS COSTED" section below is superseded by this and is kept only because it states correctly what was unknown when the options were written.

**SIZE OF THE FIVE CRATES reflow2 TAKES — 14,384 lines of `src`:**

  dynograph-storage     5,023      dynograph-graph       3,832
  dynograph-vector      2,377      dynograph-core        1,941
  dynograph-resolution  1,211

**reflow2's own tree is 53,005 lines** (reflow2-core 38,300 + reflow2-mcp 14,705). ⇒ **Absorbing all five adds 27% to the tree**, and makes reflow2 the permanent owner of a RocksDB storage engine and a Leiden implementation.

⭐⭐ **AND THE DEAD-WEIGHT MEASUREMENT, which is the "only take what we need" half of the question answered:**

  dynograph-vector      2,377 total · reflow2 uses `stats.rs` (402)  → 83% unused
                        (`hnsw.rs` 1,165 + `distance.rs` 776 are never called)
  dynograph-resolution  1,211 total · reflow2 uses `fuzzy.rs` (260)  → 79% unused
                        (`resolver.rs` 911, an EntityResolver reflow2 never calls)

⇒ For those two crates reflow2 needs **662 of 3,588 lines — 18%**. That is the only place in the set where "cannibalize and take only what we need" is literally true and measurable, and it is why option C was the recommendation.

⚠️ **NOT MEASURED, so the numbers are not read wider than they are:** how much of `core`, `storage` and `graph` is dead from reflow2's point of view. Those three were not broken down, because the recommendation did not turn on it.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📌 THE DISTINCTION THAT CAME OUT OF THE DISCUSSION, and it outlives the deferral

**Two problems look like one here and have different answers.** (a) DEAD WEIGHT — ~2,900 lines of an HNSW index and an entity resolver reflow2 never calls. (b) THE DEPENDENCY ITSELF — the pin, the treadmill, the confirmation sessions (`fact:dynograph-v0130-measured-clean-and-the-pin-is-parked`).

**Option C solves (a) and does nothing for (b).** Whoever picks this up should say which one they are solving before choosing an option; answering the wrong one cheaply is the failure mode available here.

⭐ **WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS, stated so the deferral has a trigger rather than needing to be remembered:** the pin-confirmation cost recurring several more times, or reflow2 ever needing to CHANGE foundation behaviour rather than only call it. Neither has happened.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
DEDUP: the guard surfaced `dec:idea-swap-dynograph-foundation-as-the-substitutability-demo` and `dec:idea-is-the-foundation-a-subsystem-or-a-supplier`; both were read in full and judged DIFFERENT. The first is REJECTED and asks about REPLACING the foundation with a new implementation — a cost this idea does not incur, because absorbing keeps the code. The second asks what the foundation IS; this asks what to DO with it, and would answer that one by construction rather than by argument.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-21. Nothing here is intent and nothing is settled.

HIS IDEA, in his words: "there are 2 sets of linked projects. 1) dynograph-foundation : reflow2 : flo2 and 2) dynograph-foundation : storyflow. the key (but obvious) is that dynograph-foundation is used in both. probably need to do a git pull on both dev_storyflow and storyflow repos on this machine, but all repos/reflow2 projects are on this machine. this would really stress linking multiple projects. also as we discuss making changes to dynograph-foundation, we can't make these in isolation to storyflow."

⭐ IDEA A — THE FOUR-CORNER RUN ITSELF. `dec:linked-repos-poc` composed THREE designs on 2026-08-06 (reflow2 + flo2 + dynograph-foundation) and it worked: zero skipped edges, ids namespaced, one true positive. What has never run is BOTH ARMS AT ONCE with the shared upstream in the middle. That is a different test, not a bigger one: three designs in a line exercise linking; two chains meeting at a shared node exercise whether the tooling can see a diamond at all.

🛑 IDEA B — MEASURED TODAY, IT WOULD HIT TWO KNOWN BLOCKERS, AND BOTH WERE PREDICTED. State of the four corners, read 2026-08-21:

  reflow2               2868 nodes   graph_id `reflow2`                published 3 / required 9 / internal 6
  dynograph-foundation   179 nodes   graph_id `dynograph-foundation`   published 15 / required 0
  flo2                   109 nodes   graph_id `1a97fc1f1de4d5d2`       published 5 / required 1 / internal 1
  dev_storyflow         1373 nodes   graph_id `reflow2`  🔴            published 0 / required 0 (44 internal, 9 unset)

  (1) THE graph_id COLLISION IS REAL AND STILL THERE. dev_storyflow's export and its `.reflow2/graph.id.json` both carry graph_id `reflow2`; only `label` says `dev_storyflow`. `fact:the-diamond-meets-at-dynographs-internals-not-its-interface` called this out on 2026-08-09 as "a collision waiting to happen", and nothing has changed. `compose_and_analyse` takes an explicit namespace so a run can be forced through, but anything keying on graph_id sees two designs claiming to be reflow2.
  (2) STORYFLOW'S ARM IS UNLABELLED. 53 interfaces, none `required`, none `published` — the exact state reflow2 was in before PR #130. Pairing matches complements, so storyflow's arm of the diamond CANNOT pair with anything today. A four-corner run would produce a real seam on one arm and an honest zero on the other, and the zero would need reading correctly.

⭐ IDEA C — HIS SECOND SENTENCE IS THE MORE IMPORTANT ONE, AND IT IS ALREADY AN OPEN QUESTION. "We can't make these in isolation to storyflow" is `dec:idea-a-change-upstream-reaches-the-sibling-that-never-asked` — B and D both depend on A, and A's blast radius stops at its own graph. Stated as a working constraint rather than a question, which is new: he is describing how he intends to work, not asking whether it is a problem.

⭐ IDEA D — AND THE PRIOR RECORD SAYS A NAIVE DIAMOND CHECK WOULD REPORT ALL-CLEAR. `fact:the-diamond-meets-at-dynographs-internals-not-its-interface` measured it: reflow2 consumes dynograph as a RUST LIBRARY API (5 required interfaces), storyflow consumes it as a REST API (6 interfaces). DISJOINT SURFACES over one shared implementation. So "do B and D require the same interface?" answers NO and means nothing. The question that would have caught the real incident is "did the change reach BELOW both published surfaces into shared implementation" — which is about dynograph's OWN internals and is answerable only inside dynograph's graph.

⭐ IDEA E — AND TODAY'S FINDING IS EXACTLY THAT LAYER. `fact:the-storage-seam-is-published-in-design-and-private-in-code`: `ifc:kv-backend` is the ONE node in any of these four designs that names the shared substrate beneath both consumers' surfaces, and its design says `published` while its code says `pub(crate)`. If a four-corner run is meant to find the diamond's real risk, that node is where the risk lives — not at the paired interfaces, which are exactly the places a change CANNOT reach both consumers.

📋 IDEA F — CHEAP PREREQUISITES, offered as observations rather than a plan. A `git pull` on both storyflow repos, as he suggests. dev_storyflow's export lives at `.reflow2/design.export.json` rather than under `docs/design/`, so it is not a committed record the way the other three are, and it was written by reflow2 0.26.1 while dynograph-foundation's was written by 0.16.0 — a four-way compose would span three writer versions. `dec:linked-repos-poc` already showed cross-version composition surviving eight minor versions with nothing dropped, which is evidence and not proof.

⚠️ WHAT IS NOT PROPOSED HERE: changing anything in storyflow or dev_storyflow. AGENTS.md rule 6 forbids landing work there without Anthony's word, and declaring storyflow's `required` interfaces — the step that would make its arm pair — is design about a project this session has not been asked to touch.

DISTINCT FROM the three nodes the guard surfaced. `dec:linked-repos-poc` RAN a three-design composition and is about whether the mechanism works; this asks whether both arms together are a different test. The diamond FACT measured the shape of the two consumers' surfaces on one dated occasion; this proposes an action and records what it would hit today. `dec:idea-a-change-upstream-reaches-the-sibling-that-never-asked` asks how notification should work; this asks whether composing everything at once is how you would find out you needed it.
