properties.name: OPEN — should BOTH dependency chains be composed at once as a four-corner stress test, and is the shared upstream changeable without storyflow in the room?

Captured under the brainstorm skill: recorded as ideas so nothing is lost and nothing is claimed as intent.

Searched the graph BEFORE writing, which is the lesson from earlier this session — `fact:the-seam-report-half-of-the-poc-finally-ran` records re-deriving an analysis the design already held. That search is why ideas C, D and E point at existing nodes rather than restating them.

The state table in idea B was read today rather than recalled, because the last two times this was reasoned about from memory the numbers had moved.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony, 2026-08-04, while BL-186 was mid-build: "maybe we setup an exploratory brainstorm and branch discussing the various ways that we could mass-ingest something like in dev_storyflow. then we can systematically test some different strategies and observe/measure which performs the best." Nothing here is chosen, and no option below has been costed by running it.

THE CASE, MEASURED (dev_storyflow, `/home/ajs7/project/dev_storyflow`, read-only): 1,124 markdown files, 22 MB, ~6M tokens of source text. 17 files at depth 1 and 1,107 below it, so a non-recursive ingest reads 1.5% of the corpus and reports nothing missing. docs/archive 333 files / 16.2 MB (73% of the volume, dated superseded board snapshots); memory/ 380; docs/evidence 195 md + 744 binaries; the plausibly design-bearing remainder is 216 files / 3.3 MB. The fleet's own survey (`reflow2_feedback.md`, api-boss 07426210) read samples rather than filenames and found docs/evidence is at least FIVE types, and that 102 of 334 memory files are unbuilt product intent that reflow2 already models — so a filename-level exclusion of memory/ would be wrong.

(a) INGEST EVERYTHING, RECURSIVELY, NO SELECTION. Cheapest to specify, and the only option needing no human judgement. Expensive to run (~6M tokens before the per-pass multiplier) and the yield is poor: a design dominated by 333 superseded archives. Counter-argument that is specific rather than general — the archives are dated snapshots of the SAME few boards, so they are near-identical to each other, and the DUPLICATES bridge built for corpus-scale asking would turn them into thousands of standing questions. The mechanism that makes batched asking possible is the same one that makes an unselected corpus unusable.

(b) PLAN THEN INGEST (directory triage). Walk the tree, group by directory, report counts + bytes + sample names, put THAT to the user as one batched ask about scope before any document is extracted. Cheap, one round, and it puts the judgement where it belongs — reflow2 cannot know that `archive/` is superseded, and hardcoding a skip-list is the "shaping the model until the tool goes quiet" failure docs/sharpening.md names. Honest counter-argument: directory-level judgement is wrong at file level, and the fleet's own deeper read proves it — docs/evidence holds 5 runbooks and 50 root-cause memos that are knowledge, not evidence, and excluding the directory loses them.

(c) CLASSIFY THEN ROUTE. A cheap per-document classification pass first (design intent / evidence / archive / doctrine / hazard), then route by kind: intent gets the full extraction, evidence becomes an Artifact with an anchor, archive is skipped or marked pending_expansion. More calls but each tiny, and it matches what the corpus actually is rather than what its folders are named. Counter-argument: it adds a classifier whose errors are invisible, and it is the option most likely to quietly mis-file the thing you care about.

(d) EXPLOIT THE CORPUS'S OWN SELF-LABELLING. It already declares itself: 102/334 memory files say FUTURE/parked, evidence files pin commit SHAs, grounding docs are headed "READ-ONLY GROUNDING (no code, no build)". Zero model cost for the signal. Counter-argument, measured: 117 of 334 memory files declare no type at all, and the fleet's filename convention and its frontmatter schema already disagree (`tech_` is 67 by filename and 6 by declared type) — so the labels cover most of the corpus and are silent exactly where it is messiest.

(e) HIGH-VALUE-FIRST, INCREMENTALLY. Ingest docs/architecture (20), docs/decisions (6), docs/grounding (34), briefs and the root planning docs — the 216-file remainder — measure the design that results, then decide whether more is worth it. Fastest to first value, and it composes with the resume story already settled on BL-186 (the graph IS the resume point; sweep the folder, diff against registered Fragments, the remainder is the work left). Counter-argument: it answers "is this useful" and not "does this scale", which is the question BL-186 exists to answer.

WHAT A TRIAL WOULD HAVE TO MEASURE, since none of the above is decidable by argument: documents ingested per unit cost; nodes created against merge candidates raised (signal to noise); how many candidates a HUMAN then has to rule on; coverage_report claimed against unclaimed; and the only test that actually matters, which the scope doc already states — "whether an agent reading 500 heterogeneous markdown files produces a design a human recognises is a trial, not an argument, and it should be run on a real folder before anyone promises this to a user."
properties.name: OPEN — how should a corpus like dev_storyflow's 1,124 documents actually be mass-ingested?
properties.rationale: Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the options survive as options. Anthony proposed trialling several strategies and measuring which performs best; this node holds the strategies, and dec:idea-trial-driven-choice-skill holds the separate question of whether reflow2 should have a way to run that kind of trial at all. Measurements of dev_storyflow are exact greps taken 2026-08-04; the type judgements are the fleet's own from reflow2_feedback.md, not mine — my earlier filename-level read of memory/ was wrong and is corrected above.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled.

THE IDEA: dynograph_graph::shortest_path (unused) returns the actual Path between two nodes. Two readings on a design graph:
(a) surprising_connections reports that two things bridge separate communities. It does not say through what. The path is the explanation a human needs before acting.
(b) "Why is this node in my blast radius?" propagate reports hop distance and impact direction; a named path is the artifact a person can read and check.

CHEAP: exact, already a dependency, and both call sites already hold the network.

WHERE IT LANDS: this is the BL-114 family again from a third direction — a finding that states a conclusion without stating the evidence it walked. BL-141(a) has just done exactly this for circular_dependency (name the contracts the cycle ran through), and that change was small and immediately useful on real data. The same argument applies here.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT: a shortest path is not necessarily the RESPONSIBLE path — several may exist, and showing one implies a causal story that may not be the operative one. BL-141(a) sidestepped this by naming the SET of contracts involved rather than a single route; the equivalent here might be "the edge types this coupling runs through" rather than one path. Worth deciding which before building.
properties.name: OPEN — should a finding say HOW two nodes are coupled, not only that they are?
properties.rationale: Grouped with the explain-what-you-walked family (BL-114, BL-141a) rather than presented as a new idea, because that is what it is — the third instance of the same shape.

properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, from a FIRST-PASS REVIEW OF openmbee.org — the website, the GitHub org listing and one (truncated) architecture page. Nothing here rests on reading their source or running it. Anthony intends to clone the repo for a deep review, and every reading below should be re-tested then. THE OBSERVATION: OpenMBEE's stated purpose is 'an open source collaborative engineering system' that 'enables engineers to work in the language of their choice and easily share and document their work across other tools', with the tagline 'Edit once, use everywhere'. Its answer to multi-organisation, multi-tool work is LINKED DATA — an RDF quadstore where the fourth term is a named graph, so many contexts coexist in one repository, plus transclusion so one source of truth appears in many places. WHY THIS IS THE AREA WHERE THEY ARE PLAINLY AHEAD OF reflow2, and it is not a small one: it is precisely the operating context Anthony described — several organisations with competing, partially-built, differently-motivated designs that must be made to interoperate although they were never designed to. reflow2 has `req:design-composes`, `compose_and_analyse`, `pair_designs` and `mirror_surface`, and `dec:linked-repos-poc` has sat PARKED since it was filed. Those compose EXPORTS — whole documents, pairwise — where OpenMBEE federates a live graph across repositories. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is strong: reflow2 already decided against the architecture that makes their approach possible. `dec:repo-file-embedded` (the graph lives as a repo file, embedded, not a service) and `dec:multi-writer-architecture` (many writers keep the repo file and merge on pull — no hosted service) are the opposite answer to the same question, taken deliberately. A quadstore federation is a service, and adopting the capability may mean reopening those. NOTE ALSO that `dec:central-host` and `dec:live-tier` are BOTH still proposed in this design — OpenMBEE is a fairly complete picture of what saying yes to them costs and buys, which makes it evidence for those two questions whether or not this one is ever answered. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: whether federation can be had at the EXPORT seam — `export_surface` and `mirror_surface` already publish a subset — rather than requiring a live shared store.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 federate heterogeneous designs across organisations the way OpenMBEE does, rather than composing exports?
properties.rationale: Recorded through the brainstorm skill because this is an idea from a landscape review, not intent Anthony has stated. He asked for the areas where OpenMBEE is stronger to be captured as proposed ideas ahead of a deep review, in those words. DELIBERATELY LEFT UNLINKED: `describe_schema {from: Decision, to: Decision}` reports that NO edge type models the pair and that the seventeen which validate do so only through a `*` wildcard — 'validating is not the same as meaning what you intend… prefer leaving the edge out to asserting one that is wrong'. So this will surface as an `orphan_node` info finding, exactly as `dec:linked-repos-poc` does, and that is the true description of a parked idea rather than a defect to route around.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-13, extending his own RNA analogy. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen.

HIS WORDS: "going back to the RNA pairing discussion, can we have each project have a set of defined pair types that could facilitate the combining if two projects in a much faster manner?" — and, earlier in the same message, the shape he was reaching for: "not sure if one project carries a set of one side of the pairs and that would allow the other project to only line up with its corresponding pair on the other side."

⭐ THE ANALOGY IS PRECISE ABOUT WHY PAIRING IS FAST, and that is the real content of the idea. Four bases, two valid pairs, an alphabet fixed by chemistry. Matching is a LOOKUP, not a comparison. reflow2 today does comparison: `req:complementary-pairing` keys on `medium` PLUS `transport_security` PLUS `auth`, then falls back to fuzzy name resolution with a reported middle band a human must answer. Declared pair types would replace the fuzzy step with an exact one.

🛑 AND THE ANALOGY ALSO NAMES ITS OWN LIMIT, which is the honest counterweight. Bases pair by an alphabet that chemistry fixes GLOBALLY and nobody negotiates. Two organisations have no chemistry. A shared pair-type vocabulary requires prior agreement between the parties — and working WITHOUT prior agreement is exactly what the attribute key buys, in exactly the cross-organisation context reflow2 states as its operating breadth. The idea's power and its limit come from the same property.

═══ THE OPTIONS ═══

A — NOTHING. The attribute key already pairs two designs that never coordinated. Faster matching is not obviously the constraint. CHEAPEST, and the null hypothesis.

B — A DECLARED PAIR-TYPE VOCABULARY, his idea literally: each project publishes named types, and combining is a type-name join. FASTEST when both sides share the vocabulary; USELESS when they do not, and worse than useless if two orgs use one name for different contracts — a false pair is more dangerous than no pair, which is the failure the dynograph-foundation trial already produced once from the provider side.

C — ⭐ USE `SPECIFIES`, WHICH ALREADY EXISTS AND HAS NEVER BEEN DRAWN. The schema carries it: "A machine-readable contract artifact defines an entity — an OpenAPI / protobuf / JSON-schema / IDL file SPECIFIES an Interface (its authoritative contract)", with a `format` property. MEASURED 2026-08-13: **zero SPECIFIES edges in reflow2's design.** If two designs' Interfaces are both specified by the SAME artifact, matched on content hash, that is exact pairing with NO vocabulary to negotiate — THE HASH IS THE AGREEMENT. It is the ICD made first-class, which `Interface.designation` already gestures at when it cites 10 U.S.C. 4401 and "what an ICD publishes". Needs no new node type, no new edge type, no enum change, and no stamp move.

D — HYBRID, AND THE ONE THAT DEGRADES HONESTLY: exact when a shared contract artifact is present, attribute-key-plus-fuzzy-name when it is not. Two designs that have agreed get a precise seam; two that have not still get today's answer. Costs a second matching path and a rule for which wins.

═══ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea ═══

⚠️ 1. THE STRONGEST — SPEED IS NOT THE CONSTRAINT, AND MAY NEVER BE. reflow2's own frontier reads seams 0% : ZERO of 73 component couplings run through a declared Interface. There is nothing to pair yet. Optimising the matching step while nothing is labelled is optimising past the actual blocker, which is that boundaries are unclassified.
   📌 STATUS 2026-08-13: PARTLY ADDRESSED. `cap:undeclared-seam-is-named` shipped (PR #167) and now NAMES those 73 pairs as one aggregate gap. It does not declare them — it asks. The blocker is now visible rather than silent.
⚠️ 2. THE FUZZY MIDDLE BAND IS NOT A DEFECT TO REMOVE. Asking a human about an uncertain name match is `dec:ask-not-repair` working as designed. Replacing it with exact lookup removes the question by removing the cases that raise it — which is only an improvement where the shared vocabulary is real.
⚠️ 3. A SHARED VOCABULARY IS A COORDINATION COST, and this project spends heavily to avoid exactly that: `dec:identity-out-of-band` refuses a registry that hands out ids, `dec:advisory-concurrency` refuses a lock manager. A pair-type registry is the same shape as the things twice rejected.
⚠️ 4. `SPECIFIES` IS UNUSED, SO THE SUBSTRATE IS UNTESTED. Zero edges means option C's mechanism has never run on real data, and every linking defect this project has found came from running the thing rather than reading it.

📌 WHERE THE IDEA IS STRONGEST, and it is narrower than "a vocabulary": WITHIN ONE OWNER'S NEIGHBOURHOOD. Ten reflow2 designs live under ~/project, all Anthony's. A shared pair-type vocabulary across designs one person controls is entirely achievable, needs no negotiation, and would make combining them mechanical. It is the cross-ORGANISATION case that cannot assume it — so the honest question may be whether reflow2 supports both, with the vocabulary as an optional accelerator over an attribute-based floor. That is option D.


═══════════ SHARPENED 2026-08-13, SAME SESSION ═══════════

Anthony then described the combining PROCESS step by step: "can first filter out interfaces in a graph. secondly, of the interfaces, can they be labeled as publisher, subscriber, or both. then you kind of have 3 RNA pairs. the agent then has the job of mapping publishers with subscribers (one RNA pair) and both with both. if the agent is unable to pair based on reason, you now have a gap or issue to solve."

⭐⭐ THE FIRST FINDING IS THAT HE RE-DERIVED THE BUILT ALGORITHM, and this is recorded as a NON-finding on purpose rather than filed as new. Verified against `crates/reflow2-core/src/seam.rs:464` rather than assumed: `offers = published | both`, `needs = required | both`. Three labels, four valid combinations — published↔required, published↔both, both↔required, both↔both — never like-with-like, which `two_publishers_never_pair_with_each_other` pins as a test. And the unpairable DO become findings, in five buckets: `paired` (the seam), `unmet_needs` (a subscriber nothing publishes), `dead_surface` (a publisher nobody subscribes to), `conflicts` (role-compatible but cannot connect on medium/transport_security/auth), `candidates` (the fuzzy middle band — the code comment reads "worth a human's attention, never acted on").

The RNA analogy was his on 2026-07-27 and produced `req:complementary-pairing`. Reasoning from it again nine days later reproduced the same algorithm from a different starting point. THAT IS CORROBORATION, NOT REPETITION — an analogy that regenerates the same structure twice is doing work rather than decorating a decision already made.

🛑 AND THE ONE GENUINE DELTA: "if the agent is unable to pair BASED ON REASON". His version has an AGENT JUDGEMENT step. The built version has none — pairing is a computed key end to end, and no LLM is consulted at any point. That opens three further options:

E — THE AGENT PROPOSES ON `candidates`, THE GRAPH STILL COUNTS, THE HUMAN STILL DECIDES. Let an agent argue for or against each middle-band pair in prose, ATTACHED to the candidate rather than resolving it. Exactly `dec:three-party-checks` — "the LLM speaks, the graph remembers and counts, the human decides" — applied to a band that currently arrives with a score and no argument. A score says HOW CLOSE two names are; it never says WHY they might be the same contract.

F — 📌 THE AGENT REASONS OVER `conflicts` INSTEAD, and this is the strongest narrow form. A conflict today says "you publish REST/JWT/TLS, I need REST/none/none, we cannot connect" — true, and silent on whether that is a real incompatibility or one side simply never filled in `auth`. An agent that has read both designs can tell "they left it unspecified" from "these genuinely disagree", and those need opposite actions. This is the one place a computed answer is PROVABLY incomplete, because `unspecified` is the honest default on three of the key's fields and the key cannot distinguish silence from disagreement.

G — THE AGENT PAIRS OUTRIGHT where the key is silent. RECORDED AS REJECTED-LEANING so it is not re-proposed by someone who has not read the trial: a false pair is worse than no pair, and the dynograph-foundation session already produced one from the computed side — "I require REST" matching an unauthenticated liveness probe. An LLM guessing would be the same failure with less traceability.

⚠️ 5. A FURTHER COUNTER-ARGUMENT ON E: the candidate band exists precisely so a HUMAN decides. Putting an agent between the score and the person risks the band being cleared by argument rather than by judgement, which is the erosion `dec:ask-not-repair` is written against.
⚠️ 6. AND `unlabelled` MUST STILL BE COUNTED whatever is chosen. `req:complementary-pairing` already requires it: a boundary nobody classified must not read as `internal`, or a design that never did the labelling pairs with nothing and reports a clean seam.


═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SHARPENED AGAIN 2026-08-13, AND THIS ONE MOVES THE QUESTION:
LINKABILITY IS THE USER'S ASSERTION; REFLOW2'S JOB IS REFINEMENT
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

ANTHONY'S WORDS, and they settle what pairing is FOR:

"maybe it is too much for two+ projects just to be linked kind of in an ad-hoc approach (something like a user saying 'link projectA and ProjectB' and just turning it over to reflow2 and the agent to figure out how. in defining flo2, I knew from the get go that it was going to have to use reflow2. it became a much more measured/deliberate approach of having flo2 read the reflow2 code and graph and then identifying (the agent) how it'd interface"

and then, decisively:

"I think the deliberate part of purposefully linking two projects is the user's responsibility that two projects can actually be linked. if projectA was a design for a house and ProjectB was design a python service for accounting, that is a failure on the user and ad-hoc/automatic linking can't occur (unless we do some very creative linking). I knew when I designed flo2 that it was going to use reflow2 - is the interface spec perfect? no, it is still in work, but I know the two projects can roughly interface with each other and precisely the point of all this is to use reflow2 to make a clearly defined and fully specified interface"

⭐⭐⭐ **THE CORRESPONDENCE IS AN INPUT, NOT AN OUTPUT.** That inverts the framing every option above assumed. reflow2 is not being asked whether a house design and an accounting service relate — asserting linkability is the USER'S job, and getting it wrong is a user error rather than a tool failure. What reflow2 is for is taking a roughly-known, still-in-work correspondence and driving it to a **clearly defined and fully specified interface**.

⇒ **WHICH MAKES `seam_report` THE LOAD-BEARING TOOL AND `pair_designs` THE CONVENIENCE**, and today the documentation has that backwards. `seam_report`'s own parameter doc reads: *"`pair_designs` computes these from complementary roles since 2026-07-30; supply them by hand only when a design has not declared its roles yet"* — treating the hand-supplied pair as a FALLBACK. Under Anthony's model the hand-supplied pair is the PRIMARY and correct input, and computed pairing is an accelerator for the case where nobody has asserted anything yet.

═══ MEASURED THE SAME DAY, AND IT SETTLES WHICH TOOL ANSWERS THE GOAL ═══

Full run recorded in `fact:reflow2-flo2-seam-measured-2026-08-13`. The two halves:

  COMPUTED (`pair_designs`, both designs as they stand)
    paired 0 · conflicts 10 · unmet_needs 5 · dead_surface 2 · candidates 1
    and with the role corrected in memory, the TRUE seam scores 64 while a WRONG
    match (ifc:graph-export, sharing the word "design") scores 81 and outranks it.

  ASSERTED (`seam_report`, pair supplied by hand: ifc:mcp-tools ↔ ifc:reflow2-design-api)
    agreed 3 · incompatible 0 · differs 0 · UNSTATED BY NOBODY 5
    → auth, transport_security, operations, error_model, payload_schema

⇒ **THE ASSERTED PAIR PRODUCES EXACTLY THE ANSWER HIS GOAL ASKS FOR** — the two projects are compatible as far as anything is stated, and five named axes stand between "roughly interfaces" and "fully specified". The computed path produced nothing usable on the same seam. That is the strongest evidence yet for the reframe, and it was obtained by RUNNING the two projects at each other rather than by reasoning about them.

🛑 AND IT CAUGHT REFLOW2 BEING THE UNDER-SPECIFIED SIDE. flo2 states `auth: none` and `transport_security: tls`; reflow2's own PUBLISHED `ifc:mcp-tools` states NEITHER — *"the side that assumed less finds out in production"*. Only a cross-project check surfaced it, which is an argument for linking as a DESIGN INSTRUMENT rather than only as a delivery step.

═══ WHAT THIS CHANGES ABOUT A/B/C/D, none of them yet taken ═══

· **A (nothing) is weakened.** Computed pairing found 0 on the one real seam and ranked a wrong match first; it is not currently sufficient for the deliberate case.
· **B (pair-type vocabulary) is answered rather than chosen.** Anthony's own framing supplies what B was reaching for without a registry: the user ASSERTS the pair. No shared alphabet is negotiated because the assertion is per-link, not per-vocabulary.
· **C (`SPECIFIES`) is now empirically motivated**, and is the durable form of the assertion: recording "this boundary of mine IS that boundary of yours" at the moment it is authored, with the content hash as the agreement, rather than re-deriving it from names later.
· **D (hybrid) survives unchanged** and is probably the shape: assertion first, computation as the accelerator.

📌 THE UNBUILT PIECE THIS EXPOSES: **there is no way to RECORD the correspondence.** flo2's `ifc:reflow2-design-api` exists BECAUSE someone read reflow2's `ifc:mcp-tools`; nothing in either graph says so, and the pair had to be re-supplied by hand at every run. `mirrors` on reflow2 returns 0, so the built mechanism for "I designed against your published surface, pinned at this version" has never been used on the pair of projects that most obviously calls for it. **The pairing information was free at design time and thrown away.**

NOT DECIDED.
properties.name: OPEN — how should two designs be paired: declared pair types, a shared contract artifact, or (SETTLED) the user asserting the correspondence and reflow2 refining it?
properties.rationale:
Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the thinking survives without being claimed as intent, and kept separate from the graph_id question because the two are unrelated. Worth keeping for one measured fact and one connection: SPECIFIES exists in the schema with a format property and has zero edges in reflow2's own design, so the mechanism for exact contract-based pairing is already built and never exercised; and the RNA analogy, which has already earned its place once by predicting that compatibility needs more than one point of contact, here argues BOTH ways — a fixed alphabet is why base pairing is fast AND why two organisations cannot borrow the trick.

⭐ THE AGENT-REASONING BRANCH IS SETTLED, 2026-08-13, ANTHONY'S WORD: "I agree with the approach without an agent 'reasoning'." Options E, F and G are CLOSED — no LLM enters the pairing loop, on candidates, on conflicts, or anywhere else. Pairing stays a computed key end to end.

WHAT THAT COSTS, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED LATER AS A SURPRISE: option F was the strongest of the three and it named a real hole. A `conflict` says "you publish REST/JWT/TLS, I need REST/none/none" and CANNOT distinguish a genuine disagreement from one side never having filled in `auth` — because `unspecified` is the honest default on three of the key's fields. That gap does not close by itself. It now has to be closed some other way, if it is closed at all: by a detector that reports HOW MUCH of a conflict rests on unspecified fields, by the pairing report naming which side was silent, or by a human reading the two boundaries. Declining the agent does not make the computed answer complete; it means the completion must be computed or asked, never inferred.

WHY THIS IS CONSISTENT WITH THE PROJECT RATHER THAN A NARROWING OF IT: `dec:three-party-checks` gives the LLM the speaking role, not the counting one, and everything reflow2 computes is deliberately verdict-free — `granularity` refuses to call an observation a defect, `maturity` refuses to grade a band, `ility_report` refuses a score. An agent arguing a pair into or out of existence would be the LLM doing the counting.

⭐⭐ SHARPENED AGAIN 2026-08-13 AND THE QUESTION MOVED: Anthony settled that ASSERTING TWO PROJECTS CAN BE LINKED IS THE USER'S RESPONSIBILITY, not something reflow2 discovers — "if projectA was a design for a house and ProjectB was a design for a python service for accounting, that is a failure on the user." reflow2's job is refinement: taking a roughly-known correspondence and making it "clearly defined and fully specified." The correspondence is an INPUT.

That was then MEASURED against flo2 the same day (fact:reflow2-flo2-seam-measured-2026-08-13) and the measurement backs it: computed pairing returned 0 paired and ranked a wrong match above the right one, while the hand-asserted pair returned 0 incompatible, 3 agreed and 5 axes stated by nobody — exactly the punch-list his goal asks for. It also caught reflow2's own published boundary being the under-specified side. A/B/C/D remain open, but B is answered rather than chosen (a per-link assertion needs no negotiated vocabulary) and C is now the durable form of the assertion rather than a theoretical preference.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-25, correcting the evidence base and supplying the doctrine. Nothing here is planned and #334 stands.

═══ HIS METHODOLOGICAL CORRECTION, WHICH IS RIGHT AND MATTERS ═══

*"most of these are after the fact. meaning, they were developed before reflow2 really started defining rungs. they might have been done differently if reflow2 defined rungs when these designs were first started."*

**THE SAMPLE IS CONTAMINATED.** Every design measured — flo2, qbench, dynograph-foundation, dev_storyflow, mapwright, music_graph, reflow2's own — was built while reflow2 offered no ladder concept, no instruction mentioning `level`, and no detector for depth. They are evidence of what happens with NO GUIDANCE, not evidence of what a guided user would produce. Any conclusion of the form "users only go two rungs deep, so depth does not matter" is unsupported, and one was drawn from them earlier today and is withdrawn here.

*"maybe better to use real world examples or case studies than our own, which were all done prior to a complete reflow2."*

═══ THE DOCTRINE HE SUPPLIED — LAYERS ARE SET UPFRONT, BY RULE ═══

**You do not guess the number of layers.**
1. **COGNITIVE LIMIT / SPAN OF CONTROL — 3 to 7 children per parent.** Twenty components under one subsystem cannot have their interfaces managed by a human. Add a layer.
2. **INDEPENDENT LIFECYCLES** — a part with its own upgrade cycle, testing process or supplier belongs in its own layer.
3. **CONWAY'S LAW** — layers tend to match team structure; three engineering teams usually means three main subsystems.
4. **STOP** when going deeper adds no value for tracking requirements, managing risk, or assigning work.
Standard breakdown: SoS ▸ System ▸ Subsystem ▸ Component ▸ Part/Material.

⭐⭐ THE INVERSION, AND IT IS THE WHOLE IDEA: **SPAN OF CONTROL MAKES DEPTH A CONSEQUENCE, NOT A CHOICE.** If a parent may hold 3–7 children, then the number of layers a design NEEDS falls out of how many parts it has. Nobody declares it and nobody has to know a vocabulary. That is a third answer to the ladder question that neither the closed enum nor the open ladder considered: reflow2 could COMPUTE the depth a design requires and say so, instead of asking the user to name rungs.

═══ AND IT IS TESTABLE ON CONTAMINATED DATA, BECAUSE IT IS STRUCTURAL ═══

Span of control is a property of the graph, not a preference, so the contamination does not block it. MEASURED 2026-08-25, children per parent on the CONTAINS spine:

    design                 fan-out per parent          parents over 7
    flo2 (concept)         6, 2, 2, 1, 1               0  ✓
    qbench                 5, 3                        0  ✓
    dynograph-foundation   4, 4, 3, 2                  0  ✓
    dev_storyflow          18, 11, 1, 1                2  (worst: storyflow = 18)
    reflow2 (own)          28, 25, 13, 10, 6, 4, 2, 2  4  (worst: coherence-loop = 28)

⭐ THE SMALL, DELIBERATELY-SHAPED DESIGNS ALREADY OBEY THE RULE WITHOUT BEING TOLD. flo2, qbench and dynograph-foundation are inside 3–7 everywhere. The two that violate it are the two grown by accretion over months — and **reflow2's OWN design is the worst offender in the sample, at 28 children under `sys:coherence-loop`, four times the limit.** That is a good reason to keep using it as a litmus test and a bad reason to treat it as an exemplar.

⭐ IT ALSO EXPLAINS THE FLATNESS FOUND EARLIER WITHOUT NEEDING A PREFERENCE. dev_storyflow has 84–101 components with ZERO nesting; the earlier reading was "users do not need depth". Under this doctrine that is not a preference, it is a **defect with a number attached**: 101 children under one Project is 14x the upper bound, and the design needs roughly two more layers. The rule turns a shrug into a finding.

═══ WHAT REFLOW2 COULD DO WITH IT ═══

- **A `span_of_control` detector.** Cheap, deterministic, and it fires on the graph reflow2 already has. NOT already built: `evaluate_allocation`'s `god_components` looks for ARTICULATION POINTS in the capability-coupling graph — a different axis entirely, and it would not have caught any of the five rows above.
- **A derived answer to "how many layers do I need?"** — computed from part count and fan-out, offered rather than demanded.
- ⚠️ AND THE HONEST OBJECTION, recorded beside it: 3–7 is a HUMAN cognitive bound, and reflow2's stated posture is `dec:report-dont-judge`. Shipping 7 as a threshold would embed a rule of thumb as if it were a law, which is exactly the over-modelling this project refuses elsewhere. Reporting the FAN-OUT and letting the reader judge is the version that survives that objection; a hard threshold is the version that does not.
- Rules 2 and 3 are NOT computable from the graph today. Independent lifecycles would need release/supplier data reflow2 does not hold, and Conway's Law would need team structure — `OWNED_BY` exists and could carry it, which is the nearest hook.

═══ THE EVIDENCE THAT WOULD ACTUALLY SETTLE IT ═══

Real-world case studies rather than this workshop's own output. Candidates, none pursued: published INCOSE/NASA systems-engineering case studies with documented WBS depth; open architecture documents (an aircraft, a spacecraft bus, a telescope control system); and the one closest to hand — **NSLS-II's bluesky stack, which Anthony works on and which is a real ~10-year-old system nobody at this workshop designed.** That last one is the only sample available that is both real and uncontaminated by reflow2.
properties.name: OPEN — span of control (3–7 children per parent) makes the NUMBER OF LAYERS a computed consequence rather than a declared choice; and every design measured so far predates reflow2 having rungs at all
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill: recorded as an idea, nothing promoted, nothing settled.

Kept separate from `dec:idea-is-a-declared-rung-name-the-right-shape-for-decomposition-depth` (which compares five carriers for depth, all of which DECLARE it) and from `dec:the-decomposition-ladder-is-open-not-a-fixed-enum` (which decided the ladder opens). This proposes that depth need not be declared at all — that span of control makes the number of layers a computed consequence of part count. That is a different kind of answer from any of the five shapes, which is why it is its own node rather than a sixth bullet on that one.

It also carries Anthony's correction to the evidence base, which invalidates a conclusion drawn earlier today from the same measurements.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-09, relayed via dev_storyflow's api-boss: \"If nothing else, we'll see what areas of the graph are not claimed by anyone (orphans). Not sure reflow2 has this feature to detect orphans in ownership.\"

⭐ IT IS A DIFFERENT AXIS FROM orphan_node, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE WHOLE POINT.
  orphan_node        structurally disconnected — nothing says what it is FOR.
  ownership orphan   well-connected, realized, verified, SHIPPING — and nobody accountable.

⚠️ A NODE CAN BE STRUCTURALLY PERFECT AND GOVERNANCE-ORPHANED, and that is the more dangerous state precisely because NOTHING ABOUT IT LOOKS WRONG. Every existing detector would pass it: it satisfies a requirement, a component holds it, an artifact realizes it, a check verifies it. The only thing missing is a person, and no detector asks about people.

IT IS ALSO THE THIRD MEMBER OF A FAMILY THIS PROJECT FOUND TWICE TODAY, which is why it is worth naming as a class rather than a feature:
  - req:the-design-says-what-was-built-and-never-used — built, and NOTHING CONSUMES IT.
  - req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read — declared, and NOTHING READS IT.
  - this one — shipping, and NOBODY OWNS IT.
Every existing gap asks what is MISSING FROM A NODE. All three of these ask what is missing AROUND a node, and none of the seven capability gaps can express that shape.

STRICTLY DEPENDENT ON THE EDGE. There is nothing to detect the absence of until ownership is expressible — dec:idea-ownership-is-the-third-who-axis holds that question. Recorded separately for exactly that reason: the edge can exist without the detector, the detector cannot exist without the edge, and a single node holding both could only be half-answered.

⚠️ THE HARD PART, AND IT IS A DESIGN INPUT RATHER THAN A SETTING — api-boss's, and it is the strongest objection on the table: WHICH NODE TYPES ARE OWNABLE? In their 1,127-node graph most nodes legitimately have no owner; their example is exact — \"a Constraint about prose rendering is nobody's in the accountability sense.\" A naive detector therefore fires on the MAJORITY of a mature graph and becomes a signal trained to be ignored, which is the permanently-red-check failure this project has now written down three times. But in a two-person project the design is probably mostly partitioned, so the same detector is nearly silent and genuinely useful. ⇒ OWNABILITY LOOKS LIKE A PER-PROJECT DECLARATION, NOT A FIXED RULE, and the same feature behaves very differently at those two scales.

THE SHAPES, with counters beside rather than argued down:

(A) A GAP — `unowned_region`, one per ownable node with no owner. Appears in the loop where people already look. COUNTER: the ownability problem above hits this hardest, because a gap that fires on the majority is worse than no gap.

(B) A REPORT — an ownership census: what is owned, by whom, and what is not, reported as a FACT the way granularity_report and surprising_connections are. Cannot nag. COUNTER: a report nobody runs is invisible; it would need a line in graph_report to be seen.

(C) A COVERAGE NUMBER — \"N of M ownable nodes have an owner\", one line, the same shape as the trajectory bands and the certainty line. Cheapest to read, hardest to ignore, and it degrades gracefully at both scales because a low number in a fleet graph is a true statement rather than N nags. COUNTER: a number says nothing about WHICH, so it needs (B) behind it to be actionable.

(D) SCOPED TO A DECLARED PARTITION — a project declares which types are ownable, and the detector only speaks about those. Answers the hard part directly. COUNTER: it is a new declaration to maintain, and an unmaintained one silently narrows the detector to nothing, which is the same class as an unread marker.

⚠️ WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN, and it is the trap all three of today's findings share: shipping the marker without the computation that reads it, or shipping a computation that fires on correct work. reflow2 has now met the first failure eight times over in its own edge vocabulary and has doctrine against the second in dec:read-hint-shape.

NOTHING IS PROMOTED. Anthony raised the question and said he was not sure the feature existed; it does not.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 detect OWNERSHIP orphans: well-connected, realized, shipping, and nobody accountable?
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill: `proposed`, options with counters, nothing promoted, and separated from the edge question it depends on so neither can be half-answered.

Worth stating why this one is recorded at all when it cannot be built yet: it is the third instance in one day of a shape reflow2 has no vocabulary for — absence AROUND a node rather than absence IN it — and the other two were captured as intent this session. Recording it keeps the family visible; whether it becomes a fourth requirement is Anthony's call, not a consequence of the first three.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-09, on being told that two retirement edges exist and neither is read: \"these are a new type of orphans that I never thought about and curious why until now haven't they surfaced? ... should reflow2 have something that detects these class of orphans, and are there other orphan developments (actually implemented design) that nothing detects or surfaces?\"

⚠️ PROVENANCE CORRECTION FIRST, because he asked what search produced the SUPERSEDES claim and the honest answer is NONE. It was read out of dec:one-retire-edge, which records a schema sweep another session ran on 2026-07-28. It was relayed as though freshly measured. THE MEASUREMENT BELOW WAS THEN ACTUALLY RUN, and it is what this node is for.

=== THE MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-09, against reflow2's own 1,869-node / 7,051-edge design ===

Method, stated because the first cut of it was too crude to trust: an edge type counts as REACHED if it is instantiated in this design, OR named in `structural_rule`'s propagation table (11 edges), OR named anywhere in non-test Rust outside its own `pub const` declaration. Anything failing all three is declared vocabulary with nothing behind it.

EIGHT OF SIXTY EDGE TYPES ARE DECLARED AND UNREACHED ON EVERY TEST:
  COMPLIES_WITH · CONTAINS_EPOCH · EVOLVES_INTO · IMPOSES · MITIGATES · SUPERSEDES · SUPPLEMENTS · VIOLATES_RULE

SEVEN OF TWENTY-NINE NODE TYPES HAVE ZERO INSTANCES HERE:
  Anchor · DimensionAssessment · DimensionObservation · EnvironmentRule · Flow · QualityGate · ReadinessAssessment

FIVE MORE EDGE TYPES ARE INSTANTIATED BUT REACHED ONLY GENERICALLY — not in the propagation table, never named in code: ABOUT_ENTITY (117 instances), CAUSES (9), INTERACTS_WITH (4), OPERATES_IN (3), VALID_TO (2). These are not dead; they are unnamed, which means nothing would notice if they stopped working.

⭐ THREE OF THESE ALREADY HAVE INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION, which is why this is a class and not a curiosity:
  - VIOLATES_RULE — dev_storyflow filed it HOURS before this measurement: `describe_schema{from:Component, to:DesignRule}` returns 17 candidates and VIOLATES_RULE is not among them, so a session doing the documented thing cannot discover the edge named for the job. They used VIOLATES instead and said it is presumably wrong.
  - QualityGate — dev_storyflow's governance trial, item ⑦: \"I could not find an honest use, and I think that is informative... Recording the decline, because 'the type exists and nobody instantiated it' is otherwise indistinguishable from nobody having tried.\"
  - Anchor — dec:anchor-retire-or-implement is already OPEN on exactly this: \"superseded by Snapshot but still advertised: retire it or implement it?\"

=== WHY IT NEVER SURFACED, which is his real question ===

EVERY DETECTOR IS INSTANCE-LEVEL AND THIS IS A VOCABULARY-LEVEL FACT. detect_gaps computes over nodes and edges that EXIST — unsatisfied_requirement needs a Requirement, disconnected_community needs a cluster of two or more, orphan_node needs a node. A declared type with zero instances produces NOTHING for any of them to anchor on. The blind spot is not an oversight in any one detector; it is that no detector asks a question ABOUT THE SCHEMA rather than about the design.

⭐⭐ AND THE SHARPEST PART: THE RULE ABOUT UNREAD THINGS IS ITSELF UNREAD. dec:edge-orthogonality is ACCEPTED and says a vocabulary distinction earns its keep ONLY IF A COMPUTATION READS IT — it is the decision that retired VALIDATES and ENABLES on precisely this reasoning. Nothing computes it. So the principle was applied ONCE, by hand, and the eight above accumulated afterwards with nobody to notice.

=== ARE THERE OTHER UNSURFACED ORPHAN DEVELOPMENTS? YES, AND ONE IS ALREADY OPEN ===

dec:bl-155 (OPEN): \"40 of 132 served tools were never called in the retained sample, and reflow2 cannot tell 'unused' from 'unreachable'.\" That is the same shape one level out — built surface nobody reaches — and it has the same cause: reflow2 measures how well the DESIGN covers the SYSTEM, and never how well anything covers the SURFACE reflow2 itself ships.

THE OPTIONS, with what is cheap or expensive about each:

(A) A CENSUS REPORT, NOT A GAP — a `vocabulary_census` naming declared-but-unreached types, reported as a FACT the way granularity_report and surprising_connections are. CHEAPEST, and it cannot false-positive into nagging. COUNTER: a report nobody runs is the same failure one level along; it would need a line in graph_report to be seen.

(B) A GAP AT LOW SEVERITY — `unreached_vocabulary`, one per declared type with nothing behind it, acknowledgeable. Makes it appear in the loop where people already look. COUNTER, AND IT IS SERIOUS: a demonstrator legitimately does not use Flow or ReadinessAssessment, so this would fire on correct work in every young design — the exact thing dec:read-hint-shape and the phase-nudge doctrine were built to avoid. Firing on the SCHEMA (a fixed 60/29) rather than on the user's design might dodge that, since it is reflow2's own vocabulary being judged rather than the consumer's modelling.

(C) SCOPE IT TO THE SHIPPED SURFACE ONLY — make it reflow2's own maintenance instrument (a tools/ script, like toolsnap), not a served capability. Honest about who the finding is for: a consumer does not care that reflow2 declares SUPPLEMENTS, and rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party would ask what the CONSUMER gets. COUNTER: the consumer DOES get something — describe_schema offers them these types, and VIOLATES_RULE proves a consumer can waste time on one.

(D) DO NOTHING NEW AND JUST PRUNE — decide dec:one-retire-edge and dec:anchor-retire-or-implement, delete what loses, and accept that the next accumulation goes unnoticed too. COUNTER: this is exactly what happened after dec:edge-orthogonality, and eight more arrived.

⚠️ WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN, whichever is chosen: another marker nothing reads. That is the finding this node is about, and it would be a fourth instance of it.

BOUND, stated rather than glossed: this measured ONE design — reflow2's own. A type with zero instances HERE may be in daily use in dev_storyflow or flo2, and the census would need to be per-design to mean anything to a consumer. The 8 unreached-on-every-test edges are the stronger claim, because those have no code behind them anywhere and that is a property of the SHIPPED BUILD rather than of this graph.

NOTHING IS PROMOTED.

The provenance correction is inside the decision text rather than only in conversation, because the claim that started this thread was relayed from another session's sweep as if freshly measured, and a later reader deserves to know which parts were measured today and which were quoted. The measurement in this node WAS run today, with its method stated so it can be re-run or disputed.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Source: Alex Sligar's 2026-08-05 research, specifically Understand Anything's "diff impact analysis that shows what a given change touches". STILL OPEN.

THE IDEA: reflow2's impact analysis runs design-first — add_change_event then propagate_change, seeded by the design node you are about to touch. The survey's tools run it code-first: here is a diff, here is what it touches. Those are opposite directions, and the code-first direction is the one a developer actually has in hand at review time.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, and this was checked rather than assumed: reconcile_artifacts takes observed artifact hashes and returns `propagation_seeds` — "the design nodes the changes land on" — explicitly documented to be fed to propagate_from. So the code-to-design hop is BUILT. The composition is: changed files, to registered artifacts by hash, to REALIZES edges, to capabilities and upward. Nothing is missing in the core.

WHAT IS THEREFORE ACTUALLY OPEN, and it is smaller than the survey makes it sound: (a) nothing computes the hashes from a commit — reflow2 performs no file I/O by design, so a caller must do it, and no caller currently does it from a git diff; (b) the CI gate checks the committed export for drift and open gaps, not "what does this commit touch upstream"; (c) the answer is only as complete as artifact registration, and an unregistered file lands on nothing at all, which would read as "this change is safe" rather than "this change is unmapped". That last one is the real risk and it is the same failure mode as the release-manifest problem: silence that looks like a pass.

WHAT IS CHEAP: a driver script over `git diff --name-only` plus hashing, calling reconcile_artifacts then propagate_from. That is wiring, in the same family as tools/reflow2_check.py, and needs no core change.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT: a per-commit blast radius is only as trustworthy as REALIZES coverage, and an incomplete golden thread turns it into a confident understatement — which is worse than no answer, because a reviewer will believe it. If this is built, the honest version must report unmapped files as UNMAPPED and loudly, not fold them into a clean result. The existing unrealized_capability gap is the design-side half of that problem; this is the artifact-side half and there may be nothing that detects it.
properties.name: OPEN — should a git diff be a direct input to impact analysis, given reconcile_artifacts already returns propagation_seeds and nothing drives it from a commit?
properties.rationale: Recorded as an idea rather than a gap because the machinery it asks for already exists and only the driver is absent, which makes it a small increment rather than a design question — except for the unmapped-file silence, which is a design question and is the reason this is worth a node at all.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled.

THE OBSERVATION: reflow2 uses exactly TWO functions from dynograph-vector — mean and linear_regression_slope, both in dimensions.rs. The depth axis records DimensionObservations and computes drift as a slope WITHIN one dimension over time.

THE IDEA: pearson_correlation and spearman_rank_correlation (unused) would answer a question the axis cannot currently ask — do two dimensions move TOGETHER across components? "Does complexity track defect count?" "Does coupling track change frequency?" Spearman is the rank version, so it survives non-linear but monotone relationships and is the safer default on small samples.

CHEAP: pure functions, already a dependency, and the observations are already stored.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, and there are two. First, this is the most SPECULATIVE idea in the batch — no backlog item asks for it and no trial has reported wanting it, so it is a capability looking for a user. Second and more serious: correlation invites causal reading, and a design brain reporting "complexity correlates with defects" will be read as "complexity causes defects". The schema already takes this seriously — the CAUSES edge carries a `basis` enum (observed / correlational / causal / spurious) with the instruction "do not assert causal without a mechanism" — so the vocabulary for the caveat exists, but the report would have to carry it loudly.
properties.name: OPEN — should the depth axis compute CORRELATION between dimensions, not just drift within one?
properties.rationale: The only genuinely unexplored idea in dynograph-vector; the rest of that crate is either already used (mean, slope), already a parked question (embeddings), or thin (softmax, percentile).

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-09, leaning towards discontinuing rather than phasing out: \"I don't think anybody is actually fully utilizing it anyways, so not a big deal I think if we just discontinue it now versus phasing it out.\"

HIS ARGUMENT, in his words and not improved on: (1) the bytes cannot fully live in a repo because it would become a huge object rapidly; (2) dev_storyflow's 700+ documents have been actively ingested into the graph and \"those documents are no longer really needed\" — the documents that would have been put in the blob; (3) maybe the better approach is important design artifacts directly in the git repo in something like a design_artifacts folder and forget blob altogether; (4) it is another feature that must be maintained and must grow with the rest of reflow2; (5) in flo2 the blob could end up being terabytes that has to be backed up, secured, and somehow separable per project.

⭐ MEASURED BEFORE ANY OPINION WAS FORMED, and it is the strongest thing in this node. REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN USES THE CONTENT STORE ZERO TIMES: no `--content-path` is configured in .mcp.json, no `.reflow2/content` directory exists, and 0 of 148 Fragments carry a `content_ref`. This is a 1,867-node graph that has been dogfooded harder than any other. The feature is built, tested (ver:content-surface, 5 cases), documented, and unused by its own author's primary project. That is evidence for his (4) rather than a coincidence.

CORROBORATING, from the consumer side: every dev_storyflow locator complaint filed on 2026-08-09 is about `Artifact.location`, `Fragment.title` and path resolution — a worker even wrote scripts/records/locator_validator.py because \"location is the join key between a corpus and the design and nothing validates it.\" NOBODY COMPLAINED ABOUT CONTENT HASHES, because nobody is using them. They are joining on PATHS.

⭐ AND AN ARGUMENT NOBODY HAS MADE YET, which strengthens his case: dec:where-content-lives settled on a content-addressed store whose blobs are COMMITTED TO THE REPO. GIT IS ALREADY A CONTENT-ADDRESSED STORE. So the current design is a content-addressed layer inside a content-addressed system — the dedup and the integrity hash are both things git already provides for anything committed. A `design_artifacts/` folder would not be giving up content addressing; it would be using the one underneath.

WHAT THIS WOULD RE-OPEN, stated so nothing is decided by accident: dec:where-content-lives (accepted), dec:what-lives-where (accepted), dec:content-growth-is-bounded-by-what-not-by-size (accepted), dec:content-store-implementation and dec:content-manifest. Per dec:reopen-supersedes a re-opening mints a NEW decision that obsoletes the old one; the accepted ones are never un-accepted.

⚠️ AND IT WOULD ANSWER dec:what-lives-where's OWN FALSIFIABLE TEST — which is the most interesting thing here. That decision wrote its own refutation condition: \"IF REFLOW2 WORKS, STORYFLOW WOULD NOT HAVE NEEDED dev_storyflow. One repo, code native, the design in the graph, the sources in the store. If a user still ends up splitting their repo to stay sane, reflow2 has not delivered what this decision claims.\" Anthony's observation is a DIFFERENT and sharper result than that test anticipated: it is not that the split was still needed, it is that ONCE THE DOCUMENTS WERE MINED THEIR ROLE WAS SPENT. If what mattered became nodes with Fragments recording provenance, the bytes are archival — and a repo folder (or the existing dev_storyflow repo) already archives them.

THE OPTIONS, with what is cheap or expensive about each recorded beside rather than argued down:

(A) DISCONTINUE NOW — remove content_put/content_get and the store, keep nothing. Cheapest to maintain, and honest given zero usage here. COUNTER: content_manifest answers a real question (\"I was handed this design on its own — what does it point at that I do not have?\"), and that question survives the store's removal; it would need re-pointing at repo paths rather than deleting.

(B) DEPRECATE, KEEP THE READS — stop accepting new content, keep content_get/exists/manifest so an existing store still resolves. COUNTER: Anthony's own point is that phasing costs more than discontinuing when the user count is zero; this buys compatibility nobody needs.

(C) KEEP IT, NARROW IT — retain for the one case a repo folder genuinely cannot hold (very large or non-diffable binaries) and say so. COUNTER: that is the status quo with better documentation, and the status quo has zero users; \"it might matter later\" is what the no-foreclosure rule exists to make a deliberate choice rather than a default.

(D) REPLACE WITH A CONVENTION — a `design_artifacts/` folder plus a Fragment/Artifact `location` pointing into it, no new machinery. Uses git's own content addressing. COUNTER, and it is the real one: `location` is the field dev_storyflow just filed FOUR defects about (unvalidated paths, a literal ellipsis that matched nothing, title-vs-source ambiguity, no way to ask \"is this path already in the graph?\"). Moving weight onto `location` without fixing it moves weight onto the weakest join in the schema. That is an argument for fixing `location` FIRST, not against (D).

WHAT NOBODY HAS ESTABLISHED, and it should not be guessed: whether any OTHER consumer has a populated store. This project has none; flo2 was checked and has no .mcp.json content path; dev_storyflow was not checked. A discontinue is cheap if the answer is nobody and expensive if it is somebody, and it is one call (content_manifest) per project to find out.

NOTHING HERE IS PROMOTED. Anthony stated a lean, not a decision, and the options above are recorded as considered.

Deliberately NOT recorded as a re-opening of dec:where-content-lives yet — that would assert the choice has been made and would obsolete an accepted decision on a lean rather than a decision. If he settles it, dec:reopen-supersedes says the re-opening mints its own node then.
