properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-11 on Anthony's word. NO NEW VOCABULARY WAS NEEDED, and finding that out is the whole result.

THE ANSWER: a Decision `OBSOLETES` the thing it withdrew. PUT THE DECISION AT THE SOURCE.

That dissolves the objection this node was opened over. Point (3) above says both retirement edges "presume a successor to sit at the source end. A discontinued thing with no replacement has NOTHING TO PUT THERE. You cannot draw OBSOLETES from nothing." True — but a discontinuation ALWAYS has a decision behind it even when it has no replacement, so the decision is the honest source. `OBSOLETES` is already `* -> *` in schema/inference.yaml and its hint already reads "source makes target redundant or deprecated". So: no edge type, no enum value, NO SCHEMA STAMP MOVE, and no upgrade doc — none of which option (A) or (B) could have claimed.

⭐ AND IT ANSWERS `dec:one-retire-edge`'S REAL QUESTION AS A SIDE EFFECT. That decision asked, since July, what SHOULD consult a retirement edge — "retiring something marks it and changes nothing. A retired capability still counts in every rollup, still raises its gaps, still appears in delivery arithmetic." Four readers now exist, which is four more than either retirement edge has ever had:
  · `unmotivated_capability`, `unrealized_capability`, `unverified_capability` fall silent
  · delivery arithmetic stops counting a discontinued capability as a satisfier
So OBSOLETES is no longer a marker nothing reads. Whether SUPERSEDES survives at all is still `dec:one-retire-edge`'s to settle, and it is now a smaller question: one of the two words has a job.

⚠️ ONLY AN ACCEPTED DECISION DISCONTINUES ANYTHING. A `proposed` withdrawal has withdrawn nothing; the thing keeps counting until somebody with the authority says so. That is `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` applied to the retire path, and it is pinned by a test that fails if the check is dropped.

⚠️ THE CASCADE IS DELIBERATE. Withdrawing the thing that met a need does not meet the need, so the requirement it served drops back to UNSATISFIED and is asked about again — "covered, deferred, or dropped?". Without that, a discontinuation would be invisible one hop away and the design would keep reporting a need as met by something that no longer exists. Applying this to the content store surfaces exactly that, and the two requirements it served are now open questions for Anthony rather than silent claims.

⚠️ AND THE NUMBERS SAY WHY THEY MOVED. `DeliveryCoverage.satisfied_only_by_discontinued` counts the skipped edges, because a discontinuation that made delivery fall with no mention is the silent-drop failure this project forbids everywhere else: the count drops, nothing explains it, and a reader concludes the design regressed.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN AND IS NOT CLAIMED HERE:
  · `dec:idea-does-a-capability-need-a-cancelled-state` (Alex's) is NOT closed by this. It covers the ABANDONED case; it says nothing about a WISH NOBODY EVER AGREED TO, which has no decision behind it to be the source of an OBSOLETES edge. That half is still `dec:exploratory-staging`'s.
  · A Verification whose code was deleted still reads `passing`. `ver:content-store` is the live instance. Nothing here fixes that, and marking the verification obsoleted does not change its status field.
  · Nothing reads discontinuation for Components, Interfaces or Artifacts. Only the capability detectors and delivery consult it today, which is stated rather than left to be discovered.
properties.name: DECIDED — a Decision OBSOLETES what it withdrew, and three detectors plus delivery now read it
properties.rationale: Anthony asked on 2026-08-09 for a way to say "we built this and then decided against it". Searching before building found that the vocabulary already held it, in a direction nobody had tried: the objection was that a discontinued thing has no successor for the source end of a retirement edge, and the answer is that the DECISION is the source. That costs nothing — no schema change, no stamp move, no upgrade doc — and it gives OBSOLETES its first reader in the process, which is the question dec:one-retire-edge has been waiting on since July. Shipped WITH its readers deliberately: this project has now found three markers nothing reads (enforced, SUPERSEDES, OBSOLETES itself), and a fourth would have been the defect rather than the fix.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled; recorded as a minor idea with a real objection.

THE IDEA: percentile and median (unused, in dynograph-vector::stats) would let surprising_connections report "the top 5% most surprising couplings in THIS design" rather than everything over a fixed score. A distributional cut self-calibrates to the graph it is run on; an absolute one does not, and a design with 100 nodes and one with 10,000 do not have the same natural scale.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is the projects own lesson: BL-23 established that when a detector punishes correct work, the answer is A DIFFERENT QUESTION, not a tuned threshold. A percentile is still a threshold — it just moves rather than sits still. Worse, a top-N-percent rule ALWAYS returns something, so a design with no surprising couplings at all would still be handed a list, which is exactly the false-signal failure the noise-floor work (BL-42) was about.

WHERE IT MIGHT STILL HELP: not as a cut, but as CONTEXT on a finding already made — "surprise 2.56, which is the highest in this design" is more useful to a reader than a bare number, and asserts nothing extra.
properties.name: OPEN — should surprise and severity be reported as distributional positions rather than absolute scores?
properties.rationale: Kept deliberately small and recorded with the objection first, because the naive form of this idea contradicts an established lesson and a later session should meet the objection at the same moment as the idea.

properties.decision:
SETTLED 2026-08-22 BY ANTHONY, IN HIS OWN WORDS: "if the principles are not generally applicable to any design project, then we can discard. I'm just trying to apply some of the things I've learned in developing storyflow to a wider set of projects."

OPTION A IS REJECTED. reflow2 does not ship StoryFlow's nine principles as rules, defaults, or a seeded starter set. They are one project's rules, paid for by one project's incidents, and shipping them would assert that reflow2 knows what a user's engineering standards should be.

THE CRITERION IS GENERAL APPLICABILITY, AND IT IS ALREADY THIS PROJECT'S STANDING RULE. `rule:a-lesson-is-generalised-before-it-is-built` says it from his words of 2026-08-14: "I don't want this to become like a decision tree where it is so specialized to some training data that it is no longer generalizable." A principle is carried in only if the GENERAL form is true of any design project; the specific form that produced it stays in StoryFlow.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT MEAN. It does not mean the nine were unhelpful — the opposite. They are field evidence from a real deployment, and two of them (rules A and B) name failure modes reflow2 both practises and violates. The ruling is about what SHIPS, not about what is worth reading.

THE SORT ITSELF IS A SEPARATE ACT and is not settled here. Which of the nine have a general form, which are already carried by existing reflow2 vocabulary, and which are code-level lints over a user's source that reflow2 must not attempt, is the follow-on question. The sibling ideas hold the three that survived a first pass.

⭐ ONE MEASURED FINDING SURVIVES REGARDLESS OF THE SORT, because it is about reflow2 rather than about StoryFlow: principle B ("a set reduced to a scalar is not a check of the set") is VIOLATED BY REFLOW2'S OWN INSTRUMENT. `vocabulary_coverage` counts unused properties in `properties_on_used_types` and its `unused` list names node types and edge types only — so an unused PROPERTY is counted and never named, and no report can say WHICH vocabulary a design has never touched. Found 2026-08-22 by asserting the opposite in a test and watching it fail.
properties.name: DECIDED — a StoryFlow principle enters reflow2 only in its GENERAL form; what is not generally applicable to any design project is discarded
properties.no_relation_note: Searched 2026-08-22 for existing nodes on reflow2 serving other projects vs itself. Nearest were rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself and rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party — both READ and judged NOT related in the relation vocabulary's sense. They state the PRINCIPLE that reflow2 serves other projects; this asks a narrower product question those rules do not reach, namely whether reflow2 may ship another project's engineering standards as content. A DEPENDS_ON would be false (this is answerable without either rule) and a CONTRADICTS would be false (option C is compatible with both). Recorded as a note rather than a forced edge: a false neighbour would put those two rules in front of every later reader of this question and they do not answer it. NOTE WRITTEN BY HAND because review_relations was not on this session's served tool surface — the server was rebuilt mid-session and the client's tool list is fixed at connect time.
properties.rationale: Recorded as decided rather than left open because Anthony stated the criterion directly and it matches a standing rule he had already given. Option A is closed by his word. What remains is the per-principle sort, which is work rather than a decision, and the one product finding above, which stands on its own measurement.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-21. Nothing here is intent.

HIS WORDS: "can proposed ideas (like those from brainstorm) form a graph? looking at any idea individually may give you an incomplete picture. for example, we talked about black-boxes, systems engineering, functional allocation, and a few other inter-related ideas that paint a bigger, more holistic picture about what I'm trying to link together. or when my brother mentioned that sometimes he just wants to jot down ideas for a project over time. bottomline, does reflow2 link ideas/concepts or does it rely on the agent to do this?"

=== THE ANSWER, MEASURED 2026-08-21 RATHER THAN ESTIMATED ===

    145  idea-Decisions (dec:idea-*), of which 123 still proposed
     12  edges joining any TWO of them
     68  whose ONLY edge is AUTHORED_BY — they connect to their author and to nothing else
      8  with no edges at all

And the shape of what an idea IS connected to, across the whole population:
    134  AUTHORED_BY -> Contributor
     20  GOVERNED_BY -> Decision
     19  CONTRADICTS -> Decision
     13  DEPENDS_ON  -> Decision

⇒ THE MOST COMMON EDGE ON AN IDEA IS ITS AUTHOR. **The design records WHO had an idea far more reliably than WHAT IT RELATES TO.** Roughly half the idea population is an island that says 'Anthony thought this' and nothing further.

⭐ SO: REFLOW2 DOES NOT LINK IDEAS. IT RELIES ENTIRELY ON THE AGENT, AND THE AGENT MOSTLY DOES NOT. The evidence is this session: four of the twelve idea-to-idea edges in the entire graph were drawn BY HAND in one hour, only because Anthony asked for them in as many words. Every brainstorm before that produced a node and no edges — including three captured the previous day by the same agent following the same skill, which instructs recording the idea and says nothing about connecting it to its neighbours.

=== WHY IT MATTERS, IN HIS OWN CASE ===

Four nodes carry one argument between them and none of them says so on its own: allocation-waits-for-the-last-responsible-moment (accepted), what-watches-for-the-moment-to-arrive, the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph, and is-allocation-running-ahead-of-the-seams. Read singly, each is a reasonable question. Read together they are one position about WHEN and ON WHAT BASIS a boundary gets drawn. A reader meeting any one of them alone gets an incomplete picture — which is exactly what he said.

AND HIS BROTHER'S CASE IS THE SAME SHAPE AT A DIFFERENT TIMESCALE: `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` (a body of intent accreted over years, contradicting itself and never built, can still become a design) presumes the accretion can later be READ AS A WHOLE. Ideas jotted over months with no edges between them do not accrete into anything; they pile.

=== OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ===

  (a) THE STATUS QUO — the agent draws edges when it thinks to. Measured rate: 12 edges across 145 ideas, and a third of those in the hour after being asked. This is the option that produced the number.
  (b) THE BRAINSTORM SKILL REQUIRES NAMING A NEIGHBOUR. Cheap, needs no schema, and testable — the skill already makes the agent search before writing, so the near-matches are IN HAND at the moment of capture and are currently used only to avoid duplicates, then discarded. ⚠️ Risk: an edge drawn to satisfy an instruction is an asserted relationship nobody meant, which `req:a-repair-suggestion-never-proposes-fabrication` forbids for exactly this reason.
  (c) A DETECTOR FOR THE ABSENCE — 'this idea shares vocabulary with N others and links to none'. It is the absence-shaped detector reflow2 structurally lacks (see fact:the-design-outward-blind-spot-appeared-in-three-independent-places), so building it would be the first of its kind rather than one more of many.
  (d) COMPUTE ADJACENCY, DO NOT STORE IT. `search_design` already ranks by BM25 over every node's text, so 'ideas near this one' is answerable TODAY as a READ without asserting any edge. Respects the no-fabrication rule completely: it SHOWS adjacency rather than CLAIMING a relationship. ⚠️ And its limit is the whole point — a similarity score cannot carry WHY two ideas are related, and the why is the content. The four edges drawn today each carry a note like 'option (b) here would be this one's stated trigger'; no ranking function produces that sentence.
  (e) DO NOTHING. Honest, and its cost is the measurement above.

=== COUNTER-ARGUMENT, RECORDED BESIDE RATHER THAN AGAINST ===

An idea graph could be worse than an idea list. Edges between musings are cheap to draw and expensive to trust: two ideas mentioning 'allocation' are not thereby related, and a densely-linked pile of half-formed thoughts reads as a structure when it is a word cloud. This project has twice retired metric-driven verdicts that fired on correct architecture; a similarity-driven idea graph is the same hazard one level up. WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, THE EDGE THAT EARNS ITS KEEP CARRIES A REASON — which is an argument for (b) or (d) over (c), and against any automatic drawing.

DISTINCT FROM `dec:exploratory-staging`, which asks whether a half-formed idea has a HOME (a kind, a type, a status) and lists what such a kind would buy: retirement candidates and at-a-glance readability. Neither is linking. That node is about what an idea IS; this one is about what an idea is CONNECTED TO.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐ ANTHONY NAMES BOTH HALVES, 2026-08-21 — AND THE SECOND IS BETTER THAN OPTION (d)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

HIS WORDS: "I think the brainstorm skill is the perfect place to start linking ideas. it is like when a person starts 'connecting the dots'. secondly, when as part of a search, the graph starts returning clusters of inter-related ideas to the agent instead of single ideas. like our example from earlier, we'd just to have to do one search (maybe it is limited to like 2 or 3 connected nodes from a searched idea)."

HALF ONE IS OPTION (b), and the skill is the right home for a reason the options above understated: THE NEAR-MATCHES ARE ALREADY IN HAND AT THE MOMENT OF CAPTURE. The brainstorm skill already makes the agent search before writing, and the dedup guard already returns the nodes it judged close. Today that list is used to avoid a duplicate AND THEN THROWN AWAY. The information needed to connect the dots is produced, read, and discarded, every single time.

HALF TWO IS NOT OPTION (d) AND IS BETTER THAN IT. Option (d) proposed computing adjacency by SIMILARITY. His proposal is to follow the EDGES THAT EXIST and return the neighbourhood, bounded to 2 or 3 hops. That is stronger on the exact axis (d) was weak on: a similarity score cannot say WHY two ideas are related, but a real edge carries the reason it was drawn with. It also needs no schema change — it is a READ.

⭐⭐ AND THE TWO COMPOUND. Linking at capture makes search return clusters; a search that returns clusters shows the next agent the neighbourhood it is writing into; seeing the neighbourhood makes the next link better. A virtuous cycle — but one that needs a seed, because it multiplies whatever is already there.

🛑 WHICH IS THE FINDING: THE TWO HALVES ARE ORDERED, AND MEASURABLY SO. Measured 2026-08-21, traversing every edge except attribution and bookkeeping:

    ideas that reach ZERO other ideas within 2 hops:   111 of 145
    median other-ideas within 2 hops:                  0
    at 3 hops:                                         110 of 145 still zero

⇒ CLUSTER-SEARCH BUILT TODAY WOULD RETURN NOTHING FOR 77% OF IDEAS. It would not be wrong, it would be empty — and an empty result from a new feature reads as the feature not working rather than as the graph being unlinked. HALF ONE MUST PRECEDE HALF TWO, or the second ships looking broken.

✅ AND THERE IS ALREADY A WORKING DEMONSTRATION OF WHAT IT WOULD FEEL LIKE. The allocation cluster returns 1 idea at one hop and 2 at two hops — `what-watches-for-the-moment-to-arrive` and `is-allocation-running-ahead-of-the-seams` — because those are the only edges that exist. That is exactly the "one search instead of four" he described, working, on the one part of the graph that has been linked. It is a demo and a measurement of the gap at the same time.

📌 STILL NOT DECIDED: whether the skill should REQUIRE a neighbour or merely offer the near-matches for the agent to judge. Requiring one manufactures edges to satisfy an instruction, which is the fabrication hazard recorded above. Offering them depends on the agent choosing well, which is the status quo that produced 12 edges across 145 ideas. The middle — offer the near-matches AND require an explicit "none of these" when none is drawn — is the shape `distinct_from` already uses on the dedup guard, and it is the only one of the three that leaves a record of the judgement either way.
properties.name: OPEN — do ideas form a GRAPH, or only a list? Measured: 145 ideas, 12 edges between any two of them, and 68 that connect to nothing but their author

properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, from a first-pass review of openmbee.org — website and repository listing only, deep review pending. THE OBSERVATION: OpenMBEE's Model Development Kits 'implement DocGen language for dynamic, model-based document generation using view and viewpoint concepts'. Document generation is not a side feature there; it is half the value proposition, and the tagline 'Edit once, use everywhere' is largely a claim about documents — write the model once, and every specification, review pack and report derives from it rather than drifting from it. WHERE reflow2 STANDS, and the gap is narrower than it first looks: reflow2 already has the same underlying idea. `docs/viewpoints.md` is DoDAF-informed, `dec:views-are-projections` states that a view is a pure projection of the graph and that renderer fill-ins are DEFECTS, and `tools/render_views.py` projects six viewpoints and CONFESSES anything a view needs that the graph cannot supply — with every confession counted as a finding (BL-40). That confession discipline is arguably stronger than DocGen's, because it makes the gaps in a document visible instead of filling them. THE HONEST DIFFERENCE IS PRODUCT, NOT CONCEPT: `render_views.py` is a probe in the tools directory, run by developers of reflow2. DocGen is something an engineering organisation hands to its systems engineers to produce the artefacts a programme is contractually required to deliver. reflow2 has never claimed the second, and `req:no-se-knowledge` ('the user never needs systems engineering') suggests it may not want to. THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT: a document generator is a large surface with a long tail — templates, formats, numbering, review states — and every hour of it is an hour not spent on the coherence loop, which is the thing nobody else is building. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: whether the projections reflow2 already computes are close enough to what a real programme must deliver that the remaining distance is rendering rather than modelling.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2's viewpoints become a document product, the way DocGen is for OpenMBEE?
properties.rationale: Recorded through the brainstorm skill at Anthony's request, ahead of a deep review against a clone of OpenMBEE's repository. The strength claim is deliberately hedged: reflow2 holds the concept (views as projections, confessions as findings) and OpenMBEE holds the product. Which of those is 'stronger' depends entirely on whether the user is a programme owing deliverables or a builder owing a coherent design, and reflow2 has so far chosen the second. Anthony's own position sits across both, which is why this is worth asking rather than assuming.

properties.decision:
✅ **DECIDED 2026-08-14 ON ANTHONY'S WORD: NO `cancelled` VALUE IS ADDED TO `Capability.status`, NOW OR LATER.** Abandonment is recorded by an accepted Decision drawing `OBSOLETES`, which computes `discontinued`. The question this node was opened under is answered; what remains is a measurement and a separate, narrower question, both named below.

⭐ **AND THE DETECTOR IS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT YET — THAT IS THE PART OF THE RULING WORTH KEEPING.** Three ways to make an agent find `OBSOLETES` were on the table: a hint on `set_capability_status`, a DETECTOR for abandonment words in description prose, and the command coverage. **The vocabulary fix shipped in v0.31.0** (`Capability.status` and the `OBSOLETES` hint now name each other, pinned by tests) **and has never been in front of an agent** — Alex's fleet has not seen it. Building the detector now would be guessing that the cheap fix failed before observing whether it did, and it is the only option with a false-positive cost: a capability legitimately describing that it REPLACED something dropped would fire.

🎯 **WHAT IS OWED IS THEREFORE A MEASUREMENT, AND IT IS FREE.** Alex's fleet is the only place "DROPPED in prose" was ever observed. **If it stops appearing there after v0.31.0, the vocabulary fix worked and the detector is unnecessary; if it continues, the detector is justified by evidence rather than by fear.** Same discipline Anthony applied to the allocation question — do not reason about it, measure it.

⚠️ **THE RESIDUAL IS REAL AND BELONGS ELSEWHERE, NOT HERE:** a capability **nobody ever agreed to** has no decision to hang an `OBSOLETES` edge from, so neither this ruling nor the 2026-08-11 one reaches it. That is `dec:exploratory-staging`'s, and closing this node does not close that.

════════ THE REASONING THAT PRODUCED THE RULING ════════

🛑 **ANTHONY, 2026-08-14, CHALLENGING THE PREMISE: "we already have an obsolete with discontinued or something like that — are we playing semantics with cancelled?" CHECKED AGAINST THE CODE AND THE GRAPH RATHER THAN ARGUED. HE IS RIGHT FOR THE ABANDONED CASE, AND THE ANSWER WAS ALREADY DECIDED THREE DAYS EARLIER.**

`dec:idea-discontinued-is-a-first-class-state` was **DECIDED on his word 2026-08-11**: a Decision `OBSOLETES` what it withdrew, the decision itself being the source. No enum value, no edge type, no schema stamp move, no upgrade doc.

**IT IS NOT THEORETICAL — IT IS LIVE IN THIS GRAPH.** `dec:the-content-store-is-discontinued` (accepted) obsoletes `cap:content-store` and `cap:content-manifest` (both stored `realized`) and `cap:session-artifacts` (`verified`). And `is_discontinued` has FOUR readers: `unmotivated_capability`, `unrealized_capability` and `unverified_capability` fall silent, and delivery arithmetic stops counting a discontinued capability as a satisfier (`DeliveryCoverage.satisfied_only_by_discontinued`).

⇒ **ADDING `cancelled` WOULD BE A SECOND WAY TO SAY WHAT THE GRAPH ALREADY COMPUTES — and worse than redundant, because a STORED status can disagree with the COMPUTED one.** The stored status deliberately keeps saying what was BUILT; that is why `get_node` carries `discontinued` separately and warns to read it.

═══ ⭐ WHAT ACTUALLY BIT ALEX IS DISCOVERABILITY, NOT A MISSING STATE ═══

His agents typed "DROPPED" into description prose while the mechanism existed and worked. Measured via `describe_schema`, which the served routing table tells an agent to use for exactly this lookup: `Capability.status` carried **no description at all** — four bare values and no fifth — while every neighbouring property carried a teaching one; and `OBSOLETES`'s entire hint read *"Source makes target redundant or deprecated"*, naming neither the retirement job, nor the Decision as source, nor `discontinued`. **So an agent did everything right and still had nowhere to put the fact except prose.** Both descriptions shipped in v0.31.0, with no schema stamp move.

════════ THE ORIGINAL REPORT, KEPT ════════

Alex's fleet, 2026-08-09: 'Requirements: deferred / dropped. Capabilities: no equivalent — agents stuff DROPPED into description text.' CONFIRMED AGAINST THE SCHEMA: Requirement.status is [proposed, accepted, deferred, dropped, met]; Capability.status is [planned, in_progress, realized, verified]. WHY IT IS THE WEEK'S OWN DEFECT CLASS AGAIN: a state that cannot be expressed does not disappear — it gets smuggled into prose.
properties.name: DECIDED — no cancelled state, ever: abandonment is an OBSOLETES edge, and whether the vocabulary fix was enough is a MEASUREMENT owed by Alex's fleet, not a further decision
properties.rationale: Raised by a second consumer project rather than found here, which is the useful part: reflow2's own graph never hit it because this project retires capabilities rather than cancelling them. Kept as a decision point rather than built because it is a schema enum change that would move the stamp and therefore owe an upgrade doc — the first this week that would — and because it touches an already-open question about retirement being modelled in two places. Anthony's to settle.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony pointed at chain_reflow, 2026-08-12, while working out bottom-up system-of-systems: "made me think of chain-reflow... might be worth re-analyzing that repo and doing a search for what reflow2 already has in this topic."

⚠️ THIS NODE IS THE INGEST OF `docs/chain-reflow-nuggets.md`, which is one of the four nuggets files on Anthony's ingest-then-delete list (inward-facing docs become graph, then go). It held reflow2's adoption plan for chain_reflow and NOTHING IN THE GRAPH RECORDED IT — searching for "chain reflow nuggets touchpoint matryoshka" returns nothing above 12.5, all of it unrelated. A stale inward-facing tracker holding knowledge the graph does not have is exactly why that list exists.

═══ THE AUDIT, 2026-08-12: six nuggets, planned vs actual ═══

  MATRYOSHKA / MISSING-INTERMEDIATE      adopt (now)        ✅ BUILT — hierarchy.rs; `missing_intermediate_level` fires in both hierarchy_issues and detect_gaps
  CORRELATION VS CAUSATION               adopt (now, schema) ✅ BUILT — `basis` + `validation_status` on inference edges, and the schema still credits chain_reflow by name
  CREATIVE LINKING (guarded healer)      adopt (concept)     🛑 BUILT as `generate_bridge`, then RETIRED 2026-08-10
  SoS TOUCHPOINT DISCOVERY               adopt (MEDIUM)      ⬜ the word "touchpoint" appears NOWHERE in the codebase
  ORTHOGONALITY ASSESSMENT               later               ⬜
  INTERACTIVE EXECUTOR                   later               ⬜

═══ FINDING 1 — TOUCHPOINT DISCOVERY IS HALF SHIPPED UNDER OTHER NAMES AND HALF OUTLAWED ═══

The nuggets doc specifies it as: "allow Project↔Project links, and a touchpoint-discovery pass that PROPOSES cross-project `Interface`/`DEPENDS_ON` edges (standard technical matching first; creative linking only for orthogonal, guarded). The merged graph is then diagnosed/healed like any other."

⭐ THE 2026-07 PLAN IS PARTLY FORBIDDEN BY A 2026-08 RULE. `req:a-repair-suggestion-never-proposes-fabrication` (accepted, shipped v0.28.0) removed `generate_bridge` precisely because proposing an edge that asserts a relationship nobody stated is fabrication. A pass that PROPOSES cross-project DEPENDS_ON edges is that, across an ownership boundary, where it is worse — the asserted relationship is between two designs whose owners never agreed to it.

BUT THE PERMITTED HALF EXISTS, under two different names:
  - "standard technical matching first" -> `pair_designs`, which reports `candidates` and states outright that uncertain name matches are "CANDIDATES to ask about, never actions".
  - "the merged graph is then diagnosed like any other" -> `compose_and_analyse`, which imports theirs alongside yours in memory and runs the ORDINARY checks over the whole, attributing findings ours / theirs / seam.

⇒ TOUCHPOINT DISCOVERY IS NOT UNBUILT THROUGH NEGLECT. Its safe half shipped as two differently-named tools and its unsafe half was deliberately outlawed. That is a better outcome than the plan, and it should be recorded as such rather than sitting on a roadmap as a debt.

📌 CREATIVE LINKING'S COMPLETE ARC IS WORTH KEEPING: adopted as a concept (2026-07), built as `generate_bridge`, retired as fabrication (2026-08-10). heal.rs still carries the comment "NO SUGGESTION, DELIBERATELY. `generate_bridge` used to sit..." — an idea taken from another project, built, and then argued back out on a rule the receiving project later derived. Chain_reflow also carries `validate_merged_architecture.py`, written because "Chain Reflow workflows create merged architectures but lack automated validation" — the same job `compose_and_analyse` now does, which confirms the merged graph was always meant to be validated AS A WHOLE.

═══ FINDING 2 — THE ACTIONABLE ONE: A MIRRORED DESIGN OCCUPIES NO RUNG ═══

`Component.level` already runs `component ▸ subsystem ▸ system ▸ system_of_systems ▸ enterprise`. SO SYSTEM-OF-SYSTEMS IS ALREADY A MODELLED RUNG, and `missing_intermediate_level` is pure level arithmetic over CONTAINS/DEPENDS_ON **between Components**.

🛑 BUT A MIRRORED DESIGN ARRIVES AS A **PROJECT** CONTAINING COMPONENTS (measured 2026-08-12: 1 Project, 6 Components, 5 Interfaces, 1 Artifact, with 5 CONTAINS edges from `proj:flo2`). **A PROJECT OCCUPIES NO RUNG ON THAT LADDER.** So the cross-graph black box sits outside the level system entirely, and matryoshka detection structurally CANNOT see across an ownership boundary — not because the analysis is missing, but because the thing on the far side is not levelled.

⇒ THE QUESTION, and it is one sentence: **does a mirrored Project present as a Component at some level, or does the ladder extend to Projects?** Answer it and matryoshka recurses across ownership boundaries using the detector that already exists.

This is also exactly what `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` demands in its own closing line — "an arbitrary-depth nesting that is exercised beyond two levels" — and the two had never been connected.

OPTIONS, none taken:
  A — A MIRRORED PROJECT PRESENTS AS A COMPONENT at a stated level, chosen by the mirroring side. Cheapest: no schema change, the existing detector works immediately. EXPENSIVE: the level is the HOST's judgement about someone else's design, which is an assertion about them they never made — the same class the fabrication rule guards.
  B — EXTEND THE LADDER TO PROJECTS, so level arithmetic spans node types. Truthful — a Project genuinely is a bigger box than a Component. EXPENSIVE: a schema change touching the one property the matryoshka detectors are built on.
  C — THE MIRRORING SIDE DECLARES THE RUNG ON THE MIRROR, not on the foreign node — a property of the LINK rather than of either design. Fits "foreignness is a property of the node" and keeps the host's judgement on the host's side of the line. EXPENSIVE: the link is not yet a first-class object, which is gap 1 of the linking audit.
  D — LEAVE IT. Cross-graph composition is analysed by `compose_and_analyse` and needs no levels. EXPENSIVE: then `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` is satisfiable within a graph only, and the bottom-up SoS reading Anthony is reaching for stays out of scope.

NOT DECIDED.
properties.name: OPEN — chain_reflow's six nuggets audited: does a MIRRORED DESIGN occupy a rung on Component.level, or is the cross-graph black box outside the ladder forever?
properties.rationale: Captured because pointing at chain_reflow turned up an adoption plan that existed only in an inward-facing doc slated for deletion, and auditing it against the code changed two statuses: touchpoint discovery is half-shipped under other names and half-outlawed by a rule derived after the plan was written, and creative linking has a complete adopted-built-retired arc worth keeping. The actionable residue is one sentence — a mirrored design occupies no rung on Component.level, so the matryoshka detector cannot cross an ownership boundary — which is the precise blocker under the cross-graph reading of req:recursive-black-box-decomposition.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is chosen; the options are ideas with their honest counter-arguments beside them, and the road not taken is kept on purpose.

THE PROMPT. I suggested (2026-08-10) that `compare_designs` against the committed export belongs at the OPEN of a session rather than being run when trouble is already suspected, because it was the only thing that found a record diverging from the graph on main. Anthony asked for it to be thought through rather than acted on.

WHAT SEARCHING FIRST DID TO THE QUESTION — it inverted it. The same session then found `fact:correction-the-export-loses-nothing-the-108-were-serialized-defaults`: a 2026-08-08 session ran exactly this comparison, got 108 property-level findings, concluded `export_graph` was silently dropping design, wrote that into a PR body and a handoff note, and retracted it after one probe. They were serialized schema defaults. I had just made the same false claim on the same data, 95 findings instead of 108, without having read theirs. SO THE OBSERVED RECORD OF THIS INSTRUMENT AT ORIENTATION TIME IS TWO RUNS, TWO FALSE DEFECT CLAIMS, TWO RELEASES APART, BY DIFFERENT AGENTS. That is not an argument against comparing; it is an argument that the question is not "when do we run it" but "what does it have to be able to say before running it earlier makes anyone better off".

THE OPTIONS.

(A) DO NOTHING — the null option, and it is stronger than it looks. `where-am-i` ALREADY names `compare_designs` as its first gather step. The failure on 2026-08-10 was not that the step was skipped; it was run, and misread. Adding a ritual does not fix a reading problem, and this project has already rejected the ritual shape twice (`dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written`: build the view, not the document; `dec:read-hint-shape` rejected option B because boilerplate on every return trains the agent to skim). Cheap: costs nothing. Counter: it leaves the actual observed harm — the record was wrong on `main` for an unknown number of PRs and `reflow2_check` is structurally incapable of noticing, since it reads artifact checksums and anchored gaps and never node properties.

(B) COMPUTE IT, DO NOT PRESCRIBE IT — extend `dec:read-hint-shape`'s already-chosen option C (state-derived hint, riding the orientation-shaped reads, fire-on-change) to carry DISTRIBUTION debt alongside coherence debt: "the record and the graph disagree" surfacing at the moment of attention, only when true. This is flo2's F5 filed 2026-08-09 — `loop_status` tracks what COHERENCE is owed and nothing tracks what DISTRIBUTION is owed. Fits the strongest precedent in the design and needs no new vocabulary. Counter, and it is decisive as things stand: a hint that fires on phantom findings is a hint that teaches you to ignore it. Building B before C or D would ship the cry-wolf failure into the one mechanism that currently works.

(C) FIX THE INSTRUMENT — make a property difference able to say WHICH SIDE MEANT IT, so a default never appears as a change. The 2026-08-08 correction already argues this and names the precedent: "a comparison that cannot say which side meant it is the same shape as an edge that cannot say who asserted it (DUPLICATES `basis`, which cost dev_storyflow ten proposed deletions) — the fix there was to make provenance explicit rather than to tune the detector, and the same argument applies." Most expensive; also the only option that makes the finding trustworthy rather than quieter. Counter: property-level provenance is a large surface, and `dec:certainty-derived` would argue it should be DERIVED rather than stored — which may make (D) sufficient.

(D) FINISH BL-198 — "do not serialize a value equal to the default, so an absent property honestly means nobody said". Cheaper than C, kills the noise at its source, and the exporter has evidently begun doing it already (0.25.0 wrote defaults, 0.27.0 does not) while `fact:bl-198` is still listed PLANNED in `epoch:planned-one-write-surface`. Counter, and it is the trap both incidents actually fell into: suppressing defaults does not remove the disagreement, it MOVES it to the transition. Two builds one release apart still differ on every default, and that window is exactly what produced both false claims. So D makes the steady state clean and the upgrade moment worse — which is an argument for D plus a version-aware comparison, not D alone.

(E) WRONG TRIGGER ENTIRELY — the record diverging matters when it is PUBLISHED, not when a session starts. Put the check at export/commit/CI time, where something is about to be shipped, and leave session-open alone. Cheap and well-precedented (`ci-gate` exists). Counter: it cannot catch what is already committed and wrong, which is the case actually observed here; and it inherits the same default-vs-decision blindness, so it would go red on a version bump for no reason.

WHAT IS NOT AN OPTION, said plainly so nobody re-derives it: tuning a threshold so the phantom findings fall below it. That silences the true findings at the same rate as the false ones, and it is the "reduce a SET to a SCALAR" failure this project has already written down.

THE ORDERING THAT FALLS OUT, offered as a finding and not as a decision: C or D before B, and A is a legitimate resting place if neither is worth the spend — because the value of running the comparison earlier is bounded above by the comparison's ability to be believed, and right now it has a 2-for-2 record of not deserving to be.
properties.name: OPEN — should comparing the live graph against the committed record be part of a session's opening move, when the comparison cannot yet tell a default from a decision?
properties.rationale:
Recorded as an open question rather than an answer because the brainstorm materially changed what the question is. I opened arguing for a session-opening step; the design's own memory then supplied a two-instance record of that step producing confident false defect claims — one of them mine, an hour earlier. An idea that is weaker after searching is worth keeping in exactly that state, with the evidence that weakened it attached, so a later session does not re-propose it fresh and pay for the discovery a third time.

Kept deliberately open, and NOT registered as alternatives: each option here is a paragraph, not a design, so `detect_gaps` stays quiet (`undecided_decision_point` fires only on two or more registered alternatives). If one of these grows a design of its own — most likely C, which needs a property-provenance shape — `register_alternative` is what makes it a real fork, and being nudged to choose would then be correct.

The counter-arguments are recorded beside the options rather than used to kill any of them, including against my own opening position. (A) is listed first and honestly rather than as a foil: this project has twice chosen the computed form over the prescribed one, and "the step was already prescribed and was run and was misread" is a real answer to "should we prescribe the step".

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex's idea, from the Opportunities section of his 2026-08-14 session (docs/feedback/2026-08-14-alex-grok-session.md), in his words: "Add `change_type` for as-built defects (`defect_fix` / `as_built_fix`), or officially alias `test_failure_fix`."

DELIBERATELY SEPARATE FROM `fact:defect-change-event-has-no-type-for-a-field-reported-defect`, which the near-duplicate guard correctly surfaced: that node MEASURES the problem and counts its five occurrences; this one holds the UNMADE CHOICE about the shape of the fix. Merging them would put an open question inside a settled measurement, and the fact would then read as though it had proposed its own answer.

WHY IT IS WORTH MORE THAN ITS ONE LINE: the evidence is now five forced choices, not one — two maintainer sessions, one fleet, Alex, and the very edit that recorded his corroboration, each picking a different least-wrong value.

THE OPTIONS:

(a) ADD `defect_fix` (or `field_report_fix`) — exactly what he proposed. CHEAP: enum values are not counted by the version stamp, so it is not a schema break. COUNTER, and the reason this is a question rather than a task: the five forced choices needed at least THREE different missing meanings — a defect fix, "an open question was settled" (`chg:arrival-delta-decided`), and "the design's knowledge moved while the thing did not". One value fixes the loudest instance and leaves the pattern.

(b) OFFICIALLY ALIAS `test_failure_fix` — his cheaper alternative: document that this is the bucket. CHEAPEST, no schema move. COUNTER: it makes a structured field permanently mean something other than its name, and the project rejected that reasoning once already — `baseline_established` exists precisely because forcing a record-only change through a code category "writes a fiction into the ledger that exists to prevent fiction".

(c) SPLIT THE AXIS — carry a `subject: system | record` alongside a narrower type. MOST HONEST: `baseline_established`'s own doc comment already names the axis — "every other variant answers why the thing changed; this one says the thing did not change and only the design's knowledge of it did" — then leaves it with one member, reserved. COUNTER: a real schema property on a type with a lot of history, and every existing ChangeEvent would carry an unstated subject, which is the "absent means nobody said" problem again.

(d) A STRUCTURED `reported_by` / `found_by` PROPERTY — the other half of Alex's own suggestion. Keeps how-it-was-found structured rather than narrated. COUNTER: orthogonal to the gap; it records provenance of the discovery, not the kind of the change, so (a) or (c) would still be owed.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the three missing meanings are all of them, or only the three that happen to have been hit.

properties.decision:
✅ **DECIDED 2026-08-14 ON ANTHONY'S WORD — OPTION A: ALL TWENTY SERVED SKILLS GET A SLASH COMMAND, AND THE COVERAGE IS PINNED BY A TEST.**

Raised the same day after `/capture-session` came back `Unknown command` on his work computer. At the time nine of twenty skills were fronted by a command and eleven by nothing.

He was given three options and took A over B (fix discovery instead) and C (cover only what people type by name). **TWO THINGS MOVED THE ARGUMENT, and both are dated later than the reasoning that originally held the set at eight:**

1. **THE CLUTTER OBJECTION HAD ALREADY BEEN PAID DOWN.** The case against widening was Alex's *"inserted several things into my project"*, which is why `dec:idea-init-asks-which-harness-and-installs-only-that` narrowed the install. But that shipped in PR #178 on 2026-08-14: `init` now ASKS which harness and writes `.claude/commands` for Claude Code ONLY. An OpenCode or VS Code project receives none of them, so the cost that argued against twenty files is no longer paid by the projects that complained.

2. **MEASURED THE SAME DAY — COMMANDS ARE THE CHANNEL THAT ACTUALLY GETS USED.** `fact:skill-use-measured-two-channels-2026-08-14`: across every retained transcript, `where-am-i` was invoked **37 times as `/where` against 4 `get_skill` calls**. 55 of 63 sessions invoked a skill by command or Skill tool; 35 used `get_skill`. People type shortcuts; they rarely instruct an agent to fetch a skill. **A skill with no command is reachable only by the weaker of the two channels.**

⭐ **AND THE MEASUREMENT CUTS BOTH WAYS, WHICH IS WHY THE TEST IS PART OF THE RULING.** A skill WITH a command is invoked locally and vanishes from `get_skill` counts; a skill WITHOUT one can arrive by no other route. So widening coverage will make `surface_usage.py` report LOWER apparent skill use unless it learns to count both channels. That is a measurement artefact, not a regression, and it must not be read as one.

═══ WHAT IS OWED, AND THE SECOND HALF IS THE DURABLE ONE ═══

· Eleven new command files for capture-session, ci-gate, impact-check, ingest-corpus, link-artifacts, link-projects, parallel-work, plan-increments, report-friction, retire-from-design, revise-design.
· **A TEST THAT PINS COVERAGE.** `skill_lint` already fails a command naming a skill that does not exist; **nothing fails a skill that no command names**, and nothing pins the count — which is how `dec:commands-are-the-exception`, `chg:commands-ship` and `ver:install-reaches-the-agent` all still say EIGHT while eleven ship. Without this half the set silently falls behind again the next time a skill is added.
· The three records above should be corrected to the shipped number rather than left saying eight.
properties.name: OPEN — does every served skill get a slash command, or is the shortfall the wrong thing to fix?
properties.rationale:
THE OPTIONS, WITH WHAT EACH COSTS. None is recommended here; the measurement is the contribution.

**A — ship all twenty.** Consistent, and it is the option `dec:commands-are-the-exception` already argues for: each command is four lines of pointer with no version-coupled content, so twenty rot no faster than eight. COST: twenty files in a consumer repo. Alex, 2026-08-14, on init: it *"inserted several things into my project"* — and that report is why `dec:idea-init-asks-which-harness-and-installs-only-that` narrowed the install. **Widening the command set runs directly against the complaint that was just settled**, and these are Claude-Code-only files, so an OpenCode project gets twenty it cannot read.

**B — ship none of the missing eleven, and fix DISCOVERY instead.** The server instructions already list every skill; the failure is that a user reaches for `/name` and gets a flat `Unknown command` from the HARNESS, which reflow2 never sees and cannot answer. COST: does nothing for the person typing the slash. Nothing in reflow2 can intercept it.

**C — cover the skills a user REACHES FOR by name, and say so.** capture-session is the demonstrated case. COST: the criterion is taste, and the current eleven were chosen by the same unstated taste — which is how the shortfall went unnoticed.

**WHAT IS NOT OPTIONAL EITHER WAY, and is the cheaper half:** the guard is asymmetric. `skill_lint` fails a command naming a missing skill; **nothing fails a skill that no command names**, and nothing pins the count, so the record still says "eight" while eleven ship. Whichever option wins, the intended coverage should be asserted somewhere a test can read it — otherwise the next skill ships uncovered in silence exactly as these eleven did.

**THE STANDING TRAP:** this is invisible from inside the checkout. `.claude/skills/` holds all twenty as compile sources, so Claude Code resolves every skill as `/name` HERE and on no consumer install. Any judgement about command ergonomics made in this repo is made in the one environment where the shortfall does not exist.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Raised 2026-08-13 while putting `req:linking-two-projects-is-a-served-process` to Anthony, flagged before he accepted it, and he accepted anyway — so the requirement stands and this stays open beneath it rather than blocking it.

HIS ASK USED "2+": *"a process that we can reuse when a user wants to link 2+ reflow2 projects"*. THE SKILL THAT SHIPPED IS PAIRWISE, and does not say so.

WHAT THE TOOLS ACTUALLY DO, checked rather than assumed:
  · `seam_report` takes a LIST of pairs, so it already composes across many boundaries in one call.
  · `pair_designs` takes exactly ONE other design. Three projects therefore means three runs (or six, if every pair is checked), and **nothing aggregates the results** — no report says "these five designs, taken together, have these seams and these unmet needs."

⇒ THE GAP IS NOT IN THE PROCESS BUT IN WHAT COLLECTS IT. Each pairwise answer is correct; there is no whole-neighbourhood view, and a user with five interrelated designs would have to hold that in their head.

📌 THIS IS WHERE `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` LIVES — ten reflow2 designs sit under `~/project`, all Anthony's, which is exactly the N-project case and the one place a shared vocabulary needs no negotiation (see the "strongest narrow form" note on `dec:idea-defined-pair-types-so-two-projects-combine-by-lookup`). And `req:many-people-and-many-projects-compose` already says the two axes must hold TOGETHER, which neither accepted requirement states.

THE OPTIONS, none taken:
A — SAY IT PLAINLY. One line in the skill's "Honest limits": it links two designs at a time, and N projects means N-1 or N(N-1)/2 runs with no aggregation. Cheapest, honest, and consistent with every other skill stating what it cannot do. **Does nothing for the user with five designs.**
B — LET THE SKILL LOOP. Prescribe running the pairwise process over each pair and collating by hand. No code, but it puts on the user exactly the bookkeeping a tool should carry, and it will be skipped.
C — A NEIGHBOURHOOD REPORT. Something that takes several designs and answers once — seams, unmet needs, dead surfaces across the set. Real work, and it needs the correspondence to be RECORDED rather than re-asserted per run, which is the same unbuilt prerequisite step 7 names.
D — NOTHING YET. Wait for a real three-project case. reflow2↔flo2 is the only pair anyone has actually linked, and building an N-way view off a sample of one is the mistake the pairing measurements already warn about.

⚠️ THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO MY OWN FLAG: I generalised "distrust the name matcher" from a single pair, and D says the same caution applies here. A neighbourhood report designed before anyone has linked three real projects would be designed from imagination.

⇒ A IS OWED REGARDLESS AND COSTS ONE LINE — a skill whose ethos is stating its own limits currently does not state this one. C is the interesting one and should wait for evidence.
properties.name: OPEN — the user asked for "2+" projects and what shipped is pairwise; should link-projects handle N, or say plainly that it handles two?
properties.rationale:
Recorded so a flag the user moved past is not lost. He asked for "2+", the shipped skill is pairwise, and the skill does not admit it — which matters more than usual because that skill's whole ethos is naming what it cannot do.

The measurement underneath it: seam_report already takes a list of pairs and composes; pair_designs takes one other design and nothing aggregates across a set. So the gap is in what COLLECTS the answers, not in the process itself.

Kept separate from dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects (where the graph lives for one owner with many projects) and from the pairing-mechanism decision, though both are adjacent — this one is narrowly about whether a shipped skill overstates its own scope.

properties.decision:
UNDECIDED — RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-16.

⚠️ THIS NODE'S FIRST VERSION WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE. It said reflow2 has "no SEQUENCE or GATE" and offered "stay a vocabulary and a set of detectors" as the status quo. BOTH ARE FALSE, and I wrote them before reading the skills. Corrected the same day, on the same question.

⭐ WHAT THE GUIDED PATHS ACTUALLY DO, quoted rather than characterised:
GENESIS enforces exactly the predecessor's order and uses its own labels: "Seed the brief into P0/P1 — and stop there … `add_requirement` for each thing that must be true (P0) … `add_capability` for each thing the system does (P1) … **Do NOT create Components (P2) yet.** Leaving structure unspecified is deliberate: the first DETECT round will surface `concept_without_design`, which is the right next question ('how should this be structured?'). Answer it *with the user*, not by guessing." The detector is real (`GapSource::ConceptWithoutDesign`). It also sets `mode` (`flexible` = design evolves with the build; `rigid` = design is the source of truth) at scaffold time — the predecessor's dial, with the predecessor's meaning, at the moment it matters.
ADOPT is stricter and is the path a brownfield user takes. Five phases — Gather, Scan, Analyze (static then dynamic), Recover, Validate — and its central discipline is the SE one that matters most: "NEVER INFER A REQUIREMENT FROM THE IMPLEMENTATION THAT SATISFIES IT. A requirement backed out of the code is satisfied by construction — it can never contradict anything, so a graph of those can never say anything." It demands BOTH SIDES OF EVERY CONTRACT, keeps recovered requirements at `proposed` until the user's word, and closes with `coverage_report` to say what the design has never heard of.

⇒ REFLOW2 IS NOT A BARE VOCABULARY. It ships a sequenced, opinionated process on both the greenfield and brownfield paths, and the sequence is function-before-structure.

WHY THE SELF-HOST IS NOT EVIDENCE AGAINST IT: reflow2 has no genesis epoch from a brief and was never taken through adopt. Its graph records organic growth with good bookkeeping — not a guided design. THE EXPERIMENT ANTHONY IS WORRIED ABOUT HAS NOT BEEN RUN ON REFLOW2 ITSELF. (And its functional decomposition WAS deliberate — `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition`, accepted 2026-07-23, derived with the user.)

⚠️ THE ONE PLACE THE SELF-HOST IS A FAIR INDICTMENT, and it is narrower than "no process": reflow2's own graph VIOLATES ADOPT'S OWN INSTRUCTION. "Both sides of every contract" — and there are 73 coupled module pairs with ZERO declared interfaces.

THE QUESTION THAT REMAINS, and it is Anthony's real one restated: HOW DOES A USER GAIN CONFIDENCE THAT THE PROCESS WAS FOLLOWED? Nothing today records which skill a session used, at which phase, or reports when a design departed from the sequence.

THE OPTIONS, revised:
(a) NOTHING FURTHER. The guidance is good and the field reports support it — music_graph's own wins list says "coverage_report is the single best thing in the adopt flow" and "unmotivated_capability IS the design-recovery engine, exactly as the skill claims". AGAINST: it leaves confidence resting on testimony rather than on anything the graph can show.
(b) MAKE THE DESIGN SAY WHICH PROCESS PRODUCED IT — record the skill and phase a session worked in, so "was he guided" becomes a fact rather than a hope. Cheap. AGAINST: it records the claim, not the conformance; a session can say `adopt` and do anything.
(c) REPORT DEPARTURES FROM THE SEQUENCE — "Components exist but no Capabilities", "allocated before anything was decomposed", "this boundary has no contract". Every input is already computed, and it is the house style (`dec:report-dont-judge`). AGAINST: `undeclared_seam` has reported reflow2's own missing contracts all along, at severity 0.45, under the gate — a report nobody must act on is how the self-host drifted.
(d) THE REAL EXPOSURE MAY BE NEITHER: skills are SERVED but must be REACHED FOR. `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` is ACCEPTED and says the user must never be the trigger — and it is NOT BUILT. The risk to a new user is not a flawed process; it is a session that never loads `adopt` and starts writing Components on day one.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether (d) is the dominant risk. Nobody has measured how often a consumer session actually invokes a skill.
properties.name: OPEN — reflow2's GUIDED paths do sequence function before structure; the open question is whether anything makes a design SHOW it followed one
properties.rationale: Recorded as brainstorming on Anthony's `/brainstorm`, 2026-08-16, and CORRECTED the same day after reading the genesis and adopt skills — the first version asserted reflow2 had no process, which was my error from not reading before characterising. His question and framing throughout; the measurements and the correction are mine. The self-host half is `dec:idea-should-reflow2s-own-design-be-re-derived-through-a-principled-se-process`. Nothing is promoted; that is his word.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-24, going one level under his own redb question: *"a more fundamental question after this line of thinking, but what does having a db (whether that be rocksdb or redb or other) give us versus just using the reflow2 json file as what endures? does having a db allow us to do things we wouldn't otherwise have?"* Nothing here is intent and nothing is planned.

⭐⭐ THE QUESTION IS UPSTREAM OF BOTH EARLIER ONES, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS SEPARATE. `dec:idea-a-byte-backend-that-compiles-in-seconds` asks WHICH engine. `dec:idea-the-store-becomes-a-session-cache-and-the-export-becomes-the-truth` asks WHAT IS DURABLE and still assumes a per-session store. This asks whether an embedded key-value store earns its place AT ALL. All three can be answered independently and the answer to this one changes whether the other two matter.

⭐⭐ MEASURED 2026-08-24, AND THE BUILD HAS ALREADY ANSWERED THE LOUDEST HALF. `crates/reflow2-core/Cargo.toml` declares **`default = []`** — `rocksdb` and `fulltext` are BOTH optional and BOTH off by default; only `reflow2-mcp` turns them on (`features = ["rocksdb", "fulltext"]`). Consequence, measured by running it: **`cargo test -p reflow2-core --no-default-features` passes 1,452 tests with NO database and NO search index**, against 1,760 for the whole workspace with both features on and the MCP surface included. ⇒ **The design-graph operations do not depend on a byte store.** Schema validation, the golden thread, adjacency traversal, the detectors, HEAL, propagation, the graph algorithms — all of it runs on `MemoryBackend` (`foundation/store/backend.rs:245`), which is the same `KvBackend` trait with a `BTreeMap` behind it.

WHAT A STORE ACTUALLY BUYS, then — a short list, and it is shorter than it looks:
1. **DURABILITY WITHOUT A WHOLE-DOCUMENT REWRITE.** One changed node writes one key, not 8.4 MB. This is the real one and it is the ONLY one that is hard to replicate.
2. **CRASH CONSISTENCY.** RocksDB's WAL means a killed process loses the last write, not the file. A half-written JSON document is corrupt — recoverable only by write-to-temp-and-rename, which is atomic but gives all-or-nothing at whatever cadence you write.
3. **LARGER THAN RAM.** Irrelevant at reflow2's own size: 3,142 nodes = 8.4 MB export, and it is the biggest design anybody has.

WHAT PEOPLE ASSUME IT BUYS AND IT DOES NOT — the part worth writing down:
- **Query power.** reflow2 asks graph questions — neighbours, traversals, type scans. Those come from `graph_id`-namespaced keys and an adjacency index (`keys::adj_out_key`), and `MemoryBackend` serves them by the same code path. There is no query planner and no SQL to lose.
- **SEARCH.** `fulltext` is its OWN feature, tantivy, independent of the KV store. `search_design` needs an INDEX, not a database, and an index is derived — rebuildable on hydrate from the document.
- **MULTI-SESSION CONCURRENCY.** That is the shared SERVER (a process holding one writer), not the store. Sessions share a graph because they share a process, and that stays true whatever the bytes sit on.

⇒ THE SHAPE THE ANSWER SEEMS TO TAKE, offered as a finding and not a conclusion: for one person on one laptop, an embedded store buys **durability and crash-safety and nothing else**, and the alternative is not redb — it is `MemoryBackend` plus the document at boundaries, which reflow2 ALREADY SUPPORTS FOR EVERYTHING EXCEPT PERSISTENCE. Every graph operation is proven on it by 1,452 passing tests.

⚠️ THE COST OF BEING WRONG, recorded beside the idea rather than used to argue it down. The trade is **bounded loss vs no loss.** RocksDB's durability is real engineering and hard to reproduce honestly; write-temp-and-rename gives atomicity but loses everything since the last write. Anyone taking this road is choosing a weaker durability story deliberately, and `dec:idea-what-guarantees-the-export-if-the-export-is-the-only-durable-copy` is where that half is argued.

🛑 WHAT IS UNMEASURED AND DECIDES IT: hydrate time. Parsing 8.4 MB of JSON, building the adjacency index and building the tantivy index, to first query. Nobody has taken it. Today's 2.4-second figure is an EXISTING store opening with its index already on disk — the cheap half, and not this number.

📌 THE OVER-ENGINEERING READING, in his own terms. What RocksDB currently costs this project, measured: a ~19-minute librocksdb-sys C++ compile on every clean build, the bulk of a target directory that reached 263 GiB, a pin on the historically-unmaintained `rocksdb` 0.24 with a migration to `rust-rocksdb` still owed, and 86 files of absorbed store code now in reflow2's tree to maintain. That is the price of durability for an 8 MB document. Whether it is worth paying is exactly the question he asked, and it has never been asked in that form before.
properties.name: OPEN — what does ANY embedded store buy over the export document alone? Measured: 1,452 of the core's tests already pass with no database and no index, because `default = []`
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill: recorded as an idea, nothing promoted, nothing settled.

Kept separate from the two ideas it sits above, both read in full before splitting: one asks WHICH engine, one asks WHAT IS DURABLE while still assuming a per-session engine. This asks whether an embedded key-value store earns its place at all — and unlike the other two it is already half-answered by the build, since `default = []` means 1,452 core tests run without one today.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-17, thinking out loud: "I feel like there are some other design principles that while they are my own philosophies, should apply to anybody building with reflow2 ... I think they should be advisory guidelines for any reflow2 project (of course the user can waive them if they want)."

THE SOURCE: dev_storyflow's seven ENGINEERING PRINCIPLES, which he user-set over 2026-06-17 → 2026-07-04 and MIGRATED INTO A DESIGN GRAPH on 2026-08-09 as `rule:fleet_*` DesignRule nodes. Read from `origin/main` on 2026-08-17 (the local checkout was 289 commits behind; the pre-migration prose was recovered from the commit before `57f6bbb5`).

  1. Right long-term fix — no patches or stopgaps. TWO ORDERED STEPS: determine the actual root cause FIRST (reproduce, trace, prove the mechanism), THEN fix at the root cause. "A fix without an identified root cause is a guess."
  2. No silent fallbacks — fail loudly or STOP AND REPORT. "An INTEGRITY line, not a style preference."
  3. Done = end-to-end + lens-exposed. Merged is not done.
  4. Verify your OWN claims before posting; UI work must be observed live.
  5. Real-path tests — unit-green is not live-green.
  6. No silent caps or truncation — if you bounded coverage, SAY SO.
  7. Modular, maintainable code — no monoliths (+ Python DI / typing.Protocol / flat hierarchies).

⭐⭐ THE FINDING THAT REFRAMES THE WHOLE QUESTION, and it was not obvious until the seven were lined up: SIX OF THE SEVEN ARE ONE PRINCIPLE WEARING SEVEN COATS — the report must not overstate the work. A stopgap reports a fix that did not happen (1). A swallowed error reports success (2). "Merged" reported as "done" (3). An unverified claim posted as fact (4). Unit-green reported as live coverage (5). A truncated sweep reported as complete (6). Only #7 (modularity) is about structure rather than honesty.

⇒ THAT IS `epoch:instruments-stop-overstating`, ARRIVED AT FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION. reflow2 spent this whole increment building the same principle for its own reports; his fleet derived it from agents writing code. Two independent derivations of one idea is the strongest evidence available that it is not a house style. It also changes what shipping them would MEAN: not "reflow2 has opinions about your coding", but reflow2 extending its own core doctrine — report don't judge, a zero must say which zero — outward to the project being designed.

⇒ AND REFLOW2 ALREADY IMPLEMENTS THREE OF THEM ON ITSELF, which is either the best argument or a warning about scope: #6 IS `req:a-report-says-what-it-swept-and-whether-its-checks-ran`; #4 is `dec:three-party-checks` plus the standing "claims must be evidence-backed" rule; #1 is `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap` and `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause`, accepted hours before this conversation.

THE OPTIONS, none chosen:
(A) SEEDED AS NODES. `genesis` / `reflow2_init` writes them into every new graph as advisory DesignRules. Durable, queryable, waivable per project by editing the node. COST: seven nodes nobody in that project authored, in a tool whose pitch is that the graph holds YOUR design.
(B) SERVED AS A SKILL, like every other reflow2 skill — read on demand, nothing written. Zero footprint, always current with the server. COST: skills are advice to an agent; nothing records that a project adopted or waived one, so the waiver he wants has nowhere to live.
(C) BOTH — served as guidance, and OFFERED at genesis as a starter pack the user accepts, edits or declines. The acceptance is the user's word, so nothing is asserted on their behalf.
(D) NOT SHIPPED. Documented as a recommended starting set in the kit's prose, left for each project to adopt by hand.

⚠️ THE OBJECTION, recorded beside the idea rather than argued down, and it is his own doctrine turned on this: he holds that a VIEW must be a pure projection and that renderer fill-ins are reflow2 DEFECTS — content appearing in an output that nobody put in the design. Seven pre-seeded rules are arguably that same shape one layer up: graph content no one in the project authored. Option (C) is the shape that answers it, because the user's acceptance is what puts them there; (A) is the shape most exposed to it.

⚠️ AND THE UNIVERSALITY IS UNEVEN — see `dec:idea-a-principle-has-a-universal-core-and-local-clothes`.
⚠️ AND "ADVISORY" IS NOT A FREE DEFAULT — see `dec:idea-how-does-a-shipped-principle-say-whether-it-is-enforced`.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 ship a default set of advisory design principles to every project it is installed into?
properties.rationale: Recorded as brainstorming. The reframing is the contribution: six of the seven principles are the same principle — a report must not overstate the work — which is the epoch reflow2 has spent this increment building for its own instruments. That makes shipping them an extension of reflow2's existing doctrine rather than an importing of house style, and it is the strongest argument available for doing it at all.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-21, before any flo2-driven change is made. Nothing here is intent and nothing is settled.

HIS CONCERN, in his words: "my concern is that by making the changes to reflow2 required by flo2, that it wouldn't be able to support its original use case (which is how we are currently using it now). that's why I was thinking we need to consider this early because I would hate to break the current use case because we made a whole bunch of changes to make reflow2 work for flo2."

⭐ IDEA A — THE LOCAL CASE IS DEFENDED BY INTENT BUT NOT BY A GUARD, AND THAT IS THE GAP. Three things already stand between flo2's work and a broken local path: `req:persistence` (accepted — the design lives at ./.reflow2/graph inside the repo, travelling with it), `req:invocation` (accepted — an MCP server over stdio), and `dec:one-process-many-stores`' own instruction that "the overwhelmingly common case is one project, one directory, --graph-path, and it must keep working exactly as it does", with the framing "single-graph mode is multi-graph mode with a registry of one, pre-populated at startup and with selection defaulted — NOT a second code path". That framing is the right shape and it is a DESIGN PRINCIPLE, not a check. Nothing today fails when it stops being true. The cheap answer to a regression worry is a guard, not a promise.

⭐ IDEA B — HIS STATED SCALE MAY EXCEED WHAT THE ACCEPTED DECISION COVERS. flo2 is a web app at flo2.io, collaborative (many people on the SAME project at once) and expecting on the order of 10,000 simultaneously logged-in users across DIFFERENT projects. `dec:one-process-many-stores` accepts N open RocksDB stores in one process, each carrying its own block cache, file handles and tantivy index, and names resource exhaustion as an accepted risk requiring "a cap on simultaneously open graphs, with a clear error at the cap rather than silent thrashing". 10,000 open stores in one process is not that shape. At that number the answer is partitioning across many processes — which is item #8, blast radius, which flo2's own tracker says to decide BEFORE designing the registry because "retrofitting it onto a registry designed for one process is a rewrite of the piece everything else is gated on". The decision was accepted without a number attached; the number changes which question is being answered.

⭐ IDEA C — AND THAT MAY CUT THE OTHER WAY, WHICH IS THE HOPEFUL VERSION. A sharded shape — many processes, each holding few graphs — is CLOSER to today's local behaviour than one fat process holding everything. If the answer at 10k is partitioning, the invasiveness to the local path may go DOWN rather than up, because each process keeps roughly the shape it has now. Recorded as a possibility, not a claim; nobody has designed it.

⭐ IDEA D — THE COLLABORATIVE AXIS MAY ALREADY BE MET AND IS WORTH NOT REBUILDING. "Many people on the same project at once" is `req:sessions-share-a-graph` (accepted) delivered by `cap:shared-sessions` (VERIFIED — "several sessions work one design at once, through one server"). Single-writer is not relaxed by any of this: one process holds the lock, many sessions speak to it. So flo2's collaboration requirement may need nothing new, and the genuinely unbuilt axis is the many-PROJECTS one.

WHAT IS NOT IN DOUBT, so it does not get re-litigated here: whether flo2 gets its own fork. `dec:one-process-many-stores` answers that — one reflow2, N single-writer stores, the directory stays the unit of a design — and it explicitly rejected many-designs-in-one-store. The open questions above are about SHAPE and PROOF, not about forking.

🛑 A SEPARATE DEFECT NOTICED WHILE READING, not part of this question: `dec:one-process-many-stores` carries `status: accepted` and a name beginning "ACCEPTED 2026-08-06 (conditional)", while its own body opens "PROPOSED, NOT SETTLED." The status moved and the text did not. A reader can honestly conclude either. Left alone — whether it is settled is Anthony's to say.

DISTINCT FROM the three nodes the guard surfaced. `dec:one-process-many-stores` decides the SHAPE of hosting and assumes it is worth doing; this asks what it COSTS the existing case and whether a stated scale still fits. `req:many-people-and-many-projects-compose` requires the two axes to hold together; this asks what would PROVE a third thing — the local path — still holds while they do. `dec:the-registry-root-is-the-tenant-boundary` settles where the tenant line falls inside the registry; this asks whether a registry of that shape survives 10k.
properties.name: OPEN — what would PROVE that building for flo2 has not broken the local single-project case, and does 10k tenants even fit the accepted shape?
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill: recorded as ideas so nothing is lost and nothing is claimed as intent. Anthony raised it deliberately EARLY — before the flo2-driven changes are made rather than after — which is the whole point of recording it now.

The four ideas are kept apart because they have different answers: A wants a check written, B wants a number decided, C is a possibility nobody has explored, and D may need nothing at all. Collapsing them into one node would make it answerable only in halves.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-25, immediately after deciding the adopt nesting step: *"as we defer the functional allocation step in genesis skill (not done at genesis phase), do we need some /system-depth or /functional-allocation skill that the user can use?"*

═══ THE GAP IS REAL AND IT IS PRECISELY LOCATED ═══

**Genesis is RIGHT to defer.** Its line 44 reads: *"Do NOT create Components (P2) yet. Leaving structure unspecified is deliberate: the first DETECT round will surface `concept_without_design`, which is the right next question ('how should this be structured?'). Answer it WITH THE USER, not by guessing."* That is doctrine's function-before-form, correctly sequenced, and it is more disciplined than adopt was until today.

🛑 **AND THEN NOTHING PICKS THE QUESTION UP.** The gap fires, the user is asked "how should this be structured?", and reflow2 offers no method to answer it with. Measured: no served skill mentions functional decomposition, allocation, or `propose_allocation`. So the one step doctrine says produces the architecture is the one step with no guidance attached.

⭐⭐ THE MACHINERY ALREADY EXISTS AND NOTHING POINTS AT IT. `propose_allocation` clusters capabilities by weighted coupling into groups — that IS doctrinal step 5, mechanised — and `evaluate_allocation` scores the result for modularity, god components and misplaced capabilities. Both are served tools. Neither appears in any skill. **This is the three-legs failure again** (`fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it`): a typed tool with no instruction and no detector-that-notices-absence reaches no user's design, however good it is.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**A. A NEW SKILL — `/allocate` or `/functional-allocation`.** Triggered by `concept_without_design`, or by the user asking "how should this be structured?". It would: decompose capabilities into finer functions where they are compound; run `propose_allocation`; put the proposed grouping to the user rather than applying it; create Components from what they accept; nest them and set `level`; then `evaluate_allocation` and span-of-control as the sanity check.
 ⚠️ Cost: reflow2 has 23 skills and `fact:nine-of-twenty-skills-are-edited-without-a-drift-signal` already measures that the set is hard to keep coherent. A 24th needs to earn its place.

**B. EXTEND GENESIS.** Genesis already owns the deferral, so it could own the return. Cheapest, and it keeps one skill per phase.
 ⚠️ Cost: genesis is the FIRST skill anyone runs and its whole discipline is *stop before structure*. Folding the structuring step back in risks the very thing the deferral protects — a user doing it in one breath, guessing at boxes while the capabilities are still wet.

**C. EXTEND `detect-and-ask`.** The gap already routes there. It is where `concept_without_design` is phrased and put to the user, so the method could live beside the question.
 ⚠️ Cost: that skill is deliberately generic over ALL gaps; giving one gap a bespoke multi-step procedure makes it two skills wearing one name.

**D. NO SKILL — put it in the TOOL DESCRIPTION.** `propose_allocation`'s served description could carry the method, since an agent reading the tool list would meet it at the moment of use.
 ⚠️ Cost: it is only met by an agent that already thought to look for an allocation tool, which is exactly the agent that did not need telling.

**E. A DETECTOR FIRST, SKILL LATER.** Nothing currently notices that a design has capabilities and no components, or components with no allocation. Make the ABSENCE visible, then decide whether the answer needs a skill or a paragraph.
 ⭐ This is the cheapest thing that could not be wrong, and it matches the project's own posture: the loop should ASK rather than wait to be told.

═══ WHAT THE NAME SHOULD NOT BE ═══

Anthony offered `/system-depth` and `/functional-allocation`. **DEPTH IS THE WRONG NAME** and today's work is why: depth is a CONSEQUENCE of allocation, not a thing to go and get. A skill called `/system-depth` would invite the error this session made four times — treating the number of layers as a target rather than as an output that span of control checks afterwards. If it exists, it is about ALLOCATION, and the depth falls out.

📌 AND IT WOULD CLOSE THE SYMMETRY. As of today adopt recovers the structure an artifact HAS (the nesting step, added 2026-08-25). Genesis defers the structure a design NEEDS and nothing derives it. One direction is now instructed and the other is not.
properties.name: SETTLED — option E: make the missing allocation VISIBLE first (`unallocated_component`), and decide about a skill later
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill: recorded as an idea, nothing promoted, nothing settled.

Kept separate from `dec:idea-what-does-se-doctrine-actually-prescribe-upfront-and-what-of-it-does-reflow2-have` (which establishes WHAT doctrine prescribes and which pieces reflow2 owns) and from `dec:idea-does-reflow2-enforce-an-se-process-or-only-supply-the-vocabulary` (which asks whether a design can SHOW it followed a process). This asks a narrower, buildable thing: the one deferred step has no home, and the question is which of five places it should live in — a decision that can be taken without settling either of those.

═══ RESOLVED 2026-08-25 — ANTHONY CHOSE E ═══

Option E over A (a new `/allocate` skill), B (extend genesis) and C (extend detect-and-ask). Built the same day as `cap:unallocated-component-detector` / `req:structure-with-no-function-is-asked-about` (`ce:unallocated-component-detector-2026-08-25`). **The skill question is deferred, not answered** — E's whole point is that the absence is now measurable, so whether a skill is needed can be decided from evidence rather than from taste.

⚠️ **E'S OWN PREMISE WAS HALF WRONG, AND CHECKING IT IS WHAT MADE THE FINDING.** E read *"nothing currently notices that a design has capabilities and no components, or components with no allocation."* The FIRST half was already covered — that is `concept_without_design`, firing at zero components. Only the SECOND half was uncovered, and it was bigger than the option implied: **33 of reflow2's own 95 components** are leaf boxes owning no capability at all, with every detector reporting clean. A recorded option is a hypothesis, not a specification; this one was written by a session that had not measured, and building it as stated would have shipped a redundant check beside a real one.
