═══ 🛑 THE SHARPER FINDING: THREE LEGS ARE NOT SUFFICIENT, AND IT IS ALREADY MEASURED TWICE ═══

**Case 1 — `DECOMPOSES`.** Typed tool ✓, instruction ✓, detector ✓ — **and the vocabulary stayed empty**, because `DecompositionCoverage` fires on a Requirement that ALREADY CARRIES an incoming DECOMPOSES edge. It checks whether an existing decomposition is covered; it cannot ask why none exists. reflow2's own graph reached **0 DECOMPOSES edges while shipping the detector for them.**

**Case 2 — half-idea linking.** `dec:idea-linking-half-ideas-needs-a-task-that-can-be-run` records that it **has all three legs and still left 110 ideas unlinked**, because nothing SUGGESTS candidates and nothing works the backlog.

⇒ Leg 3 has a hidden qualifier: *a detector that notices absence* is not the same as *a detector that notices ABSENCE OF THE WHOLE PRACTICE*. And both failures look like the same missing thing — no worklist, no runnable task, nobody's job.

⇒ **Is there a FOURTH leg: something that makes the practice HAPPEN, rather than merely possible and observable?**

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) RUN THE AUDIT AS A ONE-OFF.** Sweep every vocabulary item against the three legs, produce a table. Cheap, concrete, answers his actual question. ⚠️ Counter: a table dated today rots by next week, and a hand-taken census has been the answer several times already.

**(b) MAKE THE AUDIT A DETECTOR.** `vocabulary_coverage` already exists as a served tool — **whether it already computes something like this is UNCHECKED and should be looked at before anything is built.** ⚠️ Counter: possibly already built; look first.

**(c) NAME AND ADD THE FOURTH LEG.** Define what turns a possible practice into a performed one. ⚠️ Counter: the most speculative option here, and "nobody's job" may be a management problem rather than a design one.

**(d) RETIRE THE THREE-LEG FRAME as too coarse.** Two of its cases pass the test and fail in practice. ⚠️ Counter: it correctly diagnosed the other two cases, and a frame that catches most things is not worthless for missing some.

═══ ⚠️ THE COUNTERWEIGHT ═══

The three legs were derived from a sample of THREE. Generalising from three cases and then auditing 22 skills against it risks measuring conformance to a frame that was never validated, instead of measuring whether vocabulary actually reaches users. **The outcome that matters is "does a user's project acquire this", not "does this have three legs".**
properties.name: OPEN — the three legs were named and never audited across the surface; and two measured cases had all three and still delivered nothing
properties.rationale:
Kept separate from the tool-class question because it concerns ONE named contract that already exists, where that one asks whether kinds should carry contracts at all. This one could be answered by a sweep somebody runs this afternoon; that one cannot be answered without first deciding what the axes are.

The interesting content is not the uniformity question Anthony asked — it is that the design already holds TWO measured cases where all three legs were present and the vocabulary stayed empty. That moves the question from "have they been applied everywhere" to "is the test even the right test", and the second is worth more than the first. Recorded before checking `vocabulary_coverage`, deliberately: option (b) says look before building, and writing the question down is not the same as answering it.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — surfaced 2026-08-11 checking `docs/requirements-coverage.md`'s deferrals against the code rather than trusting its status column. Nothing here is intent.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. HEAL-3 says the catalogue is 8 of 13, with `unreachable`, `weak_connection`, `missing_link`, `missing_entity` and `missing_embedding` deferred. Grepping the core: the only hits for those five are a MODULE COMMENT at `crates/reflow2-core/src/heal.rs:27-29` and unrelated `unreachable!()` macros. So the five are genuinely absent — confirmed, not assumed.

⭐ BUT THAT COMMENT IS ITSELF STALE, WHICH IS THE SHARPER FINDING. heal.rs:27-29 reads: "Deferred (need `dynograph-graph` or the LLM): dead_end / unreachable / disconnected_community / weak_connection / single_point_of_failure / missing_link…". Three of those — `dead_end`, `disconnected_community`, `single_point_of_failure` — ARE BUILT and were being proposed as fixes until PR #147 narrowed them this same session. A comment naming what is missing has kept naming things that arrived.

⭐⭐ AND HEAL-14'S BLOCKER HAS EXPIRED. The row reads "⬜ Missing-intermediate Component for hierarchy — matryoshka (needs `Component.level`)". `Component.level` EXISTS: 3AX-9 is ✅, `hierarchy_issues` and `MissingIntermediateLevel` are in `crates/reflow2-core/src/hierarchy.rs` (5 references), and `missing_intermediate_level` is surfaced as a gap by `detect_gaps`. So the DETECTOR fires and the REPAIR was never written — `heal.rs` has zero references to it. The stated reason for deferring is gone and nothing noticed. This is the same shape as `cap:what-next`, whose blocker also expired unnoticed and which turned out to be buildable the moment anyone looked.

⚠️ THE COUNTERWEIGHT, and it is not optional: PR #147 (merged today) REMOVED HEAL's ability to propose `generate_bridge`/`generate_owner` for `disconnected_community`/`dead_end`/`orphan`, because inventing a relationship nobody designed is not a repair. A `generate_component` for a missing intermediate level is EXACTLY THAT SHAPE — inventing a subsystem to sit between a system and a part. So HEAL-14 may not be "unblocked and buildable"; it may be "unblocked and now forbidden by a rule accepted hours ago". `req:a-repair-suggestion-never-proposes-fabrication` is accepted. That tension is the actual question here and it did not exist when the row was written.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) Fix the stale module comment and the stale HEAL-14 blocker note — pure record-keeping, costs nothing, and stops the next reader inheriting both errors.
(b) Decide HEAL-14 on the anti-fabrication rule: either the missing-intermediate repair is legitimate (the level is derivable from the two endpoints, not invented) or it is forbidden and the row should be RETIRED rather than left ⬜ forever.
(c) Retire the five never-built categories from the catalogue. The project's own test is "unused AND redundant → retire; unused AND not-redundant → defer, and say so" — nobody has re-asked which of the five is which since 2026-07-22.
(d) Nothing. 8 of 13 has been enough for every trial so far, and no friction report has asked for the missing five.

📌 THE META-POINT, which is the reason this node exists at all: `requirements-coverage.md` carries a BINDING deferral discipline — "a deferral that isn't written down is a silent stub, which this project treats as the same integrity breach as a silent drop." Three rows were checked today and three were wrong: SP-3b says ingest cannot be called from a session (it can), GS-17 says the polished PROMPT step is deferred (`gap_to_prompt` does it), 3AX-5 says TemporalFact usage is deferred (133 instances). The table goes stale in BOTH directions, and nothing computes on it. That is the argument for deferrals living where a detector can reach them — and equally the argument against trusting this table as the source for what to build.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's question, 2026-08-16: "we used to have a planned capabilities increment / planned epochs within reflow2 — can we use these features within reflow2 to map out the triage fixes?" The reconnaissance and the options are mine.

THE SHORT ANSWER IS YES, THE MACHINERY EXISTS AND WORKS. Measured today: `plan_epoch` (future) is distinct from `add_epoch` (happened); `schedule_for` carries `modality: expected | required` with real teeth; `arrival_delta` computes five outcomes and stores none; 11 planned epochs and 27 SCHEDULED_FOR edges already exist. `arrival_delta` on `epoch:governance-becomes-expressible` returned six outstanding requirements AND volunteered "nothing is scheduled `required` … so there is no obligation to miss and it is NOT ready to cut. An increment that promises nothing has not been scoped." The tools are healthy and opinionated.

⭐ BUT THERE IS A BLOCKER THE QUESTION DOES NOT ANTICIPATE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE DECISION: `schedule_for` accepts `Requirement` or `Capability` ONLY. EVERY triage finding is a TemporalFact. So not one of them can be scheduled as it stands. The plan-increments skill says why this is correct rather than a limitation — "a plan is not intent … an item scheduled but never captured is a promise with no requirement behind it" — so the missing step is CAPTURE, not scheduling.

📌 AND THE SKILL ALREADY NAMED WHAT I WAS DOING: "if you are maintaining a numbered list of upcoming work in the conversation … that is a delivery plan living outside the graph." My ranked what-next list was exactly that, twice today, and it would have died with the session.

⚠️ EVIDENCE THAT THIS IS WORTH DOING PROPERLY RATHER THAN QUICKLY — reflow2's OWN plan has drifted, in precisely the shape the skill's §4 warns about. Of 27 SCHEDULED_FOR edges, ELEVEN still point at `rel:v0190`, `rel:v0200` and `rel:v0210`, all long shipped. Planned epochs sit at sequence 250–267 while arrived epochs reach 343. So the plan looks present and is answering nobody. Any new plan laid on top inherits that unless the stale half is dealt with.

THE OPTIONS FOR WHAT BECOMES PLANNABLE.

(a) A CAPABILITY PER FIX, at `status: planned`. Faithful to how features are tracked. ⇒ AGAINST: most of these are repair, not new function — "propose_heal stops mislabelling its scope" is restoring intended behaviour, and filing it as a capability inflates the capability count with maintenance and makes `unrealized_capability` noisier for months.

(b) A REQUIREMENT PER FIX, capabilities beneath where one is genuinely new. Faithful to the vocabulary: a fix is a statement about what must be true. ⇒ AGAINST: roughly a dozen findings would become a dozen requirements, which is a lot of intent minted in one act, and some are small enough that a requirement overstates them.

(c) ⭐ A REQUIREMENT PER THEME, several findings beneath each — and today's findings cluster harder than they look. At least four are ONE statement: "a report says whether a check was EXERCISED or had NOTHING TO EXAMINE." That covers propose_heal's vacuous zero, and it is not new doctrine — `chg:a-null-and-a-vacuous-zero-now-say-which-they-are` already did exactly this for scoped `detect_gaps`, and dev_storyflow named it a WIN. A second theme is "a reply says what it did not recognise", covering the undeclared property and the nearest-name suggestion. ⇒ AGAINST: theming is a judgement, and grouping wrongly buries a finding under a heading nobody searches.

(d) SCHEDULE NOTHING; leave them as facts and let the loop surface them. ⇒ AGAINST, and this is measured rather than argued: across this entire session `loop_status` reported the same 80 gaps and 16 defects and NEVER ONCE surfaced a triage item, because a defect FACT is not a gap. Doing nothing means they stay invisible to the loop that exists to say what is owed.

(e) EXTEND `schedule_for` TO ACCEPT A TemporalFact. Removes the blocker directly. ⇒ AGAINST: a fact is an observation, not work. Scheduling an observation is a category error, and it would let the design promise to deliver a measurement.

AND THE SECOND QUESTION, WHICH IS SEPARABLE: HOW MANY EPOCHS? One "triage fixes" epoch is easy to reason about and hard to argue with; two or three themed epochs (the detectors that misdescribe themselves, the write surface that accepts what it should question, the loop that cannot scope itself) carry more meaning and cost more to keep honest. `arrival_delta`'s own note argues for at least one `required` item per epoch, or it is not scoped.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the stale SCHEDULED_FOR edges to shipped releases should be cleaned first, retired deliberately, or left as the historical record they arguably are — that is its own decision and re-pointing them silently would erase the slip, which the tool explicitly warns against.
properties.name: OPEN — the triage findings are TemporalFacts and schedule_for takes only a Requirement or Capability, so nothing today can be planned. What becomes the plannable thing, and how many of them are there?
properties.rationale:
Anthony's idea; the blocker, the drift measurement and the five options are mine. Recorded rather than acted on because the choice mints intent.

⭐ SETTLED 2026-08-16 ON HIS WORD: "one triage fixes epoch, requirement per theme." That is option (c) for the plannable unit and ONE epoch for the container.

WHAT THAT RULES OUT, recorded because the roads not taken are the useful half: (a) a Capability per fix is declined — most of these are repair rather than new function and would inflate the capability count with maintenance; (b) a Requirement per fix is declined — roughly a dozen at once is too much intent minted in one act; (d) leaving them as facts is declined, and the measurement is why: `loop_status` reported the same 80 gaps and 16 defects all session and never once surfaced a triage item, because a defect FACT is not a gap; (e) extending `schedule_for` to accept a TemporalFact is declined as a category error — a fact is an observation, not work.

AND HE CHOSE ONE EPOCH over two or three themed ones — easier to reason about and harder to argue with, at the cost of the increment carrying less meaning in its name.

⚠️ WHAT THE RULING DOES NOT DECIDE, and was not asked: nothing is scheduled `required`. Every item goes in `expected`, because `required` is an obligation whose miss is a computed violation rather than a slip, and the plan-increments skill says to ask rather than assume. ⇒ `arrival_delta` will therefore report this epoch NOT ready to cut until somebody names at least one obligation. That is the tool being right, not a defect, and it is the next question for him.

AND THE STALE HALF IS STILL OPEN: eleven SCHEDULED_FOR edges still point at releases shipped long ago. This ruling adds a new plan beside them and does not clean them, deliberately — re-pointing them silently would erase the slip.

properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Raised 2026-08-28 from a field report, not from thinking about reflow2.

📌 The near-match offered was `fact:every-reply-was-sent-twice` — the MEASUREMENT that caused this, and the record of the choice made. This is the open question of what to do now that the choice has a named cost. Kept separate so the measurement stays a measurement.

⚠️ **THE CONSTRAINT THAT BOUNDS EVERY OPTION:** reverting to always-duplicate resurrects the refusals. `detect_gaps` was 157,785 bytes on the wire and a harness refused it outright; 26,096 after the fix. **No option may give that back.**

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══

**(a) GATE ON THE NEGOTIATED PROTOCOL VERSION.** Duplicate into `content` only when the client negotiated below `2025-06-18`. This is what MCP's own backwards-compatibility SHOULD asks for, and it costs the 2× only for clients that need it. ⚠️ Counter, the one that killed this in August: priced at threading `RequestContext` through 155 handlers and 151 `ok_json` call sites. **That price has NOT been re-measured**, and two things bear on it — the version comparison already exists and is tested (`version_is_per_request`), and `json_result` is a single choke point, which is exactly the shape that made read-only cheap on 2026-08-26 when making `write_lock` fallible let the compiler find all 98 sites. ⚠️ **SECOND COUNTER, POSSIBLY FATAL: the reporting client may have negotiated a MODERN version and still read only `content`.** If so, gating on version would not have helped it at all.

**(b) GATE ON SIZE, NOT VERSION.** Duplicate whenever the payload is small enough to be harmless — most replies are — and send the signpost only for the big ones. ⚠️ Counter: the failure becomes intermittent and size-dependent, which is worse to diagnose than a consistent one. A client would read most answers and silently lose the largest, which are the orientation calls that matter most.

**(c) A SERVER FLAG** — `--duplicate-content`, set by whoever runs the server for such a client. Cheap, explicit, no protocol guessing. ⚠️ Counter: it must be DISCOVERED, and the person who needs it is reading a stub that does not mention it. That is the addressee problem again. Mitigated only if the stub itself names the flag.

**(d) FIX THE SIGNPOST'S ADDRESSEE, and nothing else.** Rewrite the stub to speak to the AGENT, which is who reads it, naming what the agent can actually do: use `graph_report_markdown` and the prose tools, export to a file and read that, ask the operator for a flag. ⚠️ Counter: makes the outage survivable, not absent — the reporter's own words stand, that export-and-parse *'cannot replace `search_design` before a create, or `loop_status` before finishing.'* ⭐ But it is a one-string change that strictly improves every other option, so it is arguably complementary rather than alternative.

**(e) DO NOTHING; IT IS THE CLIENT'S BUG.** The spec says SHOULD, not MUST. ⚠️ Counter: `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself` makes field use the point, and this is field use. Declining should be explicit rather than by neglect.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT MUST BE CHECKED BEFORE CHOOSING ═══

1. **Which protocol revision did the reporting client negotiate?** The report does not say. If it is modern, option (a) is dead on arrival and the framing changes. **Cheapest and most decisive question here.** ⭐ ASKED 2026-08-28 — Anthony put it to Alex; an answer is expected within a day or so. `cap:the-handshake-is-written-down-beside-the-graph` was built the same day so the answer arrives in a file rather than requiring him to instrument his machine.

   📌 **THE REFERENCE POINT TO READ HIS ANSWER AGAINST, measured 2026-08-28 on this repo's own server:** a known-good client — `claude-code 2.1.241` — requested and negotiated **`2025-11-25`**, and reads `structuredContent` without difficulty. So a modern revision in Alex's reply does NOT explain his outage and points at option (c) or (d); an old one (`2024-11-05`, `2025-03-26`) points at option (a). One line of his file decides it.

2. **What does the ~300-line estimate cost today?** Made before anyone tried; the read-only precedent suggests a choke point plus the compiler may do most of it.
3. **Is one client one client, or the first of several?** n=1 for the affected population — the mirror of the n=0 that justified the original decision.
properties.name: OPEN — how does a client that reads only `content` get an answer, without resurrecting the 2× wire cost?
properties.rationale:
Raised because the field named the client the August decision was explicitly gambling did not exist: *'a large invasive change to protect a client nobody could name'*. The gamble was reasonable and it lost.

The constraint is stated before the options because the tempting move — put the payload back in `content` — undoes a measured 6× improvement and re-breaks the harnesses that drove it.

Option (d) is flagged as complementary rather than alternative: the signpost speaks to the client while being read by the agent, and that is wrong regardless of which other option is chosen.

Left as brainstorming because question 1 can invalidate option (a) entirely and nobody has asked it. Choosing before asking would be the same mistake in a new costume.

properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Raised 2026-08-28 by Anthony from `fact:manual-work-46b68cd85cf97510` — the same Python written three times in two days.

═══ THE JOB ═══

You edit some files. Before re-taking baselines you must know **which registered Artifacts cover them**. Nothing answers that, so the work is: dump the export, build a `location → node_id` map, filter.

═══ ⚠️ AND `search_design` DOES NOT MERELY FAIL — IT ANSWERS WRONGLY ═══

Measured 2026-08-28. Querying the exact path `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/coherence.rs` against `node_type: Artifact` returns **`art:tools-capture`** first, then three unrelated core modules. The right answer, `art:tools-coherence`, is not in the top four.

THE CAUSE IS MEASURABLE: of 251 Artifacts, all carry a `location`; **203 have a short name, 22 carry the FULL PATH as their name, 26 are unrelated.** BM25 indexes name/statement/description and NOT `location` — so a path query scores best against the 22 whose *name* happens to be a path. **A wrong artifact returned confidently is worse than no answer**, because re-baselining the wrong one records a change against a file that did not move.

═══ ⭐ THE SHARPEST FACT, AND IT SHAPES EVERY OPTION ═══

`reconcile_artifacts` takes `observed: [{artifact_id, present, checksum}]` — **artifact_id, not path.** So the one tool that most needs this mapping REQUIRES the caller to already have it. The lookup is a precondition of the reconcile loop and is served by nothing.

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══

**(a) A NEW TOOL** — `artifacts_at(paths) -> [{path, artifact_id, ...}]`. Exact, unambiguous, obviously named. ⚠️ Counter: the surface is 164 tools and `find_tools` exists *because it is already too large to hold in context*. A 165th for a lookup is real cost, and `fact:the-upstream-watch-is-findable-only-in-reflow2s-own-words` says a new tool is only as good as its discoverability.

**(b) INDEX `location` IN `search_design`.** One field into the BM25 index; the exact-path query then works. ⚠️ Counter, and it is the serious one: search is FUZZY AND RANKED, and this question wants EXACT. A ranked answer invites precisely the confident-wrong-answer measured above — it would rank better, not become correct. It also changes every other query's behaviour.

**(c) LET `reconcile_artifacts` ACCEPT A PATH** where it now demands an `artifact_id`, resolving it itself. ⭐ Puts the answer where the need is, adds no tool, and removes the chicken-and-egg from the loop's own reconcile step. ⚠️ Counter: an ambiguous or unmatched path needs a defined answer, and silently skipping one would be a green report over a file nobody checked — the exact failure class this project keeps finding.

**(d) EXTEND `coverage_report`.** It already takes observed paths and walks the same data, reporting what NO node claims. Making it also report what IS claimed, and by which artifact, is the inverse of what it computes. ⚠️ Counter: its whole framing is "what is the design blind to", and answering both may blur a tool whose value is that single question.

**(e) DO NOTHING — it is `scan_nodes` plus a filter.** True, and it is what happened three times. ⚠️ Counter: 251 artifacts against a size-capped reply means paging, and the caller re-implements the join every time.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT SHOULD BE CHECKED BEFORE CHOOSING ═══

1. **Is the artifact naming inconsistency a separate defect worth fixing on its own?** 22 of 251 carry a path as their name. That is what poisons the search, and it may deserve a ruling regardless of which option here wins.
2. **How often is this actually needed?** n=3 in two days, one person, one project. The `report_manual_work` record is the only evidence, and it is the same n=1-shaped evidence base that `dec:idea-should-a-finding-be-required-to-bound-its-own-claim` warns about designing against.
3. **Does (c) subsume the need entirely?** If the only real consumer is the reconcile step, a lookup tool nobody else calls is a 165th tool for one caller.
properties.name: OPEN — how does a session ask "which artifact covers this file?" — a new tool, or a field the existing ones already need?
properties.rationale:
Raised because the work was hand-rolled three times in two days and `report_manual_work` recorded it as `tool_missing` — a diagnosis re-checked here rather than trusted: `find_tools` was run first, and `search_design` was then tested against a real path and returned the WRONG artifact, which strengthens the case rather than weakening it.

The options are ordered from most obvious to least, and the most obvious one is listed with the strongest counter: a 165th tool on a surface already too large to hold is not free, and this project has just measured that a new tool is only as useful as it is findable.

Option (c) is flagged because of a fact neither the friction report nor the original diagnosis noticed: `reconcile_artifacts` demands `artifact_id`, so the missing lookup is a precondition of the loop's own reconcile step rather than a convenience beside it.

Left as brainstorming, and the second thing to check says why: the evidence is one person, one project, three occurrences. That is thin ground for growing a surface.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. A sub-question of `dec:idea-does-reflow2-ship-design-principles-to-every-project` — the guard matched it and it is deliberately separate, because that one asks WHETHER to ship and this asks a question that has to be answered even after "yes", and answers to it are what make the difference between options there.

THE COLLISION. Anthony's framing was "advisory guidelines ... of course the user can waive them". Reasonable, and it runs straight into `dec:does-enforced-default-to-gate-blocking` (2026-08-08, accepted): **`enforced` has THREE states and NO default** — `true`, `false`, and ABSENT meaning nobody has said. The default was REMOVED on purpose, because a convention recorded in passing used to assert it could fail somebody's build; that is how all four of reflow2's own enforced rules got that way, not one of them chosen.

So each way of shipping answers the enforcement question differently, and none is free:

(A) SHIP THEM `enforced: false`. Matches his words. BUT it is reflow2 asserting a policy about consequence in a project it knows nothing about — and consequence (whose build stops, who is blocked at 2am) is exactly what that decision says is the USER'S to state. A team that would want "no silent fallbacks" to stop their build is told by an unchosen default that it does not.

(B) SHIP THEM WITH `enforced` ABSENT. Honest by that decision's own lights. BUT `unstated_rule_enforcement` fires at 0.4 per rule, so a freshly-genesised project starts life owing SEVEN gaps it did nothing to earn — a gap list greeting you on day one, which is the "list that gets skimmed" failure the acknowledge tools exist to prevent, arriving at the worst possible moment.

(C) ASK AT ADOPTION. The starter pack is offered, and adopting a principle IS answering its enforcement question, one at a time, in the user's own words. Nothing is asserted and no gap is manufactured. COST: seven questions at genesis, the moment a user has least context and most to do — and the governance-proposal skill's own warning applies, that asking about a fourth rule in one session turns the asking into noise people wave through.

(D) SHIP ADVISORY, MAKE THE WAIVER THE RECORDED ACT. Default `false`; a project that wants one enforced says so. Inverts (A)'s problem rather than solving it: cheap for the common case, still an unchosen answer in the graph.

⚠️ A FOURTH QUESTION HIDES UNDER ALL OF THEM: an ENFORCED rule owes a DETECTOR (`unverified_enforced_rule`, 0.6, until a PASSING check exists). Several of these principles are judgements no detector can compute — "was this the root cause?" is the one just met head-on in `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap`, which Anthony ruled ADVISORY on exactly that ground. So a shipped principle set would arrive carrying reflow2's own open question `req:a-rule-says-whether-it-can-be-checked-at-all`, which may make that requirement a PREREQUISITE for shipping principles rather than a neighbour of it.

⭐ THE ONE THING THAT SEEMS SETTLED WHICHEVER WAY THIS GOES: whatever ships must record that a project ADOPTED or WAIVED a principle, because a waiver nobody wrote down is indistinguishable from never having heard of it — the same shape as the patch nobody wrote down in `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause`, one layer up.
properties.name: OPEN — "advisory by default" is itself a default asserting something, and `enforced` was deliberately given no default; how does a shipped principle answer that question honestly?
properties.rationale: Recorded as brainstorming. "Advisory by default" sounds free and is not: dec:does-enforced-default-to-gate-blocking deliberately removed the default, because whether breaking a rule stops a build is a claim about consequence only the user can make. Every option either asserts that answer, manufactures seven day-one gaps, or spends seven questions at the moment the user has least context.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-18, correcting the framing of a day's work: 'most of why I do any of this isn't for the sake of reflow2. it is for users who are developing a project using reflow2... we are just applying reflow2 back on itself here, but that is not the main concern. it is that reflow2 does SE for the projects that it is used on.'

DISTINCT FROM THE TWO FACTS IT RESTS ON: they MEASURE (three legs; 18 candidates). This asks WHAT TO DO, and the options below conflict with each other and with settled decisions, which is why it needs a decision rather than another measurement.

THE MEASURED SHAPE is in `fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it`: vocabulary reaches a user's design only when a TYPED TOOL writes it, an INSTRUCTION says when, and a DETECTOR notices its absence. Capability.inputs/outputs has none of the three; SPECIFIES is instructed but has no tool; DECOMPOSES has all three and still cannot fire, because the detector keys on the edge being PRESENT.

OPTIONS, unranked, each with its objection:

(a) ADD THE MISSING LEGS CASE BY CASE — a parameter on add_capability, a `specifies` tool, an absence-detector per edge type. Concrete and shippable. OBJECTION: it is whack-a-mole, and it scales with the SCHEMA rather than with the design — three cases were found by hand this week with 18 candidates and 42 edge items behind them.

(b) A DETECTOR FOR UNUSED VOCABULARY ITSELF — 'this design has never used X, and here is the tool that writes it.' One rule covering every case, present and future. OBJECTION: on a young design EVERYTHING is unused, so it fires on the whole schema at genesis and is skimmed by week two — the failure `v0.2.0-what-we-dont-know.md` names as sharpest ('a gap list you skim is worse than no gap list'). It needs a maturity threshold, and a threshold is a judgement.

(c) ASK AT THE RIGHT MOMENT rather than standing as a finding. When an agent adds a Capability, ask what goes in and what comes out — the black-box question, at the one moment the user is thinking about that capability. OBJECTION: this IS `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue`, proposed and unbuilt, and it is the same trigger problem this project has confirmed three times.

(d) DERIVE RATHER THAN ASK. A capability's inputs and outputs are partly computable — what it CONSUMES and PROVIDES is already edge vocabulary. OBJECTION: `dec:report-dont-judge`. Deriving a functional signature and storing it asserts something nobody said, and the point of the property is the designer's statement of intent.

(e) LET THE SCHEMA SHRINK. If nothing writes it and nobody misses it, the vocabulary is speculative. OBJECTION, decisive against doing this blindly: three of the four known unreachable fields were WANTED and got a parameter, and `req:declared-vocabulary-is-reachable-from-the-surface` explicitly forbids reading unreachable as deletable.
properties.name: OPEN — how does an arbitrary project using reflow2 ever acquire the vocabulary nobody thought to ask it for?
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill: ideas enter as ideas, nothing is promoted, objections sit beside the options.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE REACHABILITY REQUIREMENT AGAIN. That asks whether a declared field CAN be written. This asks whether a user's project ever WILL — a question about skills, tool descriptions and detectors rather than about parameters, and the one Anthony says actually matters. A field with a parameter that nothing ever prompts for is reachable and still empty in every design.

AN AGENT'S READING, as a finding and not an answer: (c) looks strongest because it puts the question where the user is already thinking, and (b) looks most dangerous because a list nobody reads is worse than none. But (c) depends on a requirement proposed and unbuilt since before this, so the honest first move may be to accept THAT rather than design around it.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-23: *"one thing I've noticed a bit is updating progress of development and testing of the graph … I had been using the /capture-session as sort of a way to make sure the graph is being updated, but things are getting through."*

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐ THE SHAPE, AND IT IS NOT A DISCIPLINE PROBLEM: **CAPTURE IS ADDITIVE. NOTHING ANYWHERE ASKS WHAT A SESSION MADE FALSE.**

Every mechanism in the loop adds: capture-intent adds nodes, `record_change` adds an event, capture-session adds what the conversation held, `loop_status` counts what is OWED. Not one asks *which existing assertion did this work just retire?* So a finding that motivated a fix survives the fix, and goes on proposing work already done.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📐 MEASURED ON THIS DESIGN, 2026-08-23

    TemporalFacts                                    274
      basis = measured                               274   (all of them)
      carrying a valid_to                              7   ⇐ 2.6%
      OPEN (no valid_to)                             267
        ...whose SUBJECT has since been CHANGED      200   ⇐ 74%

**The field that closes a fact already exists and is 97% unused.** `valid_to` is declared on TemporalFact, reachable, and essentially never written.

⚠️ BOUND: "has since been CHANGED" is NOT ordered against `valid_from`. A ChangeEvent carries no date of its own — it is placed by AT_EPOCH — so 200 is an UPPER BOUND on staleness candidates, not a count of stale facts. Sharpening it needs epoch sequence compared against `valid_from`, which was not done here.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 TWO SIGHTINGS, AND THE FIRST HAPPENED IN THE SESSION THAT RECORDED THIS

(1) **THIS SESSION, CAUGHT BY ANTHONY.** Asked where else to optimise, the agent read `fact:the-orientation-reads-cost-ten-seconds-and-the-store-is-not-why` and quoted its numbers as current — `open_questions` at 11.7s, `detect_defects` the hot spot — with the fact's own words *"NOTHING WAS OPTIMISED"* and *"that ratio is the next measurement and it has not been taken."* **All three were false.** PR #290 had taken the measurement AND fixed it: 56 SPOF candidates at 878ms each became 5.08ms for all 56, `detect_structural_defects` 44.5s → 4.43s, `open_questions` 11.7s → **2.95s**. His reply: *"I think we already determined candidate 3."* He was right; the graph said otherwise. `cmp:service`, that fact's subject, has been CHANGED **nine** times since.

(2) **A DIFFERENT PROJECT, ON HIS OTHER MACHINE.** An agent proposed work, he accepted, and on investigating it reported the work was already done. Same shape, different graph, no shared code — which makes this a property of the MODEL rather than of one session's carelessness.

⭐ AND THE SIBLING NODE SAW THIS COMING FROM THE OTHER SIDE. `dec:idea-search-first-fires-without-being-remembered` measured six saves in one session and found **four of six prevented WORK rather than nodes**, calling that "the more expensive thing". Searching-before-proposing and closing-what-you-invalidated are two different fixes for one symptom: *an agent proposes work that is already done.*

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
IDEAS, UNRANKED, each with what it costs

**A. A DETECTOR — `stale_measurement`.** A `basis: measured` TemporalFact with no `valid_to` whose subject has been CHANGED since `valid_from`.
   ⭐ Needs no discipline, which is the whole argument — every other option asks somebody to remember something at the moment they are least likely to.
   ⚠️ **200 findings on day one is a failure mode this project has already lived through**: per-idea, the unreviewed-ideas detector would have fired 115 times the day it shipped and the category was filtered by week's end. This must be ONE aggregate finding at low severity — or it becomes wallpaper, which is dev_storyflow's reason ① for abandoning reflow2 altogether.
   ⚠️ The ordering stays a proxy until ChangeEvents can be placed in time against `valid_from`.

**B. capture-session ASKS THE INVALIDATION QUESTION.** It captures what a session produced; it could also ask what the session made false.
   ⭐ Cheapest by far — a skill edit, no schema, no code. And it is what Anthony was already using this skill to try to achieve.
   ⚠️ It is PULL, and this is precisely the sibling node's finding: the discipline exists in writing and decays anyway. Where the question SHOULD live; not where it will reliably happen.

**C. AN EDGE: ChangeEvent → the finding it ANSWERS.**
   ⭐⭐ **THIS REVERSES A DECISION TAKEN EARLIER THE SAME DAY, AND THE REVERSAL IS THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE.** `ChangeEvent → Decision` was one of five vocabulary candidates and was DECLINED — by this agent, in this session, hours earlier — on the ground that *"I cannot name a computation that would read it."* **Option A is that computation.** A detector reading ANSWERS edges is EXACT where a subject-changed heuristic is a proxy. The decline was correct on the evidence then available and is wrong now; what changed is that a reader appeared.
   ⚠️ Still a new edge type: moves the stamp, owes an upgrade note, worth nothing until something draws it.

**D. ASK AT THE MOMENT OF THE CHANGE.** `record_change` takes an optional "this answers X".
   ⭐ The one moment the author certainly knows; by session end they have forgotten. And it is the sibling node's own option (a)/(b) shape — put the discipline on the TOOL, not in a catalogue.
   ⚠️ Another field on the busiest write in the loop, and dev_storyflow reported write-time friction is exactly what trains agents to route around typed tools.

**E. THE STOP HOOK COUNTS IT.** "You recorded N ChangeEvents and closed 0 findings."
   ⚠️ `loop_nudge.py` CANNOT READ THE GRAPH — the session's server holds the single-writer lock — so it keys only on the op tally, and `valid_to` goes through a generic `create_node` indistinguishable from any other write. Implementable only if closing a finding gets its own NAMED op, which is an argument for C and D over E.

**F. DO NOTHING — a TemporalFact is a dated observation and staleness is the reader's job.**
   ⭐ The honest defence of the status quo: the type is explicitly temporal, `valid_from` says when it was true, and 274 never-expiring facts cost nothing until somebody reads one as current.
   ⚠️ **And that is exactly what happened, twice, today.** The cost is not theoretical and is not paid by the graph — it is paid by the person who accepts a proposal for work already done.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📌 WHAT THIS IS NOT

It is NOT about agents failing to use skills — that is `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`, accepted, with three observations of its own. A session that used every skill perfectly would still leave this gap. The two failures compound and are independent.
properties.name: OPEN — capture is ADDITIVE and nothing asks what a session made FALSE. 267 measured facts stand open; 200 describe a node that has since moved
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`. Anthony, 2026-08-23, from two independent sightings — one in this session, one on his other machine. Nothing here is intent and nothing is planned.

DEDUP: read six near-matches in full.
· ⭐ `dec:idea-search-first-fires-without-being-remembered` is the SIBLING and the closest of the six. Same shape — a discipline that is written down and still depends on somebody remembering it — and plausibly the same parent, `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` (proposed, unbuilt), of which this would be a SECOND instance. **But it is a different discipline: that one prevents a duplicate on the way IN, this one closes a finding on the way OUT.** Its own sharpest measurement — *"four of six saves prevented WORK, not nodes"* — is the same symptom this node measures from the other side, which is why it is linked rather than merged.
· `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` and `fact:an-agent-stopped-reaching-...` are about agents not REACHING for the loop. **A session that used every skill perfectly would still leave this gap, because no skill asks the invalidation question.**
· `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause` (ACCEPTED) asks whether a repair reached the CAUSE — a property of the fix. This asks whether it RETIRED THE FINDING — a relation between two records.
· `dec:the-patch-record-binds-forward-not-backward` settles that 472 existing changes are not reclassified; the same courtesy would be owed to the 267 open facts.
· `dec:idea-how-do-triage-findings-become-plannable-work` asks how a finding becomes SCHEDULABLE; this asks how it becomes CLOSED.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-09: \"how can we link reflow2 and flo2 — flo2 is dependent upon reflow2; we've discussed publisher → subscriber type relationships.\"

WHAT SEARCHING FIRST CHANGED, and it changed the question rather than answering it: most of the linking machinery is DESIGNED AND BUILT, and it has already been RUN on exactly this pair. dec:linked-repos-poc (executed 2026-08-06) composed reflow2, flo2 and dynograph-foundation in a throwaway in-memory graph and found ONE true positive unprompted — ifc:core-api (ours, `library`) against flo2's ifc:model-provider-api (`REST`), 80/100 name match, \"very likely the same contract, but they cannot be connected as either is currently built.\" Nobody told it the answer. So the publisher/subscriber SHAPE is not the open question; dec:pairing-role-placement settled where the role lives, cap:publish-surface and cap:mirror-surface are built, and dec:nested-graphs settled that separately-owned designs are separate graphs.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN IS THE TENSE. Every link so far has been a THING SOMEBODY RAN — a manual composition into a temporary graph, discarded afterwards. A subscription is a standing relationship: flo2 would be continuously answerable to what reflow2 currently publishes, and would learn when it moved. Nothing in the design says how that happens, and the two projects are on different machines, different release cadences and different owners.

THE OPTIONS, in Anthony's framing and with what is cheap or expensive about each recorded beside it rather than argued down:

(A) PULL AT THE EXPORT. flo2 vendors reflow2's committed export (or its published surface via export_surface) and re-composes on each reflow2 release. Cheapest by far, needs nothing new, and rides git which both already use. COUNTER: it is a snapshot, so flo2 learns about a moved contract whenever it next remembers to pull — which is the failure mode this whole question is about, one level up.

(B) PULL AT THE RUNNING SERVER. Once one process holds many designs (cap:graph-registry, reflow2_updates #1), flo2 could hold both graph_ids and ask across them live. COUNTER: gated on the largest outstanding piece of work, and dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs is still proposed. Also flo2's graph_id is `1a97fc1f1de4d5d2` — an opaque mint beside two readable labels — so the addressing story needs a human-facing name first.

(C) A DECLARED DEPENDENCY EDGE BETWEEN DESIGNS, not just between nodes. reflow2 already has req:design-dependencies-declared (accepted, verified) for library versions; the analogue for designs would let a consumer say \"I depend on reflow2's published surface at version X\" and make a stale subscription COMPUTABLE rather than remembered. COUNTER: it is new vocabulary, and dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs and dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency are both still open about what may legitimately cross a design boundary at all.

(D) THE SEAM AS A GATE. flo2's CI composes against reflow2's published export and fails when a contract it consumes has moved — the ci-gate pattern pointed across a boundary instead of inward. COUNTER: it makes reflow2's release able to break flo2's build, which is a real coupling decision and Anthony's to make, not a technical detail.

⚠️ THE BLOCKER IS THE SAME FOR ALL FOUR, AND IT IS ONE MISSING LABEL. dec:linked-repos-poc found it and deliberately did not fix it: REFLOW2 DECLARES NO `required` INTERFACE ANYWHERE. Pairing matches complements, so with nothing required, nothing can ever pair — paired=0 on BOTH pairs, 15 of dynograph-foundation's interfaces and 5 of flo2's landing in dead surface. Its most dangerous number was `unmet_needs: 0`, which reads as \"nothing is missing\" and means \"we never said we needed anything\". Until reflow2 says what it requires, every option above links two designs that cannot be compared. That PoC called declaring them \"the cheapest next step\" — a handful of nodes — and left it to Anthony's word because it is design about reflow2's own boundaries.

AND A SECOND THING NO OPTION ADDRESSES, from reflow2_updates.md #7 (NOT DESIGNED): there are TWO version axes at this seam and only one negotiates. The MCP protocol version negotiates per connection; reflow2's 149-tool surface does not. The toolsnaps stop a surface change landing silently IN THIS REPO and tell flo2 nothing. Whatever subscription shape is chosen has to carry that, or \"clean module\" quietly becomes \"vendored fork\" — which dec:open-reflow2-as-core-module already names as the crux, with the cost falling on @ajs.

NOTHING HERE IS PROMOTED. The options are recorded as considered; the one decision genuinely waiting is whether to declare reflow2's `required` interfaces, which is small, unblocks all four, and is not an agent's to make.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
ANSWERED IN PART 2026-08-12 BY A BACKTEST — THE SUBSTRATE IS NOT THE DESIGN EXPORT
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

This node said the SHAPE was settled and only the TENSE was open. A backtest shows a third thing was open and unnoticed: WHAT THE SUBSCRIPTION WATCHES.

THE METHOD, and it is reusable: rather than build a mechanism and hope, replay real history against failures with KNOWN answers. `reflow2_updates.md` — flo2's hand-written tracker, the manual version of this subscription — went stale in two specific, dated ways. Each was given a window and three candidate signals were scored against it. Read-only; nothing was built.

  §4 CONTRIBUTOR-SCOPED loop_status. The doc was CORRECT when written (2026-08-09 10:21, against v0.26.1 — `loop_status_for` genuinely absent). It landed 3h later in PR #126 and shipped in v0.27.0. The doc became WRONG at its 2026-08-11 re-check. Window: v0.26.1 → v0.27.0.
  §7 THE SEAM CHANGES. `HealIssue.suggested_fix_type` went `&'static str` → `Option`, and five capture tools began REFUSING near-duplicates. Both v0.28.0-only. Window: v0.27.0 → v0.28.0.

RESULTS:

  signal                | §4 input contract | §7 capture refusals | §7 result shape
  design export diff    | 1 hit in 70       | 12 hits in 103      | NO — only "art:heal changed"
  toolsnap diff         | DECISIVE          | DECISIVE            | STRUCTURALLY BLIND

⭐ THE TOOLSNAP DIFF WINS OUTRIGHT ON INPUT CONTRACTS. For §4 it is mechanical and needs no interpretation: `inputSchema.properties` went `{}` → `{contributor_id: …}`. For the capture refusals, `distinct_from` appears with a description that explains the new refusal.

🛑 NOTHING SEES OUTPUT SHAPE. Toolsnaps record `annotations, description, inputSchema, name` — THERE IS NO OUTPUT SCHEMA. So a result-shape change is invisible to every signal reflow2 has, and it is exactly the half most likely to break a generated client.

🛑🛑 AND THE DESIGN EXPORT ACTIVELY LIES. `cap:owed-to-a-contributor` reads `in_progress` at v0.26.1, v0.27.0 AND v0.28.0 — three releases after the capability shipped — because status moves only on the owner's word and nobody went back. A subscription built on design-export status would have told flo2 "still in progress" about working code. THAT IS WORSE THAN SILENCE, and it fully explains how the hand-written doc went wrong: it was not carelessness, the design export AGREED WITH IT.

⇒ **DIFFERENT CONSUMERS NEED DIFFERENT SUBSTRATES.** flo2 calls reflow2's TOOLS; its contract is the tool surface. A sibling consuming reflow2's INTENT would want the design export. Treating "link two designs" as one thing conflates them, and option (A) above (pull at the export) would have watched the wrong artefact.

⚠️ AND THE WINNING SIGNAL IS NOT OBTAINABLE ACROSS THE SEAM. The toolsnaps ship in NEITHER `release.yml` NOR the kit. flo2 has already registered them as `art:reflow2-toolsnaps` with location "github.com/sligara7/reflow2 — tools/toolsnaps/*.json", i.e. GO READ THEM OUT OF OUR REPO. The strongest available signal requires a checkout of the upstream, which defeats consuming a released artifact. TWO CHEAP FOLLOW-ONS THE BACKTEST EARNED: publish the toolsnaps as a release asset, and record OUTPUT schemas in them.

═══ THE PAIRING TRIAL, same day — first time it computed on this pair ═══

`pair_designs` reflow2 → flo2: **paired 0, conflicts 10, unmet_needs 5, dead_surface 2, candidates 1, unclassified 2 ours / 1 theirs.** The blocker this node's PoC recorded (reflow2 declared no `required` interface) cleared in PR #130; reflow2 now declares 9.

  (a) ZERO PAIRS, NOT FOR A FIXABLE REASON. flo2 models `cmp:reflow2-service` as a component it CONTAINS. Pairing matches complements ACROSS a boundary; flo2 drew reflow2 INSIDE its boundary, so there is none. A legitimate model that makes the seam permanently uncomputable by pairing.
  (b) TEN CONFLICTS, NEARLY ALL SPURIOUS. reflow2's dynograph LIBRARY requirements name-matched flo2's REST endpoints at 62–83/100. The one true correspondence scored 61 and landed in `candidates`. Fuzzy names PROPOSE; only a person DISPOSES.
  (c) TWO DESIGNS CAN AGREE BY BEING IDENTICALLY WRONG. Both label the shared boundary `medium: REST`; both MEAN MCP and both say so in `spec` prose. Had roles been complementary they would have PAIRED on a shared falsehood. The tool defends against `unspecified` reading as agreement and has NO defence against two sides stating the same wrong value. A seam check verifies LABEL EQUALITY, never interoperability.

═══ THE GAPS IN LINKING, generalised so they apply to any two reflow2 projects ═══

 1. THE LINK IS NOT A THING. Nothing in either graph records the other exists. A link happens when a human hands two files to a tool: no identity, no owner, no pinned version, no lifecycle. `req:design-dependencies-declared` covers LIBRARY versions and has no analogue for DESIGNS.
 2. CORRESPONDENCE IS INFERRED, NEVER ASSERTED. No shared identifier space, so matching falls back on fuzzy names and re-guesses every run. A human should be able to say "my X IS your Y" and have it stick.
 3. AGREEMENT IS NOT INTEROPERABILITY (see (c) above).
 4. THE LINK IS A RUN, NOT A RELATIONSHIP — the tense problem this node opened with.
 5. THE COMPARISON HIDES ITS OWN SKEW. A 0.27.0 flo2 export was compared against a 0.28.0 reflow2 and nothing said so. ⭐ `dec:fix-the-comparison-before-pointing-it-earlier` step 2 ALREADY DECIDED "a comparison discloses its own confound" for the single-project case and has never been pointed at the cross-project one, which has the same confound and a worse one — the two sides are on different release cadences by construction.
 6. ONLY INTERFACES CROSS. A decision in A that invalidates a capability in B, a shared constraint, readiness gating — the vocabulary for crossing is one node type wide.
 7. READING IS SAFE; WRITING IS NOT. A comparison touches neither store. A propagated gap writes into a graph its owner never agreed to. The git-diff transport survives BECAUSE it never opens the store — a safety property, not an implementation detail.
 8. THE PRECONDITION IS BILATERAL AND NOBODY BUDGETS FOR IT. A seam is only as good as the least-labelled side, `internal` is the DEFAULT so an unlabelled project reports a confidently empty seam, and neither party gets value until both have paid. This is why the whole linking layer has zero instances.
 9. N > 2 IS QUALITATIVELY DIFFERENT AND ALREADY MEASURED. `fact:the-diamond-meets-at-dynographs-internals-not-its-interface`: reflow2 and dev_storyflow both depend on dynograph, one as a Rust library and one as REST. A naive pairwise check between the siblings reports ALL-CLEAR — confidently and wrongly — because the conflict lives BELOW both published surfaces. Shared-dependency conflict is a property of the graph, not of any pair in it. Linking N designs is not N-choose-2 links.
properties.name: OPEN — what makes the reflow2→flo2 link a STANDING subscription rather than a run somebody remembers to do?
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill: one Decision per open question, at `proposed`, options in the prose, nothing promoted to intent without Anthony's word. Kept SEPARATE from dec:linked-repos-poc because that node records a RUN and what it proved; this one asks what the relationship should be going forward, which the PoC explicitly did not answer. Kept separate from dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs and dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency because those ask WHAT may cross a design boundary, while this asks WHEN and BY WHAT MECHANISM — one node holding both could only ever be half-answered.

PARTLY ANSWERED 2026-08-12 by a backtest against two dated failures with known answers: the substrate for a TOOL consumer is the toolsnaps, not the design export, whose status field lagged three releases behind a shipped capability. The method — replay real history against failures whose answer is already known — is more reusable than the finding.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — found 2026-08-11 by breaking CI with it. Nothing here is intent.

WHAT HAPPENED, and it is the cleanest possible demonstration. `cap:capture-registers-its-source` shipped, and the first thing it was pointed at was the document that actually drove reflow2's governance work: `dev_storyflow/reflow2_feedback.md`, in a SIBLING REPOSITORY. Registered as `art:storyflow-reflow2-feedback` with `location: ../dev_storyflow/reflow2_feedback.md`, plus DOCUMENTS edges to the seven governance requirements. Local gates passed. CI FAILED:

  FAIL  DRIFT  art:storyflow-reflow2-feedback: missing_artifact

CI checks out reflow2 alone, so the path resolves to nothing. `tools/reflow2_check.py` (line 615) reads `location` and FALLS BACK TO `name` when it is absent, then joins against `--root` — so there is NO WAY to register an out-of-repo source without failing the gate. Dropping the location does not help; it makes the check try the name as a path instead.

⭐ THIS IS `req:content-reaches-every-seat` FIRING ON THE THING BUILT TO SATISFY `req:no-idea-goes-quiet`. "A pointer resolves for everyone holding the design, not only for the machine that wrote it." A relative path into a sibling checkout resolves on exactly one machine. The two accepted requirements pull against each other in this case, and neither names the other.

⚠️ THE CASE IS NOT EXOTIC — IT IS ANTHONY'S NORMAL. His operating context is several partially-built designs across repositories and organizations, with the source material for one living in another. `req:many-people-and-many-projects-compose` (proposed) is the axis; this is a concrete instance of it landing on the artifact layer rather than the design layer.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) An `external: true` / `reachability` marker on Artifact that tells `reconcile_artifacts` the file is deliberately not part of this checkout, so ABSENCE is expected rather than drift. Mirrors what `volatility` already does for expected CONTENT change — this is the same move for expected ABSENCE. Risk: absence is the one finding `set_artifact_intent` deliberately keeps at full severity, so this weakens the strongest signal in the reconcile family and needs its own argument.
(b) COPY the driving excerpt into this repo as a dated, attributed source document and register that. Honest, resolves everywhere, and is what `req:sources-are-kept-not-just-parsed` (accepted) arguably already implies — keep the source WITH the design. Cost: a copy can drift from its original, and nothing would detect that.
(c) Treat the other repo as a DESIGN rather than a folder, and reach it through the cross-design machinery (`req:design-dependencies-declared`, accepted) instead of the artifact layer. Cleanest conceptually; costs the most, and dev_storyflow's feedback file is not a design.
(d) Do nothing, and accept that a source outside the repo simply cannot be traced. Cheapest; it is also the status quo that made Anthony hand-point an agent at the file in the first place.

WHAT WAS DONE MEANWHILE: the artifact and its seven DOCUMENTS edges were REMOVED so the gate is honest, and the backward trace is once again absent. That is a retreat, not a fix, and it is recorded here so the retreat is visible rather than quiet. `cap:capture-registers-its-source` remains correct for the in-repo case, which is the case its own description scoped it to — it says nothing about reachability, and that silence is the actual defect in it.
properties.name: OPEN — how does a design register a source document that lives OUTSIDE its own repository?
properties.rationale: The capability shipped and its first real use broke CI, because the only source document that mattered lives in a sibling repo. Two accepted requirements — no-idea-goes-quiet and content-reaches-every-seat — pull in opposite directions here and neither names the other. Recording the fork rather than picking one, because option (a) weakens the strongest signal the reconcile family has and option (b) crosses a repo boundary; both are Anthony's calls.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony's question in his own words, 2026-08-11: "now the project has things that weren't supposed to be built - should they maintain, delete it accept the work done without a requirement?" Nothing here is intent.

THE SHAPE OF THE PROBLEM. Those three are a real disposition with real cost attached, and the graph has nowhere to put them. The two moves the tooling currently offers both lose information:

  (1) WRITE A REQUIREMENT FOR IT. The detect-and-ask skill warns against this in its own table: "The wrong move is to invent a requirement from the capability's own description: a requirement backed out of the thing that implements it is satisfied by construction and can never contradict anything." A retro-fitted requirement makes the gap disappear and makes the design lie.
  (2) `acknowledge_gap`. Files it under "reviewed and fine". Cannot tell "we accept this and will maintain it" from "we accept this and it is now debt somebody owns" from "this is scheduled for deletion" — three different futures, one record.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) A disposition property/edge on the acknowledgement itself: accepted-and-maintained / accepted-as-debt / scheduled-for-removal, with an owner. Cheap if it rides on the existing acknowledge_gap Decision.
(b) Reuse the retire-from-design path for the delete branch and leave the other two to acknowledge_gap. Cheapest — no new vocabulary — but the accept-vs-debt distinction stays unexpressed.
(c) Treat it as an ordinary Decision the user writes by hand, governed by nothing new. Zero build cost; costs the ability to ASK "what unrequested work are we carrying?" across a design.

⭐ WHY THIS IS NOT A NICHE CASE, and it is Anthony's actual working context rather than a hypothetical: at NSLS-II he evolves a ~10-year-old bluesky stack where several organizations built partially-overlapping things because they could not wait for each other. Unrequested-but-built is the NORM on the brownfield path, not the anomaly. `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` (proposed) is the adjacent capture; this is what to DO once it is captured.

RELATED BUT DISTINCT, so it is not folded in here: `req:the-design-says-what-was-built-and-never-used` (proposed) surfaces implemented effort nothing depends on. That is BUILT-AND-UNUSED. This is BUILT-AND-UNREQUESTED. A capability can be either without the other, and conflating them would produce a detector that answers neither question.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT: reflow2 is a design-coherence tool, not a project-management tool. dev_storyflow's own feedback rejected importing PMBOK/WBS structure for exactly this reason — "importing PM artifact structure would add a second, competing spine next to the golden thread." A disposition vocabulary is close to that line, and (c) is the option that respects it.
properties.name: OPEN — how does a project record what it DECIDED about work that was built without a requirement: maintain, delete, or accept?
properties.rationale: Anthony named three futures for unrequested work and the graph collapses all three into one acknowledgement. Recording the question keeps his framing intact; the ideas differ mainly in how much new vocabulary they cost.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony asked how to choose this after a capture pass hit it; nothing here is intent, and the options are mine unless marked otherwise.

MEASURED FIRST, because it changes the question. In reflow2's own graph today: 198 TemporalFacts, and SIX TemporalFact→TemporalFact edges — ALL of them CONTRADICTS, and FIVE of the six carry `alignment: supporting`, i.e. corroboration rather than conflict. Five earlier sessions independently reached for a negation type to say two findings AGREE. This is not one author's routing quirk.

AND THE CURRENT ARRANGEMENT IS CORRECT, which is the strongest argument against touching it. Both computations that read CONTRADICTS skip `supporting` deliberately — `heal.rs:917-923` and `report.rs:1751-1766` — and report.rs carries a comment naming the bug that once existed: reading only the edge TYPE 'turned every recorded corroboration into a structural defect'. So there is NO live defect. The cost is a word that says the opposite of its meaning, and an author who must find a property to negate the type they just chose.

THE TEST THAT SHOULD DECIDE IT IS ALREADY ACCEPTED DOCTRINE: `dec:edge-orthogonality` — 'a vocabulary distinction earns its keep only if a computation reads it'. So the real question is not which word is nicer. It is: SHOULD REFLOW2 COMPUTE CORROBORATION? 'This finding is independently corroborated by N sources' is the same evidence-strength signal the design already cares about everywhere else (`basis: measured`, `confidence`, the whole verification doctrine), and the five supporting edges cluster on exactly the findings that recurred to different people. If that number should be reportable, the relation earns a type. If not, it is documentation and the cheapest option wins.

THE OPTIONS.

(a) LEAVE IT. CONTRADICTS + `alignment: supporting`. Cheapest, five precedents, twice defended in code with a comment recording why. ⇒ Against: every future author reaches for a negation to express agreement, and only finds the escape hatch by reading the schema — which is how this came up.

(b) WIDEN `SUPPLEMENTS`. It already exists and is declared `from: Fragment, to: Fragment` (build.yaml:133). A from/to list edit is the exact shape of #198 (VERIFIES admits Constraint), which shipped this increment, and it does NOT move the stamp — type counts and names are unchanged, so no upgrade doc is owed and nobody is locked out. ⇒ Against, and it is serious: SUPPLEMENTS has ZERO edges anywhere in this design, and its documented meaning is narrow and different (an LLM-as-SME supplementary-analysis Fragment augmenting its source). Nothing computes it. So this moves corroboration from an edge that IS read-and-correctly-skipped to one nothing reads at all — arguably backwards by `dec:edge-orthogonality`'s own test.

(c) A NEW EDGE TYPE (`CORROBORATES`). Cleanest semantics, and the only option where the word matches the meaning. ⇒ Against: edge_types 61 → 62 MOVES THE STAMP, which owes an upgrade doc and makes older binaries refuse newer graphs. That is a real consumer cost for what may be documentation — and it only pays for itself under the computation test above.

(d) SPLIT `alignment` OUT of CONTRADICTS ENTIRELY, so conflict and corroboration are separate types. Most honest model. ⇒ Against: same stamp cost as (c) PLUS a migration of the five existing supporting edges, and it would delete a working distinction to replace it with an equivalent one.

(e) LEAVE THE SCHEMA AND FIX DISCOVERABILITY. CONTRADICTS's hint mentions the supporting case only as a trailing parenthetical — '(or, with alignment=supporting, reinforce)'. Lead with it instead. ⇒ Zero schema risk, zero stamp movement, and it addresses the ACTUAL failure, which was an author not finding the mechanism rather than the mechanism being absent. Weakest if the answer to the computation question is yes.

WHAT NOBODY HAS MEASURED, and it would settle (c) vs (a): whether any consumer design has fact→fact corroboration at all, or whether this is a self-host pattern produced by reflow2 being the only project that records its own defects as TemporalFacts. If it is self-host-only, that is an argument for (a) or (e) on `rule:the-self-host-always-trails-what-it-teaches` grounds.

RELATED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FOLDED IN: `dec:one-retire-edge` is the same shape one axis over — two edge types for retirement, neither consulted, and still open. If these are answered separately they may drift apart; whether edge-vocabulary questions should be settled as a batch is itself a question.
properties.name: OPEN — a finding that corroborates another has to say CONTRADICTS to do it, and two code paths then filter that back out. Leave it, widen an unused edge, or make corroboration something reflow2 computes?
properties.rationale:
Not a proposal and not a ranking. The five-of-six measurement is the part worth keeping whatever is decided: a corroboration relation is being expressed through a negation type, five times, by different sessions, and the code correctly filters it back out in two places. Anthony asked how to choose; the honest answer is that `dec:edge-orthogonality` already supplies the test, and applying it needs one thing nobody has decided — whether 'independently corroborated by N sources' is a number reflow2 should report.

⭐ THE OUTSTANDING MEASUREMENT WAS THEN TAKEN, 2026-08-16, AND IT LEANS HARD. The decision text asks whether any CONSUMER design has fact→fact corroboration. Measured across every committed export on this machine — dev_storyflow, dynograph-foundation, flo2, music_graph, quantum_benchmarking_initiative, storyflow — the answer is not 'no fact→fact edges'. It is ZERO TemporalFacts, in all six, full stop.

⇒ THIS IS A SELF-HOST-ONLY PATTERN. reflow2 is the only project recording its own defects as TemporalFacts, because it is the only project whose subject is reflow2. That is `rule:the-self-host-always-trails-what-it-teaches` pointing the other way for once: normally the self-host lags what it teaches; here it has invented a usage no consumer has reached for.

⇒ WHICH RE-RANKS THE OPTIONS, though it does not settle them. (c) a new edge type and (d) splitting `alignment` both move the stamp — an upgrade doc owed and older binaries refusing newer graphs — and would be paying a CONSUMER cost for a relation no consumer uses. (b) widening SUPPLEMENTS was already argued against on `dec:edge-orthogonality` grounds and this weakens it further. (e) fixing CONTRADICTS's hint so the `supporting` case leads rather than trails costs nothing, breaks nothing, and addresses the failure actually observed — an author not finding a mechanism that was already there and already correct.

⚠️ THE BOUND ON THAT MEASUREMENT, stated rather than glossed: these are COMMITTED EXPORTS, which may trail those projects' live stores — music_graph's is dated 2026-08-01, and F23 is precisely a case of a committed export being behind. So this reads 'zero in the record I can see', not 'zero in existence'. Six-for-six at zero is still a strong signal, and it would take only one consumer starting to record findings to overturn it.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Source: the SECOND half of Alex Sligar's 2026-08-05 exchange, relayed by Anthony 2026-08-06. In Alex's own words, the use case is: "I have a ton of domain/tribal knowledge about my project, beyond the code itself. For example, I know why certain UI sections were created or have talked with the users and want a better way to document this information for junior devs on my project. I'd like to brain dump a bunch of this info in a way that other devs can query it using an AI prompt." STILL OPEN.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A NODE RATHER THAN A NOD: Alex described reflow2's use case almost exactly — rationale, who asked for it, what constraint drove it, kept beside the code and queryable in natural language — and the research answered him with Notion AI, Confluence/Rovo and Cognee. reflow2 was not a candidate in an answer to the question reflow2 exists to answer. Whatever else is true, that is a finding.

WHAT REFLOW2 ALREADY HAS FOR IT: add_decision with a rationale, authored_by (whose word this is), the golden thread from requirement to capability to artifact, and search_design over all of it. Against a wiki it has one property no wiki has: a rationale in reflow2 can be shown to have gone STALE, because the thing it justified is linked and drift is computed. A Confluence page saying "the legacy report screen stays because finance uses it monthly" stays confidently wrong forever after finance stops. That is the same normative property recorded in dec:idea-normative-vs-descriptive-graph, seen from the tribal-knowledge angle.

THE TENSION, and it is with an ACCEPTED requirement, not a soft one: req:driving-agent states that the primary consumers are coding agents and "the human is reached only through the agent". Alex's junior dev is a human asking a question with no build task attached and no design intent to capture. Serving that reader well means a read-optimised, question-answering surface — closer to Q&A over the graph than to the capture-detect-ask-decide loop — and the loop is what the current skill kit is built around. It is a different product surface on the same store, which is either a natural projection (dec:views-are-projections would allow it, since answering from the graph invents nothing) or a second product, and those have very different costs.

WHAT IS CHEAP: nothing new is needed to try it. An agent with the existing read tools can already answer "why does this exist" from a well-populated graph. The cheap experiment is to have someone who did not build the design ask it questions and see what it cannot answer.

WHAT IS EXPENSIVE, AND THE HONEST OBJECTION: this reader wants to BRAIN DUMP first and get structure later, which is the opposite of the capture loop's order. cap:ingest and cap:corpus-ingest exist for exactly that shape, so the primitive is there — but the loop's habit of asking about gaps at capture time is precisely what a brain-dumping user will experience as friction, and the brainstorm skill's own rule (do not run detect-and-ask over material the user deliberately left soft) exists because of that. Whether a dump-then-structure mode is a mode, a skill, or a different reader's whole path is unsettled.

A CONCRETE DOGFOODING OPPORTUNITY, recorded because it is testable rather than arguable: Alex has the project, the tribal knowledge and the junior devs. Pointing reflow2 at his brain dump would test cap:ingest, the newcomer-query path and the tribal-knowledge story at once, on a design nobody in this repo authored. Anthony's word needed on whether that is wanted.
properties.name: OPEN — is a human newcomer asking "why does this exist" a first-class reader of the graph, when req:driving-agent says the human is reached only through the agent?
properties.rationale: Recorded as an idea because the tension is with an accepted requirement and therefore cannot be resolved by an agent — either req:driving-agent is narrower than it reads, or this reader is out of scope, and only Anthony can say which. Also recorded because the finding that prompted it (reflow2 absent from an answer to its own question) is the kind of thing that vanishes from a conversation and cannot be rediscovered.

properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-14 BY ANTHONY: **OPTION (c) — INIT ASKS.** Alex's literal request, taken over the recommendation recorded on this node, which was (b) *"apply the instruction-pointer policy to MCP configs"*. He chose with (b)'s argument and (c)'s stated costs both in front of him.

⭐ THE STRONGEST CASE FOR HIS CHOICE, which the pre-decision text under-weighted: **(b) GUESSES, AND A WRONG GUESS IS SILENT.** Detection reads a fresh repo that has no signal, falls back to the primary harness, and hands an OpenCode user a `.mcp.json` their tool never opens — with nothing to tell them anything is missing. Asking is the only option on the list that cannot be silently wrong, and a silent wrong install is the exact failure class this project keeps finding (`cap:degraded-surface`'s diagnosis not reaching a by-name caller; the loop nudge registered against a script that is not there; the pointer written into a file the harness never reads). **A question costs one prompt; a silent miss costs a user who concludes reflow2 does not work.**

⚠️ WHAT IT COSTS, RECORDED SO NOBODY IS SURPRISED LATER: the one-liner install becomes a conversation, which is in tension with `user-iterative-release-preference` (*one-liner install, one word to update*). So the non-interactive path is not optional garnish — it is part of the requirement: a flag must carry the answer, and a non-tty must never hang. CI, scripted installs and `adopt` runs are the common path, not the exception.

📌 WHAT (c) DOES NOT SETTLE: the instruction-pointer policy stays as it is (already narrow and correct), and the loop-nudge asymmetry is a separate open question (`dec:idea-the-loop-nudge-exists-for-one-harness-only`) where the problem runs the other way — too little, not too much. Option (d), labelling the generated files, was not chosen but composes with (c) and remains available.

═══ THE ANALYSIS THIS WAS DECIDED FROM, kept because `req:roads-not-taken` says the roads not taken are part of the record ═══

RAISED AS BRAINSTORMING by Alex (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-14.

HIS WORDS: *"`reflow2 init .` for a project should be more like a CLI wizard that asks you what agent harness you are utilizing (Claude, Grok, ChatGPT, open code, etc.) and only installs the necessary file changes based on your choice. It needs the correct mcp setup, the graph artifact that can be git committed and the agents.md reference."*

✅ HIS THREE NAMED ESSENTIALS ARE ALL ALREADY PRODUCED on HEAD (`cbb1a19`): the MCP setup, the committed export at `docs/design/<project>.json` (since PR #172), and the `AGENTS.md` reference. **Nothing he needs is missing — the complaint is that things nobody asked for arrive alongside them.**

⭐⭐ THE FINDING THAT REFRAMED THE QUESTION: `tools/reflow2_init.py` ALREADY IMPLEMENTS ALEX'S PRINCIPLE — for instruction files — AND THE OPPOSITE ONE FOR MCP CONFIGS, ABOUT 150 LINES APART. Both deliberate, each carrying its reasoning in a comment, and they contradict each other.

  · INSTRUCTION POINTERS (`pointer_targets`, `CREATE_IF_NO_INSTRUCTION_FILE`) — appends only to instruction files the project ALREADY OWNS; when it owns none, creates just `CLAUDE.md`. The comment rejects the alternative in as many words: *"writing GEMINI.md, .cursorrules and the rest into a repo that asked for none of them is **spam**, and the sidecar we create (AGENTS.md) already IS the agents.md convention that the others increasingly follow."*
  · MCP CONFIGS (`MCP_CONFIGS`) — writes `.mcp.json`, `opencode.json` AND `.vscode/mcp.json` unconditionally: *"One generator, several files — a project opened in a different tool should just work."*

⇒ So the question was never "should init ask?" but "which of init's two existing policies is right?" — and (c) settles it toward the narrow one, by asking rather than by inferring.

THE OPTIONS AS THEY STOOD.
(a) LEAVE IT — extras are inert. Counter: init's own code calls that spam one screen away, and a first-time user read it as clutter.
(b) APPLY THE POINTER POLICY TO MCP CONFIGS — detect, falling back to the primary harness. No prompt, internally consistent. **Counter that decided it: detection has no signal on a fresh repo, which is exactly when init runs, so it guesses — and guesses silently.**
(c) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — ASK, with `--harness=…` for non-interactive use.
(d) INSTALL ALL, BUT LABEL each file with which tool reads it and that deleting it is safe. Not chosen; composes with (c).
(e) ASK ONLY WHEN AMBIGUOUS — detect, prompt when detection is empty. Not chosen; two code paths, and behaviour that differs between a fresh and an established repo.

📌 SCOPE, because it makes the change smaller than it sounds: most of what `init` writes is HARNESS-NEUTRAL and untouched — `AGENTS.md`/`REFLOW2.md`, the committed export, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`. The harness-specific surface is the three MCP configs, the instruction pointer (already policy-correct), and the loop-nudge hook.

⚠️ VERSION CAVEAT: two of Alex's five notes describe defects already fixed, so he is probably on an older kit (`fact:second-user-notes-2026-08-14-two-items-already-fixed`). Measurements here are against HEAD; an older `init` may have written a different set of files than what he saw.
properties.name: DECIDED — `init` ASKS which harness you use and installs only that one's files (option c), settling init's two contradictory install policies in favour of the narrow one
properties.rationale: Raised under the brainstorm skill and settled the same day on Anthony's word. Two things are deliberately on the record rather than smoothed away: that the choice went AGAINST the option this node recommended, and the reason his choice is nonetheless the stronger one — detection guesses, and a wrong guess about which harness will open a repo produces a silent failure, which is the failure class this project has now hit four separate times. The pre-decision text is kept in full beneath the outcome because `req:roads-not-taken` makes the rejected options part of the record, and because the instruction-pointer contradiction it documents is a real finding about `reflow2_init.py` that survives whichever option was taken.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Surfaced 2026-08-05 by Anthony's multi-project question.

⚠️ CORRECTED WITHIN THE HOUR, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE USEFUL PART. This node first claimed "everything reflow2 has built for crossing a design boundary shares CONTRACTS... NOTHING CARRIES A DECISION OR A REQUIREMENT ACROSS." THAT IS WRONG ABOUT REQUIREMENTS, and it was wrong for the ordinary reason — the claim was made from the capability's one-line description rather than from the code. Reading `export_surface` shows a second, deliberate half: `published_promises()`, behind `req:publishable-promise` (ACCEPTED).
