properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, per Anthony's own standing rule that a genuinely new thing becomes a proposal one day accepted rather than a requirement written on his behalf. Nothing here is intent.

HIS WORDS, 2026-08-11: "we need to make the search the graph first a requirement that is automatic. something like anytime a user has an idea, requirement, feedback, etc - first go search the graph to see what's already there (this should prevent near duplicate nodes in the graph appearing)."

⭐⭐ THE RULE ALREADY EXISTS, IN FIVE SERVED SKILLS. Measured 2026-08-11: `capture-intent`, `revise-design`, `brainstorm`, `kpp-proposal` and `retire-from-design` all instruct it, and capture-intent's wording is almost exactly his: "Search before you add. For each candidate, `search_design` with its key words first — the design may already say this. A hit that covers the same need means you update or link the existing node, NOT create a near-duplicate that HEAL will later flag and someone must merge. No hits is also information."

So the ask is not for the rule. IT IS FOR THE TRIGGER. And the trigger is the thing this project has now confirmed three times is missing: `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` (ACCEPTED) says skill use "must be triggered by the SITUATION, not remembered — and THE USER MUST NEVER BE THE TRIGGER", measured on this repo 2026-07-31, and confirmed from the field on 2026-08-11 by the second user, who named exactly the two skills he types and neither of the two that would have fired on situations he was already in.

⭐⭐ AND THE MECHANISM IS ALREADY A REQUIREMENT, PROPOSED AND UNBUILT: `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` — "a discipline that applies mid-task is delivered at the TOOL that triggers it, not from a catalogue read once at handshake." That is precisely what he is asking for, one layer more general. This idea may not need a requirement of its own at all; it may be the first concrete instance of one that already exists and has never been accepted.

📌 THIS NODE IS ITSELF THE NINTH COLLISION recorded in fact:the-owner-uses-reflow2-as-a-funnel-for-random-order-input, and it was found BY DOING THE THING HE ASKED FOR: searching before adding. Had the search not run, this would have become a near-duplicate of a proposed requirement and a fifth restatement of an instruction already in five skills — which is the exact failure he is trying to prevent, reproduced in the act of trying to prevent it.

WHAT EXISTS ON THE DETECTION SIDE, so this is not built twice. `possible_duplicate` fires on shared allocation sets with Jaccard ≥ 0.8 and asks rather than merges (`dec:ask-not-repair`); HEAL merges only on a human-asserted DUPLICATES edge. Both are AFTER-THE-FACT and STRUCTURAL — they catch two nodes that ended up allocated the same way. Neither can see "the same idea in different words, newly written, allocated to nothing yet", which is the case he is describing. Prevention and detection are different problems here.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) Put it on the TOOL, not the skill: `add_requirement` / `add_capability` / `add_decision` return near-matches alongside the write, or refuse-and-name when a match is close enough. Reaches every session including ones that load no skill. Cost — a write tool that sometimes refuses is a new failure mode on the hottest path, and BM25 near-matches are not reliable enough to refuse on (`dec:` on BM25 scores not being comparable across queries).
(b) SEARCH ON THE WAY IN, NEVER REFUSE: the write succeeds and the response carries "3 existing nodes look close: ...". No new failure mode, no judgement, and it puts the finding where the agent is already looking. Smallest honest version.
(c) A pre-write hook or a served instruction at handshake. Cheapest to state and it is what already exists — five skills say it — so this is the option that has already been tried and is the reason he is asking.
(d) Nothing new: ACCEPT `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` and build it, since this is an instance of it rather than a separate need.

⚠️ THE TRAP: a near-match list that is usually wrong trains the agent to ignore it, which is worse than silence — the same failure `unexpected_coupling` was retired for, and the one `v0.2.0-what-we-dont-know.md` names as the sharpest thing to watch ("a gap list you skim is worse than no gap list"). Whatever surfaces matches must be precise enough to be read every time, and BM25 alone has already been shown here to score the same topic 4.48 and 35.75 across two queries.

⚠️ SECOND TRAP, AND IT CUTS AGAINST THE WHOLE IDEA: a near-duplicate is sometimes CORRECT. `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` exists precisely because a body of intent that contradicts itself is still a design. Suppressing a second statement of the same idea can erase that the user said it twice, in different words, at different times — which is signal about what they keep coming back to, and is what `dec:idea-what-gets-searched-repeatedly-is-becoming-important` asks about from the other direction.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SHARPENED 2026-08-12 — THE WRITE HALF SHIPPED; THE READ HALF IS WHERE IT EARNED ITS KEEP
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

⭐ THIS SECTION WAS ADDED BY THE GUARD ITSELF. An agent tried to create a NEW node about exactly this and `add_decision` REFUSED it, naming this node and both routes on. The write half works, in the field, against its own author. That is the strongest evidence this node will ever get, and it arrived by accident.

ANTHONY NAMED THE BEHAVIOUR AS SOMETHING HE VALUES, 2026-08-12: "every time I ask a question or propose an idea, you do a search/research what has already happened. then we either sharpen the previous or add new content or all sorts of things that continually improves the design - i think this is awesome!"

⭐ MEASURED IN ONE SESSION — six saves, each with what it prevented:
  - "a requirement that anything developed has something that uses it" -> already captured 2026-08-09 IN HIS OWN WORDS. A duplicate node.
  - "accept the 26 delivered requirements" -> ELEVEN were satisfied only by `planned`/`in_progress` capabilities. Asserting delivery that had not happened, eleven times.
  - "should we have a purge skill" -> `dec:proposed-requirements-pruned` had already settled DROPPED-NOT-DELETED. Re-deciding a settled question destructively.
  - "a tool that does the import step" -> `import_graph` already took a `path`. Building a tool that existed.
  - "treat the union of 2+ graphs as one graph" -> `dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs`, his own federation model from six days earlier. Re-deriving his own thinking.
  - "treat one side as immutable" -> `mirror_surface`, BUILT and stamping `mirror_of` / `mirror_content_hash` / `mirrored_at`. Specifying something already shipped.
  Plus a doc review that caught a section marked OUTSTANDING three days after the thing shipped.

🛑 AND THE ASYMMETRY THAT MATTERS: **ALL SIX HAPPENED ON THE READ PATH, WHERE NOTHING ENFORCES ANYTHING.** The refusal fires on add_requirement / add_capability / add_component / add_decision / add_constraint. It cannot fire when a user asks a question and an agent answers in prose. Those six happened because the agent chose to look.

That is `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`'s failure with the trigger moved one step — not the user reminding the agent, but the agent remembering — and it degrades silently in a long session precisely when the graph is large enough to make searching most valuable.

⭐⭐ THE OBSERVATION THAT CHANGES THE VALUE CALCULATION: the write guard catches a near-duplicate NODE. It cannot catch a near-duplicate DECISION TO BUILD. **Four of the six saves prevented WORK, not nodes** — and work is the more expensive thing. So the unguarded half is plausibly worth more than the guarded half, which inverts the obvious reading that the write path is where the value is.

⚠️ SURVIVORSHIP BIAS, NAMED SO SIX IS NOT READ AS A RATE. Only the times it worked are visible; NOTHING RECORDS A SEARCH THAT DID NOT HAPPEN. `dec:loop-status-cannot-say-it-never-looked` is the same shape already on the record — "clean" and "never scanned" are one answer.

OPTIONS FOR THE READ HALF, none taken:
  A — A READ-SIDE HINT on orientation reads. Rides the existing `loop_hint` carrier. EXPENSIVE: it needs to know what the user asked, which the tool layer never sees — so the agent must volunteer the query, which is the same trigger problem one layer down.
  B — MAKE THE ABSENCE COMPUTABLE. Do not fire at the right moment; record whether a search preceded a capture and report captures with none — `dec:loop-status-state-not-history` applied here. EXPENSIVE, and the asymmetry is already recorded above: a node created without a prior search is not distinguishable from one created after a search that found nothing.
  C — INSTRUMENT ONLY, so the habit's decay is visible. Cheapest; answers nothing.
  D — DO NOTHING; the write path guards where duplicates actually enter. Weakened by the four-of-six finding above.
properties.name: OPEN — how does "search the graph before you add" become AUTOMATIC, when it is already written into five skills and still depends on somebody loading one?
properties.rationale:
The rule Anthony asked for is already written into five served skills, and the delivery mechanism he described is already a proposed requirement. What is missing is not the instruction but the trigger — the same gap confirmed three times this week. Recording it as an instance rather than a new need, and noting that the search which found this is the very discipline in question.

SHARPENED 2026-08-12, and by the guard itself: an agent tried to open a new node on this and add_decision refused it, naming this one. Six measured saves in a single session, all on the READ path where nothing enforces the discipline — and four of them prevented WORK rather than nodes, which is the more expensive thing and inverts the assumption that the write path is where the value lies.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled.

THE OBSERVATION: cut_structure (used today) reports articulation POINTS — single nodes whose removal splits the network. That answers "what is a single point of failure". It does not answer "how separable are these two subsystems", which is a different and equally architectural question.

THE IDEA: dynograph_graph::max_flow_min_cut (Edmonds-Karp, exact, unused) returns the minimum-capacity set of EDGES whose removal disconnects a source from a target. Read on a design graph: "which contracts would you have to sever to split A from B, and how many?" Edge weights are already coupling weights, so the capacity has a meaning here rather than being invented.

WHERE IT LANDS: dec:mosa-conformance is OPEN and its own text says reflow2 "already computes most of the criteria" for modular open systems conformance. Severability is one of the ones it does not. req:modularity-computed is the standing requirement that severability be computed rather than asserted.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS: min-cut needs a SOURCE and a TARGET, and nothing in the design says which two subsystems a user wants separated — so either the user picks the pair (a new question to ask) or reflow2 runs it over community pairs from leiden (defensible, but O(pairs) and the communities are themselves computed rather than declared). Also, low cut capacity is not automatically good: two subsystems SHOULD be coupled where the design says they should be, and a detector that rewards separation everywhere would push toward a design nobody wants — the same over-selectivity trap is_single_point_of_failure already had to be tuned out of.
properties.name: OPEN — should severability be computed as a minimum EDGE CUT, not just as articulation points?
properties.rationale: Chosen from the unused set because it maps onto an OPEN decision rather than onto a hypothetical: dec:mosa-conformance already claims most criteria are computable, and this names one that is not.

properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Raised 2026-08-27 from a live cost, not from thinking about the model: `fact:a-findings-name-can-claim-more-than-its-data-and-the-name-is-what-search-returns`.

═══ THE QUESTION ═══

A measured fact's NAME said the seam number *"can never reach zero"* because two edge sets were *"disjoint by construction"*. The measurement was sound; the claim was a state described as a law, and it moved in an afternoon. `search_design` returns the NAME, so that is the sentence a session meets.

Should anything require a finding to say what it does NOT establish — and if so, where?

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══

**(a) NOTHING. This is writing discipline, not vocabulary.** The convention already exists and is widely followed — the exemplar itself carries a "WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE" paragraph. One instance of a badly-worded name is a reason to write better names, not to grow the schema. ⚠️ Counter: the discipline was followed and still failed, because it bounded the body while the overreach was in the name, and the name is what search returns. A convention that does not reach the field readers see is not doing the job.

**(b) A NAMING RULE, enforced by a lint.** Forbid law-shaped language — *by construction*, *can never*, *always*, *impossible* — in a TemporalFact name unless the body justifies it. ⚠️ Counter: word-blocklists are crude and generate false positives on findings where the strong claim is TRUE and earned. And a lint that fires on correct work is the alarm-on-correct-work failure this project keeps finding.

**(c) A DECLARED BOUNDS FIELD on TemporalFact** — a `does_not_establish` sibling to `statement`, returned by `search_design` alongside the name. ⚠️ Counter: `basis` and `valid_from`/`valid_to` already exist and are the schema's answer to "how strong is this claim, and when"; a fourth qualifier may be one too many. And a declared field that is usually empty teaches readers to ignore it, which is worse than prose that is usually present.

**(d) CHANGE WHAT SEARCH RETURNS** rather than what facts carry — return the closing paragraph, or the first line of `statement`, beside the name. ⚠️ Counter: it grows every search result on a design with 300+ facts, and `search_design` is already a bounded reply; this trades the cheapest read in the loop for a problem measured once.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT MUST BE MEASURED BEFORE ANY OF IT ═══

**Nobody has counted the prevalence.** n=1. Before growing a schema or writing a lint, somebody should sweep this design's TemporalFacts and ask how many names carry a claim their body does not support. If the answer is one, option (a) is obviously right and everything else is over-engineering. **That sweep has not been done, and doing it is cheaper than every option here.**

📌 SEPARATE FROM, AND ADJACENT TO, `fact:the-upstream-watch-is-findable-only-in-reflow2s-own-words`. Both are cases where the record is ACCURATE and still misleads a reader — one through a name that overreaches, one through a description written in vocabulary its users do not share. Whether they are one problem about the gap between what a record says and what a reader takes from it, or two unrelated ones, is itself unsettled.
properties.name: OPEN — should a finding have to bound its own claim, and is the NAME the field that needs it?
properties.rationale:
Raised because the cost was real and traceable: the overreaching name was cited twice as grounds for NOT doing work — once to the user, once into a ChangeEvent — before a five-minute measurement overturned it. A finding that argues against measuring is the most expensive kind to get wrong.

Left as brainstorming because the honest first move is a count, not a design. Option (a) — do nothing, write better names — is a real option and is listed first among the counters for that reason: at n=1 the schema should not move.

Recorded with all four options rather than the one that looks best, because the two strongest counters point in opposite directions: the convention already exists and failed anyway, which argues for a mechanism; and the prevalence is unmeasured, which argues against building one.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — 2026-08-11, from Anthony's observation that the governance work came from a real demand signal ("it was all taken from feedback from the storyflow project... I told reflow2 to consider it and do it"). Nothing here is intent.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, and it is the reason the question exists. reflow2's own governance requirements DID come from a demand signal: `/home/ajs7/project/dev_storyflow/reflow2_feedback.md`, the GOVERNANCE-AS-DESIGN entry by api-boss, 2026-08-08. Six Requirements carry AUTHORED_BY to `who:storyflow-api-boss`, so the authorship survived. But:

  · searched every node in the design for the string `reflow2_feedback` → 12 hits, NONE of them any of the six governance requirements
  · the document is not registered as an Artifact
  · so the origin of this work exists only in Anthony's head, and he had to tell an agent where to look

⭐ THE SELF-INDICTMENT: `req:no-idea-goes-quiet` is ACCEPTED and reads "an idea in the graph stays connected to whether it was built and to where it was written — THE USER NEVER HUNTS FOR THE SOURCE DOCUMENT AGAIN." reflow2's own governance capture violates an accepted reflow2 requirement, and no detector could see it.

⭐ AND IT COST SOMETHING MEASURABLE, twice. The feedback entry ranked THREE asks. Only #1 reached the graph:
  #1  model VERIFIES onto DesignRule so enforced+no-check is detectable   → BUILT (unverified_enforced_rule)
  #2  a Role/Seat node distinct from Contributor — duties attach to the
      SEAT, not the human                                                 → ABSENT, no such node type
  #3  an `obligation` category on DesignRule: "MUST do X AT MOMENT Y"     → ABSENT; categories in use
                                                                             are convention/methodology/None
#3 carried the sharpest sentence in the entry — "our doc map recorded WHO reads a file and WHAT it holds, and never WHEN — the missing axis was TIME, and no rule was being broken because no rule named a moment." That finding is nowhere in this design. The entry did say #1 was "the whole idea's leverage and the rest is optional", so building #1 first was RIGHT — but #2 and #3 were not DEFERRED, they evaporated, which is a different thing and the one nobody can see.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) A gap for a Requirement with no incoming DOCUMENTS/Fragment/origin edge — "what asked for this?"
(b) No new detector; instead make the capture skills register the source document as an Artifact by default, so the edge exists by construction rather than by discipline.
(c) Do nothing structural, and treat the origin as prose in the requirement's own statement.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO (a), and it is the same trap that made `rule:a-design-is-named-by-an-id-not-a-path` advisory: at genesis NOBODY has a source document — intent arrives by someone talking. A detector demanding an origin edge would fire against the entire design on day one and the only way to green it would be to fabricate origins. That argues (b) is the honest shape and (a) is only safe if it fires on requirements whose provenance says they came from a DOCUMENT.

NOTE ON WHY THE DAU FRAME FITS: of the nine DAU requirement characteristics Anthony cited, TRACEABLE is defined as connecting "directly back to top-level strategic guidance and forward to system design specs." reflow2 checks FORWARD (the golden thread; unmotivated_capability fired on exactly this) and has no check at all for BACKWARD. COMPLETE failed too — 2 of 3 ranked asks are absent in any form.
properties.name: OPEN — should a Requirement with no recorded ORIGIN be a gap? The golden thread checks forward and nothing checks backward
properties.rationale: The demand signal existed and became requirements — the process was run. What broke was traceability backward to the source and completeness across the source's three asks. Both are invisible to every detector reflow2 has, and an accepted requirement already says they should not be.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-25, across three messages: *"can an idea be linked with a requirement? should an idea be linked with a requirement or should they be kept separate? for instance, I think we have a requirement that reflow2 isn't for reflow2... I feel like attaching this to every idea scopes the idea properly. secondly, I may propose an idea that is directly contradictory to an existing requirement."* Then: *"could also extend to linking proposed, but unaccepted ideas to accepted ideas... I suppose this gets into the difference between what is difference between ideas (both proposed, but unaccepted and accepted ideas) and requirements?"*

DISTINCT FROM the two nodes the duplicate guard surfaced, and the line is clean: `dec:idea-do-ideas-form-a-graph-or-only-a-list` and `dec:idea-what-notices-an-idea-that-connects-to-nothing` are both about idea→IDEA linking and who notices its absence. This is about idea→INTENT — the edge from a musing to the requirement or rule that bounds it — and it turns out to have a different and verifiable answer.

═══ ⭐⭐ THE ASYMMETRY, READ OUT OF THE CODE AND NOT INFERRED ═══

`report.rs` builds its `accepted` set from `scan_nodes(node::DECISION)` alone, then scores `if accepted.contains(other) { contradicts += 1 }` at +2. So:

  idea CONTRADICTS an accepted DECISION     → +2, surfaces in what_next's ranked band ✅
  idea CONTRADICTS a REQUIREMENT            → edge stores, score 0, NOTHING READS IT ❌

**The more serious contradiction is the unread one.** An accepted Decision records a choice; a Requirement records intent — what must be true. An idea that contradicts intent is either the intent being wrong or the idea being out of scope, and both are worth surfacing more than a clash between two choices. The design scores the lesser case and is silent on the greater.

⚠️ It is not obviously a defect. `CONTRADICTS` between Decisions means "the design is inconsistent until settled", which is a claim about two settlements. Whether an idea-versus-intent clash is the SAME relation or a different one (proposal out of scope, vs. design self-contradiction) is exactly what is unsettled here.

═══ THE THREE KINDS, since the third message asks it directly ═══

  proposed Decision   a question someone is facing, or a musing. NOT intent. Raises no gap.
  accepted Decision   a settled choice — a HOW and a WHY. Governs other nodes. Read by what_next.
  Requirement         a WHAT MUST BE TRUE. Intent, with its own lifecycle: status, provenance,
                      priority, lineage, and an approver on settlement.

The distinction that matters for this question: **a Decision is answerable, a Requirement is satisfiable.** Contradicting a Decision opens a question; contradicting a Requirement puts something out of bounds. Same edge type today for both.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**A. EVERY IDEA LINKS TO ITS SCOPING RULE.** Anthony's proposal as first stated.
 ⚠️ The brainstorm skill's own rule turned on it: *"Two or three edges is a good outcome. Ten is a smell. Relatedness is not similarity. If everything links to everything, the neighbourhood stops carrying information."* An edge true of EVERY idea is a constant; a neighbourhood query on it returns the whole corpus.

**B. LINK ONLY THE EXCEPTIONS — `VIOLATES` / `CONTRADICTS`.** The information is in the rare edge.
 ⭐ Needs no new vocabulary, and answers the contradiction half with the same mechanism.
 ⚠️ Does nothing for the SCOPING intent: an idea that complies carries no marker, so "was this idea ever tested against the rule?" stays unanswerable — the silence `no_relation_note` exists to break one level up.

**C. `GOVERNED_BY`, NOT AN INFERENCE RELATION.** The structural edge already MEANS scoping, already carries a `note`, already has `ruling: parks`.
 ⭐ `REVIEW_RELATIONS` deliberately excludes `CONTAINS`/`SATISFIES` as "structure, not commentary"; scoping is structure, so it belongs on this side of that line.
 ⚠️ Same constant-edge objection as A if applied to every idea.

**D. A CHECK AT CAPTURE, NOT AN EDGE.** The brainstorm skill asks *"whose project does this serve?"* and the answer goes in the idea's text.
 ⭐ Matches how the rule is actually enforced today — by a person — and matches `req:detecting-is-not-asking`.
 ⚠️ Prose is not queryable, so "which ideas were never scoped?" cannot be computed and nothing notices the skip. That is the failure mode measured three times this month.

**E. FIX THE READER, LEAVE THE VOCABULARY.** Do nothing about scoping edges; widen `what_next` so a Decision contradicting a REQUIREMENT scores.
 ⭐ Cheapest thing that could not be wrong, and it is the half that is provably broken rather than the half that is merely undecided.

📌 `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself` is a **DesignRule**, not a Requirement — worth stating because Anthony recalled it as a requirement, and because DesignRules already have `GOVERNED_BY` while Requirements are reached by `SATISFIES`, which is structure a musing has no business drawing.
properties.name: OPEN — should an idea link to the Requirement/DesignRule that scopes it? An idea contradicting an accepted DECISION is scored; one contradicting a REQUIREMENT is silent
properties.rationale:
Recorded under the brainstorm skill as an idea, not intent, and linked on creation.

Kept as ONE node across three messages because they converge on a single choice — whether the edge from a musing to the intent that bounds it should exist, and in which direction it carries information. The third message's question (what separates a proposed idea, an accepted idea and a requirement) is the reason the other two are hard, so it belongs here rather than in a node of its own.

The asymmetry in the scoring was read out of `report.rs` rather than assumed, because the whole question turns on whether these edges have a reader, and an unverified claim about that would have made every option below unjudgeable.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — found 2026-08-11 while answering Anthony's question about work built without a requirement. Nothing here is intent.

THE ASYMMETRY, read from the code rather than assumed. `detect_status_contradictions` (detect.rs:2146) fires in exactly two places, and both are OVERSTATEMENTS:
  · a Capability at `verified` with no passing check          → 0.70
  · a Requirement at `met` with nothing satisfying it         → 0.70
Nothing anywhere looks at the opposite direction.

THE INSTANCE THAT SURFACED IT: `cap:governance-proposal` sits at `planned` while `art:governance-proposal-skill` REALIZES it, it is allocated to `cmp:skills`, and that component's check passes. The skill is being SERVED to sessions right now. The status claims less than the structure shows, and no detector has an opinion.

⭐ THIS IS A NAMED-AND-UNBUILT CASE, NOT AN OVERSIGHT I INVENTED. The test at detect.rs:1401-1407 records the same limit from the Release side and assigns it: "a status that claims less than the structure shows is `status_contradiction`'s territory, not this one's." It was allocated to that detector and never written there.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) Add the mirror rule to status_contradiction: a Capability at `planned`/`unrealized` with an incoming REALIZES, or with a passing check, is understating.
(b) Lower severity than 0.70. Overstating is a claim with nothing behind it; understating is a record that has fallen behind reality — arguably drift, not a contradiction, and drift already has its own machinery.
(c) Do nothing, on the grounds that understating harms nobody.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO (c), which is why this is worth asking at all: understating is what makes `graph_report`'s delivery count too LOW, and a design that under-reports its own completion is the one nobody trusts the numbers on. It is also the direction that silently accumulates, because nothing complains.

⚠️ SIZING CAVEAT before anyone treats (a) as small: `Release.status` and `Capability.status` both DEFAULT to `planned` (detect.rs:1401-1403 states this for Release). So "planned + realized" would fire on every capability whose status nobody ever set, which on a young design may be most of them. Whether that is signal or a flood is unmeasured, and measuring it is the first step, not the fix.
properties.name: OPEN — should a status that claims LESS than the structure shows be a gap, the way an overstated one already is?
properties.rationale: status_contradiction is one-directional and its own test file assigns the other direction to it. The instance that exposed it is shipped, served code recorded as `planned`. The open part is whether the mirror rule floods, because `planned` is a schema default nobody chose.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-12, second half of his CAP question. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen.

DISTINCT FROM `dec:idea-is-reflow2-itself-a-cp-store-behind-an-ap-record`, deliberately kept apart: that one asks whether CAP describes reflow2's OWN architecture. This one asks whether CAP is vocabulary reflow2 should HAND ITS USERS. One node holding both could only ever be half-answered.

SIBLING, NOT DUPLICATE, OF `dec:idea-the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph` (proposed, 2026-08-08). That node asks about the DIRECTION of inference — should the quality attribute drive allocation rather than be read off it. This asks whether a SPECIFIC well-known trade-off frame belongs in the vocabulary at all. Related, and the answers could differ: the ility→graph direction could be built without CAP ever appearing, and CAP could be added without changing allocation.

⭐ THE CONCRETE GAP, checked rather than asserted. `schema/dimensions.yaml` already carries NINE axes attachable to any node: reliability, performance, maintainability, security, scalability, observability, testability, coupling, maturity. **Consistency is not among them. Availability is not among them. Partition tolerance is not among them.** For a tool whose owner's stated operating context includes federated, independently-evolving systems, that is a real absence rather than a stylistic one.

AND ONE PIECE ALREADY EXISTS UNDER A DIFFERENT NAME: `cap:seam-incompatibility` — "say when two linked designs disagree at a boundary" — is, structurally, a consistency check across a partition between two independently-evolving replicas. The federation work (`cap:mirror-surface`, `cap:composed-analysis`, `cap:complementary-pairing`) is a distributed-design problem that has never been described in distributed-systems terms.

═══ THE OPTIONS ═══

A — NOTHING. CAP is domain knowledge the AGENT brings to a conversation, not vocabulary the graph must hold. An agent can already reason about it and record the resulting decision as an ordinary Decision node, today, with no change whatsoever. CHEAPEST, and the null hypothesis this has to beat.

B — ADD `consistency` AND `availability` TO THE DIMENSION ENUM. Cheap, additive, existing graphs unaffected. `ility_report` already reports NOT INFORMED with a reason for axes it cannot compute — so honest silence is the built-in default and nothing pretends. NOTE: a new enum value moves NO stamp count, which would be the fifth recorded instance of the stamp being blind to a real compatibility event.

C — ASK IT UPFRONT, at genesis or adopt: "is this system CP or AP under partition, and L or C in normal operation?" This is exactly the shape `dec:idea-the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph` argues for in Anthony's own words — "if you don't ask upfront, these cost a lot in having to rework services after they've been already developed." A CAP posture chosen late is a rewrite; chosen early it is a constraint everything else obeys.

D — A CONTRADICTION DETECTOR, and the only option where anything COMPUTES. A design asserting strict consistency AND high availability across a declared partition boundary is claiming something the theorem forbids. reflow2 already has the machinery: `CONTRADICTS`, `cap:kpp` for inviolable intent, `constrains`, and `cap:key-interfaces` for computing whether a change crosses a published boundary. This is a KPP breach with a known proof.

═══ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea ═══

⚠️ 1. THE STRONGEST ONE — reflow2 IS DOMAIN-NEUTRAL AND CAP IS NOT. Its stated operating breadth is greenfield and brownfield and continual, across several organisations; the owner's own context is Space Force systems engineering and a Brookhaven beamline stack. CAP is meaningless for a beamline's mechanical design or a spacecraft thermal budget. Building a distributed-systems theorem into the core vocabulary privileges software architecture over every other domain the tool claims to serve.

⚠️ 2. "PICK TWO OF THREE" IS ITSELF A MISLEADING FRAME, and shipping it would propagate the misreading. CAP forces a choice ONLY DURING a partition; in normal operation a system need not sacrifice either. That is precisely why PACELC exists. A tool that offers CAP as a first-class axis would be handing users the version practitioners most often get wrong.

⚠️ 3. VOCABULARY NOBODY USES IS THE SHAPE THIS PROJECT SPENT A MONTH REMOVING. Requirement's five-state lifecycle runs 3-of-5 unused; BL-198 was the removal work. Nine dimensions already exist and the ility report cannot inform four of them. Two more unused axes make the enum longer and the design no truer.

⚠️ 4. A PLANNED CAPABILITY COSTS THREE GAPS FOREVER (`dec:exploratory-staging`, measured: 34 of 73 open gaps came from routing wishes to Capability). Option D as a planned capability is a standing tax until someone builds it.

📌 WHERE THE IDEA IS STRONGEST, narrower than "add CAP": not as a general axis, but where reflow2 ALREADY has the substrate — the federation seam. `cap:seam-incompatibility` computes disagreement between two independently-evolving designs, which is a consistency question with a real detector behind it. If any of this earns its place, that is the door, and it needs no enum change at all.
properties.name: PARKED, NOT ACCEPTED — should consistency/availability/partition-tolerance be vocabulary reflow2 offers? The federation seam is the road if any is ever taken. Anthony, 2026-08-12: revisit later, more important things first.
properties.rationale:
PARKED ON ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-08-12: "we can add cap:seam-incompatibility as proposed, but leave it as not accepted. one day we can come back to this — it doesn't sound like it has huge applicability, so I think there are more important things to deal with in the interim."

WHAT THAT SETTLES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It settles the ROAD: if consistency vocabulary is ever taken up, it enters through `cap:seam-incompatibility` — the federation seam, where reflow2 already computes when two independently-evolving designs disagree at a boundary — and NOT as new `dimension` enum values (option B) or a general axis. It does NOT accept the idea, schedule it, or claim it will happen. Status stays `proposed`.

🛑 DELIBERATELY NOT MINTED AS A PLANNED CAPABILITY, and this is the one judgement made on his behalf rather than by his word. He said "add cap:seam-incompatibility as proposed" — but `cap:seam-incompatibility` ALREADY EXISTS and is `realized` (it is the built detector this idea would extend), and Capability has no `proposed` status: its lifecycle is planned / in_progress / realized / verified. Creating a NEW planned Capability to hold the idea would cost THREE GAPS FOREVER — unmotivated, unrealized, unverified — which is `dec:exploratory-staging`'s measured finding (34 of 73 open gaps came from exactly that routing). Parking something explicitly because there are MORE IMPORTANT THINGS TO DEAL WITH, and paying a standing three-gap nag for it, would defeat his own stated reason. A proposed Decision is SILENT by construction — `detect_gaps` fires `undecided_decision_point` only on two or more REGISTERED alternatives — so the idea is kept, findable by search, and costs nothing until someone registers real alternatives under it.

IF HE WANTS IT TRACKED AS WORK rather than kept as a thought, that is one `add_capability` call away and the three gaps are the honest price of scheduling it. The choice is his; the default taken here is the quiet one, matching what he asked for.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent.

ANTHONY, 2026-08-21: "as I state quite often, using reflow2 on reflow2 is our first proof of concept; however, reflow2 is a tool for other projects. that being said, should we introduce an /optimize skill (that would occur after black boxes have been identified) that any project could do on its modules?"

⭐ THE UNUSUAL THING ABOUT THIS IDEA IS THAT THE PROCEDURE WAS ALREADY RUN ONCE, BY HAND, AN HOUR BEFORE HE ASKED. That is not a coincidence to note in passing — it is the only evidence available about whether the skill would have content, and it is first-hand rather than imagined.

THE RUN, in the order it actually happened:
  1. MEASURED WHERE THE TIME WENT. 191.8 s across 127 test binaries. The worst thing was not the biggest file but the worst COST PER UNIT OF WORK — 2.44 s/test in one file against a 0.92 s median for a whole binary.
  2. FOUND THE CAUSE BY MEASURING, NOT GUESSING. open_in_memory 41.3 ms vs an add_capability write at 54.7 us: construction cost 750x a write. Cause: eleven include_str!'d YAML documents re-parsed on every construction.
  3. WROTE THE BUDGET DOWN BEFORE TOUCHING CODE. `con:graph-construction-is-setup-not-work`, 1 ms, derived rather than picked.
  4. OPTIMISED. Cached the parse.
  5. RE-MEASURED AGAINST THE BUDGET AND STOPPED. Suite 191.8 s -> 96.5 s.
  6. MADE THE MEASUREMENT DURABLE.
  7. PAID THE GUARDS THAT FIRED.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐ THE STEP THAT EARNED ITS PLACE: THE BUDGET MADE THE WORK STOP
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

First re-measurement after the fix read 2.79 ms — a 14.8x speedup AND OVER BUDGET. Without a number written down beforehand, "14.8x faster" is exactly where optimisation stops and everyone feels good. The warm figure was 266 us, under budget, so the work stopped there — leaving the obvious next move (Arc instead of cloning the schema, which would recover 252 of those 266 us) UNDONE, because it needs a dependency's API in another repo. **The budget produced a defensible stopping point at a repo boundary.** That is the anti-over-engineering mechanism working, and it is the strongest argument that the skill has real content rather than being a checklist.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 TWO THINGS BIT DURING THE RUN, AND BOTH BELONG IN THE SKILL
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

(1) **A DURATION ASSERTION IN A PARALLEL SUITE MEASURES CONTENTION, NOT CODE.** The first durable test asserted "a warm construction takes under 5 ms". Alone: 266 us, comfortable. Inside `cargo test --workspace` with dozens of binaries competing: **6 ms, and the gate failed.** The usual response is to raise the threshold until it stops complaining, which RETIRES THE GATE WITHOUT ANYONE DECIDING TO. The fix was to assert a RATIO — cold construction versus warm — which survives contention because both halves are slowed equally, and which asserts the thing that actually broke: the parse happening once. ⇒ **AN OPTIMISATION GUARD SHOULD ASSERT THE STRUCTURE THAT MAKES THE CODE FAST, NOT THE TIME IT TAKES.** Time is a property of the machine as much as of the program.

(2) **THE OPTIMISATION TRIPPED A DESIGN RULE, AND PAYING IT WAS ONE PARAGRAPH.** Caching the parse in a `LazyLock` is a process-global, and `no_per_design_process_globals` refused it. That test's own words: *"the door closes one convenient static at a time, each individually reasonable."* Mine was one of those. The rule's question — would a second design open in this process need a different value? — had a clean answer (the YAML is compiled in; it is a fact about the BINARY), and the cost of the global was stating it. ⇒ **OPTIMISATION IS WHERE ARCHITECTURAL RULES GET QUIETLY TRADED AWAY FOR SPEED**, one reasonable exception at a time, and a skill that does not say so is missing the thing most worth saying.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 AND HIS PRECONDITION IS THE PART I WOULD PUSH BACK ON
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

He frames it as occurring AFTER black boxes have been identified. Measured earlier today, optimising one module needs THREE things and the contract is only one:
  (i)   a WALL, so a change inside cannot leak out       — 0 of 10 subsystems publish a contract
  (ii)  a TARGET, so you know when to stop                — 1 Constraint before today, and not a budget
  (iii) a MEASUREMENT, so you can tell if you improved it — no benches, no criterion, not one Instant::now()

**AND THE RUN ABOVE HAPPENED WITH (i) ABSENT.** No contract existed for the module optimised, and the work was still correct, bounded and successful — because (ii) and (iii) were supplied. You CANNOT optimise with a wall and no measurement; you can only change things and believe you improved them. So the skill does NOT need to wait for black boxes, and gating it on them would withhold the cheapest of the three returns until the most expensive one is finished. ⇒ **THE PRECONDITION IS A TARGET AND A MEASUREMENT, NOT A CONTRACT.** A contract makes optimisation SAFER (a change that leaks is caught); it does not make it possible.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE OPTIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

(a) A SERVED `optimize` SKILL, gated on a target and a measurement rather than on black boxes. Its content is the ORDER and the REFUSALS, not the technique: measure before guessing; write the budget BEFORE the code; re-measure against the budget rather than against the old number; assert structure not duration; and when a rule refuses your change, pay it in prose rather than weakening it. CHEAPEST, and it is the leg reflow2 is best at. HONEST LIMIT: **ONE RUN IS NOT A PROCEDURE.** Everything above came from a single optimisation, in Rust, on a test suite, on one machine. A skill generalised from n=1 is a story about one afternoon wearing the costume of a method.

(b) THE THIRD LEG FIRST — a detector. `Constraint` + `budget_report` is the TOOL leg and it exists; a skill would be the INSTRUCTION leg; nothing notices a project that has optimised without a budget, or a Constraint nobody ever measured against. Candidate finding: *a Constraint with no contribution recorded* — a budget stated and never checked, which is the shape a target takes when it decays into decoration.

(c) DO NOTHING YET, AND RUN IT AGAIN FIRST. Optimise a second thing — ideally in a different language, or on something that is not a test suite — and see which of the seven steps survive contact. The strongest argument for waiting is that the two lessons above were BOTH discovered by doing rather than by thinking, and a second run is the only way to find the third.

(d) FOLD IT INTO AN EXISTING SKILL rather than minting a twenty-first. `check-health` and `impact-check` already run after a change. Cheapest on surface area; loses the thing that makes the procedure work, which is that it is a SEQUENCE with a step that must come first.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
WHAT IS NOT KNOWN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Whether any of the seven steps is reflow2-specific. Step 1 needed cargo's per-binary timings parsed out of test output — a project with no such output would need something else entirely, and a skill cannot supply it. The GENERIC part may be only steps 3, 5 and 6 (state the budget, re-measure against it, make it durable), with steps 1, 2 and 4 being "do the obvious thing for your stack". If that is the whole content, it is a short skill — and possibly a better one for being short.
properties.name: OPEN — should `optimize` be a served skill? The procedure was run once by hand and two of its lessons were found by doing, not thinking

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex's idea, 2026-08-14 (Opportunities), in his words: "`propagate_change` summary: separate 'same Component dump' from 'crossed an Interface.' Default `full` off is right; the summary still needs a 'sibling Capabilities on the same Component, not actually impacted' band."

DISTINCT FROM `fact:defect-propagate-change-distance-two-is-not-an-edit-list`, which measures what happened (~65 named, 113 truncated, the Interface signal buried). This holds the unmade choice about the fix.

THE OPTIONS:

(a) BAND THE SUMMARY BY EDGE KIND — group the impacted set by HOW it was reached: through a shared Component, across a PROVIDES/CONSUMES Interface, along the Requirement/Decision thread. CHEAP, changes no traversal, and it makes the useful signal findable rather than smaller. COUNTER: it renames the problem if the bands are not ranked — a hundred nodes in three labelled groups is still a hundred nodes.

(b) A NAMED "NOT ACTUALLY IMPACTED" BAND, his exact phrasing — siblings on the same Component, reported as reached-but-probably-irrelevant. HONEST, and it keeps the count visible rather than filtering it away, which matters because this project's standing preference is to report rather than judge. COUNTER: "not actually impacted" is a JUDGEMENT, and the tool would be making it. A sibling Capability on a shared Component sometimes IS impacted, and a band that says otherwise will eventually be believed on the day it is wrong.

(c) WEIGHT THE TRAVERSAL rather than band the output — DEPENDS_ON already carries `weight` and `weight_basis`, and CONSUMES carries `weight` too. A radius that decayed through weak couplings would shrink honestly. COUNTER: almost nothing in a real design sets those weights, so the decay would be uniform and the answer unchanged — this is a fix that requires a habit nobody has.

(d) DO NOTHING TO THE TOOL; FIX THE INSTRUCTION. The served loop says "update ONLY what the blast radius names", which is what makes a wide answer a defect rather than information. Softening the instruction costs nothing. COUNTER: it concedes that the radius cannot be acted on, which is most of what the tool is for.

⚠️ AND A COUNTERWEIGHT FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION, measured on reflow2's own graph this session: `propagate_change` seeded from a TemporalFact returned ZERO impacted, because ABOUT_ENTITY is not traversed. ANY CHANGE HERE MUST NOT ASSUME THE TOOL'S PROBLEM IS ONLY THAT IT IS TOO WIDE. It is too wide from one seed type and silent from another, and a narrowing fix applied blind would make the silent case worse.

NOT ESTABLISHED: the ratio — he did not report his design's total node count, so whether 178 is most of it or a tenth of it is unknown, and that number decides whether this is a threshold problem or a shape problem.
properties.name: IDEA — the blast radius reports one kind of reach. Should the summary band "crossed a published Interface" apart from "sits on the same Component", and name the siblings that are not actually impacted?
properties.rationale:
⭐ SHARPENED 2026-08-16 with a measurement and a doctrine tension, both of which narrow the question.

MEASURED ON REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN: a real change event (`chg:artifact-intent-stops-being-injected`) returned 19 nodes at distance 1 and 1,068 impacted in total, and the FOUR `boundary_crossings` were the only part worth reading. So the ask is real at this scale, not hypothetical.

⇒ AND HALF OF IT IS ALREADY BUILT, which is worth stating plainly so nobody builds it twice: the summary already returns `boundary_crossings`, naming the crossed interfaces by id, alongside `risk_crossings`. 'Crossed an Interface' is ANSWERED today. What remains unbuilt is only the other side of the pairing — naming the siblings that are NOT impacted.

⚠️ AND THAT REMAINING HALF IS A NEGATIVE CLAIM, which is the actual open question rather than an implementation detail. A band labelled 'not actually impacted' asserts that sibling capabilities on one Component are unaffected — and sometimes they ARE, through exactly the shared state that put them on the same Component. Propagation found them because a path exists; calling that path uninteresting is a judgement about coupling the graph does not hold. This runs straight into `dec:report-dont-judge`, and into propagate_change's own refusal to say what to EDIT (`fact:defect-propagate-change-distance-two-is-not-an-edit-list`, which the guard surfaced beside this).

THREE HONEST FORMS IF THE VERDICT FORM IS REFUSED, none of which asserts anything the traversal did not establish: GROUP the ring by Component, so twenty siblings read as one component's worth; COUNT them — '17 of the 19 at distance 1 are capabilities on the same Component as the seed' is a fact, not a verdict, and is the sentence a reader actually needs; or SORT, putting crossings first and siblings last, changing only the reading order.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is the measurement that would decide between a verdict and a grouping: how often a same-Component sibling turns out to BE impacted. Nobody has looked.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex's idea, 2026-08-14 (docs/feedback/2026-08-14-alex-grok-session.md, Opportunities), in his words: "`record_change` should refuse (or warn) if the target's current hash already differs from what the caller thinks they are snapshotting — or be a required first step inside the typed merge when `status` is `accepted`."

DELIBERATELY SEPARATE FROM `fact:defect-record-change-overwrites-the-name-of-the-event-it-is-filed-under`, which the near-duplicate guard surfaced: BOTH ARE FAILURES OF THE SAME CALL AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME FAILURE. That fact is about `record_change` clobbering the ChangeEvent's `name`, found serially; this is about the SNAPSHOT capturing state that had already moved, found under parallel writes. Whether they get one fix is part of what is open here — which is an argument for keeping them separate until somebody decides, not for merging them now.

WHAT HE HIT (his item 2): in one batch he `record_change`d a Decision AFTER a sibling `add_decision` on the same id had already merged. The Snapshot stored the NEW statement. Nothing warned. In his words: "the timeline for that revision is a lie; easy for any agent that parallelizes writes."

THE OPTIONS:

(a) REFUSE ON A HASH MISMATCH — the caller states what it believes it is snapshotting; a difference is refused. CHEAP, and it matches doctrine already applied elsewhere: `set_artifact_checksum` is a two-sided accept for this reason, and `export_graph` refuses a divergent write rather than silently discarding. COUNTER: the caller has no hash in hand today, so this needs a new argument, and an agent that cannot produce one gets a tool it cannot call.

(b) WARN RATHER THAN REFUSE. CHEAP, breaks nothing. COUNTER: the loss is silent precisely because the call reports success, and a warning nobody reads is this project's own recurring failure.

(c) FOLD IT INTO THE TYPED MERGE when `status` is `accepted` — his stronger form: you cannot edit an accepted Decision without the snapshot happening first, because the tool does it. STRONGEST; removes the ordering hazard rather than reporting it. COUNTER: it makes one write path do two things, and `dec:ask-not-repair` is the standing preference for naming a problem over acting on it.

(d) DO NOTHING; THE DISCIPLINE IS THE ANSWER. COUNTER, and it is measured rather than argued: the sibling fact was found on 2026-08-15 doing exactly this, STRICTLY SERIALLY and in the order `revise-design` prescribes, and data was lost anyway. Ordering discipline is demonstrably not sufficient for this call — which is evidence against (d) rather than for any particular replacement.

NOT ESTABLISHED: how often the parallel-write case actually occurs — one report, one session.
properties.name: IDEA — the record-before-you-edit discipline can silently snapshot the NEW state. Should `record_change` refuse when the target has already moved, or be folded into the typed merge itself?
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`, options with counters beside them, nothing promoted. Kept distinct from the name-overwrite fact after the guard named it: two failures of one call, found by two different routes, and whether one fix covers both is itself part of the open question.

⭐ UPDATED 2026-08-16 — A FIFTH OPTION ARRIVED BY SHIPPING SOMETHING ELSE, and it weakens (a), (b) and (c) without settling them. v0.32.0 gave every typed constructor a `revision` block: landing on an existing node now returns the properties the call OVERWROTE, with their prior values IN FULL, plus a `changed` flag and a `prior_content_hash`. Its own note names this exact ordering — snapshot BEFORE the merge, because afterwards it files the replacement as the prior state.

⇒ (e) THE INFORMATION IS NOW IN THE REPLY, SO PERHAPS NOTHING MORE IS OWED. A caller who merges first and snapshots second is now TOLD, in the merge's own response, what the prior value was — which is the fact the lying Snapshot destroyed, handed back at the moment of destruction. COUNTER, and it is why this does not close the question: the block reports to whoever reads the reply, and the failure mode here is an agent parallelising writes and reading nothing. A value returned to a caller who does not look is not the same as a refusal. ⇒ The open question narrows usefully: it is no longer 'how do we preserve the prior value' but 'does a returned value suffice, or must the ordering be enforced'.

📌 AND THE PRIOR-HASH OBJECTION TO (a) IS NOW WEAKER TOO: the counter said a caller has no hash in hand, so refusing on a mismatch needs a new argument. `prior_content_hash` is now returned by the constructors, so a caller who has touched the node HAS one.
