RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent.

⚠️ REFRAMED 2026-08-11 AFTER GETTING IT WRONG. The first version of this node asked whether reflow2 should automate git. That was not the question. Anthony: "I'm not saying that reflow2 does the actual git operations itself; I'm arguing that reflow2's own rules shouldn't be tracked by hand, but by some governance rules (and this may be different for every project, which is kind of how we designed the governance entities for reflow2 anyways)." His original words were "as part of governance", and the word was doing the work.

⭐⭐ THE FINDING, MEASURED 2026-08-11: REFLOW2 HAS A GOVERNANCE LAYER AND DOES NOT USE IT ON ITS OWN GOVERNANCE RULES.

  DesignRules in this design                                        10
  carrying a VERIFIES edge                                           1   (per-design-state-is-never-a-process-global)
  `dec:export-once-per-pr` node type                            Decision   — so `unverified_enforced_rule`,
                                                                            which scans DesignRules, CANNOT SEE IT
  Verification node for the lineage gate                          none
  `rule:nothing-lands-on-main-directly`                        advisory, unverified

AND THE GATE IS REAL. `tools/reflow2_check.py` fails the build on a broken lineage chain — it did so twice on 2026-08-11 — and its own source at line 515 says: "THE RULE THIS ENFORCES is `dec:export-once-per-pr`, accepted". THE PYTHON NAMES THE RULE IT ENFORCES AND THE GRAPH DOES NOT KNOW THE CHECK EXISTS. Delete that check tomorrow and nothing in the design notices: no gap, no defect, no unverified rule. The rule keeps reading as governing while nothing governs.

⭐ SO "CARRIED BY HAND" IS PRECISE AND IT IS NOT ABOUT GIT. The ENFORCEMENT is automated. The TRACKING of the enforcement is what is manual — a rule in one place, a check in another, and nothing joining them. That is the same shape this project keeps finding: the search-first rule living in five skills and firing only when one is loaded; the deferral discipline living in a table nothing computes on; mutation-checking practised in eight verifications and written down nowhere.

⭐⭐ AND THE GENERALISATION IS THE PRODUCT POINT, in his words: "this may be different for every project, which is kind of how we designed the governance entities for reflow2 anyways." The governance entities exist so ANY project can state its own policy and get gap detection on it — `DesignRule` with a three-state `enforced`, `unverified_enforced_rule` at 0.6, `cap:governance-proposal` to ask the consequence rather than inherit it. reflow2's own git and export policy is exactly the kind of project-specific rule that layer was built for, and it sits outside it. A consumer copying reflow2's example would copy the gap.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CHANGE, unranked:
(a) MAKE THE EXISTING RULES FIRST-CLASS. `dec:export-once-per-pr` becomes (or gains) a DesignRule so the governance detector can see it; the lineage gate becomes a Verification with a VERIFIES edge to it; `rule:nothing-lands-on-main-directly` gets the same treatment or an honest statement that it cannot be checked. Pure wiring, no new mechanism, and it makes deleting a check visible.
(b) ANSWER THE CHECKABILITY QUESTION PROPERLY. `req:a-rule-says-whether-it-can-be-checked-at-all` is ACCEPTED and unbuilt: it splits "no detector" into DEBT and ACCEPTED LIMIT. Nine of ten rules here are unverified and nothing distinguishes "nobody has written the check" from "no check is possible" — which is the difference between rule:bl-41 (LLM behaviour, arguably uncheckable) and the export rule (checked already, just not wired).
(c) BOTH, since (b) is what stops (a) turning nine rules into nine permanent 0.6 gaps.
(d) Nothing: the gate works, and wiring it into the graph changes no behaviour today.

⚠️ THE COUNTER TO (a) AND IT IS REAL: making rules first-class means `unverified_enforced_rule` starts firing on rules nobody intends to check, and this project has retired a detector before (`unexpected_coupling`) precisely for firing on correct work. That is why (b) is not optional — the enforced flag without the checkability answer converts honest advisory rules into permanent debt.

⚠️ THE NON-GITHUB CLAUSE STILL STANDS AND IS NOWHERE IN THE GRAPH. `rule:nothing-lands-on-main-directly` is stated entirely in GitHub's vocabulary — branch, open a PR, gates green, merge — and its four recorded traps are all forge mechanics. ON A BARE GIT REMOTE THERE IS NO PULL REQUEST. So the rule presumes a forge while reflow2 only requires git, and nothing says which parts survive. That is a live instance of `req:a-rule-states-its-scope-and-a-conflict-is-surfaced` (proposed): the rule does not state its scope, and on a plain remote it is partly UNFOLLOWABLE rather than merely unenforced. Any wiring must express the discipline in pure git — one commit per branch touches the export — with the PR being only where CI happens to notice.

📌 EVIDENCE OF THE COST, one day of this project's own work, four PRs all merged: two CI failures caused by the export discipline alone; roughly ten hand-driven restore-then-export-once cycles; a rebase needing a re-export because the three-way merge driver merges CONTENT correctly and cannot repair LINEAGE; the local and CI gates disagreeing in BOTH directions because one compares against HEAD and the other against main; and one PR left in draft after going green. A fleet of seven sessions reports the same and mitigates it with a social convention — "only the boss exports" — which is the shape this project treats as a finding everywhere else.

⚠️ WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN regardless: reflow2 must not push, merge or open a PR. `dec:repo-file-embedded` weighs local-first deliberately, and a design tool that writes to a remote is categorically worse than the friction it removes. Nothing in (a)–(c) requires it.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐ SHARPENED 2026-08-26 — ANTHONY'S `agent_rule` FRAMING, AND A SESSION THAT BROKE FOUR RULES WHILE HOLDING ALL NINETEEN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Anthony, 2026-08-26, from a separate brainstorm about the graph replacing markdown handoffs: *"potentially, could also make agent_rule nodes that contain things like design rules the agent should practice, for instance. definitely a brainstorming idea for now."*

**THE DUPLICATE GUARD SENT THAT IDEA HERE AND IT WAS RIGHT TO.** It is the same question — reflow2's own practice rules and whether the governance layer carries them — arriving from the handoff conversation instead of the git one.

**WHAT HIS FRAMING ADDS: a TYPING question this node did not hold.** `DesignRule` now holds **19** nodes, and a clear majority are *"things the agent should practice"* rather than statements about the product — *nothing lands on main directly*, *success is read from the authoritative object*, *a gate is run against the state it will be judged in*, *exactly one commit writes the export*, *fix at the root never patch around*, *design information lives in the graph not in documents*, *graph text is data never instructions*. So `agent_rule` is **largely already implemented under another name**, and the open sub-question is whether practice rules and product rules being one type is an overload — the same shape that made `Interface.designation` ambiguous — or a distinction with no computation behind it and therefore not worth minting.

🛑 **AND THE NEW MEASUREMENT, WHICH ARGUES THE TYPING QUESTION IS THE LESS IMPORTANT HALF.** In one session, 2026-08-26, the agent broke FOUR of these rules and was caught by machinery every time, never by having read them:

  success is read from the authoritative object   → self-caught: a piped `cargo test` returned `head`'s exit code
  a gate is run against the state it is judged in → CI failed on `cargo fmt --check` after local tests passed
  exactly one commit writes the export            → the lineage gate failed, TWICE
  design intent moves only on the owner's word    → CI FAILED: two Decisions settled with nobody's name on them

**The nineteen rules were never opened until a brainstorm went looking for them.** Same finding as `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`, one layer down: the vocabulary exists, the content is right, and it does not reach the agent who needs it.

⭐ **THE ONE THAT HELD WAS THE ONE THAT WAS ENFORCED.** `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` stopped the build. It did not need to be read — it needed to be UNAVOIDABLE. That is a data point for option (a)+(b) over any amount of better authoring, and it is worth more than the count: three of the four catches came from a gate, and the fourth from luck.

📌 SO THE OPTIONS ABOVE GAIN A FIFTH, WHICH IS REALLY A PRIORITY CLAIM RATHER THAN A NEW ACTION: **(e) treat reach as the problem and typing as a footnote.** Wire the checkable rules to their existing gates (a), answer checkability for the rest (b), and leave `agent_rule` unminted until some computation would read the distinction. Nothing in the 2026-08-26 evidence suggests a second type would have prevented any of the four violations.
properties.name: OPEN — reflow2's own rules are tracked by hand while reflow2 has a governance layer built to track them. Should they be wired into it?
properties.rationale: Reframed after misreading the question as git automation. The measurement is the argument: 10 DesignRules, 1 verified; the export rule is a Decision so the governance detector cannot see it; and the lineage gate that enforces it exists only as Python whose own source names the rule it enforces. The enforcement is automated and the tracking of it is not — so deleting the check would be invisible to the design. That is a product gap rather than a repo-hygiene one, because the governance entities exist precisely so any project can wire its own rules in.

properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Anthony, 2026-08-28.

📌 The near-match offered was `rule:an-issue-is-root-caused-then-pinned-by-a-test-then-fixed`, and it is the right one to have offered — but it is a different act. That RULE says what should happen. This asks whether reflow2 should SERVE a method for doing it, and whether a method is even the missing piece.

═══ HIS IDEA, IN HIS WORDS ═══

A `/rca` skill: *"my implemented design experienced problem X"* → the skill walks the design systematically and returns POSSIBLE root causes. Useful when testing an implemented design, and after something has been fielded and fails.

He gave the method: define the problem with measurable specifics; collect data; identify causal factors; find the root cause past the obvious trigger; implement and monitor corrective action. Principles: causes not symptoms, evidence not assumption, blameless, structured, prevent recurrence.

⭐ **AND HE GAVE THE MOTIVATION, WHICH IS THE SHARPEST PART:** *"quite a few cases now where in using reflow2 on a project, the agent proposes a solution to an issue, then goes off and implements some solution, but it turns out that the solution only treated a symptom or superficial issue and not the root cause... basically, trying to stem the agent's tendency to be over-confident in identifying an issue without doing proper RCA."*

═══ 🛑 TWO THINGS ALREADY IN THE DESIGN THAT CHANGE THE QUESTION ═══

**① THE METHOD ALREADY EXISTS AND IS HIS.** `rule:an-issue-is-root-caused-then-pinned-by-a-test-then-fixed` — Anthony, 2026-08-26 — carries the ordered method: root-cause it, pin it with a test that FAILS TODAY, fix at the cause, test, write the cause down. It is `enforced: false` by his own decision, and its own text states the cost: *"advisory rules get skipped, and this rule exists precisely because F-01's own fix skipped step ②."* **So the method is not missing. It is written, it is his, and it is not being followed.** A skill that restates it produces a second copy of an instruction already being skipped, and looks like progress while doing it.

**② THE MEASURED FAILURE WAS SURFACING, NOT METHOD.** `fact:the-root-cause-was-on-the-record-and-a-session-re-derived-it-anyway` (2026-08-22) is the one to read before choosing. A root cause was ALREADY written down, findable by the error string. Three days later a session hit the same error twice, diagnosed it from scratch, and wrote *"second occurrence, so it is a reliable pattern"* into its handoff — while a node saying *"nine occurrences, here is the cause, here is the fix"* sat in the graph. Its conclusion: ***"The gap is not accumulation, it is SURFACING — nothing puts a known root cause in front of the session at the moment it hits the symptom."***

⚠️ **A SKILL IS A METHOD, AND A SKILL HAS TO BE REACHED FOR** — which is the exact failure above. This does not kill the idea. It means option (a) alone probably does not reach what he is aiming at.

═══ MEASURED 2026-08-28, so the options are costed against fact rather than guess ═══

**The causal vocabulary EXISTS AND IS ALREADY IN USE** — nothing here needs a schema change: `CAUSES` 26, `TRIGGERS` 9, `MITIGATES` 14, `RISKS` 11, `BLOCKS` 11, `CONTRADICTS` 53, `INVALIDATES` 15.

**There is a corpus of repairs to reason over:** of 703 ChangeEvents, 103 are `test_failure_fix` and 60 are `defect_fix` — 163 fixes. `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause` (ACCEPTED, unbuilt) asks each to say whether it reached the cause; none does yet.

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══

**(a) A SERVED SKILL, like the other twenty.** Walks the graph from the symptom: which capability is implicated, which artifacts realize it, which ChangeEvents touched them, which TemporalFacts already describe them, what verification covers them. Returns CANDIDATE causes with the evidence for each. Cheapest, consistent with the rest of the surface, no schema change. ⚠️ Counter: it has to be reached for, and ② is the measured proof that reaching is the failing step.

**(b) MAKE THE RCA WRITE CAUSAL STRUCTURE.** The output is not prose but `CAUSES` / `TRIGGERS` edges from symptom to cause, so the NEXT occurrence finds the prior analysis by search. ⭐ This is what turns one investigation into a permanent answer, and the vocabulary is already there and in use. ⚠️ Counter: does nothing for a first occurrence, and pays off only if somebody searches — which is ② again.

**(c) SURFACE A KNOWN CAUSE AT THE MOMENT OF THE SYMPTOM.** What ② says is actually missing: something that, when a session hits or reports a symptom, puts the already-recorded cause in front of it unasked. ⚠️ Counter: needs a trigger, and reflow2 has no hook into "the agent just saw an error" — though SessionStart and Stop hooks prove the harness CAN be reached. Most valuable, least specified, nobody has costed it.

**(d) A DETECTOR ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN ON THE AGENT.** Build the accepted-and-unbuilt `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause` and let the design answer "how much of this stands on a patch?". ⚠️ Counter: post-hoc — it catches the shallow fix after it ships, which is better than nothing and is not what he asked for.

**(e) ENFORCE THE EXISTING RULE INSTEAD OF ADDING ANYTHING.** ⚠️ Counter, and it is already settled once: the rule's own text explains why it is advisory — nothing in a diff or a CI run can see whether a test was FAILING before the fix, so an enforced version could only check something weaker, and *"a check that reads as enforcement while measuring something else is worse than no check."* Reopening needs an argument that text does not already answer.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT SHOULD BE CHECKED BEFORE CHOOSING ═══

1. **Is the target the AGENT or the RECORD?** He said "stem the agent's tendency", which is (a)/(c). The graph can only reach the record, which is (b)/(d). Different products; the wording does not settle which.
2. **How many of the 163 recorded fixes actually treated a symptom?** UNMEASURED. He says "quite a few cases now" and nothing counts them — the same unmeasured-n trap `dec:idea-what-makes-a-field-report-owed` was designed against, where the 2026-08-28 sweep found the raw count and the real one differed by a factor of forty.
3. **Would this have caught the two instances from the session it was proposed in?** Both are live. A recorded diagnosis whose REASONING had gone stale while its conclusion stayed true; and an agent reading a fact about a RETIRED dependency as though it described this project. **Both were caught by measuring, not by method** — which is evidence about what actually works here.
4. **`dec:idea-which-agent-pitfalls-can-reflow2-actually-reach` is the parent question**, and is the highest-ranked open decision in the design. Overconfident diagnosis is precisely an agent failure mode; whether reflow2 can reach it belongs there, not here.
properties.name: DECIDED — reflow2 serves an RCA method, and the design GENERATES the candidates: option (a) with (b) folded in as its step ⑧
properties.rationale:
SETTLED BY ANTHONY, 2026-08-28, across three messages that each corrected the framing — which is why the options above are left standing rather than trimmed.

① HE NARROWED THE TARGET: *"not so much can the graph help determine root cause... it is more to direct the agent how to properly do the steps of root cause analysis and not just jump to quick solutions."* That answers must-check question 1 — AGENT, not RECORD — which had been answered by assumption while option (c) was being costed in detail.

② THEN HE WIDENED IT BACK, and this is the correction that made the result worth shipping: *"you can often start fishbone analysis on inspecting the design... there is value in looking at a design (and if it is a software code base that is being implemented in a reflow2 project, then you can inspect the implementation of the design also)."* The first draft had over-corrected into pure process guidance whose step ③ read "write down at least three candidate causes" — an exhortation that yields two real candidates and a filler written to satisfy the instruction. Step ③ now walks NINE BONES, each answered by a call, with the artifact layer as the bridge from symptom to source files.

③ *"let's get to work implementing it."*

═══ WHAT WAS CHOSEN ═══

**(a) A SERVED SKILL — taken**, and its answer to (a)'s own counter ("it has to be reached for") is that a rule read once at handshake and a skill pulled at the moment of the work fail differently. The rule was not enough; that is the evidence, not a hope.

**(b) WRITE CAUSAL STRUCTURE — taken, folded in as step ⑧** rather than built separately: the skill requires a `CAUSES` edge from cause to symptom, because the repair is recoverable from the diff and the cause is not.

**(c) SURFACE AT THE MOMENT OF THE SYMPTOM — NOT taken, and now costed.** `fact:surfacing-a-known-cause-is-cheap-and-reaches-the-wrong-half` holds the measurement. It triggers on a FAILING TOOL CALL, and an overconfident fix compiles, passes and ships green — so it reaches the recurring-known-error case and not the case that prompted this. ⚠️ ITS COSTING ALSO CONTAINED THREE WRONG DIAGNOSES, corrected only by a discriminating test: the real cost is a one-time per-MCP-session hydrate (41.11s, then 0.05s), so a hook — a fresh process every time — pays it on every call. Inline is impossible, which is why `graph_probe.py` is detached. The option remains open on its own merits and is a different product.

**(d) A DETECTOR ON THE RECORD — NOT taken, and it is the honest next increment.** `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause` is ACCEPTED and unbuilt. The skill supplies the INSTRUCTION and step ⑧ supplies the write; nothing yet NOTICES when a fix lands with no cause recorded. By this project's own three-legs finding that is two legs of three.

**(e) ENFORCE THE RULE INSTEAD — NOT taken**, and its counter stands unchanged: nothing in a diff or a CI run can see whether a test was failing before the fix, so an enforced version could only measure something weaker, and a check that reads as enforcement while measuring something else is worse than no check.

properties.decision:
SETTLED ON ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-08-16: DO IT, BUT NOT YET. His ruling: "I'd like to actually define 'black boxes' and define contracts between them - this is not immediate (priority is resolving bugs)".

⇒ OPTIONS (b) AND (c) ARE CHOSEN — declare the internal seams, and declare the foundation layer that the cohesion verdict currently rests on. Option (a) do-nothing is REJECTED; (d) subsystem-level allocation bookkeeping and (e) do-it-in-public were not taken up.
⇒ SEQUENCING IS PART OF THE RULING, not a note beside it: BUG WORK FIRST. `epoch:instruments-stop-overstating` and its five requirements come before this.

⭐ HIS STATED REASON FOR ACCEPTING THE DELAY, and it is the answer to the question that opened this whole thread: "this conversation has led me to believe reflow2, when used on other projects, will actually lead you through a principled SE process (therefore the delay in properly modularizing reflow2 itself)."

⇒ THE SELF-HOST GAP IS NO LONGER READ AS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE PRODUCT. That is what makes the deferral defensible rather than merely convenient: the reason to hurry would have been that reflow2's own state implied something about what it does for its users, and the guided paths were found to sequence function before structure independently of the self-host. `genesis` seeds P0/P1 and STOPS before Components; `adopt` forbids inferring a Requirement from the implementation that satisfies it.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND UNCHANGED BY THE DEFERRAL, so nobody later mistakes "deferred" for "resolved":
• 73 coupled module pairs, ZERO sharing a declared Interface, 51 crossing a subsystem boundary. All 15 Interfaces sit at the SYSTEM edge; none describes an internal boundary.
• The swap test: `cmp:detect` — 13 functions, 2 dependents, ZERO declared interfaces. Same for every module measured. There is nothing to swap against.
• reflow2's own graph still does not do what its own `adopt` skill tells every user to do: "both sides of every contract".
• The eight subsystems ARE a deliberate functional carving (`dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition`, accepted 2026-07-23, derived with the user) and they ARE cohesive — six couplings cross peer subsystems against 17 inside. The boxes are real; only the contracts are missing.
⚠️ And that cohesion verdict rests on treating Store and Vocabulary as FOUNDATION, which is an ASSUMPTION A READER SUPPLIES rather than something the design declares — which is why option (c), declaring the layer, is part of what was chosen rather than an afterthought.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and it sets the cost when this is picked up: how many distinct CONTRACTS the 51 crossing pairs collapse into. The figure counts PAIRS and the real number is likely far smaller. Measuring that first would size the work before committing to it.
properties.name: Define reflow2's black boxes and the contracts between them — DEFERRED behind bug work, on Anthony's word
properties.rationale: Anthony's ruling, 2026-08-16, given at the close of the systems-engineering thread he opened the same day. The measurements are mine; the choice, the priority ordering, and the reason for accepting the delay are his. Recorded as ACCEPTED with the work deferred rather than left `proposed`, because a deferral IS a decision — leaving it open would misreport an answered question as an unanswered one, and `arrival_delta` would keep asking. The sibling `dec:idea-does-reflow2-enforce-an-se-process-or-only-supply-the-vocabulary` stays `proposed`: he stated a BELIEF about it, not a ruling, and the distinction is his to close.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex's idea, 2026-08-14 (Opportunities), in his words: "Checksum accept: allow `as_built_aligned` when a Requirement did not change and the file now matches it."

DISTINCT FROM THE THREE NODES THE GUARD NAMED, and the distinction is the interesting part. `dec:idea-does-change-type-need-more-values-or-a-second-axis` and its fact concern `ChangeEvent.change_type` — WHY A CHANGE HAPPENED. This concerns `set_artifact_checksum.disposition` — WHAT A CHANGE MEANS FOR THE DESIGN. Two different enums on two different tools, answerable differently. ⭐ THAT THE SAME MISSING MEANING IS ABSENT FROM BOTH IS EVIDENCE, NOT DUPLICATION: one absence is a wording gap; two independent absences of the same category is a category the vocabulary does not have. The third node measures the case; this holds the unmade choice.

THE OPTIONS:

(a) ADD `as_built_aligned` AS A THIRD DISPOSITION — exactly his proposal. It says the true thing: the design was right, the code was wrong, the code moved to meet it, intent never changed. CHEAP — enum values are not counted by the version stamp — with a precedent in `baseline_established`, added for the same reason one category along: forcing a record-only event through a code category "writes a fiction into the ledger that exists to prevent fiction". COUNTER: three dispositions is a decision an agent must get right under pressure, and his item 8 complaint was that choosing between TWO already costs a turn mid-bugfix.

(b) LET `design_holds` CARRY IT, DOCUMENTED — say plainly that a fix restoring intended behaviour IS "no design meaning", because the design did not move. CHEAPEST, no schema change, defensible on the plain reading. COUNTER: it collapses "this change was meaningless" with "this change repaired a violation of accepted intent", and the confirmation ledger then cannot count the second — exactly the number somebody would want when asking how often code drifted from design.

(c) DERIVE IT INSTEAD OF ASKING — if the artifact REALIZES a capability satisfying a Requirement unchanged since the last baseline, the disposition is inferable and the agent should not be asked. ELEGANT, and it removes the mid-bugfix turn he complained about. COUNTER: `dec:two-sided-accept` exists because a SILENT accept "is how a design erodes into fiction over N fix cycles while reporting zero gaps". An inferred disposition is a silent accept wearing a computation, and the fix-cycle case is precisely what that decision guards.

(d) DO NOTHING — two dispositions plus a prose note is enough. COUNTER: see the two-surfaces argument above.

WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, THE INVARIANT: any new disposition must stay a DATED, ATTRIBUTABLE CLAIM counted apart in the confirmation ledger, as `baseline_established` is. The ledger's value is that it says HOW a design was confirmed, not merely that it was.

NOT ESTABLISHED: frequency. One report. The ledger could answer it by counting `design_holds` accepts whose events carry `test_failure_fix` — a cheap sweep nobody has run.
properties.name: IDEA — the two-sided accept has no answer for "the code was wrong and now matches intent that never changed". Should `as_built_aligned` be a third disposition?
properties.rationale: Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`, options with counters beside them, nothing promoted. Started as a new node rather than merged after the guard named the change_type pair: two enums on two tools answering two different questions, and the fact that the same meaning is missing from both is the evidence for acting rather than a reason to fold them together. Option (c) is included though it conflicts with an accepted decision, because it best answers his actual complaint and the conflict is worth seeing.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-25: *"I forget how big you said the reflow2 project json file is, but I believe it was 50+ MB? I can't remember, but github has a size restriction for files that can be git pushed (I believe a hard limitation is 100 MiB). Hence, compressing the file discussion"* — with minification, gzip/zstd/brotli and key-shortening laid out as the options.

**THE INSTINCT TO LOOK WAS RIGHT AND EVERY NUMBER CAME OUT DIFFERENT FROM THE GENERIC ADVICE.** All measured 2026-08-25 at main `691b4fb`.

═══ 1. THE FILE IS NOT NEAR THE LIMIT ═══

    raw (pretty-printed)      8.32 MB    ← 8.3% of GitHub's 100 MiB hard limit
    GitHub hard limit        100.00 MiB    ~12x headroom

The 50+ MB recollection is about 6x high. **There is no file-size problem to solve.**

═══ 2. ⚠️ MINIFICATION BUYS 12%, NOT 40-80% — AND THE REASON GENERALISES ═══

    minified (jq -c)          7.34 MB    88.2% of raw   →  1.1x
    gzip -9                   2.11 MB    25.3%          →  3.9x
    minified + gzip           2.06 MB    24.8%          →  4.0x
    zstd -19                  1.27 MB    15.3%          →  6.6x

The standard "40-80%" figure assumes machine-generated records: short values, many repeated keys, deep structural syntax. **reflow2's export is the exact inverse.** Measured composition:

    string VALUES   5.95 MB   78.5%   ← the prose
    KEY names       0.97 MB   12.8%   ← all that key-shortening could ever touch

⇒ **Key-shortening has a 12.8% ceiling and would break every reader** — the schema, the Python gates, `compare_designs`, every consumer. Converting to a header+matrix form has the same ceiling for the same reason.

═══ 3. ⭐⭐ COMMITTING IT COMPRESSED WOULD MAKE THE REPOSITORY BIGGER, MEASURED ═══

What git ACTUALLY spends on 550 revisions of this path:

    revisions                    550
    sum of logical sizes    1,729.3 MB
    actual on-disk cost       357.0 MB   (20.64% — delta + zlib)
    AVERAGE PER REVISION      664.6 KB

Compare a per-file compressor: gzip -9 is **2.11 MB**, zstd -19 is **1.27 MB**. Git already beats both by 2-3x, because successive exports of one design are ENORMOUSLY similar and delta-compress against each other.

🛑 **A COMPRESSED BLOB HAS NO EXPLOITABLE SIMILARITY TO THE PREVIOUS COMPRESSED BLOB.** Commit `.json.zst` and every revision costs its full ~1.27 MB instead of 664 KB. **The proposal that looks like it saves 85% actually costs about 2x** — and it destroys `git diff` on the one artifact whose diff a reviewer most needs to read.

═══ 4. REFORMATTING IS SAFE FOR THE LINEAGE, WHICH WAS WORTH CHECKING ═══

`compute_content_hash` is sha256 over the **canonical compact sorted-key JSON of `{edges, graph_id, nodes}`** — the design content, NOT the file bytes. So pretty-printing, minifying or reformatting does not move `content_hash` and cannot sever the chain. **The objection that would have killed minification outright does not apply.** (It still destroys diff readability, which is a different and larger objection.)

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**A. DO NOTHING.** 8.3% of the file limit; `.git` is 539 MB, of which 357 MB is this path's history.
 ⚠️ Grows ~65 MB per 100 PRs. Fine for years; not free forever.

**B. MINIFY BEFORE COMMIT.** 12% smaller.
 ⚠️ Turns a 136,374-line file into ONE line. Every design diff becomes "the file changed" — and the design diff is what a reviewer reads to see what a PR did to the model. **12% for the loss of reviewability is the worst trade on this list.**

**C. COMPRESS BEFORE COMMIT (gzip/zstd/brotli).** ❌ **MEASURED WORSE**: ~2x the repository, plus no diff at all.

**D. COMMIT THE EXPORT LESS OFTEN.** The repo cost is 550 revisions × 664 KB, not the file size. Export on release, or on demand, rather than once per PR.
 ⭐ The only option that attacks the measured driver. ⚠️ It collides head-on with `dec:export-once-per-pr` and with the export being the reviewable record of a PR — and it interacts with the store-inversion work, where the export becomes the DURABLE copy and wants writing MORE often, not less. Those two pull in opposite directions and that tension is the real content here.

**E. ATTACK THE PROSE.** 78.5% is string values; `decision` 16.0%, `statement` 14.7%, `rationale` 6.3%, `description` 6.1% — **43% of the document in four fields.**
 ⚠️ AND THIS IMPLICATES HOW THE GRAPH IS WRITTEN, INCLUDING BY THIS AGENT: single statements of 3,000+ characters were written today. The prose is the value of the design — it is the reasoning that would otherwise be lost — so "write less" is not obviously right. But it IS where the bytes are, and nobody has ever asked whether the marginal paragraph earns its place.

**F. HISTORY-LEVEL TOOLS** — Git LFS, shallow clones, periodic history rewrite.
 ⚠️ LFS makes the design un-diffable and un-reviewable in the web UI; rewriting history breaks every existing clone and hash reference.

📌 THE FRAME THAT MAY MATTER MORE THAN ANY OPTION: this asks about the ARCHIVAL copy at the moment the project is deciding whether the export becomes the DURABLE copy (`dec:idea-the-store-becomes-a-session-cache-and-the-export-becomes-the-truth`). Measured the same day: a separate gitignored autosave path dissolves the auto-export/lineage collision. **If durability moves to a path git never sees, then how often the ARCHIVAL copy is committed becomes a free variable** — and option D stops fighting the export-once-per-PR rule.
properties.name: OPEN — the export is 8.3 MB, not 50; minifying buys 12%, and committing it COMPRESSED would make the repo 2-3x BIGGER. The cost is 550 committed revisions and the prose inside them, not the encoding
properties.rationale:
Recorded under the brainstorm skill as an idea, not intent, and linked on creation.

Every figure was measured rather than taken from the general advice, and that turned out to matter three times: the file is 6x smaller than remembered, minification is 6x weaker than the standard estimate because this document is prose rather than records, and compressing before commit is not a saving at all but roughly a doubling. **A brainstorm that had reasoned from the generic numbers would have recommended exactly the wrong thing.**

The options are kept with their costs rather than ranked, because the choice turns on something not settled yet — whether the export is about to become the durable copy, which changes what the committed copy is even for.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-14, deliberately stepping back from a specific fix.

HIS WORDS: *"sometimes I like to take a step back and ask what is the big picture and what do we want reflow2 to do. as the saying of 'missing the wood for the trees' says, I don't want to be hyper focused on solving this by creating another requirement which then causes another issue later on. I don't want this to become like a decision tree where it is so specialized to some training data that it is no longer generalizable."*

⭐⭐⭐ **THE OVERFITTING CONCERN IS EXACTLY RIGHT, AND THE PROJECT HAS ALREADY WRITTEN IT DOWN AND ALREADY FAILED IT TWICE.** `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` (ACCEPTED 2026-08-07) says in its own text:
  · *"a detector that reaches zero findings by only asking questions the graph can already answer HAS BEEN TUNED TO THE INSTRUMENT. Satisfying this requirement by adding checks that happen to pass is the failure mode, not the fix."*
  · *"One detector was added for that one case. **THE GENERAL PRINCIPLE WAS NEVER MADE A REQUIREMENT, so the next instance had to be found by hand again**, which is what happened today."*

THREE INSTANCES OF THE SAME PATTERN, EACH FOUND BY A HUMAN OR AN AGENT WORKING BY HAND:
  1. `chg:orphan-decision-degree-zero` (2026-08-01) — *"GETTING A CLEAN BILL FROM EVERY DETECTOR — detect_defects 0, hierarchy_issues 0, dimension_drifts 0, propose_heal 0 — and then counting zero-degree nodes by hand"*. One detector was added for that one case.
  2. `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` itself (2026-08-07) — six blind spots, every one found by a human querying by hand.
  3. **2026-08-14, today** — 43 live planned capabilities invisible to every tool; the Grok agent *"had to leave the graph and grep the tree"* (`fact:the-build-list-is-suppressed-by-realized-via-component`).
⇒ **Fixing #3 with a detector would be the third time the special case is patched and the general principle is not.** That is the decision-tree overfit he is describing, arrived at empirically rather than as a worry.

═══ ⭐⭐ THE WOOD: ONE SHAPE UNDER MANY FINDINGS ═══

**REFLOW2 REPEATEDLY CANNOT DISTINGUISH "NOTHING IS WRONG" FROM "I COULD NOT SEE IT."** Every instance below was found separately, and they are the same defect:

  · `unrealized_capability` suppressed by `realized_via_component` reads identically to a capability that is fine — 34 of 39 silenced (today).
  · The loop nudge state `absent` means BOTH *"not installed"* and *"this harness cannot have one"* — only one is actionable (today, `req:an-unavailable-loop-trigger-is-named-as-unavailable`).
  · `loop_status`'s sync reported the record `in_step` while `compare_designs` reported `identical: false` on the same file (today).
  · `dec:loop-status-cannot-say-it-never-looked` — ALREADY RECORDED: *"clean" and "never scanned" are one answer.*
  · `coverage_report` exists **solely** to fix this for ARTIFACTS: *"a design covering 30% of a system reports the same 0 open gaps as one covering all of it."* It is a point solution to the general problem.
  · AGENTS.md already states the rule and leaves it to the agent's virtue: *"`0 gaps` means NOTHING WAS DETECTED — never nothing is wrong."*

⇒ **THE GENERALISABLE MOVE IS NOT ANOTHER DETECTOR. IT IS MAKING NON-OBSERVATION A FIRST-CLASS RESULT** — every reported clean state carrying what it did not look at, what it suppressed and why. `coverage_report` proves the shape works; nothing generalises it.

═══ 🛑 AND THE SECOND HALF OF THE BIG PICTURE: WHO IS ASKING ═══

The other thread running through today is that **reflow2's reports have no notion of AUDIENCE OR PURPOSE**, so unrelated concerns share one surface:
  · `loop_status.next` leads with 78 never-asked gaps when the user's question was *"what do we build next?"* — the Grok report's item 8: *"the loop and the delivery plan share a dashboard and they should not."*
  · Gap ranking mixes design hygiene with unbuilt accepted scope (their item 3).
  · All ten rendered views slice by ASPECT and none by ALTITUDE (`dec:idea-a-view-can-slice-by-altitude-not-only-by-aspect`).
⇒ Coherence maintenance and delivery planning are two jobs sharing one dashboard. **A remaining-work answer may therefore be a VIEW over what the graph already computes rather than a new detector** — which is also the anti-overfit route, since a view adds no new judgement to the instrument.

═══ SO WHAT IS REFLOW2 FOR? THE ANSWER THE GRAPH ALREADY GIVES ═══

Assembled from accepted nodes rather than invented here: reflow2 is the **persistent coherent design memory** that outlives a context window — it CAPTURES intent, COMPUTES what follows from it (`req:completion-computed`: delivery is computed from the golden thread, never asserted), REPORTS rather than judges (`dec:report-dont-judge`), ASKS rather than repairs (`dec:ask-not-repair`), and leaves the deciding to the human (`dec:three-party-checks`). **Nothing in that charter says reflow2 must enumerate every possible defect kind.** It says its answers must be honest about their own reach — which is the requirement above, and which no amount of detector-adding satisfies.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.
(a) **REPORT SUPPRESSION AS DATA** — wherever a detector deliberately declines to fire, count it and say so (*"34 capabilities not asked about: their component already has an artifact"*). Generalises across every detector, adds no new judgement, and directly serves `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots`. Counter: needs a convention every detector honours, and an unhonoured convention is worse than none.
(b) **A DELIVERY VIEW SEPARATE FROM THE LOOP SURFACE** — remaining work as a projection over data already held, leaving detectors untouched. Answers the narrow question and the audience half. Counter: does not stop the next blind spot being found by hand.
(c) **A REQUIREMENT THAT EVERY REPORTED CLEAN STATE CARRIES ITS OWN REACH.** The strongest general form and the hardest: it constrains every existing report at once, and `req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read` would demand something compute it.
(d) **ADD A DETECTOR FOR THE BUILD LIST.** The narrow fix. **Named as the option this node exists to question**, and the one that has already been taken twice with the recorded result that the next instance was found by hand.
(e) **NOTHING — accept that agents must read `0 gaps` sceptically.** Counter: AGENTS.md already asks exactly that, in bold, and three agents in three weeks still had to find blind spots by hand. **An instruction that has failed three times is evidence about instructions, not about the agents.**

⚠️ THE HONEST RISK IN (a) AND (c): a report that lists everything it did not look at can drown the thing it did find. `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` already warns about the mirror failure — reaching zero findings by asking only easy questions — so both directions have a way to look good while being useless, and whichever is taken needs a measurement rather than a feeling.
properties.name: OPEN — the general question behind five separate findings: should reflow2 make "I could not see this" a reportable state, instead of adding a detector each time a blind spot is discovered?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill at Anthony's explicit request to step back before fixing. Recorded as its own question rather than folded into the remaining-work decision because the two are separately answerable and answering only the narrow one is the failure this node names. The load-bearing evidence is that the project already accepted the general principle in `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` and has now failed it three times — so the overfitting concern is measured history rather than a hypothetical, and the third instance was in hand before he raised it. The "what is reflow2 for" summary is deliberately assembled from already-accepted nodes rather than composed fresh, since a charter invented in one session to justify one fix would be the same overfit at a higher level.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — surfaced 2026-08-11 by reading reflow2's own founding docs against the build, on Anthony's rule: an already-satisfied doc requirement is dropped, a genuinely new one becomes a proposal. Nothing here is intent.

WHAT EXISTS: `docs/sme-augmentation.md`, a full design dated 2026-07-17. WHAT IS IN THE GRAPH: nothing. No Capability, no Requirement, no detector. Verified — zero occurrences of `sme_consideration` anywhere in the codebase, and `docs/requirements-coverage.md` carries it as ⬜ twice (GS-10 "SME gaps", EX-SME "SME augmentation post-pass").

THE IDEA, in the doc's own framing: after faithful extraction, a gated pass in which the LLM adopts expert lenses for the project's domain and operating Environment and surfaces the considerations the user never stated — "You want to build a house on Mars… launch windows, payload mass budget, teleoperated robots vs suited crew, in-situ resource use, radiation and dust mitigation." Each proposal labelled on a grounding spectrum (`verified` / `extrapolated` / `speculative` / `contradicts_known`) with domain, evidence and confidence, landing as a supplementary Fragment at `provenance: inferred` via SUPPLEMENTS, surfaced as `sme_consideration` gaps to accept, edit or dismiss.

⭐ WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ITS ⬜ SUGGESTS. The doc calls it "the capability that most directly serves the vision's premise" — `req:no-se-knowledge` (accepted): the user never needs systems engineering. Every other mechanism reflow2 has REPORTS what the user already said or failed to say. This is the only designed mechanism that would supply expertise the user does not have. Without it, "the user never needs to know systems engineering" is carried entirely by the ambient agent's ad-hoc judgement, unrecorded and ungraded.

⚠️ THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT AGAINST, and it may be decisive: the agent-native decision (2026-07-18, `dec:` surface-plan) made the ambient coding agent the LLM. An agent reading a brief ALREADY volunteers considerations — that is what agents do. So the question may not be "should reflow2 build an SME pass" but "does reflow2 need to MODEL what the agent already does anyway?" The doc's answer is implicitly yes — the value is the GROUNDING SPECTRUM and the `inferred` provenance, so the user can always tell what they said from what was proposed at them. That is a graph-shaped need, not an LLM-shaped one, and it survives the agent-native decision intact.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) Build it as designed — a gated pass emitting `sme_consideration` gaps with the grounding spectrum.
(b) Build only the RECORDING half: a way to mark a node as agent-proposed-not-user-stated with its grounding, and let the skills do the proposing. Much smaller; keeps the honest-provenance value and drops the pass machinery.
(c) Declare it superseded by agent-native capture and retire the doc's requirement rather than leaving it ⬜ forever.
(d) Nothing — it has been ⬜ for over three weeks and no user has asked for it.

NOTE ON RELEVANCE, which is Anthony's actual question: `provenance: inferred` and the SUPPLEMENTS edge both already exist in the schema, so (b) is closer than (a) looks. Whether anyone WANTS this is unanswered — it has never been put to a user, and no friction report has asked for it.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 build SME augmentation, the LLM-as-subject-matter-expert pass? Designed in full 2026-07-17, never built, never in the graph

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-13.

HIS WORDS: "how does a requirement (actually the whole chain from idea --> fully implemented/fielded) become immutable? I suppose a user could declare at some point - this lifecycle is immutable, but for could we do something like the less times a full life cycle is adjusted/updated, the more stable it is - eventually becoming immutable - again, some parallels on Q-table from RL. like for instance, in reflow2, there are probably a few lifecycles that that have emerged as statistically stable and rarely changing"

⭐ WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE NODE FROM `dec:idea-a-satisfied-requirement-earns-a-stricter-mutability-class`. That node's triggers are all STATE-based — satisfied, verified, operational, shipped in a deployed release. This one is EVIDENCE-based: protection is inferred from observed behaviour rather than from a lifecycle position. They compose; they are not the same mechanism.

📌 AND SEPARATE FROM `dec:idea-what-gets-searched-repeatedly-is-becoming-important`, which shares the RL framing and asks the opposite question about the opposite signal: that one would raise a node's IMPORTANCE from repeated READS, this one would raise a thread's IMMUTABILITY.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SHARPENED SAME DAY — THE GOAL IS NOT IMMUTABILITY, IT IS KNOWING
WHAT A SECOND USER DEPENDS ON, AND BOTH PROPOSALS ARE PROXIES FOR IT
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Anthony, 2026-08-13, naming where the whole thread came from:

"this all started out of a comment from my brother that was 'As long as it doesn't mess with the core functionality.' however, I don't know exactly how he uses reflow2. so trying to figure out something that is either use based (something that is used a lot is probably liked and stable) or has not changed (what we just discussed)."

⭐⭐ **THAT REFRAMES BOTH PROPOSALS AS PROXIES FOR ONE UNOBSERVABLE: what Alex depends on.** "Core functionality" is HIS phrase about HIS usage, and the reason a mechanism is being designed at all is that the fact is not available. Every option below should be judged on how well it stands in for asking him — not on how elegant the metric is.

🛑 **AND THE BASELINE ANY PROXY MUST BEAT IS: ASK HIM.** He is one message away, `dec:three-party-checks` says the human decides, and a point-blank question returns the fact itself rather than a correlate of it. The honest case for a proxy is NOT that it beats asking Alex — it is that it generalises to the users who cannot be asked, which is the actual product case. Recorded so the cheap answer is not skipped on the way to the interesting one.

═══ ⭐⭐⭐ THE GRAPH ALREADY PARTLY ANSWERS "I DON'T KNOW HOW HE USES IT" ═══

`fact:second-user-report-2026-08-11` records Alex's own working path VERBATIM, and it is more specific than either proxy would produce:

  step 1  "record those at a high level"     -> capture-intent    NOT NAMED BY HIM
  step 2  "now let's order them"             -> plan-increments   NOT NAMED BY HIM
  step 3  "tackle them one at a time"        -> his own framing
  step 4  "and brainstorm"                   -> brainstorm        NAMED, he types it
  entry   "basically been using /where-am-i" -> where-am-i        NAMED, he types it

🛑🛑 **AND THIS IS THE MEASUREMENT THAT DAMAGES THE USE-BASED PROXY, taken from the one real second user we have.** A usage counter would have found `where-am-i` and `brainstorm` — the two he TYPES — and would have scored `capture-intent` and `plan-increments` at ZERO, even though he performs their function every session in his own words. **USE TELEMETRY MEASURES WHAT GETS INVOKED, NOT WHAT GETS DEPENDED ON**, and for this project the gap between those is not incidental: it is `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`, ACCEPTED, whose whole content is that the trigger mechanism does not reach the user.

⇒ Worse for the proxy: the thing Alex most obviously depends on is the thing NOTHING would count. His four-step path silently assumes the design is still there and still coherent between sessions. No skill invocation represents "the graph still says what I told it last week."

═══ THE USE-BASED BRANCH IS NOT A NEW IDEA — IT IS A DESIGNED, UNBUILT THREAD ═══

  `req:reflow2-can-say-which-of-its-own-skills-a-session-reached-for`  ACCEPTED, and it is one of the
      top open gaps: NOTHING SATISFIES IT. "recorded automatically, reported without judgement."
  `dec:how-should-reflow2-log-its-own-usage`      OPEN — where the log lives. `what_next` ranks it
      SECOND of the unmarked decisions (1 governed, 1 scheduled into an increment).
  `dec:idea-measure-the-surface`                  OPEN — should real telemetry shape the surface, how far.
  `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content`  ACCEPTED — the verb, never the object.
  `dec:the-telemetry-kpp-question-waits-for-flo2` DEFERRED, with its trigger named.

🛑 **THE FATAL CONSTRAINT ON THE USE-BASED BRANCH, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL: THE SIGNAL IS ON ALEX'S MACHINE.** Every design graph is local (`dec:multi-writer-architecture`); his usage never touches this store. So "used a lot" is unmeasurable HERE by construction, and no amount of instrumenting reflow2's own repo produces it — it would measure Anthony's usage and call it Alex's.

⭐⭐ **WHICH MAKES THE PREREQUISITE A DECISION THAT SCORES ZERO — AND ALEX ASKED FOR IT HIMSELF.**
`dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded` ("should reflow2 ask, once, whether a project wants to send feedback back, and record that consent in the graph?") is the gate on ever seeing another user's usage. `what_next` surfaced it as the **`unexplored` draw — score 0, nothing in the graph points at it.** And `fact:second-user-report-2026-08-11` records Alex requesting exactly it: *"You should put in an update that asks me if I want to collect feedback and store my decision in the graph or something. That way you get what you want."*

⇒ **THE SECOND USER ASKED FOR THE MECHANISM THAT WOULD ANSWER HIS OWN CONCERN, AND THE GRAPH SCORES IT AT ZERO BECAUSE NOTHING POINTS AT IT.** This is precisely the failure `what_next`'s exploration band exists for, arriving on a real question rather than as a worry about ranking.

📌 AND `bl-155` APPLIES TO THE USE PROXY UNCHANGED: reflow2 cannot tell "unused" from "unreachable". `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` already drew the consequence — counts may justify OPTIMISING and never, alone, justify CUTTING. A mutability class derived from use would be using counts to decide what is protected, which is the mirror of the move that rule forbids, and it inherits the same blindness: the four skills Alex never invokes are unreached, not unwanted.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE Q-TABLE FRAMING IS ALREADY SETTLED DOCTRINE HERE, AND IT
ARRIVES IN THIS DOMAIN WITH ONE TERM ANSWERED DIFFERENTLY
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

`dec:attention-is-measured-behaviourally-not-lexically` is **ACCEPTED** on Anthony's own word (2026-08-10). Its three consequences apply verbatim and should not be re-derived:

(1) **A Q-VALUE DECAYS AND A COUNTER DOES NOT.** Here it bites harder: "has not changed in three months" IS a recency statement.

(2) **VISIT COUNT IS NOT VALUE — and there, the analogy BROKE:** *"THERE IS NO REWARD SIGNAL… The RL framing supplies STRUCTURE (decay, exploration) and does NOT supply the thing that makes Q-learning converge."*
⭐⭐ **THIS IS WHERE THE DOMAINS PART.** A design thread HAS a reward signal already in the graph — 40 DriftEvents, verification runs with `last_run_at`, `OBSOLETES`, releases reaching an Environment. Contact with reality, observed rather than proxied. **Note this beats BOTH of Anthony's candidates on their own terms**: it is neither "was not edited" nor "was invoked often", but "was exercised and did not break."

(3) **THE EXPLORATION TRAP.** For stability it is a feedback loop with the sign wrong: the harder something is to change, the less it is revisited, the more stable it scores.

═══ HIS EMPIRICAL CLAIM, TESTED ON REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN 2026-08-13 ═══

  ChangeEvents per ACCEPTED requirement (110):  0→67  1→21  2→21  5→1
  ChangeEvents per Capability (152):            0→58  1→52  2→22  3→10  4→6  5→2  6→1  7→2
  whole-thread (req + caps + artifacts) zero-change:  6 of 110
  CHANGED edges land:  art 555 · cap 180 · req 87 · dec 62 · cmp 43 · other 59

🛑🛑 **AT NODE LEVEL THE METRIC INVERTS.** `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` carries an 8,842-character statement; the sibling node records +4,770 characters appended in a single session. Its history: **0 ChangeEvents, 0 Snapshots.** ⇒ **THE MOST HEAVILY REWRITTEN REQUIREMENT IN THE DESIGN SCORES MAXIMALLY STABLE.** It measures RECORDING DISCIPLINE.

🛑 **AT THREAD LEVEL IT FAILS THE OPPOSITE WAY**, and the thread is the unit he chose: only 6 of 110 are quiet, because artifact churn dominates. Intent-only scoping (req 87 + dec 62 = 149 against art 555) may rescue it.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none taken ═══

A — COUNT RECORDED REVISIONS, threshold into a mutability class. **The measurements say do not build it**: it ranks the worst offenders safest.

B — FIX THE RECORD FIRST, then count. Require a revision to a satisfied requirement to leave a Snapshot + ChangeEvent. Already named on the sibling node as "the cheapest honest option", and a prerequisite either way.

C — SCORE ON EVIDENCE OF EXERCISE, NOT ON SILENCE OR ON INVOCATION. Checks that have RUN and passed across releases, no DriftEvent, no OBSOLETES. The only option with a real reward term, immune to the recording hole, and **local — it needs nothing from Alex's machine**. Expensive: 37 of 139 verifications have never run.

D — SCOPE THE COUNTER TO INTENT ONLY (Requirement + Decision). Restores thread-level signal; concedes the code cannot be frozen.

E — WITHHOLD UNTIL THE HABIT EXISTS. `consumption.rs`'s `MIN_MODELLED_RATIO` shape: **absence is only informative when presence is the habit.**

F — USE-BASED, and it is a DEPENDENT rather than an alternative. Blocked on `dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded` (consent), `dec:how-should-reflow2-log-its-own-usage` (where the log lives) and `req:reflow2-can-say-which-of-its-own-skills-a-session-reached-for` (unsatisfied). Bounded by `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content`. **And measured against the one real second user it would have missed half his workflow.**

G — ASK ALEX. Returns the fact rather than a correlate, costs one message, does not generalise. **The baseline the others must beat.**

⇒ **C IS THE STRONGEST ON THE EVIDENCE** — it is the only candidate that is local, has a genuine reward term, and cannot be fooled by silence — with **B** as its prerequisite for anything history-shaped and **E** as the guard. **F is worth having for its own sake** (it answers "what do users reach for", which is an accepted unmet requirement) but is a poor instrument for THIS question. **G should happen regardless.**

═══ THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded beside the idea ═══

TIME-WITHOUT-CHANGE AND CORRECTNESS ARE NOT THE SAME THING, and neither are USE AND CORRECTNESS. A requirement nobody revisited may be settled, forgotten, or wrong in a way nobody looked hard enough to notice; a heavily-used path may be heavily used because it is unavoidable rather than because it is liked. Both proxies would make reflow2 most confident where it has looked least — and `bl-155`'s unused-versus-unreachable finding, now restated four times in this design, says the graph cannot tell the difference from inside.

NOT DECIDED. The narrow question worth answering first is unchanged and now trebly supported — by both mutability proposals and by the use branch, which cannot detect a silent rewrite either: **should a revision to a satisfied requirement be required to leave a trace?**

properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, from a first-pass review of openmbee.org — website, repository listing and one truncated architecture page. THE OBSERVATION: Flexo's stated guiding principle is 'to adopt open, web-compatible standards for data exchange at every interface, including for both data format and exchange protocols', realised as a layered stack of micro-services where each layer is independently developed, tested and replaced, and where the seams speak SPARQL, GraphQL, OSLC and SysML v2. WHY THIS ONE IS UNCOMFORTABLE RATHER THAN MERELY INTERESTING: reflow2 measured its own seam band at 0.0% on 2026-08-03 — 73 component-to-component couplings, none of them running through a declared contract that one side provides and another consumes. BL-179 establishes that this is a NORMAL POSITION for a design that correctly did function first, and that finding stands. But OpenMBEE is a design of comparable ambition that made seam declaration a FOUNDING principle rather than a later phase, and holding the two side by side is the fairest available test of whether function-first is a trajectory or an excuse. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is not weak: standards at every interface is a rule with a price — it is why Flexo is a multi-service deployment where reflow2 is a single binary and a file in a repository, and `dec:install-once-per-machine` plus `req:thin-install` are commitments in the opposite direction. An internal seam between two modules of one binary does not need SPARQL; it needs to exist and be named. THE NARROWER VERSION WORTH TAKING SERIOUSLY: not 'every interface speaks a web standard' but 'every seam is DECLARED', which is reflow2's own `req:key-interfaces` already, unmet at 0%. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: whether declaring reflow2's internal seams changes any computation — `dec:edge-orthogonality` says a distinction earns its keep only when something reads it, and today the seams band reads it, which is one reader more than there was a week ago.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 adopt OpenMBEE's rule that every interface speaks an open, published protocol?
properties.rationale: Recorded through the brainstorm skill at Anthony's request. The claim of strength here is about the PRINCIPLE as stated, not about its execution: the architecture page was truncated on fetch, no source was read, and whether Flexo's interfaces actually hold that line is unknown and is exactly what the deep review should test. Recorded beside the counter-argument per the skill's rule that an idea killed in conversation loses its reasoning while an idea recorded with its objection keeps both — and the objection here is real, since reflow2's single-binary posture is a deliberate decision rather than an oversight.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING. Anthony, 2026-08-20, extending the flo2 chain-effect argument: *"if we can modularize reflow2 and know which functions that each module is supposed to perform, we can then do more encompassing testing (what are the edge cases, what are the failure modes, etc) that we might not be able to perform now."*

THE THIRD LEG OF ONE ARGUMENT. Modularization has now been argued for three distinct returns, and they are not the same return restated:
  1. SUBSTITUTABILITY — swap a module for another that meets the contract
  2. CHANGE PROPAGATION — follow a flo2-levied requirement along a chain (`fact:every-boundary-reaches-the-same-36-components-so-severability-is-not-computable`)
  3. DERIVABLE TESTING — this node

⭐ WHAT IS ALREADY THERE: function IS allocated. 138 ALLOCATED_TO edges put capabilities on components, so "which module performs which function" is largely answerable today.

🛑 WHAT IS NOT: the SHAPE of the function. `Capability.inputs` / `Capability.outputs` are declared in the schema and have NO typed tool to write them, NO instruction telling anyone to, and NO detector that notices their absence — the exact three-legged failure recorded in `fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it`. Edge cases are derived from the boundaries of an input domain and failure modes from what an output promises; with neither stated, both can only be imagined.

📌 AND IT MEETS THE VERIFICATION FINDING FROM THE SAME DAY: reflow2 holds 175 Verifications, 175 of kind `verification` and 0 of kind `validation`, 168 of method `test`. Every check asks whether the code matches the spec. Failure-mode work is the other question, and `Verification.method` already carries `analysis` and `inspection` — the FMEA-shaped methods — unused.

IDEAS: (a) make inputs/outputs writable and instructed, then ask for them where a Capability is allocated to a Component; (b) a detector for an allocated capability with no stated interface shape; (c) nothing — derive edge cases from the code as today, and accept that they are imagined rather than derived.

⚠️ COUNTER, and it is the standing one: `req:design-anything` keeps the vocabulary neutral, and "inputs and outputs" is comfortable for software and awkward for a building. Whether the shape generalises is unexamined.

⚠️ NOT COSTED, and nobody has asked for it. Recorded as the third return on a modularization nobody has scheduled.
properties.name: OPEN — the third thing modularization buys: if a module's function, inputs and outputs are stated, edge cases and failure modes become derivable rather than imagined

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing is planned and nothing is claimed as intent. Anthony, 2026-08-20, thinking out loud off the black-box thread: *"if we clearly define an interface between all the black boxes, we should have the ability to change any module for another (provided it still meets the contract). One I was thinking about (mostly just as a demo/hypothetical), but maybe we change out dynograph-foundation for something easier that is actually part of reflow2?"*

DEDUP DONE BY HAND before writing (the guard was not used because long-body writes were malforming this session): `search_design` surfaced and I read `dec:idea-is-the-foundation-a-subsystem-or-a-supplier` and `fact:the-diamond-meets-at-dynographs-internals-not-its-interface`. This is distinct from the first — that asks what the foundation IS, this asks whether to REPLACE it and whether replacing it is the right demo — and it uses the second as evidence rather than restating it.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 THE ANSWER TO "CAN WE?" IS NO, TODAY, AND THAT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE

reflow2's own substitutability test says a box is swappable when it PROVIDES an interface carrying a machine-readable contract (`SPECIFIES`). Measured 2026-08-19: 4 of 15 Interfaces carry one, and they are `ifc:core-api`, `ifc:graph-export`, `ifc:mcp-tools`, `ifc:mcp-tools-http` — all reflow2's OWN. **NOT ONE of the five `ifc:req-dyno-*` interfaces has a contract.** So the thing being proposed for swapping is, by this design's own criterion, not swappable: we would be replacing it against an unwritten specification.

⭐ WHICH IS WHY THE HYPOTHETICAL IS WORTH MORE THAN THE SWAP. It is a forcing function. Writing those five contracts is work `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` demands anyway ("both sides of every contract modelled at each level"), and until they exist "can we swap X?" is not answerable, only arguable. The demo cannot start until the design does the thing it has been putting off.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📐 IT IS NOT ONE SWAP. IT IS FIVE, AND THEY DIFFER BY 48x

Measured at HEAD 2026-08-19 by what actually imports what:

  interface                     crate                  files importing it
  ifc:req-dyno-core-api         dynograph_core         48
  ifc:req-dyno-storage-api      dynograph_storage      21
  ifc:req-dyno-graph-api        dynograph_graph         3   (allocate, flow, structure)
  ifc:req-dyno-resolution-api   dynograph_resolution    2   (ingest, seam)
  ifc:req-dyno-vector-api       dynograph_vector        1   (dimensions)

🛑 `dynograph_core` AT 48 FILES IS NOT A MODULE, IT IS THE TYPE VOCABULARY. A black-box swap presumes the contract is NARROWER than the implementation behind it; when the supplier's types are the language 48 files are written in, replacing it is not substitution, it is a rewrite with a substitution's name on it. The same is largely true of storage at 21.

✅ THE OTHER THREE ARE GENUINELY SMALL — 3, 2 and 1 files — and they are the real candidates.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ ONE RISK THAT LOOKS REAL AND IS NOT

storyflow also depends on dynograph, so "does removing it break the sibling?" is the obvious worry. `fact:the-diamond-meets-at-dynographs-internals-not-its-interface` already answers it: storyflow consumes dynograph as a **REST API over HTTP** while reflow2 consumes it as a **Rust library API** — disjoint surfaces over one shared implementation. reflow2 dropping the Rust surface cannot touch storyflow's endpoints. The diamond does not meet where a swap would cut.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
IDEAS, unranked, each with what it costs

**A. WRITE THE FIVE CONTRACTS FIRST, DECIDE SECOND.** Cheapest, and required regardless. Turns the question from arguable to answerable, and may well end with "we only ever wanted to swap one of them".
   ⚠️ It is not free: a contract for a Rust library API means writing down what is actually depended on, which for `core` at 48 files is a real excavation.

**B. SWAP THE SMALLEST ONE AS THE DEMO — `dynograph_vector`, ONE FILE (`dimensions.rs`).** A genuine substitution, end to end, behind a written contract. If the mechanism works there it works, and a failed attempt costs one file.
   ⭐ This is the strongest evidence-per-unit-cost of anything here, and it makes the claim CONCRETE rather than architectural.
   ⚠️ Vector search and HNSW are not trivial to reimplement well; "easier" may mean "worse" in ways only load reveals.

**C. SWAP THE THREE SMALL ONES (graph algorithms, resolution, vector — 6 files total) AND KEEP core+storage.** Removes three external surfaces, leaves the substrate alone.
   ⚠️ Honest counter: keeping core and storage means the dependency stays, so the upgrade treadmill stays. The saving is partial and should not be sold as removal.

**D. REPLACE THE WHOLE FOUNDATION.** What the question literally asks.
   ⚠️ 69 files touch core+storage. This is a rewrite of the substrate, and the anti-over-engineering objection is at its strongest: dynograph WORKS, is maintained, and v0.13.0 was measured clean on a real build 2026-08-19 with the pin bump parked awaiting Anthony's call. Rewriting a working, maintained dependency to prove a modelling point is the textbook version of the thing he warns about — unless the demo value or the independence is judged worth it, which is his call and not the agent's.

**E. DO NOTHING AND SETTLE THE PRIOR QUESTION INSTEAD.** `dec:idea-is-the-foundation-a-subsystem-or-a-supplier` is open: is dynograph a NINTH SUBSYSTEM of reflow2, or a supplier reached across required interfaces? The swap question PRESUPPOSES "supplier". Answering the prior question may dissolve this one.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📌 WHY THIS IS A GOOD DEMO IF IT HAPPENS, stated once so the value is not overclaimed

reflow2 tells users their design will let them change one part for another. Demonstrating that on its OWN foundation is the strongest available evidence for the claim, and it is self-host used the way the standing rule permits: as evidence ABOUT the product, not as the point. The five `ifc:req-dyno-*` interfaces are also the ONLY ownership-boundary seam reflow2 has modelled at all — so this is the one place the black-box claim can currently be tested.

⚠️ AND THE HONEST BOUND: none of the above has been costed. No estimate of what replacing even `dynograph_vector` takes has been made, and "1 file imports it" is a measure of BLAST RADIUS, not of difficulty.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 replace dynograph-foundation with its own implementation, and is that the right first proof that a black box can actually be swapped?
properties.rationale:
DECLINED BY ANTHONY, 2026-08-20, in the same session it was raised: "I don't want to really swap out dynograph-foundation (it works and putting a lot of effort into this is probably not worth it if we aren't going to really swap it out)."

THE REASONING IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING, because it is a general rule and not a fact about dynograph: a demo that costs as much as the real thing is not a demo. The value of proving substitutability was never in doubt — what he refused is paying full replacement cost for evidence, on a dependency that works and is maintained. That is his standing anti-over-engineering position applied to reflow2 itself rather than to a user's design.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE, stated so the rejection is not read wider than it is:
· It does not settle `dec:idea-is-the-foundation-a-subsystem-or-a-supplier`, which stays open.
· It does not say the five `ifc:req-dyno-*` interfaces should stay without contracts. `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` (ACCEPTED) still demands both sides of every contract modelled, and those five are the only ownership-boundary seam reflow2 has. What is declined is writing them IN ORDER TO SWAP.
· It does not reject option E; the prior question is untouched.

⭐ AND THE FINDING SURVIVES THE REJECTION, which is why this node is kept rather than deleted: the measurement that the swap is IMPOSSIBLE TODAY — not one of the five required interfaces carries a machine-readable contract, so reflow2 cannot swap the one boundary it has actually modelled — is a fact about the design's maturity, independent of whether anyone ever wanted to swap. It is the sharpest available statement of how far the black-box claim is from being demonstrable, and it was found by asking a question whose answer turned out to be no.

properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, from a first-pass review of openmbee.org — website and repository listing only, deep review pending. THE OBSERVATION: OpenMBEE's active development is not its stable product. MMS 4 stores models in SQL; the successor, Flexo / MMS 5, moves to an RDF quadstore and is described as 'GitHub for graphs', exposing SPARQL, GraphQL, OSLC and a SysML v2 API. A separate experimental SysML v2 execution environment (`Systemica`, Go) is also under way. Commits across those repositories were days old when reviewed (July–August 2026), so this is a live bet, not an aspiration. WHERE reflow2 STANDS: it has its own vocabulary — 29 node types, 60 edge types — and no standard interchange of any kind. It publishes three interfaces (`ifc:core-api`, `ifc:graph-export`, `ifc:mcp-tools`), and `export_surface` already emits a subset of a design deliberately. THE QUESTION IS NOT WHETHER TO ADOPT SysML v2 INTERNALLY — the vocabulary is load-bearing and `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition` and `req:functional-vocabulary-computes` both depend on it — but whether reflow2 should be able to SPEAK it at the edge, in and out. THE ARGUMENT FOR: Anthony works in a defence/aerospace systems-engineering context and will be asked, professionally, why a design tool does not interoperate with the standard his field is converging on. An export that a SysML v2 service can ingest is a different claim from an export only reflow2 reads. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT: SysML v2 is large, its tooling is young, and a partial mapping that silently drops what it cannot express would be worse than none — reflow2's whole posture is that a lossy translation must be reported, not quietly performed. Mapping 29 types onto SysML v2 would need the same no-silent-drop discipline `changelog_view` holds with `unmapped`. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: whether a faithful SUBSET mapping exists that reports what it could not carry.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 speak SysML v2 at its boundary, given that is where the standards gravity has moved?

The strength claimed here is narrow and should be read narrowly: OpenMBEE has committed to a standard interchange and reflow2 has none. Whether their SysML v2 implementation is any good is exactly what the deep review is for, and nothing in this node asserts that it is.

properties.decision:
**DECIDED 2026-08-19 BY ANTHONY**, on a two-part question put to him with recommendations:

**(1) `Constraint` IS the right home for a closed value set with no schema file — and its framing gets fixed.** He took the recommended option over an honest refusal and over a split rule. **(2) The fix reaches ALL THREE SURFACES** that describe Constraint as numeric — the `capture-intent` routing table, the served `AGENTS.md`, and `add_constraint`'s own tool description — rather than skills-only or additive-only.

His reasoning is carried by the options he declined: an honest refusal would have been conceptually cleaner but leaves a fileless user with nothing actionable AND still requires fixing Constraint for the prohibition case anyway; the split rule ("Constraint for prohibitions, refusal for enums") asks the agent to draw a line subtle enough to erode.

⇒ DELIVERED the same day, `epoch:constraint-is-not-only-numeric`.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐⭐ THE FINDING THAT RESHAPED THE QUESTION — **THE FORK DISSOLVED WHEN SOMETHING OUTSIDE THE DESIGN WAS CHECKED**

The node originally asked whether the vocabulary has a home for an enum. **It has two, both already in the schema, and the served surface instructed NEITHER.** The method is `dec:agent-navigates-content`'s own rationale: *"before choosing between branches of a fork, ask what already exists that would make the fork unnecessary. Design inward only after looking outward."* That decision records two prior forks dissolving this way; **this is the third.**

**HOME 1 — THE SCHEMA FILE, and it is the one that scales.** `SPECIFIES` is `Artifact → [Interface, Capability, Component]` with `format: openapi / protobuf / json_schema / graphql / asyncapi / idl` (schema/build.yaml:72-81). **An enum is defined IN a schema file.** Register the file, point the edge at what it defines; the agent reads it, the graph records where it is. No schema change, no new node type, and a project with fifty enums does not get fifty nodes.
  🛑 MEASURED: `SPECIFIES` appeared in exactly ONE served skill (`link-artifacts`, "on the interface it defines"). Its Capability and Component targets were documented **nowhere**, and `capture-intent` never mentioned it.
  🛑🛑 **AND `SPECIFIES` HAS NO TYPED TOOL.** Nine typed edge tools exist (`realizes`, `documents`, `satisfies`, `provides`, `consumes`, `constrains`, `allocate`, `decomposes`, `verifies`); SPECIFIES is not among them, so `create_edge` is the only way to draw it. **`skill_lint` caught this during the fix** — the new row named a `specifies` tool that does not exist and the build went red. That is the "three legs" gap in the open: instruction now present, tool still absent.

**HOME 2 — `Constraint`, for a value rule stated as intent with no file yet.** Requires ONLY `name` and `statement` (schema/core.yaml:77-99); `quantity`/`limit`/`direction` all default null. Its own hint reads *"A limit or rule the design MUST respect… 'no PII leaves the device'"* — the same sentence shape as *"status is one of draft, submitted, paid."*
  🛑 **A KNOWN, MEASURED, UNFIXED DEFECT UNTIL NOW.** `fact:defect-the-constraint-vocabulary-is-documented-as-numeric-so-the-right-node-is-ruled-out` (2026-08-15, `basis: measured`, graded HIGH by its own author): a genesis session modelling the US federal government read the prose, concluded *"numeric budgets only"*, and **left eleven constitutional prohibitions as Requirements that would report unsatisfied forever.** Its stated cost: *"it never produced an error — it produced a confident wrong conclusion."*

🛑🛑 **AND THE ROUTING TABLE BUILT FOR ALEX'S FIRST REPORT HAD INHERITED THAT EXACT DEFECT.** `capture-intent`:50 read **"a number with a unit"** as the only Constraint row. So the fix shipped in `c863a4b` (#180) to stop the agent handing modelling questions back to the user **carried the numeric-only framing measured as HIGH four days earlier**, with no row for a prohibition, a value set, or a schema file. Not wrong sentence-by-sentence — **narrower than the schema, in exactly the way that had already produced a confident wrong conclusion once.**

⭐ SO THE TWO DIAGNOSES COLLAPSED INTO ONE. The node asked "did the instruction fail, or is there no home?" **Neither. The homes existed and the instruction never named them** — so the agent, correctly finding no matching row, did the one thing the table's last row forbids and asked the user, rather than saying "no good home for this yet". Which was not even true.

📌 WHAT IS **NOT** SETTLED BY THIS, so it is not read as closing more than it does: `req:vocabulary-covers-information` (`deferred`) asks for something genuinely different and genuinely absent — entities two components exchange **in a form a computation can read**, so the graph can tell two interfaces carry the SAME entity and map one organisation's field to another's under a different name and unit. **That is the semantic-interoperability layer and NOTHING here delivers it.** A pointer an agent reads is not a type a detector can reason over. Kept apart deliberately.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 THE RECURRENCE, WHICH STANDS AND IS THE REASON THIS WAS INVESTIGATED

  · **2026-08-14** — Alex asked what node types to store his data models as.
  · **2026-08-14** — settled as `dec:idea-the-graph-vocabulary-never-reaches-the-user`; option (c), agent judgement, CLOSED as "observed failing".
  · **`c863a4b` (#180)** — *"Never ask the user which node type to use."* Merged.
  · **2026-08-18** — same user, asked how to model "enums". His reply: *"I don't know, you figure out how to model enums."* ANTHONY: *"he considers that reflow2 + agent's responsibility (and I agree), not his job to define how to model something."*

⭐ **THE FIX WAS PRESENT IN THE SERVED TEXT AND THE BEHAVIOUR RECURRED** — and the finding above says why, which is more useful than "agents drift": the instruction shipped **with a table that could not answer the question**. That is fixable without making the instruction louder.
