🛑 STILL TRUE: a leaked question leaves no node, so `loop_status` read clean through both exchanges. Nothing in reflow2 can see this happen. `skill_lint` cannot check a table for COMPLETENESS — only that the tools it names exist.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
OPTIONS AS THEY STOOD

(a) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — fix the table at the root: rows for a value set, a prohibition and a schema file, and correct the numeric framing on all three surfaces. Fixes Alex's case AND the measured US-government case in one act.
(b) **NOT SEPARATELY ADOPTED** — generalise the honest refusal into a rule. The table's last row already carries it and the new note strengthens it; not made its own mechanism.
(c) **NOT CHOSEN** — un-defer `req:vocabulary-covers-information`. It is not what Alex needed, it is large, and `dec:agent-navigates-content` argues for the thin answer wherever a pointer will do. **Explicitly still open as its own requirement.**
(d) **NOT CHOSEN, STILL LIVE** — make the leak observable so the agent files a node when it cannot route a modelling question. The only option addressing why this went unnoticed for four days and was found by a user.
(e) **CLOSED** — agent variance; already closed once as observed-failing, and this was its second observation.

⚠️ THE JUDGEMENT ANTHONY MADE, recorded because it was genuinely contestable: an enum is arguably a TYPE DEFINITION rather than a LIMIT, and reflow2's own design carried ~1 Constraint node, so there was almost no worked precedent either way. He ruled that Constraint takes it. **If that proves wrong in use, the fallback named at decision time was the honest refusal, not a new node type.**

⚠️ UNCHANGED TENSION: some vocabulary reaching the user is CORRECT, and *"is this value set fixed by a standard, or does it vary per deployment?"* is a real question only the user can answer. It is not the question that was asked here.
properties.name: DECIDED — a Constraint need not be numeric, and a data model lives in its schema file: both homes existed, neither was instructed, and the routing table had inherited a measured defect
properties.rationale: Raised under the brainstorm skill from Alex's report 2026-08-18; investigated and settled 2026-08-19 on Anthony's instruction to take it on. The node was rewritten rather than merely answered because the investigation changed the question: "is there a home for an enum" turned out to be "there are two, and neither is instructed", which is a far cheaper problem than the one first recorded. The Constraint half is tied to fact:defect-the-constraint-vocabulary-is-documented-as-numeric rather than restated, because that defect was measured four days BEFORE the routing table shipped carrying the same framing — a future session must see that the table inherited a known defect rather than invented one, since that is the argument for checking served prose against the schema generally rather than fixing this one row. req:vocabulary-covers-information is held explicitly outside the ruling so the semantic-interop need is not read as closed. The missing SPECIFIES tool is recorded because skill_lint surfaced it during the fix and it is the "three legs" gap caught in the act.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — surfaced 2026-08-11 reading reflow2's founding docs against the build. Nothing here is intent.

MEASURED, not assumed:
  EnvironmentRule instances in this design            0
  QualityGate instances                               0
  occurrences of `unchecked_compliance` in the code   0
  occurrences of `open_violation` in the code         0
  typed constructor for EnvironmentRule               none
`docs/requirements-coverage.md` carries it as ⬜ three times (GS-9 compliance gaps, WS-4 the write side, WS-5 QualityGate) and its own "Dormant schema scaffolding" section lists Environment compliance as deferred-not-dead.

THE IDEA, from `docs/operating-environment.md` (2026-07-17): a design never exists in a vacuum. A house in Kennewick WA must meet city ordinances, county rules, state requirements, building and fire codes, seismic provisions and occupancy limits; the same house on Mars faces 0.38 g, no atmosphere, radiation shielding, pressure vessels and life support. Change the environment, change the entire constraint space. `Project OPERATES_IN Environment`; `Environment IMPOSES EnvironmentRule[]`; compliance emits `COMPLIES_WITH` or `VIOLATES_RULE`; two detectors (`unchecked_compliance`, `open_violation`) ask the human; swapping the environment is a first-class ChangeEvent that re-evaluates every compliance edge.

⭐ THE DISTINCTION IT CARRIES IS ALREADY IN THE SCHEMA AND IS GOOD: three kinds of rule, kept apart. `Constraint` is SELF-IMPOSED ("budget under $500k"). `DesignRule` is a CHOSEN convention ("branch before pushing"). `EnvironmentRule` is EXTERNALLY IMPOSED — the design cannot negotiate it, only comply, seek a variance, or fail. Only the third is dictated by the world. reflow2 uses the middle one heavily (9 DesignRules, and this session settled the enforcement question on one); it has never used the third at all.

⚠️ THE HONEST COUNTER, and it is strong: reflow2's own domain is SOFTWARE, where the operating environment rarely imposes an authoritative external ruleset, so dogfooding will never exercise this. Every instance would come from a consumer designing a house, a spacecraft or a regulated system — and no such consumer exists yet. Building it would mean building on the doc's argument alone, with no field evidence, which is the opposite of how everything else here has been decided. `rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party` cuts BOTH ways on this: the third party is exactly who would need it, and no third party has asked.

⭐ AND IT IS ANTHONY'S ACTUAL DOMAIN. Space Force systems engineering and NSLS-II beamline work both sit in heavily-regulated operating environments with externally imposed rulesets. The one person using reflow2 is in the domain the feature was designed for and has not reached for it — which is either evidence it is not needed, or evidence that nothing surfaces it. Those are opposite readings of the same silence and nothing distinguishes them today.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) Build the whole layer — constructors, the two detectors, the swap-the-environment ChangeEvent.
(b) Build only the WRITE side (constructors for EnvironmentRule + OPERATES_IN/IMPOSES/COMPLIES_WITH) and no detector, so somebody can record a regulation and see whether the vocabulary fits before a detector is written for it. Contradicts the project's own standing rule that a write side should land WITH its read side (requirements-coverage's WS-4/WS-5 note says exactly this and defers both on purpose).
(c) Retire the scaffolding — `QualityGate` and `EnvironmentRule` are two of the five node types with zero instances, and the project's own test is "unused AND redundant → retire; unused AND not-redundant → defer".
(d) Ask a consumer first. Nothing here is urgent, and the deciding evidence is a real design in a regulated environment.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
═══ 📌 SHARPENED 2026-08-26 BY THE THREE-LEGS SURFACE AUDIT ═══

*Rediscovered independently, which is itself worth recording: the audit reached this layer from the opposite direction — sweeping all 93 declared types for the three legs — and the duplicate guard caught the collision. Four of the audit's five "exists only in the schema" types are THIS subsystem. The 2026-08-11 reasoning above stands unaltered; three things are new.*

**1. THE SPLIT IS EXACT, AND HALF OF IT SHIPPED.** The `environment` domain declares five things:

| declared | tool | instances |
|---|---|---|
| `Environment` (node) | ✅ `add_environment` | 3 |
| `DEPLOYED_TO` | ✅ `deploy_to` | 63 |
| `OPERATES_IN` | ❌ none | **3** |
| `EnvironmentRule` (node) | ❌ none | 0 |
| `IMPOSES` | ❌ none | 0 |
| `COMPLIES_WITH` | ❌ none | 0 |
| `VIOLATES_RULE` | ❌ none | 0 |

⇒ **reflow2 can say WHERE a system runs. It cannot say what rules that place imposes, or whether the design complies.** The 2026-08-11 note read the layer as uniformly dormant; it is not — the locating half works and the compliance half does not.

**2. ⭐ THE SILENCE DILEMMA HAS MOVED, SLIGHTLY.** That note posed two opposite readings of the same silence — "evidence it is not needed" versus "evidence nothing surfaces it" — and said nothing distinguishes them. Something does now: **`OPERATES_IN` carries three edges and no tool writes it.** Some earlier session reached for that vocabulary and fell through to raw `create_edge`, which is precisely the escape hatch the three-legs rule says must not count as reachability. That is not proof of demand, but it is the first evidence on that side of the dilemma, and it came from inside this project rather than from the doc's argument.

**3. A PARKING MECHANISM NOW EXISTS THAT DID NOT ON 2026-08-11.** `vocabulary_coverage` groups unused vocabulary by the schema's own domains and hands back `park_with: decision:vocab:environment` — accepting such a Decision declares the domain deliberately unused, so it stops reading as a hole in every coverage report without retiring anything. That makes a fifth option available:

**(e) ⭐ PARK IT, and let a real request pull it into (a).** Cheap, honest, and the only option that is free to reverse: a parked domain a user later asks for becomes (a) with nothing undone. ⚠️ Counter: parking a specified feature is how a feature stays unbuilt forever, and this waiver lifecycle — `verified` on compliance, and `status: proposed | confirmed | rejected` on violation, where confirmed IS an accepted variance kept and documented — is better thought through than much of what does ship.

📌 A SEPARATE CASE WITH THE SAME SHAPE, recorded here so it is not lost: `SUPPLEMENTS` (build domain, Fragment → Fragment) is the audit's fifth schema-only type and is NOT part of this subsystem. It links an LLM-as-SME supplementary-analysis Fragment to the source it augments, carrying `grounding: verified | extrapolated | speculative | contradicts_known` — storyflow lineage. Specified, unbuilt, unrequested; likely the same disposition, and worth splitting into its own node only if the answer differs.

⚠️ AND (c) IS NOW KNOWN TO BE PARTLY DESTRUCTIVE. Retiring the scaffolding would remove `OPERATES_IN`, which has live edges in this very design. Whatever else is decided, that one is not a clean delete.
properties.name: OPEN — should the Environment / EnvironmentRule compliance layer be built? The schema declares it, nothing writes or reads it, and it is what makes "design a house" concrete
properties.rationale:
Three doc requirements, a schema layer, and a worked Kennewick-vs-Mars argument, all dating to 2026-07-17 with zero instances and zero code. The vocabulary distinction it carries — self-imposed vs chosen vs externally imposed — is sound and already in the schema. What is missing is any evidence a user wants it, including from the one user whose own domain is regulated.

SHARPENED 2026-08-26. The agent's recommendation, offered and not taken: **(e) park now**, on the grounds that three field reports this month (hxm_program, Alex, the storyflow fleet) mention environment compliance zero times, and parking is the only disposition that costs nothing to reverse. The counterweight is the new demand evidence — `OPERATES_IN` used three times through the escape hatch — which is thin but is the first thing to land on that side of a dilemma the original note said nothing could settle. If Anthony reads those three edges as a user reaching for the vocabulary rather than an accident of convenience, (a) or (b) is defensible and the recommendation should be overruled.

Kept as ONE node rather than split: the audit rediscovered this question from the opposite direction, and two nodes asking the same thing in different words is exactly what the duplicate guard exists to prevent.

properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-11, Anthony's word: "yes, I like option A - let's implement." OPTION A CHOSEN — speak on read, gated on the hash. B, C and D are recorded below as considered and not taken.

HIS FRAMING, and it was the right diagnosis: "It sounds like we have the tool, just not used well or surfaced."

⚠️ THE TOOL WAS ALREADY BUILT. `import_graph` takes a `path`, so an agent catches a graph up with the committed record in ONE TOOL CALL and no terminal at all. The CLI flag `--import` is a second route for people without an agent, not the only one. So nothing new was needed on the doing side — only on the noticing side.

⭐⭐ THE MEASURED FINDING THAT SHAPED THE BUILD: `provenance::last_synced` — the content hash this seat believes is at a given path — was WRITTEN BY TWO PATHS AND READ BY ONE. `record_sync` is called by `export_graph` (exchange.rs:207) and by `import_graph` (exchange.rs:382); `last_synced()` was read at exchange.rs:171, inside `export_graph`, and nowhere else. **The design knew at the first moment of a session and spoke at the last** — when you tried to export, hours later, and the stale-seat refusal finally fired. Same family as `dec:one-retire-edge`'s "a marker nothing reads is a comment", except here something did read it, at the wrong moment.

🛑 AND THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT THIS NODE FIRST CARRIED WAS FALSE, which is why the option was buildable at all. It said "I have unexported work" and "someone else's work has arrived" look similar from inside. They do not: `crates/reflow2-core/src/sync.rs` already distinguishes them exactly. File hash == `last_synced` ⇒ the file has not moved ⇒ every difference is the caller's OWN unexported work ⇒ silent. File hash != `last_synced` ⇒ somebody else has been there ⇒ actionable. One comparison, and no false-positive mode on solo work.

WHAT WAS BUILT: `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/sync_debt.rs`, served as the `sync_status` tool and carried on `loop_status` as `record_moved` when there is something to say. One finding per file this seat has synced with — `in_step` / `behind` (the actionable one) / `moved_but_current` / `missing` / `unreadable`. The judgement is BORROWED from `sync::assess_overwrite` rather than reimplemented; this module supplies the enumeration, the gate and the wording.

WHY IT LIVES AT THE MCP LAYER: `reflow2-core` does no file I/O, deliberately and repeatedly (`reconcile_artifacts` makes the caller supply hashes; `granularity` and `consumption` both say so). So the check could NOT go into `loop_status` in core, and belongs in the crate that already does this comparison for `export_graph`.

📌 A COST DECISION, PINNED BY A TEST: the export needed to compare against is the expensive half and the hash check is the cheap half, so `mine` is passed as a CLOSURE and is never built on the in-step path — the one every ordinary session takes. `the_expensive_export_is_not_built_on_the_ordinary_path` makes that a guarantee rather than a style choice.

📌 THE DESCRIPTION BUDGET FORCED THE SHAPE OF THE SURFACE: `loop_status`'s tool description was already at 1493 of 1500 characters, so the contract could not be documented there. Hence a dedicated `sync_status` tool carrying the full contract, with `loop_status` carrying only the finding — which is a self-explaining English sentence and needs no schema to interpret.

WHAT WAS NOT CHOSEN, kept because the roads not taken are part of the design's memory:
- B — AUTO-IMPORT. Closest to what was first asked for. Rejected: `import_graph` is an UPSERT, so an unasked one silently overwrites live session work, and doing it unasked makes it invisible. `dec:ask-not-repair`.
- C — REFUSE ON FIRST READ. Rejected: a refusal on READ is heavy-handed, and a session deliberately working from an older design would meet it every time.
- D — DOCUMENTATION ONLY. Rejected: the answer this project has already found wanting twice; a discipline written down and not triggered is one that does not happen.

⭐ THE DEPENDENCY STILL HOLDS: if `dec:central-host` goes the hosted way for the flo2 case, this question DISSOLVES for those users — there is no local store to catch up, because there is one graph everyone reads live. It stays live for anyone working from a checkout.
properties.name: DECIDED — a graph reports when the shared record has moved ahead of it, gated on a computed content hash, and never acts on it
properties.rationale: Anthony chose option A on 2026-08-11 after being shown that the tool already existed and only the trigger was missing. `dec:multi-writer-architecture` (accepted 2026-07-25) had already committed this project to building "merge-on-pull ergonomics" and that clause had never been cashed, so this settles an unbuilt commitment rather than adding new scope. The node keeps its own refuted counter-argument on the record: the claim that unexported work and somebody else's arrival look alike from inside was disproved by reading sync.rs the same day, and it was that refutation which made option A buildable.

properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-14 BY ANTHONY: **BOTH (a) AND (b).** A served interview step carries *when and what to ask* — in domain language only — and a served routing table carries *how the user's words map to node types*, plus which artifacts to expect for that kind of thing. His reasoning: **neither half is useful alone.** A skill without a table leaves the mapping improvised, which is the failure Alex hit; a table without a skill is never consulted. Option (c), leaving it to agent judgement, is closed — it has now been observed failing on the second user's first real project. Option (d), detecting it, stays rejected-for-a-reason: the evidence never enters the graph.

⇒ SATISFIES `req:the-kind-of-system-is-established-before-its-parts-are-captured` (captured the same day on Anthony's word, from Alex's report). This decision settles HOW that requirement is delivered; the requirement states WHAT is owed.

⭐⭐ THE PRIOR ART SETTLES THE SHAPE, AND ONLY HALF OF IT SURVIVES — `reflow/workflows/00b-framework_selection.json`, read 2026-08-14 at Anthony's pointer:
  · **THE TERMINOLOGY REGISTRY** (`definitions/framework_registry.json`: node → `service`/`gene`/`agent`/`species`) was CORRECTLY REJECTED by `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` (now `dropped`) — cosmetic renaming, plus a load-bearing claim that *"framework choice determines which NetworkX analyses are available"*, which gates capability on a self-declared label. **The routing table decided here is NOT that**: it maps the user's phrasing to reflow2's own unchanged vocabulary, and gates nothing.
  · **THE SEMANTIC-MATCHING INTERVIEW** is what survives, and it is not cosmetic. S-01A: *"Framework selection is an ARCHITECTURAL DECISION, not a configuration choice. Wrong framework = wrong insights."* LESSON-04: *"Framework abstractions must match system semantics. Workflows are state machines (not services), even though both could be 'engineered systems'."* **Its first action is "Ask user to describe the system" — domain language, not node types.**

🛑 **AND THE DROPPED REQUIREMENT HAD ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN THE SURVIVOR.** `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` closes: *"domain as a hint to EXTRACTION and phrasing — what vocabulary the agent uses when talking to the user and reading their documents — without ever gating which computations run. That keeps the honest part of reflow's insight (a biologist should not be told about 'services')."* It was dropped as a registry, its surviving half was named in its own text, **nobody built it, and the second user then walked into exactly that gap.** A road correctly not taken left a fork nobody came back for.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════

RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-14.

HIS WORDS: *"It was a little unsure of how to store the data models for my project in the graph. It asked me what node types it should store them as. I didn't really know for sure so I told it to figure it out. It worked, but that might be confusing for someone who isn't technical… it should probably ask probing questions to figure this out without exposing internal components of the graph structure to the user."*

⭐ THE INVERSION IS THE FINDING. Mapping a person's words onto node types IS the agent's job and is written down as such — `capture-intent` exists to turn what the user said into Requirements / Capabilities / Components / Interfaces, and `describe_schema` exists so the AGENT can discover the vocabulary rather than guess. **The agent had both and handed the question back to the user anyway.** The schema is not under-documented here; the labour was returned to the one person in the room with no reason to know the answer.

🛑 AND REFLOW2 CANNOT SEE THIS HAPPEN. Every detector reasons over nodes already in the graph, and a leaked question leaves no node — the user's confusion lives in the conversation, never in the record. `loop_status` would have read perfectly clean through the whole exchange. **Same shape as `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`: a discipline that exists only as an instruction, with nothing able to observe whether it held.** That is the standing argument for why the table matters as much as the skill line: a table can be wrong in public, an improvisation cannot.

📌 IT ALSO WORKED, WHICH IS THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART. He said *"I told it to figure it out"* and the result was fine. So the cost is not a wrong graph — it is that a non-technical user meeting the same prompt has no such escape, and answering it wrongly would put their design in the wrong shape without either party noticing.

THE OPTIONS AS THEY STOOD.
(a) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — an interview step in the skills: never ask for a node type; ask about the thing itself and do the mapping yourself.
(b) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — a served routing table, phrasing → node type, plus expected artifacts per kind of thing. Precedent: `capture-session` ships one and its first dogfood found a hole in it.
(c) LEAVE IT TO AGENT JUDGEMENT — **CLOSED**, observed failing.
(d) DETECT IT — rejected for a reason: the evidence never enters the graph, so any check would have to live in the harness and read the conversation.

⚠️ ONE HONEST TENSION, UNCHANGED BY THE DECISION: some vocabulary reaching the user is CORRECT. `where-am-i` reports the design back in their words and gap questions are deliberately plain, so the rule is *never make the user choose the internal category* — not *never say a word from the schema*. Drawn loosely it would produce a skill that fights `describe_schema`'s legitimate use.
properties.name: DECIDED — the agent never asks the user to pick a node type: a served interview step carries WHEN and WHAT to ask, a served routing table carries HOW their words map
properties.rationale: Raised under the brainstorm skill from Alex's report and settled the same day on Anthony's word, after reading the reflow prior art he pointed at. The reading changed the shape of the answer: reflow's S-01A turns out to contain two separable things, and reflow2 had dropped both together when only the terminology registry deserved it. Recording that split matters because the surviving half — the semantic-matching interview — was already named in the dropped requirement's own closing paragraph, and a future session finding `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` at `dropped` would otherwise reasonably conclude the whole idea was rejected.

properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-08-26: *"yes, close the contradiction explicitly. go with your recommendation."*

═══ THE CONTRADICTION, AND WHY IT COULD NOT BE LEFT ═══

`dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written` — **ACCEPTED 2026-07-31** — forbids a written orientation document: *"NO START-HERE FILE... a START-HERE.md is `dev_storyflow` in miniature — it would go stale, and STALENESS IN AN ORIENTATION DOCUMENT IS THE WORST PLACE FOR IT."* `rule:design-information-lives-in-the-graph-not-in-documents` says the same as a standing rule.

`.claude/handoff_nudge.py` — **committed 2026-07-23**, eight days earlier — blocked the agent from ending a working session until it wrote exactly such a document into `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/`. **Machine-local, uncommitted, invisible to every reflow2 tool.** Nobody reconciled them for five weeks.

Anthony reached the same conclusion independently on 2026-08-26, from TRANSPORTABILITY rather than staleness: *"I'm not a fan of markdown files... I'm not sure that handoff documents are transportable to different machines (especially if they are stored as memory and are not committed)."* He has a second box (`ajs77`); the note did not exist on it.

═══ THE RESOLUTION ═══

**① The hook is RETIRED.** `.claude/handoff_nudge.py` deleted and its two registrations removed from `.claude/settings.json` (SessionStart and Stop). `tools/loop_nudge.py` is untouched and keeps all four of its registrations — that one enforces the coherence loop, which is computed from graph state and contradicts nothing.

**② `dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written` STANDS UNCHANGED, and its scope is now stated.** It governs ORIENTATION — *"what is this project about, and what does it owe?"* — and that question is answered by `where-am-i`, `what_next`, `loop_status` and `cap:onboarding`, all built. It was never narrowed to make room for the hook; the hook was simply wrong.

**③ THE EXOGENOUS HALF ALREADY HAS A HOME, AND IT IS `TemporalFact`.** This is the part that makes the retirement safe rather than lossy, and it needed no new vocabulary. A handoff note carries two things:

- **Transient state** — *"CI was pending when I stopped"*, *"#345 is a green draft"*. Genuinely ephemeral, and already answerable from `loop_status`, `gh pr checks` and the forge. Writing it down was always a retelling.
- **Durable traps** — *"`gh pr edit` is broken, use `gh api -X PATCH`"*, *"a piped gate returns the wrong exit code"*, *"`--stop-shared` leaks a zombie"*. **These are dated observations about the world, which is exactly what a TemporalFact is**, and the design already carries dozens of them: `fact:the-stale-daemon-cost-five-merged-prs-twice`, `fact:defect-agents-md-said-an-mcp-reconnect-picks-up-a-rebuild-and-a-shared-server-makes-that-false`, `fact:the-target-dir-reached-263-gib-of-this-projects-own-test-binaries`.

⭐ **So the most valuable content of every handoff note was already being written to the graph in parallel, in the right node type, by sessions that also wrote it to a markdown file nobody else could read.** The retirement does not lose it; it stops duplicating it into a place the design cannot see.

═══ THE COST, STATED ═══

⚠️ **Nothing now blocks a session from ending without recording what it learned.** The hook's one real virtue was that it was unavoidable, and this session is evidence that unavoidable works — `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` held tonight precisely because it stopped the build, while four other rules were broken by an agent that had them available and never opened them.

The honest position is that this trades an enforced-but-wrong mechanism for a correct-but-unenforced one, and **that is a real regression on the enforcement axis**. It is accepted because a mechanism that writes to one laptop was never going to survive the second machine, let alone a consumer. Whether the TemporalFact route needs its own trigger is left open and belongs with `dec:idea-a-hotspot-node-holds-the-live-worklist-and-is-deliberately-not-history`, which asks where a working set lives at all.

📌 **A consumer copying reflow2's example would have copied the contradiction** — the hook shipped in `.claude/`, which the installer's neighbours read. That is `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself` applying to the repo's own furniture.
properties.name: DECIDED — the handoff hook is retired: orientation is computed, durable traps are TemporalFacts, and no markdown document carries either
properties.rationale:
Settled by Anthony on 2026-08-26 after the contradiction was put to him with both sides named. He chose to close it rather than let either side quietly win, which was the recommendation.

The decision retires the hook rather than narrowing the accepted decision, because the accepted decision is right and the hook was wrong: it enforced a document whose staleness was the original objection AND whose location made it untransportable, so it failed on both the axis it was argued against and the axis it was never tested on.

The TemporalFact observation is what makes this cheap. It was found by looking at what the memory notes actually contained and noticing the durable half was already in the graph under the right type — so the resolution required no new vocabulary, no new node type, and no build. The enforcement regression is written in rather than glossed, because trading an unavoidable mechanism for a voluntary one is a real loss and a later reader should meet it rather than discover it.

properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Anthony, 2026-08-26, continuing the hub thread.

📌 DISTINCT FROM `dec:idea-a-hub-owns-designs-it-does-not-absorb-...`, which asks what RELATION should express a hub. This asks about CUSTODY AND CURRENCY: where a sub-project's design physically lives, what keeps a hub-held copy from going stale, and whether a sub-project needs a design at all. That node could be answered and leave every question here open.

═══ THE IDEA, IN HIS WORDS ═══

*"each project repo in the master repo gets a `reflow2.json` file within the hub/project-brain repo. it is almost like running adopt skill on each repo, but keeping the resulting reflow2.json within the hub/project-brain repo."*

**And he names the problem in the same breath:** *"if one of the existing repos change, then the reflow2.json in the hub repo may not track that or be current with it. I think it may be unavoidable that adopt skill must be run on each sub-project repo in a master-project to keep currency??"*

═══ ⭐ THE ANSWER MAY ALREADY BE HALF-BUILT, AND IT IS WORTH CHECKING BEFORE DESIGNING ═══

A copy going stale is not a new problem — it is one reflow2 already solves twice, and neither mechanism has been pointed here:

- `sync_status` / `req:stale-seat-knows` — a seat whose graph never caught up must not replace a shared design with a complete-but-older document. **A hub holding N copies is N seats, all of which can go stale.** The refusal machinery exists.
- **A checksum makes staleness computable rather than assumed.** A hub-held copy could carry the child export's `content_hash` and say plainly *"this copy is behind"* — which is the existing hub node's item 4 (last-export-date) with a sharper answer.

⇒ **The honest first move is measurement, not vocabulary:** does a hub-held copy plus a content hash already answer this, making the gap a REPORT rather than a mechanism?

═══ 🛑 "MUST ADOPT BE RE-RUN PER SUB-REPO?" — IT TURNS ON WHAT THE COPY IS FOR ═══

- **If the copy is a CACHE of the child's own design**, re-running `adopt` is the wrong repair: the child should EXPORT and the hub should FETCH. Re-adopting re-derives from source what the child already knows — and worse, **two adopts of the same repo need not agree.** `adopt` is a guided process with human judgement in it, so the hub's copy would drift from the child's by INTERPRETATION, not merely by age. That is a nastier drift than staleness because nothing dates it.
- **If the copy is the ONLY design and the child has none**, re-running adopt is the only route, and the currency problem is real and unavoidable.

**Nothing in the question says which**, and it decides everything downstream.

═══ HIS FINAL QUESTION, AND IT IS THE SHARPEST ═══

*"can the sub-projects exist without a reflow2.json object (either within them or contained in the master hub)?"*

⭐ **This decides whether the hub is a reflow2 feature or a different product.**

- **(i) Every sub-project has its own design; the hub links or caches.** Smallest; uses `link-projects` / `mirror_surface`. ⚠️ Counter: O-02 measured zero of seven siblings exporting — blocked on a nudge problem before a vocabulary one.
- **(ii) Sub-projects have none; the hub holds one per repo.** The idea as stated. ⚠️ Counter: the currency problem above, plus interpretation drift from repeated `adopt`.
- **(iii) Sub-projects need nothing at all; the hub indexes repos directly.** Closest to the retrieval use cases. ⚠️ Counter: **reflow2 has never read a repository's source to build a graph, and `adopt` is a guided human/agent process, not a builder.** This is a new product surface, not an extension of an existing one.

═══ ⚠️ THE COUNTERWEIGHT ═══

**A hub holding N copies is a second source of truth, N times over.** `changelog_view`'s reasoning — nothing is stored, because a stored changelog could disagree with the graph — applies here with MORE force, not less. Every option except (i) manufactures records that can disagree with what they describe, and catching exactly that is reflow2's whole value.

📌 **ONE MEASURED FACT BEARS ON IT:** `fact:the-hub-hand-rolled-its-own-graph-tooling-per-repo-rather-than-waiting` records a real hub carrying `codegraphs/` with a subdirectory **per repository** — option (ii)/(iii)'s shape, already built by hand. But it PREDATES reflow2, so it is inheritance rather than a verdict on what reflow2 should do. That node was corrected twice by its owner; read it before citing it.
properties.name: OPEN — if the hub holds a reflow2.json per sub-repo, what keeps each one current, and can a sub-project exist with no design of its own at all?
properties.rationale:
Recorded as its own question because it asks about CUSTODY AND CURRENCY — where a sub-project's design lives and what keeps a copy honest — which is separate from what RELATION expresses a hub, and separate again from what may CROSS a design boundary.

The three readings of "can a sub-project have no design at all" are kept apart deliberately, because they are not degrees of one answer: (i) is existing machinery, (ii) is a caching problem, and (iii) would require reflow2 to read source to build a graph — something it has never done. Collapsing them would hide that the third is a different product rather than a larger version of the first.

The strongest objection is written at full strength: every option except the first manufactures a second source of truth about a system, which is the failure reflow2 exists to detect. And the interpretation-drift point is recorded because it is the non-obvious half — two runs of a guided process on the same repo need not agree, and no date reveals that.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-08. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen. THE IDEA, his words: allocation of functions to systems/services could be driven by what the system is for — "maybe you allocate functions based on it being fault tolerant or very highly reliable or easily maintainable or based on maximal performance" — and the agent would deduce the likely answer and then ASK ("is this design about performance or reliability or maintainability or highly secure"), because "answering that question really determines how you allocate functions to which services" and "if you don't ask upfront, these cost a lot in having to rework services after they've been already developed". It follows an earlier thought of his in the same conversation: that allocation could be decided by graph theory alone — Leiden communities for clustering, or PageRank to avoid bottlenecks and god nodes — with domain-oriented and function-oriented decomposition "thrown out the window". WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, checked rather than assumed: the `dimension` enum in schema/dimensions.yaml already carries reliability, performance, maintainability, security, scalability, observability, testability, coupling and maturity, attachable to ANY node; `propose_allocation` already clusters the weighted capability graph with Leiden and never auto-applies; `evaluate_allocation` already computes modularity, misplaced capabilities and god-components as selective articulation points; and `ility_report` (BL-184, from Anthony's own correction on 2026-08-03) already maps those computations onto the axis each one informs, emitting named findings and never a score. SO THE DIRECTION IS THE NEW PART: everything above runs GRAPH → ILITY, reading structure and saying what it implies. This idea runs ILITY → GRAPH, stating the attribute and letting it drive the allocation. Same vocabulary, opposite direction of inference, and that direction does not exist. AN OBSERVATION WORTH KEEPING WHATEVER IS DECIDED: the attribute may change not just the OBJECTIVE FUNCTION but WHICH GRAPH IS BUILT. Performance wants the call-frequency / data-volume graph and minimal cross-boundary chatter, which is what Leiden on DEPENDS_ON.weight already does. Reliability wants no articulation points and may deliberately DUPLICATE a function across services so one failure domain cannot take everything — which directly OPPOSES maximal modularity, since a modularity-optimal partition is often reliability-hostile. Maintainability wants things that change together to live together, which is a CO-CHANGE graph, a different edge set entirely. Security wants boundaries following trust and data classification with some nodes separated regardless of coupling — constrained partitioning, not clustering at all. Four attributes, four different graphs over the same functions; any single "run Leiden and allocate" answer silently picks performance. THE ONE THAT IS RUNNABLE TODAY, and it is a cheap falsifiable experiment: maintainability. reflow2 already holds 316 ChangeEvents with CHANGED edges, which IS a co-change graph, already populated, needing no instrumentation — cluster it and diff against evaluate_allocation's current map to see whether things that change together are allocated together. Performance is NOT runnable: evaluate_allocation reports total_internal 1, total_external 0, unweighted_dependencies 1 — one capability-to-capability dependency edge in the whole design, unweighted, which is why modularity reads a meaningless 1.00. Reliability and security have no substrate at all yet. COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea rather than used to argue it down: (1) a service boundary carries obligations no coupling graph encodes — deployment unit, failure domain, team ownership, release cadence, data residency, regulatory scope — so two functions Leiden puts together may belong apart because one is audited and one is not, and no resolution parameter can see that; (2) this project has already paid twice for metric-driven verdicts, retiring `unexpected_coupling` because it fired on correct architecture ("that coupling IS the product") and accepting SPOFs deliberately in dec:sanitize-spof-accepted and dec:service-spof-accepted, so a purely metric-driven allocator would flag all three and be wrong each time; (3) clustering on ESTIMATED weights is an opinion with extra steps and a modularity score on top, which is worse than the opinion because it looks objective — the schema's own weight_basis (estimated / evidence / measured) exists to keep that distinction visible. WHERE THE IDEA IS STRONGEST, narrower than "replace the old methods": it makes allocation ARGUABLE. Today domain-versus-function is unfalsifiable and the louder voice wins; computing modularity, bottleneck centrality and cross-boundary weight for candidate allocations turns it into evidence — which is the shape register_alternative / analyze_alternatives already have, with dec:parallel-alternatives putting AoA alternatives in design-space via CONTRADICTS.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐ THE MAINTAINABILITY EXPERIMENT WAS RUN, 2026-08-21, AND IT CONFIRMS THE FOUR-GRAPHS OBSERVATION WITH NUMBERS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Anthony returned to this on 2026-08-21: "should allocation be done in the graph by what communities of nodes form and then draw a boundary around them and say that is service x?" — the same idea, asked directly. Two things were RE-MEASURED rather than re-read, and one experiment this node called runnable was actually run.

RE-MEASURED, AND UNCHANGED AFTER 13 DAYS. `evaluate_allocation` still reports total_internal 1, total_external 0, unweighted_dependencies 1 — ONE capability-to-capability dependency edge in the whole design. So THE PERFORMANCE BRANCH IS STILL NOT RUNNABLE, exactly as this node said. What HAS changed is that `modularity` now reads `None` instead of a meaningless 1.00 — #261 stopped the tool reporting a perfect score over an empty structure, which is the defect fact:defect-allocation-health-is-green-over-an-empty-structure recorded.

CONFIRMED IN THE CODE: `propose_allocation` does cluster with Leiden (allocate.rs:315) and does not auto-apply. So the mechanism Anthony is asking about EXISTS and deliberately stops short of drawing the boundary.

🔬 THE CO-CHANGE EXPERIMENT, RUN ON DATA THAT NEEDED NO INSTRUMENTATION:
    562 ChangeEvents; 246 touch two or more nodes
    536 co-change observations between Components, via the artifacts they realize
    380 of 536 — 71% — CROSS A SUBSYSTEM BOUNDARY

⚠️ AND IT IS NOT A HUB ARTIFACT, which was the first thing to suspect. `cmp:service` is the router every new tool touches and accounts for 36% of observations; removing it entirely leaves 343 observations of which 241 cross — 70%, unchanged. The signal survives its own most obvious confound.

WHAT THAT MEANS, stated carefully: things that CHANGE TOGETHER in reflow2 are mostly NOT ALLOCATED TOGETHER. That is not a defect and this node should not be read as finding one. The decomposition is deliberately FUNCTIONAL (dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition: "the functional systems a design-graph tool IS"), and co-change disagreeing with function is EXACTLY WHAT THE FOUR-GRAPHS OBSERVATION ABOVE PREDICTS. The prediction was made before the measurement and the measurement agrees with it.

THE CONCRETE PAIRS ARE THE CONVINCING PART, because each is obviously right on both readings:
    8x  cmp:schema + cmp:vocabulary        (different subsystems — adding a node type touches both)
    7x  cmp:report + cmp:tools-coherence   (different subsystems — a report and the tool that serves it)
    6x  cmp:nodes  + cmp:vocabulary        (different subsystems)
    6x  cmp:nodes  + cmp:schema            (same subsystem — the kernel, correctly together)
Function says schema and vocabulary are different systems. Maintenance says they move as one. BOTH ARE TRUE, and no single partition satisfies both — which is the whole content of this idea.

⇒ SO THE ANSWER TO "CLUSTER AND DRAW A BOUNDARY" IS NOT NO, IT IS "ON WHICH GRAPH?". Leiden on the dependency graph cannot run here at all (one edge). Leiden on the co-change graph would run today and would produce a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT decomposition from the one in place — 70% of its strongest signal crosses the current boundaries. Picking either silently picks an ility, which is the trap this node named in August and now has evidence for.

📌 WHAT IS STILL NOT KNOWN, so this stays open rather than settling: whether a co-change-derived decomposition would be BETTER. 70% disagreement measures difference, not improvement. Nothing here compares the two against any outcome anybody cares about, and the counter-arguments above — a service boundary carries obligations no coupling graph encodes, and this project has twice retired metric-driven verdicts that fired on correct architecture — apply to the co-change graph exactly as they applied to the dependency one.
properties.name: OPEN — does the quality attribute a system is FOR decide how functions are allocated, and does each attribute need its own graph?
properties.rationale: Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the thinking survives without being claimed as intent. Three things make it worth keeping even if none of it is built: the ility-to-graph direction is genuinely absent while its whole vocabulary is present; the four-graphs observation would change what any future allocation feature computes rather than merely how it weights; and the co-change experiment is runnable today on data already in the graph, which makes at least one branch falsifiable now instead of after instrumentation. The counter-arguments are recorded beside rather than against — an idea killed in conversation loses its reasoning, an idea recorded with its objection keeps both.

properties.decision: UNSETTLED. Six things are mechanically decidable and none is currently reported: (1) is anything under `.reflow2/` tracked by git; (2) are the MCP configs tracked, carrying absolute paths meaningless on another machine; (3) does `.reflow2/kit-version.json` match the installed kit; (4) do local skill copies exist and differ from the served ones, given a local copy silently SHADOWS the served one; (5) is `--graph-path` absolute rather than relative-and-cwd-dependent; (6) is a committed export present, and current against the live graph. SHAPES, not a recommendation: (a) extend `reflow2_init.py --check`, which already reports what a run would change and already owns the stamp and the skill mirrors — smallest, and it means one command answers "what would change" and "what is wrong"; (b) a separate `reflow2_doctor.py` beside `reflow2_check.py`, on the argument that "would this install change files" and "is this project's reflow2 setup sane" are different questions with different audiences; (c) fold the checks into `check_kit_manifest.py`, which already compares the stamp and is closest in spirit; (d) decline, and put the six checks in a served skill instead, on the ground that an agent can run git itself and instructions are cheaper than code. WHATEVER THE SHAPE, IT REPORTS AND DOES NOT REPAIR: `git rm --cached` is a judgement about someone's history, and rewriting an MCP config is not something to do silently. Name the finding, name the remedy, let the human run it — the same split `dec:ask-not-repair` draws for merges. AND IT CANNOT BE AN MCP TOOL: `dec:agent-navigates-content` keeps reflow2 out of file IO, and every check above reads the filesystem or shells to git. The kit is the home; the machinery is half-built there already.
properties.name: OPEN — should the kit ship a command that tells a project how it is out of date, instead of every agent re-deriving the migration?
properties.rationale: Raised because the evidence arrived in an unusually clean form. `req:thin-install` is ACCEPTED and quotes Alex asking for exactly this on 2026-07-25; `cap:skills-served` delivered the forward half; and on 2026-08-08 Alex — the requirement's own author — spent eight manual steps escaping a 0.11.0 kit under a 0.24.0 binary, because nothing exists for a project installed BEFORE served skills. TWO AGENTS DERIVED THAT MIGRATION INDEPENDENTLY THE SAME DAY AND DISAGREED: his eight steps against my seven, overlapping on six. His included a regression (rewriting `--graph-path` to a relative path, the configuration `dec:no-design-here-never-looked` records as minting an accidental third graph in Anthony's own repo); mine got the stamp filename wrong on first pass. Neither was careless — the knowledge is scattered across the installer source, three accepted decisions and two verifications, and is re-derived per session. That is the failure reflow2's own instructions name as its reason to exist, pointed at the migration rather than the design. Evidence: fact:defect-a-pre-served-skills-install-is-stranded and fact:defect-installer-cannot-warn-that-the-graph-dir-is-already-tracked.

properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-14 BY ANTHONY: **ANNOUNCE THE ABSENCE (option c)** — install what the named harness can take, and say plainly when it gets no loop trigger. Option (b), registering a real per-harness equivalent, was NOT rejected: it is compatible with this and remains available wherever an event model turns out to exist. Option (a), leaving it Claude-only and silent, is closed.

⭐⭐ AND READING `cap:nudge-path-proven` BEFORE CAPTURING CHANGED WHAT THIS REQUIRES. **The absence is ALREADY announced.** That capability is VERIFIED and its backstop reports `installed | absent | broken | unknown`, carried both on the handshake instructions — *"the one channel every session reads unasked"* — and as a machine-readable field on `loop_status`. A naive reading of "announce the absence" would have rebuilt something that exists.

🛑 **THE ACTUAL GAP IS NARROWER AND SHARPER: THE ANNOUNCEMENT CANNOT SAY WHY.** The backstop looks for a registered Stop hook. On an OpenCode or Grok project it finds none and reports `absent` — which is TRUE and reads as *"you forgot to install this"*. **It tells the user to fix something they cannot fix.** That is a different state from a Claude project where the hook was genuinely skipped, and reporting them identically sends one of the two users on an impossible errand.

⇒ SO THE REQUIREMENT IS A DISTINCTION, NOT A NEW ANNOUNCEMENT: *not installed here* (fixable — install it) versus *cannot be installed here* (permanent — the harness has no hook, so the loop is yours to run by hand). `absent` currently means both.

📌 WHY THIS FOLLOWS FROM THE PREVIOUS DECISION RATHER THAN MERELY SITTING BESIDE IT. `dec:idea-init-asks-which-harness-and-installs-only-that` (ACCEPTED, same day) makes init ASK which harness. Once the user has NAMED OpenCode, handing them silence about a missing safety net is exactly the silent-wrong-install failure that decision was taken to avoid. **Asking makes staying quiet indefensible: the moment the user tells you their harness, you owe them an honest answer about what it can and cannot have.**

🛑 A STALE CLAIM FOUND WHILE READING, AND IT IS A REAL DEFECT: `cap:nudge-path-proven`'s description ends *"This matters because reflow2_init installs no hooks at all: every consumer project has no session-end nudge, and until now nothing said so."* **That is no longer true.** `ensure_hooks` registers four events (SessionStart, two PostToolUse matchers, Stop) into `.claude/settings.local.json`, measured by running init on 2026-08-14. A VERIFIED capability is carrying a claim about a peer that changed underneath it — the description was right when written and nothing re-read it. Worth correcting on its own, and worth noting as another instance of a fact that no computation reads and therefore nothing rechecks.

═══ THE ANALYSIS THIS WAS DECIDED FROM ═══

RAISED AS BRAINSTORMING by Alex (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-14 — the parenthetical half of his settings note, NOT covered by the upsert fix that closed the rest of it.

HIS WORDS: *"`reflow2 init .` should upsert `settings.local.json` **(or whatever settings file is relevant for the agent harness)** instead of replacing it."*

✅ MEASURED ON HEAD (`cbb1a19`): `ensure_hooks` writes to exactly ONE path — `project/.claude/settings.local.json`. `MCP_CONFIGS` generates three harnesses' server configs; `HOOK_EVENTS` is registered for one. **A project opened in OpenCode, Grok CLI or Copilot gets the MCP server and no loop nudge at all.**

🛑 WHY THAT IS MORE THAN AN INSTALLER ASYMMETRY: the served instructions argue for the hook in the strongest terms available — *"a discipline that depends on being remembered loses to urgency every time; fire it on a trigger, not on virtue"* — and say so because real use showed an agent under load keeps ADDING NODES while the capture→detect→ask→decide loop silently stops. Those harnesses run reflow2 with exactly the mechanism removed that exists because virtue was measured to fail.

⭐ IT COMPOUNDS WITH A SIBLING FINDING: `dec:idea-the-graph-vocabulary-never-reaches-the-user` records that reflow2 cannot observe an agent misbehaving in conversation. Here it cannot observe an agent that was never nudged either. Both are disciplines with no observer — and on a non-Claude harness there is not even a trigger.

📌 A SMALLER TELL IN THE SAME FILE: in `IGNORE_LINES`, `.mcp.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json` each carry an explanatory comment while `opencode.json` and `.vscode/mcp.json` get an empty one. The Claude path is the travelled one.

THE OPTIONS AS THEY STOOD.
(a) LEAVE IT Claude-only. **CLOSED** — after the asking decision, a named harness getting silence is indefensible.
(b) REGISTER A PER-HARNESS EQUIVALENT, same generator shape as `MCP_CONFIGS`. Not chosen now, not rejected: needs a real event model per harness, and a wrong guess produces the silently-broken hook `ensure_hooks` already refuses to create. **Ship where an event model is confirmed to exist.**
(c) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — announce the absence.
(d) MOVE THE TRIGGER OFF THE HARNESS — the server sees every tool call. Counter that keeps it unchosen: the server cannot block a session's stop, which is the one moment the nudge is worth most.

⚠️ VERSION CAVEAT: two of Alex's five notes describe defects already fixed, so he is probably on an older kit (`fact:second-user-notes-2026-08-14-two-items-already-fixed`). Measurements here are against HEAD.
properties.name: DECIDED — a harness that cannot take the loop nudge is TOLD so, and the announcement distinguishes "not installed" from "cannot be installed here"
properties.rationale: Raised under the brainstorm skill and settled the same day on Anthony's word. The capture deliberately read `cap:nudge-path-proven` in full BEFORE writing the requirement, and that read changed the answer: the announcement the decision asks for already exists, so the honest requirement is the DISTINCTION the existing announcement cannot draw rather than a second announcement beside it. Recorded that way so a later session does not build a duplicate reporter and then wonder why two things report the nudge. The stale sentence found in that capability's description is kept here as a finding rather than silently fixed, because a verified capability carrying an out-of-date claim about a peer is worth someone deciding about, not worth an agent quietly editing.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. Raised by an external agent-side field report, 2026-08-11 (fact:external-agent-side-report-2026-08-11, redacted); it is that report's own synthesis and the strongest thing in it.

THEIR SENTENCE: "reality moves outside the graph, and the loop only sees what the agent hand-carries in. Cheapening that carry (asks, re-runs, artifacts, cross-graph facts) is where the remaining leverage is."

WHAT THEY OBSERVED. The liveliest facts of their month — merged PRs, a review round addressed, a suite re-verified, work scheduled — all landed in commits and PR threads, and almost none reached the graph unless an agent chose to carry them. Three of their separate complaints turn out to be ONE complaint: re-running a check is paperwork so `last_run_at` rots; registering an Artifact is the least-rewarding capture so realization sits at zero while PRs merge; asking a question in prose does not register so the ledger nags about work already done. Each was filed as its own friction. They share a cause.

⭐ CORROBORATED HERE THE SAME DAY, WITHOUT COORDINATION. A session in this repo edited a served skill and recorded no ChangeEvent. `loop_status` reported `undispositioned_drift: 0` — which means NO DETECTOR HAD LOOKED AT THE CHANGED FILE, not that nothing changed. The Stop hook caught it; the cheap loop call could not. That is the same defect their report describes from the other side, and it is already recorded at reflow2_feedback.md:539 by a third project.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) Make the CARRY cheap rather than automatic. A one-call "this check ran, it passed, now"; artifact registration derived from a merge or a commit range; the where-am-i skill ending with a mark-asked call. Smallest, and it fixes each of their three instances without reflow2 learning to read anything new. It also leaves the carry a choice, which is the property `dec:three-party-checks` protects.
(b) Let the loop SUBSCRIBE: a webhook or a "reconcile against this repo's recent history" sweep that turns real events into ChangeEvents. Biggest leverage and the biggest risk — an ingested event is an assertion nobody made, and reflow2's whole epistemic position is that the graph stores claims and never manufactures them.
(c) Only REPORT the deficit: say how far the graph has fallen behind the repo (commits since the last ChangeEvent, merged PRs with no Artifact) without ingesting anything. Turns an invisible rot into a number, and asks nobody to trust an inference.
(d) Nothing. The carry being deliberate is a feature, and every automatic path is a way for the graph to fill with things no human said.

⚠️ THE ARGUMENT AGAINST (b), AND IT IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN DOCTRINE. `req:no-idea-goes-quiet` explicitly refuses auto-drawn SATISFIES/REALIZES because "a requirement backed out of the implementation that satisfies it is satisfied by construction — it can never contradict anything," and warns that auto-linking "would make every captured idea read as delivered and the completion reading say 100% forever." A reality bridge that writes structure has the same shape. A reality bridge that writes only ChangeEvents does not, which is the distinction worth holding onto.

📌 WHY THIS IS NOT `req:graph-catches-up` (proposed, already in the graph). That one asks whether the graph can catch up AFTER unrecorded change — a repair. This asks whether the gap should stop opening. Related, and worth deciding together rather than separately.
properties.name: OPEN — should the loop be able to SUBSCRIBE to reality, rather than only seeing what an agent hand-carries into it?
properties.rationale: An external report's three separate frictions turned out to share one cause, and the same cause was independently demonstrated in this repo the same day when loop_status reported zero drift on a file no detector had looked at. The open part is not whether the gap is real but whether closing it means cheapening the carry or automating it — and automation is exactly what this project's accepted doctrine refuses for structure.

properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Prompted by a user report, 2026-08-26: reflow2 *"still speaks its own jargon and never asks who I am"*, with the user's own guess that this is another two-of-three-legs case.

📌 DISTINCT FROM THE TWO THE GUARD OFFERED, BY ROLE. The fact MEASURES what shipped. The capability describes WHAT WAS BUILT and is honest that it is `in_progress`. **This asks what should happen NOW**, which neither answers — a measurement states a condition and a capability states an intent; the disposition is a third thing.

**The user's guess was right and the measurement is sharper than the guess.** It is not a missing leg: the delivery mechanism was **built, core-tested, and left on a branch that never merged** (`e01c760`, "WIP: lens on the skill response — core green, mcp handler tests unrun"). `reader_lens` / `lens_line` / `ReaderLens` have zero occurrences in shipped code, and `lens` is absent from the `get_skill` / `list_skills` toolsnaps.

═══ ⭐ WHY IT BITES A USER AND NOT THE OWNER ═══

The two skills that instruct asking — `where-am-i` and `capture-intent` — are exactly the ones a **regular** user runs and a **new** user does not. The owner runs `/where` constantly, so the persona works for him and silently fails for everyone else. **A mechanism that only fires on the path its author walks is indistinguishable from a working one, from where the author stands.**

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) ⭐ LAND THE BRANCH.** The work exists; six core tests pass; five MCP handler tests were written and never run. Cheapest by a wide margin, and the capability node already describes what "done" means. ⚠️ Counter: it is a month old and the surrounding code has moved — `write_lock` alone gained a `?` at 98 call sites today. Re-landing is not free, and unrun handler tests are unrun evidence.

**(b) CARRY IT ON THE LOOP RAIL INSTEAD OF THE SKILL RESPONSE.** `loop_status` and `open_questions` are what a session calls FIRST, before it knows which skill it wants; a skill response arrives only after somebody chose a skill. ⚠️ Counter: the orientation calls are already dense, and `dec:read-hint-shape` deliberately throttles what rides them. Adding a second passenger means re-opening that decision rather than assuming it.

**(c) A DETECTOR FOR THE MISSING BACKGROUND.** Nothing today notices a Contributor with no `description`, or a design with no person in it at all. That is leg three and it is absent. ⚠️ Counter: it tells the OWNER something is missing; it does nothing for the session speaking jargon right now. It closes the audit hole, not the user's complaint.

**(d) ACCEPT IT AND RETIRE THE CAPABILITY.** If the lens is not worth re-landing, saying so beats a node that reads `in_progress` forever. ⚠️ Counter: the underlying need has now been reported twice, months apart, by someone who is not the owner.

═══ ⚠️ A SECOND FINDING, SEPARABLE AND ARGUABLY WORSE ═══

**The v0.41.0 release report lists this capability under `capabilities_covered`.** That list derives from the components and artifacts a release ships, never from a capability's STATUS — so a capability whose implementation does not exist in the codebase reads as covered by a release. The capability node is honest; the release reading is not, and nothing reconciles the two. Whether `release_report` should read status is a different question and is not decided here.

═══ ⚠️ AND THE LIMIT THAT NONE OF THIS TOUCHES ═══

The capability's own description already says it: the tests prove the lens computes and is attached, *"they do not prove an agent acts on it, and nothing proves the translation is any good. This fixes 'the agent forgot'; it does not touch 'the agent translated badly'."* Every option above closes DELIVERY. **The quality of the translation remains unmeasured**, and the trial that would measure it — a real gap list narrated to a reader with a stated non-software background — is still the missing instrument.
properties.name: OPEN — the persona reaches nobody who does not run where-am-i: land the built branch, or is a skill-response field the wrong carrier?
properties.rationale:
Recorded as its own question because it is about the CARRIER — what puts the persona in front of an agent — which is separate from whether reflow2 can translate a user's domain vocabulary at all, and separate again from whether a new user can find their way around the skills.

The measurement was taken before the options were written and it changed the question. The first framing was "which leg is missing"; the answer is that the leg was built and never landed. That is a different repair with a different cost, and mis-stating it would have sent somebody to write code that already exists.

⚠️ Worth recording as a CLASS, not just an instance: a mechanism that only fires on the path its author walks is invisible from the author's seat by construction. Neither report of this symptom would have arrived without a user who is not the owner, and the same shape will hide the next one.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony thinking out loud 2026-08-24, reconsidering redb after raising it the same day. Nothing here is intent and nothing is planned.

HIS WORDS: *"I was thinking about going to redb, but after thinking about it, I'm starting to think about scalability, particularly if my brother and I move forward with flo2... let's say flo2 has 10000+ users (either collaborating on the same project OR each having their own project)... While the redb and others may compile faster, I'm concerned that they won't scale like rocksdb can. rocksdb was built to support huge amounts of data, so I'm thinking about sticking with it. That being said, there are alternate ways to do things. Maybe we stand up a redb db just for a session and the reflow.json file becomes the enduring thing between each session (may have to make safeguards to ensure that the reflow2 graph is exported at the conclusion of each session). There could be multiple iterations of this that get around using the db as the enduring/persistent storage of the graph and instead switching to making the reflow2.json object file the enduring piece?"*

⭐⭐ THE SHARP PART, AND IT IS HIS: HIS TWO WORRIES DISSOLVE EACH OTHER RATHER THAN TRADING OFF. The redb question was "which store compiles faster"; the scale question is "which store survives 10k tenants". Those look like a straight trade until the store stops being durable. **If the store is a per-session cache derived from the export, then neither property is being chosen at the same altitude any more:** durability and scale move to the export/object layer, and the embedded engine is judged only on hydrate-and-query speed for ONE design — which is small. reflow2's own design is the largest one anybody has, and it is 3,142 nodes / 8.4 MB. A store that "does not scale like RocksDB" is not being asked to.

🛑 AND HE HAS ARRIVED HERE BEFORE, FROM A DIFFERENT DIRECTION — WHICH IS EVIDENCE, NOT DUPLICATION. `dec:idea-a-hosted-tier-of-many-single-writer-tenants` (2026-08-09) already records this as its FIFTH ROAD, in almost the same words: *"OBJECT STORAGE HOLDS THE EXPORT AS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH, a node HYDRATES a RocksDB+tantivy cache on demand, and eviction is free because the cache is derived... reflow2 already has the primitive: the export is deterministic, sorted, content-hashed and self-contained — that IS a per-tenant blob, and the store is already derived rather than authoritative."* Two independent derivations two weeks apart, from a hosting question and from a compile-speed question, landing on one shape. READ IN FULL AND JUDGED DISTINCT rather than merged (`distinct_from`), because the reasons differ and both matter.

WHAT IS NEW HERE, over the 2026-08-09 record — the grounds on which it was kept separate:
1. **THE GRANULARITY IS THE SESSION, NOT THE TENANT.** The fifth road hydrates per tenant on demand, as part of a hosted tier. This proposes the store's lifetime be a SESSION — the same mechanism aimed at a smaller unit, and it applies to the LOCAL single-user case where there is no tenancy at all. That matters because **it is testable today, on one laptop, with no flo2 and no hosting decision.** The fifth road cannot be tried until somebody builds a tier.
2. **IT MAKES THE BACKEND CHOICE REVERSIBLE RATHER THAN CORRECT.** If the store is derived, picking wrong costs a re-hydrate, not a migration. `dec:absorb-rocksdb-024-unchanged-then-switch-separately` and the redb question both get cheaper, and the rust-rocksdb switch stops being a one-way door.
3. **IT NAMES THE SAFEGUARD AS PART OF THE IDEA** — recorded separately, because "what is the enduring artifact" and "what makes the enduring artifact reliable" are answered by different work.

⚠️ THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, RECORDED BESIDE THE IDEA RATHER THAN USED TO ARGUE IT DOWN. The prior node measured the thing that bites: **~9x inflation from export to store** (its figures: 1,828 nodes = 3.8 MB export = 33 MB store, RocksDB plus the tantivy index), and it flagged that `shared.rs` budgets **30 seconds for a cold open**. If hydrate-and-index is seconds rather than milliseconds, "a store per session" turns every session start into that cost — and the local single-user case, the one that works well today, pays it for a benefit only the hosted case collects. **That is the risk this idea has to clear, and it is measurable rather than arguable.**

📌 ONE DATA POINT TAKEN TODAY, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. Opening reflow2's own 3,142-node RocksDB store cold, to a served MCP `initialize`, measured **2.4 seconds** (2026-08-24, after `--stop-shared`). ⚠️ THAT IS NOT THE HYDRATE NUMBER: it opens an EXISTING store with its tantivy index already built, which is the cheap half. The measurement the prior node asks for — import an 8.4 MB export to first query, index included — has still not been taken, and it is the one that decides this.

🛑 WHAT NOBODY HAS CHECKED, and it is the way this fails LATE rather than early: whether a session hydrated from an export can still answer the questions that depend on ACCUMULATED STORE STATE rather than on the design — the confirmation ledger's dates, drift baselines, `write_gen`, the sidecar identity files (`.id.json`, `.sync.json`). The export is self-contained about the DESIGN; that it is self-contained about everything a running seat believes is a DIFFERENT claim, and nobody has tested it.

RECORDED AS A QUESTION, NOT A CONCLUSION. Nothing here says the weld should be loosened; it says the trade Anthony thought he was facing may not be one.
properties.name: OPEN — if the store is a per-session DERIVED cache and reflow2.json is the enduring artifact, does the byte-backend question dissolve rather than get answered?
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill: recorded as an idea, nothing promoted, nothing settled.

Kept separate from `dec:idea-a-byte-backend-that-compiles-in-seconds` (which asks which engine, on compile-speed grounds) and — after reading it in full — from `dec:idea-a-hosted-tier-of-many-single-writer-tenants` (which asks what a HOSTED TIER looks like at 1k/100k/1M and what must not be foreclosed). This asks a third thing settleable without either: WHAT IS THE ENDURING ARTIFACT — the store or the export? It is answerable on one laptop with no hosting tier and no tenancy, and the answer changes how much the other two cost.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🔻 PARTIAL SUPERSESSION — 2026-08-25. ONE PARAGRAPH OF `decision` IS NOW FALSE.
═══════════════════════════════════════════════

**Recorded HERE rather than by editing `decision`, deliberately** — the same discipline `dec:the-rust-rocksdb-switch-is-parked-until-the-store-question-settles` states in its own rationale: re-sending a 6,000-character field to append one note destroys its pre-image, which is the hazard `fact:the-revising-write-warning-fired-correctly-and-the-overwrite-happened-anyway` measured twice. **The `decision` text is untouched; read it with this note beside it.**

❌ **THE PARAGRAPH BEGINNING "🛑 WHAT NOBODY HAS CHECKED, and it is the way this fails LATE rather than early" HAS SINCE BEEN CHECKED.** It asked whether a session hydrated from an export can still answer what depends on ACCUMULATED STORE STATE — the confirmation ledger's dates, drift baselines, `write_gen`, the sidecar identity files.

⭐⭐ **THE ANSWER, measured the same day at main `39dbf6d` and recorded in full at `fact:a-hydrated-seat-keeps-every-confirmation-date-and-loses-only-its-sync-state`: IT SURVIVES ALMOST COMPLETELY.** 208 capability claims on both sides, the same ids, and **ZERO differing fields** across every per-capability date, drift count and accept-ledger entry. The dates and drift history are NODES AND EDGES, so the document carries them. **The fear this paragraph names is measured and false.**

🛑 **ONE THING IS ACTUALLY LOST, and it is narrow:** `last_synced`, a path→content-hash map in the `.sync.json` sidecar — not in the store, not in the document. A hydrated seat answers `sync_status` with the same empty result it uses to mean "never synced", so the stale-seat export refusal (`req:stale-seat-knows`) has no baseline on the first export after a hydrate. **That map is three lines of JSON**, and carrying it is bookkeeping rather than architecture.

📌 **SECOND, THEORETICAL TODAY:** `CF_EMBEDDINGS` has no field in `GraphExport`, so vectors would not survive a hydrate. Nothing outside tests writes any, so it becomes real only when `dec:idea-embeddings-adoption` lands.

⚠️ **THE OTHER COUNTER-ARGUMENT IN `decision` — the ~9x store inflation and the cold-open cost — HAS ALSO MOVED,** and is NOT superseded here because it was never fully stated as a blocker in this node: `dec:the-rust-rocksdb-switch-is-parked-until-the-store-question-settles` now records **load to fully searchable with no database at all: 1,156 ms; save: 265 ms**, against the 30-second budget this node worried about.

✅ **WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE NODE:** nothing here settles what the enduring artifact should BE. Three of five blockers measured away is not a decision, and the node stays `proposed`.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony, 2026-08-04, in his own words: "I kind of like this idea of brainstorming ideas for how to solve a problem and laying out trials for how to figure out which is the best approach - maybe this is a future reflow2 skill??" Raised while brainstorming the corpus-ingest strategies (dec:idea-corpus-ingest-strategies), which is the first concrete case for it.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, AND IT IS MORE THAN HALF — the design-space version of this shipped as BL-70 and nothing in this idea should be built without reading it first. `register_alternative` forks a `proposed` Decision into alternatives, each a pointer to that branch's own design export, GOVERNED_BY the Decision and CONTRADICTS its siblings, and it REFUSES unless the Decision is proposed — you fork an open choice, not a settled one. `analyze_alternatives` then compares the branches ON THE SAME MEASURES — design nodes, open gaps, structural defects, allocation modularity, capabilities verified, plus each branch's structural divergence from the baseline — in throwaway graphs, so it never touches the live one. Its own words are "makes alternatives comparable on measures, not advocacy", which is this idea's thesis already stated. `collapse_decision` picks the winner, moves the Decision to accepted, and SUPERSEDES the losers with OBSOLETES so the roads not taken stay on the record. `detect_gaps` fires `undecided_decision_point` once a Decision holds two or more registered alternatives, so an open fork nags and a musing does not.

THE GAP, AND IT IS SPECIFIC — reflow2 can compare DESIGNS; it cannot compare RUNS. Every measure `analyze_alternatives` reports is a property of the resulting graph's shape. None of them is a property of the PROCESS that produced it: what it cost, how long it took, how much of the corpus it covered, how much noise it raised, how many questions a human then had to answer, and whether the result was recognisable to the person who owns the material. The corpus-ingest strategies are indistinguishable on graph shape and completely different on all of those. A trial produces evidence about a PROCESS and there is nowhere in the graph to put it. That is the same hole [BL-187] names from the other side — the corpus records when something was true and nothing computes whether it still is.

THE SECOND GAP, AND IT IS THE ONE THIS PROJECT KEEPS FINDING — no skill drives the alternatives family end to end. `brainstorm` mentions `register_alternative` in passing, as the line where a musing becomes a fork. Nothing tells anyone to then run `analyze_alternatives` or `collapse_decision`. Same shape as `ingest_step`, which is built, served, verified, and named in no skill at all: a tool nobody is told to call is a tool nobody calls ([BL-154]).

HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea rather than used to kill it. (1) `dec:report-dont-judge` — a trial that picks a winner by number is arithmetic overruling a person, which is the move this project refuses everywhere else; the skill would have to REPORT the measures and leave the collapse to the human, exactly as `collapse_decision` already requires a stated winner and a rationale. (2) The api-boss's objection to PMBOK in `reflow2_feedback.md` applies here too: reflow2 is a design-coherence tool, and importing an experiment harness risks "a second, competing spine next to the golden thread". (3) Trials are expensive, and the cheapest honest version of this idea may be a SKILL over the existing tools plus a convention for recording run measures as evidence, rather than any new vocabulary — which is what the last two node-type proposals in this project both collapsed into after measurement (`Attestation` → `TemporalFact`, `Hazard` → `DesignRule`).

NOT PROMOTED, NOT SIZED, AND NOT MINE — recorded so the idea is findable and so the next session does not re-derive BL-70, which is the specific failure this session hit three times.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 have a skill for "brainstorm the options, then TRIAL them and let measurement choose"?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill because Anthony floated it as a question, not a request. The load-bearing content is the survey of what BL-70 already provides: the idea is substantially built for design alternatives and genuinely missing for process trials, and that distinction is what would make it worth building rather than a second name for something that exists.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, AND DELIBERATELY NOT ACTED ON. Anthony, 2026-08-19: *"let's capture the feedback, but hold off on tackling anything from it — your context is getting high, so let's tackle them in the next session."* **Nothing here has been built.** Full text: `art:ophyd-service-feedback-2026-08-19`, `art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-08-19` — REGISTERED Artifacts, PARKED under the accepted `dec:a-dated-field-report-is-registered-and-parked`, files at `docs/feedback/2026-08-19-*-agent-feedback.md`. They correctly attach to nothing and `parks` is how the design says so; an earlier pass in this session deleted them instead, on the mistaken argument that no honest edge existed — see `dec:idea-parks-shipped-and-was-still-not-reached-the-instruction-is-missing-where-the-person-is-stuck`.

Two agents, two of his work projects, filed independently on the same day. **Neither complains about the MODEL.** ophyd's own summary: *"The friction list is almost entirely about write ergonomics on long-lived nodes, not about the model."*

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ VERIFIED BEFORE RECORDING — three checks run this session

**1. THE ITEM GRADED "worst one" DOES NOT REPRODUCE.** ophyd reports `add_decision` upsert silently resetting an accepted Decision to `proposed`. Tested on 0.36.0 at BOTH layers, checking BOTH the reply and the stored value: status survives. `upsert_node` reads existing properties, extends with supplied, writes — the merge is correct. A second hypothesis (that a REFUSED call still mutates) was also tested and is wrong: the dedup guard correctly does not fire on your own existing node, so the call simply succeeds. 🛑 **Either it is already fixed, or that session ran a stale binary — and MERGED-≠-SERVED bit this very session twice. ASK WHAT VERSION THEIR SERVER REPORTED before anything is built.**

**2. THE SKILL-NAME DRIFT IS REAL, confirmed by inspection.** EIGHT advertised commands have no skill of that name: `rules`, `req`, `gaps`, `decisions`, `where`, `kpp`, `health`, `debt`. `get_skill('rules')` correctly refuses and lists 20 names, none of them `rules`. ⭐ **reflow2 already owns the doctrine that fixes it** — `req:a-refusal-names-what-would-have-worked` — the refusal simply does not map aliases. *"'rules' is served as 'governance-proposal'"* is the whole change.

**3. `description` UNDECLARED ON `ChangeEvent` IS REPORTED BY BOTH PROJECTS INDEPENDENTLY.** hxm's framing is the sharper one: the flag fires on **every legitimate write**, which **trains the caller to ignore `undeclared`** and defeats its typo-catching purpose. One schema line.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐ THREE ITEMS THIS SESSION CORROBORATES FIRST-HAND, from a third project (reflow2 itself)

· **PROMOTION ALWAYS TRIPS THE DEDUP GUARD** (ophyd #5). Hit on EVERY promotion today — decision→requirement→capability, `distinct_from` boilerplate each time.
