Their fix — a `promotes: <decision-id>` parameter that draws a real edge, skips the guard, and gives the Decision its road-taken link for free — **turns friction into structure**. Three projects now.
· **EVOLVING A LONG DECISION MEANS RESENDING ALL OF IT** (ophyd #2). Multi-thousand-word bodies resent repeatedly today, each with the revision block warning the prior text exists only in the reply. **The riskiest write pattern in the tool.** Their `resolve_decision(id, resolution_text, status)` would remove friction #1 and #2 together.
· **APPEND-ONLY EDITS GET THE MAXIMUM-ALARM REVISION NOTE** (hxm #3). Same experience. Their fix is right: a diff-aware *"new value strictly extends the prior"* **preserves the alarm's signal for the genuinely destructive case.**

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐ THE BIGGEST ITEM IS NOT A BUG — "reflow2 AS A PROGRAM BRAIN, NOT A PROJECT BRAIN"

Anthony's own framing, quoted by the agent: *"kind of a strange way to be using reflow2… managing this scattered 'project' that has multiple facets, but that are all inter-related."* Five repos, two people, a simulated beamline, a PR pipeline, one graph, three days of heavy load.

**Its central claim: the ontology ALREADY FITS.** Capabilities outliving any repo, Contributors with authorship and ownership, Verifications naming a beamline session rather than a CI job, epochs, releases, TRL/MRL gates — *"that vocabulary is program-shaped. The single-system framing lives mostly in adopt/genesis's front door, not in the schema."*

TWO NAMED STRAINS:
· **People-readiness has no node type.** The program's real gate includes *"AJ can independently build and maintain this stack"*, and readiness modelling stops at technologies. The learning ladder got smuggled into a TemporalFact's context sentence.
· **Facet-blind interrogation.** Writing 12 advisory craft rules moved unsurfaced gaps 7 → 19: the gap engine prices a craft-of-practice rule identically to a system requirement. 📌 This is the SAME SHAPE as `dec:idea-a-project-says-what-it-is-doing-now-so-the-loop-stops-pushing`, settled today — the loop asking the right question at the wrong moment — arriving from a different direction.

📌 THEIR SUGGESTION: name the use case in the docs, and have genesis/adopt **ask "system or program?" up front instead of assuming system.**

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
THE REST, UNRANKED AND UNJUDGED (see the artifacts for full text)

ophyd: review/ack records swamp `scan_nodes(Decision)` (~40 of 61); loop-debt classes have no acknowledge path, so a deliberate state keeps the loop from ever reading clean and it is unclear whether `ruling: parks` covers it; three tools needed to see all debt; token weight of `get_skill` and `propagate_change`; the `create_node`-vs-`add_*` scar tissue.
ophyd ideas: `resolve_decision`; promotion edges as first-class; a one-call `demonstration` record for *"X was seen working live on DATE in ENV"* (the commonest evidence at a beamline, currently 3 loads + 3 calls); a session-scoped write journal.
hxm: ChangeEvent `name` has no length steer; **a "sighting" mechanism for DesignRules** — ⭐ which `fact:the-gh-merge-failure-is-snap-confinement-and-nobody-was-counting` shows arriving independently from a second direction the same day; `get_skill` batch or ETag.

⚠️ NOTHING HERE IS PRIORITISED YET, and the ordering above is exposition, not a plan. The two cheapest CONFIRMED items are the `ChangeEvent.description` declaration and the alias-mapping refusal.
properties.name: OPEN — two more projects filed field reports the same day: the friction is almost entirely WRITE ERGONOMICS ON LONG-LIVED NODES, and one of them says reflow2 is being used as a PROGRAM brain, not a project brain
properties.rationale: Captured on Anthony's instruction to record the feedback and defer the work to a fresh session, so nothing is lost to context pressure and nothing is half-built. The three verification results are recorded ahead of the reports themselves because they change what should be built: the item its own author graded worst does not reproduce and may be a stale-binary artefact, which would misdirect a whole increment if taken at face value; and two other items are confirmed rather than merely reported. This session's own first-hand corroboration of three friction items is included because reflow2 is effectively a third reporting project, and three independent hits on the promotion guard is a different weight of evidence from one. The program-brain observation is given its own section rather than filed among the friction because it is a claim about what reflow2 IS, and its author argues the schema already supports it while the front-door skills do not.

properties.decision:
🛑 **WITHDRAWN BY ANTHONY THE SAME DAY IT WAS RAISED, 2026-08-14**, on noticing it contradicted his own standing practice: *"you're right that my latest guidance is contradictory to previous, so please disregard. it is just my brother and developing. anytime a new version comes out, I tell him and he usually updates. so we'll just continue with this policy."*

⇒ **THE REASON IS A FACT ABOUT THE USER POPULATION, AND IT IS WORTH KEEPING.** reflow2 has two users who talk to each other directly. A stable-baseline policy exists to tell strangers which releases are safe to adopt; **there are no strangers.** The distribution channel is a text message, and it works. At this scale a formal patch line would add ceremony to solve a problem nobody has.

⭐ AND IT DISSOLVES THE CADENCE CONCERN RATHER THAN ANSWERING IT. Three releases in three days is only a problem if users discover versions passively. They do not — they are told. **The measurement that prompted this (`fact:updating-reflow2-does-not-update-a-project-already-set-up`) stays true and stops being a reason to slow down.**

═══ ⚠️ WHAT DOES **NOT** GO AWAY WITH THIS WITHDRAWAL ═══

**The kit/binary split survives, and this withdrawal sharpens it.** *"He usually updates"* updates the **BINARY**. `install.sh` does not touch a project that is already initialised, because the files that matter to a project (`reflow2_init.py` and what it wrote) are KIT, and a project's copy is fixed at the moment it was set up.

⇒ **So the working update channel makes the remaining gap MORE visible, not less: the message arrives, the user updates, and their existing projects are exactly as stale as before.** Alex's home machine is the demonstration — binary 0.30.0, project stamped 0.11.0. The defect was never about him being told late.

📌 STILL OWED, INDEPENDENT OF ANY RELEASE POLICY: something that surfaces the KIT's version (today only the binary's is reachable), and an update path for a project that already exists. Neither needs a stable line to justify it.

═══ THE ANALYSIS THIS WAS WITHDRAWN FROM, kept because `req:roads-not-taken` says the roads not taken are part of the record ═══

RAISED as: should v0.30.0 become a stable baseline that only external feedback moves, with changes shipped as patches?

Two objections were on the record before the withdrawal, and both stand as reasoning even though the question is closed:
  · **THE RULE CONTAINED TWO RULES.** *"Only external feedback"* answers WHAT may change; *"maybe these are patches"* answers HOW BIG. `cap:init-asks-which-harness` is both external feedback and a new feature, so the halves disagreed in practice on the day they were written.
  · **A STRICT READING WOULD HAVE PARKED FOUR MEASURED DEFECTS** found the same day, none of them user-reported — the machine-wide installer writing configs for absent harnesses, 9 of 20 skills with no drift signal, the enforced rule's missing detector, and 43 planned capabilities invisible to every tool. **Users cannot report what the tool hides from them.**

OPTIONS, NONE TAKEN: (a) v0.30.x patch line, fixes only. (b) slow but not frozen. (c) baseline plus feature branch. (d) intent without policy. **The outcome is (d) by decision rather than by drift: continue as before, deliberately.**
properties.name: WITHDRAWN — a stable v0.30 baseline solves a distribution problem this project does not have; the update channel is one person telling the other
properties.rationale: Raised and withdrawn the same day, on Anthony's word. Recorded as rejected rather than deleted because the reasoning is worth more than the question: the withdrawal establishes that reflow2's user population is two people with a direct channel, which is a fact several other decisions could lean on, and it separates two things that had been travelling together all day — release cadence, which turns out not to be a problem, and the kit/binary update split, which is a real defect that the working update channel actually makes more visible rather than less.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. Anthony, 2026-08-11, and he was explicit that this is NOT a reflow2-repo question: "this isn't just a 'do it for reflow2' type task. this is a more general philosophy that test planning should be before implementation (maybe even in the design stages of a reflow2 project)... reflow2 guides a user through systems engineering processes, implementation, testing and fielding/production — I'm saying reflow2 should define a design tests philosophy prior to development of the design."

⭐⭐ MEASURED ON REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN, 2026-08-11, AND IT IS ONE-SIDED:

  verification detectors                                      6
    build_without_verification, unverified_capability, unverified_artifact,
    component_granularity_verification, failing_verification, build_without_governance
  of those, asking a REQUIREMENT how it will be verified      0

  live requirements                                         142
    with a Verification pointed AT the requirement             2
    stating a need with no stated way to know it is met       140

EVERY detector fires in the same direction: you BUILT this, where is the check? Nothing anywhere asks: you STATED this need, how will you know it is met? So reflow2 today discovers the test question at the moment it is most expensive to answer and most likely to be answered by looking at the code.

⭐ THE V-MODEL FRAMING, because it names the shape precisely. reflow2 models the descending arm (intent → allocation → build) and the ascending arm (verify → operate) — that is what the seven maturity bands measure. What it does not model is the CROSS-LINKS: in the V, the acceptance test is written when the requirement is written, and the integration test when the architecture is drawn. reflow2 has both arms and no rungs.

📌 THE SIBLING QUESTION IS ALREADY OPEN AND THIS ONE MAKES IT MATTER MORE. `dec:bl-185` (Anthony, 2026-08-03) asks how the graph can tell a test written FROM THE REQUIREMENT from one written to match the code — "a passing check written from the requirement and a passing check written to match the implementation are the same node, same status, same everything." That is the RECORDING question. This is the PROCESS one. If verification were planned at requirement time, "written from the requirement" would be the normal case rather than something the graph has to detect after the fact — so answering this one shrinks that one.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so nothing is built twice: `Verification` carries method and level and can already point at a Requirement (two do). `set_evidence_scope` records what a check PINNED versus SWEPT, and `evidence_report` reads it. `req:evidence-says-what-it-covered` is ACCEPTED. So the vocabulary for a planned check is there — a Verification at `planned` status IS a test plan. Nothing asks for one.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) A DETECTOR: an accepted Requirement with no Verification pointed at it is a gap — "how will you know this is met?". Symmetric with `unsatisfied_requirement`, which already asks "what delivers this?". Cheapest, and it is the one that changes what gets built.
(b) A SKILL STEP: capture-intent ends by asking, for each requirement, how it would be checked — recorded as a `planned` Verification. No detector, no gap pressure, and it fires only when the skill loads, which `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` says is not enough.
(c) A STATED PHILOSOPHY the project chooses, captured as a DesignRule via governance-proposal, with the consequence asked rather than assumed. This is what Anthony literally said — "reflow2 should DEFINE a design tests philosophy" — and it is per-project, which matters because the answer differs between a demonstrator and a fielded system.
(d) Nothing. The build-side detectors already catch an unverified capability before it ships, and adding a requirement-side one doubles the gap surface.

⚠️⚠️ THE STRONGEST OBJECTION, AND IT IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN MOST-REPEATED TRAP. A detector demanding a verification plan for every accepted requirement would fire on 140 of 142 here ON DAY ONE — and on every young design, and on every ADOPT, where a recovered requirement never had a test plan and could not have. That is exactly the shape of `unexpected_coupling` (retired for firing on correct work), of the short-text false positive found by CI hours ago, and of BL-179's punish-correct-work trap. Whatever is built must distinguish "nobody has planned this yet" from "this cannot be planned", which is `req:a-rule-says-whether-it-can-be-checked-at-all` (ACCEPTED, unbuilt) pointed at requirements instead of rules.

⚠️ SECOND: `req:no-se-knowledge` is accepted — the user must never need systems engineering. "How will you verify this?" is an SE question in SE words. It would have to arrive the way every other gap does, as a plain question the user can answer without knowing what a verification method is.

⚠️ THIRD, and it is the honest limit on the whole idea: planning a test early does not make it a GOOD test. Anthony's own criteria — valid, isolated, repeatable, focused, fast; happy path, edge cases, error conditions, contract-not-implementation — are properties of the test's CONTENT, and `dec:idea-who-judges-requirement-text-quality` already found that reflow2 checks structure and never text. A `planned` Verification with an empty method satisfies a detector and proves nothing, which would be a marker nothing reads in a new place.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 guide a project to plan HOW a need will be verified when the need is stated, rather than only asking for a check once something is built?
properties.rationale: Measured one-sidedness: all six verification detectors ask the build for a check, none asks a requirement how it will be known to be met, and 140 of 142 live requirements have no verification pointed at them. That is the V-model with both arms and no rungs. Anthony is proposing this as product philosophy rather than repo hygiene, which passes his own pruning test — it would change what reflow2 asks every project, not how this project manages itself. The blocker is precision: the naive detector fires on every young design and every adopt, which is the punish-correct-work trap this project has already retired one detector for.

properties.decision:
Anthony, 2026-08-26: *"yes, I like the 'any MCP client' phrase."* Option (a) chosen.

═══ HOW THE QUESTION AROSE ═══

He corrected his own vocabulary an hour after using it: *"sorry, I may not have meant 'harness'... What I was trying to describe is AI coding agents, agentic development platforms, or generative IDEs... things like Claude Code, Grok Build, Copilot CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, etc and didn't know what their official name was, so I used 'harness', but that isn't correct."*

**The problem was real and product-facing.** 85 nodes carry "harness"; it is reflow2's own coinage; no vendor uses it; and it reads to a newcomer as *the thing that runs your tests*. `init` speaks it aloud to strangers.

═══ THE DECISION ═══

**Do not name the category. Name what is assumed of it: reflow2 targets ANY MCP CLIENT.**

This dissolves the problem rather than solving it. There is no settled industry term — Anthony offered three in one sentence, which is the evidence — so any choice would be a bet on which label wins. "Any MCP client" cannot go stale as vendors rename themselves, and it is exactly and only what reflow2 depends on.

🛑 **AND IT AVOIDS THE COLLISION THAT KILLED THE OBVIOUS ANSWER.** MCP's own specification calls the product a **host**. That is precise and vendor-neutral, and it is unusable here: `dec:central-host` is the open question *"does reflow2 gain a hosted surface (one MCP over HTTPS)?"*, where host means the machine SERVING reflow2. Adopting MCP's sense would leave one word meaning both ends of the connection.

═══ ⭐ HOW THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT IS ANSWERED, BECAUSE IT WAS REAL ═══

The recorded objection to this option: *"`init` must still ask the user WHICH ONE they use, and 'which MCP client do you use?' is a worse question than 'which editor?' for someone who does not know what MCP is."* `req:init-installs-only-the-harness-you-name` makes that asking mandatory.

**THE ANSWER IS THAT INIT NEVER NEEDED THE CATEGORY NOUN — IT NEEDS A LIST.** Asking *"which of these do you use: Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot CLI, OpenCode…?"* is a better question than any abstraction, for exactly the user who has never heard of MCP. **The noun was only ever needed by the DESIGN, and the design now has "any MCP client" instead.** So the counter applies to a question nobody has to ask.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES **NOT** AUTHORISE ═══

**The 85 existing "harness" mentions are NOT swept as part of this.** He endorsed a phrase for the assumption; he did not authorise editing 85 nodes, and doing so on this word alone would be an agent deciding a migration's cost on his behalf.

**So the design is bilingual for now, and that is honest debt rather than an oversight**: new writing says "any MCP client" (or names the products); existing nodes keep "harness" until someone decides whether the sweep is worth it. `cap:init-asks-which-harness` and `req:init-installs-only-the-harness-you-name` are the two that most carry the old word into the product, and are the first candidates if a sweep is ever taken.

📌 The substantive half of his correction — that the lowest common denominator is ONE assumption rather than two, because the graph is reachable only THROUGH MCP — lives on `rule:mcp-and-the-graph-are-the-only-common-ground`, not here. This node settled only what to call the thing.
properties.name: DECIDED — name the ASSUMPTION, not the category: reflow2 targets "any MCP client", and `init` asks by product name instead
properties.rationale:
Settled by Anthony the same day it was raised, choosing the option the brainstorm marked as promising.

Recorded with the counter-argument's ANSWER rather than just its dismissal, because the objection was specific and correct as stated: init does have to ask. What defeats it is that init can ask with a LIST of product names, so the category noun was only ever needed by the design's own prose — which is precisely what the chosen phrase replaces.

The limit is written in explicitly. Endorsing a phrase is not authorising an 85-node rename, and the difference between those two is the kind of thing an agent should not decide quietly. The bilingual state is named as debt so a later reader meets it rather than discovering an inconsistency and assuming carelessness.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-25, redirecting away from measuring artifacts: *"this is more a systems engineering 101 type discussion... it should be, how do properly trained SE professionals design SE upfront? what does the doctrine say we should do?"*

═══ THE CANONICAL UPFRONT SEQUENCE (15288 technical processes 1–6; NASA SP-2016-6105; INCOSE HB) ═══

1. **MISSION / BUSINESS ANALYSIS** — the problem in the stakeholder's terms. No solution language.
2. **ConOps / OpsCon** — how the thing will be USED. Operational modes, day-in-the-life scenarios, who does what to it. ⭐ This is where SE STARTS and where untrained teams skip straight to features.
3. **STAKEHOLDER NEEDS → SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS** — verifiable, traceable, and **each one gets its verification method chosen at the same moment it is written**.
4. **FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS** — what functions must be performed, and in what sequence. Functional flow block diagrams. **Still no boxes.**
5. **FUNCTIONAL ALLOCATION** — group functions and assign them to logical elements.
6. **PHYSICAL ARCHITECTURE** — the actual elements, chosen through trade studies against stated criteria.
7. **INTERFACE DEFINITION** — every boundary gets an ICD; an N² chart is walked so none is missed.
8. **BUDGETS AND MARGINS** allocated top-down — mass, power, latency, cost.
9. **RECURSE ONE LEVEL** — repeat 3–8 for each subsystem.
10. **REVIEWS AS GATES** — SRR ▸ SFR ▸ PDR ▸ CDR, each baselining what came before.

═══ THE THREE THINGS THAT ACTUALLY SEPARATE PROFESSIONALS FROM COMPETENT AMATEURS ═══

**(a) FUNCTION BEFORE FORM.** Decompose what the system DOES before what it IS. Structure is the OUTPUT of grouping functions by cohesion and coupling — it is not chosen and then populated.
**(b) VERIFICATION PLANNED WITH THE REQUIREMENT**, not after the build. "How would we prove this?" is part of writing it, and a requirement nobody can say how to verify is not finished.
**(c) BREADTH-FIRST AND COMPLETE AT EACH LEVEL** before going deeper. One level fully decomposed and fully interfaced beats a deep spike down one branch.

⭐⭐ THE CORRECTION THIS MAKES TO EVERYTHING DISCUSSED TODAY: **SPAN OF CONTROL IS A CHECK, NOT A GENERATOR.** 3–7 does not tell you how to decompose; it tells you whether the decomposition you DERIVED from functional allocation came out sane. If grouping the functions leaves twenty children under one parent, the finding is that the grouping lacks an intermediate cohesion level or the functions were not actually cohesive — not that a rung should be inserted to satisfy a number. The whole ladder investigation approached depth as a thing to DECLARE or COMPUTE FROM COUNTS, and doctrine says it is a CONSEQUENCE of allocation.

═══ WHAT REFLOW2 ALREADY HAS, CHECKED AGAINST THE LIST RATHER THAN ASSUMED ═══

- **Functions** → `Capability`. **Elements** → `Component`. **Functional allocation** → `ALLOCATED_TO`.
- ⭐ **THE GENERATOR EXISTS.** `propose_allocation` clusters capabilities by weighted coupling into groups — that IS step 5, mechanised. `evaluate_allocation` scores modularity and finds misplaced capabilities. reflow2 can already derive structure from function, and the ladder work never touched it.
- **Requirements flow-down** → `Requirement.lineage` = original / decomposed / derived, and the decomposed-vs-derived distinction is a real doctrinal one most tools collapse.
- **Trade studies** → `register_alternative` + `analyze_alternatives`, with the Decision carrying why the losers lost.
- **ICDs** → `Interface` + `PROVIDES`/`CONSUMES` on both sides; `seam_coverage` is the N²-chart question asked at an altitude.
- **Budgets and margins** → `Constraint` with `quantity` / `limit` / `direction` and `constrains` carrying each spender's contribution; `budget_report` refuses to sum a partial set.
- **Review gates** → `QualityGate` with `phase` (P0–P5) and `criteria`.
- **V&V** → `Verification` with `kind` = verification / validation — built right vs right thing, correctly separated.
- **Functional sequence** → `Flow` + `part_of_flow` + `TRIGGERS` with roles.
- **Technology readiness** → `ReadinessAssessment` (TRL/MRL), `GATED_ON` carrying the threshold.

═══ WHAT DOCTRINE HAS AND REFLOW2 DOES NOT ═══

🛑 **NO ConOps VOCABULARY.** Checked: nothing in the schema or any served skill mentions concept of operations, operational scenario, or operational mode. `Flow` + `Actor` could carry one and nothing says so. **This is step 2 — the step doctrine puts FIRST and the one untrained teams skip.** reflow2 is aimed squarely at teams who skip it, and offers them no place to put it.

🛑 **NO Risk NODE TYPE.** A `RISKS` edge exists, but risk management is its own 15288 process and a register needs likelihood, impact, mitigation, owner and status. There is nowhere to record "this could go wrong, here is how likely and how bad, here is who owns it".

⚠️ AND A THIRD, WEAKER ONE: doctrine's reviews BASELINE the design — after PDR the design is under configuration control and changes need disposition. `QualityGate` records pass/fail; `DesignEpoch` and `Snapshot` hold history. Whether those compose into a baseline anybody can be held to is not obvious and was not checked.

═══ THE HONEST SHAPE OF THE GAP ═══

reflow2's VOCABULARY covers the doctrinal spine better than expected — the pieces for steps 3–10 are nearly all present, several of them well-modelled. What is thin is the same thing measured on 2026-08-18 for other vocabulary: whether any of it REACHES a user's design. Steps 1–2 have no home at all, and the generator in step 5 (`propose_allocation`) is a tool nobody is instructed to run.
properties.name: OPEN — SE 101: the doctrinal upfront sequence says structure is DERIVED from functional allocation, not chosen; reflow2 already owns most of that machinery, and the ladder work approached it from the wrong end
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill: recorded as an idea, nothing promoted, nothing settled.

Kept separate from `dec:idea-depth-is-derived-from-fan-out-not-declared-by-a-ladder` (which proposes computing depth from a span-of-control count, and which this reframes as a CHECK rather than a generator) and from `dec:idea-audit-the-claim-that-reflow2-does-systems-engineering` (which audits the claim against 15288 for enforcement and coverage). This asks the prior question: what does doctrine actually prescribe for the UPFRONT phase, and which of those steps has a home in reflow2 at all — which is where the ConOps and Risk absences show up, and neither of those nodes reaches them.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's idea, 2026-08-10, in his words: *"several times, I have had a brainstorming idea, and you've searched what I've already had in the graph. can we keep track of those searches for what's related because that tells you — the user had asked about something (or something similar or related) 10 times now... this node that has been searched 10 times now is becoming critical based on how many times it has been searched."*

REFINED BY HIM MINUTES LATER, and the refinement is right: *"instead of just keeping a simple integer counter, maybe relevance should also be included? for example, 5 other proposed ideas/decisions come up, but 2 of them were only 0.1 relevant, one was 0.4 relevant, and 2 were 0.8 relevant. then the critical decision path is weighted more towards the 0.8 relevant ideas versus the 0.1 ideas."* A count treats a barely-matching hit and a bullseye as the same event, and the tail of a ranked list is mostly noise — so an unweighted counter would be dominated by whatever happens to match loosely and often.

🛑 BUT THE SCORE THE SEARCH RETURNS IS NOT THE 0-TO-1 RELEVANCE THE IDEA ASSUMES, AND THIS IS THE CRUX. `search_design` is BM25, whose scores are UNBOUNDED and QUERY-DEPENDENT. MEASURED 2026-08-10, two queries about the SAME SUBJECT:

    query "export"                                                    top score   4.48
    query "the committed export document lineage content hash chain"  top score  35.75

EIGHT TIMES THE SCORE FOR THE SAME TOPIC, because BM25 rises with the number of matching terms. Accumulating raw scores would therefore weight a verbose query roughly eight times a terse one about the same thing, and would silently reward whoever writes longer queries. THERE IS NO 0.8 IN THE SYSTEM TODAY — the numbers look like relevances and are not.

⇒ THREE WAYS TO GET A COMPARABLE NUMBER, none chosen:
  (i) NORMALISE PER QUERY — divide by that result set's top score, giving 0-1 within one search. Cheap, available now, and it makes the two queries above agree. Costs the absolute signal: the top hit of a hopeless query scores 1.0 exactly like the top hit of a perfect one.
  (ii) RANK-BASED WEIGHT — reciprocal rank (1, 1/2, 1/3...), ignoring the score entirely. Immune to query length and to BM25's quirks; the standard trick for fusing incomparable rankings. Costs the distinction between a result set with one obvious winner and one with five near-ties.
  (iii) COSINE SIMILARITY FROM EMBEDDINGS — genuinely bounded, genuinely comparable across queries, and the only one of the three that actually delivers the 0.1/0.4/0.8 the idea describes. ⚠️ THIS MAKES THE IDEA A DEPENDENT OF AN ALREADY-OPEN QUESTION: `dec:idea-embeddings-adoption` ("should reflow2 adopt embeddings and the HNSW index, or stay on lexical search?"). Worth naming plainly — if relevance-weighting is wanted in the form Anthony described, that decision has to be made first, and this is a new argument for it that the embeddings node does not yet carry.

OBSERVED IN THE SESSION THAT PRODUCED THE IDEA, which is why it is worth taking seriously rather than filing as a nice thought. Across roughly eight `search_design` calls on 2026-08-10, the same nodes kept surfacing unprompted: `fact:bl-198` twice, `dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written` twice, `dec:read-hint-shape` twice, and `cap:what-next` / `req:what-next` at the exact moment a new idea turned out to duplicate accepted intent. Each of those repeats CHANGED THE WORK — one of them stopped a false claim being shipped for the second time in three days. The signal is real in at least one session.

⚠️⚠️ IT COLLIDES WITH A LINE ANTHONY HIMSELF DREW, AND THE DISTINCTION IS PART OF THE VALUE OF THIS NODE. `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` says, verbatim: *"A SEARCH QUERY is content and is the worst offender, because it names the user's domain in their own words."* Read carelessly, that kills this idea. Read properly, it does not — because that requirement's scope is stated in its first line: *"WHEN REFLOW2 REPORTS ITS OWN USAGE FROM A HOSTED DEPLOYMENT."* It governs what LEAVES a design. This idea keeps the search history INSIDE the design it came from, where the object is not a leak but the entire point. SAME DATA, OPPOSITE DIRECTION. That distinction must be written down here, because a later session that finds this idea and remembers the telemetry rule will otherwise kill it correctly-looking and wrongly — or implement it and breach the rule by exporting it.

⇒ THE DERIVED CONSTRAINT, if this is ever built: search history is LOCAL BY CONSTRUCTION and never enters the telemetry payload. `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content`'s own argument applies — a structure that CANNOT carry content beats a policy promising not to — so the two must not share a transport.

`dec:how-should-reflow2-log-its-own-usage` IS ALREADY OPEN and holds the mechanism-and-storage question for usage logging. This idea widens what that decision has to answer: not only WHICH TOOLS a session called, but WHICH NODES it reached and HOW STRONGLY. Nodes are a harder case than tool names, exactly per the rule above.

TWO CONFOUNDS, BOTH SERIOUS, BOTH MEASURABLE BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING.

FIRST: A SEARCH HIT MEASURES THE AGENT'S QUERY WORDING AS MUCH AS THE USER'S INTEREST. Anthony did not run those eight searches — I did, choosing the words. A count would partly measure how I phrase things, and would drift as agents or models change. What he actually described is narrower and better: *the user had asked about something similar ten times*, which is a fact about HIS repeated approach to a topic, not about search mechanics. NOTE THAT WEIGHTING MAKES THIS CONFOUND WORSE, NOT BETTER, UNDER RAW BM25 — a longer agent query scores everything higher.

SECOND, AND SHARPER: SEARCH IS BM25 OVER NODE TEXT, SO A VERBOSE NODE WINS MORE SEARCHES. The nodes in this design are extremely verbose — several run to thousands of characters — and length is a scoring advantage in BM25. "Searched often" may therefore partly measure PROSE VOLUME rather than importance, and the verbose nodes are disproportionately the recent ones. That is testable directly: correlate hit frequency against node text length before trusting any of it. Per-query normalisation does NOT fix this one; it is a property of the corpus, not of the query.

AND A THIRD, SEEN TWICE TODAY: THE ONE-WORD "export" SEARCH RETURNED A `decision:ack:` REVIEW RECORD AS ITS TOP HIT. Whatever exclusion list a projection carries (`fact:graph-analysis-covers-a-third-of-the-edge-types`) applies here too — review records and bookkeeping must not accumulate attention weight.

AND `dec:bl-155`'S TRAP APPLIES ONE LEVEL OVER, unchanged. That decision found reflow2 cannot tell "unused" from "unreachable", and `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` drew the consequence: usage counts may justify OPTIMISING and may not, alone, justify CUTTING. Here: SEARCH COUNTS MAY JUSTIFY RAISING SOMETHING AND MAY NOT JUSTIFY LOWERING WHAT IS NEVER FOUND — because you cannot search for what you do not know exists, and the nodes nobody finds are precisely the ones a discoverability problem hides.

THE OPTIONS.

(a) COUNT APPEARANCES IN SEARCH RESULTS, UNWEIGHTED. Cheapest. Counter: all three confounds hit it directly, and a result appearing in a list is not evidence anybody cared about it. Anthony's refinement is a direct argument against this one.

(b) COUNT ONLY WHAT WAS THEN READ IN FULL — a node that a search surfaced AND the agent then fetched with `get_node`. Much stronger evidence of relevance, and it discards the ranked-but-ignored tail where the BM25 confound lives. ⭐ NOTE THIS IS A RELEVANCE WEIGHT OF A DIFFERENT KIND — BEHAVIOURAL RATHER THAN LEXICAL — and it needs no score at all, so it sidesteps the comparability problem entirely. Counter: still an agent's behaviour, not the user's.

(c) RELEVANCE-WEIGHTED ACCUMULATION, per Anthony's refinement, using (i), (ii) or (iii) above. Closest to what he described. Counter: (i) and (ii) are approximations of the thing he means and (iii) depends on `dec:idea-embeddings-adoption`.

(d) RECORD THE SEARCH AS AN EVENT ATTACHED TO THE BRAINSTORM IT PRECEDED — "this idea was captured after searching X, and these nodes came back, at these ranks". A fact about the user's train of thought rather than about retrieval, and it composes with (c) since the weights ride on the event. Counter: covers only searches made during capture, and most searching is not.

(e) DO NOTHING; DERIVE IMPORTANCE FROM STRUCTURE INSTEAD. Measured the same day: 61 of 83 open decisions govern nothing, so structure currently has nothing to say about most of the pile — which is precisely the hole this idea would fill. Counter to the counter: that may be an argument for recording structure better rather than for measuring retrieval.

NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR EACH OTHER: this ranks by ATTENTION, `dec:idea-a-critical-path-through-the-undecided` ranks by CONSEQUENCE. A node can be repeatedly searched and block nothing, or block everything and never be searched. Whether either alone is enough, or they compose into one bounded top-5, is open in both nodes and settled in neither.
properties.name: OPEN — should repeated, RELEVANCE-WEIGHTED search hits mark a node as becoming critical, when BM25 scores are not comparable across queries and the same data is named "the worst offender" for telemetry?
properties.rationale:
Anthony's idea, with his own refinement folded in the same session rather than minted as a third node — the refinement constrains the answer to this question, it is not a new question, and the complaint driving all of this is a pile of undecided nodes.

The load-bearing addition is that the refinement is RIGHT and CANNOT BE IMPLEMENTED AS DESCRIBED on the current search. Measuring two queries about the same subject and getting 4.48 against 35.75 is what turns "use the relevance score" from an implementation detail into a decision with a dependency: the 0.1/0.4/0.8 model needs a bounded similarity, which is what `dec:idea-embeddings-adoption` is about. Recording that link is worth more than the idea itself, because a later session would otherwise reach for `score` believing it means relevance.

Option (b) is flagged because it dissolves the problem rather than solving it: what the agent chose to READ is a relevance signal that needs no score and cannot be gamed by query length.

The telemetry collision and the three confounds are kept with tests attached rather than as caveats. The BM25-length one is checkable in an afternoon and would decide whether any lexical weighting is worth having at all.

properties.decision: PROPOSED IDEA, not a commitment: give the agent a lookup from a FILE (or symbol) to the Decisions, Requirements and Constraints that govern it — "what does the design already say about the code I am about to change?" — resolved by traversal rather than by keyword search.
properties.name: IDEA — an agent about to edit a file can ask what the design already decided about it, without guessing search terms
properties.rationale:
RECORDED UNDER ANTHONY'S 2026-08-08 TEST PROTOCOL: run a task as if reflow2 did not exist, then run it leaning on reflow2, compare, and propose what would have helped. His stated aim, quoted so it is not lost: he is NOT trying to change how the agent functions, but to make available skills/tools that make the agent's job easier and better. This idea is scoped to that.

THE EVIDENCE IS TWO FIXES DONE THE SAME DAY, WITH DIFFERENT AMOUNTS OF REFLOW2.

(1) THE DUPLICATES/MERGE FIX — reflow2 CHANGED THE OUTCOME, and the whole difference was one call. dev_storyflow reported merge candidates scoring 81-85 on unrelated nodes. Read as a code problem, the obvious fix is 'the scorer is bad, raise the threshold' — a plausible, shippable, WRONG fix. A `search_design` for 'duplicate merge similarity' returned `dec:ask-not-repair` as the top hit, and that decision reframed the entire task: possible_duplicate is a DETECT gap, HEAL merges only on a human-drawn edge, a heuristic must not drive it. The bug was not a bad threshold; it was an ACCEPTED DECISION DEFEATED BY THE BUILD, and the correct fix (mark the edge's basis, re-route suspicions to the gap layer) is not reachable from the code alone. Without reflow2 this session ships a threshold bump and the design stays quietly violated.

(2) THE CLAIM-LIVENESS FIX — reflow2 helped at the FRAMING and not at all at the SOLUTION. The graph supplied the finding that mattered (`cap:claim-liveness` was status `verified` while its central claim was false under `--shared`) and `propagate_change` named exactly what to touch, including three Verifications that would be invalidated. But the fix itself — an RAII seat lease, and then a two-set registry after the first design proved unsafe — came entirely from reading code and from a FAILING TEST. No reflow2 detector had anything to say about it. Worth stating plainly rather than overclaiming: the two-set flaw was caught by `cargo test`, not by the design brain.

THE GENERALISATION, and it is the actionable part: REFLOW2'S LEVERAGE IS AT PROBLEM FRAMING AND BLAST RADIUS, NOT AT SOLUTION DESIGN. That is not a weakness — it is where a design brain SHOULD have leverage, and it argues for investing there rather than trying to help write the patch.

SO WHAT IS MISSING, CONCRETELY: in case (1) the decision was found because a lucky choice of search words hit it. `search_design` is BM25 over node text, so the agent must already suspect what it is looking for. AN AGENT ABOUT TO EDIT `crates/reflow2-core/src/heal.rs` SHOULD BE ABLE TO ASK WHAT GOVERNS THAT FILE AND BE TOLD `dec:ask-not-repair`, WITHOUT KNOWING THE WORD 'DUPLICATE'. The graph already holds every hop needed: `art:heal` REALIZES `cap:heal`, which is GOVERNED_BY the decisions that constrain it, SATISFIES the requirements behind it, and is VERIFIED by the checks that would break. That is a traversal from a path to its governing intent, and today there is no tool for it — `propagate_change` is the closest but needs a recorded ChangeEvent and answers 'what does this touch', not 'what was already decided here'.

WHY THIS FITS THE STATED AIM: it changes nothing about how the agent works. It is a lookup the agent chooses to make at the moment it is already opening a file, and it answers the one question a stateless agent cannot answer for itself and does not know to ask.

CANDIDATE SHAPES, none chosen: (a) a `governs` tool taking a path or symbol, returning Decisions/Requirements/Constraints/Verifications reachable from the Artifact at that location, ranked by hop distance; (b) the same as a skill that runs before an edit, the read-side sibling of impact-check; (c) cheapest of all and worth pricing first — have `link_artifact`/`reconcile_artifacts` responses already carry the governing decisions for the artifact named, since the traversal is the same and the agent is already there.

OPEN QUESTIONS THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: whether path-level granularity is enough (a 1,700-line file may be governed by decisions relevant to only one of its functions); whether an unregistered file — one with no Artifact — should answer 'nothing governs this' or 'this file is not in the design', which are very different statements and the second is the honest one; and whether ranking by hop distance is meaningful or merely plausible.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-24, raising it inside the ephemeral-store idea: *"may have to make safeguards to ensure that the reflow2 graph is exported at the conclusion of each session"*. Nothing here is intent and nothing is planned.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN QUESTION rather than a clause of `dec:idea-the-store-becomes-a-session-cache-and-the-export-becomes-the-truth` — read in full and judged distinct: that one asks WHAT the enduring artifact is; this asks WHAT MAKES IT RELIABLE. They are answered by different work — one is a storage-model decision, the other is a durability mechanism — and this half is worth something even if the inversion is never taken, because **the export is ALREADY the only copy that survives losing the graph directory.** `loop_status` says exactly that on every call today.

⭐ THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES THIS SHARP. Today an unexported session loses THE SESSION'S WORK and the store still holds the design. Under the inversion, an unexported session loses THE DESIGN. **The same failure changes from an annoyance into data loss, and nothing about the mechanism changes with it.** That is why he flagged it in the same breath as the idea rather than afterwards.

🛑 IT HAS ALREADY HAPPENED, WHICH TAKES THIS OUT OF THE HYPOTHETICAL. `fact:defect-the-export-was-skipped-because-the-instructions-imply-a-stop-that-is-not-needed` (2026-08-15) records an export that was skipped, for a reason nobody would have predicted: the written instructions implied a stop that was not needed. Not negligence — a correct-looking reading of a correct-looking procedure.

EVERY MECHANISM REFLOW2 HAS TODAY IS A NUDGE, AND A NUDGE IS NOT A GUARANTEE:
- The **Stop hook** (`loop_nudge.py`) blocks a finish with unchecked writes — **ONCE**, by its own design, and never twice.
- `loop_status` REPORTS unexported nodes. Reporting is not writing.
- ⚠️ **And the hook is one-harness-only.** `dec:idea-the-loop-nudge-exists-for-one-harness-only` is ACCEPTED: the mechanism is `.claude/settings.json`. A durability guarantee that exists only inside Claude Code is not a durability guarantee — and flo2's users would not be in Claude Code at all.

⇒ **THE GUARANTEE CANNOT LIVE IN THE HARNESS, BECAUSE THE HARNESS IS THE THING THAT MIGHT NOT COME BACK.** A session ends by crashing, by a killed terminal, by a closed laptop, by a container being reaped. None of those run a Stop hook. Anything depending on an orderly shutdown answers a different question from the one that matters.

ROADS, none chosen, listed so the ones not taken keep their reasoning:
1. **EXPORT ON EVERY WRITE (write-through).** Strongest guarantee, and the hosted-tier node already recorded the objection: *"the export being whole-document is correct for an archival action and fatal on a per-change path"*. Dead unless the export becomes incremental.
2. **PERIODIC / DEBOUNCED EXPORT.** Bounded loss instead of no loss. Cheap, harness-independent, and it turns "did the session export?" into "how much did we lose?" — a question with a knob on it.
3. **THE SERVER OWNS IT, NOT THE SESSION.** The shared server already outlives any one session and already knows when a design goes idle; eviction and export become the same event. ⭐ This is the road that fits what already exists — the server is the only component that observes a session ENDING without being the session.
4. **DECLINE THE INVERSION** — the store stays authoritative, the export stays archival. Costs nothing, keeps the 9x inflation and the open-instance ceiling.
5. **A WAL/JOURNAL BESIDE THE BLOB**, replayed on hydrate. Ordinary database engineering, and it re-implements part of what RocksDB already does — named here so nobody proposes it as though it were new.

⚠️ AN OBJECTION TO THE WHOLE FRAME, recorded beside the idea rather than used to argue it down: **RocksDB already solves durability, and solves it well.** Moving the durable copy to a JSON document chooses a weaker durability story on purpose, in exchange for cheap hydration and cheap eviction. That trade may be right for a hosted tier; it is not obviously right for one person on one laptop, where the store has never lost anything.

RECORDED AS A QUESTION, NOT A CONCLUSION.
properties.name: OPEN — if reflow2.json becomes the enduring artifact, what GUARANTEES it is written? Every mechanism reflow2 has today nudges, and a nudge that is skipped once has already been measured
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill: recorded as an idea, nothing promoted, nothing settled.

Split from `dec:idea-the-store-becomes-a-session-cache-and-the-export-becomes-the-truth` deliberately, and the split recorded with `distinct_from` after reading it: one node holding "what is durable" and "what makes it durable" could only ever be half-answered. This half stands alone because the export is ALREADY the only copy surviving loss of `.reflow2/graph`, so the guarantee question is live today and waits on no storage-model change.

properties.decision:
✅ **DECIDED 2026-08-14 ON ANTHONY'S WORD — OPTION (b), AND NARROWER THAN (b) WAS WRITTEN.**

HIS WORDS: *"for the pages, I'd like to only use renderings of systems engineering views the agent generates from graph content of reflow2 itself. I'd like to have some cutting edge rendering (that we periodically update) to show that contents come from the graph and that with a good agent, you can create some pretty awesome views."*

⇒ **ONLY renderings. Not "mostly", not "landing page plus renderings" — (a) and (c) are both declined.** The page is a DEMONSTRATION, and its subject is its own provenance: it exists to show that the content came out of the graph and that a capable agent can render it well.

⭐⭐ **THAT PURPOSE SETS A HARDER HONESTY STANDARD THAN DOCUMENTATION, and it is the reason this is worth stating rather than just building.** A doc that drifts is stale. **A page whose entire claim is "this came from the graph" is FALSIFIED by one hand-written fact.** So `render_views.py`'s existing doctrine is not a nicety here, it is the product: *"it may only emit what the graph states… anything a viewpoint NEEDS but the graph cannot supply goes on the CONFESSIONS list."* The confessions are not a blemish on the demo — **they are the strongest evidence the rest is real.**

⚠️ **THE COST HE ACCEPTED, STATED PLAINLY: A NEWCOMER LANDS ON SYSTEMS-ENGINEERING VIEWS WITH NO ORIENTATION.** "Only renderings" means the page cannot carry a hand-written *"reflow2 is a persistent design brain…"* paragraph. Someone arriving cold meets a functional view before they know what they are looking at. **His own next sentence is plausibly the answer to this — see `dec:idea-a-generated-explainer-for-someone-new` — and that connection is recorded rather than assumed.**

⚠️ **"PERIODICALLY UPDATE" CARRIES A KNOWN COST, ALREADY MEASURED HERE.** `chg:impact-propagation-is-rendered-not-written`: a re-render churns wording, so the diff is noisy and *"drift here will need reading as 're-rendered', not as 'the design moved'"*. A page refreshed on a schedule will do this every time. Worth deciding once whether the refresh is committed output (noisy diffs, reviewable) or an Actions deploy that never commits (clean repo, unreviewable) — which is the placement question below, now materially easier because **nothing on the page is hand-written, so nothing is lost by not committing it.**

═══ WHAT STAYS OPEN, DELIBERATELY ═══

· **WHICH views.** `docs/viewpoints.md` holds the catalogue and `render_views.py` renders several; which of them belong on a public page, and in what order, is unanswered.
· **WHAT "cutting edge rendering" means.** He asked for it and did not specify. Not inferred.
· **PLACEMENT.** `index.html` at the repo root was his sketch, prefaced *"something like this"*. This root is a Rust workspace; `/docs` already exists and already holds `loop-dag.html`; an Actions deploy commits nothing. **The ruling above makes the Actions route cheaper than it was**, but it is not chosen here.
· **REFRESH CADENCE.** "Periodically" is not a schedule.

📌 STILL NOT ASKED AND STILL NOT ASSUMED: whether this is reflow2's own design published, or a template a CONSUMER could use for theirs. His wording — *"from graph content of reflow2 itself"* — answers it for THIS page and says nothing about the general case.

════════ THE OPTIONS AS PUT TO HIM, KEPT ════════

**(a) A LANDING PAGE** — hand-written, an afternoon, and every other tool has one. **DECLINED.** It goes stale the way `dec:idea-outward-docs-are-rendered-from-the-graph` was opened about, and this project has been bitten: a doc presented eight impact kinds never implemented and referenced an edge type retired five days before it was written.

**(b) ⭐ THE DESIGN GRAPH, RENDERED — CHOSEN**, and narrowed to *only* this.

**(c) BOTH, LAYERED** — **DECLINED**, which also declines the shape `dec:idea-which-docs-can-never-be-a-projection` is open about. ⚠️ That decision stays open for the rest of reflow2's outward docs; this ruling covers the PAGE only, and does not settle it generally.
properties.name: DECIDED — the public page carries ONLY renderings the agent generates from reflow2's own graph; the page is the evidence for its own claim
properties.rationale:
Captured under capture-intent rather than built, because he sequenced it explicitly ("post release") and because the one thing that decides the size of the work — what is on the page — is the one thing he did not say.

The mechanism he described is recorded as a SKETCH rather than a specification, on his own framing of "something like this". Transcribing `index.html` at the root into a requirement would have converted an illustration into a commitment, in a repository whose root is a cargo workspace.

Recorded as its own node rather than folded into the requirement because it reaches two decisions that were already open before he asked — outward docs as projections, and which docs can never be one — and a question connecting three threads deserves to be findable from all of them. The near-duplicate guard fired on the requirement and was right to: they are the same subject, and saying so on the record is cheaper than a reader later wondering whether one supersedes the other.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing is claimed as intent, nothing is planned, and nobody has asked for this. Anthony, 2026-08-19, revisiting a use case he says he had in mind when he created the **adopt** skill: *"taking some code base, running adopt skill on it, then we translate into another language… is there anything we can take from this?"*, prompted by The New Stack on Canonical + University of Bristol translating AppArmor and snap-confine from C to Rust.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
WHAT THE ARTICLE ACTUALLY SAYS, because it reframes the use case

· *"Generating code at scale is no longer the hard part — the hard part is proving that code actually does what the original did."*
· *"Trust, not code, is the bottleneck."*
· Canonical's stated goal is not a rewrite. It is to find out **what evidence maintainers would need before trusting an automated translation of production code.** They are explicitly *"not rushing to rewrite either one"*.
· Their method: an LLM generates Rust, then fuzzing plus formal program analysis compares the two implementations, and **symbolic repair** diagnoses and fixes each behavioural mismatch.
· *"A Rust port that interprets a policy differently from the existing implementation might compile perfectly and still be wrong."*
· `unsafe` is the trap: a translator can carry hard C constructs across by leaning on it, *"but relying on unsafe too heavily would bring many of the original memory-safety risks into the new code."* Idiomatic Rust needs *"changes to data structures and lifetimes across several functions or entire modules"* — so a faithful port is not line-by-line.
· Target scale: *"entire repositories containing hundreds of thousands of lines of C."*

⭐ THE REFRAME. The naive version of this use case is "adopt the C, generate the Rust from the graph." The article says that half is **solved and is not the bottleneck**. So if reflow2 has a part here at all, it is on the trust side, not the generation side.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
IDEAS, unranked, each with what is cheap or expensive about it

**A. reflow2 holds the ORACLE, not the translation.** adopt(C) recovers what the system is FOR; that recovered intent is the specification the Rust must satisfy, and the graph is where evidence that it does accumulates per capability, dated and attributed. Cheap, in that it needs no new mechanism.
   ⚠️ COUNTER, and it is serious: adopt's intent is AGENT-RECOVERED FROM THE ARTIFACT BEING REPLACED. Using it as the oracle for a security-critical port risks a graph that is complete, confident and wrong in exactly the way the article warns a port can be. `req:adopt-says-how-much-it-got` exists precisely so recovery reports its own coverage — that number is the honest precondition, and a low one should stop this cold.

**B. A PORT IS TWO AS-DESIGNED RECORDS, AND reflow2 ALREADY COMPARES THOSE.** `cap:certify-restructuring` (status `verified`) classifies every divergence between two design records as function-bearing, structural, or unclassified, and returns preserved / not_preserved / **indeterminate** — with *"unclassified never passes."* A translation is the largest restructuring there is: function must be identical, structure is expected to differ. `compare_designs` / `pair_designs` are the same family.
   ⭐ WHY THIS IS INTERESTING: it is a DESIGN-level differential, far coarser than symbolic execution, and it catches a class those tools cannot — a capability present in one implementation and absent in the other. Nobody is looking there.
   ⚠️ COUNTER: coarse means coarse. It would never have caught AppArmor parsing a policy differently, which is the failure the article is actually about.

**C. `unsafe` is a DESIGN-level debt signal, not a test outcome.** "No capability counts as ported while its realizing artifact exceeds N unsafe blocks" is expressible today — a DesignRule with stop-the-build power, or a Constraint, or a `GATED_ON` threshold. The article treats unsafe-overuse as the thing that quietly defeats the whole exercise, which is exactly the kind of claim that should be visible in a design rather than discovered in review.
   ⭐ Also the most under-used part of reflow2 by Anthony's own measure — hard limits are built and barely used (1 Constraint node).

**D. THE BOTTLENECK THEY NAME IS THE THING reflow2 ALREADY COMPUTES.** *"What evidence would a maintainer need"* is a coverage-of-claims-by-checks question: `evidence_report`, `confirmation_ledger`, `coverage_report`, `readiness_report`. The right answer to a maintainer is not "it is equivalent" but "these capabilities have evidence, these do not, and here is what nobody checked" — and reflow2's habit of REFUSING to summarise thin evidence is the feature, not a limitation.

**E. THE CHEAP EXPERIMENT, and the only one with an answer key.** Run adopt on a real C project AND on its existing hand-written Rust port, then `compare_designs`. **`sudo-rs` vs `sudo`** is the strongest candidate: security-critical, deliberately behaviour-compatible, both public, both modest. `uutils` vs GNU coreutils is a second. The question it answers is falsifiable — *does the comparison surface anything a maintainer would care about, or only noise?*
   📌 SAME SHAPE as `dec:idea-run-adopt-on-reflow2-itself-as-a-ground-truth-test`, already in this graph: pick a case where the answer is independently known, then see whether the tool finds it.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 WHERE THIS MUST NOT GO, recorded now while it is cheap to say

reflow2 does not do differential testing, symbolic execution, or repair, and should not start. `dec:non-goal-reflow2-does-not-judge-whether-a-check-is-meaningful` already settles the general form. The fuzzing-plus-formal-analysis half is Bristol's actual research and is where the difficulty lives; a pitch that drifts into "reflow2 verifies the port" would be claiming their result.

⚠️ SCALE IS UNPROVEN. The article's target is 100k+ LOC repositories. adopt has never been run near that, and `cap:bl-211` — genesis assumes an opening BRIEF and has no shape for an opening FOLDER — is open. Any claim about repository-scale ingest is currently unevidenced.

⚠️ AND NOBODY ASKED. This is a use case its author envisioned, not one a user brought. `dec:idea-field-evidence-is-a-prioritisation-input` would rank it below anything two projects reported this week.
properties.name: OPEN — in an automated C→Rust style translation, is reflow2's part the ORACLE and the EVIDENCE LEDGER rather than the translation, and does the port become a two-design comparison?
properties.rationale: Recorded as an open question rather than a proposal because Anthony was explicitly revisiting an old idea and asking what could be taken from someone else's work, not stating intent. The article's own framing is what makes it worth recording at all: it separates code generation, which it calls solved, from evidence of behavioural equivalence, which it calls the bottleneck — and that split lands on machinery reflow2 already has (`cap:certify-restructuring`, verified, whose verdict refuses to pass an unclassified divergence) rather than on machinery it would have to build. The counter-arguments are recorded beside each idea rather than argued in conversation, per the brainstorm rule, because the strongest objection here — that adopt's recovered intent is inferred from the very artifact being replaced, so it cannot be a trustworthy oracle for a security-critical port — is the kind of thing that gets lost and then re-proposed. NOTE ON THE RECORD: the first write of this node was malformed in the same way two earlier writes this session were, sending the rationale inside the decision body; corrected in place, and the recurrence is itself evidence on fact:changing-one-sentence-in-a-long-decision-cost-a-full-6242-character-resend.

properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Raised 2026-08-28 from `fact:field-friction-is-captured-and-then-owed-to-nobody`, itself raised because three of four items in a field report said *"still true"* and *"same as 2026-08-18"*.

═══ THE PROBLEM IN ONE LINE ═══

Capture works. **190 defect-facts, 189 with nothing claiming to have answered them, 8 INVALIDATES edges in the whole design, and no `loop_status` debt class counts any of it.** A friction report enters the graph and the one call every session makes cannot see it.

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══

**(a) A NEW DEBT CLASS — `open_field_defects` on `loop_status`.** The obvious answer. ⚠️ Counter, and it is serious: **a count that can never reach zero becomes wallpaper**, and this project has already found that failure three times (`unreviewed_ideas` at 111 of 186, the undeclared-seam list, the unallocated-parts list). 189 rows on the orientation call would be ignored inside a week and would drown the seven numbers that currently mean something.

**(b) SCOPE IT THE WAY `unclaimed_findings` IS SCOPED.** That tool already solves the identical problem for a different question — it asks *"what did THIS SESSION make false?"* and returns a handful rather than hundreds, on the explicit reasoning that *"design-wide there are hundreds of open observations and a list that long is wallpaper."* The same trick may apply: not "all open field defects" but "field defects on ground you touched", or "reported more than once". ⭐ **This is the option with a working precedent inside the same codebase.**

**(c) MAKE REPETITION THE SIGNAL.** A friction item reported in two separate field reports is worth more than one reported once, and the second report is exactly when it becomes cheap to notice. Nothing today can tell that two reports describe the same item. ⚠️ Counter: needs the reports linked to their items, which is manual, and the reporter used placeholders (`cap:X`) precisely to avoid naming real nodes.

**(d) NOTHING NEW — USE `INVALIDATES` PROPERLY AND THE NUMBER FALLS.** Much of the 189 is surely fixed with nobody having drawn the edge. Sweeping and closing what is genuinely done might leave a backlog small enough to read without any new machinery. ⚠️ Counter: that is a one-time cleanup, not a mechanism; it will re-accumulate. ⭐ But it is the honest FIRST move regardless of which option follows, because **nobody knows how big the real backlog is** and every other option is being designed against a number that is a raw count rather than a measurement.

**(e) IT IS NOT REFLOW2'S JOB.** Bug triage belongs in an issue tracker, and this project has repeatedly refused to become one — the Task node type was killed on 2026-08-25 as *"the road to being a tracker"*. ⚠️ Counter: this is not tracking work, it is noticing that a recorded observation has gone unanswered — which is what `unclaimed_findings` and `invalidated_findings` already do. The line between them is real but thin, and worth stating rather than assuming.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT MUST BE MEASURED BEFORE CHOOSING ═══

**How many of the 189 are actually live?** The count is raw: `fact_type` is an optional free-string, so it both over- and under-counts, and an unknown share are fixed-but-unclosed. Designing a debt class against that number would be building for a backlog nobody has sized. **Option (d) is that measurement as well as a candidate remedy.**

📌 ADJACENT, NOT THE SAME: `fact:the-upstream-watch-is-findable-only-in-reflow2s-own-words` and `fact:a-findings-name-can-claim-more-than-its-data...` are both about a record being ACCURATE and still not reaching a reader. This one is about a record reaching nobody at all. Whether they are one problem — **the design writes faithfully and reads back selectively** — is itself unsettled.
properties.name: OPEN — what makes a field-reported defect OWED, when the loop counts structure and a friction report is a fact?
properties.rationale:
Raised because the repeats are the loudest signal in the report and have a different cause from the headline defect. Each repeated item has a local explanation and fixing all three would leave the pattern intact.

Filed against `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself` because that rule makes field use the point, and field use produces exactly the input with no return path.

Option (d) is listed last among the doing-something options but flagged as the honest first move: every other option is being designed against a raw count, and nobody has sized the real backlog. Option (e) is a genuine option, not a strawman — this project has killed an adjacent idea for exactly that reason and the line deserves stating.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. Anthony asked for it to be thought through this way rather than built on the spot, 2026-08-21: "I'd like to capture as the third leg... maybe we brainstorm on it and test out our new concept to see if it links to other related ideas? then we accept the proposed idea and then implement?"

THE OPEN QUESTION: what, if anything, should notice an idea that connects to nothing?

WHY IT IS OPEN AT ALL. The brainstorm skill now asks for the honest edges AND for a written line when none is drawn. That is the INSTRUCTION leg. `fact:vocabulary-needs-three-legs-and-a-users-project-gets-none-of-it` says an instruction without a detector leaves the vocabulary empty in EVERY project, not just this one — and the 145-ideas-12-edges measurement is what that emptiness looks like when only two legs are present. So the missing leg is named and the shape of the hole is known.

🛑🛑 AND THE OBVIOUS BUILD COLLIDES WITH THE SKILL IT WOULD SERVE. brainstorm/SKILL.md step 2 says, in as many words: "Do not run detect-and-ask over brainstormed nodes. It would ask the user to firm up exactly what they deliberately left soft, which teaches them that thinking out loud has a cost." A detector that fires on every unlinked idea is precisely that. Built naively, the third leg would tax the one activity the whole skill exists to keep free.

⭐ THE COLLISION WAS ALREADY SETTLED, ELEVEN DAYS EARLY, BY A REQUIREMENT NEITHER NODE MENTIONS. `req:detecting-is-not-asking` (Anthony, 2026-08-19): detecting a gap and inviting its closure are DIFFERENT ACTS and only one is urgent — detection stays unconditional, the invitation waits for a boundary. Every option below is really a position on WHERE this one lands on that line. That is the finding of this brainstorm, and it came out of the search the new linking step spends rather than from thinking harder.

=== THE OPTIONS ===

(a) A `detect_gaps` finding — say `unlinked_idea` — on any proposed Decision with no relation edge and no "no real relation" line. CHEAP: the detector framework exists and this is a two-predicate rule. EXPENSIVE: it lands in the list a user reads as their to-do, which is the nudge the skill forbids, and it would land there 111 times on this graph the day it shipped. A finding that fires a hundred times on day one teaches people to filter the whole category.

(b) The same rule, but the INVITATION held until a boundary — a capture-session, an increment close — while the detection itself runs always. Exactly the shape `req:detecting-is-not-asking` describes, and it keeps thinking-out-loud free at the moment of thinking. More work than (a): the detector is the easy half, the boundary is the part that has to be chosen and honoured.

(c) Not a per-node finding at all, but a POPULATION LINE in the sweep's coverage — "145 ideas, 12 linked, 111 reaching nothing" — reported as a number, never as a defect against any one idea. CHEAPEST and quietest, and it inherits the property the coverage work was built for: a detector that reports zero because it had NOTHING TO RUN ON is distinguishable from one that ran clean. It answers "is the linking step working" without ever telling any individual idea it is deficient. WEAKEST on the three legs, though: a number in a report is not something the loop asks about, and the leg was specified as a detector that surfaces absence.

(d) Nothing on the ideas; the compliance check on the SKILL is the whole third leg. Already built as `LINK_CONTRACT` in skill_lint (2026-08-21). HONEST LIMIT, stated plainly: that check guards the INSTRUCTION against deletion, not the graph against being unlinked. It would pass green over a graph where no agent ever drew an edge. It is a real guard, but it is not this leg.

(e) Do nothing and let the instruction carry it. The null option, and it deserves a fair hearing: it is exactly what was in force for the previous 145 ideas, and it is what produced 12 edges. The evidence against it is unusually direct.

=== WHAT IS NOT YET KNOWN ===
Whether the "no real relation" line can be READ mechanically at all. The skill asks for it in prose, and a detector that cannot tell "somebody looked and found nothing" from "nobody looked" would report the two identically — which is the exact failure the line was added to prevent. If it cannot be read, the line needs a structural home (a property, or an edge to nothing) before any of (a)-(c) can distinguish them. THAT QUESTION IS PRIOR TO THE CHOICE, and it is measurable rather than arguable.

=== HOW THIS NODE WAS LINKED ===
Recorded here because it is the first use of the step it is about. The near-matches came from four searches run before writing; four edges were drawn and each names its reason in `evidence`. The collision in the second paragraph and the reconciliation in the third were both found in those hits, not reasoned out — which is the case the linking step was arguing for.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ ACCEPTED BY ANTHONY, 2026-08-21 — OPTION (b), WITH THE PRIOR QUESTION ANSWERED FIRST
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

HIS CHOICE: detect always, invite at a boundary. The detector runs unconditionally so the record stays honest; the INVITATION waits for a boundary (a capture-session, an increment close) so that thinking out loud costs nothing at the moment of thinking. This is `req:detecting-is-not-asking` applied to the case it was not written for, and it is why the collision recorded above does not have to be paid for.

AND THE PREREQUISITE IS PART OF THE ACCEPTANCE, not a caveat on it. "Looked and found nothing" needs a home a detector can READ. The skill asks for it in prose today, and prose cannot be told apart from silence — so the very first thing built has to be a structural place for that judgement, on the pattern `distinct_from` already uses on the dedup guard: the guard does not infer that you considered the duplicate, it makes you say so, and then the saying is a fact rather than an inference.

WITHOUT IT THE DETECTOR WOULD REPORT THE TWO STATES IDENTICALLY — an idea somebody looked at and found genuinely new, and an idea nobody has opened — which is the exact failure the "no real relation" line was added to prevent. A detector that cannot tell those apart is not a weaker version of this leg. It is a machine for producing false findings about people who did the work.

⭐ SO THE THREE STATES THE BUILD MUST DISTINGUISH ARE:
  (A) LINKED — carries at least one relation to another node.
  (B) REVIEWED AND DELIBERATELY UNLINKED — somebody judged the near-matches and drew nothing, and said so.
  (C) NOBODY LOOKED — the only one of the three that is a finding.

Option (c)'s population line is not a rival to this and should not be argued against it: a count over the whole graph answers "is the linking step working at all", which is a different question from "which idea has nobody opened". If it is cheap once (C) is computable, it is worth having beside it.
properties.name: OPEN — what should notice an idea that connects to nothing?

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-13, from his own observation that graph_id may not be unique. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen.

⚙️ HOW THIS WAS CREATED, said plainly: `add_decision`'s search-first guard fired and named three nodes. All three were read and judged different (below). The `distinct_from` override could not be used because the parameter would not serialize as an array from this client — it arrived as a string and was refused — so the node was written with `create_node` instead. That is a workaround for a client serialization fault, NOT an evasion of the guard: the reading and the judgement the guard asks for were both done first, and are recorded here in place of the edge.

READ AND JUDGED DIFFERENT FROM THE THREE THE GUARD NAMED. `fact:two-adopted-stores-share-one-graph-id-2026-08-13` is the MEASUREMENT — two stores, one id, and why; this is the question of what to DO about it, which a fact cannot hold. `dec:identity-out-of-band` is the accepted PRINCIPLE, and this node defers to it entirely rather than reopening it. `dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs` asks whether ONE SESSION should reason across several designs at once — orthogonal: that is breadth of attachment, this is two designs being indistinguishable by name.

⭐ THIS IS NOT A MISSING DECISION. `dec:identity-out-of-band` is ACCEPTED and settles the principle: "a design's identity is a UUID minted at genesis and stored in the graph; the friendly name is a label on top of it." It names what it rejected and why — "deriving from the project name or path (TWO DESIGNS CAN SHARE BOTH, and the id must survive being copied)". The shape of the answer is decided. What is open is what to do about designs adopted BEFORE it, and that touches HIS data.

═══ THE OPTIONS ═══

A — REFUSE THE AMBIGUOUS ID AND LIST WHAT IT MATCHED. The registry stops silently overwriting; `attach` on a duplicated id fails naming both paths, and discovery reports the collision instead of hiding one design. CHEAP, LOCAL, TOUCHES NO STORED DATA. Not a new policy either: `dec:how-a-session-is-pointed-at-a-design` already states the rule, written before this case was known — "DEFAULT WHEN EXACTLY ONE DESIGN IS REACHABLE; REFUSE AND LIST THEM WHEN SEVERAL ARE. A design chosen by silence is how three graphs appeared on one repo." Leaves both designs unreachable by name, but LOUDLY rather than silently.

B — RE-MINT THE COLLIDING LEGACY IDS. Fixes it at the root and matches `dec:identity-out-of-band` exactly. EXPENSIVE: `graph_id` is part of the export's content hash, so re-minting breaks every existing export, chain link and committed record for that design — precisely what adoption was introduced to protect. Anthony's data, Anthony's call, and it needs a migration story rather than a flag.

C — ANTHONY'S COMPOSITE NAME, in his words: "can you name a graph by graph_id.first_node_unique_id". Recorded as offered, with three objections beside it rather than used to kill it. (1) A GRAPH CAN HOLD SEVERAL PROJECT NODES — dev_storyflow holds two, `proj:fleet_ops` and `proj:storyflow`, neither mirrored, and the schema says only that there is "normally" one, in an extraction hint. `Project.mirror_of` exists so a mirrored foreign project can sit alongside yours, so mirroring adds more. (2) "FIRST" IS UNDEFINED — no ordering exists; exports sort by id, so "first" means alphabetically first, an arbitrary tiebreak on a name. (3) IT IS CIRCULAR, and this is the strong one: identity lives in sidecars precisely so it is readable BEFORE opening, because opening MINTS an identity — the failure that once created a third graph beside two populated ones. `Registry::discover` and `describe_at` both depend on never opening. A name derived from a node inside the graph must be read by opening the graph you chose by name.
  📌 THE RESCUE THAT KEEPS THE INSIGHT: the composite need not be DERIVED at read time — it could be WRITTEN into the sidecar at mint or adopt, staying pre-open readable. But then it is doing option B's job with extra steps, since the sidecar already carries `label` separately from `graph_id`.
  ⚠️ THE TENSION TO NAME: deriving identity from graph content is the shape `dec:identity-out-of-band` rejected on principle — "names are assigned with zero coordination, NEVER DERIVED FROM SHARED STATE". Its rationale records the fleet DELETING a mint-race guard, because the race was an artifact of deriving the handle at all.

D — SCOPE AROUND IT. One registry root per neighbourhood so colliding designs never co-occur. Does not survive his actual case: `~/project` IS the neighbourhood and both stores live in it.

═══ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS ═══

⚠️ 1. NOTHING IS BROKEN TODAY. No transport is wired to the registry, so no session can yet select a design by id. The collision is LATENT — which argues for fixing it BEFORE the transport ships rather than after.
⚠️ 2. TWO STORES IS NOT A POPULATION. One owner's machine, and the count may never grow: the four minted designs are clean and every future design mints. Option A may be the whole of what is ever needed.
⚠️ 3. RE-MINTING IS THE EXPENSIVE KIND OF RIGHT. It repairs the model and invalidates the record; the adoption decision already weighed that trade once and went the other way, for stated reasons that have not changed.

📌 A FAIR POINT FOR ACTING: the registry's entire isolation guarantee — `ver:a-session-cannot-name-another-design`, passing — rests on ids being unique, and every fixture in it uses distinct ids. The guarantee is not wrong, but it has never been tested against the one case that is true on the owner's own disk.
properties.name: OPEN — what happens when two designs answer to one graph_id, now that the id is an ADDRESS and not just a label?
properties.rationale: Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the thinking survives without being claimed as intent. Kept separate from the pair-types question because the two are unrelated and one node holding both could only ever be half-answered. Worth keeping for three things: the principle is already settled by dec:identity-out-of-band so only the migration is open; Anthony's composite proposal is recorded in his own words with the circularity objection beside it rather than used to argue it down; and the latency point is time-sensitive, because the collision stays harmless only until a transport makes graph_id an address — which is the next thing the linking work would build.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-21. Nothing here is intent.

HIS WORDS: "as we are still in development of reflow2, if we add another file, does it automatically get added (being proactive) to a black box or is this something I have to remember (being reactive)? as a user using reflow2 is designing a new project, when do functions get allocated to a black box? again, does reflow2 do this automatically or is it something the user kicks off?" And: "the point on a new project is you don't immediately allocate functions to a black box."

⭐ THIS IS NOT A NEW POSITION — IT IS THE OPEN HALF OF ONE ALREADY ACCEPTED. dec:idea-allocation-waits-for-the-last-responsible-moment settled the PRINCIPLE on 2026-08-14: defer to the last responsible moment, per-capability scope with a project default, and never allocating is a LEGITIMATE TERMINAL STATE rather than a stalled process. What was never settled is WHAT NOTICES THE MOMENT.

⭐⭐ AND THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT RECORDED BESIDE THAT RULING PREDICTED TODAY'S MEASUREMENT, WORD FOR WORD. It was flagged to him before he accepted, and he accepted with it open: "artifacts get written against an assumed structure long before anyone calls allocate. If real files already embody a de facto allocation, then deferring the decision defers only the RECORD of it, and the graph arrives late to something the build already did... it argues the trigger should watch ARTIFACTS APPEARING rather than the allocate call." That was a worry seven days ago. It is now measured.

=== WHAT WAS MEASURED, 2026-08-21, and it is an ASYMMETRY ===

ALLOCATION IS SEMI-AUTOMATIC, and this half works. `unallocated_capability` is a real gap source: capture a capability bound to nothing and it fires on every detect_gaps, appears in loop_status, survives sessions, and the Stop hook nudges when graph writes happen with no loop check. `propose_allocation` will suggest a placement without applying it.
