properties.rationale: Deferred on Anthony's word, 2026-07-28 — but flagged as the item most deserving to be UNparked first, because it contradicts a founding requirement (req:intent-preserved, the past is never overwritten) and does so SILENTLY: record_change reported success both times and the design's own history lost a version with no warning. Deferred rather than patched because the fix is a genuine three-way choice, not an oversight: snapshot identity per REVISION (include the ChangeEvent id — truest to the founding rule, but HAS_SNAPSHOT becomes one-to-many and "the snapshot for this epoch" stops being a single thing readers can assume); REFUSE a second record_change in one epoch (cheap and loud, but epochs bound a round of WORK not a single edit, so it pushes an unrelated concern onto the caller); or keep one snapshot per epoch DELIBERATELY as the state at epoch start, making the second call a no-op (preserves the original, loses the intermediate, and needs semantics written down that are currently only implied). Each changes what a reader may assume, so it is a vocabulary-shaped call. What is NOT open: the silence. If a revision cannot be snapshotted without discarding an earlier one, the call must say so — that part needs no decision.

properties.decision: Accepted the gap gap:a961bfe399679dbf.
properties.name: Reviewed: gap:a961bfe399679dbf
properties.rationale:
Anthony's word, 2026-08-24: accept the component-granularity check once, and add a per-skill check later only where a specific skill earns its own proof.

THE GAP OFFERED EXACTLY THIS as one of its two ways on ("accept component granularity here once"), and it is the right one here. The coverage is real, not absent — cmp:skills has a PASSING check, one hop away, and these nine capabilities sit under it.

WHY DEEPENING WOULD BE CEREMONY RATHER THAN ASSURANCE. A skill is text served to an agent. What a check can actually assert about one — that it is well-formed, that it is reachable, that its trigger conditions are stated — is precisely what the component-level check already asserts across all of them, and asserting it nine more times in nine more places multiplies maintenance without adding evidence. Nine checks that all prove the same property are one check with extra bookkeeping.

⭐ THIS IS AN OVER-ENGINEERING CALL AND WAS MADE AS ONE. Anthony's standing concern is designs that get overcomplicated where a simple solution will do. A blanket rule that every capability needs its own verification produces exactly that, and the granularity detector exists to ASK rather than to demand — which is why it offers both roads instead of failing.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN IT: a skill whose behaviour is more than well-formed text — one that computes something, or whose output a person acts on directly — deserves its own proof. The review expires if these capabilities change, so this is accepted for what they are TODAY, not forever.

DISTINCT, on Anthony's word 2026-08-29. The DUPLICATES edge is deliberate and the two nodes must NOT be merged.

THE HEURISTIC WAS RIGHT TO ASK — one name's words are a subset of the other's, and they do share a mechanism: both record that `orphan_node` short-circuits on degree before it looks at pointer properties, so a well-connected node hides its broken subject. The 2026-08-26 node said it first; the 2026-08-29 node re-derived it without searching, which is itself recorded on the edge.

WHY THEY ARE STILL TWO THINGS:
• `fact:nine-temporalfacts-point-their-subject-at-a-node-that-does-not-exist` is the BROADER record — the count of nine, the 5-versus-4 split across five distinct bad ids, and the cause for five of them (an agent copied a neighbour's `subject_id` convention without checking it resolved).
• `fact:a-dangling-reference-is-only-detected-when-the-node-is-also-edgeless` is NARROWER and carries what the earlier one does not: the argument that the bias runs the wrong way (an edgeless node is the least consequential place for a broken pointer, so the detector was most reliable where it mattered least), and the rule that shipped from it as #373.

⭐ AND THEIR NUMBERS DIFFER WITHOUT EITHER BEING WRONG, which is the strongest reason to keep both. 08-26 measured 8 of 9 caught with 1 invisible; 08-29 measured 7 of 9 with 2. Between those dates `fact:defect-kit-manifest-drift-is-invisible-to-ci` gained edges and crossed from visible to invisible — the finding's own mechanism demonstrating itself on a live node. A merge would have to pick one figure and would destroy that evidence, because the pair IS the observation.

⇒ Merging would either lose content or produce one node asserting two measurements as if they were one. Linked, not merged, is the correct end state — the shape `DUPLICATES` exists for: the same thing said twice, for different reasons, both of which matter.

properties.rationale:
Anthony's own words, 2026-08-23: **"Accept it. A parked idea legitimately governs nothing yet."**

WRITTEN IN 2026-08-26, THREE DAYS LATE, AND THE DELAY IS THE POINT. He answered this on 2026-08-23 and the answer never reached the design, so `open_questions` went on reporting it as `status: answered` with the gap still open, and every session since has been offered the same question he had already settled. `loop_status` carried it as "1 answered question(s) never reached the design" for three days. Being asked twice, worded differently, is how somebody learns the tool is not listening — and here the tool had been told and simply failed to write it down.

WHY THE JUDGEMENT IS RIGHT, and it is the same principle this project settled from a different direction three days later. A `proposed` Decision asserts nothing: that is what `proposed` MEANS, and it is why `dec:idea-a-proposed-decision-asserts-nothing-so-what-may-a-structural-detector-say-about-it` (accepted 2026-08-26) now stops three finding kinds reading a brainstormed idea's edges as commitments. An unconnected parked idea is the same fact one layer up — it governs nothing because it has not been chosen, not because anyone forgot to link it. Demanding relations from every idea would add exactly the ceremony the `brainstorm` skill exists to remove.

⚠️ WHAT THIS ACCEPTANCE DOES NOT SAY. It does not say linking ideas is worthless — `review_relations` exists precisely so a session CAN record a relation or an honest "nothing was related", and the count is still computed. It says an idea connected to nothing is not a DEFECT the loop should press the user about. `dec:idea-linking-half-ideas-needs-a-task-that-can-be-run` remains open on the separate question of whether working that backlog needs a runnable task, and this acknowledgement does not settle it.

📌 THE REVIEW EXPIRES BY CONSTRUCTION if the affected set changes, which is correct here: the finding was raised at 117 of 166 ideas and stood at 110 of 192 when this was written. If the shape shifts materially the question comes back for a fresh judgement rather than staying accepted forever on a number nobody rechecked.

properties.decision: Accepted the gap gap:c628f709c27ad035.
properties.name: Reviewed: gap:c628f709c27ad035
properties.rationale:
LEFT OPEN ON PURPOSE — Anthony's call 2026-07-31. The requirement is HIS OWN idea, captured the same day; accepting this gap parks the MODELLING question, not the intent.

WHAT BLOCKS IT IS A REAL VOCABULARY PROBLEM, FOUND BY CHECKING AND RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-DERIVES IT. The first answer given was "reflow2 already has the vocabulary — model the release procedure as a Flow". THAT IS WRONG AS THE SCHEMA STANDS: PART_OF_FLOW is declared Capability -> Flow and accepts nothing else, so a Flow's steps must be Capabilities. "Bump the version in three files" is a chore, not a capability. Modelling seven release chores as seven Capabilities would put fake entries into the very set that coverage_report and the verification counts range over — 100 real capabilities plus seven chores makes every one of those reports quietly wrong, permanently. The correction is recorded here rather than edited over the earlier claim.

SO THE OPEN QUESTION IS ONE LEVEL DOWN, AND IT IS GENUINE: is a procedure step a first-class design object, or is it documentation the design POINTS AT? Making it first-class means widening PART_OF_FLOW to accept a step type — which MOVES THE STAMP and locks every older reflow2 out of the design, so it is a release-shaped decision, not a side edit. Pointing at it instead means writing the procedure as a document in the content store (which now exists) and referencing it from the Project — cheap, no schema change, but an agent reads prose rather than querying steps, which is most of what was asked for.

WHY NOT NOW: v0.20.0 was deliberately scoped to cap:changelog-view ALONE, and a schema change is not a side quest to slip in beside it. Nothing is lost by waiting — the requirement holds the reasoning and the derivability argument, and the seven recovered steps are written down outside the graph in the meantime.

THE ONE THING NOT TO DO is build it as a Flow of invented Capabilities to make this note go away. That would trade a visible open question for a silently wrong metric, which is the exact trade req:no-silent-fallback exists to forbid.

THE EVIDENCE STANDS AND IS NOT WEAKENED BY THE PARK: cutting v0.19.0 required reconstructing seven steps from `git show v0.18.0` plus a grep, and at least two of them — that an upgrade doc is owed ONLY when the schema stamp moves, and that the release manifest must be exhaustive with nothing computing it — were discoverable only from a past commit message.

properties.decision: Accepted the gap gap:f384097e7d8b01b0.
properties.name: Reviewed: gap:f384097e7d8b01b0
properties.rationale:
These 64 boundaries are held in the code, not in the design, and that is correct rather than missing. A contract is declared at the lowest level that actually defines it and higher levels answer by roll-up (`dec:idea-a-contract-is-declared-at-the-lowest-level-and-rolled-up`, accepted 2026-08-23 on Anthony's word) — so the absence of an interface between two modules of one subsystem is the rule being followed, not a hole in the record.

Measured, not asserted: at module altitude `seam_coverage` reads 72 couplings, 8 covered, 64 uncovered; lifted to subsystem it reads 11 couplings, 11 covered, 0 uncovered. Independently, all 64 pairs sit inside ONE crate with zero crossing a crate boundary, and 44 of the 55 files in reflow2-core carry `impl DesignGraph` — so the majority of these "couplings" are impl blocks of the same struct calling each other. Writing 64 interface contracts for them would document a struct's method calls as system boundaries.

THE ACKNOWLEDGEMENT IS DELIBERATELY NARROW. It accepts this finding on THIS design; it does not change what the undeclared-seam detector reports anywhere else. Defaulting the detector to subsystem altitude was offered and declined, because a roll-up answering "covered" at subsystem level says nothing about a coupling covered by no contract at ANY level — the counter-argument Anthony recorded beside his own idea before he was asked to settle it.

WHAT WOULD OVERTURN THIS: reflow2 splitting into separately-released crates. The moment one of these module pairs crosses a release boundary it becomes a real contract, and this reason stops holding for that pair. The review expiring when any of the 31 affected components change is the mechanism that should catch it.

properties.decision: Accepted the structural defect heal:6f773b6f7e7c5686.
properties.name: Reviewed: heal:6f773b6f7e7c5686
properties.rationale:
ACCEPTED AS ARCHITECTURE, NOT REPAIRED. Every path between subsystems routes through the MCP protocol because that is what reflow2 IS: an agent-native design brain whose entire surface is served over MCP. The detector is correct that the topology has one articulation point; it is wrong only in the implied remedy, `add_redundancy`, which would mean a second protocol nobody wants and no consumer asked for.

⚠️ THE COST OF LEAVING IT OPEN IS THE REASON THIS IS ACKNOWLEDGED RATHER THAN IGNORED. Three permanent warnings in one category teach a reader to skim it, and the next single point of failure — a real one, in a place nobody chose — would arrive into a list already being skipped. This project has found that wallpaper failure three times (unreviewed_ideas at 111 of 186, the undeclared-seam list, the unallocated-parts list). Moving it into `reviewed_defects` keeps it visible and counted while restoring the open list's ability to mean something.

📌 THE REVIEW EXPIRES IF THE SHAPE CHANGES, which is the property that makes this safe: the defect id hashes the category with the affected set, so if this interface stops being the sole bridge — or a different one becomes one — the new shape has a new id nobody has accepted, and it surfaces again.

⚠️ NOT ACCEPTED: that a single point of failure here is harmless. `rule:mcp-and-the-graph-are-the-only-common-ground` makes this seam load-bearing on purpose, and its availability is a real operational property. What is accepted is that the DESIGN is right and the detector's suggested repair is not.

properties.rationale:

The HTTP tool surface is one of the two transports the MCP surface is served over; every subsystem path crosses it because that is the design, not an accident of wiring. `add_redundancy` would mean a second, parallel transport carrying the same tools — which is what the stdio path already is, and the detector cannot see that they are alternatives rather than a chain.

properties.decision:
**Anthony's word, 2026-08-26: park it.** Option (e) of `dec:idea-the-environment-compliance-layer-was-designed-and-never-built`.

📌 DISTINCT FROM THAT NODE BY ROLE, NOT BY WORDING, AND THE ID IS LOAD-BEARING. That one is the DELIBERATION — the open question, its five options and the argument on each. This is the RULING, and it must carry exactly this id because `vocabulary_coverage` looks the domain's `park_with` up by it. A ruling a machine reads and a deliberation a person reads are different artifacts; merging them would leave the tool with nothing to find.

WHAT IS PARKED: the compliance half of the `environment` domain — the `EnvironmentRule` node type and the `IMPOSES`, `COMPLIES_WITH` and `VIOLATES_RULE` edges. Declared in `schema/environment.yaml` since 2026-07-17, zero instances, zero typed tools, zero instructions, zero detectors.

WHAT IS **NOT** PARKED, and the distinction matters: the LOCATING half of the same domain is live and working — `Environment` (3 instances, written by `add_environment`) and `DEPLOYED_TO` (63 edges, written by `deploy_to`). `OPERATES_IN` sits between them: 3 live edges, no tool. **Parking is not retirement and touches none of these.**

═══ WHY PARK RATHER THAN BUILD ═══

Three field reports this month — hxm_program, Alex, and the storyflow fleet — mention environment compliance **zero times**. Building a fully-specified but unrequested subsystem is answering a question the schema asked rather than one a user did, which is the over-engineering failure mode this project measures itself against.

Parking is the only disposition that costs nothing to reverse. A parked domain a user later asks for becomes a build with nothing undone; a subsystem built unrequested cannot be un-built and adds surface every future session reads past.

═══ WHY NOT RETIRE ═══

Retiring was on the table as option (c) and is now known to be partly destructive: it would remove `OPERATES_IN`, which carries live edges in this design. The design is also sound — the three-way distinction between `Constraint` (self-imposed), `DesignRule` (chosen convention) and `EnvironmentRule` (externally imposed, negotiable only by variance or waiver) is good vocabulary, and the `VIOLATES_RULE` lifecycle where `confirmed` means an accepted variance kept and documented is better thought through than much of what ships.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS ═══

**A user asking.** Specifically: any design in a regulated operating environment where an external authority imposes a ruleset the design can only comply with, seek a variance from, or fail. Brookhaven NSLS-II and Space Force acquisition both look like that from the outside, and neither has reached for it.

📌 AND ONE PIECE OF EVIDENCE POINTS THE OTHER WAY, kept at full strength because it is the only thing on that side. `OPERATES_IN` has three edges and no tool writes them — an earlier session reached for the vocabulary and fell through to raw `create_edge`, the escape hatch the three-legs rule says must not count as reachability. That is thin, it came from inside the project rather than from a user, and it was judged insufficient to justify building. If it recurs — especially from a consumer rather than from us — this parking should be revisited rather than defended.
properties.name: PARKED — the environment compliance vocabulary is deliberately unused until a user asks for it
properties.rationale:
Recorded as the domain's `park_with` ruling, which is the node `vocabulary_coverage` already names for this purpose: accepting it declares the domain deliberately unused, so unused environment vocabulary stops reading as a hole in every coverage report without anything being deleted.

That is the same principle as `ruling: parks` one layer down and the same principle as `dec:idea-a-proposed-decision-asserts-nothing-...` one layer up: a deliberate state must be COUNTED and explained rather than either reported as a defect or silently hidden. All three exist because a count that grows when somebody does the right thing teaches people to stop reading it.

The agent recommended parking and Anthony took it. The counter-evidence — three `OPERATES_IN` edges written through the escape hatch — is recorded on the decision rather than dropped, because it is the one fact that would justify overturning this and it should not have to be rediscovered.

properties.statement:
A DESIGN IS NAMED BY AN ID THAT RESOLVES TO A LOCATION. cap:select-graph-by-id frames it correctly — the server maps id to path — so the id is primary and the path is a storage detail. A surface that treats a filesystem path as the canonical identity forecloses object storage, where the location is a key and the identity rides as metadata.

ADVISORY — Anthony, 2026-08-09, splitting this clause out of rule:per-design-state-is-never-a-process-global and answering the enforcement question for both halves at once (gap:ba21fb8550a81e07): "Split it: clause 1 enforced, clause 2 advice."

WHY IT IS ADVISORY AND ITS SIBLING IS NOT, which is the reason the split was worth making rather than a hedge. The two clauses sit in OPPOSITE positions against the code. The no-globals clause is already satisfied — three runtime process-globals exist and two of them are legitimately process-wide — so a detector for it passes today and its only job is to stop the fourth one. This clause has no compliant surface at all: `--graph-path` is how a server is pointed at a design, `compare_designs` takes `base_path`, `describe_designs` answers about a path, and cap:select-graph-by-id is `planned` with nothing realizing it. An honest detector would therefore fail against the entire existing tool surface on the day it was written, and the only ways to make it green would be to block every build or to attach a check that proves nothing — which is precisely the failure the `enforced` tri-state was introduced to end (dec:does-enforced-default-to-gate-blocking: "a KPP that nothing checks is a comment").

So the flag says what is true: this is the project's rule, confirmed by its author, and no build has been stopped by it because nothing can yet tell compliance from the status quo.

WHEN IT SHOULD FLIP. The honest trigger is cap:select-graph-by-id becoming realized — once a surface exists on which a session names a design by id, "a NEW surface must not take a path as identity" becomes checkable against something other than the whole codebase. Until then this rule does its work at the moment of the decision it would break, which is the same mechanism rule:no-foreclosure runs on and the same reason that rule is also advisory.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY: nothing about WHERE a design is stored, nothing about hosting, and nothing that requires the registry to be built. It only keeps the door open.

properties.name: A gate is run against the state it will be judged in — for the design export, that means AFTER committing
properties.statement:
Run a check against the state that will actually be judged, not against a working tree that is about to change. For `reflow2_check` specifically: **run it AFTER committing or amending, never before.**

WHY, MEASURED 2026-08-14 (`fact:the-lineage-gate-verdict-depends-on-when-you-run-it`): the lineage check compares the new export against the export committed at HEAD. Run before an amend it answers about a commit that is about to stop existing. The same file, byte-identical, FAILED at step 3 and PASSED at step 5 of one sequence — only `HEAD` moved between them.

THE GENERAL SHAPE: this gate always reasons about a PAIR of commits, and both of its known failure modes come from that pair differing between local and CI. `fact:the-local-lineage-gate-cannot-see-a-stacked-export` is the mirror image — the gate PASSING locally on a commit CI rejects, because CI checks out the PR merge commit where `HEAD~1` is main. Neither is a bug in the gate; both are a bug in when it is trusted.

ENFORCEMENT: **advisory, on Anthony's word 2026-08-14.** He was asked whether somebody who ran the gate early, trusted it and pushed should have been stopped, and answered that it is advice. The reasoning that supports it: a wrong local verdict is self-correcting, because CI checks out the merge commit and gives the authoritative answer either way — so this rule saves confusion and wasted cycles rather than preventing a bad landing. It also could not honestly be enforced: the ordering happens on a developer's machine and leaves no trace in the repository, so no check could see the violation.

DELIBERATELY NOT BOUND to a node with `GOVERNED_BY`. It shapes an operator's sequence rather than any design element, and `describe_schema` reports no edge type that models a DesignRule to what it governs here — the skill's instruction is to leave the edge out rather than assert one that is wrong.

properties.name: A lesson is generalised before it is built — reflow2 is not tuned to the project that happened to reveal the problem
properties.statement:
When a defect is found in one design, ask what the GENERAL form is before building anything. A detector, threshold or guard fitted to the project that happened to expose the problem makes reflow2 better at that project and worse everywhere else.

ANTHONY'S WORDS, 2026-08-14: *"I don't want to be hyper focused on solving this by creating another requirement which then causes another issue later on. I don't want this to become like a decision tree where it is so specialized to some training data that it is no longer generalizable."*

⭐ THE PRINCIPLE ALREADY EXISTED IN THREE PLACES AND HAD NO HOME — which is why it kept being re-derived and re-failed:
  · `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` (accepted): *"a detector that reaches zero findings by only asking questions the graph can already answer HAS BEEN TUNED TO THE INSTRUMENT. Satisfying this requirement by adding checks that happen to pass is the failure mode, not the fix."*
  · BL-5's lesson, in a `detect.rs` comment: **a loud detector needs a different QUESTION, not a tuned number.**
  · `dec:idea-silence-is-reported-not-inferred`, where the concern was raised again.

THREE MEASURED INSTANCES OF THE FAILURE, each found by a person or agent working by hand rather than by any check:
  1. `chg:orphan-decision-degree-zero` (2026-08-01) — a clean bill from every detector; zero-degree nodes counted by hand. **One detector was added for that one case.**
  2. `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` (2026-08-07) — six blind spots, all found by hand.
  3. 2026-08-14 — 43 live planned capabilities invisible to every tool (`fact:the-build-list-is-suppressed-by-realized-via-component`); an agent had to leave the graph and grep the tree.

📌 THE POSITIVE FORM, because a rule stated only as a prohibition is hard to act on: `granularity_report` is the pattern to copy. It answers a judgement-shaped question — *is the build coarser than the design?* — with **no threshold and no severity**, by comparing against THIS design's own distribution and refusing a verdict. `BL-42`'s `realized_via_component` guard is the counter-example: it solved a real noise problem measured on one storyflow adopt trial and created greenfield-increment blindness that nothing recorded for six weeks.

ENFORCEMENT: **advisory, on Anthony's word 2026-08-14.** He was asked whether shipping a check tuned to one design's data should stop the build, and answered that it is advice. That is the honest answer: *"is this overfitted?"* is a judgement about why code was written, which is not a property the graph can see — so an enforced version would owe a detector nobody could write, leaving a 0.6 finding open forever. **Advisory here means findable and quotable in review, not weak.**

properties.name: An identified issue is enduring — a finding is never 'not mine to fix here'
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-08-20, correcting this agent: "I don't like when something is identified and dropped/forgotten. If it is identified as a gap/issue in the graph, that means it is enduring and we'll eventually come around to fixing it."

WHAT HE WAS CORRECTING: the sentence "which are a different defect and not mine to fix here", written about two level_spine_disagreement findings. The scoping was true — they were out of that PR — but the wording reads as dismissal, and dismissal is how a real finding leaves the record.

WHAT THE RULE DEMANDS. Name which PR or increment something is out of scope FOR, never whether it matters. And before moving on, make sure it is either (a) a durable node, (b) an asked Question with somebody's name on it, or (c) a computed finding that will fire again — never only a sentence in a conversation.

WHY HE IS RIGHT ON THE MECHANICS TOO, checked rather than assumed: gaps ARE durable. gap:4e24a202aa6f1737 carried the same id morning and afternoon, because a gap is recomputed from the condition and disappears only when the condition is fixed. So the record already endures; what does not endure is anyone's attention to it.

WARNING — THE FAILURE IT GUARDS IS NOT FORGETTING, IT IS SKIMMING. This design carried 89 open gaps of which 85 had never been put to anybody. That list endured perfectly and was useless. Two were surfaced and answered only because he said this out loud. A durable finding nobody reads is indistinguishable from a lost one, which is why the remedy is to ASK rather than merely to record — and why scheduling the resolution of a gap into an increment was built the following day.

DELIBERATELY ADVISORY, not gate-blocking: no computation can tell a scoping sentence from a dismissal, so a check here would fire on correct behaviour. Its power is `enforced: false` until somebody states otherwise, per dec:enforced-is-stated-not-defaulted.

properties.name: An identified issue is ROOT-CAUSED, PINNED BY A CI TEST, then FIXED — and the root cause is written down, not just the repair
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-08-26: *"if an issue is identified, determine root cause of issue, update CI tests to catch this, and then implement fix, and test… document the root cause of the issue as part of the design rule."*

═══ THE ORDER, AND THE ORDER IS THE RULE ═══

**① ROOT-CAUSE IT.** Not the symptom, not the instance. Ask what CLASS of thing this is and what let it happen.
**② PIN IT WITH A TEST THAT FAILS TODAY.** In CI, not locally. The test must fail against the unfixed code, or it is pinning nothing.
**③ FIX IT AT THE CAUSE.** `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap` governs how.
**④ TEST IT.** The pin now passes, and the run is read from the authoritative object (`rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object`).
**⑤ WRITE THE ROOT CAUSE DOWN.** In the test's own comment and in the design — because the repair is recoverable from the diff and the CAUSE is not.

⚠️ **THE STEP MOST OFTEN SKIPPED IS ②, AND SKIPPING IT IS INVISIBLE.** A fix without a failing-first test looks identical to a fix with one: both end green. The difference only appears when the class recurs, and by then nobody remembers whether it was ever pinned.

═══ THE WORKED EXAMPLE THIS RULE WAS WRITTEN FROM (2026-08-26) ═══

**SYMPTOM**, reported from the field by hxm_program as F-01: replaying a gap into `gaps_to_prompts` exactly as the docs instruct — *"REPLAY EACH GAP OBJECT UNCHANGED"* — was refused with `invalid GapCandidate: missing field 'suggested_depth'`.

**FIRST-ORDER READING, AND IT WAS WRONG:** *"the budgeted reply withheld a field."* True as far as it goes, and it would have led to patching the budget to keep `suggested_depth`.

⭐ **ROOT CAUSE:** `GapCandidate` promises a replay contract IN ITS OWN DOC COMMENT — *"a compact row handed straight back to `gap_to_prompt` has to deserialize"* — and enforces it field by field. `description` and `evidence` carry `#[serde(default)]`; **`suggested_depth` and `affected_ids` do not.** So the contract held for the fields somebody remembered and broke for the ones nobody did. **The cause is not the budget and not that field — it is that a stated contract was maintained BY HAND, with nothing checking it.** Two mechanisms then cancelled on exactly the designs where both matter: the budget exists so the call can be made at all on a large design, and the handshake exists so the gaps can be asked.

**THE PIN:** `a_budgeted_row_replays_into_the_handshake_it_was_meant_for` — and it pins the ROUND TRIP, not the field. Serialize every budgeted row, deserialize it back, and separately deserialize a row whose optional fields are ABSENT rather than empty. **Any future field added without a default fails it.** Pinning `suggested_depth` alone would have fixed today and left the class open.

**THE FIX:** `#[serde(default)]` on `affected_ids`, `#[serde(default = "default_suggested_depth")]` on `suggested_depth`, defaulting to 2 — the value every detector but one emits, so a row that lost the field asks for the ordinary depth rather than an invented one.

═══ ⭐ ENFORCEMENT — SETTLED 2026-08-26: ADVISORY, NOT GATE-BLOCKING ═══

**Anthony's word, put to him with three options and a recommendation.** `enforced: false`. Breaking this rule does NOT stop the build.

**WHY, AND IT IS NOT LENIENCY.** The load-bearing half of this rule is step ②, and **nothing in a diff or a CI run can see whether a test was FAILING before the fix** — CI only ever runs the merged state. The note below predicted this before the question was asked, and the prediction held.

So an enforced version could only check something weaker — *does this change touch code and add no test?* — which passes on a test written AFTER the fix. That is the failure mode this project keeps finding and just spent a day fixing three times over: **a check that reads as enforcement while measuring something else is worse than no check**, because it converts an unanswered question into a false green.

⚠️ **THE COST, STATED RATHER THAN BURIED:** advisory rules get skipped, and this rule exists precisely because F-01's own fix skipped step ②. Its author verified the pin passing and never saw it fail. The discipline now rests on sessions choosing it, and on the record saying honestly which way it went — the fixes on 2026-08-26 each recorded that they WERE observed failing first, and that sentence is the only evidence there is.

📌 **WHAT WOULD MAKE PART OF THIS CHECKABLE**, kept because the answer may change: `req:a-rule-says-whether-it-can-be-checked-at-all` (ACCEPTED, unbuilt) is where the distinction between a rule's checkable and uncheckable halves belongs. And the ⑤ half IS checkable today — `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause` (ACCEPTED) asks a repair to record whether it reached the cause. Splitting enforcement across the two halves was offered as an option and NOT taken; if step ② keeps being skipped, that split is the next thing to try rather than gating the whole rule.

properties.name: [BL-135] State the FAILURE MODE, not the rule — the guardrail principle, evidenced by a blind trial, and written nowhere
properties.statement:
State the FAILURE MODE, not the rule — the guardrail principle, evidenced by a blind trial, and written nowhere

*The strongest general finding from the 2026-07-31 case study, and the only one that is about how this project WRITES rather than what it computes.* An agent designed a whole project through reflow2 without knowing the guardrail docstrings were deliberate behavioural interventions. It read them as ordinary API prose, formed its own view of what they were for, complied, and praised the phrasing in its log without suspecting it was aimed at it — a blind trial, and they worked. It then ranked the eight that changed its behaviour, most effective first: set_artifact_checksum's *"silent accept does not exist: it is how a design erodes into fiction over N fix cycles while reporting zero gaps"* (named the single strongest intervention in the surface — it produced a named ChangeEvent for all nine artifact updates that would otherwise have been silent re-registrations); genesis's *"do not invent a brief on my behalf"* (held through THREE blank briefs with a detailed solicitation sitting in the directory, preventing the largest failure available — fabricated requirements phrased in the customer's own language, which are unusually hard to spot later); add_constraint's *"criticality is a claim about consequence, so ask the user first"*; set_requirement_status's *"promoting it yourself forges their signature"*; delete_edge's *"a link that WAS true and stopped being true is design history, not an error"*; describe_schema's *"validating is not the same as meaning what you intended"*; set_project_mode's *"the default records that nobody has chosen"*; and the stop hook's *"bookkeeping is not the loop"*. The extractable rule, in its words: it complied more readily where it was told what goes wrong if it did not, because that let it evaluate the reasoning rather than obey it — and agree. *"Ask the user first"* alone would have been weaker than the version naming the consequence. Equally informative: the interventions that did NOT need to exist — nothing had to stop it over-modelling or creating Components at genesis, because the skills sequenced the work so those temptations arrived when the right move was already obvious. The work: write the rule where descriptions are written (AGENTS.md), with this ranked evidence, so it is a standard rather than a habit — and consider a skill_lint check that a guardrail sentence names a consequence. The counterexample is already filed: [BL-124] shows a guardrail whose reasoning is the same quality as the rest and whose IMPLEMENTATION contradicts its intent, which the case study called the highest-value fix in its document. Good wording does not survive a mechanism that defeats it. CORROBORATED FROM INSIDE THE OTHER PROJECT, which is the strongest form the evidence could take: that session adopted the same pattern in its own code without being told to, and it caught a real error — a guardrail written two entries earlier asserted that all calibration anchors miss in the same direction, and when the same agent later fitted a coefficient to one anchor, the assertion failed with its own text: *"anchors now disagree in direction; the models were probably tuned to fit one of them."* Written before the mistake, and it named the cause. The principle is not a style preference about API prose; it transfers to any assertion a person will read at the moment they are getting something wrong. Their honest division of labour is worth carrying into the docs alongside it: *reflow2 is where reasoning persists; tests are what stop you being wrong* — which is also the argument for the out-of-scope line on [BL-126]. Size S

Migrated from docs/backlog.md BL-135 on 2026-08-07 (epoch:backlog-retired). Size estimate carried from the row: S.

properties.name: [BL-212] A folder of documents carries no recoverable chronology, so EVOLVES_INTO and SUPERSEDES — both directional — can never b
properties.statement:
A folder of documents carries no recoverable chronology, so EVOLVES_INTO and SUPERSEDES — both directional — can never be drawn from a corpus

*Found 2026-08-04 while capturing [req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design].* The vocabulary for "someone changed their mind over years" is already there and is entirely unused for this: CONTRADICTS carries alignment: opposing\ | supporting with confidence and evidence, EVOLVES_INTO is literally *"source is an earlier form that becomes target over time"*, SUPERSEDES/OBSOLETES retire on the record, and TemporalFact holds a time-bounded assertion with VALID_FROM/VALID_TO. All of it needs to know which document came FIRST, and a folder cannot say. File mtimes lie (checkout, copy, sync all rewrite them), a document corpus may have no git history at all, and the dates inside documents are prose. This is the exact inverse of the bug fixed in this same increment: there, arrival order wrongly decided the canonical NAME and the fix was to stop consulting order; here order genuinely carries meaning and there is no way to learn it. So the honest default is that a corpus ingest draws CONTRADICTS (symmetric, needs no direction) and NEVER EVOLVES_INTO/SUPERSEDES (directional) unless a human or an explicit in-document date supplies the arrow — which makes "you changed your mind here" answerable and "this replaced that" a question. Candidate signals worth measuring before choosing: an explicit date in frontmatter or filename, git log --follow --diff-filter=A first-commit date where a repo exists, and the corpus's own supersession language ("replaces", "superseded by"). Do not infer the arrow from mtime. Size S

Migrated from docs/backlog.md BL-212 on 2026-08-07 (epoch:backlog-retired). Size estimate carried from the row: S.

properties.name: [BL-41] Graph text is data, never instructions — and nothing says so
properties.statement:
Graph text is data, never instructions — and nothing says so

S half done, 2026-07-19 — the standing rule is stated in the three places an agent looks: a section in the consumer AGENTS.md, one line in each of the eight skills at the point where it starts reading graph text, and the server's get_info instructions (so a session that loads no skill still gets it in the handshake). The one genuinely uncovered LLM failure mode in [partnership.md](partnership.md): every skill tells the agent to read node text and act on the design, and a hostile or careless statement rides that trust. Bounded today (single user, local graph); real the day a graph is shared (BL-12) or an adopted repo's prose flows through INGEST (BL-27). Mechanical mitigation (provenance-aware trust, quoting boundaries — [BL-12](#bigger-threads) sketch idea 2 is its design seed) is M and should wait for a real multi-writer case
