RELATED AND SETTLED THE OTHER WAY, named so this does not reopen it: `dec:report-dont-judge` says reflow2 reports and never ranks. This is not a request to judge — it is a request to READ A RULING THE DESIGN ALREADY MADE, the same move `designation: required` made for `unprovided_interface` on 2026-08-09.

⚠️ BOUND THE REPORTER STATED AND I HAVE NOT CLOSED: they did not check whether the guard built for the `DOCUMENTS`/`REALIZES` asymmetry was meant to cover this case and misses it, or whether this case was never contemplated. Those are different reports and only the second is evidenced.

REPORTED BY dev_storyflow's fleet, 2026-08-04 and 2026-08-15.

properties.name: A design can say what crosses each boundary between its parts, at the level the boundary is actually defined
properties.statement:
Where two parts of a design depend on each other, the design must be able to record WHAT PASSES BETWEEN THEM — what crosses, in which direction, over what — and a coupling with no such record must be reachable as a question rather than left silent.

THE CONTRACT IS RECORDED AT THE LOWEST LEVEL THAT ACTUALLY DEFINES IT, and higher levels answer by projection. Asking "is there an interface between A and B?" at any altitude must be answerable, and the answer must name where the contract really lives rather than asserting one between the boxes that were asked about.

ANTHONY, 2026-08-23, IN HIS WORDS: "defining contracts for the components is a key part of my vision for reflow2" — said of the product, and confirmed as product intent when asked directly rather than inferred from the remark.

DISTINCT FROM `dec:idea-a-contract-is-declared-at-the-lowest-level-and-rolled-up`, which stays `proposed` and is the QUESTION about reflow2's own model: which level should carry its contracts, and whether DEPENDS_ON between two impl blocks of one struct is a dependency worth recording. This is the PRODUCT requirement — what reflow2 must let any project do. The two can be answered independently, and the design one may yet be answered "leave it at module level" without touching this at all.

WHY IT IS ABOUT THE PRODUCT AND NOT HOUSEKEEPING ON THIS DESIGN: reflow2 is a tool for other projects, and the test of any vocabulary is whether it reaches a user's design, where real crate, service and organisational boundaries exist. reflow2's own 64 uncontracted module pairs were the first exercise of it and a poor one — measured 2026-08-23, all 64 sit inside a single crate and most are impl blocks of one struct, so they were never the seams this is about.

IT CAN FAIL INDEPENDENTLY of anything built for it: a design that records couplings and contracts in vocabularies that never meet violates it however either is implemented — exactly the state `fact:coupling-and-contract-are-recorded-in-vocabularies-that-never-meet` measured, and what `cap:a-contract-answers-at-the-altitude-you-asked` began to answer.

properties.name: A design records the quality attribute it is built for, and is asked if it has not
properties.statement:
A design SHALL be able to record which quality attribute it is built FOR, and SHALL be asked when it has not.

WHY IT IS INTENT AND NOT A NICETY: the attribute decides WHICH GROUPING IS RIGHT, and the four disagree. Performance wants the least chatter across boundaries. Reliability wants no single part everything depends on, and may deliberately put the same function in two places — the opposite of maximal modularity. Maintainability wants what changes together to live together, which is a different edge set entirely. Security wants boundaries following trust and data classification, which is constrained partitioning rather than clustering. A design that allocates without answering silently optimises for performance.

IT IS A TARGET, NOT A SCORE. `DimensionAssessment` records what a system IS on an axis; nothing recorded what it is FOR. Measured 2026-08-25: 0 DimensionAssessment and 0 DimensionObservation nodes exist, so the nine-axis vocabulary had been fully defined and never once used.

ABSENCE MUST READ AS "NOBODY WAS ASKED". The property carries no default, because a detector over the absence is the only thing that notices the question being skipped — and because a default would be materialised onto every existing Decision when an export is read back.

NOT KNOWING YET IS A FIRST-CLASS ANSWER. A design that weighed the question and has not committed SHALL be distinguishable from one nobody asked, and SHALL keep being asked until it settles. The two must never be reported identically, and a deferral must not be closeable by an acknowledgement that never expires.

ASKED EARLY, ALLOCATED LATE. The question is asked at genesis because asking is cheap and the cost of asking late is reworking services already built; the allocation it informs still waits for the last responsible moment. These are different questions and only one of them is deferred.

properties.name: A detector reads the properties that qualify its own finding, so recording something correctly never manufactures a defect
properties.statement:
A structural detector must consult the properties that change whether its finding IS a finding — on the edge and on both endpoints — so that modelling something the way the design prescribes never adds a defect.

THE OBSERVATION IS `fact:defect-recording-a-refutation-correctly-adds-a-structural-defect`; this is the intent behind fixing it.

THE ARGUMENT IS THE PROJECT'S OWN, ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN. `heal.rs` was fixed once for exactly this shape: reading the CONTRADICTS edge TYPE and never its `alignment` property meant "every correctly-modelled corroboration came back as a structural defect", and the comment ends "A PROPERTY THE DETECTOR IGNORES IS A PROPERTY THAT LIES." The same sentence applies one property across — the detector still never reads either endpoint's `status`, so a `rejected` Decision contradicting its successor is reported as a conflict when it is the healthy case.

⚠️ WHY THIS IS AN INCENTIVE PROBLEM AND NOT A NUISANCE: recording a refutation correctly ADDS a warning-severity defect, and burying it in prose adds none. The tool mildly penalises the discipline `rejected` exists to support, at the moment a seat is least likely to push back. The cheap wrong response is to delete the rejected node or the edge — the erasure the record exists to prevent.

MEASURED HERE: our four reported contradictions have no rejected or superseded endpoint today, so it does not fire — but the design holds 10 superseded and 1 rejected Decision and ZERO such edges, which is itself weak evidence that the relation is not being recorded.

WHAT MUST NOT BREAK: `acknowledge_defect` already handles this well — it stores the REASON rather than the suppression, and the review expires if the defect's shape changes because the id hashes the category with the affected set. Any fix must leave that intact.

NOT DECIDED: whether `superseded` and `rejected` are treated identically, and whether such pairs vanish or move to a separate band.

properties.name: A discipline that applies mid-task is delivered at the tool that triggers it, not from a catalogue read once at handshake
properties.statement:
SKILLS SPLIT INTO TWO KINDS AND THEY NEED DIFFERENT DELIVERY. A **task-skill** (genesis, adopt, capture-intent, governance-proposal, plan-increments) is reached for at a recognisable task boundary — the agent is STARTING something and asks what covers it. A **discipline-skill** (revise-design's snapshot-first, capture-intent's search-before-you-create, link-artifacts' hash-after) applies at an arbitrary instant INSIDE another task, when the agent is mid-flow and not asking anything.

THE CATALOGUE SERVES THE FIRST AND STRUCTURALLY CANNOT SERVE THE SECOND. `dec:skills-served` put the skill catalogue into the server instructions, which every client injects at handshake — deliberately, as "progressive disclosure rebuilt by hand", and it is the price of never being stale. It works: an agent that has read the catalogue reaches for the right task-skill. But a catalogue is read ONCE, and a discipline applies thousands of tokens later at a moment nothing announces. **The delivery mechanism and the trigger moment are mismatched, and no amount of restating the catalogue closes that gap.**

⭐ MEASURED ON THIS SESSION, which is the evidence rather than the theory (2026-08-09, `fact:which-skills-a-session-reached-for-and-why`): every skill used unprompted followed a task boundary the user had just created. Every skill MISSED was a discipline applying incidentally inside other work — two revisions made without loading revise-design, and two Contributors minted without the namespace search capture-intent prescribes. The snapshot discipline was followed ONLY because a consumer's report quoting it happened to be open in context. That is a near miss, not self-direction.

THE MECHANISM THAT ALREADY WORKS AND IS NOT APPLIED HERE: `loop_hint` rides on tool RESPONSES — `add_requirement` returns "when this capture batch lands, run detect_gaps" — and it demonstrably changes behaviour, because it arrives at the moment of the action rather than at the start of the session. The same carrier should name the discipline: a revising `create_node` saying "this is a revision; revise-design takes the snapshot FIRST, and after the edit it cannot be recreated"; `delete_node` / `delete_edge` likewise. This is `rule:bl-135`'s guardrail principle — state the FAILURE MODE, not the rule — applied to routing rather than to warnings, and that principle carries a blind trial behind it: an agent complied with those docstrings without knowing they were interventions.

⭐⭐ AND THE STRONGER FORM, WHICH DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE AGENT AT ALL. `dec:loop-status-state-not-history` holds that loop debt is computed from GRAPH STATE, never from run history. Apply the same rule to discipline: do not track whether a skill was INVOKED — compute whether its OUTCOME IS PRESENT. A node revised with no Snapshot at the current epoch is detectable from graph state alone, and that survives an agent which ignores every hint. dragon Boss (dev_storyflow) proposed the identical shape independently: "have delete_edge / a revising create_node report whether the target has a snapshot at the current epoch — NOT BLOCK, JUST SAY."

⚠️ THE ASYMMETRY THAT LIMITS THIS, stated so the requirement is not read as covering more than it can: a revision with no snapshot IS computable; a node created without a prior search is NOT — nothing distinguishes it from a node created after a search that found nothing. So discipline-skills split a second time. Those whose neglect leaves evidence get a detector; the rest can only ever get a hint, and a hint is what they get.

WHAT THIS MUST NOT BECOME: a blocking gate. A tool that blocks becomes a tool people route around, and then the graph stops matching reality — the one failure it cannot survive. And not another restatement in AGENTS.md: four skill-versus-tool drifts are already on record, and `req:a-rule-knows-where-else-it-is-written-down` exists because restatements rot.

RAISED BY ANTHONY, 2026-08-09: "continue to think how do we continue to improve the probability that an agent will use reflow2's skills and tools without being reminded."

properties.name: A Verification has somewhere to put its evidence that is not its title, and a self-contradictory result cannot read as passing
properties.statement:
A Verification must have a durable place for what a check FOUND, separate from what the check IS — so evidence stops being written into the title, and so a result can be read by something other than a human eye.

⭐ THREE INDEPENDENT RECORDS OF ONE ROOT, which is why this is a requirement and not a style note. The near-duplicate guard surfaced a THIRD: `fact:defect-a-finding-has-no-bounds-so-grading-goes-in-the-name` was already in this design before today, saying the same thing about grading. Both facts the guard named are OBSERVATIONS on different days; this is the INTENT that answers them.

MEASURED on reflow2's own graph, 2026-08-16: 160 Verifications, MEDIAN `name` LENGTH 79.5 WORDS, 72 over 100, 17 over 300, longest 654. A `name` is what a list renders; these are reports.

THE TWO FLEET REPORTS:
(a) 2026-08-07 — a Verification held a self-contradictory result and stayed `passing` forever, because THE RESULT IS FREE TEXT. It recorded "EXIT 0, verdict 'STALE — 4 of 11'"; the tool's true exit was 1 and its source is `return 1 if stale else 0`, so `EXIT 0` meant the exact opposite of the verdict beside it. `status` is structured; the evidence is prose, and nothing in the loop can notice the disagreement.
(b) 2026-08-08 — `loop_status` is documented as "one cheap call" and is cheap to CALL and expensive to READ: `verifications.attention[0].name` came back as a single ~450-word paragraph holding a full graded walk report. Their diagnosis is the requirement: "workers write the full report into the `name` because there is no other durable place for it on the node — A MISSING FIELD BEING PAID FOR IN EVERY FUTURE READ OF THAT NODE."

⚠️ AND I AM THE LARGEST SINGLE CONTRIBUTOR. Four of the six Verifications written on 2026-08-16 exceed 300 words, and `ver:a-claim-reads-back-with-its-age` at 435 words is the FIFTH LONGEST IN THE DESIGN. I was not working around a limitation I had noticed; I had not noticed it.

WHY IT IS MORE THAN STYLE: the cheapest call in the surface, the one every worker is told to make routinely including before finishing, returns a payload dominated by prose nobody asked for. A cheap call that is expensive to read is a call people stop making — the same signal-trained-to-be-ignored failure `req:the-loop-can-say-what-this-session-owes` was built to end, arriving through a different door.

THEIR TWO ASKS: give Verification a `findings` / `report` property; and truncate `name` in `loop_status`'s rollup, or return `name` + `detail` separately.

⚠️ THE LOAD-BEARING UNCERTAINTY, to answer BEFORE building: WOULD A NEW FIELD ALONE CHANGE ANYTHING? A declared field nobody writes to leaves the corpus exactly as it is — precisely the trap `dec:how-should-a-temporal-fact-carry-its-date-when-there-is-no-epoch` documented, where 112 nodes wrote an undeclared property because the declared route did not fit. And the 160 existing names cannot be migrated cleanly, because a property once written cannot be removed — the best available repair writes evidence to the new field and SHORTENS the name, duplicating rather than moving. Truncating at the rollup is the cheaper half and asks nobody to change how they write; whether that is pragmatic or merely lets the hoard grow unchecked is unmeasured.

properties.name: A finding names the remedy, not only the problem — including when the honest remedy is to declare the state deliberate
properties.statement:
When reflow2 reports that something is wrong, the report names what the reader can honestly DO about it. A finding that describes a problem and stops leaves the reader to invent a repair, and the repair they invent is often worse than the state being reported.

THE CASE THAT FORCED IT, measured 2026-08-19. `orphan_node` reported two registered documents as attached to nothing, and its repair note said "No mechanical repair. Linking this node to something would assert a relationship nobody drew." True — and it reads as THERE IS NOTHING YOU CAN HONESTLY DO. There was: `governed_by(..., ruling: "parks")` declares the unattached state deliberate and is purpose-built for exactly that genre. It is documented on the TOOL. The reader is looking at the FINDING. The documents were deleted instead.

TWO PROJECTS, SAME DAY, OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. ophyd-service asked in writing whether `parks` covered their case and said "neither the tool docs nor the skills say... I wasn't confident enough to try", and backed off. Hours later an agent in this repo did not find it at all and deleted the evidence. One under-used the mechanism; one destroyed data for want of it.

WHAT THIS DEMANDS, AND ITS LIMIT. The finding names the remedy AND the remedy's SCOPE — "read by these detectors and not those" — because a mechanism named without its boundary produces the first failure above rather than the second. It does NOT demand that reflow2 apply the remedy: `dec:ask-not-repair` and `repair_is_a_judgement` stand, and naming an option is not taking it.

DISTINCT FROM `req:a-refusal-names-what-would-have-worked`, which is accepted and covers REFUSALS — a rejected argument returning its legal values. `orphan_node` refused nothing: it succeeded, reported accurately, and described a dead end that was not one. A report is not a refusal, and the gap between them is where this sits.

PROMOTED FROM `dec:idea-parks-shipped-and-was-still-not-reached-the-instruction-is-missing-where-the-person-is-stuck`, which records the observation and stays open as the finding. The dedup guard named that Decision twice and was answered twice — the node was read (this session wrote it) and judged different in kind: the Decision says what happened, this says what must be true.

properties.name: Evidence a value was fitted to cannot also count as that value's validation
properties.statement: When a value in the design was derived from a piece of evidence, the design must record what it was derived from, and must not let a check resting on that same evidence count as independent validation of it. Agreement with the anchor a value was fitted to is a fit, not a test, and must be reported as consumed. A capability whose only passing checks are consumed in this way must read as not independently verified. This cannot be computed from the strength of the evidence, only from its structure: no check internal to a design can establish its own independence, so the design must record the relation rather than attempt to detect the circularity.

properties.name: A fix says whether it corrected the cause or worked around it, so "how much of this is standing on a patch?" is a question the design can answer
properties.statement:
A change that repairs something must record WHICH KIND OF REPAIR IT WAS — the cause corrected, or the symptom worked around — and a workaround must name the correction it is standing in for. The design must then be able to answer, without asking a person: what is still resting on a patch?

DELIBERATELY DISTINCT FROM `rule:fix-it-properly-while-it-is-still-cheap`, which the guard matched, and the split is the point rather than a technicality. The RULE is how the people building reflow2 work; it binds this project and can never bind anyone else's. This REQUIREMENT is the product carrying the same philosophy, so every project using reflow2 inherits the question. Anthony asked for exactly that on 2026-08-17: "this is my philosophy on how to build something - so ensuring that it is built into the design of reflow2." A rule states it; a requirement makes it something reflow2 DOES.

⭐ THE QUESTION HE ASKED IS CURRENTLY UNANSWERABLE, and that is the whole case. "I'm not sure how many fixes have been patches versus going back to the drawing board, planning how it should have been done correctly, and then re-implementing proper fix." MEASURED ON REFLOW2'S OWN GRAPH, 2026-08-17: 472 ChangeEvents across eleven change types — new_feature 156, test_failure_fix 101, refactor 89, scope_change 59, baseline_established 25, resync 14, defect_fix 11, requirement_creep 6, deprecation 6, constraint_change 4, performance_optimization 1. EVERY ONE OF THOSE NAMES WHAT MOVED. NOT ONE SAYS WHETHER IT WAS THE RIGHT FIX. A `test_failure_fix` is equally the record of a root-cause rewrite and of a shim that made a red test green, and nothing downstream can tell them apart.

CHECKED AND FOUND NOT TO BE THE PROBLEM, so the fix is not aimed at the wrong thing: `test_failure_fix` is the DEFAULT for a `design_holds` drift accept, so the obvious hypothesis was that the commonest fix type is an unchosen default. It is not — 55 of the 101 are auto-minted accepts and ALL 55 carry written reasons, with 46 more named deliberately. The discipline is there. THE VOCABULARY IS WHAT IS MISSING.

⭐ THE SHAPE IS ALREADY PROVEN ONE LAYER OVER, which is why this is buildable rather than aspirational. `dec:two-sided-accept` made accepting drift a two-sided act: you say the content moved AND you take a position (`design_holds` / `design_updated`), because "accept the file, leave the design alone, say nothing" is the option that erodes a design into fiction. A FIX IS THE SAME SHAPE AND IS CURRENTLY ONE-SIDED. Silent patching should be as impossible as silent drift-accept, for the identical reason.

WHAT IS OWED, in the order it is worth building:
(a) A repair records its ROOT DISPOSITION — cause corrected, or symptom contained. Not defaulted, on `req:defaults-do-not-assert`: whether a fix reached the cause is a judgement, and inventing an answer records a claim nobody made.
(b) A contained symptom NAMES WHAT THE PROPER FIX WOULD BE. This is what turns a patch from an invisible cost into a stated debt with somewhere to be read. A workaround nobody wrote down is indistinguishable from a design decision six weeks later.
(c) The count is REPORTABLE — what still rests on a patch, and where. That is the question above, answered by the graph rather than by anyone's memory.

⚠️ WHAT THIS MUST NOT BECOME, stated now because the failure mode is predictable and this project has met it twice this month. It must NOT judge. reflow2 records the claim and counts it; the human decides whether a patch was right (`dec:report-dont-judge`, `dec:three-party-checks`). A detector that tried to INFER "this was a patch" from graph shape would be exactly the confident answer to a nearby question that `req:a-report-says-what-it-swept-and-whether-its-checks-ran` was written about. And a workaround is often the CORRECT call under a deadline — the requirement is that it be VISIBLE, never that it be forbidden.

⚠️ HONEST LIMIT, and it bounds what can ever be claimed here: this records what the author SAYS about their fix. It cannot detect a patch someone reports as a correction. That makes it the same class of instrument as `provenance` and the drift dispositions — worth having because the alternative is no signal at all, and worth never overselling.

NOT YET DECIDED: whether the root disposition belongs on the ChangeEvent, on the artifact accept, or on both; and whether it is retro-fittable to the 472 events already recorded or, like `dec:the-authority-check-guards-forward-not-backward`, binds only forward. Anthony's own words — "I'd like to start now" — read as forward-only, but that is his call to make explicitly rather than mine to infer.

properties.name: A hint that names a skill must name it as the next CALL, not as a parenthetical — a citation is read as attribution, not instruction
properties.statement:
Where reflow2 tells an agent which skill to use, it must phrase it as the call to make next rather than as a trailing reference. MEASURED, and this is the whole evidence: `add_capability` returned `loop_hint: "loop: wire satisfies to the requirement this serves, then run detect_gaps when the capture batch lands (detect-and-ask)"`. The agent that received it DID wire `satisfies` and DID run `detect_gaps` — and did NOT load `detect-and-ask`. The imperative clauses were obeyed; the skill name in parentheses was read as an attribution for where the advice came from, not as a step to take.

So the pointer already exists and already names the right skill — `cap:read-loop-hint` and the write-side `loop_hint` are both `verified` — and it still failed. That makes this cheaper than anything else in this family: the mechanism is built, delivered and correct, and only the wording is losing the effect. `run get_skill("detect-and-ask") first` is a step; `(detect-and-ask)` is a footnote.

SCOPE: every place reflow2 names a skill to an agent — the write tools' `loop_hint`, the read-side hint, `loop_nudge.py`'s Stop message, the SessionStart orientation, and the MCP server instructions. The rule is one line: if a skill is worth naming, name the call.

NOT PROPOSED: making the hints longer or more numerous. The finding is about grammar, not volume, and a hint that grows is a hint that gets skimmed — the failure `dec:read-hint-shape` already guarded against by firing only when the debt is real.

properties.name: A node can declare who may change it, so "what may I change alone?" is answerable from the graph rather than from prose
properties.statement:
A design node can carry a declared CHANGE POLICY — who may alter it, how many approvals it takes, and whether the approval must be recorded before or after the change. reflow2 REPORTS violations ("changed without the declared approval") and NEVER blocks the write.

THE GAP THIS CLOSES. reflow2 can say who AUTHORED a node — AUTHORED_BY carries role author/reviewer/approver — which is a record of what DID happen. It cannot say who MAY change it, which is a constraint on what MAY happen. Those are different facts and only the first is modelled.

WHY REPORTING AND NOT ENFORCING, which is the load-bearing half: a tool that blocks writes becomes a tool people route around, and then the graph stops matching reality — the one failure it cannot survive. Enforcement is itself a policy choice, so making it the mechanism would be reflow2 taking a position that belongs to the project. The value is that the boundary becomes QUERYABLE: "what may I change alone?" is the question every arriving session actually has, and today it can only be answered by reading prose that session may never read.

WHAT IT MUST NOT BECOME: roles, permissions, identity, or a review workflow. Just a declared constraint and a report of whether it held. Who someone IS stays the harness's problem; Contributor is enough.

GENERALITY, tested rather than assumed — the source applied the standard "could a solo hobbyist, a two-person team and a regulated enterprise each express THEIR policy with this, without reflow2 having an opinion about which is right?" Solo: nothing declared. Two people: "my areas and my brother's". Team: "two reviewers on a migration". Regulated: "QA sign-off, recorded, before release".

EVIDENCE, frequency rather than drama: one storyflow session hit "this is not mine to decide" FIVE times in a single sitting — a rule change needing multi-party agreement, an idea that must not be promoted to intent by anyone but its author, a gate-blocking flag that was the human's call, a shared file two other parties depended on, and a scope question about someone else's earlier ruling. Every one is this same missing primitive.

SOURCE: storyflow fleet governance report, api-boss (05af57c1), 2026-08-09, reflow2 v0.26.1, written to a deliberate MECHANISM-vs-POLICY frame at Anthony's request ("keep it generally applicable — give reflow2 the set of tools that can make most governance strategies possible"). Their own stated bound: one project, one month, one fleet shape, biased toward multi-agent operation — "treat the shapes as hypotheses worth testing against other projects, not as requirements."

properties.name: A write can tell it lost a race
properties.rationale: MEASURED, NOT SUPPOSED (fact:defect-write-response-describes-the-write-not-the-state): a deliberate experiment on the live 7-seat graph established that same-property concurrent writes are SILENT LAST-WRITER-WINS — no error, no warning, no version conflict, no indication a value was replaced — and, more sharply, that THE WRITE RESPONSE DESCRIBES THE WRITE RATHER THAN THE STATE: a racer received a success payload reading `statement: RACER_ONE, priority: high` when both fields were already false in the store. There is no version, rev, etag or updated_at anywhere in the payload, so a client cannot detect that it lost and has no primitive to compare-and-swap with. WHY THIS IS SHARPER THAN IT LOOKS: on a solo graph response == state, so trusting your own write-response is free, and every habit formed under the old stdio transport does exactly that. A session that writes a value and later reasons from its own return value is reasoning from something that was never durable — and nothing tells it. THE REPORTER EXPLICITLY DID NOT ASK FOR ENFORCEMENT: even an unenforced rev, merely RETURNED, lets a caller notice it was superseded, and that is most of the value. WHAT THIS MUST NOT COST, from the same experiment: per-property merge held under concurrency (a partial write EDITS and does not reset omitted fields) and concurrent writes serialize cleanly with both racers' distinct properties surviving. The reporter calls per-property merge the single most important safety property for a shared graph and lists it under what-not-to-change.
properties.statement: A node SHALL carry a monotonic revision returned on read and on write, and writes SHOULD accept an optional if_rev precondition — so a client can detect that its value was superseded. At minimum, a write response SHALL say when the node was also written by another seat since the caller's read. Requested as the #4 fleet ask by dev_storyflow's api-boss 5d608b85, 2026-08-07.

properties.name: A part can be MOVED to a different place in the decomposition, not only given an additional parent
properties.statement:
Reorganising a decomposition must be reachable as ONE operation. Where the only available act is 'add a parent', a part acquires a second one and the design silently gains a defect the user was never warned about.

THE NEED, stated from the failure rather than from what was built. A session asked the tool surface, in a user's words, how to move a component to a different parent; the discoverable answer was `contain_component`, which ADDS a parent and never removes the old one. Following the tool's own recommendation therefore CREATES a `multiple_parents` defect. Measured by hitting it first-hand, 2026-08-20.

THIS CAN FAIL INDEPENDENTLY of anything built for it: a surface that offers only additive containment violates it however the move is implemented, which is what makes it a requirement rather than a restatement.

properties.name: A design records how its project actually ships
properties.statement:
A design that has Releases shall also record the ordered procedure for producing one — the steps, their order, and the external conventions they depend on — so that cutting a release is read from the design rather than reconstructed from what was done last time.

ANTHONY'S WORDS, 2026-07-31, raised while watching the v0.19.0 cut: "should every reflow2 project have a requirement to describe its 'release instructions'? ... having a set of release instructions (what are all the steps that need to occur) would be nice. Then the agent doesn't have to look at what was done previously to release or whether it was released on pypi or whatever makes sense for the project being developed."

THE VOCABULARY ALREADY EXISTS AND SHOULD BE USED RATHER THAN EXTENDED. A release procedure is an ordered process, which is what Flow models: add_flow, part_of_flow with step_order, TRIGGERS transitions carrying a role, read back by flow_report. This wants no new node type and no new document.

WHY THIS IS NOT dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written IN REVERSE. That decision refused a START-HERE file because orientation is DERIVABLE — a projection of design state, so the answer was build the view. Release steps are NOT derivable from the graph: which registry (PyPI / crates.io / GitHub releases / a manufactured build), which workflow, which credential, what the tag format is, which files carry a version claim. These are facts about the world outside the design, and no projection can compute them. The same derivability test therefore argues FOR recording them. That distinction is the load-bearing part of this requirement: record what cannot be computed, compute what can.

EVIDENCE, from the v0.19.0 cut itself. The procedure was reconstructed from `git show v0.18.0` plus grepping AGENTS.md for "release" — seven steps that exist nowhere as a list: the version in three files plus the lockfile; the CHANGELOG heading plus a fresh empty Unreleased; an upgrade doc REQUIRED IF AND ONLY IF the schema stamp moved; version claims in docs/overview.md and AGENTS.md; the graph manifest, release epoch and prior-release retirement; export exactly once onto the committed file; tag and push. At least two of those are unguessable and were discoverable only by reading a past commit message.

WHERE IT BITES AS A DETECTOR: a Project holding Release nodes with no release Flow is a gap worth surfacing, the same shape as unrealized_capability. Scope deliberately unsettled here — whether this is a reflow2-wide obligation on every governed design or advice the genesis/adopt skills ask for is Anthony's call, not this requirement's.

PROPOSED — captured in his wording, not yet his signature.

properties.name: A gap put to the user arrives with the agent's recommendation — recommending is not deciding
properties.statement:
When reflow2 puts a gap to the user, the agent's READING of it travels with the question: what it would do and why, and what would change that answer. The user still decides; the agent stops pretending it has no view.

THE READING HAS A SHAPE, AND THE SHAPE IS PART OF THE REQUIREMENT — added 2026-07-31 on Anthony's word after the pattern was used on him for the five standing gaps: "I really like when I say something like 'go through the decisions I need to make... put them in plain and simple english and offer a recommendation' and then you give me the options to select with your recommended choice on top. I believe there is already a proposed idea... but I really like this process (I think other users will really like this process also), so I'd either like to update the proposed req or cap or backlog item to CEMENT THIS BEHAVIOR."

Three obligations, and they are separable:

(1) THE OPTIONS ARE SELECTABLE, not buried in prose. The user picks rather than composing a reply. Prose that describes three courses of action still leaves them to name one; a list they can choose from does not.

(2) THE RECOMMENDATION COMES FIRST and is marked as such. Position carries meaning: an unordered menu makes the user infer which the agent favours, which is the analysis req:no-se-knowledge exists to spare them. Marking it also makes an overrule VISIBLE — the user knows they are departing from the agent's view, which is the precondition for the finding below.

(3) EVERY OPTION STILL CARRIES ITS CONSEQUENCE, including the ones not recommended. A list of bare labels is worse than prose, because it looks complete while withholding what each choice costs. The counterweight rule below is not relaxed by the format; it is what makes the format honest.

AND THE LANGUAGE IS THE USER'S, NOT ENGLISH — Anthony, same exchange: "with agents able to understand multiple languages, the 'simple english' should be 'simple whatever_language_user_is_writing_in'." The plainness obligation is about REGISTER, not about English: no jargon, no ids, short sentences, in whatever language the user is writing in. cap:surface already says "in the user's WORDS", and this makes the wider reading explicit so nobody implements it as an English-only rule. Every English-language phrasing in these design notes is an example of the register, never a specification of the language.

WHAT IS MISSING TODAY, and it is an omission rather than a prohibition. `detect-and-ask` is explicit that the agent must "never invent an answer on their behalf", which is right and must not be weakened. But the skill says nothing about offering a reading, so the default behaviour is a bare question — `gap_to_prompt` returns "is it covered, deferred, or dropped?" and the agent relays it. `cap:surface` ("turn a gap into a question in the user's words", `verified`) delivers the translation and nothing more.

WHY THAT IS A DEFECT AND NOT NEUTRALITY. `req:no-se-knowledge` says the user never needs systems engineering. A bare gap question hands them back the analysis the agent has already done and asks them to redo it in their own head — which is precisely the SE work that requirement exists to spare them. The agent has read the graph, seen the precedents, and formed a view; withholding it is not impartiality, it is making the user pay for the agent's caution.

IT IS ALSO WHAT `dec:three-party-checks` ALREADY DESCRIBES: "The LLM speaks, the graph remembers and counts, the human decides." Offering a reading IS the LLM speaking. The decision stays with the human, untouched — and `dec:certainty-derived` still governs the write, because a recommendation changes no status until the user answers.

THE LINE THAT MUST NOT BE CROSSED, stated so this cannot be read as licence. Recommending is not deciding: no requirement moves off `proposed`, no decision reaches `accepted`, no gap is acknowledged on a reading the user has not confirmed. And a recommendation must carry WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT — the condition under which the other option wins — or it is steering rather than advising. An option presented without its counterweight is a decision taken quietly.

THE PART WORTH RECORDING, and the reason this is design rather than style: WHEN THE USER OVERRULES A RECOMMENDATION, THAT IS INFORMATION. A design where the agent advised one way and the human chose another has learned something neither party knew alone, and today it is invisible because the recommendation was never on the record. Whether the recommendation itself should be stored beside the question is left open here rather than assumed. NOTE that obligation (2) sharpens this: marking the recommendation is what makes an overrule an identifiable EVENT rather than an unremarkable choice among equals.

MEASURED, not theorised: every gap put to Anthony on 2026-07-31 needed the recommendation added by hand, and he asked for it explicitly TWICE that day — "provide your recommendation", "present them in simple english and your recommendations for how to proceed" — and a THIRD time in the same session, at which point he asked for the behaviour to be cemented rather than repeated. A shape a user has to request each time is a default in the wrong place. This requirement's own evidence therefore accumulated by the exact mechanism it describes.

SCOPE, stated because the third request widened it: this began as a rule about GAPS, and Anthony's framing — "the decisions I need to make" — is broader. The obligation is read as covering any point where the agent puts a CHOICE to the user, not only where detect_gaps produced it. Whether that widening needs its own capability rather than riding this one is left open rather than assumed.

TENSION NAMED SO IT IS NOT CONFLATED: `dec:report-dont-judge` says the confirmation ledger reports claim history and never judges a claim. That governs what a COMPUTATION may assert about evidence. It does not govern whether an agent may advise a human who asked — different actor, different act. Conflating the two would silence exactly the party `dec:three-party-checks` puts there to speak.

properties.name: Relationships BETWEEN records are first-class, not wildcard leftovers — a check can name the file that runs it, a rule can name the rule it stands beside, and a retired check can say it was replaced
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-08-23, choosing the scope after the three candidates were measured against `dec:edge-orthogonality`.

THE CLASS, named by dev_storyflow across three independent reports before anyone looked for a pattern: **relationships between RECORDS are thinner in reflow2's vocabulary than relationships to Requirements.** The golden thread — Requirement ← Capability ← Component ← Artifact — is richly modelled. Verification-to-Artifact, rule-to-rule and check-to-check are not, and each time a session reached for one it found only a `*` wildcard or a refusal.

THREE INSTANCES, each with the computation that will read it — which is the filter `dec:edge-orthogonality` sets and the reason two further candidates were left out:

1. **A check has no way to name the file that RUNS it.** `describe_schema {from: Artifact, to: Verification}` answers honestly that no edge type names both. `REALIZES` is wrong (the script does not implement the capability, it interrogates it), `DOCUMENTS` is wrong (it is executable, not a doc), `CALIBRATED_AGAINST` is wrong (nothing was fitted to its output). Filed by dragon Boss 2026-08-19, who left the edge out rather than assert a wrong one — the honest choice, and it left the check an orphan Artifact. ⇒ READ BY: `loop_status.verifications.never_run`, which today cannot distinguish *a check nobody has run* from *a check with no executable form at all*. Two very different debts, one number.

2. **Two DesignRules that deliberately stand beside each other cannot say so.** `DUPLICATES` is actively wrong and invites a merge that would destroy the distinction; `SUPERSEDES` is wrong (neither replaces the other); `DEPENDS_ON` is wrong (each stands alone). The reporter used `CONTRADICTS alignment=supporting` and wrote a paragraph begging future readers not to merge them. ⇒ READ BY: the `possible_duplicate` heuristic and HEAL, which would then REFRAIN. This is the only one of the three that prevents a destructive act rather than enabling an expressive one — today a prose paragraph is the only thing standing between two complementary rules and a merge.

3. **A superseded check goes on reporting a stale status.** `SUPERSEDES` is refused between two Verifications, and `Verification.status` has no `superseded` value; the reporter used `EVOLVES_INTO` through a wildcard and `skipped`, which means something else. ⇒ READ BY: `loop_status.verifications.by_status` and `graph_report`, which count a retired check as `skipped` or, worse, as still `passing`.

⭐ WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT FROM EXPRESSIVENESS FOR ITS OWN SAKE, and it is why two other candidates were declined: `ChangeEvent → Decision` and a "which repo does this decision govern" property were both raised the same day, both from real friction, and NEITHER has a computation that would read it. They are deferred rather than built, because vocabulary nothing reads is exactly the defect `req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read` exists to catch, and adding it while that requirement is open would be filing the defect and committing it in one motion.

⚠️ THE CONSTRAINT ON HOW THIS IS BUILT, carried over from `VERIFIES`'s own schema comment: **enumerate endpoints, do not reach for `*`.** A wildcard would ACCEPT these pairs — nothing was ever broken — but it would not MODEL them, so `describe_schema` would go on ranking them as merely tolerated and no detector would treat them as real. The wildcard is also what stopped a reporter asserting a wrong edge, and that distinction must survive: what is added must be a modelled fit, not a widened loophole.

properties.name: A recorded risk reaches someone — RISKS is a finding source, not an edge only propagation can see
properties.statement:
A RISKS edge is surfaced by the routine calls people actually make — `loop_status` reporting recorded risks to what you own, and `detect_gaps(scope=…)` including risks that terminate inside the region — rather than being reachable only by someone who already suspects a change and asks for its blast radius.

THE EVIDENCE IS A SUCCESS STORY WEARING A FAILURE'S CLOTHES, which is why it is worth a primitive. In storyflow, `cap:fleet_step_reset` --RISKS--> `req:fleet_no_idle_worker` was recorded in advance, verified in the committed export. Hours later that exact causal chain ran: the user reset seats, the reset seats were invisible to every boss because a roster row is the product of a WRITE and an arriving seat has not written, a boss measured an empty pool and staffed nobody, and workers idled while a boss with lanes stood by. Somebody modelled their own incident correctly and in advance — AND IT REACHED NO ONE. `loop_status` never mentions RISKS. `detect_gaps` scoped to the owning component returned 12 gaps and this was not among them, because RISKS is not a gap source. Writing it down was never the hard part.

MEASURED IN REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN, 2026-08-09: ONE RISKS edge in 7,097. And the source tells the rest — `RISKS` appears in exactly one place in the entire codebase, `crates/reflow2-core/src/propagate.rs:34`, inside a `RISK_EDGES` constant. It is therefore reachable ONLY through `propagate_change`, which a caller reaches by already knowing something changed. No detector, no gap source, no report. `BLOCKS` (2 edges) and `MASKS` (0) sit in the same constant and have the same problem.

⭐ THIS SHARPENS AN OPEN QUESTION RATHER THAN DUPLICATING IT. dec:idea-detect-vocabulary-that-nothing-reaches counts an edge type as REACHED if it is instantiated, named in the propagation table, or named anywhere in non-test Rust. RISKS PASSES THAT TEST AND IS STILL WRITE-ONLY. So the census as specified would clear it, and a second test is needed: not "is this vocabulary named in code" but "can a reader who does not already know about it ever be shown it". Declared-versus-code and code-versus-retrieval are different failures, and only the first is currently modelled.

THE COUNTER-DISCIPLINE, recorded because it is part of the proposal rather than an objection to it: two edges in a whole graph means the type is effectively unused, so surfacing it will not be noisy. If it later becomes noisy, the answer is to require an assessment date on the edge — not to stop reporting.

SOURCE: storyflow gap A of the peer set — found by storybug Boss (47accf78), filed by api-boss (05af57c1), 2026-08-09, v0.26.1.

properties.name: A refusal names what would have worked — a rejected argument comes back with its legal values, not just a verdict
properties.statement:
WHEN A SERVED TOOL REFUSES AN ARGUMENT BECAUSE IT IS NOT ONE OF A FIXED SET, THE REFUSAL NAMES THE SET. The caller should not have to make a second call to learn what would have worked.

THE GAP THIS CLOSES. `parse_enum` — the single helper every enum argument on the served surface passes through — refused with `unknown change type: "correction"` and nothing else. No enumeration, no nearest match, no pointer to `describe_schema`. The caller is usually an AGENT MID-TASK, for whom a refusal that does not say what would have worked costs a whole round trip and a context switch into schema reading.

⭐ THE VALUES WERE NEVER UNAVAILABLE, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS A DEFECT RATHER THAN A FEATURE REQUEST. serde already builds `unknown variant `correction`, expected one of `requirement_creep`, `new_feature`, …` and the helper was DISCARDING it with `map_err(|_| …)`. The answer was constructed and thrown away on every rejection.

WHY THE FIX BELONGS IN THE SHARED HELPER, not at the call site that was reported: a hand-maintained list per tool rots the first time a variant is added, and one function serves every enum argument reflow2 exposes. Fixing it there means every refusal gains the list at once — which is what the reporter meant by \"this alone kills three of the eight\".

EVIDENCE. Filed by dev_storyflow 2026-08-03 (api-boss): \"enum rejections should list the legal values… this alone kills three of the eight.\" RE-CONFIRMED STILL LIVE 2026-08-09 by dragon Boss (`cca98fbf`), who recorded the cost precisely: \"one wasted call, then describe_schema{node_type: ChangeEvent, required_only: true} to learn the 11 legal values.\" And reproduced a third time the same day by a session in THIS repo while recording a correction — which is how it came to be fixed.

WHAT THIS REQUIREMENT DOES NOT SAY, so the scope is not read wider than it is: it does not ask for fuzzy nearest-match suggestions, and it does not ask that every refusal of any kind enumerate an alternative — only that a CLOSED SET, which the surface already knows, is stated rather than withheld. Where the message shape is unrecognised, the honest fallback is the underlying error's own words rather than a silent return to the bare verdict.

⚠️ A SEPARATE AND UNRESOLVED HALF, recorded here so it is not mistaken for closed: dragon Boss's second point was that NONE of the eleven legal `change_type` values means \"the record was WRONG about reality\". `resync` connotes reality moving and the design catching up. Adding a value would move the schema stamp and is Anthony's call; this requirement is only about the refusal being useful, not about the vocabulary being complete.

properties.name: A release that has gone out and records shipping nothing is reported
properties.statement:
A Release that is pinned to an epoch and deployed, and carries no INCLUDES edge, shall be reported as a gap — a release record claiming to have shipped nothing.

THE SCHEMA HAS ALWAYS SAID THIS AND NOTHING ENFORCED IT. The INCLUDES extraction hint ends: "The as-released view is read off these edges; a Release with none is a version number, not a manifest." That sentence described a state the design could not detect.

MEASURED, AND THE COST WAS A PUBLISHED RELEASE. On 2026-08-21 v0.38.0 was tagged, built, published and asset-verified with 0 INCLUDES against v0.37.0's 275. `release_includes_all` defaults to a dry run — correctly, so a cut can read what it is about to package — and its reply carries "applied": false beside "added": 304. The 304 is a forecast. It was read as an accomplishment twice, and every check that ran passed over the empty manifest: isError false both times, reflow2_check green, release_report never called.

THE DEFECT IS THAT A DRY RUN AND A WRITE ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE TO EVERY CHECK THAT RAN. This is `rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object` failing on a third surface after `gh pr merge`. The detector is that reading, performed by something that cannot forget to perform it.

THE RULE MUST NOT CONSULT `status`, and that is the load-bearing clause. Its sibling `release_without_epoch` exempts a `planned` release because an epoch is minted at the cut. Carrying that exemption here would have exempted the one real instance: rel:v0380 was published and deployed while its status still read `planned`, because nothing makes anyone move it. A status property records what somebody remembered to write down; a DEPLOYED_TO edge records that the thing went out.

ASKED, NEVER REPAIRED. What a release shipped is a judgement, and a genuinely contentless release — a re-tag, a docs-only republish — is a real state to accept. apply_heal must not invent a manifest (`cap:no-fabricated-repair`).

DISTINCT FROM the TemporalFact recording the v0.38.0 incident: that says what happened once, on a dated occasion, to one release; this says what the design shall detect from now on, for every release. DISTINCT FROM the capability that delivers it: that describes the mechanism built, its severity and its guards, and could be replaced by a different mechanism without this obligation changing.

properties.name: A repair suggestion never proposes fabricating a relationship — where no honest fix exists, the finding says so
properties.statement:
A HEAL suggestion must not propose creating a link that does not exist. Where a finding has no honest mechanical repair, the finding is reported WITHOUT a `suggested_fix_type` that would manufacture one, and says plainly that the repair is a judgement rather than an operation.

THE CONCRETE CASE. `disconnected_community` reports a cluster with `suggested_fix_type: generate_bridge` — create edges to connect it. Where the separation is CORRECT, acting on that suggestion fabricates relationships that do not exist, in order to silence a warning about a separation that is right. In dev_storyflow's words: \"acting on the suggestion would fabricate relationships that do not exist, to silence a warning about a separation that is correct. That is manufacturing connectivity, and it is the same act as formatting coverage into existence — WITH THE DIFFERENCE THAT HERE THE TOOL PROPOSES IT.\"

⭐ WHY THIS SHIPS FIRST AND ALONE. Anthony, 2026-08-09, settling `dec:legitimate-islands-need-the-detector-fix`: \"C now, A next with the read-back, not B, not D.\" This half is a LIVE HAZARD and is true whether or not partitions ever become declarable — a tool that proposes corrupting the graph is wrong on its own terms. It needs no schema change, so it does not wait for the schema increment that `req:a-cluster-can-be-declared-deliberately-separate` belongs to.

THE GENERAL PRINCIPLE, which is what makes this a requirement rather than a one-line patch: reflow2 already refuses to let a check be attached in order to close a finding (the governance-proposal skill's standing warning against green-washing), and `dec:ask-not-repair` already holds that suspected duplicates are ASKED, never merged. THE SAME RULE HAS NOT BEEN APPLIED TO REPAIR SUGGESTIONS. A proposal to write a false edge is the mirror image of a passing check that tests nothing: both make a report go quiet without making anything true.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY: it does not ask `disconnected_community` to stop firing, and it does not ask HEAL to stop proposing repairs generally. Mechanical repairs that restore a fact the design already holds remain correct. The line is narrow and it is about INVENTION: a suggestion may reorganise or restore, never assert a relationship nobody stated.

⚠️ RELATED AND SEPARATE, so the two are not conflated: `fact:apply-heal-would-have-destroyed-the-wrong-contributor` records a different HEAL failure found the same day — a merge proposal that named the wrong survivor and DISCLOSED its own arbitrariness (\"THE ALPHABET CHOSE THE VICTIM\"). That one is about which node a correct operation destroys; this one is about an operation that should not be offered at all.

SOURCE: storyflow gap D of the peer set — raised by storybug Boss (47accf78), characterised and filed by api-boss (05af57c1), 2026-08-09, v0.26.1. Reproduced in this design the same day at 5 nodes and again at 7.

properties.name: A person reporting a problem can name what was talking to what, without going through the channel that may be broken
properties.statement:
When someone reports a problem with reflow2, they SHALL be able to state which client connected, which server answered, and which protocol revision the two agreed to speak — read from a record the server itself wrote at connection time, rather than assembled by hand from whatever files happen to be nearby.

That record SHALL be reachable without a working structured tool reply, because the channel being reported on may itself be the fault.

It SHALL record what the negotiated revision CONTAINS, and SHALL NOT assert what the client actually reads: a negotiated version is what a client claims to speak, never evidence of what it implemented.

Driven by the 2026-08-27 field report, which had to hand-assemble a four-row table of sources to answer this question, one of which was stale and misleading.

properties.name: A report says what it swept and whether its checks were exercised, so a zero cannot be mistaken for a pass — and a zero-degree node is never reported as clean
properties.statement:
A report that contributes no findings must say whether it was EXERCISED AND FOUND NOTHING or HAD NOTHING TO EXAMINE, and must describe the scope it actually covered rather than a narrower one it was never given.

DISTINCT FROM THE FACT THE GUARD NAMED: `fact:defect-propose-heal-describes-neither-what-it-swept-nor-what-it-considered` is the OBSERVATION — what was measured, on which day, by whom. This is the INTENT — what must be true. A TemporalFact cannot be scheduled; a Requirement can.

THE THEME IS ALREADY ACCEPTED DOCTRINE rather than a new idea: `chg:a-null-and-a-vacuous-zero-now-say-which-they-are` gave scoped `detect_gaps` exactly this treatment, and dev_storyflow's dragon Boss independently named it a WIN — "flags its own vacuous zeros". This generalises what that change did in one place.

⚠️ THE STAKE IS NOT TIDINESS: a fleet runs `propose_heal` as the read-only evidence step of a standing stop on `apply_heal`, which DELETES NODES. A vacuous zero there is one skim away from lifting a gate on an irreversible operation.

── PARTLY DELIVERED 2026-08-16 (#210) ──
`propose_heal` now carries `scope`, `projects_in_scope` and `merge_candidates_considered`, and no longer names a Project the caller never chose. `merge_candidates_considered` is dev_storyflow's own idea (1) and their field name.

── STILL OWED, ADDED 2026-08-16 after the full fleet-log triage ──
Three further instances the #210 fix did not touch, each measured in real use, and the second is the worst thing in the whole log:

(a) ZERO-DEGREE NODES ARE NOT REPORTED. `detect_defects` answered `clean: true` with `structural_defects: 0` over a DesignEpoch carrying NO EDGES AT ALL — in two separate packages, through every health call of a session. A node with no edges is the most detectable structural defect there is, and it needs no judgement to identify, unlike the modularity cluster the tool did report. `heal.rs:879` does this for Decisions only. **Reflow2's own health check returned a false green on the pass whose job is structural soundness.**

(b) `disconnected_community` COMPUTES MODULARITY AND SPEAKS THE WORDS OF UNREACHABILITY — "disconnected from the rest of the design". The four nodes it named were all reachable by an undirected walk; the genuinely unreachable node was never mentioned. Either rename it to what it computes ("tightly-coupled cluster") or make it compute what it claims. A confident answer to a NEARBY question occupies the attention the right question needed.

(c) `open_questions` RETURNING 0 READS AS AN ALL-CLEAR while `loop_status` in the very next call reported 31 other owed items — and it is the orientation call a new session runs FIRST. Naming the other non-zero counts would be enough.

NOT IN SCOPE, unchanged: whether every reporting tool needs this treatment or only those whose zero is read as permission.

REPORTED BY dev_storyflow's fleet across 2026-08-08 to 2026-08-15, by three seats independently.

properties.name: A rule the project follows is recorded with its consequence stated, and a violation is computed rather than remembered
properties.statement:
A project's own conventions — how it merges, who may sign off, what the build refuses — are part of its design and must be recordable as design, with the CONSEQUENCE of breaking each one stated by the person whose project it is. A rule whose power over the build was never chosen by anybody is not a rule the design can act on.

⚠️ STATUS: `proposed`, and it stays there until Anthony has read these words. He chose the SHAPE on 2026-08-11 — "a new requirement, mirroring KPPs" — when asked what need `cap:governance-proposal` serves (question:3f04e352bc497c5b). The wording below is an agent's draft of that shape, not his sentence, and `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` is the reason the distinction is being made explicitly rather than quietly resolved in the agent's favour.

THE SHAPE, deliberately mirroring `req:inviolable-intent` one layer along. That requirement says intent that must hold no matter what is recorded as inviolable, and a violation is COMPUTED, not remembered; `cap:kpp-proposal` is the capture half that asks the user whether something is a KPP rather than deciding for them. This is the same sentence about RULES rather than about intent, and `cap:governance-proposal` is its capture half. The parallel is the argument: a project's policy deserves the same treatment as its performance parameters, because both are things a person committed to and neither survives as prose.

WHAT IT REQUIRES, in three parts:
  (1) A rule is recordable as a design object rather than as a paragraph in a markdown file nobody diffs.
  (2) Its CONSEQUENCE — gate-blocking, advisory, or unstated — is the user's to state, never inherited. `DesignRule.enforced` is now genuinely three-state (schema/core.yaml:127, "Never defaulted"), so absence reads as "nobody has said" instead of as a choice.
  (3) A rule declared gate-blocking OWES a detector, and the debt is computed. That is `unverified_enforced_rule` at 0.6, and it is the part that stops governance-in-graph being prettier prose.

WHERE IT CAME FROM, recorded because this requirement exists partly BECAUSE that trace was missing. The demand signal is the GOVERNANCE-AS-DESIGN entry in dev_storyflow's `reflow2_feedback.md`, filed by api-boss (`5d608b85`) on 2026-08-08, carrying Anthony's own framing: "every project will be managed differently and have differing sets of people running it with their own practices and policies about merging and who can merge and other governing mechanisms — but allowing reflow2 to setup a generic set of nodes/edges that allow a user or set of users to define their own project management policies/governance in graph form is something that I think would be really helpful. additionally, by putting in graph form, you can start seeing issues and gaps in their policies (like we are experiencing in storyflow) and help resolve them properly."

⭐ WHY IT IS BEING WRITTEN NOW, MONTHS AFTER THE WORK SHIPPED. `cap:governance-proposal` was built, realized by `art:governance-proposal-skill`, and served to sessions while satisfying no requirement at all — surfaced as gap:3f04e352bc497c5b (unmotivated_capability, 0.55) and put to Anthony on 2026-08-11. Six sibling requirements from the same feedback entry DO exist and carry AUTHORED_BY to `who:storyflow-api-boss`; this one was the gap in that capture, not the whole of it. The honest reading is that the process ran and missed a step, not that the work was unrequested.

WHY NOT `req:defaults-do-not-assert`, considered and declined on 2026-08-11 by Anthony. That requirement names `DesignRule.enforced` explicitly and predates this skill by six weeks, so it is a genuine historical driver rather than a retro-fit. It was declined as the parent because it covers TEN defaulted-and-unread properties of which this addresses one, and because the default-asserting half has since been fixed in the schema — so a SATISFIES edge would make a tenth of that work read as delivered while nine properties stay untouched. It remains at `proposed` with nothing satisfying it.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. It does not require any rule to be enforced — advisory is a first-class answer and six of reflow2's nine rules are advisory by the owner's explicit choice. It does not require every convention to be captured. And it says nothing about WHO may state a rule's consequence; that is `req:a-node-can-say-who-may-change-it`, still `proposed`.

HONEST BOUND: the capture half only helps a session that invokes the skill. A rule recorded by an agent that never loads `governance-proposal` still lands with `enforced` unstated — which is now reported rather than asserted, so the failure is visible, but it is not prevented.

properties.name: A rule knows where it is authoritatively stated and where else it is repeated, so an amendment can find its own stale copies
properties.statement:
A rule can name the artifact that AUTHORITATIVELY states it, and the artifacts that merely REPEAT it — and a report answers "if I change this rule, what documents claim to state it?"

THE GAP THIS CLOSES. A rule that lives in the graph is usually also written in a README, an onboarding doc, a code comment, a CI config. Amending the graph does not tell you where else the old wording lives, and a stale restatement does not lag quietly — it keeps issuing the superseded instruction to whoever reads it. `DesignRule` today has name, statement, category and enforced, and NOWHERE to put the source of record; the storyflow trial ended up writing "Source of record: PROTOCOL.md" into the free-text statement of all eight of its rules, putting the property that most needs to be queryable into prose no detector can read.

WHAT THE EDGE MAKES POSSIBLE, and this is the argument for modelling it rather than adding a string property: a rule with TWO authoritative sources is a duplication risk; a rule with NONE is folklore; an artifact that changed since the rule was recorded is a rot candidate. None of those three questions can be asked today. reflow2 already has DOCUMENTS — "this file describes that node"; what is missing is its inverse in spirit — "this file REPEATS that node's content and will go stale when it changes."

EVIDENCE. One rule existed in FIVE places. A correct amendment fixed the two a MACHINE reads and missed the three that bind HUMANS — for two days, during which the stale copies were ordering work the ruling had explicitly removed. Nobody was careless: there was no way to ask "where else is this stated?"

THE HARD HALF IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED. Detecting a CONTRADICTION between a rule and its restatement defeats every keyword method, because both copies contain the same words. reflow2 should not pretend to do it. LISTING the restatements would have prevented the incident on its own — the graph supplies the list, the human eye does the comparison.

ADJACENT SCHEMA FINDING, recorded because it is the same neglect: `describe_schema` reports that NO edge type models DesignRule → Component either. Both GOVERNED_BY and CONSTRAINS accept the pair only through a `*` wildcard. DesignRule is the least-connected type in the schema — odd for the one whose whole job is to bind other things, and precisely the catch-up debt dec:governance-integrates-not-splits names.

SOURCE: storyflow fleet governance report, api-boss (05af57c1), 2026-08-09, v0.26.1. Bound as stated by its author: one project, one month, one fleet shape — hypotheses to test, not requirements.

properties.name: A rule says whether a check is even possible, so "no detector" splits into debt and accepted limit
properties.statement:
A rule or requirement can declare its VERIFIABILITY — detectable / detectable-but-unwritten / undetectable-by-nature, with a required reason for the last — so that "which of my rules have no check?" splits into a backlog and a set of accepted limits, and only the first is debt.

THE GAP THIS CLOSES. "No check is possible" and "no check yet" are OPPOSITE states that read identically today. Both surface as "unverified". A rule about INTENT — "do not shape data to satisfy a tool" — has no detectable signature by construction, because the compliant and non-compliant artefacts are byte-identical. A rule about a file layout is merely unwritten. Reporting them the same way makes the report untrustworthy: a reader cannot tell a permanent limit from a to-do.

REFLOW2 HAS ALREADY SOLVED THIS EXACT SHAPE ONCE, one domain over, which is the strongest argument that the distinction is real and not a special case. `granularity` distinguishes `opaque` — a subtree claimed as a unit ON PURPOSE — from `pending_expansion` — a PLACEHOLDER for work not done — and reflow2's own tool documentation says they "look identical to every report today and are opposite states: a decision versus unfinished work." The same distinction is missing for verifiability. It is also the same principle as dec:does-enforced-default-to-gate-blocking, where a rule's power is stated rather than defaulted.

WHY IT MATTERS TO THE REPORT AND NOT ONLY TO THE RECORD. Of nine rules recorded in the storyflow trial, two got checks, one was detectable-but-unwritten, and THREE were undetectable by construction. Filing those three as unverified debt would misreport a third of the set forever — and a permanent red nobody can clear is how a report loses its readers.

RELATED, AND THE REASON THIS IS URGENT RATHER THAN TIDY: `unverified_enforced_rule` already fires today on `enforced: true` with no incoming VERIFIES, and rule:bl-41 is currently caught by it. Without this distinction that detector cannot tell a rule that is waiting for a detector from one that can never have one.

SOURCE: storyflow fleet governance report, api-boss (05af57c1), 2026-08-09, v0.26.1. Bound as stated by its author: one project, one month, one fleet shape — hypotheses to test, not requirements.

properties.name: A rule states the scope it binds in, and a conflict between two rules is surfaced — because a rule conflict selects against the careful
properties.statement:
A rule states the SCOPE it applies in, so a reader can tell whether it binds them; and where two rules cannot both be satisfied, that conflict is surfaced by the design rather than discovered by whoever loses work to it.

⭐ THE GENERAL FINDING, and it is not about export: WHEN TWO SAFETY RULES CONFLICT, THE PARTICIPANT WHO REASONS MOST CAREFULLY ABOUT THE CONFLICT IS THE ONE WHO DOES NOTHING — and doing nothing is often the destructive option. A conflict between two safety rules is not neutral; IT SELECTS AGAINST THE CAREFUL. That is the mechanism this requirement exists to break, and it generalises far past the case that exposed it.

THE CASE. Two rules, both correct in isolation: any session that changed the design EXPORTS BEFORE STANDING DOWN (durability), versus the export is produced ONCE PER PULL REQUEST, LAST OF ALL, because two exporting commits on one branch break the lineage chain silently (integrity — dec:export-once-per-pr here). On a shared branch with several writers, BOTH CANNOT BE SATISFIED. A storyflow boss wrote two Requirements, one Contributor and two edges, then reported: "I am NOT exporting, because I will not risk the lineage chain on a guess — and the cost of that correct-looking caution is that my writes exist in one untracked RocksDB directory on this host and nowhere else," which is precisely what the durability rule exists to prevent. Another session exported four times the same day. NEITHER BEHAVIOUR IS WRONG UNDER THE RULES AS WRITTEN.

REPRODUCED HERE THE SAME DAY, and by the careful route: this session declined to export after recording dec:governance-integrates-not-splits and four requirements, because PR #132 was open and dec:export-once-per-pr applied. The design's own answer to the tension was to leave a session's work unexported — the identical outcome, arrived at by the identical reasoning, in the project that authors the rule.

WHAT IS MISSING, in two parts. FIRST, SCOPE: the lineage warning does not say whether it is branch-local or any-branch, so a reader cannot tell whether it applies to them. This is the same missing field as req:a-decision-states-what-it-binds, one node type over — and where a single-writer discipline is required on shared state, reflow2 should be able to SAY so rather than leaving each project to find out by having someone lose work. SECOND, DETECTION: reflow2 surfaces a contradiction only where a human has already drawn a CONTRADICTS edge — two of this design's five current structural defects are exactly that. Nothing DISCOVERS a conflict between two rules nobody suspected, which is the only case that matters, because a suspected conflict is one somebody is already handling.

FILED AS A REFLOW2 SEMANTICS GAP, NOT A PROJECT ONE, in the reporter's words: a project may rule its own cadence, but it should not have to discover the conflict first.

SOURCE: storyflow gap C of the peer set — storybug Boss (47accf78), filed 2026-08-09, v0.26.1.

properties.name: A scoped answer actually narrows, so "my part" is a different answer from "the program"
properties.statement:
Scoping a detector to a part of the design must return an answer materially different from the unscoped one, or the narrowing is decoration and the number beside it is misleading.

(Distinct from the FACT, which records the measurement, and from the DECISION, which proposes one specific default. This is the intent both of those serve: the fact is evidence, the decision is one answer, and this says what must be true whatever answer is chosen.)

THE MEASUREMENT THAT MAKES THIS A REQUIREMENT RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE. Driving the built binary over all 56 Components of reflow2's own design (2487 nodes, 83 gaps), at the DEFAULT depth of 3: every single component returns 50-60 of the 83 gaps, median 55, over a region of 595-903 nodes. The spread across all 56 is 50..60 — indistinguishable. `in_scope: 55, out_of_scope: 28` reads as "your part has 55 gaps" and says the same thing to every team about every part. Shallower depths discriminate sharply: depth 1 gives 0-19 gaps over 17-139 nodes, depth 2 gives 2-27 over 267-601. Evidence: `fact:defect-a-scoped-detector-at-its-default-depth-returns-two-thirds-of-the-design`.

WHAT IS OWED. Not a number — a property. A scoped read should be checkable against the claim it makes: if scoping to any seed returns most of what the unscoped call returns, the tool should be able to SAY SO rather than leaving the reader to compare two numbers they were never shown together. The specific default is `dec:the-default-scope-depth-should-be-two`, which is separately open and is the owner's to settle.

THREE THINGS THE SAME MEASUREMENT TURNED UP, worth carrying together because they are one confusion about what a region is:
(a) `scope.rs` justifies the default of 3 by saying the third hop is needed to reach a contained child component's capabilities. `scope_region` puts the whole containment closure into the seed set BEFORE taking the radius, so those capabilities are ONE hop from an owned node. The stated reason is not a reason the code needs.
(b) `detect_gaps`' description claims its region is "the same computation claim_region uses for 'the part I hold', so 'my area' means one thing everywhere". It is not: the MCP defaults differ (3 vs 2) AND `scope_region` adds the containment closure that `claimed_region` omits.
(c) That second divergence is already recorded in `scope.rs` as possibly a defect in the claims layer, deliberately left unfixed because changing what a claim covers changes what two people believe they hold. Reconciling the two is a bigger question than a default and is NOT assumed here.

SCOPE OF THIS REQUIREMENT, so the increment can be argued with: it is about the scoped DETECTORS and the words they use about themselves. It does not decide (c), and it does not touch `design_regions`, which already reports its own depth and coverage.

properties.name: A seat learns the shared record moved when it ORIENTS, not when it writes
properties.statement:
When another contributor's work has arrived in the shared design record and this graph has never seen it, the seat is told so at the point it orients itself — not at the point it tries to write, hours later.

WHY THE MOMENT IS THE REQUIREMENT AND NOT AN ERGONOMIC PREFERENCE: the signal already existed and was already correct. `provenance::last_synced` was maintained by both the export and import paths, and `sync::assess_overwrite` already turned it into a three-way verdict. It was consulted in exactly one place — inside `export_graph`. So the design knew at the first moment of a session and spoke at the last, by which point the session had done its work against a record it did not know had moved.

WHAT SATISFYING THIS MUST NOT COST: silence during ordinary work. A seat that is merely AHEAD of the record — unexported work in progress — is the normal state of every working session and must never be reported, or the signal is ignored inside a week. The distinguishing test is whether the RECORD moved, not whether the two differ.

AND IT REPORTS RATHER THAN ACTS: taking the arrived work in is an upsert over live session state, so it stays the human's call.

⚠️ WORDING IS AN AGENT'S DRAFT. Anthony chose the MECHANISM (option A, 2026-08-11) and directed the build; he has not ruled on this statement's text, which is why this sits at `proposed`.

properties.name: A payload says whether the session reading it is alone on the graph
properties.rationale: THE ROOT CAUSE BEHIND EVERY SHARED-GRAPH FAILURE THEY REPORTED, in their words: A SESSION CANNOT TELL THAT IT IS NOT ALONE. Nothing in any payload reports concurrency, so every seat reasons as if solo and the output actively encourages it. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE (fact:defect-rollups-became-fleet-numbers-without-saying-so): defects 42->6->5->12 and gaps 48->55->69 on one graph in one day by non-coordinating sessions, including a 5->12 jump delivered to a session that had done nothing; TWO BOSSES, one of them the reporter, attributed a global movement to their own change — in the flattering direction, which is the one nobody catches unaided. The reporter told the user '42 -> 6' twice as their own result. It was not. Their argument for this specific field: a seat seeing `attached: 7` CANNOT HONESTLY CLAIM A ROLLUP AS ITS OWN, so one number prevents the whole class. The alternative in force today is a hand-maintained fleet convention requiring every citation to be labelled FLEET or SCOPED — a discipline layered on a tool that could just say it, and by their own standard a defect routed around rather than fixed. NOTE THE MIGRATION HAZARD THIS ALSO NAMES: loop_status and graph_report read IDENTICALLY before and after `--shared`; only the MEANING changed, so every citation of those counts written before the migration is now subtly wrong and nothing says so.
properties.statement: Tool responses that report graph-wide state SHALL make concurrency visible — at minimum the number of currently-attached sessions, and ideally last_write_at and last_write_by — and rollups SHALL label themselves as graph-wide rather than leaving scope to the reader. Requested as the #2 fleet ask and as the single 'if only one thing changes' item by dev_storyflow's api-boss 5d608b85, 2026-08-07.

properties.name: A session bound to one design cannot read or write any other design in the same process — and this must be proven before multi-graph hosting ships
properties.statement:
When one process holds several design graphs (dec:one-process-many-stores, accepted 2026-08-06), a client session attached to design X must not be able to read or write design Y through any tool on the surface — not by passing a graph_id it was not attached to, not by a path, not by reconnecting, and not by a handler that resolves the wrong entry from the registry.

THIS IS THE SHIPPING CONDITION, not a nice-to-have. Anthony accepted dec:one-process-many-stores on 2026-08-06 conditional on exactly this: the isolation guarantee carried as its own requirement, with a check, landing BEFORE any of the multi-graph work ships. The reason is the failure mode rather than the principle — an isolation regression does not error, it CORRUPTS: a handler that reaches the wrong graph writes one design's nodes into another, and nothing in the loop would report it because both graphs would still be internally coherent. That is strictly worse than a crash, and it is invisible to every detector reflow2 has.

THE SECOND HALF, and it must be stated rather than assumed: reflow2 HAS NO AUTHENTICATION OF ANY KIND. Whoever fronts a hosted reflow2 — flo2 today — owns authentication and authorization: deciding WHICH designs a given human may reach. reflow2's obligation is narrower and absolute: given that a session has been attached to design X by the layer in front, reflow2 must not let it touch design Y. Those two are not the same guarantee and neither substitutes for the other. If this split is not written down and held, accepting dec:one-process-many-stores quietly converts an accepted "no hosted service" into a hosted service with no security story — the drift dec:reopen-supersedes exists to prevent, and the counter-argument that decision's own rationale already records.

SCOPE NOTE: this says nothing about the single-graph case, which has this property today for free because the process holds exactly one store. The requirement exists because that free guarantee is what the registry removes.

properties.name: A session bound to one design cannot address another, and that is a security property rather than a tidiness one
properties.statement:
Raised by @ajs from flo2, 2026-08-05, as the single highest-risk part of multi-graph hosting.
