{"decision":"UNDECIDED, and RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-07-25, explicitly not convinced by the collaboration design and thinking out loud: \"could you have small/mini reflow2 graphs inside itself... coming from a system of systems engineering approach, reflow2 may lay out the graph and how all the systems need to interact and where there are gaps, but what if we now had a mini-reflow2 graph for each system? And a mini-mini-reflow2 of the components in the system... the idea is that reflow2 has the tools to analyze the graph at each level and ensure there are no gaps and that it works with the higher level systems or system-of-systems.\" WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE, because it changes what the idea is asking for. Levels exist and are already checked: Component.level is an enum of component / subsystem / system / system_of_systems / enterprise, CONTAINS between Components is the axis-Y spine, and hierarchy_issues already reports level_mismatch, missing_intermediate_level and orphan_level — the carburetor-to-body problem, imported from chain_reflow's matryoshka insight (docs/three-axes.md). And the multi-graph primitive exists unused: every node and edge carries graph_id, pinned to the constant \"reflow2\". So the question is not whether reflow2 can express nesting. It can. The question is whether a level should be a SUBTREE of one graph or a GRAPH OF ITS OWN. THREE OPTIONS. (a) ONE GRAPH, ZOOM BY LEVEL — today's shape. What is missing is not nesting but SCOPING: no read takes a subtree as its subject, so detect_gaps and graph_report always answer for the whole design. Adding a scope argument is a filter, not an architecture, and it delivers most of what was asked — the tools analysing each level. (b) A GRAPH PER SYSTEM, COMPOSED — Anthony's idea. It buys four things one graph cannot: an independent write lock per system, which is a different and stronger answer to the collaboration problem than region claims, because separate graphs are PHYSICALLY separate where a claim is only advisory; an independent lifecycle, so a subsystem can be released, adopted or handed to a vendor on its own; selective publishing, which is exactly req:design-reachable-without-the-repo; and per-level scale, since detectors run over hundreds of nodes instead of tens of thousands. (c) A GRAPH PER OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY, LEVELS INSIDE EACH — the hybrid, and the shape federated systems engineering actually uses: you split where AUTHORITY splits, not where the hierarchy happens to have a layer. THE FOUR HARD PARTS of (b), each one real: the golden thread cannot cross a store boundary, because the schema validates both endpoints of every edge — so a parent's Component pointing at a child's design needs a typed COORDINATE (graph id + node id + the export's content hash at the moment the reference was made), which is precisely the choice dec:fork-point-address already made for fork points over a native ref layer. Gap detection goes blind at the seam: a parent requirement whose satisfying capability lives in a child graph would fire unsatisfied forever unless the child's evidence rolls up — and that roll-up is cap:derived-completion's computation applied one level higher, which is encouraging rather than novel. Freshness becomes load-bearing: a parent's view of a child is a claim about a VERSION of that child, so it is a dated examined claim and never a live truth (the cap:freshness and confirmation-ledger shape). And the seam becomes the new collision point: two people changing the interface across the boundary still collide, now in the one place with no merge machinery. THE TENSION WORTH KNOWING ABOUT: docs/org-scale-vision.md records the opposite destination — \"one graph the whole company plans in\", with the CEO's objectives at the top and everything tracing upward. Federation and one-big-graph cannot both be the end state, and nothing in the design has ever chosen between them. THE DISCRIMINATOR, offered as a finding and not a decision: depth alone does not justify a separate graph. Nesting three levels of graphs costs a coordinate, a roll-up and a freshness check at every seam, and buys nothing that a scope filter would not have delivered — unless something at that level is separately OWNED, separately RELEASED, or separately SHARED. Where those hold, a graph of its own is right. Where they do not, it is ceremony.","name":"OPEN — one graph with levels, or a graph per system composed into a bigger one?","rationale":"Recorded 2026-07-25 because Anthony said plainly he was not convinced by the collaboration design, and an unconvinced author is a finding rather than a disagreement to be argued down. PROMOTED THE SAME DAY on his word (\"let's promote both\"): the brainstorm produced two accepted requirements and stays open on the mechanism, which is the split that keeps both halves honest. req:analyse-at-any-level is the part he needed day to day and is ALREADY DELIVERED by cap:scoped-analysis (option (a), built first because it forecloses nothing). req:design-composes is the federation intent — a system's design as a unit that composes through interfaces — GOVERNED_BY this decision, so nothing gets built toward it until the mechanism is chosen. THIS DECISION THEREFORE STAYS PROPOSED, and that is not hedging: promoting an idea to intent is not the same act as choosing between three architectures, and collapsing this one would assert a shape Anthony has never chosen. Its options and the four hard parts of federation are unchanged above. The discriminator recorded then still stands as the thing to test when it is decided: depth alone does not earn a separate graph — ownership, separate release, or separate sharing does. NOTE FOR WHOEVER COLLAPSES IT: docs/org-scale-vision.md still records the opposite destination (one graph the whole company plans in), and req:design-composes now sits in the graph as accepted intent pointing the other way. That tension is real, on the record, and undecided; it is the strongest reason this decision should be made deliberately rather than discovered.","status":"proposed"}

{"decision":"Anthony, 2026-08-26, thinking out loud: *"what are some things we can do to increase the probability that an agent will use reflow2 skills and tools in a project? what would make the agent say, I have the perfect skill or tool needed for problem X? hopefully, by adding depth and layers, we can start seeing much more clearly why and when some skills/tools are used."*

**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Nothing here is decided; the options are put down so a later session meets the reasoning rather than re-deriving it.

═══ THE FRAME BEING PROPOSED: FOUR LAYERS, AND A SKIP HAPPENS AT THE WEAKEST ONE ═══

For an agent to use a skill, four things must all hold. They fail independently, they want different fixes, and reflow2 has not worked them equally:

① **KNOWN** — the agent is aware the thing exists. *(Worked: `list_skills`, `get_skill`, served-not-installed, the handshake catalogue, 24 slash commands.)*

② **RECOGNISED** — the agent notices THIS MOMENT is that skill's moment. *(Worked hard: `cap:skill-triggers`, the three-event loop nudge, `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue`.)*

③ **WORTH IT** — the agent believes the skill beats what it would do unaided. *(BARELY WORKED AT ALL. There is no node arguing that a skill produces a better answer than competent improvisation; the whole surface argues that skipping is non-compliant, which is a different claim and a weaker motivator for something that is not trying to comply.)*

④ **VISIBLE** — something can see whether it happened. *(PARTLY BUILT — see the correction below.)*

⚠️ **CORRECTION MADE IN THE SAME SESSION, AND THE MISTAKE IS WORTH KEEPING.** This node first asserted that layer ④ was DEFERRED, reasoning from `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`, which says so in its own text. That was true when that requirement was written and is now FALSE: `req:skill-adherence-is-measured` is **`accepted`**, and `cap:skill-loads-are-counted` is **built and `verified`**.

**The error is the one this project keeps recording: reading a claim out of one node's prose instead of the node it is about.**

**What layer ④ actually holds now:** skill LOADS are counted, and their absence is announced at session end. **What it still does not hold:** any notion of which skill SHOULD have been loaded for the work that was done.

═══ THE EVIDENCE THAT ③ IS THE BOTTLENECK ═══

`req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` records the same failure twice, six days apart, and the second is the damning one: **`cap:skill-triggers` was `verified` and firing correctly, and the user still had to be the reminder.** Layer ② was WORKING and it was not enough.

It also names the structural ceiling on ②: every shape that capability recognises is a shape in the GRAPH-WRITE stream, so it requires the agent to have already touched the graph. *A skill load is not a graph write.* No amount of work on ② reaches an agent that never started.

⭐ AND THE MEASUREMENT MOST WORTH REPEATING: both observations were made on sessions with **more** context about reflow2 than any consumer's agent will ever have. That is a BEST case, not a typical one.

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) Attack layer ③ directly: make the skill's ADVANTAGE legible at the moment of choice.** ⚠️ Counter: self-promotion inside a tool result, and it cannot be honest without evidence.

**(b) Keep hardening ② and accept the ceiling.** ⚠️ Counter: measured twice as insufficient, and the ceiling is structural.

**(c) Finish layer ④ — the half that is missing.** ⚠️ Counter: `dec:loop-status-state-not-history` may forbid the obvious implementation, and that must be settled BEFORE anything is built.

**(d) Reject the frame.** Perhaps the real variable is CONTEXT BUDGET: a skill costs tokens to load mid-task, and an agent under pressure economises. **Nothing has tested this, and it would explain the measured facts as well as ③ does.**

═══ WHY THE FRAME MIGHT EARN ITS KEEP ═══

It gives every future idea a place to attach: a proposal that improves ① when the bottleneck is ③ can be recognised as such before it is built. **It is a diagnostic, not a design.**

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
═══ 📌 SHARPENED 2026-08-26 BY A USER REPORT — AND THE FRAME HAS A HOLE ═══

*A user reported, relayed, that they were "probably not understanding all the skills in reflow2". Recorded here rather than as a new node because this node's own rationale says splitting would "lose the comparison, which is the only part that does any work". Written without the user's domain or employer; the design record is public.*

⭐ **EVERY ONE OF THE FOUR LAYERS IS ABOUT THE AGENT. NONE IS ABOUT THE PERSON.** The frame reads "for an AGENT to use a skill, four things must hold" — and a human who does not know what reflow2 is FOR fails before layer ① is reached. That is a candidate **layer ⓪ — ORIENTED: the person knows what this tool does and what it will ask of them.**

Whether ⓪ belongs in the frame is the open part. Two readings, and they lead to different work:

- **⓪ IS REAL.** reflow2 asks the human questions — gaps, decisions, who they are. A user who cannot answer *"what is this for?"* cannot answer those either, and no amount of agent-side triggering helps.
- **⓪ IS A MIRAGE, and the report is really ① or ③ seen from the user's chair.** reflow2 is AGENT-DRIVEN. The user never picks a skill; they see the consequence of the agent picking one. *"I do not understand the skills"* may be *"the agent never reached for one, and I noticed."* **Then a tutorial teaches the wrong party.**

🛑 **NOTHING WE HAVE DISTINGUISHES THESE**, and that is the same hole layer ④ already names: loads are counted, but not whether the RIGHT skill was owed. `dec:bl-155`'s warning applies exactly — it could not tell *unused* from *unreachable*, and this cannot tell *uninformed user* from *unreaching agent*.

📌 **WHAT IS ACTUALLY MEASURED TODAY, so ① is not overstated:** 22 served skills, 163 tools, `list_skills` / `get_skill` / `find_tools`, `docs/skills-and-tools.md`, 24 slash commands. All answer *"what is there?"*. **None answers *"where do I start?"*** — `genesis` covers a new PROJECT, `adopt` covers existing CODE, and nothing covers a new PERSON.

⭐ **AND A WORKED EXAMPLE OF THE FRAME FAILING BELOW ALL FOUR LAYERS**, measured the same day: `fact:the-lens-that-carries-the-persona-was-built-on-a-branch-and-never-shipped`. The mechanism that would carry a reader's background to the agent was built, core-tested, and left on an unmerged branch. That is not ①, ②, ③ or ④ — the thing was never in the surface at all, while the design recorded the capability as existing. **A fifth failure mode: the mechanism is in the DESIGN and not in the BUILD.** Whether the frame should carry that too, or whether it belongs to release hygiene rather than adoption, is unsettled.

⚠️ **THE COUNTERWEIGHT ON ALL OF IT:** n=1, relayed, from a user who cannot share specifics. This project's own history says the tempting fix is the wrong one. {"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent.

ANTHONY, 2026-08-21: "now that we've developed the 9 subsystems of reflow2, can we work on coming up with more exhaustive tests for each subsystem? things like edge cases and identify failure modes and other tests."

📌 FIRST, TWO CORRECTIONS OF FACT, both small and both worth having straight before anyone plans work against them. There are TEN subsystems, not nine. And one of them, `cmp:packaging`, carries a `cmp:` id at subsystem level with ZERO components under it — a naming and containment oddity that predates today and is not a defect anyone has been asked about yet.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑🛑 THE FINDING: EXHAUSTIVE TESTS CANNOT BE DERIVED FROM THIS DESIGN TODAY, AND THE REASON IS ONE NUMBER
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

    Capabilities:                          192
    ... declaring their INPUTS:              3
    ... declaring their OUTPUTS:             3
    ... declaring a SIGNATURE:               0
    Constraints (where a hard limit lives):  1

EDGE CASES ARE DERIVED FROM THE BOUNDARIES OF AN INPUT DOMAIN. FAILURE MODES ARE DERIVED FROM WHAT AN OUTPUT PROMISES. With neither stated for 189 of 192 capabilities, both can only be IMAGINED — which is what 1376 hand-written tests already are, and they are good ones, but imagining more of them is not what "exhaustive" means. `dec:idea-stated-module-function-is-what-makes-failure-mode-testing-derivable` (Anthony, 2026-08-20) said this a day early and named the mechanism: `Capability.inputs`/`outputs` exist in the schema with NO typed tool, NO instruction and NO detector — the three-legged failure again.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 AND THE PER-SUBSYSTEM PICTURE IS NOT TRUSTWORTHY YET
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

    subsystem              components   verifications
    sys:coherence-loop         28            68
    sys:agent-surface          25            31
    sys:store                   2            16
    sys:foundation              6            14
    sys:time-history            6            14
    sys:intake                  4             6
    sys:vocabulary              2             6
    cmp:packaging               0             4
    sys:human-channel           2             2
    sys:documentation           1             0

    181 Verifications; 27 of them reach NO subsystem at all.
    127 real test FILES on disk; 47 are pointed at by an Artifact.
    ⇒ 80 TEST FILES THE DESIGN HAS NEVER HEARD OF.

⭐ SO "sys:documentation HAS ZERO VERIFICATIONS" MAY WELL BE FALSE. With 80 of 127 test files unmodelled, a zero in that table is as likely to be a MODELLING gap as a TESTING gap — and acting on it would mean writing tests for something already tested while something genuinely bare stays quiet. **A detector that reports zero because it had nothing to run on reads exactly like one that ran clean**, and this table currently has that defect. Anything built on these counts should re-measure first.

📌 AND THE OTHER AXIS IS STILL UNTOUCHED: 181 of 181 Verifications carry `kind: verification`. ZERO carry `validation`. reflow2 ships the built-right / right-thing split and has never once used it on itself. "More exhaustive" in the built-right direction is already 1376 tests deep; the axis with nothing on it at all is whether each subsystem does the RIGHT thing.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE OPTIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

(a) DECLARE THE SHAPE OF THE FUNCTIONS, THEN DERIVE. Populate `inputs`/`outputs` on one subsystem's capabilities, and generate the edge cases from the input boundaries and the failure modes from the output promises. THE ONLY ROUTE ON WHICH "EXHAUSTIVE" MEANS SOMETHING CHECKABLE rather than something claimed. EXPENSIVE, and it needs all three legs built first (a typed tool, an instruction, a detector), because 3-of-192 is what two missing legs look like. Worth doing on ONE subsystem as a trial before committing to ten.

(b) TEST AGAINST THE INTERFACES THAT ALREADY EXIST. 17 Interfaces, 13 carrying a spec — and a spec clause is a failure mode waiting to be written down: violate each clause in turn and assert the refusal. CHEAP AND AVAILABLE NOW. LIMIT, stated plainly: only 4 of the 10 subsystems publish an interface, and the other six present nothing because nothing consumes them. This covers 4 subsystems well and 6 not at all.

(c) START FROM THE THIN ROWS — documentation, human-channel, packaging. Intuitive and probably WRONG as stated, for the reason above: the thin rows are where the MODEL is thinnest, which is not the same as where the TESTING is thinnest. Do not do this without re-measuring.

Four nodes carry one argument between them and none of them says so on its own: allocation-waits-for-the-last-responsible-moment (accepted), what-watches-for-the-moment-to-arrive, the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph, and is-allocation-running-ahead-of-the-seams. Ideas jotted over months with no edges between them do not accrete into anything; they pile.

  (a) THE STATUS QUO — the agent draws edges when it thinks to. Measured rate: 12 edges across 145 ideas, and a third of those in the hour after being asked. This is the option that produced the number.
  (b) THE BRAINSTORM SKILL REQUIRES NAMING A NEIGHBOUR. THE ANSWER TO THE DIRECT QUESTION: NO — ZERO OF TEN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

FOUR of the ten subsystems declare a provided interface at all. Of those four:

  sys:store         -> ifc:graph-export   spec = the same kind of correction note
  sys:human-channel -> ifc:reasoning-channel   NO SPEC
  sys:time-history  -> ifc:temporal-api        NO SPEC

⭐⭐ THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN LAZY
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

    designation   count   with a substantive spec
    required        9            9  of 9
    published       4            2  of 4   (the other two are correction notes)
    internal        4            0  of 4

REFLOW2 HAS WRITTEN CAREFUL CONTRACTS FOR EVERYTHING IT DEPENDS ON AND ALMOST NONE FOR WHAT IT OFFERS. That is not an oversight anyone made; it is what happens by default. You specify what you CONSUME because you must know what to expect from someone else. You leave what you PROVIDE unspecified because you are on both sides of it and nothing ever forces the question. `internal` — module to module, exactly where a swap would happen — is 0 of 4.

⭐ AND THIS IS PRECISELY WHAT BLOCKS BOTH THINGS HE NAMED. Substitution matches what a module OFFERS. A mock stands in for what a module offers its callers. Both need the PROVIDED side specified, and the provided side is the side nobody wrote.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐ ONE MISSING THING, NOW TRACEABLY THREE RETURNS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  1. SUBSTITUTABILITY / MOSA        — swap a module that meets the contract (2026-08-20)
  2. DERIVABLE FAILURE-MODE TESTING — edge cases from input boundaries, failure modes from output promises (2026-08-20)
  3. MOCKABLE TEST DOUBLES          — NEW TODAY, and the cheapest of the three to demonstrate

All three are blocked by the same gap, and the gap already has a number: 192 capabilities, 3 declaring inputs, 3 declaring outputs, 0 declaring a signature. `set_capability_signature` EXISTS and is verified — it was built precisely because the fields were unwritable at 0 of 170. It is now used on 3 of 192. **The TOOL leg is built. The INSTRUCTION and the DETECTOR are not.**

📌 MOCKING IS THE SHARPEST ARGUMENT OF THE THREE and it is worth saying why. Substitutability is a someday benefit — nobody is swapping the store this quarter. Derivable tests are a maybe: it is still unmeasured whether declared inputs produce cases nobody had thought of. **A mock pays immediately and locally**: a test that stands `sys:store` up against a fake instead of a real RocksDB is faster, and it is the only way to test the failure modes of a dependency you cannot make fail on demand. It is also the return with the shortest path to proving the contract is REAL — a contract you can mock is one you have actually specified, and a mock that diverges from the real module is a contract violation you can detect.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 A REAL TENSION, RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Earlier reasoning held that six subsystems present nothing BECAUSE NOTHING CONSUMES THEM, and that declaring interfaces for symmetry would FABRICATE CONTRACTS — asserting an agreement no two parties ever made. That argument is good and it is still good.

His MOSA argument cuts the other way: a contract is what makes substitution possible, so it is needed whether or not anything consumes it TODAY. An interface nobody consumes is not a fiction if the point of writing it is that someone else could implement it.

**BOTH ARE RIGHT ABOUT DIFFERENT THINGS.** The fabrication risk is real for a CONSUMES edge — that asserts a relationship. It is much weaker for a PROVIDES spec, which asserts only "this is what I offer", a statement the module can make alone and be held to. That distinction is not currently drawn anywhere, and drawing it may dissolve the tension entirely.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE OPTIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

(a) SPECIFY ONE SUBSYSTEM'S PROVIDED CONTRACT AND MOCK IT. `sys:store` is the candidate: 2 components, it already provides `ifc:graph-export`, and it is the dependency most worth faking in a test (real RocksDB is the slowest thing in the suite). Write the spec, build a mock against it, and see whether the mock catches anything. SMALLEST THING THAT PROVES ALL THREE RETURNS AT ONCE, because a contract you can mock is one you have really written.

(b) THE THREE LEGS FOR CAPABILITY SIGNATURES. Instruction plus detector for `inputs`/`outputs`, since the tool exists. Cheap, and it moves 3-of-192 rather than answering a question. It is the ENABLER for (a) at scale but proves nothing on its own — and building the legs before knowing the vocabulary earns its keep is how 189 empty fields happen twice.

(c) DECLARE THE MISSING PROVIDED INTERFACES for the six silent subsystems. Directly answers his question. RISKS exactly the fabrication the earlier reasoning warns of, unless the provides-versus-consumes distinction above is settled first.

(d) MEASURE WHETHER A CONTRACT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT ANYTHING. Take the last N real defects and ask how many a specified provided interface would have prevented or caught. Answers "is this worth it" before any of the above, and it is the option that could kill the whole line of work honestly.

NOT KNOWN: whether reflow2's own architecture even permits module substitution. Nearly every function is an `impl DesignGraph` method on one shared struct — which is also why attributing a test to a module mechanically was so hard today. A design where everything hangs off one god-struct may be UNSWAPPABLE regardless of what contracts get written, and that is measurable before committing to any option here.","name":"OPEN — zero of ten subsystems publish a contract. Every brainstorm before that produced a node and no edges — including three captured the previous day by the same agent following the same skill, which instructs recording the idea and says nothing about connecting it to its neighbours.

=== WHY IT MATTERS, IN HIS OWN CASE ===

Four nodes carry one argument between them and none of them says so on its own: allocation-waits-for-the-last-responsible-moment (accepted), what-watches-for-the-moment-to-arrive, the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph, and is-allocation-running-ahead-of-the-seams. Read singly, each is a reasonable question. Read together they are one position about WHEN and ON WHAT BASIS a boundary gets drawn. A reader meeting any one of them alone gets an incomplete picture — which is exactly what he said.

AND HIS BROTHER'S CASE IS THE SAME SHAPE AT A DIFFERENT TIMESCALE: `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` (a body of intent accreted over years, contradicting itself and never built, can still become a design) presumes the accretion can later be READ AS A WHOLE. Ideas jotted over months with no edges between them do not accrete into anything; they pile.

=== OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ===

  (a) THE STATUS QUO — the agent draws edges when it thinks to. Measured rate: 12 edges across 145 ideas, and a third of those in the hour after being asked. This is the option that produced the number.
  (b) THE BRAINSTORM SKILL REQUIRES NAMING A NEIGHBOUR. Cheap, needs no schema, and testable — the skill already makes the agent search before writing, so the near-matches are IN HAND at the moment of capture and are currently used only to avoid duplicates, then discarded. ⚠️ Risk: an edge drawn to satisfy an instruction is an asserted relationship nobody meant, which `req:a-repair-suggestion-never-proposes-fabrication` forbids for exactly this reason.
  (c) A DETECTOR FOR THE ABSENCE — 'this idea shares vocabulary with N others and links to none'. It is the absence-shaped detector reflow2 structurally lacks (see fact:the-design-outward-blind-spot-appeared-in-three-independent-places), so building it would be the first of its kind rather than one more of many.
  (d) COMPUTE ADJACENCY, DO NOT STORE IT. `search_design` already ranks by BM25 over every node's text, so 'ideas near this one' is answerable TODAY as a READ without asserting any edge. Respects the no-fabrication rule completely: it SHOWS adjacency rather than CLAIMING a relationship. ⚠️ And its limit is the whole point — a similarity score cannot carry WHY two ideas are related, and the why is the content. The four edges drawn today each carry a note like 'option (b) here would be this one's stated trigger'; no ranking function produces that sentence.
  (e) DO NOTHING. Honest, and its cost is the measurement above.

=== COUNTER-ARGUMENT, RECORDED BESIDE RATHER THAN AGAINST ===

An idea graph could be worse than an idea list. Edges between musings are cheap to draw and expensive to trust: two ideas mentioning 'allocation' are not thereby related, and a densely-linked pile of half-formed thoughts reads as a structure when it is a word cloud. This project has twice retired metric-driven verdicts that fired on correct architecture; a similarity-driven idea graph is the same hazard one level up. WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, THE EDGE THAT EARNS ITS KEEP CARRIES A REASON — which is an argument for (b) or (d) over (c), and against any automatic drawing.

DISTINCT FROM `dec:exploratory-staging`, which asks whether a half-formed idea has a HOME (a kind, a type, a status) and lists what such a kind would buy: retirement candidates and at-a-glance readability. Neither is linking. That node is about what an idea IS; this one is about what an idea is CONNECTED TO.

So the ask is not for the rule. IT IS FOR THE TRIGGER. And the trigger is the thing this project has now confirmed three times is missing: `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` (ACCEPTED) says skill use "must be triggered by the SITUATION, not remembered — and THE USER MUST NEVER BE THE TRIGGER", measured on this repo 2026-07-31, and confirmed from the field on 2026-08-11 by the second user, who named exactly the two skills he types and neither of the two that would have fired on situations he was already in.

⭐⭐ AND THE MECHANISM IS ALREADY A REQUIREMENT, PROPOSED AND UNBUILT: `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` — "a discipline that applies mid-task is delivered at the TOOL that triggers it, not from a catalogue read once at handshake." That is precisely what he is asking for, one layer more general. This idea may not need a requirement of its own at all; it may be the first concrete instance of one that already exists and has never been accepted.

📌 THIS NODE IS ITSELF THE NINTH COLLISION recorded in fact:the-owner-uses-reflow2-as-a-funnel-for-random-order-input, and it was found BY DOING THE THING HE ASKED FOR: searching before adding. Had the search not run, this would have become a near-duplicate of a proposed requirement and a fifth restatement of an instruction already in five skills — which is the exact failure he is trying to prevent, reproduced in the act of trying to prevent it.

WHAT EXISTS ON THE DETECTION SIDE, so this is not built twice. `possible_duplicate` fires on shared allocation sets with Jaccard ≥ 0.8 and asks rather than merges (`dec:ask-not-repair`); HEAL merges only on a human-asserted DUPLICATES edge. Both are AFTER-THE-FACT and STRUCTURAL — they catch two nodes that ended up allocated the same way. Neither can see "the same idea in different words, newly written, allocated to nothing yet", which is the case he is describing. Prevention and detection are different problems here.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) Put it on the TOOL, not the skill: `add_requirement` / `add_capability` / `add_decision` return near-matches alongside the write, or refuse-and-name when a match is close enough. Reaches every session including ones that load no skill. Cost — a write tool that sometimes refuses is a new failure mode on the hottest path, and BM25 near-matches are not reliable enough to refuse on (`dec:` on BM25 scores not being comparable across queries).
(b) SEARCH ON THE WAY IN, NEVER REFUSE: the write succeeds and the response carries "3 existing nodes look close: ...". No new failure mode, no judgement, and it puts the finding where the agent is already looking. Smallest honest version.
(c) A pre-write hook or a served instruction at handshake. Cheapest to state and it is what already exists — five skills say it — so this is the option that has already been tried and is the reason he is asking.
(d) Nothing new: ACCEPT `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` and build it, since this is an instance of it rather than a separate need.

⚠️ THE TRAP: a near-match list that is usually wrong trains the agent to ignore it, which is worse than silence — the same failure `unexpected_coupling` was retired for, and the one `v0.2.0-what-we-dont-know.md` names as the sharpest thing to watch ("a gap list you skim is worse than no gap list"). Whatever surfaces matches must be precise enough to be read every time, and BM25 alone has already been shown here to score the same topic 4.48 and 35.75 across two queries.

⚠️ SECOND TRAP, AND IT CUTS AGAINST THE WHOLE IDEA: a near-duplicate is sometimes CORRECT. `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` exists precisely because a body of intent that contradicts itself is still a design. Suppressing a second statement of the same idea can erase that the user said it twice, in different words, at different times — which is signal about what they keep coming back to, and is what `dec:idea-what-gets-searched-repeatedly-is-becoming-important` asks about from the other direction.

⭐ THIS SECTION WAS ADDED BY THE GUARD ITSELF. An agent tried to create a NEW node about exactly this and `add_decision` REFUSED it, naming this node and both routes on. The write half works, in the field, against its own author. That is the strongest evidence this node will ever get, and it arrived by accident.

ANTHONY NAMED THE BEHAVIOUR AS SOMETHING HE VALUES, 2026-08-12: "every time I ask a question or propose an idea, you do a search/research what has already happened. then we either sharpen the previous or add new content or all sorts of things that continually improves the design - i think this is awesome!"

⭐ MEASURED IN ONE SESSION — six saves, each with what it prevented:
  - "a requirement that anything developed has something that uses it" -> already captured 2026-08-09 IN HIS OWN WORDS. A duplicate node.
  - "accept the 26 delivered requirements" -> ELEVEN were satisfied only by `planned`/`in_progress` capabilities. Asserting delivery that had not happened, eleven times.
  - "should we have a purge skill" -> `dec:proposed-requirements-pruned` had already settled DROPPED-NOT-DELETED. Re-deciding a settled question destructively.
  - "a tool that does the import step" -> `import_graph` already took a `path`. Building a tool that existed.
  - "treat the union of 2+ graphs as one graph" -> `dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs`, his own federation model from six days earlier. Re-deriving his own thinking.
  - "treat one side as immutable" -> `mirror_surface`, BUILT and stamping `mirror_of` / `mirror_content_hash` / `mirrored_at`. Specifying something already shipped.
  Plus a doc review that caught a section marked OUTSTANDING three days after the thing shipped.

🛑 AND THE ASYMMETRY THAT MATTERS: **ALL SIX HAPPENED ON THE READ PATH, WHERE NOTHING ENFORCES ANYTHING.** The refusal fires on add_requirement / add_capability / add_component / add_decision / add_constraint. It cannot fire when a user asks a question and an agent answers in prose. Those six happened because the agent chose to look.

That is `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`'s failure with the trigger moved one step — not the user reminding the agent, but the agent remembering — and it degrades silently in a long session precisely when the graph is large enough to make searching most valuable.

⭐⭐ THE OBSERVATION THAT CHANGES THE VALUE CALCULATION: the write guard catches a near-duplicate NODE. It cannot catch a near-duplicate DECISION TO BUILD. **Four of the six saves prevented WORK, not nodes** — and work is the more expensive thing. So the unguarded half is plausibly worth more than the guarded half, which inverts the obvious reading that the write path is where the value is.

{"decision":"PROPOSED, NOT TAKEN — this changes what every existing scoped caller sees, so it waits on the owner's word.

THREE PARTS, and they can be answered separately:

(1) `DEFAULT_SCOPE_DEPTH` becomes 2. At 2 the same sweep returns 2-27 (median 4) over regions of 267-601. See `fact:defect-a-scoped-detector-at-its-default-depth-returns-two-thirds-of-the-design`.

(2) The docstring that justifies 3 is corrected whatever is decided about the number. It argues the third hop is needed to reach 'a contained child component's capabilities' — but `scope_region` puts the whole containment closure into the seed set BEFORE taking the radius, so those capabilities are one hop from an owned node, not three. The reason given for the default is not a reason the code needs.

(3) `detect_gaps`' description stops claiming its region is 'the same computation claim_region uses ... so "my area" means one thing everywhere'. Also rejected: making `design_regions` quietly use a different depth from the scoped detectors, which would have hidden the defect behind a second opinion instead of naming it.

{"decision":"🛑 **ANTHONY, 2026-08-14, CHALLENGING THE PREMISE: "we already have an obsolete with discontinued or something like that — are we playing semantics with cancelled?" CHECKED AGAINST THE CODE AND THE GRAPH RATHER THAN ARGUED. HE IS RIGHT FOR THE ABANDONED CASE, AND THE ANSWER WAS ALREADY DECIDED THREE DAYS EARLIER.**

`dec:idea-discontinued-is-a-first-class-state` was **DECIDED on his word 2026-08-11**: a Decision `OBSOLETES` what it withdrew, the decision itself being the source. No enum value, no edge type, no schema stamp move, no upgrade doc.

**IT IS NOT THEORETICAL — IT IS LIVE IN THIS GRAPH.** `dec:the-content-store-is-discontinued` (accepted) obsoletes:
```
cap:content-store       stored status: realized   -> discontinued: true
cap:content-manifest    stored status: realized   -> discontinued: true
cap:session-artifacts   stored status: verified   -> discontinued: true
```
And `is_discontinued` has FOUR readers, which is four more than either retirement edge ever had: `unmotivated_capability`, `unrealized_capability` and `unverified_capability` fall silent, and delivery arithmetic stops counting a discontinued capability as a satisfier (`DeliveryCoverage.satisfied_only_by_discontinued`).

⇒ **ADDING `cancelled` TO `Capability.status` WOULD BE A SECOND WAY TO SAY WHAT THE GRAPH ALREADY COMPUTES — and worse than redundant, because a STORED status can disagree with the COMPUTED one.** The stored status deliberately keeps saying what was BUILT; that is why `get_node` carries `discontinued` separately and warns to read it.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT IS GENUINELY NOT COVERED, AND IT IS MUCH NARROWER THAN ALEX'S FRAMING ═══

The 2026-08-11 decision names its own residual: it *"covers the ABANDONED case; it says nothing about a WISH NOBODY EVER AGREED TO, which has no decision behind it to be the source of an OBSOLETES edge."* **A capability that was only ever an idea has no decision to hang the edge from.** That half belongs to `dec:exploratory-staging`, not to a status enum.

═══ ⭐ SO WHAT ACTUALLY BIT ALEX IS DISCOVERABILITY, NOT A MISSING STATE ═══

His agents typed "DROPPED" into description prose while the mechanism existed and worked. The plausible reason: an agent reads `Capability.status`, sees four values, and **nothing at that point hints that abandonment lives on an edge instead.** `retire-from-design` is the skill that covers it, and measured 2026-08-14 it is among the least-reached-for of the twenty (`fact:skill-use-measured-two-channels-2026-08-14`).

⇒ **THE OPEN QUESTION IS THEREFORE RESHAPED, NOT ANSWERED, AND STAYS ANTHONY'S:** not "does Capability need a cancelled state" (no — measured above) but **"what makes an agent holding an abandoned capability find OBSOLETES instead of typing DROPPED into prose?"** Candidates, none chosen: a hint on `set_capability_status`, a detector that notices abandonment words in description text, or the command coverage now accepted under `dec:idea-does-every-served-skill-get-a-command` putting `retire-from-design` one keystroke away.

{"description":"BUILT 2026-08-20 as tools/wall_check.py, against req:modularity-computed. A decomposition is declared once, early, when it is cheapest to get wrong, and every later answer about severability and blast radius is computed through it. Nothing checked it.

What it computes: the real Rust import graph (comments and string literals stripped), lifted to the declared subsystems through each Component's CONTAINS placement. It reports (1) module-level cycles, (2) SUBSYSTEM-level cycles - the walls that cannot be severed because traffic crosses them both ways, (3) Components whose design says nothing depends on them while their same-named module is coupled in the source, and (4) Components placed in no subsystem at all.

Why it reads the SOURCE and not the graph: every detector reflow2 ships checks the consistency of edges that EXIST. A missing coupling edge is a defect of ABSENCE, and the design cannot notice its own silence - measured here as a cycle detector correctly reporting zero over a subsystem layer that holds zero edges.

{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony asked to think through the mechanics of using git to capture epoch and increment snapshots; these are the options and their costs, not a settlement.

THE TENSION THAT ORGANISES EVERYTHING: git can only store the past. A commit is something that happened. A planned epoch is a claim about a future that has not happened, so there is nothing for git to hold unless someone AUTHORS a speculative design and commits it.

(a) EPOCH BRANCHES — Anthony's original idea, 2026-07-28: "epoch branches: project_x:epoch_1 captures what we expect the graph to look like at epoch_1." A branch is a real place to work: you can draft a future design there, run the detectors on it, and diff it against main with machinery that already exists.
    Costs, recorded beside it rather than against it: a branch is a MOVING POINTER and a plan is a DATED CLAIM — when the plan changes the branch moves, and nothing records that it moved, which is exactly what `req:plans-move-honestly` needs. A speculative full export also restates the entire design to express a delta about a handful of requirements, so it is expensive to author and stale on the next merge to main. And N repos times M epochs is N times M branches, each drifting independently.

(b) PLANS LIVE ONLY IN THE GRAPH. A planned epoch is a node plus scheduled edges — no git object at all, because there is no past to point at. "What does the design look like at epoch 3" becomes a COMPUTED view (today's design plus what is scheduled to be satisfied by then) rather than a stored artifact.
    Cost: you cannot open a future design in an editor or run a detector over it as a whole; you get a projection, not a document.

(c) BOTH, SCOPED DIFFERENTLY — the shape the costs seem to point at. Branches are a fine WORKSPACE for exploring a future architecture and a poor RECORD of a plan. The record lives in the graph as a dated, versioned claim; a branch is somewhere to prototype one when a person wants to see it whole.

WORTH KNOWING BEFORE DECIDING: the forward half of the CAPABILITY view already exists in the vocabulary. `Release.status` is `planned | built | deployed | retired`, so a planned increment is expressible today. The forward half of the TIME view does not: `DesignEpoch.epoch_type` is `baseline | revision | milestone | incident_response | release_cut` with no value meaning "this has not happened yet". That asymmetry is real and is the smallest concrete gap found while thinking this through.","name":"OPEN — does a planned epoch live in git, or only in the graph?","rationale":"Anthony's idea and Anthony's question; recorded so the reasoning survives whichever way it goes. The framing "two paired views of the same architecture" and the epoch-branch mechanism are both his (2026-07-28), as is the request to work out the git mechanics (2026-07-30).

Not argued down: option (a) is recorded with its virtue stated first, because a branch genuinely is the only place you can look at a future design as a whole, and that is not nothing.","status":"proposed"}

{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.

ANTHONY'S CLARIFICATION, 2026-07-30, and it corrects the framing this node was first written with: what he wants committed is NOT the realized product or a future codebase. It is a SLICE OF THE REFLOW2 GRAPH ITSELF — "this is the planned capabilities of epoch_1, epoch_2 … epoch_n" — so that he can open the repo and see "that is when I get capability X", or "capability Y is not expected until increment_13". His words: "it isn't the realized product/artifact of the project, but snapshot of the project at epoch or increment that I'm looking to capture in git." He is explicitly open to something other than git.

THE FIRST FRAMING HERE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED. This node originally organised everything around "git can only store the past, and a plan is not a past". That is too glib. A plan document is a PRESENT artifact describing a future, and committing one is ordinary — git stores plans perfectly well. The real objection was never to committing plans; it was only ever to using BRANCHES as the record, and that narrower objection stands.

(a) BRANCH PER EPOCH — `epoch_1`, `epoch_2`, each holding a projected design. Matches the mental model directly: check out `epoch_n`, look.
    Costs: checking out a branch normally makes the whole REPO reflect that state, and here there is no future code to reflect, so the branch buys nothing the file would not. A full export is 1.6 MB today, so N epochs is N × 1.6 MB of near-identical JSON, rewritten on every replan. Branches also invite merge semantics that do not apply — nobody merges epoch_2 into main. And the plan's MOVEMENT stays invisible: a branch pointer moves silently, which is exactly what `req:plans-move-honestly` needs to see.

(b) A FILE PER EPOCH ON MAIN — `docs/design/epochs/epoch_3.{md,json}`. Browsing is easier than a checkout, there is one history rather than N, and every replan is an ordinary commit to that file.
    THE PROPERTY THIS BUYS FOR FREE: `git log -p docs/design/epochs/epoch_3.md` IS the plan's revision history. A large part of `req:plans-move-honestly` — "when a planned epoch's content moves, the plan's own change is a dated event on the record" — would be satisfied by git doing what git is good at, rather than by new machinery in reflow2.

(c) RENDER IT, DO NOT AUTHOR IT — and this is what (b) should probably be generated BY. An epoch slice is a VIEWPOINT. `tools/render_views.py` already renders viewpoints as pure projections of the graph, already confesses anything a view needs that the graph cannot supply, and ALREADY RENDERS THE EPOCH CHAIN BACKWARD ("Axis Z as a viewpoint: the epoch chain, and what happened at each"). The forward direction is the same renderer reading scheduled edges instead of recorded ones. Under this option the graph holds the schedule as single source of truth, the renderer emits one small file per epoch, and git holds their history.
    Cost: a generated file can go stale against the graph — which is a drift check reflow2 already knows how to do, and the same one `dataflow.html` staleness already gets in another repo.

WHAT A SLICE ACTUALLY CONTAINS, since "slice" is the word he used and it is much smaller than an export: the epoch and its date, capabilities expected by then, requirements expected satisfied, KPPs required by then, the version combination pinned once it arrives, and the delta against the previous epoch. Kilobytes, not megabytes.

THE OPEN QUESTION IS NARROWER THAN IT WAS: not "git or not git", but WHICH JOB GIT DOES. Git looks right for the HISTORY of the plan document and for pinning arrived epochs; the graph looks right for the schedule itself. The failure mode to avoid is making git the source of truth for the schedule, because then two places disagree about when capability X arrives and neither is wrong.","name":"OPEN — how per-epoch slices of the design become browsable: branches, files, or a rendered viewpoint","rationale":"Anthony's idea, his clarification, and his invitation to suggest something better; recorded so the reasoning survives whichever way it goes.

Kept rather than tidied away: the original framing of this node ("git can only store the past") was mine and was misleading, and the correction is recorded rather than silently overwritten because the prior text is what a reader would otherwise have found and believed. The snapshot at `epoch:wire-planning-cluster` holds the earlier wording.

Not argued down: option (a) is his own original mechanism and is recorded with the mental model it serves stated first. Its costs are listed beside it, not in place of it.","status":"proposed"}

{"description":"`Artifact.audience` records `consumer` or `internal`, set through `set_artifact_intent` alongside granularity and volatility. The `internal_only_delivery` finding then names a Requirement whose every DECLARED delivering artifact is internal, with none declared consumer. Per-requirement rather than aggregate, because accepting \"this need is served by our own tooling on purpose\" is a claim about one need. Never inferred from a path: a directory rule would encode one project's layout, which is the failure the requirement exists to prevent. An undeclared artifact is evidence of neither side and its count goes in the evidence. KNOWN INCOMPLETE: a design that has declared no audience anywhere is silent in every surfaced report, because vocabulary_coverage names unused node and edge TYPES but never unused PROPERTIES.","name":"A deliverable declares who it is for, and a need nothing consumer-facing delivers is reported","provenance":"authored","status":"realized"}

{"lineage":"original","name":"A project can tell work that serves its own machinery apart from work that reaches its consumers, so "did we close a user-facing need with an internal fix?" is answerable from the graph","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"A deliverable must be able to record WHO IT IS FOR — a consumer of the product, or the project's own machinery — and the design must then be able to answer, without asking a person: is there a need here that nothing consumer-facing delivers?

DELIBERATELY DISTINCT FROM `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself` and from `rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party`, and the split is the point. Those RULES are how the people building reflow2 work; they bind this project and can never bind anyone else's. This REQUIREMENT is the product carrying the same philosophy, so every project using reflow2 inherits the question. That is the identical shape as `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause`, which exists because Anthony asked on 2026-08-17 for his building philosophy to be "built into the design of reflow2" rather than merely stated at its developers. A rule states it; a requirement makes it something reflow2 DOES.

ALSO DISTINCT FROM `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause`, which was surfaced as near: that one asks whether a repair reached the CAUSE or worked around it. This one asks who the work was FOR. A root-cause fix can still land entirely in internal machinery, and a workaround can ship straight to a consumer; the two axes are independent and both are currently unrecorded.

⭐ THE DISTINCTION IS UNIVERSAL, NOT REFLOW2'S. Every project that ships anything has internal machinery and a delivered product, and confuses them under pressure: a team's own scripts against what the beamline actually does, CI configuration against the library, a build tool against the API. The failure it enables is the same everywhere and it LOOKS LIKE COMPLETION — find a hole, patch it in the internal half, mark the need met, and leave every consumer with the hole. The repo goes green and nothing is true of anybody else.

⚠️ NEVER INFERRED FROM A PATH. A first sketch of this proposed classifying deliverables by directory — `.github/` internal, `crates/` shipped — which encodes ONE project's layout and is exactly the failure it exists to prevent. The audience is DECLARED by the project or it is unknown, and unknown is a true answer.

⚠️ AND NEVER A JUDGEMENT. Internal work is legitimate and necessary; a release procedure, a coordination board and an export discipline are real work that reaches no consumer. The requirement is that the difference be VISIBLE, never that internal work be discouraged (`dec:report-dont-judge`).

🛑 THE DETECTOR MUST SAY WHEN IT HAD NOTHING TO RUN ON. If no deliverable in a project has declared an audience, the reading is "I cannot judge this", NOT zero findings. A detector reporting zero because its population was empty reads exactly like one that ran clean — `loop_status` already refuses an unknown contributor_id for this reason, and this is the same trap one level over.

HONEST LIMIT, the same class as `provenance` and the drift dispositions: this records what the author SAYS a deliverable is for. It cannot detect an internal tool declared consumer-facing. Worth having because the alternative is no signal at all; worth never overselling.","status":"proposed"}

properties.statement:
MEASURED ON REFLOW2'S OWN GRAPH, 2026-08-17, while deciding how far to widen `disconnected_community`. Recorded because the NUMBER survives and the reasoning that stopped it becoming 176 defects would not.

The design network holds 1133 of 2413 nodes and breaks into 183 components:
  1 main body        940 nodes
  6 islands          5, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2 nodes   -> REPORTED (minus containment-attached ones)
  176 SINGLETONS                              -> REPORTED BY NOBODY

And 167 of those 176 HAVE EDGES IN THE FULL GRAPH. They fall through both detectors by construction: `orphan_node`'s degree-zero rule needs zero edges and they have some, while `disconnected_community` filters to clusters of >=2 and a singleton is never a cluster. Mostly Decisions whose only edge is AUTHORED_BY, plus Actors reachable only by INTERACTS_WITH and Contributors only by authorship — none of which are traceability edges.

⛔ NOT TURNED INTO FINDINGS, AND THE REASON IS THE POINT. A Decision carrying only AUTHORED_BY is a recorded thought that governs nothing YET, which `heal.rs`'s own `repair_is_a_judgement` text already calls "a parked thought that correctly governs nothing yet", and which `req:a-deliberate-state-is-not-a-defect` exists to protect. Reporting 176 of them would have raised the defect count roughly sixfold in one release, and would have been the exact failure the epoch this work belongs to is named for. The temptation was real: the sweep was already being widened that day and these were sitting in the same measurement.

SO IT IS A MEASUREMENT AND AN OPEN QUESTION, not a defect list. What it says is that "attached to the design" has THREE states, and reflow2 currently models two: joined to the thread, joined to nothing, and joined only by edges that are not traceability. The third is populous, ordinary, and invisible.

RELATED AND UNANSWERED: `req:a-cluster-can-be-declared-deliberately-separate` asks for a way to declare separation deliberate so islands can be reported as undeclared rather than as a permanent warning. That answers the same shape one size up — a marker for PARKED would let the 176 be counted and named without being called defects. Whether the singleton count belongs in the `disconnected_community` message (where it now appears as scope) or as its own reported number is not settled.

⭐ TWO PULL REQUESTS EXPORTED AGAINST THE SAME MAIN, AND MERGING THE FIRST SILENTLY BROKE THE SECOND'S LINEAGE WHILE GITHUB REPORTED IT `MERGEABLE / CLEAN` THROUGHOUT.

Measured 2026-08-26 on PRs #345 and #346. Both exported against the same committed export, `c7138a4f`. Merging #345 moved main's export to `fd93ff0b`, leaving #346's `prev_content_hash` pointing at a hash no commit on main held any more.

    before merging #345    main export = c7138a4f    #346 prev = c7138a4f    chain intact
    after  merging #345    main export = fd93ff0b    #346 prev = c7138a4f    CHAIN BROKEN
    git's opinion, both times: MERGEABLE / CLEAN

🛑 **GIT CANNOT SEE THIS AND NEVER WILL.** The two exports have no textual conflict — they are complete documents that merge cleanly — so every signal a forge offers stays green. The lineage chain lives INSIDE the file as a content hash, and only `reflow2_check`'s LINEAGE finding looks at it. Same class as `req:stale-seat-knows`: *a stale export is a COMPLETE document, so it merges cleanly and the missing work simply vanishes.*

⚠️ **THE CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY PROJECT RUNNING TWO PRs AT ONCE**, which is the general form and the reason this is worth keeping: `dec:export-once-per-pr` makes each branch export once, chained from main. **Two branches open simultaneously both chain from the same main, and whichever merges second is broken by the first.** Nothing warns at open time; the break appears only when the second branch's gate runs after the first merges. On a team this is the common case rather than the exception.

⭐⭐ **AND A CORRECTION WORTH MORE THAN THE FINDING: THE MERGE DRIVER REPAIRED THE LINEAGE, WHICH THE STANDING NOTE SAYS IT CANNOT.** The release-cut lore held that *"the three-way merge driver merges CONTENT correctly and cannot repair LINEAGE"* — recorded after a rebase needed a re-export. Rebasing #346 onto the new main on 2026-08-26 produced:

    reflow2: merged 3229 node(s) and 14029 edge(s) — 53 divergence(s) resolved automatically, no conflicts
    prev_content_hash after rebase: fd93ff0b   (== main's content_hash — REPAIRED)

The restore-from-main-and-re-export was still performed, because trusting an unverified repair on the one field the gate checks would be exactly the false-green habit this session hit five times. **But the driver did the right thing unprompted, and the note claiming otherwise is now wrong.** Whether it repairs lineage in every case or only when the branch's export is a superset is NOT established — one observation, one shape.

📌 VERIFIED AFTER THE REPAIR, three ways rather than assumed: `prev_content_hash` equalled main's `content_hash`; #345's `ver:graph-algorithms-unit-suite` survived the merge; exactly one commit on the branch touched the export.

properties.statement:
FOUND 2026-08-20 by running the loop honestly rather than by looking for it: epoch:the-declared-walls-hold was set arrived with BOTH its capabilities delivered, and arrival_delta reported BOTH as `outstanding`.

=== THE MECHANISM, read from the source and not inferred ===

crates/reflow2-core/src/temporal.rs, item_is_delivered:

    node::CAPABILITY => Ok(self.capability_is_realized(item_id)?
                        && self.capability_has_evidence(item_id)?)

and capability_is_realized (detect.rs) is: an Artifact REALIZES the capability, OR an Artifact realizes a Component the capability is ALLOCATED_TO.

So delivery requires A FILE ON DISK. `Capability.status` is never consulted. Verification evidence alone is not enough - measured directly: a capability at status `realized` WITH a passing system-level Verification attached still came back `outstanding`, because the AND requires both halves and the artifact half cannot be satisfied by a check.

=== WHY THIS IS NOT 'JUST SET THE STATUS' ===

The governing doctrine is right and should not be weakened: delivery is COMPUTED from the golden thread, never asserted, and there is deliberately no `achieved` modality, because a plan that records its own success is a plan lying about itself. The defect is not that delivery is computed. It is that the computation admits exactly ONE kind of evidence - an artifact - while reflow2 itself models several.

=== WHAT IT COSTS AN ARBITRARY USER'S PROJECT ===

A large share of real increment content produces NO NEW FILE:
  · a re-decomposition, or any boundary change
  · a retirement - something correctly leaving the design
  · a governance decision, an accepted rule, a settled question
  · a correction to a model that was wrong about the world

Every one of those sits `outstanding` forever. And `outstanding` is DEFINED as 'still pointed here, not delivered, and nobody has said which of deferred or discontinued it is - that is the question to put to the user'. So the tool asks the user a question about work that is finished, and keeps asking. A plan that cannot mark model work delivered will, increment after increment, accumulate a backlog of phantom incompletions - and the natural response is to stop scheduling model work, which is precisely the work systems engineering is FOR.

It bites hardest on exactly the modularization and black-box work reflow2 is meant to support, because almost all of that is model change.

=== A SECOND TENSION, IN THE SAME REPLY ===

arrival_delta also said: 'nothing is scheduled `required` ... so there is no obligation to miss and it is NOT ready to cut. An increment that promises nothing has not been scoped.' That is a fair criticism. But the plan-increments skill instructs the opposite - `required` is the scheduling face of a KPP, so 'ask, never assume' - and this plan used `expected` BECAUSE THE SKILL SAID TO. A user following reflow2's own guidance therefore builds an increment reflow2 then reports as unscoped and never ready to cut. Two pieces of correct guidance, in tension, with no way for the follower to satisfy both.

=== STATED HONESTLY: NOT ACTED ON ===

The epoch is being LEFT reporting `outstanding`. Editing the plan to match what happened is what the skill forbids, and the false reading is itself the evidence. This is recorded for Anthony's decision, not fixed.

THE 87 PRESERVED VERIFICATION TEXTS ARE NOW SPLIT: what the check IS stays in `description`, what a RUN FOUND moved to `findings`. 65 of the 87 gained findings; 22 did not, and that is the right answer for them — they are `planned` checks or single-statement ones with no run to report, so an empty `findings` there says 'nothing has run' rather than 'nobody sorted it'. || THE METHOD IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART AND IT IS THE SAME ONE THE RENAME USED: the halves were SLICED FROM THE STORED TEXT BY SEGMENT INDEX, never retyped. The text was cut into 472 sentence-level segments across the 87 nodes (median 5), the segmentation was proven lossless by re-joining it, and each segment was assigned to one side or the other. So the only thing authored was a list of integers. Corruption in transit was impossible BY CONSTRUCTION, and every split was asserted lossless before any write and re-verified afterwards on the live graph: no character lost or duplicated across the two halves, no name disturbed, findings present exactly where intended and absent everywhere else. ⇒ WHEN A BULK EDIT MUST PRESERVE TEXT, MAKE THE MODEL CHOOSE BOUNDARIES AND LET A SCRIPT MOVE THE BYTES. || THE CLASSIFICATION RULE, applied consistently rather than case by case: FINDINGS are reported outcomes of runs that happened — `MUTATION-CHECKED N WAYS`, `WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIX: n failed`, `MEASURED ON THE REAL DESIGN`, `PROVEN ON THE REAL SURFACE`, `VERIFIED END-TO-END`, `FOUND BY RUNNING IT`, field observations with numbers. DESCRIPTION is what the check is, its cases, its counterweights, why it exists, and — deliberately — its stated limits, because `NOT COVERED:` is a fact about the check's SCOPE and not about any run. || SEGMENT 0 WAS NEVER MOVED. It carries the claim, and on most of these it also carries `— N cases, all passing DATE`, which is a finding welded to a description in one sentence. Splitting mid-sentence would have meant retyping, which would have given up the only property making an 87-node edit safe. The date is on `last_run_at` anyway. ⇒ A MIXED SENTENCE STAYS WHERE ITS FIRST HALF BELONGS; the safety of the method outranks a tidier field. || SOURCE: 2026-08-23, reflow2 0.38.0, on top of `fact:a-name-is-not-a-report` (#308) which put the text into `description` in the first place.

properties.name: VERIFIES cannot target an Interface, so no contract in any reflow2 design can carry a check — and interfaces are the nodes MOSA turns on
properties.statement:
FOUND 2026-08-21 while fixing the finding "nothing verifies ifc:core-api". The fix was refused by the edge validator:

  Invalid edge: VERIFIES cannot connect Verification to Interface

The schema enumerates VERIFIES targets as **Capability, Requirement, Artifact, Component, DesignRule, Constraint**. Interface is absent.

SO REFLOW2 CAN ATTACH EVIDENCE TO A RULE, A BUDGET, A PART, A FILE, A CAPABILITY AND A REQUIREMENT — AND NOT TO A CONTRACT. Every Interface in every design using reflow2 is unverifiable by construction. reflow2's own 17 interfaces have zero incoming VERIFIES edges, and that reads as "nobody wrote one" when the truth is "nobody could".

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A MISSING EDGE TYPE USUALLY WOULD. A contract is the node a modular open-systems approach turns on — `set_interface_designation`'s own description calls `published` "the distinction a systems-engineering ICD publishes and that MOSA calls a modular system interface". The question "does this boundary actually hold?" is the most natural thing anyone would want to check about a published contract, and it is the one question this vocabulary cannot express. `ifc:mcp-tools` is specified 9 of 9 fields, is the surface every user's agent calls, and cannot carry a single piece of evidence that it behaves as specified.

⭐ IT MAY BE THE THIRD INSTANCE OF A PATTERN THIS EDGE HAS ALREADY RECORDED ABOUT ITSELF. `schema/verify.yaml` carries a long comment on VERIFIES under-enumerating its targets twice: the extraction hint named three types while four were true, and later the `to` list itself was derived from a census that found five types by edge count and MISSED TWO carrying one edge each — which made an existing export unimportable by the binary that wrote it for four days while every gate read green. Its own words: "a schema tightening that silently orphans existing data is a breaking change wearing a validation error's clothes." Interface may simply be the next unlisted-but-wanted target, never censused because no edge existed to count — an absence cannot appear in a survey of what is present.

WHAT THIS FACT DOES NOT SETTLE: whether Interface SHOULD be added. That is a schema change and Anthony's call. Two things argue for care rather than speed — the same comment warns that narrowing this list broke a real design, so widening it deserves the same scrutiny in reverse; and it is worth asking first what a check on a contract would MEAN, since a conformance test against a specified boundary is a different kind of evidence from a unit test on a capability.

NOTE ON THE STAMP: the schema stamp carries node and edge TYPE NAMES, not their target lists, so adding Interface to this `to` list would not move it and would owe no upgrade note.

A DANGLING `node_ref` PROPERTY IS REPORTED ONLY WHEN THE NODE CARRYING IT IS ALSO EDGELESS, SO A WELL-CONNECTED NODE POINTING AT NOTHING IS SILENT. Measured 2026-08-29 on reflow2's own graph, on the nine dangling `TemporalFact.subject_id` references that #366 identified and deliberately left for 'detection over the graph as it stands'.

THE MECHANISM IS IN THE FINDING'S OWN WORDS, so this is textual rather than inferred. `orphan_node` reports: 'points at nothing that exists — its subject/target id resolves to no node AND IT CARRIES NO EDGE EITHER, so the record is about something the design no longer has.' The conjunction is the defect. Dangling-reference detection is not a rule; it is a side effect of the orphan rule, and it inherits that rule's precondition.

THE MEASUREMENT, and the correlation is exact:

    edges on the fact   dangling target          reported by detect_defects?
    2                   cap:thin-install         NO
    1                   prj:reflow2              NO
    0  (x7)             the other seven          YES, all seven

So 7 of 9 surfaced and 2 did not — 22% invisible — and the two invisible ones are exactly the two that were attached to something. `detect_defects` returned 62 findings in that same run and neither was among them.

⚠️ WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A PLAIN ABSENCE: the rule LOOKS like it covers dangling references, and on this graph it covered 78% of them. A reader checking whether the class is detected finds seven examples of it being detected. The failure is invisible in exactly the way a partial detector always is — it produces evidence of working.

⭐ AND THE BIAS RUNS THE WRONG WAY. An edgeless node is by construction the LEAST consequential one to have a bad pointer, because nothing else reaches it. A node with edges is embedded in the design, so its pointer is read by more paths — and that is precisely the one this misses. The detector is most reliable where it matters least.

🛑 SCOPE, so this is not read wider than it is: measured on ONE property (`TemporalFact.subject_id`) on ONE graph. `node_ref` is a schema flag and other types may declare it; whether they do, and whether any of those carry dangling values, was NOT measured. The `create_node` guard shipped in #366 stops NEW bad values on any `node_ref` property, so this concerns only values written before that guard, or broken later by a rename — which is the residue #366 named as needing a different fix.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a rule that walks every property declared `node_ref` and reports an unresolvable value on its own terms, independent of the node's degree. The write-side guard already knows which properties those are.
