properties.name: With NO persistent database and the full-text index built in RAM, reflow2's own design loads to fully searchable in 1,098 ms and saves in 1,168 ms — and the dominant remaining cost is build_export_doc on the WRITE side, which nobody has looked at
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-25 at main `39dbf6d`, immediately after the write-buffer index landed (#330). Release build, **in-memory backend, tantivy `create_in_ram`, no RocksDB, nothing on disk**. reflow2's own design: 3,149 nodes / 13,414 edges / 8.10 MB document.

    LOAD (session start)                        SAVE (session end)
      parse JSON            196.1 ms              build export doc   1,137.3 ms
      open graph             10.0 ms              serialize to JSON     31.0 ms  (7.13 MB)
      import + index        890.6 ms              ---------------------------------
      first search_design     1.4 ms              TOTAL save         1,168.3 ms
      ---------------------------------
      TOTAL to searchable 1,098.1 ms

⭐⭐ THE OBJECTION THAT BLOCKED THIS IDEA IS GONE. When the question was first recorded, hydrate was 8,828 ms and the honest read was "viable for typical designs, a research project for this one". The write-buffer index took import from 8,398 ms to ~890 ms INCLUDING the full-text build, and the whole load is now **1.1 seconds for the biggest, densest design that exists**. Nothing about the storage architecture changed to achieve that — it was a `Vec` being linearly scanned.

⭐ THE FULL-TEXT INDEX IS CHEAP, WHICH NOBODY KNEW. Every earlier figure in this line of work had `fulltext` OFF and was explicitly labelled a lower bound. Measured with it ON, building the entire tantivy index from scratch in RAM costs roughly **190–280 ms** on top of the graph import, and the first `search_design` after it returns 10 hits in **1.4 ms**. The index does NOT have to be persisted to be affordable — it is genuinely derived, and rebuilding it per session is a rounding error against a session's length.

⭐ AND THE DOMINANT COST MOVED TO A PLACE NOBODY HAS LOOKED. `export_graph`'s document build is **1,137 ms**, while serializing the result is 31 ms. So the save side is now 36x more expensive than the JSON encoding it exists to produce, and it is the single largest cost in the whole model — larger than the entire load path. It is the same SHAPE as the import defect just fixed (an internal read pattern, not I/O), and it has never been profiled. **If this model is taken, that is the next measurement, and it is very likely another `Vec` somewhere.**

⇒ WHAT THE ROUND TRIP ACTUALLY COSTS A SESSION: ~1.1 s in, ~1.2 s out, **~2.3 s total**, once, for a design larger than any real tenant would hold. Against a session measured in minutes or hours that is not a performance question any more. It is now purely a DURABILITY question, which is the trade `dec:idea-what-guarantees-the-export-if-the-export-is-the-only-durable-copy` holds.

🛑 STILL UNMEASURED, AND EACH COULD STILL SINK IT:
1. **Accumulated store state.** Confirmation-ledger dates, drift baselines, `write_gen`, the `.id.json` / `.sync.json` sidecars. `fact:export-import-export-is-lossless-but-not-a-fixed-point-until-one-normalising-pass` proved the DESIGN round-trips (3,140/3,140 nodes); it proved nothing about what a running seat believes. This is the way the model fails LATE.
2. **Crash durability.** RAM dies with the process. The trade is bounded loss vs no loss and it is a judgement, not a measurement.
3. **The shared server.** Several sessions share one graph through one process today. In-RAM state does not change that — the process IS the state — but nothing has tested what a server restart means when there is no store to reopen.

📌 BOUNDS: one machine, one design, one run per figure, release build, OS page cache uncontrolled. No sub-sampled curve was taken with fulltext on, so the SHAPE of the index cost against design size is unknown — only this one point.

THE DESIGN'S ONLY CIRCULAR DEPENDENCY, RESOLVED 2026-08-23, AND IT WAS NEVER A DEPENDENCY.

`dec:exploratory-staging` and `dec:idea-do-ideas-form-a-graph-or-only-a-list` each carried a DEPENDS_ON to the other. Reading both edges settled it in minutes:

  KEPT   exploratory-staging → do-ideas-form-a-graph. Dated 2026-08-21, confidence 0.8, and carrying real evidence: exploratory-staging turns on whether ANY COMPUTATION would read the idea-kind distinction, and cluster-search over an idea's neighbourhood is a candidate for exactly that computation — so the older question cannot be settled until this one is answered. That is a genuine ordering claim.

  RETRACTED   do-ideas-form-a-graph → exploratory-staging. No date, no confidence, no evidence. Its whole content was the note *"that node asks what an idea IS; this asks what it is CONNECTED TO"* — which is not a dependency claim at all. It says the two are DIFFERENT.

⭐ AND THE SENTENCE WAS ALREADY IN THE NODE'S OWN PROSE, WORD FOR WORD: "DISTINCT FROM `dec:exploratory-staging`... That node is about what an idea IS; this one is about what an idea is CONNECTED TO." So the edge duplicated, in the wrong edge type, something the node already said better. Deleting it lost nothing and made a real dependency readable again.

🛑 THE VOCABULARY GAP IS THE FINDING, NOT THE CYCLE. There is NO EDGE TYPE MEANING "RELATED BUT DISTINCT" between two Decisions. `describe_schema` for that pair returns nothing that models it: DEPENDS_ON, EVOLVES_INTO, CONTRADICTS and the rest accept Decision→Decision only through a `*` wildcard on both ends. So somebody with a true and useful thing to say — "these two questions are adjacent and must not be confused" — had one honest option, prose, and one available option, a wrong edge. They took both, and the wrong edge outlived the prose in every computation that walks the graph.

⚠️ THIS IS THE SECOND OBSERVED INSTANCE OF THE SAME SHAPE, and Anthony raised the first from another session the same day: SUPERSEDES is `Fragment → Fragment` only and has ZERO edges in this design, while sessions reaching for a replacement relation between two same-type nodes get refused and fall back to EVOLVES_INTO — which also only wildcard-accepts the pair. A third instance appeared in this session: linking two TemporalFacts, nothing models the pair either.
  ⇒ THE PATTERN: when the schema models no edge for a real relationship, the relationship does not go unrecorded. IT GETS RECORDED AS SOMETHING ELSE, and the something else is then read by every detector as if it meant what it says. A wildcard-accepted edge is not a neutral fallback; it is an assertion in the wrong vocabulary.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: whether to add such an edge type. That is a schema change and Anthony's call. Three instances is a pattern worth naming, not yet a mandate — and `schema/verify.yaml` already warns from its own history that widening or narrowing an endpoint list deserves scrutiny in both directions.

properties.description:
⭐ THIS IS `dec:reflow2-is-built-for-observability` APPLIED WHERE IT WAS NOT. That decision binds future work with: *'a part that reports on something must be able to say it could not tell, and any new detector owes an answer for the case where it had nothing to run on.'* It is stated about DETECTORS AND TOOLS. Nothing states it about the RECORDS THE DESIGN WRITES ABOUT ITSELF — and a finding whose name overstates its data misrepresents what the design knows in exactly the way that decision forbids, one layer along.

═══ THE MECHANISM, and it is specific rather than atmospheric ═══

`search_design` returns a TemporalFact's **`name`**, its `node_id`, and `age_days`/`as_of`. It does NOT return `statement` or `description`. So the sentence a session meets when it goes looking is the name, and the bounded reasoning sits in fields the reader must take a second, deliberate step to reach.

🛑 AND THE EXEMPLAR *DID* BOUND ITSELF — WHICH IS THE SHARPEST PART. Its body ends with a full paragraph headed 'WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE': which level should carry contracts, and whether DEPENDS_ON between two impl blocks of one struct is worth recording. The convention exists and was followed. **It simply bounded a different claim than the one in the name.** So this is not a discipline nobody practises; it is a discipline that does not reach the field a reader actually sees.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH — written first rather than last, because a finding about overreach that overreached would refute itself ═══

- **n = 1.** One fact, examined because it misled a live session. **Nobody has counted how many of this design's 300+ TemporalFacts carry a name stronger than their data.** That measurement has not been made and this must not be read as though it had.
- **It is not stale-ness, and the existing machinery does not reach it.** `invalidated_findings` reports a finding some record CLAIMS to have answered; `age_days` reports how old a claim is. The exemplar was neither stale nor claimed — it was CURRENT and CORRECT about its data. There is no signal here to detect with what exists.
- **A second wrong recommendation the same session was NOT this class**, and folding it in would be the same error. Seven components were nearly relabelled from reading a `sys:` id prefix; that is treating a NAMING CONVENTION as evidence, and it was corrected by reading the containment. Related in outcome, different in mechanism. Kept apart deliberately.
- **No remedy is asserted.** Whether anything should change — a naming discipline, a bounds field, a lint, or nothing at all — is open in `dec:idea-should-a-finding-be-required-to-bound-its-own-claim`.

═══ WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING AT n=1 ═══

Because the cost landed on a real session rather than in theory: the overreaching name was cited TWICE as grounds for not doing work, once to the user and once into a ChangeEvent, before a five-minute measurement overturned it. A finding that argues against measuring is the most expensive kind to get wrong, and 'by construction' is precisely the phrasing that argues against measuring.
properties.name: n=1, MECHANISM IDENTIFIED, PREVALENCE UNMEASURED — a measured fact's NAME asserted an impossibility its data did not establish, and `search_design` returns the name rather than the bounded body
properties.statement: ONE DOCUMENTED INSTANCE, 2026-08-27. `fact:coupling-and-contract-are-recorded-in-vocabularies-that-never-meet` is named: 'The undeclared-seam finding CAN NEVER REACH ZERO: couplings are read from DEPENDS_ON and contracts from PROVIDES/CONSUMES, and on this design those two sets are DISJOINT BY CONSTRUCTION.' The measurement behind it was sound. The claim in the name was not: the sets were disjoint because contracts had been declared at the SUBSYSTEM boundary while couplings sat between MODULES — a state, not a property of the schema. Declaring three contracts between coupled modules moved it 8/72 → 13/72 in one afternoon. 'By construction' and 'can never' are the two words that made a measured state read as a law.

MEASURED ON THE v0.30.0 CUT, 2026-08-13, and it produced a WRONG COMMITTED RECORD that every other check passed.

THREE BINARY VERSIONS WERE IN PLAY ON ONE MACHINE:

    live MCP server    0.29.0 image   (the session's own tools)
    target/release/    0.28.0, Aug 11 (**what `tools/reflow2_cli.py`'s DEFAULT_BIN resolves to**)
    target/debug/      0.30.0         (built minutes earlier, the only correct one)

The release procedure's replay exists precisely to avoid the live server's old stamp: import into a temp store, export from it with the NEW binary. I ran that replay and passed `C.DEFAULT_BIN`. **The committed export came back stamped `0.28.0` — with PERFECTLY CORRECT LINEAGE**, `prev_content_hash` equal to main's `content_hash`, 2144 nodes, 8447 edges, `graph_id: reflow2`. Every property anyone checks was right except the one that says which reflow2 wrote it. Caught only by reading `stamp.reflow2_version` out of the written file before committing.

⭐⭐ AND THE EXISTING STALENESS CAPABILITY CANNOT SEE THIS, WHICH IS THE FINDING. `cap:the-server-knows-its-own-currency` reports whether **the server's own executable has been REPLACED SINCE IT STARTED** — `ver:the-server-says-when-it-is-stale` demonstrates it by relinking a binary under a running daemon and watching the same server flip to `stale: true`. A server freshly spawned from a THREE-VERSION-OLD build has had nothing replaced under it, so it reads a definite **`stale: false`** and is telling the truth.

⇒ **"MY EXECUTABLE CHANGED UNDER ME" AND "I AM AN OLD BUILD" ARE DIFFERENT FACTS, AND ONLY THE FIRST IS DETECTED.** The second is the one that mis-stamps a release record, and it is undetectable from inside the server: the binary is internally consistent and confident. It is visible only by comparing the stamp against the version the SOURCE claims.

📌 THE NARROW FIX IS FREE AND IS NOW IN [[reflow2-release-cut-procedure]]: name the freshly built binary explicitly in the replay, never `DEFAULT_BIN`, and READ `stamp.reflow2_version` OUT OF THE WRITTEN FILE BEFORE COMMITTING — every cut, every time.

📌 THE WIDER ONE IS NOT TAKEN AND IS NOT OBVIOUS: whether `reflow2_cli.py` should refuse, or at least say, when the binary it is about to drive reports a version older than the workspace's `Cargo.toml`. That is a comparison the CLI can make and currently does not, and it is the same shape as every other finding in this increment — the information existed and did not reach the person.

⚠️ STILL TRUE AT SESSION END: `target/release/reflow2-mcp` on this machine remains **0.28.0**. CI builds its own release artifacts, so the PUBLISHED v0.30.0 binaries are unaffected; anything local defaulting to that path is driving a three-version-old server.

properties.name: Third independent measurement that reflow2's FUNCTIONAL decomposition disagrees with its coupling: 80% of component dependencies cross the new subsystem groups. Expected, not a defect — a layered carving maximises cross-group edges by construction
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-25, immediately after the coherence-loop and agent-surface splits, as a deliberate check on whether a grouping arrived at BY JUDGEMENT survives contact with the dependency data.

═══ THE NUMBERS ═══

    Component -> Component DEPENDS_ON edges, whole design      72
    both ends inside the two newly split systems               15
       WITHIN a group   3   (20%)   <- cohesion
       ACROSS groups   12   (80%)   <- coupling
    one or both ends elsewhere in the design                   57

    top cross-group couplings
       4  Telling  -> Finding
       2  Finding  -> Change and structure
       2  Telling  -> Change and structure
       2  Telling  -> Evidence

⚠️ BY A MODULARITY STANDARD THIS IS POOR COHESION, AND REPORTING IT IS THE POINT. The grouping was proposed by an agent, accepted by the user, and then measured against data that could have embarrassed it. It did. That is recorded here rather than omitted, because a design that only keeps the measurements which flatter it is not a design record.

═══ ⭐⭐ AND IT WAS NEVER GOING TO VALIDATE, FOR THREE REASONS ═══

**1. THE SAMPLE IS SMALL BECAUSE THE GRAPH IS A STAR.** Only 15 of 72 edges have both ends inside the split systems; 57 reach outside. The adopt trial measured why: fan-in `foundation` 49, `graph` 42, `nodes` 41, and 45% of core modules importing ONLY those three hubs. Most dependencies point at the foundation, not at siblings, so intra-system cohesion has little to be computed from.

**2. THE DOMINANT CROSS-EDGE IS THE CUT WORKING.** `Telling -> Finding` at 4 edges is the reports depending on the detectors — a DIRECTED LAYER dependency, and exactly what the observability cut predicts: the instrument is separate from the presenter, and the presenter reads the instrument. **A layered carving MAXIMISES cross-group edges by construction**, and modularity metrics penalise them regardless of direction. Scoring a layered architecture on undirected modularity measures the wrong thing.

**3. IT IS THE THIRD INDEPENDENT ROUTE TO ONE CONCLUSION.** The adopt trial (2026-08-25) found the functional carving unrecoverable from source, by directory and by imports. The co-change experiment (2026-08-21) found **71% of the strongest maintainability signal crossing subsystem boundaries**. This finds 80% of the dependency signal crossing the new groups. Three different signals, three different days, one conclusion: **reflow2's functional decomposition is not its coupling-optimal decomposition, and `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition` chose that deliberately in 2026-07-23.**

📌 WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY TEST THE GROUPING, and it has NOT been done: whether a change to one group forces changes in another — co-change restricted to these components, computable today from 500+ ChangeEvents. Dependency coupling tests a property the carving never claimed to optimise. **Do not read this fact as evidence the split was wrong; read it as evidence that this is the wrong instrument for judging it.**

⚠️ BOUNDS: one design, one day, one direction. Edges counted are `DEPENDS_ON` between Components only — not capability coupling (which holds ONE edge across 212 capabilities and can measure nothing), and not co-change. No comparison against an alternative grouping was run, so nothing here says another carving would score better.

properties.name: Every clippy gate passed locally and BOTH CI jobs failed on the same lint — the flags were identical and the COMPILER was the narrow gate, which is the one axis skill_lint's gate-list cross-check structurally cannot see
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-24 landing increment 4 (PR #329). All six local gates were run and reported green — fmt, clippy on both crates with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`, the core and workspace test suites, eleven python gates and the design gate. Both CI jobs then failed, on one lint:

    error: using `chunks_exact` with a constant chunk size
      --> crates/reflow2-core/src/foundation/store/engine/mod.rs:605:29
      = note: `-D clippy::chunks-exact-to-as-chunks` implied by `-D warnings`

COMMAND IDENTICAL, FLAGS IDENTICAL. Local was rustc/clippy **1.94.0**; CI runs `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`, which is **1.98.0**, and 1.98 added `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`. The lint did not exist on the developer machine, so no local invocation of any width could have produced it.

⭐ WHY THIS IS NOT BL-159 AGAIN, THOUGH IT LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE IT. BL-159 was the same SYMPTOM — documented gate followed exactly, build still red — and its cause was a FLAGS difference (`-p reflow2-core` clippy lacking `-D warnings`). `skill_lint.py` now cross-checks AGENTS.md's gate block against `ci.yml` for coverage, identity and fidelity, and it closed that hole properly. **It cannot close this one.** Both records it compares are TEXT IN THIS REPOSITORY, and the toolchain version is in NEITHER: `@stable` names a moving target, so AGENTS.md can name the exact command with the exact flags, skill_lint can confirm all four checks, and the gate is still narrower locally than in CI. The cross-check is complete over what is written down and blind to what resolves at run time.

FIXED AT THE CAUSE rather than by chasing the symptom: `rustup update stable` (1.94.0 → 1.98.0), then the whole sweep re-run, which found exactly ONE more finding and no others. Fixing the reported line alone would have left the machine two minor versions behind and the next lint would have arrived the same way.

⚠️ THE FINDING WAS THEN ALLOWED, NOT FIXED. clippy is right that `as_chunks::<4>()` is better, and `dec:absorb-the-foundation-subset-and-end-the-dependency` requires the absorbed files to stay byte-diffable against dynograph-foundation v0.12.0 — the same ground as `graphalg`'s `#![allow(dead_code)]`, where Anthony said "don't trim now - if we decide it isn't necessary, then we can trim in the future." The allow carries that reasoning at the call site. **Absorbed code makes every future lint bump a provenance decision, not a cleanup**, and that cost was not named when the absorption was scoped.

⭐⭐ THE SHAPE THIS BELONGS TO. This is the FIFTH instance in two days of a narrow gate read as a wide one: `#[cfg(test)]` invisible to the test run; feature-gated files invisible to `--no-default-features` clippy; doctests invisible to build and clippy; a non-snake-case test name invisible without `--all-targets`; and now a lint invisible to an older compiler. The first four are a local HABIT and can be fixed by remembering. **This one cannot** — no amount of care with flags reaches it, because the gate's width is set by a binary nobody versioned in the record. Recorded here rather than as advice: the only defence that worked was CI running the wide form, and the only durable fix is keeping the local toolchain pinned to what CI resolves.

📌 OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, worth knowing before the next session: the toolchain update means the next cargo command pays a full rebuild including the ~19-minute librocksdb-sys C++ compile.

properties.name: check_doc_versions' hermetic suite passed before, during and after its fact-reading function was replaced wholesale — it only ever exercised the claim-matching half, so a green suite said nothing about the half that changed
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-24. `tools/check_doc_versions.py` has two halves. `foundation_tag()` READS THE FACT every doc claim is measured against, out of the tree. `claims()` MATCHES prose against that fact. Its hermetic suite `tools/test_check_doc_versions.py` had three tests, all on the second half: the repo as it stands passes, a stale claim is caught, and rewording the prose fails loudly rather than disabling the check.

Increment 4 deleted the thing `foundation_tag()` read — the `dynograph-*` git-tag pin in the workspace `Cargo.toml` — so the gate went red, correctly, with `FAIL: could not find any dynograph-foundation tag pin`. The function was then REPLACED WHOLESALE: it now reads `^//! tag      vX.Y.Z` out of the provenance headers the absorption decision requires every absorbed module to carry, with new failure modes for no-header-anywhere and for modules naming different tags.

🛑 **THE SUITE PASSED 3/3 BEFORE THE REWRITE, AND 3/3 AFTER IT, AND NEVER ONCE TOUCHED THE FUNCTION.** `grep -n 'foundation_tag\|tag = "v\|provenance' tools/test_check_doc_versions.py` returned NOTHING. A green suite was reported for a rewritten function it did not reach, and the green was true and worthless in the same breath.

⭐ WHY THIS ONE IS WORTH KEEPING. The near-miss is not "a function was untested" — that is ordinary. It is that **the suite's green was read as evidence about the change**, in a session that had already been caught twice that day reading a narrow gate as a wide one. The check that caught it was not a tool: it was asking, before trusting the pass, WHICH LINES THE SUITE ACTUALLY EXECUTES. That is the same habit `rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object` names — the value you read is not the value you think you are reading — applied to a test suite rather than to an exit code.

CLOSED BY ADDING WHAT WAS MISSING, not by noting it: three tests now pin that the provenance headers are where the tag comes from, that losing every header FAILS rather than passing empty, and that modules absorbed from different vintages are caught — the successor to the old "five pins that drifted apart" check. Suite is 6/6. The two failure-mode tests mutate the real source files and restore them in a `finally`; restoration was verified by grep afterwards, because a test that corrupts provenance headers on a crash would be worse than the gap it closes.

⚠️ GENERALISES, AND IS NOT MEASURED BEYOND THIS ONE CASE: reflow2 has eleven python gates, most with a paired hermetic suite, and NOTHING checks whether a suite reaches the whole of the gate it guards. Whether the others have the same shape is unknown — stated as an open question, not as a finding.

properties.name: Store-state round-trip test: all 208 confirmation-ledger claims survive hydration field-for-field, ZERO differences. The only real loss is last_synced — the seat forgets every export it has synced with, and sync_status then answers with the same empty result it uses to mean 'never synced'
properties.statement:
THE TEST `dec:idea-does-reflow2-need-a-byte-store-at-all-or-only-durability` NAMED AS "the way this model fails LATE", run 2026-08-25 at main `39dbf6d`. Question: does what a RUNNING SEAT BELIEVES — as opposed to the design itself — survive being rebuilt from the export document?

METHOD: import the committed export into an empty store, then run the same tools against the hydrated store and the live one and diff the answers field by field.

⭐⭐ THE CONFIRMATION LEDGER SURVIVES COMPLETELY. **208 capability claims on both sides, the same capability ids, and ZERO differing fields across all of them.**

    claims 208 | confirmed 208 | drifting 0 | unexamined 0
    stale_verification 112 | unknown_verification_freshness 90     (identical both sides)

Every per-capability field matched: `last_claim_at`, `last_confirmed_at`, `last_verified_at`, `drift_events`, `unresolved_drift_events`, `design_holds_claims`, `design_updated_claims`, `baseline_claims`, `confirmations`, `design_edits`, `state`, `verification_freshness`. **The dates, the drift history and the accept ledger are all NODES AND EDGES, so the document carries them.** The fear that a hydrated session would silently forget when it last checked something is measured and false.

🛑 WHAT IS ACTUALLY LOST, AND IT IS ONE THING: `last_synced`. It lives in `.reflow2/<graph>.sync.json`, a sidecar file BESIDE the store, not in the store and not in the document. The live seat holds six entries mapping export paths to content hashes; the hydrated seat holds none:

    live       sync_status -> 6 entries, each in_step with its file
    hydrated   sync_status -> {"behind": [], "checked": 0, "sync": []}

⚠️ AND THE FAILURE IS QUIET BY THE TOOL'S OWN ACCOUNT. `sync_status` documents that *"AN EMPTY ANSWER MEANS THIS SEAT HAS NEVER SYNCED WITH ANY FILE — never that all is well"*. A hydrated seat produces exactly that answer while having a full design loaded, so the reading "this seat is new" is TRUE of its sync state and FALSE of everything else. What rests on it: `req:stale-seat-knows` and the export-overwrite refusal, which compares a file's current hash against what this graph believes it last wrote. With an empty map there is nothing to compare, so the guard against silently deleting a colleague's work has no baseline on the first export after a hydrate.

⭐ THE GAP IS NARROW AND FIXABLE, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART. `last_synced` is a small map of path -> content hash. Making it endure is a choice between carrying it in the document, keeping the sidecar file beside the document, or recomputing it by hashing the files a seat knows about. None of those is architecture; all are bookkeeping. **The model does not fail late on accumulated state — it fails on ONE map, and that map is three lines of JSON.**

📌 SECOND, SMALLER GAP, THEORETICAL TODAY: `CF_EMBEDDINGS` is a real column family and `GraphExport` has no embeddings field, so vectors would not survive a hydrate. Measured: nothing outside `engine/tests.rs` calls `set_embedding`, so the store holds none today. It becomes real the moment `dec:idea-embeddings-adoption` lands, and it is worth knowing BEFORE that rather than after.

✅ REGENERATED CORRECTLY, so not gaps: `<graph>.id.json` (the empty store adopts the document's name via `adopt_on_import`) and `<graph>.meta.json` (derived from the schema).

📌 BOUNDS: one design, one direction, one machine, debug binary. Two tools compared (`confirmation_ledger`, `sync_status`) plus the sidecar files on disk — NOT an exhaustive sweep of everything a seat can believe. `write_gen` was not separately exercised.

MEASURED 2026-08-22 while building `incomplete_published_contract`. THE FIRST CUT OF THE DETECTOR WAS GREEN OVER EXACTLY THE THING IT EXISTS TO CHECK, and the cause was a schema default.

Five of the nine interface agreement axes are enums DEFAULTING to `unspecified` (`medium`, `paradigm`, `payload_format`, `auth`, `transport_security`). The store MATERIALISES defaults on write (`Schema::validate_node`), so every Interface ever created already carries the word. A presence test — is this property set? — therefore counts `unspecified` as an ANSWER.

MEASURED BEFORE THE FIX, on reflow2's own three published boundaries:
  `ifc:mcp-tools-http`   read 9 of 9 COMPLETE while its `medium` said `unspecified`
  `ifc:graph-export`     reported 4 unset axes where there are 6
  `ifc:mcp-tools`        9 of 9, and this one is genuinely true

⭐ SO A COMPLETENESS CHECK OVER DEFAULTED FIELDS MEASURES NOTHING, AND REPORTS SUCCESS. It is not that the check was slightly wrong; it is that the property it tested was guaranteed true for every node in every design. The fix reads `unspecified` as UNSET.

⚠️ AND THE OPPOSITE ERROR IS JUST AS AVAILABLE: `none` IS AN ANSWER. `auth: none` and `transport_security: none` on an unauthenticated local pipe are deliberate statements, and `ifc:mcp-tools` makes exactly them. Sweeping `none` in with `unspecified` would nag a design that had answered honestly. DECLARED ABSENCE AND UNDECLARED ABSENCE ARE DIFFERENT FACTS, and only a vocabulary that separates them can tell a finished contract from an untouched one.

🛑 THIS IS THE THIRD TIME IN ONE DAY THAT MATERIALISED DEFAULTS DECIDED A DESIGN. (1) `vocabulary_coverage` can never name a DEFAULTED property as unused, so what it reports is the undefaulted optional only — an under-count, stated as an honest limit. (2) `no_published_boundary` had to exist at all because `Interface.designation` defaults to `internal`, making "unclassified" and "deliberately internal" indistinguishable, while `Artifact.audience` needs no such companion BECAUSE it is undefaulted. (3) This.

THE GENERAL FORM, and it is the argument `req:defaults-do-not-assert` was accepted on, now with a mechanism rather than a principle: A STORED DEFAULT DOES NOT MERELY ASSERT SOMETHING NOBODY SAID — IT MAKES THE ABSENCE UNDETECTABLE. Every later computation that tries to find out whether anyone answered gets `true`, and no test written against the schema alone can see it, because the schema is where the lie is. The three cases above differ in what they cost: an under-count, an extra detector, and a check that could not fail.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: that defaults are wrong. `Requirement.status` defaulting to `proposed` is right, because `proposed` is a true statement about a requirement nobody has ruled on. The distinction is whether the default is a FACT about the unset state or a GUESS standing in for one — and `unspecified` is the rare case of a default that honestly names its own emptiness, which is why the repair here was cheap. The expensive ones are defaults that name a plausible value.

87 VERIFICATION NAMES HELD WHOLE REPORTS AND NOW HOLD NAMES. Moved verbatim into `description`; `findings` untouched. Longest name 654 words → 60. Distribution over all 199 checks: 173 at 0-25 words, 26 at 26-60, ZERO above 60. ⇒ `graph_report {include_verifications: true}` fell 165,207 → 55,520 bytes, which is the real payoff — the escape hatch the #305 digest points at was itself unreadable, so 'withheld but reachable' was only half true. The DEFAULT report is unchanged at 15,485; the names were never in it. || ⚠️ THE COUNT I FIRST GAVE WAS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION WAS THE WHOLE JUDGEMENT. I reported '113 names to fix' — but 113 is how many exceed the ROLLUP TRUNCATION threshold of 25 words, which is a DISPLAY limit, not a defect. The bottom of that band are real names that merely run long (`ver:merge-driver`, 29 words: 'Real git branches: disjoint edits merge with no human, a both-sides conflict leaves the path unmerged and names itself...'). The defect separates by STRUCTURE, not length: of the 26-40 word band 0 of 16 are multi-sentence, while of the 101-200 band 32 of 34 are, and every one of the 201-700 band is. Anthony chose the >60-word boundary: 87 rewritten, 26 dense-but-legitimate names left alone. ⇒ A THRESHOLD BORROWED FROM A RENDERER IS NOT A DEFINITION OF A DEFECT. || HOW IT WAS DONE SAFELY, and the method is the transferable part: the new names were AUTHORED (extracting a first clause yields another fragment, not a name), but the preserved text was COPIED BY SCRIPT from the committed export and never retyped, so corruption in transit was impossible by construction. Then verified: all 87 descriptions byte-identical to the original names, all 87 names as authored, and no property lost to the constructors' merge semantics. || WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not sort the originals into 'what the check IS' versus 'what a run FOUND'. Most of the 87 mix both. That split is 87 judgement calls and a wrong one writes narrative into an evidence field, so `findings` was left alone deliberately rather than filled in on a guess. || SOURCE: 2026-08-23, reflow2 0.38.0, driving the built binary over real stdio.

properties.name: A parsing bug that silently shrinks the evidence reads exactly like an honest 'no evidence found' — the vacuous zero, one layer down in the input stage
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-21, in a tool written the same hour. Kept because the SHAPE recurs, not the bug.

`link_tests.py` attributes a test to a component only if the test calls a function that component's source defines. It reported that `crates/reflow2-core/tests/heal.rs` calls NOTHING `heal.rs` defines — a clean, plausible, honest-looking negative.

THE CAUSE WAS IN THE READER, NOT THE CODE READ. Before scanning, the tool strips string literals so prose can never become structure. It did so across the WHOLE FILE with one regex. Regex quote-pairing is greedy and positional: one unbalanced quote — a Rust raw string, an escaped quote, an apostrophe the comment pass missed — pairs with the next quote far below, and everything between is deleted. heal.rs went from dozens of visible `pub fn` definitions to ONE.

⭐⭐ THE GENERAL FORM: **A PARSING BUG THAT SILENTLY SHRINKS THE EVIDENCE IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM AN HONEST "NO EVIDENCE FOUND".** Both print zero. Both look like the tool working. No error, no warning, no partial result to be suspicious of — the tool is MORE confident, not less, because it found a smaller world and searched all of it.

📌 THIS IS THE VACUOUS ZERO ONE LAYER DOWN. The known form is "a detector reporting zero because it had nothing to run on reads exactly like one that ran clean" (req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots; loop_status already refuses an unknown contributor_id for this reason). The NEW form is that the emptiness can be manufactured by the tool's own INPUT STAGE, after which every downstream count is honest arithmetic over a corrupted set.

🛠️ WHAT CAUGHT IT: not a test — a human-scale sanity check. "heal.rs defines one function" is absurd to anyone who has seen the file. Nothing mechanical was going to flag it, because the number was internally consistent everywhere it was used.

⇒ THE PRACTICE THIS ARGUES FOR: a stage that REDUCES its input should report what it REMOVED, not only what survived. The fix was to strip line by line, which cannot span lines; the durable part is the named regression test, so the next person who simplifies it back to one regex meets the case.

MEASURED 2026-08-12, and self-reported because it produced a false green in this session.

WHAT HAPPENED: `cargo test --workspace 2>&1 | grep -E "^test result:|FAILED" | tail -20` was run as the pre-PR gate. It was reported to the owner as passing. ⚠️ THE EXIT CODE OF A SHELL PIPELINE IS THE EXIT CODE OF ITS LAST COMMAND — `tail` — which is 0 whether cargo passed, failed, or never compiled. The `tail -20` also truncated the evidence to the last 20 result lines, so the absence of a FAILED line in what came back proved nothing about the other 83 suites.

Caught only by noticing the totals looked low: 20 suites / 250 tests against a project that runs 103 suites / 1,138 tests. The re-run with cargo's status captured directly (`cargo test --workspace > log 2>&1; echo $?`) reported exit 0, 103 suites, 1,138 tests, 0 failures — so the answer was right and the METHOD that produced it could not have known.

⇒ THE GENERAL FORM, which is why this is worth a node: PIPING A GATE THROUGH A FILTER CONVERTS ITS VERDICT INTO ITS OUTPUT. Everything the filter drops is unfalsifiable, and the status that survives belongs to the filter. This is the same class as every finding this project already holds about self-report — a green that describes the reporter rather than the thing.

It is also unusually well-camouflaged HERE, because filtering long cargo output is the obviously sensible thing to do, and the filtered output looks like exactly what a passing run looks like.

THE RULE THAT FALLS OUT: redirect a gate to a file and read `$?` from the gate itself; filter the FILE afterwards. `set -o pipefail` also works and is easier to forget. Never take the presence-or-absence of a pattern in filtered output as the verdict.

NOT BUILT INTO ANYTHING. Recorded as a fact rather than a rule because nothing detects it — an agent's shell pipeline is not something reflow2 can see, which is precisely why it needs to be written down where the next session will read it.

AN OPEN PR'S EXPORT GOES STALE WHILE ITS BADGE STAYS GREEN, AND MERGING IT WOULD SUBTRACT DESIGN. Measured on reflow2's own repo, 2026-08-16, on THREE PRs at once — not a hypothetical, and not caused by anything anyone did wrong.

MEASURED, per PR, against `origin/main`:

    #190  export 63 nodes BEHIND main   intended to add 9   — all 9 ALREADY IN MAIN
    #191  export 59 nodes BEHIND main   intended to add 13  — all 13 ALREADY IN MAIN
    #194  export 56 nodes BEHIND main   intended to add 16  — all 16 ALREADY IN MAIN

All three were green on both CI jobs. #194 read `MERGEABLE`.

⭐ THE MECHANISM IS THE SHARED STORE, AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS. The design graph does not branch with git (`dec:multi-writer-architecture`), so a later session's export from the same store CARRIED EVERY EARLIER BRANCH'S GRAPH WRITES INTO MAIN. Each PR's design content therefore arrived in main WITHOUT that PR being merged. What was left on the branch was a document that could only subtract — `req:stale-seat-knows`'s prediction arriving in practice: a stale export is a COMPLETE document, so it merges cleanly and the missing work simply vanishes.

⚠️ THE HALF THAT MAKES IT DANGEROUS: nothing on the PR says so. The gate runs against the BRANCH's export and its own artifact checksums, so it passes; the branch is internally coherent. The subtraction is only visible by comparing the branch's export against MAIN, which no check does. A reviewer sees green, mergeable, and a diff of one JSON file.

⇒ THE CHECK, cheap and reusable — TWO questions, and the second is the one that decides:

    1. Does this PR's export ADD anything main lacks?
         set(branch nodes) - set(main nodes)          -> 0 means it can only subtract
    2. Are the nodes it INTENDED to add already in main?
         set(branch nodes) - set(merge-base nodes), then test each against main

When (1) is 0 and (2) is all-present, the PR's design half is ALREADY DELIVERED and the export is pure liability. #190 held nothing else, so it was CLOSED rather than merged — refreshing its export would have left an empty PR. #191 and #194 held real code, so each was rebased with `git checkout --ours docs/design/reflow2.json`, its artifact checksums re-accepted against its OWN existing ChangeEvent in main, and re-exported once.

📌 AND THE TRAP INSIDE THE REPAIR: those three PRs were GREEN because their stale exports carried their own artifact checksums. Restoring main's export makes them go RED on DRIFT immediately — which is correct, and must be fixed by re-accepting, never by keeping the stale export that was hiding it.

NOT ESTABLISHED: how long a PR can sit before this becomes true (all three were under 24 hours old), and whether anything could detect it automatically — the comparison needs main, and the gate deliberately only reads the committed export in front of it.

properties.statement: THE REPORT A SESSION READS TO DECIDE WHAT TO LOOK AT WAS 91.5% ROLL CALL. `graph_report` measured 166,934 characters AFTER the duplicate emission was already removed — 152,803 of them the full verification roll. 197 checks, 196 of them passing. The one read that exists to point a session somewhere spent nine tenths of itself saying '196 passing, 1 planned'. It is also what the where-am-i skill reads, so 'where does this design stand' was refused on a mature design. || AND 93% OF THE ROLL WAS ONE FIELD: `name`, 129,994 chars over 197 entries. 113 OF THE 197 NAMES RUN OVER 25 WORDS AND THE LONGEST IS 654 — whole reports written into a name because `description` was declared and unreachable from `add_verification` for a long time. ⇒ THE BULK WAS NOT INFORMATION, IT WAS A DATA-ENTRY SCAR, and the sharpest clue was already on the wire: `graph_report_markdown` renders THE SAME REPORT for a human in 6,172 bytes, 27× smaller. || BOTH MECHANISMS ALREADY EXISTED AND NEITHER HAD BEEN POINTED HERE. `vocabulary_coverage` withholds its flat list unless asked (`include_unused`); `loop_status` already returns a verification DIGEST with names cut at 25 words and the cut announced. Reusing that same digest is why the truncation is not written twice — and it is also why `loop_status`'s `full_list` pointer had to move from `graph_report` to `graph_report {include_verifications: true}`, or a withheld list would have been left with a stale retrieval instruction, which is worse than never withholding it. MEASURED: 166,934 → 15,480 bytes on the wire, roll still reachable at 165,207. || ⚠️ THE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: the digest keeps every check that is NOT currently passing IN FULL, because that is what a reader acts on. So it is flat in the PASSING remainder, not in the check count. Here 196 of 197 pass and the saving is 11×; ON A DESIGN MID-BUILD WITH TWO HUNDRED `planned` CHECKS THIS REPORT WOULD BE LARGE AGAIN. That case is real, UNMEASURED, and deliberately not built for — the same 'measure before you cut' rule that cancelled the planned `loop_status` work an hour earlier. || A SECOND LIMIT WORTH SAYING: budgeting the report stops 113 essay-length names flooding a reply; IT DOES NOT MOVE THE REPORTS OUT OF THE NAME FIELDS. `add_verification` now reaches `description` and `findings`, so new checks land correctly and the existing 113 stay stranded. || SOURCE: measured 2026-08-23 on reflow2 0.38.0, driving the built binary over real stdio.

properties.name: A fact whose subject is a RETIRED dependency goes on reading as though it describes this project — it misled an agent and then the owner, in one session, about the KvBackend seam
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-28. Nothing is wrong with the record; the hazard is where it points.

WHAT HAPPENED. An agent read `fact:the-storage-seam-is-published-in-design-and-private-in-code` (2026-08-21) and reported to Anthony that reflow2's design designates `ifc:kv-backend` published while the code makes it `pub(crate)` — a live design-versus-code defect in THIS repo. It is not. That fact was measured by reading /home/ajs7/project/dynograph-foundation, and its `subject_id` is `dep:dynograph-foundation`. It describes THAT project's design graph.

REFLOW2'S OWN NODE IS CORRECT, and was the whole time: `ifc:kv-backend` carries `designation: internal` and an `endpoint` reading "crates/reflow2-core/src/foundation/store/backend.rs — `pub(crate) trait KvBackend: Send + Sync`". Design and code agree. Only three Interfaces here are designated `published`: ifc:graph-export, ifc:mcp-tools, ifc:mcp-tools-http.

THE SECOND HALF, AND IT IS THE PART THAT ACTUALLY WENT STALE. That fact concludes: "Swappable from INSIDE dynograph-foundation, not from outside it. A new backend — object storage, a networked KV, something sharded — is a change to that repo, not something reflow2 or flo2 could supply." TRUE WHEN WRITTEN AND FALSE THREE DAYS LATER: `dec:absorb-the-foundation-subset-and-end-the-dependency` completed 2026-08-24 and a new backend is now a change to reflow2's OWN repo. Verified 2026-08-28: no active `dynograph` dependency line in any Cargo.toml (every mention is a comment recording what was removed), `cargo tree -p reflow2-mcp` returns zero matches, and the trait is in-tree at crates/reflow2-core/src/foundation/store/backend.rs.

⭐ THE GENERAL SHAPE, which is why this is recorded rather than just corrected. A fact carries a `subject_id` naming a dependency. The dependency is later RETIRED and its code ABSORBED. The fact keeps its wording, keeps reading as current, and now describes ground this project owns — while its conclusions were reasoned about a boundary that no longer exists. `loop_status` cannot see it: a TemporalFact is not a debt class. `unclaimed_findings` scoped to the absorption's ChangeEvents is the mechanism that WOULD reach it, and whether it was run at absorption time is not established here.

⚠️ THE 2026-08-21 FACT IS NOT CLOSED, DELIBERATELY. Its first half — that dynograph-foundation's design designates the seam published while its code has it pub(crate) — was true of that repo when read and nobody has re-checked it. Closing the whole record would assert something unmeasured about another project. `valid_to` claims the WHOLE thing stopped being true, and only the reflow2-facing half did.

⚠️ WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: how many other facts name a retired dependency as their subject. One instance, found by being misled by it. It is not known whether this is a class.

properties.statement:
REPRODUCED LIVE 2026-08-17 on a throwaway graph, before designing anything, and it reframes the requirement.

TWO ARTIFACTS, IDENTICAL EXCEPT FOR ONE EDGE. Both registered with no claim edges, exactly as the fleet's ruling prescribes. One also GOVERNED_BY an accepted Decision recording why no claims were extracted.
    art:bare  (no ruling)      -> orphan_node REPORTED
    art:ruled (GOVERNED_BY)    -> orphan_node NOT reported

⇒ SO THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS AND THE PATH TO IT IS NOT TAKEN. GOVERNED_BY is not in `ARTIFACT_BOOKKEEPING`, so it counts as attachment; a node governed by its ruling is not an orphan. The fleet's 88 -> 97 climb across ten writes happens because the reason is recorded somewhere that is not an EDGE. This is the third time in one day that reflow2's vocabulary was present and unreached — after `description` (declared, unreachable from the constructor, 1 use in 164) and SUPERSEDES (declared, 0 edges, successor named in prose 9 times of 9).

⚠️⚠️ BUT SILENCE IS NOT WHAT THE REQUIREMENT ASKS FOR, AND THAT IS THE REAL GAP. Its words are: a marker "with `orphan_node` SKIPPING IT AND REPORTING `parked: N` SEPARATELY". Today the detector cannot COUNT a deliberate state — it can only fail to mention it. "Deliberately parked" and "never looked at" produce the identical answer, which is a vacuous zero wearing different clothes and exactly what `epoch:instruments-stop-overstating` exists to end. A boss reading "97 defects" cannot tell deliberate from real; a boss reading "34 defects, 8 parked" can.

AND THE SILENCE IS INCIDENTAL RATHER THAN INTENDED. `orphan_node` is not READING the ruling; it is seeing AN EDGE. A node governed by a completely unrelated Decision is silenced identically. So the requirement's ask — "a detector must be able to SEE that ruling and report the node accordingly" — is not met by what happens to work.

⭐ AND THE REPORTER'S OPEN BOUND IS NOW CLOSED. They wrote: "they did not check whether the guard built for the DOCUMENTS/REALIZES asymmetry was meant to cover this case and misses it, or whether this case was never contemplated." IT WAS NEVER CONTEMPLATED. BL-176 widened attachment to count REALIZES/DOCUMENTS/SPECIFIES/PRODUCES/SATISFIES — it is about artifacts that DO carry a describing edge and were wrongly called orphans. The fleet's case is an artifact that deliberately carries NO describing edge. Different case; the guard neither covers nor misses it.

CASE (b) IS GENUINELY UNSOLVED AND DIFFERENT. A Requirement deliberately left unsatisfied is reported by `unsatisfied_requirement`, a DETECT gap that looks for incoming SATISFIES — a GOVERNED_BY edge does not silence it and should not. That half needs the ruling to be readable, not merely present.

A SECOND PROJECT HIT `dec:idea-remaining-work-has-no-answer-in-the-graph` AND WORKED AROUND IT THE SAME WAY, WHICH IS THE CORROBORATION THAT NODE DID NOT HAVE. Alex's Grok 4.6 session, 2026-08-14 (Opportunities), in his words: "Remaining-work / increment view: this session used an accepted Decision's PROSE plus Capability `status` as the MVP list. `what_next` ranks open Decisions and does not answer 'what is left to build.'"

WHY IT MATTERS AS EVIDENCE RATHER THAN AS A NEW COMPLAINT: the open question already exists and already names the cause — the artifact layer is modelled at COMPONENT granularity, so it cannot answer a build question asked at capability granularity (see also `fact:the-build-list-is-suppressed-by-realized-via-component`). What was missing was whether anyone outside this project actually needs the answer. They do, and the workaround they reached for independently is identical: read an accepted Decision's PROSE as the plan, and use `Capability.status` as the checklist.

⭐ THE WORKAROUND IS THE FINDING. Both projects fell back to reading a decision's narrative text — unstructured, uncomputable, and exactly the thing a design graph exists to replace. When the graph cannot answer a question people must answer daily, they do not stop asking it; they answer it from prose, and the prose becomes load-bearing without anyone deciding that it should.

HE ALSO NAMES WHAT `what_next` DOES INSTEAD, which is accurate and not a criticism of it: it ranks open Decisions. That is a different question — what needs a human — from what is left to build, and the two are being conflated by callers because only one of them has a tool.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether an increment view should be derived from Capability status, from a Release manifest, from a plan-increments epoch, or from something new — that choice is the open question's, not this fact's.

properties.name: MEASURED: reading ${PIPESTATUS[0]} one command late reports 0 for a run that exited 7 — a false GREEN produced by a cosmetic separator, twice in one session
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-29, after reporting a passing test suite that had actually FAILED.

═══ THE DEMONSTRATION, run both ways ═══

```text
bash -c 'exit 7' 2>&1 | tail -1
echo "--------"                      <- a cosmetic separator
echo ${PIPESTATUS[0]}   ->  0       <- WRONG, and it reads as a pass

bash -c 'exit 7' 2>&1 | tail -1
echo ${PIPESTATUS[0]}   ->  7       <- correct
```

`PIPESTATUS` describes THE MOST RECENT PIPELINE, so any intervening command — `echo` included — overwrites it with that command's status, which is almost always 0. The separator that makes output readable is the thing that destroys the evidence.

═══ HOW IT ACTUALLY PRESENTED ═══

TWICE in one session, both times as a confident green:
1. `cargo test` printed `test result: FAILED. 7 passed; 1 failed` AND the line under it read `CARGO TEST EXIT=0`. The suite genuinely had a failing test; the exit code shown was the separator's.
2. `<binary> --import <doc> | tail -12` reported `IMPORT EXIT=0` while the import had exited 1 and written nothing. Here the fault is the sibling one — bare `$?` after a pipeline is the LAST element's status, so it measured `tail`.

⭐ BOTH ARE THE SAME FAMILY: the status read did not belong to the command being judged. And both are silent — the wrong number is a plausible number, in the right place, in the right format.

═══ 🛑 THE CAUSE I FIRST RECORDED WAS WRONG, WHICH IS THE SECOND FINDING ═══

The first diagnosis written down was *"`systemd-run --user --scope` does not propagate exit codes"*. It is FALSE and was refuted by one measurement: `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=1G bash -c 'exit 7'` returns 7, identically to running it bare. The wrapper was innocent and was blamed because it was the unfamiliar element in the line — the plausible suspect rather than the measured one. It had already been written into a handoff note before the check was run, and would have taught the next session to distrust the wrong thing.

═══ WHAT TO DO INSTEAD ═══

Read the status in the SAME command as the thing that produced it, and prefer having the runner say so itself:

```text
systemd-run --user --scope ... bash -c 'cargo test ...; echo "INNER_EXIT=$?"'
```

⚠️ WHY THIS IS WORTH A NODE IN A DESIGN GRAPH: `rule:a-green-gate-is-the-weakest-evidence` is the project's standing stance, and this is a mechanism that FABRICATES one from a run that failed. The reflow2 gate list in AGENTS.md is run by hand by agents, and an agent that reports the list green on this idiom has told the user something false about every gate at once.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any committed script or workflow in this repo reads a pipeline status late. Grepped for `systemd-run` in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .github/workflows and tools/ — one hit, in AGENTS.md prose, and it is not a gate. CI itself uses plain `run:` steps, so the hazard measured here is the AGENT'S shell, not the committed pipeline.

properties.name: ROOT CAUSE of skills going unused: an agent loads a skill when something ALREADY IN ITS HAND demands it, and otherwise substantially not at all — and no reflow2 tool demands any reflow2 skill
properties.statement:
REACHED 2026-08-28 by running the `root-cause` skill on the question "why does the agent not reach for reflow2 skills and tools?". Steps in order; the discriminating measurement refuted the investigator's own leading hypothesis.

═══ THE CAUSE ═══

**A skill is loaded when something the agent is ALREADY HOLDING makes it a precondition. Unprompted self-invocation is close to absent.** Counted over one long session, of the five skills loaded out of twenty-three served: THREE because the user typed a slash command or asked; ONE because a tool the agent had to call anyway said it MUST load it first (`Artifact` → `artifact-design`); ONE genuinely self-invoked. **No reflow2 tool makes any reflow2 skill a precondition of itself.**

═══ WHAT THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT KILLED ═══

The leading candidate going in was the investigator's own: that capture/orient skills get used and change-governing ones get skipped because the first fill a pause and the second must INTERRUPT work in flight. **REFUTED.** All twenty-three skills are mirrored identically into `.claude/skills/`, and `impact-check`, `revise-design` and `link-artifacts` all have slash commands — so neither reachability nor command-availability separates the two groups. The capture/change split was a pattern in the sample, not a cause. What actually separates them is WHO INITIATED.

═══ WHY IT IS THE CAUSE AND NOT THE INSTANCE (step ⑥) ═══

It explains the earlier occurrences, which is the test. `fact:an-agent-stopped-reaching-for-reflow2-and-a-second-one-reproduced-it-the-same-day` (2026-08-23, a different fleet, a different model, asked directly and writing from inside the failure) reports constant use of `search_design`, `get_node`, `create_node`, `loop_status`, `get_skill` — the things it was already holding — and ZERO use of `detect_gaps`, `gap_to_prompt`, `impact-check`, `detect_defects`, `reconcile_artifacts`, `coverage_report`, `evidence_report`. **Nothing it was already calling required any of them.** Its own reason (3) states the mechanism in different words: *"skills are PULL, and the thing that would tell you to load one is itself a lookup you must remember to make."*

⭐ AND IT MATCHES THE ONLY DISCRIMINATOR ANYONE HAS MEASURED. That same fact records that three BLOCKING gates each produced an immediate fix and zero passive hints did — *"the Stop hook worked BECAUSE IT BLOCKED, not because it spoke."* Today reproduced it a third way: the Stop hook blocked and was obeyed within one turn; `reflow2_check` blocked and four drifted artifacts were repaired; `loop_hint` appeared on nearly every call and was acted on ZERO times.

═══ WHAT THIS IMPLIES, WITHOUT PRESCRIBING IT ═══

The repair shape the evidence points at is `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue`, which is ALREADY ACCEPTED: put the precondition on the tool the agent is already reaching for, the way `Artifact` does. This is the first measurement of that mechanism working on an agent that skipped everything else. **The choice is Anthony's and nothing is pinned or built here** — step ⑦ was deliberately not taken, because pinning a test before the fix is chosen would pin the instance.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH (step ⑨) ═══

- **n=5 invocations in one session, one agent, one model**, plus one corroborating report from another fleet. The "who initiated" reading FITS those five; it is inference, not proof.
- **One alternative is NOT ruled out:** that the change-governing skills have narrower or worse-matching trigger descriptions than the capture ones. Separating that needs the trigger text compared against the moments each skill was owed, which nothing measures.
- **It says nothing about consumers.** Both observed sessions had far more reflow2 context than any consumer's agent will have, which makes them a BEST case.
- **It does not explain the `root-cause` author case by itself.** There, the skill was known, valued and still missed — the trigger named only the loud failure while the moment was a merely odd number. That is a RECOGNITION failure inside the same session, and it is a second cause rather than an instance of this one.

properties.statement:
ROUGH SIZING, and it is the number that set the build order for the requirement it hangs off.

MEASURED 2026-08-17 by comparing every property declared across `schema/*.yaml` against every parameter name any served tool accepts, read from the committed toolsnaps: 215 declared properties across 29 node types, 180 distinct tool parameter names, and 70 OF THE 215 (32%) HAVE A NAME NO SERVED TOOL ACCEPTS. Worst by count: Fragment 9/11, EnvironmentRule 7/9, Capability 6/10, Project 5/11, TemporalFact 4/8, DriftEvent 4/6, Question 4/8.

A SECOND READING FROM THE SAME SWEEP, sharper because it is exact rather than heuristic: `embedding_field` is declared 26 TIMES across 11 schema files, and NO CODE IN REFLOW2 TOUCHES EMBEDDINGS AT ALL. `dynograph-vector` is a direct dependency of reflow2-core and contributes exactly two functions, both statistics (`linear_regression_slope`, `mean`, in dimensions.rs); the entire HNSW index is unused and `search_design` is BM25 through `dynograph-text`. That is the reachability pattern one level up: not a field no tool can write, but a whole declared CAPABILITY nothing computes. Bears directly on `dec:idea-embeddings-adoption`, which is open.

⚠️ THE 32% IS AN OVERCOUNT AND MUST NOT BE QUOTED AS A DEFECT COUNT. It matches on NAME only, so it misses properties a tool sets under a different parameter name and properties written indirectly by tools like `record_change`, `reconcile_artifacts` and `link_artifact`. A live example from this same session: `TemporalFact.valid_from` appears in the unreachable list, and it IS writable — through `create_node`'s generic props, which the requirement explicitly says must NOT count as reachability.

WHY IT WAS RECORDED ANYWAY, and what it changed: the requirement as first written asked for a detector. This number says a detector run against a heuristic like this one would report dozens of findings on its first pass, most of them noise, which is how a new instrument loses its reader in one release. So the accepted build order became: draw the SPECIFIES edges, MEASURE PROPERLY AND SHOW ANTHONY, then build the detector. The rough number is the argument for not skipping the middle step, not a finding in its own right.

`acknowledge_gap` RECORDS THE USER'S JUDGEMENT AS AN ACCEPTED DECISION AND NEVER RECORDS WHOSE JUDGEMENT IT WAS. It takes `gap_id`, `affected_ids` and `reason`, and mints `decision:ack:<hash>` — settled intent with no `AUTHORED_BY role=approver` edge and no parameter to supply one. MEASURED 2026-08-23: acknowledging 50 gaps in one detect-and-ask pass produced 49 nodes that FAILED this project's own `check_intent_authority` gate, in one stroke. ⇒ THE ONE TOOL WHOSE ENTIRE PURPOSE IS TO RECORD THAT SOMEBODY DECIDED SOMETHING CANNOT SAY WHO. || IT IS THE SHARPEST FORM OF ITS OWN RULE. `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` and `req:intent-authority-is-checked` exist because settled intent must carry a name; the gate that enforces them says so in its own failure text — 'ask him, and record his answer with authored_by(role=approver)... adding the id to the grandfathered set is NOT [honest]'. An acknowledgement IS the owner's word by definition, and it is the one write that drops it. || THE FIX IS SMALL AND THE SHAPE IS ALREADY DECIDED ELSEWHERE: `acknowledge_gap` and `acknowledge_gaps` should take an optional `contributor_id` and draw the approver edge themselves, exactly as `claim_region` takes one. Backfilling by hand — which is what was done here, 49 `authored_by` calls after the fact — works and is the wrong shape: it depends on somebody noticing the gate went red, and a session that acknowledges three gaps rather than fifty may never look. || WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL NOW: acknowledgements were rare enough that the grandfathered set (356 nodes, a dated boundary) absorbed the historical ones, and no previous session had acknowledged enough gaps at once to push the failure past the noise. A defect that only shows at scale is one the tool's own dogfooding was too small to find. || SOURCE: measured 2026-08-23 on reflow2 0.38.0 while working a 77-gap list to 4.

properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-25, closing a line of investigation that had been reading the symptom as a user preference.

⚠️ PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED THE SAME DAY — READ THE NOTE AT THE FOOT BEFORE QUOTING THE HEADLINE. Left OPEN rather than closed, because only half of it moved.

ANTHONY'S FRAMING, which is what made the measurement possible: *"if I gave you the adopt task for storyflow, you should be able to see all the services (roughly equal to a subsystem). then inspect inside each service to see all the different scripts (getting into components) and then probably into the individual function and classes to determine the sub-component level and so on. **the hierarchy is there.**"*

── WHAT ADOPT ACTUALLY INSTRUCTS ──
`getting-started/skills/adopt/SKILL.md` grepped for every hierarchy word: **`contain_component` ZERO times. `nest` zero. `parent` zero. `subsystem` zero. `depth` zero.** `hierarchy_issues` appears ONCE, as a detector to run afterwards — so the skill checks a spine it never tells anyone to build. `level` appears once, in unrelated prose about test levels.

── WHAT ADOPT PRODUCED, measured across four designs ──

    design            components   containing another component
    dev_storyflow (ajs77)   101          0
    dev_storyflow (local)    84          0
    mapwright                15          0
    music_graph              25          2

⇒ **EVERY ADOPTED DESIGN IS FLAT.** dev_storyflow puts 101 components directly under the Project — and 10 of them declare `subsystem` or `system`, so the design CLAIMS a hierarchy that structurally does not exist. Contrast flo2, the only design in the sample shaped by genesis rather than adopt: 12 components, depth 3, fan-out 6/2/2/1/1, zero span-of-control violations.

⭐⭐ THE FLATNESS IS A SKILL DEFECT, NOT A USER PREFERENCE, AND THAT INVERTS AN EARLIER READING. Measurements taken hours before were read as "real designs are two rungs deep, so nobody needs depth" — with the caveat that it might be the absence of instruction. It is the absence of instruction: the systems adopt was pointed at HAVE observable hierarchies (storyflow's services ▸ scripts ▸ functions/classes), and adopt walks past them.

── WHY THIS IS A GAP IN ADOPT AND NOT A FAILURE OF THE IDEA ──
`dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition` (ACCEPTED 2026-07-23, derived with the user) already drew the line Anthony redrew today: *"A functional carving comes from the product's PURPOSE (a genesis input), not the code, and cuts across crate boundaries, so **adopt on the code can only re-derive the module view.**"* That is right and it is NOT an excuse for flatness. The module view is itself hierarchical — package ▸ module ▸ class — and recovering it is exactly what adopt is for. Adopt cannot produce the FUNCTIONAL carving; it can and should produce the STRUCTURAL one.

📌 AND A SECOND, RELATED GAP MEASURED EARLIER AND STILL OPEN: of 178 `ALLOCATED_TO` edges on reflow2's own design, **177 point at a leaf MODULE and exactly ONE at a subsystem**; `DECOMPOSES` is zero. Doctrine allocates functions at EACH level as it decomposes — functions to the system, then to subsystems, then to components. reflow2 records allocation at one level only, and the per-subsystem function counts are computed by walking CONTAINS rather than being stated. Anthony's own description of the process — *"you allocate functions to a system, then within a system allocate functions into subsystems or components and so on"* — is not recordable today.

⚠️ BOUNDS: four adopted designs, all produced by the same person with the same agent, so this measures how THIS adopt is followed rather than how it must be. The skill text is the stronger evidence — an instruction that is absent cannot be followed inconsistently. Nothing here says what the right depth for storyflow is; it says adopt never asked.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
🔻 PARTIAL SUPERSESSION — 2026-08-25, LATER THE SAME DAY (PR #335, merged as 323d11f)
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

**THE FIRST HALF IS NOW FALSE. THE SECOND HALF IS STILL TRUE.** Nothing above has been altered; this section is added beside it, because a closed measurement is evidence and an erased one is a hole.

❌ **FALSE AS OF #335:** *"adopt's instructions never mention nesting — `contain_component` ZERO times, no depth guidance."* PR #335 added a nesting step to Phase 1 of the adopt skill, in all three mirrors. One bullet, no code — `contain_component`, `Component.level` and `hierarchy_issues` all already existed and worked; the only thing missing was the instruction. **Re-grepping the skill today would contradict the paragraph above, which is why this note exists.**

✅ **STILL TRUE, and untouched by #335:** the four measured designs remain flat — nobody has re-adopted dev_storyflow, mapwright or music_graph, so 101/0, 84/0, 15/0 and 25/2 all still stand. The counterfactual run before the edit recovered depth `{1:1, 2:5, 3:73, 4:2}` on a SCRATCH graph only. **An instruction added is not a design re-derived.**

✅ **ALSO STILL TRUE:** the second gap in the 📌 paragraph — allocation recorded at one level only, `DECOMPOSES` zero. #335 did not touch it.

🛑 **NOT CLOSED, AND DELIBERATELY.** `valid_to` asserts the WHOLE thing stopped being true, and the measurement of what adopt PRODUCED is the durable half. It becomes closable when some real system is re-adopted under the new instruction and the component/nesting counts are taken again — that measurement has not been made, and claiming it would be exactly the false-green this project exists to prevent.

THE EXPERIMENT PLANNED IN JULY 2026 (BL-83b) WAS FINALLY RUN, 2026-08-20, on Anthony's word. Option (b): on a copy, contracts harvested, NO requirements recovered.

SETUP, with every precondition the decision named honoured: a scratch store outside the project tree that MINTED ITS OWN `graph_id` (818eb25bd9c0f823) rather than being told one; all access through `tools/reflow2_cli.py --graph <probe>` so no MCP write tool could touch the live graph; scope DERIVED from `git ls-files` minus two named rules rather than hand-picked — which is how `schema/` (11 files) came into scope, the exact directory a hand-picked sweep missed for eleven releases.

RECOVERED: 153 nodes, 411 edges — 69 components, 14 interfaces, 91 CONSUMES.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 THE HEADLINE IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE PREDICTION, AND IT IS THE USEFUL RESULT

The decision predicted "a RECOVERED CONTRACT SET reflow2's own graph does not have" and called it THE PRIZE. On raw counts it looked won — 91 CONSUMES against the real graph's 17, and 60 of 69 components on a boundary against 14 of 56.

**IT COLLAPSED ON INSPECTION.** Of 33 modules the scan said CONSUME `req-dyno-core-api`, the references are: `Value` ×76, `DynoError` ×18, `PropertySpec` ×1. **95 of 95 are TYPES. Not one call.** Separating behaviour from type-vocabulary across all five suppliers:

  dynograph_core        behaviour 0    types 47 modules
  dynograph_storage     behaviour 1 (graph — StorageEngine)   types 16
  dynograph_graph       behaviour 3 (allocate, flow, structure)
  dynograph_vector      behaviour 1 (dimensions)
  dynograph_resolution  behaviour 2 (ingest, seam)

⭐⭐ THOSE ARE EXACTLY THE EDGES REFLOW2'S GRAPH ALREADY HAD, redrawn by hand the day before from the same imports. **THE HAND-AUTHORED SPARSE SET WAS RIGHT AND THE MECHANICAL DENSE SET WAS WRONG.** Importing the 57 proposed edges would have added 33 to a supplier whose every reference is a type, made "what breaks if dyno-core changes?" answer "everything", and buried the five real dependencies in noise.

⇒ THE FINDING ABOUT ADOPT, which is what the decision said the run would MEASURE: **A MECHANICAL SCAN CANNOT DISTINGUISH IMPORTING A TYPE FROM CALLING BEHAVIOUR, AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE CONTENT OF A CONTRACT.** Adopt's Phase 1 says "both sides of every contract — this is where the structural findings come from", and it is right that the findings are there; it is wrong that reading imports gets you contracts. It gets you coupling, which is a different thing.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ WHAT IT DID FIND, AND IT WAS WORTH THE RUN: THREE CIRCULAR DEPENDENCIES

  mcp-service ↔ mcp-skills
  mcp-proxy ↔ mcp-shared
  core-artifact → core-temporal → core-verify → core-artifact

All three verified line by line and ALL THREE FIXED THE SAME DAY. **None was a bug.** A module cycle inside one crate is legal Rust and compiles silently forever — nothing in the build was ever going to mention them, and nothing had, for as long as shared mode has existed.

⚠️ AND THE FIRST PASS REPORTED A FOURTH THAT WAS NOT REAL. `core-graph ↔ core-hierarchy` came from a rustdoc link in a COMMENT — the exact trap the adopt skill warns about in as many words ("structure from imports and calls, never from prose"). Stripping comments removed 26 of 175 coupling edges, **15% of the model was prose**, and the correction did not merely delete a false finding: it REVEALED the real three-hop cycle the noise had masked.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📌 THREE FURTHER FACTS THE RUN ESTABLISHED

(1) **21 of 66 modules have NO Component in the live design**, including `cmp:seam`, which the CONSUMES repair had hit from the other direction the day before.
(2) **reflow2's source cannot be a BLIND adopt subject.** 207 files name design ids in their comments (`dec:ask-not-repair` alone appears 29 times). A code-only copy was made at /home/ajs7/project/reflow2-code-only with docs, skills and every top-level markdown stripped — and it is still not blind, because the intent is IN THE CODE. Deleting files cannot undo that.
(3) The predicted "NEAR-ZERO functional agreement" was not testable as stated: no capabilities were recovered, so `evaluate_allocation` returned `modularity: None` — which is the fix shipped the same day working correctly on an independent graph rather than manufacturing 1.00 over nothing.
