properties.name: Adopt trial on reflow2: depth IS recoverable — 4 rungs, hierarchy_issues 0, span of control clean everywhere — while the hand-built functional design violates span of control in 4 places. The functional carving is unrecoverable, confirmed twice
properties.statement:
RUN 2026-08-25 at Anthony's instruction, into a SCRATCH graph; the live design was untouched throughout (3,162 nodes before and after). No repo copy was needed — adopt reads source and writes a graph, so only the GRAPH must be separate, which `--graph-path` gives.

── PHASE 1, TWICE, AT TWO GRANULARITIES ──
First by directory (29 nodes), then at CONTRACT granularity per the skill's own rule (94 nodes — 1 Project, 81 Components, 6 Interfaces, 3 Verifications, 3 Artifacts; 182 DEPENDS_ON from imports). The skill calibrates reflow2 at ~100 nodes; the contract-granularity pass landed at 94 without that number being aimed at.

Scope DERIVED, not listed (`dec:coverage-scope-is-declared`): 625 of 697 tracked files, two named exclusions — the design graph itself (a design cannot be its own subject) and harness config.

⭐⭐ THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION ASKED: **DEPTH IS RECOVERABLE, AND ADOPT SIMPLY NEVER ASKS FOR IT.**

    ADOPT trial (recovered)        81 comps  depth {1:1, 2:5, 3:73, 4:2}   hierarchy_issues 0   span-of-control 0 over 7 ✓
    live design (dec:bl83a)        95 comps  depth {1:13, 2:80, 3:2}       hierarchy_issues 0   span-of-control 4 OVER 7
                                                                            (coherence-loop 28, agent-surface 25, reflow2 13, foundation 10)

No capability was added to adopt — the nesting step it omits was simply performed. `system ▸ subsystem ▸ component ▸ part` fell out of the artifact, and the recovered design obeys span of control EVERYWHERE while the deliberately-built functional one violates it in four places. **The structure derived by inspection is better-shaped than the one derived by hand**, and this is the first time reflow2's own decomposition has been checked against that rule.

📌 It is also the first non-toy use of the open ladder (#334): `part` is a rung that did not exist the previous day, and the trial's Project declares `[part, component, subsystem, system]`.

── AND `dec:bl83a` IS CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY, BY TWO INDEPENDENT ROUTES ──
That decision (accepted 2026-07-23) says *"a functional carving comes from the product's PURPOSE... so adopt on the code can only re-derive the module view."* Both routes agree:
1. **BY DIRECTORY** — 86 of reflow2-core's modules sit loose in one directory. The filesystem has no grouping for them.
2. **BY IMPORTS** — the dependency graph is STAR-SHAPED, not hierarchical. Fan-in: `foundation` 49, `graph` 42, `nodes` 41, then a long tail; **45% of core modules import ONLY those three hubs and nothing else.** Clustering that yields three hubs and a hundred leaves, never the eight functional subsystems.

⭐ AND THE STAR TOPOLOGY HAS A NAME. `impl DesignGraph` spans **44 of 57 top-level core modules (77%)**, and `graph.rs` alone carries **54 pub fns**. The coupling is star-shaped because nearly every operation is a method on one struct. That is a god-object finding about reflow2's own code that no previous pass surfaced, and it is exactly the class of structural finding adopt exists to produce.

🛑 A DETECTOR THAT IS BLIND TO ADOPT'S OWN OUTPUT. `evaluate_allocation` returned **all zeros** — `components: 0`, `modularity: null`, `unweighted_dependencies: 0` — on a design holding 81 components and 182 dependency edges. Cause read from source: it starts at `current_allocation_map()` (capability → component), so with no Capabilities every downstream number is zero. **Adopt Phase 1 produces structure without capabilities, and Phase 2 of the same skill instructs you to run a tool that must return zeros on it.** Related to but distinct from `fact:defect-allocation-health-is-green-over-an-empty-structure`: that one is about a green score over sparse data; this is a total blind spot over data of the wrong SHAPE.

── PHASE 4 DISCIPLINE APPLIED, AND IT CAUGHT MY OWN METHOD ──
`detect_defects` reported 20 findings, all `dead_end`. Held to the skill's test — *true of the system, or an error in the model?* — **most are MODEL ERROR.** `main.rs`, `shared.rs` and `nudge.rs` each declare modules with `mod` and use `use crate::` ZERO times, and my extraction only matched `use crate::`. So module DECLARATIONS were never turned into edges, and a binary entry point reads as unconnected. The finding is about the scan, not about reflow2.

⚠️ WHAT THIS TRIAL IS NOT. Phase 3 was deliberately skipped — **no Requirement was inferred from the code that would satisfy it**, which is the skill's one inviolable discipline. No dynamic phase (tests not run into `reconcile_verification`), no `coverage_report` sweep, checksums on three artifacts only. Interfaces were authored from knowledge of the system rather than extracted, so they are the weakest part of the model. This answers "can depth be recovered" and nothing more.

AGENT-GENERATED FEEDBACK from a Grok 4.6 session on one of Alex's projects (2026-08-13, two entries: a remaining-MVP readout and an encouragement capture session), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-14. Produced by telling the agent *"reflow2 is still a development project - please note any issues or gaps or opportunities to improve reflow2 at path/to/feedback.md"*.

⭐⭐⭐ THE REASON THIS NODE EXISTS: **FOUR OF ITS ITEMS WERE INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED BY A DIFFERENT AGENT (Claude Opus 5), ON A DIFFERENT GRAPH (reflow2's own), IN A SESSION THAT HAD NOT READ THE FEEDBACK.** One agent reporting friction is an opinion; two agents on different models and different designs hitting the same edges is a defect report.

═══ ✅ CORROBORATED — hit in this session before the file was read ═══

**1. THE NEAR-DUPLICATE GUARD FIRES ON SIBLINGS AND ACROSS NODE TYPES** (their items 1 and 2, second entry). Six refusals in one capture session, every one of them a genuine non-duplicate:
  · a Requirement refused because its OWN governing Decision was "close"
  · a Capability refused because the Requirement it satisfies was "close"
  · a Requirement refused because a Capability created MINUTES EARLIER in the same batch was "close"
  · one Decision refused TWICE, each refusal naming a DIFFERENT batch of near-matches — the declared ones are excluded and the next-nearest surface, so `distinct_from` grows by retry
⇒ **A Requirement, the Decision that governs it and the Capability that satisfies it are the GOLDEN THREAD. They are supposed to share wording.** A guard that reads them as candidate duplicates fires hardest on exactly the capture pattern the skills prescribe. Their words: *"Each refusal named a sibling I had just created, not a true duplicate."*

**2. `add_decision` CANNOT MERGE WITHOUT RESENDING THE BODY** (their item 3, second entry). Schema requires `id` + `name` + `decision`. Confirmed by cost, not just by reading: prepending a DECIDED header to three already-written decisions this session meant resending ~7 KB bodies verbatim each time. Their report adds the sharper risk: **the loop hint on such a merge still reads *"a Decision lands `proposed`"* even when merging an ACCEPTED node** — observed here too, status correctly stayed `accepted`, but the hint invites an agent to "fix" a status that was never wrong.

**3. CAPTURING CORRECTLY INFLATES THE LOOP DEBT** (their item 5, second entry). Their measurement: 62 → 66 never-asked gaps after a capture session, because each new `planned` Capability immediately owes a verification it cannot yet have. **Measured identically here: 74 → 79 gaps across this session's captures.** Their sentence is exact: *"this session created more of them by doing capture correctly."*

**4. `get_node` MISSES SILENTLY** (their item 5, first entry). REPRODUCED ON REFLOW2'S OWN GRAPH: `get_node {node_type: Project, id: "proj:does-not-exist-12345"}` returns `{"node": null}` with no hint — **and this graph holds exactly ONE Project, `proj:reflow2`.** That is precisely the case they describe: *"A miss on a type that has total: 1 should name the existing id."* ⚠️ A NEARBY EDGE, hit here the same day: passing `node_id` instead of `id` is REFUSED loudly and helpfully (*"unknown field `node_id`, expected `node_type` or `id`"*). So a malformed ARGUMENT is diagnosed and a missing NODE is not — the wrong way round, since the second is the commoner mistake.

═══ ⚠️ NOT REPRODUCED HERE — recorded so it is not treated as confirmed ═══

**`get_instructions` TRUNCATION** (their item 6, first entry): they report ~22.6 KB cut mid-sentence, with the standing rules after the cut never arriving — serious, because the repo file is only a pointer. **Called here the same day and the payload arrived COMPLETE**, ending cleanly on its closing line. ⇒ Likely CLIENT-SPECIFIC (an MCP payload budget in their harness) rather than server-side, which makes it a worse defect in one way: it is invisible from this side and the affected agent cannot tell that rules are missing. Their mitigation — serve it in named sections — survives regardless of cause.

═══ 📌 THEIR ITEMS NOT YET ASSESSED HERE ═══

First entry: (1) *"what is left to build?" is not a first-class query* — `what_next` ranks open DECISIONS, and a graph with one open Decision and a large build backlog gets nothing useful; four sources disagreed (Decision prose, Capability `status`, computed delivery, the repo). (2) status-vs-computed-delivery drift. (3) top gaps are hygiene, not product work — wrong default ranking for *"what do we build next?"*. (4) two sources of truth on one increment. (7) orientation tax. (8) *"the loop and the delivery plan share a dashboard and they should not."* (9) **decision-as-checklist is invisible to the temporal axis** — they propose a detector for an accepted Decision whose statement is a running delivery list with no `SCHEDULED_FOR` edges. Second entry: (4) `detect_gaps(scope)` explodes via Project CONTAINS at depth 3 and returns unrelated planned work rather than the seed's own thread.

📌 THEIR OWN PROCESS GAPS, WORTH KEEPING BECAUSE THEY ARE HONEST: they did not run `compare_designs` or `detect_gaps`, guessed a Project id rather than scanning, and did not export after graph writes — the last being the same omission `fact:second-user-first-run-report-2026-08-13` is about.

⚠️ THEIR KIT SIDECAR READ `0.11.0` / `0ec473e` (a 2026-07-25 tarball) WHILE THE LIVE SERVER SERVED A MUCH NEWER SURFACE. **Third independent signal that consumers run stale kits** — with `fact:second-user-notes-2026-08-14-two-items-already-fixed`, which concluded the same about Alex from different evidence. Their suggestion: write the running binary identity where `loop_status` or `graph_report` already expose it (`served_by` exists on `graph_report`).

properties.name: MEASURED across 93 sessions of two OTHER reflow2 projects: 88% of skill loads had no slash command behind them, so agents DO self-invoke at scale — and what predicts a skill's load count is being named in the always-injected SessionStart hook, not being in the served catalogue
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-29 over the Claude Code transcripts on the peer box (ajs77), read-only: `dev-storyflow` 91 sessions / 4157 real user turns / 21993 tool calls / 5240 reflow2 tool calls, spanning 2026-07-29 to 2026-08-29; `OpenLotR2` 2 sessions / 52 user turns / 440 reflow2 tool calls. 175 and 7 skill loads respectively, via `get_skill` (151) and the `Skill` tool (24).

═══ ⭐ IT REFUTES THE STRONG FORM OF fact:a-skill-is-loaded-only-when-something-already-in-hand-demands-it ═══

That node says an agent loads a skill when something already in its hand demands it "and otherwise substantially not at all", generalising from ONE session where 3 of 5 loads were user-typed. At n=93 sessions the shape is the opposite: **154 of 175 loads (88%) had NO matching slash command anywhere earlier in the session.** Agents self-invoke reflow2 skills constantly. Where a matching command did exist, the median gap was 1 user turn, so those are genuinely command-driven and the split is clean.

The WEAK form survives and is what the data supports: loading is driven by an instruction already in context. reflow2 HAS such a mechanism — the SessionStart hook and the MCP server instructions — and it is working. The earlier node's error was treating 'no reflow2 TOOL demands a skill' as 'nothing demands a skill'.

═══ ⭐⭐ WHAT ACTUALLY PREDICTS THE COUNT: THE HOOK, NOT THE CATALOGUE ═══

    skill              loads   /cmd typed   ratio
    where-am-i            42        5        8.4x   ← NAMED IN THE SessionStart HOOK
    brainstorm            22       10        2.2x
    capture-session       19       18        1.1x   ← essentially all user-typed
    link-artifacts        15        0         —
    capture-intent        15        0         —
    revise-design         12        0         —

The MCP server instructions name ALL 23 skills and usage across them is 42..0 — a catalogue that lists everything predicts nothing. The SessionStart hook names only three (genesis, adopt, where-am-i), and `where-am-i` is the most-loaded skill by a factor of two over anything else, self-invoked 8.4x more often than it is asked for. The other two hook-named skills are one-time by nature (genesis 0, adopt 2), which is the expected reading rather than a counterexample.

⭐ This is direct evidence for `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue`: an always-injected surface moves behaviour, a catalogue read once does not.

═══ NEVER LOADED IN 91 SESSIONS ═══

ci-gate, genesis, kpp-proposal, link-ideas, optimize, parallel-work, plan-increments, root-cause.

🛑 FOUR OF THOSE EIGHT ARE NOT EVIDENCE OF ANYTHING. `genesis` and `ci-gate` are one-time setup and the project is long past both; `adopt` at 2 fits the same shape. `root-cause` shipped in v0.42.0 on 2026-08-28 and could not have been used in a window that mostly precedes it. The four that are genuinely unexplained by situation are **kpp-proposal, link-ideas, optimize, parallel-work, plan-increments** (five, on a stricter reading).

═══ ⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH ═══

- Whether a never-loaded skill went unused because nothing triggered it or because its SITUATION never arose. Nothing here separates those, and for plan-increments and parallel-work the situation genuinely may not have arisen. This is the same unused-vs-unreachable ambiguity `dec:bl-155` names for tools.
- Causation for the hook. `where-am-i` is also the most generically useful skill in the set, so hook-presence and intrinsic usefulness are confounded. A second skill added to the hook would test it, and that is the cheap discriminating experiment.
- Attribution was measured as loads-per-skill against commands-for-that-same-skill, NOT by turn adjacency. Two earlier adjacency-based passes returned a false 100% self-invoked because Claude Code records tool results as `type: user` and records a slash command and its expansion as two separate user turns, either of which resets a naive 'previous user turn' flag. The ratio method avoids both.
- OpenLotR2 at 2 sessions is far too small to read alone; it is reported for shape only.

properties.statement:
ALEX'S EARLIER GROK BUILD SESSION NOTES (~2026-08-07/08, binary 0.24.0, a real monorepo, 361 nodes / 621 edges) TRIAGED AGAINST 0.32.1 — a SECOND file, distinct from the 2026-08-14 report already captured as `art:alex-grok-feedback-2026-08-14`. Confirmed distinct by checksum: the 08-14 artifact is `sha256:0318c290…` and this one is `sha256:007e2868…`. It had never been triaged.

⭐ HIS TOP-PRIORITY ASK DID NOT REPRODUCE, AND THAT IS THE HEADLINE. §1.1: `set_decision_status` failing with `Node not found` immediately after a successful `add_decision`, 'especially in a parallel tool batch', which he ranked #1 of six and called 'top pain'. TESTED HERE on 0.32.1 against the shared server, twice: a 2-call batch (create + set status in one message) and a 6-call batch (three creates + three status sets interleaved in one message). ALL EIGHT CALLS SUCCEEDED; every decision came back `proposed` from the create and `accepted` from the set. Scratch nodes deleted afterwards.

⚠️ NOT REPRODUCED IS NOT REFUTED, and three differences could each explain it: he ran 0.24.0 and this is 0.32.1, eight minor versions apart; his harness is Grok Build and this is Claude Code, which may serialise MCP calls within a turn even when they are issued together; and his load was heavier than a six-call batch. ⇒ The honest status is that the reported failure does not occur in THIS configuration, and nobody has yet tested the one where it did.

WHAT IS ALREADY ANSWERED, so it does not need re-asking:
• §2.3 (revising an accepted Requirement by re-calling `add_requirement` erodes intent silently; he asked for a warning) — SHIPPED in v0.32.0 as the constructor `revision` block, which reports the properties overwritten WITH their prior values in full. Exactly his ask, arrived independently from four other reports.
• §4.3 (Capabilities have no `deferred`/`dropped`, so agents write DROPPED into the description) — SETTLED by Anthony as no cancelled state, ever. The ask is declined rather than open.
• §3.1 (large results truncated, `get_instructions` named) — measured during the 08-14 triage and attributed to HIS CLIENT rather than the server.

WHAT SURVIVES AS GENUINELY OPEN, in his own priority order:
① `get_node` BY ID WITHOUT `node_type` (his #3). An agent holds an id from `search_design` and not its type; the lookup then fails. Distinct from the already-fixed 'unknown node_type is refused rather than answered null'.
② SESSION-SCOPED `loop_status` (his #4): 'always dirty on mature graphs — agents ignore or thrash', asking for a 'debt introduced this session' filter. ⭐ CORROBORATED FIRST-HAND AND HARD: across this entire session `loop_status` reported the identical 80 unsurfaced gaps and 16 structural defects from first call to last, and the only way to say anything useful was to compute the delta by hand and report 'unchanged from session start' each time. The per-CONTRIBUTOR scoping that exists is a different axis and does not answer this.
③ IDEMPOTENT LINK HELPERS with a result flag (his #5) — whether re-calling `satisfies`/`allocate`/`contains` is a no-op or an error is undocumented.
④ A HARNESS-AGNOSTIC SESSION-END NUDGE (his #6): on Grok Build `loop_status` reports `nudge: absent` and there is no alternative, so under load agents capture and skip detect-and-ask. He suggests a `session_wrap_up` tool an agent can call. Note this is the SAME failure the loop nudge exists to prevent, arriving on the harness that cannot host it.
⑤ OPTIONAL `status` ON `add_decision` (his #2) — and this is CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY by dev_storyflow's dragon Boss the same week ('there is no one-call path to an accepted decision', six times in one session). ⚠️ BUT BOTH RUN INTO ACCEPTED DOCTRINE: `add_decision` deliberately stopped defaulting to `accepted` on 2026-07-25, and `dec:certainty-derived` holds that moving a status is the owner's word. Alex concedes the point himself — 'default proposed is correct for honesty' — and asks only for an optional override. That makes this a question for Anthony rather than a defect.

HIS FRAMING TO KEEP, and it is a priority instruction rather than a finding: 'DO NOT spend meaningful engineering effort on one-time migration' from the early-adopter era (dropping old skill folders, untracking RocksDB layout, rewriting long AGENTS.md). 'Most users will never have to do that upgrade.' Invest instead in keeping future upgrades boring — install.sh replacing binary and kit while never touching graphs, which he names as already the right model.

properties.statement:
THE THIRD OBSERVATION OF `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`, and the first from OUTSIDE this repo — followed within hours by a fourth, in the session that read it.

WHAT dev_storyflow REPORTED. Anthony asked its driving agent directly whether it was using reflow2 to the fullest. It answered no, and wrote the account from inside the failure. Over ~12 hours it built a four-lane feature across two repos — a library, two gates, three endpoints, two panels, two browser probes — and REGISTERED ZERO ARTIFACTS until challenged. Used constantly: search_design, get_node, create_node, create_edges, export_graph, loop_status, get_skill. Used once, too late: propagate_from — and that single call immediately found a stale Interface no grep would have surfaced. NEVER USED: detect_gaps, gap_to_prompt, impact-check, detect_defects, reconcile_artifacts, coverage_report, evidence_report.

⭐ ITS OWN DIAGNOSIS, AND IT IS THE FINDING: "the tools worked — I STOPPED REACHING FOR THEM, and that is a design problem, not a discipline problem." Seven reasons, most load-bearing first: (1) `loop_hint` is on every response, identical and enormous, so it became wallpaper — it appeared ~40 times and the number moved by one or two all day; (2) 391 is not a number anybody can act on, it reads as someone else's permanent backlog, where THREE GAPS ON THE NODE I JUST EDITED would have been a task; (3) skills are PULL, and the thing that would tell you to load one is itself a lookup you must remember to make — by the time you recognise an impact-check situation you are three files into the refactor; (4) for CODE questions grep genuinely beats the graph, and that correct local habit hardened into skipping the graph for DESIGN questions too; (5) write-time friction (add_change_event cannot set rationale; get_node needs node_type) trained it to route around typed tools, and once routing around one you stop reaching for its NEIGHBOURS — add_artifact was a neighbour it never tried; (6) skipping has NO COST AT THE MOMENT OF SKIPPING — code compiled, 93 tests passed, ratchets stayed green, and the only thing that got worse was the graph's accuracy, which is invisible from inside the build; (7) the framing is "the loop OWES" — bookkeeping FOR reflow2 — and nothing in it says THIS WILL SAVE YOU AN HOUR, which propagate_from then did inside one call.

⭐⭐ THE CORROBORATION, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A FACT AND NOT A REPORT. The Claude Code session that READ this feedback reproduced FOUR of the seven reasons on reflow2's own repo, the same day, with the hooks installed and the skills served: (i) `loop_hint` came back on nearly every call and was acted on ZERO times — reasons 1 and 2; (ii) a skill was loaded only when the Stop hook forced it, and it then reported the impact step had been skipped twice — reason 3; (iii) a Decision was edited with no `record_change`, and nothing failed — reason 6; (iv) THREE REGISTERED ARTIFACTS were edited and none reconciled, caught by `reflow2_check.py` and NOT by the agent. Two independent agents, two fleets, one wall.

⭐ WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGED BEHAVIOUR THAT DAY, MEASURED: three BLOCKING gates (artifact checksum drift, intent authority, toolsnap goldens) each produced an immediate fix. Zero passive hints did. The Stop hook worked BECAUSE IT BLOCKED, not because it spoke. That is the discriminator this fact exists to record — the evidence favours FEWER, HARDER interventions over more, softer ones, and it is this requirement's own candidate mechanism (2) rather than (1).

🛑 AND THE ASK THAT CANNOT BE BUILT AS WRITTEN. Its highest-rated fix (b) was "fire on the first Edit of a file that IS A REGISTERED ARTIFACT, saying what is downstream". `tools/loop_nudge.py` CANNOT DO THIS AND SAYS SO: the hook deliberately does not read the graph, because the session's own MCP server holds the single-writer lock and the committed export can be a session stale. Its comments already rule out the sibling case in the same words — "that rules out the spec's 'an artifact checksum drift names link-artifacts' AS LITERALLY WRITTEN: drift is a fact about the graph versus the disk, and nothing here can see either". So the hook can only key on the session's OWN OP TALLY. The thing that CAN read the design is the GATE, which runs outside the lock against the committed export — exactly the surface that caught the unreconciled artifacts.

BOUND, stated rather than glossed: reason (4)'s claim that grep beats the graph for code questions is the agent's own judgement and is probably right, but nothing here measures it. And the four reproduced reasons were observed by the agent reporting them, which is the same self-report weakness the first two observations of this requirement carry.

MEASURED 2026-08-23, and worth more than the report that produced it. dev_storyflow filed `detect_gaps` as returning 328,654 characters with "no `limit`, no `offset`, no `brief`" and named it the loop's central call. IT WAS ALREADY FIXED: `budget_chars` (default 30,000) with a three-tier degrade landed in f0ce3e1 (#303) at 01:29 THE SAME DAY, roughly eighteen hours before the session that filed it. The reporter was running a pre-#303 binary.

THE REPORTER NAMED THE CAUSE IN ITS OWN ENVIRONMENT NOTE WITHOUT CONNECTING IT: "`.reflow2/kit-version.json` absent — could not read a version." An agent that cannot name the version it is running cannot tell a live defect from a closed one, so it spends its credibility on bugs that are already fixed — and the maintainer spends time re-verifying them. No amount of reply budgeting fixes that.

THE SAME TRAP IS LIVE ON THIS SIDE, and this session hit it: `loop_status.served_by` reported `stale: true` — the shared server's executable had been replaced since it started, so every computed rollup it returned came from code no longer on disk. reflow2 CAN say this about itself and does, in one tool. What a CONSUMER gets is a file that may simply be absent.

WHAT IS OWED, and it is small: a served surface that answers "what version am I talking to?" without depending on a file the installer may not have written. `loop_status.served_by.reflow2_version` already computes it; nothing puts it where a friction report would pick it up.

MEASURED 2026-08-09 ON THIS GRAPH, ON A REAL MERGE ANTHONY AUTHORISED. `propose_heal` offered to merge the owner's two Contributor nodes and CHOSE THE WRONG SURVIVOR: keep `ctr:anthony` (8 edges, no description), destroy `who:ajs` (161 edges, the full description, and the id form `add_contributor`'s own parameter description gives as its example).

⭐ AND IT SAID SO ITSELF, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. Verbatim from `would_destroy`: "deleting 'who:ajs' keeps only 'ctr:anthony's properties; also replaced: description. THE ALPHABET CHOSE THE VICTIM: both carry the same provenance, so the smaller id survived (BL-29) — nothing about the design decided which of these two lives." The disclosure is exemplary and it is the only reason the merge was not applied as proposed. A tool that names its own arbitrariness is doing the right thing; a tool whose arbitrariness DECIDES is still wrong.

WHY THIS IS EVIDENCE AND NOT AN OPINION: `dec:merge-survivor-provenance` (ACCEPTED) says the survivor is chosen by provenance with id breaking ties. Here both nodes carry the SAME provenance, so the tie-break ran — and the tie-break is alphabetical, which has no relationship to which node the design actually depends on. `fact:defect-merge-survivor-ignores-priority-and-status` already contradicts that decision and the pair has been a standing structural defect (`heal:7456a4d260ca45ce`). THIS IS THE FIRST TIME THE DEFECT HAS BEEN OBSERVED COSTING SOMETHING ON A REAL MERGE rather than argued in the abstract.

A CHEAP SIGNAL THE RULE COULD READ, offered because naming the fix is more useful than naming the fault: EDGE COUNT. 161 against 8 is not a close call, and neither is "has a description" against "has none". Degree is already computable and would have picked correctly here without any new vocabulary. Provenance-then-alphabet is the rule that produced the wrong answer; provenance-then-degree would not have.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY DONE: the merge was performed BY HAND — `record_change` first so the snapshot holds `ctr:anthony` and all 9 of its edges, then the 8 AUTHORED_BY edges re-pointed to `who:ajs` with `role` and `acted_at` preserved and checked for pre-existing overlap (none, so nothing was overwritten), then the node deleted. `detect_defects` went 7 findings to 6 with the duplicate gone.

📝 ONE THING THIS DOES NOT SHOW, stated so the finding is not read wider than it is: `propose_heal --conservative` proposed NOTHING for this duplicate, and only `--aggressive` offered the merge. So the dangerous proposal is not the default. What the default gives instead is silence on a duplicate a human had explicitly asserted, which is its own question.

properties.name: REPRODUCED: two exports between commits sever the lineage chain and turn the design gate RED — the collision is real, not an artifact of committing. And the hypothesis that 'no commit, no push' avoids it is FALSIFIED, because the chain is built from the FILE, not from git
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-25 at main `8ba3198`, deliberately falsifying an agent hypothesis rather than confirming it.

═══ THE HYPOTHESIS THAT WAS WRONG ═══

The agent proposed that `dec:idea-does-the-graph-write-itself-through-to-the-repo-on-every-change`'s unresolved collision might be ILLUSORY, reasoning: the proposal is *"no commit, no push"*, `dec:export-once-per-PR` is a rule about COMMITS, and a working-tree file that is never committed cannot violate a rule about commits.

❌ **FALSIFIED.** The chain is built from **the file already at the target path**, not from git. Writing that file twice between commits chains the second export through an intermediate that will never enter history — whether or not anything is committed in between.

═══ THE REPRODUCTION ═══

One graph write, export, one more graph write (a single AUTHORED_BY edge), export again — then run the gate against the working file:

    committed hash   sha256:29d103c800e9...
    working prev     sha256:00255feac6d8...   <- the intermediate, never committed
    working hash     sha256:7b4e7b2c4ee1...

    FAIL  LINEAGE  'docs/design/reflow2.json' does not link to the export it
                   replaced: it records 00255fea... where 29d103c8... is expected.
    reflow2 check: FAILED — 1 finding(s), 10 note(s).

This is exactly cause (2) named in `reflow2_check`'s own message: *"The design was exported MORE THAN ONCE since the last commit, chaining through an intermediate that will never be committed."* ⇒ **AUTO-EXPORT ON EVERY CHANGE, WRITING TO THE COMMITTED PATH, TURNS THE DESIGN GATE RED ON EVERY BRANCH.** The blocker is real and it is not about discipline; it is arithmetic on a hash chain.

The documented fix works and was confirmed: `git checkout <path>` then export ONCE — the gate returns to OK.

═══ ⭐⭐ AND THE SAME EXPERIMENT NAMES THE WAY OUT ═══

The chain breaks only because the durability write and the archival write TARGET THE SAME PATH. They are different acts with different audiences — one is "do not lose this", the other is "this is the record of the branch" — and nothing requires them to share a file.

**Auto-export to a SEPARATE path** (`.reflow2/<graph>.autosave.json`, gitignored) and the collision disappears entirely: the committed export keeps its one-per-PR chain untouched, while the durable copy is refreshed as often as anybody likes. Measured cost of a save: **265 ms**. No change to the lineage rule, no git awareness in the core, and `dec:export-once-per-pr` stays exactly as written.

⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: whether a gitignored autosave is a good enough durable copy to hang the inversion on — it is not in version control, so it survives a crash but not a lost working tree. That is the same question `dec:idea-what-guarantees-the-export-if-the-export-is-the-only-durable-copy` asks, and this only removes the lineage objection from it.

⚠️ BOUNDS: one design, one path, one machine, debug binary. The gate was exercised in its pre-commit form (working file vs HEAD); the CI form (HEAD vs HEAD~1) was not separately reproduced, though `_export_pair` states both use one rule.
[BL-105] The degraded surface ignores --http, so the outage it exists to explain is silent again on the new transport — shipped in v0.14.0. FIXED 2026-07-26, same day

So when the graph is already held and --http was asked for, reflow2 serves its one-tool explanation on stdin/stdout while every session that was told to dial http://\u2026:8787/ gets connection-refused. That is precisely the failure req:never-silently-absent (accepted, field-reported by the StoryFlow fleet) exists to prevent \u2014 *\"exiting at startup makes the outage indistinguishable from reflow2 was never configured\"* \u2014 reintroduced on the transport added two commits later. Fix shape (small, and the same shape as the Ok arm): branch the Err arm on cli.http too \u2014 serve DegradedService over serve_http when an address was given, stdio otherwise. Both arms then answer on the transport that was requested, which is the invariant worth naming in the code. Second half, and the part that keeps it fixed: tools/test_degraded_server.py has *no* occurrence of http \u2014 hold the graph, start a server with --http, and assert an HTTP client still handshakes and still receives reflow2_unavailable with the reason. Recorded as ver:degraded-follows-transport (failing, observed by hand, not yet automated) against cap:degraded-surface, whose stdio check ver:degraded-surface remains honestly green. Size estimate carried from the row: ~~S~~."}

properties.statement: [BL-110] Nothing computes whether the design ever reached git, and git is where the design lives
properties.value: {"evidence": "*Found by me, 2026-07-29, answering Anthony's question \u2014 \"is reflow2 git aware? when an agent calls a reflow2 skill, does it remind the agent to commit and push?\" The honest answer is that reflow2 is git-aware everywhere except the surface that would act on it. Not yet in the graph; belongs in capture-intent when the server is reachable, likely as a requirement rather than a defect.* Where the awareness is real: .reflow2/graph is gitignored, machine-local and single-writer, so the committed export is the only copy anyone else can see; merge.rs ships a driver git itself invokes, taking its ancestor from git merge-base; reflow2_check.py reads git to validate the export hash chain against HEAD~1 ([BL-107]); and sync.rs:91 hands an agent literal recovery steps \u2014 *\"This is not a merge conflict and git will not catch it\u2026 1. git pull --rebase\"* \u2014 on a stale-export refusal. Where it is absent is the loop. report.rs, where loop debt is computed, contains zero occurrences of git or export, so loop_status is structurally incapable of reporting that the graph is ahead of the committed file. The nudge strings never mention committing. The Rust core never invokes git at all \u2014 no Command::new(\"git\") anywhere in crates/. So an agent can design productively for an entire session, never export, never commit, and nothing in the loop notices that the work exists on exactly one machine \u2014 the same failure mode as a stale seat, one layer up, and the one the gitignored-graph architecture makes possible by construction. This is load-bearing for work now in flight: req:graph-indexes-snapshots and dec:epoch-roadmap-storage's (c-refined) shape both divide labour as *git stores the snapshots, the graph owns the index* ([roadmap-and-planned-epochs.md](roadmap-and-planned-epochs.md)) \u2014 a division with nothing verifying that git received its half, before the first planned epoch is ever written. Fix shape, and it is cheap: the graph knows its write generation and the export carries content_hash; comparing the live graph's hash against the committed export's answers *\"is there undeposited work\"* without any new vocabulary, and reflow2_check.py already proves the git side is reachable from the Python tier. Two constraints that must hold. First, git may be absent and its absence is not an error \u2014 the answer is skipped, never guessed, exactly as BL-107's gate already does outside a working tree. properties.statement: [BL-114] A detector's message claims more than the detector checked
properties.value: {"evidence": "*Found 2026-07-31 by an adopt pass over a real design-review document in another organisation \u2014 a pre-construction design with no code \u2014 and independently reproduced in reflow2's own graph the same day. A 63-node cluster was likewise reported *\"disconnected from the rest of the design\"* while its parent subsystems carried DEPENDS_ON edges outward and everything shared one Project. In every case the machinery was right and the sentence was wrong. Reproduced here the same day: disconnected_community fired on a Requirement that had just gained an acknowledgement Decision, reporting an island for two nodes sharing the Project \u2014 the [orphan-requirements-hide-from-heal] shape from the other side. This is not a detector bug; it is the class req:schema-prose-is-checked already names \u2014 prose that promises breadth the code does not implement, which is exactly why Project.mode's description was fixed at the source rather than annotated. Same defect, different surface: there it was schema prose, here it is finding prose. Fix shape: every finding states the edge kinds it considered \u2014 *\"no runtime (PROVIDES/CONSUMES/DEPENDS_ON) path; containment edges exist but do not count\"*. Cheap, changes no computation, and it is the difference between a finding a user acts on and one they learn to distrust. The orphan_node half may additionally be a real rule gap: DOCUMENTS arguably *is* ownership for artifact_type of document/spec/diagram, and if so the detector should say so rather than every design document reading as an orphan forever. Decide that separately from the wording. THE CONTROL EXPERIMENT THIS ITEM LACKED, supplied 2026-07-31 by a case study designed end to end through reflow2: propagate_change returned impacted: [] for a change that materially activated a regulatory Constraint sitting three nodes away \u2014 correct given the edges, badly wrong about the world, because the CONSTRAINS edge had never been drawn. Later in the SAME session, same tool, ~16 nodes both times, with edges present, it produced a genuinely valuable answer with correct upstream hop chains that caught two requirements about to be orphaned. Edge density, not graph size, decided whether the tool was useful \u2014 and the output is identical for \"nothing depends on this\" and \"you never drew the edges\", which is the overwhelmingly common case early in a design's life, i.e. exactly when users decide whether to trust the feature. Same disease as this item: the machinery was right and the sentence claimed more than it checked. Fix, one line: when few or no nodes are impacted, report the seeds' connectivity \u2014 *\"0 impacted; note these seeds carry 2 edges total, so this design may be under-linked rather than genuinely isolated\"*. The data already existed: detect_defects had ALREADY flagged that exact node set as a disconnected community in the same session. Two detectors knew and neither told the tool that mattered. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION OF THIS ITEM'S PROPOSED FIX, arrived at from the other end (2026-07-31, same case study): disconnected_community's SUGGESTION does not know about the detector's own SELECTIVITY. Connectivity is measured over traceability edges; MITIGATES/RISKS/CONTRADICTS do not participate. So a user told to bridge the island draws a TRUE edge of a type that does not count, re-runs, and gets nothing back \u2014 not \"closer\", not \"that edge does not count\", nothing. This is exactly the fix already proposed above, reached independently: *state the edge kinds considered*. Plus a refinement worth taking: if the island already carries non-traceability edges outward, say so \u2014 *\"semantically connected to the design but structurally isolated\"* is a completely different finding from *\"isolated\"*, and in that project it was the true one. Four artifacts reported *\"realizes nothing\"*: a doc that DOCUMENTS the project, a doc that DOCUMENTS a capability, one that is PRODUCES-d by a Verification *and* DOCUMENTS, and a MIDI corpus that SATISFIES a requirement. properties.statement: [BL-124] acknowledge_defect can never close a disconnected_community, and each attempt writes a junk Decision
properties.value: {"evidence": "*Found 2026-07-31 by a case-study project designed end-to-end through reflow2 (quantum_benchmarking_initiative), confirmed in this codebase and reproduced live in that graph \u2014 the cluster has grown 8 -> 9 -> 10 nodes across attempts.* The two documented behaviours are individually right and jointly fatal. acknowledge_defect (crates/reflow2-core/src/heal.rs:490) creates the review Decision and then draws a GOVERNED_BY edge from *every* affected node to it, deliberately, so \"the review is reachable from the design\". disconnected_community (heal.rs:~734) computes its id by hashing the category with the affected set. For most categories that is fine, because the acknowledgement does not alter what the detector measures. For this one it measures precisely what the acknowledgement modifies: cluster membership. The Decision joins the island it acknowledges, enlarging it by one, minting a new id, resurrecting the defect one node larger \u2014 without limit. So an entire category is permanently unclosable, and the failure is the exact one acknowledge_defect exists to prevent \u2014 its own docs say the point is that \"a list that can never reach zero gets skimmed\". The case study ended three sessions running with loop_status reporting \"1 structural defect outstanding\" for a defect that had been reviewed, understood and accepted, while generate_bridge was correctly *refused* because nothing in the design models the relationship. The honest disposition is the one the bug blocks. Fix shapes, any one sufficient: (1) exclude acknowledgement Decisions from design_network() \u2014 an acknowledgement is a statement *about* the design, not a participant in it, and this also stops them distorting centrality, SPOF and coupling wherever a review has been recorded; (2) compute the defect id from the affected set MINUS acknowledgement nodes; (3) store the affected ids as a property rather than as edges. (1) is the most correct and the widest, and the caller list settles it: design_network() (crates/reflow2-core/src/structure.rs:220) has three callers, not one \u2014 heal.rs:732 (disconnected_community, the reported symptom), propagate.rs:389 (betweenness / centrality) and surprises.rs:88 (surprising_connections). So acknowledgement Decisions are silently perturbing centrality and surprise detection too, in every design where a review has ever been recorded \u2014 unreported distortion in two more places that nobody has looked at. Option (2) would fix the visible symptom at the hash and leave the other two callers still wrong. *Caller list contributed by the case study and verified here.* THE PRACTICAL ARGUMENT FOR PRIORITY, from the same source: that project has now spent FOUR sessions unable to close a defect it correctly understood and correctly judged should be accepted. It tried the acknowledgement route \u2014 blocked by this livelock. It tried the bridge route \u2014 blocked by the selectivity problem folded into [BL-114], which advises an edge whose only correct forms do not count. Both correct routes are shut, so the honest disposition is unreachable by any path, and loop_status reports outstanding debt that is actually a reviewed and settled judgement. That is the skimmed-list failure the acknowledge tools exist to prevent, produced by the tool built to prevent it. Relates to [BL-114] (same detector, message half) and to the review-expiry tension already recorded on req:review-expires-when-what-it-judged-changes: that one expires too *late* on content, this one expires too *eagerly* on membership, and both come from keying a review to a hash of a set. BUILT 2026-08-01 \u2014 fix shape (1), at design_network(). A new is_review_record id rule excludes the decision:ack: prefix that both acknowledgement paths already mint and already strip to recognise their own records, so it is the codebase's existing marker rather than a new convention. ver:acknowledgement-not-structure passing, 5 cases, written before the fix: the two bug cases failed and all three counterweights passed. THE MEASUREMENT SETTLED WHAT THIS ITEM ONLY ASSERTED, and corrected it in both directions (tools/bl124_instrument.py, run on reflow2's own graph \u2014 125 review records carrying 610 edges): *centrality* was distorted badly \u2014 four of the eight most central nodes were acknowledgements, outranking every Component and Capability, and are now none, with real nodes rising into their place (rel:v0170 +75%, cmp:detect +41%). *Surprises* moved the OPPOSITE way from the prediction: zero acknowledgements ever appeared in that list before or after, but the count went 16 \u2192 32 \u2014 the bookkeeping edges were suppressing half the real surprises by tying communities together, rather than polluting the list. *Islands* could not be measured here at all, because reflow2's own graph has none; the unit test and the field reproduction carry that consumer. A review remains recorded, reasoned and reachable \u2014 excluded from the NETWORK, not from the GRAPH \u2014 and still appears in a blast radius, because a review genuinely is affected when what it reviewed changes. properties.statement: [BL-143] No vocabulary for "it runs but the answers are wrong" — so an opinion gets recorded as a measurement, which is the evidence-quality family's FOURTH axis

Those three say a check can be stale in TIME, narrow in INPUT SPACE, or not INDEPENDENT of what it validates \u2014 all answering *how good is the evidence*. This one is one step earlier: there is no criterion, so there is nothing for the evidence to be evidence OF. A failing with no threshold and a failing against a stated one are indistinguishable, which is the same flattering-collapse the family exists to break. [BL-106], [BL-126] and [BL-136] all REPORT the gap rather than refusing the work: an unscoped check is counted unscoped, an undated one unknown, a consumed one consumed, and none is forbidden. Not foreclosed; it simply answers a different question. properties.statement:
TWO DEFECTS FIXED 2026-08-23 FROM ONE FEEDBACK READ, AND THEY ARE THE SAME DEFECT. Both told a caller something reassuring that was false, and neither could have been found by anyone who believed the tool.

① THE SNAPSHOT WARNING WAS FALSE AND ITS REMEDY WOULD HAVE CAUSED THE LOSS IT WARNED ABOUT.
`snapshot_preserving` compared the WHOLE node's content hash against every snapshot. So after the ordinary sequence — record_change, write field A, write field B — nothing hashed to the state B replaced, and the revision block said "NO SNAPSHOT HOLDS THE STATE IT REPLACED — checked, not assumed" about a value sitting in the snapshot verbatim. It then prescribed a three-step undo: write the prior value back, record_change, re-apply. **A session that believed it would have snapshotted a RECONSTRUCTION over a timeline that was already correct.**
  🛑 THE PHRASE "checked, not assumed" IS WHAT MAKES IT DANGEROUS. It was added to earn trust and it succeeded; the check behind it was answering a coarser question than the sentence claimed. A message that says it looked must have looked at the thing it names.
  FIXED at the root: `prior_state_coverage` answers whole-node AND field-by-field, and the strong warning now fires only on fields nothing holds — naming them, and explicitly excluding preserved ones from the undo, because applying the undo to a preserved field IS the corruption.

② THE DURABILITY AID WAS WRITTEN, TESTED, AND FILTERED OUT OF EVERYTHING SERVED.
`loop_status.sync` reported `state: in_step` beside `export_nodes: 2897, live_nodes: 2899`. The sentence explaining that — *"2 node(s) here have never been exported… export before you finish"* — ALREADY EXISTED in `SyncDebt::message`, on the in-step line, with a comment saying it was placed there "because that is the line a session reads before standing down". It reached nobody: `loop_status` surfaces `message()` only for `is_actionable()` debts, and `in_step` is not actionable.
  ⭐ SO THE FIX WAS NOT TO WRITE ANYTHING. It was to stop discarding what was already written. The first attempt at this fix ADDED A SECOND SENTENCE saying the same thing, which was reverted on finding the original.
  🛑 AND THE VERDICT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE. The obvious fix — derive `state` from the counts so `in_step` cannot appear beside `live > export` — would break `ver:the-record-moved-is-surfaced`, which pins "ordinary unexported work is NEVER reported" because `state` answers whether the RECORD moved ahead of this seat, not whether your work is durable. Changing it would fire on nearly every session mid-flight. **What was missing was never a different verdict; it was that the verdict could be read ALONE.**

⭐⭐ THE COMMON SHAPE, AND IT IS THE REASON THESE ARE ONE NODE. A tool that is wrong in the ALARMING direction gets investigated within minutes — somebody chases the alarm. A tool that is wrong in the REASSURING direction is believed, and the cost lands later on somebody who never saw the reading. Both of these were found by a reporter who refused the reassurance and paid for a control: one read the snapshot back by hand, the other re-exported and got `wrote: "changed"` against a green verdict. **Neither is reachable from inside the system, because from inside both look exactly like working.**

⚠️ AND REFLOW2 HAD ALREADY SHIPPED THE COUNTS FOR ② IN AUGUST, specifically to make the green falsifiable. They did make it falsifiable. They did not make it falsified — the reporter's words are the finding: *"`state` is the field a session reads, and the counts are the field it skims."* Adding evidence beside a verdict does not change what a reader takes away; the verdict has to carry it.

MEASURED FIRST-HAND IN reflow2's OWN REPO, 2026-08-19 — corroborating ophyd's friction #2 ("evolving a long decision means resending all of it"), and the first report of it with numbers attached.

⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-19, SAME DAY, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE USEFUL PART. The first version of this fact claimed `resolve_decision` "removes both failure modes at once". IT DOES NOT, and the error was the ordinary one of filing two things together because they happened in the same session. Anthony asked the claim to be walked through, which is what caught it.

═════════════════════════════════════════════
FAILURE 1 — THE RESEND. This is what `resolve_decision` fixes.

TWO full-property resends of ONE node (`dec:idea-two-more-projects-...`), each to change ONE SENTENCE:
  · 6,242 characters — two Artifact ids became two file paths, after the artifacts were deleted
  · 6,455 characters — the same sentence back again, after the artifacts were restored and parked
≈ 12,700 characters retyped for two one-sentence edits. No tool patches part of a node: `add_decision` merges at PROPERTY granularity, so the smallest possible edit to one sentence is a full retype of everything around it.

THE EXPOSURE IS STATED BY THE TOOL ITSELF, on every one of them: *"NO SNAPSHOT HOLDS THE STATE IT REPLACED — checked, not assumed. The prior value above is now the only copy in existence, and this reply is the only place it appears."*

VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, and this is the part worth keeping: for both resends the intended text was written to a file BEFORE the write and diffed against the stored value after. Byte-identical both times. Without that check a single dropped character anywhere in 6,000+ would have been unrecoverable and silent — and the risk scales with the length of the node, so THE NODES MOST WORTH EDITING ARE THE ONES MOST DANGEROUS TO EDIT.

📌 EVIDENCE FOR A FIX ALREADY PROPOSED BY THE REPORTER, NOT A NEW IDEA: ophyd's `resolve_decision(id, resolution_text, status)`, or any field-level patch, removes this failure. Four projects have now reported the pattern; this is the instance with measurements.

═════════════════════════════════════════════
FAILURE 2 — THE MALFORMED WRITE. `resolve_decision` WOULD NOT HAVE PREVENTED IT.

TWICE in the same session, a Decision was written with a closing tag and the `rationale` ARGUMENT embedded inside the `decision` body. Both calls SUCCEEDED, storing trailing tool-call markup in a prose field and no `rationale` property at all. Caught by reading the reply; nothing else noticed.

🛑 WHY THIS IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR `resolve_decision`: BOTH were FIRST WRITES OF NEW NODES. `resolve_decision` appends a resolution to an EXISTING decision — it was not reachable in either case and would have changed nothing. Filing them together was the mistake.

WHAT THEY ARE EVIDENCE FOR is its own item: `dec:idea-a-prose-field-silently-absorbed-tool-call-markup`.

HONEST BOUND ON THE CORRELATION: both malformations were on parameters over 4,000 characters, and none of roughly thirty short writes the same session malformed. That is suggestive that long free-text arguments are where boundaries get mis-emitted, and it is n=2, observational, and confounded — the long writes are also the ones carrying the most retyped text. It does not support more than "worth watching".

properties.statement: CORRECTION TO fact:defect-rebuild-strands-the-shared-server: THE STRANDED SESSION IS RECOVERABLE WITHOUT AN MCP RECONNECT, AND THE WORKAROUND IS ONE COMMAND. That node states the failure is 'unrecoverable for the life of the session — every later respawn resolves the same dead inode, and only a full MCP reconnect clears it.' The first clause is right and the second is WRONG, proven here on 2026-08-08 by hitting the failure and recovering from it mid-session. WHAT HAPPENED: after the shared daemon's binary was replaced by a `cargo test` relink, the daemon exited and the client's auto-respawn failed with 'could not spawn the shared reflow2 server: No such file or directory (os error 2)' — the documented symptom, including the misleading advice to check a server log that cannot contain the cause. THE RECOVERY, verified by execution: start a replacement daemon BY HAND from the on-disk path, `setsid nohup ./target/debug/reflow2-mcp --graph-path ./.reflow2/graph --serve-shared &`, and the next tool call from the SAME session attached to it and worked normally (claim_report returned, then mint_seat, claim_region, open_questions, and a dozen further calls). No reconnect, no session restart, no context lost. WHY THE ORIGINAL CLAIM WAS WRONG: it reasoned that because the CLIENT resolves the binary through `current_exe()` and that inode is dead, every attempt must fail. True — but only of the client's SPAWN path. Attaching is a separate act: the client looks for a published server for that graph, and a server started by any means satisfies it. The dead inode blocks the client from CREATING a daemon; it does not block it from FINDING one. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE WORKAROUND: 'unrecoverable, restart the session' is expensive advice for ephemeral seats that are already dying on context exhaustion, and it was written into the graph as measured fact on reasoning alone. The original node's own evidence field says the diagnosis was 'recorded in session handoffs as worth filing and still unfiled' — so the recoverability clause was inherited, never tested. NOTE THE SHAPE, which is the same one this file keeps producing: a claim that was true about one mechanism (spawn) stated as true about the whole situation (the session), with nothing marking which part had been measured.

properties.statement:
CORRECTION, SAME SESSION, BEFORE ANYTHING ACTED ON IT: I recorded a defect saying `export_graph` silently deletes property values and that the divergence guard cannot see properties. IT WAS WRONG, AND THE GUARD'S OWN MESSAGE WAS RIGHT. The offending node has been DELETED rather than retired, because it was never true — a mistake is deleted, history is retired (retire-from-design's one question). WHAT I OBSERVED, and it was real: a live export wrote `granularity`/`volatility` on 54 artifacts where the committed file carried 162, while the tool said 'nothing in it would be lost'. WHAT I THEN ASSUMED WITHOUT TESTING: that the missing 108 were VALUES, and therefore that a guard which failed to flag them was blind to property-level loss. THE PROBE THAT SETTLES IT, which cost one command: round-trip the SAME live graph through the repo's freshly-built binary with tools/export_via_binary.py and count again.
    live via 0.24.0 server          artifacts=162  with granularity= 54
    re-exported via 0.25.0 binary   artifacts=162  with granularity=162
    committed                       artifacts=162  with granularity=162
Identical to committed. NOTHING WAS LOST. 162 is EVERY artifact in the design, which was the clue sitting in plain sight: a property present on literally all of them is a DEFAULT being serialized, not intent somebody recorded. v0.25.0 writes schema defaults into the export and v0.24.0 does not, so the 108 are `atomic`/`stable` defaults and the 54 are the ones actually set by hand. THE REAL FINDING UNDERNEATH, and it is worth more than the false one: THIS IS THE MEASUREMENT BL-198 ASKED FOR. That item (`epoch:planned-one-write-surface`) says 'stop serializing defaults, but measure the cost to compare_designs and the merge driver FIRST'. Here is the cost, measured on live data: two builds one release apart produce 108 phantom property-level `changed` findings in compare_designs for a design nobody edited — enough noise to make an agent invent a data-loss defect and block a PR on it. Serialized defaults are not free, and the instrument that reports them cannot tell a default from a decision. A COMPARISON THAT CANNOT SAY WHICH SIDE MEANT IT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS AN EDGE THAT CANNOT SAY WHO ASSERTED IT (DUPLICATES `basis`, which cost dev_storyflow ten proposed deletions) — the fix there was to make provenance explicit rather than to tune the detector, and the same argument applies. HOW THE ERROR HAPPENED, since that is the reusable part: `compare_designs` reported 108 property differences and I read a DIFFERENCE as a LOSS, then reasoned three steps forward from it — through 'the daemon holds the lock so no other process could have written' — to a confident mechanism, and wrote it into a PR body and a handoff note before running the one command that checks it. THE TOOL NEVER CLAIMED LOSS; I DID. This is the session's own theme turned on its author: a confident answer from something that never looked. The standing lesson holds in both directions — evaluate the tool independently, and evaluate your own reading of the tool just as hard.

properties.name: The undeclared-seam finding can never reach zero: couplings are read from DEPENDS_ON and contracts from PROVIDES/CONSUMES, and on this design those two sets are disjoint by construction
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-21 on reflow2's own design (2845 nodes), while starting work on the gap 'x72 pair(s) of parts depend on each other with no contract written down'.

THE NUMBERS:
  component couplings (Component DEPENDS_ON Component)      72
  ...of those, with a two-sided contract                      0
  declared contract pairs (an Interface with both a
    PROVIDES and a CONSUMES side)                            26
  ...of those, carrying a DEPENDS_ON edge                     0

The two sets are COMPLETELY DISJOINT. `seam_sets` computes `couplings` from DEPENDS_ON alone and `declared` from PROVIDES/CONSUMES alone, then subtracts. Since nothing in this design is recorded both ways, the subtraction is a no-op and the finding reports 100% undeclared no matter how many contracts anyone writes. WRITING A CONTRACT DOES NOT CREATE A DEPENDS_ON EDGE, so the number cannot move. This is a list that cannot reach zero, which is the third instance of that pattern found in one day.

THE CAUSE IS A LEVEL SPLIT, AND IT IS VISIBLE IN TWO LINES:
  all 72 coupled pairs are cmp <-> cmp (module level)
  22 of the 26 contract pairs involve a sys: subsystem; only 4 are cmp <-> cmp

So the design records CONTRACTS at the subsystem boundary and DEPENDENCIES at the module boundary, and the detector compares one against the other.

THE 72 ARE NOT SEAMS. Every one of them is INSIDE A SINGLE CRATE - zero cross a crate boundary, measured by mapping each component to its realizing artifacts' paths. And 43 of the 54 files in reflow2-core are `impl DesignGraph`: they are one type split across files for readability, not clients across a contract. Demanding a published contract between two impl blocks of the same struct is an alarm on correct work.

THE REAL BOUNDARIES ARE ALREADY DECLARED, which the finding's wording hides. The four cmp <-> cmp contract pairs are exactly the genuine ones - cmp:service <-> cmp:graph (reflow2-mcp to reflow2-core), cmp:service <-> cmp:registry, cmp:skills <-> cmp:service, cmp:init <-> cmp:export - and every external dependency is specified too (6 of the 17 Interfaces have no provider at all because they are things reflow2 consumes: the dynograph APIs, the ambient agent, the MCP protocol, an authenticating gateway, an exclusive local store).

=> SO THE STANDING READING OF THIS DESIGN WAS WRONG. '0 of 10 subsystems publish a contract - reflow2 specifies everything it depends on and almost nothing it offers' is not what the graph says. It publishes 11 interfaces with providers and consumes 6 it does not own. What it does not do is draw DEPENDS_ON at the boundaries it has published, which is the only reason the seam metric reads zero.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, and it is a modelling decision for the owner rather than a defect to repair: which level should carry contracts, and whether DEPENDS_ON between two impl blocks of one struct is a dependency worth recording at all.

THE `contradiction` DETECTOR FIRES ON THE EDGE AND NEVER LOOKS FOR THE RESOLVING DECISION ITS OWN SKILL PROMISES — SO A CONTRADICTION CAN BE ACKNOWLEDGED OR ERASED, BUT NEVER RESOLVED. Found here on 2026-08-08 by running check-health, and only because a contradiction was deliberately recorded earlier the same session. THE DOCUMENTED CONTRACT: the served check-health skill's category table reads `contradiction` = 'two nodes joined by CONTRADICTS **with no resolving Decision**', and `suggested_fix_type` on every such issue is `generate_decision`. Both say plainly that recording a Decision is how this defect goes away. THE ACTUAL BEHAVIOUR (crates/reflow2-core/src/heal.rs, the CONTRADICTS loop): it walks every CONTRADICTS edge, skips only those carrying `alignment: supporting`, and emits an issue. IT NEVER CONSULTS ANY DECISION. Verified by execution: two TemporalFacts were joined by CONTRADICTS (a measured correction against a claim it disproved); `dec:the-stranded-server-correction-stands` was created, ACCEPTED, and edged GOVERNED_BY from BOTH endpoints, stating explicitly which clause survives and why; `detect_defects` re-run reported the identical issue id, unchanged. SO THE ONLY WAYS OUT ARE BOTH LOSSY: acknowledge_defect, which files a resolved disagreement in the same drawer as an unresolved one and so destroys the distinction the acknowledgement list exists to preserve; or delete the CONTRADICTS edge, which erases that the disagreement ever happened — and for a graph whose whole premise is that history survives, that is the worse of the two. THE IRONY IS TWENTY LINES ABOVE THE BUG, in the same loop's own comment, about the `alignment` property this detector was taught to read in July: 'the only ways out were to acknowledge a defect that is not one, or to stop recording corroboration at all. A property the detector ignores is a property that lies.' The identical sentence applies one step along: A RESOLUTION THE DETECTOR IGNORES IS A RESOLUTION THAT DOES NOTHING. The fix that was applied to `alignment` was never applied to the resolution half. FIX SHAPE: before emitting, check whether a Decision is linked to both endpoints (GOVERNED_BY from each, or a Decision naming both in an edge) and skip if so — which is exactly what `generate_decision` invites the user to build. Open question worth settling rather than assuming: whether the resolving Decision must be `accepted`, since a `proposed` one is somebody thinking out loud and should probably not silence anything. THE CLASS THIS BELONGS TO, and it is now the fourth instance this week: documented behaviour and actual behaviour disagreeing, with the documentation being the more generous of the two — alongside claim_region's schema describing the pre-shared-server architecture, cap:claim-liveness promising a `gone` that was unreachable, and check-health calling node deletion mechanical.

properties.statement: A DEFERRED MCP TOOL CALLED BEFORE ITS SCHEMA IS LOADED FAILS INDISTINGUISHABLY FROM THE TOOL NOT EXISTING — AND THE WRONG CONCLUSION IS DURABLE, BECAUSE IT GETS WRITTEN INTO DOCS AS A CREDITED CORRECTION. Reported by w-613d836b (dev_storyflow, 2026-08-07), WHO STATED THE BOUND UP FRONT: they did NOT reproduce the failure themselves, so the MECHANISM is reported-not-measured and `confidence` here is set below 1 to reflect that. THE MECHANISM AS REPORTED: in some harnesses reflow2's ~114 tools are DEFERRED — listed by name but requiring a schema load before they can be called, and calling one first yields InputValidationError. WHAT IS MEASURED IS THE CONSEQUENCE, and it is well evidenced: `mint_seat` was reported absent from the served surface by one session; that was written into the fleet's worker-onboarding doc as a CREDITED CORRECTION ('There is NO mint_seat tool'); two further sessions and one boss then repeated it. FIVE HOPS, and NOBODY RAN THE TOOL until the fifth person did — at which point it worked on the first call. The `CORRECTED` framing made the claim MORE credible at each hop, not less. A SECOND SESSION INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED THE OTHER HALF: w-10f94d47 found the same onboarding block still carrying that correction and verified mint_seat does exist on 0.24.0 — noting the correction was true when measured and rotted when the binary moved. WHY IT BELONGS TO REFLOW2 RATHER THAN ONLY TO THEIR HARNESS: a large deferred surface makes 'this tool does not exist' a cheap and sticky conclusion, and reflow2's surface is large. FIX SHAPES: (1) where the server can see a request for an unknown tool name, respond 'no such tool; did you mean ...' and, where the name IS in the served surface, say so explicitly — the distinction between UNKNOWN and NOT-YET-LOADED is the whole problem; (2) advertise `find_tools`/`list_skills` in the server instructions as the entry point for 'does X exist?', so the question has a cheap authoritative answer that does not require guessing a call signature. NOTE THIS SESSION IS ITSELF EVIDENCE FOR THE PREMISE: every reflow2 tool used to capture this report had to be loaded by name through ToolSearch before it could be called.

properties.statement: A VERIFICATION HAS NOWHERE TO PUT THE CAVEATS THAT QUALIFY ITS RESULT, SO dev_storyflow HAS RATIFIED 'CARRY THE GRADING AND ALL BOUNDS IN THE NODE NAME' AS FLEET DOCTRINE — AND THE DAMAGE IS VISIBLE IN REFLOW2'S OWN OUTPUT, NOT ONLY THEIRS. Reported 2026-08-08 by dragon Boss f96eccd3 and independently by w-02baf79f. A Verification carries name, status, kind, method, level, last_run_at and NO field for the qualifications on the result. Because a bare `passing` reads to a session six weeks out as uniform coverage, the fleet arrived independently at the workaround and then adopted it on the bus as practice. THREE MEASURED CONSEQUENCES. (1) graph_report.top_gaps[0].title is a ~2,000-CHARACTER ESSAY, because a gap title embeds the verification's name; loop_status.verifications.attention[] is unreadable for the same reason; w-02baf79f measured one `name` at ~450 WORDS carrying a full graded walk report — verdict, L0/L2/L3 legs, a correction with six measured field counts, refuted mechanisms, file:line citations, bounds and an evidence path. Their judgement, which is the fair one: THAT IS EXCELLENT CONTENT IN THE WRONG FIELD. `name` is what a list renders. (2) THE NAMES ARE NO LONGER USABLE AS NAMES — they cannot be scanned, sorted or shown in a list. (3) THE BOUNDS ARE PROSE INSIDE A STRING, SO NOTHING CAN ACT ON THEM: `ver:fleet_compaction_hook` carries `status: passing` while its own name argues at length that it is FAILING, and no detector can see the contradiction because one half is a field and the other half is an essay. THIS IS NOT ONLY THEIR PROBLEM. reflow2's own loop_status verification digest reads the same way for the same reason — see ver:a-session-cannot-name-another-design, whose `name` is a multi-paragraph rationale — so this design has been paying the cost of the missing field without diagnosing it. THE SECOND-ORDER COST w-02baf79f NAMES: loop_status is advertised as the one cheap call and every worker is told to make it routinely, and it now returns a payload dominated by prose nobody asked for, which is a direct disincentive to the habit the loop depends on. FIX SHAPE, theirs: a first-class `bounds`/`caveats` field and ideally a `grade`, so `name` can go back to being a name and the qualifications become data the loop can reason about; plus a `findings`/`report` field so a walk's evidence has somewhere to live that is not its title; and truncate `name` in loop_status's rollup, or return `name` + `detail` separately. WEIGH WITH fact:defect-verification-evidence-is-prose-so-passing-can-contradict-itself — that report asks for structured RESULT fields (exit_code, command, observed/expected) for the same underlying reason, and the two proposals should be settled together rather than one at a time.

properties.statement:
`basis: measured` IS THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE CLAIM THE SCHEMA OFFERS AND THE ONLY ONE THAT DECAYS — and a CONSTRAINS edge carries no date, so a measurement is believed forever. music_graph F22, 2026-08-15; MECHANISM CONFIRMED IN THE SCHEMA HERE.

THEIR CASE: `con:frame-rate` recorded `cap:spectral-decomposition` contributing 6.9 fps with `basis: measured`, and `budget_report` duly reported a total of 6.9 against a 40 fps minimum. The true measured value was 55.06. The number was RIGHT WHEN TAKEN and had been wrong for days. Their framing is the one to keep: 'an estimate stays an estimate, but a measurement is a statement about a system at a moment.'

CONFIRMED IN `schema/core.yaml`: the CONSTRAINS edge declares exactly three properties — `note`, `contribution` (float) and `basis` (enum estimated | evidence | measured, default estimated). THERE IS NO DATE FIELD OF ANY KIND. So `budget_report` cannot say 'measured, but before the last 40 commits', and an agent reading it cannot tell a fresh measurement from a stale one. Nothing in the design records when the number was taken.

⭐ THE SHARP PART IS THAT REFLOW2 ALREADY HOLDS THIS DISCIPLINE ELSEWHERE, twice, and did not apply it here. `ver:evidence-quality` has a whole TIME axis: an accept dated after the check reports STALE, a re-run after the accept is current, and an undated side is UNKNOWN and counted rather than silently passed. `Artifact.last_confirmed_at` exists for precisely this reason, and its own description says a confirmation 'says nothing changed' so it is stored as a dated property. ⇒ DATING EVIDENCE IS ESTABLISHED DOCTRINE HERE, applied to Verification and to Artifact, and a budget contribution — the one number a KPP verdict rests on — has none.

THEIR SUGGESTION: a timestamp on the CONSTRAINS edge beside `basis`, and have `budget_report` age it against something — they propose the contributors' artifact checksums, which is the same trick `reconcile_artifacts` already uses to decide whether a file still matches.

⚠️ AND A SECOND, SMALLER FINDING IN THE SAME ENTRY, worth keeping because it cost them the time: for a MINIMUM budget the verdict went to `within` while a contributor was still `unstated`. For a MAXIMUM that would force `incomplete`, correctly, because a missing number can only make the total worse; for a minimum it can only make it better, so `within` is defensible. But the asymmetry is UNEXPLAINED IN THE PAYLOAD and 'looked like a bug until I reasoned it through'. The verdict is right and does not say why it is right.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a date belongs on the edge or on a separate observation node (the same question `Artifact.last_confirmed_at` answered by choosing the property, on the grounds that confirmations are high-frequency non-events); and whether ageing against artifact checksums is sound when a contribution can go stale without any file changing.

properties.statement: `req:thin-install` IS SATISFIED FOR NEW INSTALLS AND NOT FOR OLD ONES, AND THE REQUIREMENT'S OWN AUTHOR HIT THE GAP FOURTEEN DAYS AFTER RAISING IT. Alex asked for this on 2026-07-25 — quoted verbatim inside the requirement: 'you wouldn't need to change anything in your repo again and updates would be confined to the reflow package.' It was accepted. `cap:skills-served` then delivered the forward half: skills come from the binary, the installer copies nothing, and an upgrade leaves a project byte-identical (ver:served-skills, 23 cases in tools/test_init.py). WHAT NOBODY BUILT IS THE ROUTE OUT FOR A PROJECT INSTALLED BEFORE THAT. On 2026-08-08 Alex's project was running binary 0.24.0 against `.reflow2/kit-version.json` 0.11.0 — thirteen versions of frozen kit, exactly the state the requirement's statement describes ('it otherwise freezes at install time while reflow2 keeps moving'). Getting out took EIGHT MANUAL STEPS derived by his agent from first principles: export the design, untrack `.reflow2/`, delete committed skill copies, untrack the MCP configs, replace a long AGENTS.md with the pointer, update .gitignore, rewrite the MCP configs, add a committed export. THE MEASURE OF THE PROBLEM IS THAT TWO AGENTS DERIVED IT INDEPENDENTLY ON THE SAME DAY AND DISAGREED. His agent produced eight steps; I produced seven; they overlap on six. HIS INCLUDED A REGRESSION — rewriting `--graph-path` from absolute to RELATIVE, which is the configuration `dec:no-design-here-never-looked` records as having minted an accidental third graph in Anthony's own hxm_program repo, and which that node calls the severe one of six because it 'produced a WRONG ARTEFACT in the user's repository, silently'. MINE GOT THE STAMP FILENAME WRONG on first pass (`.install-stamp` for `kit-version.json`) and I shipped it to the user flagged as unverified. NEITHER OF US WAS CARELESS; the knowledge is simply scattered across the installer source, three accepted decisions and two verifications, and is re-derived per session. THAT IS THE EXACT FAILURE reflow2's own AGENTS.md names as its reason to exist — 'a stateless agent re-derives the design every session and decides silently over a scope bigger than its memory' — here applied to the MIGRATION rather than the design. WHAT IS MECHANICALLY CHECKABLE AND CURRENTLY IS NOT, every item drawn from a real miss today: is anything under `.reflow2/` tracked by git (the installer has this check and a one-line fault skips it — fact:defect-installer-cannot-warn-that-the-graph-dir-is-already-tracked); are the MCP configs tracked, carrying absolute paths that are meaningless elsewhere; does `kit-version.json` match the installed kit; do local skill copies exist and differ from the served ones, since a local copy SHADOWS the served one silently; is `--graph-path` absolute; is a committed export present and current against the live graph. SIX CHECKS, ALL DECIDABLE, NONE REQUIRING JUDGEMENT. NOTE WHERE IT CANNOT LIVE: not the MCP surface. `dec:agent-navigates-content` keeps reflow2 out of file IO, and every check above reads the filesystem or shells to git. The kit already ships tools that do exactly this — `reflow2_init.py --check`, `check_kit_manifest.py`, `reflow2_check.py` — so the home is there and the machinery is half-built.

properties.statement:
A PROPERTY THAT NAMES A NODE ID IS ACCEPTED WITHOUT CHECKING THE NODE EXISTS — while an EDGE to the same missing node is refused by sixteen helpers and a dedicated test file. The guard was built for one shape of reference and the other shape has none.

MEASURED 2026-08-16, and found sideways rather than by looking: `create_node` was called for a TemporalFact carrying `subject_id: "cap:questions-are-tracked"`. It was written and echoed back with no complaint. `get_node(Capability, "cap:questions-are-tracked")` then returned `{node: null}` — THE CAPABILITY HAS NEVER EXISTED. The id was invented while writing the node, and nothing objected. Corrected to `cmp:detect` only because the write was read back on the habit AGENTS.md prescribes; nothing in the tool's own reply would have revealed it.

⭐ WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH RECORDING IS THE CONTRAST, not the slip. `ver:edges-need-both-ends` is an unusually thorough guard: an edge to a missing node is refused through ALL SIXTEEN typed helpers, with an atomicity case, a size-floor so the table cannot shrink, and a mutation check that found fourteen of sixteen depend on the shared guard. That work exists because `authored_by` once accepted `person:anthony`, which was never created, and a phantom AUTHORED_BY sat in the graph until somebody noticed BY EYE. ⇒ The identical failure is still reachable through a PROPERTY, and it lands in the same place: a dangling reference nothing reports.

WHY IT IS NOT SIMPLY THE SAME BUG: an edge endpoint is structurally a reference and the schema knows it. A property is a string, and the schema does not record that `TemporalFact.subject_id` MEANS a node id — so there is nothing for a generic guard to key on. Any fix needs the schema to say which properties are references before validation can act, which is a real change rather than an oversight to patch.

BLAST RADIUS, NOT ESTABLISHED and stated as such: `subject_id` is the case measured. Other properties across the schema plausibly name nodes the same way (`ABOUT_ENTITY` has an edge for this, which is the modelled route, so the property may be the redundant one) — nobody has enumerated them, and the count of already-dangling values across this design is unknown and unmeasured.
