properties.statement:
AN UNDECLARED PROPERTY, ONCE WRITTEN, CANNOT BE REMOVED — and I found out by writing 16,000 characters into one.

⭐ CAUGHT BY THE FEATURE BUILT FOR IT, ON ITS FIRST LIVE USE, ON ITS AUTHOR. Hours after `create_node` gained `undeclared` (#213), the very next ChangeEvent I wrote came back carrying `"undeclared": ["description"]`. `ChangeEvent` declares `name`, `change_type`, `subject`, `summary` (fulltext) and `rationale` — there is NO `description`. I had been writing long accounts into an invented field all day.

MEASURED: SIX ChangeEvents carry it, all mine from 2026-08-16, roughly 16,000 characters between them. And the cost is not cosmetic — THE CONTENT IS EFFECTIVELY UNFINDABLE. Searching a phrase that appears ONLY in one of those descriptions ranked its node THIRD, below nodes that merely matched on `name`; `summary` is declared `fulltext: true` and `description` is not indexed for this type at all. So the reasoning is stored, readable if you already know the id, and invisible to the search that exists to find it.

⚠️ AND HERE IS THE DEFECT THAT MAKES IT WORTH A NODE RATHER THAN AN APOLOGY: THERE IS NO WAY TO DELETE A PROPERTY. `create_node` MERGES — what you pass overwrites, what you omit survives — which is correct and load-bearing (BL-46), and it means a property can be overwritten but never removed. The only route to a clean node is `delete_node` + recreate, which destroys every edge attached to it. ⇒ So the honest repair for a typo'd property is either to leave it, or to accept collateral damage that is worse than the typo. The near-duplicate guard, the edge-endpoint guard and now the undeclared-property report all catch mistakes at the WRITE; nothing can undo one.

WHAT IS OWED, and deliberately not done in the change that found it: the six should have their content moved to `summary`, where it is indexed. That is ~16 KB re-passed through tool calls and it duplicates rather than moves, since `description` cannot be dropped — the least-bad form is to set `summary` to the text and overwrite `description` with a short pointer. It was left because it is cleanup, not the requirement being built, and doing it half-way is worse than doing it deliberately.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether other node types are being written with an undeclared `description` the same way (only ChangeEvent was checked), and whether a `delete_property` operation is wanted at all — it is a small hole in an otherwise deliberate merge contract, and adding a way to remove things has its own risks.

properties.statement:
`answer_question` CAN ONLY REACH A QUESTION WHOSE ID IT CAN DERIVE, so any Question created by a route other than `gap_to_prompt` is PERMANENTLY UNANSWERABLE — and the loop keeps telling the next seat to follow up on it forever. Reported by api-boss (`79e8e8d5`) 2026-08-15 22:40 on the StoryFlow fleet graph; MECHANISM CONFIRMED IN SOURCE here, and their own diagnosis (i) is the right one of the three they offered.

CONFIRMED, not inferred: `detect.rs:872` `answer_question(gap_id, answer)` delegates to `set_question_status`, which at `detect.rs:888` computes `question_id = asked_question_id(gap_id)` — and that helper is pure string derivation, `format!("question:{}", gap_id.strip_prefix("gap:"))` (`detect.rs:700-702`). It then does a single `get_node(QUESTION, &question_id)` and returns not-found if that exact id is absent. THERE IS NO LOOKUP BY QUESTION ID AND NO SEARCH. A Question stored under any other id cannot be addressed by this tool at all.

THEIR MEASURED CASE: `open_questions` returned `question_id: "q:fleet_ops_as_reflow2_subproject"` alongside `gap_id: "gap:fleet_governance_has_no_executable_model"`, `status: asked`. `answer_question{question_id: ...}` was rejected as an unknown field naming `gap_id` as the legal one; `answer_question{gap_id: ...}` then answered 'no recorded question for gap'. BOTH IDENTIFIERS CAME FROM THE SAME OBJECT IN THE SAME LISTING AND NEITHER IS ACCEPTED. The derivation would have wanted `question:fleet_governance_has_no_executable_model`, which is not what their Question is called.

⭐ THE SHARP EDGE IS THE LOOP EATING ITSELF: `unanswered_questions` keeps counting it, `loop_status` keeps printing 'follow it up rather than asking again', and because the tool that implements following-up cannot close it, a later seat re-asks the user something they already ruled on — the exact failure the instruction exists to prevent, caused by the tool implementing the instruction.

THEIR WORKAROUND IS THE RIGHT SHAPE AND IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: they recorded the ruling as an accepted Decision. The substance is durable, the LINKAGE is not — nothing connects that Decision to the Question, so it still reads as open.

⚠️ REFLOW2'S OWN GRAPH SHOWS THE SAME CLASS FROM THE OTHER SIDE, unresolved for days: `loop_status` here reports '1 answered question(s) never reached the design', and `open_questions` returns `question:9d265ef455a2e245` at `status: answered` carrying the user's full reply about grandfathering the 121 settled items. There the derivation MATCHES (it was made by `gap_to_prompt`) and the answer still never became design — so the gap between 'answered' and 'written in' is real independently of the id scheme.

FIXES, cheapest first, theirs and sound: (1) accept `question_id` too, since `open_questions` publishes it — the id a caller holds should work; (2) make the second rejection name what it looked for and what exists, which is the same list-the-legal-values ask already in their log from 2026-08-03; (3) let a Decision CLOSE a Question with an edge, making the linkage first-class and surviving whichever id scheme wins.

NOT ESTABLISHED: how many hand-authored Questions exist across consumer graphs, and whether `withdraw_question` (same derivation, `detect.rs:878`) leaves them equally unreachable — by inspection it does, but that was not exercised.

properties.statement: THE THING dev_storyflow WOULD MOST LIKE CLOSED: NOTHING LINKS A CAPABILITY TO THE AUTHORING SURFACE THAT FEEDS IT, SO A CAPABILITY CAN BE `realized`, BUILT, RENDERING — AND DEAD. Reported 2026-08-08 by sb-boss ab2291fa, item 5, explicitly labelled 'the thing that would have saved the most time today' and 'the gap I would most like closed'. `cap:storybook_output` was status `realized`, its component was built, its proposer existed, its frontend rendered — AND THE CAPABILITY WAS DEAD, because no UI writes the field it consumes. EVERY EXISTING EDGE TYPE WAS SATISFIABLE WITHOUT THAT SURFACE EXISTING: REALIZES, SATISFIES, DEPENDS_ON and CONSUMES were all present and all honest. THE DIAGNOSTIC COST IS THE MEASURE OF IT: three people produced three different root causes, and all three were greppable mechanisms — because a greppable mechanism is the only kind of cause a search can find. The true cause, 'nobody ever writes this', HAD NO ARTIFACT TO FIND. THIS IS A VOCABULARY GAP, NOT A DETECTOR BUG: detect_gaps cannot ask about a surface the design has no way to say is required, which is req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots in its sharpest form to date — a detector that finds the missing half of something BEGUN, over a thing that was never begun and cannot be expressed. REFLOW2 HAS ALREADY MET THE INSTANCE AND NOT THE GENERAL CASE: req:the-store-is-reachable-from-a-session says 'a capability nothing can call is not delivered - the content store needs a surface', which is this same insight scoped to one capability and written by hand. Nothing generalises it and nothing detects it. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY WORTH THINKING ABOUT: the missing edge is not another machine-to-machine dependency, it is the HUMAN INPUT PATH — where a person or an upstream system actually puts the data the capability consumes — and reflow2 models actors INTERACTS_WITH capabilities but never that an interaction is REQUIRED for the capability to function at all.

properties.statement: A FORCE-PUSHED REBASE ON AN OPEN PR RAN NO CI, AND THE PR WENT ON REPORTING ITSELF READY TO MERGE. Found here 2026-08-08 while landing the storyflow HEAL stack. PR #105 was rebased onto main after #106 squash-merged, and force-pushed. `gh run list --branch` showed ONE run, against the PRE-REBASE sha `5d097f9`; the rebased commit `16d6e11` had none and never got one. Meanwhile `gh pr view 105` reported `mergeable: MERGEABLE, mergeStateStatus: CLEAN` and `gh pr checks` reported nothing at all rather than reporting an absence. A reader doing the normal thing — checking the PR is clean before merging — would have merged a commit no gate had ever seen. THIS IS THE HOUSE FAILURE SHAPE, in the house's own words: a green that belongs to something other than what you are about to ship. Same family as BL-206 (`reflow2_check` reported OK over 20 artifacts it never swept), `dec:no-design-here-never-looked` ('no design here' asserted without looking), and `loop_status` reporting `unsurfaced_gaps: 0` before detect_gaps has ever run. Here the green was real — it just belonged to a different commit. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` triggers on `push: branches: [main]` and an unfiltered `pull_request:`, so nothing in the configuration explains the miss; GitHub simply did not raise a `synchronize` for that force-push. CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED, and saying so matters: the retarget from a feature-branch base to `main` happened seconds after the push, and either the race or the base change may be responsible. NOT TESTED. WORKAROUND THAT WORKED, one command pair: `gh pr close 105 && gh pr reopen 105` fires `pull_request: reopened`, which is in the default trigger types, and CI queued immediately against the correct sha. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS PR: reflow2's own release procedure and [[branch-then-pr-practice]] both rest on 'mark ready only on green', and this is a case where green is present, current-looking, and about a commit that no longer exists in the branch. The check a human can actually perform is `gh run list --branch <b>` and compare `headSha` against `gh pr view --json headRefOid` — two commands, and neither is in any documented routine here. FIX SHAPE: add that comparison to the pre-merge routine in AGENTS.md / the release procedure; or have the gate itself refuse when the head sha has no completed run, which is the stronger form because it does not depend on remembering.

properties.statement:
WHEN A TYPED CALL IS REFUSED FOR A FIXABLE REASON, A CAPABLE AGENT DOES NOT RETRY — IT WRITES THE STRUCTURE INTO PROSE AND MOVES ON, AND NOTHING CAN READ IT AFTERWARDS. Self-reported, which is why it is worth more than an ordinary complaint. `authored_by` refused a call whose target was an `Actor` rather than a `Contributor`; the error named the accepted FIELDS but not that constraint. The seat then wrote 'USER-RULED, in their own words:' into the Decision PROSE about TEN TIMES. It felt like diligence. It put the user's authorship somewhere no tool can read, and it is the direct reason `what_next` had nothing to show in its most important band — a consequence surfaced only because a NEW tool later exposed it. ⭐ THE TRANSFERABLE POINT: THE FAILURE MODE OF A REJECTED TYPED CALL IS NOT AN ERROR, IT IS PROSE. The result reads beautifully and quietly drops the structure — the prose looked BETTER than the edge would have. FIX SHAPE: when a refusal has a fixable cause, say WHAT WOULD HAVE WORKED, not only what was wrong. `add_decision`'s near-match refusal already does exactly this — it names both routes and says overlap is not proof of duplication — so the pattern exists inside this toolset and simply has not been applied to the other refusals. || SOURCE: Observed by the dev_storyflow fleet on 2026-08-15, on reflow2 0.31.0 with served == installed verified through /proc/<pid>/exe. Three agent seats, one shared graph, one day.

▸ PARTLY ADDRESSED 2026-08-15 (epoch:a-refusal-names-what-would-have-worked). `authored_by` and `owned_by` now distinguish a wrong TYPE from a missing node and name `add_contributor` — the reported instance. VALID_TO IS DELIBERATELY NOT SET: the claim above is about EVERY refusal with a fixable cause, and only these two were changed. Closing it here would report a class as fixed on the evidence of one case.

properties.statement:
AN ARTIFACT RETIRED BY AN ACCEPTED DECISION STILL REPORTS `missing_artifact` AND STILL FAILS THE GATE. THERE IS NO WAY TO SAY A REGISTERED FILE WAS DELETED ON PURPOSE. Found by doing it, 2026-08-15, carrying out Anthony's policy that reflow2's own feedback documents are removed once captured (`dec:reflow2s-own-feedback-documents-are-removed-once-captured`).

MEASURED. Both Artifacts were retired the modelled way — `OBSOLETES` drawn from an ACCEPTED Decision, which `dec:idea-discontinued-is-a-first-class-state` establishes as how something leaves a design. The files were then deleted. `reflow2_check.py --export docs/design/reflow2.json` → **FAILED, 2 findings**: `art:alex-grok-feedback-2026-08-14: missing_artifact` and `art:usgov-genesis-feedback-2026-08-15: missing_artifact`. The retirement changed nothing about the finding.

AND THE REMEDY THE GATE OFFERS CANNOT BE PERFORMED: it says 'Reconcile and accept two-sided (`set_artifact_checksum`), then re-export.' There is no checksum to set, because there is no file. THE TOOL NAMED IN THE ERROR IS INAPPLICABLE TO THE ERROR.

WHY IT HAPPENS, and it is a coherent omission rather than an oversight in one place: the `OBSOLETES` hint enumerates exactly which findings fall silent on a discontinued node — 'the unmotivated / unrealized / unverified capability gaps fall silent' — and drift is not among them. The retirement concept was built for Capabilities and the artifact layer was never taught it. `set_artifact_intent` does not help either, and `ver:artifact-intent` says so in terms: 'a MISSING append_only artifact still fires at FULL SEVERITY, because declaring content volatile never says the file may vanish.' That sentence is correct about volatility and leaves deliberate deletion with no expression at all.

THE THREE WAYS OUT, none clean: (1) `delete_node` the Artifacts — makes the gate green and ERASES that the documents ever existed, discarding the checksums that are the only proof of what was captured and orphaning six `ANNOTATES` edges from the Fragments that quote them; (2) leave the gate RED, which blocks the branch and trains people to ignore it; (3) teach the drift detector to honour `discontinued`, which is a code change and the only one that keeps the record honest.

⭐ WHY (3) IS THE PRINCIPLED ANSWER: the design SHOULD go on saying these documents existed, carried these checksums, and produced these findings — that is the history retirement exists to preserve. What it should stop saying is that the files are still on disk. Those are different claims and the artifact layer currently conflates them, exactly as `Capability.status` conflated 'built' with 'still current' until `OBSOLETES` was taught to `get_node`.

A POLICY THAT REMOVES CAPTURED DOCUMENTS THEREFORE CANNOT BE FOLLOWED WITHOUT EITHER LYING OR BREAKING THE BUILD, which makes this a prerequisite for that policy rather than a nuisance beside it.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any other detector reads artifact existence and would need the same treatment, and whether `discontinued` is the right signal or an artifact wants its own `removed_at`.

properties.statement: THE SERVED-VS-ON-DISK VERSION GAP IS REAL, SILENT, AND THE SERVER CAN DETECT IT ITSELF WITH ONE SYSCALL — `/proc/self/exe` IS ALREADY MARKED `(deleted)`. Two sessions, w-613d836b and w-6904efa6, filed this the same hour on 2026-08-07 from the same incident, and the second carries the cheaper fix. WHAT HAPPENED: `graph_report.served_by.reflow2_version` reported `0.22.1` while `reflow2-mcp --version` on disk reported `0.24.0`. The shared server had been up since before the upgrade and `--serve-shared` is detached on purpose, so every session that restarted RE-ATTACHED TO THE SAME STALE PROCESS and nothing anywhere reported a problem. WHY THE EXISTING GUARD DID NOT WORK: the served_by block exists specifically to catch this, but it reports a LITERAL that a human must compare against a number the block does not contain. The fleet's own stand-down post said 'demand served_by: 0.22.1', so a session matched that literal four days later and reported a PASS — the literal was satisfied and the invariant was broken. Four sessions in that fleet read `0.22.1` out of that block on two different days and drew OPPOSITE conclusions from the same true value, which is the reporter's argument that the comparison should not be left to the reader. Also measured: `binary_mtime_unix` came back `null` in the same block, so the one other advertised freshness signal was unavailable too. THE CHEAP FIX, verified on the live server by w-6904efa6: when a binary is replaced under a running process the kernel marks that process's `/proc/self/exe` as `(deleted)`. They demonstrated it — `readlink /proc/2264267/exe` -> `/home/ajs/.local/bin/reflow2-mcp (deleted)`, `/proc/2264267/exe --version` -> `0.22.1` (still executable, the inode lives on), on-disk -> `0.24.0`. So `stale: true` is derivable from the server's OWN `/proc/self/exe` with no path re-resolution, no second binary read, and no assumption the launch path still exists. It answers the actual question — 'has my executable been replaced since I started?' — directly, whereas a version-string comparison answers it indirectly and breaks entirely if two builds share a version number. REPORTERS' PREFERENCE: report BOTH — the `(deleted)` bit as the reliable trigger, the on-disk version as what a human needs in order to act. NOTE THIS REPO ALREADY KNOWS THE `(deleted)` INODE FAILURE MODE from the other end: fact:defect-rebuild-strands-the-shared-server is the same kernel behaviour biting spawn_daemon via current_exe(). Same signal, two symptoms, and one of them is the fix for the other.

properties.statement:
DEV_STORYFLOW'S COMMITTED EXPORT CANNOT BE RE-IMPORTED BY THE BINARY THAT WROTE IT, AND HAS NOT BEEN RESTORABLE SINCE AT LEAST 2026-08-11. Reported by their api-boss sidekick (`551d9718`) 2026-08-15; the checkable half VERIFIED HERE.

WHAT FAILS: `import_graph` refuses their export with two invalid edges — `VERIFIES ver:integration_tests -> proj:storyflow` (Project) and `VERIFIES ver:side_e_slo_gate_unwired_2026_08_09 -> con:side_e_perf_slos_are_enforced_nowhere` (Constraint). The import is all-or-nothing, so NOTHING is written, and `reflow2_check.py` exits 2 without ever reaching gap detection.

VERIFIED HERE: `schema/verify.yaml` carries the `to:` list `[Capability, Requirement, Artifact, Component, DesignRule]` and the comment they quote, word for word — 'THE LIST MUST KEEP ALL FIVE. The first four are DERIVED from live edges… narrowing to fewer would invalidate edges that exist today. Re-derive before ever trimming it.' POSITIVE CONTROL: reflow2's own graph holds 161 VERIFIES edges across exactly those five types and ZERO outside them, which is precisely why this project could never have found it.

⭐⭐ AND THE FILE ALREADY RECORDS THE SAME MISTAKE ONE LAYER UP, which neither reporter saw. The `extraction_hint` on that very edge reads: 'Requirement was already true and unlisted here — three such edges existed while this hint named only three types, WHICH IS HOW A HINT STOPS BEING A DESCRIPTION AND BECOMES A GUESS.' So the HINT under-enumerated, was caught, was fixed, and the lesson was written down — and then the `to:` LIST made the identical error against the same edge. THE COMMENT GUARDS AGAINST TRIMMING THE LIST AND SAYS NOTHING ABOUT THE ENUMERATION BEING INCOMPLETE WHEN FIRST DERIVED. Their census found 5 types at 95/27/13/2/1 edges and missed two carrying one edge each: a long tail, invisible to a count.

⚠️ THE CHANGE WAS PROPOSED BY DEV_STORYFLOW AND BROKE DEV_STORYFLOW. The derivation was almost certainly run against that graph. While `to` was `*` every edge was legal; the moment it became an enumeration, every unlisted-but-existing edge became unimportable. A SCHEMA TIGHTENING THAT SILENTLY ORPHANS EXISTING DATA IS A BREAKING CHANGE WEARING A VALIDATION ERROR'S CLOTHES.

⭐ THE GENERALISABLE HALF, AND THE REASON THIS OUTRANKS ITS OWN SEVERITY: NOTHING EVER IMPORTS AN EXPORT. The graph is written incrementally by a long-lived server and the export is written OUT, never read BACK — so it has never been exercised as an INPUT. An export can be un-restorable for an unbounded time while every signal stays green: `loop_status` clean, `sync_status` `in_step`, the `content_hash` chain intact. ALL OF THOSE VERIFY THE EXPORT AGAINST ITSELF, NEVER AGAINST THE IMPORTER.

⚠️ AND THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT CI. `.reflow2/graph` is gitignored, machine-local and single-writer; the committed export is the ONLY copy of the design that survives losing that directory. Their disaster-recovery artifact would not restore today. The failing gate is the lesser casualty.

WHAT REFLOW2 GOT RIGHT, recorded because it is most of the value: exit 2 rather than a silent pass, all-or-nothing so nothing was half-written, and BOTH offenders listed at once 'so you can fix them in one edit rather than learning them one import at a time'.

THEIR ASKS, in their order: (1) a ROUND-TRIP CHECK — export → import → re-export as a gate, the only probe that catches this class and one needing no knowledge of any particular schema rule; (2) treat narrowing a `from`/`to` from `*` to an enumeration as a MIGRATION that ships its census; (3) have `export_graph` validate what it emits, since an export that cannot be imported is arguably not a valid export and the write side is where the author is still present.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and explicitly left to reflow2: whether `VERIFIES → Constraint` is a MODELLING NEED rather than a mistake. `ver:side_e_slo_gate_unwired` checks whether a constraint holds, which reads legitimate. Their own note is the right one: ask before deleting data to satisfy a validator.

properties.statement:
MEASURED on reflow2's own design (2487 nodes, 9975 edges, 83 gaps) by driving the BUILT binary against a temp store imported from docs/design/reflow2.json, scoping detect_gaps to each of the 56 Components in turn.

AT THE DEFAULT DEPTH OF 3, SCOPE DOES NOT NARROW. Every one of the 56 Components returns between 50 and 60 of the design's 83 gaps — median 55, i.e. two thirds of every gap in the design, whichever component you pick. region_size runs 595-903 nodes (24-36% of the design). The spread across all 56 is 50..60: the answers are indistinguishable, so a team reading `in_scope: 55, out_of_scope: 28` is being told 'your part has 55 gaps' when every other team is told the same thing about theirs.

SHALLOWER DEPTHS DISCRIMINATE, SHARPLY:
  depth 1: region_size 17..139 (median 28), in_scope 0..19 (median 1)
  depth 2: region_size 267..601 (median 330), in_scope 2..27 (median 4)
  depth 3: region_size 595..903 (median 686), in_scope 50..60 (median 55)

THE MODULE'S OWN ARGUMENT FOR 3 DOES NOT SURVIVE READING scope_region. scope.rs:76-80 justifies 3 as 'the smallest number that reaches a Component's whole thread: its capabilities are one hop away, the requirements they satisfy and the artifacts and checks that realize and verify them are two, and A CONTAINED CHILD COMPONENT'S CAPABILITIES ARE THREE'. But scope_region is containment_closure(seed) THEN propagate_from(owned, depth) — contained children are already IN `owned`, unboundedly, so their capabilities are ONE hop from an owned node, not three. The third hop buys only what the same doc calls 'the neighbours' neighbours, which is the program again'. By its own reasoning the default should be 2.

TWO DEFAULTS FOR ONE STATED COMPUTATION. detect_gaps' tool description says the region is 'the same computation claim_region uses for "the part I hold", so "my area" means one thing everywhere'. It is not the same on two counts: the MCP default depth is 3 for scope and 2 for claim_region, and scope_region adds the containment closure while claimed_region takes the radius alone — a divergence scope.rs:38-42 already records as possibly a defect in the claims layer and deliberately left unfixed.

NOT FIXED HERE. Changing DEFAULT_SCOPE_DEPTH changes what every existing scoped caller sees, and reconciling claim_region with scope_region changes what two people believe they hold. Both are put to the owner rather than taken.

A STALE `.reflow2/kit-version.json` IS NOT A WRONG VERSION LABEL — IT IS AN INPUT TO A LIVE DECISION, AND THAT COST WAS THE ⚠️ LEFT UNVERIFIED IN `fact:updating-reflow2-does-not-update-a-project-already-set-up`. That node closed with two open ⚠️ items, one of them: 'Whether a stale kit costs anything concrete — NOT VERIFIED.' This answers it with a first concrete cost, read out of the source rather than inferred. `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/nudge.rs:175` — `recorded_harnesses()` — READS `.reflow2/kit-version.json` and pulls `harnesses` out of it, and `nudge.rs:151` branches on the answer: a project whose recorded harnesses do not include `claude` is told `NoHookForThisHarness` (its harness cannot have a nudge), and only `None`/matching falls through to `Absent` (a real gap worth reporting). SO THE RECEIPT OF AN INSTALL EVENT IS BEING READ AS A LIVE FACT ABOUT THE PROJECT, which is precisely the misreading the parent fact identifies one layer up ('a receipt for an install EVENT, not a live reading') — recorded there about humans reading it, true here of reflow2's own code reading it. OBSERVED, 2026-08-14, Alex's home machine via his Grok 4.6 session (docs/feedback/2026-08-14-alex-grok-session.md): live MCP 0.31.0, sidecar 0.11.0 / 0ec473e dated 2026-07-25 — twenty versions of drift — and the same session's self-assessment records 'I did not install the loop nudge; loop_status was called by hand', which is the downstream symptom sitting one line from its own cause without the two being connected. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: the file is read; the read decides which of three nudge answers a project gets; that project's copy is twenty versions old. WHAT IS NOT: whether his stamp actually lacks a `harnesses` key (a 0.11.0 stamp predates `--harness`, so it most likely returns `None` and falls through to the SAFE branch) — i.e. THE BUG MAY NOT HAVE BITTEN HIM YET. That is the honest reading and it does not make the coupling safe: the branch that misfires is the one where an OLD stamp names harnesses that a NEWER kit would name differently, and nothing anywhere compares the stamp's generation against the binary answering the call. THE ASYMMETRY THAT HIDES IT is already on the record in the parent fact: `~/.local/share/reflow2/kit` is a SYMLINK to the checkout on the maintainer's box and a frozen tarball for a consumer, so the maintainer's stamp cannot go stale by construction. FIX SHAPES, smallest first: have the nudge treat a stamp older than the running binary as `None` (unknown) rather than as an answer, since this module's own doc comment at nudge.rs:170 already argues that not-knowing and knowing-it-is-absent must not share a reply; or surface the kit generation next to the binary version so a human sees the split; or restamp on `reflow2 update`.

properties.statement:
THE 2026-08-08 SEAT-LIVENESS FIX LANDED ON THE TRANSPORT THAT DID NOT NEED IT AND MISSED THE ONE THAT REPORTED IT: A SEAT RETURNED BY THE `mint_seat` TOOL IS NEVER REGISTERED, SO `gone` IS STILL UNREACHABLE FOR IT — AND THE TOOL NOW PROMISES OTHERWISE IN ITS OWN OUTPUT. Follows fact:defect-claim-liveness-is-the-servers-pid-not-the-sessions (w-613d836b, 2026-08-07), which #100 answered with a SeatRegistry: register on attach, remove on drop, so a departed session reads `gone` instead of borrowing the daemon's pid. That mechanism WORKS. Nothing on the served path populates it. MEASURED HERE 2026-08-08 against v0.25.0 source, by running the tool handler and probing liveness directly:
    tool-minted seat   before=Live   after release_seat=Live    <- gone unreachable
    registered seat                  after release_seat=Gone    <- the fix, on a path nothing calls
THE MECHANISM, three links, each directly readable: (1) the registry is populated ONLY by `identity::SeatLease::attach()`; (2) the only callers are service.rs wrap_at and share, which build the service's OWN seat; (3) `seat_for_claim` uses that seat ONLY when the caller OMITS `seat`, and `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/claims_tools.rs:114` mints the tool's seat with bare `identity::mint_seat()` and never registers it. So the registry answers for the session-held seat, and `dec:stateless-seat-handle` REFUSES the omit path on the sessionless transport — which is precisely where a caller must pass a tool-minted seat, and precisely the deployment (`--shared`) the original defect was reported from. WORSE THAN A MISS, AN OVERCLAIM: the same change added `liveness_is_this_session` to mint_seat's output — 'Your claims read `live` while you are attached and `gone` once you are not — including if this session crashes rather than exits cleanly.' That is FALSE for the seat that tool returns. The field it replaced said the opposite and WAS TRUE. A correct caveat was traded for an incorrect promise, which is strictly worse than the original defect: a reader who believed the old text was right to distrust liveness, and a reader who believes the new text is wrong to trust it. WHY THE CHECK DID NOT CATCH IT, AND THE PRECEDENT THAT SAYS WHAT TO DO: `ver:claim-liveness` is `passing` and its own name states its scope — 'Proven end to end over stdio with a genuinely exited server process'. Stdio is the one transport where the caller may omit `seat` and get the registered lease, so the check proves the fixed path and never touches the broken one. crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/ contains NO liveness test at all; the regression test lives in reflow2-core/tests/claims.rs and calls `register_seat` BY HAND, supplying the very step the server omits. That is what made a real fix look proven. This project has already split a check for exactly this reason — ver:a-session-cannot-name-another-design was carved out of ver:sessions-cannot-cross-designs on 2026-08-07 because a green check standing for an untested clause is worse than an absent one. Same remedy applies. REPORTED INDEPENDENTLY THE SAME DAY by dev_storyflow w-aa0607ff (api-boss fleet, ~18:12 EDT), who measured two different sessions' seats sharing pid 3840196 = the --serve-shared process, and correctly concluded `gone` can never fire. They were running 0.24.0 (their export stamp), so they had not seen #100; the finding stands on v0.25.0 regardless, which is the part worth knowing. THEIR GENERALISATION IS THE MOST VALUABLE LINE IN THE REPORT AND SHOULD BE RUN AS A SWEEP: `--shared` 'turned a session-local metric into a shared-state one WITHOUT CHANGING ITS INTERFACE' was already ratified about loop_status counts, and nobody re-audited the other tools whose meaning --shared silently changed. The greppable question: WHICH OUTPUTS DESCRIBE A SESSION BUT ARE COMPUTED FROM SOMETHING THE SERVER OWNS? FIX SHAPE: register the seat the `mint_seat` tool hands out (it is the seat that will be carried), or — since nothing ties that seat to a client connection — make the field say what it can actually observe, per their proposal: `liveness: "unknown (shared server - cannot observe client sessions)"`. A field that cannot produce its negative value must not present its positive one as information. Either way the mint_seat advisory must stop asserting the behaviour it does not have.

A VERIFICATION HAS NOWHERE TO PUT ITS EVIDENCE, SO EVERY AUTHOR PUTS IT IN THE NAME. Median Verification `name` in this design is 79.5 WORDS.

MEASURED on the committed export, 2026-08-16: 160 Verifications — median name 79.5 words, 72 over 100 words, 17 over 300. The longest is 654 words. A `name` is what a list renders; these are reports.

⚠️ AND THE AUTHOR OF THE WORST OF IT TODAY WAS ME. Four of the six Verifications written in this session exceed 300 words, and `ver:a-claim-reads-back-with-its-age` at 435 words is the FIFTH LONGEST IN THE ENTIRE DESIGN. I was not working around a limitation I had noticed; I did not notice it. Every one of those nodes now costs its full length on every future read, in the field a list renders.

REPORTED BY dev_storyflow's fleet, 2026-08-08 10:12, worker `w-02baf79f`, and their diagnosis is better than the symptom: `loop_status` is documented as "one cheap call", and it IS cheap to call and expensive to READ — their `verifications.attention[0].name` came back as a single ~450-word paragraph holding a full graded walk report, verdict, L0/L2/L3 legs, six measured field counts, refuted mechanisms and file:line citations. Their words: "That is excellent content and it is in the WRONG FIELD."

⭐ THE SHAPE OF IT, which is what makes it a defect rather than a style complaint: "workers write the full report into the `name` because there is no other durable place for it on the node — so this is A MISSING FIELD BEING PAID FOR IN EVERY FUTURE READ OF THAT NODE." The workaround is universal, undirected and invisible: nobody chose it, everybody does it, and it degrades the one call every worker is told to make routinely. A cheap call that returns prose nobody asked for is a call people stop making — the same signal-trained-to-be-ignored failure `req:the-loop-can-say-what-this-session-owes` was built to end, arriving through a different door.

THEIR TWO ASKS, recorded as filed:
(a) give Verification a `findings` / `report` property, so a walk's evidence has somewhere to live that is not its title;
(b) truncate `name` in `loop_status`'s rollup, or return `name` + `detail` separately.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is the load-bearing question: whether (a) alone would change behaviour. A declared field nobody writes to leaves the corpus exactly as it is — the same trap `dec:how-should-a-temporal-fact-carry-its-date-when-there-is-no-epoch` hit, where 112 nodes wrote an undeclared property because the declared route did not fit. The existing 160 names cannot be migrated automatically either: a property once written cannot be removed ([[fact:defect-a-property-once-written-cannot-be-removed]]), so the best available repair is to write the evidence to the new field and SHORTEN the name, which duplicates rather than moves.

ALSO NOT ESTABLISHED: whether (b) alone is enough. Truncating at the rollup makes the cheap call cheap again without asking anyone to change how they write — which is either the pragmatic fix or the one that lets the underlying hoard grow unchecked, and nobody has measured which.

properties.statement:
`add_decision`'s LOOP HINT SAYS 'lands proposed' EVEN WHEN THE WRITE LEFT THE NODE `accepted`, SO THE HINT INVITES A DEMOTION THE CALLER DID NOT MAKE. Alex's Grok 4.6 session, 2026-08-14, item 10, reported with unusual care: 'I did not accidentally demote this time; the hint still invites it.'

THE MECHANIC: `add_decision` is a merge. On a NEW node it lands `proposed`, and the hint is correct and useful. On an EXISTING node that is already `accepted`, the merge leaves the status untouched — correctly — and the same hint fires anyway, telling the caller a thing that is not true of the write they just made. An agent that believes it and 'corrects' the status with `set_decision_status` would demote a settled decision to `proposed` while thinking it was tidying up.

WHY THE BLAST RADIUS IS LARGER THAN A WORDING BUG: `dec:certainty-derived` makes status the carrier of the user's word, and `where-am-i` reads accepted Decisions back to the user as 'what you decided'. A silent demotion does not lose data — it withdraws a settlement, and the next session reads an open question where the user believes they closed one.

OBSERVED TWICE IN THIS PROJECT'S OWN HISTORY, which is what makes the hint dangerous rather than untidy: the brainstorm skill records that its step 2 ONCE READ 'this call is not optional: add_decision defaults to accepted' — true until 2026-07-25, then quietly false, and two dev_storyflow sessions measured and filed it independently on 2026-08-08. The skill was corrected to CHECK WHAT THE TOOL RETURNED rather than to name its default. THE HINT ON THE TOOL ITSELF WAS NOT GIVEN THE SAME TREATMENT.

FIX SHAPE: emit the hint only when the write actually created a node at `proposed`, or state the status the node now holds rather than the status a new node would have had. The information needed is in hand at the moment the hint is written.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any Decision in any project has actually been demoted this way — he explicitly did not do it, and nobody has swept the snapshots for an accepted-to-proposed transition with no user behind it.

`add_verification` CANNOT SET `description` OR `location`, SO A CHECK RECORDED INCREMENTALLY CANNOT SAY WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS. Reported with a proposed `create_node` merge as the retrofit; a peer then corrected the prescription within the hour with the better answer — `import_graph` takes a DOCUMENT, and a document reaches the WHOLE schema, so BULK creation already has a route that does not need the constructor widened. ⚠️ THAT DOES NOT RETIRE THIS: bulk has a document route and INCREMENTAL work does not. Recording one verification mid-session is a typed call, and that call still cannot reach the field. The constructor is still too narrow; it is just no longer the only door, and it is the wrong door for bulk. SEPARATELY AND CHEAPLY: the `adopt` skill ALREADY recommends the document route but justifies it on TOOL-CALL COST — a reader who does not care about call count reads that as a performance tip and skips it, which is exactly what happened. Fidelity is the better reason and one sentence in that skill would have prevented both this retrofit and a second seat's. || SOURCE: Observed by the dev_storyflow fleet on 2026-08-15, on reflow2 0.31.0 with served == installed verified through /proc/<pid>/exe. Three agent seats, one shared graph, one day.

▸ HALF ADDRESSED 2026-08-15. The cheap half is done: the `adopt` skill now justifies the import document on FIDELITY — a document reaches the whole schema and the constructors do not — instead of on tool-call count, and says out loud that there is no incremental equivalent. The constructor itself is UNCHANGED: `add_verification` still cannot set `description` or `location`, so VALID_TO stays absent.

properties.statement: `add_verification` CANNOT SET `kind`, `status` OR `last_run_at`, SO RECORDING ONE VALIDATION TAKES FOUR CALLS AND THE NODE IS BORN AS THE VERY THING THE GAP SAID WAS INSUFFICIENT. Three reporters, dev_storyflow, 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-08. (1) w-ec25cf2c, answering an `unvalidated_capability` gap for ONE capability, had to run: add_verification -> set_verification_kind(validation) -> verifies(...) -> set_verification_status(passing, last_run_at). `add_verification` accepts `method` and `level` but NOT `kind`, so a node created specifically to satisfy an unvalidated_capability gap is born `kind: verification` — which is exactly what that gap says is already present and not enough. THE DEFAULT IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE INTENT IN THE ONE WORKFLOW THAT MOST OFTEN CREATES THESE. (2) w-fb7d30ab hit the other missing parameter: `add_verification` upserts name/level/method but has no `last_run_at`, so a node UPDATED to describe a NEW run keeps the OLD run's date. They re-ran stack_currency.py on 2026-08-07 and recorded the result into `ver:fleet_stack_currency_gate`; the node's text then described the 08-07 run while `last_run_at` still read `2026-08-03`. The node was internally inconsistent AND THE WRITE REPORTED SUCCESS with nothing saying so. They looked for a route out and could not find one — `reconcile_verification` looked like the intended path but takes real test-run outcomes, which is a different act from 're-ran a measurement script'. (3) 2026-08-08, w-4d05e937 (LANE UNSUSPECTED-VALIDATION-WALK) ADDS THE THIRD MISSING PARAMETER AND THE REASON IT IS WORSE THAN INCONVENIENT. `status` is missing too, so the node is born `kind: verification, status: planned` — THE EXACT TWO VALUES THAT MAKE IT NOT ANSWER THE GAP. Their framing is the one to keep: BETWEEN CALL 1 AND CALL 4 THE GRAPH HOLDS A NODE ASSERTING SOMETHING NOBODY MEANT, and on a `--shared` graph THAT WINDOW IS VISIBLE TO EVERY OTHER ATTACHED SESSION. What was a four-call annoyance on a single-writer store is a publication of a false claim on a shared one, for as long as the sequence takes. They filed it knowing the `kind` half was already reported, per the file's own no-dedup rule. FIX SHAPE, from all three: accept `kind`, `status`, `last_run_at` and a `verifies` target on add_verification, collapsing four calls to one; or have the gap's own prompt name the exact call sequence; and either accept `last_run_at` or have the upsert WARN when name/description change while last_run_at does not. THE REUSABLE FRAMING: a date that silently belongs to a previous run is the same failure class as 'a documented constant is not a measurement' — and an intermediate state visible to other writers is the same failure class as a non-atomic write.

properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-17, AND IT COST THE OWNER A DELIBERATE ACTION THAT DID NOTHING. AGENTS.md said: "every new session and every `/mcp` reconnect serves a fresh binary automatically", and "you must `/mcp` reconnect reflow2 (or restart the session) for the live tools to pick it up". THAT IS FALSE WHENEVER A SHARED SERVER IS RUNNING, WHICH IS THE NORMAL CASE IN THIS REPO. `--shared` re-attaches to the long-lived `--serve-shared` daemon, and the daemon goes on executing the image it started from; the reconnect spawns a fresh CLIENT against a stale SERVER, so it looks like it worked and changes nothing.

THE NUMBERS. heal.rs was widened and the binary rebuilt at 22:13:23. Anthony ran `/mcp` at 22:16:28 SPECIFICALLY to make the change live, which spawned pid 2334559 (`--shared`). The `--serve-shared` daemon pid 2227071 had been up since 18:18:47 and kept serving. `detect_defects` answered `total: 20` — the pre-change number — from code no longer on disk. After `--stop-shared` and a respawn the same call answered `total: 34`.

⭐ THE PART THAT MAKES THIS THIS REQUIREMENT'S BUSINESS RATHER THAN A DOC TYPO: THE SERVER KNEW. `req:the-server-is-the-authority-on-its-own-currency` is built, and `STALE_NOTE` in service.rs has said the right thing since 2026-08-11 — "A SESSION RESTART ALONE, WITHOUT `--stop-shared`, CHANGES NOTHING". But `served_by.stale` rides on `graph_report` ALONE. `loop_status` and `detect_defects` — the calls a session actually makes to read debt and defects — carry no such block, so every number they returned came from a replaced binary with nothing saying so. A report that cannot say whether its own code is current is the same failure as one that cannot say whether its checks ran.

FIXED HERE: AGENTS.md now names `--stop-shared` and records that the old wording was wrong, and points at `served_by.stale` as the authority.

STILL OWED: carrying the staleness block on `loop_status` and `detect_defects`, or a reason it belongs only on the rollup. NOT DONE ON A GUESS — whether every read should pay for the `/proc/self/exe` check is a cost question nobody has answered.

THE TWO INSTRUMENTS THAT WOULD REVEAL AN UNPOPULATED DECOMPOSITION BOTH REPORT SUCCESS. Measured 2026-08-07 on reflow2's own design while answering Anthony's question about recursive black-box decomposition. (1) evaluate_allocation returns modularity 1.0 with total_external 0 and total_internal 1 — a PERFECT modularity score computed over exactly ONE dependency. Every one of the 44 listed components reports external_weight 0 and internal_weight 0. The graph holds 171 DEPENDS_ON edges; the allocation evaluator sees one, so the metric is structurally starved and the number it prints is 1/1. graph_report_markdown renders this as "Allocation health: Modularity 1.00 across 44 component(s); 0 misplaced capability(ies). No god-components." (2) hierarchy_issues returns count 0 on a hierarchy that is TWO levels deep and INCOMPLETE: 8 subsystems contain 42 components, and 6 ordinary components sit outside every subsystem — 14 component roots in total. Neither the shallowness nor the six orphans is reported. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN EITHER NUMBER: req:recursive-black-box-decomposition is original intent — Anthony's words, "one of the primary things I designed it for" — and the reason it went unnoticed is that the design's own health readout says the decomposition is perfect. This is the exact pattern the standing feedback names: a green gate is the weakest evidence in the building, and 0 gaps / 0 defects / loop clean held throughout eleven releases in which ten schema domains were invisible. Here the same shape appears one layer in: the allocation analysis cannot distinguish a well-modularised design from one with almost no modelled dependencies, and reports the second as the first. THE COMPANION MEASUREMENT, which is the real hole: 5 Interface nodes and 5 PROVIDES / 5 CONSUMES edges for 56 components. The trajectory already reports this honestly as seams 0% (0/73) and calls it the frontier — so the SEAM metric is candid where the ALLOCATION metric is not, about the same underlying emptiness. NOT A REQUEST TO CHANGE THE MODULARITY FORMULA: dec:report-dont-judge is deliberate and granularity_report's refusal to rule is right. What is wrong is a metric reporting a value at all when its denominator is one, instead of saying it has too little to measure — the same distinction dec:loop-status-cannot-say-it-never-looked already raises for unsurfaced_gaps, where "clean" and "never scanned" are the same answer.

properties.statement:
A PROJECT CAN RUN REFLOW2 WITH NO KIT INSTALLED, AND NOTHING IN THE SURFACE SAYS SO. A STALE KIT IS DETECTED; AN ABSENT ONE IS SILENT. Reported by dev_storyflow's api-boss sidekick (`551d9718`), 2026-08-15, measured on their own project.

WHAT THEY MEASURED: dev_storyflow has been designed in reflow2 since 2026-07-21 — MCP tools, served skills, a live shared server on 0.31.0, 1,590 nodes, and a committed export tracked in git. It does NOT have `.reflow2/kit-version.json`, `tools/reflow2_check.py` or `tools/loop_nudge.py`. A find across both their repos returned zero hits.

⇒ THE CONSUMER CI COHERENCE GATE HAS NEVER EXISTED IN THE PROJECT IT WAS BUILT FOR, and its one prerequisite — a committed export — has been satisfied the whole time. `getting-started/SETUP.md` says '`tools/reflow2_check.py` (in the kit)', which is true OF THE KIT and false of this installation.

⭐ WHY THE ONE SIGNAL PRESENT DID NOT HELP, and this is the sharp part. `loop_status` does emit `"nudge": "absent"` with an advisory — but that advisory is about the SESSION-END NUDGE. A fleet with its own harness Stop hook (this one has) reads it, correctly concludes 'covered, not my problem', and moves on. NOTHING ANYWHERE SAYS THE CI GATE IS ALSO MISSING. Two absences, one report, and the report names the wrong one.

CORROBORATED FROM THIS SESSION'S OWN SURFACE: every `loop_status` call here returned `"nudge": "installed"` and NO kit field of any kind. Installation state is not something the tool can be asked about.

⭐⭐ THE ARGUMENT THEY OFFER RATHER THAN THE REQUEST, and it is the better half: `check_kit_manifest.py` already answers 'does an installed kit agree with its source?' — a question that PRESUPPOSES A KIT. The unasked question is 'is there one?', and it is the one that fails toward calm. A STALE KIT IS DETECTED, AN ABSENT KIT IS SILENT. Same family as the directory-artifact crash: a check honest about the case it was built for and mute about the case one step outside it.

PAIRS WITH `fact:defect-a-stale-kit-receipt-silently-decides-whether-the-loop-nudge-is-owed`, from Alex's report the same day, and TOGETHER THEY SAY SOMETHING NEITHER SAYS ALONE: `.reflow2/kit-version.json` is READ (the nudge branches on its `harnesses` key) and NEVER REPORTED. One file, consulted for a narrow harness decision, carrying the only evidence of whether the consumer half of the product is installed at all — and no tool surfaces it. Alex's case was a stamp twenty versions stale; theirs is no stamp at all; both are invisible for the same reason.

THEIR ASK, cheapest first: have `loop_status` or `graph_report` report kit installation state as ITS OWN FIELD, distinct from nudge state — `kit: absent | stale | v0.31.0`. And their framing of the tone is right: 'a project running reflow2 without the kit is not a broken project and should not be scolded, but it is STRUCTURALLY UNABLE TO GATE ON DRIFT.'

BOUND THEY STATE THEMSELVES: they did not test whether running `reflow2_init.py` on that repo now is safe — it writes into `.claude/`, which their fleet hand-built. Nothing here claims the install is a one-command fix, only that its ABSENCE is currently unreportable.

NOT ESTABLISHED: how many other consumer projects are in this state. dev_storyflow is one of three known designs and the only one measured.

properties.statement:
AN ACCEPTED DECISION WAS WIDENED BY AN AGENT'S DEBUGGING HYPOTHESIS, AND NOTHING ASKED WHETHER THE RULE WAS CHANGING OR THE CODE WAS WRONG. Alex's Grok 4.6 session, 2026-08-14 (item 4, graded by him as one of the report's most serious).

WHAT HAPPENED, in his words: 'The UTC/civil-date bug and the \"just joined\" waiver are different claims. I merged a GENEROUS WAIVER into an ACCEPTED Decision while debugging the UTC bound... The user had to walk it back.' He notes correctly that graph-text-is-data did not stop him and should not have — this was his own write, not injected content.

THE MISSING QUESTION, which is the whole finding: 'Nothing in revise-design asks \"are you changing the rule or fixing as-built to match the rule you already have?\"' Those are opposite acts with identical mechanics — both are a typed merge onto a Decision — and only one of them is the user's to authorise.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE SESSION: `dec:certainty-derived` holds that moving a status is the user's word and an agent doing it forges their signature. WIDENING AN ACCEPTED DECISION'S TEXT IS THE SAME ACT WITHOUT TOUCHING THE STATUS FIELD — the decision still reads `accepted`, so every reader downstream treats the agent's hypothesis as something the owner settled. The protection is on the status and not on the content it certifies.

HIS PROPOSED FIX, recorded as his: 'when merging an accepted Decision, require an explicit \"this is a new rule\" vs \"restore prior accepted text / as-built was wrong\". Or refuse to widen an accepted gate without `set_decision_status proposed` first.' The second form has a precedent in this design — `set_artifact_checksum` refuses a silent accept and demands a disposition for exactly this class of erosion.

RELATED, AND MEASURED THE SAME DAY: `dec:idea-should-record-change-refuse-a-snapshot-of-state-that-already-moved` holds the sibling question about the snapshot, and `fact:defect-record-change-overwrites-the-name-of-the-event-it-is-filed-under` is a third failure of the same call. Three findings now converge on `record_change` and the typed merge onto accepted nodes.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any accepted Decision in reflow2's own design has been silently widened this way — the snapshots exist to answer that and nobody has swept them.

They closed it properly for `cap:counterability_guarantee` with a passing `kind=validation` check, and `unsurfaced_gaps` stayed at 69 — because the gap is still open for the other 47. THAT IS ARITHMETICALLY CORRECT AND OPERATIONALLY USELESS: a worker cannot see their own contribution, and a boss cannot see progress against it. The cost compounds with the ownership problem reported the same day — a standing number that never moves in response to real work is the definition of wallpaper, and five consecutive seats reported the identical rollup with none of them moving it. FIX SHAPE, from the reporter: either emit per-capability items, or report a `remaining`/`closed` count on the aggregate so partial progress is legible.

properties.statement: "WHICH OF MY RULES HAVE NO DETECTOR?" IS NOT A QUESTION THE GRAPH CAN BE ASKED — AND REFLOW2'S OWN ANSWER IS FOUR OUT OF FOUR. Proposed by dev_storyflow's api-boss 5d608b85, 2026-08-08, as the one high-leverage item in a GOVERNANCE-AS-DESIGN opportunity built on Anthony's own words. MEASURED HERE THE SAME DAY, and the number is the argument: reflow2 has 5 DesignRules; FOUR carry `enforced: true` (rule:bl-135, rule:bl-212, rule:bl-41, rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party) which the schema defines as 'violations are gate-blocking'; and NOT ONE of the five has an incoming VERIFIES edge. Four rules that block the build, zero detectors, and no report names it. THE MECHANISM: `schema/verify.yaml:80` declares VERIFIES as `from: Verification, to: "*"`. The wildcard ACCEPTS a DesignRule target — nothing is broken — but it does not MODEL it, so `describe_schema` ranks it as merely accepted and no detector treats rules as verifiable things. AGENTS.md already warns about exactly this distinction: 'several will validate, and validating is not the same as meaning what you intended.' Here the cost of the wildcard is not a wrong edge but an unaskable question. THEIR EVIDENCE, which is stronger than ours: in ONE session that fleet found five rules with no check — a routing rule naming a file that names no worker entry point; a verification step that false-negatives on a shared tree; a comms rule whose quoted example is a forgeable handshake; a claim protocol with no detector for its own bypass; and a detector built for that bypass that was blind to it. Their words: 'Every one is a RULE WITHOUT A CHECK, and no report could have listed them, because the graph cannot currently be asked.' FIX SHAPE, theirs, and it is small: enumerate VERIFIES' `to:` explicitly rather than leaving it wildcard, then make `enforced: true` with no incoming VERIFIES a detectable defect. CHECKED BEFORE PROPOSING, twice. (1) THE STAMP DOES NOT MOVE: it carries `edge_type_names`, `edge_types`, `node_type_names`, `node_types`, `schema_version` — not endpoint lists — so modelling the endpoints owes NO upgrade doc, which makes this far cheaper than a normal schema change. (2) THE SAFE ENUMERATION IS KNOWN: VERIFIES today points at Capability (126), Requirement (3), Artifact (3), Component (1), so narrowing must include all four or it would invalidate live edges. THEIR COUNTER-ARGUMENT IS THE BEST PART AND MUST SURVIVE INTO THE BUILD: 'A GRAPH NODE GREEN-WASHES EXACTLY LIKE A DOCUMENT' — proven twice in their own graph, where nine directory artifacts swallowed 373 files while the check read green. Governance-in-graph without executable checks is prettier prose with identical blind spots, which is why the DETECTOR is the proposal and the vocabulary is not.

properties.statement:
THE PROTECTION CURVE IS INVERTED: A NEAR-TWIN ID GETS A PARAGRAPH OF CAREFUL REFUSAL, AND AN EXACT ID — THE ONLY CASE THAT DESTROYS CONTENT — GETS NO SIGNAL AT ALL. Reported by dev_storyflow's api-boss sidekick (`551d9718`), 2026-08-15, and CORROBORATED FROM THIS SESSION'S OWN TRANSCRIPT, which exercised both halves heavily.

THEIR MEASUREMENT: they overwrote one Decision THREE times by exact id, and 'the tool's response was byte-shaped identical to a clean create every time. No `created: true|false`, no \"this id already existed\", nothing.'

CORROBORATED HERE, 2026-08-15: this session called `create_node` on existing ids repeatedly and deliberately — merging a corroboration into a TemporalFact, repairing a Decision whose text had a stray tag, restoring a ChangeEvent name — and every reply was shaped exactly like a create. THE BEHAVIOUR IS DOCUMENTED ('An existing id MERGES: the props you pass overwrite') AND IS NEVER REPORTED AT CALL TIME, which are different things: a caller who did not intend a merge has no way to learn they performed one.

⭐ AND THE GUARD IS THE PROOF IT NEED NOT BE, which is why they filed praise and defect as ONE item rather than two. This session hit the near-duplicate guard FIVE times, and it was right every time: it refused, NAMED the neighbouring node, declined to assert a duplicate ('this is not a duplicate accusation'), and offered `distinct_from` so that 'I read it and judged it different' became a RECORDED act rather than an unexplained near-twin. Their four-point analysis of why it is good is accurate and worth keeping: it does not merge for you; it names the node; it declines to claim what it cannot know; and it makes the judgement durable.

⚠️ THE CASE THAT MATTERS IS NOT THE REPORTER'S OWN, and they say so: theirs was recoverable — own node, seconds old. The dangerous one is a worker acting on a brief that NAMES AN ID, landing on a node another session wrote. There the overwrite is silent, the response reads as success, and the loss is somebody else's work. dev_storyflow's own `AGENTS.md` warns workers in bold before their first write that 're-using a node id is a WRITE that overwrites' — A PROJECT SHOULD NOT HAVE TO TEACH IN PROSE WHAT THE SURFACE COULD REPORT IN A FIELD.

THE ASK IS ONE FIELD: return `created: true|false` (or `overwrote_existing`) on every `add_*` / `create_node`. Cheap, non-breaking, and it makes the mistake legible IN THE TRANSCRIPT rather than discoverable only by someone re-reading the node later.

⚠️ ONE REFINEMENT TO THEIR REPORT, from evidence they did not have. They file as friction that the guard 'reports neighbours not already in `distinct_from`, ONE CALL AT A TIME', making five siblings a walk. THIS SESSION SAW IT NAME THREE AT ONCE, twice — so the behaviour is not a hard one-at-a-time limit; it is whichever neighbours score above threshold on that call. Their walk is real and the cause is narrower than stated.

SAME FAMILY, FOUND HERE THE SAME DAY: `fact:defect-record-change-overwrites-the-name-of-the-event-it-is-filed-under` — a different call silently replacing a property the caller did not mean to touch. TWO INDEPENDENT INSTANCES OF WRITES THAT REPORT SUCCESS AND SAY NOTHING ABOUT WHAT THEY REPLACED.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any real cross-session overwrite has occurred — both measured cases were the author's own node, and nothing sweeps for it.

properties.statement:
A PROPERTY THE SCHEMA HAS NEVER HEARD OF IS ACCEPTED, STORED AND ECHOED BACK — so a plausible-sounding invented field looks exactly like a real one, and the setting it was supposed to control silently does nothing.

MEASURED 2026-08-16, on my own write, and found only because a gap fired that should not have. Recording a DesignRule I intended to be advisory, I passed `enforcement: "advisory"`. `create_node` accepted it, stored it, and echoed it back in the reply. `get_node` returned it. THE SCHEMA DECLARES NO SUCH PROPERTY — `enforcement` appears nowhere in any schema file for DesignRule; the real field is `enforced`, a BOOL (`schema/core.yaml:107`, three states: true / false / unset), and the detector reads exactly that (`detect.rs:2634`).

⇒ SO THE WRITE SUCCEEDED AND MEANT NOTHING. The rule stayed in the `unstated` band and `detect_gaps` raised '“…” does not say whether breaking it stops the build' at severity 0.40 — correctly, since nothing had said. The gap firing is what exposed it. Had that detector not existed, or had the rule been of a type nothing checks, the invented property would have sat there indefinitely, readable, plausible, and inert.

⭐ WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH A NODE IS THE PAIRING WITH THE GUARDS THAT DO EXIST, which is the same argument as `fact:defect-a-property-naming-a-node-is-unguarded-while-edges-are-not` and strictly stronger. That one is about a DECLARED property (`subject_id`) holding a dangling value. This is about a property the schema never declared at all. Meanwhile `ver:edges-need-both-ends` refuses an edge to a missing node through sixteen typed helpers with an atomicity case and a size floor, and `create_node` itself refuses an unknown NODE TYPE by name rather than answering null. ⇒ The vocabulary is guarded at the type level and at the edge level, and unguarded at the property level in BOTH directions — unknown names in, dangling references out.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, because it is a real design position and not an oversight to patch: the store is a property BAG, and open-world properties are what let a project record things reflow2 did not anticipate. Refusing unknown keys outright would break that. ⇒ The question is therefore not 'validate strictly' but 'can a caller tell an EXTENSION from a TYPO', and today it cannot — the reply is identical.

CHEAPEST FORMS, in rising cost: (1) ECHO WHAT WAS UNRECOGNISED — the reply already lists the properties it stored, so naming which of them the schema does not declare costs one comparison and no policy; (2) name the nearest declared property, since `enforcement` vs `enforced` is one edit distance and the near-duplicate guard already does exactly this kind of suggestion for node ids; (3) a strict mode nobody has asked for.

📌 REPORTED AGAINST MYSELF, and the honest half is that a schema read would have prevented it: `describe_schema {node_type: "DesignRule"}` lists the real fields and I did not call it before writing — I called it for the REQUIRED fields only (`required_only: true`), which by construction omits the optional property I then invented. That is a small trap of its own: the compact answer is the one most likely to be used before a write, and it is the one that cannot show you the field you are about to get wrong.

properties.statement: `volatility: append_only` IS A PROPERTY OF THE FILE WHILE 'DOES THIS CHANGE CARRY DESIGN MEANING' IS A PROPERTY OF THE EDIT — SO A STRUCTURAL REWRITE INSIDE AN APPEND-ONLY ARTIFACT IS EXEMPTED SILENTLY. Reported by api-boss `5d608b85` (dev_storyflow, 2026-08-08), and the report opens by crediting the Stop hook for catching an omission of theirs. WHAT HAPPENED: they made 5 graph writes (a concurrency probe, created and deleted, net zero) and also edited `P.md`, a REGISTERED Artifact, changing a BINDING worker rule. They ran loop_status and it reported `undispositioned_drift: 0`. That zero means NO DETECTOR HAD LOOKED AT THE CHANGED FILE, not that the file was unchanged. The Stop hook — not loop_status — is what said 'file(s) changed this session with no ChangeEvent recorded'. They state plainly they would otherwise have finished the session believing the loop was clean. THE DESIGN ISSUE UNDERNEATH: `art:fleet_bus_p` carries `volatility: append_only`, which is correct and useful for a bus, where a routine post should not owe a drift disposition forever. But their edit was NOT an append — it was a structural rewrite of binding rules inside the same file. An append-only marker therefore exempts EVERY change to that file, including ones that move the design, and nothing anywhere reports that an exemption was applied. Today an exemption and a genuinely clean file look identical. FIX SHAPE: have append_only suppress drift REPORTING while still letting a caller record a `design_updated` disposition — or better, have the reconcile output say 'N artifacts exempted by volatility', so the exemption is visible rather than silent. WHAT THE LOOP BOUGHT THEM, reported because they expected bookkeeping and got a finding: propagate_change on the recorded event returned 55 impacted nodes and, at distance 3, a RISK CROSSING on `req:fleet_no_idle_worker` — their change inserts a mandatory orientation step between a worker being claimed and starting work, and the graph flagged the tension with the fleet's own never-idle requirement, which they had not considered and no reviewer had raised. They judged the tension acceptable but say they would not have known to make the judgement at all. They also recorded the disposition properly via set_artifact_checksum(design_updated, chg:...) and called the refusal-to-accept-silently good design that should be kept.

properties.statement: `describe_schema`'s HINT FOR `CAUSES.validation_status` NAMES FOUR VALUES, AND THE ENUM ACCEPTS FOUR DIFFERENT ONES. Found here, in this repo, on 2026-08-08, by following describe_schema and being refused. The hint reads: 'Whether the causal claim has been tested (observational / intervention / mechanism / temporal).' The enum is `["unvalidated", "hypothesis", "validated", "refuted"]`. NOT ONE OF THE FOUR WORDS IN THE PROSE IS ACCEPTED. I called describe_schema BEFORE writing the edge — which is what AGENTS.md says to do instead of guessing — read the parenthetical as the value list, and the write was refused. THE REFUSAL WAS EXCELLENT and is why this is minor: it named the edge, the property, the offered value and all four accepted ones, so the fix took one retry and no investigation. The cost is one round trip; the significance is the class. THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE brainstorm/add_decision DRIFT REPORTED BY dev_storyflow THE SAME DAY, one layer lower: two halves of the SAME served surface, shipped from the SAME binary, disagreeing about that binary's behaviour — there a skill against a tool, here a property's description against its own validator. And it is the more troubling instance of the two, because a description sitting beside the enum it describes has NOTHING between them: no build step, no separate file, no drift window. Whatever guard dec:idea-a-skill-may-assert-the-defaults-it-relies-on settles on for skills, a description and its enum living in one struct ought to be checkable mechanically and is not. FIX SHAPE: correct the hint to the accepted values; and consider a lint that fails when a property description contains a parenthesised slash-separated list whose members are not the property's enum values — crude, but it would have caught this one and it is the pattern every such hint uses. NOTE THE HONEST BOUND ON MY OWN CLAIM: I did not audit the other property descriptions. This is one instance found by tripping over it, not a survey, and the survey is the obvious next step.

properties.statement:
`add_change_event`'s `change_type` ENUM HAS NO VALUE FOR A DEFECT FOUND IN THE FIELD, SO RECORDING ONE FORCES A SMALL FICTION. Hit here on 2026-08-08 recording the DUPLICATES/merge fix. The enum is `requirement_creep | new_feature | test_failure_fix | performance_optimization | refactor | scope_change | constraint_change | environment_change | deprecation | resync | baseline_established`. The change being recorded was a defect REPORTED BY A USER of the built system — dev_storyflow's fleet — and diagnosed here. No test had failed; there was no test at all, which was part of the defect. `test_failure_fix` was chosen as the nearest fit and the event NAME says explicitly that no failing test existed, so the ledger is not silently wrong — but the structured field still says something untrue and only the prose corrects it. WHY THIS IS NOT PEDANTRY, and the schema itself makes the argument: `baseline_established` exists precisely because forcing a record-only change through `refactor`/`test_failure_fix` 'writes a fiction into the ledger that exists to prevent fiction' (its own description, BL-157). That reasoning applies unchanged one category along. THE DISTINCTION WORTH KEEPING if a value is added: a defect found by a CHECK and a defect found by a USER are different provenance for the same repair, and reflow2 already cares about that difference everywhere else — `set_provenance` grades authored/inferred/reconciled, and `cap:independent-evidence` refuses to let evidence a value was fitted to count as validating it. FIX SHAPE: add `defect_fix` (or `field_report_fix`); or, smaller, let the event carry a `reported_by`/`found_by` property so the how-it-was-found is structured rather than narrated. NOTE THE MILD IRONY, recorded because it is the same class the fleet reported six times: this is a structured field that answers a slightly different question than the writer's, and the only thing preserving the truth is prose beside it — which is exactly fact:defect-verification-evidence-is-prose-so-passing-can-contradict-itself, one node type over.

═══ CORROBORATED BY A SECOND PROJECT, AND THE COUNT IS NOW FIVE (2026-08-15) ═══

This stopped being one maintainer's papercut. Alex's Grok 4.6 session, 2026-08-14, hit it INDEPENDENTLY on a different project with no knowledge of this node, and filed it as its number-one issue (docs/feedback/2026-08-14-alex-grok-session.md, item 1): it tried `bugfix`, was refused, and settled on `test_failure_fix` for a client cache leaving a derived flag stale — 'The enum forces a lie.' It reached the same fix shape unprompted: 'a type for \"implementation defect against existing intent\" (or document that test_failure_fix is that bucket).' TWO AGENTS ON TWO PROJECTS DERIVING THE SAME MISSING VALUE FROM THE SAME ELEVEN OPTIONS is the evidence this node lacked on 2026-08-08, when it was a single observation.

AND THE LEDGER ALREADY CONTAINS THE PATTERN, which nobody had counted: (1) `chg:duplicate-merge-needs-a-human-20260808` — `test_failure_fix`, no test existed; (2) `chg:accept-acb06c45b63a7b6d` — `test_failure_fix`, whose own name says 'recorded under test_failure_fix because the enum has no value meaning \"the code was wrong\"'; (3) `chg:arrival-delta-decided` — `scope_change` 'used as least-wrong: nothing in the enum means \"an open question was settled\"'; (4) Alex's session, 2026-08-14; (5) `chg:change-type-gap-corroborated-by-a-second-project` — THIS VERY EDIT, filed under `resync` because nothing means 'the design's knowledge of an unchanged fact improved'. FIVE FORCED CHOICES, and reflow2's own ledger is where four of them are written down.

⭐ THE SHARPENING, and it changes the fix: (3) and (5) are NOT the missing defect value. 'An open question was settled' and 'what we know moved while the thing did not' are two further meanings with no home. So the enum is short by at least three, which makes 'add `defect_fix`' the wrong shape of answer — it fixes the loudest instance and leaves the pattern. THE PATTERN IS THAT `change_type` CONFLATES TWO AXES: what happened to the SYSTEM (new_feature, refactor, deprecation) and what happened to the RECORD (baseline_established, resync, and the three missing ones). `baseline_established`'s own doc comment already says so — 'the odd one out, and deliberately so. Every other variant answers why the thing changed; this one says the thing did not change and only the design's knowledge of it did' — which names the second axis while leaving it with exactly one member and a reservation preventing its use. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether splitting the axes (a `subject: system|record` alongside a narrower type) is better than adding three values; that is a schema question and Anthony's call. NOTE the enum values are NOT counted by the version stamp, so adding values is not a schema break — established when the `medium` enum question was dissolved.

properties.statement: A `verified` CAPABILITY WHOSE CENTRAL CLAIM IS FALSE IN THE INSTALLED DEFAULT DEPLOYMENT: SEAT LIVENESS IS THE SHARED SERVER'S PID, SO `gone` IS UNREACHABLE AND EVERY CLAIM OUTLIVES THE SESSION THAT MADE IT. `cap:claim-liveness` is status `verified` and its description states that claim_report 'COMPUTES liveness by asking the operating system whether that process still exists' and that 'a claim whose session exited is reported `gone`'. Measured by w-613d836b in dev_storyflow 2026-08-07: mint_seat returned `ajs77:2304014:4265e97f`; pid 2304014 is the `reflow2-mcp --serve-shared` daemon, while their own session's shell was 2315377 — different processes entirely. CONFIRMED IN THIS REPO: crates/reflow2-core/src/identity.rs:388 mints the seat as `format!("{}:{}:{mint}", machine(), std::process::id())`, and under `--shared` that code runs IN THE DAEMON, so the pid recorded is the server's for every seat it ever mints. The daemon is detached and outlives every client by design. THEREFORE the liveness probe asks whether the server is running — which it is, or nothing could have answered — and the answer is `live` for every claim, forever. IT FAILS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: (a) a worker that died hours ago still reads as holding its region, so a peer defers to nobody, which is precisely the advisory report starting to lie that the capability's own description says exclusion from overlaps exists to prevent; (b) after a `--stop-shared` bounce the replacement daemon has a new pid, so EVERY seat minted before it is orphaned at once and nothing surfaces that. WHY THE CHECK DID NOT CATCH IT: the property was true under the old one-process-per-session stdio transport, where the serving process WAS the session. `--shared` became the installed default and the world moved; the verification did not, and nothing recomputes a check when the deployment model changes underneath it. This is the same class as the served-version gap the same fleet hit the same day — a literal that stayed satisfied while the invariant it stood for broke. FIX SHAPE, from the reporter and consistent with the design: record the CLIENT's identity — the Contributor handle claim_region is already given — alongside the server pid and compute liveness from that; or at minimum have claim_report mark any seat whose pid differs from the currently-serving pid as `stale: server-restarted` rather than `live`. The `stale` array already exists in the response shape.

properties.statement: `claim_region`'s OWN DESCRIPTION DESCRIBES THE PRE-`--shared` WORLD AS FACT, AND ITS `seat` PARAMETER DOCUMENTS A REFUSAL THAT DOES NOT HAPPEN. Reported three times across two weeks. (1) The description states the claim is 'only as fresh as the last pull, because the design lives as a file in each checkout WITH NO SHARED SERVER (dec:multi-writer-architecture)' — read by api-boss `5d608b85` while running exactly a shared server with 7 attached processes. THIS REPO CONFIRMS THE TEXT IS STILL SHIPPED: the CLAIMS edge hint in the schema reads 'the design lives as a file in each person's checkout with no shared server to hold a lock'. Both architectures are supported; the description asserts one of them as fact, so a session reading it in a `--shared` deployment builds a wrong mental model of what a claim even IS. (2) The `seat` parameter's docs say that on the SESSIONLESS transport a handler is built per request, so omitting `seat` 'is REFUSED rather than answered with a seat that would change on your next call'. w-10f94d47 omitted it. It was NOT refused — the call succeeded and the server returned `seat: "ajs77:2304014:0e0681c1"`. Either the behaviour changed or the transport there is not the sessionless one; either way the schema text and the behaviour disagree, and a reader who believes the schema will either mint a seat they did not need or read a success as a bug. They flagged it as not-blocking and reported it anyway because a silent workaround forfeits the fix. (3) w-8da9c31c reported on 2026-08-03 that the description still described the pre-`--shared` world. THE PATTERN THESE SIT IN, named by w-10f94d47: three version-dependent facts landed in copied instruction blocks in ONE DAY with no version stamp and no expiry — the served_by 0.22.1 literal, the mint_seat correction, and this schema note. Their suggestion: have the SERVER be the authority, stating 'as of 0.24.0' next to any tool-existence claim, so a copied doc can be CHECKED against the running binary instead of trusted. A doc that cannot be distinguished from a stale doc is indistinguishable from a wrong one.

properties.statement: cap:content-store is built and its surface check passes, yet the shipped binary does the one thing that check says it must not do: it INVENTS a blob directory nobody chose. ver:content-surface passes and claims 'A SERVER WITH NO --content-path CONFIGURED REFUSES BY NAME instead of inventing a directory'. But crates/reflow2-mcp/src/main.rs:30 declares #[arg(long, default_value = "./reflow2-content")], so main.rs:809 and :881 always pass Some(default) and the refusal at service.rs:2464 is UNREACHABLE from the real binary. The test proving the refusal, a_server_with_no_content_store_says_so_instead_of_choosing_one (crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/tools.rs:2795), builds ReflowService::in_memory(), whose builder default is content_path: None (service.rs:2425) — a state the shipped server can never be in. So the check is green against a configuration that does not ship. The store has also never held anything: content_manifest returns entries [], total_bytes 0, store_root './reflow2-content' for a directory that exists nowhere on disk, and of 136 Fragment nodes ZERO carry a content_ref, so missing:[] is honest rather than reassuring. Both ver:content-store and ver:content-manifest remain PLANNED. Consequence, unexercised only because content_put has never been called: the first put would create ./reflow2-content relative to the server's CWD, while .gitattributes already carries 'reflow2-content/** binary' assuming repo root and .gitignore never mentions it — so committed-by-design blobs would land at a cwd-dependent, unignored path. service.rs:2458's own doc comment already states the correct rule, citing req:no-silent-fallback: 'Fails loud rather than defaulting to a directory nobody chose.' Two adjacent files contradict each other and the default is the culprit.

properties.statement: TWO SURFACES SHARE THE NAME `create_node` AND HAVE OPPOSITE SEMANTICS, and every consumer-facing document describes the wrong one. The MCP TOOL `create_node` MERGES: crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/query.rs:64 calls `g.upsert_node(...)`, and its own tool description says so ("An existing id MERGES: the props you pass overwrite, every stored property you omit survives"). The RUST method `DesignGraph::create_node` REPLACES (graph.rs:220, "Create (or replace)"). An agent can only call the tool; it cannot call the method. THREE PLACES TELL THE AGENT THE METHOD'S SEMANTICS FOR THE TOOL: (1) the served `revise-design` SKILL — "Do NOT reach for the generic `create_node` to revise. It is create-or-replace, so passing only the changed field resets every other property to its schema default — which silently downgrades an `accepted` requirement to `proposed`, reopens a settled Decision, and drops an artifact's checksum." (2) ver:constructors-preserve's description — "create_node and import_graph deliberately still REPLACE". (3) crates/reflow2-core/tests/upsert.rs module doc. MEASURED FALSE 2026-08-07 on invented nodes in a throwaway graph, using the skill's own scare case: a Requirement set to status=accepted, then `create_node` with props={statement} ALONE. Result — statement changed, and status stayed "accepted"; name, priority, provenance, concern, designation, kind and lineage all survived. Nothing was reset. Confirmed twice more in ordinary use the same day, on a TemporalFact updated with one property at a time. CONTRADICTED WITHIN THE GRAPH ITSELF: chg:merge-integrity-bl47-bl46 records "create_node on an existing id merges instead of replacing (the revise-design contract, now real)" — so the fix landed and the documents were never followed. ver:constructors-preserve PASSES while its description misstates this, and it can: grep shows the test asserts nothing about create_node at all. WHAT IT COSTS, hit today rather than imagined: several node types have NO typed constructor — TemporalFact is one, and TemporalFact is what dec:defects-are-temporal-facts makes the standard way to record a defect found by use. For those, `create_node` is the ONLY route, and the skill tells the agent that taking it will destroy the node. An agent that believes the skill either does not record the defect or passes a whole property set it had to reconstruct by hand, risking the very reset it was avoiding. The skill's advice (prefer typed constructors) stays right; the REASON given for it is false, and the reason is what an agent reasons from when the advice does not cover its case.
