properties.statement:
THE create_node MERGE-VERSUS-REPLACE CONTRADICTION IS ALREADY FIXED ON MAIN AND HAS NEVER BEEN RELEASED. Verified from source and git rather than reasoned about, 2026-08-09.

WHAT WAS REPORTED (dragon Boss cca98fbf, storyflow, v0.26.1): two served surfaces contradict each other on a destructive operation. `create_node`'s tool description says an existing id MERGES; the `revise-design` skill said it is create-or-REPLACE and "resets every other property to its schema default". The reporter observed merging (N=2) and correctly declined to say which surface was authoritative.

GROUND TRUTH, read from the code: the MCP tool calls `upsert_node`, not `create_node` — crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/query.rs:64. IT MERGES. The core does expose both semantics (graph.rs:232 create_node replaces, graph.rs:257 upsert_node merges) but no MCP caller can reach the replacing one. THE TOOL DESCRIPTION WAS RIGHT AND THE SKILL WAS WRONG — wrong in the safe direction for data, expensive in effort: it scared agents off the safe call.

⭐ AND THE FIX ALREADY EXISTS. Commit 9b16162 (PR #126, 2026-08-09) rewrote that paragraph, and the corrected text ALREADY CITES THIS FLEET: "It cost a dev_storyflow worker a hand-assembled whole-property write (filed 2026-08-09)." So an earlier report from the same fleet produced the fix, and the fleet then re-filed the same defect because THEY CANNOT SEE MAIN.

⚠️ THE ACTIONABLE FINDING IS THEREFORE NOT THE DEFECT. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 9b16162 v0.26.1` → FALSE, and `git tag --contains 9b16162` → EMPTY. storyflow runs v0.26.1. EIGHT merged PRs sit unreleased on main (#119 #120 #121 #126 #127 #128 #130 #131) and a ninth is open. The trial case for reflow2's governance is evaluating a build that predates every governance fix made in response to it, and is spending real effort re-filing things already repaired.

THIS IS THE SECOND CONFIRMED INSTANCE OF THE SAME PATTERN: a 2026-08-08 review found 2 of 4 storyflow reports had already shipped an hour before they were filed. The gap is DISTRIBUTION, not detection — and rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party makes it a product problem rather than a repo one, because every consumer is on the same released build the fleet is.

WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY UNFIXED from the report: nothing about create_node. The reporter's wider point stands and is NOT closed by the release — two served surfaces can still disagree, and nothing checks a skill's claims about tool BEHAVIOUR. That is a standing hole with four prior instances.

CORRECTED 2026-08-07, SAME DAY, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS — the first write of this fact called it a doc-vs-code disagreement that would bite consumers. IT WOULD NOT. Anthony asked the diagnostic question directly ("is it because the version of reflow2 is the developmental version only available on this machine? If this were installed via the standard method, would we be seeing this error?") and the answer is: NO, a standard install would not see it, and the documentation is correct for the audience it is written for. VERIFIED, not assumed: `release.yml:108` does `cp tools/loop_nudge.py kit-stage/reflow2-kit/tools/`, so the script IS in the released kit tarball; and `install.sh:124` extracts with `--strip-components=1`, which drops the tarball's `reflow2-kit/` wrapper so the kit lands directly at `~/.local/share/reflow2/kit/`. After `curl ... install.sh | sh` the documented path `~/.local/share/reflow2/kit/tools/loop_nudge.py` therefore EXISTS, the snippet in getting-started/AGENTS.md is right, and flo2's tracked settings.json is right.

WHAT THIS ACTUALLY IS: a DEVELOPER-LAYOUT artifact, not a consumer defect. Two install layouts existed on one machine and one project was configured for the other. reflow2 here runs from the checkout at ~/project/reflow2 and the consumer installer was never run, so `~/.local/share/reflow2/` did not exist at all — while the GLOBAL hook in ~/.claude/settings.json correctly points at the checkout. That is why reflow2 worked in its own repo and broke only in flo2: flo2's project-level hook was written for the consumer layout this machine does not have.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND WORTH KEEPING: the failure SHAPE is still the worst available. A PostToolUse hook that cannot start its script returns a BLOCKING error, so every single `mcp__reflow2__*` call in that project is interrupted rather than degraded — the opposite of cap:degraded-surface's promise that the server explains its own absence instead of vanishing. A missing hook script is a configuration problem, and it presented as reflow2 being unusable. That is a real and separable finding: whatever the cause, the blast radius of a mis-pathed hook should not be every tool call.

WHAT IS NO LONGER CLAIMED: that the prose defeats the installer's guard. `ensure_hooks` skipping a nonexistent script and the docs naming a literal path are both correct in their own contexts, and there is no contradiction between them. The earlier framing generalised one machine's mixed state into a defect in the product, which is the error `rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party` exists to prevent — this repo is the test rig, and a finding true only of the test rig is not a finding about the kit.

ORIGINAL REPORT FOLLOWS, kept because the symptom and the diagnosis path are worth having on the record. Reported live by Anthony while working on flo2: every `mcp__reflow2__*` call returned `PostToolUse:mcp__reflow2__get_skill hook returned blocking error — python3: can't open file '/home/ajs7/.local/share/reflow2/kit/tools/loop_nudge.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory`. flo2's `.claude/settings.json`, git-tracked and clean, registers three hooks (SessionStart, PostToolUse, Stop) at that path. WORKAROUND APPLIED: `~/.local/share/reflow2/kit` is now a symlink to /home/ajs7/project/reflow2, so the documented path resolves, flo2's tracked settings stay correct as written, and no tracked file was edited. Verified by running the hook from flo2's directory — exit 0, correct orientation output. THE CAVEAT THAT MAKES IT A WORKAROUND rather than a fix: the symlink points at a WORKING TREE rather than a checksum-verified release, so flo2 now runs whatever is in that checkout including uncommitted changes. Convenient for a developer, wrong for a consumer, and not what install.sh means by that path — running the real installer would replace it with a verified kit.

properties.statement: FIVE DUPLICATE FINDINGS WERE REALLY TWO HUB NODES, AND THE COUNT IS WHAT MADE THEM LOOK INDEPENDENT. Reported 2026-08-08 by w-3f408ab0 (dev_storyflow, LANE STORYBOOK-WALK). A detect_defects scoped to cap:storybook_output (depth 3, region_size 71) returned `in_scope: 5`, every one `category: duplicate` / `suggested_fix_type: merge`. Reading the MEMBERS rather than the count: `dec:edge_reads_derive_from_schema_not_allowlist` appears in THREE of the five pairs — against three decisions with nothing in common but being decisions — and `req:backend_as_product` appears in the other two. So five findings are two nodes the scorer pairs with everything. WHY THIS IS A REPORT AND NOT A SHRUG, in the reporter's words: their fleet is stood down from apply_heal because 'mechanical' merges were proposed off false duplicates, and FIVE SEPARATE WARNINGS READ AS FIVE SEPARATE JUDGEMENTS CORROBORATING EACH OTHER, while 'one node the scorer pairs with everything' reads as what it is — a property of the SCORER, not of the design. The grouping would have made the stand-down diagnosable from one call instead of from a human reading five messages. FIX SHAPE: when a node appears in >= N duplicate pairs, say so in the output (`hub: true`), or group the pairs by shared member. The detector already holds every pair, so the grouping is free. THE REPORTER FRAMES IT AS THEIR OWN RULE POINTED BACK AT US: a set reduced to a scalar is not a check of the set — here the scalar is the finding count. NOT FIXED BY THE 2026-08-08 DUPLICATES.basis WORK (PR #99): that stops a suspected edge licensing a deletion; it does not stop five findings over two nodes reading as five independent judgements.

properties.statement:
A VERIFIES EDGE CARRYING AN EXPLICIT `pinned` LIST SILENCES `unverified_enforced_rule` EXACTLY AS AN UNQUALIFIED ONE DOES — the evidence scope is stored and never read by the detector. REPORTED by the dev_storyflow api-boss fleet (`05af57c1`, 2026-08-09, governance trial-case report, finding ①) as `coverage: partial` failing to soften the detector. INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED HERE THE SAME DAY, on a different graph, a different rule and by a different author, within roughly an hour of the rule being created — which is why it is recorded as measured rather than relayed.

THE REPRODUCTION, one variable: rule:per-design-state-is-never-a-process-global was set enforced=true and given ver:no-per-design-process-globals, a real detector with a run negative control. `set_evidence_scope` was then called on the VERIFIES edge pinning three parameters — struct_field_scoping, runtime_behaviour, and whether_a_global_is_semantically_per_design. That third pinned parameter IS THE RULE'S OWN STATED TEST: the rule says in so many words that 'the test is not is-it-a-static but would-this-need-a-different-value-for-a-second-design'. So the edge now declares, in a structured field, that the check does not exercise the rule's central question. `detect_gaps(scope=that rule, depth=1)` afterwards: `unverified_enforced_rule` DOES NOT FIRE, and nothing in the output mentions the pinned list. Before and after are identical.

THE DIRECTION IS THE POINT, and the fleet stated it best: supplying MORE information made the graph LESS accurate, because the extra information is stored and not read. An author who calls set_evidence_scope honestly and an author who never calls it are indistinguishable to the detector — so the tool that exists to record a check's limits cannot make those limits count anywhere.

AND IT IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN WRITTEN GUIDANCE ARRIVING AS A MECHANISM RATHER THAN AS ADVICE. The check-health and governance-proposal skills both say, verbatim: 'Never attach a check to close a finding. Attach it because it detects the violation, and if it does not, say so and leave the finding open.' Both authors DID say so, in the structured field provided for it, and the finding closed anyway. The guidance is currently enforceable only by conscience — which is the same class of defect as an enforced rule with no detector, one level up.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: the two cases differ in severity and that difference matters. The fleet's check never exercised the only path its rule existed to protect (an uncontested CAS standing in for a contended one), so their rule read as detected while its central case was untested. This check DOES cover its clause as literally worded — a new process-global fails the build, proven by planting one in a third crate — and what it pins is the rule's broader semantic test, which no source scan could decide. So the defect being reported is not 'these checks are bad'; it is that THE DETECTOR CANNOT TELL THE TWO APART, and neither can a reader of loop_status.

FIX SHAPES, the fleet's, cheapest first and recorded as theirs rather than adopted: (1) have `unverified_enforced_rule` treat a pinned/partial scope as not-yet-verified, or fire a softer sibling naming the pinned string, since the author already wrote the reason and the gap can quote it; (2) at minimum surface pinned/swept in loop_status's verification digest so a partial check is visibly partial without opening the node; (3) the general form, which is their ratified rule: presence of a check is not adequacy of a check, and a detector that reduces 'is it verified' to 'does a VERIFIES edge exist' can only ever detect the edge disappearing.

properties.statement:
ON A `--shared` GRAPH, `export_graph` WRITES EVERY ATTACHED SEAT'S IN-FLIGHT WORK INTO THE CALLER'S FILE AND REPORTS NOTHING ABOUT IT. Measured repeatedly: 28 foreign nodes in one export, 17 in the next, both landing in the caller's git commit under a message naming none of them; separately a seat declared 67 added of which 30 were not theirs, and a third pre-announced its own carry before it landed. THE SECOND-ORDER EFFECT IS WORSE THAN THE FIRST: the seat whose work was carried then exports and gets a NO-OP against an identical content hash, which reads to them as a failed save. Filed five times across three dates by three seats from three directions — receiving, writing, and pre-emptively — and the recurrence is itself the finding. `sync_status` answers the opposite direction well and explicitly declines this one ('BEING AHEAD OF THE RECORD IS NOT REPORTED'), which is right for a single-writer seat and wrong once 'ahead' can contain work that is not yours. The only reliable discriminator today is diffing the export against HEAD BY NODE ID, a discipline three sessions had to invent separately. FIX SHAPE: `export_graph` already computes what it is about to write and every node is seat-stamped — return a delta naming how many nodes and edges the file gains and which contributors or epochs they carry, plus an explicit `unchanged: true` so 'wrote nothing' and 'wrote something' stop being the same reply. A `dry_run` would be better still. THE ASK IS NOT THAT THE EXPORT REFUSE — only that it stop being silent. || SOURCE: Observed by the dev_storyflow fleet on 2026-08-15, on reflow2 0.31.0 with served == installed verified through /proc/<pid>/exe. Three agent seats, one shared graph, one day.

▸ VERIFIED BY EXPERIMENT 2026-08-15, against the running 0.31.0 build — two seats attached to one `--shared` server, one export file. TWO CLAIMS HOLD AND ONE DOES NOT, and the one that does not hides a sharper defect than the one reported. 
(a) HOLDS. Seat A states a requirement and does not publish it; seat B exports; A's node IS in B's file. Confirmed directly by reading the written document, not inferred. 
(b) HOLDS. The reply carries exactly `bytes, content_hash, edges, nodes, path, prev_content_hash, stamp` — no attribution of any kind, so a caller cannot tell whose work it just published without diffing the file themselves. 
(c) DOES NOT HOLD AS REPORTED. The report says the victim's own export then returns 'a content_hash DIFFERING from prev_content_hash'. It does not. On an export that changes nothing, `prev_content_hash` comes back NULL. 

⭐ BUT THE REAL DEFECT IS UNDERNEATH IT, AND IT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE WHO-EDGE ONE: `prev_content_hash: null` MEANS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND SAYS NEITHER. Measured: a FIRST-EVER export returns null, and an export that WROTE NOTHING NEW returns null. Same reply, opposite facts — 'I have started the chain' and 'somebody already published my work, so I added nothing'. That second reading is exactly what the reporter experienced and mis-described. 

FIX SHAPE, REVISED BY THE MEASUREMENT and now in two independent parts: (1) DISAMBIGUATE THE NULL — an explicit flag distinguishing first-export from wrote-nothing. Small, self-contained, and it is `dec:three-party-checks` and the `revision` block's principle applied to a third surface. (2) SAY WHOSE WORK IT IS — the delta the reporter asked for: how many nodes and edges the file gains and which contributors or epochs they carry. Larger, needs attribution the export does not currently compute, and it is the half that addresses the ORIGINAL harm of a commit carrying work under a message naming none of it. 

NOTE ONE THING THE EXPERIMENT FOUND BY ACCIDENT: the near-match guard on `add_requirement` fired ACROSS SEATS — seat B was refused because seat A's unpublished node was close in wording. So one cross-seat channel already exists, incidentally, in the one place nobody designed it as such.

▸▸ CORRECTING MY OWN VERIFICATION, MINUTES LATER. THE ▸ NOTE ABOVE IS WRONG ABOUT (c) AND THE ORIGINAL REPORT WAS RIGHT. I wrote that (c) 'does not hold' because a no-op export returned `prev_content_hash: null`. That was an ARTIFACT OF A TWO-STEP TEST: `chain_after` gives an unchanged export the PREDECESSOR'S OWN prev, which was null only because the predecessor was itself the first-ever export. On a chain of any real length it is a hash. Re-measured across five exports: 
    1. first ever          content=9552429a  prev=None
    2. changed             content=f617f1ee  prev=9552429a
    3. UNCHANGED           content=f617f1ee  prev=9552429a   <- byte-identical to row 2
    4. changed again       content=6bf44741  prev=f617f1ee
    5. UNCHANGED again     content=6bf44741  prev=f617f1ee   <- byte-identical to row 4
⇒ AN EXPORT THAT WROTE A CHANGE AND AN EXPORT THAT WROTE NOTHING RETURN THE SAME REPLY, exactly as reported. `content_hash != prev_content_hash` in BOTH cases, so that difference discriminates nothing. The null-vs-hash story in the note above applies only to the first two exports of a file's life and is not the defect. 

THE LESSON, and it is the same one this file keeps producing in a new place: my probe was too short to be representative, and a too-short probe produced a confident refutation of a true report. Three reports checked today, three where the OBSERVATION held; the two consequences I doubted, one was genuinely overstated (the checksum item) and one — this — I refuted wrongly by measuring an unrepresentative case. A verification is evidence about the case you actually ran.

▸ HALF ADDRESSED 2026-08-15 (epoch:an-export-says-whether-it-changed-anything). `export_graph` now returns `wrote: created|changed|unchanged`, plus a note on the `unchanged` case saying what it usually means on a shared server. That closes the part a caller cannot otherwise compute — a no-op and a save were byte-identical replies. VALID_TO IS NOT SET: the ORIGINAL harm is untouched. The export still does not say WHOSE work it is about to publish, so a commit can still carry another seat's nodes under a message naming none of them. That half needs a decision about what attribution means on an export — per contributor, per epoch, or per seat — and is a design question rather than a bug fix.

properties.statement: FOUR DIFFERENT NUMBERS DESCRIBING WHAT READS AS ONE SET WERE ALL LIVE AND ALL CORRECT, AND NOTHING IN THE SURFACE SAYS WHICH QUESTION EACH ANSWERED. Reported 2026-08-08 by dragon Boss f96eccd3, who credits the find to their worker w-4d05e937 for refusing to inherit a number from the brief. The boss had quoted '53 capabilities claim built' from scan_nodes. The worker produced four, all live at the same moment: status in {realized, verified} = 53, a STATUS-FIELD question; capabilities_verified = 56, has ANY Verification attached; realization.realized = 37, has an ARTIFACT that REALIZES it; and the population of gap:0a77650b58242054 = 48, the gap's own set. FOUR DIFFERENT PREDICATES OVER THE SAME NODE TYPE, EVERY ONE LEGITIMATE, AND NEITHER graph_report NOR loop_status LABELS WHICH IS WHICH — so a fleet quotes one of them for weeks believing it is THE number. THIS IS FIELD EVIDENCE FOR AN ACCEPTED REQUIREMENT NOTHING SATISFIES: req:a-surface-states-its-own-scope ('an output says which question it answered, and what it could not see') is accepted and currently sits in gap:45e43cc49581b991 with no capability delivering it. The half usually argued is 'what it could not see'; this report is the OTHER half — WHICH QUESTION IT ANSWERED — and it is the half that produced the error here, because all four numbers were complete and none was ambiguous about coverage. FIX SHAPE, theirs: name the predicate inline next to each count (`capabilities_verified: 56 (have >=1 VERIFIES edge)`), and/or let a rollup return the SET behind it so a denominator is auditable without re-deriving it by hand. properties.statement: A SESSION THAT READ A SKILL AT MINUTE 0 AND ACTS ON IT AT MINUTE 90 HAS NO WAY TO KNOW THE SERVED SKILL CHANGED UNDERNEATH IT, BECAUSE `get_skill` OUTPUT CARRIES NO VERSION OR HASH. Reported 2026-08-08 by w-02baf79f (dev_storyflow), and filed by them as an ADJACENT risk rather than a reflow2 bug — the honest framing, which is worth preserving. WHAT HAPPENED TO THEM was not in reflow2: their binding rulebook PROTOCOL.md grew from 801 to 819 lines WHILE THEY WERE READING IT, the delta was a new binding rule, a peer had committed into the shared clone, and their working tree was clean so nothing warned them. THE REASON IT IS FILED HERE IS A COMPLIMENT AND A GAP IN ONE: reflow2's skills are SERVED, NOT INSTALLED, explicitly so they cannot go stale relative to the binary (dec:skills-served) — which the reporter notes solves exactly the class of problem they just hit in a file that is NOT served. THE RESIDUE: served-ness makes the skill current at the moment of the CALL; it says nothing across a long session. A skill can be revised between minute 0 and minute 90 of the same session and nothing in the response would differ. FIX SHAPE, theirs: stamp get_skill output with a version or content hash, so a long session can cheaply detect that the instructions it is following have been revised. THE SECOND-ORDER VALUE THEY NAME IS THE BETTER ARGUMENT: it makes 'I read the skill' A CHECKABLE CLAIM RATHER THAN A DURABLE-SOUNDING ONE — which lands directly on cap:skill-loads-are-counted, where the count currently records that a skill was opened but not WHICH TEXT was opened.

properties.statement:
112 OF 205 TEMPORAL FACTS CARRY A DATE NOTHING READS — AND THE OTHER 76 CARRY IT SOMEWHERE ELSE. ZERO CARRY BOTH.

MEASURED on reflow2's own committed export, 2026-08-16:
  205 TemporalFacts
  112 with a `valid_from` PROPERTY
   76 with a `VALID_FROM` EDGE
    0 with both
   17 with neither
(`valid_to`: 6 properties, 2 edges.)

THE SCHEMA DECLARES ONLY THE EDGE. `VALID_FROM` is an edge type, TemporalFact → DesignEpoch (temporal.yaml:103). TemporalFact's declared properties are subject_id, fact_type, statement, value, basis, confidence — there is no `valid_from` among them. `readiness.rs:653` walks the EDGE (`self.outgoing(&fact.node_id, Some(edge::VALID_FROM))`), and grepping the whole workspace for the property name as a string finds NO READER AT ALL. ⇒ The dates on 112 facts — over half the design's time axis — are inert. They render, they export, they look like time bounds, and no computation has ever consulted one.

⭐ THE CAUSE IS A VOCABULARY GAP, NOT CARELESSNESS, and the zero overlap is what proves it. Two populations with two conventions and no node caught between them is not sloppiness — sloppiness would be mixed. `VALID_FROM` demands a DesignEpoch. A writer who has a DATE has nothing to point the edge at, and creating an epoch per date would flood the time axis with points that mark nothing. So they write the date as a property, which the store accepts silently, and get a record that reads correctly to a human and is invisible to every machine. The 76 are facts written by code paths that already had an epoch in hand; the 112 are facts written by hand.

⚠️ THE EXTRACTION HINT DOCUMENTS THE FIELDS THAT DO NOT EXIST. TemporalFact's own hint reads "a requirement creep = a satisfaction fact whose VALID_FROM is a later epoch; a dropped requirement = a fact with VALID_TO set" — phrasing that invites exactly the property form the schema does not declare. The guidance and the schema disagree, and the guidance is what a writer reads.

HOW IT SURFACED: writing `fact:defect-a-property-once-written-cannot-be-removed` returned `"undeclared": ["valid_from"]`. The undeclared-property report (#213) fired on the very node recording an earlier instance of itself, and the second instance was two orders of magnitude larger than the first. See [[fact:defect-a-property-once-written-cannot-be-removed]] — and note that its "NOT ESTABLISHED: whether other node types carry an undeclared property the same way" was answered within one call of being written.

WHAT IS NOT SETTLED, and is the user's to settle: whether the fix is to DECLARE `valid_from`/`valid_to` as date-string properties and teach the readers to prefer the edge and fall back to them; or to keep the edge as the only truth and migrate the 112 (which needs 112 epochs that do not exist); or to let VALID_FROM point at either a DesignEpoch or a date. The first is cheapest and legitimises what people already do; the third makes the edge's `to` polymorphic, which nothing else in the schema is. The 112 are not deletable either way — a property once written cannot be removed.

properties.statement:
IMPORTING AN EXPORT MATERIALISES SCHEMA DEFAULTS THE DOCUMENT NEVER CARRIED, SO A FRESHLY RESTORED GRAPH REPORTS ITSELF CHANGED AND BLOCKS THE NEXT COMMIT ON A MACHINE WHERE NOBODY HAS DESIGNED ANYTHING. music_graph, fourth pass, 2026-08-15, reflow2-mcp 0.31.0 on both sides — the run-book's own §0b restore procedure, walked on a fresh clone.

MEASURED: `--import` took 327 nodes / 939 edges; `--diff` of that same file against the store it had just built reported `design_changed: 35`, `edges_changed: 0`. ALL 35 ARE ARTIFACTS — every Artifact in the graph — each differing in exactly two properties absent from the document and present in the store: `granularity: null → atomic`, `volatility: null → stable`. The content hash moves with them, and the pre-commit gate blocks: 'COMMIT BLOCKED — the design export is behind the live design graph.'

THEIR DIAGNOSIS IS PROBABLY RIGHT AND IS A MIGRATION, NOT AN EXPORT BUG: that store was built under 0.20.0, those two Artifact fields arrived later, the original store was never backfilled — so 0.31.0's export wrote faithfully what was there and 0.31.0's import filled in what was missing. AND IT CONVERGES: exporting the restored graph and re-importing that diffs `identical: true`. One cycle, then a fixed point.

⭐⭐ THIS IS THE EXACT CLASS THE ROUND-TRIP GATE SHIPPED TODAY (PR #196) DETECTS — AND IT WILL FIRE ON THEM. `check_round_trip` compares node properties after an export→import→re-export and would report '35 node(s) came back with different properties'. THAT IS A TRUE POSITIVE BY ITS OWN DEFINITION (the document does not survive being read back unchanged) AND WILL READ AS A FAILURE ON ANY DESIGN BUILT BEFORE THOSE FIELDS EXISTED. reflow2's own design does NOT fire, because its Artifacts already carry both properties — the self-host blindness pattern for the fifth time today: the maintainer's graph cannot produce the input that breaks the consumer's.

⚠️ SO THE GATE I SHIPPED TODAY AND THIS DEFECT ARE ONE DECISION, NOT TWO. Their option (b) — exclude default-valued properties from the content hash, so materialising a default is not a change — would settle both at once. Options (a) backfill on import and open, and (c) have `--import` print what it defaulted, leave the round-trip check reporting a difference that is real but uninteresting.

THEIR FRAMING OF THE COST IS THE PART TO KEEP: 'the first thing reflow2 does on a new machine is tell an agent the design has changed when it has not, and the honest fix (refresh the export, commit it) is INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE DISHONEST ONE (--no-verify) unless somebody diffs it property by property first.'

NOT ESTABLISHED: how many consumer designs predate those fields; whether any other node type has the same unbackfilled shape; and whether excluding defaults from the hash would weaken the hash anywhere it matters.

properties.statement: `ingest_corpus_step` KEYS ITS ANSWERS ON A HASH OF THE DOCUMENT TEXT, AND THE DRIVER IS AN LLM — THE ONE COMPONENT LEAST ABLE TO REPRODUCE PROSE VERBATIM ACROSS TURNS. Measured by api-boss `3fbdc241` (dev_storyflow, 2026-08-07) driving the tool over 8 documents. Round 1 returned 40 prompts. They answered all 40, called again, and got `unused_answers: 40` — EVERY ANSWER DISCARDED — with 36 brand-new prompt ids, an EMPTY known-entities roster, and zero id overlap between rounds. ROOT CAUSE, DIAGNOSED NOT GUESSED: the prompt `id` is a hash over the prompt text, which embeds the DOCUMENT text. Re-sending the same documents is required, and they had re-typed 6 of the 8 more concisely on the second call. They diffed them: 3342->2204, 2930->2134, 2103->2012, 2943->2407, 3533->2575, 3155->2400 chars. THE 2 THEY HAPPENED TO COPY VERBATIM KEPT THEIR IDS AND WORKED. So the mechanism is exactly 'text drifted -> hash changed -> answer orphaned'. WHY IT IS A REPORT RATHER THAN JUST THEIR MISTAKE — and they were explicit that it IS their mistake, and that they are reporting the trap not excusing it: (1) the contract asks for byte-stability from the component worst at providing it, since summarising is an LLM's default behaviour; (2) it fails silently-ish AND expensively — `unused_answers` is present and correct, but it is a LIST OF IDS, and the run still returns `status: needs_llm` with a fresh prompt set that looks like normal progress; they only caught it because the roster came back empty. At 8 docs that cost one wasted round (~100k chars); at the 138-document corpus they were ingesting it would have burned an enormous amount before anyone noticed; (3) it is invisible in the happy path — a driver that pastes verbatim never sees it, one that paraphrases never gets past round 2, and there is nothing in between. FIX SHAPES, in the reporter's own order of preference: (a) echo a per-document `content_hash` in the response and on a later round return `documents_changed: [fragment_id...]` naming the ones whose text moved — cheap, turns a mystifying 'all answers unused' into 'you changed these 6 documents', and the one they would build; (b) key answers on (fragment_id, pass) instead of a hash of the prompt text — arguably wrong for correctness since the answer WAS about different text, but it makes the failure impossible rather than merely visible; (c) let the server hold the documents for a run (run_id returned round 1, documents omitted after) — removes the resend, kills the 3x text cost, makes drift structurally impossible, but trades away the statelessness the design deliberately chose; (d) at minimum one line in the tool description: 'the SAME documents means BYTE-IDENTICAL — a reworded document is a different document and its answers are discarded.' They noted the description says 'SAME documents' twice and they still got it wrong, because 'same' reads as 'the same SET of documents'. CREDIT THE REPORTER GAVE, worth keeping: documents_pending counting down 3->2->done, per-document outcomes with node counts, and `failures: []` being explicitly present made it obvious the run had actually worked — and 'nothing is written until the final round' meant the botched attempt left NO half-design behind, so they could simply restart. They called that exactly the right guarantee and said it saved them.

properties.statement: CORPUS INGEST WRITES THE `DUPLICATES` EDGE THAT `dec:ask-not-repair` PROMISED ONLY A HUMAN WOULD DRAW — SO HEAL PROPOSES IRREVERSIBLE DELETIONS FROM A STRING SCORE, AND THE check-health SKILL CALLS THAT HALF THE SAFE ONE. Reported by dev_storyflow 2026-08-07 as the highest-severity item that channel has sent; ROOT CAUSE DIAGNOSED HERE, and neither reporting session had it. WHAT THEY MEASURED, from opposite ends and without connecting them: (a) api-boss `5d608b85`, during ingest_corpus_step, saw 6 fuzzy merge candidates scoring 81-85 on semantically UNRELATED nodes, and filed it low-priority because the auto-merge threshold of 90 held and nothing merged; (b) hours later sb-boss `ab2291fa` ran propose_heal(balanced) on the same graph and got 10 operations, EVERY ONE a Merge that DELETES its remove_id, including `req:graph_is_the_content_bible`, a load-bearing node. They verified four pairs by READING them: `dec:local_uses_brand_hostnames_not_ports` (local dev selects a brand by /etc/hosts subdomain, not port) paired against `dec:scorecard_is_generated_never_hand_edited` (the benchmark runner generates the scorecard). No shared subject, vocabulary, or edges. Three bosses stood the whole fleet down from running check-health. THE MECHANISM, read out of this repo rather than inferred: crates/reflow2-core/src/ingest.rs:1517 `suspect_duplicate` PERSISTS a near-match as a real `DUPLICATES` edge whenever the score lands in the ASK band — at or above the type's fuzzy_threshold and below auto_merge_threshold, defaults 70 and 90 (identity via resolution_thresholds, ingest.rs:1629). The score is `token_sort_ratio` over NAMES ONLY, case- and order-insensitive, explicitly 'no embeddings' (ingest.rs:1654) — a character-ratio over sorted tokens, which is why two long design-node names sharing ordinary English words reach 81-85 with no shared subject. That edge is then indistinguishable from a human's: heal.rs:798 fires `duplicate` on ANY `DUPLICATES` edge, propose_heal turns it into a Merge, and apply_heal deletes. WHY THIS IS A DESIGN VIOLATION AND NOT A TUNING PROBLEM: `dec:ask-not-repair` is ACCEPTED and reads 'possible_duplicate is a DETECT gap; HEAL merges only on a human-drawn DUPLICATES edge', with the rationale 'apply_heal deletes a node with no undo, so merge is safe only because the endpoints were asserted; a heuristic must not drive it.' Ingest makes that premise false. The irony is documented in the code: ingest.rs:1492 says persisting the edge 'is what makes dec:ask-not-repair affordable at corpus scale', reasoning that the edge turns a transient suspicion into a standing QUESTION detect_defects can batch. The reasoning is sound about batching and wrong about safety — nothing downstream reads the edge as a question, because nothing can tell it from an assertion. THE THIRD LINK, and it is the one that closes the circuit: the served check-health skill tables `duplicate` as 'machine — merged by apply_heal', and step 3 says in terms 'requires_human_review being true does not mean you should withhold the mechanical merge', two paragraphs before conceding 'a merge deletes a node and cannot be undone'. AN AGENT FOLLOWING THE SKILL EXACTLY DELETES TEN DESIGN NODES. sb-boss stopped at step 2 only because the pairings looked implausible enough to read. WORSE ON A SHARED GRAPH: one seat's apply hits every attached session instantly, with no undo and no notification — 7 client processes were attached that day. FIX SHAPE, not yet chosen: the ingest-written edge needs to be distinguishable from a human's (it already carries `confidence`, but that property is OMITTED for a structural token-subset match, so its absence does NOT mean human) — a provenance marker on the edge, with HEAL merging only unmarked ones; and 'delete a node' should not be classed mechanical regardless of source. The scorer is a separate, smaller question: 81-85 on unrelated nodes means token_sort_ratio over names is not measuring duplication of meaning at the band that matters.

properties.statement: THE INSTALLER HAS A GUARD FOR 'IGNORING A TRACKED FILE DOES NOTHING' AND IT STRUCTURALLY CANNOT FIRE FOR `.reflow2/` — THE ONE ENTRY MOST LIKELY TO BE ALREADY TRACKED. Reported 2026-08-08 by Alex, an early adopter who started on v0.0.5: his `.gitignore` contains `.reflow2` and git is nonetheless tracking `.reflow2/graph/LOG`, `.reflow2/graph/fulltext/meta.json` and `.reflow2/graph/fulltext/.managed.json`. His question was whether the installer or his agent had written the ignore line, and what he is supposed to be committing at all. BOTH HALVES ARE THE INSTALLER'S. `tools/reflow2_init.py ensure_gitignore()` writes the block, and `IGNORE_LINES` carries `.reflow2/` — so the ignore line is ours, not his agent's. The same function then loops the ignore lines to warn about any git is ALREADY tracking, because `already_tracked`'s own docstring says it plainly: 'gitignore does not untrack a tracked file, so saying "ignored" without saying that would be a half-truth.' THE LOOP OPENS `if line.endswith("/"): continue`. `.reflow2/` is the ONLY entry ending in a slash, so the warning is skipped for exactly the path it matters most for — and it matters most there because the store is created the moment you first use reflow2, long before anyone runs the installer that would ignore it, so `git add .` in between tracks it forever. MEASURED, NOT REASONED, AND IT CORRECTED MY OWN HYPOTHESIS. I assumed the check would also fail on a directory path and that the skip was therefore a workaround. Reproduced in a scratch repo — commit two files under `.reflow2/`, add the ignore rule afterwards — and `git ls-files --error-unmatch '.reflow2/'` returns 0, correctly reporting the directory as tracked. SO THE UNDERLYING CHECK WORKS AND THE SKIP IS THE WHOLE BUG. FIX SHAPE: drop the `endswith('/')` skip; the existing `already_tracked` call is correct for a directory as written. Optionally report the count and the remedy per path — `git ls-files -- '.reflow2/'` names the tracked files, and `git rm -r --cached .reflow2` is the fix a user needs to be told. WHY IT IS WORTH MORE THAN ITS SIZE: this is a silent wrong answer to a user who did everything right. Alex read his .gitignore, saw `.reflow2`, and reasonably concluded the graph was excluded. The installer ran, said nothing, and the store stayed in version control — which is the class of failure req:no-silent-fallback exists for, in the one tool a new user meets first. A SECOND, UNTESTED RISK WORTH STATING AS UNTESTED: a committed `fulltext/meta.json` is tantivy index metadata, so checking out an older commit would restore a stale index descriptor over live segment files. I did not test whether that corrupts the index or is merely ignored; `.reflow2/graph/LOG` is RocksDB's info log and is only noise.

properties.statement: THE KIT MANIFEST CANNOT BE GATED IN CI, AND THAT IS WHY ITS DRIFT SURVIVES. `.reflow2/` is gitignored (.gitignore:22), so `.reflow2/kit-version.json` is NEVER COMMITTED — `git ls-files .reflow2/` returns nothing. A CI checkout therefore has no stamp at all, and any check over it finds nothing to examine and passes. Wiring ver:kit-manifest-agrees into ci.yml would produce a permanently green check that inspects nothing, which is the failure mode this project already names: a green gate is the weakest evidence in the building. FOUND 2026-08-07 while writing that verification, which had sat `planned` since 2026-07-25 — thirteen days in which the stamp went from four releases stale to describing kit 0.22.0/8ed097f against a source at 0.24.0/a5b0f0d. The friction report that raised it said "reflow2's own manifest is four releases stale and nothing noticed"; the reason nothing noticed is structural, not inattention. THE CHECK ITSELF IS WRITTEN AND RUNS (tools/check_kit_manifest.py, 14 cases in tools/test_check_kit_manifest.py), and against this repo it reports exactly one real finding — stale_version — with the ten skill mirrors correctly classified as notes rather than drift. WHERE IT CAN ACTUALLY RUN IS THE OPEN QUESTION, and it is a design question rather than a wiring one: candidates are orientation time (the SessionStart hook already prints an orientation line and already knows whether a design is present), a loop_nudge shape, or folding the hash and file-set claims into `reflow2_init.py --check`, which already reports the VERSION half and is the run people trust before letting anything touch a repo. TWO THINGS THE CHECK GOT WRONG FIRST, both corrected by reading the installer rather than reasoning about it, and both worth keeping as calibration: (1) a manifest entry for a retired file looked like drift and is the installer's INTENDED steady state — install() writes new_manifest[rel] = recorded on purpose at reflow2_init.py:1031 for an edited retired file, so flagging it would make the gate permanently red on any project that ever edited a skill; (2) the six `.claude/skills/` and four `.grok/skills/` copies here are deliberate byte-identical mirrors of getting-started/skills/, enforced by skill_lint (skill_lint.py:45-46), so flagging their mere presence would make the gate red on the one repository that maintains them correctly. A first cut flagged all ten, and a doubled path segment (`skills/skills/...`) made every mirror read as drifted — a path that could not resolve looked identical to a difference.

The chain was internally sound (main 85b17257, base 486ecbac, first export 8b5471e9, second 2b536b9a, every prev matching its predecessor), so the agent's first diagnosis was that the GUARD was defective, and a backlog row was filed saying so. The guard was right. dec:export-once-per-pr has been accepted since 2026-08-01 and says exactly: a branch may hold as many commits as it likes, exactly ONE may write docs/design/reflow2.json. THIS IS THE THIRD RECORDED REDISCOVERY of that decision, which dec:idea-backlog-belongs-in-the-graph already characterised as 'accepted, invisible, violated and then re-announced as new'. The message's two stated causes (exported elsewhere and copied in; exported twice since the last commit) both invite 'restore the file and export once', which had already been done and cannot help. The real remedy is fold-to-one-exporting-commit, and the message does not say it.

properties.statement: `link_artifact` ACCEPTS A REQUIREMENT AS ITS `target_type` AND WRITES A REALIZES EDGE ONTO IT, WHICH THE SCHEMA DOES NOT MODEL. Reported by Alex's Grok 4.6 session, 2026-08-14 (docs/feedback/2026-08-14-alex-grok-session.md, item 11), which could not tell whether the tool was deliberately wider than the skill text or accepting by accident. MEASURED HERE, 2026-08-15, and it is the accident: `describe_schema {from: Artifact, to: Requirement}` returns `exact_matches: 0` and its own note says 'No edge type names both Artifact and Requirement'. REALIZES is declared `Artifact -> *` and its hint reads 'An Artifact implements/realizes a Capability or Component' — so the edge validates through a WILDCARD on the target while the hint names the two types that were meant. `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/built.rs:342` passes `target_type` from the request straight into `LinkArtifactOptions` with no check, and the tool's own description says 'the Capability/Component it implements'. THE SHARP VERSION, and the reason this is worth more than a validation patch: `describe_schema` ALREADY RANKS EXACT MATCHES ABOVE WILDCARD ONES and exists to answer exactly this question — and the served instructions warn agents about this precise trap in the capture step ('several will validate, and validating is not the same as meaning what you intended'). The warning is aimed at agents hand-writing `create_edge`. The TYPED CONVENIENCE TOOL, whose whole promise is that you do not have to reason about the edge, never applies the check it tells its callers to apply. A tool that spares you a decision inherits the duty to get it right. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: an Artifact REALIZES a Requirement puts as-built directly onto intent, bypassing the Capability that is supposed to carry delivery — so the golden thread records delivery as ASSERTED at the file, which is what `req:completion-computed` exists to forbid ('computed from the golden thread, never asserted'). NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any detector currently reads such an edge and mis-counts it, or how many exist in the wild — Alex's session made one and it succeeded silently, which is the only instance measured. FIX SHAPE: `link_artifact` refuses a `target_type` that is not Capability or Component, naming the two that are legal, in the same style as the `add_change_event` refusal his session praised for naming the legal values.

properties.statement: `link_artifact`'s `artifact_type` ENUM HAS `test_result` BUT NOTHING FOR THE TEST ITSELF, SO A TEST FILE MUST BE FILED AS GENERIC `code`. Reported by w-deac0a1e (dev_storyflow, 2026-08-07) registering a new vitest contract test. They reached for the obvious value and got: `invalid enum value 'test', expected one of ["code","config","document","spec","diagram","model","drawing","test_result","binary","data","asset"]`. The enum carries `test_result` — the OUTPUT of a run — but nothing for the source that produces it. So the one artifact class whose entire purpose is to BE a check cannot be told apart from the implementation it guards, and a query like 'what checks guard this decision?' cannot be answered from artifact_type at all. FIX SHAPE: add `test` (or `test_source`). THE ERROR MESSAGE ITSELF WAS EXPLICITLY PRAISED and should be preserved as the pattern: it printed the full list of valid values, so they fixed it in one retry instead of guessing. The reporter's framing — that is the failure mode done right; the gap is only that the right value does not exist.

properties.statement:
MEASURED ON REFLOW2'S OWN ORIENTATION CALL, 2026-08-16, and it is this epoch's own theme firing on the instrument a new session reads FIRST. `loop_status` reported '1 answered question(s) never reached the design — write the answer in, or acknowledge the gap'. The answer HAD reached the design: `dec:the-authority-check-guards-forward-not-backward` is accepted, dated 2026-08-11, carries an AUTHORED_BY role=approver edge to who:ajs and a GOVERNED_BY edge from the rule it shapes, and records the ruling, both rejected options and the measurement behind them. The claim was false and I repeated it to the user as fact before checking.

THE CODE CANNOT SUPPORT WHAT THE MESSAGE ASSERTS. report.rs:755 is `questions.iter().filter(|q| q.status == "answered").count()`. That knows one thing — the question is answered and its gap is still open — and the message turns it into a claim about whether design nodes exist. Nothing looks for them.

AND THE STATE IT FLAGS IS DELIBERATE, which is what makes this `req:a-deliberate-state-is-not-a-defect` rather than a wording bug. The decision says in its own text that it does NOT close the gap: the gap is `unverified_enforced_rule`, it needs a PASSING Verification, none exists, and closing it would record a judgement the owner did not make. So the correct action — rule, record it, leave the debt honestly open — is exactly what makes the instrument report false debt, and the only ways to silence it are to acknowledge a gap that is real or to stop recording rulings.

THE FIX IS NOT OBVIOUS AND IS NOT ASSERTED HERE: 'was this answer written into the design' has no general computation, since an answer may land as a Decision, a Requirement, a status move or an edge. The narrow honest repair is for the message to say what it actually knows.

`loop_status`'s OWN `next` LIST NAMES THE DESTRUCTIVE SKILL AS THE IMPERATIVE, AND IT IS THE FIELD A FRESH SESSION TRUSTS MOST. Reported by w-abbb53d2 (dev_storyflow, 2026-08-07). loop_status returned, verbatim: `"26 structural defect(s) outstanding — run check-health (detect_defects)"`. That line is the tool telling an arriving session what to do next, and it is the single most authoritative-feeling string in the payload for a seat that has just cold-started and is looking for its footing. On that night it named the one skill three bosses had stood the entire fleet down from running — because check-health step 3 applies the 'mechanical' operations without review, which on that graph was 10 irreversible node deletions from duplicate detections scored 81-85 on unrelated nodes (see fact:defect-ingest-writes-duplicates-that-heal-then-merges). The safe half, `detect_defects`, is in the parenthetical — the part most likely to be skimmed. A session that follows `next` literally, which is what `next` is FOR, walks into it. THE REPORTER WAS EXPLICIT THAT THIS IS DISTINCT from the apply_heal reports already filed and asked for it not to be deduped: those are about the skill and the scorer, this is about THE LOOP'S OWN GUIDANCE FIELD POINTING AT THE HAZARD, so the routing survives even for a reader who never opens the skill. THIS REPO CONFIRMS the wording is still shipped: loop_status's `next` on reflow2's own graph today reads `"1 structural defect(s) outstanding — run check-health (detect_defects)"`. FIX SHAPE, small and mechanical: have `next` name the NON-MUTATING call as the instruction and the skill as context — `"run detect_defects (scoped to your area); see check-health for the workflow"` — rather than the reverse. GENERALISATION THE REPORTER OFFERED: when a skill contains an irreversible step, the loop's own to-do list should not name that skill as the imperative. ---- 2026-08-08 UPDATE: THREE MORE INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTIONS, AND THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE YET THAT A STRING CAN BECOME DOCTRINE. sb-boss ab2291fa (item 1): *'It printed into my session TWICE and I read past it BOTH TIMES'* — from the seat that issued the stand-down. w-9d1d1499: *'I received that conflated string personally, in the call I am REQUIRED to make'*, and named the precise conflation — check-health is the SKILL and it reads AND APPLIES, detect_defects is the TOOL and it only reads, and the string names the destructive one first with the safe one parenthesised as if they were the same act. w-02baf79f filed it a THIRD time ten minutes after a peer, deliberately and with the reason stated: *'one report reads as one seat's opinion while two reads as the tool doing it to everyone.'* THE MEASURE OF THE COST IS THE COUNTERMEASURE: this fleet now runs a STANDING STOP-ORDER POSTED AT THE TOP OF THE WORKER BOARD, so every worker reads a `## 🛑` warning before they are allowed to trust the output of a required call. In w-02baf79f's words, *'the doctrine patch is load-bearing where a string change would do.'* ---- STATUS: FIXED ON MAIN, NOT YET IN ANY RELEASE. `req:a-hint-names-its-next-call` was accepted and the wording changed in PR #102 (main `51e3c63`, 2026-08-08). THIS FACT STAYS OPEN — no VALID_TO — BECAUSE THE FLEET RUNS 0.24.0 AND STILL RECEIVES THE OLD STRING. Closing it on the merge rather than the release would assert a fix reached a user it has not reached, which is the same class of error as a status believed forever. THIS IS THE CONCRETE REASON THE RELEASE CUT IS OWED.

properties.statement: CLOSED 2026-08-07, same day, by dec:sidecar-loss-guarded-by-store-evidence — the refusal now exists in code (identity::resolve_on_open + store_has_content), ver:sessions-cannot-cross-designs passes 5/5, and the whole workspace is green. Read the rest as the record of what was true inside VALID_FROM..VALID_TO; the closure is PARTIAL IN ONE NAMED WAY, which is why it is stated here rather than left to be rediscovered: the refusal STOPS the loss but does not RECOVER a design already lost, because the id can still not be read back off the store. The clause below beginning "NOT YET FIXED" described the fix that was not taken — a scan for a design under ANY id — and it was not taken because dynograph-storage exposes no such enumeration and is pinned by git tag v0.12.0, i.e. it lives in another repository. What shipped is a filesystem proxy for that scan. --- ORIGINAL RECORD FOLLOWS --- A store that loses its identity sidecar is OPENED EMPTY rather than refused, and the open destroys the evidence — the exact failure cap:hosted-state-on-a-volume forbids in its own statement ("a store without its identity sidecar is refused rather than opened empty"). Found 2026-08-07 by ver:sessions-cannot-cross-designs, written as the precondition dec:one-process-many-stores was accepted conditional on; measured, not reasoned: original id 55f9907b65553b63, id after reopen c485cd821d5a263b, real design reachable false. MECHANISM: identity lives in `<path>.id.json`, a SIBLING of the store, so the two can be parted. identity::resolve (crates/reflow2-core/src/identity.rs:126) finds no file and asks holds_default_design(), which probes ONLY for a design under DEFAULT_GRAPH_ID (graph.rs:146-148). That probe is the legacy migration path and CANNOT SEE A MINTED DESIGN BY CONSTRUCTION — every design created since identity landed is under a minted id. So the probe answers false, a NEW id is minted, and resolve() WRITES IT to the sidecar (identity.rs:171). The design is still on disk, now unreachable because graph_id namespaces every stored key, and the id needed to reach it has been overwritten. The graph then reports itself healthy and empty; nothing errors. THE SHARPENING, found by propagating chg:isolation-check-written rather than by reading code: this capability IS ALREADY BUILT — art:dockerfile realizes it, satisfying req:hosted-state-outlives-the-image — and THE DOCKERFILE ALREADY DOCUMENTS THIS EXACT FAILURE IN CAPITALS, at Dockerfile:78-82: "THE SIDECARS ARE NOT OPTIONAL AND NOT SEPARABLE. A store opened without the identity sidecar it was created with finds nothing and PRESENTS AS AN EMPTY DESIGN, reporting nothing wrong. Because they sit beside the store rather than inside it, mounting only `.../graph` and not its parent directory is a plausible-looking mistake that silently loses a project. MOUNT THE PARENT." So the failure mode was known, written down, and mitigated with A COMMENT ASKING THE OPERATOR NOT TO MAKE THE MISTAKE — while the capability the Dockerfile realizes says the store must be REFUSED rather than opened empty. The design says enforce it in code; what shipped was a warning. A mis-scoped `-v` is not an exotic input, and the operator who makes it is the one person who cannot see the warning, because it is in the image's source rather than in the error they get — which is no error at all. ADJACENCY THAT SHOWS THE RULE WAS ALREADY KNOWN IN CODE TOO: an UNREADABLE sidecar is correctly refused with "reflow2 will not guess" (identity.rs:138-145, tested at tests/design_identity.rs:139), so corrupt was refused and ABSENT was not — and absent is the more likely of the two on a volume.

properties.statement:
art:main (crates/reflow2-mcp/src/main.rs) REALIZES cap:snapshot-read and cmp:main, and nothing else — so the file that carries the whole CLI surface is traced to one capability it barely touches and NOT to the ones it actually serves. Measured 2026-08-06 by reconcile_artifacts, which returned propagation_seeds ['cap:snapshot-read','cmp:main'] for a change that was entirely about cap:content-store's --content-path argument. CONSEQUENCE: the reconcile-driven path from a code change back to the intent that justified it — the loop link-artifacts step 6 exists to close, and which the skill calls 'the loop the original Reflow never closed' — lands on the wrong capability for any CLI change. The correct blast radius was only obtained because the agent hand-named cap:content-store in add_change_event from judgement; had it trusted the graph, ifc:mcp-tools would never have appeared as a boundary crossing and a tool-surface change would have shipped unnoticed. THE UNDERLYING SHAPE is that main.rs is one atomic artifact standing for many capabilities (content store, HTTP/shared serving, export, import, merge driver, latent mode), which is the pending_expansion case link-artifacts describes: a placeholder standing in for files that should each become their own node, where an atomic registration buys a false tick. Not yet decided whether the fix is more REALIZES edges from the one artifact or a finer artifact decomposition.

═══ SECOND OCCURRENCE, 2026-08-29 — 23 DAYS LATER, SAME COST, SAME WORKAROUND ═══

Surfaced by `unclaimed_findings` during a capture-session pass, as the ONE candidate returned for that session's three ChangeEvents (subjects_examined 13), reached via art:main. Examined and left OPEN: the session changed main.rs (an import now prints unresolvable node references) but changed nothing about what it REALIZES, so every word above is still true.

⭐ WHAT MAKES IT WORTH RE-DATING RATHER THAN JUST NOT CLOSING: the session REPRODUCED the defect's cost without noticing at the time. All three of its ChangeEvents carried `affected` lists typed out from judgement — art:export, art:graph, art:main, art:schema-temporal, art:repair-notes-lifted-test, and later art:heal, art:service, art:tools-coherence — read off `reflow2_check.py`'s drift output rather than obtained from the graph. That is the identical workaround the 2026-08-06 entry describes, arrived at independently, by an agent that had not read this node.

🛑 SO THE HAND-NAMING IS NOT AN ANOMALY OF ONE SESSION; IT IS THE STANDING PRACTICE THIS DEFECT FORCES. The drift report names the FILES that changed, and mapping those to intent stays a human judgement — which is exactly the loop step this defect breaks. Two occurrences, 23 days apart, both silent, both only visible because someone looked.

The fix remains undecided (more REALIZES edges vs. finer artifact decomposition). What the second occurrence adds is evidence about COST: the workaround is cheap and reliable enough that nobody is forced to fix the cause, which is why it has survived 23 days.

properties.statement: THE PROPOSED MERGE WOULD HAVE DELETED A `critical`/`proposed` REQUIREMENT IN FAVOUR OF AN UNRELATED `accepted` ONE, BECAUSE SURVIVOR SELECTION CONSULTS NEITHER PRIORITY NOR STATUS. Reported 2026-08-08 by w-9d1d1499 (dev_storyflow, LANE PROSE-JOIN) — a fourth independent seat reaching the duplicate-detector conclusion. They read BOTH nodes of one pair rather than trusting the score. `req:graph_is_the_content_bible`, priority CRITICAL, status PROPOSED: characters, locations, events, dimensions, dialogue, props and factions flow FROM the graph INTO every rendered panel, so rendered media is grounded rather than re-invented per render. `req:backend_as_product`, priority medium, status ACCEPTED: any authorized client - third-party frontend, phone app, CLI, editor plugin - can consume the narrative-graph capabilities WITHOUT our UI, API key with per-key rate tiers and a daily ingest budget. One is about grounding rendered media; the other about strangers building against a public API. NO SHARED REQUIREMENT, SURFACE OR ACTOR — the similarity is prose alone. TWO DISTINCT DEFECTS IN ONE CASE. (1) SCORING: name/prose similarity with no weighting by shared referents (actors, surfaces, components), so two requirements that touch nothing in common score as covering the same ground. (2) DIRECTION: the destructive half lands on the more load-bearing node. dec:merge-survivor-provenance settles the survivor by PROVENANCE with id breaking ties, and neither priority nor status is consulted anywhere in that rule — so an accepted, medium-priority node can eat a critical one that is still awaiting the user's word, which is exactly the certainty dec:certainty-derived says a status carries. THIS IS THE HALF PR #99 DID NOT COVER, and the distinction matters: #99 made a heuristic edge non-mergeable, so this case no longer proceeds automatically — but the moment a human DOES assert a duplicate, the same rule still picks the same survivor. FIX SHAPE, theirs: weight similarity by shared referents rather than prose; and never propose a merge that deletes a higher-priority or differently-statused node without saying so in the proposal.

properties.statement: BETWEEN LEARNING A CAPABILITY'S CLAIM IS FALSE AND BEING READY TO RESTATE IT, THE GRAPH GOES ON ASSERTING THE FALSE THING, BECAUSE THERE IS NO WAY TO MARK A STATUS AS UNDER CHALLENGE. Reported 2026-08-08 by sb-boss ab2291fa, item 4. They demoted `cap:storybook_output` from `realized` to `in_progress` after a failing walk. Between the walk and the demotion the graph asserted something false WITH NO WAY TO SAY SO — and on a `--shared` graph that window is not private: every other attached session reads the stale claim as current. The status enum (planned / in_progress / realized / verified) has no value meaning 'disputed pending evidence', and demoting early is itself a claim — it asserts a position on work that may turn out fine. FIX SHAPE, theirs, and they offered two: a lightweight `contested` marker; OR let a FAILING `kind=validation` VERIFIES edge automatically flag the capability's status as unsafe to trust, which needs no new status value and is computed rather than remembered. THE SECOND SHAPE FITS THIS DESIGN BETTER ON ITS FACE — dec:passing-is-verified already computes 'verified' from a check that passes rather than from a status field, so computing 'contested' from a check that fails is the same move in the other direction. WORTH NOTING THE ADJACENCY: req:blocking-is-partial ('work that drifted can be frozen without freezing the work that did not') is the same instinct applied to drift rather than to a failing check.

properties.statement:
A DESIGN CAN RECORD THAT SOMETHING VIOLATES A CONSTRAINT, A DESIGNRULE OR A REQUIREMENT, AND NO DETECTOR WILL EVER MENTION IT. Raised indirectly by the US-government genesis session, 2026-08-15 (docs/feedback/2026-08-15-usgov-genesis-session.md, item 3): 'reflow2 already has a VIOLATES edge type and does not appear to use it for this.' Measured here the same day, and the honest result is NARROWER THAN A FIRST PASS SUGGESTED — recorded with the correction because the overstatement is the kind this project keeps catching.

WHAT IS TRUE: `grep VIOLATES` over `crates/reflow2-core/src/detect.rs` returns NOTHING. No gap type is computed from the edge. Nothing asks 'does anything violate this?'.

WHAT IS NOT TRUE, and was claimed before checking properly: that the edge is read by nothing at all. It is named at `crates/reflow2-core/src/propagate.rs:34` in `RISK_EDGES` (`RISKS, BLOCKS, CONTRADICTS, VIOLATES, MASKS`), so `propagate_change` counts it as a risk crossing, and reflow2's own design holds 4 instances. A case-sensitive search for the Rust-style `Violates` finds nothing while the string constant `VIOLATES` is used — which is how the wrong conclusion was reached. NOTE that this also places it OUTSIDE the eight declared-and-unreached edges measured in `dec:idea-detect-vocabulary-that-nothing-reaches`: by that node's own three-part test VIOLATES is REACHED, and it is right about that.

SO THE DEFECT IS THE ASYMMETRY, NOT DEADNESS: the edge is storable, propagatable, and undetectable. Every other traceability claim in the design gets a detector that asks whether it is missing — an unsatisfied Requirement, an unallocated Capability, an unrealized Capability, an unverified claim. A VIOLATION is the one claim the design can hold that no report will surface, so it is visible only to somebody who already went looking at the node it hangs off.

WHY IT MATTERS AND WHERE IT CAME FROM: the governance session's suggestion (c) was that a prohibition is checkable against a design — 'you look for something that VIOLATES it'. That is exactly right, and once prohibitions are modelled as Constraints (see `fact:defect-the-constraint-vocabulary-is-documented-as-numeric-so-the-right-node-is-ruled-out`, which shows they should be) the noise problem that prompted the suggestion disappears on its own, because `unsatisfied_requirement` stops firing on them. WHAT REMAINS IS THE BETTER HALF: a positive check. A design that has recorded a violation should say so, once, where people already look.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: no detector reads the edge; propagate does; 4 instances exist here. WHAT IS NOT: whether a violation detector should fire as a gap (a recorded violation may be a KNOWN and accepted tension rather than a fault — this design uses CONTRADICTS with `alignment` for exactly that nuance and VIOLATES has no such property), and whether severity would need to come from somewhere.

properties.statement:
`loop_status.sync` REPORTS `in_step` WHILE LIVE NODES ARE ABSENT FROM THE EXPORT, AND NOTHING ELSE IN THE LOOP REPORTS THEM EITHER — so the only recoverable copy can be stale with every signal green. Reported by dragon Boss (`e41c6fb8`) 2026-08-16 against the StoryFlow fleet graph; REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY in reflow2's own session the same day.

⚠️ THEIR DIAGNOSIS IS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION IS THE FINDING. They hypothesised a measure-itself check that 'can only ever agree with itself'. The mechanism is real but it is NOT a bug: `sync_debt.rs:199` takes a cheap gate — `if &found == expected` where `found` is COMPUTED from the file on disk and `expected` is the hash recorded when THIS graph last wrote it — and returns `in_step` via `bare()`, which hardcodes `nodes_not_here_total: 0` (`sync_debt.rs:272`). So on that path the count is structurally always zero, exactly as they guessed. BUT `ver:the-record-moved-is-surfaced` names as a COVERED, TESTED property: 'that ordinary unexported work is NEVER reported, which is the property the whole design rests on.' The feature answers ONE question — has the SHARED RECORD moved ahead of me — and answers it correctly. `req:a-seat-learns-the-record-moved-before-it-writes` is about ANOTHER SEAT's work arriving, never about this seat's work leaving.

⭐ SO THE DEFECT IS NOT IN sync. IT IS THAT NOTHING COVERS THE OTHER DIRECTION. `behind` detects 'someone else exported work I do not have'. There is no state, on `sync` or anywhere on `loop_status`, for 'I hold work I have not exported' — and `in_step`, in a field called `sync`, is read as if it were both. The word is doing damage the code is not.

MY OWN REPRODUCTION, which is why this is recorded rather than filed as their claim: at the start of this session `loop_status.sync` reported `state: in_step` for `docs/design/reflow2.json` with `expected == found` and `nodes_not_here_total: 0`. A direct diff of the live store against that same committed export then found TWO TemporalFacts present live and absent from the file — `fact:defect-import-materialises-defaults-so-a-restored-graph-reads-as-changed` and `fact:defect-the-latent-surface-never-re-probes-after-a-cli-restore`, an earlier session's entire triage of music_graph F23 and F24. The previous session's handoff had recorded, on the strength of that same green, 'Graph in_step with the committed export, nothing behind.' It was not. Two facts were one machine failure from gone, and the only reason they survived is that this session exported for an unrelated reason.

COST, and it is asymmetric: the loss is SILENT, the graph keeps answering normally, and it becomes visible only when the machine does. dragon Boss's framing is the one to keep — a session that checks sync, sees `in_step`, and stands down reasonably believes its work is durable.

CHEAPEST HONEST FIX, and it is theirs: report the LIVE node/edge count beside the export's on every sync entry. It needs no export build (the file is already parsed and `count_nodes` is cheap), it preserves the property the design rests on, and it converts an unfalsifiable green into a readable one. A caller today cannot tell 'I compared and they match' from 'I compared the file to its own recorded hash', and those are different claims with the same output.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a count comparison alone is sufficient (equal counts with different ids would still pass), and whether the right home is `sync` or a separate loop debt class.

properties.statement:
THE NUDGE SELF-CHECK REPORTED A PRESENT, WORKING HOOK AS BROKEN WHENEVER ITS PATH WAS HOME-RELATIVE. Reported by flo2 (F1, 2026-08-09) and CONFIRMED IN THE SOURCE rather than from the report: `script_path` in crates/reflow2-mcp/src/nudge.rs resolved `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` and nothing else, so a literal `~/...` was not absolute and fell through to `project.join("~/.local/...")` — a path that can never exist — and every `loop_status` said BROKEN. A shell expands `~` at run time, so the hook itself worked the entire time.

WHY IT IS THE WORST PLACE FOR A FALSE ALARM, which is flo2's framing and is right: this is the one advisory whose entire job is to be trusted when nobody is watching, and it cried wolf about itself. It cost flo2 a real commit (538b460) documenting a problem that did not exist, and it trains a reader to ignore the advisory — the opposite of the lesson.

SCOPE, CORRECTED AFTER ANTHONY PUSHED BACK TWICE, and the correction matters more than the bug. The first framing was 'every consumer following the shipped instructions hits this'. THAT WAS WRONG. The normal install path does NOT produce a tilde: tools/install.sh calls tools/reflow2_install.py, whose `hook_command()` is `python3 "{nudge}"` over a RESOLVED ABSOLUTE Path, and the old code handled that form correctly. So anyone who ran the installer was never affected. The exposed population is those who wire the hook BY HAND from getting-started/AGENTS.md, which documents the `~/.local/share/reflow2/kit/tools/loop_nudge.py` form three times — flo2 did exactly that. The real shape is a DOC-VERSUS-INSTALLER MISMATCH: two shipped surfaces disagreed about the hook's form, and the code only supported the installer's.

ALSO RULED OUT, because Anthony asked directly: it is NOT an artefact of flo2 running against a development build. `git diff v0.26.1..HEAD -- crates/reflow2-mcp/src/nudge.rs` is EMPTY, so the released 0.26.1 binary carries the identical unexpanded `script_path`.

THE FIX, and its direction is deliberate: resolve `~/`, `$HOME/` and `${HOME}/`, and treat anything still unresolved — `~someuser/`, an unknown `$VAR` — as UNKNOWABLE rather than missing, which `status` already reads as Installed. Reporting a working net as broken is the expensive direction; declining to judge a path we cannot resolve is the cheap one. The home directory is passed in rather than read inside, so the tests never mutate a process-wide `HOME` other tests share.

PROVEN BY NEGATIVE CONTROL, not by the tests passing: with only the home-resolution disabled, four of the new tests FAIL — including `a_tilde_path_pointing_at_nothing_is_still_broken`, which is the positive control proving the fix did not simply turn the check into one that approves everything. `the_installers_own_quoted_absolute_form_still_resolves` pins the form that was already working, since that is the one a regression would silently take away.

properties.statement: `open_questions` RETURNING `count: 0` READS AS AN ALL-CLEAR AND IS NOT ONE — AND THE PROOF IS THAT A DOWNSTREAM DOC HAD TO GROW A HAND-WRITTEN WARNING. Reported by api-boss `5d608b85` (dev_storyflow, 2026-08-07), and previously by api-boss `07426210` on 2026-08-03, so it has now bitten twice. open_questions answers a narrow and correct question: what did we already PUT TO THE USER that is still waiting. In the SAME session that read `count: 0`, loop_status owed 69 gaps never asked, 26 structural defects, 20 capabilities claiming built with no check, and 20 built-but-never-checked. BOTH NUMBERS ARE CORRECT. They are answers to different questions, and nothing in either output says so. EVIDENCE IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL: the fleet's own boss cold-start card had to grow the line '⚠ count: 0 is NOT an all-clear' because arriving seats were reading it as one — and the reporter's own framing is the sharp part: a caveat maintained in a downstream document is a defect that was routed around rather than fixed. FIX SHAPE: when count == 0, have open_questions say what it does NOT cover and point at loop_status. One clause in the payload retires the caveat everywhere it was copied to. THE REPORTER GROUPED THIS with two others from the same day as one actionable class — three cases where a reflow2 surface returned a REAL, CORRECT number that answered a different question than the reader's: merge scores that silently feed deletions, open_questions vs the loop's debt, and per-session vs fleet-wide totals. In all three the fix is the same shape: LET THE OUTPUT STATE ITS OWN SCOPE.

properties.statement: THE MOMENT A SESSION HAS THE MOST TIME AVAILABLE IS THE MOMENT THE DESIGN BRAIN IS LEAST USABLE, BECAUSE EVERY ORIENTATION TOOL WANTS A SEED AND A SESSION AT CHECK-IN HAS NONE. Reported 2026-08-08 by w-02baf79f (dev_storyflow), sitting AVAILABLE in the pool with no lane. Every piece of guidance they are given says ORIENT BEFORE YOU TOUCH ANYTHING. The orientation tools are shaped around a seed: detect_gaps and detect_defects want a `scope` node id, claim_region wants a `seed_id`. A worker at check-in has no lane and therefore no seed. THE ONLY SEEDLESS CALLS ARE GLOBAL ROLLUPS, WHICH THEIR OWN DOCTRINE FORBIDS THEM TO ATTRIBUTE TO THEMSELVES (see fact:defect-rollups-became-fleet-numbers-without-saying-so). So the honest options were (a) call nothing, or (b) call an unscoped tool and hedge the number in a paragraph. THEY CHOSE (a) AND RECORDED WHY, which is what makes this a measurement rather than a complaint. THE INVERSION IS THE FINDING, in their words: the moment with the most time available — sitting available, nothing to do — is the moment the design brain is least usable, and the moment they are busiest, mid-lane, is when they are told to orient. NOTE WHAT REFLOW2 ALREADY HAS AND WHY IT DOES NOT CLOSE THIS: search_design is seedless and works, but it requires you to already know the WORDS — which is the same guessing problem recorded in dec:idea-what-governs-this-file, where an accepted decision was found only because the right search term was guessed. FIX SHAPE, theirs: a search_design-backed 'what regions exist and how big are they' summary, or let detect_gaps take a FREE-TEXT TOPIC instead of a node id, so a seedless session can FIND its seed rather than needing one to start.

properties.statement:
DOING THE RIGHT THING RAISES THE STRUCTURAL-DEFECT COUNT BY ONE, EVERY TIME, AND THE TOOL ALREADY CONTAINS THE SENTENCE THAT EXONERATES THE NODE. Reported by dev_storyflow's api-boss (`79e8e8d5`), 2026-08-15.

THEIR CASE. The fleet has a standing ruling for a genre of document — dated per-increment scope proposals whose increment has since shipped: REGISTER the Artifact, RECORD why no claims were extracted, and draw NO claim edges. Both alternatives are false. A `DOCUMENTS` edge would count a superseded document as coverage in their ingest ledger, which buckets on exactly that edge. Leaving it absent would leave 'a pretend backlog someone re-mines'. 'Registered, no doctrine, on purpose' IS the correct end state.

`detect_defects` reads that state as `orphan_node` at warning severity — 'attached to nothing — no edge says what it is for'.

⭐ AND THE FINDING'S OWN `repair_is_a_judgement` FIELD DESCRIBES THE NODE CORRECTLY WHILE THE FINDING IS STILL COUNTED: 'whether it belongs somewhere, or IS A PARKED THOUGHT THAT CORRECTLY GOVERNS NOTHING YET, is a judgement.' The tool holds the sentence that says the node is fine, and files it as a problem anyway. This is `dec:report-dont-judge` half-applied: the PROSE refuses to judge and the COUNT does not.

MEASURED, and the pre-existing case is what makes it a report rather than a complaint about their own writes: `art:equipment_item_allocation_grounding`, registered by a PREVIOUS seat under the same ruling, carries the identical finding. Their defect total moved 88 → 97 across ten artifact writes, eight of them deliberate no-claim registrations.

⭐⭐ THE PART THAT MATTERS IS THE DIRECTION, AND IT IS THE BAD ONE. Their remaining backlog in this genre is 31 documents. Doing the right thing with all of them adds 31 warnings to a number three bosses read as a health signal, and 'a boss looking at 97 structural defects cannot tell the deliberate ones from the real ones'. ⇒ THE DISPOSITION RULE AND THE DEFECT DETECTOR MAKE EACH OTHER UNREADABLE. It is also SELF-REINFORCING: a later seat who watches the count climb has an incentive to stop registering and leave documents absent — which is precisely the state the ruling was written to end. THE CORRECT ACTION DEGRADES THE INSTRUMENT, AND THE INSTRUMENT THEN DISCOURAGES THE CORRECT ACTION.

WHAT THIS DESIGN ALREADY HAS THAT BEARS ON IT: `acknowledge_gap` moves a judged-acceptable gap into `reviewed_gaps` so the open list keeps meaning 'still needs attention', and `acknowledge_defect` exists alongside it. So the escape hatch is there — but it is per-instance, and their case is a GENRE of 31 documents governed by one standing ruling. `req:a-cluster-can-be-declared-deliberately-separate` is the same shape solved once for islands: a cluster can be DECLARED deliberately separate so the detector reports undeclared ones instead of one permanent warning. NOBODY HAS ASKED WHETHER AN ARTIFACT CAN BE DECLARED DELIBERATELY UNATTACHED.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether acknowledging 31 defects one at a time is merely tedious or actually wrong; and whether reflow2's own graph holds any deliberate no-claim registrations — it holds 14 DOCUMENTS-only artifacts, which is a different state and not this one.

properties.statement:
`propagate_change` FROM A CAPABILITY ON SHARED COMPONENTS RETURNED MOST OF THE DESIGN, AND THE ONE SIGNAL WORTH HAVING WAS BURIED IN IT. Alex's Grok 4.6 session, 2026-08-14, item 7.

MEASURED: seeded from a Capability allocated to a shared API and a shared client. Distance-1 was useful — the two Components plus the Requirement/Decision thread. DISTANCE-2 WAS EVERY OTHER CAPABILITY ON THOSE COMPONENTS: ~65 named, 113 truncated. His verdict: 'Edit only what the radius names is UNUSABLE. The useful signal (Interface PROVIDES/CONSUMES) was buried.'

WHY THE RADIUS BEHAVES THIS WAY AND IS NOT WRONG TO: sharing a Component is a real relation, and on a design where two Components host most of the system, one hop through them reaches most of it. The traversal is correct; what is missing is that IT REPORTS ONE KIND OF REACH. 'This Capability sits on the same Component as yours' and 'this change crosses a published Interface into something you do not own' are findings of completely different weight, arriving in one undifferentiated list.

THE INSTRUCTION THIS BREAKS is reflow2's own: step 4 of the served loop says 'Update ONLY the impacted capabilities/components/tests the blast radius names.' At 178 nodes that instruction cannot be followed, so an agent either ignores the radius or edits nothing — and both are worse than a smaller honest answer.

WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT, and he says so: the default is a bounded SUMMARY with the full dump behind `full=true` (`chg:bl48-bl49-tool-surface`). The problem is not volume control, which exists; it is that the summary has no BANDS.

HIS PROPOSED SHAPE, held as an open question in `dec:idea-should-propagate-change-separate-crossing-an-interface-from-a-component-dump`: separate 'same Component dump' from 'crossed an Interface', and give the summary a 'sibling Capabilities on the same Component, not actually impacted' band.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether 178 is large for that design's size — he did not report the total node count, so the ratio that would make this a threshold question is unknown. This session hit the mirror image on reflow2's own graph: `propagate_change` from a TemporalFact returned ZERO impacted, because the edge connecting a defect to what it indicts is not traversed. THE SAME TOOL IS TOO WIDE ON ONE SEED TYPE AND SILENT ON ANOTHER.
