UNWATCHED: `ci-gate`, `detect-and-ask`, `genesis`, `impact-check`, `link-artifacts`, `report-friction`, `retire-from-design`, `revise-design`, `where-am-i`.

⭐ HOW IT SURFACED, WHICH IS THE POINT. Two served skills were edited the same hour — `ci-gate` (three documented omissions) and `parallel-work` (a contradiction with the lineage rule). `reflow2_check` reported **exactly one** finding: `DRIFT art:parallel-work-skill`. **`ci-gate` changed materially and the gate said nothing**, because no Artifact points at it. Had only `ci-gate` been edited, the gate would have reported OK and the change would have gone in unwatched.

🛑 **THIS IS TODAY'S GENERAL FINDING ARRIVING UNPROMPTED FOR THE FIFTH TIME** (`dec:idea-silence-is-reported-not-inferred`): *reflow2 cannot distinguish "nothing is wrong" from "I could not see it."* Here, **"nothing drifted" and "nothing is watched" are the same answer**, and the answer looks like health. The prior four instances that day: `unrealized_capability` suppressed by `realized_via_component`; the loop-nudge state `absent` meaning two different things; `loop_status` sync reporting `in_step` against an uncommitted graph; and `hierarchy_issues` returning 0 against 14 unparented components.

⚠️ TWO ENTRIES ON THE UNWATCHED LIST ARE POINTED:
  · **`link-artifacts`** — the skill whose entire job is registering artifacts and keeping as-designed honest against as-built — is itself unregistered.
  · **`report-friction`** — the skill for reporting reflow2's own problems — is unregistered, so a change to how friction gets reported leaves no trace.

✅ THE INSTRUMENT THAT WOULD CATCH THIS ALREADY EXISTS AND WAS NEVER POINTED HERE. `coverage_report` is built for exactly this class — its own contract says *"every other detector reasons about nodes ALREADY in the graph, so without this a design covering 30% of a system reports the same 0 open gaps as one covering all of it."* It answers only as wide as the sweep it is handed, and **nobody has ever swept `getting-started/skills/`**. This is not a missing capability; it is a built capability never aimed at the tree it was built for.

📌 WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: whether the 9 are unregistered by oversight or by a deliberate choice nobody wrote down — the 11 that ARE registered have no obvious property in common (they span `adopt`, `brainstorm`, `capture-intent`, `capture-session`, `check-health`, `governance-proposal`, `kpp-proposal`, `parallel-work`, `plan-increments`, `ingest-corpus`, `link-projects`), which weakens the deliberate reading but does not kill it. **Also unchecked: whether the same registration hole exists for `tools/`, `crates/` or `docs/`** — only the skills tree was counted, and the honest generalisation of this finding is that nobody knows the coverage of any of them.

🛑 NINE TEMPORALFACTS CARRY A `subject_id` THAT RESOLVES TO NOTHING, ACROSS **FIVE DISTINCT BAD IDS** — and `subject_id` is not validated on write, so each became a permanent dangling reference.

    prj:reflow2              5   the Project is `proj:reflow2` (26 facts use it correctly)
    cap:reconcile-artifacts  1
    cap:thin-install         1   capability ids that do not exist — renamed, or never minted
    cap:link-artifacts       1
    cap:gap-to-prompt        1

⚠️ **TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS NODE'S OWN FIRST DRAFT, both found by measuring rather than assuming, and both make the finding SMALLER and more precise.**

**① IT IS NOT ONE TYPO.** The first draft said nine facts carried `prj:reflow2`. Only five do. **Four point at capability ids that do not exist at all**, which is a different and arguably worse cause: a fact about a capability outlives the capability's id. So this is not an agent's slip, it is a class — pointer properties rot when the thing they name is renamed, and nothing notices.

**② THE DANGLING CASE IS MOSTLY ALREADY DETECTED, AND THE REAL GAP IS ONE LINE NARROWER.** `heal.rs`'s orphan check reasons about exactly this and its comment says so: *"a pointer to a node that no longer exists resolves to nothing and is still reported, which is the dangling case, not the ordinary one."* Measured against the live design: **8 of the 9 ARE caught** — as `orphan_node`.

🛑 **The one that is not: a node with a dangling pointer AND at least one edge.** The orphan check short-circuits on `degree > 0` BEFORE it ever looks at the pointer properties, so a fact that is attached to anything hides its broken subject completely. One fact is in that state today (`fact:reflow2s-black-boxes-hold-no-functions...`). **The better a fact is linked, the less likely its dangling subject is to be seen** — which inverts the usual relationship between connectedness and visibility.

📌 THE CONSEQUENCE THAT MOTIVATED LOOKING: `unclaimed_findings` walks from a session's ChangeEvents to the open observations their changed subjects carry. The `capture-session` skill names this exact case as out of reach — *"an observation whose `subject_id` names a node that does not exist"*. A dangling fact can never be offered as a candidate for closure, however much work is done.

⭐ HOW FIVE OF THEM HAPPENED, on the session that then found this: the agent read an existing fact, copied its `subject_id` convention, and never checked that the id resolved — **in a session that had already corrected three other claims-copied-from-a-neighbour errors.** The pattern reproduced while being actively hunted, which is the argument for a check rather than for care. All five were repaired the same day; the four capability-id ones were not, because repairing them means deciding what each fact is now about.

📌 NOT ESTABLISHED: whether `Snapshot.target_id` and `Question.gap_id` — the other two pointer properties `heal.rs` names — carry the same rot. Nobody has swept them.

properties.name: Every design available to measure grew organically — ours predate reflow2 having rungs, and the bluesky stack was never designed by SE at all — so nothing in reach can say what a WELL-DECOMPOSED design looks like. flo2 is the only deliberately-shaped one, n=1
properties.statement:
MEASURED AND THEN REFRAMED, 2026-08-25. The question being chased was empirical: how deep should a decomposition go, and what carries depth? Two rounds of measurement were taken and BOTH turn out to answer a different question than the one asked.

ROUND 1 — SEVEN REFLOW2 DESIGNS (flo2, qbench, dynograph-foundation, dev_storyflow x2, mapwright, music_graph, reflow2's own). Anthony's correction: *"most of these are after the fact... they were developed before reflow2 really started defining rungs. they might have been done differently if reflow2 defined rungs when these designs were first started."* CONTAMINATED — evidence of what happens with NO guidance.

ROUND 2 — THE BLUESKY STACK, chosen precisely because nobody here designed it. Measured from public trees: bluesky 42 source modules / top package fan-out 22; ophyd 43 / 24; databroker 59 / 27; event-model 29 / 10; tiled 207 / 28 with 8 packages over seven. Every core repo exceeds the 3–7 span-of-control bound at its top package by 3–4x.

🛑 AND THE READING GIVEN OF THAT MEASUREMENT WAS WRONG, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THIS NODE. It was reported as "the stack obeys the doctrine perfectly at the SYSTEM level — five core repos, inside 3–7, and independent lifecycles draw the same cut, two rules agreeing." Anthony: *"the bluesky stack has grown somewhat organically and iteratively. probably if we'd used systems engineering upfront, it would have been designed differently... it was never designed from a systems engineering perspective"* — offered explicitly as hypothesis, not fact.

⭐ THE CORRECTION IS SHARPER THAN "THAT WAS A COINCIDENCE", AND IT HAS A NAME. **CONWAY'S LAW — rule 3 of the same doctrine — PREDICTS a five-way split without anyone doing systems engineering.** Structure mirrors the communication structure that produced it. So finding a five-repo boundary inside 3–7 is NOT evidence that SE happened; it is equally consistent with the split being organisational and the doctrine merely DESCRIBING what organic growth produces. **Two of the four rules cannot distinguish a designed system from a grown one, because one of them is about growth.**

⇒ THE CONSEQUENCE FOR EVERY MEASUREMENT TAKEN TODAY: an organically-grown system tells you what organic growth produces. It cannot tell you what a well-decomposed design looks like, because no such design is in the sample. **THE EVIDENCE CLASS DOES NOT EXIST YET** — not because it was not looked for, but because designs shaped by SE upfront, with reflow2, have not been built.

⭐⭐ THE ONE EXCEPTION, AND IT IS n=1. **flo2** is the only design measured that was shaped deliberately and EARLY — still in concept phase, 12 components. It is also the only one that satisfies the doctrine on every axis measured: depth 3 (the deepest per-component ratio in the sample), fan-out 6/2/2/1/1 with ZERO parents over seven, and 7 interfaces for 12 components. The smallest and youngest design is the best-decomposed one. That is either the strongest available evidence that shaping early works, or a sample of one — and it is honestly both.

📌 WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE LADDER QUESTION. Anthony: *"that is kind of one of the main goals of reflow2 in doing systems engineering upfront and properly (particularly for users that don't do systems engineering — bluesky stack was a bunch of scientists that made something work, which got it momentum, and then added to, and so on)."* The bluesky stack is not a counter-example to reflow2; **it is the target case.** It is also his real operating context — NSLS-II, a ~10-year-old stack being evolved on the fly — so it belongs in the design as a BROWNFIELD adopt subject, not as an exemplar to imitate.

⚠️ BOUNDS, and they are wide. The bluesky figures are file-tree structure from public GitHub metadata, NOT a design decomposition — and the distinction is the other half of round 2: a Python package holding 22 modules is a namespace managed by tooling, whereas a design node's children are things a person must reason about together, which is what span of control actually bounds. Nothing here was cloned, run, or read beyond public trees. The claim that flo2 is well-decomposed rests on structural measures only; nobody has asked whether its decomposition is USEFUL.

`CONSTRAINS.note` and `GOVERNED_BY.note` were INSTANCES 5 AND 6 of the pattern this requirement names, and the requirement's own statement still says "four times in two days". Both were declared in schema/*.yaml, neither was reachable from its typed constructor, and both request structs carry `deny_unknown_fields` so the refusal named a shorter allowlist with no hint that a longer one existed. Fixed 2026-08-23.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE TWO FIELDS: this requirement asks for a COMPUTATION over the schema and the served surface that answers which declared properties no typed tool can set, and clause (b) says the computation must not count raw `create_node`/`create_edge` as reachability. That computation is still not built. Instances 5 and 6 were found the way the first four were — BY HAND, and this time not even by us: a consumer hit them, fell back to raw `create_edge` twice in one session, and reported it. Every instance so far has been found by a person noticing, which is precisely the evidence that the detector is owed rather than optional.

A CHEAP TEST NOW EXISTS FOR WHOEVER BUILDS IT: `describe_schema(from, to)` already reports each edge type's declared properties, and the toolsnaps in tools/toolsnaps/ already pin every served tool's accepted parameters. The two sources needed to compute the answer are both committed and machine-readable, so the detector needs no new plumbing.

MEASURED 2026-08-24 on the committed export, and it is what decided claim-over-computation.

    ChangeEvents                                    631
      written by the RECONCILE paths                192   carrying detected_at: 161  (84%)
      written by hand via add_change_event          439   carrying detected_at:  37  (8%)

THE DIFFERENCE WAS NOT CARE. `detected_at` was declared on ChangeEvent and written internally by fielded.rs, drift.rs, verify.rs and artifact.rs — which pass it through their own options structs — while `AddChangeEventReq` had no parameter for it at all. Authors could not date a change through the constructor every skill points at. This is INSTANCE 7 of the pattern in `req:declared-vocabulary-is-reachable-from-the-surface`, and unlike instances 1-6 it was load-bearing rather than merely lossy: ordering a change against a Verification's `last_run_at` is the whole of a computed staleness detector, so the missing parameter is why that detector could not be built honestly and why the design chose a CLAIM instead.

FIXED THE SAME DAY — `add_change_event` now takes `detected_at`. The percentage above is therefore a measurement of the PAST and should be re-taken before anyone argues from it: it will drift upward as dated events accumulate, and the computed bucket becomes buildable at some coverage nobody has yet named. Naming that threshold is open.

BOUND, stated rather than hidden: the 8% figure counts events whose id does not start with `chg:accept-` or `chg:drift`, which is a proxy for hand-written and will misclassify any hand-written event that happens to use those prefixes.

MEASURED ON THIS DESIGN 2026-08-10 (docs/design/reflow2.json at 5180a41, 183 Decisions excluding decision:ack: review records): the orphan_node rule for Decisions fires on 2, and 32 MORE sit in the state the rule's own comment describes as the harm, silenced by an edge that does not relieve it.

    degree-zero, detector fires                                     2
    edges ONLY of type AUTHORED_BY — silenced, still unreachable    32   (31 proposed, 1 accepted)

WHY THIS IS NOT THE NAIVE CLAIM. I first said AUTHORED_BY should not count toward the degree, and READING heal.rs:823-885 refuted that before it was written down. The degree-zero rule is deliberate and was settled by measurement, not taste: the narrow form (an accepted Decision with no incoming GOVERNED_BY) fires on SIX of reflow2's own, five of which have degree 1-3, and the comment names that as BL-42's shape exactly — the detector that became 20 of 31 defects and had to be cut back to one rule. The stated virtue is that ANY edge silences it, 'so it cannot grow into a per-convention nag'. That reasoning is sound and should not be undone.

THE NARROW THING THAT IS STILL TRUE. The rule's SILENCING CONDITION (any edge) is broader than the HARM IT NAMES. Its own words: a Decision with no edges 'cannot be reached by propagation, so it never enters an impact analysis; and for a disposition specifically it can never EXPIRE, because expiry is computed from the affected set'. AUTHORED_BY does not relieve either. The tool's own description says it is 'deliberately not a traceability edge, so it never enlarges a blast radius' — so a Decision whose only edge is AUTHORED_BY is exactly as propagation-unreachable as one with no edges, and exactly as unable to expire, while reporting clean. The population carrying that state is 16x the population reported.

THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST IS THE ACCEPTED ONE. dec:commitment-edges-survive-snapshots is accepted with a single AUTHORED_BY edge. The rule grades accepted orphans at WARNING with the message 'is accepted but governs nothing — nothing links to it, so it shapes no part of the design, cannot appear in any impact analysis'. That sentence is true of this node and the detector does not say it.

THE SKILL AND THE DETECTOR INTERACT TO PRODUCE THIS. The brainstorm skill instructs authored_by on every brainstormed Decision (step 3.5, 'whoever's idea it was'). Following it correctly moves a parked decision from degree-0 to degree-1 and out of the report. 31 of the 32 are proposed and most are dec:idea-* — this is the brainstorm population, made structurally invisible by doing the right thing. Reproduced live: dec:idea-does-a-session-open-by-comparing-the-record was created and authored the same day and did not appear in detect_defects.

WHAT WOULD BE THE WRONG FIX, recorded so nobody reaches for it: excluding AUTHORED_BY from the degree count would fire on 32 nodes at once, which is precisely the BL-42 explosion the degree-zero rule exists to prevent. If anything is done here it is probably narrower — the accepted-only case is ONE node today — or a distinct lower-severity reading rather than more orphan_node findings. Recorded as an observation with its own counter-argument, not as a repair proposal.

CONFIDENCE 0.9 rather than 1: the 32 is computed from the committed export at 5180a41, which trails the live graph by the two nodes this session added, and 'propagating edge' is taken from AUTHORED_BY's own documented non-traceability rather than from reading propagate.rs's edge set directly.

MEASURED ON reflow2's OWN GRAPH, 2026-08-19, while parking two field reports under `dec:a-dated-field-report-is-registered-and-parked` — NEW EVIDENCE FOR INSTANCE (b) OF THIS REQUIREMENT, which said `disconnected_community` cannot see a ruling.

**`parks` DID ITS JOB EXACTLY.** Both Artifacts left the `orphan_node` list and appeared in `detect_defects`'s `swept.parked` — visible and counted, not silenced. That half works as advertised.

⚠️ **AND THE DEFECT COUNT WENT UP ANYWAY, 36 → 37.** The two parked Artifacts plus the ruling Decision that parks them immediately formed a 3-node `unthreaded_cluster` (`heal:ad4ec5186566ff68`, warning): *"3 nodes form a cluster with no traceability edge to the main body."* Parking a genre CREATES an island by construction — the ruling and the things it parks are joined only to each other, which is precisely what a ruling over an unattached genre looks like.

**SO ONE DETECTOR READS THE RULING AND THE OTHER DOES NOT.** `orphan_node` honours `ruling: parks`; `unthreaded_cluster` never sees it. Doing the right thing still degraded the instrument, just through a different rule — the same direction this requirement exists to reverse.

**WHAT MADE IT GO AWAY HERE, and why a user may not have it:** a second, ORDINARY `GOVERNED_BY` edge from the ruling Decision to this Requirement, drawn because it is true — the ruling exists because of this requirement and `parks` is its answer. Defects returned to 36, so the final cost of registering two documents was ZERO. But that edge existed to be drawn only because the ruling happened to have a parent already in the main body. A user whose standing ruling has no such parent — the ordinary case for a house rule about incident reports or customer complaints — gets a permanent `unthreaded_cluster` warning for doing exactly what the design told them to do, and the only ways out are to draw an edge nobody means or to stop parking.

📌 SCOPE OF THE CLAIM: measured once, on one graph, with one ruling over two artifacts. Whether `unthreaded_cluster` SHOULD honour a `parks` ruling, or whether a parked island is genuinely worth reporting, is a judgement nobody has been asked for — and this fact does not settle it. Not established: whether `disconnected_community` (the sibling rule named in instance (b)) behaves the same way, which was not exercised.

properties.statement:
GAP B OF THE STORYFLOW PEER SET, recorded as dated evidence ON the vocabulary census question rather than as a requirement of its own — Anthony's call, 2026-08-09.

STORYFLOW'S MEASUREMENT: PRECEDES = 0 across their entire graph, against PART_OF_FLOW 14, CONTAINS 210, RISKS 2. The worker lifecycle's order is stored ONLY in the leading digits of name strings — "1. Check in to the pool", "2. A boss CAS-claims the row", ... "7. User resets the session". So a tool cannot ask what comes before step 4, cannot detect a skipped step, and cannot notice two steps ordered inconsistently in two places. IT MATTERED THE SAME NIGHT: the root cause of their invisible-worker incident WAS an ordering defect — announcing existence is gated behind reading the two largest governance documents, so a worker is unobservable for ~15 minutes by design, and the remedy is purely a reordering. The graph modelled the steps and did not hold the one property that mattered.

REFLOW2'S OWN NUMBERS, measured against the committed export at 7,097 edges on 2026-08-09: PRECEDES = 38, PART_OF_FLOW = 0. SO GAP B DOES NOT REPRODUCE HERE, AND CANNOT — the Flow node type has ZERO INSTANCES in this design, which is already on this decision's own zero-instance list. reflow2 has ordering and no flows; storyflow has flows and no ordering.

⭐ WHY IT IS EVIDENCE FOR THIS DECISION RATHER THAN A SEPARATE NEED: the reporter's own conclusion is that NOTHING NEW IS REQUIRED — "PRECEDES already exists. The gap is that nothing prompts for it and nothing notices its absence." That is this decision's question exactly, approached from the opposite side. The census asks which vocabulary NOTHING READS; gap B is vocabulary that a project's own data is CRYING OUT FOR and that nothing offers them. A flow whose steps carry ordinals in their names and zero PRECEDES edges is a detectable, high-confidence smell, and it is the first concrete candidate detector this question has been given.

BOUND: one graph each, two projects, and the reflow2 half is measured from the committed export rather than the live graph.

SOURCE: storybug Boss (47accf78), storyflow fleet, filed 2026-08-09, reflow2 v0.26.1.

MEASURED 2026-08-18 against eight anti-over-engineering strategies Anthony brought from military acquisitions — his framing: 'designs get so overcomplicated when often a simple solution will do... engineers often over design something, it is kind of their nature.'

SEVEN OF THE EIGHT ARE BUILT TO SOME DEGREE. One is genuinely absent, and one is built-but-unused.

(1) DEFINE CLEAR REQUIREMENTS AND JUDGE EVERY CHOICE AGAINST THEM — BUILT, and it is the golden thread itself. `unmotivated_capability` fires on a Capability satisfying no Requirement, which is 'a part nobody asked for' exactly. MEASURED ON REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN: 18 of them.
(2) MVP, ADD ONLY IF ASKED — PARTIAL. `Requirement.provenance` and the 'Requirement certainty' line separate user-confirmed intent from asserted, so the graph can say which requirements somebody actually asked for. Nothing computes an MVP boundary.
(3) SET HARD LIMITS — BUILT AND BARELY USED. `Constraint` is a node type, CONSTRAINS is an edge, `req:inviolable-intent` models KPPs, `budget_report` exists. Reflow2's own design holds ONE Constraint node and SEVEN CONSTRAINS edges. The declared-but-unused pattern again, on the strategy he rates most highly.
(4) USE STANDARD PARTS — THE ONE GENUINE GAP, and the most acquisitions-shaped of the eight. `Interface.designation: required` models a dependency on something outside the design, but NOTHING DISTINGUISHES A COMPONENT THAT WAS BOUGHT FROM ONE THAT WAS BUILT. There is no make-versus-buy property, so 'how much of this design is custom?' is unanswerable, and a custom part where an off-the-shelf one existed is invisible.
(5) REVIEW DESIGNS OFTEN — BUILT: the check-health skill, acknowledge_gap/reviewed_gaps, and the whole ask-don't-repair posture.
(6) VALUE SIMPLICITY — BUILT: granularity_report, hierarchy_issues, evaluate_allocation, modularity computed rather than asserted.
(7) TRACK FEATURE CREEP — BUILT, and it is the brainstorm skill: an idea enters as a `proposed` Decision and is NOT built, which is 'write down new ideas for later, do not put them into the current build' as a mechanism rather than a habit. `requirement_creep` is also a declared change_type, used 6 times.
(8) TEST EARLY — BUILT: Verification, and `req:evidence-says-what-it-covered` for what a passing check actually covered.

⭐⭐ THE ANTI-OVER-ENGINEERING HALF IS ALREADY BUILT AND DELIBERATELY RESTRAINED, which is the part worth knowing. `cap:built-and-consumed-by-nothing` (verified) asks what is SURPLUS rather than what is missing. Run on reflow2's own design, `consumption_report` REFUSED TO NAME the 122 capabilities with no recorded consumer: only 10 of 132 have one (8%), below the 50% at which absence carries a signal, so it reported the RATIO and said naming them 'would report the modelling style rather than what was built'. It also lists three things it cannot see, including 'whether being unconsumed is a problem — a capability built ahead of its consumer, a deliberate extension point, and genuine surplus all produce this same shape. That judgement is not reflow2's.'

That restraint IS the anti-over-engineering discipline applied to the tool itself: it does not hand anyone 122 delete-candidates it cannot honestly justify.

MEASURED 2026-08-13 by RUNNING reflow2 against flo2's committed export (`~/project/flo2/docs/design/flo2.json`, 106 nodes, graph_id `1a97fc1f1de4d5d2`, minted, stamp 0.27.0 against reflow2's 0.29.0). flo2 was NOT written to; the one designation experiment below was made on an in-memory copy.

═══ 1. COMPUTED PAIRING FINDS NOTHING BETWEEN TWO PROJECTS BUILT TO WORK TOGETHER ═══

`pair_designs`, both designs exactly as they stand:

    paired 0 · conflicts 10 · unmet_needs 5 · dead_surface 2 · candidates 1
    unclassified 2 ours / 1 theirs

flo2's `ifc:reflow2-design-api` ("reflow2 design tool surface") lands in DEAD SURFACE. Cause: both sides declare their half of the same contract as `published` — reflow2 publishes `ifc:mcp-tools`, flo2 publishes `ifc:reflow2-design-api` — and published↔published never pairs, which is the complementary-role rule working as designed. flo2 models that boundary from its own inside ("THE SEAM between the two halves of flo2"), which is locally defensible and makes cross-design pairing impossible.

═══ 2. 🛑🛑 FIXING THE ROLE DOES NOT FIX IT — THE NAME MATCHER RANKS THE WRONG ANSWER HIGHER ═══

Experiment, in memory only: flip flo2's `ifc:reflow2-design-api` to `both`. STILL 0 PAIRED, and the three considerations it produces are:

    81  ifc:graph-export  ↔ ifc:reflow2-design-api   WRONG, and ranked FIRST
    64  ifc:mcp-tools     ↔ ifc:reflow2-design-api   RIGHT, stuck in the candidate band (60-85)
    61  ifc:mcp-tools     ↔ ifc:model-provider-api   WRONG

⇒ **THE ONLY TRUE SEAM THESE TWO PROJECTS HAVE IS OUT-RANKED BY AN INCORRECT MATCH**, because "Design export document" and "reflow2 design tool surface" share the word *design*. WHAT PREVENTED A FALSE PAIR WAS THE ATTRIBUTE KEY, NOT THE NAMES: `medium` disagreed (`data` vs `REST`). Had flo2 said `data`, reflow2 would have confidently paired the wrong two boundaries — the failure `dec:idea-defined-pair-types-so-two-projects-combine-by-lookup` already recorded from the dynograph-foundation trial. Most of the 10 conflicts are the same noise: reflow2's `req-dyno-*` (`medium: library`) matching flo2's REST APIs at 77-83 on *-api* overlap alone.

⭐⭐ THIS IS THE EMPIRICAL CASE FOR OPTION C (`SPECIFIES`, where the content hash IS the agreement). It was argued theoretically on that node; here the name matcher is observed producing a wrong answer ABOVE the right one, on the only real seam available.

═══ 3. ✅ THE ASSERTED PAIR ANSWERS THE ACTUAL GOAL, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT TOOL ═══

`seam_report` with the pair supplied BY HAND — `ifc:mcp-tools` ↔ `ifc:reflow2-design-api`:

    agreed 3 · incompatible 0 · differs 0 · UNSTATED BY NOBODY 5

⇒ **THE TWO PROJECTS ARE COMPATIBLE AS FAR AS ANYTHING IS STATED, AND FIVE NAMED AXES STAND BETWEEN "roughly interfaces" AND "fully specified"**: `auth`, `transport_security`, `operations`, `error_model`, `payload_schema`.

🛑 AND REFLOW2 IS THE SILENT SIDE ON THE TWO THAT MATTER. flo2 states `auth: none` and `transport_security: tls`; reflow2's own PUBLISHED `ifc:mcp-tools` states NEITHER. The report's own wording: *"we assume `unstated`, they require `none` — the side that assumed less finds out in production"*. reflow2 has not specified its own published boundary, and only a cross-project check surfaced it.

📌 NOT EXAMINED, and it is named in the output rather than left implied: THE TYPES THAT CROSS the boundary (`con:pairing-stops-at-the-boundary`). Every axis above is a property OF a boundary; a struct travelling through one is invisible to the check.

═══ 4. TWO OPERATIONAL NOTES ═══

· `mirrors` on reflow2 returns **0**. The machinery for "I designed against your published surface, pinned at this version" is BUILT and has never been used on the one pair of projects that most obviously calls for it.
· The by-name CLI degraded to `pair_designs: tool not found` because a `--serve-shared` daemon (pid 892293) held the store lock — `fact:the-degraded-surfaces-diagnosis-never-reaches-a-by-name-caller` again, third sighting. THE CURE THAT WORKED: spawn the client with `--shared` so it attaches through the daemon instead of taking the lock.

⚠️ THIS NODE OPENED WITH A FALSE CLAIM ABOUT REFLOW2'S OWN HISTORY AND IS CORRECTED HERE. It said the eight subsystems were "drawn afterwards as containers" and that reflow2 has no functional layer. BOTH ARE WRONG, and `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition` — ACCEPTED, 2026-07-23, DERIVED WITH THE USER — was in the graph the whole time saying so.

WHAT THAT DECISION ACTUALLY RECORDS: "reflow2's own decomposition IS the functional systems a design-graph tool IS — vocabulary, store, coherence-loop, human-channel, time-history, intake, agent-surface [+documentation] — with the 38 Rust modules RE-PARENTED UNDER THEM as implementation. The as-built crate grouping (reflow2-core / -mcp / kit) is RETIRED from the as-designed view." And its rationale states the principle outright: "A functional carving comes from the product's PURPOSE (a genesis input), not the code, and cuts across crate boundaries, so adopt on the code can only re-derive the module view." ⇒ THE FUNCTIONAL DECOMPOSITION WAS DONE, DELIBERATELY, FIRST, AND WITH THE USER. The eight boxes are the functional layer. The file tree is what they REPLACED.

⭐ HOW THE ERROR HAPPENED, because it is the session's own recurring lesson landing on its author: I MEASURED THE EDGES AND INFERRED THE HISTORY, without reading the Decision that recorded the history. Three times in one day a stale or unread document sent this session down a wrong path; this is the fourth, and the unread thing was the design's own governing decision. A graph that holds WHY is only worth having if the why is read before the shape is interpreted.

── WHAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION, all still measured and still true ──
56 Components: 8 at `level: subsystem`, 48 at `level: component`, `CONTAINS` over 42 of the 48.
• Of 178 `ALLOCATED_TO` edges, 177 point at a MODULE and ONE at a subsystem; `DECOMPOSES` is ZERO. So per-subsystem function counts (65 / 40 / 20 / 15 / 7 / 6 / 4 / 3 for coherence-loop, agent-surface, time-history, store, intake, vocabulary, human-channel, documentation) are computed by walking `CONTAINS` and are recorded nowhere. THAT IS STILL A REAL GAP — but it is an ALLOCATION-RECORDING gap, not the absence of a functional layer.
• Six components sit in no subsystem (`degraded`, `identity`, `nudge`, `packaging`, `registry`, `sync`); two capabilities are allocated to nothing (`cap:capture-session-skill`, `cap:update-is-one-word`).

THE DECOMPOSITION IS COHESIVE. Treating Store and Vocabulary as foundation layers — everything may legitimately use the store and the type system — coupling splits 50 to/from foundation, 17 INSIDE a peer subsystem, and only SIX CROSSING peer subsystems. ⚠️ THAT FOUNDATION JUDGEMENT IS MINE, NOT THE GRAPH'S: counting their use as violations instead gives 51 crossings against 22 and reads as a hairball. Nothing in the design declares a layer.

NO GOD NODES. Capability load per module: median 3, max 16 (`cmp:skills`), top 12 of 48 carrying 57%. The two hubs — `cmp:nodes` (six subsystems) and `cmp:graph` (five) — sit in the foundation subsystems, where being a hub is correct.

⭐⭐ THE FINDING THAT SURVIVES INTACT AND IS THE REAL ONE: 73 COUPLED MODULE PAIRS, ZERO SHARING A DECLARED INTERFACE, 51 CROSSING A SUBSYSTEM BOUNDARY. All 15 Interfaces sit at the SYSTEM edge; NONE describes an internal boundary between two of the eight functional systems. Measured on the swap test Anthony proposed: `cmp:detect` has 13 functions and 2 dependents and provides ZERO declared interfaces; `cmp:heal` 4 and 1 and ZERO; `cmp:search` 1 and 0 and ZERO. There is nothing to swap AGAINST. ⇒ THE BOXES ARE REAL AND FUNCTIONALLY DERIVED; WHAT THEY LACK IS CONTRACTS. `undeclared_seam` has been reporting exactly this as one aggregate gap at severity 0.45, under the 0.8 gate.

RECOMMENDED, unchanged by the correction and strengthened by it: do NOT re-derive the functional decomposition — it exists, it is accepted, and it is sound. DO declare the internal seams. That is the whole distance between eight functional systems and eight black boxes.

NOT ESTABLISHED: how many distinct CONTRACTS the 51 crossing pairs collapse into — the figure counts PAIRS and the real number is likely far smaller.

properties.statement:
⭐⭐ REFLOW2 SERVES ANY AGENT, BUT MOST OF ITS MECHANISMS FOR MAKING AN AGENT *USE* IT REACH ONLY ONE PRODUCT. Surfaced when Anthony corrected the scope of a brainstorm: *"it is for every reflow2 project and any agent (Claude, grok, openai, etc)."*

COUNTED ON REFLOW2'S OWN INSTALLATION, 2026-08-26:

    REACHES ANY MCP CLIENT       ~150 MCP tools, 21 served skills (`get_skill`/`list_skills`),
                                 every gap and detector, the served instructions
    REACHES CLAUDE CODE ONLY     3 hook events / 4 registrations in `.claude/settings.json`,
                                 23 slash commands in `~/.claude/commands/`,
                                 the handoff memory directory (RETIRED 2026-08-26)

📌 **A DISTINCTION THE TABLE INVITES A READER TO MISS, AND IT CHANGES WHAT IS WORTH FIXING: THE SKILLS ARE NOT IN THE RIGHT-HAND COLUMN.** All 21 are served from the binary and reachable by any MCP client — `dec:skills-served` exists precisely so they never drift from the running version. **What is Claude-Code-only is the SHORTCUT, not the skill.** A slash command is a markdown file in one product's config directory; the skill behind it answers `get_skill` for everybody.

⚠️ **BUT THE INSTINCT BEHIND THE MISREADING IS SOUND, AND THIS IS THE PART TO WORK.** A skill that is only ever REACHED through a shortcut is, in practice, available only where the shortcut exists. `fact:the-commands-cover-nine-of-twenty-skills-and-the-checkout-cannot-feel-it` already measured the shortfall from the other side. So the open question is not *"are skills portable"* — they are — but **"is a skill without a shortcut actually invoked by anyone?"**, which is `dec:idea-where-does-tool-use-actually-fail-four-layers` layer ② (recognising the moment) wearing different clothes.

🛑 THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THAT FOUR-LAYER DIAGNOSIS, AND IT WAS NOT STATED THERE: **layer ② is the layer whose only shipped mechanisms are product-specific.** `cap:skill-triggers` and the loop nudge are hooks. A grok, Cursor or Copilot session on the same design gets the tools, the skills and the detectors, and gets NONE of the triggering. **Every measurement of trigger effectiveness so far therefore describes the best-supported product and says nothing about the others.**

⭐ THE DESIGN GRAPH AND THE MCP SURFACE ARE THE ONLY THINGS EVERY PRODUCT SHARES — which is `rule:mcp-and-the-graph-are-the-only-common-ground`, settled the same day. `dec:skills-served` already made this argument for skills; a working set, a task list, a practice rule and a TRIGGER are the same shape of problem and have not had it applied.

📌 AGREED NEXT SESSION (Anthony, 2026-08-26): *"I don't like having skills that only work with claude code."* Return to this table. **The work is the right-hand column, and the first question is whether the 23 commands can be replaced by something the MCP surface can carry** — not whether the skills are portable, which they already are.

📌 STILL NOT ESTABLISHED: whether other products HAVE a hook equivalent reflow2 has simply not wired, or whether MCP is genuinely the only channel to them. Nobody has looked, and the answer decides whether this is an install-time gap or an argument for putting triggering INSIDE tool results — which `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` already argues on other grounds.

It compares PAIRED BOUNDARIES ACROSS TWO LINKED DESIGNS (`req:seam-incompatibility`): it takes `other: &GraphExport` and a list of `(our interface id, their interface id)` pairs, and answers whether the two sides agree on medium, paradigm, auth and the rest. It has nothing to do with the couplings inside one design. || THE THING THAT DOES OWN THAT DEFINITION IS `seam_sets`, in `maturity.rs` — `pub(crate)`, deliberately extracted so the maturity `seams` band and `detect_undeclared_seams` cannot disagree about what a contract is, and reachable from no tool at all. || MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, 2026-08-23: asked where a within-design seam roll-up should live, an agent read the NAME and recommended `seam_report`; the user chose that option on the recommendation. The mistake surfaced only on opening the source. The reason he gave for choosing it — one definition of a contract, no second place that could drift — was correct and was preserved by extending `seam_sets` instead, so the outcome was right and the route to it was luck. || ⭐ THE GENERAL SHAPE, and it is what makes this worth recording rather than filing as a personal slip: A NAME IS A CONTRACT WITH THE READER, AND ON A 156-TOOL SURFACE IT IS THE ONLY PART MOST CALLERS READ. `find_tools` ranks over name, description and parameter names, so a tool whose name describes a different job than it does is mis-discoverable by construction — and `cap:tool-search` exists precisely because the surface is too large to hold in context, which means nobody is going to read the body first. || NOT ESTABLISHED, and deliberately not fixed here: whether the right answer is renaming `seam_report` (a published-surface change with toolsnaps and existing callers behind it), renaming the internal `seam_sets`, or leaving both and letting the new `seam_coverage` carry the within-design meaning. Recorded so the next reader meets the ambiguity before it costs them the same detour.

ALEX (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-13, reporting a FIRST RUN ON A REAL WORK PROJECT — the second user again, and the same class as `fact:second-user-report-2026-08-11` and the installer-wording fix: **found by somebody meeting the output for the first time, where nobody who already knew what it did had reason to look.**

HIS WORDS: *"I initialized a new project to try this out with my work. It inserts a .gitignore into the repo. That .gitignore ignores .reflow2 folder. Where does it store the JSON file that can be committed for the graph? I can't find the artifact that can be shared by other project members."* And: *"the init should not write over the .claude/settings.local.json if it already exists."*

BOTH REPRODUCED against HEAD by running `tools/reflow2_init.py` on a scratch project.

═══ 🛑🛑 DEFECT 1 — THE EXPORT EXISTED, WAS DOCUMENTED, AND STILL COULD NOT BE FOUND ═══

⚠️ A FIRST VERSION OF THIS NODE CLAIMED THE CONVENTION WAS UNDOCUMENTED. **That was wrong, and Anthony caught it by asking "didn't we already export the .json file of the graph?"** Corrected here, because the true shape is narrower and more interesting than "nobody wrote it down".

WHAT ALREADY EXISTED:
  · `export_graph` — unchanged, and not the problem.
  · `getting-started/UPDATING.md:19` NAMES IT: *"`docs/design/<name>.json` | the committed export — the durable record | yes, it is in your repo"*.
  · The `ci-gate` and `parallel-work` skills both reference that path.
  · **init ALREADY EXPORTED** — `backup_graph` writes `.reflow2/backups/design-<stamp>.json`.

🛑 AND THAT LAST ONE IS THE DEFECT IN ONE LINE: **`git check-ignore` confirms `.reflow2/backups/design-<stamp>.json` is covered by the `.gitignore:22 -> .reflow2/` rule the same installer writes.** The one export init produced landed INSIDE THE IGNORE RULE. A user who went looking for the shareable artifact found an export that was invisible by construction. The machinery was all present and its output fell in the one directory git was told to skip.

THE SECOND HALF, MEASURED: **nothing INSTALLED INTO THE PROJECT said any of it.** `grep` over what a new project actually receives — `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, the closing summary — returns ZERO hits for `export` or `docs/design`. The only trace is a parenthetical inside the `.gitignore` (*"the durable record is an export"*) which parses only if you already know the word. The real documentation lives in a file about UPDATING and in skills that must be deliberately loaded — **a first run reaches neither.**

⇒ SO IT IS NOT A DOCUMENTATION GAP BUT A REACHABILITY ONE, which is `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue`'s shape arriving in the installer: the information existed where the person was not.

📌 KNOCK-ON: `ci-gate` was unreachable for a new project — `reflow2_check.py` runs against a committed export that nothing had produced.

═══ ⚠️ DEFECT 2 — MERGED CORRECTLY, REWRITTEN WHOLESALE, INDISTINGUISHABLE ═══

HIS CLAIM IS HALF RIGHT, AND THE HALF THAT IS WRONG STILL DESCRIBES A REAL DEFECT. Measured with a pre-existing `.claude/settings.local.json` holding a `permissions` block and his own `Stop` hook:

  permissions preserved ......... TRUE (byte-identical)
  his own Stop hook survived .... TRUE (reflow2's appended as a second group)

NOTHING IS LOST ON HEAD. `ensure_hooks` merges, leaves a repointed reflow2 hook alone, and SKIPS on malformed JSON. That landed in `fc6c6d4`.

🛑 **BUT THE WHOLE FILE WAS RE-SERIALISED AT A FIXED 2-SPACE INDENT, so every line changed** — a compact 10-line file came back as 58. **In a `git diff` that is indistinguishable from an overwrite**, and an installer that appears to have rewritten your settings is one nobody trusts near their settings again, which is the standard `ensure_hooks`' own docstring sets for itself.

⚠️ NOT RULED OUT: that Alex is on an OLDER kit whose behaviour genuinely did lose content. `fc6c6d4` is not recent, but a consumer kit can sit releases behind — `ver:kit-manifest-agrees` exists because reflow2's own manifest was four releases stale and nothing noticed. **His version was not established. Ask before concluding the reformat is the whole of what he saw.**

ALEX (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-14 as five written notes — the THIRD report from the second user, after `fact:second-user-report-2026-08-11` and `fact:second-user-first-run-report-2026-08-13`.

⭐⭐ THIS NODE RECORDS THE TWO NOTES THAT ARE NOT IDEAS: THEY DESCRIBE DEFECTS ALREADY FIXED ON MAIN. That is the finding, and it answers a question the previous fact node left explicitly open.

═══ 1. THE SETTINGS UPSERT — CLOSED, AND NOW MEASURED BY RUNNING IT, NOT BY READING CODE ═══

HIS WORDS: *"`reflow2 init .` should upsert `settings.local.json` (or whatever settings file is relevant for the agent harness) instead of replacing it."*

✅ MEASURED 2026-08-14 by running `tools/reflow2_init.py` on HEAD (`cbb1a19`) against a scratch project holding a settings file the USER owns — 4-space indent, their own `permissions` block, their own `Stop` hook:
```
permissions identical  : True      (byte-for-byte)
their own Stop hook    : survived  (reflow2's registered as a SECOND group)
indent preserved       : True      (4-space in, 4-space out)
diff                   : 38 changed lines, 0 REMOVALS — purely additive
21 -> 59 lines, entirely from reflow2's four hook-event registrations
```
⇒ **IT IS A GENUINE UPSERT ON HEAD.** Nothing removed, nothing reformatted. The original defect was never an overwrite — `ensure_hooks` always merged — it was that the whole file came back re-serialised at a fixed 2-space indent, making a merge INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A REWRITE in `git diff`. `detected_indent(raw)` closed that, and the run above confirms it end to end.

⚠️ THE ONE RESIDUAL, recorded because it is what a user actually sees and it is not a defect: a 21-line file becomes 59. The growth is real content — four hook events in verbose JSON — not reformatting, and zero lines are removed. But a first-time reader watching their small file nearly triple may still read it as being taken over, which is the same PERCEPTION problem the indent fix was aimed at rather than a separate bug.

═══ 2. THE MISSING SHAREABLE ARTIFACT — CLOSED IN PR #172 ═══

HIS WORDS: *"I wasn't sure where the graph artifact was (reflow2-export.json) … none of them were the graph json file that could be committed to a repo and pulled down and utilized by another project member."*

✅ FIXED in PR #172 (`fadc197`, 2026-08-13), and confirmed by the same scratch run above, which reported: *"docs/design/upsert-probe.json (CREATED — the shareable design record. .reflow2/ is machine state and ignored; THIS is the file to commit)"*. `write_shareable_export` now ALWAYS writes it, including on a brand-new project: an empty export is a real document (stamp, `graph_id`, `content_hash`, zero nodes) and committing it means the first real export CHAINS FROM IT.

═══ 🛑 SO THE STANDING QUESTION IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER MATTERS MORE THAN EITHER FIX ═══

`fact:second-user-first-run-report-2026-08-13` ended with: *"NOT RULED OUT: that Alex is on an OLDER kit … His version was not established. Ask before concluding."* **Two of five notes describing behaviour that no longer exists — both now reproduced as WORKING on HEAD — makes the older-kit reading the strong one.** The alternative, that both fixes are ineffective in the field, is now measured against and did not hold locally.

⚠️ CONSEQUENCE FOR HOW HIS REPORTS ARE READ: a report from an old kit is still a true report about the version he ran, and it is NOT evidence about HEAD. Every idea captured from this batch was therefore measured against HEAD before being recorded.

⇒ **ASK HIM WHAT VERSION HE IS RUNNING, AND WHETHER UPDATING WORKED.** The gap between what shipped and what a real user is running is itself unmeasured, and `user-iterative-release-preference` states the goal as a ONE-WORD UPDATE. If the second user is releases behind while fixes for his own reports sit in main, **the update path is the defect** — and nothing currently reports it.

📌 THE LIVE HALF OF NOTE 1 IS THE PARENTHETICAL, not the upsert: *"(or whatever settings file is relevant for the agent harness)"* — reflow2 registers its loop nudge ONLY in `.claude/settings.local.json`. That is `dec:idea-the-loop-nudge-exists-for-one-harness-only`, and it is now downstream of `dec:idea-init-asks-which-harness-and-installs-only-that` (ACCEPTED 2026-08-14): once init ASKS which harness, the hook has an answer to follow.

📌 PATTERN, NOW THREE FOR THREE: every defect in the last increment was found by a first-time user or by running two real projects at each other — none by reading code, none by a gate. `dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded` — the mechanism ALEX ASKED FOR HIMSELF — remains unbuilt, which is why his findings keep arriving as a relayed email.

THE SECOND USER DESCRIBES HIS OWN WORKING PATH, AND IT IS INDEPENDENT FIELD CONFIRMATION OF AN ACCEPTED REQUIREMENT. Alex (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-11. His input is ADVISORY per rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word and nothing here moves any status.

HIS PATH, VERBATIM: "I know I want to do the following things (...). Record those at a high level. Now let's order them. And finally, let's tackle them one at a time and brainstorm." Plus: "I've used brainstorm. I said I want to brainstorm on how to do this and it launched the skill. I have basically been using /where-am-i but I'll be more explicit about it."

⭐⭐ CONFIRMS `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` (ACCEPTED) FROM THE FIELD RATHER THAN FROM SELF-MEASUREMENT. That requirement's own statement, measured on this repo 2026-07-31, says: "exactly two skills were loaded all session, and both only because THE USER TYPED A SLASH COMMAND" — and names capture-intent, report-friction and four others as never loaded. Its rule is that skill use must be "triggered by the situation, not remembered — and THE USER MUST NEVER BE THE TRIGGER."

Map his four-step path onto the served kit and the pattern is exact:
  step 1  "record those at a high level"        -> capture-intent      NOT NAMED BY HIM
  step 2  "now let's order them"                 -> plan-increments     NOT NAMED BY HIM
  step 3  "tackle them one at a time"            -> (his own framing)
  step 4  "and brainstorm"                       -> brainstorm          NAMED, and he typed it
  entry   "basically been using /where-am-i"     -> where-am-i          NAMED, and he types it

HE NAMES EXACTLY THE TWO HE TYPES. The two that would fire on a situation he is already in are the two he does not mention — and both exist, are served, and do precisely his steps 1 and 2. He is not failing to read; the trigger mechanism does not reach him, which is what the requirement says.

⭐ AND THE SHARPEST INSTANCE IS IN HIS SECOND TOPIC. He asked for a feedback skill to be built — "put the skill in your skills" — and `report-friction` IS ALREADY SHIPPED IN THE KIT, one of eighteen under getting-started/skills/. A user asked for a capability he already has. That is the same requirement firing a third time in one message, and it is the most expensive form of it: not a skill unused, but a skill REQUESTED WHILE INSTALLED.

HIS SECOND TOPIC, VERBATIM, and the genuinely new part: "You should put in an update that asks me if I want to collect feedback and store my decision in the graph or something. And put the skill in your skills. That way you get what you want." The skill half is already satisfied. The CONSENT half is not — see dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED HERE: one user, relayed rather than observed directly, and his path is a description of intent rather than a transcript. It confirms the shape the accepted requirement already states; it is not new evidence about how often skills are missed.

FIELD EVIDENCE FROM A FULL DAY OF 3 BOSSES + 4 WORKERS ON ONE `--shared` GRAPH: WHAT HELD, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT TRADED AWAY WHILE FIXING WHAT DID NOT. Peak concurrency measured: 7 `--shared` client processes plus 1 `--serve-shared`, across 3 boss seats and 4 worker sessions over ~5 hours (dev_storyflow, 2026-08-07, api-boss `5d608b85`, written from a live shift rather than from docs). The reporter asked for these to be stated BEFORE the complaints. (1) ZERO LOCK CONTENTION, not one instance, all day. This is the headline. Under the old stdio/exclusive-RocksDB behaviour a second session was SILENTLY BLINDED, and their PROTOCOL literally instructed workers NOT to run reflow2. Seven sessions read AND wrote concurrently with nobody blocked, queued or blinded — and the `REFLOW2-HOLD`/`RELEASE` ritual they used to run on the boss channel is simply GONE. A whole coordination protocol deleted, not merely eased. (2) SERVER-SIDE BEHAVIOUR REACHES EVERY ATTACHED SESSION WITH NO RESTART. When the server rolled to 0.24.0 the fixed detectors reached all attached seats MID-SESSION — one seat watched defects 42 -> 6 happen live in its own tool output. Only the TOOL LIST is negotiated at connect, so a session needs restarting ONLY if it needs a genuinely new tool. Measured consequence: they restarted 1 session instead of 6 and five kept their context. The reporter calls this major, non-obvious, and asks that it be kept and documented loudly. (3) `claim_region` BEING ADVISORY RATHER THAN A LOCK IS THE RIGHT CALL and they explicitly defend it: it makes overlap visible without inventing a blocking primitive; nobody deadlocked, nobody waited on a peer, and no claim ever had to be force-released after a session died. A lock would have recreated the exact problem `--shared` just solved. (4) `mint_seat` + `add_contributor` AS SEPARATE CONCEPTS held up once the roles were clear — seat = this session for claim_region, contributor = durable authorship. (5) CONCURRENT READS OF THE SAME NODES WERE COMPLETELY UNEVENTFUL, including reading nodes while workers wrote elsewhere — no staleness, no error, no surprise. (6) WORKERS RUNNING THE DESIGN BRAIN CHANGED THE QUALITY OF THEIR REPORTS: findings came back as graph evidence with node ids the boss could re-resolve, instead of prose that had to be taken on trust. THEIR EXPLICIT 'WHAT NOT TO CHANGE' LIST: advisory-not-lock claims; the refusal to accept an artifact checksum silently (design_holds vs design_updated vs baseline_established called a genuinely good forced question); per-property merge; skills served rather than installed, so they never go stale in a repo; and `--shared` itself.

properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-28 over `getting-started/skills/*/SKILL.md`, prompted by Anthony noticing that "we keep finding that a successful skill does something another does not" and wanting the good mechanic applied automatically rather than rediscovered.

═══ THE NUMBERS ═══

    graph-text-is-data rule    23/23   ← THE ONLY ONE skill_lint ENFORCES
    says what it CANNOT do     18/23
    honest limits section       8/23
    loop_status before finish   8/23
    an anti-pattern list        7/23
    names what it is NOT        5/23
    a MEASURED example          5/23

⭐⭐ **PRESENCE TRACKS ENFORCEMENT EXACTLY.** The single checked mechanic is universal. Every unchecked one is between a fifth and four-fifths, and which skills have it is a matter of what its author happened to write that day. This is not a claim about diligence; it is what an unenforced convention looks like at n=23.

═══ ⭐ AND IT ANSWERS THE NODE'S OWN TEST, IN THE SKILL DOMAIN ═══

That node poses the cheapest honest test as: *"name a change that WOULD have required editing all 173 tools. If one exists, the factory earns itself."* Posed for tools, it was unanswered. **For skills it is answered now: "every skill states its honest limits" requires editing 15 of 23.** A class change needing N edits exists today, and there are at least four more in the table above.

═══ 🛑 BUT THE MECHANICS ARE NOT ONE KIND, AND THAT IS THE REFINEMENT ═══

The node's counterweight 1 stands — *"a factory guarantees the mechanics are PRESENT, never that they are RIGHT"* — and the measurement shows it applies to some mechanics and not others:

**① BOILERPLATE, where presence IS correctness.** The graph-text-is-data line; having a slash command. One right answer, no judgement, and a linter cannot be satisfied dishonestly. **A factory owns this class completely, and the 23/23 proves it works.**

**② JUDGEMENT, where presence is NOT correctness.** "Honest limits", "a measured example", "what it cannot do". Forcing these into 15 skills yields 15 sections written to satisfy a linter — exactly the `internal`-by-default trap the node already names, manufactured at scale. **A factory can require the SECTION and cannot supply the HONESTY.** What it can do is make the omission visible and attributable rather than invisible.

**③ TOOL-SIDE, which cannot be fixed by editing skills at all.** The mechanic measured to actually work today is not in any SKILL.md: the `Artifact` tool's own description says the agent MUST load `artifact-design` before writing the file. Of five skills used in a long session, three were invoked because the user typed a command, one because a tool demanded it, and one was genuinely self-invoked — see `fact:the-author-of-a-skill-did-not-use-it-an-hour-later`. **No reflow2 tool makes any reflow2 skill a precondition of itself.** That is a class change across the tool surface, not the skill surface, and no amount of editing SKILL.md files reaches it.

⚠️ **SO THE FACTORY QUESTION SPLITS.** For ① it is cheap and demonstrably effective. For ② it risks manufacturing the ambiguity the node warns about. For ③ it is aimed at the wrong artifact entirely — and ③ is the one with evidence of changing an agent's behaviour.

⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the seven mechanics were chosen by the measuring agent and detected by regex over prose, so both the list and the counts are approximate — a skill may honour a mechanic in words the pattern missed. The claim that presence tracks enforcement rests on ONE enforced mechanic; a second enforced one would test it properly. And nothing here says which mechanics are WORTH having, only which are unevenly present.

properties.statement:
**ANTHONY, 2026-08-14: "always trying to improve the probability that an agent uses a reflow2 skill or tool — we can probably look at the stats." MEASURED ACROSS EVERY RETAINED TRANSCRIPT. TWO FINDINGS: THE TREND IS ALREADY STEEPLY UP, AND THE INSTRUMENT THAT WOULD TELL HIM SO UNDERCOUNTS BY A THIRD.**

═══ ⭐⭐ THE TREND, BY WEEK (get_skill channel, sessions with ≥1 reflow2 call) ═══
```
week         sessions   with-skill   rate
2026-07-13       4          0         0%
2026-07-20      16          1         6%
2026-07-27      22         14        64%
2026-08-03      15         15       100%
2026-08-10       6          5        83%   <- 5 of 6; the one miss is THIS session
```
**The headline aggregate (35 of 63 = 56%) is an artefact of averaging over the era before the fix.** On current behaviour the rate is 83–100%. ⚠️ The last two buckets are small (15 and 6 sessions) and the trend is not proof of causation — nothing here isolates WHICH change moved it.

═══ 🛑 THE INSTRUMENT MEASURES ONE OF TWO CHANNELS ═══

`surface_usage.py` counts skill use as **`get_skill` calls**. In the reflow2 checkout a skill is far more often invoked as a **slash command** — Claude Code loads `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` as `/<name>`, and that path never touches `get_skill`. Counting only invocation markers (`<command-name>`, the Skill tool's base-directory line), never mere mentions of a path:
```
sessions with >=1 reflow2 call         63
  get_skill  (what the instrument sees) 35   56%
  slash-command / Skill invocation      55   87%
  EITHER                                60   95%
  invoked a skill, counted as ZERO      25
```
⇒ **25 sessions used a skill and register as total failures.** `where-am-i` is the clearest case: **37 local invocations against 4 `get_skill` calls**, because `/where` is one of the shipped commands.

⚠️ A FIRST ATTEMPT AT THIS MEASUREMENT WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH: matching `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` anywhere in a transcript reported 90%, because it also matched `ls` output, greps of the skill tree, and the SessionStart hook's own catalogue. **Mentions are not invocations.** The numbers above use invocation markers only.

═══ ⭐⭐ WHY THE BIAS IS THE SAME BLIND SPOT FOUND TWICE ALREADY TODAY ═══

The local channel **exists only where the skill files do** — the reflow2 checkout, which holds all twenty as the compile sources. A CONSUMER INSTALL HAS NEITHER THE SOURCES NOR MOST COMMANDS, so `get_skill` really is their only channel and the instrument is correct for them. **It is wrong precisely and only for the maintainer's own sessions**, which are the ones he reads.

This is the third instance in one day of one structural fault: `fact:the-commands-cover-nine-of-twenty-skills-and-the-checkout-cannot-feel-it` (the checkout resolves all 20 as commands, a consumer resolves 9) and `fact:updating-reflow2-does-not-update-a-project-already-set-up` (the developer's kit is a SYMLINK, a consumer's is a frozen tarball). **`req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` keeps arriving in the ENVIRONMENT rather than in a detector.**

→ AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS ON `dec:idea-does-every-served-skill-get-a-command`: a skill WITH a command is invoked locally and vanishes from `get_skill`; a skill WITHOUT one can arrive by no other route. **The eleven uncovered skills are the only ones the instrument can see honestly.**

═══ 🛑 TWO SKILLS HAVE NEVER BEEN INVOKED BY EITHER CHANNEL, IN ANY RETAINED SESSION ═══

**`ingest-corpus` and `link-projects`** — zero `get_skill`, zero invocations. link-projects was WRITTEN 2026-08-13 (PR #169) to make the linking process reusable, and the process has not been run through it since. A skill nobody reaches for is not evidence it is unneeded, but it is the sharpest case `dec:bl-155` describes: reflow2 cannot tell UNUSED from UNREACHABLE.

═══ THE SESSION THAT PRODUCED THIS MEASUREMENT IS THE ONE MISS ═══

🛑 Session `809c87ed`, 2026-08-14: 43 reflow2 calls, **zero `get_skill`**. It invoked `/capture-session` locally — so the instrument's verdict is wrong in MECHANISM — **and it is right in SUBSTANCE anyway: building the decomposition detector, `impact-check` was never opened before changing an existing design, and the Stop hook had to point out that `propagate_change` had been skipped.** Recorded rather than argued away: the honest reading is that one skill was used where two or three applied.

═══ SEPARATE SIGNAL WORTH KEEPING: THE SURFACE IS MISSING BULK FORMS ═══

45.3% of tool-to-tool transitions are the SAME tool called again (3474/7671). Worst: `release_includes` 989 self-loops over 1010 calls in 8 sessions (~126 per session) — and `release_includes_all` already exists, so this is a DISCOVERABILITY failure, not a missing feature. Then `set_artifact_checksum` (288/522, 40 sessions), `create_node` (150/393). **Nobody calls one tool 126 times because they want to.**

⇒ 118 of 149 served tools were called at least once; 35 never were. Absence stays WEAK evidence — only retained transcripts are visible, and a tool used before the window looks identical to one never used.

properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-28, costing option (c) of the RCA brainstorm — "surface a known cause at the moment of the symptom".

═══ FOUR OF THE FIVE PARTS ALREADY EXIST ═══

**① RETRIEVAL WORKS, MEASURED ON THE CASE THAT ACTUALLY FAILED.** Searching the raw error string `git: 'remote-https' is not a git command` returns `fact:the-gh-merge-failure-is-snap-confinement-and-nobody-was-counting` as hit #1 at score 30.19. That is the exact root cause a session re-derived from scratch on 2026-08-22 while it sat in the graph. A second real symptom, `invalid GapCandidate: missing field suggested_depth`, returns the F-01 fix ChangeEvent at 39.76 with the root-cause rule second. **The information was always retrievable. Nobody called the search.**

**② A THRESHOLD SEPARATES SIGNAL FROM NOISE, on n=4.** Real symptoms with recorded causes: 30.19, 39.76. Plausible errors with nothing recorded: `connection refused ECONNREFUSED port 5432 postgres` → 13.35; `segmentation fault core dumped libssl undefined symbol` → 8.38. A cutoff near 20 fires on both true positives and neither control — a 2.3× margin.

**③ THE HOOK INFRASTRUCTURE IS INSTALLED.** `reflow2_init.py` already registers four hooks: SessionStart, PostToolUse on `mcp__reflow2__.*`, PostToolUse on `Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit`, and Stop. SessionStart already prints into the session's context, which is the surfacing mechanism this needs.

**④ LATENCY IS A NON-ISSUE, AND THAT WAS THE BIG UNKNOWN.** A COLD process — open the graph, initialize, run one search — is **0.08s**. Compare `graph_probe.py`'s own numbers, which exist because this constraint bit before: `loop_status` 22.6s, `loop_status since_export` 37.5s, `claim_report` 0.04s. Search sits with claim_report. **It can run inline; the async-probe pattern is not needed.**

═══ WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE BUILT — small ═══

Register PostToolUse on `Bash` (the tuple list already has the shape; today it matches reflow2 tools and edit tools only); read `tool_response`, which the payload carries and `loop_nudge.py` does not currently consume — it reads `tool_name` and `tool_input`; detect failure and extract a symptom string; search, threshold, format; suppress repeats within a session so a retried command does not fire the same hit every time.

═══ 🛑 AND THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST: IT REACHES THE WRONG HALF ═══

**This mechanism triggers on a FAILING TOOL CALL. The problem Anthony described produces none.** His words were that an agent "proposes a solution to an issue, then goes off and implements some solution, but it turns out that the solution only treated a symptom." That fix COMPILES. Its tests PASS. It ships green. There is no failing command anywhere for a PostToolUse hook to see.

So option (c) as costed solves the **2026-08-22 problem** — a recurring KNOWN error whose cause is already recorded and nobody searches, measured at 11+ occurrences of one issue — and does **not** solve the problem that prompted the brainstorm. Both are real. They are not the same problem, and one cheap mechanism should not be described as answering both.

⚠️ **COVERAGE IS 65%.** Of 192 defect-facts, 124 carry an error-like or quotable symptom that a string search could retrieve; 68 are abstract findings ("a finding can outrun its own data") that no error text will ever match. The abstract third is where the conceptual mistakes live — which is again the half Anthony is aiming at.

⚠️ **IT REACHES ONE HARNESS.** Hooks are Claude Code's. `dec:idea-the-loop-nudge-exists-for-one-harness-only` is DECIDED and says a harness that cannot take the nudge is told so. Alex's Grok Build TUI cannot. **The second user — the one generating the field reports — would not get this.**

⚠️ **THE THRESHOLD IS CALIBRATED ON FOUR POINTS.** BM25 scores are unnormalised and scale with query length and corpus size, so 20 is a fitted guess, not a constant. Shipping it wrong in the permissive direction produces a hook that fires on everything, which is the wallpaper failure this project has already killed three times (unreviewed_ideas at 111 of 186, the undeclared-seam list, the unallocated-parts list). A real calibration set is a prerequisite, not a nicety.

properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-20 on the folded #262 tree, comparing reflow2's design-graph coupling against reflow2's ACTUAL Rust import graph (comments and string literals stripped first, because 2026-08-19 measured that 15% of a naive model is prose).

=== WHAT AGREES, AND IT IS MOST OF IT ===

The two models have THE SAME SHAPE and name THE SAME KERNEL. Blast radius = how many things transitively depend on you.

  design Components (56): median 0, mean 2.9, bimodal - 35 at zero, then nodes 30, provenance 29, schema 29, graph 28
  reflow2-core modules (53): median 1, mean 6.2, bimodal - 26 at zero, then nodes 46, provenance 44, identity 44, schema 43, graph 42

Four of the five kernel names are identical. The hand-authored DEPENDS_ON set is a FAITHFUL coupling model, sparser than the truth but not a different story. This is the same verdict the adopt run reached from the other direction: the sparse hand-authored edges were right.

=== WHAT DOES NOT AGREE, AND IT IS THE DANGEROUS HALF ===

18 Components carry NO PROVIDES, CONSUMES or DEPENDS_ON edge of any kind. Ten of those 18 map to a real source module by name. ALL TEN OF THOSE MODULES ARE COUPLED IN THE CODE - ten of ten, no exceptions:

  cmp:dto            design degree 0, code degree 11
  cmp:identity       design degree 0, code degree 5, and 44 of 52 modules transitively depend on it - a KERNEL module the design models as an island
  cmp:claims         0 / 4      cmp:alternatives  0 / 4
  sys:vocabulary     0 / 3      cmp:merge         0 / 3
  cmp:nudge          0 / 2      cmp:readiness     0 / 2
  cmp:degraded       0 / 1      cmp:sync          0 / 1

The remaining eight are the subsystems and cmp:docs / cmp:main / cmp:packaging, which have no single module to compare against.

=== WHY IT MATTERS FOR AN ARBITRARY USER'S PROJECT, NOT JUST THIS ONE ===

Ask reflow2 what breaks if you change cmp:identity and it answers NOTHING. The source says 44 of 52 modules. A false ZERO is the worst answer a coupling model can give: it is the most reassuring reply available and therefore the one least likely to be questioned - the exact doctrine reflow2 already applies to loop_status(contributor_id), where an unknown id is REFUSED rather than answered 'nothing is owed to you'.

And NOTHING IN REFLOW2 NOTICES. Every detector checks the CONSISTENCY OF EDGES THAT EXIST. A missing coupling edge is a defect of ABSENCE, and absence is the one thing the detector set does not ask about. The design is not wrong where it speaks; it is silent where it should speak, and silence reads as safety.

=== HOW IT WAS COMPUTED, SO IT CAN BE RE-RUN ===

Module graph: every crate::, super::, self:: and crate-name path in crates/*/src/**.rs after stripping comments and both string-literal forms, resolved to the longest known module prefix; grouped `use crate::{...}` forms confirmed absent (0 occurrences). Design graph: Component-to-Component DEPENDS_ON, plus CONSUMES-to-PROVIDES resolved through the Interface. Reverse-reachability closure on both. Cycle check re-run on the same model: reflow2-core 53 modules / 137 edges and reflow2-mcp 25 / 34, ZERO cycles at both top-module and file granularity - #262's claim independently confirmed.

STATED LIMIT, because the same trap is one day old: an import graph is COUPLING, not a contract. These numbers are the right input for 'where could a wall go' and the WRONG input for CONSUMES - importing them as contracts is exactly the mistake fact:adopt-ran-on-reflow2-and-the-mechanical-contract-recovery-collapsed records.

77 OPEN GAPS WERE WORKED TO 4 IN ONE PASS, AND 77 WAS NEVER 77 DECISIONS. Grouped, the list was SEVEN: recorded intent not yet built (26), backlog rows imported when docs/backlog.md was retired (19), capabilities BUILT that nothing asked for (5), capabilities unallocated / unrealized / unchecked (14), the two published contracts (5), rules set to stop the build with no detector (4), and two historical rollups (468 changes with no stated axis, 117 ideas connected to nothing). Anthony answered seven questions; everything else followed. ⇒ A LONG GAP LIST IS A SHORT DECISION LIST WEARING A COSTUME. Ask what the DECISIONS are before asking the questions, or a person is asked seventy-seven times for seven answers. || ⚠️⚠️ THE MISTAKE, AND IT IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING HERE. Closing the `incomplete_published_contract` gap on `ifc:mcp-tools-http` I set `medium: REST` — and THAT NODE'S OWN `spec` FIELD ARGUES AT LENGTH THAT `unspecified` IS THE HONEST ANSWER AND THAT REST IS POSITIVELY WRONG (a single endpoint carrying JSON-RPC 2.0 is not a resource tree; the enum simply has no value for MCP over streamable HTTP). I overwrote a documented decision to make a detector go quiet. Reverted within the minute and acknowledged instead, with the mistake recorded on the acknowledgement so the next reader knows `unspecified` was DEFENDED rather than overlooked. ⇒ THIS IS `docs/sharpening.md`'s NAMED FAILURE MODE — shaping the model until the tool stops complaining — COMMITTED BY AN AGENT WHILE WORKING A GAP LIST, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHERE THE PRESSURE TO COMMIT IT IS HIGHEST. ⇒ THE GUARD THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT: READ THE NODE BEFORE FILLING IN ITS EMPTY FIELD. An unset field with a long `spec` beside it is not an oversight waiting to be corrected; it may be a conclusion. Nothing in the tool surface said so — the gap reported six unset axes on `ifc:graph-export` and one on this node in identical words, while one of those absences was a hole and the other was an ANSWER. || WHAT WAS WRITTEN, and the shape of it matters: 50 gaps ACKNOWLEDGED with the user's reason on each (never deleted, and each expires if its node changes); 5 Requirements written FROM THE RECORDED FINDINGS rather than from the capabilities' own descriptions — the distinction that keeps a requirement able to FAIL, since one back-derived from what implements it is satisfied by construction; 4 rules moved to advisory under one accepted Decision, because the `enforced` flag was asserting a gate nothing enforced; 14 allocations and links read off where the code actually lives; and both published contracts specified from `export.rs`. || THE 4 THAT REMAIN ARE THE HONEST STATE OF THE MODEL, LEFT OPEN ON PURPOSE: 64 component pairs coupled with no contract, 9 capabilities verified only at whole-component granularity, one capability no file realizes because it is a statement about the DECOMPOSITION rather than about code, and the HTTP surface nothing consumes. || SOURCE: 2026-08-23, reflow2 0.38.0, detect-and-ask over the served surface.

⭐ TWO LAYERS OF ONE GRAPH ANSWERED THE SAME QUESTION DIFFERENTLY, AND NOTHING IN REFLOW2 ASKS THEM BOTH. The question is "which part holds this function?" — the allocation layer answers with ALLOCATED_TO (Capability→Component), and the artifact layer answers with REALIZES (Artifact→Capability, Artifact→Component). Measured across all 212 allocated capabilities of reflow2's own design: 59 AGREE, 23 DISAGREE, 130 carry no file evidence either way.

NINETEEN OF THE TWENTY-THREE DISAGREEMENTS NAMED A COMPONENT THE DESIGN WAS REPORTING AS EMPTY. `unallocated_component` said "33 of 85 parts hold no function"; 31 of those 33 were real source modules with a linked, checksummed file, and for most the module HEADER cited by id the capability the design had filed against a neighbour — coverage.rs names `cap:coverage` (allocated to `cmp:drift`), regions.rs names `cap:a-session-with-no-seed-can-find-one` (allocated to `cmp:scope`), corpus.rs names `cap:corpus-ingest` (allocated to `cmp:ingest`). After correction the finding fell from 33 to 14, and to 2 once the tool-surface slices were ruled.

⚠️ THE FAILURE IS THE CHECK'S, NOT ONLY THE DESIGN'S. A detector that reads one layer and reports ABSENCE, while a second layer in the same graph holds the ANSWER, states something stronger than it measured. That is precisely what `dec:reflow2-is-built-for-observability` forbids: an answer that misrepresents what the design knows. The headline was not merely imprecise — it was actionable and wrong, and a session working it top-down would have invented functions for parts that already had them.

🛑 THE COMPARISON WAS DONE BY HAND, IN PYTHON, OVER THE EXPORT. Nothing in reflow2's 150+ tools offers it. `reconcile_artifacts` compares the design against the FILES ON DISK; `compare_designs` compares two AS-DESIGNED records. Neither compares two layers of ONE record against each other. Stated without reflow2 nouns, the user's version of this is: "my design says this module does nothing, but the file underneath it implements something the design credits to the module next door — and nothing told me."

📌 NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the 130 capabilities with no file evidence hide more of the same. They are unmeasurable by this method, not clean, and reading their silence as agreement would repeat the exact error this fact records.

properties.name: The four-layer frame's first clean separation of ② from ③: the author of a skill did not use it an hour after writing it — and the skip pattern across one session is SYSTEMATIC in a way the frame does not predict
properties.statement:
OBSERVED 2026-08-28, in the session that built `cap:root-cause-skill`. Anthony asked, after the fact, *"are you using reflow2 skills and tools to implement this design?"* — which is itself the THIRD dated instance of the user being the trigger, after 2026-08-06 and the pair already on `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`.

═══ ⭐⭐ OBSERVATION 1: LAYERS ① AND ③ SATURATED, FAILURE AT ② ═══

The agent wrote the `root-cause` skill, and roughly one hour later investigated a latency question WITHOUT INVOKING IT — producing FOUR wrong diagnoses in series, each replacing the last: that `search_design` was slow (refuted: `get_node` equally slow), that every graph call was slow (refuted: the session's own calls were not), that the cost was per-TCP-connection (refuted: calls 2 and 3 on one connection were 0.05s), and that it was contention from concurrent probes (refuted: a clean run was still 31.35s). The mechanism is STILL not established.

⭐ **THIS IS THE FIRST OBSERVATION THAT SEPARATES ② FROM ③ CLEANLY.** In every prior sighting both could plausibly have failed. Here ③ (WORTH IT) cannot be the explanation: the agent had just spent the session ARGUING FOR the skill's value, writing its rationale, and pinning it with a test. ① (KNOWN) cannot be either: it authored the text. The failure was entirely at ② — RECOGNITION.

⭐ **AND THE RECOGNITION FAILURE HAS A SPECIFIC, FIXABLE CAUSE.** The skill's own trigger description begins *"Use when something has FAILED"*. The agent was taking A MEASUREMENT THAT SURPRISED IT, which did not match that shape. **The trigger was written for the reported-defect case and not for the I-am-measuring-and-the-number-is-odd case — which is exactly where overconfident diagnosis begins.** A skill whose trigger names only the loud case is invisible during the quiet one.

═══ ⭐⭐ OBSERVATION 2: THE SKIP PATTERN IS SYSTEMATIC, AND THE FRAME DOES NOT PREDICT IT ═══

Across one long session the split was clean:

**USED, properly and before the work:** where-am-i, capture-intent, capture-session, brainstorm, artifact-design. Plus `loop_status` at every phase, `detect_gaps` after every capture batch, `unclaimed_findings`, `review_relations`, `report_manual_work`, and `search_design` before every create — where the duplicate guard correctly caught the agent twice.

**SKIPPED, where they applied:** impact-check, revise-design, link-artifacts, `gap_to_prompt`. **`propagate_change` was never called ONCE**, although the server's own instructions say *"on any change, add_change_event + propagate_change to see the blast radius BEFORE editing"*. Source files were edited first and the ChangeEvent recorded after — the BL-163 shape the Stop hook exists to catch. `revise-design`'s snapshot-before-edit was skipped twice, and the tool warned both times that no snapshot held the prior values.

⭐ **THE FOUR LAYERS APPLY EQUALLY TO BOTH GROUPS, SO THEY CANNOT EXPLAIN A SPLIT THIS CLEAN.** What distinguishes them is WHEN they are invoked: **the used skills fill a pause — a session start, a natural break, an explicit "capture this". The skipped skills must INTERRUPT work already in flight.**

⚠️ **THAT IS EVIDENCE FOR OPTION (d), which this node says nothing has tested.** Not context budget exactly, but its close neighbour: a skill that asks the agent to STOP AND GO BACK costs more than one that occupies a moment with no other agenda. If that holds, hardening ①–③ for the change-governing skills is work aimed at the wrong variable.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH ═══

- **n=1 session, one agent, one model.** The split is clean but it is one observation, and this project's own history says the tempting fix is usually the wrong one.
- **The pause-versus-interrupt reading is INFERENCE**, not measurement. It fits the data and so might other explanations — for instance that the capture skills have slash commands the user typed, while the change-governing ones must be self-invoked. That alternative is NOT ruled out here and would point at a completely different fix.
- **It says nothing about consumers.** This was a session with far more reflow2 context than any consumer's agent will have, which the frame already notes makes it a BEST case rather than a typical one.
