properties.description: A withdrawn Decision contradicting its successor is not reported as a defect (crates/reflow2-core/tests/heal.rs) — 5 cases. THE CASE: a `rejected` Decision linked by CONTRADICTS to what replaced it is the HEALTHY shape — tried in thought, refuted, here is what we did instead — and reporting it as a warning made recording a refutation CORRECTLY cost a defect while burying it in prose cost nothing. `superseded` is pinned as the same shape by a different route. TWO COUNTERWEIGHTS, and they are what stop the fix becoming a hole: two ACCEPTED decisions that contradict each other are still reported, because a live disagreement is the whole reason the detector exists and trading a false positive for a false negative is strictly the worse bug; and `proposed` is NOT treated as withdrawn, because undecided is not abandoned and silencing it would hide exactly the disagreements a brainstorm exists to surface. The sibling `alignment: supporting` rule is pinned separately so the two skips cannot be collapsed into one.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED TWICE: removing the status check fails only the two withdrawn cases; widening it to "anything not accepted" fails ONLY the proposed counterweight, which is the case proving it does not silence too much. MEASURED ON THE REAL DESIGN: 16 defects and 4 contradictions before and after — reflow2 holds 10 superseded and 1 rejected Decision and ZERO CONTRADICTS edges from any of them, so nothing here was silenced.
properties.name: A withdrawn Decision contradicting its successor is not a defect

properties.description: A write names the properties the schema does not declare, and still stores them (crates/reflow2-core/tests/a_write_says_what_it_did_not_recognise.rs) — 6 cases. THE CASE is the exact write that exposed this: `enforcement: \"advisory\"` on a DesignRule, where the real field is `enforced`, a bool. TWO COUNTERWEIGHTS DECIDE WHETHER THIS IS A REPORT OR NOISE: an ordinary write using only declared properties says NOTHING, because a signal that fires on correct work is one people stop reading; and the correctly-spelled `enforced` is never named, since the pair is one edit apart and reporting it would make the check actively misleading. A THIRD holds the line the other way: an unknown NODE TYPE reports nothing rather than every key, because that case is already refused loudly by the write itself and answering \"all of them are undeclared\" would bury the real error. AND THE LAST IS THE POINT OF THE WHOLE THING: the undeclared property is STILL STORED. This reports; it never refuses — the property bag is a capability, not an oversight, and a fix that started rejecting unknown keys would break the thing it was meant to make honest.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED BOTH WAYS: reporting nothing fails the two positive cases; reporting EVERY key fails those plus the silence counterweight, which is the case proving it does not become noise.
properties.name: A write names the properties the schema does not declare, and still stores them

properties.description: An acknowledgement is a statement ABOUT the design, not a part of it (crates/reflow2-core/tests/acknowledgement_not_structure.rs) — 5 cases. Acknowledging a disconnected_community CLOSES it and it stays closed on re-detect, which is the livelock: the review Decision is wired GOVERNED_BY into the affected set and the defect id hashes that set, so the acknowledgement used to join the island it acknowledged and mint a new, larger, unaccepted id without limit. Withdrawal still reopens it, and reopens the SAME defect rather than a differently-shaped one. THREE COUNTERWEIGHTS, which are what keep the fix from being a way of silencing a detector: an ORDINARY Decision still counts as structure (excluding all Decisions would pass the livelock case and island everything a real decision governs), a genuinely isolated cluster still fires, and the review record is still stored with its reason and still reachable by GOVERNED_BY from what it acknowledges.
properties.findings: WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIX: the two bug cases failed and all three counterweights passed.
properties.name: An acknowledgement is a statement about the design, not a part of it

properties.description:
crates/reflow2-core/tests/an_acknowledgement_says_whose.rs, 5 cases.

THE CASE THAT EARNED ITS KEEP IS `an_approver_who_does_not_exist_is_refused_and_nothing_is_written`, AND IT FAILED ON THE FIRST ATTEMPT. The Decision is minted before the approver can be checked, so the obvious implementation left an ACCEPTED Decision with no name behind on every refusal — the exact state the parameter exists to prevent, produced by the code meant to prevent it. The check now runs before anything is written.

The rest: a named approver lands as `AUTHORED_BY role=approver` (author or reviewer would not satisfy the intent-authority rule, so the role is asserted rather than the edge alone); an absent approver is ALLOWED and invents nobody, because refusing would leave a design that has modelled no Contributor unable to accept a gap; the gap is acknowledged and reaches `reviewed_gaps` either way, since attribution is not about whether the judgement took effect; and the old `acknowledge_gap` signature still compiles and still records nobody, which is what makes this additive.
properties.findings: 5 cases passing, alongside `cargo test --workspace` (45 suites, 0 failures), fmt, core and mcp clippy, skill_lint, smoke_mcp and all 156 toolsnaps. Driven against a scratch design over real stdio, all three paths behave: no approver records the Decision and returns `approved_by: null` with the `unattributed` sentence; `approver: who:ghost` is refused naming the id and pointing at add_contributor; a real approver lands `AUTHORED_BY {role: approver, acted_at}`. THE REFUSAL CASE FAILED ON ITS FIRST RUN and that is the finding: the Decision is minted before the approver can be checked, so the obvious implementation left an accepted Decision with no name behind on every refusal — the exact state the parameter exists to prevent. The check now runs before anything is written.
properties.name: An approver is recorded, an absent one is reported, and a name nobody can check leaves nothing behind

properties.description: A swept file is not called unobserved because a parent also claims it (crates/reflow2-core/tests/a_claim_is_not_hidden_by_its_parent.rs) — 6 cases, all passing 2026-08-16. music_graph F10, REPRODUCED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED on their exact shape: one directory artifact plus two file artifacts beneath it, both files swept, both returned in `unobserved_locations`. The cause was `.find()` — the first claim covering a path absorbed the observation and every other claim covering it was left unmatched. WHY IT IS WORTH SIX CASES rather than one: the field answers "did you forget to sweep something", so a false entry is an alarm on CORRECT modelling, and the reporter's own grading is the argument — "harmless here, but it makes the field untrustworthy as a 'you forgot to sweep this' signal, which is what it is for." THE COUNTERWEIGHTS ARE THE POINT, because the cheapest wrong fix is to make the field SILENT, which is strictly worse than the bug — silence reads as "nothing was missed". Three cases block it: a genuinely unswept claim is still named; a sibling that merely shares a prefix (`src/foo` vs `src/foobar`) does not count as swept; and an EXCLUDED path does not mark its claim swept, so an exclusion rule cannot launder an unswept claim into a clean report. A fourth pins that the COUNT stays one per observed path — two claims covering one file is one file, and counting per claim would trade this bug for an inflated `claimed`. NOT COVERED: nothing here exercises a real sweep of a real tree — every case supplies its observations directly, so this is about the matching rule, not about what a filesystem would hand it.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS, each killed by the right tests: reverting to `find()` fails both defect cases; counting per claim fails the count case; reporting nothing fails three, including both counterweights.
properties.name: A swept file is not called unobserved because a parent also claims it

properties.description:
Twenty-one tests across two files. `crates/reflow2-core/tests/an_upstream_design_is_watched_not_imported.rs` (14) pins the JUDGEMENT, which is pure: unchanged, moved, never_seen, missing, unreadable, graph_id_mismatch, not_watched, not_observed, and the manifest round trip. `crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/an_upstream_export_is_read_without_being_imported.rs` (7) pins the half only a filesystem can answer.

⭐ THE TWO THAT CARRY THE FEATURE. `reading_never_updates_the_baseline_so_a_move_keeps_being_reported` reads three times and asserts the STORED hash is untouched, not merely that the report repeats — a check that refreshed its own baseline would report a move once and then be permanently quiet, which is worse than no check because the silence reads as agreement. `reading_an_upstream_does_not_pull_a_single_node_into_this_design` asserts the node count is unchanged, that a node existing only upstream is absent here, and that this design still carries its own graph_id — because the failure an import produces is subtler than extra nodes: the host keeps its name and the upstream's content arrives under it.

`a_stale_self_stamp_does_not_hide_a_real_change` appends a node to an export by hand WITHOUT restamping — the shape a merge produces — and asserts the computed hash moves anyway. That is `sync_debt`'s 2026-08-11 defect written as a test before it could happen again here.

FOUND A REAL DEFECT WHILE BEING WRITTEN, fixed at the cause rather than in the test: `an_unwatched_dependency_emits_no_watch_fields_at_all` failed on a leftover `design_export_seen_at`, which is a baseline date for a target nobody named — a record of a check that never happened, reading to anyone scanning the manifest exactly like one that did. The hash and its date are now stored and emitted only inside the path.
properties.findings:
GREEN, and read from cargo's OWN exit code rather than from a pipe: `cargo test --workspace` exit 0, 165 suites, 1856 passed, 0 failed. The 21 tests of this check are inside that. Ran under `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=6G` with output to a file, because `cargo test | grep | sort | head` returns head's exit code and says nothing about cargo — a trap this project has hit repeatedly.

🛑 AND A GREEN `cargo test` IS NOT A GREEN CI, which this run proved again: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` FAILED at exit 1 on three reflowed `if let` chains while all 1856 tests passed. Fixed and re-verified at exit 0. Every other gate CI runs was then run locally and is green: `skill_lint` (all checks, including the description cap that had already caught this feature's first tool description at 1569 chars against a 1500 limit), `smoke_mcp` against the real binary over stdio, `validate_schema`, `test_init` (100 tests), and `cargo clippy -p reflow2-core --no-default-features --all-targets` with zero warnings.

`toolsnap.py` reported the two intended surface changes — `declare_dependency` gaining `design_export` and `design_export_seen_at`, and the new `upstream_status` tool with no golden — and the goldens were regenerated deliberately with `--update` and re-checked clean.

⚠️ ONE ORDERING MISTAKE WORTH RECORDING: the artifact baselines were taken BEFORE `cargo fmt` ran, so three of them were stale within minutes and had to be retaken as `design_holds`. Format first, then baseline.

properties.description: An artifact's declared granularity and volatility change what a report says about it, and change nothing else (crates/reflow2-core/tests/artifact_intent.rs, 9 cases). THE COUNTERWEIGHTS ARE THE POINT and are half the file: a stable artifact still reports checksum_change (the default does not move), an unchanged append_only artifact still reads as unchanged rather than as an expected change, an ordinary artifact is not named as a placeholder, and — the one that keeps this honest — a MISSING append_only artifact still fires at full severity, because declaring content volatile never says the file may vanish.

properties.description: All of it or none of it, and every failure in one round trip (crates/reflow2-core/tests/bulk.rs + crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/tools.rs) — 14 cases. ATOMICITY: one bad item rejects the whole batch and the good items BEFORE and AFTER it are both absent; an edge into a missing node rolls back the good edge beside it; one unknown artifact leaves every other baseline unmoved. EVERY FAILURE: two bad items in a batch of four come back as two failures with their indices, and a failure carries its POSITION so two entries sharing an id are still distinguishable. PER-ITEM JUDGEMENT: two accepts with two DIFFERENT dispositions produce two different change-event records and design_holds never borrows design_updated's event; two acknowledged gaps keep two different rationales. COVERAGE: one bulk edge form produces byte-identical properties to the typed helper it replaces, defaults included, so nothing is silently dropped. SURFACE: a rejected batch is an ERROR carrying every failure in its data rather than a payload that reads as success; two gaps whose prompts share an id are each replayed against ONLY their own answers; a half-answered ask batch is refused naming which half and writes nothing; an empty ask batch is refused rather than treated as a no-op.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS, each failing exactly the tests that name it and nothing else: commit instead of discarding on failure and the three atomicity cases fail; break at the first failure and exactly the two collect-every-failure cases fail; hoist item 0's disposition onto every item and ONLY the per-disposition case fails while the other eight stay green, which is what proves that test is not passing for free. PROVEN ON THE REAL SURFACE: driven over stdio JSON-RPC against the built binary on a copy of reflow2's own 1205-node design — 138 tools served, 20 nodes and 20 edges each in one call, a rejected batch returning BOTH failures with the good item before them unwritten, and two accepts carrying two different change types.
properties.name: A bulk write is all of it or none of it, and reports every failure at once

properties.description:
Nine cases over `relation_candidates` and the `what_next` intent-contradiction fix, in `crates/reflow2-core/tests/candidates_are_offered_never_drawn.rs`.

THE REFUSALS CARRY THE WEIGHT, because every way this feature goes wrong is a false neighbour: a word true of everything must not manufacture seven neighbours; a candidate that cannot say why it surfaced is never offered; something already related is excluded AND reported rather than silently dropped; an empty answer names which of three empties it is; and an unknown node is refused by name.

TWO CASES EXIST BECAUSE THE FIRST DRAFT WAS WRONG AND THE TESTS CAUGHT IT. The background-term filter rejected EVERY term on a small pool — any shared word is 50% of a two-node pool by arithmetic rather than by being common — and shared vocabulary could outrank a shared neighbour, which was fixed by making structural presence the primary sort key rather than by tuning a multiplier.

Also pinned: an idea contradicting SETTLED intent now scores and says which kind of clash it is, while one contradicting intent the user settled OUT (`dropped`) scores zero, because contradicting something already abandoned is not a live tension.
properties.findings:
9 passed / 0 failed. Whole workspace alongside it: `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` WS_EXIT=0, 157 result lines against 152 test files, 1,795 passed, 0 failed. Core-only: 129 suites, 1,486 passed, 0 failed.

TWO OF THE NINE EXIST BECAUSE THE FIRST DRAFT WAS WRONG, and both are recorded rather than quietly fixed. The background-term filter rejected EVERY term on a small pool, because any shared word is 50% of a two-node pool by arithmetic rather than by being common — the proportional rule now applies only once the pool is big enough for a proportion to mean anything. And shared vocabulary could outrank a shared neighbour, fixed by making structural presence the PRIMARY SORT KEY rather than by raising a multiplier until the example passed.

⚠️ THE SUITE ALSO COST THE MACHINE SOMETHING WORTH KNOWING: on a 4-core box, `--workspace --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=2` drove load average to 5.8 and the user reported interactive lag. Renicing the run to +19 dropped it to 4.4 within seconds and it finished green at 1.99. That is the tail of `dec:the-gate-runs-every-test-binary-before-reporting`: a run that executes every binary costs more wall-clock and more CPU than one that stops at the first failure. The trade is still right — a red run should yield every fact it has — but the pre-push gate is not free on a small machine, and renicing it is the cheap mitigation.
properties.name: candidates_are_offered_never_drawn.rs

properties.description: The shipped gate checks the pins, and bites when they disagree (tools/reflow2_check.py, run against reflow2's own design 2026-08-06, 3 cases). GROUPING: five Cargo crates (dynograph-core/-storage/-graph/-resolution/-vector) match ONE declaration because observations are keyed by SOURCE, not by name — matching on name would have produced four false 'undeclared' findings and one backwards 'unobserved'. HONEST SILENCE: a project whose pins this gate cannot read reports 'N declared, and this gate could not read any build file to check them', rather than reconciling against an empty observation set, which would fire `unobserved` on every declaration and punish the correct behaviour.
properties.findings: POSITIVE: 1 declared, 1 observed across Cargo.toml and two crate manifests, reported as agreeing. NEGATIVE, which is the case that matters: the dynograph-foundation tag was temporarily bumped to a version that does not exist and the gate FAILED the build with `version_mismatch — declared v0.12.0 but the build resolves v0.99.0`, then passed again when restored.

properties.description: A digest is a digest whichever dialect it arrives in (crates/reflow2-core/tests/checksum_dialect.rs) — 14 cases, 9 new for BL-160. PREFIX (BL-125): a bare hex digest matches its own `sha256:`-prefixed baseline and vice versa, the drift event id is identical whichever dialect was observed, and both counterweights hold — a genuinely different digest still reports `checksum_change` with its `realizes` edges intact, and a non-hex fingerprint is left verbatim. LENGTH (BL-160): a full 64-char digest matches a 16-char baseline and a truncated observation matches a full baseline, on the drift comparison AND on `set_artifact_checksum`'s would-move-the-baseline guard — the half that is not a gate problem at all but a BL-157 bulk sweep failing on every short-registered artifact for a change that never happened. When the two dialects agree the LONGER digest stays on the record, which also makes the accept idempotent ACROSS dialects: re-stating it coarsely mints one claim, not two. FIVE COUNTERWEIGHTS, and they are what keep the length rule from being a way to stop noticing: two FULL digests sharing their first sixteen characters are still drift (the case a truncate-both-to-N would pass); a truncated observation that disagrees WITHIN its own length is still drift; a genuinely different digest is still refused as a first baseline, still naming the disposition that would be honest; prefix tolerance does not escape the `sha256:` dialect, so `blake3:zz` and `blake3:zzzz` stay different; and an EMPTY digest agrees with nothing, because every string starts with the empty string. No minimum prefix length is imposed, deliberately — a short baseline is a weak baseline, but its strength is decided when it is REGISTERED, and a read side refusing to honour what the write side accepted is the same write/read disagreement this suite exists to close. `tools/reflow2_check.py`'s Python workaround is DELETED, and tools/test_reflow2_check.py pins the pair end to end: an untouched file registered short gates GREEN, and the same short baseline on a genuinely edited file still gates RED.
properties.findings: WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIX: the four bug cases failed and all five counterweights passed. MUTATION-CHECKED SEVEN WAYS, each failing exactly the tests that name it: make agreement always-true and all seven counterweights fail while every bug case passes (which is what proves the counterweights carry the weight); revert to `==` and exactly the four bug cases fail; drop the sha256-dialect restriction and only the two dialect-boundary cases fail; truncate both sides to 16 and only the two sharing-a-prefix cases fail; drop the both-non-empty guard and only the empty-digest case fails; fix drift.rs alone and only the two accept-path cases fail; drop the longer-digest-wins rule and only the idempotence case fails. THE TEST WAS CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT: the first version of the still-refused counterweight used a SHORT baseline, and against a 16-char baseline `NEAR` is a legitimate extension rather than a different digest — a 16-char baseline only ever pinned 16 characters, which was established by writing it wrong rather than assumed. PROVEN ON THE REAL DESIGN, and it is the row's own scenario replayed: the built binary driven over stdio JSON-RPC against a throwaway copy of reflow2's own 1221-node design, sweeping all 109 registered artifacts off the actual working tree with the FULL 64-char digest — 51 truncated baselines, all 51 unchanged, and the only 4 `checksum_change` findings are the four files this change edited.
properties.name: A digest is a digest whichever dialect it arrives in

properties.findings: Proven end to end over stdio with a genuinely exited server process: gone vs live, zero false overlaps, the ghost named in `stale`.

properties.description: The ledger's word for "nothing moved" (crates/reflow2-core/tests/confirmation_vocabulary.rs + crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/tools.rs) — 14 cases. BL-157: a first baseline records `baseline_established`, not a `refactor` of a file nobody touched; the same first baseline twice mints one claim; the ledger counts first baselines APART from accepts, because folding them into design_holds would report a judgement nobody made. BL-158: a clean reconcile stamps last_confirmed_at and returns what it confirmed, and one clean pass moves a never-examined capability out of `unexamined`. FIVE COUNTERWEIGHTS, which are what keep this from being a way to silence the two-sided accept: a baseline_established that would MOVE an existing baseline is refused; an accept against NO baseline is refused naming the disposition that is right; looking still writes nothing; a partial sweep confirms only what it saw and a drifted artifact is never confirmed; and a first baseline does not feed last_claim_at, so registering a long-missing checksum cannot age the passing check that covers it.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED FIVE WAYS, each failing exactly the tests that name it: let baseline_established move a baseline → only the laundering counterweight fails; allow an accept with no baseline → only that refusal fails; blind the ledger to the new change_type → exactly the three tests naming it, including the freshness counterweight; write an undated confirmation anyway → only the skipped-out-loud case; confirm everything observed rather than only what matched → only the drifted-artifact case. PROVEN ON THE REAL SURFACE, and it is BL-158's own scenario replayed: the freshly-built binary driven over stdio JSON-RPC against a throwaway copy of reflow2's own 1218-node design, sweeping all 109 registered artifacts off the actual working tree — 109 unchanged, ZERO drift, 109 confirmed, and `loop_status` went from "1 built capability never checked against reality" to entirely CLEAN. The capability that cleared was cap:skill-triggers via art:nudge-detect, which is the exact claim the live loop had been asking about all session. The row's own measurement was 107 artifacts, 106 unchanged, zero drift and the number moving by ZERO. FOUND BY THE GUARD ITSELF: two changelog.rs fixtures had been passing a checksum as add_artifact's LOCATION argument for as long as they existed, so their accepts had been accepting nothing and nothing had ever checked. FOUND BY WRITING THE PROOF: the first sweep reported 51 phantom drifts on a clean tree because it hashed to the full 64 hex chars while the design registers checksums anywhere from a 16-char prefix up — reflow2_check.py compensates for that in Python, and the core's canonical_checksum does not, which is BL-125's dialect problem in a second form.
properties.name: The ledger's word for "nothing moved" is not its word for a change

properties.description: Re-calling a constructor does not erase what the design already knew (crates/reflow2-core/tests/constructors_preserve.rs) — 9 cases. THE COUNTERWEIGHTS ARE WHAT KEEP THE FIX FROM BEING A DIFFERENT BUG: a first call still writes schema defaults rather than inheriting, a named property is still overwritten, and an explicitly-passed optional still wins — so `merge` never became `first write wins` or `you may never change this back`. create_node and import_graph deliberately still REPLACE, because an import document is a complete statement of a node and merging there would resurrect properties it meant to omit.
properties.findings: WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIX: all 6 defect cases failed and all 3 counterweights passed. THE AUDIT, not the instance, is the finding: 16 of 18 public add_* helpers named a SUBSET of their node type's properties and wrote create-or-REPLACE, so re-calling one to revise a node reset every unnamed property to its schema default. add_interface lost 13 including `designation` (which contracts are published boundaries, req:key-interfaces); add_requirement lost `status`, which IS certainty (dec:certainty-derived), so rewording forged the user's signature in reverse; add_capability un-built a verified capability; add_artifact was BL-166 still reachable one call away, that fix having landed on link_artifact only. It survived BL-46 and BL-166 because it is INVISIBLE until a property has been moved off its default. It violated req:no-silent-fallback, accepted and priority CRITICAL.
properties.name: Re-calling a constructor does not erase what the design already knew

properties.description: A built capability with no recorded consumer is surfaced, and the report never says "unused". COVERS THE CAPABILITY SIGNAL ONLY — the three consumption edges read (incoming DEPENDS_ON, outgoing PART_OF_FLOW, incoming INTERACTS_WITH), the realized/verified population, discontinued capabilities and discontinued CONSUMERS excluded, the MIN_MODELLED_RATIO withholding rule with its ratio note, MIN_POPULATION, the stated signal boundary, and the wording discipline (the finding may not contain "unused"/"dead"/"delete"/"surplus"/severity, scanned over the OBSERVATIONS so the caveats may still name the failure mode they prevent). DELIBERATELY NOT COVERED: the generalisations the capability's description mentions in passing — a Component whose Interfaces nothing CONSUMES, and an Artifact realizing only unconsumed capabilities. Neither is built, and this check must not be read as standing for them (the ver:sessions-cannot-cross-designs precedent, 2026-08-07: a green check covering a clause it never tested is worse than an absent one).
properties.findings: 15 cases, each mutation-checked — all eight mutations tried (dropping each of the three signals, admitting `planned` to the population, disabling either threshold, and removing either discontinued check) were killed.
properties.name: A built capability with no recorded consumer is surfaced, and never called unused

properties.description: The image builds, runs unprivileged, and a design survives replacing the container (run by hand on a real Docker daemon, 2026-08-06, 6 checks): builds clean on BOTH bases (ubuntu:22.04 the release base, ubuntu:24.04 the dev fallback); the container reaches `Up (healthy)`, so the HEALTHCHECK's /dev/tcp probe works and the port is only bound after the store is open; `id` inside reports uid 1000 on both bases; the volume gets the designed layout with graph.id.json and graph.meta.json BESIDE the store rather than inside it; and THE ACCEPTANCE TEST FROM req:hosted-state-outlives-the-image PASSES — stop the container, start a new one against the same volume, and graph_id is byte-identical (4934a26b7cc87ed2 both times) with ZERO re-mint warnings, so the new container adopted the existing design rather than opening an empty one beside it. WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER, stated because the gap is invisible otherwise: the release.yml `container` job has never run — publishing needs a version tag — so registry login, push, multi-tag and the pull-back verification are unexercised. The Dockerfile is proven; the publish path is written and untested.

properties.description: Manifest completeness, both directions: every content hash the graph references appears in the manifest with its original filename and what points at it; a referenced hash whose bytes are ABSENT is reported by name (the case someone holding only the export hits); a blob present but referenced by nothing is ALSO reported, because orphaned bytes are how a store silently grows; and `.gitattributes` marks the blob directory `binary`, pinned by a case that would otherwise let line-ending conversion corrupt a PNG. properties.description: The store on the MCP surface (crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/tools.rs, 5 cases): text round-trips and a re-put reports `already_present` rather than looking like new work; NON-UTF-8 BYTES survive the JSON boundary as base64 and come back base64 unchanged, which is the whole reason that field exists; passing both `text` and `base64` is REFUSED rather than resolved by picking one, and passing neither is refused as a mistake rather than stored as an empty blob; `exists` answers false for an unstored hash without erroring, because that is the call someone makes to ask "do I have everything?"; and A SERVER WITH NO --content-path CONFIGURED REFUSES BY NAME instead of inventing a directory — blobs are committed, so where they live is a decision about the consumer's repo.

The load-bearing four: two specs naming the same component converge on ONE node while each keeps its own provenance Fragment; three documents pin to ONE epoch, not three; a re-run reports the already-ingested document as SKIPPED and not failed, so resume is derived from the graph rather than bookmarked; and a document that cannot be taken is NAMED with why while its siblings still ingest. properties.description: An unmodelled subtree is reported and a modelled file is not; ONE OPAQUE ARTIFACT LEGITIMATELY CLAIMS THE MASS BENEATH IT (900 vendored files under a single registered directory report zero unclaimed — the trap a file-count ratio would fall into, since it would score correct coarse modelling as 1-of-901 and call it failure); a shared name prefix does not claim across a directory boundary; exclusions come back NAMED with the rule that excluded them and their mass does not inflate the silence; regions rank by mass so the biggest silence sorts first; a registered location the sweep never mentioned is named; and an empty sweep claims nothing rather than reading as full coverage (crates/reflow2-core/tests/coverage.rs, 7 cases)

properties.description: A cycle finding names what it walked (crates/reflow2-core/tests/cycles.rs) — 6 new cases of 15. A loop through ONE shared contract names that contract and says no DEPENDS_ON is involved; a genuine TWO-contract service cycle is NOT blamed on the model but still names both; a plain DEPENDS_ON tangle says it is direct and names no contract; a MIXED cycle claims neither pure case, because saying 'no DEPENDS_ON' there would send a reader to check their interface model while real code coupling sits in the loop. PLUS the medium pair, which is the case that matters: a round trip through two library/data contracts reports the medium, and THE SAME SHAPE over REST makes no foundation claim — without that counterweight the medium sentence would print on every contract cycle and mean nothing.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS: collapse the interface-count discriminator and exactly the two-contract counterweight fails; drop interface attribution entirely (the pre-BL-141 behaviour) and exactly the three tests naming the new behaviour fail while the direct-DEPENDS_ON case stays green; force the foundation-medium claim always-true and exactly the REST counterweight fails. THE DESIGN WAS CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT, not reasoning: the first discriminator keyed on the INTERFACE COUNT (one shared contract = coarse model), and reproducing the reporter's own cycle on their real design showed it misses their actual case — their loop runs through TWO interfaces and is structurally identical to a genuine service cycle. Only the `medium` separates them. Verified end to end by reconstructing their pre-workaround model from a read-only snapshot of their live graph: the exact loop they reported, `cmp:fundamental-detection → cmp:midi-renderer → cmp:fundamental-detection`, now names both contracts and the medium.
properties.name: A cycle finding names what it walked

properties.description: A decomposition is asked what it dropped: the question fires per decomposed parent and names the parent; a requirement nobody split is silent; only DECOMPOSES counts, so satisfaction and derivation never raise it; the recorded answer stops the question and survives in reviewed_gaps; CHANGING THE SPLIT RE-ASKS with a new id, because the earlier answer was about those children; a parent already reporting delivered outranks one still open AND says so; and the finding NEVER names what is missing (crates/reflow2-core/tests/detect.rs, 7 cases).
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED FIVE WAYS, each killed by exactly the test that names it: dropping the detector registration (5 dead), flipping is_aggregate to true so a stale answer silences a changed split (1), anchoring only the parent (2), removing the delivered severity bump (1), and making the finding suggest what to add (1).
properties.name: A decomposition is asked what it dropped

properties.description: The schema's declared defaults are readable, checked, and injected only where injection is a statement (crates/reflow2-core/tests/schema_defaults.rs, 7 cases). WHY THIS EXISTS: `default:` in the schema YAML is executed by dynograph-core at WRITE time (schema.rs:507 inserts any missing property that declares one), which is where 3,207 stored values across 59% of this design came from — an injected value and a chosen one stored identically, so absence meant nothing. THE CASES: declared_defaults() parses all of them from the embedded YAML with no new dependency, and a floor assertion fails loudly if the line shape ever moves and the parser silently stops seeing them; schema_default() resolves by type and property, and answers None rather than guessing for a property that declares none — GATED_ON.min_level is deliberately undefaulted because defaulting it would pick a risk posture for the user; the ten properties removed for BL-198 step 1 are asserted ABSENT after a plain constructor call, which is the behaviour change itself; a value the caller DOES supply is still stored, so absence and choice are finally distinguishable. AND THE COUNTERWEIGHTS, which are the point rather than an afterthought: `Requirement.status = proposed` and `provenance` are asserted STILL INJECTED, because the whole certainty doctrine reads them and removing those would break derivation rather than clean it; `Requirement.lineage = original` is asserted still injected too, and it is there because it CAME OFF the confirmed removal list — requirement_lineage.rs refused the change, since `original` is the base case of a three-way classification whose other values (`decomposed`, `derived`) are set explicitly by operations. THE CASE THAT EARNS ITS KEEP BEYOND THIS ROUND: every_declared_default_is_a_legal_value_of_its_own_enum is a cross-check nothing could previously make — the validator checks stored values against `values`, the parser ignored `default` entirely, so a default naming a value its own enum forbids was invisible to both. WHAT IS NOT COVERED, stated rather than discovered later: nothing here proves the ten removed are the RIGHT ten. That was a per-property judgement made by the owner on measured evidence (single-valued in the data, no string-literal occurrence anywhere, no setter), and three mechanically-obvious candidates were kept on evidence — the reflex that single-valued means informationless was wrong three times in ten.
properties.name: Declared defaults are readable, checked, and injected only where injection is a statement

properties.description:
crates/reflow2-core/tests/delivery_kind.rs, 10 cases.

WHAT IT PINS: that model work with a passing check reports delivered; that model work WITHOUT a check does not, so the declaration loosens which evidence is required and never whether any is; that an artifact capability still needs both halves; that an UNDECLARED capability keeps the stricter rule, so nothing written before this quietly loosens; that a bad delivery kind is refused naming the legal values; that declaring on an absent capability is refused; and that the setter preserves every other property, which is the BL-183 shape where a sharpening write silently unbuilds a verified capability.

THE TWO THAT EARN THEIR KEEP MOST:

an_unbuilt_capability_with_a_passing_check_is_not_delivered pins THE REJECTED FIX — the version first proposed and first APPROVED, before reading the code showed it was wrong. Inferring `model` from a missing artifact reports unbuilt work as delivered the moment any check is pointed at it, because the commonest reason a capability has no file is that nobody has built it. Without this test the cheaper rule is one refactor away from being reinstated as a simplification.

an_outstanding_item_with_a_check_but_no_file_names_the_remedy pins DISCOVERABILITY, with a sibling asserting the note stays SILENT when there is no check at all. Fixing the rule while leaving the declaration unmentioned would have reproduced, inside the very change that documents it, the failure found four separate times that day: the mechanism exists, is tested, and is unreachable from where the person is stuck.

NOT COVERED, stated rather than left to be found: nothing checks that an author declared the RIGHT kind. That is a judgement about their own work, and reflow2 records what a person knows rather than second-guessing it — the same position REALIZES.conformance takes.
properties.findings:
RUN 2026-08-20: 10 passed, 0 failed. Whole crate 1121 passed / 0 failed across 107 binaries, exactly +10 tests and +1 binary against the 1111/106 baseline — a foundation module and the schema were touched and nothing else moved. PROVEN ON THE LIVE GRAPH, not only fixtures: both capabilities of epoch:the-declared-walls-hold were declared `model` through the served tool, and the increment went from two `outstanding` to two `delivered`. The discoverability note fired on the real case beforehand and correctly disappeared afterwards.

A DEFECT THIS RUN CAUGHT THAT NOTHING ELSE COULD: inserting the new tool between an existing #[tool(...)] attribute and its function SWAPPED TWO SERVED DESCRIPTIONS — set_interface_designation described capability delivery and set_capability_delivery described interface designation. cargo build, cargo clippy -D warnings, cargo fmt and 1121 tests were all clean. Only the toolsnap gate saw it. An attribute is legal Rust wherever it sits; which function a description belongs to is a fact about the SERVED SURFACE, and only a check that reads the served surface can hold it.

properties.description: A dependency that is itself a reflow2 design can say so, and one that is not stays silent (crates/reflow2-core/tests/depends.rs, 2 cases added, 12 passing in the file). LINKED: graph_id round-trips through the store and appears in reflow2.toml as `graph_id = \"dynograph-foundation\"`. UNLINKED, which is the case that carries the doctrine: a second declaration without one round-trips as None AND its manifest entry contains no graph_id line at all — absence is stored as absence, so a reader can tell \"this dependency has no reflow2 design\" from \"nobody recorded whether it does\". BLANK IS NOT A VALUE: a whitespace-only graph_id is treated as unstated rather than as a design whose id happens to be blank.
properties.findings: A TEST-AUTHORING SLIP WORTH KEEPING: the first version of the blank case asserted the whole manifest contained no \"graph_id =\", which passed for the wrong reason and then failed for the right one — the [reflow2] header always emits the design's OWN graph_id, so the assertion had to be scoped to the dependency entry. The test caught the test.

properties.description: The manifest is derived and the derivation never rewrites history (crates/reflow2-core/tests/write_side.rs) — 8 cases. Every Artifact and Component enters the manifest with its checksum frozen; looking writes nothing (the release_report is still empty after a non-applying call); a re-run adds nothing and, after the live baseline has MOVED, still reports what shipped; an artifact with no checksum still ships and is named in without_checksum; an exclusion that names nothing is refused with the whole call written back out; an exclusion that names something comes back by name rather than by omission; an unknown release is refused; and the end-to-end payoff — one call clears the unreleased_component gap that a partial hand-typed manifest leaves open.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS, each failing exactly the one test that names it and nothing else: force apply always-true and only the looking-is-not-writing case fails; drop the exclude validation and only the typo'd-exclusion case fails; drop the already-present guard and only the frozen-checksum case fails — which is what proves the guard is doing work rather than the test passing for free. properties.description: A discontinued thing stops being unfinished work, and the marker is READ (crates/reflow2-core/tests/discontinued_is_read.rs, 6 cases). THE DEFECT CASE: a capability withdrawn by an accepted Decision raises no gaps — the content store had read `realized` with a `passing` check for two days after its code was deleted. THE AUTHORITY CASE: a `proposed` decision to withdraw has withdrawn nothing, which is rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word on the retire path. THE CASCADE: the requirement a withdrawn capability served drops back to unsatisfied and is asked about again, so a discontinuation is not invisible one hop away. THE VISIBLE COUNT: delivery falls AND reports satisfied_only_by_discontinued, because a number that moves with no explanation is the silent-drop failure forbidden everywhere else. TWO COUNTERWEIGHTS carry the weight: a live capability beside a discontinued one is still asked about, and OBSOLETES from something that is NOT a Decision (a superseding epoch) does not discontinue — without that, any obsoleting edge would silence a capability. NOT COVERED: an OBSOLETES edge whose target no longer exists, and discontinuation is read for Capabilities only — Components, Interfaces and Artifacts have no reader.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS, each verified applied before running: dropping the accepted-only check fails the authority case alone; accepting OBSOLETES from any source fails two; disabling all three detector reads fails the defect case. ⚠️ WRITTEN AFTER THE IMPLEMENTATION, not before — the third such instance recorded on 2026-08-11 (fact:implement-first-cost-an-edge-case-2026-08-11), and the cost showed up as a first draft asserting the wrong detector would fire: deleting the only artifact zeroes unrealized_capability's population, so unverified fired instead. The assertions now name the PROPERTY (it is asked about at all) rather than a detector, which is closer to the contract.
properties.name: A discontinued thing stops being unfinished work, and the marker is read

properties.description: An edge to a node that does not exist is refused, not written — THROUGH EVERY TYPED HELPER, not only through create_edge. Found 2026-07-25: authored_by accepted contributor id "person:anthony", which was never created; the edge was stored, get_node returned null for its target, and a phantom AUTHORED_BY sat in the graph until noticed by eye. THE GUARD LANDED IN create_edge (graph.rs:297, 2026-07-28) AND WAS ALREADY TESTED THERE — write_side.rs holds four cases: missing target refused, missing source refused, refusal leaves nothing behind, a legitimate edge still accepted, and an unknown edge type still named FIRST (vocabulary errors before instance errors). What none of those covered is the helpers: every one of them calls create_edge directly, while the original defect was in a typed helper. So crates/reflow2-core/tests/edges_need_both_ends.rs is an AUDIT over all 16 public helpers that join two pre-existing nodes, plus a size-floor test so the table cannot quietly shrink, an atomicity case (a refused authored_by leaves no edge on its source), and a counterweight across three modules so breaking all sixteen is not the cheapest way to pass. The audit shape is deliberate: BL-183 found exactly this divergence on the node side, where 16 of 18 add_* constructors had drifted from the generic path. OUT OF SCOPE and named: constructors that create their own source node, the bulk form (covered by bulk.rs under dec:bulk-is-all-or-nothing-with-per-item-findings), and gate_on, which takes a struct and validates a rung range first.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED, AND THE RESULT WAS NOT THE EXPECTED ONE: disabling the guard failed 14 of 16, not 16 — `documents` and `release_includes` carry their own existence checks before delegating (artifact.rs:519/525, operate.rs:336) and still refused. That is safer rather than broken, and it is recorded because it changes what the file proves: fourteen helpers depend entirely on the shared guard and would regress together, two would hold.
properties.name: An edge to a node that does not exist is refused through every typed helper

properties.description:
Fourteen tests over `detect_defects` / `open_defects`, in four bands.

THE THREE FIXED KINDS, each with its counterweight: two parked ideas that contradict raise nothing, but two ACCEPTED decisions still do; an anticipation involving a parked idea raises nothing, but one between accepted decisions still does; an island of only parked ideas raises nothing, but an island holding anything asserted still does.

⭐ EACH KIND STATES HOW IT COMBINES THE PREDICATE, AND THEY DIFFER. `contradiction` needs BOTH endpoints parked; `unresolved_setup` skips on EITHER; `unthreaded_cluster` needs EVERY island member. That asymmetry is pinned rather than left to a reader: `an_accepted_decision_anticipating_a_parked_idea_is_not_an_unresolved_setup` and `a_measurement_anticipating_a_parked_idea_is_not_an_unresolved_setup` hold the either-side rule, while `a_parked_idea_against_settled_design_is_still_reported` holds the both-sides rule one detector over. A single rule for all three would break one of them.

⭐ THE SWEEP SAYS WHAT IT DID NOT REPORT. `a_suppressed_finding_is_counted_rather_than_silenced` asserts a skipped finding lands in `SweepScope.suppressed_by_parked_idea`, so `reported + suppressed` reconciles instead of findings vanishing. Its counterweight `a_clean_sweep_reports_nothing_suppressed` asserts the map is EMPTY when nothing was parked — that one is what makes the field trustworthy, because a wired-but-never-incremented field otherwise reads exactly like a design with no parked ideas.

THE ASSUMPTION-KILLERS, all written after a wrong cut. `a_decision_has_no_unlabelled_state` records that `Decision.status` defaults to `proposed`, so silence is unreachable and this change is NOT inert on existing designs; it fails if that schema default ever moves. `a_proposed_requirement_still_asserts` is the scope counterweight: `CONTRADICTS` is `from: "*" to: "*"` and `Requirement.status` also defaults to `proposed`, so the predicate checks the node TYPE — and the TemporalFact case above is why a type-scoped predicate cannot be the whole rule for an edge whose other end is any type.

⭐ THE CLASS GUARD, which is the point. `every_category_states_whether_it_reads_proposed` is an EXHAUSTIVE match over `HealCategory`: a new category cannot compile until its author has written down whether it reads a parked idea. It asserts nothing about the ANSWER — both are legitimate — only that somebody gave one. Sibling of `every_category_is_listed_in_all`, which exists one rule over for the same reason.
properties.findings: 14 passed / 0 failed, after THREE cuts, and every cut was OBSERVED FAILING FIRST. Cut 1: 4 of 10 red, all three finding kinds reproduced, counterweights and the class guard green beforehand so they are not vacuous. Cut 2: two new pins red before `unresolved_setup` widened to either side. Cut 3: `a_suppressed_finding_is_counted_rather_than_silenced` was run against the field wired but the increments deliberately NOT added, and went red for exactly that reason, while its counterweight `a_clean_sweep_reports_nothing_suppressed` was green throughout — which is what distinguishes a counted zero from an uncounted one. Full core suite after: 1504 passed / 0 failed across 130 binaries; `cargo fmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` clean; all 161 toolsnaps match, since this changes a result shape rather than a tool schema. Measured on reflow2's own design through the served binary: 89 -> 78 -> 61 reported, and the sweep now declares 33 suppressed (contradiction 3, unresolved_setup 27, unthreaded_cluster 3), so reported + suppressed reconciles.
properties.name: A parked idea is not read as a commitment, and every finding kind states where it stands

properties.description:
Two checks in `tools/skill_lint.py`, run by CI. The first asserts every skill carries a `composes:` declaration — an undeclared skill is invisible to the second, so silence there would read as compliance. The second checks each skill against the obligations of the classes it declares AND NO OTHERS, which is the property no other check in the file can express: everything else there is a predicate over all skills.

⚠️ WHAT IT CANNOT CHECK, and it is the same limit the whole idea carries: whether the obligation was met HONESTLY. It confirms a skill says something that carries the meaning; it cannot confirm the sentence is true or useful. Requiring a section produces a section.

📌 THE OBLIGATIONS ARE TUPLES OF ACCEPTABLE PHRASINGS deliberately, because a single literal fails on wording rather than substance — measured at 13 false failures out of 29 on the first run. The governing line is in the code beside them: adding a phrasing for the same obligation is legitimate, removing the obligation is not.
properties.findings:
PASSING 2026-08-28, after fourteen real omissions were fixed. `python3 tools/skill_lint.py` — all checks passed.

⭐ IT WAS OBSERVED FAILING FIRST, THREE TIMES, AND EACH FAILURE CHANGED SOMETHING:

RUN 1 — 29 unmet. Reading them showed 13 were MATCHING ARTIFACTS rather than deficiencies (`brainstorm` says "searched before", `check-health` says "lose" not "lost"). Obligations became tuples of acceptable phrasings.

RUN 2 — 16 unmet, of which 11 were the SAME obligation. That concentration was the signal: "search before creating" is not owed by every writer, because `genesis` runs on an empty graph, `impact-check` records an event and `parallel-work` records a claim. MINTS was split out of WRITES. **The class was wrong, not the skills.**

RUN 3 — 14 unmet, every one real: 8 skills that mint concept nodes never said to search first; `impact-check` and `link-artifacts` did not bound what they failed to establish; `parallel-work` did not name what a merge can lose; `root-cause` did not name the loop check. Fixed with prose written for each skill.

RUN 4 — 1 unmet, and it was the documented trap: the new `impact-check` text wrapped "could not\\nestablish" across a newline, which `OPTIMIZE_CONTRACT`'s own comment predicts ("fails on reflow rather than on meaning, which trains people to weaken the check"). THE LINE WAS REFLOWED; THE CHECK WAS NOT WEAKENED.

The existing tool-reference check then caught `accept_divergence` named as a tool when it is a parameter of `export_graph` — added to NON_TOOL_TERMS in the same diff, as that check instructs.

Full suite green alongside: `cargo test --workspace` exit 0 from cargo's own code, 165 suites, 1865 passed, 0 failed — byte-identity across all three trees re-verified after 69 frontmatter edits and 33 appended sections.
properties.name: Every skill declares its attribute classes, and meets the obligations of the ones it declares

properties.description: Eight probes across engine and tool. ENGINE (tests/evidence_has_somewhere_to_go.rs): the constructor can reach `description` at all — the half that would otherwise have been missed, since the field was declared and unwritable; a run records `findings` beside its outcome; omitting `findings` LEAVES IT ALONE while a supplied `last_run_at` still moves; a later run can replace it, so "leaves alone" is distinguishable from "cannot update"; and name/description/findings survive independently, since conflating any two is the state the requirement exists to end. Written the new way as its own first demonstration: this check's name is 9 words against a corpus median of 76, its account is in `description`, and this sentence is in `findings` — the three fields the requirement asked to be separable, used separately.

properties.description: The evidence-quality family, all three axes with their counterweights (crates/reflow2-core/tests/evidence_quality.rs) — 18 cases. TIME: an accept dated after the check reports stale, a re-run after the accept is current, an undated side is UNKNOWN and counted rather than silently passed, and a failing check cannot refresh a claim. INPUT: a parameter every passing check pins is reported narrow, ONE check that sweeps it ends the narrowness however many others pinned it, one suite is broad about one claim and narrow about another through the SAME node (the case a per-node property would have to average away), a check stating no scope is unscoped and never read as broad, a comma in a parameter name is refused, and scoping a pair with no VERIFIES edge is refused. INDEPENDENCE: a check the target was calibrated against is CONSUMED, a check that produced the anchor is consumed, a calibration on the realizing artifact counts, correcting the anchor reaches what was fitted to it through the impact table — and the two counterweights, that an independent check beside the fit restores the claim and that a calibration against evidence no check rests on is not circular.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED ON ALL THREE AXES: force freshness never-stale and exactly the two stale tests fail while both counterweights stay green; drop the swept-beats-pinned filter and exactly one test fails; mark every check consumed and BOTH independence counterweights fail — which is what proves the rule does not simply condemn every calibrated design. FOUND BY DOGFOODING BEFORE IT SHIPPED: comparing dates as whole strings called 2026-07-28 stale against 2026-07-28T14:52:00-04:00, an ordering nobody recorded, asserted by the very report that exists to stop that — now same-day is Unknown, pinned by a test, with the counterweight that an earlier DAY is still stale.
properties.name: The evidence-quality family: time, input and independence, each with its counterweight

properties.description: The CONTRACT is checked, not the judgement. skill_lint asserts detect-and-ask states all of it: offer a reading; carry what would change it; present the options as a SELECTABLE list; put the RECOMMENDATION FIRST and mark it; give every option its consequence including the ones not recommended; and answer in the USER'S language, stated language-independently. Plus two negative checks that are the load-bearing half: NO served text hardcodes English as the answer language (so the rule cannot be implemented as English-only — the trap Anthony named), and NO requirement status, decision status or gap acknowledgement is written in the same act as a recommendation. Whether a recommendation is GOOD, and whether the language was correctly matched, are semantic and stay evidenced by trials — deliberately no LLM evals in CI. PLANNED.
properties.name: The contract of how a choice is put to the user is checked; the judgement is not

properties.description: The granularity reading stays quiet when it should (crates/reflow2-core/tests/granularity.rs) — 9 cases, and most of them are silences. Anthony's objection is what shaped this suite: "avoid monoliths" IS a subjective design principle, so the module deliberately does not detect monoliths — it detects that two records the design already holds disagree about how many things there are (N Capabilities vs one Artifact) and refuses to say which side is wrong. THE LOAD-BEARING TEST IS `a_uniformly_coarse_design_is_not_punished`: eight artifacts each swallowing four capabilities produce NO finding, because a breadboard-phase design where everything lives in one file has nothing to be out of line with — dec:maturity-restructuring-delta's trap as an executable guarantee. `the_observation_carries_no_verdict` asserts the serialized report contains none of severity / suggested_fix / monolith / too big / should be split / violation / defect. `two_capabilities_in_one_file_is_not_worth_saying` pins MIN_DISTINCTIONS against a real statistical weakness found while writing the tests: counts pile up at one, the standard deviation collapses, and the distributional cutoff alone fires on noise — the test asserts z clears the bar and that the finding is suppressed anyway. `several_coarse_artifacts_mask_each_other` records z-masking as a known property rather than leaving it to be discovered in the field.
properties.findings: Verified against reality twice: run on the committed design it names exactly one artifact (art:service, 10 capabilities, z=6.46, alone in the design), and run on the v0.21.0 export — BEFORE the observation was ever made — it names the same one at 9 capabilities, z=5.75, which is what makes this discovery rather than a rule fitted to a known answer.
properties.name: The granularity reading stays quiet when it should

properties.description:
`crates/reflow2-core/tests/granularity.rs` — two checks holding `con:granularity-reads-scale-with-artifacts-not-edges`, both COUNTS rather than durations.

`the_reading_costs_one_store_read_per_artifact_plus_a_constant` runs at 10, 40 and 120 artifacts and asserts total reads ≤ N + 2, plus `get_node == 0`. Three sizes, because a budget checked at one size cannot tell a constant from a coefficient.

`adding_edges_does_not_cost_the_reading_anything` is the one that makes the budget mean something: it quadruples the edges while holding the artifacts fixed and asserts the read count is UNCHANGED. The old shape would have quadrupled it. Without this, a budget that happened to pass at one density would look healthy while the defect it forbids was still present.

⚠️ A COUNT, DELIBERATELY, NOT A CLOCK. A duration assertion in a parallel suite measures machine contention, and the standing response is to raise the threshold until it stops complaining — which retires the gate without anybody deciding to. Per-read cost was also measured FLAT (58.0µs over 2853 nodes against 55.1µs over 199), so what the module controls is how many times it asks, not how long each ask takes.

MEASURED BOTH WAYS. Reverting the fix — putting the per-edge `get_node` back — fails both checks and names the constraint in the message ("10 artifacts: 32 reads against a budget of 12"). Restoring it passes 14 of 14. A guard that has only ever been seen green is indistinguishable from one that cannot fail.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CHECK: wall-clock time, deliberately. The change halved the reads and moved the clock not at all (~201ms to ~216ms, noise), because a scan returning 199 nodes costs about what 199 point lookups cost. The budget buys a structural property and buys no speed, and it would be dishonest to guard it with a timer.
properties.findings:
2026-08-21: 14 of 14 granularity tests pass, including both budget checks. Measured on reflow2's own design (2853 nodes, 218 artifacts) via `CountingRead`:

  BEFORE   552 reads   1 scan_nodes, 333 get_node, 218 outgoing   ~201ms
  AFTER    220 reads   2 scan_nodes,   0 get_node, 218 outgoing   ~216ms
  BUDGET   220 (N+2, N=218)

AT BUDGET, so the work STOPPED. Two changes, measured separately: replacing the per-edge `get_node` type-check with one `scan_nodes(Capability)` took 552 → 227, still over; keeping the artifact nodes from the scan already performed rather than re-reading the seven flagged ones took 227 → 220, exactly at budget. Under budget means stop, even though a third change is visible.

⭐ THE CLOCK DID NOT MOVE AND THAT IS THE HONEST RESULT. Reads more than halved; wall time went from ~201ms to ~216ms, which is noise. A `scan_nodes` returning 199 nodes costs about what 199 point lookups cost, so this bought the structural property — cost scales with what the reading reports on — and bought no speed. The budget said so in advance, which is the whole reason for writing it first.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT UNDONE: the 218 `outgoing` calls, one per artifact. Removing them needs a bulk edge-scan the storage contract does not offer, so it would mean changing dynograph-foundation's API — another repo. At budget, so it stops here rather than reaching across that boundary.

AND THE REAL SPEED TARGET IS ELSEWHERE, UNMEASURED: `graph_report` costs ~78s in the same configuration against granularity's ~216ms. Granularity is 0.3% of it. Nothing here touches that, and optimising granularity for wall clock would have been manufacturing work.
properties.name: The reading costs one store read per artifact plus a constant, and adding edges costs it nothing

properties.description:
The 47 `#[test]` cases carried inside `crates/reflow2-core/src/graphalg/`, run by `cargo test -p reflow2-core --lib graphalg` and by both CI jobs. Distribution: communities 10, graph 9, betweenness 7, cuts 6, cycles 5, components 5, scc 5.

⚠️ THIS IS A `partial` CHECK AND THE MISSING HALF IS NAMED ON PURPOSE. The capability claims "reflow2 OWNS the graph theory it analyses designs with". These tests were ABSORBED WITH THE CODE — they are upstream's, and they verify the ALGORITHMS ARE CORRECT IN ISOLATION. That is a weaker statement than the capability makes, in three specific ways:

① **Nothing tests that the absorption preserved behaviour.** The risk peculiar to reflow2 is not whether Tarjan is right — it is whether the move changed anything. `cap:certify-restructuring` exists for exactly this question and was not run against it.

② **`paths.rs` and `error.rs` carry ZERO tests**, and `paths` appears in no reflow2 call site at all — it is likely among the eight `#![allow(dead_code)]` items Anthony deferred trimming on 2026-08-24. A file nothing calls and nothing tests is not covered by this check in either sense.

③ **The tests exercise the algorithms directly, not reflow2's consumption of them.** The consumed surface is EIGHT entry points — `Graph`, `GraphBuilder`, `betweenness_centrality`, `connected_components`, `cut_structure`, `find_cycle`, `leiden`, `strongly_connected_components` — reached from three call sites (`structure.rs`, `allocate.rs`, `flow.rs`). Those three carry their own passing checks (`cap:heal`, `cap:allocate`, `cap:model-process`), so the algorithms ARE exercised end to end — but by checks that verify the DETECTORS, and which would keep passing if a detector were correct for the wrong reason.

⭐ WHY IT IS RECORDED ANYWAY RATHER THAN LEFT OPEN. `unverified_capability` fired because no Verification node existed, not because nothing had been checked — a RECORDING gap, not a coverage hole. Writing a new test purely to satisfy a recording gap would be the tail wagging the dog. What this node must not become is a green light read as covering ①–③; the honest close of those is a test that runs the three consumers over a known design graph and asserts the structural answers.
properties.findings:
`cargo test -p reflow2-core --lib graphalg` on 2026-08-26: **47 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored** (154 filtered out). Run against the v0.40.0 tree at d68bb88.

WHAT THE RUN DID NOT COVER, restated so a reader of the status alone meets it: `paths.rs` and `error.rs` contributed 0 of the 47; no case compares pre- against post-absorption behaviour; and no case enters through the eight entry points reflow2 actually consumes.
properties.name: The absorbed graph algorithms have 47 unit tests, inline in the module

The ratio pins the structure that makes the code fast - the parse happening once - which is what actually broke and was actually fixed.

properties.description: heal.rs — the structural detectors, plus propose/apply atomicity. PLUS the degree-zero Decision rule (2026-08-01, crates/reflow2-core/tests/unreachable_decision.rs, 6 cases): a Decision with NO edges in either direction is reported by `orphan_node`, Warning when its status is `accepted` and Info otherwise. `disconnected_community` cannot see it: it reports clusters of ≥2, and a node joined to nothing is never a cluster. THE STAKE IS NOT TIDINESS — a zero-degree Decision is unreachable by propagation so it never enters an impact analysis, and a disposition specifically can never EXPIRE, because expiry is computed from the affected set (`ver:reviewed-defects`), so a conditional judgement silently becomes permanent. Degree-zero fires on ONE and is self-limiting: ANY edge silences it. THREE COUNTERWEIGHTS, and the first is the one measurement demanded: a Decision reached by any edge at all (a CONTRADICTS, not a GOVERNED_BY) is silent; a `decision:ack:` review record is silent, because structure.rs already excludes those from the design network as judgements ABOUT the design (`ver:acknowledgement-not-structure`) and all twelve of reflow2's own are accepted by construction; and a proposed decision point is Info, never a defect, because firing on a legitimate parking spot is firing on correct work. The pre-existing Artifact-realizing-nothing rule is pinned unchanged, so BL-42's cut-back is not reopened.
properties.findings: FOUND BY RUNNING THE HEALTH SKILLS ON OUR OWN DESIGN AND DISBELIEVING THEM: check-health and detect-and-ask both returned clean — detect_defects 0, hierarchy_issues 0, dimension_drifts 0, propose_heal 0 operations — and a hand count of zero-degree nodes then found `dec:sanitize-spof-accepted`, an ACCEPTED single-point-of-failure disposition with no edges at all, the only one of five such dispositions not linked to what it disposes. THE RULE IS DEGREE-ZERO, AND MEASUREMENT CHOSE IT AGAINST THE STATED RECOMMENDATION: the narrow-looking form, an accepted Decision with no incoming GOVERNED_BY, fires on SIX of reflow2's own, five with degree 1–3 — connected, merely not through that edge. That is [BL-42] exactly, where this same detector reported a well-connected Capability missing one named link, became 20 of 31 defects, and was cut back to a single rule. MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS, each failing exactly the one test that names it: key on missing GOVERNED_BY → only the any-edge counterweight fails, which is BL-42 reproduced; drop the review-record exclusion → only that case; grade everything Warning → only the proposed-is-Info case. MEASURED ON THE REAL DESIGN with a freshly built binary against a throwaway import of the committed export: 3 findings across 1225 nodes — one Warning (`dec:sanitize-spof-accepted`, now fixed by wiring `cmp:ingest GOVERNED_BY` it, matching the four sibling dispositions) and two Info, both proposed decision points.
properties.name: The structural detectors, propose/apply atomicity, and the degree-zero Decision rule

properties.description: Computed evidence reaches its axis without becoming a verdict (crates/reflow2-core/tests/ility.rs) — 11 cases, weighted to the refusals. THREE LINES DEFENDED AT ONCE. (1) NO SCORE IS EVER DERIVED — asserted as JSON field names rather than prose, because the report legitimately says the words 'grade' and 'score' while explaining what it refuses to do, and the first version of this test tripped on its own explanation. Collapsing findings into maintainability: 0.62 is the lossy move dec:readiness-is-an-observation-the-threshold-is-the-judgement already refused for TRL. (2) ADVERSE IS INHERITED, NEVER RE-JUDGED: a finding counts against an axis only where the computation that produced it already calls it a defect. Modularity is a ratio, a trajectory band is a POSITION `maturity` refuses to grade, a granularity observation is one `granularity` refuses to call a defect, and a surprising connection may be hidden coupling OR a creative link — all reported as context, because relabelling them here would overrule a module that deliberately declined to judge and would smuggle back the thresholds those modules were built without. (3) IT MUST NOT PRETEND: performance, security, scalability and observability report NOT INFORMED with the reason rather than reading clean. THE ASYMMETRY IS DELIBERATE AND TESTED: an asserted good score over adverse evidence is flagged, but an asserted LOW score over a quiet axis is NOT — 'no detector fired' is an absence of evidence, and treating it as evidence would be the reading claiming a clean axis is healthy, which it cannot know.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED against five seeded regressions. Four were caught. THE FIFTH WAS INERT AND EXPOSED A MIS-NAMED TEST RATHER THAN A HOLE: deleting the HealSeverity::Info guard fails nothing, because all four mapped categories are Warning-or-Critical by construction and orphan_node is already excluded by mapping to no axis — so the test was renamed from an_info_defect_... to an_unmapped_defect_category_..., which is what it actually proves, and the guard's unreachability is stated at its site. A surviving mutation is not proof a test is weak; check the mutation first.
properties.name: Computed evidence reaches its axis without becoming a verdict

properties.description: The bulk import door describes itself, reports every fault at once, and stops demanding the receiver's own identity (crates/reflow2-core/tests/export.rs, 6 new cases of 18). BL-138: a document of nodes and edges and nothing else — which is literally what the adopt skill instructs — imports, and the edge list may be omitted entirely; `graph_id` was demanded from hand authors and then NEVER READ by the operation demanding it, which is what made it worth removing rather than documenting. COUNTERWEIGHT, and the reason this is not just deleting a requirement: `mirror_surface` still REFUSES an unidentified document by name, because mirroring records where a surface came from and guards against mirroring a design into itself, and neither question is answerable without the id — the same shape as BL-119, where one requirement was right for a round-tripped export and wrong for a hand-authored one. BL-118: four faults in one document now cost ONE round trip instead of four, each reported with its position (`nodes[1]`, `edges[0]`) so a 9,000-line document can be navigated; ATOMICITY IS PINNED SEPARATELY — a rejected import writes nothing at all, including the items that were valid, which is the half the reporting session named as working notably well and the row said must not be touched. The shape is `dec:bulk-is-all-or-nothing-with-per-item-findings` reused rather than reinvented, and it still returns an ERROR rather than an ok-with-failures report, so a rejected import can never read as success. BL-117: the document shape now rides `import_graph`'s own description — the envelope, the optionality of every metadata field, that endpoint types are recovered rather than stored, and that each node must be COMPLETE (BL-139's honest half, delivered whichever way the merge question goes).

properties.description:
`tools/check_intent_authority.py`, gated in CI against the committed export, with `tools/test_check_intent_authority.py` as its hermetic regression net — 10 cases, stdlib only, building their own minimal designs.

BOTH DIRECTIONS: a Decision `accepted` with no approver fails; the same Decision with an `AUTHORED_BY role=approver` edge passes; a grandfathered node is exempt; a `proposed` Requirement is not a settling at all, because an agent may propose anything. All three settling acts are covered — a Requirement off `proposed`, a Decision `accepted`, a DesignRule's `enforced` — since an early draft that checked only Decisions would have passed on the other two. A `reviewer` edge does NOT satisfy it: a review is not a signature.

⭐ FOUR OF THE TEN EXIST ONLY TO PIN THAT IT CANNOT PASS QUIETLY. Missing rule, missing ruling, a ruling still only `proposed`, an unreadable export — each exits 2, never 0. That is the property that matters most here: the rule guards against an agent writing in the owner's voice, and a check that reports success when it could not run would be that failure wearing a green badge.

THE FIXTURE FOUND ITS OWN BUG. The first draft's minimal design tripped the check on its own scaffolding — the rule node and the ruling node are themselves settled intent, and the fixture had not signed them. That is the check working, and the fixture now signs them explicitly.
properties.findings:
2026-08-21, first run. `tools/test_check_intent_authority.py` — 10 of 10 passed. `tools/check_intent_authority.py docs/design/reflow2.json` — exit 0: "419 node(s) assert settled intent; 63 carry an approver; 356 are grandfathered."

PROVED IT CATCHES THE THING, not just that it runs. A Decision with `status: accepted` and no approver edge was injected into a copy of the real 2837-node design; the check went red naming that node and exited 1. Clean before, red after, on real data — because a check that has only ever been seen passing is indistinguishable from one that cannot fail.

THE RED RUN THAT MATTERED WAS ITS OWN FIXTURE. The first draft of the test suite failed on its own scaffolding: the rule node and the grandfathering decision are themselves settled intent, and the fixture had not signed them. The check was right and the fixture was wrong — which is the strongest evidence available that the rule's three settling acts are actually being read.
properties.name: A settled node with no approver fails the build, and every way of not knowing exits 2

properties.description:
`tools/check_kit_manifest.py` — version, file set and per-file hashes.

⚠️ THE NAME USED TO CARRY THE REPORT, AND THE WORD IN IT WAS `unwritten`. It read: *"friction 2026-07-25: reflow2's own manifest is four releases stale and nothing noticed; unwritten"* — while `status` said `passing`. Both halves were wrong by 2026-08-28: the check HAD been written, and it was not being run.

⭐ WHAT WAS ACTUALLY TRUE ON 2026-08-28, measured rather than read off the node: the check existed and FAILED on a clean tree — *"installed by kit 0.30.0, but this source is 0.41.0"*, plus three shipped command files the manifest did not record. It appeared in neither `ci.yml` nor the AGENTS.md gate list.

THE DRIFT WAS CLEARED: the installer was re-run and the manifest read back OUT OF THE FILE as 0.41.0 / d3cb4ab / 36 files — not trusted from the installer's own summary, because `fact:the-v0380-manifest-shipped-empty-because-a-dry-run-reads-like-a-write` records a dry run reading exactly like a write.

🛑 BUT THIS CHECK IS NOT GATED, AND CANNOT BE, IN THIS REPOSITORY. Adding it to `ci.yml` was tried and REVERTED: `.reflow2/` is gitignored and nothing under it is tracked, so a CI checkout has no installation at all and the check exits 2 there — every build would go red. The fresh-install case that could run in CI is already covered by `test_init.py`. `fact:the-kit-manifest-gate-cannot-run-in-ci-because-ci-is-never-installed-into` carries that measurement, and `fact:defect-kit-manifest-drift-is-invisible-to-ci` stays OPEN and sharpened rather than closed.

⇒ SO A PASSING STATUS HERE MEANS SOMEBODY RAN IT BY HAND. Nothing runs it on a schedule, and the next drift will accumulate exactly as this one did.

📌 The report that used to live in this name is here in `description` instead, which is where it belongs — `fact:a-findings-name-can-claim-more-than-its-data-and-the-name-is-what-search-returns` (2026-08-27) measured that `search_design` returns the NAME, so a report written into a name is what every reader meets first.
