properties.description: The nudge's counting AND its own promise are both trustworthy (tools/test_loop_nudge.py) — 47 cases, 11 new in BL-163 on top of the 8 across BL-161 and BL-111. BL-163 · PRECEDENCE, NOT PRESENCE: a session that edits code, records a ChangeEvent and never calls propagate_change is nudged — the defect was that the impact-check shape keyed on `changes == 0`, firing only when a session recorded NOTHING, so writing the ChangeEvents up AFTER the edits satisfied the very trigger meant to catch writing them up after the edits. ROOT CAUSE IN ONE LINE: `CHANGE_OPS` held `record_change` and `add_change_event`, both RECORDING ops, and no set counted `propagate_change` or `propagate_from` at all — the hook could not separate recording from looking because it never counted looking. THE COUNTERWEIGHT THE ROW DEMANDED AND THE CASE PINNED FIRST: a session that propagated gets NOTHING, and `propagate_from` counts as looking too, because the impact-check skill sends a speculative "what would this touch?" straight to it. THE CONJUNCTION IS THE GUARD, all three clauses load-bearing and each with its own test: `edits > 0` (a pure design session has no blast radius to compute), `changes > 0` (what keeps this from becoming a second, thresholdless bypass nudge), `propagates == 0`. BL-161'S PRECEDENT HELD: "you never propagated" is a NEGATIVE claim, so a tally rebuilt after an unreadable one drops it, exactly as "the graph was never consulted" does. BL-161 · STATE INTEGRITY: a 60-hook CONCURRENT burst against a seeded tally lands every increment and wipes no sticky field; against the pre-fix script the same burst returned touched=false, artifacts=0 and 6 of 60 edits, because a non-atomic write plus an error-swallowing read let one hook store zeros over the session's record. COUNTERWEIGHT: a tally rebuilt after an unreadable one keeps counting — an existing case required that and was right — but can no longer support the hook's negative claims, because the calls that would refute them are exactly what was lost; and the POSITIVE claim, "N writes went unchecked", still fires after a restart, so the flag is not an off switch. BULK FORMS: set_artifact_checksums, create_nodes and gaps_to_prompts tally as the singular forms they replace. BL-111 · FIRES ONCE: a second stop CYCLE does not nudge again (the promise is per SESSION, and it rested on the harness's stop_hook_active, which is per cycle and never persisted), all THREE blocking branches keep it, and TWO CONCURRENT HOOK PROCESSES on the same Stop produce exactly ONE message — which is the case it was filed from and is not exotic, since reflow2 installs machine-wide AND a project may carry its own registration and the two command spellings do not dedupe. COUNTERWEIGHT: the claim is spent by NUDGING, not by STOPPING, so a session with nothing owed stops silently and keeps its one nudge.
properties.findings: THE WRITE NUDGE STILL TAKES PRECEDENCE and that test is not vacuous — disabling the write branch fails it. MUTATION-CHECKED SEVEN WAYS, each failing exactly the tests that name it: never count propagation (6 failures, both counterweights); drop `changes > 0` (7 failures, including BL-90's ENTIRE bypass family — the measurement that proves that clause is what stops this swallowing the older branch); drop `edits > 0` (1); drop `propagate_from` (1); drop the once-only claim (1); remove the branch entirely, i.e. ship the defect (5); and disable the write branch (14, including the precedence case). A FOURTH DEFECT WAS FOUND BY THE TESTS FAILING, not by reading: `update_state` re-serialises from an explicit key whitelist — a THIRD hand-kept copy of the state's key set beside `blank_state` and `parse_state` — so the new counter incremented in memory and was silently dropped on every write. That is BL-159's shape a third time, inside one file. THE MUTATION CHECK ONCE CAUGHT MY OWN TEST PASSING FOR FREE: the first concurrency helper looped communicate(), which blocks until each child exits, so the children ran serially and the test stayed green against the UNFIXED script.
properties.name: The nudge's counting and its own promise are both trustworthy
report.rs

properties.description: loop_status answers what is owed to ONE NAMED PERSON, and a scoped answer can never be read as the design being clean (crates/reflow2-core/tests/report.rs, 5 cases). SPLIT OUT of ver:owed-to-a-contributor rather than widening it, because that check's statement is about the COUNTER and it was passing before any of this existed — a green check that quietly grows to stand for behaviour it never exercised is the failure this project has now written down twice. THE CASES: assigned decisions are LISTED, not merely counted, carrying decision_id, name and approver_id (flo2's F4, hit independently here the same day where finding two meant jq-ing the export); scoping to one contributor returns only their assigned decisions and names them in `next`; scoping does NOT make an unassigned musing somebody's problem, so the deliberate quiet around thinking out loud survives; an unknown contributor_id is REFUSED rather than answered with an empty list, with a positive control proving the same call succeeds for a real id — because a typo would otherwise produce 'nothing is owed to you', the most reassuring possible reply and the one least likely to be questioned. THE LOAD-BEARING CASE is a_scoped_answer_never_reads_as_the_design_being_clean: a contributor with nothing assigned gets clean=true, AND scope.not_attributable is non-empty, AND `next` says in words that the rest carries no per-person attribution, AND the design-wide counters come back unchanged by scoping. That is the guard against the defect class this project has now met four times — a value that cannot tell a real NONE from an I-CANNOT-SAY. WHAT IS NOT COVERED, stated rather than left to be discovered: nothing verifies attribution for any relationship OTHER than the approver edge, because none is attributed. Claim-derived ownership and gap-to-judge attribution are unbuilt, and req:the-loop-says-what-is-owed-to-a-person names that as a real open question rather than an oversight.
properties.name: loop_status answers what is owed to one named person, and never reads as clean

properties.description: A position never becomes a verdict (crates/reflow2-core/tests/maturity.rs) — 10 cases, most of them restraint. THE LOAD-BEARING CASE IS `a_function_first_design_is_located_not_condemned`: function done, structure undeclared, and the profile must locate the design without calling it broken — it asserts the serialized profile contains none of severity / defect / violation / "should be" / "too low" / failing, and that `not_observed_about` says outright that where the design SHOULD be is not reflow2's to state. THE FRONTIER IS RELATIVE — the lowest-scoring band — so there is NO THRESHOLD anywhere in this reading to default, argue with or quietly tune, which is stronger than the stated cutoffs `granularity` needed. An empty population reads as UNMEASURED with its reason, never as zero, because scoring an absence invents a deficiency; an empty design reports as empty rather than immature. Bands scoring ABOVE the frontier are reported as NORMAL, since real designs run ahead of themselves — reflow2 itself has shipped 22 releases and 84.5% passing assurance with 0% of its 73 component couplings declared through a contract. A one-sided contract does not count as a declared seam. Assurance counts a PASSING check, not an existing one (dec:passing-is-verified). Requirements the user settled OUT leave the intent population, because dropping something is their word too.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED against five seeded regressions — frontier as the highest band, empty populations scored zero, one-sided contracts counting, assurance ignoring status, and dropped requirements still counted — all five caught. The first attempt at the one-sided mutation was a no-op and was rewritten the way the bug would actually be written before it counted as evidence.
properties.name: A position never becomes a verdict

properties.description: A repair suggestion never proposes fabricating a relationship (crates/reflow2-core/tests/no_fabricated_repairs.rs, 4 cases). THE CASE THAT WAS FILED: a disconnected cluster is reported with NO suggested_fix_type and WITH repair_is_a_judgement naming it a judgement — `generate_bridge` used to sit there, and where the separation is correct, following it fabricates relationships nobody stated to silence a warning about a separation that is right. Same for a dead-end component, and for an orphan, which used to be offered `generate_owner` — a link nobody drew. THE COUNTERWEIGHT CARRIES AS MUCH WEIGHT AS THE THREE ABOVE, and is why this is not a general refusal: honest_repairs_keep_their_suggestions pins that `break_cycle` still suggests (removing an edge that EXISTS is not invention), that `generate_decision` still suggests (writing a node recording a judgement somebody must make asserts nothing about what already relates to what), and that a finding WITH an honest operation does NOT also claim to need a judgement. If a rule against invention ever became a refusal to help, that test fails first. WHAT IS NOT COVERED: nothing here proves the three chosen findings are the only inventions in HEAL. `add_redundancy` on a single point of failure was considered and LEFT — adding a redundant path is a design change somebody makes, not an assertion about what already exists — and that judgement is recorded rather than tested.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED: restoring generate_bridge on the island fails EXACTLY the filed case and no other.
properties.name: A repair suggestion never proposes fabricating a relationship

properties.description: A process-global that is secretly per-design cannot be added without accounting for it. Owed by rule:per-design-state-is-never-a-process-global from the moment it was set enforced (Anthony, 2026-08-09). BOUND, stated rather than left to be discovered: it detects DECLARATIONS only. It says nothing about whether a struct field is correctly scoped — the per-design metadata riding on ReflowService today (graph_path, write_gen, read_hint) is not a global, and moving it per-graph is cap:graph-registry's planned work rather than a violation. A second test guards the guard — an allowlist entry naming a global that no longer exists fails, because a stale exemption pre-authorises the name for whoever adds it back.

properties.description: OWNED_BY attributes gaps to a person and never drags them into a blast radius (crates/reflow2-core/tests/report.rs, 2 tests). CASE 1, gaps_standing_on_ground_you_own_are_attributed_to_you: owning nothing attributes nothing (an unowned design is the ordinary state, not a finding); after taking ownership, the gap on that node appears in gaps_on_owned_ground naming WHICH owned node it stands on and never a node owned by someone else; scoped `clean` goes false, because a gap on your own ground is owed by you as surely as a decision you were asked to settle; and the `next` line says it in words. POSITIVE CONTROL: a second contributor who owns nothing gets an empty list from the identical call — without it, an implementation that attributed every gap to everybody would pass every other assertion. AND A CONSERVATION CHECK: the design-wide gap count is unchanged by scoping, so narrowing never makes the design look smaller. CASE 2, owning_something_does_not_drag_a_person_into_a_blast_radius: propagate_from over an owned node at depth 5 must not reach the Contributor — the exclusion AUTHORED_BY and CLAIMS already carry, asserted rather than assumed for the third of the kind. WHAT IS NOT COVERED, stated rather than left to be found: nothing verifies that ownership is the RIGHT attribution for any given node, because that is a judgement; and no check exists for unowned ground, because none was built.
properties.name: OWNED_BY attributes gaps to a person and never drags them into a blast radius

properties.description: The function-preservation check refuses what it cannot classify (crates/reflow2-core/tests/preserve.rs) — 15 cases. The suite defends the REFUSAL half, because a classifier that recognises ALLOCATED_TO and calls everything else benign hands out green certificates for changes it never looked at (BL-170's fourth quadrant). So: an unknown node type blocks certification, an unresolvable edge endpoint blocks it, a reworded capability blocks it (a rename and a scope change are the same bytes), and a known function change OUTRANKS an unknown, because more information cannot un-move a capability. `every_schema_node_type_has_a_class` walks the live schema — all 29 types — and fails the build when a new one lands with no class, so the omission is caught before a release rather than by a false green; it also asserts three known types are present, so it cannot pass by iterating an empty set. The load-bearing case is `depends_on_is_read_from_its_endpoints_not_its_type`: DEPENDS_ON is the functional DAG between Capabilities and packaging between Components, and classifying by edge type alone would file all 51 of this design's cross-system dependencies as function changes.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED against four seeded regressions (unknown types falling back to structure, the verdict order inverted, one function endpoint sufficing for a function edge, a reworded function node waved through) — each was caught, none silently.
properties.name: The function-preservation check refuses what it cannot classify

properties.description: Readiness gates an increment and the roadmap says why (crates/reflow2-core/tests/readiness.rs) — 15 cases, plus 7 driven over real stdio in smoke_mcp.py §7b2. THE WORKED EXAMPLE IS THE ROW'S OWN: laser satellite refuelling, where the demonstrator and the fielded increment demand TRL 3 and TRL 7 of the SAME converter and get two different answers — which is the whole reason the threshold rides the edge rather than either endpoint. THE TWO REFUSALS ARE WHAT IS ACTUALLY PINNED: an increment with no stated threshold reports `ungated` and NEVER ready (mutating that verdict to achievable_now fails exactly the one test the item rests on), and a gate whose technology has no level and no clearing forecast makes the whole answer `indeterminate` — skipping it instead, and computing a date from the gates that happen to carry evidence, fails FIVE. That second one is the subtler half: an optimistic date built by ignoring the inconvenient record is exactly the undefendable slide-roadmap BL-68 exists to replace. ALSO PINNED: the slowest gate decides (an increment waits for its slowest dependency) while within one gate the earliest clearing forecast wins; a measured TemporalFact is not a projection; TRL and MRL are not interchangeable on EITHER the measured or the forecast path; the highest measured level wins rather than the latest, because readiness is ratcheted evidence and picking by date would make the answer depend on how completely history was backfilled; a rung outside 1-9 is refused at both ends rather than clamped; a Capability is gated by the same machinery as a Release; and GATED_ON is a traceability edge, so a slipped technology reaches the blast radius of every increment gated on it.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED NINE WAYS, each failing exactly the tests that name it. THE MUTATION CHECK FOUND A HOLE IN THIS SUITE RATHER THAN CONFIRMING IT: dropping the ladder filter from the FORECAST path passed everything, because every existing case exercised only the MEASURED path — so an MRL projection silently clearing a TRL gate would have shipped a date built on the wrong evidence entirely. The sibling case was added and the mutation now fails it. AND THE SURFACE BUG ONLY THE REAL BINARY SHOWED: the typed Rust tests were green while the served JSON carried `Ungated` and `{"GatedUntil": ...}` — Rust's default enum tagging in an otherwise snake_case surface — caught by driving it over stdio, which is AGENTS.md's "every other layer is a client we wrote" landing on new code the same day it was written.
properties.name: Readiness gates an increment, and the roadmap says why

properties.description:
Seven cases in `crates/reflow2-core/tests/record_to_record_relations.rs`.

WHAT IT PINS, and the shape is deliberate: each case asserts on the COMPUTATION that reads the new vocabulary, not on the edge being writable. `dec:edge-orthogonality` says a distinction earns its keep only if something reads it, and a test that merely wrote an edge would prove the opposite of what is claimed.

· IMPLEMENTS — two checks, one with a script and one without, come back with different `has_executable_form`. That is the split `never_run` could not make.
· IMPLEMENTS is a MODELLED fit, not a tolerated wildcard — asserted by checking the endpoints REJECT an unrelated type, since a wildcard accepts everything. Widening it to `*` later fails here rather than silently.
· COMPLEMENTS — HEAL refuses to propose a merge for a pair declared complementary.
· ⭐ AND THE SAME PAIR WITHOUT THE EDGE IS PROPOSED FOR MERGE. This is the case that makes the guard mean something: if HEAL declined to merge two DesignRules for some unrelated reason, the guard above would pass vacuously and prove nothing. Same graph, one edge removed, opposite answer.
· superseded — a check flipped from `passing` to `superseded` stops counting as live coverage.
· SUPERSEDES accepts a Verification pair, which it refused before.
· The widening did not strand the original Fragment pair — checked rather than assumed, because narrowing an endpoint list is what makes already-written edges unimportable, and this schema records that trap on VERIFIES.
properties.findings:
7 of 7 cases pass. Full workspace suite green alongside them: 125 suites, 1312 passed, 0 failed.

⭐ TWO GUARDS CAUGHT THIS CHANGE BEFORE THE SUITE DID, and both were right. `schema::tests::all_domains_merge_and_validate` and `vocabulary::tests::vocabulary_covers_the_whole_schema` both pin the edge-type count at 61 and failed at 63. That is the mechanism working: a pinned count is what forces whoever adds an edge type to notice they moved the stamp and owe an upgrade note. Both updated to 63 with the reason recorded beside them.

🛑 AND THE REASON THEY WERE MISSED FIRST TIME IS WORTH KEEPING: `cargo test -p reflow2-core --test record_to_record_relations` passed while the LIB tests failed. Running one test target is not running the suite, and a green single-target run reads exactly like a green suite.

THE CASE THAT MAKES THE COMPLEMENTS GUARD MEAN ANYTHING is `without_the_edge_the_same_pair_is_proposed_for_merge`: the same two DesignRules, one edge removed, ARE proposed for merge. Without it the guard could pass vacuously — HEAL declining to merge for some unrelated reason would look identical to the guard working.
properties.name: Each new record-to-record edge is read by a computation, and the merge guard is proven non-inert

properties.description: Search-before-you-add fires from the TOOL and forces a choice, and the check cannot quietly stop working. SIX CASES in crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/search_first_fires_at_the_tool.rs. THE DEFECT CASE: two requirements stating one idea in different words — the second is REFUSED, and the refusal NAMES the match and BOTH routes, so it is a choice rather than a wall. THE ROLLBACK CASE is what makes the design sound: the node must be written before it can be searched (it needs to rank for its own text to give an in-query baseline), so a refusal that left it behind would create the very duplicate it refused — asserted by reading the node back and requiring null. BOTH DELIBERATE ROUTES are tested because the refusal recommends them: SHARPEN (call with the existing id — a revision, never refused, and its neighbour is seeded so the guard is the only reason it passes) and CREATE ANYWAY (`distinct_from` naming what was read and rejected). THE COUNTERWEIGHT decides whether this is usable at all: an unrelated requirement is created with no friction and no advisory — a check that refused often would be routed around, and a rule people route around is worse than no rule. CROSS-TYPE: a Capability restating a Requirement is caught, the pair most worth catching because a capability backed out of a requirement's own words is unmotivated_capability waiting to happen.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS, each verified applied before running rather than assumed: disabling the refusal fails 3 cases; removing the rollback fails the rollback case alone; ignoring `distinct_from` fails both deliberate routes. ⚠️ A FOURTH MUTATION EXPOSED A VACUOUS TEST OF MY OWN and is why the neighbour seeding exists: the first revision test passed whether or not the guard was there, because a revision with no near neighbour has nothing to report either way — the same vacuous-branch failure ver:the-server-says-when-it-is-stale was written about, reproduced here and caught by mutating rather than by reading.
properties.name: Search-before-you-add fires from the tool and forces a choice

properties.criteria: PASSING as of 2026-07-24, proven by an automated test, not by an upstream claim. Location: crates/reflow2-core/tests/search.rs, featured arm (`cargo test -p reflow2-core --features fulltext --test search`), three cases. (1) `a_natural_language_question_finds_the_requirement_it_asks_about` — two full questions phrased in a person's own words, each of which shares only some vocabulary with its target, must rank that target first against a distractor sharing common words; pins the CLASS, not the instance. (2) `one_unmatched_word_does_not_erase_a_real_match` — the minimal pin reduced to one variable: `upgrade` matches, and `upgrade zzzznotaword` must still match. (3) `a_question_the_design_does_not_answer_still_returns_nothing` — the other half of the contract, because a disjunction that matched everything would destroy the information content of 'no hits' and bring the duplicate problem back from the other direction. REGRESSION PROOF, the step that makes this more than a decoration: the pins were temporarily reverted to dynograph-foundation v0.10.0 and the suite re-run. Cases (1) and (2) FAILED against the pre-fix build with exactly the reported symptom (SearchResult { hits: [] }) and PASS against v0.11.0; case (3) passes against both, correctly, since AND semantics also refused an unrelated question. A test that passes on the broken build proves nothing, so this was verified rather than assumed. Root cause fixed upstream in dynograph-foundation v0.11.0 (PRs #76, #77): TextIndex::search now matches tokens as a ranked disjunction — at least one token required, BM25 ordering — instead of requiring every token.
properties.name: A natural-language question finds the requirement it is asking about

properties.description: skill_lint.py — the contracts the build refuses to let drift, enforced in CI on every push. (1) THE SKILLS' contract with the served surface: every tool a skill names is served, the three mirrors are byte-identical, frontmatter, the standing rule, the tool-convention register and its description budget, the detect-and-ask obligations. (2) THE BUILD'S OWN GATE LIST (BL-159, 2026-08-01), four checks over AGENTS.md's "A change is done when all of these are clean" block and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — two hand-kept records of one contract, where following the documented one exactly still produced a red build (PR #27). COVERAGE: every cargo/python3 gate ci.yml runs is either in the block or named in the blockquote as deliberately omitted, because a gate in neither is one a developer cannot know to run. FIDELITY: a listed gate is spelled exactly as CI runs it, FLAGS INCLUDED — and this is the load-bearing one the row did not ask for, because the defect that filed BL-159 was a flags difference on a gate that WAS listed (`-p reflow2-core` clippy lacking `-D warnings`), which coverage alone cannot see. Both rot directions are closed too: a documented gate ci.yml does not run, and an omitted name ci.yml has stopped running. THE SPLIT THAT KEEPS IT HONEST: the lint OBSERVES (is this line a gate at all — mechanical) and the document JUDGES (does it belong in the everyday subset — in AGENTS.md, where a human reads it). 14 hermetic cases there covering the parsing the real files cannot exercise.
properties.findings: FOUND ON DAY ONE: `cargo test -p reflow2-core --no-default-features` and `test_check_doc_versions` sat in ci.yml and in neither list — the second being the exact trap the design anticipated, since `check_doc_versions` is a SUBSTRING of it and a substring match would have called it covered. MUTATION-CHECKED SEVEN WAYS, each failing exactly the check that names it: an undeclared gate in ci.yml → coverage; stripping `-D warnings` from the block → fidelity, which is BL-159's own defect reproduced; ci.yml dropping a listed gate → the phantom check; ci.yml dropping an omitted one → the stale-omission check; dropping the comment stripper → fidelity plus its own hermetic case; dropping the paragraph scoping → its two hermetic cases; dropping scoping AND the runner-word exclusion → the stale-omission check. THE CHECK CAUGHT A DEFECT IN ITSELF ON ITS OWN COMMIT: scanning the whole blockquote read the backticked words `cargo` and `python3` out of the new paragraph describing the lint and reported them as gates CI had stopped running. AND ONE REDUNDANCY IS REPORTED RATHER THAN HIDDEN — reverting the paragraph scoping ALONE leaves every real-file check green, because the runner-word exclusion covers the only two words today's prose backticks; the two are not redundant in general, so the scoping is pinned on synthetic text in tools/test_skill_lint.py where the redundancy cannot hide it.
properties.name: The contracts the build refuses to let drift

properties.description: A session that did design work, moved files, and never opened a skill is told so before it ends — and the correct sessions around it are not (tools/test_loop_nudge.py, class SkillLoadsAreCounted, 9 cases). MOST OF THE CASES ARE COUNTERWEIGHTS, because this branch ARMS a nudge where cap:skill-triggers only ever refined one: loading a single skill silences it; listing skills does NOT count as loading one (knowing the menu is not reading the recipe, and counting it would let a session tick the box); a session below the edit floor is left alone; a session that never touched reflow2 gets the blunter bypass message and NOT this one; and where another branch already fired, exactly one message is printed. Plus the two invariants every blocking branch here owes: it fires once per session, and a tally rebuilt after an unreadable one never makes the negative claim, because the get_skill calls that would refute it are exactly what was lost. THE LINE dec:adoption-is-reported-the-loop-still-computes DRAWS IS HELD AS A PROPERTY: the hook leaves the designed project byte-identical (no export, no store, no stray file), and a grep with a positive control asserts no skill counter is readable by anything in reflow2-core that computes debt.
properties.findings: FOUND BY RUNNING IT: the first implementation incremented both new counters in memory and threw them away on every write, because the state key set is duplicated in three places and only two were updated — the same defect BL-163 hit, in the same file, under a comment that warns about it by name.
properties.name: A session that did design work and never opened a skill is told so

properties.description: Shape-matching fires on the situation and stays silent otherwise: a file edit with no ChangeEvent names impact-check; a change recorded but never propagated ALSO names impact-check (BL-163); a recorded change with no artifact link names link-artifacts; a capture batch with no gap pass names detect-and-ask; a rendering with nothing stored names session-artifacts. AND THE COUNTERWEIGHT, which is the case that matters most: a session that did the right thing gets NOTHING — a trigger that fires on correct work is the failure BL-23 and BL-42 both name, and this capability exists to reduce nagging rather than add it. BL-163 CHANGED WHAT "THE RIGHT THING" MEANS, and the counterweight fixture with it: the sequence edit → record_change → link_artifact → add_requirement → detect_gaps used to pass this test, and now correctly fires, because it never once asked what the change reached. The assertion is untouched — correct work is still met with silence — and the old fixture is pinned by its own test as the defect. THE SHAPES STILL CANNOT ARM THE HOOK (`test_shapes_never_arm_the_hook_by_themselves` passes unchanged); the one branch that arms is BL-163's and lives outside the matcher, because the session it catches has no unchecked writes and has touched reflow2, so no nudge existed for a shape to refine.

properties.description:
`python3 tools/test_loop_nudge.py` — the `AsksTheGraph` case set (~20 cases inside the file's 79).

THE CASE THIS EXISTS FOR is `test_a_level_never_fires`. Every other case in the set would pass on an implementation that nudged whenever the design carried debt — and that implementation would speak in every session forever, which is the fire-on-correct-work failure `ver:skill-triggers` names and the one BL-23 and BL-42 both name. The delta is the feature; the counts are only how it is computed. reflow2's own design has carried 7 unsurfaced gaps and 60 structural defects for weeks, so a level-keyed nudge is not a hypothetical.

WHAT ELSE IS PINNED, each because getting it wrong is silent rather than loud:
  • No baseline, one reading, a fallen count, a class missing from one side, an unreadable file, no probe at all — every one is silence, not a guess.
  • `structural_defects` is NOT a trigger class. HEAL's count moves on edits nobody made to it, so a delta there would report a session for something it did not do.
  • Every class the probe MEASURES has a sentence the nudge can SAY, asserted as a set equality across two processes that share no module.
  • It never adds a second interruption: `claim_nudge` is one flag for the whole session, so a session already being nudged is not nudged twice.
  • THE HOOK RETURNS IMMEDIATELY. Asserted in wall-clock against a real spawn at a closed port. `loop_status` is 22.6s; if this ever blocks on the probe, the feature has become the thing the async shape was chosen to avoid.
  • A failed probe does not erase the last good reading, and a carried reading keeps its OWN age.
  • The RELEASE WORKFLOW stages `graph_probe.py`. `spawn_probe` is silent when the script is not beside it — correct for an older kit, and indistinguishable from a graph with nothing to say — so a sibling added here and not to the kit would ship a hook whose graph branch never runs and never says why.
properties.findings:
`python3 tools/test_loop_nudge.py` — 80 tests, 0 failures, ~21s, run unpiped with the exit code captured on its own line (`| tail` reports tail's status, and this repo has been burned by that three times).

Beyond the suite, the branch was exercised END TO END against the live shared server, on this session's own real numbers rather than fixtures: a baseline of 7 unsurfaced gaps measured before any design write, `graph_probe.py` run for real (23.3s, stateless MCP over `.reflow2/graph.server.json`), and the hook then emitting

    reflow2: this session ADDED design debt and left it — the graph itself says
    so — measured by loop_status against the live graph 23s ago, not counted
    from your tool calls: open gap(s) nobody has put to the user 7 → 10 (+3) —
    run detect-and-ask.

The three gaps were the ones this session genuinely created. It found its own author.

⭐ AND THEN THE SAME RUN FOUND THE FEATURE'S REAL LIMIT, which no fixture would have. Those three gaps did not survive: wiring SATISFIES / ALLOCATED_TO / VERIFIES closed them, and a CONSUMES edge closed a fourth that had been standing, so the session ENDED at 6 — below where it started. A verdict collected from a mid-session reading can therefore name debt already settled. Not fixable by waiting (that is the 23-second block the design exists to avoid), so the message states the reading's AGE and directs the agent to confirm with `loop_status`. Pinned by `test_it_tells_the_agent_to_confirm_because_the_reading_can_be_stale`.

ONE ASSERTION WAS WRONG ON THE FIRST RUN and the correction is worth keeping: `test_it_never_adds_a_second_nudge_to_an_interrupted_session` asserted that the counting nudge's text does NOT contain "detect-and-ask" — but the generic write nudge already names that skill, so the assertion was testing the other branch's wording rather than which branch spoke. Re-keyed on the graph branch's own words ("not counted from your tool calls"). A test that fails for a reason other than the one it is named for is not evidence.
properties.name: The graph nudge fires on a DELTA and never on a level
Schema validation and graph-store round-trip suite (cargo test --no-default-features: schema, nodes, graph, storage tests)

A supporting CONTRADICTS edge produces no contradiction; an opposing one still does; and one with no alignment still does, so no design written before the fix changes behaviour (crates/reflow2-core/tests/contradiction_alignment.rs, 3 cases). MUTATION-CHECKED: removing the alignment check fails exactly the supporting case and leaves the two counterweights green — which is what proves the fix did not simply silence the detector.
llm.rs

properties.description: 6 cases, crates/reflow2-core/tests/change_axis_unstated.rs. THE LOAD-BEARING ONE IS ZERO USAGE: a design with changes and no axis on any of them must be asked, which is precisely what a consistency-shaped check cannot see — decomposition_coverage keys on a Requirement already carrying a DECOMPOSES edge, so a project that never decomposed reads clean with all three legs apparently present. Also pinned: the complement (a fully stated design is not asked, so the detector cannot pass by always firing), silence on a design with no changes at all, the partial case reporting only the unstated ones, and the DENOMINATOR appearing in the title, because a numerator alone cannot distinguish a drifting design from one that just started. THE AGGREGATE PROPERTY HAS ITS OWN CASE: the gap id must survive the population growing, or the user's standing acknowledgement is undone by the next change anybody records — the trap unvalidated_capability fell into and was re-acknowledged about twenty times for, and sharper here because ChangeEvents are the fastest-growing node type in any active design. The sixth case pins that a blank axis cannot be written at all (the schema enum refuses it on every path including import_graph), which is what licenses the detector to be a plain presence check rather than carrying an emptiness guard that could never fire.
properties.findings: 6 of 6 passing. Also exercised against this design's live graph rather than only fixtures: it produced ONE gap reading "468 of 594 recorded change(s) do not say what kind of change they were", at severity 0.30. That run is the evidence against the reason this detector was nearly not built — 468 unstated events yield one question, not 468, because the aggregate keying already existed.
properties.name: change_axis_unstated fires at zero usage, aggregates, and stays silent once answered

properties.description: The conduct rule is pinned where an edit that drops it turns red: both capture-intent and genesis must forbid asking the user which node type to use AND name describe_schema as the alternative (forbidding a question without naming the alternative is half a rule), and capture-intent must carry the routing table as a lookup table that names where it runs out. 2 cases in crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/served_skills.rs, 8 in the file, all passing. THE POINT OF PINNING IT HERE: this is a rule about how an agent behaves in conversation, and conversation leaves no node — loop_status reads perfectly clean through a session that breaks it, so a test on the served text is the only place it can be observed at all.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED: replacing "Never ask the user which node type" with its opposite across all three skill trees turned exactly the conduct test red and left the routing-table test green; reverting restored both.
properties.name: The capture skills never ask the user which node type to use

properties.description:
Runs tools/wall_check.py, which builds the module import graph from crates/*/src/**.rs with comments and string literals stripped, lifts those edges to the declared subsystems through each Component's CONTAINS placement, and runs Tarjan over the induced subsystem graph.

PASSES when that graph has no cycle: every declared wall is crossed one way only, so a change can be handed to a boundary and stop there.

WHY THE CHECK IS NEEDED AT ALL, and this is the part worth keeping: reflow2's own circular-dependency detector cannot answer this and is not broken. It reasons over DEPENDS_ON edges in the design, and the subsystem layer held exactly two coupling edges, both CONSUMES to an external interface. Zero subsystem-to-subsystem edges means the detector has nothing to run on, and its green reads as 'your subsystems are acyclic' while meaning 'your subsystems have no modelled coupling'. This check reads the SOURCE instead, so it cannot be fooled by an unmodelled edge.

STATED LIMIT: an import graph is coupling, not a contract. This says a boundary is severable in principle; it does not say the dependency across it is contracted, which maturity_report reports separately and which stood at 0 of 73 when this check was written.
properties.findings:
RUN 2026-08-20 on the compare-stops-reaching-into-report branch, after both changes of epoch:the-declared-walls-hold: "NO SUBSYSTEM CYCLES — every declared wall is crossed one way only." 9 subsystems, 43 components placed, 25 code edges inside a subsystem and 72 crossing one, all one-directional.

THE TRAIL, because the number moved twice and both moves were earned:
  before either change   2 cycles — sys:store <-> sys:vocabulary, sys:coherence-loop <-> sys:time-history
  after change 1 (#264)  1 cycle  — the kernel was reunited as sys:foundation, no Rust touched
  after change 2         0 cycles — the design-type list moved down to `nodes`, one import removed

WHAT THIS RUN DOES NOT SAY: 10 Components still report no coupling in the design while their same-named module is coupled in the source (cmp:dto at code degree 11 the worst), and 0 of 73 dependency pairs are mediated by a contract. A boundary being severable in principle is not the same as the dependency across it being declared, and neither of those numbers moved.
properties.name: Every declared subsystem boundary is crossed in one direction only

properties.description: The LINEAGE clause of tools/reflow2_check.py, run in CI on every pull request: the committed export must record `prev_content_hash` equal to the content hash of the export it replaced, and a severed chain FAILS the build. Deliberately narrower than `ver:gate-suite`, which verifies `art:check` as one artifact — the gate makes several distinct guarantees (drift, orphan attachment, dependency reconcile, lineage) and one Verification standing for all of them cannot say which clause is still working. This one stands for the lineage clause and nothing else, so `rule:the-export-is-written-once-per-branch` has a check that is ABOUT IT. WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, stated so the green is not read wider than it is: it checks the CHAIN, not whether the export is CURRENT with the live graph (that is the drift clause), and it cannot see a second export that was never committed. It also cannot distinguish a deliberate re-baseline from an accident — the message names three causes and asks the reader to pick, which is a refusal to guess rather than a hole.
properties.findings: FIELD-EVIDENCED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: it fired twice on 2026-08-11 in one day's work — once on a double export across a `commit --amend`, chaining through a content hash no commit would ever hold, and once after a rebase where the three-way merge driver had merged CONTENT correctly and could not repair the chain. Both were real, both were caught before merge, and both are recorded in the rule's own how-to-follow-it text.
properties.name: The committed export records the hash of the export it replaced

properties.description: A committed export survives export → import → re-export (tools/test_reflow2_check.py) — 5 cases. END TO END through the real binary: a coherent design round-trips clean and gates 0. THREE DETECTION CASES against a stub re-export, because driving these through the real binary could only ever produce a FAITHFUL round trip — which is the case that must NOT fire: a dropped node is caught AND NAMED, a dropped EDGE is caught and named (the dev_storyflow case was two VERIFIES edges, so a check watching only nodes would have missed it), and a property that comes back different is caught (import is an upsert and the schema has defaults, so a document can return COMPLETE and still not be the same design — the half a count cannot see). THE COUNTERWEIGHT IS THE FOURTH: a faithful round trip reports NOTHING, because a check that fires on a correct design runs on every commit and would be switched off inside a day.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED TWICE, each killing exactly what it should: forcing the comparison to always agree fails the three detection cases and leaves the counterweight passing, which is what proves the counterweight carries weight; ignoring edges fails exactly the edge case and nothing else. PROVEN ON THE REAL DESIGN: run against reflow2's own 2,308-node export through the built binary, the round trip is clean and the gate's only finding was the checksum of the file this change edited.
properties.name: A committed export survives export, import and re-export

properties.description: crates/reflow2-core/tests/reply_budget.rs (10 cases) plus three checks in tools/smoke_mcp.py driving the built binary over real stdio, and one regression case in tools/test_reflow2_check.py. What it pins: an answer that fits comes back whole with no note; an answer that does not drops the cheapest information first (affected_ids capped, then the prose from EVERY row, never from some); `count` and `by_source` cover every open gap in every tier; the last resort — where a gap is genuinely absent from the list — says how many and keeps the highest-severity ones; a budget smaller than the empty reply does not underflow; a compacted row deserializes as a GapCandidate and asks the SAME question as the full one, because gap_to_prompt fills it back in from the graph; and a scoped answer is budgeted too, with different advice, because telling a reader who scoped to scope is advice they cannot follow. THE GATE CASE IS THE ONE THAT NEARLY GOT AWAY: reflow2_check.py judged a gap anchored by affected_ids, so a budgeted reply would have turned the build GREEN on 100 open critical gaps. Verified live by reverting the fix and watching the test fail.
properties.findings: 10 core cases, 3 smoke checks over real stdio, 1 gate regression case — all passing. MEASURED EFFECT on this design (77 open gaps, 2,920 nodes): the unscoped reply fell from 157,785 bytes on the wire to 53,181, a 66% cut, and `count` stayed 77. TWO DEFECTS CAUGHT BY THE TESTS RATHER THAN BY REVIEW. (1) reflow2_check.py judged a gap ANCHORED by `affected_ids` being non-empty; against a budgeted reply it printed 'OK — design and build agree (103 notes)' on 100 open critical gaps. Proven live by reverting the fix. (2) A budget of 0 reached the last-resort truncation with an empty list and underflowed `len() - lo`; `[]` still costs 2 characters, so the guard cannot be inferred from 'nothing to drop'. Also proven live by removing the guard and watching it panic. Both tests were checked for being INERT before being believed.
properties.name: detect_gaps answers within a budget, and a shorter answer is never a quieter one

A moved record reaches an ORDINARY read and names import_graph, an untouched one stays silent, and the installer writes both halves of the merge rule while leaving a driver somebody else set alone (crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/the_record_moved_and_the_session_is_told.rs + tools/test_init.py, both CI gates)

properties.description:
Two suites, one capability.

`cargo test -p reflow2-core --test nothing_asks_what_a_session_made_false` — 10 cases on the computation.
`python3 tools/test_loop_nudge.py` — the `AsksWhatWasMadeFalse` case set inside the file's 91.

THE CASE THE HOOK HALF IS JUDGED ON is `test_it_never_arms_a_nudge_by_itself`. Anthony chose ask-don't-block deliberately, and every other assertion in that set would pass on an implementation that blocked. That one would not.

WHAT THE COMPUTATION PINS, each because getting it wrong is silent rather than loud:
  • A closed observation, an already-claimed one, a Verification, and an unanchored one are each excluded — separately, so a single over-broad filter cannot pass by accident.
  • `a_check_is_never_raised_as_a_candidate` is what keeps this from reversing `dec:verification-freshness-not-a-gap`.
  • `work_that_touched_nothing_anchored_says_so_rather_than_saying_nothing` — `subjects_examined: 0` distinguishes "nothing to check" from "checked, all clear". A short list and a blind one look identical without it.
  • `an_event_id_that_names_nothing_is_reported_not_skipped` — a typo would otherwise return an empty shortlist, the most reassuring answer available.
  • `it_reaches_an_observation_anchored_the_other_way_round` — both `HAS_TEMPORAL_FACT` and `ABOUT_ENTITY` are in live use, and reading one would halve coverage while looking like it worked.
  • `it_is_a_candidate_and_never_a_verdict` — asking closes nothing.

WHAT THE DELIVERY HALF PINS: the ride-along preserves the host message; an empty shortlist adds nothing; a long one names three and COUNTS the rest; ChangeEvent ids are captured from the call's own input, deduplicated, and bounded at 25; and an ask the last session never heard surfaces once at the next SessionStart.

BEYOND THE SUITES — exercised end to end on real data through the built binary over stdio, against the whole committed export (3,096 nodes / 13,231 edges) rather than a fixture, because the bug this family exists to prevent only appears at scale.
properties.findings:
`cargo test -p reflow2-core --test nothing_asks_what_a_session_made_false` — **10 passed, 0 failed**, 0.07s.
`python3 tools/test_loop_nudge.py` — **91 passed, 0 failed** (was 80), ~25s.
Both run unpiped with the exit code captured on its own line.

⭐ EXERCISED END TO END ON REAL DATA, through the built binary over stdio against the whole committed export (3,096 nodes / 13,231 edges) rather than a fixture — because the class of bug this family exists to prevent only appears at scale, and a rollup that walks the graph has shipped past ten green tests on twelve-node fixtures before on this project. Results: `chg:stop-hook-asks-the-graph` → 1 candidate from 7 subjects; `chg:the-repair-capability-gets-its-thread` → 6 from 2; `chg:bl89` → 40 from 8; a typo'd id → `unknown_events` named and `count: 0`. Warm calls 0.03–0.04s.

🛑 AND THAT RUN IS WHAT CAUGHT THE MEASUREMENT ERROR, which no unit test would have. The counts came back far higher than the design note predicted, because the note's "78% silent, median 1" was measured against an EDGE-ONLY reader covering 56% of observations, while the shipped computation reads `subject_id` too and covers 97%. Re-measured against the real implementation: **71% silent, median 1, mean 4.3, p90 13, max 40.** The conclusion survived; the number did not. Every doc comment, the tool description, the skill and the test's own header were corrected to the honest figures.

⚠️ NOT COVERED BY EITHER SUITE, and stated rather than implied: nobody has yet watched a session be shown a shortlist and act on it. Both suites prove the computation and the plumbing; whether the shortlist is USEFUL is a field question, and the ask-don't-block choice exists precisely so that question can be answered before the trigger is allowed to interrupt anyone.
properties.name: The ask surfaces what was touched, judges nothing, and never blocks

properties.description:
Thirteen checks in two places. Six unit tests in `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/handshake.rs` pin the logic: the negotiation rule mirrored from rmcp, the revision threshold (`2024-11-05` and `2025-03-26` report as NOT having `structuredContent`; `2025-06-18` and later do, `>=` not `==`), the sidecar path beside its siblings, a file round trip, and that an unwritable path is survived rather than propagated — a diagnostic must never be able to fail a handshake.

Seven checks in `tools/smoke_mcp.py` drive the REAL BINARY over stdio, which is the only layer that proves the file is actually written during `initialize`: the sidecar exists, names the client, records what it asked for and what was settled, and — the one that matters — that **the negotiated version came from the exchange rather than from nowhere**, asserted as `negotiated ∈ {client_requested, server_offers}`.

⭐ ONE CHECK EXISTS FOR A REASON THAT IS NOT ABOUT CODE. `it disclaims the reading it would otherwise invite` asserts the file's own `note` contains the sentence saying `protocol_has_structured_content` does NOT mean the client reads it. The file is meant to be pasted into a field report and read by somebody who has never seen this module, so its self-description has to hold up alone. Naming that field `supports_structured_content` would have asserted the one thing it cannot know.

VERIFIED LIVE, not only by tests: the server was restarted against this session's real client and wrote `client-name: claude-code, version 2.1.241, requested and negotiated 2025-11-25, protocol_has_structured_content: true`. That is also the first data point for the comparison the file exists to enable.
properties.findings:
GREEN, read from cargo's OWN exit code: `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` exit 0, 165 suites, 1862 passed, 0 failed. `smoke_mcp.py` exit 0 with all seven handshake checks passing against the real binary over stdio.

🛑 THE FIRST RUN WAS RED AND THE NOTIFICATION SAID OTHERWISE. The background task reported "exit code 0" — that was the shell wrapper; cargo's own code was 101 and one test had failed. Believing the wrapper would have shipped over a red suite. Same family as the piped-gate trap, in a new costume: read the exit code of the thing you ran, not of what ran it.

WHAT FAILED, and it was a real ordering mistake rather than a defect: `a_served_skill_is_byte_identical_to_its_source` compares the skill COMPILED INTO THE BINARY against the source on disk. `report-friction/SKILL.md` was edited after the last build, so the two diverged and the test caught exactly what it exists for. Rebuilt; that suite is 8/8 and the workspace is green. **A served-skill edit needs a rebuild before the suite means anything** — the sibling of "format before baselining".

VERIFIED LIVE as well as by tests: the shared server was restarted against this session's real client and wrote `claude-code 2.1.241, requested and negotiated 2025-11-25, protocol_has_structured_content: true`. That is the comparison point the file exists to produce — a client that negotiates a modern revision AND reads structuredContent, against which Alex's report can be read.
properties.name: The handshake sidecar is written, and does not overclaim

properties.description: Three of four harnesses were made to LOAD reflow2 from the file the installer writes — OpenCode reports it CONNECTED, Copilot CLI lists it as a workspace server, Claude Code is daily use. VS Code remains unconfirmed and is named as such. THIS IS THE CHECK THE 96-CASE SUITE CANNOT MAKE: those cases assert which FILES are written, and assert nothing about whether any harness reads them.
properties.findings: Run 2026-08-14 on Ubuntu 24 by installing the harnesses (npm, no sudo) into a project set up by tools/reflow2_init.py, then asking each tool what it sees: `opencode mcp list` -> "✓ reflow2 connected", `copilot mcp list` -> "Workspace servers: reflow2 (local)". It also CORRECTED the registry rather than confirming it — `copilot mcp --help` names its sources as ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json and workspace .mcp.json / .github/mcp.json, so Copilot CLI does NOT read .vscode/mcp.json and the entry labelled "Copilot / VS Code" was promising a harness that file does not serve.
properties.name: Three of four harnesses were made to load reflow2 from the file the installer writes

properties.description: `docker/smoke.sh`, run by release.yml against the candidate image BEFORE the push. Starts the container on a uid-1000 volume, refuses immediately if the process exited (the failure this exists for is an instant exit, and waiting on a health probe would report it as a timeout instead of naming the cause), then waits on the image's OWN HEALTHCHECK, then makes one request from OUTSIDE the container — because an in-container probe cannot catch a bind to loopback. DEMONSTRATED 2026-08-15 both ways on a locally built image: PASSES in ~8s on the fixed Dockerfile, and FAILS in ~3s on a Dockerfile with the pre-v0.27.0 `--content-path` restored, printing `error: unexpected argument '--content-path' found` and exit 2. SCOPE, stated so this is not read as more than it is: it has not yet run in CI, and it proves the image SERVES, not that any tool behaves correctly.
properties.name: The published image starts, reports healthy, and answers on its port

properties.description: The loop can be asked what the record does not yet hold, and says so when it cannot tell (crates/reflow2-core/tests/debt_since_the_record.rs) — 5 cases, all passing 2026-08-16. THE BASELINE IS THE LAST EXPORT, which is the only session boundary the graph can compute without a clock or a session identity: `debt_since(&baseline)` diffs the live node ids against the ids the committed export holds, and reports the difference plus only those gaps and defects whose `affected_ids` intersect it. THE CASES, by their real names: `a_node_the_record_lacks_is_reported_as_new`; `a_fully_recorded_design_reports_no_new_ground`; `debt_on_recorded_ground_is_not_called_new` — a gap standing entirely on old ground is NOT reported as this session's, which is the whole point; `an_empty_baseline_says_it_cannot_tell`, the difference between "you added 205 things" and "I have no record to compare against", which are opposite answers and would otherwise be the same one; and `the_note_always_states_the_baseline_and_that_it_moves`, which pins that the reply never leaves the reader to guess WHICH boundary was used — a scoped number whose scope is implicit is a worse number than none. COST WAS A DECIDED HALF, NOT AN OVERSIGHT: `since_export` is `#[serde(default)]` so the extra diff runs only when scoping is asked for and every existing caller is byte-identical; a failure to read the sync state inserts `since_export_unavailable` rather than failing the call, because a loop that refuses to answer is worse than one that answers narrowly. NOT COVERED: nothing here tests the boundary against a REAL multi-session history — every case builds its baseline in-test, so the claim is about the computation and not about what a week of real use would put in front of it.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED, each killing exactly one test: ignoring the baseline entirely fails `a_fully_recorded_design_reports_no_new_ground`, and removing the empty-baseline branch fails `an_empty_baseline_says_it_cannot_tell`. VERIFIED END-TO-END over stdio on a scratch graph: `unexported_nodes: 1`, `sample: ["req:new"]`, and the unscoped call omits the block entirely. TRIPLE-CORROBORATED IN ORIGIN — Alex twice (§3.3 on 0.24.0 and his 2026-08-14 Opportunities), dev_storyflow independently, and reproduced first-hand across a whole session on 2026-08-16 where loop_status reported the identical 80 gaps and 16 defects from the first call to the last.
properties.name: The loop can be asked what the record does not yet hold

properties.description: The two absences are told apart, and neither is invented: an OpenCode project reports no_hook_for_this_harness with an advisory that asks for nothing to be installed; a Claude project with no hook still reports absent; a project that never named a harness reports absent rather than impossible; and a hook the user wired themselves wins over the recorded harness, so a working nudge is never called unreachable. 7 cases in crates/reflow2-mcp/src/nudge.rs (19 in the module, 190 in the crate, all passing).
properties.findings: ALSO DEMONSTRATED LIVE against real projects with the rebuilt binary — loop_status returned {"no_hook_for_this_harness":{"harnesses":"opencode"}} for an OpenCode project and "absent" for one that never said. THAT LIVE RUN EARNED ITS KEEP: the unit tests passed while target/debug/reflow2-mcp was still the previous build, so `cargo test --lib` was proving the library and not the binary a user runs — rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object, caught on the day it was enforced.
properties.name: The two kinds of absent nudge are told apart, and neither is invented

properties.description: A record that moved ahead of this seat is reported, and one that has not is silent. COVERS: the three consumption-free states (in_step / moved_but_current / behind) and the two fault states (missing / unreadable); that ordinary unexported work is NEVER reported, which is the property the whole design rests on; that two targets are independent and neither hides the other; that every known target is listed so an empty answer cannot read as all-clear; that the finding names both `import_graph` and the path and never reads as a refusal (no "refused"/"error"/"cannot"/"blocked"); that the expensive export is NOT built on the in-step path and is built exactly once when needed; and THE REGRESSION THAT MATTERS MOST — a record edited without restamping is still caught, because the check computes the content hash instead of believing the one the document states about itself. NOT COVERED: the live MCP surface end-to-end (the served tool was exercised against a scratch graph via the CLI, not against a running server), and any behaviour of `import_graph` itself.
properties.findings: That last case was found end-to-end rather than by any unit test, after the first cut shipped believing the stamp and reported "in step" while somebody else's work sat in the file.
properties.name: A record that moved ahead of this seat is reported, and one that has not is silent

properties.description:
`flow_report(flow:release-cut)`, read back after the Flow was written.

WHAT IT CHECKS: that the RECORD is complete and legible to the next session. Eight steps come back in stated order 1–8; nine TRIGGERS transitions come back, every one carrying a `role`; `confessions` is empty, meaning `flow_report` found nothing left unstated — no unmatched entry or exit point, no step without a `step_order`, no transition without a role. The two backward edges are reported as a cycle, which is correct and is why cycles in a Flow are reported rather than judged: a process's loops are its design.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CHECK, said plainly rather than left to be assumed: that a human or agent actually FOLLOWS the procedure. Nothing here observes a cut. The step that closes that hole is step 8's own detector (`ver:a-release-that-shipped-nothing-is-reported`), which turns the gate red when a release goes out with an empty manifest whether or not anyone read the Flow.

WHY IT IS AN INSPECTION AND NOT A TEST: the subject is a design record, not code. Calling it a test would claim an automated check that does not exist, and `dec:certainty-derived` makes a status a claim about evidence.
properties.findings:
2026-08-21, first run, immediately after the Flow was written: 8 steps returned in order 1–8, 9 transitions returned, every one carrying a `role`, and `confessions: []` — flow_report found nothing left unstated. One cycle reported, over all 8 members, which is the two deliberate "forces resync" edges: step 8 → step 4 (an empty release_report sends the cut back to re-run the derivation with apply: true) and step 4 → step 1 (a manifest frozen on a pre-bump checksum sends it back to accept the version drift first).

CONTEXT WORTH RECORDING: this is the FIRST Flow node in reflow2's own design. The count was zero before today — `cap:model-process` shipped, was never used on this project, and so the vocabulary had never been tested against a real process by its own authors. It held: nothing about the release cut needed a node type that did not exist, and the one thing worth saying that the model does not carry — which steps are destructive of the session's own tooling — went into the Flow description rather than into a new property.
properties.name: flow_report returns the cut as eight ordered steps with every transition's role stated

properties.findings:
PASSING 2026-08-28. `cargo test -p reflow2-mcp --test served_skills` — 11 passed, 0 failed.

⭐ IT WAS OBSERVED FAILING FIRST, which is the step the governing rule names as most-often-skipped and invisible when it is. The failure was real rather than staged: after the skill was revised to generate candidates from the design, this test failed with "the skill must require more than one candidate cause" — the edit had moved the word THREE into a sentence. The requirement was intact and the assertion was matching formatting, so the ASSERTION was corrected rather than the skill, and the reason was written into the test.

skill_lint also passes on this skill: frontmatter name matches its directory, a description exists, it states the graph-text-is-data rule, and every tool it references exists on the served surface.
properties.name: The root-cause skill keeps the clauses that make it force steps rather than describe them

properties.description: crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/the_same_paragraph_fifty_times.rs, 5 cases. Because nothing is withheld here, what has to hold is that the saving cannot make a reader WRONG: every finding still resolves by `row.repair_is_a_judgement ?? map[row.category]`; a row whose text differs from its category's keeps its own, so the fallback is never merely probably right; the lift fires on BOTH list shapes (`defects` unscoped, `items` scoped); and it does not fire on a category with one row, where a map entry plus the sentence explaining it costs more than the paragraph inline. THE SHAPE CASE IS PINNED DIRECTLY RATHER THAN THROUGH A FIXTURE, and that is the finding: the first version of it passed against the bug it was written for, because the categories carrying a repair note are the ones whose findings are disconnected by definition, so its scoped region held none and the assertion loop never executed.
properties.findings: 5 cases passing, alongside `cargo test --workspace` (50 suites, 0 failures), fmt, mcp clippy, skill_lint, smoke_mcp and all 155 toolsnaps. MEASURED: detect_defects 46,314 → 26,169 bytes on the wire, all 50 findings present, every one resolving to its explanation; scoped proj:reflow2 at depth 3 also lifts (10,243 bytes, 18 rows, none left inline). PROVEN NON-INERT TWICE, and the second time is the finding: with lifting removed entirely one case fails; with the SCOPED-BLIND bug restored (looking only for `defects`, so `Scoped<T>`'s `items` is untouched) the shape case fails. IT DID NOT, IN ITS FIRST FORM. That version drove a real fixture whose scoped region contained no note-bearing findings, so its assertion loop never executed and it stayed green against the exact bug it was written for. Rewritten to pin both list shapes directly.
properties.name: detect_defects sends each repair explanation once, and every finding still resolves to its own

properties.description:
CONFORMANCE OF AN IMPLEMENTATION AGAINST A PUBLISHED CONTRACT, which is what a check on an Interface asserts and what a check on a Capability does not. `ifc:mcp-tools` promises that `tools/list` returns every served tool with its JSON Schema, and that the field-level contract "travels with the surface and cannot drift from the build". This is the check that the promise is still kept: one committed golden per tool in `tools/toolsnaps/`, holding the WHOLE served object — name, description, inputSchema, annotations — compared against the live binary driven over real stdio. 155 goldens as of 2026-08-22. A real surface change becomes a deliberate `--update` that shows up in the diff, named tool by tool.

IT DRIVES THE BUILT BINARY OVER REAL STDIO rather than an in-process client, on AGENTS.md's rule that every other layer is a client we wrote and only the shipped wire format is trustworthy. That is also why it verifies THIS boundary: the stdio transport is the one it actually speaks.

═══ WHY IT EXISTS: a bug FAMILY, not a worry ═══
Three defects where the surface an agent binds to changed and nothing noticed — a parameter lost its type (BL-28), a stale binary served an old shape (BL-32), prose moved into the wrong envelope (BL-48). The gate turned that family into a mechanical tripwire.

═══ WHAT THIS GREEN DOES NOT COVER, so it is not read wider than it is ═══
· NOT THE HTTP BOUNDARY. It speaks stdio, so it says nothing about `ifc:mcp-tools-http` — which remains unchecked, and is the half flo2's `ifc:reflow2-design-api` actually pairs with.
· NOT THE ERROR MODEL. `ifc:mcp-tools` specifies TWO layers a consumer must handle — JSON-RPC transport `error`, and tool-level failure as a normal result carrying `isError: true` — and a golden of the `tools/list` payload cannot see either. The most expensive defect this project has had (v0.38.0 shipping an empty manifest) was precisely a caller reading a reply's shape and not its content, and this check would not have caught it.
· NOT WHETHER THE SCHEMA IS RIGHT — only that it has not moved. A wrong shape frozen on day one stays green forever.

═══ THE GATE'S OWN DEFECT, found and fixed 2026-08-16 ═══
It defaulted `--bin` to `target/debug/reflow2-mcp` and reported "ALL 149 TOOLSNAPS MATCH" against whatever stale build was sitting there — a check that could not fail reporting a pass, the shape this project keeps finding. CI was never exposed (ci.yml builds debug in the same job first), so it was a local-developer defect and specifically bit whoever followed the RELEASE PROCEDURE, which builds release and leaves debug behind. Fixed by `chg:the-surface-gate-says-which-binary-it-read`: every verdict now NAMES the binary and its build time and warns when any source is newer. The default must stay debug, because CI builds debug.
properties.findings:
ALL 155 TOOLSNAPS MATCH — the served surface is unchanged. Run 2026-08-22 against target/debug/reflow2-mcp, and THE VERDICT NAMED THE BINARY AND ITS BUILD TIME, which is `chg:the-surface-gate-says-which-binary-it-read` visibly working: before that fix this gate reported "ALL 149 MATCH" against a stale build and could not fail.

SECOND RUN THE SAME DAY REPORTED DRIFT (2), AND THAT WAS THE POINT. Adding `documentation` to ChangeType changed two served descriptions — `add_change_event`'s tool description and `set_artifact_checksum`'s `change_type` parameter. The gate named both, they were blessed with `--update`, and the diff shows exactly what moved. A deliberate surface change is therefore distinguishable from drift, which is the whole reason the goldens are committed.

WHAT THIS GREEN DOES NOT SAY, restated because a passing check gets quoted wider than it is: nothing about `ifc:mcp-tools-http` (this drives stdio), nothing about the two-layer error model (a `tools/list` golden cannot see `isError`), and nothing about whether the frozen schemas are RIGHT — only that they have not moved.
properties.name: Every served tool's name, prose, schema and annotations match a committed golden (tools/toolsnap.py, CI on every push)

properties.description: `served_by` STATES staleness rather than leaving a literal to be compared: the block carries `stale` and `stale_note`; an intact binary reads a definite `false`; `stale` is three-valued and a null SAYS unknown rather than borrowing the wording of a definite answer; the stale note names `--stop-shared`, says why a bare session restart changes nothing (`--shared` re-attaches to the same daemon), and warns that the respawn itself fails when the client's binary was replaced too. Five cases in crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/the_server_says_when_it_is_stale.rs.
properties.findings: VERIFIED LIVE ON A RUNNING DAEMON, not only in fixtures, because the `true` branch cannot occur in a test process: a fresh daemon reported `stale: false, binary_mtime_unix: 1786248674`; `cargo build` was then run to relink the binary under it, and the SAME server reported `stale: true, binary_mtime_unix: null` on the next call. That second observation also settled an old puzzle — the `null` mtime dev_storyflow reported as 'best-effort, unavailable' is THIS SAME SIGNAL, since current_exe() returns a path carrying the `(deleted)` marker and metadata() fails on it. The note's wording is asserted against public constants rather than inside `if stale == true`, because a first draft guarded those assertions with that condition and they silently never ran — the vacuous-branch problem this work exists to catch, reproduced in its own test.
properties.name: served_by states staleness rather than leaving a literal to be compared

properties.description:
`crates/reflow2-core/tests/heal.rs` — two checks holding `con:a-sweep-builds-its-network-a-fixed-number-of-times`.

`the_sweep_does_not_get_quadratically_slower_as_candidates_grow` builds two chains of components, 40 and 160 long. Every interior node of a chain is an articulation point, so candidates scale directly with length — which is what makes the test measure the thing the budget is about. It asserts a RATIO under 10x for a 4x size increase.

⚠️ A RATIO, NOT A THRESHOLD, DELIBERATELY. Both halves run on the same machine under the same load, so contention cancels. A bare millisecond bound here would measure the test runner, and the standing response to that is to raise it until it stops complaining — which retires a gate without anybody deciding to. The bar is 10x rather than 1x because 4x the nodes IS genuinely more work: more edges to walk, more nodes to scan. What it forbids is that cost growing with candidates ON TOP of that.

`masking_a_node_gives_the_same_verdict_as_rebuilding_without_it` is the correctness half: on a 5-chain the ends are not single points of failure and the middle is. The optimisation replaced "rebuild the network without this node and recount" with "mask this node in the network already built", and those must agree.

⭐ THE REAL GUARD IS THE TYPE SIGNATURE AND THIS TEST GUARDS WHAT A SIGNATURE CANNOT. The old `is_single_point_of_failure(&self, node_id)` could rebuild because it held `&self`. The new `is_single_point_of_failure_in(&DesignNetwork, baseline, node_id)` is handed the network and has no graph to rebuild from, so the per-candidate cost cannot return inside that function. What it CAN do is return at the call site, by hoisting nothing and calling in a loop — which is exactly what the ratio test catches.

MUTATION-CHECKED, and it bites hard. Putting the per-candidate rebuild back at the call site fails the ratio check at **19.8x** with a message naming the constraint: \"4x the candidates cost 19.8x the time (0.259s -> 5.132s) — the network is being rebuilt per candidate again\". Restoring passes 50 of 50. A guard seen only green is indistinguishable from one that cannot fail.
properties.findings:
2026-08-21. 50 of 50 heal tests pass, whole core suite green, 0 failures.

MEASURED ON reflow2'S OWN DESIGN (2871 nodes), in-memory debug, before and after:

  detect_structural_defects   44.50s  ->   4.43s
  all_defects                 56.32s  ->  16.65s
  is_single_point_of_failure  878ms PER CANDIDATE  ->  5.08ms for ALL 56
  defects found                   54  ->      54   (unchanged)
  structural issues               13  ->      13   (unchanged)

ON THE PATH USERS ACTUALLY TAKE — release binary, real RocksDB, driven over stdio through the real tool surface:

  open_questions   11.7s -> 2.95s     <= the FIRST call of every session
  loop_status      11.4s -> 2.50s
  graph_report     10.9s -> 2.18s warm
  detect_gaps      0.51s -> 0.53s     (untouched, as expected)
  get_node/scan_nodes unchanged

AGAINST THE BUDGET, WHICH IS WHAT DECIDES WHETHER TO STOP: `con:a-sweep-builds-its-network-a-fixed-number-of-times` allows 4 network builds per sweep, independent of candidates. Now 3 — two design networks and one operational network. UNDER BUDGET, SO THE WORK STOPPED.

DELIBERATELY LEFT UNDONE, and each would be a further gain: `sweep_scope` is now the largest remaining part (15.3s of ~32s in-memory), of which `rule_populations` is 9.1s; and `design_network` is still built TWICE per sweep — once in `sweep_scope`, once in `detect_structural_defects` — which sharing would remove. Both are inside budget, so they stop here rather than being taken because they are visible. Reopening them wants its own measurement and its own number.

MUTATION-CHECKED: restoring the per-candidate rebuild fails the ratio check at 19.8x and names the constraint in the message.
properties.name: Four times the candidates does not cost four times the sweep, and masking a node gives the same verdict as rebuilding without it

properties.description: The served vocabulary connects the two halves of retirement: Capability.status's description names OBSOLETES, names `discontinued`, and says `cancelled`/`dropped` is absent ON PURPOSE rather than merely missing; and OBSOLETES's hint names the Decision as the source end, names what it computes, says only an ACCEPTED decision discontinues anything, and says the target's own status does NOT move (crates/reflow2-core/tests/discontinued_is_read.rs, 2 cases, 8 in the file). Pinned rather than trusted for the reason the standing rule is pinned in every skill — a description nothing reads back is one edit from silently disappearing.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED BOTH WAYS: reverting Capability.status to the bare enum kills the first and nothing else; reverting OBSOLETES to its old one-line hint kills the second and nothing else.
properties.name: The served vocabulary connects the two halves of retirement

properties.description: The dependency check works without tomllib, and says what it cannot read (tools/reflow2_check.py, 2026-08-06, 3 cases). HONEST ABOUT ITS LIMITS: on a synthetic manifest holding a multi-line inline table and a [dependencies.X] sub-table, it read the one shape it understands and NAMED BOTH it did not — \"'spans' spans lines, not read\" and \"[dependencies.subtable] sub-table form not read\" — rather than returning a short list that would read as a complete one. No `tomli`, no pip: the kit installs into other people's projects and a runtime dependency is a cost they did not agree to.

WHY IT EXISTS: the check shipped reading only tomllib and its first CI run on reflow2's own repo reported \"could not read any build file to check them\", because ubuntu-22.04 carries Python 3.10. Correct locally, inert on most CI in the world.
properties.name: The dependency check works without tomllib, and says what it cannot read

properties.description:
Eleven cases over the `unallocated_component` rule, in `crates/reflow2-core/tests/structure_with_no_function_is_asked_about.rs`.

THE COUNTERWEIGHTS CARRY MORE WEIGHT THAN THE POSITIVES, because every plausible way this rule goes wrong is a false positive on correct modelling: a parent is not a finding (it is allocated through its children); the parent exemption does NOT extend down to its empty children; a design with no capabilities is not asked, because there is no allocation to have performed yet; and allocating only to a parent must not be reported as never having started, since that claim is about the whole design and would be false in the one sentence its author would act on.

Also pinned: the rollup is ONE finding however many empty boxes (BL-73 anti-flood), its id does NOT move when somebody adds a component (aggregate keying, so an acknowledgement is not expired by an unrelated write), the finding names `propose_allocation` as the method, and a box beside a Flow is still asked what it holds — deliberately NOT inheriting `unallocated_capability`'s PART_OF_FLOW exemption, because "which box performs which step?" is a real question.
properties.findings:
11 passed / 0 failed, on the final tree (`cargo test -p reflow2-core --no-default-features --test structure_with_no_function_is_asked_about`). The whole core suite alongside it: 127 suites, 1469 passed, 0 failed, exit 0.

TWO OF THE ELEVEN EXIST BECAUSE THE FIRST DRAFT WAS WRONG, and both are recorded rather than quietly fixed. `never_started` was derived from "every leaf is empty", which is a different statement wearing the same words — a design that allocated only to its parents has empty leaves and has plainly done the step, and it would have been told "nothing in this design is allocated at all". It now tracks allocation over every component, parents included. The Flow case was undecided rather than wrong, and is now pinned as deliberate in either direction.

⚠️ HOW THE FIRST GREEN ON THIS WORK WAS FALSE, recorded because the mechanism outlives this change: the first full-workspace run was piped through `grep`, so the reported exit code was grep's and not cargo's, and 60 of 150 test binaries had run when it reported success. `fact:a-piped-gate-reports-the-pipes-exit-code-not-the-gates` describes exactly this and it still caught nobody until the suite count was compared against the number of test files on disk.
properties.name: structure_with_no_function_is_asked_about.rs
A coupling with no contract is named as one aggregate question, asks rather than drafts, and stays silent where there is nothing to declare (crates/reflow2-core/tests/detect.rs)

properties.description: `reflow2 update` keeps its word distinct from `init`: a project carrying an install receipt may be updated; a project that was never set up is REFUSED and told to run `reflow2 init`; a project holding a DESIGN but no kit is refused too and told WHY (machine-wide install, in-repo half never run) rather than silently receiving a first install; and the shipped wrapper both dispatches `--update` and states that it never downloads, so nobody expects a new binary from it (tools/test_init.py, 4 cases, 100 in the file). Pins the DISTINCTION, not the refresh — the refresh is `install` and every other case in the file covers it.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS: accepting any directory kills two cases, dropping the design-without-kit branch kills exactly the one that names it, and dispatching `update` as a plain `init` kills the wrapper case. All refusals exit 1, verified by running them.
properties.name: reflow2 update keeps its word distinct from init

properties.description: tools/test_wall_check.py, 11 cases, run in CI on every push. The wall check reads a project's SOURCE from outside reflow2 and compares the coupling it finds against the boundaries the design declares, with no configuration — the design already says where its code lives. Distinct from the structural detectors, which reason about the graph: this one reads the tree and can therefore contradict it.
properties.findings: Run 2026-08-23 on this checkout: 11 cases, all passing (0.739s). Also runs in CI on every push (.github/workflows/ci.yml).
properties.name: A declared wall is checked against the coupling it actually contains

properties.description: what_next answers in four bands, the exploration slot is not optional, and liveness is what makes the shaping band readable (crates/reflow2-core/tests/what_next.rs, 11 cases). THE ONE THAT MUST NEVER REGRESS is a_marked_decision_is_never_ranked_however_it_would_score: a `proposed` Decision carrying AUTHORED_BY role=approver is the user's own durable self-prioritisation — it already existed and was simply never named one — and no computed score may reorder it or demote it into the ranked band, so the test gives a marked decision every scoring signal available and asserts it still never appears there. THE SECOND LOAD-BEARING CASE is a_decision_nothing_points_at_is_still_surfaced. Every ranking signal here is built on connectedness, so a decision nothing points at scores zero forever and would never be shown — dec:bl-155's unused-versus-unreachable trap arriving through a ranking instead of a usage count. A suite that only checked the ranking would stay green while the fifth slot was dropped as over-engineering, which is precisely what the two independent derivations of that slot (the Q-table framing, and Anthony's own "top 4 and bottom 1") exist to prevent. THE SHAPING BAND'S CASES PIN A CAVEAT THIS DESIGN RECORDED BEFORE THE CODE EXISTED: cap:what-next warned that raw GOVERNED_BY in-degree is the wrong signal because its top hit was a pruning decision governing ten DROPPED requirements, and a_decision_governing_only_retired_work_does_not_shape_anything IS that fixture — a 9-dead-node decision must lose to a 3-live-node one. ALSO PINNED: retired governed nodes are COUNTED and reported rather than silently dropped; the shaping band holds only ACCEPTED decisions, never open ones, because it answers a different question for a different reader; `alignment: supporting` on a CONTRADICTS edge is corroboration and must not raise the score, which heal.rs paid for once already; `decision:ack:` review records are excluded both as decisions and as governed sources, because they dominate raw GOVERNED_BY counts (measured, excluding them took that edge type from 867 to 255) so leaving them in makes the answer confidently wrong rather than merely noisy; the unexplored pick is stable across two readings of an unchanged design and ADVANCES when a decision is settled, since the core takes no clock and no RNG and the rotation is derived from the count of accepted decisions; and `not_shown` accounts for every open decision the answer omitted. WHAT IS NOT COVERED, stated rather than left to be discovered: nothing here checks that the WEIGHTS are right. They are a deliberately coarse guide against a stated acceptance criterion of "general ballpark", and the tests assert the ORDER the signals produce, never the absolute numbers.
